reviews.comment: I had her for a different class than the one I had listed here. But the points still remains that she is not really capable of teaching and has a huge ego and I guess the department is making her teach some other classes for the fall.
Beware any class she teaches, she's not good at this and it isnt worth the stress i'm enduring with her. She's teaching other classes this fall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very slow to grade things with very minimal feedback
The reviews check out, unfortunately I didn't check before taking her.

had her for INB-337. All she does is read off the slides, no emotion, no care, nothing interesting in teaching style. She's showed up late to her own class so many times. As of right now she's been late more than on time. Class is boring and she's intentionally vague on assignments.
literally marked me absent EVEN THOUGH I WAS IN CLASS. man she for the love of god can't do her job
Very hard to follow.

NEVER take this class or anything with this teacher. She does not know what she's doing and will make you stress over the class until the last-minute. Not sure why there are random positive reviews here.

This was definitely one of the harder anthropology classes, especially bc I had no genetics background. She lectures very quickly, & I got points off for unimportant stuff, but she's knowledgeable. You can tell she cares more about her research than teaching. Admirable professor but not an easy class - check prior syllabi before registering.
I hated Anthropology after her
Teaching is clearly farrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr from her strong suit.

I liked anthropology.... until her....
I really did try to like her class but she made it downright awful. Now I dislike her class and the topic altogether. :(

reviews.comment: no, just no

reviews.comment: There's better options for sure
Normally I don't write reviews but she was so bad that I had to let others know that if she's teaching then you should stay away.

Lots of reading (~2 scientific papers by the start of each class). Lectures were often too fast to make time for class discussion and student lectures which were unproductive in my opinion. Very disorganized, most assignments had no rubric or clear guidelines and instructions would be changed at the last minute. Was hard to discern what she wanted.
She doesn't know how to teach or really what she's doing
She doesn't do much and doesn't give much information. This class, in her words, is supposed to be easy but she intentionally makes it more difficult.
She doesn't give any rubric, just throws you into the water and expects you to figure it out. Avoid this class if you can
Prof Childebayeva wants you to succeed, just show up to lectures and work with the TA.

The courseload was very heavy, office hours were often cancelled. Had to read 2 scientific research papers and a textbook chapter by every class, had a 5,000-word research paper due at end of the semester and 2 exams worth 30% of the grade. Found it hard to keep up with slides in lecture due to the speed of her lectures and lack of explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best math teacher I've ever had. I took her for calc one and for lectures you would read the textbook before class and then complete a really short online assignment. The weekly homework load was very manageable. subject was explained very well and always answered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a new professor at UT but friendly. Lectures are straightforward. Homeworks are short. She offers plenty of support if you're confused. Participation work is required on Mondays, but she gives makeups for it. Exams closely follow the practice materials and HW, though they can get tricky—especially the final. Highly recommend!

The course content itself is incredibly easy. If you get stuck, she is very helpful over email/office hours. I did very well on the HWs and midterms, but I just barely got an A bc of the final, which is weighted 30%. In-class activities once a week for a participation grade. Handwriting is a bit difficult to read at times.

Really great experience taking her for Probability 1. Explains everything very clearly and tests are pretty easy as long as you are familiar with the material. Gives a lot of really good prep material for the tests too.
Really great and caring professor. Good lecturer as well, although attendance wasn't mandatory — take if you can.

Dr. Adams is a great lecturer, but it's the lengthy daily readings that made me dread going to this class, as well as the weekly quizzes.  You truly will learn a lot, but unless you like learning out of an online textbook and then going and being talked at about it, I don't recommend.  If you're looking for an easy a though, take her Rome class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I fell ill and had to drop.  The nature of the course is fast paced but I love the way she has the course structured and once I understood the flow it got so much easier.  It takes time to learn another language but the way she teaches does make it really fun. I plan to take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT I'm a classics minor but I feel like even if you don't know anything about classics it's very accessible. Dr. Adams pairs the readings and movies so well and it is just such an interesting class. I'm also not a big horror movie person but still loved it, definitely recommend. Also not too much work!

Overall decent and lenient professor. I definitely recommend taking one of her classes for a VAPA. I took her in Fall 2024, and we had no tests, just daily annotations, weekly quizzes, and one final project. The final project is also very vague and you get to be pretty creative with it.

This class is a simple but engaging VAPA that Dr. Adams structured to be easy. The class is beyond manageable and has little to no workload as long as you pay attention to the lectures, do the readings, and study a bit for the weekly quizzes. There were no exams in the class, and instead of a final, there is a fun final project. Highly Recommended!

I'd die for Lizzy. If you didnt like her you probably thought you could get away with doing nothing, which is just plain lazy and you only have yourself to blame. Loved her lectures, she's so funny. Have to buy tophat for attendance. No tests, just weekly quizzes with 2 drops and a final project. Loved this class so much, it was really interesting.

Every day I woke up for MWF, I hoped for a lime scooter to bulldoze through me on speedway for the sole reason of not attending this class. I dreaded even opening my eyes and having to walk to this class. Tears.. straight tears... this professor drove me to insanity. Take her if you want permanent migraines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory and even though I was in the hospital I wasn't able to exempt the weekly quizzes or attendance making this drop my GPA. Teacher did not care and was told some quizzes were mandatory even though I could not make it because of my medical condition.

Dr. Adam's is a lively and compassionate professor, who clearly understands her class is a VAPA that's not meant to be hard or time consuming. Graded mainly by participation in class and 2-ish weekly reading assignments that are chill. Quizzes every Friday that are specific, but no tricks and are pulled straight from lecture. Super chill class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for my VAPA, but she doesn't include a lot of content about art, so if you aren't an art person this class is for you. Dr. Adams is super understanding, kind, and funny. The quizzes are nitpicky, but you get used to it. She is a very entertaining lecturer and I learned so much!

The professor includes small details on the quiz so If you're not really interested in Ancient Rome, it's hard to get good grades on them unless you put in a lot of effort. The lectures can be interesting at times but as mentioned if you're not passionate about the subject, it's just not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures. Have to pay to use tophat. She records lectures but doesn't upload slides. Didn't study and still did fine. Towards the end turned on location tracking bc people were skipping. overall not bad and interesting, just thought she was a bit too upset about attendance things that weren't a big deal as that happens in every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Every Thursday night I'd stare at my ceiling fan wondering if I could launch into another universe—one where Rome had never been founded. I studied, cried, studied more, and still got obliterated. Took this for an art credit and found less art than on tax forms. I'd rather eat cement than take this class again. Emotionally shattered. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams's lectures are always engaging and interesting, and the content of the course is intriguing. There are daily readings that are a bit tedious but can be completed in 15 min or less. There are no exams, just weekly quizzes that take questions directly from the lectures and a final project. Overall a very easy and fun vapa.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams and the TA Lane are super knowledgable! i took this class for my CEHET and the material was pretty interesting imo. attendance is graded, but i never talked ehe. quiz due every day of class (therefore a bit of reading) but its calm. there r no exams, only projects! super lit and easy and fun take her if u can!

Loves to talk and elaborate on topics, especially if you engage. Weekly quizzes with no exams (experimental, 1st class to do so), readings to annotate, and a creative final project. If you love reading and/or Ancient Roman history, you will excel in this class. Attendance is also a must; they are recorded based on effort (quizzes are code-locked).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: EASY VAPA! Her lectures were interesting and she knows what she's talking about. The grade was based on homework readings (persuall) + quizzes (every Friday based on lectures) + participation (tophat questions). Take her if you can!!

Horror in Classics and Film was a LOT of fun, and this was my favorite course of the semester. Dr. Adams is a very fun lecturer, and I enjoyed all of the readings and movies that she selected for this class. There is a good amount of reading, but if you like mythology, you will enjoy them all (I did!).

Dr. Adams is a great prof and made the content pretty engaging. I took for GC credit and think its pretty easy A if you just do the work. Grade made up of annotations (2/week), weekly quiz, in-class participation (not accuracy), and final proj. Fun times I love Ancient Rome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was a blast. As a STEM major, I took this class as my VAPA, and I honestly could not have asked for anything better. Lectures were engaging, the material was interesting, and it really wasn't that difficult. There were a lot of readings, but they didn't take too long. As long as you show up to class and do the hw, you're guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't particularly love history, but Professor Adams made the content really interesting. Her lectures were really funny and informative. Grade was made up of annotations (2-3 times a week), quizzes (once a week), and participation (during class). Quizzes were fair and relatively easy if you took good notes and studied a little beforehand.

Heavy on reading between classes, though the annotations that were required were graded very easily. Weekly quizzes on Friday, but they were pretty easy to do well on if you just studied for half an hour. Relatively entertaining lectures, definitely tries to accommodate well for her students.

Professor Adams was superb! Her lectures were so engaging and interesting, she is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about this course. Homework readings consist of a few annotations. Mandatory quizzes every Friday with questions from lectures and hmwrk readings. No final. Participation is recommended. Easy A for a VAPA. Take her!!!!

Professor Adams is an engaging lecturer and makes it easy to get an A if you do the work. Grading was based on attendance questions during lectures, assigned readings, and an in-class quiz at the end of the week with the final being an open-ended project on the course subject. If you follow the readings and attend class, you'll be fine.

Lectures were good but there was homework after every lecture, which could sometimes be long. We had weekly quizzes, which were fairly easy as long as you did the homework and paid attention in the lecture.

Dr. Adams is great! She is very clear with how she describes topics during lecture, and the homework is not too hard. The class is very easy as long as you pay attention to lectures and show up to class. Grade is based off of attendance, participation, homework (one is due before each class), and quizzes. The quizzes are fair; take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Very fascinating lectures, found myself very interested. Participation polls during class. Weekly quizzes covering lecture material, pretty easy. Tests are also relatively light.

Professor is very down to earth and easy to approach. Gives material to read outside of class - sometimes a lot, but rarely boring.

Overall, very enjoyable class.

I agree that this class is not an easy A for VAPA. Her weekly quizzes are hard, especially the select-all questions. Midterm is not cumulative. The first midterm is hard but the rest are much easier. I enjoy her lecture and have fun learning about Ancient Roman. Pay attention in the lecture, review nots before the exam. All answers are on the slide

I had Dr. Adams for Intro to Ancient Rome (VAPA and Global Cultures Flag). An A in this course requires some effort but is not overwhelming. Attend class, take notes, do the assigned readings, and study for the quizzes and midterms, and you will be fine. Dr. Adams wants students to succeed in her class and is there to help you. No complaints.

Dr. Adams is a really thoughtful professor. I took her Ancient Rome class for my VAPA, and in the beginning it was QUITE intimidating, however, as the semester progressed I did better in the class. This class isn't an "easy VAPA" but it's doable. Beware of weekly quizzes, they have tricky questions. The tests are reasonable, and I did well on them.

Dr. Adams is chill and tries to make her lectures entertaining; however, she provides so much material that it can feel like you are drowning in it. Grade is made up of 3 exams, which you should definitely study for if you want to pass because she makes oddly specific questions, weekly quizzes, in class participation, and a few discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Adams is very passionate about what she teaches, and as a result assumes that students have a foundational knowledge of Classical Myth, and starts teaching harder material from day 1. Attendance is taken through TopHat and the worst part of this class by FAR are the mandatory Friday quizzes which are unnecessary and oddly specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is a cool, hilarious, and compassionate professor. Her lectures were so funny, and she made mythology so interesting and fun to learn about. There are weekly quizzes on Friday, and one exam before the final. They're all very easy so long as you keep up with the material. I really liked her for mythology. Take Dr. Adams!

Dr. Adams is so much fun to have as a professor. Her lectures are engaging and funny and made even the boring parts of the class fun to learn! Super lenient grader, just had to do a handful of discussion posts, weekly quizzes, and the midterm + final. The exams & quizzes are easy and straight forward if you do the reading and pay attention in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There's assignments due every Thursday and Sunday and aren't too bad. Quizzes aren't hard just make sure you're familiar with some of the material. ID assignments aren't graded hard, they only take points if the information is incorrect or if you did the same topic as someone else. Overall, a good class especially if you want to learn about Rome

I took this as an online course for my vapa, so I didn't interact with Dr. Adams. But I emailed a few times with the teaching team and they responded quick! Assignments were due weekly on Thursdays and Sundays. 3 quizzes and a small discussion post per week, so not terrible. Just make sure to prioritize time for the course and don't blow it off!

I really love professor Adams. Her class is very engaging and she is super accommodating. She makes the course as fair and easy as possible. While there is still a lot of reading and effort in the final project, the material itself is not difficult. My only critique is that she does not answer her email. But she is still understanding/accommodating

I took Intro to Ancient Rome online with Dr. Adams. Since the class was online, I never interacted with her but she seemed very sweet from her recordings. Don't be fooled by the fact that this class is online, there is still a lot of work that you have to put in. However, if you do your assignments (they're not hard at all), it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It was a lot of work to go through all the modules and the exams weren't easy, but I really enjoyed the class, and it was nice that I could do it on my own time.

Professor Adams is a great lecturer. She makes the class very interesting and involves the students too. But, the class requires loads of reading and she isn't someone who will just give you an A. You have to work hard and be very good at writing to get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Lizzy for Intro to Classical Mythology and it was definitely my favorite class I have taken at UT. Lizzy is hilarious and I genuinely enjoyed her class. Best professor by far! Her lectures are also amazing. There is a lot of reading required for the class but they are super easy and enjoyable for the most part. Take this class if you can!

Took Introduction to Classical Mythology. Lizzy is an amazing professor. She is young, super cool, and hilarious. The lectures are super interesting and very helpful in understanding the material. She is easy to reach through email and highly responsive. Exams aren't bad - just study. Go to SI! One downside - lots of reading, like, every night.
Lizzie's great--- always answers questions, super chill
Overall Lizzie was a great TA and definitely helped clarify issues I had within the class. She was always very helpful and timely with her answers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy, you just have to keep up with your work, but you can definitely put it off until the last minute if you really want to lol. The module quizzes were pretty sucky because the questions vary in difficulty and sometimes you get stuck with a whole bunch of hard ones, but other than that it was a pretty awesome class.

Really sweet guy, but like other reviews said he kind of struggles with lecturing in a clear, easy-to-understand way if you don't already know the subject material. It's clear he knows a lot about what he's teaching, but you'll definitely need to study outside of class. Overall a pretty average class experience.

He does seem very sweet, and I can tell he's trying, but for the portion I was there for (electrochemistry) I genuinely never had any clue what was going on during class. I felt like he was just saying things, but I could never follow the lecture. I did manage to do well on the first exam somehow, but honestly try for another professor if possible.
I found it kind of hard to be engaged with his lectures, but it's clear he knows what he's talking about. It was a pretty normal class I'd have to say, and he is very friendly and approachable.

For his materials chemistry course his test reviews did not actually prepare us for what would be on the tests. Topics would be on there we hadn't even really covered. He seems like he knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgeable, just not the best at preparing us for exams and thus our grades kind of took a hit because of this.

Dr. Aubrey class wasn't the best but it was manageable. He gives you two attempts on the reading and lecture quizes which is pretty nice. The problem is that if you dont do the reading before lecture you will be lost in his lectures. He's a great professor to talk to about research and he will try his best to help you out. He's very approachable.

Dr. Aubrey seems like such a sweet, knowledgeable professor, but he can't teach. His lectures are quite scattered and he struggles to simplify things for the intro-level course this is. The lecture quizzes are also absurdly difficult. It's his second year, so hopefully he'll figure it out soon. But for now, brace yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: very disorganized; posted the study guide the day before the test; hated lectures; I liked the material I was learning but boring lectures and intense readings make it hard to engage with the class; it is an especially hard transition from laude to aubrey... good luck :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he is trying his best, as he has just started teaching. however, exams do not resemble quizzes and reviews are not at the level of the exams, so studying is difficult. feels like the level is way too high for a gen chem class. i am biased since i did not take ap chem, so i do have to put in extra effort since this material is completely new.

I would definitely avoid Dr. Aubrey for CH302C if possible. It was his first time teaching the course, he wasn't clear on how grading worked and didn't attempt to explain concepts in class whatsoever. I pray that Laude goes back to teaching it because he is not good with underclassmen. Harsher ratings were suspiciously removed...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Aubrey is knowledgeable about the topics he taught, but it was his first time teaching this course, so his lectures were confusing even after reading the textbook pages that were assigned. This was often due to his wanting to talk about real-life applications of these topics. He also taught us inorg chem instead of prepping us for ochem.

As everyone said, he's a brilliant man. He clearly knows what he's teaching but doesn't yet know how to deliver it (at least not to freshmen). He records his lectures, so I would advise skipping class and watching them on your own time. The books are difficult to understand, but the lectures contain relevant information that is tested on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is a very kind and smart man, but he probably shouldn't be teaching first-year students. I am sure his upper division and graduate courses are amazing, he just expects a bit too much for gen chem. That being said, the class is extremely doable if you work hard to understand the concepts and you will be better off because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is an incredibly smart and kind man, but his class is difficult and he doesn't seem to have much experience teaching freshman. Textbook is hard to understand, and the course is almost entirely self-taught. There's hardly any homework to cushion your grade (5%), and quiz questions are made from scratch which makes them hard to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aubrey is a brilliant professor, he doesn't have experience teaching a freshman, general chemistry audience though. I'm genuinely confused why he was picked to teach this class, but it was clear he tried his best to deliver factual, relevant information. Tips to succeed: Housecroft will not help you, but study groups and ChemLibre will.

Lectures are hard to follow and are frequently focused on interesting but ultimately irrelevant applications or details of course content, making tests and quizzes very difficult. The textbooks are the best way to learn the test/quiz relevant material. He's kind and clearly very knowledgeable about the content, but doesn't convey it well.

Prof. Aubrey makes Gen Chem 2 pretty challenging because he chooses to cover very complex topics other professors don't, but it's still a very doable course. No homework outside of class besides readings, and the quizzes over lectures. Exams are fair game, but definitely have to take good lecture notes and put work in to grasp concepts

I don't think Dr. Aubrey should be teaching Gen Chem 2. His quizzes are hard and you can't study for them because he puts a harder version of the example that you have never seen, he makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. He doesn't explain things during lecture and expects us to know a lot (we are 2nd semester first-year students).

Prof. Aubrey is new at teaching this class and pretty bad at it so far. His quizzes are inconsistent, difficult, and have had lots of mistakes. He does not explain things at all and assumes we should know everything. This is Gen Chem 2 for chem majors and makes me want to change my major. :(

This class is recommended for the chemistry major/honors track and so most of us thought we had to take it, but you do not have to! Dr. Aubrey is one of those guys that are just way too smart to be teaching intro to gen chem. Because he is so smart he does not explain nor teach very well. He is not a good teacher, but he is nice, I don't recommend.

The semester started rough with difficult quizzes that tanked grades, but slowly the structure of the class got better and more organized. Lectures are sometimes pretty boring, but you can tell Dr. Aubrey puts effort into his class and is always willing to help if needed. Dr. Aubrey is very nice, but I don't know if I would recommend his class yet.

She cares more about instapoll than attendance/learning. The content for this class is learnable but not through her lectures. If you do understand the material (outside sources), the hw and tests are pretty easy. Lots of partial credit.

The class structure is very consistent, and it is always obvious what is expected of you. Show up to class and understand concepts and you'll be fine. Grading is generous and allows you chances to learn through your mistakes. Overall, would recommend!

I went back here to say that I am so glad Im taking other BME professors rn that are genuinely qualified to teach at this level and material. After going through several of her classes, I almost lost faith in pursuing BME. She dropped my grade by a letter grade for not taking an instapoll during an exam I literally took and directly handed to her.
every day i drove to this class without wearing my seatbelt in hope of going to the hospital instead of class. genuinely one of the worst professors ever!!! made me switch to mech e.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Instructor is condescending in Office Hours. TA never shows up to Office hours. LA was very helpful tho so go to them for help. Heat transfer is pretty difficult and instructor struggles with teaching it because of staffing issues so be prepared. 1 exam is dropped so try to do well for them and don't take final exam unless you have to.

She was good for fluids but not heat transfer at all. That unit was an absolute nightmare. Be sure to go to every class because she has pop quizzes. She goes through instapoll later in the semester and cross checks to ensure proper attendance.

Professor has a very disorganized style of teaching. Very difficult to follow. Never solved problems fully in class, claiming that she would mess up on the math (which ig she did anyways). Never paid attention to her in class because its frankly a waste of time. I recommend watching Dr. John Biddle's lectures on youtube.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She cares way more about Instapolls (which she takes even during exam days), than showing your mastery of the material. Wish she just had a sign-in sheet. Lecturing style is monotone with slow pacing; shows no enthusiasm in the material. You'll learn way more from watching CPPMechEngTutorials, who saved me during the heat transfer unit.

Lectures didn't make sense to me, but watching a YouTube video would always suffice. Exams are super easy. Attendance is mandatory, and if you miss more than 6 lectures, you receive a 10% grade deduction.
She emphasizes showing your work and gives most of the credit for the process, which makes it easier to get a good grade

Even when I was physically in class and completed Instapoll, I was marked “absent” because I had not taken the optional bonus quiz. No clear communication, policies that were not detailed in the syllabus were suddenly enforced later. One additional absence results in a 10% drop from your overall grade. Grade dropped from A to B.
Instructor cares more about instapoll than actual learning - even when there was proof that you were jn class.
Just be ready for her to single handily ruin your entire life and any future prospects of you enjoying your major. I hope to never set foot in her class again. Please avoid at all costs.
Dr. Adams spends most of the lecture giving a poor explanation of concepts and limited or incorrect application to the field of BME.
I loved the consistent structure of Adams' classes. She is very fair and has a fun personality. You get a lot of credit for just showing your work on homework, quizzes, and exams.

Hands down my favorite BME professor at UT! She's incredibly caring, energetic, and funny. Her ability to simplify complex concepts makes them easy to grasp, and she teaches consistent problem-solving strategies that work no matter the difficulty. The extra credit practice problems are a huge help for exams!

No idea why she is teaching so many classes for being new here. It's very apparent how stretched thin she is with her basically learning as she reads the slides, so be warned bc the bme department does not gaf at all. Good luck getting through a single lecture, you'll be learning outside 100% of the time.

Professor Adams was nice but didn't really know how to teach biomechanics. She wouldn't really go over what was going to be covered each day--she would just start doing an example and you had to figure out what was going on. Homework sometimes took an incredibly long time, and the grading system was pretty harsh on tiny mistakes.

I liked Dr. Adams approach to the class(ie: cheat sheets on exams, weekly quizzes, ect), but a lot of the class was teach yourself to do well. The weekly quizzes were often difficult, and covered stuff in the lab, which means you were cooked if you had lab after the quiz. Overall, would take Dr. Adams again, shes a sweet professor.

Dr. Adams is a caring professor. It was her first time teaching BME313L so she didn't always know what was going on, but I thought she was pretty good for BME344. Quizzes and homework were tough but manageable if you put in the time and effort. Opportunities for extra credit if you are willing to put in the work. I enjoyed being in her class.

Strict on attendance with no leniency w those instapolls. Tests are only doable if you get outside help from anyone else. Difficult experience with her methods of teaching, which include reading off of slides and struggling to get through a single problem. Wish she was more understanding

You will have better luck taking anyone else. She doesn't understand the material, or care, so her lack of understanding will rub off of you. She is not accommodating at all; she won't come to any sort of understanding with you about attendance or any other concern. Probably THE most difficult professor I had to deal with and you will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, I never hated this professor until it came to how unmoving and disingenuous she is. No matter the situation you are in she does not care, dog died? too bad. Mental health crisis? good luck! You relay on teaching yourself and TAs, steer clear of her if you can especially for numerical methods. (i've taken 3 of her classes)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Adams clearly did not want to teach Numerical. Not her fault due to lack of BME staff, but she could have put more effort into understanding the material herself. Quizzes were difficult w/avgs around 14/20 but exams were easy. Labs were difficult as they would occur BEFORE we learned the material. It seemed like Adams was learning WITH us.

I love Adams! (as a person) while her circuits class was amazing, she's not that well suited for biomechanics nor numerical methods. She's sometimes as confused as we are, while this is no way her fault (due to the little amount of bme professors). Honestly, teach yourself before lecture, stay on top of your work and it should be a breeze.

I had three of her classes and I wish I was with another professor. Everyone I talk to also agrees that she is not good at teaching; she sounds just as confused reading the slides as I am. Weekly quizzes and attendance is graded.
She is a great professor and is very kind and welcoming when students have trouble understanding the content.

This was her first time teaching the class so it was a bit unorganized at times. However, she is very nice and helpful when you are confused in class. Always tries to make class more engaging when the content may be boring at times. Lots of homework so try to stay on top of the work. The midterms and final are graded pretty fairly.

Dr. Adams is new, so she's developing her teaching style. She grades very generously and uses the GUESS method to give points, so follow it and you'll be fine. Exams are similar to exam reviews and homeworks are much harder than the exams so don't worry. Weekly quizzes and potential extra credit makes going in person worth it. I enjoyed her class.

Dr. Arredondo is the most kind and caring professor I have had throughout my time at UT. You can tell she truly cares about her students and has compassion for them as human beings! Her classes are easy and you actually learn useful things! Her lectures are engaging, lots of videos and activities! So fun! Take her classes!

Dr. Arredondo is incredibly kind and her lectures and tests are extremely easy and somewhat common sense. Her powerpoints are super easy to understand and help a lot with the tests. The grading distribution is very fair and you will without a doubt get an A, highly recommend her class!!

I had her this semester and I was scared because she had little reviews. However, she was so so sweet and literally will help you with anything. Super approachable as well. I didn't pay attention in class also 6 free absences and I studied the day or two before the exams and I did well on the exams. Memorization based exams mostly. Just take her!

I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and interactive. The content wasn't hard to follow, very straightforward. Studied on the day of the exams and made an A on all of them. Just do your work and pay attention and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Arredondo! The class is easy - just common sense with some extra detail.   All of the assignments had clear-cut grading criteria; if you ever have trouble, she and her TA were very helpful. Exams were simple as well, Quizlet was great for studying. Readings were assigned but I rarely did them.
It is an easy class. Go to class, take notes, and review the PowerPoints. The only way to fail is if you don't pay attention or go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance is worth 10pts but you get 6 free absences! Exams are straightforward and most questions are given to you on the in class review.Homework is due every Saturday, but it is not hard. Sibo is a great TA and gives good feedback. Take her class!

1 homework per week due on Saturday, 3 exams, and 1 article  review split into two assignments. Her grading is very clear, and she is always gives feedback or clarity. Exams are straightforward; most questions come from the study guide given in class. Participation is mandatory but you get 6 free absences
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's passionate and very well-versed in conservation, but in turn means she's a harsh grader. Will take off points for grammar, formatting, punctuation, etc. Also a very slow grader; did not start receiving grades til the start of March (mid-sem). Expect to do a homework assignment due before every class. Exams are FRQ heavy.

reviews.comment: this course felt like so much work. Always hard to find big project assignment instructions on canvas. disorganized. Very harsh grader. Curriculum is very interesting! Good lecturer, not much class interaction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I genuinely struggled trying to get myself to show up to this class. I was excited to take ecology but it was nothing like I expected. She didn't give us anything to prepare for exams. This class was so much harder than it needed to be & very unorganized. It was disheartening because I've heard other 373 classes are so much easier. Not an easy A
I genuinely struggled trying to get myself to show up to this class. I was excited to take ecology but it was nothing like I expected. She cod

Class was interesting honestly. It felt like she was learning content for the first time with us, and honestly lots of what was on the slides was very surface-level. Exams were odd, and she refuses to give practice problems otherwise she's "giving us the answers". Not the worst professor ever, but I expected better.

She knows her stuff and loves her field, but she does not know how to teach. The entire class is her lecturing at students, making it difficult to stay engaged. Students often slept while she lectured lol. Three exams and no drops, so if you bomb the first exam (our class average was a 69!), there's no way of getting an A. Very discouraging.

This man is NOT accessible outside of class, doesn't answer emails, and isn't clear in his lectures. He rambles about easy concepts and speeds through the difficult stuff. His exams are only 3 q's. If you take this class DON'T FORGET THE QUEST HW he won't mention it in class or put it on Canvas. The material itself seems easy, he makes it hard.

DO NOT TAKE if no experience in calc. 2 exams, 3 questions each all purely based on bad lectures. notes and lectures not posted, does not respond to emails, must rely on your own notes to study. discussion and HW not what is related to exams. there are better calc teachers. avoid or get ready to get a C for getting 1 question on the exam wrong.

LITERALLY THE GOAT! Didn't show up to class for a whole month or two but still end up with an A. The exam is basically what is covered during exam review session, and final is not cumulative. 3 quizzes drops, 2-4 HW drops. THIS IS FOR M 427L.

Horrible teaching style, boring lectures, and unclear grading. Grades everything last minute so you don't know your actual standing until the end of the semester. Class time with the TA every other day gets you nowhere-- it's all busy work with a group you're randomly assigned to and nobody pulls any weight.

Macedo requires you to solve the questions in his own way which can be really annoying for tests. I struggled with Calculus and did not find the lectures that helpful. Most people generally get good grades but the instruction was not great.

TAKE AVI!!! I absolutely loved his class. He crafted slideshows just for us and according to the topics that WE wanted to learn about. He's so kind and funny and cares so much for his students' success.

Avi is an absolute GEM of a professor. His classroom feels like home. He's so kind and welcoming, and he TAILORS THE CLASS MATERIAL TO THE CLASS based on our interests in subject material. He's also accessible out of class at Schulchan Ivrit or by email. He will improve your Hebrew drastically, and you'll have fun learning!

Dr. Blitz is one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. He will go out of his way to help you, and he cares tremendously for his students. Loved the atmosphere of his class. I am shocked to see that others claim to have not liked his class: I have a feeling they weren't expecting Hebrew to be so difficult. Take him, you'll learn so much!

I would definitely not recommend. This professor demonstrates a lack of care for his students and total apathy about the subject im interested in. A very poor experience I give 0 as a score if I coyld
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he grades really tough on homeworks (i got a lot of 60s) and there's hw everyday + weekly quizzes. good at teaching, supportive but sometimes unsympathetic (or has too high expectations of how easily we can retain words). accessible through groupme or text, not email. class discussions sometimes became anti-Palestine which was uncomfortable

I can't say enough great things. Very caring and gives wonderful feedback. By far the most supportive and invested professor I have had. Her students are lucky to have her. Expect a well-structured class that you will really learn from.

Took for Rhetoric of City Streets. You get to choose a topic related to Austin that interests you to research for the whole semester. Most smaller assignments are completion pass/fail, with two large essays, and one final multimedia project. Definitely recommend!

I loved taking Rhetoric of City Streets with Professor Taylor so much that now every time a new course schedule comes out, I check for her name specifically to see if she's teaching a new class that I could take. There is writing, obviously, but she gives you plenty of class time to work on the projects and offers great, constructive feedback.

a true hidden gem for a writing flag. tookrhetoric of city streets with her and do not regret it. super flexible and caring and the class is actually very interesting. papers do tend to be on the heavier side, but taylor is always willing to help and grades leniantly. you also have a lot of opportunities for extra credit!

Dr. Barchas is unclear on what is expected from students and gives contradictory information on assignments. She is good at lecture, but cannot communicate assignments. She also didn't tell us we had to come up with a UNIQUE object for the final assignment until the day we were allowed to choose objects, so start thinking now if you have her.

Not a bad class, definitely can be fun if you like close reading and Jane Austen. Relied mostly on TA, I had Emma and she was super nice and accessible. Lots of reading and writing super early though. Midterm annd quizzes isn't that bad if you just pay attention to lectures though. Tons of extra credit opportunities, total 5% extra possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Not as bad as others say it is. Lots of reading but you can get by skimming it.
As long as you write according to the professor's style in class, you'll do fine on the three writing assignments. Quite a unique class. Mandatory discussion attendance but you get 3 skips. Amazing and helpful TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Barchas has a psycho-sexual relationship with Jane Austen. She obsesses over her to the point of sucking out all the fun of her novels. When first signing up, I read the warnings of this class, and ignored them. I thought I would be the exception - I love to read, write, and I'm well versed in Austen. Listen to me now: you are NEVER the exception.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You will enjoy this class if you enjoy reading and literature. It is VERY ready heavy, so be prepared to annotate and keep track of details, but lectures were super helpful when it came to essay writing and quizzes. If you can write well, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting, but the class is so difficult for no reason. The TAs do all the grading, and they are both really different in terms of grading, as one is really harsh while the other one lets bs slide. Don't take this class if you have a choice, find something else in the first week, because I promise you ITS NOT WORTH IT.
this prof is ruder than a b and is a cheeky nancy just flat out annoying to be in class

This class was HARD, don't get me wrong. The reading/paper-writing was overwhelming at times, but honestly, it was worth it as someone who genuinely loves Jane Austen and was okay with committing a lot of time to learn more about her books. Just DO NOT take this class unless you also love Jane Austen!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of writing, with no writing flag. Quizzes are heavily based off of what is said during lecture. Grades are also based on what TA is grading, so if you have a harsh TA, then you might not score as high in the class as others.Lots of reading in short periods of time as well (4 novels). Honestly, I only read and wrote about the first 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class as a UGS was VERY challenging. It was a lot for me to balance with other classes that were much more important. I ended up getting an A but it was a lot of trial and error which I struggled with. Be ready to put in more effort than expected but you will be fine if you're in this class! Professor Barchas is very fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you are taking this UGS beware. It's so difficult for no reason that everything is graded very hard. It is possible to get an A but only if you put in a lot of effort which was a real struggle for me since I had a lot of other classes to juggle. DO NOT TAKE THIS IF YOU HAVE A CHOICE. It was honestly awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: GET READY TO READ FR. there are three books you have to read. there are no clear rubrics for any assignments, so you have no idea where your grade is coming from. She's honestly an icon, so I can't be mad at her. Also, if you max out on extra credit, an 89 is an A (because you can get up to 5 points on your average added).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For an UGS, this course was unreasonably difficult. Dr. Barchas is a harsh grader and it is almost impossible to an A on an assignment. The only thing that saved me was my TA. The lectures are interesting and Dr. Barchas is passionate about Austen. This UGS is not for the weak. Beware and good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas is somewhat unapproachable and has very strict views when it comes to grading. Students never get access to the rubric and expectations for all assignments are not made clear whatsoever. Lectures are somewhat useful as they serve as material for the quizzes, research papers, and midterm. Attendance is mandatory for discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Do not listen to most of the negative reviews on this. This is not a blow-off class, but I think it's worth it. Barchas doesn't take BS, and it made me a better writer. I got an A+ in the class and I didn't read every book all the way through. If you aren't completely incompetent, you will be totally fine. Interesting content, smart professor!

Barchas is harsh but she is very knowledgeable and teaches a lot of information well. This course was definitely challenging for a UGS but our class became a community. Grading is determined mainly by your TA and there are no rubrics which made essay writing hard. The canvas is a bit outdated and confusing but office hours will be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nearly impossible to receive a grade higher than a B+. Considering this is a UGS, that's unreasonable and laughable. Barchas' main statement was, "We do not read for plot." Course should not be titled "Jane Austen on page & screen" if we are just looking at the historical context + significance/meaning of specific words/objects during the time.

Dr. Barchas is super funny and I can tell she wants the best for her students. A lot of the class is trial and error which can be frustrating. If you are looking for a blow-off UGS, this is not the one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of fun extra credit. So much reading. Prof is a tiny bit unapproachable but not in a bad way. The essay topics are interesting and make you think, but are totally doable. She's also a good lecturer and knows so much about Austen. I will say it was a bit much for a simple UGS class and was kind of more of a pain (at times) but overall was nice
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory on Fridays for discussion with the TAs. Hard graders and doesn't provide a lot of information for each assignments which are only 3 mini essays, oral presentation and weird museum scavenger hunt. Lecture at 8am on Tuesday and Thursdays are so pointless and boring, fell asleep almost every time I attended. Hard & weird class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. B is difficult to please. The course content is interesting, but the pace of reading 4 novels in a semester is grueling. The learning curve is high and Barchas can be condescending at times if your ideas don't match her own. Overall, there are easier UGS classes. My saving grace is that my TA was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was my third class with Prof. B, and I  have so much respect for her. She can undoubtedly be intimidating, and her grading is a bit harsh, especially on your first assignments. However, her main goal is always to make you better and she is very good at doing so! This class was a great course to cover the inquiry flag and learn about research.

This class is grueling, but I honestly think Prof B made me a better writer. The feedback on research papers is extremely constructive, but 4 difficult novels was a LOT of reading for one semester. The TA was incredible, but unless you have a passion for literature that feels unbreakable, there are easier UGS courses. Know what you're getting into.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Barchas will make you wish you never knew how to read. She's extremely rude, and will make you feel ashamed if you have reach out and ask for help. Expects her students to be obsessed with Jane Austen, even though we are taking the class to earn a mere credit. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas has high expectations and can be a tough grader. However, her lectures are some of the best I've had, and her curriculum improved my essay-writing skills immensely. She is extremely knowledgeable and well-respected in the Jane Austen community.

I never cried over assignments before taking this professor. My problem with this course is, as a UGS, the pacing can be very overwhelming. She is a tough grader, and the assignments require a lot of brainpower to conceptualize. She can also be very condescending in feedback. Amazing lecturer but there are much less stressful UGS' you could take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked Jane Austen until I took this class. Hard grader, claims that we don't read for plot but for vague pass by references you would never get. I thought I was a good writer until this class. When I asked for help, I felt looked down on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. B is very challenging but so worth it! She's a harsh grader, and you'll probably have a bit of a learning curve at the start of the semester, but as you understand her expectations and grading style you'll improve. Her critiques are harsh but are genuinely meant to make you better. She rewards improvement and wants to see you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a class for the faint of heart when it comes to reading/writing. Although perhaps Professor Barchas took a different outlook on classes this semester because she was totally awesome. Super witty, perhaps a bit condescending at times. Regardless, her class was great, and I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: If you're not willing to devote some serious time to this class, I wouldn't take it. Professor Barchas can come across as scary or intimidating but she really does root for your success. The workload was definitely a little bit heavy, but she was extremely open to suggestions from students. We were all at least a little sad when we said bye to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Burchas was my UGS professor and it was rough. It felt like no matter what I did, I could not be successful. Especially when writing papers. I ended up dropping the class because I refused to let a UGS drop my GPA as much as it was going to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I must admit my writing, in general, has improved since taking her class. However, she is challenging and is very vague on how she grades essays. She will make you question everything you write in an essay. She can be condescending sometimes to. I would not recommend her class if you don't like Jane Austin and if you are an ok writer.

The grading criteria for essays is unclear and vague. The professors and TAs are stubborn and slightly condescending. The only good thing about this class is that the quizzes are easy. I wouldn't recommend this class for anyone. Even you like Jane Austen, I'm sure this class would kill whatever passion you had for her works.

reviews.comment: Professor Barchas' "Jane Austen on Page and Screen" is an obsessive and impossible course that is headed by someone whose passion for Jane Austen has turned them into a pretentious scholar who cannot relate to nor teach their students. If you were a good writer in High School, you will find that none of your skills will be good enough for her.

reviews.comment: I took the class because I love Jane Austen novels, but that love is gone now. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm a Sophomore now and this is easily the worst professor I've had in my three semesters. Had her for my UGS. I attended all the lectures, went to office hours often, and did all the homework and still did poorly. If i could do it again, I would definitely have Q dropped the class. Avoid at all costs.

Her grading system is very unclear. You could turn in an essay she calls "full of merit"and yet she'll give you a B. She had a lecture on writing well but spent the whole time making fun of examples of our peers' papers. She's a great lecturer, I'll give you that. It was a very stressful class though, and I wouldn't ever ever ever take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Slightly intimidating, personally made me feel kind of dumb sometimes, but she does genuinely care about your success and knows how to engage everyone. Grades consisted of three papers (one of which you discuss with her and revise), one test, and one in-class essay. The class was really interesting, but make sure to keep up with the reading.

If you don't love Jane Austen, DON'T take this class. Barchas is passionate about what she does, but there is just too much work for a UGS course. Essay projects that aren't really explained very well, hour discussions every week, oral presentations, plus reading 4 novels. The tests are very long, so you must have a good understanding of the novels
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took her Jane Austen UGS: Too much work!! You have to read 4novels, write essays, oral presentations etc. The expectations for assignments are unclear and grading is very tough. reviews.comment: When you enter this class you think its going to be an easy UGS compared to the other UGSs UT provides. Most activities/assignments are irrelevant extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Being in this class is a little like being in a cult: do not take it if you're not obsessed with Austen, you will not enjoy being called a Janeite or being around others who are obsessed. Barchas is not the nicest, I would recommend asking the TAs questions instead of asking her because she will accuse you of being illiterate.

reviews.comment: Friendly, qualified and passionate about the subject material, but sometimes got carried away discussing her own accomplishments. 3 research projects count for most of the final grade and introduce students to resources/databases which was a huge help in other classes. Avoid if you're looking for an easy UGS or hate writing essays/doing research.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The Jane Austen film and literature class is incredibly interesting but also incredibly difficult. Just make sure to utilize the TAs and ask lots of questions. Dr. Barchas is very knowledgeable and exciting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading and the three essays given are graded really tough. The essay prompts are also pretty stupid so don't take this class unless you are confident in your BSing skills. Otherwise, there was some interesting things learned in this course, and Dr. Barchas and the TAs were okay.

I took this class because I needed to have a UGS, thinking it would be interesting because it is covering Jane Austen. I have to admit the material was interesting, but the way papers are graded ultimately hurt my score in the class. Papers are graded heavily on views that you're supposed to have on specific topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had her for a Jane Austen class. I absolutely hated the class and the TA but Barchas herself was pretty cool. Funny, and passionate about what she teaches. Class itself was dreadful but she was sweet and taught me a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Barchas is hit or miss, you either love or hate her. Do not sign up for this class unless you are a good reader and writer, truly it is not for the faint of heart. But you learn so much and get exposed to so many amazing things. This is not an easy A course, but is the kind of course you will be thankful for later in your college career

Pros: she is so entertaining and funny, lectures are amazing, she improves your writing and research skills exponentially, tons of extra credit, interesting content. Cons: VERY unclear grading, does not accept any opinion but her own as right, can be harsh and judgmental Overall, I would definitely recommend her- its painful but worth it!!

Barchas is obnoxious, over-the-top and thinks she's really funny. reviews.comment: If you're a Jane Austen fanatic, and are ready to join a cult dedicated to her excellency, I still wouldn't recommend this class. reviews.comment: Knowledgable about what she is teaching but is very difficult. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very hard to please professor and TA's in the Jane Austen class. If your papers don't really reflect what they have in their minds then you won't do great (difficult to truly figure out what they want). Unreasonable amount of reading. To me the class is just ran by people overly obsessed with Jane Austen. Waste of money and no purpose to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's animated and obviously loves what she's teaching. I'm a film major and have read very little 19th century novels before this and only for class. reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever met in my life. She knows nothing about teaching. She just grades your paper whatever she wants and she ruins many students' GPA. If you want to take her class, please prepare for a C or D for this class.l

Ridiculous standards for what she wants from her essays (not difficult, she just has her own ideas for what SHE thinks your writing should look like, and will crucify you if you don't give her what she wants to see). Prof. Barchas was hard.  I'm a music major and I don't particularly like english, but I thought learning about Jane Austen would be fun. Boy was I wrong.  The TAs do your grading, but they are just as hard to please as Prof. Barchas. If you're looking for a fun UGS, this is not it.

reviews.comment: It's definitely a tough class, but I learned a lot - not only about Jane Austen/the regency era, but also about how to conduct research and write effectively. She is very passionate about her work, and her passion is contagious.  Don't take this class if you can't commit to reading 5 Jane Austen novels and writing 3 papers.

Shes a good professor for helping you tune up your writing, but is insanely into Jane Austen and expects the moon from your essays. All the reading sucks and only discussions are mandatory. Lecture is a joke that is naptime for half the class.
Prof. Barchas is with out a doubt an amazing  professor. She's very thorough. But if you don't like English courses, or have trouble keeping up with readings, this class probably isn't for you.

Grading is harsh. It's her way or the highway. For papers you practically have to invent the moon. I love Jane Austen and overall I found enjoyment in the class but if you value grades or free time I would not recommend this UGS.

I love Dr. Barchas' lectures because  she's very animated. You have to read A LOT and take a lot of notes during her lectures. If you are looking to take an easy UGS, don't take this.
Very long papers and very hard grading. Tests are near impossible to study for because of multitude of materials. Lots and lots of reading.

Prof. Barchas knows her stuff when it comes to Jane Austen. She presents interesting and engaging lectures, but you'll have to read the 4 books she assigns to remain interested and do well. My TA was really helpful when it comes to writing the 3 papers, and Prof. Barchas always gives examples in lecture. Challenging class, but definitely worth it!

Dr. Barchas knows her stuff when it comes to Jane Austen. Most of the people in the class were Jane Fanatics and Barchas is as well; if you don't have much interest in this genre I would not take her. Barchas is funny and witty and likeable, but sometimes can be moody and not the most helpful. I made an A- in the class mostly because ofessay grades
This class was a complete joke.

Super interesting and fun class, it's definitely a lot of reading but it is manageable. Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston were both great

Exceptional lecturer. He is very interested in what he says and very open to different theories and ideas than his own. Make sure to attend lectures for 10 bonus points to your grade, read the books, and you'll be fine!

The tests are highly specific though and require a lot of reading.

reviews.comment: The lectures were very interesting! Lectures are recorded so you can go back and watch them if you miss them. That said, they drop your lowest grade and have in-class quizzes for extra credit, so you'll be fine if you put in the work.

Great class with interesting lectures. Be prepared to read the books included in class materials. A lot of the info from the books is in the tests. Both teachers for this class were really great and had done a lot of research on the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed these lectures so much. Attendance is not required but it was honestly so interesting you just wanna stay. exam based but offer extra credit question every lecture so incentive to go to class. hes a great teacher and his research is really neat.

Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston's class was definitely tedious and required a lot more work outside of class than I was anticipating. It took me the first two exams to realize that you really do need to read and take very good notes. Basically, if you read for this class you'll do fine.

I loved the material & Cindy and David are very fun professors. If human sexuality/human psychology is interesting to you, TAKE IT!! Don't expect this to be a blow off though.

Don't waste your time with Buss.  The class was poorly developed using outdated materials. Buss presented as fact many things that clearly weren't. Overall, the class had a chauvinistic tone that was hard to ignore.

There's nothing I can't say about the professors (Buss & Meston) that hasn't been said. They're by far the most interesting professors I've listened to. From witty jokes to stories about their friends to recalling documentaries. The lectures are engaging & fun. The tests are simple but really specific... make sure you listen to everything.

I can't thank Dr. Buss & Meston enough for such a great course; they're both hilarious & excellent professors. The lectures couldn't be any more fascinating. Dr. Buss is a gem of a professor - insightful, well-respected, and brilliant.
Dr. Buss is such an impressive and respectable professor. I wish I couldve seen him lecture in-person.

Buss and Meston are funny but you have to pay attention during lectures and do the readings since the exam questions are VERY specific. Speed up lectures/videos to save time. 5 exams (1 is dropped) based on lectures, textbook, articles, and videos- lots of work but it's an interesting course.

reviews.comment: Dr. Meston and Dr. Buss are phenomenal professors. Their lectures are very engaging, and they are clearly very knowledgeable. It's not extremely easy, but definitely doable. I got a 91.5 in this class which is barely an A, by just watching all the lectures and taking notes. You take 5 exams, and your whole grade is made up of the 4 highest grades.
Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston did an incredible job lecturing. I was in the asynchronous class and the only thing I have to say is stay on top of the lectures and make sure to read the textbook.

I took the asynchronous version of PSY306 and absolutely enjoyed it. The material was actually very interesting, it's just that the tests were extremely specific (so be prepared for that). Dr. Buss (and Dr. Meston) are great professors and I absolutely recommend taking PSY306 with them.

This class taught by both Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston was very fun and interesting. However, you can not slack in this class at all. Your grade relies heavily on taking very structured notes and doing the readings precisely. If you do not study hard or watch all the lectures you will not do well in the class. But it is worth putting in the work.

The most interesting class I've taken at UT! I took it over the summer session, so my experience was a bit different but the class was still amazing. Grade was just based on exams every week. Some test questions were tricky, but if you watch the lectures and do the readings, it should be an easy A. Really changed how I think about sex >:)

Dr Buss and Dr Meston taught a super interesting class together. There were a lot of lectures and it seemed like we had tests every other week but as long as you take detailed notes the tests are not too hard. I learned so much and am actually going to miss their class! They are both very knowledgable and fun to listen to.

Your grade is going to be made up of 6 exams but as long as you take detailed notes and keep up with the lectures you'll do fine. He co-taught with Dr. Meston and his sections are a little more dull but him and Meston have a good dynamic so it's not too bad. The lectures are really interesting.

reviews.comment: Would definitely take any class with him again. He's very informative and is constantly making references and jokes that make class more fun. His tests are challenging but not harder than you would expect.

I took this class online, very enjoyable. Dr. Buss is hilarious and him and Dr. Meston make a great team. Don't hesitate to take this class! I'm really, really going to miss it

Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston taught this class together. The subject matter was very interesting, tests were not too difficult if you watched lectures and read/watched the assigned material. There is a quiz for almost every lecture, so don't miss those. 5 exams and one is dropped.
Buss and Meston are hilarious and make this class so much fun. Dr. Buss knows so much about his respective field. I was sad that this class ended.
As long as you actually are logged on to canvas and paying some attention you should be fine! Dr. Buss is pretty cool and they play videos and there is no homework
As long as you actually are logged on to canvas and paying some attention you should be fine! Dr. Buss is pretty cool and they play videos and stuff to keep you interested
Dr. Buss and Dr. Meston co-taught online live lecture course. Talk show style, hard to decipher important info from tangents. Tend to associate correlation with causation. Tests are ambiguous.

He made the class very interesting and I could say that I learned a lot in the class. There are four exams and each one is 25% of your grade. Don't think just because the stuff seems common sense that you don't have to study. Make sure you read the material and question your self. Being terrible at multiple choice style exams I did okay.

Wonderful professor. Very fair, very fun. Makes class entertaining and easy to relate to. He likes class participation, and his TA was very awesome. I would definitely take more courses with Buss in the future if presented with the opportunity.
Great prof!! Funny, helpful, smart, makes the subject matter interesting and relevant.

I was worried about this class, but Iverson made this class not only easy but so interesting. I looked forward to every lecture because of how he explains everything. Exams are fair and he offers many resources to do well.

Amazingly kind professor. As a chemical engineering major, I almost wanted to switch to medicine. He not only teaches the content you need to know, but includes valuable life lessons within the coursework. One of my favorite professors in the university. Very rewarding class if you put in the work!

The best prof. I had. SO many resources and his lectures are amazing (don't skip). Tests are fair if you know your stuff. I had an A in the class the whole semester but the final got me and dropped my grade unfortunately. Go to problem solving office hours to ask TAs HW questions to get 100s on all HWs. I wish he offered a real curve on tests

no other ochem prof can be better than him. offers old exams so you know exactly what will be on the exam, and sooo many resources. he truly wants his students to do well and is so caring and forgiving. content is still hard but he makes it manageable and digestable. TAKE HIM, no other prof is as good as him.

Having Iverson for Ochem 1 and 2 was an absolute privilege. Outstanding lectures, tons of resources to help (previous tests), and a fair amount of content that didn't feel overwhelming. A professor with so much experience teaching that the class is damn near perfect. Earning an A does require fairly good test scores though, so be prepared to work.
My Goat I love you Dr. Iverson
One of the best professors I have ever had.

I could talk all day about how much I love Dr. Iverson. He cares for all his students, not only as students but as people. He makes Ochem easy and provides so many resources for students to do well. I would take him for every subject if he taught them. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it. He really is changing peoples lives.
Ochem is hard anyways, but he makes it as easy as he can

i love brent. brent is the kindest, most caring, and brilliant professor i have ever had. not only does he truly care for his students as chemists, he cares for them as people (cue: run for the water plug). if you get the chance, you should take him. getting to experience a professor who is truly passionate is once in a lifetime! dr. iverson = king

Amazing professor! He's great at teaching, and he makes things as easy to understand as possible. He as a lot of resources to help if you struggle. There are several office ours throughout the week, all are recorded (as well as lectures).

Professor Iverson made me absolutely love organic chemistry. I didn't do too well in basic chem 1 & 2 so I was nervous coming into Ochem. He is genuinely the most caring and engaging lecturer. If you have the chance to take him, do it!!

BESTTTT Ochem professor could not ask for someone to explain better. Has a plethora of resources and is genuinely committed to ochem. Also brings in inspirational people and cares about health just as much as learning! Def not an easy A but if you put in the time its achievable.
BEST OCHEM PROFESSORRR
