Keep grades off for the semester, as they are not accurate. For reference, I had a 40% most of the semester but still ended with an A. Keep up with content/practice heavily to succeed.

I had Prof. Iverson for both ochem 1 and 2, and he's one of the best professors I've had. You can tell he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed, and he made ochem understandable and a bit enjoyable. He also stressed the importance of physical health, especially running.

Geniunely the best professor I've had at UT. For reference, I got a C in OCHEM I, and I thought OCHEM 2 would be worse; however, Iverson's commitment to explaining things in lecture and office hours, plus the numerous practice exams he gives (I did all of them before every test), made the class so doable and amazing. I would 1000% retake him.

If you're not good at learning on your own you def gotta pay attention in class, ochem did NOT come naturally to me so it took a lot of extra practice outside of class and homework, practice practice practice it's all about recognition.

Actually the GOAT. Had him for both semesters (320M and 320N) and got As in both. 
Seemed more manageable compared to Ochem 1 since I was used to the material.
Do everything he says, hammer the old exams, and you should be fine. This class is not an easy A - it is a sacrifice for sure- but your effort will pay off

BEST PROFESSOR EVERRR!! For reference, I got a B- in ochem 1 w/ Straumanis. Very glad I was able to change profs! He really cares about his students. He makes ochem so easy to understand and has many resources that help to prepare for exams. I won't lie, his homeworks were lengthy at times, but they did have problems that pertained to the midterms.

Dr. Iverson is by far one of the best lecturers I've had at UT (definitely the goat of Ochem!) Overall solid though grading is slow (except when the final was graded in one day?!), Canvas grade is not accurate at all whole semester, and your entire grade is exams (90%, t-score in place but not really helpful, no extra credit except 1 pt pop quiz).

Dr. Iverson is by far the best professor I've had at UT. His lectures are super engaging and he explains ochem in a way that makes sense and also shows how ochem is important to our lives and our careers. I hated chemistry before his class and I thought I just wasn't a chemistry person, but Dr. Iverson helped me realize that wasn't true.

He is super sweet and does care about his students. Ochem II did have a steep learning curve esp if you come from an easier ochem I professor like Callmann. I didn't do great on the first two midterms however he gives you the opportunity to replace final with a midterm so though midway through semester I thought I'd get a B, I ended up with an A

One of the few professors who really, REALLY cares about his students. He wants you to succeed in life not just in his class. Only thing I did not love was that the TA's were not active at all on EdDiscussion, but that's not his fault.

While lectures are a bit yap-full (sorry), Dr. Iverson explains difficult concepts in ways that make Ochem easy to understand. Recorded lectures are great, as I did the class completely on my own time (do at your own risk). The course is test-heavy, but worthwhile. He is extremely accommodating to students' needs and genuinely cares about teaching.
I'm begging you guys if you can take him please do it best decision in my life woke up everyday thanking god I had him. If you are a hard working student and not lazy you guaranteed an A.
His Aura is too much, I cannot fathom.

the goat of ochem. took 320m and 320n with him, his grading policies are graded off only 3 things but is extremely understanding with one exam drop and your final can replace a test. ochem2 is harder than 1

Iverson has a passion for teaching and displays a love for ochem that intrigues everyone to be excited to learn. Even though ochem is content-heavy, he connects stuff we learn to real-life situations and products we use and its mind-blowing. I recommend Iverson 100% for ochem; he will change your view on education and make you love learning ochem!

I LOVE THIS MAN. He has seriously changed my life, and I don't think I could get through Organic Chemistry II without him. He wants us to learn, understand, and apply material rather than memorize it. I know its tough, but please try to get into his lecture it will be 10000% worth it.

He made me love ochem. Very engaging and clear lecturer. Homework's and old exams heavily resemble exams. If you memorize the mechanisms, reactions, do, redo, and understand homework's and old practice exams, you will do great.

Iverson is an amazing professor. His lectures are engaging, and he provides great resources to succeed. Redo homework and practice old exams - Unstuck ai also helped me prepare. Take this class, you won't regret it!

Dr. Iverson is simply the best in every way you can imagine. I took his OChem class back in Fall 2019, and not only was he the best professor I had for my STEM classes, he was my favorite professor at UT hands down. He's incredibly patient and compassionate with his students, and his lectures are very informative and engaging. Take him if you can!

Iverson is easily the BEST professor I have here at UT. By the end of the semester, I have a really strong grasp of OChem and genuinely enjoy the material. That being said, he is definitely not easy as some say. His class requires a lot of work and effort, and the tests can get REALLY difficult and unforgiving if you don't study well for it.

He makes me find ochem interesting. Class is test heavy but duh, do the old exams they help so much, and learn your mechanisms. He'll say it's not memorization and it's all about critical thinking but tbh it's a mix of both, do whatever works better for you. Overall loved him and 10/10 would take again.

Absolutely incredible. Some of the best lectures I've had at UT so far and he actually makes a class that seems daunting interesting and fun. You do have to work hard to succeed in this class, but as long as you put the work in & take his advice on how to approach the class & study, you should be able to do well.
You won't regret it.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've ever met at UT. I went to his office hours every week because he actually made ochem fun. He told us so many inspirational stories, and mentions that there is no stupid question to ask. I highly recommend taking him!
This man is him

reviews.comment: the best. caring professor, engaging, interesting lectures, EXTREMELY patient - answers everyone's questions and encourages any/all questions to be asked. best professor i've ever had

Genuinely the BEST class I've taken at UT. I cannot even explain how good of a professor Dr. Iverson is. I was genuinely so sad in the last lecture at the end of the semester. If you can take him, I definitely recommend having him as a professor.

Honestly best science class I have ever taken!! I would have never imagined saying that for O Chem 2 but Iverson seriously made it that good. He made lectures so entertaining and truly taught why orgo is so important for our world. Tests are very similar to HW and past tests, so just work hard and practice and you should be fine.
He seriously is the best professor at UT. If I would have tried a little harder and didn't have so much going on this semester, an A would have been easily attainable.

He is a phenomenal professor at UT. Take him for O chem, you will not regret it! He is very passionate and attentive to the needs of his students. Make sure to go to his Office hours, do the HW (and redo them), and do the previous exams! His tests are fair to what he teaches, and he has clear expectations of what he will be testing on.

ochem2 is def much harder than 1 but iverson made it way better. the way he explains things is so good but ngl had to rewatch some lectures bc i didn't get it the 1st time. previous tests for practice and redoing the hws helped prepare for the tests.

truly the goat. hes been in the game for 30+ yrs so he truly knows what hes about. it says a lot that ive taken chem 1, 2, and ochem 1 here at UT and this has been my first A in a chem course. his website is a treasure trove. take practice exams, listen to his advice on the hw, and give yourself time to truly understand the material and youre solid

Very easy and doable class. Sometimes, I wished it was more to the point. Professor often goes on tangents to make the class easier (dumbs it down to the max so if you struggle w/ chem take him), which is not the best for ADHD students, however he makes good connections to pharma and chem-bio concepts. Overall, nice guy and nice TAs, so I recommend

Absolutely loved him. He kept the whole class engaged through his witty comments and analogies. He taught in a way that made you understand and learn the material rather than memorizing. Homework +
 quizzes, but quizzes were due the next day and were easy. Exams were a bit tricky but just practice the released exams + hmwk! Made synthesis easy!

My favorite professor so far! His lectures are engaging and fun, and he cares about your academic and personal well-being. He fosters a great learning environment and provides ample resources to do well. Office hours are very helpful and he is very approachable. Exams were not bad at all if you studied. Dr. Iverson is seriously a national treasure!

IM HIS BIGGEST FAN. Hands down the best professor, he truly cares about students, he is the BEST lecturer, content can get difficult but he truly explains things so well and is super approachable. He fosters the best learning environment, the tests are not hard and they a lotttttt like the homeworks. Go to office hours!!!! Iverson is awesome

The best professor I've ever taken. His lectures are amazing and he really cares about the content he teaches. He loves to promote health and exercising and it's really helped me overall outside of class too. Course has so many resources so if you're lost, you definitely have a chance to get back on track. Exams are very predictable and easy.

Amazing, amazing professor, take him if you can!! Orgo 1 & 2 are so fun with him, you don't even feel like you're in class. He tells lots of fun stories to help remember concepts and holds lots of review sessions. Practice exams are very helpful in preparing for exams. I didn't need to take CH 328N and I took it anyway because he's that good.
Iverson makes this class so enjoyable! Learning the content requires some effort, but the midterms and final are very doable.

I took Dr. Iverson for both OChem 1 and 2. There is no person better suited to teach this class. Lectures are clear, he provides a multitude of resources for practice, and has some sort of office hours almost daily. He makes OChem a manageable class. There's a reason why so many people like him, he's the best professor I've had while at UT.
Dr. Iverson is one of the BEST Professors around!! I came in thinking I wouldn't like ochem, but Dr. Iverson made me love it!!

Could not ask for a better professor. I was lucky enough to have him for CH320M and CH320N and it was an awesome experience. He really gives you all of the tools to succeed. Best way to study is to do old exams and re-do the homeworks. If you struggle with a concept then use the textbook but aside from that I didn't need it.

I LOVED DR. IVERSON!! I had Dr. Shabbir for CH320M and I thought I hated ochem, but Dr. Iverson made me love it!! He is very accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about his students' success. His exams were all very challenging, but very fair. Although he is not an easy A like everyone says, if you work hard you can earn an A.

The GOAT. Iverson is the golden standard for incredible lectures at UT. He goes above and beyond to maximize the learning experience, using effective strategies to make his lectures as helpful as possible. His genuine passion for the subject shines through, and he will do everything that he can to make sure you thrive in his course.

Having Dr. Iverson for O chem II truly was a gift. His lectures are engaging and if you pay attention, and take good notes, you will do very well in his class. Treat the practice problems like exams, and always take full length practice exams when studying. He truly cares about his students, and treats them like people.

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is the gem of UT. He restored my faith in professors for he is someone who ACTUALLY cares about his students. Having him as an Ochem professor is the greatest gift anyone could get in their academic career.

I thought he wouldn't live up to the hype, but oml this man is frickin amazing. If you can take him, DO IT, I feel so honored to have taken his class fr. Tests are very fair, but they are worth a lot, and ochem is not easy content so make sure to study! He gives tons of practice hw and exams, so do those and your set.

Dr.Iverson made me believe that professors are genuinely good people again. He is the sweetest ever and genuinely cares about people and made the hardest subject in the world possible to understand. He is so fun and makes lectures actually interesting. If you have the luck of getting him, hold on tight!

Dr. Iverson is easily one of UT's best professors. He loves teaching and shows up with a smile every day. It's ochem, so the material isn't easy, but he works really hard to help you understand it. His exams are difficult but nothing on them is a surprise. If you can, Iverson is a must-take professor.

Dr. Iverson comes to class everyday in a suit, and hosts surf-themed office hours evenings in a Hawaiian shirt. His years of expertise never dulled his enthusiasm for teaching, and even as an expert he never gets frustrated as he congratulates us with "good question" every time we ask. Thank you Dr. Iverson, for supporting us in and out of class.

This man is everythingggg. I loved Ochem because of him. I heard the worst things about this class, but Iverson made it possible to do well. He really cares and enjoys teaching. Pay attention to what he emphasizes. Make sure to understand the HOMEWORKS, do PRACTICE EXAMS, and take advantage of the help they offer. Ochem is hard, but it's possible

Dr. Iverson is amazing and the best professor I've had. It is evident that he genuinely cares for his students. Overall, ochem was hard for me, but he presented the material in a fun and straightforward manner. He is receptive to student feedback, and there are many opportunities to get help. Also his TAs (especially Qifan) are the absolute best.
Hands down best professor EVER! Lectures were inspiring and Dr. Iverson truly provides you with everything you need and more to earn an A! Also, go to office hours!!

Iverson was born to teach. He makes ochem extremely approachable but also recognizes what a hard class it is. You MUST go to lectures and sometimes even rewatch them a few times. He gives so many resources to practice and has great TAs. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS! YOU CAN DO WELL IN OCHEM!! He is a great lecturer and his test averages are pretty high.

Dr. Iverson is THE Organic Chemistry prof. He is amazing, him and his TAs have office hours everyday of the week to ensure you understand the material. He records everything, all the time so you don't need to worry about missing anything. There are tons of practice he gives so there's no reason for you to be lost. 10/10 if you can get him, do it.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING !! His classes are always the first ones to fill up - and his amazing lectures explains that a lot. He truly cares about his students and makes ochem a breeze. He is promoted now so he doesn't teach ochem anymore, but if he comes back definitely try to sign up !

Amazing professor! Just make sure to study your mechanisms and read the book. Practice problems are essential!! Also, make sure you take and do well on as many practice exams as you can!! Have a great time. He is truly amazing and cares about you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I have ever had in my life. If you have the chance to take this class, take it immediately. He is kind and listens to his students and somehow packages Ochem into an interesting format (which is not any easy thing to do). Please take this course, he is amazing

All I have to say is that Iverson was the best professor I have ever had, and he is an OChem prof. His TAs are also amazing, and he gives so many opportunities to talk to him and learn. Please take him

He makes Ochem so fun and interesting to learn. He is also very very passionate about the subject so he will tell a lot of interesting stories or facts during class. He loves and cares about his students too!
Literally the best professor at UT!

Don't buy the textbook. Iverson is a great professor with fair, but difficult, tests. Do not get behind no matter what you do and take advantage of all of the resources available! The final is worth a lot and no matter what, he'll make you take a test at the exact day/time it's set for (maybe with a time extension) or use it as your drop.

Loved him. I took him during the corona semester of Fall 2020. OChem is tough, but he makes it doable. Don't need the textbook but it helps. Make sure to do old. practice tests as those resemble the real thing and look at the rules of the day resources. Do physical synthesis practice problems before Exam 3 and final. Rewatch lectures before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've ever had. He takes a personal interest in your success and he was also very accommodating with the pandemic. His lectures are absolutely incredible and always engaging. That said, it is ochem. You will have to work really hard for the grade you want, but Dr. Iverson does his best to help you out.
Best professor I've ever had. Makes learning fun. Class is hard but he makes it doable. Take if you can. 10/10

You are LUCKY if you have the chance to take him. I was so scared to take Ochem bc I'm an average student and I loved his class and he is hands down my fav prof. He is super accessible outside class despite corona. He goes above and beyond to help you learn and keep you interested in lecture. He also provides a ton helpful materials and practices.

By far the best professor at UT!! Dr. Iverson cares so much about his students and it really shows. OCHEM is hard no matter what but he does all that he can to make it as fun as possible. Daily quizzes, weekly HW, 3 midterms, and a final. He provides so many resources for his students and is honestly so funny and makes his lectures interesting.

Dr. Iverson is by far the most amazing professor I've had at UT period. Not to mention that Organic is already super difficult, Dr. Iverson makes it a class that is definitely doable while inspiring you to push yourself in other ways. He genuinely cares about his students and I can feel his support even through the Covid Pandemic. 10/10 professor

Simply put, I never thought I would like ochem as much as I did! Dr. Iverson is extremely kind, approachable, and encouraging. I've never had a professor work so hard for his students He always stayed late for all of his reviews to answer everyone's questions and understands most students are pre-med and accommodates to that! I love Brent :)

Fall 2018.3 curved midterms with a drop, one final, homework and quizzes which are weighted lower. Be prepared to read the textbook, practice the material off the notes packets, and do the homework if you want guaranteed success. At least 6-8 hours of work per week on this class. However, excellent Ochem foundation and Dr. Iverson is very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great professor! Such an honor to listen to Dr. Iverson. He is so smart and cares about the well-being of his students. He records all lectures no instapoll, but he makes going to class fun. Ochem is a hard subject that you have to work to understand, but Dr. Iverson makes the class interesting. Tests are difficult but not impossible.

Iverson is an incredible professor. He makes learning organic chemistry fun! I would try your hardest to get him. Graded primarily on tests the cover literally everything you were taught but you get one drop.

Everything people have written here about Dr. Iverson is true - he is the most inspirational, wholesome, funny, caring, and whatever positive adjective you want to insert professor you'll have. Organic chemistry isn't easy, but you'll learn a lot more than chemistry in his class. Register quick if you want him though, his class fills up fast!

The hype is 100% true! Iverson is the best professor I've ever had. Engaging lectures, clear explanations, and tons of resources (old tests, hws, and mechanism sheets). Don't think I would have loved/understood ochem nearly as much if it wasnt for him. Just wish he also taught ochem 2! (tip: dont buy the molecular model kit he recommends)

Prof Iverson was amazing. He did everything he could to help us do well in Ochem. There was a lot of resources that he gave, and a lot of office hours, problem solving sessions, and past exams posted for us to do. Iverson is amazing, but Ochem was hard in itself. A lot of work was put in this class to get an A, but it's definitely doable.

Believe the hype-- Dr. Iverson is an awesome professor! However, it is very important to note that while he is a stellar teacher, ochem is an inevitably difficult class. This class is conceptually hard to understand, and it does require a lot of work to do well. You learn so much that it makes up for it, though! Love this class!

Unpopular opinion: Iverson is overrated. He seems like a great person and genuinely cares about the students, but he overwhelms students with too many resources and things to do. It's excessive. Lots of deviations in lecture to irrelevant topics. Tests are long (3hours) and late at night. Overall, just an average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: best professor I have ever had at this school. he really cares about you understanding the material and gives you an abundance of resources on his website to pass the class. smartest man on this campus

He explains the concepts really well, has visuals for everything, and uploads every lecture online. The tests are difficult but this is ochem so idk what you expect. He does his best to help you tho! His website has tons of online resources - past exams, recorded lectures and office hours, etc. - and he drops the lowest exam score. 10/10 professor!

Iverson was a great professor! He genuinely cared about his students and his method of teaching really worked for me. Probably the best professor I've ever had at UT. Take him for ochem 1, if you can! I wish he taught ochem 2 the following semester
The best professor I have ever had. That is all I have to say.

MUST TAKE HIS CLASS! You'll not only acquire more than enough knowledge to tackle subsequent UT courses (& MCAT) but he also imbues his class w/ wholesome lessons in life. In brief, Dr. Iverson is a prof who enjoys pointing out how smoothly he segues from one topic to the next, providing his class with "time capsules," & advocating to run run run!

He was a really awesome OCH1 professor. Really cared about the material as well as the general well being of his students. The course was challenging, but you really will learn in his classroom. Thanks Dr. Iverson

Whenever someone asked me who I had for organic chemistry and I said Iverson, they gasped like I'd said I had a literal angel. Iverson is the greatest and you're super lucky if you manage to get ochem with him. Go to office hours! They're so helpful! Pretty much everything on his website is, it's a goldmine. He records every lecture as well

All the comments are right. Man's a legend. Teaches from handwritten notes. Short quizzes every class based on textbook readings. Homework is really helpful. A great professor, but ochem is tricky naturally.

Iverson is AMAZING. People always look forward to his lectures- he knows how to explain the same topic in a million different ways so every kind of student will understand. He works tirelessly to make sure every student has the opportunity to do extremely well in his class, and the head TA (Chris) is great too. You will love this class!!!!

If you are between Iverson and Shabbir, but Shabbir fits better in your schedule, then change your entire schedule, switch your major if you have to so that you can fit this man's class in your schedule. People always talk about how great Iverson is, AND IT IS TRUE! This man is truly extraterrestrial.

Believe all the hype that has already been posted here. If you see Iversons name pop up on the registration site and youre due to take organic chemistry, then you need to move your schedule around in order to take his class. After two semesters of inorganic hell, Dr. Iversons teaching got me to fall in love with chemistry all over again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Iverson is without a doubt the best professor that I have had here at UT. He is funny and will bring in speakers. He is a huge believer in running and will give extra credit if the class does a fun run. records and posts all his lectures online. Its still Ochem so be prepared to work but with Dr. I you'll be ok. Truly an amazing professor
Great lecturer, really cares about his students. You will come out of this class really understanding the material. He provides with tons of resources in order to succeed in his class

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He records his lectures, but I highly recommend going to class because the vibes he gives off are great and he's an amazing lecturer. He has old exams posted which help a lot when it comes to studying for exams. His tests are a challenge, but definitely doable. He is the best ochem professor.

If you are going to take organic chemistry, you HAVE to take it with Dr. Iverson. He's such an inspirational lecturer who will go the extra mile to make sure you understand all the concepts that he teaches. His lectures are entertaining and kept me engaged throughout the course. He makes you work for the grade, but it is all worth it in the end.

O-chem is not an easy subject to make enjoyable and he did it. BEST professor ever! So funny and so knowledgeable! 3 exams and 1 gets dropped + final exam. He also gives homework packets that are optional, but they are extra credit on the exams if you complete them, so I would do them! He also has SO many opportunities for help outside class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Iverson is one of the best professors i've ever had. He cares soooo much. you can really tell that he wants you to do well in his class. has office hours almost everyday. subject material is very difficult but that's to be expected. overall, i love this man and if you have the chance to take him, it'd be a huge mistake not to!!!!!

Best professor ever, by far. He makes the subject as interesting as he possibly can and office hours are available basically everyday with live online office hours. Everything is recorded in case you had trouble understanding something. Take him. I wish he could've taken him for first semester of organic.

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! Dr. Iverson is such an amazing person, his lectures are always entertaining and he is genuinely passionate about his job. Ochem is a really hard subject but he makes sure you really learn it. I absolutely loved him. He created his own website with lots of helpful resources! I definitely recommend him! He's the best!!

Iverson truly loves teaching and his job, and it definitely shows in the way he runs his class. There are 3 exams, and 1 is dropped, plus a final. The homework counts as EC, so do them! Go to class if you can, it really helps. Also study with friends, it'll make life a lot easier. Use old finals he gives you to study and you'll do great!

He is the first professor I've met who loves his job. 3 exams (1 dropped) and a final. The homework are extra credit so do them!!! Look over the rules of the day (T/F & fill in the blank come from those). Go to the Problem Solving sessions. And study with friends! For the final & (exams), study the past finals & (exams) & corresponding hws.

I actually didn't finish his class. I had to drop it due to non-academic health reasons, but HE was the professor that made me love science, especially biochemistry, all over again. I'm going to do the research I want to do now because he's inspired me so much, but in the end his class wasn't required anymore. Take him. You won't regret it. GOAT.

Dr. Iverson is the BEST professor I've ever had. I absolutely loved going to lectures and I he made me like organic chemistry even though I sucked at it. He's great and if you just keep trying you will understand it if you just keep doing what he tells you.  It took me a long time to understand the material but his class is so worth it.  TAKE IT.

If you have the opportunity to take Dr. Iverson's class, do it. Don't even question it. Just take his class, you'll learn so much & have a great time. He genuinely cares about you and gives you all the resources you need to be successful at Ochem.

I don't have enough space on here to say all the amazing things this professor is, but this is definitely going to be the class I miss once I graduate. I didn't just laugh all the time in his class, but I definitely learned more than I ever expected to learn in an organic chemistry class. Bless UT for this amazing person.

Dr. Iverson is hands down my favorite professor so far! His lectures are so interesting and his exams are very representative of the homework he assigns. He gives 3 exams (the lowest of the 3 exams is dropped) and a final. He gave me a newfound appreciation for O Chem!! Seriously, take him!!! He is as great as everyone says he is!!!

Dr. Iverson is absolutely phenomenal. Take his class!! Ochem 2 can be hard at times but he makes so much effort to break and down and easy to understand. He literally gives you so many resources to succeed. On top of that, he genuinely cares about each and every one of his students and tries super hard to make lectures entertaining! Love him!

Dr. Iverson is hands down one of my favorite professors I've had so far. He cares a lot about his students and provides so many opportunities for you to get help to understand the material. I went to all of his office hours and thought they were very helpful. His lectures are funny, and his homework is very similar to how tests are formatted.

I liked having Iverson for ochem 2. His lectures are always clear and entertaining. You won't even have to crack open the book if you pay attention in class. However, he does seem to spend a significant amount of time discussing topics unrelated to ochem, and at a certain point in the semester I found myself thinking "really, more fish??"
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Respected by students--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Iverson was great but everyone overrates him. He provides countless resources to succeed and do well in the class, however theres so much that at times it makes the material more confusing. His lectures are amazing, but at times a waste of time and annoying. His test seemed harder then all the previous practice exams he posted. Overall great!

He is too hyped up. Many undergrads will defend his teaching style because it is relatively easy to reproduce answers on a test rather than actually understand the organic chemistry that is going on. He is great for premeds that are looking for an relatively easy A in orgo2. lots of supplemental help as well. Overall, nothing special.

Unpopular opinion: Iverson is overrated.  He talks about running, fish, and plays his trumpet.  Everything is always a "time capsule." He has dad humor and is the definition of doing the most. But, he's not a bad teacher, is super passionate about organic chemistry, and provides you with excessive amount of supplemental help.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor I've had at UT! He truly wants you to do well in his class. Ochem 2 is not an easy class, but he made it my favorite. If you go over class notes and his old exams that he posts, you will do fine on the tests. Love him!
Great teacher. Would take his class again.

Dr. Iverson is the best! He taught organic chemistry very well and he is able to make it doable and deliver it well! He's very clear, provides excellent foundations and fundamental basics for you so that you can combat complex problems. Provide old tests that you can practice and encourage you to ask questions and participate. Lectures clear + good

If you have to take Ochem, take this professor. I  have never been more satisfied with a class. Iverson's interest in his students is unmatched by any professor I have taken thus far. That is not say this class was an easy A. He uploads practice tests from 2006 and on which helped tremendously. I went from a C+ first semester to an A. Take Iverson!

Dr. Iverson made ochem II very interesting. The rumors are true, he is one of the best professors on all of campus. I didn't do so great in ochem I but I participated way more and "caught the wave." (You'll know what that means). He posts his old exams, which are great practice. Going over notes and going to problem solving help a lot!
Dr. Iverson, if you read this. You made me love a class I once used to hate. I was having anxiety over Ochem, but you changed that. Thank you for being there for your students, thank you for caring.

It isn't often you come across an individual, let alone a professor, as genuine and inspirational as Dr. Iverson. He's the image of what every educator should strive for. Only downside to taking his class is that he'll set a the bar high for what a professor should be, and you'll be disappointed with just about any other professor down the road.

Dr. Iverson is the best professor you will ever take. This class is hard, but he will make you love organic chemistry. Hands down the most amazing man you will ever meet. I will really miss this class.
The best professor I have ever had. One of the nicest people you will ever meet!
The most AMAZING Professor I have ever gotten.  He's so great that I don't think i'll ever meet another professor or anyone else like him again.

He turned a difficult course into my favorite class of the semester. He is very patience and approachable. He'll do whatever it takes to get a student to understand the material. He makes his lectures clear and concise. Go to class and do the his hw and ochem will be easy.

By far THE best professor I've ever had. He really knows the material and teaches extremely well. Very clear on all the assignments. DO THE WEEKLY HOMEWORKS AND THE BOOK PROBLEMS! This will almost guarantee you a high grade!
Had him for CH310M and N. By far, without a doubt, THE best instructor I have ever had in my life. There's a reason the entire university knows his name.

Dr. Iverson makes the class entertaining and material relevant. He provides past tests, which are great practice. Organic chemistry can be challenging, but if you keep up with the material and practice a lot, you'll do well.

GREAT PROF!!! He rele knows how to teach and he gives u all the tools u need to do well in his class. He presents the material rele well and really cares that his students understand it. He knows that ochem is hard and tries to make it as simple as possible. I took 310M n am taking 310N w/ him and both have been my favorite classes each semester!

Iverson is a god! I've always hated Chemistry but he makes it interesting. He's fun and keeps you engaged. There's no way you can fall asleep. Plus he tells us stories & sings for us. And he's very inspiring. Tests are straight forward. Go to class, keep up with your work, and getting an A in the class won't be hard. SOOO glad I took him!!
He is so amazing take him if possible. O Chem is hard but he makes it fun!
Amazing! O Chem is awesome because of Dr. Iverson. I actually look forward to my MWF classes because of this class!
Best Teacher ever!!!

If you have the chance to take Organic Chemistry with Dr. Iverson, take it!! He really makes it easy, believe it or not, to understand. The exams are fair and his class is just plain interesting. He takes this class above and beyond any learning experience you have ever had!
He sings for us on the last class day!

Iverson is an absolutely amazing professor. You have to take his class if you get the chance. Ochem is difficult, but the homeworks and TA recitation sessions really help clarify the material. Tests are very fair, and if you've done the homeworks and put forth some effort, you'll do great!
iverson is easily the best teacher i've ever had.  i came away actually enjoying the subject.
BRENT IVERSON IS A BEAUTIFUL MAN!!!  ORGANIC CHEMISTRY IS NOTHING WITHOUT BRENT IVERSON!!!
he'll actually teach you organic chemistry, he made me love it!!! and the underwater slides he shows you are awesome...
He's maybe one of the best teachers at UT- Austin.  Makes Orgo understandable.

he is honestly not a bad professor but sometimes lectures are boring. the exams are very fair and are similar to the practice ones that he uploads but they definitely felt very rushed. the case studies and hw take forever to complete though. overall not as bad as what these reviews are making him seem like.

reviews.comment: Bickel was a mixed bag. He gave great lectures explaining finance in a way that applies to real life, but the assignments felt like busy work because they weren't hard, just many problems to solve. The material was really easy, but you had to rush through the exams and there wasn't enough time to check your work. Going to lecture made it an easy A

This was by far the worst ME course I have ever taken at UT. Bickel has no empathy for the students with his low exam averages, and his condescending attitude makes it difficult to ask him questions. The exams are filled with niche concepts from the textbook and excel cell knowledge. My TA couldn't even explain concepts from Test 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Studied the material he gave us + textbook for weeks in preparation for the final. Did not matter he decided to test us over software formulas and stuff that was not on the textbook or any class work. There was no way to study for that final. A lot of people failed even with his “holiday bonus”. Condescending when you ask questions. Bad teacher.
Out of all the MechE courses I've taken, by far the worst experience thanks to Professor Bickel. I hope he gets in trouble for the way he graded students

Absolute worst professor I have ever had in my life. Failed the class my senior year and now I will have to be behind a semester. Test questions were nothing like the homework's and quizzes and instead were completely random and never really taught. He should be fired

Worst professor I've ever had. Homework didn't match exams, quizzes were useless, and he referenced group projects on exams without notice. Final required Excel formulas for paid software we barely used. Curve was 6 percentage points, leaving half the class failing or with a C-. Unhelpful, arrogant, and spiteful—avoid at all costs.
Poorly written final exam that included content NOT mentioned would be on the final.

The homeworks and case studies are fine if you put in the effort, but some of the exams felt more like trivia rather than Engineering Finance. Students were tested over content not covered in homework or TA sessions, making them artificially difficult. Overall, this was my least-favorite class at UT.

Bickel has the biggest ego I have ever seen in college. He is condescending when you ask him questions, wastes everyone's time in an 8am clicking through slides, and makes ridiculous exams. Bickel must think I'm Alex Trebek the way his exams felt more like playing obscure jeopardy completely unprepared than actually testing over a class I took.

The homework isn't the worst and sure the cases are long but the exams are just ridiculous. On the second exam and on the final, he heavily weighted questions that were not covered by ANY homework problem or TA session, but rather briefly mentioned in class. It seems he is actively punishing students and this is not acceptable. Avoid if possible.

Bickel fails to create an environment where students feel their effort to learn the course content is rewarded.

Reading the textbook and completing supporting material, like the homework, will not help you succeed on tests. Test content tends to be artificially difficult, with questions requiring methods we never used or random @risk knowledge.
Tests should be to test learning but he decides to make it about very niche topics. Do not take.

The exams are significantly more challenging than the material covered in class or the homework. He does not test students over relevant topics and does not want students to succeed. As a mechanical engineer, finance with Bickel is the hardest class I have ever taken.

This professor strives to create tests that are malicious towards students, with convoluted prompts for questions, to testing students on methods that are never used in the real world such as the Pool Method. His lectures were very hard to follow and the cases took a long time, avoid this malicious teacher at all costs.
hardest class in meche degree for no reason, pulls most of his exam questions over things he glazes over in 5 seconds in a class that nobody goes to cuz he's so boring and its at 8 am
Bro has nothing better to do so he on a power trip teaching mechanical engineering students finance.

If you want to fail and hate yourself take this class. I don't even think he knows what he's writing in these exams. He made this semester so much more rigorous than he did last semester. He took away a test drop and designed his exams for 60 averages. I used a grade calculator at least 3 times just for this class. Students are scraping by for C's
FIRE BICKEL!
Bickel wants engineers to take a 5th year so we can continue to give him terrible course evaluations and RMP's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He intentionally misdirects students on the content that will be on the test and throws pointless curveballs that have no objective other than crushing the grades. My TA literally didn't know how to solve a question worth 25% of Exam 2, which he then repeated on the final. If you take this professor, don't bother studying because it doesn't help.

I wish this thing didn't have a word count. Just came of his final confident in none of my answers. I have put in more work in this class then an actual upper level division engineering course. This guy must hate himself and wants his students to hate him too. If I have to retake this class, absolutely nothing will make me retake it with Bickel.
No aura. Don't take Bickel

He writes his exams to fail his students. He does not test on your understanding of finance he wants you to attend his classes so you can remember what a button does on @RISK. TA's treat the exam setting like a highly guarded prison facility. Cheat sheets are unhelpful bc you cannot prep for his exams. Condescending attitude during office hours.

Avoid this guy if you can. His exams are hard, w/ concepts that are barely touched on in class. Grading feels almost vindictive. The class doesn't feel like an educational experience—it feels like a punishment for not deciphering his convoluted teaching style. Case studies are lengthly, discussions mandatory, 8am, no exam drops, steer clear of him.

I wouldn't wish 8ams w/ Bickel upon my worse enemy . His exams are intentionally designed to trick students, often covering obscure material barely mentioned. His grading is incredibly unfair, with little room for partial credit. This class is an unnecessarily stressful experience,he is trying to punish us for not remembering made up techniques.

4th years are failing eng finance. Exams are known for being unrealistically difficult. They frequently include obscure topics that were glossed over in class, making studying impossible. This course demands alot amount of time and effort, and the disconnect between the workload, instruction, and evaluation makes it feel unnecessarily grueling.

This class is supposed to be about finance not if you can remember excel and rick cell formulas. The workload is heavy, with case studies that require time and effort. The exams are designed to be difficult,bc lecture attendance is low, and the tests often center around abstract, poorly explained concepts to punish students for not attending class

Professor Bickel's exams are unrealistically difficult, often covering topics barely mentioned in lectures. He provides minimal resources to prepare, leaving students to teach themselves most of the material. The disconnect between lectures and assessments makes the class unnecessarily frustrating and stressful. Extremely heavy workload with cases.
Hardest exams, made up methods to trick his students. He wants his students to fail.

He is very knowledgeable and cares about the subject matter on a level different from his students. He is difficult to follow through the course and the tests and case studies often came from nowhere. Many engineering students do not want to devote the work and knowledge he requires for finance, because it does not feel relavent.

Took this class as a requisite, it has been heavier than most labs and project-based courses. Exams are purposely made more difficult due to the low attendance in lecture with abstract concepts being a majority of the exams. TA's also grade very harshly on exams. Lectures consist of him talking about himself and very little on content.

Exams are a lot harder than content covered and HW. He often throws an unreasonable curveball on the exams, doesn't care about students' understanding of the topic, and gives trick questions to punish students for not reading every small topic in the book.

She cares but she sucks at teaching. The amount of homework for this course was also way too much. Tests were also very inconsistent in difficulty meaning some only needed an hour or two of studying were others needed weeks of prep to get even a C. Would NOT take again

Cabrera is the sweetest woman, but she can NOT teach! She constantly got problems wrong in class and gave no curve even when test averages were failing; the only redeeming quality is that the final replaced a test grade (then changed to two test grades). I only passed this class by having previous knowledge of the topic. AVOID IF YOU CAN!!

Don't get me wrong, Professor Cabrera is a very sweet woman- but I could not learn from her. I attended office hours and TA office hours; if you did not have a specific question, then it was of no help. I would be stuck on whole concepts and wasn't given the opportunity to understand them with her or the TAs.

Professor Cabrera is incredibly caring and engaging. The coarse is standardized and easy to follow if you keep up with the learning modules. She was always checking in with students and relieved our stress before exams. I would highly recommend taking her classes!

She was very kind but often makes mistakes during lectures that make it hard to understand new concepts that you're learning for the first time. I stopped going to lectures and really struggled with this class because it seemed like I had to teach myself the material.

The class is lecture heavy except the professor is not a good lecturer at all. She is super nice but it sucks that her teaching is more often confusing and not helpful. Stopped going to lectures halfway through the semester and only used notes from my senior year in highschool.

Mrs. Cabrera was a chill teacher who is very passionate about teaching. However, the class itself is pretty challenging because of the tests and homework (she does not have any control over them). The tests were very similar to the reviews so make sure to go over those. The discussion classes are skippable.

Most of the course structure/ exams is set by the department. She leaves a LOT of class time after teaching material for practice sets (similar to hw/ exams) where you can ask as many questions as you want. Also she's the only professor I had this semester that actually tried to connect with students.

I think Dr. Cabrera did the best she could with what she was given but the class seemed like you were set up to fail unless you did really good in precal/calculus in high school. Dr. Cabrera was super caring and wanted to make sure we understood the content but some things were not explained very well. Not a horrible choice for calculus.

By far the most caring professor I've had this semester! She will explain things 5 times if needed and will stay after class to help you. Very reasonable with her grading criteria (reevaluated letter grade cutoffs after seeing final scores). There is a lot of homework but it's honestly for the best because the extra practice is much needed!!

Very sweet professor, horrible at teaching. As someone who had no previous experience with calculus, her teaching style made everything seem more complicated. ChatGPT and Youtube were the only things that pulled me through. Averages on exams were low and the final is ur saving grace. If you can take this class with someone else, do it.

Professor Cabrera is a kind and caring person that holds a great understanding of mathematical concepts. More than 50% of your grade is three midterms, which are often quite difficult/tricky. While her lectures can be useful at times, it is best to teach yourself outside concepts for the best test results. Taking her isn't peak, but not too bad.

She is super sweet, but her lectures are confusing and unhelpful. Attendance is not mandatory and honestly not advised. The class is essentially self-taught and your grade will depend on the exams and the final.

Professor is very kind but does not teach well. I had to learn everything on my own and had a very difficult time understanding. Spent hours studying and was not able to do good. Final is mandatory and it is the only way you can save your grade which did not work for me.

If you do not need to take this class, just don't. She is a super sweet person, but can not teach. You have to learn everything yourself. As someone who took calc before it was hard to follow her teaching. I just watched my old hs teacher's videos to learn.

If you can, take this credit in CC, she makes everything overcomplicated. Practically had to learn everything through youtube. Exam are majority of class so if you mess up, theres only the final to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher but since I had already taken calculus before the class was easy do not recommend to anyone trying to get a good grade there is no extra credit and your fate is sealed after the first two exams.

She is a very kind and caring professor, but horrible at teaching. She can not explain concepts well at all. I made a great grade in this class, but I had to teach myself everything. Averages for exams were in the 60-70 range. Don't take her unless you are going to put the time in to teach yourself. Our TA wasn't helpful at all either.

By far the best professor I have ever had, she was attentive and willing to explain something 3 times if it was needed to grasp a concept. Fairly lecture heavy but the homework assignments are fairly easy as long as you pay attention in class and stay on topic.

She is a sweet professor.That is the only positive quality of her teaching style. The "discussions" are a waste of time and the content we work on in those classes is meaningless compared to what we learn.On our second test of the year, there were about 4 questions that we had never seen before and the average grade was a 58 FOR THE WHOLE CLASS.

She is a lovely person who cares about her work, however, she is not a good professor. She overcomplicates simple concepts and underexplains the more difficult ones. Exams are weighted heavily making the other assignments seem unimportant even when they take a lot of time. I would recommend avoiding her and taking calculus with another professor.

Just horrible at teaching, nice person and passionate at math, but she makes so many little mistakes while teaching it makes someone who already took calculus worse at calculus. Would not recommend. If you get this teacher I would recommend self teaching and tutors. Good luck.

Professor Cabrera is obviously very passionate about teaching. But she consistently gets practice problems wrong and explains concepts in overly complex ways. If you can do well with this teacher that means you already took calculus or you completely learned the course on your own time. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Getting in contact with her is very hard. She overcomplicates subjects, and her lectures are very hard to understand. Many of the assignments you do seem unrelated to what you are learning. In addition, on the tests, there is a lot of material that you will feel like you never learned. Take calculus with someone else.

I had Dr. Kilic for waves (my review is somewhere below) and now for quantum- unlike an electron's position, I can say with absolute certainty that he is probably my favorite phys prof I've had so far. He made something complex understandable, especially after setting a solid foundation in PHY 315. I'm gonna miss having him as a teacher next sem :(

Despite the uncertainty principle, I am 100% certain of Dr. Kilic's position as the GOAT and of his momentous pedagogical skills. I've taken 315 and now 373 with him, and he goes through ALL steps of the derivations and makes concepts amazingly clear and intuitive. I have given several lectures myself now and he is my greatest inspiration for them.

Amazing lecturer who explains concepts and derivations clearly, I felt like I had a thorough understanding of the content. Lectures move a little fast but lecture notes are always uploaded pretty promptly afterward.

Dr. Kilic, my goat! I was terrified for this class, but he made waves very accessible and I finally felt like a true physics major after taking the class. For the exams: just keep calm. Most questions aren't terribly difficult, just tricky. I only wish I'd studied more for the weekly quizzes. 10/10, might consider taking this class again. Lol.

Dr. Kilic is the professor to take for any physics course. He explains everything incredibly well, and if you don't understand after lecture, you will after office hours. Tests are *tricky*, but not difficult, and use strategies from homework/practice sets. Incredibly caring and accessible. This is the class that made me "get" physics.

Dr. Kilic made this 315 very manageable for me with difficult homework's and good lectures that balanced each other out. You have a week to complete homework's with one quiz a week. Office hours were very useful for me as they helped a lot with mastering/practicing the content. Exams could be regraded on request as well. I would recommend taking.

I've worked with Dr. Kilic for 3 semesters out of my college career, and this man is my favorite professor I've had at UT. Funny, brilliant, and so adept at presenting information. He made quantum mechanics feel so accessible and natural. I owe a lot to Dr. Kilic, and would recommend him to anyone. Go to office hours and talk to him!

Dr. Kilic focuses on building a real understanding of waves concepts rather than relying on memorization. The class is difficult but also fun and rewarding. Lectures can be hard to follow since they move quickly, but he's always willing to review material during office hours. I might have mild PTSD from this class, but honestly, I'd take it again.

I had Kilic for Mechanics as well as Waves. He is a very good professor and always communicated really well. Class is non physics major friendly (like me) because of how well he explains the material. A large chunk of grade depends on homework grade + quiz, so working hard will definitely get you to pass! Exams based on homework but with a twist.

Waves in an incredibly difficult class. That being said, Kilic makes it manageable. Lectures go about 100 mph, so review topics after class (rewatch lectures/redo notes). Exams are a little less difficult than the homework. He's a nice guy, I wish I got to go to office hours. Very daunting class (it's the weed out), but Kilic is a good professor.

Amazing lecturer and all around great person to talk with. If you show up to class, attend office hours and spend time thinking about the course material, you will succeed in this class and grow as a physicist. It is the first difficult physics class you will likely take and the exams require thinking outside the box but are doable if you prepare.

I found that the questions on the midterms were overly difficult, not because of their complexity, but because we had been ill-prepared for them.  The lectures and homework weren't effective, as every test problem required methods never seen before.  I would have appreciated questions I knew how to solve for a class I'm taking for a grade.

Kilic is a great, engaging lecturer, but be warned that PHY 315 is a very difficult class. The average for the midterm exams was around a 62, but he does drop one exam. Also, while you don't have to have taken M 427J beforehand, I advise that you at least be familiar with linear algebra because the first exam relies heavily on it.

Great professor, loved the demos. Course load was fine and midterms are quite straightforward to study for. Easy enough to get an A if you have good intuition about physics. After being disappointed by other courses, this one was the one that finally taught me how to do a Fourier transform.

Took his class because his ratings were good and while I can see why people rate him so highly , beware this is an EXTREMELY difficult class. Which is annoying , considering this is a "lower division" physics course, a real weed out class for sure. Average for the first test was a 30%. And he is the "best" professor for this class so good luck.

Getting a good grade in this class was very difficult because the midterms and final were insanely all so difficult,  his exam questions were so WILDLY DIFFICULT and we never had a passing average for any exam. If you're naturally good at physics and want to learn I would say you're fine but if you just want a decent grade I wouldn't recommend.
Very good at explaining complex subjects in a way that even those with no background knowledge can follow. Highly recommend.

I had Dr. Kilic for Mechanics as well as Waves, and he was amazing for both classes. He's such an engaging lecturer and is always available via email or in office hours if you need help. His tests are tough, but if you practice diligently, you will do well. Dr. Kilic is easily someone I'd immediately recommend to any student.

Extremely smart particle physicist. You will learn a lot. 80% exams, 20% HW. Ridiculously hard class, but curved several letter grades up. Exam averaged around 50-60%. Dropped lowest of 3 midterms. Final worth 40%. Lectures go really fast but you leave feeling like you learned years worth of material. It will be hard but it's possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very patient/caring professor who clearly wants to help students learn. Pop quizzes usually once a week but if you review your notes in between classes you should be fine. Don't wait until the last minute to do homework and use office hours when you can. Exam questions are almost identical to the homework questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stay on top of homework and start early. Don't wait to start studying, and work on practice problems rather than memorization. That being said, Kilic is an incredible educator who truly cares for his students. Go to office hours! Kilic is such an interesting, approachable person who loves talking to students. He's everything a professor should be.

Dr. Kilic is one of the smartest people I have ever met. Being in his class has been inspirational as a physics major. His expertise in the field shows during lecture. Try to meet with him outside of class!! He is truly a genius and breaks down difficult concepts effectively. 

PRACTICE > memorizing concepts, you learn physics by solving problems.

kilic is a sweetie, but boy is it easy to get lost in his lectures. imo, i think he presented some of the concepts in a way that was hard to understand, so make sure you are going over the concepts later instead of memorizing the methods used to solve the problems. the hw was annoying (quest), and his midterms were pretty hard. form a study group!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kilic is AMAZING! I had to take PHY110C as a part of my FIG and it was more of a discussion/seminar class with him giving you a topic over the weekend and then discussing during class. He was so nice and the way he presented the topics in class made it easy to follow. You can tell he loves doing what he does! Take PHY110 if you have room!

Few professors can present Physics in such a natural and caring way. Even if you struggle in class, he's always happy to provide every possible avenue to understanding the material, whether that be his incredibly helpful office hours, getting his TA's to host pre-exam reviews, or meaningfully exploring concepts in lecture. A gem of the University.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Out of all my professors so far, Kilic is the one I enjoy talking to the most. Go to his office hours and he will answer any question you have about the class or something unrelated to the test. Additionally the lowest test grade is dropped so if you study and make 100s on the first few you can skip the last one. Only con is iClicker.
Easy Class. Teaches the material very well. Tests have easier questions than the hw. Just go to class and pay attention. Pretty much only the bare minimum is required to get an A in this class.

The professor is very approachable and please don't hesitate going to his office hours for any help. Three midterms and one final but one midterm is dropped. The only thing I want to complain is that he doesn't give out material slides (nor he teaches by that) so if you want to systematically go over the material you will have to read the book.

3 tests and a final (lowest test is dropped). book isn't needed but does help. He gives pop clicker quizzes and uses clickers for attendance. homework is due every Wednesday. final grade is determined by your rank in the class (no other specifics are given on his syllabus)  Kilic is great at explaining stuff and extremely patient. would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kilic is the best undergrad physics prof. at UT. What separates him from other prof. is that his course structure makes you always prepare + depth of physics/math knowledge that he can recall without hesitation. I took electrostatics with him 2 yrs ago, and it still resonates today. Take any class you can with him, and prepare for pop quizzes.
Weekly pop quizzes, hard class because of the subject matter, but he's friendly and clear most of the time.

As a nonphysics major, I needed to read the book cover to cover.  He will explain things if you go to his office hours.  He's one of the better physics professors and heavily weights homework, quizzes, and attendance when calculating your grade.  He makes you work to get a good grade.

He is definitely one of my favorite professors at UT. Not only is it hard to find a professor that is this good at explaining confusing/difficult concepts, having that plus the fact that he cares about the students a lot makes him very valuable. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN! He makes you like physics.
Seems to be his first year being a professor, so the first test was quite hard, but then again it is just a difficult class. He does a pretty good job teaching, but you will need to read the book.
Great teacher

This class is one of the easiest but most enjoyable courses I've taken this year. You have to genuinely try not to get an A, because the entire course is online and open-note. Dr. Bradbury is really funny, and her lectures can be super interesting. I recommend taking this class if you need something easy and fun to fill up your schedule.
Such an amazing and truly funny professor. Never hesitate to take her course!
Super easy class, and super fun professor. Recommend this class if needing a PSY lower division!

I love Dr. Bradbury! Her lecture were so informative of the material covered and she also offered so much advice in life, like how to stay positive and optimistic. Class was graded on 1 quiz per week on the lecture material and there were 2 video projects.

Not a psych major, took this class cause online/async/easy and it was. But writing this RMP because Dr. B is genuinely such a kind soul, sometimes her positivity helped me during the semester for other things. I wish I had her optimism and positivity...
Genuinely the most interesting and easiest class I have taken

EASY A. Take this class if you need a UGS class! Amazing professor who is super understanding and laid back. Very few not hard assignment. Laid back about due dates and can miss about 10 classes without it effecting your grade. Genuinely a good person to talk to and have as a recommendation.
Good lectures and a good class.

Clinical psych with Bradbury is one of the best classes in the psych major. TAKE IT. Her lectures are super interesting and easy to understand and readings aren't too heavy. Quizzes could sometimes be hyper-specific but as an online asynch course I get that. She was very nice and helpful over email too!
One of the best and most inspirational teachers I've had.
Love love love love LOVE her. Taken her FOR ANY COURSE if you can

Professor Bradbury is the whimsical, interesting professor you're expecting when you pick psychology as a major. She is someone who enjoys the topics she teaches and provides several connections to help you understand!

I really hated how this class was formatted. We had quizzes almost every other day, and the material itself wasn't hard but rather the amount of readings and lectures she provided was too much to do in a short amount of time. Each quiz was spaced out 2-3 days. Dr. Bradbury herself is fine, lectures tend to be repetitive and unnecessarily long.

I've taken Dr. Bradbury twice now, and both times she has easily remained my favorite professor of the semester. She is so kind and understanding, which is reflected in her recorded lectures and assignment leniency. The class itself is asynchronous and incredibly easy to do well in. I'd recommend her to anyone who needs a nice course to fill hours.

Weekly lectures & quiz. 2 video assignments, & weekly journaling. Bradbury made watching online lectures super engaging and great. Easy class & quizzes are in-line with lecture & attached sources. She is such a kind, caring prof. Big emphasis on well-being/positivity. Very clear and understandable lecture style. AMAZING PROF, can't recommend more!

Dr. Bradbury cares about her students and lets her students work at their own pace for the asynch class. She's positive, even through the videos without direct contact. Quizzes every week (all various types of questions), two video assignments, and self-graded journaling. Easy class. She also provides post-grad resources, so you know she cares
Kindest professor and interesting content

I love Dr. Bradbury's lectures! She made personality such a fun topic to learn about and broke down each personality theory in such an easy way. There was one 10 question quiz each week about the lecture. 2 video assignments also make up the grade, which were a fun way to showcase what we think of in terms of personality.

Everything is done on your own time/pacing except for two video assignments. Class content is so easy you hardly have to pay attention to the material, but it is all very interesting so you might want to, anyway! Dr. Bradbury is a great professor and easy grader who clearly wants students to succeed.
AMAZING LOVE HER TAKE HER! quizzes are so doable and so are the video assignments. completely async & i have nothing else to say other than she's wonderful!
this class is very easy and is completley asynchronous
Bradbury was super nice. This was an easy PSY course that I would def rec and take again. Simple asynch assignments are majority of the grade.

Really enjoy this prof. This is my second class with her and I definitely recommend her. She cares and knows a lot about what she teaches. Modules with lecture videos, some readings, and a quiz. 2 1-minute video assignments that are easy with clear grading. Open lectures and open notes for quizzes. Lectures and readings are actually interesting.

Easy A class with engaging content. Professor Bradbury is super helpful and understanding. Quizzes are straightforward, and deadlines are flexible. unstuck ai was a great study tool alongside the video assignments.
Dr. Bradbury is the best! Manageable class and reasonable assignments. Quizzes can sometimes have trick questions but, overall, great class.

Took the 5 week summer course. Super easy class, multiple quizzes that are not difficult, and a couple of assignments here and there. The professor herself was not easy to get in touch with despite sending multiple emails, for the most part the TA handled all the work and was wonderful.
Dr. Bradbury is always a joy to have as a professor, and there are really useful basic skills to be learned from her intro to clinical course.

mega easy class. 14 modules- vids, quiz (2 dropped) + ethics journaling assignment (self-graded) each week,  due at the end of the semester, and 2 short video assignments (the only hard deadlines). they're pretty accommodating w those too lowkey. dr.b's lectures are super positive n peppy n i appreciated that. def a really easy A and a fun course.

What an easy A. On the level of Jazz Appreciation. Weekly quizzes and optional journaling assignments (lol) that are supposed to be done week by week, but are technically due at the end of the semester. So you can def speedrun this class in the last week. Except for 2 video assignments, which are the only hard deadlines in this class.

One of the easiest and most interesting classes I've ever taken. Dr. Bradbury is truly so interesting to learn from. This class is very forgiving and is self-paced. Quizzes were open-note and were based on the lectures and readings. There were 2 easy video projects and self-graded journaling assignments. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!

This is the easiest class I've ever taken and its also fun and interesting! There's no enforced due dates so you can take the class at your own pace, but it's very easy to allow things to pile up. She's so sweet and her lectures are fun, highly recommend her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradbury genuinely cares about each student succeeding. Class is divided into modules all due at the last class day. Quizzes are straightforward and untimed. Overall a really enjoyable class that is probably the most stress-free it can get
Super caring and wants you to succeed! Watch online lectues, complete (untimed, online) quizzes, and do few easy projects and you will be good. Super easy yet interesting course!

Prof. Bradbury is the epitome of an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about her students, not only their grades but their mental health too. There are modules broken down for every week with clear instructions and a simple quiz with every module that covers the material. Highly recommend.

Bradbury is knowledgeable and passionate. She has good advice for after college. The class is a bit boring but easy. It's fully online so make a designated time each week to complete the weeks work. There are a couple lectures, a quiz, and a journaling assignment each week, no exams. There are 2 video assignments that are fairly easy and short.

There are no hard deadlines so it is easy to get behind, but also easy to get ahead! This is the kind of class you can finish 2 weeks before finals and spend your time on other classes. This class had interesting content, however, so it is not like you'll be glad to be done because it is not hard!

so easy- weekly quiz for each module and two video assignments as well as journaling. journaling isn't checked and is self-graded. quizzes are easy if you do what's in the module and take good notes. all quizzes were due last class day, so there's no real "deadlines" but it's easy to fall behind because of that. highly recommend !

I took her into to clinical psych course for my degree, but found it really helpful Tbh. it was all lecture based with some small journaling assignments, but overall was a really good (and doable) class when compared to my other content heavy classes.
So sweet. Lectures are interesting and quizzes follow them, no surprises. Video assignments are fun, great class.

The class is pretty easy, but it's laughable how little the professor or lead TA care. The TA just straight up told me the professor has NO involvement in the course, and it's all run by her lead TA. It is literally impossible to get a hold of the professor whose name is on the course. And the lead TA (Cherry) is rude and condescending to students.

Although the class was asynchronous, Dr. Bradbury's kindness and genuine care for her students is incredibly evident! Feels a bit lecture-heavy sometimes but it is all very tolerable. I highly recommend this course.

I absolutely enjoyed this class. Dr. Bradbury seems like a very understanding and caring professor. I personally seeked a lot of help from her TAs and shout out to them because they are absolutely amazing. They are so understanding and friendly and I couldn't thank them enough. There's a clear grading criteria and it's very easy to get an A! :)

Also took for PSY 364. These online classes with Dr. Bradbury were amazing! The self paced classes were great for getting the work done and Dr. Bradbury is extremely flexible. Two short video assignments and weekly quizzes were the major assignments.

Easy Online Class. Grade is determined by 15 quizzes (one on each topic), 2 video assignments, and private topic related journaling for every chapter (not required to turn in). Lectures are fun to listen to and quizzes are 10 mc questions based on lecture + reading material given for the week. Well organized. TA's are responsive and work with you.

Enjoyable class as always! Bradbury has a good structure to her classes and is a great lecturer. Only thing is, make sure to stay on top of your work as this is an asynchronous class (wish it had more deadlines). The quizzes would sometimes also have content that felt like it wasn't in the lectures; don't take the quizzes entirely too lightly.

Was a very fun and educational class. HIGHLY recommend to psych major or anyone just curious to take it. Dr. Bradbury is very fun and clearly passionate about the topic, which makes it more engaging. Huge applauses to her and would love to take another class from her soon!
all asynchronous online, super easy quizzes, 2 video assignments easy to get full credit. take for an easy A and learn more about personality psychology

I'm in the minority on Dr. Bradbury but I really did not like her as a professor. I lost one point on an assignment and she refused to explain why. It felt very frustrating to not receive any feedback. She is well informed and passionate about the topic which is a plus! But, I wish she gave more feedback instead of making everything an easy 100%.

She such a good professor and one of the easiest classes i've taken while at the same time furthering my education of psych and personality. She has lectures that are actually engaging which helps you do better on quizzes. Also quizzes are open everything which helps you look for the answer on your own, which helps you understand it more. Very easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradbury is extremely caring and passionate about clinical psychology. The class is super easy and interesting.
Such a good prof! So caring about her students and wants you to succeed. lectures are interesting and content is easy to learn.

Dr. Bradbury is so nice and really cares about her students. I took this class online, but her and her TAs were always super understanding and lenient with students. Plus, the material was interesting. It is self-paced with no exams. I definitely recommend this class.

I loved taking Personality Psych with Dr. Bradbury! The class is all online, so you can complete the weekly quizzes on your own time or by the end of the semester. You have weekly quizzes based on her single lecture video and very small readings. I would recommend it if you are a BS in psychology and want a stress-free and interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Bradbury's Summer Course and despite the course having a lot of material to get through in only 5 weeks, I truly learned so much from this class. Bradbury is an amazing lecturer know material and provides incredible insight of a clinical setting. My only complaint is that I wish I took it during a full term to really let it all sink in.

very interesting class, but Dr. Bradbury was even better. She made the class what is was and was very easy to follow and made it clear what was expected. Very caring and understanding, easy class and wonderful content! Please take her!

Dr. Bradbury is incredibly knowledgable in her field and SO SO passionate about her work. She organizes the class in a way that is catered to students and with an understanding that we have lives outside of class. Lecture material is all super interesting - do the work and you are certain to end the class with a solid grade.

She is so energetic and radiates positive energy! Her lectures are very easy to understand, and they're entertaining. The class is structured with a quiz each week (open note and untimed), weekly journaling assignments, and two video assignments. I will say, you will have to really understand the content to do well on some of the quizzes!

She has a great personality, and her energy just brightens up the room! She's very passionate about what she teaches and is a great advocate for recognizing issues in practice and beyond the classroom.
literally my fav course i have taken at UT i love dr. bradbury and cannot recommend her enough
Take this class. Dr. Bradbury is one of the best professors at UT, she is very kind and understanding and her lectures are just phenomenal.
Have taken her twice, incredibly easy but also filled with great info, she definitely cares about her students, provides lots of great resources, encourages you to work with classmates, no tests
