350 letters are not enough to talk about how much I love Professor Bradbury! Caring professor who wants the best for her students. Class is graded on open-note quizzes and two video assignments and she makes it really hard to not do well. Do not miss the chance to take her!!

She is so awesome, I loved having her an have taken several classes with her - I wish I could take every class with her. She's so accommodating and lenient and cares about her students more than anything else.
You can tell she knows so much about psychology and is extremely passionate! I recommend taking her personality psychology class as it is both interesting and an easy A if you attend lecture.

Dr. B is an amazing instructor! She combines her clinical experience really well with her pedagogic methods, which makes learning psychology pleasant and effective for students.
She goes above and beyond to accommodate students' needs. Definitely take any of her classes if you can!

Professor Bradbury is great, she's so nice and you can tell she really cares about her students. This was a very interesting class, not stressful or too time-consuming (she makes it clear that this is not a class you should worry about). The grade is only made up of quizzes, a journaling grade (self-graded), and 2 video assignments.

This class is so easy: you get to work with friends during quizzes and you can work ahead and be done with the class way before the semester ends. There are no late grades either besides two easy video projects! The only complaint is that Dr. Bradbury doesn't respond to Canvas emails, so you have to go through the TA for questions.

I honestly forgot I was taking this course throughout the semester how easy it was. You can work ahead and easily finish the coursework and be done with it. Though if you do want a consistent work schedule be wary because modules are posted at nondescript times.

Dr. Bradbury is a very engaging and intelligent lecturer. She is deeply fascinated by the field of psychology, and she really wants her students to not only learn but thrive! It is easy to fall behind in this class, so I would recommend working on it bit by bit rather than leaving it all to the end. The content is also very interesting. Take notes!
This class was so much fun! I had an incredible time taking this course and I would definitely recommend!
Dr. Bradbury clearly loves what she does. This is probably the best psychology course I have taken. 10/10 recommend.

A quiz per week on her lectures and two video assignments - straightforward and very easy to follow. Only spent two hours per week and quiz questions are directly from lectures and its open note. She doesn't have office hours and she doesn't reply to emails that fast so make sure to use TA's before you go to her. Anyone can get an A!

This class was great, as long as you read the supplied materials and looked at the lecture you were able to answer the 10-question quizzes every week. There were two video assignments that were one minute each which corresponded to a topic in class. If you need help with anything just reach out to her and the ta's, they really care.

This class was great, as long as you read the supplied materials and looked at the lecture you were able to answer the 10-question quizzes every week. There were video assignments that were one minute each which corresponded to a topic in class. If you need help with anything just reach out to her and the ta's, they really care.

I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Bradbury. She's so passionate about her work and extremely kind, she really wants everyone to succeed in her class! I loved this course, and I never found it a chore to watch her lectures or supplemental material. I would love to take more of her classes, she was a delight to learn from!

LOVED LOVED LOVED THIS CLASS!!! Took Intro to Clinical Psych. It's async so you can do everything on your own time. Really amazing and I loved it. You get what you put in and she really cares about the content of this class. TAKE HER!!!

Great professor! Took this class as a business major to fulfill an upper-division non-business course and got through it with ease! Dr. Bradbury cares about her students and makes sure to provide useful resources throughout the course. Take this class if you need the credit!

Literally the most forgiving and understanding professor I've ever had at UT. I've taken multiple classes with her and she's been constantly great. I always look forward to her classes at the beginning of each semester. Take her if you can!

Where do I begin with Dr. Bradbury?! She's an absolutely fabulous professor and makes all of her course material SO interesting! Her class is relatively easy, with modules that have lectures, readings, and other videos, then a quiz. None of the modules are due until the end of the semester, so there aren't hard deadlines.

Definitely take this professor!!!! Shes amazing! Her classes are interesting and she is one of the most caring and comprehensive professors i have taken! So far i have taken 3 courses with her and I definitely recommend!!!

Dr. Bradbury has to be one of the best professors in the psychology department or at UT in general. I love her energy and her quizzes as they really are not difficult to answer if you watch and can engage with her lectures. Which are great in my opinion. I did not struggle much in her course and would say it was my favorite course this semester.

she is an amazing and caring professor, psych personality is such an interesting class! just manage your time with the modules (since it's asynchronus) and you will be fine! there's 2 video projects and 12 quizzes, all open note.
TAKE THIS CLASS! Even if you're not a psych major, it's easily understandable, fun, and not very difficult. Professor Bradbury is an absolute gem!!!

Dr. Bradbury cares so much for her students which makes taking her class so nice. The class consists of 12 quizzes (if you watch and do all the required stuff you will do good) and 2 video assignments. You can take this class at your own pace which was great for me. I had so much fun in this class and I highly recommend taking a class with her!

I love Dr. Bradbury. I truly can't say enough positive things about her - her lectures are engaging, she gives you a sweet self-care tool kit, and she genuinely WANTS you to get an A in her class. She'll give an extension if you need one and is honestly one of the sweetest people ever. I've taken almost all of her classes.

I LOVE DR B!! Take her if you have the chance. Her lectures are such a treat! She's funny, relatable, and overall awesome! for each module you have a lecture/reading (but it's good!) and then a quiz (one try, not timed, VERY doable) and a journaling assignment. Couldn't recommend her enough, I just want to be her bestie. Also PSY 309 is so cool!!

She is an angel!! Class is engaging and challenging, but not extreme. Most assignments for her asynchronous class are due at the very end of the semester so you basically move at your own pace with the exception of a few assignments. Love her and she makes it so easy to learn!! She is also so knowledgable and helpful!

Please take her if you can. She is so nice and genuinely cares about everyone doing well. Her lectures are super fun and the quizzes are all open resource and easy. You won't have to worry about your grade at all she offers so much extra credit. Everything is due at the end of the semester and consists of mainly quizzes and fun video assignments.

Whatever class you're considering to take with Dr.B: JUST TAKE IT! She's an angel! Super caring and extremely knowledgeable--you can see she wants her students to succeed & she goes out of her way to help when needed. Class is structured in a very friendly-non-pressuring way that allows you to succeed at your own pace. One of my fave profs so far!

TAKE HER! She was super chill and makes the class so easy, yet so fun. Never had to worry about my grade. She is super caring and kind. She really wants everyone to succeed. If you have any problem getting work done just talk to her and she will happily help. Loved her so much I will be taking one of her other courses. No text all materials free.
I enjoyed watching Dr. B's recorded lectures. There are required readings and video projects, but they were not hard to follow and the quizzes were straightforward. She also offers extra credit!

Prof B is super sweet and her recorded lectures are very engaging. She wants to see her students succeed and she gives them plenty of room to do so. Although the course felt laid back, it was packed with meaningful material. I really enjoyed it!
Dr. B is a great professor, she is clear on her grading system. Lectures are enjoyable and so are the readings she assigns (most of them). She genuinely cares for her students' success.

Dr. Bradbury is very sympathetic, understanding and has the best lectures. The course format is all online and due dates are all set by you with recorded lectures and given material. There are only 12 quizzes, 2 video assignments and a self graded journal. I highly recommend this professor, she has been my favorite at UT so far!
SHE IS THE QUEEN OF PSYCHOLOGY. SO KNOWLEDGABLE, SWEET, AND CARING. NOT TO MENTION FANTASTIC LECTURES. TAKE HER!!!

This is my 2nd time taking a class with this professor and she is the BEST professor at Austin in my opinion. This class is graded on a few things: 12 quizzes (2 are extra credit/optional) and 3 video assignments that are EASY. Quizzes are super easy too if you pay attention to her online video lecture. No textbook used and class is asynchronous.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You HAVE to take this class. It's amazing and an easy way to get an A. The tests are not hard at all, if you pay attention in class you will get A's on them. The quizzes are super easy! The class is all online and no textbook is used. You watch her online lectures and take a small quiz after each module. The lowest 8 quizzes are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bradbury is my favorite professor at UT. This is my third class with her and she is the best! All of her classes are super easy. Class only entailed self graded journals, 12 quizzes and 2 video assignments. I recommend her to everyone. She is super caring and respects her students

This is the second course I've taken from Dr. Bradbury. She can ramble a bit, but the lectures tend to be interesting and easy to digest. The course consists of Modules (asynchronous due dates) and two assessment projects that have harsh deadlines (these are very easy). Take this class and learn about child behavior problems!

Loved this class and her! You can tell she's passionate about the subject and does a great job explaining it in lectures. Also makes the assignments fun and interesting. I feel like I could have learned a lot more, but I still recommend taking her classes if you're a psych major! Also, she's very difficult to contact in email or office hours.

Dr. Bradbury was an amazing and very understanding professor with classes being online due to covid. The class material was very straightforward and easy to understand as well as interesting to learn about. Due to the workload and grading criteria, I did not need to worry about this class during all this uncertainty which was very helpful mentally.

one of THE best professors ever. if you have the chance to take professor bradbury, DO IT! her lectures are like watching TV!! extremely interesting, and what makes it better is that there is no textbook for the class! youll want to go to class if you take her:) she has a passion for psych, and cares so much about her students.

She's a real gem and so wholesome. Her class does have a bunch of quizzes but as long as you watch the lectures and study a bit you'll be fine. I will definitely try and have her again in the future for other psych classes. Her journal assignments are self-graded and the projects are really fun to do. Loved her class, and her lectures are awesome.

Dr. Bradbury is AMAZING. Her quizzes are straightforward, the lectures were interesting and she offers extra credit. You have 3 video assignments, 10 quizzes and a self-graded journaling. Its self paced and everything has to be in by a certain date, but if you do a quiz a week, you'll finish a week before the deadline. HIGHLY recommend.

Easiest class. just had to watch the required lecture material and take quizzes. no test, no finals. only quizzes, 2 video assignments, and self-graded journal activities. the kindest teacher ever, 100/10 would recommend, protect this woman at all costs. the lectures were super interesting and so easy to follow along.

She's my absolute favorite prof at UT. She gives information so clearly and concisely, and the way she explains it makes it super easy to understand and interesting. A year later, I still think about her classes. Pay attention to random hours for deadlines though - messing this up once brought me from an A- to a B+ for Clinical Psych.
Dr. B is a sweetheart. She really cares about what she's teaching and for her students. The TA's can be picky when it comes to assignments so be sure to follow all directions.

I took Abnormal and Clinical Psychology with Dr. Bradbury because she was just so wonderful. Even if you aren't interested in psych (I'm not a psych major) she is such a warm and incredible person who will teach you how to live a rich and happy life. She's also the only reason for my 98th percentile score on the psych section of the MCAT. Take her.

Dr. Bradbury is an amazing online professor! Her lectures were always so interesting and she made them a lot of fun. The tests aren't too difficult if you keep up with the material and do the study guide or rewatch lectures right before the test. If you can, I highly recommend to take a class with Dr. Bradbury!

Dr Bradbury is by far one of the best online professors. She makes material so easy to understand and takes the time to explain harder concepts. (There are not really any hard concepts in this class). Super easy online class allows you to take tests at home

I loved this class! Dr. Bradbury was very knowledgable and had lots of experience in many fields. All you really have to do is watch the lectures and take the 3 question quizzes before the due dates. The tests were based off of notes and the readings/videos for the lectures. There are two assignments outside of watching lectures. Take this class!!!

Dr. Bradbury's lectures were eye-opening and really inspired me to change my outlook on the world. I took it online so I could do it at my own pace. The quizzes were easy. The exams were more difficult, you have to remember detailed info and dx criteria. Take good notes and study well before exams because they are worth most of the grade.

This class is pretty easy. Pre-recorded lectures and modules to go with them. You get plenty of drops so there's room for error. The exams were easy as well but they compromise most of the grade so bombing one could hurt you. Her lectures were fun and interesting. She's very respected among her students and for a good reason!

The lectures are already pre-recorded, so attendance doesnt matter. Dr. Bradbury does a really good job at translating content straight from lecture to test. It was super easy. Theres a benchmark for every module and I could get 3/3 on almost all of them without trying. Best way to navigate the class is to take really good notes on the lectures.
10/10 recommend clinical psych online, easy, structured and Dr. B is the best. Absolute legend

Took Abnormal Psych online with her. Hands down the best class and the best professor I've had here at UT! Lectures are incredibly interesting and engaging, she presents material in an informative and entertaining matter. Required materials will help inform you further on the subject matter, and the optional material will do so further.
Amazing professor. She makes me love psychology and genuinely enjoy doing work for it. Her lectures are inspiring and interesting, I wish I could take her for every class
You could literally never watch any of lectures or read any of the material for this class and pass.

Took this as a web based class. As long as you read the slides, watch all of the lectures, and take notes, you will pass. Class consists of 5 short, 500-word writing assignments and 4 exams which were all pretty straightforward and from the lectures.

Don't be fooled by the word "abnormal", the class isn't nearly cryptic as it sounds. That doesn't mean the material isn't worth learning though. Lots of self-help material included. She's EXTREMELY knowledgeable, hard-working, and honestly over-qualified to be a professor. She does it because she loves teaching that much. Can't recommend enough.

Dr. Bradbury is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had! She's caring & her lectures will interest you. Only 4 exams, 4 writing assignments, and module quizzes, which are all very easy. Plus, Dr. Bradbury provides tips on how you can give a happier life! If you need a GPA booster, take this class! You'll learn a lot from Dr. Bradbury.

Dr. Bradbury is a wonderful, upbeat woman who actually cares about her students unlike most professors. Even if you're not going into the psychology field, this class is super interesting and helpful. Extremely easy A, definitely a GPA booster. Highly, highly recommend.

Best class and professor I have ever had at UT. She really cares not only about her students success, but their mental health. Easy benchmark Quizzes and writing assignments. Exams are pretty straightforward however there were some weird exam questions . Averages on exams have been 88, 89, 87, 90. Take HER!!!

Lovely person, lovely class! Take it if you have the opportunity - the workload is doable, and the information is really interesting. You can do the modules at your own pace, but the exams are on specific dates. Ill definitely take any class from her I can, she seems so sweet, patient, and knowledgeable.
Love, love, love her! I wish she was my professor for every class! She keeps things fun and interesting and I don't dread lectures.

I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Bradbury. I took her online abnormal psych class but it felt like I could still get to know her. Her office hours always have a wait because of how welcoming she is. She's a great person and professor alike.

Dr. Bradbury's online Abnormal Psych class was so much fun and very interesting. She clearly outlined her expectations in grading. Some of the quiz questions were a bit tricky, but there was a fair appeal process in place. Overall, her class was enlightening and I recommend her particular section of anything because of her bubbly personality.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love her so much she is so awesome and open minded! Just watch the lectures and do the readings and you will be fine, I feel like the purpose of the class is to learn instead of stressing out about tests and I can tell she understands that. Also on the side note she reminds me of Tina Fey lol

One of my favorite classes I've taken! Dr. Bradbury cares about her students and their well being. The material was very interesting and relevant. I have nothing bad to say!!! She's awesome, love her story.

I absolutely loved Bradbury's class because she was very relatable and funny during her lectures which gave me a mental break from my more difficult courses. When I joined the course, I thought it was going to take up a lot of time, but it took an hour to prepare for it. To ace the benchmarks, rewatch the lectures and take solid notes on them.

Dr. Bradbury is by far my favorite professor at UT. She is so caring and knowledgeable. I love her enthusiasm and genuine interest in her students and the material she's teaching. There are benchmarks (quizzes) everyday, so don't skip class. There are also assignments that are As as long as you do them. I enjoyed this class so much and learned tons
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I don't have a single bad thing to say about Dr. Bradbury. Abnormal psych was fun and interesting, which made it easy to study for and easy to get an A. Just take this class, you won't regret it.

Dr. Bradbury is so sweet. I took this online, so we had to watch the lectures and take a quiz on them after. I got to meet her in person and she's very knowledgable and very passionate about her work. As long as you watch the modules her tests are very straight forward. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Bradbury is amazing. I have taken 2 of her online classes and I have never had a professor teach so clearly and entertainingly. I don't know why anyone would say anything negative about her or the classes. There were some technical issues at times but the TA's and Dr. Bradbury were very understanding. I learned way more than regular lectures.

Maybe I'm just sad deep down, but I found her excessive happiness to be artificial and annoying. If you take this class online, it ISN'T live. It's a recording of a class from 2 years ago (imagine the problems this creates w/ dates). The class itself is a joke. Use Ctrl-F you can ace her daily quizzes (90% of you grade) without paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradbury changed the way I look at education, people, the world, and myself. She is one of the best, if not the absolute best, professors I've ever had. I'm not kidding when I say when her class ended I cried literal tears. Taking one of her classes changed my educational career, and I've considered transferring back to UT just for her. No joke

I took this class online and was kind of hard, 26 Benchmarks (1 x class) and 4 short essays (under 500 words). The benchmarks (quizzes) are a mess, we had "SEVERAL" of them graded incorrectly due to their wrong answers. You have to pay close attention to them to make sure they are graded right. *I had to email the TAs several times on such matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I didn't learn a whole lot taking online Abnormal Psych. The online format allowed you to easily blow off the class. Although it's an easy A, I wouldn't recommend if you actually want to learn this material. There are no tests-- only daily quizzes which you can use your notes for. So naturally, I didn't study because I didn't really need to.

Best professor I've ever had. Got to meet her in person and she is super cool and nice. Awesome voice and super smart. Very passionate about her field and about teaching. Likes to make jokes and is all around an amazing professor and person. Take her if you can!

I took online Abnormal Psych with Dr. Bradbury that had been recorded during a previous semester. The class was amazing, well-structured, and informative. Grades are based on 8 question open-note benchmarks at the beginning of each class plus a couple one page papers that are graded for completion. I learned so much from this class.

Dr. Bradbury is so sweet! I had her for abnormal psych. I don't really like the online broadcasting format, but the good news is there are no tests. Instead, at the beginning of class, you take an 8-question quiz. This does mean you can't get behind and you have to do the readings and take good notes, but she offers great destress & life advice <3

Dr. Bradbury is a wonderful professor who genuinely cares about her students. She's positive, inspirational, and always happy to meet students. 4 writing assignments (short, super easy), no exams but daily benchmark (8 questions about the previous lecture), and a one-question quiz at the end of each lecture. Not the easiest A, but definitely doable
Great professor and person, University needs more professors like her! you can tell she cares about her students. Very well spoken and smart professor. Highly recommend!

She really cares about her students and does a great job of explaining concepts. No tests no final just daily benchmarks worth 60% of your grade. Class topics were very interesting and engaging. Easy A and interesting class.
This class was very informative. The online setting was wonderful. It was obvious that she genuinely cared to get to know her students and cared for their well-being.
wonderful professor. Definitely recommend. Online abnormal psych was my favorite class this semester!

Dr. Bradbury is hands down the best professor I have had at UT. She is one of the smartest people I have ever met, while also being incredibly kind. Her lectures are so engaging, she knows her stuff, and she knows how to get students to really understand. I plan on taking every class that she teaches, because her intro psych class was so wonderful.

I can't even begin to describe how amazing Dr. Bradbury is. She genuinely cares about all her students. Office hours are amazing and engaging. I already had AP credit for psych and was skeptical about taking psych again with her, but it is so worth it. She is such an amazing human all around and so respected by all of her students. Take her class!

Dr. Bradbury is AMAZING! She makes her lectures extremely interesting and she is really funny. She loves talking to students and helping, so make sure to attend her office hours. There are only two exams and they are pretty difficult but the end-of-the-year project and the 2 writing assignments are very easy.
Dr. B is a great teacher and a great person to just go and talk to. Take the time to go to her office hours-very worth it

Dr. B is so great! I am so glad I got to have her my first semester. The big project at the end of the class is worth the bulk of your grade, and pretty much everyone makes an A. However, her class is AMAZING. You won't mind getting up in the morning. Her lectures are so entertaining, and she is so caring towards her students.

Love, love, love Dr. Bradbury! She gives out random extra credit, so go to class. She literally reviews the entire exam the class before the test. And she actually cares about her student. By far my favorite professor!

Dr. B is my favorite professor I've ever had! Her lectures are FASCINATING. I never want them to end. She's also very flexible and always there for you if you're having trouble with something. Just go to office hours. I wish she taught more classes so I could take them all.
Wonderful inspirational professor. She embodied what she taught and always seemed happy to teach. You won't regret taking this class.

Dr Bradbury was truly an inspirational and wonderful profesor. I had her for intro to Clinical Psych and she exemplified to me the ideal therapist while teaching it. The class went beyond psychology and into my daily life as well. Everything was easy gradewise as long as you paid moderate attention.
More than just an easy "A" class: you will leave every lecture in a better mood (: she is passionate, entertaining, and worth every minute of your time.
Easily one of the best psych lecturers at UT. Get to know her if you can. She's very personable, a great lecturer, informative and keeps class interesting.
Take this class! Dr. B is awesome, entertaining, and if you at all try you can make an A (she has the test in her hand the class before exam day, and tells you everything that you need to know...)

Dr. B is so awesome! She makes her class very interesting and fun to attend. She doesn't take roll, but I wouldn't recommend missing class because whatever the little anecdotes she mentions are always included on exams. I really loved her class am looking forward to having more classes with her!

Dr. Bradbury is a professor who truly loves what she does, and she's good at doing it. On top of being a mother, wife, and professor, she also has her own clinical practice. Yet she still puts 100 percent into teaching. She makes psychology come alive and relates everything she teaches to how it personally affects you. She's really one of a kind!
bradbury is the best professor i have had at UT! everyone needs to take her for PSY301 or any other class she teaches!
No Comments

Professor is frequently confused in her own lectures and does not answer questions well. There are pacing issues as the most difficult content is often skimmed over. The exams/assignments are moderately challenging, and you need to self-teach most of the content. Start studying for exams a week in advance- content is dense. There is EC though.

Cambronne is a nice and intelligent woman. However, she is not able to translate her knowledge in a digestible manner. She often confuses herself in lecture and is not proficient in the calculations she's teaching. Concepts are not clearly explained or stated. She's kind, but I had to teach everything myself. Disappointing.

Dr. Cambronne was contagiously passionate about the subject, and tried to make the lectures applicable to life. The class was difficult for me and the exams were all open ended, but she has extra credit and I heard she rounds end of sem. I think this is the only class she teaches so she learns everyone's names and makes a point to reach out to you.

Dr. Cambronne is really nice and very knowledgeable. I just wish I could've gone to more of her reviews/office hours and asked more questions in class. I wish I knew how to study for this class. The extra credit she offered this semester saved my grade, so do all the extra credit worksheets! The old midterms that she had posted were helpful.

Very lecture heavy class however she is good at thoroughly explaining the content and making it engaging. TA's are kind and knowledgeable. Do ALL the extra credit opportunities she provides and you'll get a good grade. There are no curveballs on exams. If it's not on the lecture slides, it's not on the tests. Very manageable class.

Dr. Cambronne is very nice and knowledgeable. Her class is tough, but a lot of that isn't her fault. However, she does tend to over emphasize things that won't be tested, and underemphasize things that will be tested. Biochem is inherently not easy, but the TAs are super helpful. Go to discussion sections!

lectures are usually hard to get and prof cambronne stumbles often, mostly when a student doesn't understand first try or asks any question. i would probably feel better if i went to office hours. TAs were great, very helpful at discussion sections. content is application, not memorizing, on the midterms, but study past exams and you'll be fine

Horrible lecturer, and unkind. She was often lost and confused by her own content and stumbled to answer students questions. If you were unable to answer her questions she gave a judgmental face .Very difficult tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are difficult to follow most of the times. I was usually left confused. The course is very exam heavy and is hard to prepare for the tough exams. She is sweet and the teaching team is helpful, but overall, the material should have been presented in a more digestible format, with more practice similar to exams. I barely passed.

Good lecturer. Midterm exams was not that bad at all if you attend lecture and understand what she said. Be sure to attend the discussion because TA will help solve Canvas quizzes. Final was application based but you're allowed a cheatsheet. She curves final and offer 2% extra credit so an A is very doable.

Exams are heavily application based. There is little to no opportunity to get that type of application practice, so exams are very difficult to prepare for, and she does not offer a curve. To do well in the course, you need to be the type of student that thinks above and beyond the things taught in class. TAs are amazing though, ask them for help

Dr. Cambroonne has her own pace of teaching style which sometimes could be difficult for the students to understand, but overall the TA is very helpful in this course, their review slide is going to be the most important thing in this whole course as it covers everything that you expect in the midterms.

Dr.C's teaching team has been very supportive and reachable throughout the semester.She offers many ways for you to do well in this class.But 339F is definitely not the easiest and I tried really hard to do well.Dr.C is very accommodating and helpful, and although still somewhat of a new professor,she is nonetheless very exceptional when teaching.

Cambronne is clearly knowledgeable (studies NADH) and is keen on the topics taught in the class. However sometimes it doesn't translate well. 4 exams and a drop that are not difficult if you know the material. Studying is very important for this class as things can quickly become complicated. Must understand chemistry to do well.
Her teaching style may NOT be for everyone. However i will say she does make passing the class VERY doable. Extra credit can be worth more than an exam.

Dr. Cambronne cares about learning and that her students are also effectively learning the expected material. She makes course adjustments oriented towards what is best favored for her students' to build a growth mindset and become interested within the field of biochemistry, especially cell metabolism. The textbook and youtube videos are helpful!

I'll be honest and say her lectures were a little hard to follow at the beginning. I could tell she was a relatively new professor. However with that being said, she is super nice and I saw a lot of improvement through out the term. She is extremely qualified to be teaching the course, and I felt she was very compassionate with her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Cambronne taught the second half of BCH 339F with Prof Barrick. Barrick was great! Cambronne is not a good lecturer. She doesn't seem to fully know the material at times and doesn't explain information well. I'm sure she's usually better (this was during COVID online classes), but if you want to learn in class and not from google, avoid her.

Past reviews are definitely out of date, and she has taken the feedback. She's not the sweetest lady, but she teaches everything that's on the exams. Also answers questions really well. 5 homework assignments that are chill. Pop quizzes as a way to get attendance (super easy quizzes). I'd recommend.
Professor Gorback was tough but fair, I genuinely enjoyed her lectures

I really enjoyed taking her class and I don't think the past reviews are reflective of her current teaching. The grading consisted of 5 homework assignments, 3 mandatory guest lectures, attendance, the midterm, and the final. Nothing was too heavily weighted, and I believe everything was graded very fairly. Highly recommend!

This is by far the worst class I have ever taken in my time at UT. Not because of the material, but because of how insensitive and rude Gorback was. She showed zero remorse for her students. Two exams - mainly long/short answers. Mandatory attendance. 2 HWs over complicated topics never discussed in lectures. Avoid her at all costs. Not worth it.

Final exam was mainly on a topic she told us we wouldn't be tested on... There goes my grade! I understand this is her first year teaching but didn't even seem like she was willing to learn how to improve herself. Also a real estate class, not an economics class? Weird. Would not recommend this professor to anyone unless she cleans this class up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've taken at McCombs. Two exams (7 questions free response), two difficult homework assignments, and quizzes with complicated wording to make you fail. She always sounds like she hates answering questions, and to make matters worse, we were expected to memorize over 400 slides for each exam. AVOID AT ALL COST!!!

Pls do not take. Your gpa will tank. Professor is passive aggressive. Exams are nearly impossible. Grading policies wack. Attendance policy wack. The homeworks are wack (take hours even after working on it with others and going to office hours). Be warned if this is the only intro class available skip out on the RE minor and take another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst experiences that I have had at UT and that is not an exaggeration. Don't have much to say as the other comments are all you need to know...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: avoid at all costs, take anyone else as a matter of fact. Passive aggressive teaching style, don't know how she was even hired. Expects us to be tested on creating numerous pro formas for a final exam without any notes, after maybe doing 1 assignment in class that took us days to do. Honestly a terrible experience.

This is the best example of someone that is a good researcher but has a hard time conveying information to students. Lectures were not engaging and she often made passive aggressive remarks. The material itself could have been easy if it had been clearly communicated, but there were often contradicting statements and mistakes on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most boring classes I've ever sat through. She is snarky, very passive aggressive, acts like she knows everything and nothing at the same time, and is a tough grader with wacky grading policies. The guest lectures were the best part and she would consistently interrupt them to ask her own questions. Take any other professor if into RE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some of the most dry lectures I have ever been through. And grading depends primarily on open ended tests that cover over 400 slides worth of material. She teaches like a robot and attendance is mandatory. Wouldn't recommend to anyone at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most difficult, sour professor I've ever had. Professors w/ 40+ years of teaching hold more grace and kindness than her, she just started. She'll dock more points if she regrades, 80% of grade=2 HWs + 2 exams, always has a pessimistic attitude, HW/quizzes/exams are intensely difficult, all free responses. I admire her commitment to misery!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this class has made me check the degree audit to see if i really wanted to be a neuro major. the class isn't hard, it's the exams and the homeworks. exams cover things that were mentioned maybe once and tested in confusing wording. the grading is so harsh, especially in exams. you miss one mcq and you're at a 96. please don't take this class!

the old comments are a good summary of what this class is like now. rough midterms and sometimes the questions are things she doesn't explicitly teach (-4 points for every missed MCQ). harsh FRQ grading in homeworks. Has LO's but doesn't follow them to make the test. dont be a neuro major is what I've learned. content isn't hard; grading is.

This was a difficult course, but highly rewarding. You walk out with an amazing understanding of neuroscience, and scientific writing. 3 Lab reports, almost weekly quizzes, and in-person assignments. Go to Dr. Chancey's OHs, and ask questions! She is very kind, and helpful.

This is a difficult class. You are graded mainly by 3 lab reports and a final project. Quizzes can be difficult. However, Dr. Chancey is an incredible person and professor and WANTS you to grow and succeed. She approaches all student interactions with compassion and is very passionate about electrophysiology. I learned a lot in this course
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Dr.Chancey this recent spring semester, and she was AMAZING. Dr.Chancey truly cares about her students and makes a tireless effort to make her class a suitable learning environment. Her lectures and demonstrations are both engaging and interesting. I couldn't have asked for a better professor for my first neuroscience course :) 10/10

Grades very hard and your grade is based primarily on 3 lab reports and one final project. She quizzes based of lectures which she is reluctant to record and she glosses over complex topics very fast. Very inconsiderate and poorly explains concepts. Take someone else if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her Sp24 when she was completely new to teaching the course. Exams can be challenging but I think that's just the nature of the course. As she gets more experience with the intro course I'm sure things will smooth out and from what I've heard, she's better than Mauk!

i loved dr. chancey's class. you can tell she cares about her students and is definitely approachable. only thing is, some of the midterm questions are worded poorly and they grade frq questions pretty harshly. but i think they fixed that problem later on in the course. there's a ton of extra credit and she also does really cool demos in class!!

Chancey is nice but she is also a new professor. She graded hw very harshly, & most missed questions on exams were due to confusing wording. At times, it was hard to understand what she was asking for. Really goes in depth & lays a solid foundation in neuroscience. Invested alot of time and still ended w a B, more time would get you an A for sure.

Dr. Chancey was an amazing professor and was extremely collaborative with us. She genuinely wants her students to learn and succeed. With that said, the weight distribution was intense, exams are 80% of your grade, but it's manageable with the "fudge" points you can earn and if you do well on the hws and instapolls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First two exams very difficult and tested on specific details hardly emphasized in class (large time commitment for an A). The last two exams were more straightforward. Overall averages for midterms around 70s. Generous extra credit. One of the first HW assignments was confusing and poorly made, TAs tried to help and gave incorrect explanations.

I LOVE Dr. Chancey. NEU330 is a very difficult class, but she makes an effort to be caring and understanding. The lectures are definitely fast paced, but that is the nature of the course. The exams are fair and she offers an extra 5% at the end of the class. I would love to take her again and I had a great experience with her. One of my favorites.

Idk why there are so many bad reviews, I LOVED Dr. Chancey! The course material was so interesting and applicable to real life. Chancey truly cares about her students, is very accessible & helpful. Lectures were engaging (but fast-paced) and exams were fair. Textbook is great for supplemental learning but not required to do well. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just really a meanie poo
Very unreasonable and condescending towards students.
She's nice but disorganized. Classes aren't well structured. Fun course though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everyone I talked to in class seemed to be taking it as they hoped to pursue higher studies and thus, cared about their grades and put in much effort. However, still, the class avg. on most exams ranged around a 75. She is easy to talk to but disorganized & she graded very harshly (looking for specific answers) on both test questions and hws.

Chancey really is a kind professor and she does care a lot, but her lectures are a bit confusing and don't necessarily help much when studying for her exams. This being said, it was still her first semester teaching at UT; she definitely graded a lot harsher than expected, especially on HW's and FRQ on exams. Overall, I don't recommend taking her.

Neuro is an inherently hard class, and this was Dr. Chancey's first time teaching 330, she tried her best and you can tell! With that being said, I feel like I did everything I could to succeed in this class but still wasn't able to. The content is interesting, but the unfair grading of HWs/exams kind of ruined it for me. She will get better tho!

My experience was Dr. Chancey's first time teaching NEU 330, so please take the reviews with a grain of salt. She will likely improve with practice. If you want to do well, you really have to put in the work to rewatch lectures and understand the homeworks. Go to SIs and OHs. Tests are doable and give tons of partial credit, you just have to try.

The class is test heavy, but doable. There were extra credit opportunities and the HW came in clutch. Dr. Chancey wants you to genuinely understand the material, and the homework is representative of this. Lectures are recorded (and worth rewatching). The class certainly wasn't for everyone, but for an introductory neuro course it was mostly fair.

Chancey is not great at teaching, doesn't teach details she expects you to know on the exams, TA's carried, very strict and specific grading criteria that isn't clear or specified before tests/homework. Frustrating due to grading criteria + could test a large proportion of the test on a tiny detail she mentioned once during class. Extra credit +4%

Dr. Chancey's neurobiology lab was wonderful. It was certainly difficult, especially at the beginning of the course, but Dr. Chancey made her expectations clear while pushing us to *really* understand what was going on in each experiment. I had to ask a lot of questions and spend a lot of time with the material, but it was very worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so passionate and I love her! She knows her stuff and I like her conceptual approach to class. Exams are detail oriented so I rewatched all the lectures before them. Content super interesting

Dr. Chancey has her moments of being too disorganized in her lecture, and oftentimes can make it hard to follow, however, she is attentive to the needs of her students. The first neuro class is always the hardest (since it's a lot of new things), but she did the best she could to meet our needs. She is very kind and knowledgeable!

This class covers lots of detailed material and her lectures can get fast, but rewatching the lecture videos is effective for studying. Lots of extra/partial credit (including up to 4 bonus points on the OVERALL grade!!) and super generous with points on exams. Exams are reasonable. Super accessible and willing to explain concepts in office hours.

Professor Chancey was overall a great professor. If you rewatch lecture videos and just take some time to understand the material outside of class, then you will most likely do fine like I did. Her exams are not difficult in my opinion and are very doable with proper studying; they're just a graded a bit weirdly but doable.

The material is difficult but the class is doable as long as you use the resources provided such as recorded lectures, TA reviews, and SI sessions. I never read the textbook and fell asleep during lectures, but ended up with an A-. Lots of extra credit.
horrible horrible professor

you have to be joking with this class, she makes it so hard for no reason. it is so unorganized the TA's, her, and lecture slides all say a different thing. She is nice sometimes but other than that super condescending and gets mad if we have a single question. tests are so so hard no matter what you do. DO NOT TAKE HER!!!!

I am a Jessica Chancey lover. Best professor on campus and I have nothing but love and respect for her. Her teaching methods are so easy to follow, and the class is very easy, even with it being mandatory attendance. Everyone rating her class 1.0 are just salty they can compete intellectually with individuals such as myself.

Don't fall for the good reviews, avoid at all costs!! A very sweet person, but not a great professor. Very unclear grading criteria on exams and homework. FRQ questions are a nightmare. Lectures are difficult to follow and the slides are mostly pictures.

The content is difficult yes but Chancey's lectures are fine, she explains things well, is very easy to approach. The exams are not that bad, if you take notes during lecture, answer the learning objectives, review and talk through the different concepts it is extremely doable if you put the effort it. I love Chancey and she made neuro so fun.

Attended lectures, re-watched lectures, studied ahead of time, went to the SI sessions, read the textbook... and still struggled with this class. Honestly, the content is interesting and not hard to retain, but the way exams and HWs were graded made it way more difficult than it needed to be.

Very unclear grading rubrics for the free response on exams and looks for specific details not asked for to get full credit. Lectures are very unorganized. Slides are just graphics and very few words. Explain material in very confusing manner even though it's an intro class. Must memorize word for word what she says to do well. Would not take again
simply cannot teach and exams are just awful

The worst professor had ever. Unfair grading criteria. unclear wording and grading rubrics on exams. seems to be a nice person but horrible horrible teacher. extra credit is offered. I put in over 12 hours a week into this class and still not doing good. have to go above and beyond. should not be this difficult. gives me a learning disability

She says she wants feedback until you give her honest feedback. She gives extra credit, but the way she grades the exams makes no sense. She counts off for things she didn't even specify in the question. I submitted a regrade request, and she rudely told me I was abusing the regrade policy and dismissed my concern without addressing my question.

all the good reviews are from people that are cracked. she is the worst professor i've ever had. even if you word for word memorize what she says in lectures some points will be taken off of exams. her grading rubrics make no sense whatsoever. on top of this her lectures make no sense. even if you take good notes lectures are incoherent ramblings

Pro: Lots of extra credit, recorded lectures, class groupme, seems nice
Con: Unclear grading criteria for exams, conflicting answers from TAs, contradicts her lectures/slides, bad lecturer
You might get a good grade in the class but she is overall not someone you wanna take Neuro One from. As a friend described "she's incompetent"

DO NOT let the positive reviews fooI you. The TAs, SI instructors, and professor would give conflicting answers on HW so no one would know what to write. Wasn't explicit for exam questions but would still be graded harshly. Contradicted herself in lectures/slides. Discouraged submitting regrade requests and made the process intentionally difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I genuinely felt like if she had made her slides less picture based and more info it would've been fine, the other reviews are treating going to office hours, rewatching lectures, and meeting w/ her outside of class as normal, you should be able to go to lecture do the required homeworks and understand material well not have to do 10 extra steps

bro swear to god I would rewatch lectures after attending class and still not understand how to answer the learning objectives & HW w/o missing something or getting something wrong. The exams have such weirdly worded questions u feel incompetent reading them. idk made me feel like I didn't belong in neuroscience wouldn't recommend tbh.

Major complaint is the grading criteria for this class. Questions on hw are sometimes unclear. Exams have several free response which is fine, but would sometimes lose points for not mentioning things that she wasn't clear on requiring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nah the ppl here just salty because they had to study. Medians were 80 which is fair. I rewatched lectures to do well on the exams. She gives so much partial & extra credit that i don't understand why people are complaining. Her lectures are diagrams, so you should rewatch the lectures to understand. My only complaint is required attendance.

Don't listen to all the terrible reviews! They just didn't put in any effort into the class, or didn't study in the way that Dr. Chancey explicitly told us to.
She was so passionate about neuroscience and was very knowledgeable in her lectures. 
Exams are very similar to lectures and they are recorded. Rewatch for a good grade. 
Not easy, not hard.

This class is hard, but not because of the professor, it's just difficult content, but so much good info. Chancey is so understanding and will meet with you outside of class time, she really wants us to succeed. there's a bunch of random extra credit and bonus added in here and there. TAs also very helpful with exam prep

I LOVE Dr. Chancey and this class. The lectures are good and her slides are good, as long as you pay attention in lecture, take notes, study the learning objectives, and ask questions you will be fine. Im genuinely confused by these reviews, Chancey is amazing, the material can be difficult but that just requires effort. TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!

Class was so bad, I'm changing my major. The lectures are incoherent ramblings. The TA's are mean and incompetent. The exam grading is so vague and unpredictable it is impossible to foresee what points will be deducted. The only way to study is to watch her lectures and memorize her exact wordings. No reward for actually learning the content.

Her practice problems are pretty bad overall. I know the TA review sessions are what a lot of students lived off of for the exams. Immense detail is wanted on the free response questions, it is pretty ridiculous. I guess it makes sense to not have a document of key concepts to know for the exam because she basically wants you to know everything.

Lectures are hard to follow but are the only resource other than the textbook. She is unapproachable, doesn't know how to explain, and knows that the class is struggling yet keeps moving forward. The exams are detail-oriented and grading is very particular. If this intro course is your first introduction to neuro I would not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Idk who is leaving such constant bad reviews but this class is not bad. If you take lecture notes, discuss concepts thoroughly, study ahead of time, and attend review, you WILL do fine. Her tests are basically explain the concept or experiment & memorize the facts/pathways. The content is all new, so you may struggle, but study & effort are key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course is disorganized which disadvantages students who are paying to learn. The structure of the lectures make learning more difficult than need be. The professor contradicts herself and randomly mentions information that was never discussed before. "As I told you..." (she has not, in fact, told us). No thorough explanations of content in OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the lectures are extremely convoluted and topics that are in great detail on the test might be 1 slide in the lecture. grading scale needs some work as homework criteria makes no sense and the tests are so quick one after another

This class was fine as long as you watch the lectures and take very detailed notes. It's important to memorize everything she says in lecture because they will probably be covered on tests. TA reviews are helpful because they sometimes go over very similar questions to the exam.

Dr Chancey is obviously very knowledgeable in her subject, but does not know how to convey this knowledge in a manner that is needed for an intro class. The grading criteria for this class is outrageous. One mistake on the hw could drop grade 30-40 pts. Unfortunately, she was the only prof teaching this class at the time, otherwise, would not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's sweet, and somewhat approachable. But her lectures are confusing, office hours explanations are contradictory, and tests are unbearable. I'd STRONGLY suggest avoiding her class unless her class is restructured. And the TAs are pretty much useless.

Has unclear grading criteria on exams. Asks for one thing then expects you to mention details from lecture that was not explicitly asked for. Had select all questions that gave "partial credit" just to take not give you credit. Talks in jargon and 2x speed during lectures. Honestly good luck.

Hardest to follow lectures I've ever encountered; it makes me feel like I have a learning disability. Resources outside of the lecture are super limited so you kind of have to view the lectures. Class is also required or you lose points.

The class is so disorganized and scattered. The actual content is interesting and not too difficult to learn, but the way she organizes this class is messy. Lectures way too fast and skims over important details. Vague and tests over minor details she never went over. No grace/compassion outside of class/doesn't budge and is not the nicest.

Lectures are super unorganized and slides are just graphs/images. she is very knowledgeable on the topics, but she goes way too fast and acts like we should understand what she says immediately. Exams are tricky and have frq and select all questions; select all questions are graded SUPER unfair; you can get 0 points even if you pick correct answers

This class was shamefully bad. Lectures are shockingly bad. It is unclear what the scope of the course is and what concepts are important for exams. She will take off free response points for not mentioning specific details that you had no way of knowing were required and then asks random questions from the textbook. I AM FLABBERGASTED

Cheng does a decent job at explaining concepts, but be prepared to link concepts outside of class on your own. I HIGHLY recommend going to SI sections, as it's the only way to guarantee understanding (Colby is the goat). Make a study group, memorize the graphs and what he emphasizes in lecture, you'll be fine.

Loved this class. Exams were mostly recall and you could get up to 10 pts of bonus on them. Really funny guy, super knowledgeable. Lectures are interesting. Probably one of my favorite classes at UT. TA's are good. Study discussions and instapolls for exams.

Physiology is a difficult class, but it is still manageable. You definitely still have to put in a lot of work. Exams were tricky with a lot of the questions. Go to discussions, FRQ portion of the exams are exactly the same as the discussions most of the time. Spend a decent amount of time reviewing and studying and you'll be fine

Go to lectures, rewatch lectures, do practice on SquareCap, take reading quizzes, and homeworks. You get an A. It's a hard class, but the way Dr. Cheng structures his class is VERY POSSIBLE to get an A. JUST DO THE WORK! If you can go through the tedious work of ochem,biochem, you can do Dr. Cheng Physio. I love him, HE TALKS ABOUT HELLO KITTY!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher and class! He got so much hate in previous years. Go to the discussion sections and the worksheets are exactly like the tests. Go over lecture notes and the TA reviews. So easy to succeed and Cheng has some funny lectures.

Not the worst but not the best either. You have to memorize whatever he says during lecture to understand the material for exams. Exams themselves were difficult with more than one above correct as a frequent option to make sure you really know the material but each exam had bonus point questions and one exam is dropped, def manageable not easy.
Is great lecturer, GO to discussions (for FRQ), DO the study guides he puts, you can get an A by just REWATCHING THE LECTURES and going off the slides. THATS ALL YOU NEED.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was nervous to take this class because of the old reviews, but he was great. He's updated the class and exam format since then. He offers extra credit on every test, and while some questions are tricky (still some select all multiple choice) the exams are very doable if you study. Plus, he's a really funny lecturer. There's also not too much HW.

Honestly he's not as bad as people warned me. You do have to go back through the lectures and truly understand the concepts because the exam questions are based on understanding the material rather than memorizing content. Discussion sections are the cheat code!

You have to understand the lectures to do good on the tests instead of trying to memorize. I think he's a really good lecturer tbh. Exams can be hard and typically contain some really obscure material from the lectures, but they are fair imo. Also, discussion sections are basically mandatory for the exams.

Horrible professor. The lectures were the main source of content and were required because of Squarecaps, but the tests are insanely hard. Averages were 60s and below and does no curving of letter grades. First C I have ever gotten.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny and a great lecturer. Homework + discussion exercises are easy and are essential for doing the FR on the exams. Exams are very fair, but difficult to get past high B-low A bc of tricky wording and a few highly specific questions (none correct, more than one correct, select all). Memorize lectures + study guide, curve was A- to A for me.

Prof. Cheng is a traditionalist. Very anti-cell phone during lectures and demands you understand the details of the concepts he discusses. His exams are difficult and sometimes his questions can be hyper specific. But, he doesn't make it feel unreasonable, and actually is a pretty funny lecturer if you pay attention. I liked him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cheng was an overall good professor, although his exams were all pretty difficult. With exams being 75% of the final grade, you pretty much have to do well on those and can't rely much on homeworks or reading quizzes to boost your grade. 4 exams before a final was also a lot, but it's doable.

Dr. Cheng is a great professor! His lectures are funny and engaging, and he does a great job of explaining the material. The exams are tough, with a lot of "choose all that apply" multiple choice questions, but they are doable if you go over lectures and discussions carefully to study. Overall, would recommend this class.

Do NOT take Dr. Cheng!! If you can find another professor for Physiology I would highly recommend it!! Dr. Cheng's exams are extremly hard. I studied a week in advance and sometimes would still not pass my exams. Discussions are essential to go to to do good on his free response section of the exam.

Pretty good lecturer— explains concepts pretty well and makes them relatable to the students.
The exams, however, are a real beast. He gets tricky with the wording and answer choices, so there's no "common sense"ing them. They are also 75% of your grade. The SquareCap polls give you a taste of the formatting, but you just have to know the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked his lectures, even at 8am. He is clearly intelligent but I was very unhappy with the way that he makes the exams. Really really tricky, asks specific info from one of dozens of charts to memorize, 'multiple correct answer' problems. Exam averages were all in the 60s. I would study 10+ hours for low Bs. Don't take with other hard classes!!

Attendance by geo-located Squarecap. Highest section average for the first test was a 72%. He says "understand the concepts to do well on tests." Total lie. Just memorize everything that comes out of his mouth. Discussion mandatory if you want to know how to do the short answer on the test. Test is all trick questions. Incredibly hard grader.

The lectures were okay; physio is overall just a hard class. His tests are super tricky so good luck with that. I had a terrible TA named Riya Patel, not sure if she still TAs, but she made me super discouraged about even passing the course, she showed no desire to help students who were really struggling.

one of the hardest but most rewarding classes i've taken so far at UT. prof cheng def knows his stuff and includes great analogies and stories in his lectures (he's also surprisingly super funny). however... those exams were HARD (from someone that still did well on them). for two exams some of the questions had to be regraded due to tricky wording

Dr. Cheng was a great lecturer and a very nice and helpful prof. 4 exams (+1 optional final), 3 easy homeworks, reading quizzes (that you don't even need to read the textbook for, material comes from lectures), and squarecap used for attendance. Watch his Ian's A&P youtube lectures to review content and make sure you really know all the concepts!

def the best lecturer at UT, he's great at breaking down concepts in a way that is easy to understand! tests were pretty difficult b/c of the answer choices (none of the above, all are correct, more than one above correct) but if you review all of the lectures, discussions, and HWs, they are doable. also stan keroppi ⋆｡°✩

He does curve the class at the end of the year, so don't stress too much about your grade if the exam averages are like in the low to mid 70s. His lectures are very fun to attend, was very fun and good explanations. I felt like I learned so much in this class. Tests are definitely tricky though.
This dude is really funny and cute. He drew a frog during class. Genuinely the best lecturer I had at UT. His lectures are enough to succeed in the course.

I like that he post his lecture online. His test is VERY TRICKY, so remember to RE-READ everything and choose the best answer. Tbh, I found his class somewhat easy. I play his lecture 2x and learn overnight still got 90s on test (never go to class so attendance grade ~50%). Overall, just take detailed note and you're good

Professor does not want students to succeed. Tests are made up of trick questions and does not have any practice questions to reference and study with. He has the final and 4th test in the same week and did not release the exam 4 grades before the "optional" final thus making students extremely stressed and put at a disadvantage.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: professor gave exams that didn't let students really demonstrate their knowledge. full of trick questions, doesn't want students to succeed.

Dr. Cheng is a great guy but I did not enjoy his teaching style. The tests were worth 75% of the final grade and were really difficult. It seems like he purposefully tries to trick you during the tests as they are nothing like the homework, discussions, or reading quizzes. The TA's were nice but their explanations did not help my grade at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His physiology course definitely gave me a jump start compared to my peers from other institutions. I love his lectures and humor. He explains concepts extremely clear and gives you all the information you need to not only be successful in his class but also build a strong foundation for med/health schools. The most rewarding class I took at UT.

There is no denying that this class if hard. You must attend discussions for the FRQ section of the exams. Cheng is a genius, and he is a good teacher. If you pay attention to lecture and study hard, you will succeed. I ended this class with over 100% because he curves everyone if the class average is below a B-. The lab is tough, but doable.

Great lecturer and one of my favorite profs by far, this is just a hard class. Multiple test questions were unfair and worded to trick you, but you can get an A by paying close attention to & recording lectures, going to discussion and reworking each discussion exercise multiple times before each test, and watching "ian's a&p" youtube videos.

The class is difficult because of the way exams are formatted. The free response is exactly what you see in discussion to be sure to attend those. I found that the best way for me to study for the multiple choice was to read the textbook as I fill out the exam study guid. Then re do it from memory as many times as possible.

FRQ are fair and straight from discussion, however, MCQ and MMCQ virtually hold no difference considering almost all the MCQ have answer choices where all, some or none are options. Minute details will make the answer wrong and it honestly seems like he's laughing at students when creating these instead of trying to foster understanding of material

Exams are difficult as you will be penalized in MCQ for not knowing the correctness for one of the statements ("More than one above correct"). Dry humor occasionally in lecture. Final grade average curved up to B, which depends per section. Exam FRQ is heavily based on discussion exercises, but you can attend any section. Material itself not hard.

Cheng is good at lecturing using active recall on students. He is great on explaining topics, but does not explain it deeply enough. The exam are extremely tricky, especially the question choices are often misleading and there is no partial credit. You must study a lot of this class. TAs weren't the greatest. No lecture recordings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Use his YouTube (Ians A&P) for recorded lectures. GO TO DISCUSSION. Portion of tests come straight from discussion and the TAs are amazing. They are the only reason I passed this class. Exams are hard and you must thoroughly know the content. Hard class but I would take him again. I just wish I studied harder than I thought I needed to.

Use his YouTube videos (Ian's A&P), study guides, jeopardy reviews, HW, discussions, & lecture slides to study. The exam questions are tricky bc the multiple choice has "all correct", "none correct", "A&B are correct", etc. Read the textbook for the reading quizzes and use TA's and Cheng's OH! MEMORIZE LECTURE SLIDES, USE DISCUSSIONS AND HW 4 EXAMS

Dr. Cheng is great at explaining concepts. The material is not hard to grasp. However, he purposely writes test questions/answers in the most confusing way possible. Most students I spoke to from past/present semesters agreed this was one of the most stressful classes taken at UT, because of the tests, not the material. I would AVOID taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is what you make of it! The TAs are readily available, as is Dr. Cheng. His MC come straight from lecture and the frq come straight from the hw and discussions word for word. He posts a study guide that contains each topic that's tested. While memorization-heavy, it's easy to understand, and you'll do well if you put in effort to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are very boring, and the slides are also very disorganized with limited information on them (only pictures). It seems like he really wants to make the class difficult without putting in the effort to teach to that level of difficulty. Exams are designed to trick you and question your abilities. Only the TAs were helpful.

Class was more difficult then it had to be. I felt as if he purposely made the last exam for our class more difficult than it had to be since our class averages were higher than other classes. Averages went from mid 70s to a 60 on the last test. Tests based on really tricky/miniscule details.

Not an easy prof but not super hard. Lectures are important but can find them on Youtube. Only 3 short HWs, 4 exams, & optional final. Discussions aren't required but important for exams and aren't recorded. Exams can be worded trickily with answers like A,B,C, A and B, or all. TAs help a lot. Squarecap for attendance. No group work. Overall fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never read the text book and averaged an A for my final letter grade. Pretty simple, easy class. Just read the powerpoints and understand it in depth. Test were kind of tricky but if you knew your information youre good. Easy biology credit, just go to lectures and discussions. Median class grades were around 70s -80s.

Tests worth 75% of grade. Purposely tries to trick you in tests. No extra credit. Test scores average in 60-70s. Discussion is optional but then test requires material learned in discussion. Discussion PowerPoints and lecture are not posted. Homework criteria and reading quizzes not clear and are made and scored by undergrad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved his lectures and it's clear he is passionate about physiology. That being said, his exams were extremely difficult and worth 70% of your grade. It felt like they were designed to trick you, rather than test understanding. Do NOT take this class if you have a heavy course load already, you will not have enough time to do well.

One of my favorite lecturers at UT. One of my least favorite test writers. Lots of content, but it is relatively easy stuff. BUT unnecessarily difficult exam questions + 70% of ur grade is exams. Advice: rewatch lectures and pay close attention to/retake notes over topics in the Exam Study Guides he gives. Again, FOCUS ON THE STUDY GUIDE TOPICS!

Dr. Cheng is a good lecturer, but makes his exams super unfair and insanely difficult. I studied so hard for this class, and could never get the grades I wanted. However, out of the two physiology professors, he is the better option. This is by far the hardest class at UT. In the end, he does curve half a letter grade (ex: A- to A).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wasn't a big fan of him, his lectures don't really cover everything you need in order to do well in the class. He has a very dry personality and makes jokes here and there but rather bland. exams are quite difficult, and really feel like you are being pushed to the extreme when the lectures don't really provide you with everything you need.

Physio is just hard no matter what. There's a lot to cover. Dr. Cheng does the best job I could imagine at making it understandable through engaging lectures, availability of office hours/discussion sections, and recorded lectures- but you do need to do ALL of those things in my opinion to be successful. Possible but not easy. He's fun!

I loved Dr. Cheng's teaching style and explanations of concepts. However, the tests can be pretty difficult but he curves so that the average will end up being around a B-. You really have to focus during his lectures and remember small details that aren't written on the slides. USE his youtube channel to review(super concise, Ians a&p).

This class will make you question your ability as a pre-health student. The exams are very very tricky, if you do not understand the material or even just miss parts of the material, you will feel like you have understood nothing when taking the exam. About 75% of the grades are based on exams. I have struggled a lot in this class. Good luck

Take Dr. Cheng's class!! He is a wonderful lecturer and I would highly recommend him for physiology. I am currently in med school and I learned so much from this class that is now applicable for me as a medical student. The way Dr. Cheng explains things is so clear and it really helps you understand what's going on, instead of rote memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take Cheng over machart! He explains concepts in non-science ways which was really helpful in getting a better understanding of physiology. The content is definitely challenging but he tries to make his lectures engaging. Listen to what he says in class and you'll be fine (concept > memorization of facts)

Very hard class, but Cheng is a top 3 professor at UT. He could teach me about the history of doorframes and I would still be interested. Textbook is very well written. He makes the content very digestible and if you go to class regularly + have a good study schedule a good grade is very doable. Daniela is also a great TA for discussions.

His exams are very easy compared to Macharts (got a preview of them in physiolab). GO TO DISCUSSION Most of your success will come from your TA (RUBY) bc they lay out the entire outline for you for the exams. Do not stress about the amount of content bc his youtube BIO365S has every video you need in MORE than half the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cheng really wants his students to succeed despite the difficulty of the course topics. He is funny, caring, and very respectful. His lecture pacing is superb and really drives in real world examples so students can apply their knowledge. The exams were fair, as long as you put in the work, this class will be a very positive experience

This class, overall, is a very difficult course. If you want to succeed, you must rewatch lectures, make flashcards, and attend discussion sections. The exams are formatted in a way where it seems like they're designed to trick you, so read every word carefully. The TAs are amazing and super helpful, and this class is great for MCAT prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment:
class average for tests hovered between 60-70 for the entire semester. class average on final was 50. cheng is an ok lecturer, but as others have said, the format of his tests are incredibly difficult. negative points for wrong answers and lots of "select all"

the final curve for the class ended up being half of a letter grade (ex. B to B+)

Dr. Cheng is a great professor! He teaches physiology at an advanced level so expect difficult content and questions. Tests are lecture-heavy so be sure to take good notes (even verbatim). Probably one of the more difficult classes at UT but overall not too bad. Just pay attention during lectures and go to office hours.

Physiology is a hard class no matter what. With any professor, you will have to study A LOT to get the grade you want. But, Dr. Cheng makes the class much more bearable. Tests can be tough but not awful you really make sure to understand everything when you study. TAs are great, and the discussion section exercises are the exact same as FR on exams

Easily the hardest class I've taken at UT. Material is interesting however exams are TOUGH. Almost all of the questions are worded to be trick questions.
