Must know information inside and out to do decent on the exams. Optional final is tough. No curves. Homework is easy and quizzes are alright. Discussions are vital for exams. Daily square cap.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This class is really interesting (if you're into it) but it is HARD. The homeworks (3) aren't terrible but the quizzes (10) and exams (4) feel as if they are meant to trick you. You need to take REALLY good notes and know this information backwards, forwards, inside, and out. 

However, of the two physiology professors right now, he's better.

I really enjoyed the information, but this was the hardest class I've taken (senior). His tests and quizzes are extremely tricky in the way that he words things -- kinda makes it seem like his #1 priority is not our learning. Make sure you know every tiny detail before going into an exam.Take advantage of textbook + go to lecture. Don't fall behind

I'm not going to lie, you have to know the material inside and out to make an A in this class. However, discussion really helped me learn the material and reading the textbook clarified difficult topics as well. His tests are tricky, but you could do well if you understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Cheng- he's funny and good at communicating info! However, even though I had a physio background going into the class, it was a STRUGGLE. Exams are unreasonably tricky, even as multiple-choice. Definitely get a feel for the math you see in discussion section. Quizzes were ok- ctrl+f is your friend :) interesting class tho!

5 exams & 10 quizzes, 1 drop for each. I had no physio or anatomy background & I struggled. Supplement info you don't understand with the textbook, otherwise the textbook isn't needed. The tests are difficult. Almost every question has the option "more than 1 answer correct," so you can't do process of elimination. Know the material inside & out

Almost all of the content for the exams comes from the lectures, and his lectures are good and engaging. However, I studied for this class and rewatched the lectures before the exams, but somehow, my studying never translated to a good grade on exams. The way he formats his questions is very confusing and tricky.

Take this from someone with prior human physio knowledge before taking this class--find a different professor. The course material itself is interesting but this prof made the exams so terribly difficult that it was impossible to study for this class. Easy quizzes but impossible exams that comprise 90% of the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exams were incredibly difficult. Would study a week in advance and understand everything do good on the quizzes and then struggle on the exam. I love the content I find it interesting but the exams are way too hard for no reason. EASILY hardest class I've taken at UT

When 90% of the grade is based on exams, you would hope that studying hard would lead you to success. I wish that was true. I did so well on the quizzes and spent extensive time on the readings, but every exam was full of confusing language and/or trick questions that wore me out. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The issue with this class was the lectures. Every Tuesday and Thursday I struggled to motivate myself to wake up and go to class. This is a difficult topic that I hard to be engaged in, especially at 8 AM. Professor Cheng did nothing to help with this issue. Topics discussed in class were never in-depth enough to prepare you for any tests.

He clearly doesn't want to teach and hates it when students make requests. He LOVES that his class is overly difficult and praises his "bell-shaped" distribution. His lecturing is not good. He leaves a lot of gaps in your knowledge and goes on unnecessary tangents, which can make studying hard. 90% of the class is also tests now.

I have never struggled so hard in a class in my life. Cheng's exams are 90% of the final grade. He gives one drop exam, but there is no way to do well in his class if you are not a good test taker. He is so tricky with his multiple choice. He is rude & non-receptive toward students who are struggling. Do not take this class if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was awful. He really had us watching Youtube videos for lectures. It was not interactive, and at times, it was confusing. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cheng pre recorded all his lectures so attendance is not required. The class was hard but he presented the information well. He can be witty and funny at times. Tests were tough but an A is possible if you study for about a week in advance. The TA was great shoutout KAI.

Dr. Cheng's "lectures" were just of him playing his prerecorded youtube videos in class, therefore I stopped going to class. He makes his tests way too specific and detailed- MC portion constantly makes you second guess yourself to end up choosing the wrong answer. Was only able to survive this class because of the TA, Kai.

Dr. Cheng did not adjust to the online format as well and only played pre-recorded videos from last semester for our lecture material. Quizzes and homeworks were easy and open notes, but tests are proctored and a lot trickier. Go to the TA Kai's office hours to get an A! Kai made this class a lot more bearable! Doable to make an A with effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely brutal class. Cheng does not care about his student in the slightest and is extremely unforgiving. You basically have to teach yourself everything to do decent in this class. He is one of the worst profs I've had

reviews.comment: Cheng is not a helpful or accommodating prof. Even if you had surgery 1 day before and exam, do not expect him to work with you, hell simply say this can be your dropped exam. The only reason some of us did decent on exam was because of his TAs OH & discussion videos, his TA is AMAZING. The lectures Cheng uploads are useless.

The only reason I consider Dr. Cheng smart is because he has found a way to get paid for doing absolutely nothing. Lectures and discussions are prerecorded and messy due to schedule changes and the only time you hear from him is when he tells you every week that he has to cancel his weekly office hours again. I don't know how UT hired him.

This professor did not engage his students for their understanding. The lectures consisted of him playing pre-recorded videos then asking questions at the very end of the lecture section. In addition, this professor did not prepare the students well for the ways the material would be presented on the exam. IF TAKING CLASS, GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS.

It's possible to get an A in this class but you have to work for it. The exams are based on the discussions and what is mentioned in lecture, so take notes and watch the Kai's discussions. Study two weeks in advanced because it's a lot of material you have to learn in order to get a good grade.

Don't take for an easy A course, even though the UT+ distribution looks amazing. Class average was a B- this semester & said he won't curve the grade & not even bother emailing him asking him to. Tests are based more on whether or not you can pick up the deception he is trying to trick you on more than how much you studied. Don't bother w/ textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Physio is a hard class but he made it very understandable; lecture was funny and interesting. Use the book if youre confused but its not mandatory. Do the worksheets (theyre like the free response on tests).

This is by far the far professor i have ever had. You literally only have 5 grades fo the whole semester . Which is the 5 test he gives . He doesnt do much explaining. He reads directly from the PowerPoints for his lecture . You cant afford to mess up On any test. You fail 2 test you might as well drop the class .

I enjoyed going to Prof. Cheng's class! He is super funny and tries to make students laugh. Go to discussions even though they are not mandatory! His exams are fair but also super-specific. Make sure you really know your stuff. He has multiple-multiple choice questions which are tricky. If you study thoroughly, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Cheng is a good teacher, but his tests are super specific to the point where there's no guessing. You either know it or you don't. If you want a good grade, you really have to work for it, including going to discussion section.

Ian was a great professor. With that being said, this class was really hard. The tests are extremely tricky and you pretty much have to know the material in your sleep to do well on them. His lectures are funny and very informative. The best resource for this class is by far the TA, Kai. Go to his office hours every week and you will be less lost
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. I highly recommend him over anyone else teaching Phys. That isn't to say that the class isn't hard, because it definitely is. Here's how you do well: Pay very close attention in lecture, take good notes (maybe listen to recorded lectures again), go to discussion sections, and keep up with everything.

reviews.comment: Must take diligent lecture notes, iClicker 2 nearly every lecture, discussions very helpful. Definitely would recommend taking Ian over Machart. A very doable class. Tests are hard but it makes sense because the info is very important for majors who need this class! Kai Ybarbo was my TA and he is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny dude, makes lectures interesting with his hilarious anecdotes; definitely difficult course material but discussions help and if you put the work into it, you'll be fine. Don't expect like an A but working somewhat hard can get you a B/B+

This professor is very funny and engaging in lectures. You don't need a textbook, as long as you take good notes over what he goes over in lecture. Discussion is optional but necessary to attend for FR portion of tests. This class was in no way easy, but Dr. Cheng broke down the content in a way that you can understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought Ian was really fair in his expectations. The exams are meant to make you second-guess yourself, so keep up and GO to discussion (he skips calculations in lecture). Ian is soft-spoken, but he's pretty funny with his explanation of concepts. His optional final also gives those who messed up in the beginning a second chance.

Discussion sessions are optional but material covered in them make up at least 30pts on the exam, so go to them! The best way to study for exams is to use the study guide and supplement lecture slides /notes with the book to fill in any gaps. The class is hard but Dr Cheng is engaging and readily accessible, along with the TAs, outside of class.
Dr. Cheng is great. He's funny and tries his best to be engaging. Physiology is a tough class, but he definitely teaches in a way that's easy to understand.

Ian was the best biology professor i have had at ACC. He has entertaining lectures and tells you exactly what will be on tests or lab practicals. Wish I could have took him for A and P II. TAKE HIM!!!

Ian's class was really tough. His lectures are engaging because he's a hilarious professor, but his exams are very difficult. He gives study guides before the exam but they are very vague. He does not offer extra credit in the class, but he does curve the class a great deal. I had a B and got curved to an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: genuinely the worst diff eq professor you could take at UT. tests were unbeleivably difficult and conceptual. half of the class would leave the exam room with only 2.5/5 questions done. so much unnecessary work assigned as well. reading quizzes, application quizzes, and worksheet assigned every week, homework every other week. stay away from rene.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The best office hours ever. Love him so much

Overall seemed like a great guy but his lecture style was more theory/proof based than most students prefer. First exam wasn't great, and the lecture didn't really align but after that he fixed it and gave representative practice exams and homework. Having a great TA for discussion helped TONS!

His lectures were very proof-based and didn't follow the logical flow of how you would like to learn content for the first time. This made it difficult to parse what was important or not. However, he is a caring professor and will help you should you ask. 2 midterms and a final, lowest is dropped, first test was a lot harder than the other two.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome guy, very funny and caring. Definitely recommend both TA and professor office hours, if you are trying and asking questions, he will try his absolute best to help you. He does give practice exams which are very helpful for the real thing.

His lectures were not helpful for the most part, I ended up just teaching myself and did just fine. I do think he lacks communication and understanding. He came off as rude, making little remarks to me during our short conversations as I tried to fix a mistake on an exam. I just warn you to avoid running into any issues with him, he is no help.

Cabrera is a very nice professor and seems like a great person but the course is 70% reliant on exams. His lectures don't make sense so prepare to teach yourself but he is very open during office hours. He told us we would receive partial credit on exams since he doesn't curve but he didn't put any of it in causing our grades to go down.

Professor Cabrera really tries his best to make Intro to Real Analysis doable for students. He provides test reviews that really help for the exams, and is readily available to help folks out during office hours. Not only does he know his stuff, he's also a sweet professor and does his best to liven up the lectures and makes folks laugh.

Professor Cabrera is a nice guy! At the beginning of the semester I will admit his lectures did not align well with the first midterm/ homework assignments but he quickly changed his teaching style and began engaging with students more, put time aside to go over homework problems, and even offers partial credit on exams to help you out.

M361K is hard regardless of the prof. However, Rene does a good job giving you all of the materials you need to succeed - exam Qs were similar to (or the same) as HW and practice exam Qs. The HWs are difficult and take time, but he helps a lot during office hours. This sem., he made the final optional. He is a caring guy who wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People are really dramatic, Rene is a good guy. He wants his students to do well and took measures to improve his class after people tanked the first midterm - that's why there's a drop guys!! He takes time to work together on the homework DURING lecture time on Thursdays and ensures the exams are based on HW/practice - even held review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't have prior calculus knowledge. His lectures are unnecessarily confusing and don't help with home works, quizzes, or tests.

Calc is hard. That's why this class is hard. Professor Cabrera is such a nice person when talking to him individually, but I have been teaching myself a lot of the content which is not ideal. Therefore, this class is not an easy A, you have to put in the work but it's doable.

You can tell that he genuinely wants his students to learn and pass the class. Calc is hard, but it is even harder if your algebra skills are low. He usually slows down the lecture for some confused students, and frequently pauses to see if ppl get it. For exams, there are two midterms and a final, and he drops the lowest. So if you tank one, it ok

If you want to keep your will to live avoid this class at all costs. You are given zero resources. You have to pay to access your homework and when its time for the tests be prepared bc the test questions are nothing like the homework you are given. Majority of my class dropped out and theres only a few of us left and we are fighting to survive.

Cabrera is great if you have prior calculus knowledge because he lectures on the theory but not much about how to do it in an exam. Quizzes in TA sections were easy, but when it comes to Quest its an entirely new subject. Overall the only people who were able to catch up had prior knowledge or taught themselves the missing content. Not worth it.
Avoid at all costs

reviews.comment: im still in his class but he jsut sent out a canvas announcement that makes zero sense. gradescope isn't working for some students and instead of extending the deadline he said the syllabus allows for drops?????? he doesn't care for students, im not dropping even though the class is half empty after first midterm, but sheesh hes getting really bad

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Cabrera is a good person and I'm sure he knows his stuff but he doesn't know how to teach it. His lectures are disorganized and don't cover most of what is on the homework or exams, so I've had to teach it to myself. Avoid him at all costs.

reach out to current students in his class and ask if they think its a fair class (exam wise), its not. the guy was ecstatic that the first test had a mean score of 57. do yourself a favor and take this at community college and avoid rene cabrera at all costs.

AVG WAS A 57 ON THE FIRST EXAM. I cannot stress enough how much I would advise you not to take it with him. He took pride in that score and boasted how there's no curve, and the points we get from partial credit won't change much. I am begging you NOT to take him.

I don't look when I cross the street on my way to his class in hopes that I never have to go again. His midterm had questions covering content we never learned, averaging a 57. Exams are worth 70%. His lectures are also overly complicated compared to the HW and discussion periods. It's his first year teaching M408N and I hope it's his last.

Looking forward to dropping this class, can't stand the way he administers tests. In short, the midterm is uncurved and 14 questions , so you mess up two and you're screwed. He doesn't teach the content btw ask anyone.

Dude I came on here to see if his RMP dropped after that midterm and it quite literally did. This guy used to have a 4.7/5 and within the span of a day the dude tanked his own ranking to a sub three. He is a great guy and loves to teach, doesn't teach you well though. I promise you you will take that test unprepared and he won't curve or help you.

i was looking forward to taking this class with dr. cabrera bc he's such a passionate lecturer, but i can say that the way that he administers exams does not make sense i will 100% be dropping his class after this last test. he doesnt curve and throws stuff on there that we dont study, and two tests make up 70% of your grade. avoid him please!!!!!

glad to see someone else wanted to talk about the discrepancies on the midterm. it was genuinely unfair and had questions we just never went over. im probably going to drop the class after that midterm. i can say that Dr. Cabrera wants you to succeed and he's a great educator, but his exam had no reason being like that. he doesn't curve btw.

Just got out of my exam. He gave us a midterm that had multiple questions that didn't reflect the exam review. Studied for hours and still left the room unsure. His teaching style does not prepare you for the tests at all, better off taking it at community college and using OChem Tutor. That midterm was unwarranted and had questions we didn't cover

Rene is a very nice guy, but he clearly is a bit inexperienced when it comes to teaching rigorous upper-div proof-based math. He struggled to answer questions from students on a number of occasions. He clearly has a passion for math and teaching, but it might be best to take this class with a more experienced prof if you find analysis difficult.

reviews.comment: Rene is very kind and accommodating to students. Analysis is a difficult course but he explains concepts colloquially and intuitively. Sometimes he makes mistakes in lecture which leads to confusion regarding proofs or definitions. Homeworks were more difficult than lecture but that is standard for an analysis course.

He's very nice and funny, clearly passionate about math, but didn't know how to organize or pace the class. I had to do a lot of external reading
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cabrera is amazing!! He genuinely wants you to succeed; office hours are super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cabrera is incredible! He was super passionate about math and really dove deep about why the math works the way it does, all while keeping exams a little lower stakes so you would not have to worry about your grade while still digging deep into subject matter. Great professor!

Great professor overall. He's really chill and approachable, nerdy in the fun good way. Course has quest homeworks, discussion quizzes, and exams. Practice exams somewhat prepare you for the exams, but the exams can be unexpected and require things that aren't directly taught in class but you have to derive.

Rene is so chill. If you put a tiny amount of effort into the class you should be okay. He is relatable and makes difficult concepts easy to grasp. He's also a very lenient grader and gives you lots of opportunities to improve.

He is a very fun and energetic professor. The work load is very reasonable. The practice exams are very similar to the actual exams. His lectures are engaging and he answers a lot of questions. The exams are not weighted as heavily in comparison to other math classes, so even if you do poorly on the midterms, you could still get a B. Drops amidterm

Nice and gives his time to students, but disorganized and made mistakes each lecture. Homeworks were fairly difficult because he would introduce new content on the actual assignments but they were doable. On one exam no one could do 1/3 problems and there was no curve. Other professors told him his class was "on steroids" due to difficulty and pace
He really wanted his students to succeed. Did a very good job explaining what you needed to know and prepares you very well for the tests.

Gave generous curves, respected what his students had to say, and passionate about his teaching. His class sometimes seemed messy (it wasn't structured well), probably because he was new to teaching. Homework and quiz every week which help you stay on top of the material. Practice tests for exams that were similar in structure to the actual exams.

Dr. Cabrera was amazing and the kind of professor you will rarely be lucky enough to have. He genuinely cares about his students and is super understanding. If you put in the work and do what is asked of you, you will succeed. The practice exams model what you should study for. If you are thinking about taking him, DO IT!!

Cool professor!
He is very approachable and would do his best to help students with the material.
I just you read and try to understand material before coming to lectures. It makes it a lot better.

Lectures aren't that interactive but he will answer questions if you have them. Professor didn't have office hours at the beginning of the year so it was a bit hard to get ahold of him until things settled down because this was his first semester teaching. His handwriting and written explanations are abysmal, but he's a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof was postdoc so he wasn't a genius at teaching, but was compassionate and curved our second midterm. Exams are very similar to the exam reviews he gives out. We had 3-question quizzes every Thursday during discussion section but the lowest you could score is a 70%. You should do fine if you put in a moderate amount of work.

eric "de goat" waal... on a serious note, amazing lecturer, he practices giving them before class lol. cell bio is a dense class in general, but he provides SO many resources for his students to succeed. frqs give clear instructions to follow and if you answer correctly what they are asking, you won't lose points. lots extra credit as well.

Just take the other professor(s) offered. Tests are extremely difficult. His lectures are good, but he does too much with the tests. Wouldn't recommend taking during a busy semester because it requires a lot of time outside of class to study and prepare for exams. If you want a life outside of this class, don't take it with him!

This class was really difficult for me, and the exams killed me a little. FRQs were graded harshly in my opinion, but the MCQ portion was okay. It's a lot of memorization and content but he himself was a good lecturer. He broke things down relatively well and does give resources. I recommend doing the worksheets to prepare but its def a heavy class

So much content and memorization, but he explained everything really really well which makes the content so much more digestable. Very organized professor and clear expectations. Quizzes come straight from homework and lecture questions, exams are a bit harder since they're longer and you really need to understand everything to do well.

Very enjoyable - great lectures and very organized study materials. Content can be dense, but it's very possible to do well. Make use of his study guides and his virtual office hours to do well on exams. Discussion sections are extra credit. One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT.

Crazy hard class, but he was a great lecturer. Something that really annoyed me was that FRQs are graded extremely harshly because he wants details in your answers that aren't always clearly asked in the question. All MCQs were fair. The final was significantly easier than the midterms. A is doable.

Content heavy but taught by one of the best lecturers I've had. Tries his best to make everything digestible, but there is still lots of memorization involved. Try to actively listen/absorb what he's saying in lecture as that really helps. Also be precise on the FRQs! Make sure you know each step in whatever process you're writing about.

Exams are pretty hard & FRQ portion on exams can be tedious & specific. However, DeWaal is a really good prof. He'll give you everything you need to prepare for exams. No curveballs, everything on the exam is something he's talked about. It is a time consuming class, so be aware. Taking biochem before this class helped.

The tests are extremely hard, the frqs have to be super specific and the mcq is very tricky. He is a good proffesor in the sense that he knows a lot about the topics and he is a good lecturer, but he does not really care about his students.

I really liked Dr. De waal even tho I dropped. He cares a lot about his students, but the exams killed me. I studied multiple days before each exam and didn't pass a single one. Content is interesting but very complex and memorization heavy. Taking with a diff prof next semester.

He grades way too strictly and harsh on FRQ portion of every exam which is why the class average for every exam is like a low 70. Makes getting an A very hard if you don't write exactly what he wants in detail. Very structured and most content dense course I've taken at UT so far. I would avoid if you already have heavy course load semester.

Amazing and interactive professor. It is abundantly clear that he cares about students and wants to see them succeed. The exams are pretty difficult- he grades pretty rigorously, so be prepared to study.

One of the best upper div professors I have had at UT. I had cell bio with him and enjoyed his class a lot. I am currently taking molecular with him (MBS344) and the class is certainly difficult but I have hope to get through it.

Amazing lecturer but your grade is dependent upon mostly exams that he intentionally makes very difficult down to the finest details. FRQs are graded tough but they come from discussion sections and HWs for some so it is doable. Study like no other if you want to get near an A.
Idk who is saying his exams are hard, they are genuinely doable if you go to class and put in the work. Really engaging class and currently enjoying it very much.
good at explaining topics

One of the best lecturers at UT imo. If you pay attention, everything is so comprehensible because he explains everything so well. Quizzes + exams weren't that hard and homeworks were completion. Also, saved me a lot of times on the mcat.

Arguably the hardest class I have taken and will ever take. The exams are difficult with extremely strict criterion for points, or even partial credit. Studying took ~1 week in advance and still felt somewhat ill prepared on test day. Would take Stevens in a heartbeat.

This class in general is hard, but De Waal isn't too bad! My main complaint is the specificity of exam grading - you need to put exactly what he expects to get full credit, and it's often worded weirdly. He's a pretty good lecturer, and accessible in office hours/friday virtual hours. Take the time to actually understand the information!!

This class took me through the 5 stages of grief and is the most difficult class I've taken. De Waal is a good lecturer but expects you to know A LOT and intentionally words his questions to be tricky. He also grades the free response extremely harshly so you lose points on little things. I managed to get an A by studying ~25 hours for the final...
This was a really hard class due to the amount of contents covered, but I have learned so much coming out of it. He is undeniably the best lecturer I have ever had at UT.

The exams were insanely hard. Sure, there was a lot of material, but he will nitpick on the specific criteria he determines for points for FRQs even though other open-ended answers are correct. He will take away any information that is 'incorrect'. The high school was not even a 100 for any of the exams except the easiest one (exam 4).

De Waal is a really good lecturer, maybe the best I've had at UT. I won't lie, his quizzes and exams were tricky, but he gives you 1 drop for each, and once I got the hang of his style of questions I was able to get the grade I wanted. If you can put in the work you'll get so much out of this class.

EdW is a really good professor who is teaching a very difficult course. The exams are very challenging and graded harsher than probably any other class I've taken. I learned a LOT but I would only take his class again if I could devote the majority of my time to it. (I am not premed so idc but I've been told this class is good prep for MCAT)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class was really fair and the tests were challenging but doable if you stayed on top of your content. He is an amazing lecturer and balances student interaction with good instruction.

this class was HARD. That being said it is possible to do well with ALOT of work. If you are juggling a lot of STEM classes that are difficult, get ready to hit the PCL. He is good at explaining things though. Sometimes he has few inaccuracies which can be confusing but can be understood on your own and with google search.

Genuinely one of the best professors Ive ever had. Lots of drops, one drop for quizzes, one drop for the exam, one drop for papers, and a drop for homework. By the way the homework is participation, quizzes have cheat sheets (and are super easy), and the study guide is insanely helpful for active learning and covering all your bases.

I've never felt like I've learned so much. His grading on the exams can be tough, but if you have a good study strategy then you will do fine. He also gives a little bit of extra credit for discussions which help a lot in the end. I took cell bio and mol bio with him simultaneously, and there was some overlap, so if you want to do that, you should.

Such an amazing lecturer. His exams were pretty straight forward and mainly took from lecture content. Plan to take him again for molecular bio purely from how much I enjoyed lectures. Absolutely recommend.

Dr. Dewaal is one of the best lecturers I've had at UT austin. He's very passionate about cell bio and makes a lot of connections to the medical applications which I enjoyed. The class itself is pretty difficult though with exams often being graded pretty hard. There's some extra credit and a lot of resources to study for exams.
Cell bio is hard, de Waal is great. Use all of the resources he offers and you'll be fine. He's very organized and wants you to succeed. You just have to be willing to put in the effort.

Awesome guy. He's literally an AI...He's the best lecturer in terms of wording accuracy and content that I've seen at UT. Literal raw science no bs straight to the point each day. Class is not conceptually difficult but it is hard to internalize everything because it is a LOT of content so plan time accordingly. You need to know all the details.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult from the beginning. Exams are very specific and he expects you to know all of it. He gives a lot of study materials though, but just a lot of material on the exam, and very very oddly worded questions that are difficult to understand.

Best lecturer ever. BUT, the FRQ sections on the exams are graded insanely hard. The UGCA's + Dr. de Waal are picky about what you say and how you say it - points are taken off for incorrect info! The content isn't hard, there are just SO many details you're expected to remember, especially from the papers (the paper is tested in the FRQ section).

Dr. De Waal is one of the best professors I've ever taken in UT. I took molecular bio with him. It was a lot of inf, I  learned a lot! He really cares about students succeeding, helped me a lot during office hours. Highly recommend for premed - teaches you rigor and discipline!

Amazing and engaging lectures. By the nature of the content, the class was difficult, but studying a proper amount of time and engaging in all the numerous methods he provides to prepare for exams will ensure a high grade in the class. Highly recommend taking Dr. De Waal because he makes a course with hard material as easy as it can be.

Glad I took/did well on the MCAT before DeWaal's cell bio class, bc he would have made me panic. Teaches useless details and claims that they are necessary. Learning was not prioritized - professors like him make life stressful and a bad learning environment. Take someone else for cell bio.

Graduating as a bio major and worst bio professor at UT. Lectures have lots of tiny details and exams are not aligned with what is taught. Has been one of the worst classes at UT - both material and professor wise. Save your stress.

As someone who aced the MCAT/is accepted into med school, do not be stressed by Dr. DeWaal's remarks on "what material is on the MCAT". He claims certain topics are on the MCAT to get premeds in his class to focus more, but people who have already been through the path know that DeWaal's information is filled with ridiculously extraneous detail.

Mol bio is one of the toughest UD biology classes at UT, but Dr. De Waal is the best choice. He's the best lecturer I've had in college by a huge margin and is clearly very passionate about the subject. The content is quite difficult and tests are tricky, though it's totally feasible to get an A if you understand the content really, really well.

Took mol bio and cell bio with De Waal this semester. Lectures are great and engaging but the tests are REALLY hard. Class average usually around 70%. Overall I really liked the classes and I highly recommend taking both with him, but don't do them at the same time; it's a lot of material and studying for both.

(Mol bio) Dr. De Waal is a master lecturer, however, this class is tricky and does require a lot of effort to do well in. Here are my tips for an A: 1) rewatch lectures before quizzes and exams. 2) most questions on quizzes and exams are answered in the slides—aim to know EVERYTHING on the slides, including all details and figures. You got this :)

Beware if you are not a good test taker. Merely knowing the content from the slides is not enough. Be ready to be tripped up by the MCQ section and aggravated by the extremely harsh and narrow grading criteria of the FRQ section. Good lecturer though, but don't be fooled by how easy the content seems, the test will be way harder.

FRQ grading is ridiculous bc if u don't use exact words, u get no points. MCQs r vague & 'tricky,' so even if u know material, u still miss q's bc he's trying to trip u up. He's stingy w/ regrade requests & defensive. I'd rather have a professor who works w/ students than 1 focused on being right. He can't answer q's unless they're from his slides.
Avoid this class. Free response and multiple questions are hard and TAs take points off of every tiny detail you missed. I would take another professor, way too challenging

Dr. Dewaal is one of the best lecturers I have had at UT. However, his class is extremely difficult. Quizzes and homeworks are not bad, but free response test questions are graded way too specific.There is very little room for error and he expects you to have specific details that were barely said in class. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful lecturer! The class is hard content wise, but he provides a lot of supplemental material to help study such as study guides. Amazing powerpoints, good at explaining and always available for questions. Exams are difficult and mostly free response but doable, just a lot of work. Almost failed, but great professor.

He is a great lecturer but had to drop the class before it ruin my grade with a C. Although you might know everything the multiple choice is really hard and worth around five points each meaning that if you missed more than 3 you are already on a B and the FRQS are really specific meaning that the questions are broad and graded really specifically

Dr. De Waal is genuinely the most impressive lecturer I've had in my six semesters, I even decided to take him for mol bio too. The class material itself is pretty boring but the grading structure is good with lots of points assigned to participation, homeworks, and other non-exam stuff. MC and fill-in-the-blanks on the exams are pretty difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: De Waal is a great lecturer but it doesn't make up for how difficult the course is. Exam MC are tricky/FRQ are graded harshly, overall not worth it. Felt like I was learning the same material as people taking other professors but was getting mediocre grades the entire semester. Does not curve/round, exam averages in the 70s, overwhelming overall.

De Waal's lectures are very well set up and digestible. He is great to talk to outside of class as well as can deepen your understanding of cell bio. Exams are manageable and quizzes help prepare you for them. HWs are kind of annoying but also helpful.

Dr. de Waal is the best lecturer I've ever had. His powerpoints are very detailed and lectures are engaging. He truly cares about his students' success and gives great study tips--I followed all of his study tips and aced the class. He is very accessible during office hours and makes an effort to get to know you/help you.

Dr. de Waal is easily the best professor I have had at UT. His lectures are incredibly good, and he does a great job teaching concepts and helping us apply them to the real world. This class has a ton of real-world applications which makes it very interesting. Yes, there's a lot of material to keep up with, but it's your job to stay on it. 10/10

THE Cell Bio professor. You will be golden if you take his class. Papers reviewed in discussion sessions so you know what to write. The best lecturer I have experienced in my academic career. Extremely well organized notes and study guides. Make use of the videos he posts in the modules and attend his OH and you are set. GOATed.

CRISPR Lab. I took his new maymester CRISPR lab and it was great! All hands-on and intense but you learn/practice a lot of lab skills. It was a small lab so he was very accessible for help. The lectures were very helpful and you can tell he is very interested in the material. Labs were 4 hours and we had a lot of downtime to work on homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The reviews for De Waal are shocking. This was easily the best professor I've had at UT. The class is very difficult and I had a hard time digesting the information from class alone. Going to his OH was the key to understanding missed concepts from class. He wants to see you succeed you just have to put in the extra effort to get there.

Most overwhelming class I've ever taken at UT. MC questions were tricky. I found the FR questions easier. Way too much material to study. Courses like this don't consider the healthy amount of information for the human brain. I wouldn't take him or this course again. It ruined my GPA despite my hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 60% of grade comes from exams which are based 100% off lecture. other 40% comes from assignments/hw that you can easily get nearly full credit for. If you are able to answer all the study guide questions you should be able to get an A in the class easily. Exam averages were around 70 though..

This is not a very good professor. He does not have any industry experience and his background is just physics and water. I don't get why UT Austin keeps hiring inexperienced professors being so close to Houston. His lecture notes and writing are a mess. He makes us show memes every class, because of how boring it gets!
Best class I've ever taken. People say it's hard, but it's so light if you just lock in. 10/10 would take again, all thanks to Professor DiCarlo
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Is it fun? No, its thermo. DiCarlo makes it as enjoyable as thermo could possibly be though, and makes an effort to know all the students. Topics are not digestible just through lectures, and required lots of reviewing notes, textbooks, and office hours (always very approachable). Test heavy, but if you understand concepts, they aren't that bad.

He is very disorganized and sloppy. He makes many mistakes. He is very hard to understand. No one understood what he was saying. The only thing good about him is that he had a good sense of humor, other than that, he is a terrible prof. I wouldn't recommend anyone taking a class with him.

Genuinely an amazing professor that really cares and makes you want to come to class. Great lectures make it super easy to pay attention, and the smaller class size helps you feel more comfortable asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor DiCarlo makes coming to class fun he stops the lectures halfway through class so students can stand up and tell dad jokes, a much needed break from a 1.5 hour lecture of heavy material. He cares about each student and makes an effort to learn everyones name and interests. Thermo is a hard subject but he keeps you invested and tests easy.

Class is so unnecessarily difficult. There are almost no pre-worked homework problems, so there is almost no way to practice. Unorganaized. He'll forget to add crucial info, or it will be unclear where it is. Prof is funny, but that doesn't mean much when you have no idea how you're performing. Unfortunately, this class is required for PGE.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Dicarlo is not the best lecturer as he goes through material very quickly and does not explain concepts deeply enough. For most of the homeworks, you will have little idea on how to do a majority of the problems and so going to office hours is highly recommended. Tests aren't that bad if you get the general concepts and homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awesome guy. Class is super hard but he's an awesome professor. He is super funny, has really good understanding of the material, and will help students out. His class is super test heavy (85%), so try and do well on exams.
Class is hard in nature. Exams can be very difficult. However, he really does try and look after the students.
Amazing lectures, I wished he taught more classes on formation evaluation.

Sweet guy and never gave us a lot of homework. He allows 1 page for cheat sheets and midterms weren't hard to get an A. Just review his slides and put everything on your cheat sheet. He also gave a super easy 10 point bonus question on a midterm once, so the average was like a 103. I am definitely going to take his sustainability course too.

Dr Daigle is awesome! Exams are very similar to homework and lectures and you get a cheat sheet. He curves HEAVILY. Lab reports are long and tedious (like 30 pages...), but you only have to do 3 ish and he is a light grader. He also pushes due dates if he feels there is too much on his students' plates. Very passionate about rocks!
Great Professor, very easy class. Labs take a lot of time.
Most condescending professor I've ever experienced. Extremely rude.

Dr. Daigle is very wholesome. He is clear he is very passionate about teaching. Even though the topic is mostly boring, it is nice listening to his lecture. A single pop quiz in the semester. Homeworks were easy/graded generously. TAs were nice. Open note exams. The exams were straightforward, some math, some T/F. 3 lab reports were written.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Daigle is very caring, knowledgeable, and passionate about renewable energy. His class is an easy A and very interesting. His passion towards the subject makes his student passionate about renewable energies and sustainability as well. Highly recommend this class.

Dr. Daigle's course is a great introduction to the many challenges that come with using more renewables. Assignments and presentations were straightforward, and the content was interesting. I would recommend this class to anyone who meets the prerequisites. Virtually all of the open note final could be completed by referencing the slides.

Dr. Daigle's class sustainability issues in energy is the easies A there is. Grades are 3 easily graded group presentations, 4 HW and a final essay about what you learned. The professor is very knowledgable about the subject and always gives his funny takes about everything. Take this class!

So fun and easily manageable while taking calc 1. There are lectures 2 a week, and they're really interesting. You read 1 chapter a week and do in-Quizitive every Tuesday by 8 pm. He does do in-class Kahoot's and Think-Pair-Shares for participation points, but we have 3 weeks left of classes, and almost everyone already has enough points.
Amazing lecturer.
Love Prof. Mateer, he's very funny and keeps his lecture engaging. If you are thinking about taking this class, I highly suggest you do. (Winners of his kahoots win $10-$20 btw)

My fav class this sem!!! He gives super amazing lectures, makes all the concepts very easy to understand and always cares about making students engaged during class. Very kind, funny and knowledgeable man who cares about his students' success. Take his class, you'll never regret it!!!

I was dreading taking an economics class—I was a mostly straight A student in high school, but nearly failed macro. I took micro with Dr. Mateer, and honestly, it was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He makes lectures fun and engaging with games and activities that demonstrate key economics concepts. I highly recommend! Take this class!

Dirk has easily been my favorite professor so far. He wants you to care about Econ as much as he does. Every day, he made class entertaining with fun class demonstrations, and he would offer prizes for participation. The class itself is not that difficult; read the textbook, go to lectures, and you'll be fine.
Very light class! Tests essentially mirrored practice exams in Canvas. Weekly discussions were boring but will boost your grade. Professor Mateer himself is amazing
good teacher and really easy to get an A, i just got busy halfway through the semester

Dirk is the best professor I've had. Fantastic lecturer and a super forgiving grading system (everyone should get A's as long as they show up and try). Don't need to study too much for tests and very engaging in class as he gives out candy for participation & money for kahoot wins. Only downside to this glorious man is his nephew Mateer (OU's QB).

Love Prof. Mateer! He's such a kind and funny guy. Engaging class, lots of extra credit to help out your grade. Love him for making the final optional. InQuizitives are easy and helpful, tests are straightforward, textbook is interesting to read. I grew to love econ through this class. Take Mateer, you won't regret it.

if you're looking for an easy, non-time consuming, and somewhat engaging ugs, take economics and ethics. Mateer doesn't just do a great job of teaching the material, he really tries to get everybody engaged with it. If you're not an econ major, please consider taking this class. If you are, consider it less, you won't learn much.

Dirk is the GOAT. King made everything easy and he was just so real. Nothing about the course was hard and exams were similar to the Kahoots and the homework. He's funny and always gave out prizes for first in the Kahoots or for participating when he needed volunteers. He bought me a frosty from Wendy's one time and also brought donuts to class.

Dirk is probably one of the best professors here on campus. He makes all the concepts easy to understand and genuinely cares that his students learn them. So much opportunity for extra credit and the exams are not hard to prepare for (a lot of questions are pretty much what you see in class). He also bought me a Frosty from Wendy's 🐐.

In-class demos are fun and helpful, attendance is greatly encouraged. He's kind, funny, and understanding. Notes are easy to follow. Tests are very straightforward; he posts a topic list, as well as the number of questions per topic. The extra credit saved me from taking the final. Grade is based off cumulative points earned throughout the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made learning Microeconomics interesting with lectures and interactive examples. While attendance is technically not required, the more you show up, the more points you will get due to the Kahoot/TPS, and the extra credit you can gain from that. He also goes over example questions that are similar to what is on our test.

Dr. Mateer is an amazing professor. The class is relatively easy, and it's not difficult to earn an A if you put in some study time. Class participation is part of the grade. He offers extra credit. The InQuizitives are an easy 100 too. He's super engaging and gives out money and candy each class.

amazing professor, go to lectures! the way he explains things in person makes it 100x easier to understand. Gives more skips on tests than other econ professors and he wrote the textbook they all use! super easy class to pass and he genuinely wants to get to know his students

Dirk was genuinely so funny and caring. I would say some of the demonstrations didn't necessarily help with economic concepts, but they were very fun. I attended every lecture and stuff from in-person lectures were brought back at tests so definitely attend even though it's not mandatory. The tests were easy if you just study.
Dr. Mateer is amazing. Super engaging, and makes sure the material sticks with you. If you put in effort and show up to most of the lectures, you'll have no problem getting a good score. Take him!!

Dirk is friendly and passionate about teaching, but lectures are often inefficient/irrelevant. The textbook has the important content for exams, while in-class “activities” meant to be engaging are a waste of time (ex: donut eating contests). Exams are fair but get harder through the semester. Class attendance is needed for participation points.

Prof Mateer is the best! He has so many fun lectures throughout the semester and we do kahoots pretty much every day, so the class never feels too boring. As long as you read the textbook, do the Inquizitives, and pay attention in class, this class is overall not too challenging  and very light on homework.

Professor Mateer made this UGS super fun and interactive! He gives out free candy and treats throughout the year and has 1-2 kahoots pretty much every class, so the class feels like a break from other classes. If you study the practice exam questions he gives you, you're pretty much guaranteed an A. He's also super approachable and down to earth.
Easiest Micro professor, attending lectures is not required but extremely beneficial. Exam questions might be ripped straight from kahoots or class discussions

BEST ECON TEACHER EVER!! He makes economics so interesting and makes you want to come to class even though it isn't technically mandatory... (you should go since he has in-class participation). Exams are relatively easy if you study and look back at past Kahoots, TPS, and InQuizitives. He gives out $10-$20 if you get 1st place in Kahoots! TAKE HIM!

Dirk is an amazing professor who makes a big class feel small and is genuinely funny. He uses hands-on activities and even hands out about $10 every class. His three test skips are generous, and his exams are fair. He also wrote the textbook. I couldn't recommend him more.

Dirk is amazing. Most of your grade is Kahoot and TPS, which is so free. He gives money to the winners of the Kahoot, ranging from $10-20. Dirk makes every lecture easy, understandable, a good time, and worth it. Kahoot and TPS are used for your attendance, which earns you points. The exams are exactly what you learn during class.

Dirk is amazing. Most of your grade is Kahoot and TPS, which is so free. He gives money to the winners of the Kahoot, ranging from $10-20. Dirk makes every lecture easy, understandable, a good time, and worth it. The Kahoot and TPS are what are used for your attendance, which gives you points. The exams are exactly what you learn during class.

Dirk is a super fun teacher who wants all of his students to succeed, there is extra credit and three tests in this class, but they are all easy tests where you can get three skips on each test that if you skip it gets counted as correct. I would 100% take this class again.

Mateer makes econ engaging every step of the way. He makes me want to come to a traditionally unpopular subject and learn. His text book is fun to read and his weekly assignments are easy and take about an hour. Overall, best class I've taken my freshman year.
its econ, its hard. but dr mateer makes his lectures fun and engaging. he also cares about us a lot (he bought be a frosty hehehe) and he gives out money in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mateer is awesome. Would highly recommend this class. Professor Mateer is a great lecturer and makes a huge class still feel personal. Exams are not too hard, and many questions are pulled directly from the practice problem he gives so study and you will do great.
Professor Mateer is the absolute goat
Most engaging professor I have ever had. Also deeply knows what he is talking about and is able to explain it in a way that anyone could understand.

Professor Dirk is very kind and tries to make lectures engaging, but the Kahoots and TPS (Google Forms) are stressful, tricky, and timed, making the class high-pressure. The point-based grading is confusing, and it's hard to know your actual grade. If you prefer traditional lectures, this class is not for you. Lots of reading, high stress envirnmnt

Mateer makes lectures fun and interesting and will use videos, interactive activities, and Kahoots to teach. I recommend going to class, as 20% of your grade is in class stuff, and once you hit 100% in class points, it becomes extra credit. If you do the chapter problems and Inquisitives, you will do well on the test. You get cash for a Kahoot win.
Dr. Mateer tried to make lectures engaging with demos. Super generous since he gives out cash and food for winning kahoots and going up on stage. Very manageable to get an A
He is just awesome. Such a great professor; really cares about making the class feel fun and not boring; tests are quite easy and is very conversational. Sticks to his values which I respect heavily.

I love this professor so much. He clearly loves what he does, participation and extra credit is kahoots and surveys in class. He is so fun, interactive, and his lectures are incredible. Honestly, best class I've taken, I'm not even an econ major or anything related, but loved this class so much. Take this class very very highly recommended.
Very easy class, we are given everything we need to do well. Mateer is very engaging and has been one of my favorite professors here at UT. Take him.

I took him for micro, not having much prior knowledge. His lectures were engaging and he seems very excited what he is teaching. Lots of resources given for tests making it easy to do well. Attendance is important to get the points (200 based off of kahoot). Inquizitive HW could take a while but very helpful. You get 3 skips on exams too!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is one of my favorite professors so far. His lectures are awesome and engaging. He clearly outlines what is going to be on the exams (you have seen all of the questions prior) and gives tons of extra credit. He cares about his students and is a great guy overall

A truly excellent economics professor—just attend class and you'll do well. I'm not an Econ major, and I still really enjoyed his course. The exams aren't too difficult since he clearly outlines exactly what to study. He's not only a great professor but an even better person. His final lecture was incredibly inspiring!
He's a dog. Class was always super entertaining and plenty of extra credit/outside of class materials to help with grade.

Good professor. Engaging class with lot's of interactive activities throughout and working with others is encouraged. Easiest testing style I've seen. Every question was already on a Kahoot, in class, or on InQuizitive. Realistically could be more difficult but you get out what you put in. Dirk is great.

Aside from academics, Dirk is just a great man. He is very level-headed and even tempered. He loves his job. He runs from one end of the class to the other engaging with people. Good luck on the kahoots, winner gets 10 bucks and their are plenty of prizes 2nd and 3rd. There are even prizes for participation. Thanks so much Dirk. All love homie.

I took “Economics and Ethics” with Professor Mateer, and he was fantastic! He's a passionate and engaging lecturer who makes the material interesting. The class is easy, with in-class Kahoots and Google Forms for participation grades. Weekly Inquisitive assignments are straightforward, and the sample exams on Canvas closely match the actual tests.

He's SO NICE and very approachable.  This class felt fun going to and he PAYS you to participate (candy for activities and $10 for winning Kahoots).  The exams have 3 skips and are relatively easy (some questions from random class examples though).  Discussions are redundant and boring, but everything counts for points.  Lectures are engaging!

This was an amazing ugs that wasn't very time consuming. It is definitely easy to get an A with the loads of resources provided. The test are also pretty easy as long as you paid attention and there's a lot of room for mistakes in the grading criteria.

This was an ok ugs that I took because it seemed easy since I took econ in my senior year. However it is extremely boring if you dont like econ. Super forgiving grading and it is very easy to get a good grade. the professor is very nice and good at teaching. Doesn't fulfill any flags so pretty much useless unless you are a business/econ major.

Mateer's lectures have plenty of examples and tries to keep things funny. Unfortunately he speaks very quickly and can be hard to follow. KHAN ACADEMY SAVED ME IN THIS CLASS. I would recommend that plus re-reading the textbook to make sure you have an understanding of the list of concepts he publishes before exams.

Duffey-sensei is truly a gift! lots of homework, tests, and a daily quiz, but as is to be expected when learning such a hard language. it is a lot of work, but it truly does pay off! lots of opportunities to raise your grade, just study hard! she is so sweet, and is always willing to help you when you are struggling. cannot recommend enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Duffy-sensei fosters a really comfortable and fun learning environment. As long as you show up every class and give your best effort, you will do well. She has been my favorite instructor so far at UT, please take her class!

Duffey sensei is always caring and considerate of her students and very available outside class through office hours. There's definitely less work than the lower division courses, but there are short tests every two weeks. There is a major project that you shouldn't procrastinate on, but if you put some work into it everyday it's very manageable

I LOVE DUFFEY SENSEI! If I could take her for all of my Japanese classes, I would definitely! She is the sweetest and super nice. As long as you're on top of the content and stay prepared for the quizzes, you will be okay. Learning Japanese is hard, but definitely take the initiative to learn. If you fall behind, this class will be very hard!

Actual reading class that will let you pick what you're interested in to read & check your understanding. Amazing professor with an awesome personality, classes go by quickly and never boring. Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Duffey Sensei was amazing! She was extremely enthusiastic for every class and incredibly friendly. She is also very approachable and accommodating. It is very easy to get an A in her class as long as you finish all the work. There are daily assignments and quizzes most days, but as long as you show up to class you'll be fine. Would 100% take again!

Duffey sensei is amazing on what she teaches to her students. Go to her office hours if your behind or haven't understand the hw she will help you a lot. She also cares for her students and gives us snacks. There's pop quiz everyday so study hard and 2 oral exams plus 2-chapter exams. Have fun and make some friends along the way in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was an incredible professor! I learned so much from her and she was also so incredibly kind. Her classes were always fun but still educational. The class itself was easy to follow in terms of syllabus. Could not recommend enough, TAKE HER!!

I took Duffey sensei for JPN 601 and 601D and I wish I could take her for ALL my Japanese classes! She is an amazing teacher, her lectures are very engaging and mixed with a ton of group activities so you can practice what you learn. You can tell she really cares a lot for her students and wishes for all of us to succeed!

Duffy Sensei is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She really cares about you and wants to see you improve your understanding of Japanese. This is a 6-hour class, so expect a lot of work, but you can do it. I would recommend this class to anyone looking for a rewarding, challenging experience.

Duffey Sensei is an amazing professor and an amazing person! She genuinely cares about her students, and will always make sure that you understand what you are learning. She will never assign anything as busywork-every single assignment has a purpose and will help you to understand Japanese better.

Duffey Sensee is the best teacher I have had at UT Austin so far. She is awesome!! She always made sure that students felt welcomed! I am an international student, and Duffey Sensee clearly made UT closer to my home! Her office hours are really good, and she is always very good giving feedback to students.

Please take Duffey Sensee if you can! Be prepared for the quizzes/homework; they're not difficult, but make sure not to fall behind. Daily cold calling was initially scary, but they're super nice so you get used to it and it helped me learn a lot. They make class really engaging and fun, and this was my favorite class so far at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Duffey sensee. As long as you show her you are trying, she will help you! I love teachers that care about their kids' understanding as their first goal. Quizzes every week, 3 tests, 1 final exam, 2 oral exams. Languages at UT are really immersive, so just be ready to work!

Duffey-sensei is an amazing professor. Really kind, cares about her students and good lecturer. There's almost daily quizzes and daily HW, but study a bit everyday and you'll be fine. If you're going to take Japanese, take it with Duffey! You will not regret it. This class was the highlight of my final semester at UT.

I took her during the middle of the pandemic, so everything was through zoom. There is daily homework and almost daily quizzes. She is the sweetest I love her class and she takes in late work. As long as you attend class daily and pay attention the test and quizzes aren't that challenging. She teaches whats going to be on the test/quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Duffey-sensei is not only a great teacher, but is also a very caring person who wants to make sure that everyone learns Japanese and gets an A while doing so.

Duffey is honestly the reason I'm continuing Japanese. She's so kind, genuinely cares about you, and wants you to succeed. As long as you keep up with the material and homework, as well as put the effort in to learn and attend each class, this class is an easy A. You'll learn so much more than you thought you would! Def take her for 601D :)

Duffey Sensee is the best!! If you're reading this, take her class! She's a really kind professor, you can tell she cares about her students, she's also really funny! I learned a lot in Japanese 1 and think she set a good foundation for the next classes. The class felt very comfortable. If you come to class and do the HW you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: A GEM. I absolutely adore her! She is so kind & understanding. She will hold you accountable to actually do the work, so don't slack off but she will understand if you accidentally forget to turn in something. Just don't take advantage of her kindness! She truly is a great person. If I could take her for ALL of my semesters of Japanese I would!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Y'all this woman is my goat. I had her for LAH 350: Best Pictures (which wasn't an option on RMP oops) and it was my favorite class I've ever taken. She knows everything about film formalism and I respect her so much. Just do the assignments and stay engaged in class and she'll love you. I can't hype her up enough I loveeeee her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a fun class! We just talked about animated films the whole time, wrote a couple of very easy papers, and did a lot of joking around! Love love love her!

Took E 344S. Really liked it, and I learned a lot about film analysis! Professor Kornhaber is very nice, and takes a pretty laid-back approach to work that emphasizes class discussion - which definitely made the course even more enjoyable.
I took this class for my additional english requirement. The class somehow made me want to fall asleep but was interesting overall. There are lots of papers you have to write and exams are open notes

She's really nice, but doesn't give very good feedback. On my first short paper assignment I was given a 100, but no feedback. Then on the second an "A-" with no real grade and no feedback, and then on my final 8 page paper I received no grade back, and then once grades were reported I found I got an "A-" for the class. Recommended, but be careful.

Easy class for your VAPA. You don't even really have to read all of the assigned literature because she goes over what you need to know during lecture. The assigned movies are good, so you should definitely watch those anyway! Writing-heavy exams and assignments, but open-note. TA's grade easy. Lecture style can get boring, but it's not that bad
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber is one of the best professors I've had so far at UT. I'm a math major but her film and lit class was so much fun!! I always anticipated going to lecture because I knew she would have something interesting to teach. We got to watch classic films in this class and she made me appreciate stylistic techniques of filmmaking.

Loved taking this class! Graded assignments were exclusively essays, but they werent very difficult if you paid attention to the lectures. Dr. Kornhaber is a delight and she truly sparked my interest in film.

Dr. Kornhaber is incredible! I've never been so glad to have taken a class. She's incredibly brilliant and engaging. Everything she says is worthwhile and I always left her lectures in awe. She's very accessible and genuinely cares about her students and their insight. Her course truly enhanced the way I view film; I can't recommend her enough.

I took Dr. Kornhaber's class as my VAPA. It honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting, but she did change the way that the class is done from being essay based to literary/film analysis during your discussion section. But even then, it wasn't a bad class. Dr. Kornhaber is incredibly talented in film, but she makes it approachable for new learners.

Dr. Kornhaber is THE most chill professor. It's honestly hard to not get an A in this class unless you just never show up. You also learn so much about analyzing films, and honestly, the films that we watched were a lot more interesting than I thought they would be. Definitely my favorite class this year. Dr. Kornhaber is super sweet, def recommend

I would recommend this class for anyone who needs a VAPA. Dr. Kornhaber is very knowledgeable and it is fun to listen to her lectures. Exams are open note so you do need to be in class to take notes. I wasn't sure what to expect going into the class but the class had us watch really good movies and now I can't watch a film without analyzing it!

The class is about analyzing films and novels, which I took as a VAPA. We had two in-section exams (20% each) and a final (40%). There are 3 outside-of-class papers that just contribute to the 20% section participation grade. Dr. Kornhaber was passionate and knowledgeable, and I really enjoyed her class! Get ready to take lots of notes though.

I took a film noir class professor Kornhaber taught. The class was enriching, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I encourage anyone considering taking her class to do so. Both she and her husband David are English professors. I loved every course I took with each of them.
has great credentials and encourages student participation, but her lecture style could get boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As an RTF student, this was the best possible VaPA credit I could've taken. Her lectures took you step by step through the cinematography and mise en scène choices made in important films, so by taking the class you learn about the visual hints filmmakers have been giving you all along. It was cool hearing an Academy Film Scholar's perspective!

Kornhaber is a great professor and cares about her class. She's really passionate about film and helping her students understand the concepts. If you're taking this for your VAPA don't expect an easy A. She makes you work for it, but it's a fun class to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber's class is interesting and teaches you a lot about film. The course load seems daunting with all of the books and films you are assigned, but you can get away with just writing about films. I would recommend watching the films (which are all classics anyway) and just spark-noting the readings. The discussions are boring but required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention during lecture. I think that the discussion sections are a waste of time but you have to go to them for attendance. You can sparknote all of the novels and still get all of the questions right. Definitely, watch the movies because you can analyze those instead of the books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is kind, funny, and overall made me want to attend lecture every time. If you read the novels and watch the films, you should have no problem. Quizzes in discussion are multiple choice and matching with a word bank. Easy 100 and you learn a LOT.
Dr. Kornhaber is very educated in her field of film study and makes it easy for people new to film to understand and follow along. TAKE HER CLASS... she is awesome.

This class will seem like a lot of work but you can get by without doing all the reading and still easily make an A. If you're already a proficient writer, you will ace this class. She is so nice and genuinely cares about all of the students thoughts. Plus she's so smart and knowledgable and cool, definitely take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kornhaber is amazing!! She is the most kind and flexible professor I've ever had. Every opinion, insight, or thought is welcome in her classroom and she never makes a student feel stupid. The content is amazing and has changed how I watch movies for the better. Highly recommend to take her, she is beyond great!

As an RTF student and an avid cinephile, this class was a real treat for me. Dr. Kornhaber is so knowledgable and passionate about films and literature, and is always so bubbly during every lecture. HIGHLY recommend.

My favorite professor! She's so nice, loves what she does, and makes it easy to succeed. The quizzes are super easy, the essays are graded fairly, and there are no tests - just in class essays (called mini exams). The movies and books we looked at were super interesting and I learned a ton.

This class was very interesting, and the professor made the material very accessible. The concepts were easy to understand and the content overall was engaging. Level of feed back will vary depending on the TA but the expectations are pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: You can tell Prof Kornhaber really cares not only about film, but also about the students in her class. The books and movies we get to read/watch were super awesome and fun, but if that isn't your thing, you can totally get by with just watching the movies and Spark-noting the books. There are a few short essays and super easy vocab quizzes.

Very fun class! Watching movies as homework was great. Except when you watch movies in class you might fall asleep. She is very flexible with watching the movies and reading the books because she understands we have other classes. Grading depends mostly on TAs however, but still an easy A.

I got A's on my papers and very little feedback, so don't know what that was all about. But she really knows her stuff, there was basically no reading in the class because it was based off of music videos. Participation does help, but I don't know how much she takes off for not. More than three absences your grade lowers dramatically.

The class can be very interesting or boring but shes very nice and really wants you to learn the material. You do not have to do too much work on the essays and she gives you plenty of options to write on so you aren't limited.  The class was fun and very interesting. Make sure to use the university writing center. It helps a ton in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's extremely knowledgeable about the material. You can get away with not doing the readings because it's mostly focused on the films. If you don't show up and take good lecture notes, you won't have much to work with for the essays. I don't recommend the class if you're not genuinely interested in film analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kornhaber is an excellent lecturer. She really shows her knowledge in a way that is interesting and easy to follow. There are 4 essays- two short essays (20% each), a midterm(25%), and a final (35%). The TAs grade the essays. The grading was fair. As long as you watch the films/read the books the writing should come easily.

I am currently taking Kornhaber's Literature/Film/Other Arts class. Lectures can get very boring, but the bad part is your notes are vital to your grade. Only grades are  2 short papers, midterm & final, ALL essays. Exams are take home. She has 3 TAs, some grade harder than others so an A can be nearly impossible, but a high B-A is very possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS
