reviews.comment: very funny and pretty nice! sometimes he can be blunt but i think its more of his sense of humor ... dont take him too seriously lol

Dr. Sackey lectures, TA's grade. His lectures are very interesting, random, and engaging. Just engage with him during lecture to make him feel a little more love. He is a great source of advice when doing the actual assignments for the class, but make sure to give him time to respond. He also had a great dynamic with Dr. Laude in joint lectures.

Dr. Sackey is the best! I've taken him for a few classes and he is a very understanding professor who likes to push his students to perform WITHOUT hurting their grade. I wish all my professors were like him.

Topic: Rhetoric & Data Visualization | Excellent (and hilarious) professor! I'd recommend this to any STEM major. You'll not just learn to write but make great PowerPoints. Btw, don't be scared by "98 = A". Like 75% of the grade is participation *and* there's enough extra credit opportunities to bring that down to a de facto 94.

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I had at UT so far. He always gives extensive feedback, makes lectures super interesting, and has a lot of office hours outside of class. He's kind, caring, helpful, and hilarious. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches! Would love to take a class with him again.

Professor Sackey is literally the best. He is funny, engaging, and cares about each one of his students. His grading isn't too harsh, and he wants to see each student succeed and put in effort. He is readily available via office hours/email. In-class discussion is thoughtful and fun. Reading isn't too extensive.

Regarding UGS 303 (Originality in the Arts & Sciences) Sackey provides engaging lectures, some of which really random, but he does get his point across. In this class you get three projects: a humanities inquiry, a science inquiry, and a group project that incorporates a little of both. If you ask him for help, he'll happily assist you.

Took him as one of two professors for UGS 302: Originality in the Arts and Sciences. We were graded by only 3 projects but the TAs who graded us did not follow the rubric at all and the expectations for our projects were never clear. I liked his lectures though and he's a really cool speaker to listen to (even if you aren't paying attention).

Took UGS: Originality in Arts and Sciences. Lectures were mandatory to attend but were often dry and boring. No tests over content but humanities project assigned was a pain. TAs did not grade this project to the given rubric and would not explain why they gave a certain grade. Dr. Sackey seemed like a nice guy but I did not like the lectures.

Dr. Sackey is a great professor. I took his Info. Design course, and he is very accommodating and really wants the best for all of his students. He assigned a lot of readings, but you could skim them and be fine in time for class. Overall, this was an easy class, and Dr. Sackey made it enjoyable.
I definitely recommend taking him for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sackey was very accomodating during the pandemic. The assignments were good and career-focused. While he occasionally had opaque grading requirements, the assignments were useful (I was able to get a job in technical writing after taking this class). Most of the readings were short but useful. The projects help you to build a good portfolio.

Professor Sackey is one of the best professors I've had. The class was online and asynchronous. Sackey gives really great feedback and allowed for corrections on some assignments. He's super accessible if you have any questions, and clearly cares about his students, and he wants you to pass.

I took the digital rhetoric class when COVID shut the university down and we switched to online. Before, Professor Sackey was super easy to follow, not boring at all, and the class was so interesting! Post-COVID, he was super accomodating and always gave helpful feedback on the assignments I turned in without being demeaning in any degree.

Great digital rhetoric class with an amazing professor. Dr. Sackey allows you choose what you want to write about, so long as it relates to the course content. Reading responses were easy and meant to boost your grade. We made video documentaries for our final project and Dr. Sackey was very helpful and understanding throughout the process.

The quizzes, exams, and course content of this class are extremely difficult. If you are not religious, find a religion and start praying. Would not recommend this class or professor to anyone. The proffesor is very hard to communicate with via email, does not release keys to anything, and will laugh in your face for asking questions.
Dr. Edison called us slow once and I thought that was the funniest thing ever. What a G

Very knowledgeable, but does not post keys to very tough home works/quizzes. Lectures are a lot of information thrown at you, but he knows his stuff. Nothing matters but exam grades, need 60 average. Can be condescending. Plays favorites. Incredibly difficult, don't expect an A. Jump from HW to exams is very unreasonable. Not great professor

Dr. Edison is one of the most difficult professors I've ever had but also has taught me the most in such a short amount of time. Honestly, the quizzes aren't that relevant to your course grade but will be very difficult. I'm very grateful to have a break from how all consuming his class is, you will need to set aside probably 10 hours every week

I wasn't sure that ChemE was the degree for me at first, but when I took Dr. Edison, I realized that it was everything I wanted to learn. Dr. Edison takes chemical engineering and shows you exactly how it applies to the real world, and you can very clearly see how passionate he is about the subject. He's a great professor, take him if you can.

overall very smart guy who knows his stuff, but get ready to spend obscene amounts of time in his office hours. his weekly homework sets are incredibly time consuming and he gives no feedback/solutions. transport is and should be a hard class but he makes it annoyingly difficult with no clear grading criteria and not adhering to his own syllabus.

Dr. Edison is one of the best professors I've had at UT so far. His lectures are extremely helpful because he's a really good professor. He values effort and genuinely wants to see you succeed in his class and as an engineer. But, I'm looking forward to a sem without a weekly 2 hr quiz, plp every class, and the worst tests known to man. 🥀

One of the harshest professors I've had. He says anyone averaging below 60 on his three exams fails, yet the exam averages were 49, 46, and 46.5. At that point the low scores reflect his teaching or test design. Grading feels arbitrary, small errors lose full credit, and no partial credit is given on multi-part problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worse professor ever

Edison is the best professor in the ChE department at UT. He is a very strong lecturer who challenges you with homework and PLP problems. Exams are very challenging often being a problem not seen before on homework, PLP, or quizzes. Don't take Edison to get a good grade, take him to learn. He prepared me extremely well for Ops 1.
if you don't have a religion now, get one, and start praying

If you have the option to not take Edison's, DO IT. Save yourself! The only way to do well is to go to office hours for hw and questions. Not even the TAs knew what they were doing most of time because Edison would make up random things about problems and you just have to go by his word. Failing quizzes and exams are pretty standard for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every chemE should take Edison in order to say they graduated. So difficult but so worth it. You will learn more than you thought imaginable and push yourself hard. If you go to office hours, he wants you to succeed and know you are capable of it. Prioritize his classes (its expected), take few hours. You can do it. Expect lots of homework

Dr. Edison makes his courses tough, but you will definitely learn a lot. He is extremely helpful and knowledgable and always there to help students. However, his classes are time consuming and require a lot of time to be dedicated to them. As long as you care about the class and try, you will be fine.

Lots of HW, weekly quizzes, 3 exams, 1 final. He did allow a makeup exam for the 1st exam because the class did poorly on it. 
He's tough, but cares. Go to office hours, whether it's his or the TA's. Ask questions. The worst thing you can do for this class is not participate or ask questions. Sets up a strong foundation for future courses.
His reactor class was so much work!
cool guy, I'm just bad at math

Edison is a very difficult professor. This class will make you work the whole semester. However, you will be very prepared for the next classes. He's very available and willing to work with you to make sure you learn. The only bad part about this class was the lack of answer keys for homework, making studying difficult.

I thought i was about to die in this class. He genuinely wants you to learn but he makes it overly complicated. If you are stuck in it, go to every office hour, the TAs are very helpful. He pretty much does whatever he wants at the end of the semester grade wise/grade drops are unclear. There are NO keys posted for any hw/reviews and it's horrible.

If the devil was present on earth, his name would be Thomas Edison. This guy constantly disrespects students who want to learn, and takes over your life. If you're taking reactor with him, be prepared to dedicate your entire semester to him, as he single handedly ruined my senior year of college. He plays favorites to certain students -- AVOID HIM.

My senior year was ruined by this professor. Long weekly homework assignments, shorter homework due when you walk into every lecture. He claims he wants you to learn by coming to office hours, but laughs at questions and constantly disrespects students who are doing their best to learn. Exams are on Thursday/Friday nights and three hours long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Edison is extremely demeaning to students and rude. Not only are his tests extremely difficult he also makes you feel awful any time you ask for help. The test averages ranged from 47-53 and there are no curves. In order to pass the class you must have a test average of 60 before the Q drop date.

It was hard to keep up with the course material, and it was difficult to track where we stood because grades were posted vaguely. Lectures often felt overly complicated, and Professor Edison seemed to favor certain students. He also rushed through the content, making it hard to follow along. Overall, the course felt very unorganized.

Dr. Edison is a professor known to make his students work hard the entire semester. I learned a lot, and I feel overly prepared for the next courses, but I feel mentally exhausted. He makes a three-credit class feel like 12 credits. Everyone should take Dr. Edison once to say they graduated from UT. His exams are challenging... averages are 40s.

Edison's classes are generally tougher than other professors, but I believe his methods of teaching make you grow a lot as a student. Lectures are not mandatory, but you need to go. The tests are very hard, but mostly fair. As long as you show effort edison will help you, and he remembers what participating individual students are weak on.

Thomas Edison wants his students to succeed, and provides plenty of opportunities to for you to practice and ask questions. If you want to do well the most important thing to do imo is to go to his office hours every week. His class will be tough, but you'll understand the material much better than with other professors. Pressure makes diamonds

Avoid at all costs. Obviously plays favorites-- make the same mistakes and your grade will be different. Will go the entire semester without grading homework, quizzes, or projects. Makes attendance mandatory-- expect pop quizzes. Refuses to provide keys for homework, quizzes, and exams. Exams VERY difficult and lengthy, most averages below 70%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Edison genuinely wants his students to do well, but you have to put in the effort yourself. 317 is a very homework heavy class with a lot of commitment outside of class time, with weekly quizzes. Also the exams were from 7-10 pm on Friday. so. take from that what you will.

You can't avoid taking Dr. Edison because he teaches a majority of the upper-division classes. He tends to overcomplicate things but he genuinely wants his students to succeed in the industry, and he does this by grading VERY harshly. He WILL diverge from his syllabus and surprise you with pop quizzes you just have to be ready for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For a 2hr credit class, this class was a soooo much work. 2 HW's and a quiz per week, and the HW took a very long time to do. Edison is an alright teacher, he makes the class a whole lot harder than it needs to. The class avg for each test have all been below 75, but grade in class depends on class avg. (ClassAvg B-) There were 4 tests and a final

I have taken several classes with Dr. Edison, and the main thing to know about him is that he will demand a lot of time and work from you in order to understand the material he is teaching, but you will learn a ton from him if you put in the time. His 348 class can be difficult if you have no coding background, so learn a bit yourself beforehand.

Process Safety with Dr. Edison should be an easy A - unlike most other classes he teaches, he does not put a limit on the number of A's he will give in Process Safety. Whatever you do, though, go to the sponsored safety lectures - he gave an extremely difficult final to students who did not attend them! Great class, great professor, learned a lot!

The man cares, but he is one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Focuses on theoretical ideas not related to the class and never finishes his sentences/thoughts. There was such a large workload, it took up as much time as transport. and by all means, stay away from his stat class. Used to be an easy class, but difficult under him for same reasons

This was a confusing class. Two in-person labs and several virtual projects+self-design project. All performed in groups. Dr. Edison had several classes to teach so this was relatively easy because grading wasn't strict and if you did the work in lectures+off the manual you get full credit. Have to attend lectures for various quizzes+for the final.

Edison is a hard professor BUT extremely caring and dedicated. He will make you work for a passing grade but seems to really want everyone to succeed. The department would not stand a fighting chance without him. Taking a class with Edison (he teaches nearly all of them) is a right of passage. Go into the class ready to work and itll pay off
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a lot to learn and you always have homeworks, but the material is not hard to learn and if you reach out to Dr. Edison in office hours you should get an A. Graded on a curve, 3 exams and optional final. Homeworks are graded for completion. Exams are take-home, with one as an in-class portion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Talk to anyone in UT's CHE program and you can get more details on Dr. Edison. He is undeniably smart and knows his stuff extremely well, but it can often be hard to understand what exactly he is trying to communicate. He wants his students to succeed, but won't give anything away for free. Work hard and attend his office hours for good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Edison is hard but teaches you the basis you need for chemE. He is one of the best CHE profs at UT because his problems prepare you well for industry. He is always ready to help in office hours and wants you to succeed. Tests are hard, but knowledge you gain is rewarding and a good foundation going forward. Go to tutoring you will thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Edison is a great professor who wants to make you learn materials. However, he gives so many time consuming assignments that many students try to avoid him in future classes. He was willing to help answer any questionss, but sometimes he told us to do on our own. He said he didnt care about attendance, but he gaves pop quiz to check that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Edison did a poor job at teaching the material. He often would solve a problem and realize he did it wrong and not know how to fix it or show us the solution. The exams were much more difficult than the homework, and he blamed the class for not knowing the material. He even said "the problem with you guys is..." during class. Terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Edison is a tough professor, but he really makes you learn the materials. The homeworks are long and often challenging but do an excellent job to prepare you for the exams. Study groups help make the class easier. Attend lectures and follow his packets during class. Make sure you take advantage of your TA and tutors - they are there to help you!
100% tests. Extremely hard. I know all of the evolution professors are meh but just stick with the duo
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Theriot had some fun and interesting lectures. He also makes himself available to students whenever help is needed. The grade is only based on exams. There were some practice worksheets, but I found them to be pretty easy and did not feel like they prepared me much for the exams. Exams were open note and online, but very difficult.

Dr. Theriot is a genuinely good guy. 4 midterm exams (1 drop) and the final make up your grade, no need to worry about busy assignments. Go over lecture slides and make a google doc to reference during exams- they are online, open resources. If you are confused about something, go to office hours. He will do everything he can to help you out.

the absolute worst. lectures did not help with tests & ranted abt random topics. doesnt explain anything & brags abt how tests are so hard/ how no one gets a 100. all your grade is from exams (1 drop) even though they're open everything NOTHING helps. has select all that apply questions that will BREAK your grade. terrible prof needs to retire!!!!!

His class is graded on 4 midterms and a final. Group tests but the questions come from a bank so you're not going to have the same questions as the person next to you. Lectures are incredibly boring and it doesn't help that he goes off topic every two sentences. Get ready to rewatch the lectures and read the textbook and still do bad on the tests.

Summer 2023. All exams, but everything web based with in-person lectures recorded. Exams were relatively difficult, but the professor's lecturing and presentation style made it clear what would be assessed and what would be good factoids beyond exams.

Recorded lectures. Only grades come from tests and discussion participation. Tests are tricky but open internet and open collaboration. Doesn't do +/- grades (only need 90 for an A but any 80s will be a B). Very available via Canvas email and Zoom. I found the lectures boring and the test structure annoying, but it's doable. Take good notes!

Clearly cares about his students, approachable, entertaining and engaging lectures. Tests are a little tricky but come entirely from lectures and are open notes + open people. One of my favorite profs I've had at UT!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Theriot takes his time to explain concepts thoroughly during office hours. Test content is based heavily on lectures (which you can watch online at 2x, taking good notes), I never looked at the textbook. Even though the exams are difficult (choose-all-that-apply), you are allowed to collaborate w/ others and only need a 90 for an A.

I think his main goal for this class is to make sure that you get tricked. Every single exam question is unnecessarily elaborate and difficult to follow. Lectures are boring, and he gets side tracked really often. I am not sure why he prides himself on "no one gets a 100 on my tests" because that is a reflection of him and not the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams drew largely from lecture content, but most students in the course found his lecturing style really challenging to follow. He frequently gets side-tracked so it's hard to know what information to pay mind to and what to ignore. He does curve the highest exam grade up to 100 though. Overall doable but you might be better off with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Evolution is a really hard course, but Dr. Theriot is really caring and does everything he can to help students. The exams are hard but there's usually a really big curve, and a good portion of the grade is just attending discussion. Evolution is gonna be hard no matter what so you might as well take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are recorded, and will offer office hours and help any time you need. He gives curves based on the highest grade of each exam, so just hope no one gets a 100 in your class, but these exams are also open note and open person. I recommend reading the textbook and revisiting the lecture PowerPoints, since about 90% of grades are exams.

Dr. Theriot was not only such a great guy that cared about the material he taught, but he is always available to help you if you fall behind. The class works as you have to attend 1 Discussion Section per week (during summer) out of two chances, quizzes are open group/note/online, and the same goes for the exams. Dr. Theriot is the best.

Dr Theriot was super chaotic but really awesome! He was super entertaining and had a bunch of stories, and his research was very interesting (diatoms). He fundamentally changed how I thought about biology, and the class applies concepts of evolution in a ton of different ways. Questions are tough and sometimes weirdly worded. An A is def doable!
2nd hardest class i've taken at ut. Learned a lot about evolution, but hard nonetheless. He's probably the best professor for evolution though.
He was a good professor but hard exams and super disorganized. Prepare to study hard.

Took class online over the summer and it was really fair. Class was really just 5 exams and daily quizzes. The quizzes weren't too difficult but the exams can really make you think and question yourself. The saving grace is that this class is open note, open internet, people collaborative, etc. Theriot is a solid prof if you take this class. :)

Probably one of my favorite professors! Online format included open resource/open note exams and quizzes. Group work is openly allowed, but exams were very difficult. He replies to any emails if you have questions on exams and quizzes. Tells really good and funny stories after class. TAKE FOR EVOLUTION! An A is doable with big effort.

This class set up was ideal. Class collaboration, email clarification and no attendance required was great. HOWEVER, this man makes sure you know the material test are tricky and are meant to trip people up. He is a good and interesting professor. Take if you can

Dr. Theriot clearly explained all the material during lecture, taking time to point out the little details/nuances. All the exams/quizzes in this course allow peer collaboration, but that doesn't make them easy. Spent about 18 hrs taking each exam for 4 exams, but I was rewarded for my effort on each exam. One of the best courses I have ever taken!
He is probably the best professor for this class. He genuinely cares for the students and has a cool way of doing quizzes and tests (groups!)

I took Ed's class for the summer, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Weekly quizzes were extremely tough, but the whole class was allowed to work together. Getting an A was challenging but definitely doable. If you email regrade requests, Ed tends to give a few points back for a solid explanation. Ed is one of the quirkier professors you will have :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Entertaining guy. He really wants his students to learn. my semester was online so he has the tests open note and my class worked together. 30 people each put in maybe 15 hours a weekend on these tests and the averages were still not great. Way harder and way more work than an undergrad class should ever have. Never rounds and is stingy on points.

Probably my favorite professor at UT. Theriot cares about you learning the material and goes out of his way to explain things in depth. Multiple choice on his tests can be pretty challenging but he adjusts according to the class performance on exams. He's also very understanding of any problems you might have. Easy to talk to in office hours.

This man is amazing. I love his class. I'm not going to lie he makes you work for that A, but genuinely cares for his students. His test can be tricky at times, so watch the wording of his test. This was my second time taking evolution since Kirkpatrick/Linder was not a great combination. I think he's your best option for making an A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Theriot is very high and mighty in his own head. Even if you understand the concepts and study the material you may get a horrible grade on his tests and quizzes because of the way he words his questions. He is indirect and very pompous. The only pro to this class is that I did learn a lot even though my exam grades did not show it.

So i took this class as part of my Biology major, and this is one of the hardest classes i have taken at UT. Biochemistry is already a hard enough subject, but this class makes it unnecessarily hard. Dr. Theriot tries his best, but the structure of the class, and his lecture heavy style make it very hard to get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Theriot is a great lecturer who can be reached outside of class if needed! He likes to discuss personal examples and sometimes makes jokes to engage the class more with lecture. Tests and discussion assignments are important for performance and discussion assignments count for participation! Tests are very straightforward and doable!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Even a semester later I randomly think how Dr. Theriot is doing. He was a wonderful professor. Other than being passionate about this class and his research, he is an incredibly caring man to students. He will extend his office hours for as long as you need, even to talk about things like his personal passion for duck-hunting! Take him if you can!

I always think back to how wonderful of a professor Ed is. Sometimes lectures can seem to go on forever and seem very confusing, so I recommend reading the chapters before class so you can follow along. Tests and discussion section matter. Very caring guy - to the extreme. Will sit down with you for two hours to make sure you understand a subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is hard ranked, which can push your grades down on tests. However, at the end, he fills up most of the F slots with the students that dropped the class. NEED TO READ. Class based on just 4 tests, no final. Great guy, passionate and involved in the material, very helpful in class. If you put in the effort, hell work to help your grade too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Theriot is a good man, but he grades on a curve where an A is the top 12% of the class, an A- is the next 12%, and so on. I scored a 92 on the first exam and that was a B+, so be ready to study HARD. He also insists on discussion sections with TAs being cancelled the week of an exam, which doesn't make any sense to me. Exams are 80% of grade.

MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS CAN BE TRICKY! DR. THERIOT CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS! MAKE SURE TO GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! IF YOU PUT THE EFFORT, AN A ISN'T IMPOSSIBLE! UNLIKE OTHER BIO 370 CLASSES, THERE IS MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS! TA TAHMIN IS THE BEST!

OMG I LOVE THIS MAN. He's the best. He takes time to get to know his students and he is always willing to go out of his way to help them. He genuinely cares. His tests were actually quite hard for me (his MC is tricky sometimes), but if you just go into his office hours and explain your thinking, he'll give you points back. Highly recommend.

Ed is the fookin man. Never seen a professor care so much about his students until him. The material is fairly easy and has long office hours and review sessions that he does himself. Pretty funny dude. Take him if you can! Gives out practice tests too. Very easy going and doesn't overwhelm you with material. The best BIO370 prof hands down.

Dr. Endl is really funny, and his lectures can be really interesting. I didn't pay all that much attention in class, which is my own fault, but half of your grade comes from just showing up. The tests aren't that difficult, but if you don't come/don't pay attention, you may get stuck. Overall, this was a great course to take for science credit.

Super easy and interesting course. Information on tests is easy to learn but very specific so attendance and good listening and note taking are important (we're in college this isn't hard). As long as you take notes this is a free A.

Good professor. Class has 4 Tests and 4HWs and that is it for your grade. Tests were usually chill; you can find flashcards online. There is extra credit if needed. I found the class pretty intresting. Definitely made me think of the universe in ways I had never before, and it's really cool if you are interested in space and possibilities of life.

Easy course for a science credit. Endl was funny and super engaged with the material. Lectures could get boring and repetitive. If you study for the exams, regardless of whether or not you paid attention, you'll be fine because they are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy!!

I love Professor Endl! He is extremely sweet and super passionate about this course! He somehow made this content interesting although most of his students weren't even astronomy majors! As for the actual class, you do need to go to lectures and study occasionally for the exams, but nothing too difficult at all. PLEASE TAKE ENDL! He rocks!

love this guy! super fun class, you will have to at least kind of pay attention to do well on the exams but homeworks are unlimited attempts hehe thank u kinggg and up to 3 percentage points of extra credit!!! my goat fr
Endl is my dawg

You can tell the professor is not only an expert in the field, but also passionate to the point that he makes every single lecture fascinating to a room of people likely entirely disconnected from his field of study. Grade is comprised of 4 exams, attendance, and 4 homeworks. The exam questions are exactly adjacent to what is covered in lecture.
Super easy/self explanatory class! Professor Endl is so funny and a great lecturer. Definitely take this class if you're not good in science and want to take an interesting fun class.

Dr. Endl made every lecture about the class interesting and never had any surprise content on tests. Tests usually were comprised of things directly from the slides to the test review, pay attention in class, use the study guides he provides, read the slides over before the tests, and 309L is the easiest A.

This class is about astrobiology, not speculating on aliens. However, it was easy. There's 4 homeworks that are similar to the 4 unit tests, no final. Attendance "mandatory" but it's taken through instapolls, and you only need 70% to get full credit. Professor Endl is genuinely passionate about astrobiology, but prefers subs over canceling class.

There are 4 exams but the questions are very straightforward. Takes attendance via Instapolls, but lectures are recorded so you can rewatch them. 4 homework quizzes total. Gives extra credit if you raise your hand often. Sends out a review sheet the week of the test. If you watch all the lectures and do the review then the tests are easy.
One of the best classes I have taken at UT. He's very passionate and his energy is contagious, a very interesting class and easy to follow. If you show up and do the homework tests will be easy

Goated professor. The class is super interesting, and the professor is great at lecturing. The majority of the grade is made up of 4 exams, and they're not too difficult (def study though). Study the lectures intensively, and you'll easily get a 100 on the exams. Quizlet is great too.
Great professor and very passionate about the topic, easy class for science credit. He also likes making jokes all the time.
Hard to reach. Tests are very easy if you look over the slides and instapolls. There is nearly no homework. Overall about similar difficulty to an on level high school science course.

I was looking for a science credit. I am so glad I chose this class. Usually, I'm not very interested in biology or chemistry aspects, but the professor manages to make this class engaging. He has the perfect intonation to follow along in notes and is very passionate when lecturing. His tests are extremely easy if you attend the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't required but if you want to do well on tests, show up to class. If you show up to class and do the work, you will pass. The tests are super easy if you do the homework. Don't buy the textbook, we never used it at all. The lectures are fun and interesting too, although sometimes he can be a little rude responding to questions.
I loved Professor Endl's class! He offers extra credit to those who participate and he is very passionate about what he teaches. I'd def take him again.

Do NOT trust these comments of this being an easy class! This class was definitely not an easy A. Participation matters and you NEED to pay attention during lectures if you want to do well in the test. If you're not interested in astronomy, I suggest to take another class cause this one was boring. However the Professor was nice. GO TO CLASS!

Just be careful entering this course, if possible take it after 11am or sometime that you know you'll be there. Showing up to this course is not a choice, he will say it is, but it really isn't. The work is simple but the exams are tricky and worded weird. If you're looking for an easy A, this is not it. Maybe a C+ for good work ethic. Goodluck.

Dr. Endl's class was amazing!!! I took this for an easy Natural Science credit and it did not disappoint. Lectures were interesting, and as long as you show up, easy A. Endl is super accessible and loves to talk his stuff. Please take this class it'll make him so happy!

The professor tricked me x:( 
Don't take this class if you want to learn about big-brained aliens; the real name of this course should be 'Astrobiology (geology + chemistry + astronomy).' Still, it is a tiny bit more interesting than other science and tests are not difficult if you study

Easy, relatively interesting class coming from a non-science major. However, Prof. Endl is very touchy about phone/laptop usage, sleeping in class, or leaving early. He WILL call you out. Not the most pleasant in class experience but very little work & tests are easy. Attendance is mandatory and taken through instapoll questions at end of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Endl was fine. There are Instapols in every class for attendance that are based on the lectures, and if you get less than 70% of them right then your grade will be affected, but the questions are usually not that hard. For a science class, it's not that bad, but I thought it would just be more fun. Just wasn't the content I expected.

Endl is very kind, but peeved easily by ppl sleeping or on their phone in class. Tests are only multiple choice-very easy. He records all the lectures so although attendance is mandatory (70% attendance gives you full credit) you can easily catch up on what you missed. Nice guy, easy exams, no final, would take again
he understands we are not interested in science and tries to make it fun as possible! i also like his voice and personality. also please don't leave while he's lecturing, it's rude

And i thought college was supposed to be easier than highschool.
Endl is probably a great professor. I wouldnt know, because his lectures were so easy they were boring. This is awesome if you are, like me, a humanities major who just needs the credit and doesnt care about aliens that much. Easy tests, easy class, and a really likable guy in general

Be aware of Instapolls he takes for attendance each class, but doing it 70% is still a 100. I'm pretty sure I only attended 60% of his lectures but I was still doing great. Funny, and you don't need to study much to do well on the exams. Use Quizlet to prepare. Also, no final. Very very light on hw too! Easy science credit.

I really liked Dr. Endl, but I will say the third test was so confusing and hurt my grade!! It might have been just me that felt that way, but if you take this class, lock in for the third test... Either way, the class was pretty easy to keep up with; I just got bored during lectures and found it hard to pay attention. All mainly my fault, not his.

This class is pretty easy for non-science majors. 4 tests and 2 assignments per unit, no cumulative test. Lectures were kinda hard for me to pay attention, but what he says in class is important due to limited text on slides. Tests were sometimes confusing to understand what content it was on.

I am a government student who needed an easy science course, and I greatly enjoyed this class! Professor Endl does a great job during lectures and shows he is extremely passionate about what he is teaching, which makes the content even more interesting.  Boing!

GOAT. if interested in extraterrestrial life, take this class. Will establish fundamental knowledge required to understand sci-fi films better. Exam difficulty may vary (difficult for remake; easy for in-class).
Make sure you pay attention to lectures for exams. I loved this class so much and I have always hated science. Professor Endl ignited a love for science I never had before

This class was extremely frustrating. This teacher was not helpful and graded VERY harshly. The tests were proctored and over HALF of the points you could receive from the exams were open-ended, and no matter how much information or specifics I gave, he would always KILL my grade. Would not use this professor again, no matter what.

Looking for an easy science credit? This is the class! Great professor, easy to understand and interesting content, recorded lectures, minimal homework, easy tests. No need to buy the textbook either- just take notes during the lecture. As a non-science major, this class is a 10/10.
Great professor, fun and engaging. Dont buy the book if you plan on going to lectures

Dr. Endl is great. Really passionate and it spreads to you too. He's a great person who obviously cares about his students. Just show up to class and you'll be fine. If you need a science core <<< TAKE THIS CLASS.

Loved him, he was a great professor and lecturer. Another astronomy class with a hint of biology. Attendance technically isn't required but there is an instapoll every class that counts for a grade so you need to know when it is posted to take it. Exams are pretty easy. Just take notes of the slideshows and you'll be fine.

Professor Endl is an amazing Professor and I cannot recommend him to enough people. My B was a mistake of my own, all but one exam was 100-100+. Mostly memorization and he will not test over anything that was not in the lecture. If you'd like to get taught Astrobiology by Arnold Schwarzenegger, he's your guy. This class is not about UFOs!!!!!!

Easy science credit for non-science majors. Lectures can get a little boring, but made studying for tests so much easier. Attendance wasn't mandatory and it was super easy to catch up if you missed a day or two because the lectures were recorded. Super funny guy too and it was clear he is very passionate about what he teaches!

Material was easy to understand and engage with, as well as super interesting if you're a non-STEM student looking for a fun science credit. Dr. Endl is patient and likes to see students succeed. Attendance isn't mandatory, but each lecture has an Instapoll that is used for a participation credit.

This class is one of my absolute favorites! The professor is funny, charming, and knowledgeable. I highly recommend taking this class. The exams are 25 MCQ with 2 bonus questions, and the questions are all from lecture material. Minimal HW, super interesting content. If you have any interest in space, this class is the perfect one for you

Easy science credit and the exams are easy as long as you go over your notes. Lectures are recorded, so attendance isn't necessary, but he does instapolls for "attendance" and it counts towards your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Endl was a great lecturer and easy to understand. Extra credit is everywhere. Tests have two bonus questions on them that are easy to answer. Attending lectures is important since that is 100% of the exam. Don't be afraid to ask questions and don't be scared if science isn't your thing. As a non-STEM major, my final grade was a 100.08.

Even though the tests were pretty easy most of the questions were not from the slides like he claims but rather quick things he says in class. You really need to pay attention to everything he says. However, he records lectures so if you miss something it's easy to look back and find what you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for a science credit; I'm SO happy I did! I'm not the best at science, but he is very concept heavy and a good explainer. He is extremely charismatic and funny as well! Tests are based on homework and lecture, which you can access after class. Rewatch the recorded lectures to study and you'll do well on the tests and homework!

For all my non-science majors, do yourself a favor and take this class. This has probably been the most interesting, straightforward class I have ever taken. Only 4 assignments are due throughout the semester which will take about 2 hours at most to complete each time. The exams are very simple. The attendance policy is very lenient.

Endl is super sweet and a super fun lecturer. This class is pretty easy, but some parts are a but hard to wrap your head around if you aren't interested in space. I took this together with AST301 for  and they complement each other pretty well and helped me understand harder concepts. My friend never came to class and still passed. Easy and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are interested in space, this class may be a breeze. Personally, I rarely was able to stay awake in class. Even after taking notes and studying the homework, I would still make low B's on every test. Regardless, Prof. Endl is a super sweet man.

Endl was an awesome lecturer and a super nice guy. Very approachable and kind when I had questions about grades or homework. Homework is super easy but tests were where I struggled because even after attending every class and taking notes, a lot of the wording of his test questions would confuse me. Overall I would recommend this class!

Endl is funny and passionate. Really interesting class and easy in a good way. Just study learning goals and HW questions. 10/10 recommend for science credit, but also just if you want to learn about space and life! So cool he made it really fun. He does an okay job preparing us for tests, but it's fine because they're not that hard to begin with.

Professor Endl is very passionate about astronomy, unlike me, so this class was still interesting yet hard to keep my engagement at times. Nonetheless, I would still recommend taking this class if you are either interested in Astronomy or just need an easy science credit. Tests are essentially based off the lectures so no need for a textbook.

He's a great guy and he clearly is very interested in Astrobiology. This isn't a hard class but it also is not an easy A class. Not too much work outside of class, but if you are not familiar with astronomy and biology make sure you study for the tests.

Dr. Endl was an amazing professor to have. The class is generally easy if you keep up with lectures, and the exams are exactly like the homework questions. The homework is very easy and able to be completed two hours before it's even due. If you miss a lecture or two, you can rewatch the lectures and look at the slides online.

Professor Endl is very passionate about astronomy. Since I am not the course was pretty boring. The difficulty however was below average in my opinion. Only a few homework assignments with a few tests and he gives extra credit questions on all the tests. All the information is in his lecture so the key to a good grade is just showing up and trying.

He is very passionate about astronomy and likes participation. It is very lecture heavy, so although attendance is not required, it will be hard to pass the tests (60% overall grade) if you skip frequently. Assignments include 1 DB prompt, 4 tests, 4 homeworks (used as study guide for test), and instapolls randomly given each class. Textbk is free.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I actually really liked the professor himself, and it is really clear that he cares about the topic he's teaching, but it is simultaneously one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. It might be because I'm not a STEM major, and don't have a brain for it, but I was constantly about to fall asleep. It might be for you, but it wasn't for me.
Lectures are probably the most boring thing ever. No homework, but hard to actually stay awake in class. Tests were alright, usually got B's on them with moderately studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class really wasn't that hard. Its an easy science credit. Endl's lectures can be a little boring but they are pretty much parallel to the text. The power points are great study tools and the homework questions were word for word on the test. If you relatively pay attention and study, you will pass. I didn't use the textbook once.

There is NO homework for this class except just studying for the exams. Studying for the exam involves lots of cramming and rewatching the videos which takes up a lot of time. Also, he talks about the content instead of leaving it on the slides so it will be easier to retain. Other than that, exams are pretty straightforward!

Many of the complaining students were the same ones asking for study guides and lecture notes a day or so before the exam. If you know how to study, the exams aren't super challenging. Endl's exam questions only come from lecture content, so the textbook isn't necessary. Make mock-questions out of your lecture notes to study for exams!

Lectures were SO boring. I don't have a hard time paying attention in classes, but this class was the death of me. Tests are reweighed at the end of the semester, with you best test grade weighing more than your worst. I never read the textbook and did fine. Tests only cover material explicitly mentioned during lectures. Lots of extra credit opport

He's a great professor, but make sure you know what he is looking for in the tests. The first two exams I got a 72 and an 80 because I was studying based on the textbook and not on his lectures, and the tests heavily rely on lectures. If you take his class online I 100% recommend you watch the cloud recordings and take notes twice.

I have no interest in any type of science so taking this class is really hard for me. Although you can tell the professor is really passionate and excited to teach, it was not really enough to keep me awake during class. The class isnt hard, tests are a little tricky but not impossible, mostly graded on Homeworks and tests, no final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He does easy quizzes for attendance in class. Tests are multiple choice, 25 questions, easy if you pay attention to lectures. Nice guy, super accommodating w the transition to online classes. Lectures are kinda boring. Take notes under the learning objectives to study for the exam and you should be fine.

"We are going on a journey through the universe and I shall be your guide." Love this guy. Super knowledgeable and loves to teach his students. Take notes during lecture and add them to printed out powerpoint slides. Exams are strictly from lectures; don't worry about the book. Lots of material to study so do not cram but tests are not hard.

I ADORE Prof Endl! He's amazing & by far my fav prof at UT. The txtbook is not necessary, key to doing well in his class is to take notes on what he says, and then go back and add in stuff from the slides later. Tests correspond to the lecture. Grading policies are clear, lots of extra credit. Has an accent so listen careful. he posts recordings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best astronomy professor for AST301! He uploads recordings of his lectures, and his tests are 100% from his lectures. The textbook is free online, and only read it if you need more help. Two extra credit questions on the 5 exams. Extra credit for going to the UT Star Party, and extra credit on the HW. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Endl is hilarious and respected. His lectures are interesting and easy to follow. You're graded by 4 exams and have to facilitate 1 discussion post. He also offers extra credit opportunities that are doable and worth a good part of your final grade! The exams can be tough so you have to know your stuff, but it's nothing too hard to handle for core
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He LOVES what he teaches and it shows. He is a good teacher but his tests can be hard if u plan on cramming. Doesn't take attendance but does instapolls. Tests make up majority of your grade and there are extra credit points offered for tests and for overall grade. I would take him again and if u need a science and think astronomy is cool take it

Had my doubts as a COLA student taking a CNS class. Dr. Endl, however, gave me an incredible semester. I learned way more than I thought I'd stay awake to. He's a fantastic lecturer, a great person, and the class is a breeze. Wish I could give him a 6/5!

I def. recommend taking it if you need a science credit. His class consists of 5 exams (no cumulative final), daily homework of about 7-8 questions online (sometimes they include extra credit), there is also 2 participation grades. Exams are lectured based, book is online. Exams are usually about 25 questions and questions are based on lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Endl is very passionate about astronomy and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He provided a free online copy of the textbook and study guides for exams. Lectures were engaging and easy to follow. 5 exams and your lowest grade is weighted less. Would definitely recommend this professor for astronomy!

Endl is really passionate about his class, which makes it a lot more enjoyable. He does go kind of fast, so I had a hard time keeping up sometimes, but you'll be fine if you're a good note taker. Attendance isn't mandatory but everything is lecture based so it'd be beneficial to show up. Quiz every class period, weekly assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I suck @ science, but Endl was awesome, he cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Endl is clearly passionate about astronomy and cares about his students. There's 5 exams (lowest one weighted less), online homework every week (tons of extra credit from these), and in class mini quizzes for participation. He also started making study guides for each exam, and there's other extra credit opportunities too.

I am an RTF major and took intro to astronomy for my science credit. Professor Endl is one of the best professors I've had at UT. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches. He really just wants to share his knowledge with his students. I came away from this class having a deep interest in astronomy, which I never ever thought I would have.

Endl was hilarious he always made little jokes during lectures and just made astro tolerable. 5 exams drops one, weekly homework, tons of extra credit throughout, mini-quizzes every lecture. The funniest thing I remember him saying was "the biting and the kissing of the alien." literally like striking gold especially if science is not your thing.

Very easy to make an A! The lowest I got on an exam was a 95. He posts the lecture notes on canvas, but they're mostly graphs and pics so just go to the *free* online textbook and get more in depth notes and take notes in class and you're fine. He offers extra credit a lot too. There is quizzes every day, but they're not bad. Definitely take!!

Professor Endl is my favorite prof, UT or otherwise! Very good at describing complex ideas in lecture for us non-science majors and the FREE textbook is only needed if you want more depth. Not even necessary to read for tests. There are always quizzes at the end of class but they're easy. Extra credit is offered and lowest test is dropped.

Professor Endl is a pretty good professor. He really knows his field but can also break it down for the rest of us non-science majors. He gives 2 extra credit opportunities and class is mandatory due to the quiz after each lecture (super easy-all about participation on these). Tests are fairly easy but can be detailed ( get ready to memorize).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to understand- but the exercises that she provides for the exams are extremely helpful- and I don't see how anyone wouldn't get an A in this class. Use your resources and you'll be fine. She likes open discussion, so will try to get you to talk during classes. She is sweet, and cares a lot about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately I didn't have a great time in this class, mostly due to the lectures. The powerpoints were somehow both overly complex and vague at the same time, and I ended up using the textbook to understand many of the topics we had to cover. Exams were fine though, but I wouldn't be surprised if she changes things up in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Santos disappointing. The course lacked clear guidance and structure, making it difficult for students to understand expectations or succeed. Opportunities for meaningful feedback and support were minimal, and most times, the instructor's tone felt discouraging rather than constructive. Avoid if possible.

I would say the only downside of this class is the grade distribution, but I really love her resources like her practice sets. I re-took CH301 after taking Laude last semester. She is SO incredible and straightforward and the way that she teaches makes perfect sense to me. We learn exactly what we need to do well on the exam, no fluff!

If you have to take any sort of Chemistry at UT, TAKE HER. This is probably the most caring and thoughtful professor I have ever had. Her lectures are actual fun and she goes out of her way to make sure students understand. Uploads all here lectures online and offers so many resources for studying. Occasional extra credit during class
This is the best professor EVER. Love her. She makes my day. Records all the lectures and posts them online with so many resources

I took chem last semester and I didn't too well because I felt I did not understand it too well but Dr Eman makes me feel very good and confident in chem as a subject. She is so amazing and sweet you can tell she deeply cares about her students!!!!

Prof Eman is such an incredible professor, really gives you all the information you need to get an A in the class. There was no homework but instead self-paced quizzes that were a completion grade and review material for the exams. Take her if you can!!

Truly an outstanding professor. She goes above and beyond to support her students and provides an exceptional amount of resources to help you succeed. She is deeply invested in making sure students actually understand the material and is always willing to spend extra time explaining concepts. PChem could use slightly more rigor, but she's great

I LOVE Professor Eman, she is so knowledgeable, respected, inspirational, and just overall an amazing professor. I learned so much from her class and was actually able to retain what I learned. She offers lots of extra credit which is also a plus. I recommend that everyone whether you are a science major or not take a class with her!

Professor Eman was the best chemistry professor ever!! She is super sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She offered 2 makeup exams at the end of the semester that will replace your lowest two exams. She is hilarious and lectures were always engaging. You do have to study and put in some time/work, but all the material is accessible and organized.
Best professor ever, she sets the standards for how a professor should be, will for sure miss her class and the way she taught!

Even if you've had bad experiences with chemistry, I totally recommend taking Dr.Eman. If you reach out, watch her YouTube videos, do the modules and practice quizzes/exams, you are sure to get an A in this course. She is extremely dedicated and respectful to students. Take her if you have the chance.

She is the best professor I have EVER taken at UT. I think she deserves a 6/5 tbh. She teaches so sincerely, her exams are very representative of the content, and she prepares you very well and gives you everything you need to succeed.
Dr. Alasadi is one of the best professors you will take. She provides summarizing annotated lectures, YouTube videos, and extra credit. You will not fail her, and she will not fail you!

Professor Eman is THE GOAT. I don't enjoy chemistry at all, but his class actually made it bearable for me. The class is extremely well structured, has tons of resources, extra credit, but most importantly, the professor truly cares about each and every one of her students. If you have the chance to take a class with her, you should 100% do it.

Dr. Eman is an awesome person and great at explaining difficult topics. If you attend most classes, complete the extra credit homework and you put in the effort, you'll be fine.  She gives you a TON of resources but once you find what works for you, just stick to it. (But the practice exam with explanations are a lot of help.)

The best professor I've ever had. She gives out: extra credit, participation quizzes, practice questions, multiple practice exams for each unit, cheat sheets, FAQ's, annotated lectures, her YT channel and transcripts, a STUDY SCHEDULE, and keys to go with everything I just mentioned. Hilarious, laid back but caring. Exam grading is clear. TAKE HER.

The definition of her class is literally "you're not cooked, you will cook." If you can take her class, PLEASE DO! Professor Alasadi is absolutely magnificent with great lectures, annotated notes, and exam resources. I wish I had to take OChem so I could have another semester with her. The only way to fail is not to do the bare minimum to pass.

Genuinely the best professor I had at UT. She goes out of her way to provide help with ample resources and explains content well. Exams are like the practice ones. This course is an easier version of normal PChem, so while she's a great professor, I'd probably go with PChem I (CH 353) if it's a pre-req for another class.

My goat #eman i genuinely could not say enough about professor alasadi she not only is sweet and caring but she provides so much amazing resources for exam and understanding content.Additionally she pays well attention to her students that attend class and I have so much respect for her and the way she runs the class would always take her again.

LOVE DR. EMAN!! She is an outstanding professor who makes chem an enjoyable subject. Her youtube vids and other resources are phenomenal and will guarantee to prepare you well for exams. many extra credit opportunities too, my overall grade rounded up 4 whole points!!
If you can take this class, take it. There is no better chem professor at UT Austin. She's amazing, and so kind and caring about her students. Love her and her class!

Very passionate and kind professor. Lots of resources to help you succeed (YouTube videos and practice exams were very helpful). Easy exams with medians in the high As and homework sets graded on completion are the only grades. Great for an easy pchem credit, but I might avoid if you need a stronger pchem foundation for future courses.

Had a 100 in the class with extra credit. She gives so many useful resources. I was so close to accepting my AP Chem credit and taking Ochem, but I am honestly glad I didn't because this class is a really good GPA booster. Pay attention and use the resources she provides. Not only is she an amazing lecturer, but also a super kind professor.

Took her class for both CH 301 and 302. love love love. She is very caring and teaches everything so clearly. Her youtube channel also explains the topics which is a helpful resource if you miss lecture (which I was in the 8am so you can imagine). Would take her class again if she taught ochem next semester, but she's teaching 301 again

One of the BEST profs I've had. Caring, funny, smart. Exams were never unfair, always on what she taught. She inspired me to take Pchem 2. She would give us donuts on exam day, extra credit galore, and optional finals. She made P-chem such a fun class and I genuinely found myself enjoying what I was learning. If she is teaching, TAKE HER!!

If you get the chance to take Professor Eman, consider yourself blessed. She is so passionate about teaching and truly wants every student to succeed. She has an educational YouTube and TikTok account aimed at helping students understand chemistry and biology. Take her!!!!!!

I absolutely loved this class her teaching style is so easy to understand, and her youtube channel is the most helpful. She provides lecture notes which helped feel more comfortable and prepared for lectures. She's full of humor and she actually cares about her students.

She writes the lectures, and they cover everything on the exams. I just took the class early, so I slept through a lot of them. Fun teacher that gives very helpful resources like her own videos and her exam study sessions. Very good extra credit added like 3.5% onto my total grade.

Prof Eman was by-far the best professor I've had this semester (and probably at UT as well). She made P-chem so digestible with all the resources she provided without sacrificing on rigor. I feel that I have actually learned physical chemistry without wanting to die. If only she could teach all my classes

Very good professor. 80% of your grade is dependent on 4 midterms, but that's standard for most UT Austin gen chem 1 & 2. There's no homework, but you have 4-6 quizzes to complete asynchronously (+ unlimited attempts) before tests that make up the remaining 20%. Tests are easy to cram for if you remember AP chem.

Professor. Eman is hands down the best professor you could ever ask for, she is such an angel. She effortlessly made a course deemed challenging so enjoyable. The amount of ORIGINAL resources (Annotated notes, YouTube videos, Recorded lectures, Quizlet flashcards, etc.) provided are beyond me. love her

Professor Eman is easily the best professor I had this semester. She genuinely cares so much about her students and makes great effort to make chem as simple and accessible as it should be. She has such a talent with communicating ideas, the tests are all extremely easy if you just attend lecture and listen. So much study material. She is the GOAT

I dont usually write reviews on here so that just goes to show how great of a professor she is. I used to hate chemistry before her class but she helped me really come to love the subject because her teaching style and the effort she puts into her classes is unmatched. Yall should defo take her best professor ever!

Professor Eman loves her job and her students, and it shows. Her lectures are fun, and she provides so many resources. She has a YouTube channel where she goes over content, and it is all so detailed. Went to her office hours just to chat, and she's so sweet. She wants everyone to succeed; I couldn't recommend anyone better
Prof. Eman is literally the Michael Jordan of teaching chemistry. Hands down the best Professor I've had thus far at UT. If you have the opportunity to take her, TAKE HER!

Professor Eman is one of the best teachers here at UT. She truly cares about each student in her class and makes a difficult subject easy to understand. She also makes youtube videos, practice problems, and flashcard decks. If I could take her for any chemistry related class I would. 100% recommend her.
Hands down the best professor you will ever have. Nothing more needs to be said.

I don't really like Chemistry, so I did not like studying Chemistry at all. However, she encouraged all the students and gave a lot of extra credit opportunities. 100% I would take her class again if I need to learn more about Chemistry. 100%.

Uploads all lectures and so much more (annotated lecture, practice questions, additional learning modules) to the Canvas you could go through the course and only show up for exam days. Lectures are easy to grasp. No quizzes, just exams. Finals are optional if you get the 4 midterms down. Sometimes fell asleep during lecture though (8am)

Love how many resources Professor Eman gives for her students, from online lectures to problem sets to practice exams. She really cares about her students and even tries to learn all of our names. Lectures are very easy to follow thanks to her digital notes. Would recommend to anyone, one of the best chem professors.

Professor Alasadi is a unicorn. I am not a STEM major, but I took this class after taking CH301 many years ago. The resources that she provides are IMMENSELY helpful, and they mirror exactly what will be on the tests, if not harder than the tests. She is also kind, caring, and understanding of her students. If you need any chemistry, take her.

Professor Eman is the GOAT! I mean it, she is so awesome, so caring, and so thoughtful of her students. She wants you to succeed and wants to get to know her students. If you get the chance to take her, please do. She is a blessing and truly wonderful. THANK YOU EMAN!!

Prof Eman's chem class was very easy. She provided a bunch of practice questions for you to study for the exams. And as along as you understand those questions, you'll be fine on the exams. She didn't curve but the questions were all mcq.

CH302, Amazing professor provides so many resources and worksheets that reflect exactly what's on exam. Don't need to attend lecture if you keep up with her videos. Only graded on practice sets which she provides key for and 25 MC test that she gives tons of useful material for. No final unless you want to retake 2 lowest test grades.

I took CH 302. If a student did poorly, it's because they didn't put effort into their studying. We're given all the tools needed to do good in class. She may be the best professor I've ever had. I appreciated her energy through the course, especially during our 8 am lectures. I would hope to have more professors like her as I keep taking courses.

She is such an angel, I have never had such an amazing teacher. She provides many resources over every single question type you can think of, and extra credit is given randomly, but just a simple participation is what gets you it. Nothing hard. I can go on and on about how much I love her, she is the goat.

She has the best possible resources with youtube videos, practice quizzes, anything you need for no matter your learning style. It was her first semester teaching and she was literally the best professor I ever had and I learned so much.

You really couldn't ask for a better professor on a subject deemed "difficult". She is incredibly resourceful and so helpful. Her lectures aren't mandatory but they are the most enjoyable, she explains clearly, always open to questions, and makes you feel heard. The class is exam heavy but there are makeups and sooo many good preparatory resources.

THATS WHY SHE IS THE GOAT, THE GOAT. 
Professor mean is super good she is supper attentive and her class is basically based on exams which are 80% of grade but you get to retake two at the end of the semester. she has YouTube videos explaining everything we see in lass and also she posts a review before every exam. Best professor ever take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eman is AWESOME!! She's easy to reach out to, super funny, and extremely caring to her students. She provides a ton of resources to stay on top of the class, including her very own YouTube channel!?!? It's insane how much work she puts into supporting her class, and she makes chemistry feel so easy. I never had to struggle in her class, 10/10 rec.

CH 301 with Professor Eman was amazing, I really like her teaching style. You can tell she cares for her students and wants them to succeed. She has her own youtube channel where she explain her lectured throughly again (not just a recorded lecture). You can tell she really passionate about teaching!

Lemme tell you, absolutely goated. She is extremely professional, patient, and respectful. Lectures are a bit slow, but it really helps if you need the material at a slower pace. (All of the TAs are helpful) I'll be biased here, but I have taken other chemistry professors, and Professor Eman has made it by far the easiest to understand.

Professor Alasadi is truly a blessing. Her lectures were always very thorough and thoughtful. She has a YouTube channel with amazing videos to help with test reviews and complicated topics. She also gave multiple opportunities for extra credit and wanted everyone in the class to succeed. If you get the chance to have Professor Alasadi TAKE IT!!

prof eman is so kind, and she teaches extremely well! i had her for chem 1, and lots of kids in my class including myself emailed the hiring department asking them to hire her to teach chem 2. she dumbs down complicated topics, and you know exactly what to expect on her exams if you just do her reviews and watch her videos!

I said no textbook, but she offers links to resources online, she has a YT channel, her lectures are relevant and soo helpful, and she makes notes to help you know what to study for tests. She's amazing for chem!! Communicate with her and she is very understanding. Make sure to do practice questions she offers, show up, and you'll be set!!!

If you read any reviews, read this one. Professor Eman was easily one of the best professors I've had at UT. I dropped Chem 301 first semester of freshmen year because I could not learn with either Caudill, the older guy or Viviani. I enrolled in Eman's class and passed with an A+. She offers so much extra credit and makes her own yt videos!! GOAT!

im a senior that retook it for a better grade, and she's like SO much better than the other gen chem profs at UT (idk why she taught in the off semester...). she dumbs chemistry down for you from the START, which is pretty rare for any PHD level/highly qualified prof. Her TA's were all rlly nice and taught j like her (s/o abdullah). take her trust

Even though she was new, she went ABOVE AND BEYOND to help her students. She reads EVERY SINGLE student's feedback and take it into account for the next topic of CH301 (extra practice problems, exam review class time, extra credit, etc.) She teaches well and is really funny too!! Would love it if she taught CH302 next year

I LOVE Eman. I hated CH301 last semester (I had to end up doing course switch) but I loved chem. Class is mostly based on exam grades but possible by attending lectures and doing all the practice problems (ample posted and all very representative of what is on test). Eman is a great lecturer and explains big concepts in an understanding way.

The. Best. Professor. Ever. 

Her lectures were not boring at all considering it was at 8 am. If you can PLEASE TAKE HER. I need her to teach Ch302 and o-chem because that's just how good she was. She cares about her students and has many resources and a YT channel that thoroughly explains everything.

If you have the availability in your schedule, PLEASE TAKE HER. I hate chemistry, and I dreaded taking it this semester, but Professor Eman was so amazing and super sweet. She had YouTube videos, study guides, and multiple review sessions available to us to help with the exams. Just study and use the materials provided, and you'll be fine.

SHES GOATED! She is such an amazing professor and lecturer! She is so easy to talk to and will never make you feel dumb. She has a YouTube channel called “Professor Eman” and you can just see there how great she is. She truly provides you with all the resources you need to succeed. TAKE HER!!!

TAKE HER! She a new professor at UT but she explains content thoroughly and cares ab her students. I took her ch 301 class n never got bored. Because shes young, shes relatable and funny. 4 exams worth 80% but u can retake at end of sem and a "5th exam" that's just 200 participation points you get from in-class aissgnments or learning modules.

Her teaching style isn't effective for most students. She confusingly explains concepts. She goes off topic frequently, spending a lot of time talking about her personal life instead of focusing on chemistry. She goes through slides without providing clear explanations or taking meaningful notes. Because of this, I had to teach myself the material.

I don't recommend Professor Caudill; she frequently goes off topic, goes on random tangents about her week, taking up time out of class instead of lecturing, forcing her to rush content at the end. Very unorganized, indirectly passive-aggressive, and overcomplicates the material. She stops class when she hears people whispering. Quiz every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Caudill's class does not feel super organized. Her lectures are generally very scattered. Her lectures do not dive very deep into the content and focus more on teaching specific question types for the exam. The class focuses more on passing the test than actually learning chemistry.

Her teaching style could be better, but all the resources you need to do well are available on Canvas. There's a decent amount of extra credit, but there's also a lot of homework. There's a quiz every class though. Overall lot of stuff to pad your grade, and prof is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures add very little to what you learn in learning modules, really just focus on the provided modules and question types and you will do fine.
Her lectures are completely pointless and serve no benefit. She also gets extremely upset when people leave even when classes are subsequent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not important to doing well in the class. Often times she does not add much info from what is on her slides. She is really great at helping one on one in office hours and you should definitely take advantage of that if you are struggling in the class

Don't like the way she talks, lectures are her straight up reading the slides, is always complaining about someone whispering but no one is whispering?? She doesn't teach at all so your basically teaching yourself. When she asked the class on their opinion about something, she completely disregarded it and ended up doing her own thing.

Professor Caudill is the most unlikeable chemistry professor. Her voice tells you she doesn't want to be there. I found the lectures to be disengaging and hard to follow. The exam proctoring and academic integrity process was handled unfairly in my case, but the dean cleared me. She does NOT want the best for you. Do NOT take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took her for CH301 and got an A in that. She is very caring and tries, but the actual lecture is a waste of time. You have to self-study for her exams. The class is test-heavy, with 4 midterms at 20%, you can replace two. The in-class quizzes for 302 were harder. I would say to avoid this professor if you care about learning from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is generous with quiz drops and extra credit, and she practically gives you the exam questions ahead of time with "question types" which are also what the daily quizzes are based upon. Many students leave the lecture after the quiz because she doesn't have enough additional information in lecture compared to online learning resources.
