He offered extra credit
Just don't. Trust me.

He was a good professor in the beginning but he started using handouts for notes which did not help me learn the info. Weekly hw quizzes with an exact hw problem and 3 exams that were textbook problems. Wish he was more accessible outside of class but he gave a lot of extra credit opportunities and curved an exam. Go to class bc no notes posted.

Fey is a very poor instructor with little regard for his students' learning. He somehow managed to take an interesting subject and make it feel like a punishment. Grading is brutal and communication is nonexistent.

reviews.comment: if you see fey for dynamics take it next semester

Weekly quizzes on one of the HW problems for that week. To study for the test its best to do textbook problems near and around those that were on the HW.
Having graduated, I can confidently say this is the worst class and professor in the entire ME department. Truly horrible in every respect.

Midterm is extremely difficult and homework can be a bit challenging, but if you are interested in the class I wouldn't let that scare you. The rest of the class is graded extremely fairly and there is an opportunity for extra credit.

He was a decent professor. Lectures were okay but followed the textbook, which was much more of a resource than the professor. Fairly reasonable exams, with decent partial credit. Would recommend over some other profs for Dynamics.

Dr. Fey was a decent professor. The lectures were kind of hard to follow and tbh I didn't really pay attention to any of them, but he clearly is interested in the material and the assignments themselves are informative and graded easily. The midterm is hard but he allows for corrections, and the final project is fun and graded easily.

He seems to care for his students during class time, but his office hours pretty much don't exist and he is difficult to get ahold of during email. The TA's also don't really know what's going on, so it can be difficult to seek help when you don't understand something from help. His exams are similar to the content taught in class though.

Not my favorite class (though I would've preferred to take it in person), but Dr. Fey was accessible and clearly cared about his students as well as the material. I'm taking another class with him this semester and am excited to do so!

reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is super sweet and was my favorite professor! She made class interesting and collaborative! As someone who always struggled with writing and English she was always willing to help and genuinely cares about everyone! I would 100% take her class again!

Such a great professor! She was so kind and caring. She really knows what she is talking about and loves to help her students. She made this class way more interesting and enjoyable because of how flexible and helpful she was!

Lover her! She was easy with grading and there was only 4 projects, which she gave us lots of time to work on. Every day assignments were easy and she was the sweetest professor ever. Very understanding and there to help you out!
Great Professor, one of the best at UT. I would definitely take her class again, her lectures were fun and the homework was very straightforward.

One of the best professors at UT. She would make it fun with group projects and the whole class would just be having a good time. She cares for her students and makes time to do one-on-ones. Instructions were always clear, she would always give us example papers of what to do and not to do so we could do better. You will NOT be disappointed.

She is an amazing teacher, very caring, accessible, and she does her very best to make sure everyone gets the help they need. She does have a lot of writing/project assignments but she will help you do your very best to achieve the grade you want or at least close to it.
She was such a great professor! All of her assignments were clearly laid out and easy to follow. If anything was ever tricky she would go above and beyond to help.

Amazing professor. Was honored to be one of her first students here at UT. Easy and fun lectures with class discussions that make class like a family meeting. 4 major papers but her lectures and her assistance,it makes it super easy. Light HW. I love this professor to death. If you want to make english fun (which is rare) take this professor. TRUST
Dont take this class.

This class sucks don't take it the midterm averages are in the 40s. Frank cant lecture or answer questions at all. If you took AP stats you will have a slight leg up at the start but still I would take another prof.

PLEASE AVOID IF YOU CAN. RUN.  Frank Yan is first off EXTREMELY hard to understand (not sure if he has linguistic issues). Mangolini should teach all core classes in the MSE graduate program. Nothing else to add.

The MSE graduate program is ridiculous. There are profs who do not want to teach and do not know the subject and then there is Mangolini. A lot of work, but at least I learnt something! Great instructor. Truly passionate about the material and teaching. He cares about the students' success. 1-to-1 is impressive: young guy, but super sharp!

Dr. Mangolini has perfected his craft. Canvas, HWs, lectures, and exams are all carefully curated and he is extremely organized. He's also super caring. Make sure to attend lectures and actually listen, because he's always dropping valuable information. Exams weren't too bad and relied heavily on info from daily canvas quizzes and handouts. 10/10.

Geez, this Material Science course can be a GPA killer! The concepts are complex to understand, and the lecturer always made us feel confused about those topics. The exam preparation is soooo time-consuming and wastes a chunk of students' free time. Overall, not recommended; avoid this course if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: GOAT! No other comments necessary!

Fantastic instructor. He should teach other core classes so that students could learn something! This is the only core class in which you learn something. PhD students do not appreciate that! They complain about being challenged. Mangolini should be rewarded to make us learn how to critically think!

This is a conceptually heavy class, but Mangolini breaks the concept down in an impressively easy way. He knows the subject matter in such a depth! The negative comments on his ME/MSE386 come from students who do not want to spend time on coursework. Mangolini deserves recognition for his efforts on teaching! He deeply cares about the students.

Two midterms and the final exam take up way too much of the course grades. Dude, there are no extra credits and the credits U can earn that easily. Take his homework seriously; the final is a hard version of the homework.  Overall, this course is challenging and can be a significant GPA drain.

Dr. Mangolini is a brilliant, humble professor who genuinely cares for students and sparks curiosity in materials engineering. Though outside my geoscience major, his engaging teaching made me wish I'd chosen his field.

In my opinion, he was the only professor in the UT materials graduate curriculum whose class offered the appropriate amount of theory and rigor. He's a bit serious, and a little impersonal. But at the end of the day he is willing to put in the largely unrewarded work of making his class difficult enough that the students actually learn something.

Lectures are rigorous, and this course is overall time-consuming. You have to put a lot of time into it to get an A or A-. Every person in TMI and the material science track of ME needs to take it. Don't mess up with any exams, or your grade will drop a lot. This professor needs to explain those complex concepts in more detail.

reviews.comment: This Italian man is a harsh grader and places a lot of stress on students. He is not a suitable professor for teaching this course since he can't explain the concepts well enough. reviews.comment: Great professor that cares about his students

Absolutely phenomenal prof that is super caring and accomodating. He clearly cares about our success and wants us to do well on his exams. His lectures and PPT slides are great. Exams aren't the easiest but they're fair. He is the best professor at UT for materials and its not even close. He got us cookies multiple times throughout the semester.

Dr. Mangolini is my favorite professor at UT, literally no competition. He is a genuine, goofy character who really wants his students to succeed. I found the class to be pretty easy (but I like materials). Generally, 1 HW a week, 1 quiz every 2 weeks, 3 tests and a final all worth 20% each. Reading the textbook is helpful + participate in class!!
Dr Mangolini was a great professor. He's not only super knowledgable but extremely clear and easy to understand. He's absolutely been the best professor I have had at Cockrell so far.
Very good professor
My favorite engineering professor at UT to date. Taught Materials to me a couple semesters ago. Excellent dude who structures his class very well and makes it easy to learn. F1 Ferrari fan.

Dr. Mangolini is easily the best professor I have had at UT. He gives detailed lectures, is a fair grader, and is compassionate about helping his students. Although the class isnt easy, he sets a clear criteria of what you need to know for the test by making detailed study guides. He is also very easy to talk to outside of class. Great teacher.
Dr. Valdez is a very knowledgable person. He explained concepts in a very simple way. Some topics were very interesting and he occasionally brought artifacts to class, so that was interesting.

Loveeee him and his class. Professor Valdez is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he's doing. Great lectures and def worth attending. Exams are simple as long as you pay attention in class/read the textbook. Def take it if you can!

His classes are pretty easy. You don't even have to attend, just read the textbook. Be sure to attend the labs, though. He's a very nice man and tells interesting stories in lectures that allow you to form real-world connections.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture isn't mandatory, only the labs are. No make up labs or exams, but the lowest exam was dropped. There are a total of 5 exams online that can be taken at home and one required book, but overall not too much reading.

i took this class as my last science credit needed, but missing a few didn't change my experience too much. again, lecture isn't mandatory, but labs are! the labs are very easy and TA dependent. exams are online and can be taken at home. allows for extra points if you talk to him in office hours. didn't "need" the book, so i just used lecture notes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love Valdez. Graded mainly through lab assignments and exams. Exams are easy, take notes on the textbook, and you'll be fine. Lectures are optional, but very interesting! Lab attendance is required, but the TA will give you everything. Valdez is a very knowledgeable guy who's an expert in his field. Go to his office hours and get to know him.

my favorite class this sem! lectures are enjoyable -- go to them! labs are very doable as long as you actually put effort into them and the prelab stuff. exams are simple -- no trick questions + can pull up notes if needed. you can email him and explain your answer for pts back on exams. Incredibly nice and funny guy. I will miss his class!!
go to lab!! lab is the only participation that really matters, but it matters a lot!! prof is very nice and passionate about what he does.

This class is pretty straightforward. There are 5 tests worth 80% of your grade but the lowest is dropped so if you do well enough on the first 4 you don't have to take the last one. They're open note, not cumulative, and online so not too bad. Lectures are optional but labs are mandatory so make sure you pick a good lab time.

easy easy class! valdez left half way through the semester, but the time he was in class was so enjoyable. he is so passionate about the topics and is very understanding with grading (just go to office hours!!) would recommend to anyone!!
Easiest science credit I've ever taken. Grade is comprised of 5 tests (lowest test grade dropped) and weekly labs. Labs are harder than lecture content though.

Professor Valdez was great! If you can take this class with friends I highly recommend it. He was easygoing and was nice to talk to. I would definitely recommend taking this class, especially if you need to kill to birds with one stone and get a science credit and a language culture credit.

TAKE IT! So easy and straight foward. Everything he lectures about is in his textbook. You can not go to lecture and still get all the same info from reading the textbook for the online tests (that you take at home or in library). Super easy and he loves what he teaches and is super straight foward with what information you need to know.

Prof Valdez is super chill and gives solid lectures. Labs are mandatory and they suck, especially if you don't have a great TA, but they're not horrible. Only graded on tests (that are super easy if you take notes) and lab assignments. If you take notes in lecture you don't need to read the textbook, I never did and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class only had weekly labs and exams. I liked the lectures and the exams were super easy but the labs were downright dreadful. Liked the professor though and the class was super interesting!

Labs are necessary, if you miss 3 you automatically fail the course. The exams are elementary and there are a lot of Quizlets for them. If you choose not to buy the textbook, which Valdez wrote, you need to go to lectures.

It's possible to get an A without buying the textbook, but you'll have to attend his lectures to learn the material instead. Overall a great guy, easy to reach out to outside of class. The labs can be tedious, but they're worth a very small percentage of your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is easy to get an A in. There are exams that are open note and you can take them from your bed; he drops the lowest score. Lectures and exams are almost verbatim to textbook.The topic itself is interesting and this is an easy A class, if you at all find archaeology interesting. The TAs on the other hand? They're a whole 'nother story.

Lectures were somewhat interesting. Professor Valdez reads straight from his textbook so either attending the lectures or buying the textbook will be enough to get an A on the tests. Labs are sometimes difficult but the TA was really nice and helpful. Take this class if you want an easy A.

Fred is awesome! This is a great class for human behaviors credit and global cultures/cultural diversity flag! Attendance is not mandatory; however, sometimes, he gives some of the questions that will be on the exam within the class. 

Make sure to READ THE TEXTBOOK, it is very brief and clear on what you should know for exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Valdez was great. Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but if you want to have an easy time on the exams, attend them. The most difficult thing about this class was the labs. The homework was ambiguous which made it difficult. Grading took forever and the exams were often graded wrong so make sure you double-check them after they are graded!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Valdez is a great lecturer, AND his lectures are not attendance mandatory. Beware labs are worth half of your grade and attendance is mandatory for them. They can either be great or horrible depending on your TA, but the other half of the grade is tests, and he essentially gives test answers in lecture, go to class and lab, take notes= easy A
Dr. Valdez is awesome however, the labs are worth a good portion of your grade and getting a good TA really matters.

Professor Valdez is an incredible professor and human being. He has great lectures (they are not mandatory) and gives answers to the test in class. The only downside to the class is the mandatory attendance for the labs but they are usually very straight forward. If you miss questions on the test you can go to his office hours to get points back.

If you want to learn nothing and get the world's easiest A, take this class. Don't get into a habit of taking classes like this that teach 0 and hand out A's to everyone. They're a waste of your money and time.

Favorite man on planet Earth. Took two classes with him and will be going on his field school to Belize this summer for Mayan archaeology. Would trust him with my life, social security number, and firstborn. Funny, experienced, and a genuinely good person. If you do one thing at UT, it should be taking a class with him!

Attendance for lecture is not required but he will give hints about whats on the test during his lectures. Lab attendance is required, but the labs are fairly easy and super fun. Dr. Valdez is, maybe, the best professor at UT, and I would take his class again in a heartbeat.
If you need a non-science credit class, take this class very interesting on the lettuces. The labs are mandatory so do not miss those and you should be find.

This was the best and easiest science credit I could ever ask for. Professor Valdez is a great lecturer, and if you show up to class and the lab, you will get an A+. This class was interesting and he is a great lecturer. Take him if you need a science credit

If you are looking for a science credit, choose this one! tests are no longer online, but easy and most of the questions are straight from textbook and the TA's make study guides. Labs can be hard, but are only 20% of your grade, and finding a buddy helps! If you miss points, he lets you get points back. lectures are interesting and he is so sweet!

Attendance at lectures is not mandatory but recommended. You can get good grades on tests without going to class by reading the textbook, but he is more accommodating to those who wish to challenge their grade/get points back if you come to class. The grading is very test-heavy but go to all the labs to balance it out.
Dr. Valdez is so sweet! Lectures aren't mandatory, and most of the information on the exams are from his textbook. The lab for this class is also super easy.

I never went to class besides the first day and when he gave tests back- He even barely came. All questions on the tests are from the book, except for a few, but he'll give you points back on what you miss. TALK TO HIM AFTER GETTING TESTS BACK, he's given me full credit back on every one. You can find some test questions on quizlet. 10/10 class
Class doesn't teach much outside of the labs. Just memorize the short review sheet and the exams are really easy. Take Valdez if you want the free Science A but you won't learn much.

Interesting, straightforward lectures that are not mandatory but I highly suggest attending as he gives many answers for exam questions in class. Exams are easy as long as you put in a little effort to knowing the concepts! Labs are occasionally more difficult, but the TAs are very helpful. This class is a great choice if you need a science credit!

Prof. Valdez is a straightforward and intelligent lecturer. His tests are no longer open-book though, so you will need to attend lectures and read the textbook chapters to pass. I'd say the only challenging aspect of the class is that tests are worth 80% and labs 20%. As long as you prepare well for the tests and don't miss labs, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Valdez is a great lecturer. His lectures are nearly identical to chapters in the textbook for ANT304, so if you ever miss class you can always go back and read. There are 5 tests in total, but they are not difficult if you read the chapters or make quizlets. I would highly recommend taking his class.

Professor Valdez taught a straightfoward & interesting class. TA's were accessable and actually wanted to help you. Tests were closed book, but as long as you read the chapters of the free textbook and looked at the study guide, you'll be sure to pass. Labs were engaging and fun. Would recommended for non-stem majors who need a science core.

No longer allowing open-note for tests anymore. Lectures are not mandatory; without them, you will not pass the second or third exams. The class consists of 5 Tests that are 80% and semester-long labs that count for 20%. Do not recommend taking this class if looking for an Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Whole class is changed; in person on paper tests. Tests are very broad and questions are usually unclear. Most information is found in textbook but tests often have questions that are nothing related to topic. Very smart and nice guy but this class is not an easy A anymore.

I love Dr. Valdez so much. Studied with him on his field school in Belize and highly recommend if you want to learn more about Mayan Archaeology. He has the best grad students too! Also took his intro the archaeology and adored him. One of the funniest professors I have met and is super passionate about what he does and loves to share it!
Professor Valdez ANT 304 is a must take for a science credit and/or a GC flag. Attendance is not mandatory and the test are very straightforward. This is an easy and enjoyable A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class if you need a science credit!! I only showed up to one lecture all year and got a 100. He's a funny professor who knows his subject material really well. The only downside is labs are mandatory, but they are only 45 mins once a week and they are basically guaranteed 100s. Trust me, take this class.

This is the easiest class I have taken at UT. Prof is amazing and gives extra credit if you just show up. The tests are online and not proctored, most of the test answers are in the textbook, or he gives the test answers in the lecture. Attendance is optional but he gives extra credit if you go, plus he gives test answers during the lecture.

The class is INCREDIBLY easy and hard to fail. 80% tests and 20% labs, but missing 3+ labs without an excuse will cause you to automatically fail. Do not skip labs! There are 5 tests, but he drops the lowest one. Every test is open note, open resource, open people. Easy labs, easy work. Just pay attention in lecture/get the book. Take this class!

A must-take if you are looking for credit. Super easy class and Professor Valdez is absolutely amazing. The grade is based off tests and labs only. Attendance is only mandatory for labs, not class. Only negative is that there is no visual aid for the lectures. However, if you have the textbook, the lectures correspond directly to the text.

Professor Valdez's ANT 304 was an super easy class. Grade consists of tests, which are open-note, and labs, which are easy to complete when you attend the lab sessions. Professor also seems like a chill person who loves what he teaches. Would recommend taking this class for credit.
Easiest class I have ever taken. Only attendance mandatory is the labs and they are extremely easy. The tests are very straightforward and all online. Free A+ for anyone who needs a science credit.

- Class is not mandatory, you can even technically skip all the lectures and still ace the exams if you read his self-written textbook (basically the class notes) - what i did

- If you attend class, he's hilarious and has many stories, highly recommend (if you can wake up in time for his class

- Take for an easy science credit!

- Great person:)

Professor Valdez is the best! No lecture attendance required (but I always went because he was so sweet), MCQ tests that are pretty much straight from lecture/the textbook that he wrote, and you can petition if you miss any test questions. Just go to labs and you'll be good! 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Valdez is a super caring guy, and his material is genuinely interesting. He doesn't do slides or homework, so take really good notes and read the textbook. His TAs are also cool as well, they all want you to do well and enjoy the content

Easiest class of my entire life tbh. Prof Valdez is the literal GOAT. Makes it EXTREMELY easy to get an A. If you can take him, TAKE HIM. 5 multiple choice tests (drops lowest so really 4) that are extremely easy, and some random labs. Just get his textbook and everything u need for the whole class is there. He wants u to get an A.

Because of COVID, the class was structured so that labs and some lectures were online, although lectures were also given in-class. As long as you listen to the lectures or go to class, you'll be fine! Making an A is really really easy and the lectures are interesting. There's a textbook that's required but the readings are interesting too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy science credit, tests are all online, but lectures are super boring.

There were a total of 5 exams (last one is exemptible if you are satisfied with your grade). Around 6 labs too, which were easy to do. Lectures with him in person were pretty funny. Exams are straight to the point and OPEN NOTE. They are m/c and t/f. Totally recommend Valdez! He was super nice and funny! Do your work and you'll easily pass!!

This class is basically a guaranteed A. Tests are online and open everything. Questions are straight from the book, literally copy and paste. You could attend 0 classes and end the semester with 100%. Definitely take this class to knock out a science or business requirement.

I loved this course! Dr. Valdez was great, lectures were straight to the point and interesting. Valdez really prepares students well for the exam. If you go to the lecture and take notes you'll pass! Take this course, it's really interesting and enjoyable. I learned a lot and it wasn't difficult at all.

Prof. Valdez genuinely wants students to succeed! Just do the labs, pay attention to the lectures, and take good notes, and you'll likely get an A. I def recommend joining his office hours even if you're minimally interested in archeology. He has a good sense of humor and a lot of great knowledge to share!

Dr. Valdez was an amazing professor. His lectures were always really interesting! Plus he's funny! You need to go to lectures and take good notes because that is basically all that is on the test. If you take good notes you will definitely do good on the exams. He also really cares about helping his students do better, he wants you to get an A!

Honestly if you put a good amount of effort into this class you will get an A. Prof. Valdez is a really good lecturer, and seems like he cares a lot about his students. This class was super straightforward, I actually learned some interesting things despite it being asynchronous. Great class, I wish I could've had it in person.

GREAT PROF! Makes it SO clear from the beginning what is expected. 6 easy "Labs" and he posts the answer keys. Tests are available to take in a pretermined time frame and you can use notes. All you need to do is listen to the lectures, write down the terms on the word doc he gives you, and you're good. Also, Fred is so nice and pleasant. recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class to take as a science credit! The labs are posted with the key, and are 20%. 5 tests make up 80%, but you are exempt from the 5th if satisfied with your grade. You have to purchase the textbook, but the exam has a lot of questions that are verbatim from it. The online (asynchronous) format allowed for CTRL+F, so that was a blessing!

Tests are straight off of the lectures and are worth 80% of your final grade. The other 20% are simple labs that take around 30 min every week. If you need any help, do not be afraid to send Prof Valdez any question, he answers almost immediately and is always happy to help. Just wish I could've met him in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: professor valdez was great! i really wish i had him in person, but he made class extremely easy. definitely recommend!! you need the textbook, but overall, probably one of the easiest and most interesting classes ive taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Valdez in ANT 304 was great. Definitely recommend this course to fill one of your science credits. Textbook is necessary because a few of the test questions (open note) come from it and it has answers to some of the labs. Lectures were straight forward and easy to understand!

There are about 5 exams (one optional if your grade is good enough to skip it) and a few (REALLY easy) labs. The exams rely on the textbook and lectures but if you just read and understand them, then the exams are super easy. If you don't do well, he drops the lowest exam anyway. This class is super easy and not that time-consuming.

Love this guy. He uses emojis in emails. Very down to earth and caring. His materials aren't hard at all, stress-free, and final is optional. If you think you should get partial credit on a question just email him and explain your thoughts, he gives points back very easily. I wish all profs are like him.

If you are going to take ANT304 take it with Dr. Valdez! The class was made up of four exams, which were really simple if you just attend lectures and read the specific textbook pages he mentions. I've heard this is the best ANT304 class, I did not need to prioritize it too much but I still learned a lot and really liked my professor and TA.

Truly an excellent professor that is knowledgeable about the subject he teaches. However, this is an easy A class and it is treated as such by Valdez and the TAs. I would caution against taking this class if you are passionate about the subject and want to study it in-depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Valdez is literally the easiest professor at UT. Never have I taken such a chill class. I never showed up to class and just got the lecture notes from someone else. Ended with a solid A. Take his class if you need a science & tech or behavioral science credit!!!

Y'all. Dr. Valdez is seriously the nicest professor ever and he truly cares about your success. He helps you in office hours and even lets you fight for credit on test back if you simply just talk to him! TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grade based off 5 tests with one drop test. The A requirement was a 91.01, so it wasnt too hard to get the A. Tests were fairly easy and based from the lectures. Valdez is also a good lecturer and makes all content clear. Labs were also participation so you just had to show up and do whatever the TA has planned.

Dr. Valdez is an exceptional prof. 5 easy tests with the lowest scored exam dropped (he also lets you argue points on each exam). Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but it is for discussion sections which are very easy but very boring. He was a very interesting prof. and gives engaging lectures. Would highly recommend!

Fred Valdez is an understanding and outstanding professor. One exam gets drop and the exams themselves are easy and rely heavily from the lectures. Lectures are optional but that's basically the class. Labs were easy, we watched movies for this semester but the TA would get upset if you feel asleep. I learned a lot and the grading was fair.
There are 5 exams and you can drop one of them. The exams are from the material Professor Valdez talked in class. Definitely recommend to take his class.

Valdez was one of my first professors at UT. He made his class pretty interesting despite the incredibly boring subject. The class is based off 5 exams with the lowest one dropped. This is a great class for a science credit and GPA booster, definitely recommend it. He also lets you argue for points when you get your multiple choice exams back.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's important to take good notes during lecture because he will definitely highlight things he wants you to know for the tests. He also lets you argue for points back after you get tests back if you can give a plausible reason based on what he taught or the textbook. Labs are purely attendance based. A very manageable amount of reading is assigned
Super cool guy! Professor Valdez is super intelligent and all he cares about is that his students pass with a good grade. I totally recommend :)

Valdez does a great job of teaching the course, and he respects your time. There are 5 tests in the year, out of which he takes the highest 4 for your grade. No homework, no midterm, no final. Show up and take good lecture notes and you won't have to read (if he doesn't say something in lecture, he'll give points back on tests). Excellent prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Seriously the chillest teacher at UT. Easy A for ANT 304. Hes a good ole boy and lectures are interesting too
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof Valdez is respected in the Anthro department. He usually does lectures without powerpoint slides, which I felt could have aided with the presentation of the material. His lower division archaeology class doesn't involve much class participation, but if you need it for a requirement, it is a solid choice. He is very receptive in office hours.

I absolutely loved this course! I took it as part of my major requirements, as I am an anthropology major. Professor Valdez has a great sense of humor, and he is very educated on the subject matter at hand. He was also great at explaining the content of the course, so it was not hard to understand even if you had no background in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Easiest class. There are four test and an optional fifth. All you need to do is show up to class and he gives out questions. Is also funny in a sarcastic sort of way.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Valdez is awesome. Easy class and interesting material. He has a great sense of humor during lectures. Tests are based almost completely on lectures so you just have to write down essentially everything he says in lecture and you'll be fine. He goes slowly so it's not hard at all. Readings helped a bit. Would recommend this class!

One of the most straightforward courses I've taken at UT. Dr Valdez is pretty chill, and literally mentions what is going to appear on the tests. Takes notes during class, most of what appears on the tests is said during lectures. No trick questions on the tests, and overall an easy A if you put in a little effort.

Dr. Valdez is a great professor, I took this course to get rid of a requirement for my degree but I've enjoyed it so much. Learning about the Maya is so great and fascinating! He is a great lecturer, shows a lot of films, and his tests are very doable& fair. He's available to you if you need any help! Just pay attention to his lecture and read! :)

Great professor, lectures are good and useful. He even lets you out ten minutes early on most days. The test themselves aren't difficult if you really study: take GOOD notes and attend the discussion sections. Discussion sections r usually just videos and documentaries but content in the videos WILL be on the tests. Reading the textbook also useful

He is great! Easy A if you pay attention in class! 5 exams (drop the lowest one) is 90% and lab is 10% (you will get full credit for lab if you attend lab every time). If your average grade is above A after the 4th exam, you will directly get an A and don't need to come to class to take the final. He is very nice and passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There are 5 tests, you can drop 1, and the rest are equal to 90% of your grade. The rest of the grade is for showing up to labs. Lectures can be dry but so are bones and archaeology in general so.  He has been teaching for a long time and is very respected. Textbook use seems intimidating at first but he always consolidates the original assignments

If you want an easy A, you've come to the right place. Your entire grade comes from 5 tests, of which the lowest is dropped, and showing up to labs every week. His lectures are straightforward, he plays no tricks on test questions, and he even gives out 4-5 test questions during lectures. Dr. Valdez himself is great, and his class is enjoyable.

I'm not an Anthropology major and I took this for my science credit, but I really enjoyed his lectures and learned a lot in his class! Fred is extremely generous about his test grading, so you won't have to worry about failing the class or anything. It was really easy to get an A so take him!

I was a fool and took this at 8 a.m. and kept missing class. Make sure you don't skip any classes or else you will not make a good grade. I wouldn't even suggest buying the book, I never really used it. Tests are based on lectures and he'll even tell you during a lecture what might be a question on the test. Very easy class and very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a chill professor. The class is extremely easy. 4 tests. All are basically based on his lectures so DO NOT SKIP his class. I haven't touched the book also you can find summaries of the subsections from the chapters online. If you need a science credit, take ANT 304 with him!

Professor Valdez has a unique style of dry humor about him. When it comes to his tests, he will give you the pages to pay close attention to and also makes sure you know if something will be on the test by expressly stating it as such. He isn't very animated with his movements so it can seem a bit boring. But if you pay attention, you'll have fun.
Lectures get kind of boring if you're sleepy but aside from that, very charismatic teacher. He is very clear in what is on the test and that's not something you come by often.

I've had Fred for 2 classes at my time at UT and they have been the highest grades i've made here. Lectures are extremely straight forward, the books over-lap but are important. His tests are SO EASY! It's an easy A if you take good notes and do the readings. He's also the nicest person ever, really knows his stuff.

Valdez is witty, interesting, and gives great anecdotes! He is very clear about what is on the test and will repeat things that will show up on them. So just go and listen to class. 5 test and you can drop one, & no daily work. He makes the class fun and interesting, so take it.

Dr. Valdez is funny, witty, and overall amazing. His classes are so interesting, and the tests are super easy as long as you go to class. The stories he tells about his experience as an archaeologist are awesome. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Dr. Valdez rewards attendance to his class by very clearly outlining what will be on the test. Very relaxed class that often got out early. Definitely an easy A for a science class and learned interesting revelations and applications about anthropology though it never interested me before. Pretty cool guy
Not an easy A, that's for sure. I studied hours to make As on his tests. If you're taking this class just for a science credit, think again.
Took his field study course in belize, I'm from umass but I just had to say how much of a great guy he is! So helpful and witty. Seconds!

I actually took two of his courses this year, one lower and one upper level. He's a great professor. The class itself is what you make it. Tests come mostly from lectures and you can contest a wrong answer.

I honestly can not understand why this class got so many great reviews. Dr. Valdez himself seems like an okay guy, but I really felt like he was dumbing everything down. His lecture notes were unclear and seemed irrelevant. I do not believe his class is an "Easy A," so if that is your only incentive for taking this class, you need not bother.
Professor is very interesting. He relates terms to the real world and doesn't want to babysit the class into paying attention. You get what you make out of the class.
sooo boring...I wanted to fall asleep almost every day.

Class was pretty easy, most of his test questions come from his lecture notes however quite a few can also come from the book.  Can be pretty boring at times and tests take forever to get back to you.  Overall, if you're looking for an easy A, take this class.
great professor, easy easy easy
Impossible not to make an A in his classes-he tells you what you exactly what you need to know. Also gives incredibly simple extra credit on exams. Take ANY of his classes! He's just amazingly easy.
No Comments

Reviewing for BCMS. First semester is a lot of work, but he is flexible with due dates so it's manageable. Heavy emphasis on conversation, and by end of first year you will be speaking Croatian. He's responsive and available outside class time for support if you are proactive in communicating.

I cannot speak to the experience of Frane's Russian class (it didn't give me another option on here but I'm taking is BCMS classes). The first year was also a huge volume of work, but by the end of the year we basically spoke BCMS- he was incredibly flexible with deadlines and understanding of how much work he assigned was actually possible.

(Spring 2025, Online course) He is great as a person, but the workload is heavy. Daily modules and it's recommended by him you study 4-6 hours per module...Theres 2 speaking tests and 9 “major” tests that are formatted like the modules/assignments. I'm not going to lie it's a big decision to take this class. Unless you're passionate, be prepared.

Loved Frane as a person, but not a professor. Not only does he expect an insane amount of work out of you considering it is a 4 credit hour course, but ontop of that TA grades extremely harshly and acts as if we already speak the language when this is a first year introductory language course.

I was doing 5 to 6 hours a week for his course. Most of the time, things were poorly explained and I felt poorly supported. I have hope that the rest of the Russian department at UT is better, but for now, I do not recommend online Russian 1 with this professor unless you want to be up late every night teaching yourself Russian.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Despite this being a 3 hour evening class, it was my favorite this semester! Dr. Fourmy fostered amazing discussions every week over our assigned sources. She is also very real and FUNNY! For such a heavy class she was the perfect professor. 10's across the board. The actual course was reading heavy and your grade depends heavily on participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My worst subject is history. I don't like it, I was never too good at it. This class is heavy, but Dr. Signe is one of the best professors I have ever had. I learned thing I would have never known from this class. She is funny, honest, informational and REAL. Take this class and fight for it to stay!

This class was great! Interesting lectures made a 9 AM history class bearable. Lots of extra credit. In class essay quizzes weren't bad if you prepared. Go to office hours! She'll help you with anything.

This class was difficult, but rewarding. Most of your grade is made up of in-class, hand written essays. Most people do poorly on the first one, but there is time for improvement. Go to office hours because she will give you hints about which sources will be on the quiz. There will be a lot of extra credit, definitely do all of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This women's history course was rly interesting w/ lots of unknown topics covered! You can earn up to 26 points of extra credit that you can apply to your low essay grades. There is reading (~30 pages) for every class (MWF), but you can still earn an A if you skip the reading one day bc the class is very Socratic seminar-heavy. Fourmy is funny too!

Half your grade is based on 4 essays you write in class for 50 minutes, and only TAs grade that so hope you get an easy one. Good thing is Fourmy hints at which sources you will choose to write about on the quizes. If you took APUSH and did well on that in high school then this class would be easy for you. Also weekly quizes are open note thank god
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fourmy is a solid professor for a 300-person history class. She offers a ton of extra credit and is always open for help or questions. The papers are graded pretty harshly, but that's because of the TAs. If you catch yourself struggling, make sure to show up to office hours. For a huge class, Fourmy makes the best of it and teaches well in lectures

She is very nice,  very passionate a great storyteller, and very nice (she is sarcastic at times). However, insane amount of reading with reading checks, really harsh grader and didn't give that much feedback. Attendance and participation are essential and mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor with a gift for story telling but the Primary and Secondary Source Quizzes take a lot of preparation and theres a lot of readings.

You can truly tell Dr. Fourmy is genuinely interested in what she's teaching. The hardest part about her class was the writing assignments. The essays are pretty self explanatory though. Also, there was a LOT of extra credit (37 points) so just do that and you'll get an A. Keep in mind that you need a 89.5 or above to be exempted from the final!

Id say she was a teacher trying to be cool but failed, hence the discrepancy. Extra credit can raise your overall grade by 6 pts, more if you exempt the final. Essay grades depend on the TA, expect Bs. Most of the actual learning was done by hw reading, class was for analyzing the text (I only read what I expected was on the exam and did just fine)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy really is great. The course was NOT difficult, and I dreaded having a history class. She gave 32 extra credit points that could added to exams. It is true that a crappy TA could make things difficult. The textbook used is free and available online. Honestly the entire course was really entertaining and enjoyable. Extremely easy to pass.

Dr. Fourmy is engaging, funny, and genuinely interested in what she's teaching. The hardest part about her class was the writing assignments. Still, I did pretty well so if you're a decent writer it shouldn't be too hard. It does depend on who your TA is though. Also, there was a LOT of extra credit (37 points) so just do that and you'll get an A.

This class will make you historically cry if you're not on top of everything. Depending on the TA you get your grade will either be semi-good or just bad. A (B) in this class is basically a D, so if you don't have the specific grade requirement to be exempt from the final exam, good luck. Readings can be time-consuming. Attendance mandatory.

Ignore every 5 star review. Signe Fourmy is evil on earth. Tests are essay based and graded harshly, so if you have a bad TA your screwed. Lectures aren't posted or recorded so attendance is necessary to pass. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. It counts towards anything you want to at the end of the year. The "tests" are essays that you have limited time to write, but not that bad if you prep for it. Lots of analysis of primary and secondary sources. Overall Dr. Fourmy is a good professor who really cares to educate her students. Attendance mandatory, come to class.

Dr. Fourmy really cares about her students. In office hours she answered my questions and helped me understand what to do to do better on my in-class quizzes. They were harder than I thought they would be but when I prepared better, I did better. Definitely not a blow-off class. But over half the class has an A and won't have to take the final.

This class is very doable if you have good study habits. Most of your grade comes from primary and secondary source quizzes. Primary source quizzes are manageable if you have a general idea of what sources she may use - if you don't, go to office hours. For secondary source quizzes, just study one source. A good TA is important. Do extra credit!!!!

Basically an English class. 70% of the grade comes from timed writes? due to fears about cheating with AI. DO NOT take if you are not a history major. Focuses on reading primary sources to learn about history but isn't successful due to the large time period and lack of class time. TA's are cryptic with help and grade harshly on differing scales.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Great lecturer. That is, if you're actually interested in history.
The grading is harsh, mostly composed of writing assignments. However, there is an insane amount of extra credit. If you want to succeed in this class, you should do all of them. That is the sole reason I got an A.
The downside to Dr. Fourmy is that she can be spiteful sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In class exams are challenging. It's a history class, so lots of reading. TAs and professor are very helpful. Definitely, talk to them before the exams.
In class exams are challenging. It's a history class, so lots of reading. TAs and professor are very accessible and willing to help. Overall, great class.

Toughest course I've ever taken. The TA's grade incredibly harshly, but lots of EC opportunities are provided (DO THEM). Transfer APUSH credit to CC first if you can to avoid this class. Go to her office hours and ask for help and make sure to go to the TAs as well for help with essays. Heavy reading and difficult "quizzes" (basically exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class would be so doable if it wasn't for the in-class essays. Tons of reading required, but you could get by as long as you read for the essays. Essays are graded extremely harsh and will tank your grade, but she does offer some extra credit...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is mostly based on discussion, reading, and participation; however, if you don't participate in class, she allows you to contribute via the discussion board. Overall, I felt that this class was straightforward if you did the reading. Professor Fourmy is very understanding, and this class is super interesting. I definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are a STEM major and don't excel at writing essay's don't take this course. The essay's are graded very harshly and you must commit lots of time preparing for the in class handwritten essays. Only get 45 minutes and you only know the topic when you enter class. You won't know what readings it will be over as well. Just take it in the summer.

Don't take this class whatsoever. In class essays are the major grades, and they are graded very harshly. Extra credit is offered, but the assignments are time consuming and boring. Teacher is interesting, but in no world should a core class be this difficult. Make your life easier and take any other prof.
informative and engaging lectures. she is very knowledgable and passionate about history. tests are in essay form and graded very harshly.

Honestly I was considering not writing a review but warning don't take this class if you care about your GPA. This is an intro level history class but honestly is graded harsher than most upper division courses. Your grade is entirely dependent on essays which are graded by TAs. Would not take again.

This class is so informative and will help you become a better writer. If you do the extra credit, attend class, go to office hours before exams, and participate you should do well. Dr. Fourmy is very engaging, caring, and wants to see her students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Took me from a B to an A. Interesting lectures but awful grading scheme, just essays and attendance. Essays are graded harshly as if you had weeks to craft them, not 45 mins. Super strict and kinda petty about attendance, did an instapoll 1 min after class started once and anyone who came in during/after was marked absent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There's reading to do before every class. Tests are all writing which was stressful but you have a week in advance to prepare a notecard on the reading to use on the test and she talks about each source that will be tested in class. Extra credit is due every Sunday and it's usually listening to an hour-long podcast and writing a summary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her lectures were fantastic! She is really engaging and she provides a lot of information. She wants you to succeed so really engage in the class and go to office hours. All assessments are hand-written so be sure to go to your TA's office hours often because they have high standards. Also, and I can't emphasize this enough, do the extra credit!!

Worst professor I've ever had at UT. All grades are handwritten, timed essays that are graded as if we had a month to perfect them. She is weird about attendance and basically won't excuse absences for any reason from what I've observed. She loses her temper and takes things out on the class. Don't take if you are easily frustrated or have a life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is engaging but her class is graded entirely by in-class essays, graded by her grad student TAs. She instructs them to grade hard. Do all the extra credit and participate in class. The extra credit can boost your grade significantly and is completion grade. Understanding the lectures and participating sets you up well on the essays.

Go to class and listen! SOO many extra credit opportunities DO THEM ALL and you will be fine. Grade is based off in class essays. Everyone does badly on the first one, then go to your TA and ask for feedback and you should get better after that. Fourmy is an entertaining lecturer and the TA's really do know a lot.

I see a lot of positive reviews and I suggest that the average student just looking to complete their basics do not take her class. Fourmy's class is structured where your grade comes from attending the interesting lectures, and only in-class essays. There is also extra credit which I suggest doing. She would lose her temper sometimes as well.

She is a great professor. I enjoyed her lectures a lot. Despite learning about a lot of stuff in high school, she still made them very engaging. One thing I should've done is to do all of the extra credit, as it definitely would've boosted my grade. The grades are determined by four in-class essays, and you can bring a notecard to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yes, a difficult class if you are not prepared to read, analyze, or make an effort with your writing. Dr. Fourmy, if you attend class and try to get to know her through office hours is a huge help. Truly does want her students to succeed while simultaneously encouraging them to become better writers by pushing them out of their comfort zone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Fourmy is passionate about what she does, which translates to interesting lectures if you're paying attention. Grades are based entirely on writing assignments, 2 in-class essays, 2 take-home essays, and 3 reflections. The grades are issued by TAs who seem to be inconsistent. Do all the extra credit, even if you don't think you need it.

Her lectures were intensive but extremely useful to the written exams, and she offered lots of extra credit throughout the semester. Most of the work was reading and writing, so be prepared to analyze and write about the assigned readings. Assignments and exams work similarly to an AP History class; some readings aren't necessary for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Beware that this class is all essays. (Including the final) Half are in class while the other half are written at home and turned in. I struggled getting above an 80 on the essays but she does give lots of extra credit (DO IT ALL!) I did end up with a 94 on the final though! So def passable and she'll exempt you from the final if you have an 89.5+

Dr. Fourmy was an amazing lecturer that never ceased to make class intriguing and fun. Her lectures made me think deeply about the foundation of our country and I took away a lot from this course, besides the credit. Her grading scheme is tough with most of your grade depending on the essays but she gives a hefty amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you are really passionate about history and writing. All of the assignments in the class are writing assignments that are graded very hard. Make sure to go office hours with your TA if you want to do good in the class. Did not read any of the assigned readings. Make sure to do extra credit as it bumped me to an A+.

Dr. Fourmy is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about her areas of study. However, her class is difficult for an intro history class and requires some effort, but she does provide a large amount of extra credit that increased my grade by 6 points. I recommend participating in class and going to office hours as well.

Probably one of if not the best professor I've ever had when it comes to lectures. Mandatory attendance and really tough essay grading, but if you're confident in your writing and frequently go to your TA for help and feedback, you'll do great in the class. There's a ton of extra credit as well (~30 pts), should you choose to do it.

Dr.Fourmy is a great lecturer. Your grade is essentially dependent on 4 essays. The TA's grade very harsh but if you go to office hours they help a lot . Do NOT take this course if you're not confident in your writing. Do the extra credit. ALL OF IT! it helps so much. There are definitely easier professors but overall the class is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great and informative lectures, Dr. Fourmy is obviously very passionate about the subject matter. Do not take if you're not a good writer as your grade will consist solely off writing assignments and the TAs can be very harsh. Lots of extra credit is offered (around 30 points) and can bring your up grade significantly.

As a professor, Fourmy really helps students to interpret historical sources analytically and her lectures are engaging. HOWEVER, your grade is mostly determined by 4 essays, they are time consuming and grading is strict. DON'T TAKE if you aren't confident in your writing, other professors are easier. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT it got me from 89 to 96.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WOW! What an amazing professor. This lady cares about each and every student. She walks in every day with a great attitude and is always prepared to give an amazing lecture. Wow! You have to put in effort but there is extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is a very engaging and caring professor. Her lectures are great because she's energetic, and you can tell she's passionate about the topic. The class is graded on essays, so to do well you must be good at writing or willing to put in the work to enhance your writing and analysis skills. A lot of extra credit is also offered.

Dr. Fourmy is very amazing and passionate; I absolutely loved the lectures and she really challenges you to think differently about things and completely subvert what you already know. Fair warning the TA's grade very hard, so I would recommend really putting work into the writing assignments, there's only a few so it's not bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is so funny and her lectures are engaging. This class is graded on 4 essays (2 in-class, and 2 outside of class) and 3 podcast reflections (the lowest PR gets dropped). She doesn't grade any of the essays or PRs so your grade is all determinant on your TA. I had a good TA (Alyssa) that was available to give feedback and was very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you do not like writing, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. All the work is writing. We do not do any multiple choice. The lectures are amazing. She is super passionate about the subject and encourages discussion in her class. DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT. The TAs grade super strictly.

Fourmy gives excellent, engaging lectures. However, the class is very hard. The final grade is 90% essays, which are graded harshly by the TA's. She offers a lot of extra credit, which can bring your final grade up by as much as 4 points.

dr fourmy was a nice professor in the beginning of the semester. her snarky remarks and favortism began to show as the semester goes on. she is very strict on grading essays and makes you question whether or not you can actually write. when she provides essay feedback all she writes is "?" and when you go to her office hours, she doesnt help either
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The main emphasis in this class is your writing skills. Most of the assignments were group essays and projects, and prof was a very hard grader regarding your writing. There aren't as many extra credit assignments as I was expecting, and you'll have at least 40 pages of reading before each class. Expect to do a lot of reading and writing in groups.

Dr. Fourmy was a great professor. She teaches engaging lectures and is very approachable. The grades are mostly made up of analysis essays of sources. The rest are attendance. TA's do grade a bit strict BUT Dr. Fourmy gives out a lot of extra credits for you to make up the points. If you put in the work, you'll walk away with a good grade.

DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Class will be difficult if you struggle with writing. Go to your specific TA office hours since they grade YOUR PAPER and you can write to their style. Grades consist mostly of written papers and final exam which you can skip with an A. Highly recommend you participate in your class since it will help. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Make sure you do the extra credit. The TAs grade all the exams (which are all handwritten and done in person) VERY harshly, and you won't get an A if you skip on the extra credit. If you get an A, though, you can skip the final exam. The professor is tough, but she's passionate about teaching, and her lectures are entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: TAs grade most essays. PARTICIPATE IN CLASS, you will need your TAs and professor to feel like you care. The readings aren't necessary to succeed in the course; meeting with your TA is. The grading standard is extremely rigid. They look for a very specific format in the essays which isn't difficult but you have to follow it if you want above B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fourmey is a very great professor, she is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material discussed in class. She is a phenomenal speaker and a very entertaining lecturer. However, the class can be difficult since the final grade is based on 6 essays. There is a lot of extra credit though, to boost your grade. Grading can be harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a very love hate relationship with this class. I kept getting low 80's on papers and was worried about my grade and got frustrated. I participated in 95% of the extra credit opportunities and office hours and this paid off by raising my grade significantly. This ended up being one of my favorite classes. Teacher is incredible!

Fantastic lecturer who is knowledgeable and passionate about her subject, but very difficult for a core class. Grade is determined by six essays (graded by postdocs) - don't take unless you're a good writer! Lots of extra credit opportunities though, I was able to raise my grade from a B to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy's class was so good that I added history as a major! I highly enjoyed her class, and through her lectures, I viewed history in a brand-new light. The extra credit for this class is really key: I think it would be very hard to get an A without any extra credit. I'd recommend doing all of the extra credit opportunities she gives you!

Dr. Fourmy is an amazing professor & extremely passionate on what she teaches. The lectures and topics were well thought out and i loved the class. however, your grade is based on several essays that your ta grades & they all grade quite differently, which can be frustrating. also most of her tas can be demeaning in their comments. but great topics
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The issue is not with her but with the TAs. You will HAVE to go to office hours because the TAs will grade ALL essays extremely subjectively and unfairly. Pour your blood, sweat, and tears into a paper and watch them unmercifully tear it apart. They are rude, biased, and condescending. DON'T TAKE!

Took this class Fall 2023. It stressed me out a lot and made me wish I'd taken history at community college. But looking back, I'm glad I took it. Race/gender discussions were surprisingly interesting. Many essays, graded harshly, but they genuinely promoted critical thinking. Ask TA for help on thesis/drafts. 30+ EC points boost grade (B+ to A+).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she is extremely knowledgeable and her lectures are super interesting but unfortunately this class is way too hard for a core class. your entire grade depends on 5 essays which are graded super tough. a shame bc she really makes the content interesting but the writing expectations are way too high. dont take unless you are a good writer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Fourmy is an amazing professor and lecturer. Read the sources and the textbook, it will help so much, and take good notes on the sources since that is what the essays are about. We had in-class essays which were challenging so be cautious. DO THE EC it will help immensely. Overall great class would take it again.

Fourmy is a great lecturer who approaches history uniquely (mandatory attendance). The course heavily emphasizes essays, which are graded rigorously, but TAs offer some assistance. There are abundant easy bonus opportunities. If you're a decent writer, this class is recommended, but be sure to capitalize on the bonus points.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very interesting and she is very knowledgeable, however the TAs are extremely unhelpful and are typically post-doc or doctoral students who grade EXTREMELY hard and offer little feedback. The class only has 6 total grades, and all of them are essays. Essays often have an average of ~70. Class is made way too difficult by TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor and my TA were super nice and helpful, but the grading is tough and every single assignment is an essay. The extra credit is so helpful to bring your grade up but this class is so hard for being an INTRO class.  Definitely avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very difficult grader. Full grade is based almost entirely on 4 essays, 2 of which are on full length books. Core class should not be this difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Grading consists of attendance and five essays, the last one being the final. Essays are graded very seriously, returned in 2 weeks with feedback. Professor is passionate about the subject and lectures are typically very interesting.  

Do NOT miss out on extra credit. You will need it.

Very fascinating lectures, but this class will take up way too much time as papers must be publish-worthy to get good marks, so there are endless amounts of extra credit assignments to compensate. Consistently go to TA office hours to discuss your paper; they will nitpick everything when grading. Avoid unless you absolutely love US history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is a great lecturer and is insanely knowledgeable. The only grades are from 5 papers, and the grade will vary depending on the TA grading, making the course very difficult. If you are not a strong writer I would strongly recommend doing all of the extra credit assignments to significantly bring up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy was a very passionate professor who made learning about history so entertaining. A large portion of the class was focused on slavery, which I really liked because she covered in more depth than a high school class. However, this course is graded on only a few essays, and the TAs grade veryyy tough, but the extra credit is very generous.

Dr Fourmy is very passionate about her work. She is very understanding and cares about her students. The class is based on attendance/instapolls and 4 essays. The TA grades super hard but if you go to his office hours you should be fine. She also gives a lot of extra credit.

Dr. Fourmy is very passionate to teach her classes. The class was difficult, but this class helped me improve the papers I wrote. She offered a whopping 32 points of extra credit towards any assignment, but the final. She does have high standards for your 4 essays. Not the TA's fault they grade harsh, since she encourages them to.

Dr. Fourmy made history as interesting as it should be. No memorizing names or dates, just understanding the culture over time. The grade depends entirely on a few papers and my TA was pretty picky, but the amount of extra credit available is insanely generous. Brought me up a whole letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So funny, teaches history very engaging. Unapologetic about teaching through lens of gender and race. Essays graded rough, but BUNCH of extra credit that really negates that. 10/10.

The scope is very focused on slavery given Fourmy is an expert on American Slavery. The class is graded by 4 essays and a final essay so DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT which will almost guarantee you an A. The final essay has a huge scope, so if you want to do well, at least read all the primary source readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would recommend this class if you consider yourself a good writer. Class is graded only off attendance and 4 essays plus a final essay. Grading is very tough and seemed overly subjective, but she gives a ton of extra credit which gives at least a letter grade difference at the end of the semester. Do the extra credit and talk to your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is a great lecturer and incredibly passionate about African-American history. I genuinely learned a lot in this class and she made me laugh a few times. I also became a better writer. The TA can be a hard grader, but the essays are short and a lot of extra credit is offered, so you can easily make up for poor essays.

Worse history class I've taken. If you think you're an okay writer, that's not enough.TA is a tough grader and is looking for hyper-specific answers for the writings. I've never struggled to write essays until I took this course. The professor is pretty decent, it's just the TA that is the problem, and they're responsible for grading EVERYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had a B average, extra credit got me an A. doesn't post slides; she offers extra credit for volunteer notetakers -- TAs give you the notes, just ask. She encourages new opinions and pushes students to actually learn the material. She teaches real college classes. If you want to grow academically and actually learn, take her classes and get ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is so educated in her department. But, as a basic level history course, it is very hard. The extra credit is fantastic, but grading on regular papers is SO tough. Lectures also contain a ton of information which isn't vital to papers. She tries to make lectures engaging, throwing candy when you speak. I'd recommend if you like history.

This class is absurdly difficult. The course consists of 4 essays + final (also essay) + attendance, but extra credit is offered BUT VERY MINIMAL. Essays are graded very harshly for no reason (don't think anyone has gotten a 100 on an essay so far). Doesn't post the slides from her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fourmy makes history interesting as she gives you a whole new perspective on things. Your entire grade consists of essays that are graded based on an extremely specific rubric. Do ALL of the extra credit. Do NOT procrastinate. Do major readings early and don't wait until the last day to write essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Fourmy was an AMAZING lecturer. She really knows her stuff, and teaches in an efficient/fun manner. That being said, this class was hard. Only assignments are four papers and final project. If you are "sufficient" at writing (80-90s on papers) you can get an A in this class with extra credit. DO ALL OF IT (a lot to distribute across papers).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are engaging you can tell she has a lot of passion for the subject. She likes to focus on the perspectives of underrepresented minority groups which makes us history more interesting. There are no exams, just essays, but she offers a ton of extra credit options. If you score B's on your essays and do all extra credit you will succeed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! your whole grade is made up of 5 essays that are graded extremely harshly. I had a C- all semester until extra credit was applied to my grade. Professor and TA's don't work with you about what you did wrong in your essays, class average was always a C/C+, save yourself the headache and take a different class for a history!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Before this class I wasn't super into history, however, I thoroughly enjoyed the class and found a new appreciation for it. Professor Fourmy was engaging, genuinely cared about students and was readily available to help with assignments. Lots of extra credit so it is easy to make the grade you want. Grade is dependent on ta grading.

Do not take Fourmy unless you are passionate about history and willing to go the extra mile. This class is not an easy A and it is very hard to take notes because the slides only have a few words on it, and all of the info is conveyed verbally with no written record.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't take this class, there is zero reason for an intro history class to be this difficult. Your entire grade is based on attendance (through Instapoll) and five papers. However, she does offer a lot of extra credit, which is the only reason I gave her a two instead of a one. Too tough of a grader, would not recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do every single piece of extra credit you can. EVERY SINGLE ONE. Go to your TA OH and ask them for help with your thesis and body paragraphs. You have to put in this much of work to do well in the class.

The course topic is very interesting, and lectures are mandatory, but some information is not as essential to the papers needed to write. Your grade consists of attendance, 4 papers, and a final paper. The grading of papers is based on TA, but if you take advantage of all the extra credit, it helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Signe and all of our reality TV discussions. I took this course for fun, and while it was hard and I had to put in work, I got it done and it WAS possible to get an A. You MUST take advantage of extra credit, go to office hours, and not be afraid to ask questions. Some of y'all are overreacting in this!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Fourmy as a professor - she is brilliant! However, you're only graded on a few essays and depending on your TA they could be graded strictly. It made the class stressful, BUT I was able to get an A because I racked up 30 points of extra credit. DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT SHE OFFERS and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is not an easy class by any means but I truly think you should take it if you get the chance. Prof Fourmy is so passionate in her lectures which makes staying engaged easy.
