She wants to hear from her students and makes an effort to get to know everyone. The class grade is 4 papers, 1 final project, participation, and extra credit (DO IT).

While she's an interesting lecturer, her class is organized extremely poorly. Your grade is made up of five essays and attendance. The essays are graded by TAs who are unnecessarily strict and nitpick the smallest mistakes. There is no reason for an intro history class to be this hard and your diet coke addiction is not funny. Wouldn't recommend
Awesome class! Not hard at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy is an EXPERT. Her lectures are engaging and she has a jovial sense of humor that keeps things light but on-topic during class. Lots of extra credit, but only 5 assignments and they're graded very harshly (not one 100 was given thus far). Nearly impossible to cover everything within word count. So much reading. Avoid if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy knows what she's talking about, but the entire class is based on essays and attendance. The only grades are essays and attendance, but she does give out a lot of extra credit opportunities that would considerably raise your grade (B+ to A- for example) if you do all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A very passionate professor in the classroom but not ideal to talk to outside of class. Attendance is mandatory and the few assignments are graded very harshly.  As a humanities major, I found this class difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. Your whole grade is based on attendance and 5 papers (including 1 final take-home). There is a looooot of reading, and it is impossible to keep up with the readings. The grading is extremely strict. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing, engaging lecturer who's passionate about what she teaches. However, this class is graded only on 5 papers and attendance (and papers are graded harshly). Must be a concise and purposeful writer. Average essay scores are a B-. Lots of extra credit, but this class is still pretty difficult for those who struggle w/ writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The papers are graded so harshly that the extra credit won't affect your grade much, she has a lot of energy while lecturing and she enjoys teaching. There is no second opportunity if you don't do your best on the final as it weights 30% of the grade and you can't use extra credit for it. If you want to keep your GPA high,take another history class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Pros:
Very interesting class + thought provoking discussions.
Very important course content, you learn a lot.
There was an assignment where we had to watch a film, which was fun

Cons:
Although likely unintentional, I felt overlooked in class. Many students would be called on upwards of 4 times, when I'd be lucky if I was even once. It made me sad.
I quite enjoyed this class. Professor Fourmy is very smart and a good lecturer. This class is incredibly paper heavy with difficult prompts, so if you are not a good writer I would stray away.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fourmy's class consists of several essays graded very strictly by her TAs. You'll need to read lots and write gold. Moreover, you must extend your writing beyond just regurgitating dates. Luckily, lectures are engaging and facilitate the deeper thinking needed for the essays. The class is well worth the effort, even if you're a premed like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Entirely graded on papers analyzing primary sources or assigned readings, graded by TA's. Professor Fourmy is entertaining during lectures, and is strict on mandatory attendance. She offers lots of extra credit that boosted my final grade 3 points. A very fair history course but do NOT procrastinate on her papers, they are very content heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Two analysis papers, two book reviews, final essay, attendance, extra credit. All take-home. Sometimes annoying/anxiety-inducing when talking about grades; she thinks 84.5 average on the final is high. Medians have been mid 80s (graded by TAs), extra credit boosts a lot. Only really time-consuming the week before essay deadlines. A = 94+.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took HIS315k as my last history requirement. Dr. Fourmy is an amazing professor, gives substantial lectures that make American history actually interesting. Attendance is required, you get a few passes though. Never read the textbook. ONLY essay based exams, I am warning you if you are not a strong writer you will not get an A.
Worst professor ever, grades only in their point of view.

Dr. Fourmy is so educated and I never got bored in her lectures. She genuinely cares that you understand the concepts. Course is work heavy so be prepared to have lots of reading. Grade is based on 4 papers + final. Get to know your TA b/c Dr. Fourmy doesn't grade this class.  You get 3 unexcused absences before it counts against your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was insanely good. It's one of those classes that are difficult but worth it, instead of taking an easy A course and it having no impact. She offers a lot of extra credit, which helps when you don't get the grade you wanted. A LIFE changing course. You really go into depth about African American history. Professor Fourmy is AMAZING! =

Dr. Fourmy was absolutely amazing! Her lectures were so interesting and she made everyone feel comfortable with speaking in class! Offers LOTS of extra credit which makes up for the TA's harsh grading! This course is so eye-opening, not only due to the material, but also the way that Dr. Fourmy delivers the material! TAKE THIS CLASS! Insanely good!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You might be nervous about taking an African American history class that is taught by a white woman, but Dr. Fourmy does a great job at teaching history fully and in truth. The required readings for this class are very interesting and she offers lots of extra credit! She is engaging and you can tell she is passionate about the material.

I took Dr. Fourmy for HIS 317L and the class lectures were extremely invigorated and eye-opening. No exams, only papers. Lots of extra credit opportunities, but lectures did not help with the papers at all. Grading is extremely tough and is more of a "write it my way or get a bad grade." This is not a blow-off class... hard to get an A.
Yall need to read her other RMP for Austin community college
Had her at ACC and now here. No, just no. Literally not sure what she wants from us even after taking in 110% of her feedback. Such a stickler.
She always moved around her office hours so if was impossible to get help all the while she graded wayyyyy tooo strict. She also showed up late to her own class bruh
*sighs* (in depression)

Im guessing (could be wrong) that she has tenure because she literally does not care about anything. So many arbitrary rules. She doesn't respond to emails on weekends (fine), needs two business days to respond (okay), then doesn't respond. But she said she "saw it though". She also changes her office hours all the time so you can really attend it.
She goes on a tangent alot which wastes class times about the most random topics too, kid you not she talked about her and her husband's favorite types of "drinks" and how they like to "drink"

Something that I know it's not really talked about enough is her accent, which makes it difficult to understand what she's saying. She attempts to speak in Spanish, which is kind of ironic because this is an English class.
There's easier ones for sure

took her last semester- DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE. Grades aren't put in until the last week of classes, doesn't respond to any emails whatsoever, zero expectations are set for the course so not only will you have no idea what to do, you will be punished for it, literally only gives out B's. Literally worst class you can take, save yourself!!!
5 foot 3 and an attitude. That's all imma say about her

Currently in her class, she has this evil smug looking face. Had to ask her a question at the end of class. She pretended not to see me waiting. I ended up waiting almost 15 minutes after class to ask a simple question because she does not respond to emails.
I had her in one of her past English classes. She was great. She doesn't smile anymore. She's seems to have lost her spark and interest
She was verbally rude outside class and made me cry after I talked with her about why I was getting the grades that I was
rubrics seem fair but unfortunately she is not

Love this class! In comparison to other World Lit classes this one has minimal long reads, and she is very understanding to students. She allows absence makeups and essay redos, definitely gives students the benefits of the doubt. All of our essays were graded either 85, 90, or 95 so not a big variety. And an A is 90 +!
Hugo ego and expects students to write like her

What makes me mad is how she doesn't really seem to care about what she does. She doesn't care to give full attendance points to anyone even if they show up all the time to class and is extremely slow to grade things to the point where we got stuff pushed back and had cramped deadlines. She always whined about stuff such as her leg, job, or family.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I regret taking this class. She acts nice and all but man she is extremely rude when you try to speak one-on-one and does not respond to emails very well. Did not improve as a writer in this class

Lectures were all over the place and not very helpful. The assignments and readings were fascinating, but her instructions were super unclear. Her feedback was confusing, but she offered plenty of revision opportunities. I liked that she offered office hours to make up for absences!

required to take it
i shouldn't have
Do not be misguided by her false cloak of kindness, it's a red herring

She literally does whatever she feels like. (not to your benefit) If she doesn't feel like teaching, she won't. If she doesn't fee like grading, she won't. If she feels like bringing you down in office hours, she will. Not sure where all these good reviews cam from. I looked at them & thought she was going to be a good professor but I was mistaken.

Her hair is dyed blue for a reason, she sucks. She sucks at responding to emails, sucks at grading stuff on time, and sucks at giving feedback. She took 4 months to grade assignment until the last week of class. She's so political and isn't even a good teacher in the slightest. Who hired her?

She was super unhelpful in office hours, rants on useless stuff in class, grades harsh (btw no one makes above 95 on assignments in her class-in her own words) and talks about innapropaite stuff in class such as her and her husband's alcoholic habits. Even after attending EVERY SINGLE class she took attendance points off because it'll be above a 95
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: In no way was this a "liberal humanities class" like the other reviews are saying. Just because an author dyes her hair and cuts it short doesn't mean her work should be thrown out. The class itself is really easy, and the lectures are honestly not that important. I went for the extra credit, but there is only 20 minutes of teaching per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take unless you are politically liberal. I was super excited to cover Beowulf, until I realized it was feminist Beowulf (author has affinity for the word daddy and the F word). Listened to drag queen recitation in class. Prof read short story about 16 year old lesbians s*xual awakening in class. Super weird all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have nothing good to say. Her lectures are useless. She spends more time giving the facade of being jolly than she does coming up with quality assignments. All supposedly analytical writing assignments actually require us to support one of her biased views, and she rarely provides quality feedback. Professors like her give humanities a bad name.

Really nice class. Professor definitely expands the scope of world literature beyond the European canon and incorporates independent texts such as film projects. There is no A-, so it's pretty easy to get an A overall, even though she caps essays at 95.
this class was just too boring as a stem major, easy otherwise, but you have to read the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Highly recommend this class and professor. The material was interesting to read and as long as you did the readings the class was an easy A. Best part of the class was that we watched two films that were pretty entertaining. There's also bonus points on the midterms for attending the lectures and doing the Instapoll questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I rarely attended class and got an A+ in this course. That being said, this class was an adjustment. The old English was hard to read and comprehend, but the longer I engaged in the material, the easier it got. There were also 1-2 assignments due every single week, so this course was quite manageable with everything being open note and online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A cutoff is 90, which is huge. Didn't read a single text all semester, and got an A. Going to lecture isn't required, but gets a decent amount of extra credit on exams. I was dreading humanities, but I feel like I got out of this awful requirement with Dr. Garcia's class. If you hate reading but need a Lit credit, I promise this is the best one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course involved quite a bit of reading, but it really isn't too bad. As long as you attend discussions and review the lecture slides, you'll do just fine in the class.

Professor Garcia is very sweet and understanding. She assigns a lot of group projects and a few writing assignments, but nothing too difficult. She's pretty good with grading and gives ample extra credit opportunities. Overall, she's a very caring professor and I would definitely take her class again.

LOVE Garcia! She's so passionate about this class which really shows through in lectures. Her class is so fun and allows us to explore course themes in a more relaxed way. She only grades between a 85-95 but if you show more effort (go to office hours) she will help you improve your essays and get a better grade. Readings are really interesting!

Prof Garcia is a very laid back professor. This class had two units and the assignments were the same in each unit they just covered dif things. The tests were open note and pretty simple and straightforward. Attendance isn't required but you get extra credit if you attend class. Such an easy class, I would DEF recommend!!

Super easy class. I got away with not reading most of the stories for class, even though I felt like the texts were interesting. Exams/quizzes are open note and you can find most answers online. No essays and any writing assignments were really simple. The TAs grade all of your work, but my TA was sweet + didn't grade harshly, so I had no problem

Pretty easy, straightforward course. Some books were more difficult than others, but thankfully no essays, just two open-note tests and ~6 open-note short quizzes in total. Lecs were a liiittle boring, but the info is great for tests/quizzes. only mandatory attendance was the 1x/w discussion sections with TA, which were easy (depends on TA, ig)

Easy class with clear rubric. No written papers just 2 unit tests worth 40% of grade. Attendance for lecture is not mandatory (but extra credit is given if you go), but discussion is mandatory. Grading depends on TA, but usually work is simple and straightforward.

simple for a brit lit class. i like professor garcia, but the lectures felt like a waste for me. just know enough about the readings and follow the rubrics for all the assignments. grading is really fair and expectations are clear. discussion is mandatory but lecture is not
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia was great to take for Brit Lit. There was not any papers and only 2 exams based off of the readings and lecture material. The class was also hybrid, so you only had to go to mandatory discussion once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia was great to take for Brit Lit. There was not any papers and only 2 exams based off of the readings and lecture material. The class was also hybrid, so you only had to go to mandatory discussion once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class exceeded my expectations! Grading is super fair and although there is a lot of readings they are engaging. Attendence isn't neccesarily mandatory but it helps a lot to show up! Be careful when it comes to tests, there's only two and they're 40% of your grade!

The best decision I made was taking Brit Lit with Garcia. She picks the best readings (sometimes they're long but it's manageable). The grading is seriously so easy as long as you give it some thought. I have a 102 in the class right now. Dr. Garcia is so caring and interesting and I love listening to her lectures. I recommend her 100%.
Attendance is mandatory although showing up really boosts your grade. Didn't read a single text all semester and got an A. The grading scale for A is 90-100 which is nice.

What makes this class so special is Dr. Garcia's way of teaching. The readings she gives are genuinely interesting and not long at all compared to most Plan II teachers. Dr. Garcia deserves the world and nothing less. If anyone has the opportunity to take Dr. Garcia they should. Follow the rubrics and you'll get an AQ.

I loved Dr. Garcia's class! I was nervous about taking my first honors world literature class at UT. She's super welcoming and does her best to engage her students. She's very available to her students. I also love how she focused on more modern novels from different countries rather than starting with ancient literature. I miss being in her class!

I made and A in this class without doing any of the readings. If you go to lecture and discussion, and read summaries you can slide by. Super easy, but discussions are mandatory. They suck if your TA sucks, like mine did, but Garcia is very patient and understanding with extensions and grading criteria. She also extends deadlines sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia's class is easy enough and she is a nice lady. I will say, all this class talks about is feminism. Every reading she picks, she ties back to feminism. And many of the interpretations of text are eisegetical.

Such a sweet person and gave great lectures! I loved the class topic and it was clear she did too--she always seemed so excited for class and was so informative. Very accommodating with Zoom and accessible in office hours. Only complaints are grade scale (capped grades at 95) and slow response to emails. Amazing professor otherwise!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia is an amazing professor who takes the extra step to engage with her students, even though this is difficult through Zoom classes, through discussion of our readings, which were almost always really interesting. She was also very accomodating during COVID and the freeze and genuinely cares about her students' wellbeings.

Dr. Garcia is an amazing professor. I've taken two of her classes now, and I've loved them both. She truly cares about her students and she's a great lecturer with interesting topics to teach. As long as you demonstrate interest in what you write about, it's an easy A. I really recommend taking a class with her!

Loved Professor Garcia! The assignments and readings were always interesting, our class discussions were engaging, and she gave great feedback on our writing assignments. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it!

If you don't put off the readings, this class should be an easy A. Dr Garcia is a good lecturer, and her tests and assignments are straightforward. Poll points are taken in class, but you can miss up to 3 days without consequence. The TAs do most of the grading, and they give good advice and feedback. I highly recommend Dr Garcia.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the UT Austin's best professors, Dr. Garcia's Literature Courses are very good, she provides good feedback, is accessible outside class, very good and helpful TAs, good sense of humor, amazing lectures, and provides opportunities for group discussion projects. Altogether, Dr. Patricia Garcia is a great professor, and is highly recommended!

NOT an easy A! She is a really nice professor, but the material isn't very engaging. You have to read the assigned material or you will not do well on the exams or quizzes. She uses Squarecap in class and the questions weren't always easy so make sure you pay attention in lecture! Participation matters in discussion, all in all it was BORING.

Very good and interesting English class. Left leaning but thats a given. Still an awesome and super nice prof. Best English class I have probably ever taken. Made an A+. Supposed to be three tests and three short papers. Covid changed the class format but first test and first two papers were very straightforward, clear, and graded fairly. Cool TAs.

British Literature are two scary words. With professor Garcia, Brit lit is actually interesting. There is more text to cover than with American literature (since Brit history starts from the 10th century not 17th), which means that the details required for you to know per text is not much. Go to her lectures and turn in your work, A, no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Garcia has been one of my favorite professors at UT. She really cares about what she's teaching and the class discussions are always nice to have. She handled the switch to online classes very well and I will miss having her as a professor.
Professor Garcia is great! Her lectures are super informative and detailed and she is genuinely a nice person. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'd have to TRY to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Garcia really makes British literature more relatable and interesting to read. Lectures were very interesting and she broke down readings to really convey the meanings/relationships. Great professor, go to class and read and youll be fine

Professor Garcia is amazing. She has such a wonderful insight on topics regarding gender, sexuality, race, and class. All the readings are interesting. Graded on 3 essays, a group presentation, and discussion posts. Really enjoyable class .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is so much potential for this class to be much more interesting, but it was only okay. Assignments, quizzes, and exams were easy enough- about on par with other English classes. Not too much work. Avoid if you don't want to act. Overall the class and prof were just average.
The class is pretty easy as long as you go to class and pay attention to what she says you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: TAKE DR. GARCIA!!! This was probably the easiest English course I have taken in my entire college career, and I'm a senior. If you read the plays, you'll get 100 on quizzes. 3 exams all easy if you literally just know the plot. She is very caring and understanding, and the class is amazing. Take her if you can, automatic A+.

Garcia's lectures are quite interesting and in depth and hit the main points that are on the frequent quizzes. Exams (4) consist of objective, short answer, and an essay question. There were 2 standalone extra credit opportunities and another on a close reading installment (4 CRITs total, 16%). We also went to the HRC for to see original books.

She really heard the students out when we were struggling on her exams, and modified her curriculum for the better. She gives out extra credit for exams and honestly the class was definitely doable as long as you fill out the learning objectives. Her class was not hard as long as you stayed consistent with your studying and learning objectives.

Dr. Gonzalez was amazing. Focuses on research & group work more than most, which may be good or bad. Lectures could be dry, but slideshows had everything you needed. Tests had few questions but were never surprising, & there were ample opportunities for practice & EC. Gives great feedback and cares about your academic growth. Highly recommend!

Dr. G is nice but her lectures are so boring. She just mumbles all the time and her TA makes things even more confusing. Her exams are okay, they give out partial credits but you gotta know what you're talking about for sure. A lot of discussion with classmates and people don't participate at all, very boring class

Gonzalez is an amazing professor! She records all lectures so you can study at home too. Every class is lecture besides exam days, and grades are based off presentation + exams. If ur in TIP, go to CSS bc learning off those slides is most helpful for exams. This class is scary at first but gets easier. Very generous with extra credit!! She's lovely
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Gonzalez is an engaging professor who truly cares about her students. She is constantly checking in and creates a space where you feel comfortable to ask questions. Her class is very interactive which I found allows the chance to make study groups and also helps you to retain the information faster. Could not ask for a better bio 2 prof!

This class was VERY easy for an UD bio. 6 asynch open-note quizzes worth 48% (1 drop), no exams or final. There is a group project but it is also pretty easy since you'll have around 6-8 ppl. Lots of EC, lecture attendance isn't required (recorded) but discussion is, she is super sweet and always checked in on us, tbh could not recommend her enough

She is very nice and sweet and tries to make lecture engaging, even if there is a lack of student participation. There are many small extra credit opportunities after each lecture, after each biweekly quiz (no final), and other misc EC assignments. Personally did not have a hard time understanding her accent, but others have said it can be tough.

Discussion attendance is mandatory but lecture is not (lectures recorded). I didn't use the textbook. 2 xtra credit opps per week. 1 group project presentation. Exams (6, biweekly, online) are easy and open notes. One of the kindest professors I have had at UT. She is incredibly understanding and it is clear she loves her job. Love Dr. Gonzalez.

I love the professor, she is very caring about her students. My only nitpick is that I didn't enjoy the lectures as much as I did because they seemed very slow-paced. I think the pacing of this class could be better, but the quizzes were all open book, so it was an easy class.
really caring professor. gets to know her students which is so awesome. there are so many opportunities to get a great grade.

Lectures aren't mandatory and she does record them (but you should go unless if you want to be super confused by the time the final comes around). There's only quizzes (no exams, just a final). She's a decent professor and her class isn't very difficult. The final is also pretty easy if you've been paying attention to lectures.

Professor Gonzalez is amazing! She's super clear and breaks down tough topics. Her teaching style is engaging, and she really cares about making sure everyone gets it. You can tell she wants us to succeed, and she's great at explaining things without making it overly complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Gonzalez is so chill, and explains concepts so uniquely. She has 6 open book quizzes, group assignments, weekly assignments, and a final (was easy!). Make sure to pay attention in class. TAs are very kind and helpful in explaining content. Beware, wording of quizzes can be confusing at times, so be prepared! Also ample extra credit!

All major grades are with the same group throughout the semester, so hope you get a good group. If everyone does their job, work loads are very manageable, and deadlines are fair. She gives great feedback and allows for multiple corrections before the finals grades are given. Not my favorite class, but definitely not one you have to worry about.

Compared to other BIO 311D professors, Gonzalez was great. She is incredibly understanding and gives out extra credit for doing simple assignments weekly. There are no midterms, just 6 quizzes and a final which are both tested online. If you read the lecture handouts and her notes you should do just fine in this class.

Dr. Gonzalez just read her lecture slides which consisted of only pictures with a few notes. No final but biweekly quizzes that are tricky as some questions contain more than one answer choice. Would take someone else if possible; I don't think I learned a single thing in this class.

No midterms, only biweekly quizzes based on recent lectures/readings. There is a group presentation which was initially unappealing but it was made easy through splitting up the requirements into multiple grades over time. Prof learned EVERYONE'S NAME which is so incredible. She is also a good resource for CNS research/study abroad opportunities.

Very sweet and caring professor who truly wants the best for her students. However, a good 50% of the test questions will come from things she breezes over within lecture, making the class much harder if you don't study notes. Thankfully, she provides all the notes for you within the comments of her presentations. I learned a lot from her class.

There is only a final exam, no midterms. Biweekly quizzes that cover ONLY lecture notes so textbook is optional. Group assignments are a big role in grading, so it's easy to get redemption. Encourages collaboration and communication, and is always trying to make lectures more engaging with the students. She even tries to remember EVERYONE'S name!

No midterms and bimonthly quizzes. Lectures are daily and are recorded. She is a good lecturer and often tries to get engagement from the class. Quizzes are open-book and straightforward. Handouts provide supplemental information on lectures and are more in-depth. The textbook is "not required" as lectures and handouts cover everything on quizzes.

Went in with zero lab experience and came out with lab and field experience. She was very helpful and as long as you complete the assignments correctly and on time, this is an easy A. There is some writing but worth it.

I adore Dr. Gonzalez. She really cares about her students. She will bend over backwards to make your experience positive, both in her class and outside of it. Go to her office hours! She's an awesome person. She made the UGS FRI lab so enjoyable and doable, even for those who had 0 experience with research. Put in the time, and you'll get an A.

This class was fire, Dr. Gonzalez isnt a super energetic professor but her class is very straightforward. She is a super serious person but she does have a dry sense of humor. Master the learning objectives and youre guaranteed an A on the test, there really are no surprises on the tests. Some of the quizzes are tough. so keep up with the class.

I took Scientific Inquiry: Innovation UGS course with her last semester, and I was not disappointed. Although, we had a lot of assignments and coursework, she was a very understanding professor who always made her expectations clear and graded fairly. Overall, it was an excellent experience completing a research project for this class in a group.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Gonzalez is a nice professor that is available during office hours or through email. Her tests/quizzes can be very specific so make sure to read the textbook if you want to get all the information. Also, she does multiple answer multiple choice to help you but it makes you second guess yourself a lot. Lecture attendance is extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Gonzalez is a great professor. She made sure to be very accessible and her tests weren't bad once the format was understood. I honestly felt like a learned a lot. Just make sure to skim the textbook in the sections she puts on the syllabus and you will be good for the quizzes/ tests.

Not sure why she has bad reviews. Lectures are sort of dry, but give basically all the info you need for exams which are very straightforward. I recommend getting an online textbook and use the textbook and learning objectives to take lecture notes. With minimal studying I easily got an A. Group project is a chore but grading is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is okay. Definitely not the worst but I would avoid her if you can. She is hard to understand in lecture and goes very fast, and does not explain things thoroughly. Exams are based on the lectures mostly.
You need to answer the questions her way. I wrote Answers verbatim from the book and got them wrong. She doesnt care about her students at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Material is easy to understand but you must learn how to answer questions HER WAY, even if her answer wasn't even what the question asked. Unprofessional, fell asleep while grading my group presentation & assigns readings then says they are wrong on test questions. Even when she is wrong, she is right in her head. Harder than it should be. Avoid!
Great professor! She is always available if help is needed. Be sure to download her PowerPoints, and write notes in class because that's what quizzes and test come from.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She really isn't that bad. Her questions are multiple-answer multiple choice but the questions itself aren't terrifying. Completely doable.

Although the class is VERY difficult, she will do everything in your power to help. Whenever you are struggling with understanding the material after class, she will be answering questions 30 minutes after lecture, helping you plan appointments with other professors in the field, or even lending you her own textbooks. Tip: choose a partner wisely!

Loved the prof, but her lectures are boring & hard to pay attention to. Sadly quizzes were almost always far-reaching from the material taught. Exams sometimes had confusing wording or were not clear enough. ASK questions @ exams to clarify. Take notes of what she says!!! (use a computer please), read the txtbook, and review review review.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Never, ever miss class. Lectures are boring. Read assigned material, and never miss a discussion section. If these bases are covered, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super annoying and boring lectures that make you fall asleep.

Hard to understand. Also, because she puts up her notes online, you don't feel like going to class. Her outlines are supposed to be for you write notes in but she often doesn't follow the outline. She goes way too fast and generally, you will be forced to look up the lecture online anyway because you will miss stuff.  Save yourself!
The best prof! Music of Asian Americans is my fave class this spring.

his class was one of the easiest i have taken. attendance and a weekly 200-400 word discussion post is what your grade is. show up and do the discussion post. also helps that he is very passionate about his job and brings cool guests to share their music journeys. take him if possible

I'm a journalism senior taking his Multimedia Music Journ as elective and I've learned more from this class in 5 weeks than my actual required majors! He gives great 1-1 feedback that has already made me a better writer! The activities are really fun like this week we're doing reporting on live shows. Highly recommend Professor Gabrillo!

You can feel his passion during his lectures. Super fun most of the time. His Canvas page is well organized and communicates frequently with the whole class on there. Brings cool guest lecturers a few times during the semester!

Probably the easiest UGS. 200/400 word responses each week on whatever the topic in lecture was. I fell asleep during most lectures, so it's not hard to BS the responses. Professor is passionate about the topic, so if you care about the material you'll like him.
Honestly I took this class for a credit and while I didn't find it interesting I will say I liked this class because you could tell professor Gabrillo is so passionate about the class.
He is so awesome. Super passionate in his lectures. Workload is not bad at all. Take his class.

One of the very best professors I've had in UT. He has a relaxed calm aura so the entire class is very chill. No actual tests or exams, just essays and a solo creative project at the end like a recording or performance. Highly recommend!

Very easy UGS, highly recommend. Attendance is mandatory; it's like half of your grade, but the lectures are interesting, and you explore a lot of new areas of music. If you're a music person, this is the UGS for you.
Thanks for a great semester, Global Pop is my favorite class. This guy rocks.

If you need to take a UGS, take global pop music with Dr. Gabrillo! His lectures are super interesting and fun, especially since he brings up popular and familiar music from different genres! He only assigns weekly short essays (200-400 words) where you write about topics discussed during lectures. I DEFINITELY recommmend!!

I'm in Global Pop Music now and my reco is to take this class in fall!! Great prof and TAs are all super cool (they're his phd students). Mon&Wed lectures are super fun and you can see how much effort he puts into then. Thurs labs are small groups with TA. On friday night you submit a short essay based on fun prompts. My fave class in UT so far!!!

I love Professor Gabrillo in Multimedia Music! He seems like a really nice and caring human. Super interesting topics and case studies. We wrote essays based on a complex question of the week, then did couple of creative individual projects. He's super smart and assigns lots of readings (legit full books) but I just skimmed and survived!

Roommate highly recommended him and he was great last Spring so I'm recommending him too. Cool calm collected. Manages to talk about things like hyperpop, tiktok, Japanese bands and MTV in smart and thought provoking but not corny way. Passes the vibe check for sure.

One the best professors! I was a slacker but Dr. Gabrillo was sincerely helpful and understanding, giving me opportunities to catch up. Global Pop as UGS is easy overall, but if you miss the weekly essays they pile up, so just meet the deadlines and you'll have an amazing time! 100+ students vibing together to pop music was wild. Five stars lol
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are looking for an easy class to fulfill your UGS credit, this is the one. Our main assignments were weekly short essays, which were not time consuming at all. We also had a weekly lab session on Zoom, which seemed pretty useless but it did not require much participation. Overall, this class was an easy A and required minimal effort.

I love Drs Lewis and Gabrillo in Music and Culture! They planned a great diverse series of lectures, hands-on demos, guest performances and field trips. We even danced together in a community jam which tbh is my
fave class session ever in college. They're both super engaging in class and very sweet, making sure we're all doing good.

Really great professor, clearly very passionate about music. There is a short assignment every week with around 400 words, and also a lab every week where you share ideas. Overall great UGS if you are interested in learning about music and pretty easy to manage.

Professor Gabrillo is the best! The waitlist was long for Global Pop Music and now I get it. It's an amazing class taught by a really caring dude who's the real deal. He really wanted all of us to finish with an A. Lots of bonus activities. The community jam was the best class experience I've had. I hope to take him again in another class someday.

Currently in UGS Global Pop. It's registration so am here to say take this class! Didnt expect a required UGS to be such a vibe. Prof Gabrillo has a chill approach with very enjoyable lectures. Did fun stuff like actual jamming (like all 100 of us) & field trip to an amazing museum. Even brought in this cool Austin rapper who produced for Ariana

Take him for Global Cultures flag. He's amazing! You learn so much but work is not overwhelming at all. He's a really nice understanding professor and really wants you to gain something from his lectures. Attendance is mandatory (you get 1 point for each class then it all adds up) and you write a weekly essay. That's it. Global Pop is so much fun!

Dr. Gabrillo is the best! I took him and Dr. Dell Antonio for 312C and they were both amazing together. Learned so much and you can really see how they care about us as freshmen. It's an easy A tbh. Super fun. I saw my TA's phd syllabus with Dr. Gabrillo tho and he makes them read like 300 pages/week!! But our class was super lowkey! The best!

I love Dr Gabrillo! I took his big non-major class Global Popular Music and it's a really amazing class to get the globalcultures flag. He is very smart but super nice and approachable. Prep for each class is usually 2 readings and an audio/video playlist. The materials are very fun and interesting and this class is always happy vibes. TAKE HIM!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor and class (Pop Music Multimedia) I've taken. I'm an engineering senior but absolutely enjoyed and learned so much from James. Class was always packed, lectures were amazing, great happy vibes, work load managable--- 5 labs, midterm exam (essay), final creative project. I produced and recorded a pop single and James was so supportive!

I've taken Professor Gabrillo's Pop Music Criticism ansd Digital Cultures.. he's the best!! Grear classes to take as 342 / 379 electives. He does really great lectures.. like on kpop, Spotify, and Kendrick Lamar who he is super obsessed in an adorable way... We did fun lab activities like pretending we're coaches on The Voice and creating mixtapes!

Great class and great human being of a professor! Hes Cambridge Univ & Princeton educated but Professor Gabrillo is super down to earth, chill & caring. Amazing & lively lectures that focus on thinking deeply and analyzing pop culture and tech. So happy I took this on my last semester of school, one of the best highlights of my college life!!
Really cares about musicology and ethnomusicology, engaging lectures that incorporated the current pop culture landscape. Can't recommend him enough!

Katie is a really good teacher and makes the material easy for everyone to understand. I thought the class was really easy, so I never attended office hours. However, if you need to she makes herself very available for all students. She really cares about all of her students and is a really good resource.

Great professor! Great lectures, responsive to email, does a good job overall. Group project was kinda confusing but overall not too difficult. Got an A- but could've gotten an A if I put a little more effort into studying. Would definitely take again if I had the opportunity.

Anyone taking someone else for MIS 301 is missing out!

Katie is the best mis 301 professor!! Her lectures prepare you for the exam content the best and all of her classes are recorded on zoom if you can't attend. The final group project was trickier than the rest of the class but she made herself available for any questions. Overall, I found better success in her class than my friends with other profs

This professor is absolutely the best professor out of all MIS professors. If you go in person to class, she will teach you the content that will be on the test. She does offer Zoom classes, but I say go in person so you can do better. Overall, she genuinely cares about all her students, and I really liked her and her class.
Katie Gray was awesome! She truly cares about her students and helped me so much outside of class time when I needed review. Take her for this course if you can!

The only professor to take for MIS 301. She's the best-- so caring, kind, interesting, and actually applies what you learn to things outside of class. Tests are very straightforward and she gives a pretty comprehensive review. A few group projects but they are graded pretty easily.

Professor Gray is one of the best. Her expectations are clear, and her standards are appropriate. She is wonderful person and a wonderful lecturer. She always simplifies concepts, slicing through jargon to get to the meaning of a term. I cannot recommend her enough.
Katie Gray is one of my favorite professors I've taken at UT. She inspired me to declare MIS as a major. She also made the class a lot easier than many of the other MIS301 professors.

She's an incredible professor who is real and straight with you. She make it easy for you to either be in person or take the class online. Since she teachers the same class 3-4 times a day, she allows you to go to any lecture that best fits your schedule, regardless of the time bock you signed up for. Tests are the main thing here.

Great professor as she uses a lot of real world examples when teaching concepts, so it is easier to keep up and remember. Studying for exams is hard at first because you don't get an official study guide, but SI sessions have a practice test that can help. She covers all the important parts (that's what is tested) and cares a lot for the students.

Katie is the sweetest and genuinely cares about her students. MIS may seem intimidating, but in class she says exactly what will be on the exams. I found it hard to pay attention in class so I rewatched all the lectures right before the exams and that really helped me get an A. Attending SI sessions and reviewing instapolls are great for studying!

Amazing instructor; group projects can be slightly messy if your group is bad but do tell her if that is you. She will be glad to help. Super nice and super awesome; made the class an awesome experience.

She is SO sweet! The tests are verbatim what she says in class, so just pay attention and you'll do great. There are 3 group projects near the end that are a little bit annoying, but overall not bad.  Also, Instapoll for attendance is open on Zoom.  I would HIGHLY recommend her for MIS 301. She loves to chat, is easygoing, and very approachable!

Katie is so caring. She really tries to emphasize support and learning over anything else. Her lectures are very informative and hands on, and she builds on her experience as a UT alum to support her students. There's three exams, and you will want to take notes, but she lets you attend any of her sections, and you can attend on zoom. She's great!
I leave most of my classes early because I cannot focus and get bored. Prof. Gray class is the only one I stay in class till it is over, just because she is that good at teaching.

Katie is so caring, I loved her! Some of the other MIS teachers can be tough, but she really teaches to the test and wants you to succeed. She lets you go to any of her in-person sections or join on zoom. Whatever time is convenient. She helps with whatever you need. Some group projects, but clear criteria and chill grading.

I love Katie!!! She makes a very confusing subject a lot more digestible and interesting for beginners. Tests and expectations are very straightforward and not too difficult. I would 100% take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a wonderful professor and very caring. You don't have to read the textbook, but it does help. She does instapolls every class, but you are allowed to zoom or attend any of the class periods you want to. There is one opportunity for extra credit, which is not a lot. The exams are not crazy difficult.

Such a good and flexible prof. Even if you got the 8:00am slot, she said you could attend ANY of the time slots. Records and streams lectures so you can do class virtually. Passionate about MIS. Easy assignments. Always there to help. Easy tests.

Katie was a very engaging lecturer who connected with students and made sure that they learned the content. As long as you attend class and pay attention, the exams shouldn't be too difficult. There are weekly assignments and a few projects, but nothing too hard. I would definitely recommend her for anyone taking MIS 301.

Katie is by far the best MIS301 professor. Her lectures are extremely helpful and she will often hint at test questions in class, so attending lecture is super important for this course. This course is not easy, but Katie tries her best to make it accessible for all students.

Katie is kind, caring, and an excellent lecturer. She's highly knowledgeable and makes her class interesting. Her tests are harder than most because they're application-based, and there's no curve, but if you listen and take good notes, you'll do well. I learned a lot and found her class very engaging. Highly recommend!

I LOVE KATIE GRAY! Highly recommend her for 301. She is a great person, teacher, and lecturer. Her exams all come straight from the lectures, but make sure you study for the exams. I wish I had studied more for mine. She is so kind and accessible outside of class, as well. Go to class, take notes, do the assignments, ask questions, and you're good!

Katie is the best professor I have had at UT. She is so genuinely caring about her students and loves to get to know everybody. Her lectures are silly and engaging, her exams are straightforward and she will tell you exactly what you need to know and the best ways to prepare, and she uses many real-world applications.

Katie Gray is one of the nicest, most passionate, and caring professors I've ever had. She wants to see students perform well and gives them all the tools needed to get there. She emphasizes key things for the test so go to class or watch the recorded lectures. I could not recommend her enough, and I wish more professors were like her.

I LOVE KATIE! She's super understanding and her class is really conceptual in nature, so it's easy to understand and not solely memorization. The only reason my grade suffered was because I performed poorly on the midterm. Overall, it does not take a lot to really succeed in this class. Workload is manageable and Katie is amazing. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gray rambles a lot which makes it hard for me to focus on what we learn about. Other MIS301 sections have tests over vocabulary but Gray makes it to where there's scenarios and you have to understand the material. It's not memorization based. Group projects and weekly assignments were easy but tests were a little hard.

Gray made learning about software bearable. She tends to ramble about things but her slides are very clear and she gives outlines for every chapter so studying for tests is easy. I got a low B on the first test but managed to get an A. Very understanding and cares about students and responds quickly.

MIS is inevitably difficult for most, but Katie is incredibly kind & graceful with her students. I've never had a professor so clearly want her students to succeed in their professional and personal lives. While this has been my most difficult class, Katie always tries her best to help you make the connections (especially if you go to OH!)

She is really nice, but her exams do not really reflect your knowledge of the class. Her exams are kinda tricky as the answer choices trick you up as they can be right answers, but not in her opinion of how the question was asked. Because of this, if you are a bad text taker, I do not recommend her as a teacher because it is test HEAVY!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hard class but professor explains everything, is very clear and lenient about things, creates a great learning environment, and overall a good professor.

Katie is a gem. Understanding, always willing to help, and knows how to communicate material so well. Favorite class I've taken at UT - the final project is challenging but she is willing to help and it's a great learning experience.

Genuinely cares for students. Very understanding and reachable at nearly all times. She essentially holds your hands through every homework. The only difficult part of the class is the final project, but that is why the class is called Killer K.

She's an okay teacher. Just follow along with the slides, and you'll be fine. The homework isn't that bad, tests are kind of difficult. The group project at the end? That's the killer in Killer K. You think you got started early? Wrong. Get started earlier. The project was hell on earth, designed to not be finished. Pray for a lenient grader on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Katie is a legend. Had to say that. Anyways, this is a hard class with a lot of material, but Kaite covers it all pretty well I feel and provides good examples for HWs. She cares about her students so she is very accessible outside of class and is willing to help :). "Help is given to those who ask for it"! Also start early on the group project!
Katie rocks

Katie is a nice professor who cares about her students; however, she is not a great teacher. The class notes are very hard to follow b/c she presents it in a bad way. For the homework you basically copy and paste code she gives you and then for the project she expects you to know how to code everything on your own.

Katie is an okay teacher. This is a hard class with tons of information, which she does not present it in the best way. You really need to spend time understanding her notes and past Homeworks to do well on tests. She isn't phenomenal and she's not bad. Also keep doing pieces of the final project as you finish Homeworks 5-7.

The class is really cool. Katie is a super nice and amazing teacher. (btw people refer her to Katie). She will try her best to help you succeed. The end project is hard, but people taking this class should be fine.
She really cares about her students. The class is tough, but you learn a lot and the skills you gain are relevant in the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Katie is a great professor and makes 333K enjoyable, despite it being an incredibly tough class. She knows her stuff and makes it evident that she really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a very nice professor but she does not spend enough time on the material and her examples in class do not help with the homework. The homework takes forever to complete even if you read the chapter and listen to the lecture. I would definitely recommend taking another professor for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Katie is awesome. Just understand all of the logic behind the homework assignments as the exams are nearly identical to the homeworks. Also, you get a double sided cheat sheet where you should primarily fill it up with screenshots of code examples. Easy A if you try.

The class wasn't hard, but not the easiest. Lectures are interesting. The professor is nice. Tests aren't super hard, but make sure to study. There are attendance checks from time to time, but still go to class because you learn a lot from the lectures.

Highly recommend taking this prof! Straightforward class, tests made sense if you came to class. Canceled almost every friday which was awesome. She gave us a study guide with everything that would be on the tests, I studied for like 2 hours and got an A on both tests. Attendance optional but lectures were very helpful and short.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I retained a lot through this class. The tests are very straightforward as long as you go to the lectures. Attendance is "required" but she does randomized attendance checks like once a month and cancels friday class often!

Instructions are kind of all over the place, but it doesn't really matter cause there aren't a lot of assignments. Homework is minimal, and the teacher is honestly such a chiller. Heavy on lectures, but the class is only 45 minutes so it's manageable.

Class is a guided discussion as opposed to lectures. Know this going in. It is necessary to participate a little bit, but if you do the readings, you should have no problem doing so. No exams, they are replaced by an timed essay in class. Grading on it was not incredibly difficult however, and it proved to be a great and insightful class.

Professor is very knowledgeable about the subject, but the readings are not always very easy. You don't have to pay for a textbook for the course. Readings are on canvas. You'll also have to watch movies for class. Her feedback does help you build skills for writing and gaining confidence in the college setting. Grading seemed quite lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor is passionate about the subject, but there are a lot of reading and many are complex. That said, readings all together made up the best course packet of any course I've had at UT. You're also required to watch movies for class. Attendance and participation count. Professor is caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor is fair and cares deeply about her subject. There are a lot of readings and films you'll have to watch for class, but grading is lenient. Sets the bar high for course content. Attendance is required for the grade. Students self-assess part of the participation grade. I'd take one of her courses again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures were super boring and felt like she would just ramble and write random things on the whiteboards. There were a ton of readings and questions that didn't always align with what we were doing in class. Exams weren't too hard though. The class overall wasn't that bad but pretty time-consuming and kinda boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory which are quite honestly boring, but most of the content is learned there with the other part of the content learned by the constant journal entry assignments. Speaking of those, there is so much reading that goes with this class, which I would not expect of an elective class. The professor is chill and nice though honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's very nice and seems to really care about the students in her class, and is passionate about the subject. BUT there is SO MUCH reading + 2 journal entries every week, so be prepared to read. This class/ her lectures are pretty unorganized and all over the place, which made the exams more daunting (but the exams weren't as hard as I expected).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There are multiple readings assigned each week. While the instructor attempts to keep them minimal, there is a lot of material included. Exams can be a bit challenging due to unclear instructions, and it can be difficult to know the best way to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Gutierrez for ANS 335 Animals in Asia, and it was a free A. Quite a bit of reading, but the grades for them are free. 2 short papers which are graded extremely leniently. Friendly classroom environment, very nice professor. Content was much more philosophy based than I thought it was going to be and many of the readings were very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful lady with a wonderful heart, and I would take her if the course was actually shorter than the tests, which last for around two hours and include a large number of open-ended questions that must be written. Do better with the curriculum Yoga professors!

Class is confusing and feels unorganized; it's hard to keep track of what we're covering and what you should take away. Prof accepts late work, which is nice. Class attendance is based half on instapolls and half on a self-grade given at the end of the semester. Class is generally okay, exam requires you to do the readings, which there are tons of.

She gave a lot of readings throughout the semester. Some were easy reads, but most were very lengthy. There were only a few bigger writing assignments and some shorter reading reflections for completion. She isn't a tough grader, but she is a bit more stingy about full points on graded assignments. The class is good for flags and UGS credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof is very enthusiastic about the topic and always ready to help. Grading guidelines are often vague and inconsistent. The course is mostly reading and analyzing papers, many of which are long and confusing. The class is not easy for a UGS, and I would not recommend taking it if you don't need the flags.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gutierrez is a fantastic professor, enthusiastic about her niche field - Asian Environmental Humanities. Wrote 3-4 papers during the semester, graded so leniently the class was practically a completion grade. The material generally was thought provoking, but discussion was often dry and esoteric, and readings lengthy. Recommend for easy flags.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy is literally the goat best prof in the whole department easily super chill and a good lecturer take this class. Best lab I've taken in undergrad!
Dr. McDonald is the GOAT

I liked this lab! The format was recently changed, so many things were a bit of trial and error, but it's really clear how much he cares about us learning skills applicable outside of this course. Graded mostly on a few quizzes, mid semester report, and final report + lab performance. Very hands on, and I really enjoyed coming to lab!
Love Dr. McDonald. Knows his stuff!! Great lab. Not stressful, but I learned so much and was able to apply it to my other biochem/molecular classes.

Dr.McD is honestly so sweet. Although he can be a little sassy at times but he tries really hard to sure we have everything in order to do well in this course. His lectures are also very helpful. Dr.McDonald honestly is such a chill guy and he deserves the world.

Dr. McDonald does a great job making sure we're prepared for labs. He truly cares about student success and gives good feedback and opportunities to make up points. Overall super enjoyable and useful lab class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was really well structured!! It's not as time consuming as you might think, lecture isn't mandatory. Dr. McDonald is really nice and depending on your TA, grading is really chill. Lots of writing but not unmanageable. Plus the experiments are highkey fun and techniques are useful to learn.

Dr. Gene McDonald is an amazing professor who works extremely hard everyday to ensure his students are receiving the best possible biochemistry lab education that they can. The course is structured very well, and the experimental proposal is crucial in developing the necessary skills for graduate school and professional careers; I highly recommend.

An expert in his field. He's very reasonable if you have to miss class, but he does take attendance very often. There is a ArcGIS lab exercise due every week, detailed steps given. Lab attendance required. Short quiz checks on lecture materials. 1 big group project. Super chill guy for how much work he has published and done in the industry.

Dr. Mai is incredibly knowledgeable about GeoAI and, importantly, makes it accessible to those new to the field. His course is well-structured to gradually ramp up to complex reading material, and he is very patient and eager to break down every aspect of the topic for a clear, intuitive explanation.

Dr. Mai is very well-known in the GeoAI fields, and he has strong records in publication and industry collaboration. I'd say you took his class is something you could put on a resume. However his lectures were hard and the labs were unforgiving. Take lots of notes during lecture, and beware of attendance checks at the start of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Graduate-level seminar course, with 2–3 papers each week. The readings are challenging but comprehensive, covering a broad range of topics the GeoAI. Gengchen is very knowledgeable and always willing to help. He has great expertise in geospatial modeling and always provides valuable suggestions for my research projects

Dr. Mai's lectures are clear and easy to follow. Assignments are manageable because each one comes with detailed, step-by-step instructions. The course final is a project presentation, undergraduates present in groups, graduate students present individually.

Madame Haesen is a fantastic professor. She cares a lot about all of her students, and makes the class very easy to understand. It is a hybrid class, so it is a commitment to show up in person having done the readings and assignments prior to class. Strongly reccomend, don't be scared if you need to take it for a language requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Fantastic teacher, best one that I have had so far at UT. She is incredibly caring and understanding while still giving amazing feedback on assignments. I learned so much French from her, and she made everything so easy to understand without making the class TOO easy. 110% would recommend.

She is so kind and a great teacher. The class is overall easy, especially if you have done French in the past; it basically reviews what you've previously learned. She is super accessible, helpful, and willing to accommodate. There are hw and weekly quizzes, but they both only take max 30 min to do/study for. The tests are not too bad either.

Dr. Haesen is super caring. She provides feedback on how to improve on your pronunciation and grammar while providing positive feedback on your responses. I had her for FR406 & FR407, I wish she teaches FR412K. The only thing I disliked was the amount of work (about 8-10 assignments due per week) which are simple but SUPER time consuming. Take her!

F601C (Spring 25). One of the best professors at UT! This course was truly designed for beginners and she made everything approachable and engaging. Her teaching style made class enjoyable and exciting. Class went by fast. Could not recommend enough!

I love Madame Haesen. She was my first French professor, and the class was my favorite. Enjoyable and engaging activities, and she truly cares about each of her students and is not a harsh grader. I learned so much in this class, highly highly recommend.
Professor Haesen is truly amazing. One of the best French professors at UT. She cares for her students and is great at explaining the French language.
Love her. She is very supportive and her lectures are so clear.

Unless you work in a lab, this is a wasted time class. She does not have any practical experience, and it shows. She does demand a lot from students making it impossible to have a nice academic experience. Please bring experienced professionals from Houston. UT is too expensive to make us learn from inexperienced people. She is nice, though.

Professor Heidari is the GOAT of PGE professors at UT Austin. She is great at lecturing and handling examples you will see on homework and tests. I am not a morning person yet I was able to remember what she taught more than the other professor who taught this class. She is easily a 10/10 professor and I can't praise her enough.
She was teaching Advanced Petrophysics for the first time. She is well equipped with the topic and always helpful inside and outside of the class. During the classes, she was very student-friendly.

really fun guy, makes history engaging and clearly loves the subject. going to lectures is definitely necessary, but as long as you do the tests aren't too bad. he's a good lecturer, would take his class again.
Such a fun guy. Really great class, can tell he is passionate about his job. Would totally take again.

Tests are reasonable and easy if you go to lectures and pay attention. Readings are light, you're not tested hard on them. Prof is pretty engaging and funny during lectures, tries to make things interesting, relatable, and relevant. A bit hard to understand because of heavy Australian accent but not a detriment. His class is very test-heavy though.

Dr. Horewood is a wonderful professor. His passion for history shines in this class (HIS 315K: United States History, 1492–1865), creating intriguing lectures that help one navigate the nuanced stories of US History. Also, he makes his lectures incredibly concise and emphasizes all of the key information, further helping one succeed in his class.
The things she says in lecture are beyond belief. Not what you should be paying for, she's there to trick you not help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She uses pictures during her lectures and writes all over them and it was very unorganized I would often be left confused. She speaks in a riddle. You could ask her a yes or no question and you will walk away very confused. She provides old exams as review, but they aren't very helpful.

Was very clear that she was passionate about biology, but knowing everything doesn't necessarily make her a good teacher; she would get mad a lot in class at the students, and definitely gave off an air that she didn't care or was there because she had to be. Overall, lectures were pretty boring and the class wasn't engaging. Material was easy tho.

Says that students shouldn't become doctors because she doesn't believe in being premed, wants you to fail so bad she'll put "hypotonic" and "hypnotonic" as answers on the final to try and trick you, even if you know the material, poor lectures, often crashes out, overall pretty sad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: you can get an a but not because of her. the ugca slides will be the most helpful. she just uses pictures and talks about them, and it is very hard to follow. she tries to trick you in lecture and on exams.   she says she does this to get you to improve and develop study/test taking skills, but she's the only professor who's made me rage like this.

Sometimes being in this class feels like I'm being punked. She's clearly very passionate but randomly gets angry at the class and goes on rants. That said, the tests were not THAT difficult. As long as you study, you'll be fine, and the UGCA's are a great resource for what you do and don't need to know.
