The 311D final was tough, but 311C's was worse. Ignore her lectures and study everything.Weekly TA reviews helped a lot, and Asthma the UGCA was AMAZING (she's graduated now).Good luck!

I took Fritz in the Fall for Bio 311C, so I knew how her midterms were structured. I started skipping lectures because she would honestly go on a ramble and I barely learned anything. The only reason why I still got an A in the class was because of the TA's, discussion sections, and review sessions. You get tons of extra credit which is nice.

Okay the final was a bit tough, but honestly nothing THAT difficult imo. Sure there was a tricky question here and there but most of it was stuff that was covered or simple concepts. Im sure the 12% STRAIGHT POINT more than covered any unfair Qs. Lectures were a bit confusing. Overall good prof, funny lectures, easy midterms, tough final, W TAs.

Tests were mostly straightforward, all free response. Lectures felt scattered so I struggled to learn in class, however TA review sessions were very beneficial. She likes to trick rather than test knowledge. She gives a lot of extra credit through tests. Read the textbook! She takes quiz and homework questions straight from the book. She's ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Reviews are a bit harsh, yes the final was unbelievably hard and not fair for the students (Since it didn't cover what we were told to study). Though, if you look past that, she was genuinely a good and engaging professor who cared about her students. If not for that final, she would've been a 5/5 for sure, but to say she's a 1/5 is blasphemous.

Funny professor who stays engaged with her students, and gives midterms based on what she taught (Learning objectives). But I can say the same about that final, as it had nothing to do with what she wanted us to go over. Fritz made that final less about comprehension and more about confusing you and it showed. She is great, but beware of that final

Good professor, I enjoyed her funny lectures and overall vibe! I wish that she was less tricky on exams, although they weren't that difficult, there were always 10 points that you could miss because of a tricky question. Final exam was pretty bad, not what anyone expected though. Easy to get an A though. Get to know TAs, they're really helpful!!

Honestly crazy that I was considering her to be one of my better professors. Throughout the year, the exams were straightforward and genuinely over what she taught. Yet, we took the final and it had NOTHING to do with what she told us to study. Positive and negative feedback loops? Fritz prides herself on tricking test takers and she was successful

I had no issue with her before today. But after that final, I've lost all respect. The test wasn't just tough, it was unnecessarily tricky. None of the questions felt fair, and some weren't even relevant to what we studied. Maybe she wanted to even out class averages after the high test scores. Regardless, grade ruined bc of a horrible final.

Dr. Fritz was a great prof and a big improvement on my previous bio prof. Very funny and lecture slides are helpful. And exams are only 30% of your grade with abundant extra credit. I do wish she was more clear about what exams would cover and practice questions but as long as you keep up with homework and quizzes, you'll do fine

Her teaching style was solid until the final. It felt like the exam was less about testing knowledge and more about tricking us. The questions were obscure and honestly didn't reflect the content we covered. It left me mentally drained and frustrated, definitely an unfair way to test students. She'll excuse the difficulty with a five point curve ig

She promised that 60% of the final would focus on genetics, but that wasn't true. In reality, the majority of the exam had little to do with what she said it would. It was misleading and left many of us unprepared. The final felt like a bait-and-switch, and it completely undermined our trust in her exam promises. Amazing professor until the final.

You can tell Dr. Fritz has a genuine passion for biology, which is reflected in her teaching and energy. Before the final, I would have given her a higher rating and an easier difficulty. Everything else in the class, including midterms, was very doable and straightforward. The final, however, was difficult and had random (trick) questions.

Had high hopes for her, but that final was a joke. I'd give her a 5/5 before, but after today, no chance. The exam was filled with random, hard-to-answer questions that didn't reflect what we studied. It felt like she was trying to trick us rather than assess our knowledge. Her test strategy completely ruined my view of her as a professor.

311d with Fritz was pretty easy and had a very light workload. that being said, i felt that dr. fritz's "teaching" methods were ineffective and i had to rely on TAs/UGCAs and self-teach to understand content. the TAs/UGCAs were life saving though and i definitely learned a ton from them

Absolutely love Dr. Fritz! She is so passionate about biology and truly cares about her students. Just a heads-up: her tests are not multiple choice — expect fill-in-the-blank, labeling, drawing, or short explanations. Personally, I think this is way better than multiple choice and not overly difficult. Study guides are a bit time consuming.

Dr. Fritz is the best professor that I've taken at UT thus far! Her class can be tough but as long as you put in effort and attend lecture as well as discussion sections you will be fine. Exams can be difficult as they are all opened ended, but partial credit is award as well as built in extra credit! She cares for students. Take her if you can!

SO UNDERATED!! This class is pretty test heavy, but her lectures are great with her covering exactly what will be on the exam. She assigns a good amount of assignments out of class but they are fairly easy and you can knock them out in an hour or so. Some of the TA's arnt great so if you find one you like make sure you attend their discussion!

Love Dr. Fritz genuinely best professor I've had so far, I had her last semester too for Bio 311C and I couldn't have been happier. The tests are free response format allowing for partial credit. If you pay attention in the lectures and take notes you'll be good for the tests. Super fair grader and enjoyable lectures. Highly recommend her class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A lot of people complain about her on rmp but the class is set up for you to get an A without much studying. Of course you need to do your homework assignments but they're usually easy and based off the lecture slides. There's 3 midterms that are very fair in my opinion, usually frq's but not too complicated. Tells you everything you need to know.

She literally yaps every single class. Her exams are free response with like 2 MCQs, all are worded vaguely. It's chill to get the A cause of the extra credit and her assignments, but I have spent an insane amount of time screaming at her in my head.

Professor Fritz is super nice and wants to help you learn the material. The class isn't hard, and extra credit is embedded into the exams. People complain about her not being clear on what will be on exams, but she literally hints at it in class and gives us plenty of resources to do well. If you take this class and try, you'll get an A.

She gives 10% extra credit on ALL exams and is a lenient grader. She can be really inspiring but can also be a bit sassy. Anyone who complains about her courses will not survive pre-med, easiest STEM class ever. The best study strategy is to review the TA Exam Reviews for each unit. I dosed off in class, didnt read textbook and got perfect grades.

I took her for 311C/D and honestly she's fine.I never attended discussion and it was not that bad.311C is more work with the study guides but they were completion. She was moody in 311C but she seemed to love 311D and the class had less busy work.Exams are hard but there's a TON of built in extra credit and i needed like 30 on both finals for an A.

It's hard to understand what Fritz wants from you when you study for the midterms; the reviews can be ambiguous. She teaches with passion but she tends to ramble about plants. However, she is thorough and her TAs are great at condensing her lectures for exams. Not a bad prof but I would explore my options.

TAs are the actual professor. My personal experience was setting up a private meeting with her to discuss how to do better in her class as I was at a B+ at the time. She was condescending and bragged about how many students dropped her class then told me I should drop her class instead of actual feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I made the mistake of taking her class as a non-pre-med/non-major student. Her tests are detail-oriented and her lectures are basically an info dump (mostly because of how the course is structured). She's kind of funny and is passionate about biology. If you want to be prepared for harder bio classes, consider taking her. If not, avoid taking her.
She gives really good lectures, and is always willing to answer any questions after class.

The tests are all on paper, you need your student ID, not a single MCQ, and no questions during the tests. Her lectures are funny and she is nice. The discussion section is important and the lecture is too but not mandatory. There's not that much homework. Chances of a good grade if you don't study for test are low.

The class grading criteria makes it easy to get an A. Workload is a little bit more intense that it should be. Lots of homework and quizzes and not to mention the long study guides. She rambles a lot in her lectures. Her tests are pretty doable. She has lots of extra credit. Overall, put in the work and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class grading criteria makes it easy to get an A. Workload is a little bit more intense that it should be. Lots of homework and quizzes and not to mention the long study guides. She rambles a lot in her lectures. Her tests are pretty doable. She has lots of extra credit. Overall, put in the work and you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Even understanding the material inside and out it is extremely hard to do well in this class. The test are not based off the information you learn and the lectures are confusing. I didn't learn any material from them and had to teach it all to myself. Professor is also not very responsive and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures were so boring and hard to follow. I would often times leave wondering what she even talked about the entire time. A lot of assignments given every week that were pretty unnecessary like study guides every week that were 10+ pages. She also has random mood swings and will start yelling at the class.

Rambles in lectures and has a short temper. But, pay attention in that rambling as she mentions VERY small things that will be on the test. A lot of Canvas HW that are super long but really helpful for retaining info as lectures are eh. I will say that the grading is really lenient and she gives out a good amount of extra credit. Easy to get an A.

I don't really know what to say about this course because I never understood a thing that happened in lecture and the tests were completely foreign to what was covered in lecture. It's not a hard class but Dr. Fritz isn't the best lecturer and switches from very sweet to hostile very quickly. Also, no laptops in class.

Just a senile lady who only talks about F1 and sugar free red bull and not the actual class. Lectures are confusing and not helpful. Childish and rude. The only saving grace is the amount of extra credit she provides in her exams which are essentially meant to trick the student. Easy if you took AP BIO.

Does Dr. Fritz give more busy work compared to other 311C? Yes, but it makes the test count for less. Studying can be a little confusing as it's not super clear what is tested. However, the test have built in extra credit, which evens out when she throws a tough question. I would take her again. She loves bio and wants you to do well.

If can be avoided, do not take Fritz. Unless you are coming in with a very solid understanding of bio, you are screwed. Ungodly amount of assignments weekly (def the heaviest workload of 311C), with frequent study guides over 20 pages long. Her test questions were intentionally tricky & hard to predict. She yells at the class and crashes out often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so confusing and she assumes you already know all of the content. So if you took AP Bio and remember everything, maybe this class would be easy. Her tests are very hard because she tests you on the tiniest details. Online work is easy, which is very helpful in bringing your grade up.

Dr Fritz was often scattered and disorganized throughout her lectures. I barely learned anything during class and would have to use other resources to understand the content. Her midterms are free response and were very tricky and confusing. The amount of assignments you get weekly are insane. Overall, take her at your own risk.

I honestly loved Dr.Frtiz!! The workload was massive but I felt like I learned Bio. I especially liked her teaching style because she taught in a way that helped me make a connection between the material and the real world. If you were to ask me if I would choose to take her class again...I would say yes. she is v quickwitted.. keep that in mind.

I don't know what happened this semester but truly everyone I have talked to in my class has had the same negative experience as me. You will spend most of your time trying to complete her crazy amount of assignments per week you won't have time to comprehend the material. Also her midterms are HAR

Absolutely terrible. You aren't allowed to ask any questions on the final despite multiple typos and mistakes. Way too much homework and quizzes-plus she's off topic all the time. I only got a good grade because there's built in extra credit. I'd still avoid her if you're pre-med/pre-health. You won't learn a thing.

Honestly, RUN. She'd spend ten minutes of lecture complaining. Most complaints were about the exams and the professor being mean to everyone. She told our class to "stfu" during the end of lecture, completely losing all respect. Her exams are hard and there's a lot of homework. I'm taking again because I was assigned her, not because I want to.

ALL SHE DOES IS TALK ABOUT HER SUGAR FREE RED BULL AND F1! HER LECTURES ARE SO SCATTERED AND THE CLASS IS OVERALL UNORGANZIED! HER MIDTERMS ARE HARD FOR NO REASON BECAUSE SHE TRIES TO TRICK YOU WITH CONFUSING WORDING! I ALWAYS THOUGHT I UNDERSTOOD THE MATERIAL UNTIL I GOT MY GRADE BACK! THERE ARE LIKE SEVEN ASSIGNMENTS DUE EACH WEEK! PLZ AVOID HER

Take into account what everyone is saying. RUN. Maybe it is just our semester, but she was always on one. She lost my respect immediately when she decided to throw a tantrum and said to the class 'tell your neighbors to stfu.' I'm not kidding, those were her words. It's not hard to get a good grade if you get enough points from the insane workload.

Take someone else. She was often mean. Only reason I got a good grade is because I put ungodly effort outside of class to get good grades on all the assignments. WHICH ARE A LOT. Midterms are unpredictable no matter how much you study. I asked a question once after class and she degraded and belittled me. I considered transferring because of her.

This class is too tough with the midterms all being difficult free response and the final NOT being online/open notes anymore. For this type of class an open notes and take home final was vital to having students be successful. Now, I'm not even sure I want to be at this school. We deserve to have the final online like previous years
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: At first in this semester I actually wrote a positive review for her. However, she has been horrible since. I prepare over 40 hours for each midterm, and they are still unpredictable. Each midterm is about 7 questions free response. Questions are often not what was covered. Attended every discussion, review, etc. by far the worst class at UT

Do not take her. The tests are so hard & she does not prepare you for them, they are purposefully made to trick you. There are weekly quizzes that are also very hard. She assigns so much homework. She also gets angry really fast & is not willing to make accommodations. The lectures were pointless but attendance was required

she is terrible at making tests, they have maybe 10% of the stuff you studied because there is barely any questions. she's quick to get an attitude and acts like a child throwing a tantrum sometimes when people talk or have a laptop out. i did like her lectures and the amount of hw/material she gave but i would not take her again.

Her lecture style isn't great, she doesn't explain or teach things and just talks about topics as if you already know what they are. If you didn't take AP bio you will have a really really really hard time. If you did take AP bio which I did , you will still have a hard time.

Professor Fritz is a very caring person ... outside of class. In individual meetings she was very accommodating  and understanding that students don't always have great days. Pros: extra credit built into tests and weekly review sessions (GO TO THEM) Cons: HW heavy, rambling lectures, ambiguous test questions.

Terrible at lecturing, tends to ramble, and is very moody. She talks about not wanting to baby students like they're in high school but pauses to lectures about student behavior every time she sees or hears something she doesn't like. You must pay $12 for a "square cap" to answer Q's in class + attendance. DO NOT TAKE. Pros: TA's and +5 on midterms

Lots of HW. Tests mostly open ended and HARD, but extra credit is built into tests (65 points possible but graded out of 60). Prof rambles and expects u to know material, almost belittles students. I would take another bio professor if possible. Go to review sessions and KNOW ur material as the tests are tricky and use confusing wording.
Dont take this class you WILL REGRET IT

I would not say she is a bad professor but there are 100% better to take, her midterms seemed like more a trick than most tests that genuinely test your knowledge. I felt like I knew the material really well but could not perform well with how her questions were worded. Def try to take someone else if you have the option!!

A lot of material tested or on quizzes are not in lecture or modules, they're mostly in the textbook. All exams are 90% free response. In total, it's a lot of work. Go to review sessions, the SI sessions also help as well. She is a good person and has made me excited about bio, it's just more difficult than what I hear about other bio professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were hard to follow along and she rambles most of the time, but there's extra credit built into the tests, so it isn't hard to get an A. The tests are hard though and there is SO MUCH homework (Canvas modules, masting bio, quizzes, study guide, studying). Def the most hw out of all my classes. Quizzes are hard. Go to the review sessions

Nice lady, but okay professor. Passionate but rambles and gets behind/ doesn't cover all content equally. Very visual based. Tests have partial credit but are mainly open ended and very confusing. Very workload heavy. Not super hard to get decent grade but I don't feel like I've actually learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has made the test so much harder. Please don't take this class with her.

I would not recommend Fritz to any future bio students. Her exams are majority open ended FRQ questions, and she has increased the difficultly of the exams from past years. Compared to the other bio professors, she gives far more homework out of class (learning modules, textbook assignments, quizzes, 15-28 page study guides, etc.).
Horrible talks about anything but the subject matter
She seems very prepared and knowledgeable. She makes it exciting to learn about biology. I am look forward to learning from her this year for the first bio in fall and second in spring!

Worst professor at UT. Will belittle students and go on rants about Freshmen acting like high schoolers in the middle of lecture. Seems really nice at first but is actually mean. Does not care if student's get behind. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF NO MATTER WHAT

Professor Fritz is engaging and makes the material enjoyable. While the midterms can be challenging, her clear expectations and study guides are very helpful. Using unstuckstudy ai alongside the lecture slides helped me prepare effectively for exams.
I hate her all she does is do random rants and doesn't teach

This prof is super relatable. She's pretty nice and tests are kind of the same format as AP exams. MAKE SURE YOU GO TO DISCUSSION AND PAY ATTENTION. Most of the tests are pretty concept based, but fair. You can also take quizzes with friends, but that doesn't mean they're easy! Tests are easier than the quizzes
Shes awsome

Dr. Fritz includes a lot of opportunities for extra credit, so it's easy to get a good grade in her class. However, some of her lectures could be vague and homework was more helpful for understanding content. She is very clear about expectations and the study guides she provides are a good reflection of exam difficulty. Laptops aren't allowed.
LOVED FRITZ! Always had amazing lectures. The midterms are a bit tricky but you will be okay if you study.

Professor Fritz was okay. I'm still not over her calling me out one time for not getting the iclicker question right tho (after asking if I got it and me saying yes but I was def zoning out bc it was very easy to do so). She frequently gave inspirational talks which are def memorable for the freshman brain. She is more than fair on test grading.

I genuinely think Fritz is your best bet for 311C. Lectures can be slow and off-topic, but you learn all you need to know from modules and lecture slides are online. Fritz is hilarious and made going to class enjoyable. Tests are short and easy if you study (recommend looking at TA notes). She provides extra points that make a huge difference.
Awesome professor and TAs! Midterms can be tricky but if you do the work, you'll be good. No electronics ex: tablets.
Great professor and cares a lot about student's well-being! Also, all the TAs were amazing, but specifically Ryan and Cade were 10/10!

Dr.Fritz is absolutely amazing! She is the best bio professor and explains very thoroughly! The only prior knowledge of biology I've had has been from freshman year biology of HS. Trust me, anyone can get an A! The lectures and slides are most important for exams. She is also genuine, funny, and always making the class laugh!

Funny and has an upbeat attitude. Rambles a bit sometimes and made following along hard. I mostly learned by reviewing the lecture slides. Has an e-textbook for homework and readings, but I never did the readings, mostly just went over the lecture slides and would be fine. Has weekly optional review sessions that are helpful and recommend going to.

Dr. Fritz is one of my favorite professors I've had. Her lectures are easy to understand, and she's very funny and engaging. The teaching team and reviews with Ryan saved my studying before midterms! Be sure to create a good study group for quizzes and studying. Midterms were straight-forward and a good assessment of the application of content.

the class is easy to get an A in due to the grading point system, but even as someone with a strong AP bio background and genuine interest in bio, I found her lectures to be extremely monotonous with lots of rambling. the midterms were hard and it seemed like she was trying to trick you at any moment. def don't recommend her for 311c.

Gives lots of extra credit and uses a point system to decide grading so an A is easily achievable. Quizzes were very detailed oriented and tests were fairly easy. Very sweet and a genuinely interesting person but hated her teaching style, it was hard to follow and she went over too many details.

Her class was easy to make a good grade in and she structured it to benefit students. However, I was not a fan of her teaching style and often thought that she was rambling and hard to follow. I did most of my learning through the TAs or outside resources like Khan Academy. Her exams were straight to the point and similar to the reviews.
tough class, she is pretty funny though, no electronics besides iPads!

I found her lectures to be really uninteresting and kind of boring, even though I did genuinely like the material itself. Discussion sections are super helpful, as are the reviews she gives for each midterm. Attend discussion and study the review (both the one she gives and the UGTA ones) and you'll be fine.

Wish I could have taken Fritz again for 311D because 311C was incredibly easy despite not taking AP BIo in HS. Midterms were graded out of 50 but up to 53 points and very doable, given few attempts on canvas homework and textbook, and only really challenging part were quizzes which are take home and online which she recommends doing with friends.

She wants her students to pass and will give you many opportunities to do so. Focus on her diagrams cause that's her favorite thing to test on. Overall my favorite class I took this semester but she is tough so go to class and at least study a little.

At the beginning of the semester, Dr. Fritz seemed nice and understanding but once I had a personal interaction with her, I realized she was rude and sometimes unwilling to help. As for the class itself, the quizzes were difficult but taking them in a group setting helped. The midterms were also hard, but she tells you what to study for.

Love Dr. Fritz so much! The whole teaching team was great at communicating where students were struggling and filling in/curving the gaps. You could tell that she wanted you to go into 311D with all the knowledge required and more. Super accessible, esp during office hours. Only requires 85% attendance for full credit and a super easy grader.

Dr. Fritz is very passionate and it shows. I found her class difficult to understand, but she makes it easy to get by with a good grade. Her tests are mainly all free-response and can be different from what's taught in lecture, as she values skills over memorization. If you build a relationship with her she will be kind and accommodating to you.

Go to discussions and office hours. Shoutout to Ryan he was an amazing TA. Midterms were FR and application based (can't answer the questions unless you know your shit) but final was online. Quizzes are open-note but study at least a little for them. Overall okay, there are better professors.

Dr. Fritz is super caring and wants everyone to do well in her class. Lectures are not mandatory and are recorded but I highly recommend going. Sometimes she can be a little bit vague on certain topics so be sure to read the textbook for clarity. She clearly states what you need to know for the tests so study what she says.

Although Professor Fritz looks and sounds like a good person, she is certainly not. The entire year I felt like I was on my toes whenever it came to her quiz and test questions, even though I knew the content very well. I felt like she cared more about tricking us with her questions, rather than actually testing our knowledge over the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class had me stressed throughout the year. Professor Fritz definitely has a unique testing style which takes some time to get used to. Luckily, the course is designed to give you extra credit which helps relieve some of the pressure. Although lectures and the readings helped introduce concepts, the TAs helped in learning content.

Dr. Fritz cares about her students and her lectures are entertaining with discussions. There is a bit of homework to do online as she follows a flipped classroom teaching style.
She also puts a lot of emphasis on learning how to learn with her ELP activities.

Generally, assignments were easy with exception to the open-resource quizzes.

Dr. Fritz is kind and compassionate towards her students. The test are very similar to the discussion activities, so be sure to attend those. She is reasonable about grades, and most of the exam expectations are described in lecture prior to test day. Overall she is a good choice for 311c imo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz was a great professor, her lectures can get boring but she sometimes pops jokes out of nowhere. Her exams are all application based so you need to know the topics. The Canvas hw and discussions are great resources for exam studying. The quizzes are open resource so it's best to have friends in the class who you can work with.

Semi-easy A. Forgiving grading & easy points. A lot of this class is teaching yourself because Dr. Fritz's lectures are not that helpful. But, she's very kind & knowledgeable and will help you tremendously in office hours (so go!). Teaching team is also great! Weekly review sessions.

Professor Fritz is such a kind soul! I really loved talking with her and asking her questions because she is so caring and welcoming to her students. Lectures can be repetitive at times and somewhat confusing, but prepares you for tests well. Pretty easy class as long as you pay attention and work a little for the A. Her TA's are also so helpful!

Great class, the lectures can be confusing and repetitive at times but Fritz is funny and does a good job of keeping people engaged. Attendance is mandatory but taken through i-Clicker and curved heavily (you can miss a few days of class and still get an A). Her grading policy is clear and makes it much easier to earn an A in the class.

I truly don't believe that I took any knowledge away from this class. Her lectures are extremely tedious, full of rants, and she teaches her own version of biology that contradicts online sources and textbooks. Her canvas page is incredibly disorganized and she will trick you into spending $50 on an iclicker that you can just use an app for.

She writes her long/complicated syllabus in comic sans, if that isn't enough of a red flag idk what is.  But actually... she is awful.  Random tirades/rants in class, ambiguous grading policy, and teaches you nothing.  10/10 recommend taking someone else for 311C.

Fritz is a nice professor but the lectures are tedious. There are a lot of homework assignments and external learning assignments that keep your grade up if you don't do well on exams. My biggest advice is to do extra learning outside of class and read the learning outcomes for midterms. Also, go to the discussions; that's where you'll understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Fritz has great resources for learning the material inside and outside the classroom. Discussion sections and Supplemental Instruction meetings are really helpful too. Weekly quizzes/homework assignments make the material manageable and digestible. Exams are all free response but practice exams have a good outline of the material tested.
Dr. Fritz was kind and taught us a lot. She is easy to reach and would definitely take her again.

Professor Fritz is one of the best professors I've had at UT. She is extremely clear about what to expect for exams and quizzes so as long as you pay attention you will be fine. I personally put minimal effort into this class and still got an A. Just make sure you understand any major topics discussed in class & go to office hours for help!

I did the Maymester in Nice, France and it was a 10/10 experience. You can do no wrong by going on this trip for this class. The content was demonstrated with real-life experiences, it was easy to pass the class and still learn at the same time, and it was basically a month-long vacation with my now closest friends. Dr. Fritz is so caring and kind.

Had her for 311C and 311D. Overall it's easy to get an A in her class. Everything except the midterms are open-note, and I got an A w/ just going to class + review sessions and w/o using textbook to study. Her midterm questions are pretty vague tho, and TAs often had to clarify questions during the test even if Fritz insisted they're well-written
I think she would rather be a biochem or chemistry professor rather than straight up biology but she was still good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very caring and has a bit of a quirky personality which is great. Lectures are very engaging as she wants you to learn and be prepared.She does reviews the lecture before test that cover pretty much exactly what will be on the test. Test averages are pretty high and the final(and quizzes) are open note where you can work with peers as well.

Dr Fritz is a really fun prof and she clearly cares a lot about bio, especially plants. The tests are all free response but weekly quizzes and the final are online and open book. She is really helpful if you ask questions in class and the weekly TA review sessions are incredibly helpful especially before a test. GO TO THEM.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Fritz is a fun and understanding professor. Her lectures are easy to follow, and if you choose to read the textbook, she outlines exactly what you need to read. Everything is open-note except for the midterms. The midterms are all free response and mostly conceptual. It's more important to understand application than memorize fine details

Fritz is the gold standard of bio professors, take her class if you get the chance. material is interesting and in depth. grade depends on exam scores mostly, but exams are very fair and give clear objectives of what to know for them. quizzes can be tricky but not bad, most content is open note except exams. exams are all FR but don't be scared

Personally I didn't really like her teaching style. Exams aren't too bad and are application based but I felt her lectures were very surface level and I don't feel like I retained or really learned anything from her class. Very easy to get an A but I'm worried about not knowing enough fundamentals for my upper division classes.

Dr. Fritz was an amazing professor! Her grading criteria was clear, and the class wasn't test-heavy. The exams were very application-based, which encouraged comprehension and not memorization, and she always took the time to make helpful reviews for each of them. Her lectures were also very engaging. 10/10 would recommend to 311C/D students!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Study the topics that are on the review heavily and quickly review everything else and you should make an A on every test. I made the mistake of not memorizing a table for one test, which single handedly earned me a 68 on that test. Few questions, but easy if you study right. Take the quizzes seriously, they add up. Overall great professor.

Dr. Fritz does a great job on making Intro Biology relatively easy. She gives you a lot of resources and is tricky with her questions, but once you're a student of hers for a little it comes naturally to you. 311C and D are by no means difficult if you go to lecture and put in some time in discussion or review sessions. Really good TA team as well

Dr. Fritz really cares about her students and makes sure to make all assignments easy to manage. She gives extra credit which really improves your grade and grades on a scale that is easy to pass. Dr. Fritz has an amazing TA team and tries to maintain fairness for everyone. If you need help going to office hours or discussion is your best bet.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz was amazing and took into consideration students' feelings. There are 3 midterms and an online final that consists of two parts but you can take it whenever you want and use your resources. The midterms are not multiple choice but short answer/fill-in-the-diagrams which were usually pretty easy. Go to office hours or discussion for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fritz was alright, I had no serious problems with her. She moved pretty fast through lectures, so be sure to pay attention. There is a textbook, but I was able to make it through the semester without reading it that often. However, she gives a lot of extra points, which brought my grade up a lot. I'm taking her for 311D as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is an amazing professor! Her clear grading criteria (point-based system) provides you with outline to follow throughout the semester. There are 3 midterms, each of which are open response- but they all are fairly easy if you study the material. The homework and small quizzes make up a majority of your grade (+plus lots of extra credit!)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she offers so much extra credit that it makes it easy to get a good grade. Just do all the homework and quizes and study the lecture ppts and midterm review for the midterms. there were 3 midterms that were frq, but it was more like filling in diagrams and answering short questions. Final was online. point-based, so just get as many as you can.

My favorite professor this semester! Also somewhat of an easy A but you also do learn the material, for sure. You have to study to understand some harder content but Dr. Fritz makes it clear what she wants you to know and learn for tests vs. quizzes. So many easy points to earn in this class. Tests are 5 FR questions so I loved that too.

This class honestly grew on me throughout the semester. Dr. Fritz gives out so much extra credit and as long as you do the homework and study guides youll do just fine on the test and class in general. Her lectures can be confusing but the resources and UGTA review sessions make it easy to get a A in this class.

She often gets on tangents in lectures and falls behind schedule, but she is very clear about what will be on exams. Exams are free response, short answer, which were harder for me. However, her 500 point grading system means with an okay grade on the final and the exams, you can still easily obtain an A. It's not a super stress heavy class.

SO CARING! Clear that she cares about her students and is trying to set them up for success for genetics.  I didn't do great on 2/3 of the midterms and still ended with an A because of her 500 point system! CLEAR WHAT SHE WANTS!! Study the "skills tested" she lists out before the test! Diagrams are her favorite.

Dr. Frtiz is a very charismatic professor. I would say her lectures covered more than you needed to know ,but the UGTA 2 hour review sessions solidified what material was actually important for the exams. Exams are all FRQ but only 10 percent of the grade + theres a lot of extra credit / drops that helped me get an A!

Fritz is funny. Sit towards the front to get to know her. The tests are difficult, but easier if you attend all the TA reviews. The quizzes are tough because of the time limit. There is enough room for error in this course and my poor performance in the very beginning didn't hurt me terribly in the end, which is important for an intro level course.
Her lectures are interesting and quite sporadic. Exams are on the easier side if you attend the UGTA reviews. Should be a relatively easier A

Fritz is nice but I didn't really like her teaching style. The quizzes are hard and the 3 exams are really conceptual. The tests are all FRQ and you have to really understand the material to do well. There's a lot of HW too. There's a ton of extra credit and Fritz can be lenient tho. You just have to put in effort to make an A.

Dr. Fritz is a very interesting professor, but I ended up enjoying her class in the end. She tells you exactly what is going to be on her exams which is great. However, there is a lot of homework and her quizzes can be quite difficult. She grades through a point system which allows you to make a pretty good grade pretty easily.
Very great professor. She is kind and caring. I would say there's a lot of homework but I would take her class again as the tests are easy if you full end the content being taught.

Dr. Fritz is a very caring professor. The tests are very conceptual so you really have to understand the material. Her class is set up so that there are many, many ways to up your grade with extra credit, surveys, etc. You definitely have to put in the work, but it's relatively easy to get a good grade in her class.
She is great at giving you the information but the subject can be overwhelming. Biology 1 has a lot of information and requires you to study everyday to get an A.

I love Dr.Fritz 10/10 she's hilarious. there's a decent amount of homework but it leads to not having to study as much cause the assignments are the studying. Love this woman, I plan to take 311d with her. Overall I didn't think the class was too hard.

She's super good at explaining concepts and the big picture, and I really enjoyed her energy! However, quizzes can be pretty tricky and midterm questions can be worded a bit more vaguely than what I would consider to be a comfortable difficulty.

Really enjoyable lectures and clearly has a deep understanding of the content. Her exams are not difficult and the TAs are nice and helpful. However, I found myself spending many hours doing homework (15-20 hours) a week. The book work in this class is VERY tedious and a lot of the information learned is not essential. Overall, a mediocre class.

Dr. Fritz is a nice person, but not a great teacher. Her tests are only over a few things when shell lecture over many things and even go on tangents. You never know whats going to be on the test because theyre not a great cumulative review of all the material. Its just what she feels. I got an A but didnt learn much. I wouldnt take.

Fritz is very passionate about her subject matter & a wonderful teacher! She offers a decent amount of extra credit on exams, which help raise your overall grade. Her exams can be difficult, but she is a fair grader. If you attend review sessions and discussions, you will do very well in her class. She also encourages group work and collaboration.
Love her teaching

I really did like Dr. Fritz as a person, and she's clearly passionate about bio, but I wasn't the biggest fan of her teaching style. The tests are really weird and are a lot more conceptual/abstract than the material you learn in class, but going to lecture helps A LOT when it comes to quizzes and tests. It's really easy to get an A though.

Fritz's quiz questions are all completely random and asks weird stuff that we were never even taught or expected to learn. Her tests are supposed to be tricky but are still somewhat fair. Her lectures are not that engaging in my opinion. Only take her if there are no other professors.

If you plan to take Dr.Fritz, don't expect to learn much from her.  Her whole class is listening to her talk about plants and memorizing a ton of diagrams. Her exams were all about labeling diagrams and weren't that challenging, but were very hard to understand what she was asking at times.

Fritz isn't clear about what'll be tested on her exams, but they were easy as long as you actually study her lecture slides. Everything you need is there. She was passionate about bio and was a caring professor. Many people complained, but she was one of the easier bio profs imo. Besides the test, the other assignments were super easy to ace.

I actually genuinely liked her as a person, but I just didn't feel like I could grasp her teaching style. The exams were constantly about labeling diagrams, but sometimes I didn't feel like it really pertained to the course. Also if you don't find botany interesting, don't take her class for 311D. The homeworks are easy A's to bump your grade tho.

Fritz has very surface level lectures, I learned way more in my high school AP bio. The tests aren't hard they're just WEIRD. All pictures/drawing, everything open ended. If you want to interpret the digestive system as 4 circles with an arrow take her class. I don't feel well prepared for future bio classes because this was so vague and thematic

This class is kinda too easy. The midterms are 3 free-response questions that are extremely surface level. If you actually want to learn in depth intro bio don't take fritz; but if you want an easy A take fritz

Dr. Fritz is super passionate about her job and the success/well-being of all of her students. She's very clear in class, and what you see in the lecture slides pretty much directly correlates to what will be on the exams. The exams are not multiple choice though, so memorizing charts and graphs is necessary.

I personally loves Dr. Fritz. I am an international student and she remembered my name when most time I only use my preferred name! She really respects every student and I absolutely love that. Class is easy to pass, I got like a 30+ / 75 in the final and still got an A, thanks for all those extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is a good person and passionate about biology. Personally, I didn't attend lectures and learned the content the day before the exam, and never had any problems. Hence, I would say her class is very easy. I like her class but I never felt challenged throughout the semester.

Professor Fritz is very passionate about biology. However, this class is quite intensive. The homework is pretty easy but the exams are open-ended and difficult and I could barely pass them even when utilizing the open-internet policy. Lots of material covered in little time. It's graded fairly, but you need to attend lectures and study often.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found Professor Fritz's class to be pretty difficult, as I did not have much background in biology. However, there are lots of built in extra credit opportunities. I thought the TA's seemed disinterested in helping students expand their knowledge.

Dr. Fritz is the best out there! SO sweet and funny. Pros: - lots of EC - straightforward quizzes and tests - lays it all down for you Cons: - I wasn't a big fan of the TA's. It felt like they didn't want to be there at all - 1 group project, if you have bad partners then you're gonna have to do it all

Dr. Fritz is really passionate about what she's teaching. However, I found the class to be incredibly homework heavy. There was so much outside work to be done in order to grasp the material effectively. Her tests were pretty easy since they were free response style questions that asked about basic concepts, and she gives A LOT of extra credit!

Fritz is a really sweet lady. If you want a pretty easy A, take Fritz. If you actually want to learn, don't take Fritz. Her teaching/tests are EXTREMELY surface level. She does a surprising amount of spoon-feeding for a college class. There's also lots of homework, which isn't bad but can be pretty time consuming during busier weeks.

Lectures were not amazing but Fritz allows for a lot of room for error. If you haven't taken AP Bio you will have a harder time. If you do the work and pay attention you will do fine. There are a lot of resources available to get a better understanding of the content. Fritz is very laid back and easy to talk to. I would recommend course.

Dr. Fritz offers plenty of extra credit throughout the semester - don't miss out on that. I barely attended class and was able to do well because of the grade cushioning built into the course. The course is relatively fast-paced, so it might be challenging if you haven't taken AP Bio. Most of the exams are based on the material on canvas (hw+quiz).

Dr. Fritz had a clear point system with weekly Canvas modules (to supplement lectures), Mastering Biology modules (which serve as the textbook), quizzes, and discussion section. She builds in a bit of extra credit, but I found her tests, which were FRQ style, very application based and pretty tough. Overall, I found it challenging to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures and easy to talk to, but there is so much to cover in this course that you *must* do a lot of reading on your own time. There are weekly quizzes and group homeworks that are *really* time consuming: I found the group projects very stressful and tedious. Make sure you do your reading: lecture isn't enough to prepare for tests/quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this class Spring 2021. The course was completely online and, to me, was an easy A. She is super sweet and cares for her students! She builds in so many extra points in the weekly quizzes, so you could get 3 questions wrong and still get the points needed for an A in the class! Group study guides leads to less overall work. TAKE FRITZ!!

AVOID HER!! Dropped after a few weeks; work was excessive and she expected a lot of prior knowledge. There were hw, quizzes, study guides, & mastering biology modules EVERY WK (difficult when taking other math/science courses). Tests were difficult, didn't match guides. TAKE BIO311C W/ DR. LATHAM she genuinely wants you to learn & amazing prof

Lecture was very good. There were weekly, time consuming study guides between 7-15ish pgs, then there were several textbook questions, Friday quizes were a bit difficult to get an A on, and the mandatory discussion sections were no help (probably bc of my TAs). There were also "experimental learning projects" that were a waste of time but required.

A lot of people love Fritz but I did not. She is a very sweet woman but all of our homework was due before she taught in class which was frustrating if you did not have a strong background in biology or have trouble teaching yourself. I also thought this class had a heavy out of class workload. We had to do homework, a quiz, and a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There are a lot of assignments in this class but it is a fairly easy class to manage if you keep up and attend/watch all her lectures. She is very caring and offers A LOT of extra credit, especially on her weekly quizzes. TA team is also really good and as long as you turn everything in and study, you can be successful in the class.

Dr. Fritz is a ball of positive energy who's clearly passionate about biology. Her quizzes are highly application based. While the MasteringBiology homework and module study guides help further your knowledge, her lectures are KEY to doing well. If you pay attention to her teaching and attend discussion reviews you won't need the textbook at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor, lecturer, and person. Made the class very engaging even though it was all virtual and genuinely cares about her. If you are pre med she will prepare you well for the mcat.

Alot like AP bio; you learn the material yourself from the textbook (quite a bit of reading) and doing the textbook and canvas problems. Lecture was mostly to reinforce/ clarify ideas, but she sometimes asked questions straight from it. Study guide and quiz questions are often similar or the same. GO TO THE UGTA SESSIONS!! Literally saved my grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr Fritz is sooo kind and enthusiastic. As for her quizzes, they are pretty tough but they are open note and she gives out a lot of extra credit. She gives you pretty heavy study guides to complete each week instead of midterms which I honestly preferred. Go to TA office hours!!! The TAs are incredible.

Anything harsh on here about her is blown way out of proportion. It was basic difficulty for a college class. If you do the study guides and genuinely understand them the quizzes arent that bad. I went to lecture maybe 5 times. I highly encourage forming a study group because thats what helped me the most.

This ranks in one of the worst college classes I've ever taken in the last 2 and a half years. She would be very passive-aggressive towards students for not understanding material which made it harder to learn. The weekly quizzes are insanely hard & the study guides & hws DON'T help. Please pick another teacher for your GPA and sanity. :)

Dr. Fritz is amazing! I'm not sure if the material would've been as "easy" if we were in person but regardless she did an amazing job of explaining the course material. However, I 100% believe the only way I was able to do well on her weekly quizzes was because of the TA's. They SAVED my grade in this class, especially the UGTA review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I LOVED DR. FRITZ!! She's so caring and funny, but her quizzes were no joke. I liked the predictability of her course (2 homework, 1 study guide, 1 quiz per week). GO TO THE UGTA REVIEWS, they were so helpful for quizzes!!! She encouraged group work to work on study guides and quizzes, but even so her quizzes were still tough. I loved the class!

Some reviews are saying that Fritz's quizzes didn't cover the material we learned in class, but I kinda disagree. Usually, several questions came straight from the study guide word-for-word. Once in a while, there was a question about something we didn't really talk about, but there's extra credit worked into every quiz so it wasn't a big deal.

Dr. Fritz is kind and cares about her students. There's a lot of homework that sometimes feels like busy work (takes me 4-6 hours a week) and weekly quizzes, but the grading system is really lenient. You can get solid Bs on every quiz and still have an A in the class. Deadlines are pretty flexible too. There's a textbook, but I never read it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is very much a homework based teacher. A lot of the time the quizzes felt like they didnt match up to her lectures and they would remain locked after you take them so there was no way to review them on your own so you had to go to office hours to see it. This class didnt fit my learning style and I dont see myself taking her class again.

Fritz is a caring teacher but taking her class online was horrible. The lectures are absolute trash and on the weekly quizzes she expects you to not know things so you have to look it up. Study guides are sorta useless for the quizzes and she just doesnt teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is a phenomenal professor. The class is online-based this semester and consists of weekly quizzes matched with study guides. Dr. Fritz and the TAs are super helpful and accessible. Review sessions are offered every week to review the material before the quiz. I would take her again if I could, and I highly recommend her.

Dr. Fritz is very understanding and compassionate. Provides so many resources to do well in class and TAs are absolutely amazing. The bulk of information comes from canvas homework and weekly study guide you have to fill out. She doesn't lecture much but really likes breakout rooms. UGTA reviews are extremely helpful. She is weird which is funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took her class before COVID and honestly didn't think it was bad at all because I had a background in bio from high school. Only one test that I can recall was pretty tough, and that one got dropped. Overall, fairly easy to get an A if you're comfortable with AP Biology.

I was super scared to take this class from these reviews but she must've adjusted the class structure for COVID as I've had a good time so far. The TAs are great and there are many ways to reach out for help (office hours, discussion section, etc.) Start on the study guides early because there's a quiz every Friday. You can do well in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is an amazing professor. This was my first semester as a college student, and she really made the class enjoyable and doable while in the midst of a pandemic. She grades fairly easy and her assignments are fairly easy as well. Her quizzes are a little more difficult than the homework, but nothing you would not expect out of a coll. course

reviews.comment: worst professor ive ever had. her lectures dont match the book then she marks you off for not following the book. annoying lectures. if you've taken other classes she will count you wrong for using outside knowledge (ochem, gen chem). contradicts everything she says, the tas dont even like her

I brought my grade from a 65 to an 85 bc of how much easier the work was w COVID19, so don't let my B grade deceive you: this class was nearly impossible for me. Last time I took bio was my freshman year of hs. If this is you, I would not take her class. Tests were difficult and discussions were useless. My TA wouldn't cover the worksheets assigned
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Homework before every class which can be very time consuming. Tests are entirely based off of the lectures. The textbook is just for reinforcement, read it a couple times only. In the past, biology has always seemed like a jumble of facts. But Fritz connected things well and helped you understand rather than just memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall pretty decent, show up and pay attention, you should be fine. Tests are a little more on the difficult side but nothing no doable.

Fritz isn't awful. Lots of HW and can be challenging, especially if you haven't taken bio in awhile. The TA team was outstanding and office hours/hands-on helps as well. Fair warning though, the tests are HARD. Hard. Decent amount of questions in a short amount of time all designed to trick students. You must know the material well to get above a B
no just no, you don't want her I promise you. Save your GPA as much as you can.

Overall okay. If you haven't taken bio since the 9th grade or it's just not your thing, making an A or B can definitely be achievable. Her lectures were entertaining for the most part and the TAs were great, but her tests were pretty wack. Test questions were specifically crafted to trick students.

Ok I have no clue who's out here giving her 5/5 but Fritz was awful. I did fine in BIO311C but I was one of the few. The material isn't hard, but there's so many bs trick questions that you will get hit. To get an A: go over her lectures, do the study guides, look at the testable skills. You'll survive but Fritz is still the last resort imo.

reviews.comment: Great professor who really cares about what she is teaching. She says in class you don't need to read the textbook but I think reading it and taking notes really helps you prepare for tests! If you do that the tests will seem pretty straight forward but they are mostly applied knowledge questions so know your details!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her exams are what most people complain about, but they arent impossible. She doesnt test about surface-level concepts, so memorizing isnt enough. She requires students to really understand the material and be able to apply knowledge. She provides a list of testable skills and also adds a few extra points. Extra credit for disc attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz's class is not easy, but you can definitely get an A. If you're struggling: REACH OUT TO HER! terrible professor. does NOT curve tests, and averages are in the low 70s to 60s. still won't curve. blames grades on lack of students studying but in reality her tests are very surface level and does not prepare you for the exams whatsoever. you will end up teaching yourself the entire course material and still do poorly in the class.

reviews.comment: Fritz was absolutely amazing. Exams were fair, she gave a list of testable skills so there were no surprises. Great lecturer with a good sense of humor. Would take her again in a heartbeat.

reviews.comment: I would avoid taking this professor at all costs. She is rude and condescending during class, and her tests are absolutely nothing over what you have learned in class. Not a good professor. Don't take. Terrible tests, irrelevant material, bad grades.

reviews.comment: Fritz is a funny friendly professor famous for fabulous factual assessors. Her laugh is contagious, her lectures are outrageous, and her attitude is courageous.

I absolutely LOVE Dr. Fritz. She does a great job making sure all her students are up to date with the information while moving the class at a rapid pace. Her tests are fair and definitely manageable if you pay attention. I highly recommend you take her class if you're incoming.

I studied for the second midterm heavily during the previous weekend, yet none of it actually mattered as she tests you on material that is not presented in her lectures, considering her lectures are very superficial about Bio. Moreover, she manifests herself as a weird, middle aged woman, on crack, that is unwilling to work with your questions.

reviews.comment: Just got out of my bio midterm 2 after studying for 8 hours straight. Was warmly welcome to a midterm that did not follow any of the learning outcomes and with questions that didn't include any of the information from the textbook. Dr. Fritz cancels lectures at will and responds sarcastically to several questions asked in class. You've been warned.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz was an amazing biology teacher. Lectures were engaging, discussions were worthwhile to attend, and tests were easy. As long as you keep up with reading, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I don't know why Fritz gets so much hate. As long as you go to class and can read questions on the test, there's no reason that you can't make an A. She is pretty obvious about what's important based on lecture, and she bases her tests on the Testable Skills that she gives you. It's not a hard class especially with an AP BIO background.

Dr. Fritz is very knowledgeable about biology and it's evident. I did not like the way she structured her tests at all. She always gave us "testable skills" to study before the exam, but when the exam came around, only a few of those testable skills would be on there. Tests are MC and short answer. Very tricky wording and sometimes confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very surface level; as a student who had taken AP bio (& got a 4), they didn't get me thinking and I didn't find them valuable at all. Be prepared to self-teach a lot of the content in prep for the exams. If anything, look to your TA for help. The grading weights are in your favor, though, so take advantage of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was my pleasure to study under Dr. Fritz. Her lectures were incredibly thought provoking and in order to succeed in this class we had to develop a deeper understanding of the material. I HIGHLY recommend her classes for any pre-med or science majors because she is hands down one of the most intelligent people Ive ever encountered. GO TO CLASS!

Great caring professor. Really wants you to learn processes rather than memorize material. Go to EVERYTHING including office hours. Do the homework before class, go to discussion and hands-on, and do all of the quizzes. Those are easy points to earn. I dropped out of UT 19 yrs ago and this was my first class back so if I can do it, YOU can too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great professor. Shes a great lecturer and really helps you understand biology and the concepts, not just memorize stuff. The tests can be tough because of that - its not rote memorization, but application. If you want an A, you have to really study! Her lectures slides actually follow exactly what she tests on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content isn't bad, and she knows what she is talking about, but the questions on the exams are always worded really vaguely or in a weird way so that you need to ask for clarification to even know what she is asking.

She's an okay teacher, not too memorable. Be prepared to shell out 50 bucks for that mandatory iclicker piece of garbage. This class is boring, but good thing is that it's kinda easy. If you pay even a little attention in class, the exams will be a breeze and they are curved a lot too. You can get above a 100 on every exam so take advantage of that

Very detail-oriented exams, she'll find something mentioned once in the textbook and put 5 questions about it on the test. You can petition to get credit back on the short answer portion of an exam, but she won't give it to you. If possible, take the class with Dr. Buskirk.

I had taken AP bio in hs so granted, a lot of the material was easier for me to grasp. But she prints out her powerpoints and gives them as handouts, which is very useful. The short answer can be a little convoluted at times, so make sure you ask questions during discussion sessions (which are extra credit if you go to enough) to understand content
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to teach yourself the entire course, Fritz is the one for you. Also set aside around $200 for the materials needed. This is technically a flipped classroom except you barely learn in class. Most lectures consists of "talking to your neighbor" about diagrams and "movies" that she puts up in class. Fritz is sassy and annoying.

If you are on a budget then do not take this class, she charges you 75$ for a pearson account in order to complete your homework and you have to buy one of those 40$ iclickers for her class. The other bio teachers dont make you buy either of those things... She is not too nice either.
horrible. have had her for maybe three classes and i just know she's an absolute mess. doesn't cover anything in lectures but the HW and readings are so long. also textbook is super expensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, this class was difficult. However, an A IS ATTAINABLE if you put in the work. Go to her office hours, ask questions, pay close attention during lecture, and study days in advance for her exams. DON'T MEMORIZE, you won't do well. You absolutely have to understand the information and apply it to other situations. Don't give up! :)

I love Dr. Fritz. She is passionate about what she does and knowledgable, as well. The class is an easy A (I didn't take AP bio either), the textbook goes in too much depth, but you'll get an A if you understand what's in it. Listen in lecture she always repeats things that will show up on the test (usually word for word how she says it).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: study powerpoint slides in depth and discussion activites come up very often in the free response. Textbook is a waste of time because that's what I studied and I never did well. Understand general applications of the topics because her tests are more of a general understanding and it can trip you up if you only study specifics.

A midterm was so disorganized that some questions had several correct answers and other questions had no correct answer at all. As an apology of sorts, Dr. Fritz created the opportunity for more points on the next exam. This class is not necessarily difficult, but in an attempt to create rigorous exams, Dr. Fritz ends up playing herself and you.

- Study lectures and testable skills (prov. by her), masteringbio, quizzes in this order. DON'T STUDY THE TEXTBOOK UNTIL AFTER EVERYTHING ELSE! Test material comes from lectures and even off the cuff statements she makes. - She has some very edgy humor which I appreciate - It's not harder than APBio just covers slightly dif. material more in depth

Not going to lie, Fritz's tests can be really tricky, but her teaching style really enforces deep, conceptual learning of the material. If you're looking for an easy A, she is definitely not the professor for you. The key is listening to what concepts she puts an emphasis on during lecture and really knowing the testable skills back and forth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is genuinely a great person, but her class is extremely difficult. In order to attain a high grade, you must study for at least a week or more in advance. Her course is centralized by her exams, which are unnecessarily difficult. It would be beneficial to go into her class with some background in biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are a complete waste of time and do next to nothing to prepare you for the exams. She is not a good lecturer yet requires her students to attend them for credit. The tests are either made to be confusing intentionally or perhaps they are a reflection of the lack of care and effort that this professor puts into her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take her. The TAs and discussions are more helpful than the professor and lectures. She would spend a lot of time covering irrelevant topics that arent tested. The tests are tricky and worded in ways meant to confuse you. I took AP Bio, got As and passed the AP exam but still found her class difficult. Attendance is mandatory

I believe this class to be for people who STRONGLY retained the information from AP Bio in high school. Her lectures are broad, but her exam covers specific details on application, and questions that were very vague on what to answer. You pretty much teach yourself reading the textbook, and learn how to pass tests rather content. Pro: TAs are good

Challenging, but great and caring professor. Exams focused on information covered in lecture slides. Don't worry too much about extra information covered in homework or assigned readings.. Weekly quizzes are a VERY good indicator of the information that you will be tested on. As long as you pay attention and put forth the effort, you'll be fine.

I got a 6 on IB biology, and SUFFERED in this class. I thought I was going to fail it for MOST of the semester. It is do-able, if it's ALL. YOU. DO. You can know everything you're supposed to and still fail, because it's more about how to take an exam than what you've learned. She makes inappropriate jokes in class, and is overall unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tests are MC and FRQ and can get specific at times. However, her lectures stress test-related material and she provides several avenues for getting more help. Weekly HW assignments and discussion sections are useful (discussions are EC). An A is definitely attainable with effort. Overall, she's a great lecturer and a pleasantly sarcastic person!

Main advice -- go to office hours. She will give you tips and advice on how to do well on not only her tests, but future tests in other classes. Everything you are tested on is fair and has appeared on her lecture slides or during discussion. Plus, the final is fairly easy and has extra credit on it! Also, not a boring lecturer. Great professor.

I came into the class with no background of biology (except from my freshman year of high school taught by the football coach) and I managed to do well in the class. She definitely makes you work for it, but it is very doable. Pay attention in lecture and GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! She's a hard professor, but definitely cares and wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fritz is a good lecturer and overall really nice professor so it's really hard to dislike her. Nonetheless her exams are extremely hard and detailed. You MUST MUST MUST put in a lot of work and practice in order to do well. If you don't have a strong background in Biology (like I didn't) choose another professor.

DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU DIDN'T DO AP BIO IN HS. She was a great professor and I learned a lot from her, but the test questions are VERY detailed/analytical and she grades it very particularly, so if you don't already have a strong background in biology, it's near impossible to get an A.

BIOLOGY WILL BE 38482 X MORE DIFFICULT THAN HS NO MATTER THE TEACHER!! Fritz is known to be a harder bio teacher but she's amazing. Tests count for 80% of the grade. To do well on the tests, USE THE SWBATS AND KNOW THEM BACK AND FORTH! You have to put in the effort if you want to do well but that's college for you!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: HER CLASS IS HARD IF YOU DO NOT HAVE A STRONG BACKGROUND IN BIOLOGY. BUT OVERALL FRITZ IS A GREAT PERSON AND A GREAT PROFESSOR

reviews.comment: This professor tailors her class to people who have a background in biology. Tests are so extremely detailed and half the information she never even covered. reviews.comment: Difficult class. Biology is MY subject and I ended up with a terrible grade. She does not give A- and As are very hard to get. Also, good luck if youre right on the edge of an A! She lacks all empathy for students in need of assistance. Take an easier bio professor. You dont learn any more from having a hard teacher like Fritz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is a decent professor. She's definitely not the best professor I've had but she taught the material well and made it easy to digest. Her tests and the final were fairly difficult but she didn't give too much homework and the at home quizzes were very easy. She also made chapter study guides which helped a lot in learning the test material

Professor Fritz is an amazing woman and teacher, she cares about students and if you are a science major I really recommend you take her class, it might hurt your GPA, but what your going to learn from her class is priceless. She is really dedicated and motivated, she was a great inspiration to me. (Im not a science major and I loved her class)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very animated so class was never too boring. I understand why people think the tests are difficult: very specific, but if you put in the time it isn't bad at all. I only read the textbook for clarity on some topics. Do the study guides and study with a friend, practice past exams. Homework is easy but not helpful. Go to discussion for extra credit

Personally loved her. Every single bio class involves a LOT of reading and memorization, so dont hate a prof for that. Had a roommate in another prof at the same time and Fritz had easier tests. She's pretty funny, answers questions patiently. The homework is graded SUPER easily, barely any points taken off if you get something wrong.
tests are challenging but she gives her students plenty of opportunities to learn outside class. attendance is not mandatory but necessary for success!

The Unsalty Honest Truth::: Her class is tailored towards students who are already familiar with Biology. Her lectures and study guides are easy to understand, however, the tests are very detailed and tricky. Thankfully, I figured this out early on and decided to drop before my GPA did. Please do not take a chance and risk being given an L.

reviews.comment: Overall a great professor. Loved the course material, and it was well organized. She also kept lectures interesting with jokes and such.

reviews.comment: take this at your own risk, it was the hardest class i have ever had to take. i truly believe that i studied my very best and i studied everything. the exam questions either go into too much detail or are too broad for you to piece information together in your brain. i would try my best to get another professor

3 exams later & I still never understood how or what to study for her exams. I think Fritz is a super nice person, but her exams will kill you no matter how hard you study. An A is possible, but majority make B's & below. After 2014, she had to make her exams harder, & you can't find any old exams online ANYWHERE. hope yall have a better experience

reviews.comment: Dr. Fritz is a great professor and a good lecturer. I truly learned a lot in her class. She provides you with all the material you need (lectures, textbook, discussion, homework, study guides) to do well, but you have to put in the work.
