reviews.comment: Great professor! She provides copies of her slides and the readings she covers in the textbook. Read those chapters/sections in the textbook and you should do fine on the test as a lot of her questions are straight from the book. Not a hard class if you put the effort in

If you aren't willing to put in time outside of class, you WILL fail. I never made less than a B on any test but I really had to work for it. READ THE TEXTBOOK, do the study guides, and you'll do fine. If you want to understand the material it its entirety, take Fritz. She's hardcore but very knowledgable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lots of salty students on here... final was easy if you prepared well and she offers extra credit. Solid biology professor. Lots of students dont know what hard work is I guess.

I've seen some harsh reviews about Dr. Fritz; she is honestly a wonderful lady who brings a lot of energy to her lectures. She cares about the well being of her students! The tests (3+final) are hard; you have to work hard for your grades. Weekly quizzes and daily hw can help your grade. I didn't always use the textbook, but it's a good supplement.

Dr. Fritz is a fantastic professor. Her lectures are interesting and she is very funny. She does give hard tests, but if you put forth the effort to understand the material, you will be fine. An A is most definitely attainable as long as you are willing to work for it.

reviews.comment: I don't recommend taking her if you don't have a strong biology background. Her lectures are too broad and general compared to her tests.

Lectures are easy to understand. however the tests are much harder than she portrays. It is important to take the time and study regularly. Keep up with the lectures and material because you will be learning new and testable material up until the class day before the exam. She also makes a lot of awkward sex and alcohol jokes.

reviews.comment: Even though I heard a lot of bad things about her, she is one of the best professors I've had so far. Her study guides list out what she wants to know from the textbook, and her lectures cover everything else. Just take good notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've heard a lot of bad things about Dr. Fritz, but she is a great lecturer and makes sure her students understand the information very precisely. The study guides and lecture notes help a lot. If you're pre-med, she is probably the best professor, but be ready to study hard because this is definitely a weed out course.

She is by far one of the best professors i've ever had. Her teaching style is pretty simple. First exposure readings, second exposure homework, third exposure in lecture. People who are complaining about the grades they are receiving simply didn't put in the hours or the effort mindfully. She is fantastic and inspirational! Would take again.

This class is more tailored towards students with strong bio backgrounds, even though she says otherwise. She claims that her lectures and study guides are the key to doing well, but her lectures are too broad and the guides are too detailed for the test. Loves having tricky MC's on her tests, which weigh more in comparison than the simple SAQ's.
DO NOT TAKE FRITZ FOR BIO311C. Lectures are all over the place and the exams are unnecessarily confusing. I had to drop and take someone else
Maybe went to lecture 3 times the whole semester. Exams are based on the textbook. As long as you do her reviews, you can get a solid A in the course.

Tests are so unnecessarily difficult, and the workload is insanely high. Lectures are often confusing, and she treats students like high-schoolers. Would definitely not recommend her if you want to actually make a good grade with your work. I've studied upwards of 20 hours per test and have averaged low C's on every single one.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! If you have to take bio take a different prof. She isn't a good teacher and her test are impossible. I have studied more for this class than I have for any other class and I have not passed a test yet. I don't recommend.

reviews.comment: Professor Fritz is a really nice person but has a hard time really explaining in depth the material we learn in class. Suck it up and work hard.

reviews.comment: Horrible. Worst professor ever. Tests are nearly impossible. You have to read and understand the entire textbook to even get a C on a test. Dropping this class ASAP. reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Worst class I've taken at this campus. Tests are ten times more in depth than what she teaches or tells you to learn about. reviews.comment: She changed the test this semester and they are nearly impossible even with reading the book and doing the study guides. She blames the student for doing bad on the exam and says its because everyone doesn't attend class when I haven't missed a class yet and still made a 64 on the first exam. I do not recommend having her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Treats students like they're in high school by calling on them for problems and berating them for being on their laptop/phone. Tests often go beyond what is talked about in class and frequently have trick questions. Makes you buy iClicker knock off app and Pearson online program which felt like a waste of money but was required in order to get an A

I really enjoyed this class. Fritz tries to keep things interesting. Definitely a fast paced course and you will have to read ALOT but if you are prepared to buckle down and work hard an A is completely achievable. Lecture can be overwhelming but the test are straight forward. I would totally take this prof again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a professor she was kind, funny, and knew what she was talking about. To pass the class you NEED to read the chapters, since the test questions are taken verbatim from the text. Study question sheets were helpful but not necessary, since all of the answers were found in the book. There was plenty of time to get everything done for her class.

Dr. Fritz is amazing!!! If you are pre-med, TAKE HER!!! Her class really forces you to actually LEARN the material. Tests are not THAT challenging--do the study guides (emphasis on this!!!), pay attention in class, read the book, and go to discussion. Commit to the class and you will get an A for sure!

Dr. Fritz is probably the most amazing prof I've had here so far. I love her sense of humor and her determination to really teach her students everything the class has to offer. I thought I had a C+ in the class but she bumped it up to a B! I'm waiting to take her for 311D because she's just that good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is ridiculously hard. You need to read all the chapters, know all the study guides, and know all the details or else you wont do well. the lectures alone are not helpful, you need to do a lot of outside work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty diffult because you have to actually read all the chapters from the textbook and do the study guides that go with them and make sure you know all the details. The lectures do not go in enough detail to prepare you for the test, and her tests are really tough. I wouldn't recommend taking her unless you already know a lot about biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: My school hired this botany professor from UT Austin to teach at American Embassy School in New Delhi. So much homework and teacher wont teach anything. Get a tutor for sure if you want to do well on IB exam
Fun lectures and gives a lot of extra credit. Tests are extremely confusing. Attendance is taken through clicker points.

Great class, when I showed up. If you miss class often, expect 70s on the tests, because she takes about 30% of her tests from in-class anecdotes.  Great lectures, occasional ham-fisted weed joke here and there (420 was the best class yet). I would recommend her if you are passionate about the subject, or you plan on continuing Bio.

Tests aren't really THAT hard you just need to cram study and read the textbook and her lecture slides which she posts before the tests. It's not a blow off class, but her point system allows attendance to make up for her hard class. For me it was a pretty easy A, and I hate bio. Lectures are pretty entertaining too.

Her lectures are very broad and the tests are difficult. With the discussion sections and the homework and clicker questions its not impossible to a decent grade (B)but I would not say this was an easy class.

Fr. Fritz is a wonderful woman, but her exams are difficult. You have to go through the powerpoints and pay attention to the "Learning Objectives." She loves to talk about the material, so don't be afraid to ask questions and go to her review sessions. She also takes attendance in class through clickers.

Okay, so Fritz is an awesome PERSON but not so awesome when it comes to running the class. Her lectures weren't so bad, and 20 percent of the class is just clicking and turning in homework. However her exams were extremely difficult in comparison to everything we discussed in class. So if you do take her, prepare for extremely tough exams.

test questions don't only come from her powerpoints, even though she said they do. class out of 500 points, which is nice because i didn't pass a single test but ended up acing the final and getting a B in the class.

although it was a hard class, its not hard to get an A. If you read and look over powerpoints, especially the part where is says "what to know", you should be fine. She is hilarious and I loved going to class!

Dr. Fritz' lectures were very fun and easy to follow, but her tests were extremely difficult. It required applying the basic principles to an extreme. With that though there are quizzes once per week, clicker questions every day, extra credit for attending discussion, and a heavily curved final. It is extremely possible to make an A in this class.
People with no prior knowledge of biology, be warned. This class is not for you. You had to go to class for clicker questions. Her tests were hard in comparison to what she taught.

Dr. Fritz was one of those professors I was never able to fully understand. Her lectures did not consist of core content that showed up on her exams. Her class objectives and expectations remained ambiguous no matter how many times I reached out to her during office hours. I did not learn a lot from flipped classroom setting & would not recommend.

Fritz is a great professor and very entertaining. Took this class because of good reviews and high distribution of A's and B's. However, half way through the semester, Fritz announced she would be making the test more difficult due to instructions of the dept. Tests were random, scattered info and were unlike topics and material covered in class.

Dr. Fritz is the worst bio professor i've ever had. Test material is completely random and not covered in class or discussion for the most part. Reading is helpful but only to an extent. She's a nice person, but not an easy A, or B for that matter.

Professor Fritz is good at explaining basic biology concepts in a way anyone can understand. She has a sense of humor too, and occasionally works funny videos and comments into her lectures. I really enjoyed taking this class - it's pretty easy to get an A as long as you pay attention and do all the assignments. Recommended!

She is super sweet and makes the class really entertaining! You need to always be there because there are clicker questions. Homework is once a week but extremely easy. Tests are not bad if you look over notes the day before. You can zone out in lecture with no problems. Quizzes are online and you just need to pass them. I also just love her.

Dr. Fritz's class was one of the most difficult classes I have taken. The material isn't too hard to grasp as long as you read the book. However, her tests are made to make sure you know everything about that subject. Her questions are very easy to get tricked on. She offered a lot of extra credit/hw points so this is what saved my grade.

I enjoyed Dr. Fritz as a person, but as a professor, she was a little all over the place. Her tests are a lot harder than you'd expect since her class is so laid back. Reading the book is VERY helpful, but VERY boring.  Overall, the class was just okay. She really is nice though, so office hours can really be helpful.

Such a nice person. She is incredibly funny and her lectures are quite interesting, not to mention she deeply cares about her students. The only setback is the difficulty of her exams. Some of the free response can be VERY difficult, along with her MC. Reading is definitely a must for her, and understanding the applications of the reading.

Dr. Fritz is funny. She has great energy so her lectures are enjoyable. You will probably have to read from the book, because she tries to use lectures for additional material rather than to review what the book gives you. This class is really easy if you have a strong background in science.
She's a good teacher but she's not an easy a. Definitely possible as long as you study and pay attention!
So nice and really helpful. I didn't open my book once and got an A just from going to a majority of the lectures and discussions. Posts ppts online which helps to study. Great teacher!

Dr. Fritz is enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and personable! She encourages questions, presents funny videos, and holds informal coffee groups to get to know you better. Her lectures are really helpful in prepping for the upcoming tests, which aren't too hard if you feel like you really understand the concept. The grading is fair and simple.

Fritz is a really nice professor and her lectures are very clear and helpful. BUT her test are soo hard! I failed 3 of her exams even though I understood the powerpoints. In order to pass w/an A, you MUST attend office hrs and read the textbook over and over again. MEMORIZE EVERYTHING! Memorization is the key in being successful in her class.

Extremely helpful, one of the few professors I have met that is so willing to help her students. College biology is not easy, but she adds humor to her lectures to make them less painfult to sit through. Her knowledge of the subject makes up for the fact that her T.A. is a tad clueless about most of it.

Dr. Fritz was very helpful during my semester and even had an open discussion on Tuesday mornings, allowing students to meet with her informally to discuss biology.  Her tests are hard and very specific, but reading the book will help. This is not a blow off class but a good grade is possible. You will learn a lot.

Dr. Fritz is very interested in her students. She encourages class discussion and tries to make material relevant. She knows her stuff and is an educator more than a researcher, which makes her great for introductory Biology.

Not sure whether it was me not understanding the class at all, or whether she was horrible at explaining. I had to study an extra lot to barely make a C in her tests. As someone else said, it didn't feel like bio. for non-majors.

Go to class to get attendance points. Her tests are HARD and require application of the material. Make sure you take advantage of the prep u questions (come with textbook), because she uses questions off that on her tests. She loves to be tricky with test questions so read carefully. It really did not seem like a non science major class.
ATTEND EVERY SINGLE LECTURE. don't blow off the quizzes in discussion, and prepare to be thoroughly confused about the short answer sections. i hated this class

One of the worst teachers i have had my college career.  I regret taking her class.  She tries to be funny and interesting but is quite the opposite of that.  Her tests are vague and ridiculous, essay and short answer format with some multiple choice.  I hate her class....stay away from her, far away!

Dr. Fritz is a nice lady, but don't let her fool you. Her tests are hard. Made up of a free response section worth about 25 points and multiple choice worth 60. Free response questions are difficult, you have to apply what you know to a sometimes strange question. Put forth A LOT of study time, and I mean a lot. Read the book and the powerpoints.

She's a good, fun teacher and very helpful but this course isn't easy. You need to know all the material and then be able to APPLY it. Read the book throughly. Pay close attention to pictures from powerpoint slides and book and understand whats happening in them. Tests are wordy and very big on application instead of straight memorization.
bottom line, she's a fun teacher. not a hard class at all. she does A LOT to help you out. she can teach you and make you laugh at the same time. take this class. its an easy B (at least).

Awesome teacher, she is entertaining and doesn't drift too much. Office hours are a students friend, she will help you with ANYTHING you need, go to them! Don't be nervous, she is super cool! Much of the exam is free response and fill in the blank, but as long as you have a basic understanding of the material, you will ace it :) extra credit given
Love the class, love Dr Fritz! I'm an Liberal Arts major, so Bio has never been my thing, but she's adorable and funny and very helpful!

OMG Ms. Fritz is the best teacher at UT period. I hate bio but, I LOVED her class. She made it super funny and in the end I'm walking away with a lot of Bio Knowledge. My exam avg is a very very low C but, I did everything else and I'm getting an A!! Best Teacher Ever!
Read the book, go to lectures, and study. You'll be fine. She's a great teacher especially for intro bio kids.

I really enjoyed her class...but if you want a good grade there is no doubt you will have to study/read. Attendance is very important as what she goes over during lectures is basically the outline of what you should study. Shes very clear and humorous so the class isnt dry. Going to her during office hours also really helps.

Professor Fritz is a funny, energetic professor that tries to keep information interesting.  Her tests are somewhat difficult, consisting of many short-answer problems and in-depth diagrams.  However, she does give extra credit, and there are easy homeworks and slightly harder quizzes to buffer your overall grade.

lectures are really easy and quick. exams are hard though. you must know the material. even though she says her exams area lecture based, you have to read the book to do well. she's energetic and tried to keep lectures fun, despite the subject matter.

The most boring lecturer ever. ACC311 isn't even hard content wise but he speaks in a monotone voice, read directly off the slides, and didn't listen to mid semester surveys. Had to do a lot of self teaching because lectures were hard to follow. If this is who is teaching iMPA classes, we should be scared for our future CPAs.

Nice guy but incompetent lecturer. Uses slides that the textbook creates and doesn't give any other information besides what's in the textbook. I expect class to be an extension of topics discussed in the textbook to provide more clarity. Doesn't listen to mid-semester reviews. Boring/lazy lecturer. Doesn't even know how to do the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: class was so boring and hard to follow. he lets you out early but lectures aren't very helpful. exams are important and lots of hw.

I had serious health issues this semester, and every time I missed class, I submitted doctor's notes. When I missed in class assignments, he gave me partial or no credit for them. My appeals were met with cold no's, even after explaining my condition. By the Q drop deadline, my grade was 5 points lower than it should have been due to his policies.
Great class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I don't know how many times I had to sit through his lectures (attendance optional but not really, cause he gives paper quizzes in most classes) while he struggled to solve practice problems. Not an engaging teacher at all. 90% of classes consist of him pulling the online textbook objectives and practice problems, then giving quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are a bit confusing and slightly boring, but he is a great guy who will help whenever there are questions. I just mainly fw how chill he is.
Very sweet man! His class is a bit boring but he lets you out early. He lets you work in groups for in class quizzes. If you need help with anything him or his TA are great help.

Dropped this class. Do not take. He is an incomprehensible lecturer who does not release any problems or show how anything is done in a legible or memorable way. He also gave pop quizzes. In accounting. Enough said.

Class is an 1 hour and 15 minutes but he only uses 30 minutes normally. He rushes through the lecture slides that he won't even post for you to easily access. We go through in class work that he passes out and he doesn't even understand the answer key when working through it. Students have stopped asking questions because of how confused they are.
Spends 45 minutes dancing around one question. Feels like we're learning it with her. But she is so nice that I feel bad.

This was Dr. Chen's first time teaching this class, so she was getting a feel for it just as much as we were. The class was a bit disorganized at times and behind schedule, which the students suffered for. The HWs did not prepare you much for the exams and were unnecessarily long. She gives 10 pts extra credit on midterms for completing 3 surveys.

lectures are hard to follow, not engaging, and do not explain much. she is really sweet and seems to care about her students. Every physics 302K class is formatted the same way: Homework's on quest heavily resemble the exams which are only 12 questions. She let students have a formula sheet for each exam & final.

Hardest class Ive ever taken at UT. Ive taken calculus and tought this would be easier. I was WRONG. She is horrible at teaching, especially our TA. I had to drop the class because it was super difficult. If youre a STEM Major, take this at a Community college to save your GPA. Attendance is graded which practically is manditory too

Attendance is mandatory. Horrendous lecture. Even some people who took physics BEFORE was confused, and I had exam conflicts with one of my classes. The professor was not accommodating at all. Basically told me to show up or not at all. Maybe redeeming quality was that she let us "retake" the exam for half credit back... with six questions.

The lecture did not correlate to the homeworks or exams. She knew we cared about our grades and allowed for us to have our own formula sheet. She tried to help do retakes twice which helped a little. I found that it was hard to work outside of class when the lectures were not correlated to the questions on homeworks or exams.

This was the last section they had and it was the absolute worst. My friend who was in Professor Markert's had exam retakes. Dr. Chen's exams were nothing like the HW. There was absolutely no extra credit and before I dropped she hadn't even had it where the final could replace your lowest midterm grade. Her lack of empathy is appalling.

Assignments can be somewhat long, but they are manageable. Exams are generally similar to the homework, so they are fair and not overly difficult. He also allows the final exam to replace the lowest midterm, which is helpful. Lectures are recorded, but the notes can be disorganized at times, which made them harder to follow.

He is insanely nice, like one of the nicest teachers i have ever had. The homework is a lot, but it is helpful. Tests are weighted pretty heavy but they arent too hard and he grades them pretty lax. would recommend if you have to take fluids.

Dr. Liljestrand is a very kind and caring person. He always checked with us if we were understanding the material.

There is decent amount of homework, but I would do it and understand it.

Go to class and ask questions.

It took him a while to grade the exams, but if you put in effort, you will do well! Great guy imo.

3 midterms 80%, labs 10%, and homework (completion) 10%. Final can replace a midterm grade. Lectures unorganized, notes hard to read, does all homework in class with lots of other example problems. Cheat sheet for exams and as long as you get the general process correct, he's a very nice grader. Didn't know final grade until last class day though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Liljestrand is the best! If you're a type A person like myself, his disorganization will probably bother you. However, he's an easy grader, goes over lots of problems in class (including homeworks), and his tests are fairly easy. Definitely take fluids with him if you're looking for an easy A.

Exams are worth 80% of your grade but he grades them very easily. The final is optional and can be used to replace your lowest test grade. Labs are completion based and homework is kind of annoying to do. This class is really hard not to get an A as long as you do some review before the exam. Exams are open notes and include the FE fluids manual.

Assigns alot of homework but it's pretty beneficial to tests if you complete them. He goes over example problems often during lecture and includes real-world examples and demonstrations. He offers sample exams but returns your previous test and your score after you have taken the next test. Approachable, disorganized, easy to follow, understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Liljestrand was a pretty cool guy. His class was relatively easy if you did the homework, and the exams were representative of the material learned in lecture. The organization of the class could have been better but that's okay because the professor was worth it!

Easy but you also won't learn much fluids. He also didn't give us a single test grade back until the very last day of class despite saying he would release them every week after we took the test. I had no idea how I was doing until the LAST DAY OF CLASS which was annoying. 2 makeups tests instead of a final if you did bad on them tho. Pretty slay.

Howard (as he asked us to call him) is a brilliant person and a good professor. This class was basically a review of linear algebra. Howard is flexible and helped us through the labs and homework. The only thing I didn't love was how disorganized he is, but I think most brilliant people are. He is very nice though.

Dr. Liljestrand (or Sexy Howard, as some refer to him) was simply the best! The class was very fair, given exams that were easy to get an A on with minimal studying. Labs are difficult, but this is the case across all UT labs (they're all miserable). Lectures were great, he always made jokes while getting the material across. 10/10 would take again

This was such an easy class. He went over all of the homework in class before it was due and walked us through each lab step by step. He gives test reviews that are exactly like the tests. It would be difficult to not get an A. He's also just a very very nice person and is super lenient with deadlines and is super welcoming. 10/10
One of the best professors I had at UT. I recommend him for computer science methods. He was a very good professor and few are as good as him.

Liljestrand is a very nice professor and caring about his students. I'd definitely say its an Easy A as long as you do all the Labs and Homeworks. In lecture, he rambles a lot about information you don't necessarily need to know for anything and is also a bit unorganized, but he explains how to do every lab beginning to end.

Kindest & most caring professor in my 3 years at UT. More than understanding & would walk you through labs so you understood every piece of code. Attendance optional & was available twice a day M-F, which is unheard of. Always answered ALL questions & made tests/grading more than fair. Welcoming person & shared loads of cool stories from his life.
Great professor. Lecture is a little rambling but it gets the job done. Does the labs step by step. Tests are cake. HW takes some effort but doesn't weigh too heavy.

Very easy tests, although you are pretty much exclusively graded on tests. Takes you through labs himself, gives all the answers. Practically gives all the answers to the tests too, though. SLOW AT TYPING, makes for boring classes. Worth it for the easy A, though.

Easy A. Amazing guy. A little out of touch, but he is incredibly understanding and knows that you are under a lot of pressure and have a lot of work. Not a huge fan of learning Matlab and FORTRAN instead of Python or something more recent, but it was still a great class. DEFINITELY GET LILJESTRAND FOR CE311K!!!

I had him for both fluids and computer methods. Honestly, you'll get an A in the class unless you try not to, but he's not the best teacher. You'll do fine in his classes. However, I'm worried about not doing great in future classes because I didn't learn much during his class. If you're extremely motivated you may be able to learn some things

Liljestrand is one of the best professors I've ever had. Smart, funny, and really cares about his students. I'm a professor now at UT, and having taken two classes from Liljestrand when I was a graduate student has helped make me a better teacher for my own students. I learned a lot more than just the course content from being in his class.

Dr. Liljestrand is one of the nicest professors I've had. He is always happy to help, and answer any question you have. He offers a lot of help for tests such as review sessions or practice tests. In terms of the test, as long as you did homework and understand the concepts, you'll do fine. He also lets you use a note sheet for tests.
GREAT GREAT professor. SUPER NICE AND UNDERSTANDING. Final is optional and replaces one of your previous test. WOULD DEFINITELY TAKE AGAIN
Easy to get an A, just do the practice tests. The final is optional and replaces your lowest test grade. Honestly this was the easiest class that I have taken at UT so far.

Take Liljestrand if you want an A. If you complete your homework and labs and work the practice problems he provides before each test, you won't have a problem in this class. His lectures are boring but not mandatory, and he is a slow grader, but your class grade redeems that.

He's great! Any chance you can take him, do it! Finals are usually optional and will replace a previous test grade. No other professor in CE will do that for you. He is very understanding and an all around great man.

Professor Liljestrand is very nice and approachable. He is there during lab and basically walk you through everything you need to do. When he does sample problems during class, he often makes small mistakes and talks to himself while trying to find the error. It makes it a bit confusing. Other than that, the class was pretty easy.

i cannot reccommend dr. engler enough! she is so kind and genuinely cares for all her students. genuinely no idea why she has a 3.9 here, dr. engler is genuinely the goat and she makes bio so easy. her distribution is also amazing, no quizzes, 70% exams (all the bio dept is like this), 10% instapolls 10 % hw and 10% discussion. take her if you can!

Engler is such an amazing and caring professor. You can tell through every interaction and lecture that she genuinely cares so much about her job. She is such an engaging lecturer and has active student participation. Really recommend taking her if given the chance. I actually know what to expect on the test, unlike other professors…

Very nice professor, cared a lot about student success and how she could help us do better. A lot of study materials are provided, which I found more helpful than lecture. My only complaint is the way she pronounces "genome".
love love love Dr. Engler. Had her for Bio 2 and Genetics. Genetics is difficult, but study the quiz questions and instapolls and you will be just fine!

she bumps an A down to a 92, plus the other extra credit it was like a 91. her lectures are so good and i would watch them before each test fully to study, got a 70, 95, 90, on the exams respectively. 50% of final was questions from our past exams we had access to and it was a very attainable A. would reccomend over any genetics prof.

Great professor, genetics is a hard subject! She's the best for genetics. She gives 0.1 points of EC per lecture if you get QoTDs correct. Review her Powerpoints with speaker notes, those have QoTDs, Instapoll questions, and main concepts to know. Those help with the quizzes, which help with tests. She also boosted our grades by 1 whole point.

I hit a learning curve for this course. The first unit wasn't great, but I bounced back. Her lectures are chaotic and you really only need to be there for the 0.1 EC on your exam and instapolls each day. The exams are honestly the easiest part of the class (20 MC). Quizzes are hard but KNOW all the questions for the exams. HW didn't really help tbh
Class is easy to do good in but shes a boring lecturer. Shes probably the best option out of all the genetics proffs.

Out of all the genetics professor she's the best one. Textbook hw is not helpful because it's so difficult instead study QODs and instapolls for exams. Exams are very fair 20 questions but very little extra credit given. Final replaces lowest exam.

there was a lot of hw, but most of it was optional. id stray away from her class, but if you do take it, watch the lectures on 2x speed, do the problems u have time for (or go to discussion), take the quizzes, put the quizzes in a flashcard set and make sure you can do all the problems in that set for the exam.

I cannot emphasize this enough but GO TO OFFICE HOURS, the TAs go over what will/could be covered in the exams. There is wayy too much homework but its optional and you don't need to do it to understand. Go over the quiz and instapolls and your set! Engler will take take the time to explain to you and genuinely cares for her students.

All genetic professors suck but out of them all she's probably the best. The tests are the majority of your grade and so you can't even afford to miss more than 2 questions per test if you want an A. Her lectures are kinda pointless, TA's carry(especially the goat Anthony). Good luck

Here's how to score well: lowkey forget hw, it's useless -- do the quizzes, instapolls, and QOTDs to score well on the exams. GO TO DISCUSSION (Anthony & Julian are great!), they review the most important content from lecture (only do hw's on discussion slides, those are actually helpful). Don't rely on EC, there's virtually none. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Engler is a very nice lady, but this course is hard by nature. The TA review session before the test (slides are put on canvas) are very helpful for potential problems that will be tested. The quizzes are also very similar to test questions. The class did change a lot this year, and the material and tests are very hard so be prepared for that.

Very sweet professor. Wish I utilized her office hours and UGCA team more; they are quite helpful. People get mad at her because she was recently nerfed by the department and was restricted from giving out as much EC as before; that's their fault. Study the Instapoll and QOTDs that you will do during lecture. Textbook is mediocre.

Take any other genetics teacher, her lectures are so confusing as she jumps around when she teaches and can't focus on one thing. Graded by a few things. Homeworks aren't even graded and aren't helpful for exams. I learned more from teaching myself.

Dr. Engler is a sweet professor but can make lectures confusing with the way she tries to explain concepts. You have to teach yourself a lot from textbook readings & make sure to go to discussions- Julian was so helpful! Exams are similar to quizzes & hw problems from textbook. She offers opportunities for EC and replaces one exam with the final.

I did not enjoy 311C or 311D, even with Engler, but Genetics is a different story. This class makes sense with Engler and was much more enjoyable than intro Bio courses. Her tests are extremely fair as questions are seen in quizzes/instapolls/QotDs. I needed an A on the final to get an A in the course, but she prepared us for the final well!

I ended up with over 100% in the course after finals & I'd say it's manageable. I came into this class feeling nervous bc genetics isn't an easy subject, but this is a class where the effort you put in really pays off!! Go to discussion/review sections (especially if Julian is your UGCA)!! Do the homework even they're ungraded. Dr. E is sweet too!

Spr 25': Her class was pretty fair. Decent amount of content with okay amounts of homework. The biggest breakthrough for me was realizing that a lot of here test questions were similar to questions from the textbook. Studying the textbook questions helped me prepare for her tests the best.

Honestly, not hard at all. Her daily questions are the exams. She's nice and tells you what you need to know for the exam. Offers a lot of extra credit. The first midterm had the lowest average ( which was a high 70) and people still complaining. The 3rd exam had a average of an 89. You'll be fine. Take her so easy.
GOAT. do your hw and quiz questions and you'll be just fine on the exam. also, go to discussion. this class is a lot of work, but if you put in the work, it will def pay off on your exams.

Genetics is arguably the second hardest pre-med course, so yes it is not an "easy" A, like Bio 1, but it is most definitely an attainable A. I find her lectures to be amazing, especially when rewatching them before exams, and she genuinely cares for her students so much. The department got on her for extra credit, but still she's an amazing prof.

She's a good lecturer and has instapolls and extra credit Question of the Days every class. The extra credit has been nerfed down to like 1 total EC point per exam, but it's still appreciated. Class is hard but you get a lot of open book quizzes to help you prepare. Lot of work, but she's still good. Better than the other profs.

This class is such a headache. Everything you do is self-taught. Lecture prepares you for nothing. You will have to teach yourself the info on the quizzes and homework (or have ChatGPT teach you). The only way to do well on exams is to teach yourself all of the material bc we're never prepared for the exams, which are a huge part of your grade.

The class is okay and tests are sorta doable if you study hard before and do the assigned homework problems. The problem is the stuff she teaches in class is easy, but the homework is quite difficult. You don't feel that prepared for the tests based of her lectures. Kind lady, but not the best lecturer
Not accommodating at all, tests were hard and like nothing is recoverable if you do poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Engler is very sweet, but the class can be boring. I barely paid attention and skipped most discussions, but self-teaching before exams worked fine. Her tests aren't too hard if you do the homework and review the lectures + qotds. Never read the textbook. An A is definitely doable. Just wish there wasn't a cumulative final lol

Honestly so genuine and cares so much for her students, providing opportunities for extra credit or career development. You can see she loves the topic. Exams are easier than the quizzes, can score pretty high as long as you study lecture/TA provided review. Fun class if you like processes and Engler will always answer your questions. Love her

Genetics is an inherently frustrating topic. Dr. Engler was very hands-on and helped me when I asked—the other reviews are honestly misdirected anger. There's limited extra credit due to the force of department's hand on her course. Study the quizzes & instapolls HEAVILY for the tests, and you'll be fine! Talk to Engler 1 on 1, she's a sweet prof!

Dr. Engler is such a nice professor and was very helpful when I met with her outside of class. The first test was lowkey very hard, but because I met with her and went through the slides thoroughly, I felt pretty prepared. You def have to do more than the bare minimum to do good!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was really hard, but what else can one expect from an upper division bio class? Engler fostered such a healthy learning environment and she truly cared about my success. Make sure you study and go to office hours because it is test heavy, but if you do that you will be fine. I would definitely take a class taught by her again.

Dr. Engler is a really great professor! I was really struggling in genetics, but made the effort to go to office hours bc I knew it was a competitive and difficult class from students I talked to last year. Also, I was really scared for the exam 😭. She is always available to help, and it's clear she wants her students to succeed.

Everyone took the first test and is mad they werent prepared. Dr engler is an amazing and caring professor, and if they put in the work instead of expecting an easy A, then they would have done better. It is not her fault that they expected it to be easy. Genetics is hard, she makes it bearable.

Out of all the genetics professors, ig she's the only good one, but her class is nothing special. Her AND her ta's are not helpful, exams are tough, hw's are useless, and the quizzes are proctored but open note??? EC being 1 point is an actual joke bc the EC is so difficult. Just take her and get ready for a semester of migraines and tears.
Lectures, hw and quizzes do not prepare you for her exams well & the 1pt EC is laughable. TA's aren't helpful, so save yourself the headache and don't take her.

Dr. Engler is hands down one of the best professors I have had at UT! She is so kind and cares so much about her students. She is easily available to ask questions, and she makes the content super fun to learn! The genetics content can seem hard, but she makes the concepts feel simple and easy. If you can, take Dr. Engler!!!
Engler is the goat of genetics, comparable to Iverson for organic chemistry. Take her if you can for genetics, and if you can't, push it back so you can take it with her.

Dr. Engler is the best professor. Not only is she great at teaching, but she's also a very genuine person at her core. This class is hard, but manageable if you put in the effort. Also, just wanted to add that Julian is the best UGCA. I have personally told him myself that he needs a raise. Whatever he's getting paid is not enough.

alr bro the people that be complaining and giving this awesome lady 1 stars have a skill issue. THE CLASS REQUIRES STUDYING. but i can promise you, we dont have to study as hard compared to the people in other genetics classes. Use her resources she offers and you chilling.


tldr: ppl complaining about the class being hard don't know how to study.

She's pretty bad at lecturing and the hw and quizzes are much harder than the lectures. BUT, her tests aren't that bad especially compared to other profs. They're all MC and pretty straightforward if you go to discussion and attempt the hw. So ridiculous how the EC is 1 pt total though

Engler is nice but her grading scale is crazy given she has no EC and her tests are fairly difficult compared to her simple letures that are somehow confusing still; optional homework is crazy and nothing like the lectures (basically getting taught by chatgpt); teach better or assign extra credit !!

I have priority registration and willingly chose this professor, and this is one of the biggest mistakes I have made all of college. I took this classes thinking I would do good because of all the good reviews she had, and now I am struggling to do good at all. Do not take this class.
Tests are so unfair and she does not teach to the tests/quizzes.

Listens to student feedback, exams are very fair. The exams are at least 50% quiz questions / instapolls, and questions of the day, which you can review anytime. It's pretty easy to predict what content will be on it because she emphasizes key points. Of the genetics profs, she is EASILY the most attainable A. (Little EC is the only tradeoff)

I took her for 311D, and she was great. She's redesigned what her quizzes look like, doesnt give exam reviews that actually help you, instapolls are part of your grade and not just for learning, and the extra credit is .1-.9 points.The quizzes got proctoring software added after the year began. A went from 92 to 93. Not a fan now if I am honest.

The reviews from last year are a sham!! I took this class thinking she is a great professor who curves students grades and truly cares about them. That was a LIE. All the PowerPoints are filled with so many details most of which isn't even on the exam. On top of that the exam is worded so complicated where u overthink urself and well FAIL.

reviews.comment: take this class if you want ChatGPT to be your teacher and you want to teach yourself everything. lecture slides are rudimentary compared to the quizzes and homeworks. therefore, everything you see on your quizzes and homeworks (and EXAMS!) will have to be self taught.

do NOT take this professor!!!! this is the worst professor i've had at UT. she's not far off from Brock-- my friend who is in Brock's class said that their exam 2 average was an 80 and and englers last average was around a 77. Dr. Engler is an amazing professor. She is responsive to student emails (even on weekends), is extremely hardworking, and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. She's very kind and empathetic. I've always had a great deal of respect for Dr. Engler, having had her for both Biology and now Genetics. She's everything you'd want in a professor.

I shouldn't have to teach myself every single thing in the course material. Lectures are hard to follow and rushed. I picked Engler because her discussion time was the only one that worked for my schedule, but it doesn't exist because she created her own. reviews.comment: This class was much harder than last years and other professors given we are tested on same content BUT given a max of 1 point of EC added to each exam. The EC is hard to obtain and the "easy" grades like Instapoll and quizzes are not so easy. The quizzes that are open-note are proctored?? Lectures are not focused on test material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Engler for Bio 2, finished with an A, and really wanted to take her again for genetics. After 2 quizzes she added proctorio, which was not listed in the syllabus at all. In bio 2, she encouraged collaboration and now it just feels like I am taking a class destined to not do good. The 1 point of extra credit for the exam is laughable.

Overall very good professor, Dr. Engler is extremely nice and one of the best professors I have had yet. As long as you study the material, and listen to the lectures, you will do good in this class. Dr. Engler is also very good at giving good feedback if you ever need help.

Dr. Engler is really nice, herself, but the department had her change her policies. So the "easy" class you think you were getting doesn't exist anymore. This class is now very exam-heavy and the lectures don't reflect upon the tests. Not her fault though

Took this class because of her great reviews but she is COMPLETELY different. The homework is irrelevant to her lectures (which are insanely hard to understand) and the class penalizes you for learning (instapolls are graded for accuracy during class without practice on content, quiz can be taken twice but both grades count). Not worth it.

She had genuinely changed. This class is hard. The lectures don't match the homework/quiz so I have no idea what they are talking about. Tests r difficult as well and basically no extra credit opportunities.

She stopped doing EC (now 1 point only); lectures are crazy long and often too simplified for the HW. The HW also usually made 0 sense and didn't follow the lectures. Basically everything good you've heard about her class has stopped. Can't tell if she hates us now (this is coming from someone who had her for 311D) Genuinely surprised. She changed.

went into the class thinking she could explain topics well, but nope. lectures are long and often feels like she doesn't know what she's talking about. Her EC is 1 singular point per test that she adds. I've never struggled more in a biology class.

i studied for a combined of 24 hours for that test and did horrible. she writes the questions herself and they are wordered horribly. she has been on edge this semester and been so unforgiving with students grades. these past rmp's do not reflect how she is this semester i promise.

very kind and approachable which made it easy to ask questions in class. tends to read off the slides a lot which also doesn't really keep me engaged as i found it pointless to take notes as everything was already on the slidesdeck. plus the fact that dr. engler has a super soothing voice, i would get real sleepy real fast in class.

She is the sweetest professor ever! She always makes lectures as engaging as possible and usually starts class by sharing relevant information or news to us - mostly pre-health students - such as research opportunities or minors/programs we might be interested in. Her exams are honestly really fair and she offers enough extra credit too!
do yourself a favor and take her. enough said. she is the best professor. she is the most caring professor I have ever had.

Engler is probably the best Bio311D professor at UT. Her tests are pretty easy with mostly mc then some frq, coming from someone who didn't take AP bio. The workload was also super light compared to what I dealt with in Fritz Bio311C with no quizzes and two hw assignments a week (easy to get 100s). There's a ton of memorization and instapolls tho

So sweet! I came in without AP Bio and thought that the difficulty was just right. The TA team led by Damini were always helpful and getting the help you need takes little to no effort. Such a welcoming environment. Dr. Engler also mentions academic and career development opportunities. Instapolls as participation/attendance, but reasonable.
Sweetest soul ever. so caring and genuine. everyone needs to take her. she gives the perfect amount of work and cares so much. Exams aren't hard

Dr. Engler is amazing! She is super nice and you can tell that she wants you to succeed in her class. Her tests are pretty easy as long as you study the review guide, and she drops the lowest test with the average of the 3. reviews.comment:
I love Dr. Engler shes literally the best professor ever, she is just the best idk what else I have to say.

I love her TA Domini she is so chill and understanding, would retake it a thousand times if I could.

Her exams are pretty average/ on more difficult side (coming from someone w a 4.0). I think people just claim they're easy bc they've already taken AP bio, but engler cannot do anything about that. reviews.comment: loved how she encouraged us to answer questions as groups during lecture. lectures are really fast, but going to office hours is probably helpful. she cares a lot about her students and it shows. slides were easy to understand and informative. she explains concepts fairly well. exams were very reasonable and pretty easy to study for.

Love Dr. Engler. Her Exams are not hard at all and she offers a lot of small extra credit opportunities. She wants you to succeed. There are instapolls but a lot are for completion. If you go to class you will be fine. I love her so much I am taking her again next semester!

I LOVE her already! She is literally the best and sweetest professor I've had so far! I hope I get her for genetics next semester! Her tests are very similar to the slides, discussion assignments, and instapolls. Her tests are also not that hard and her UGCA's and teaching specialist Damini is so good! Totally recommend!

For exams, study quizzes, QOTDs, and the discussion slides. Dr. Engler is great (highly recommend her) and so was the TA team and their review sessions.

Dr.Engler is an alright professor. You really do need to read the textbook to understand much of the concepts in this class. reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Engler's class. Since we ended up not having a final, our grade was only quizzes and tests. She had a lot of TAs, so there were many options for office hours. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love professor Engler so much! She was so caring, funny, and approachable. She doesn't grade homework and homework is self led but is super super important to get good grades on quizzes. Extra credit offered every single class day helped me get a 105 on the first test. Best class I've taken at UT so far!

Engler was phenomenal; her lectures were always very interesting, and the TA group was very helpful. The course grade is composed of quizzes and tests. The quizzes/ optional homework are very similar to the tests, so definitely should be the go to when studying. Overall not the hardest class, just show up to lectures even thought its optional.

the tests were pretty straight-forward. go through her slides in advance. i never really used the textbook or did the practice homework. attendance is not mandatory but you can get up to 5% extra credit on each test if you go to class

Genetics can be difficult, but Dr. Engler and her TA's had many opportunities for office hours and discussion sections. If you do HW's and quizzes, you'll be good for the exams. Lectures weren't the most interesting at times, but attendance was extra credit for exams.

Genetics with Engler was very straight forward. Quizzes were very similar to homework's, and exams were very similar to quizzes and lecture examples (exams were usually easier versions than the problems). Very lenient grading and LOTS of extra credit.

She was very nice and passionate about the content. However, lectures felt a little boring and disorganized at times. If you review lecture slides and get most of the extra credit during the lecture, you will do fine.

reviews.comment: Dr. Engler is the best!! She is so funny and makes genetics very fun. She offers extra credit on exams through class practice problems that you can do in a group. reviews.comment: Genetics is a difficult subject, so do not come in thinking it will be light work. Dr. Engler structures the class to be very forgiving. Lots of EC opportunities and tons of practice problems! Just put in the work and you'll be good. I got an A even after bombing the first midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Take Engler for genetics!! Easy at-home quizzes (2 attempts) and un-graded homework. Dr. Engler does a great job at making some of the complicated concepts easy to understand! I've taken 311D and 325 with her and have no regrets!

Very, very generous grading (exam EC for going to class, open-note quizzes with 2 attempts), a walk in the park compared to Chad or Fisher's class. Consequently, you aren't forced to do much learning unless you're gonna take the MCAT or you're very interested in the topic. Exams are very easy (all MCQs, similar to quiz Qs). Really nice person, too

Grading scheme and exams were not tough; you get EC from attending lectures.

Engler is the way to go if you want a good grade in genetics but I didn't learn much from her. Lectures are long/lots of unnecessary info + she reads straight off speaker notes. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

Dr. Engler is hands down the best genetics professor there is!! She makes the content so straightforward that as long as you do the homeworks and quizzes you should be set for the midterms! I really really liked Dr. Engler. The class was structured in a way that worked well for me and the exams were very fair and based on content we'd see in class or on the homework. engler is the best genetics professor here (the bar really isnt that high)

Dr. Engler was the best professor I have ever had. She genuinely cares about her students and how well they understand the material. There is many opportunities to get extra credit and she makes the topics sound super interesting. She made me love my

Amazing prof! heard she was disorganized before I took the class, but that was not an issue this semester. Encouraged learning, I skipped every class after the first exam and was fine. Excited to take Genetics with her!

Dr. Engler is the best teacher ever. She explains her lectures very well, and her exams cover everything she talks about. No quizzes, and homework is kind of different from her lecture but super easy. She gives some extra credit and really cares about her students.

Dr. Engler is a great professor. She is not easy. Her lectures are informational, but boring. She LOVES instapoll (study them for your exams). This course is fine but studying for exams...its rough. One exam could cover over 360 slides of content--there is no study guide. Damini TA is only helpful in one on one office hrs otherwise very moody.

Great lecturer, content was very organized. TAs were AMAZING! Go to recitation before the exams for a clear overview of every topic you'll be tested on. I don't know how anyone could rate Dr. Engler bad. She is so caring and extremely passionate about the subject. Such a sweet professor who genuinely cares for her students. As a new professor, she did great - she was clear on expectations, had helpful slides (with notes), and her tests and assignments were extremely lenient (though this may change in the future).

I really enjoyed this class. Grades are the majority the three exams (with one drop) and the quizzes (which you have 2 tries for). She's clear on expectations and the content is super interesting. Dr. Engler was also very helpful during OH and walked us through our questions.

She's a very sweet and energetic teacher, however her lectures where a bit confusing. Overall her test where very fair (like quizzes) and she has extra credit opportunities during each class. As long as you read the textbook and attend discussions you will be fine :)

Dr Engler was probably the best professor I had this year. Her lectures are very well organized and rather engaging, you get extra credit opportunity every class, and her exams are very fair. One of the best professors I've had! She's a good lecturer, but she is also very accessible outside of class. She was very happy to write a recommendation for me. Overall, Dr. Engler's class was very manageable. Grade is comprised of quizzes and exams, extra credit opportunity during every lecture. Textbook and discussion were the most useful resources. I'm still taking this class but so far, this class is extremely doable! I love Liz. I took Ethics with her first and then MF (current). She is what I would say the ideal lecturer. reviews.comment: Dr. Ibarrola is one of the best professors in the department. She cares a lot about her students and is an amazing lecturer. She is very passionate about the topics she discusses, which makes her lectures interesting. I would highly, highly recommend one of her classes.

Prof. Ibarrola is caring and attentive to her students. Her lectures are interesting, and she kept the class entertaining and active. She was understanding and easy to communicate with. Dr. Ibarrola was great! Her class was very manageable, and although she takes a long time to grade, she gives very good feedback! reviews.comment: I can't remember where I read this, I had written it down a while ago, but it really reminds me of Dr. Ibarrola: "Every subject, however dull they had seemed in the hands of others, became animated in hers." Would take her class again, it seems like most do.
Great lecturer; explains topics and concepts very clearly. Also just so patient and welcoming. She really makes an effort to get to know you. Amazing professor.

Professor Ibarrola is one of the best professors I've ever had. She really cares about what she teaches, which makes her lectures and readings interesting and fun. She is very clear about assignment criteria and gives meaningful feedback. Good balance of independent and group work.

reviews.comment: I really like Ibarrola and the class she teaches. Ibarrola is great! Leads an interesting class with wide variety of readings. Prof Ibarrola is great! She is knowledgable about the material, passionate about the field of archaeology, and the readings were interesting.
