Dr. Molineux has been my favorite professor at UT!! The class is really intimidating at first (graded only on FRQ exams, a presentation, and some in-class participation points) but prof is super sweet and knowledgeable. Lectures are very dense with important details, so utilize his office hours+textbook as much as you can! Logic > pure memorization

He is a sweet guy but is so educated that I fear there is a gap of knowledge that he has a hard time bridging with his undergraduate students. His tests are some of the hardest I have ever taken, but he curves a lot. Pretty inaccessible and not very technologically savvy. His lectures were very boring and he talks so quiet its hard to hear him.

Dr. Molineux is so kind. However, his tests were very difficult (all FR). I was able to be successful on exams by re-watching his lectures/taking detailed notes/understanding the logic behind the points he was making. Write everything you know during exams. He also grades participation and he will remember whether/how many times you've spoken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Molineux is a nice guy in person and he really just wants his students to get something out of the class. That being said, his lectures are sometimes hard to follow and at times the class feels like a survey course. His exam setup is really nice as it allows for you to drop questions you have no hope of answering. Grades are curved immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nicest man ever but mumbles often in lecture so sit close or rewatch lectures. He expects very specific answers on tests but will curve at the end of the semester. This is a very challenging class and while most don't, I found textbook very helpful in clarifying details he expects us to already know. Study at least a week in advance for tests

Dr. Molineux is nice, but he tends to mumble during lecture so unless you sit towards the front you can't really hear him. His tests are all free response, but you get to pick which 8/10 you answer. However, he wants very specific answers, so the class average on the tests was always low (but he curves the whole class at the end so you're fine).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Review below sums it up, but note: *Would highly recommend studying at least 5-7 days in advance to be successful. *Know the power-points cold, he can ask you over any slide. Memorization and reproduction of key ideas and concepts in power-points slides is the best way to study for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His tests were difficult, but he curves at the end of the semester so everyone ended up doing fine. The class is graded just be 3 in class exams, all free response. For us they consisted of 10 questions and you had to pick 8 to answer. Overall I don't think the class is bad at all.
the goat. please never stop lecturing... *takes socks off*
irving dai is the goat

Super nice professor but not the best at explaining. If you took BC Calc in high school and did well, class will be sooo easy. Does not fully explain concepts in class and will have to learn at TA sessions. Exams are exactly like weekly quizzes and he allows a notecard to write anything for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. Often times proves all concepts in his lectures, which can be irritating for students with AP credit who couldn't get out of the course. Gives plenty of in-class examples. Textbook not mandatory. Quizzes & HW are harder than tests, but final was harder than all midterms.

Dr. Dai explained things really clearly, mainly from a mathematical proof perspective, which I liked but may not be the best for others. He allowed us to use a notecard on all tests, which was really nice, and the quizzes are fine as long as you look at the practice quiz. My only complaint is that he sometimes explains too quickly.

Nice professor w/ clear grading criteria and material! Lectures not recorded, but references heavily from textbook. HW is very time consuming but quizzes + tests way easier. Tests are 75% of grade but just redo quizzes/do practice midterm q's and you'll be fine.

Overall great professor. His explanations can be a bit hard to follow through at times but he makes a good job at trying to help you understand. The homeworks are a bit hard at times but they prepare you for the quizzes and exams.

Dai was overall a caring and intelligent professor. The exams are structured based on the quizzes, although it was a little harder. No practice exams only reviews that are harder than the exam. 2 midterms and 1 final. TA was goated tho, shoutout to Nathan. Just be a little "clever" and you can do well in this class.

He overcomplicates a lot of things and goes into irrelevant detail about it. Obviously good if you love calculus but for the sake of doing good on exams and quizzes it's just easier to learn the steps to do it through youtube and homeworks as opposed to trying to understand the minuscule details about how something relates to something not covered.

Very good professor! Gave extra credit, uploaded his notes online, and explained most concepts in detail. The tests are 75% of the grade but the questions he gives are pretty easy and also allows a notecard for each test.
Genius of a guy, could answer any question you'd have, and he explained stuff intuitively. Tests were fair and predictable. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Homework is significantly more difficult than the weekly quizzes and tests, but as long as you studied for them you'll be fine. Can get up to an extra .25 added to your grade from extra credit at the start of the semester. Professor Dai is really nice and patient, and he seems really passionate about math.

By far my favorite professor at this school. His lectures are quite interesting, and they cover what you need to know for the homeworks/exams. He teaches based on the textbook, so you can always refer to that if you are confused. He wants his students to succeed, and he seems like a very genuine guy.

Pretty cool material, and his lectures are good. Homework and exams are very reasonable. He posts lectures notes for all lectures which are very descriptive. Take care to not miss too many classes, its kinda hard to catch up. Complex projective plane my beloved.

Awesome professor. He really knows his material, and he seems very passionate about it as well. He explains concepts in a very intuitive manner, so his lectures can actually be quite interesting! On top of that, he is extremely nice, and he does truly care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework heavy, but very resourceful and helpful when help is needed. Clearly goes over what will be on exam and lectures are interesting and fun!

He is clearly knowledgeable and manages to make his lectures really fun to listen to. His weekly homework can be quite time-consuming, but is graded lightly. The material is not particularly difficult but requires practice. His exams are comparable to the homework and not anything crazy. A very pleasant experience, especially for mathematics!

The lectures themselves sometimes felt kinda useless. Most of my learning was from the textbook as Professor Irving does take his lecture and homework problems from it. His grading is pretty easy when it comes to homework and his tests are pretty simple as long as you studied for it.
Amazing and funny lecturer! Genuinely cares about his students understanding the material and clarifies important concepts from the textbook.
why did i take this class? first time a teacher has made me cry.
It's hilarious this guy is still allowed to teach. Avoid at all costs. Even his graduate students are afraid of him
do not take his course under any circumstances. awful human in a position of power.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: cruel professor with an appetite for public humiliation of his students and TAs-

Wow, well I should really have listened to all the warnings and rumors. He is an awful professor, rude and a gotcha artist. He has made several cry. He clearly loves flexing on his students - he clearly knows a lot, but just doesn't teach it and he gives the feeling that he is too good to teach. way too much work for so little pay off.

Prof talks at you rather than teaches, and uses complex terminology; hard to follow. Presentations are huge component of grade. Often made discouraging remarks or rudely corrected students during presentations. Literally did not know my grade until he submitted it to the registrar; did not know if i'd have C or A the whole sem. Curve saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Finkelstein is a really smart guy, no doubt about that. He knows what he's talking about. Except, he does not teach the material. Rather, he just says it. Lots of primary article presentations are more like stresses rather than learning points. Try to take someone else, especially if a pre-med who cares for their grade

Though I did learn a lot, there is too much work for too little reward in this class. I had to work harder in this class than any other class I took at UT. Quizzes were difficult and had class avgs of about 60. There was a lack of transparency about final grade cutoffs. He told us an 85-87 would likely be an A, but I got an 89 and received an A-.

I greatly learned a lot from Dr. Finkelstein's course, he is very knowledgeable in the course subject and shows that he really wants us to learn the material. You do have to put in the work for the course and have make sure to read your articles and go beyond to make sure you fully know your machine. He is a very caring and wishes our success.

He was very accommodating and nice throughout all the trouble we faced during this semester: pandemic, winter storm, other personal situations, etc. The majority of your grade comes from group presentations where you work with your group to explain an article. He does post grades very late, but he's an overall good guy and an excellent lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A difficult class for sure. The quizzes are pretty detailed but the majority of the grade was based on group presentations of research articles. As long as you put in the work and thoroughly understand what you are presenting, you'll be fine. Asks hard questions so be prepared. Nice guy, seemed to care about the topics he was teaching about
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: His course was crazy hard, and a large majority of the grade is on our article presentations. But I learned so much from this class and he was so accommodating and knowledgable! Be prepared to stay on top of things but if you do, you'll do fine!! He did grade everything really late though which sucked, but he gave lots of EC and curved:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Be ready to ready to read the article assigned to you. He will be able to tell if you didn't and give you hard questions so its on you. He did grade late but plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think I am doing well but I have no way of knowing because he hasn't graded a single thing that wasn't auto-graded for him by canvas (the quizzes). We just turned in our final presentation and the very first one in the first month of the semester hasn't been graded. Too lazy to even come up with quiz questions makes you write them. Doesn't care!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst prof at UT. Grades mostly based on quizes and presentations with tough Q&As where he would thrive off of roasting you. He seemed very uninterested in the class until he had the chance to rip you to shreds with questions. That's the only thing he seemed to enjoy. The quizzes were fine and based on lectures. Try taking another prof, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell his research is more important to him than teaching. The class is poorly organized and he gives you little time to do projects. You don't know any of your grades until the last day of class. He makes you feel stupid even though you're in undergrad and he has a literal PhD. Doesn't respond to emails either :)

Avoid this man. You have group projects where you focus on a research article he assigns you. The project itself is not too bad but he does not care about you or your well being. Publicly insulted my groups project and was very rude. You can tell during lecture that he does not care to teach he is a researcher before a professor and it's obvious

The worst Biochem class & professor I've ever taken. Smart guy, but terrible at teaching. Hardly anything from the lectures or office hours are actually on the exams. You study so much material to get tested on none of it. Test averages were in the 60s, yet he barely curves; a 66 to 69 is a C. What a joke. Oh, & he's not caring at all whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: We had weekly quizzes instead of psets and they can't put problems which require lots of thinking on the quizzes, unfortunately making the class very mechanical. Dr. Dillig goes very fast in lecture, but she's willing to stop and explain if needed (and she brings candy!). Curve is also very generous; I wouldn't stress over exam grades.

Dr. Dillig is not a good professor. She lectures way too quickly, is barely accessible outside of class, and mostly dismisses student questions. She also assigns HW due the day before the test, even though the material is assessed on a later exam. Despite the generous curve, wouldn't recommend taking her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are dense and move very quickly. Knowledge is tested through weekly quizzes, so even though homework is optional, completing it is essential to understand the topics. Tests are quite difficult and make up a large portion of the grade, but the final grade is generously curved. Dr. Dillig is nice, understanding, and very open to feedback.

Isil is an exceptional lecturer and person. Her course might pose a challenge if you're new to this level of mathematical rigor, but both she and the TAs are readily available to support. Grading is prompt and precise.  While the exams are very hard, the class is curved, offering a fair assessment. Btw, chocolates are distributed during lectures!

This class is no joke, but Isil is a fantastic professor. She knows her stuff extremely well and is very helpful during office hours. Lectures are fast-paced and challenging, yet they are clear and organized. Accessible online as well. Collaboration isn't allowed, but you can always consult the (optional) textbook for extra help. Highly recommend.

I really enjoyed Isil's lectures and the material in the course. I've both taken this class with her and TA'd, and I think she presents the material in a very accessible way. As long as you are able to put in some work outside of class (going to OHs, etc.) if you don't understand something, then you will get a good grade in the course.

Very knowledgeable and amazing lecturer. She does go very fast, so you need to continuously remind her to slow down and re-explain, which she is happy to do so. Problem sets are difficult, but through office hours, they are doable. Tests are very challenging. Beware of the 1st exam (much more hard than expected). Class is nicely curved at the end.

Exams are very difficult but the class is curved. Homework is very similar to lectures, but often goes more in depth/ties 2 concepts together. She always welcomes questions in lecture (which is on Zoom) and usually does a good job at explaining things. The slides are all on her class webpage and are helpful to reference later on.

Isil cares a lot about her students and has a great understanding of discrete math. Homework is difficult and tests are really hard but the class is curved so if you're above average on everything you'll probably end up with a good grade. Grading is 50% homework and 50% tests. Lectures are on Zoom. Try really hard cause content is very difficult.

Absolutely wonderful professor who knows discrete math very well. Open to questions and participation in class. Homeworks became more doable/got used to them toward the end. Exams are challenging but classed is curved. Do textbook problems, discussion problems, and redo homework to succeed on exams. Office hours are useful. sometimes fast-paced
GOAT professor. Really cares about her students. Exams are difficult but graded generously and there's a nice curve at the end.

Isil is a great person and always wants to help students succeed. She is very smart and course material sometimes flew over my head but she is very open to questions. Homeworks and exams are hard but help you learn. Looking online and at the textbook can help you with the HW.

Isil is amazing. First of all, her lecture slides are very thorough. She works through problems, is very interactive, and also got us in groups to work through stuff ourselves too. Drops the lowest homework assignment. Tests were pretty hard, but its a curved class. Your understanding of Discrete Math will be far better after you take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great instructor, reasonable workload, and very interesting topic. Lectures were easy to follow and well organized. I definitely recommend her courses!

Isil is a great teacher. Her course is well-organized, and she explains the topics crystal clear. She also cares about the students. Don't hesitate to ask questions.  Course workload is medium. There are some assignments and exams, but no project. If you do the assignments, the exam won't be hard.

The class is very well prepared, it has very good slides. The presentation is extremely clear. If you ever read Isil's paper, you will know why. Even if there are things unclear, if someone asks, Isil would like to explain in more detail.  No project at all. Light homework, but there are exams. Workload OK.  BTW, I took the class three years back.

Isil is one of the best professors that Ive ever met at UT Austin. She can explain the course material clearly and make everything easy to understand. The course is well-designed and slides are well-organized. It is fantastic overall.

Isil's a terribly professor overall, but she's great as a person. She also gives out candies in class. Well, honestly, her lectures and TAs were both pretty terribly when I took the course, so I hope you at least get decent TAs. The key to doing well in the class is to get the textbook (pdf available), read it, practice the problems before lecture.
Very hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There's a lot of material. Though Isil explains it well, it's covered too quickly during class. I recommend going to class, reviewing notes afterwards, doing the homework, and looking in the textbook for extra problems to practice for the challenging tests. Just doing what's required may not be enough if you want to excel. Practice is key to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Monaco is the best professor I have had at UT! He is very understanding with his students and obviously wants us to succeed. The exams are all free response, but if you study in advance then you'll do fine. Understanding the labs is imperative to your success in this class so make sure you ask lots of questions- he is very approachable!

Professor Monaco is amazing. He kept the class interesting and always had a story. Relatively simple workload, a few reflections, weekly quizzes, and a midterm/final. He is very easy to talk to and did his best to make sure we were prepared for all grades. I definitely recommend Dr. Monaco for KIN 310.
Dr. Monaco is very engaging and helpful. His lectures focus on his own experiences and how they apply to the content.

Professor Monaco is amazing! I had him for my 8AM lecture and even though I felt sleepy, he kept the class going and made it lecture interesting! The course work is very simple, just quizzes on each topic that has to be done before class and 2 overall exams which is very similar to his exam reviews. He is very chill and gives extra credit!

He is truly the best professor. You will learn a great deal from this course and will actually apply the knowledge you gain. This is a professor whom I highly recommend getting to know! I will be taking the other courses he has to offer, as his lectures are very engaging. Extra credit is offered, and I highly recommend taking it as you may need it.
Dr. Monaco was a fantastic professor and very kind.

Dr. Monaco was one of the best teachers Ive ever had at UT. He truly cares about us and wants us to succeed. Even at 8am I would look forward to class as his lectures were great. Quizzes and reflections aren't too bad if you read the textbook and follow the instructions. The tests take a little bit of preparing for but going to class helps a lot.

One of my favorite classes! Dr. Monaco is so passionate about what he's teaching and makes the lectures super engaging. Attendance is mandatory and the exams are easy if you pay attention in lecture and do the readings. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities that are so fun to participate in. Definitely take this class!!

Dr. Monaco is a great professor! He makes lecture intriguing and somehow always finds a way to tie in real life experiences into what he teaches. He offers lots of extra credit opportunities and makes learning fun.

Dr. Monaco is amazing! I enjoyed this class so much. He offers extra credit if you want to take advantage of that. He's very helpful and his personality makes lecture so fun. His story times in lecture are usually very entertaining too. Take this class guys! It's easy and he's a great professor!

TAKE DR. MONACO'S CLASS!!!! If you get the opportunity to take any of his classes, do yourself a favor and take it. Dr. Monaco was my favorite professor that I've had at UT so far and I loved his class. Attendance is mandatory, but his lectures were very engaging, even at 8am. Also, this class has a textbook but he gives you a PDF of it for free!!

Dr. Monaco is one of the best professors at UT. Even at 8 am, his engaging lectures and great stories make you want to show up. He cares about students and learns your name. Quizzes and reflections are simple, the project is fun, and exams are straight from lectures. Take him!

Dr Monaco is the best! Despite it being an 8am, I was always excited to go to class! He does a great job explaining content and keeps the class engaged through relevant stories that are actually entertaining. Dr. Monaco also really cares about every student and makes it a point to know your name if you show up and participate! Take his class!

Dr. Monaco is an excellent professor; his class is organized well and is very manageable. A textbook is used for this course, but, is given to you for free. He is a very engaged professor, asking students questions and allowing students to ask questions, and providing reliable feedback. Overall, I would take a course with this professor again.

Dr. Monaco is great!!! I took this class because it's a major requirement, but I really liked it! Attendance is mandatory but his lectures are really engaging so you actually want to go. He tells many personal stories and examples so that you can connect the content being taught/read from the textbook. It was a really chill class, take it 100%.

Dr. Monaco is a great teacher. The lectures are very engaging, and the weekly quizzes are very simple for that upcoming lecture. Reflections are very simple if you follow the rubric, with a nutrition project that is fun to document. Overall, his exams are on what we learned in the presentation. Amazing professor; hopefully you can get him 10/10.

Dr. Monaco is such an amazing professor, definitely take his class!! He has attendance quizzes which is just a simple question followed by his given answer. The class is lecture based but it's pretty simple, Dr. Monaco is really caring, and he will help you pass this class! Definitely do the extra credit if you need it, it's simple and fun :)

Dr. Monaco is absolutely amazing! I was dreading having an 8am but he made this class so fun and engaging! I enjoy every lecture as they are interesting and he always adds his own stories/experiences that make lecture that much better. We have weekly assignments but they are not bad at all and are pretty easy. Offers extra credit opportunities.

Professor Monaco teaches very well, and the content is pretty simple to remember as long as you review the lectures. His class is filled with interesting stories of his experiences, and he explains the topic well. The tests are simple as long as you study the lecture slides. Before the test, he has a jeopardy game to help review before the test.

Exams are difficult, but if you prepare well ahead of time by spreading out your studying, you will do fine! He may seem intimidating, but he cares, is preparing you to understand the content, and be able to apply it irl. Pay attention in labs, they help in exams greatly.

His class is genuinely so fun, and he brings in a lot of real life stories into class to make it more engaging. He offers lots of extra credit, and the workload isn't bad. He also does good reviews before exams that are very helpful.

Great professor, was scared to have a 8am class but he makes you want to show up! Attendance isn't mandatory but you do get points counted towards you when you show up. Just read the textbook and you will get a A in the class
Even though class is at 8 AM, the lectures are interesting and Monaco has a good speakers presence so your not bored often. Highly recommend the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Monaco is a gem at UT! He keeps lectures interesting by relating the content to his personal experiences. Read the textbook and you'll ace the quizzes and exams, no tricks! Take. This. Class. TONS of extra credit opportunities as well he really wants you to succeed!
Always had relatable, funny stories to keep you interested even in 8am class

Dr. Monaco is one of my favorite professors at UT! His grading is fair and clear. There are weekly quizzes that are short and simple as long as you read the assigned chapter from the textbook. He does great in-class reviews for the midterm and final. Study and submit assignments on time and you should do well!

Dr. Monaco loves what he does and cares about his students. He does his best to make lectures engaging and has so many funny stories to share. Exams are exactly what you would expect, and the material is straight from the textbook. The weekly quizzes are also pretty easy as long as you read the textbook. You won't regret taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best KIN professor I've had, cares a lot about what he lectures on which makes it more engaging. Does an awesome test review in class that makes it easy to do well on exams. Has tons of extra credit opportunities too. Would recommend it!

Loved this class and loved Professor Monaco, the type of class that I actually feel like I gained something out of. He is so interesting to listen to during lectures and tells some funny stories. I would definitely take him again. Review sessions are extremely helpful so I wouldn't miss those for tests. Highly reccommend!

Dr. Monaco is one of my favorite professors I've had at UT. He really cares about his students and enjoys teaching which shows in lecture and lab. This class builds on the intro class material and is very useful for a clinical setting. Discussions are lengthy but lab assignments are easy. Tests are all free response so STUDY, but overall easy A.
My first kinesiology class has been very enjoyable because of Dr. Monaco! He makes lectures engaging with his personal stories. Overall, this class is very manageable to get an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Monaco is my favorite professor I have had so far. I took this class at 8 am and genuinely looked forward to it. His lectures are engaging and he tells a lot of stories that connect to the material which helps (he's also hilarious). There are two exams, a take-home quiz each week, and four written reflections. He offers EC so you'll be okay!

Dr. Monaco is the funniest and most lighthearted professor you'll ever have. I won't lie; I was a little intimidated by him at first, but after talking to him and getting to know him, you'll understand that he truly cares about his students and is passionate about what he does. Take him!!!!
Dr. Monaco is a great professor who really cares about his students learning experience. Knowledge I gained in his class was foundational and useful for future courses.
Dr. Monaco was an amazing professor. He is passionate about what he teaches and also brings such good energy to the classroom.
Professor Monaco, really takes interest in his students and tries to set them up for success.Exams are open ended so make sure to attend lecture. Overall class was engaging and labs were fun!
Great professor, lectures aren't mandatory as long as you keep up with the textbook you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super cool guy who makes it easy to pay attention in class

Dr. Monaco is a very nice professor, and his lectures are interesting and funny. There are weekly quizzes based on the readings. The exams are manageable; you just need to put in some effort. There is extra credit available - exercise study, but it's so easy and fun because you get to learn some info about your physical fitness and flexibility.

Great class overall. Beware that all of the tests are free response, but it really forces you to know the material by heart. It is super interesting/helpful for those who want to pursue PT school and athletic training. Dr. Monaco keeps the class entertaining and fun and I highly recommend it

It's an easy A as long as you put in effort. Exam reviews are super helpful, and throughout the semester, there's opportunities for extra credit. He really wants you to succeed. Although it is mostly lecture-based, he ties the lectures in with his own personal experience, which helps you understand the material from a real-world point of view.
Dr. Monaco was a great professor I'd definitely take his class again. He gives weekly quizzes and as long as you do them on time and study for the exam you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class for my own interest and felt like I actually learn so much about health and wellness. There are some short reflection paper you do that make you realize what areas of your life you should improve to be a little healthier. Exam are easy and straightforward. Really enjoyed this class

Dr. Monaco is a real chill guy and Utes fan!! If you want to go into the PT/OT field take I recommend. Plenty hands on experience and insight on every day clinic life in lab. Exams are entirely free response so KNOW YOUR STUFF, but you should be fine just pay attention in lecture and use time wisely in Lab.

My GOAT. Great personality, great humor, and very knowledgeable over the subject. One of the few classes I've taken that directly applies to my future career as a pre-PT student. Cannot suggest Monaco enough.

Dr. Monaco is easy to talk to, responsive, and kind. There are quizzes on the textbook, reflections, and extra credit. There's a midterm and a final. Extremely do-able by simply studying. I enjoyed his lectures and stories he told the class that were funny, engaging, and always were associated with the topic for those lectures. I 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Monaco gave interesting and worthwhile lectures that were relevant to what is expected on the exams and papers. The materials provided during class were incredibly helpful for the tests. Just show up to class and you will get the grade you want.

Very easy professor to meet with & is attentive to his students. Lectures are simple to keep up with as attendance is not mandatory but off the textbook, Midterm & final are off a jeopardy game. Would definitely take again.

Dr. Monaco was a great professor. His lectures were very clear and easy to be engaged in. There are easy weekly quizzes over a textbook chapter, and you do not actually have to buy the textbook because they post a pdf copy to download. The reflections and tests were very easy as well. Overall a very great class and I really recommend taking him!

Dr. Monaco is an excellent professor who clearly cares about his students. The course format and expectations are clear, and it is easy to succeed in the course. His lectures are straighforward and easily digestible and he does the best he can to keep it interesting for the occasional lecture when the material is dry

Dr. Monaco's Class was very straightforward and organized. There are opportunities for extra credit and the overall workload wasn't what I would consider heavy. His lectures are engaging and he cares about what he teaches, making you want to continue learning. Take his class.
Dr. monaco is really chill and the assignments are pretty easy as long as you take some notes during class. easy A. funny guy too and gives extra credit assignments which are easy too

Dr. Monaco is a great person, but his lectures are not mandatory to learn or attend. If you take good notes to prepare for the weekly quizzes and use the reviews to study for the midterm and final, I think you'll be alright. The other assignments are open throughout the semester. The textbook is where you will spend most of your time learning whether you go to lecture or not. She cares for students' mental health, gives extra credit, and has quizzes as participation.

Overall a passionate professor about biology but cannot translate it into lecture. Never learned much during lecture as it was difficult to follow her. Study guides are vague and exams will pull specific questions under your feet. Very hard to know what will be on test day so you better be prepared to learn EVERYTHING.

Dr. Hansen is a very amazing person. With that said, I had a really hard time learning in her class. The structure always felt a bit odd and I never really understood the realm of what we need to know, it was always kind of a shot in the dark. Very self-oriented class. The lectures were hard to follow. She gave a ton of extra credit.

Such a boring bio class. Her slides are never clear and you basically have to teach yourself the class. Hansen does a terrible job of teaching the material.She asks you more questions than actually lecturing. Her exams have minor details that we probably only talked about once. She does give some assignments to help your grade which is nice I guess
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the goat

She made it extremely difficult to pay attention to lecture with just how dry and boring it was. The slides were inundated with information and nothing was really clear. She does provide plenty of resources, but she is not quality in any sense of the word as a professor.

Easy class, disorganized professor. She is the sweetest person, very kind and available outside of class, but doesn't communicate with her TAs, gets easily distracted, and lectures usually feel like repeats of the text. Turn in work on time and read the text and you get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take Hansen. She does not do her job.

I genuinely believe that Dr. Hansen is a nice woman, but if you can avoid her please do. I took AP Bio and got a 5, and I failed the tests. They are extremely specific, and her lectures are not helpful at all. She either reads the textbook or talks about nothing. You have to teach yourself and it feels like there is no way to prepare for exams
Lectures are pretty average but she genuinely cares about her students and listens to feedback to continuously evolve her course.

Tests are hard; some trick questions are over tiny details only mentioned once in lecture. Class is lax, but you'll be totally fine IF you can hold yourself accountable, show up, and pay attention. Don't let the reviews scare you; a lot of them are from slackers who never went to class/crammed last minute. Dr. Hansen is caring and willing to help.

Dr. Hansen is very sweet and cares about students' mental health. However, her lectures are lacking in depth. Reading the textbook is needed in order to know all the material, as her lectures were very surface level. She has a lot of assignments to pad your grade. Tests are very difficult, but they are curved. Overall, easy A. Hard to learn though.

I took Plan II Bio with Dr. Hansen and I found all the material so interesting! There wasn't really any homework "due" each week, but it was so helpful for the tests to stay up to date with the weekly handouts. Dr. Hansen was so passionate about all the material, and even took us on a field trip! Loved her!
Her exams are awful. Terrible lectures, the only thing helpful about this class is one of the TAs names Tri. If you take this class prepare to do a lot of self studying
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were often convoluted and overly specific. It was mostly a game of guessing what she was trying to ask b/c it didn't match the lectures. I had to read the textbook for the test. Weekly quizzes also ate into the lecture times bc some of them took forever. It felt like I could never catch a break with those. I wouldn't take her again

Dr. Hansen was not that bad, but I gave her this rating because of how every test LAST semester was online  and no backtracking allowed (going back to an old question). That made things very hard for me. Outside of that, everything was fine. She is a very nice person and is willing to meet with you if you need help/anything outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen's class requires a great deal of independence, as her lectures can be fast and confusing. Having taken her two semesters, it's clear that she is still figuring out how to structure her course. Her class consists of 3 exams, weekly quizzes, and misc. assignments. Read the textbook and review her slides to study!

I loved Professor Hansen! She was a great Plan II Bio teacher who's obviously super passionate about her field. Lectures could sometimes feel a little dull because I'm not someone super into biology, but she always made an effort to keep things interesting. Super manageable tests and lots of fun in field trips!

I would not recommend taking Hansen. She is a very kind woman, but she does not know how to teach. Her lectures are heavy and full of jargon, so if you haven't taken AP bio you will be behind. Her quizzes are 3-6 questions, so very difficult to score well. However, she ended up making everything completion since we were all failing and I got an A.

Dr. Hansen is a really kind woman, and you can tell she cares about her students a lot. But, I would not take her! The only way to learn the content is to read the textbook, and her lectures just gloss over the content. Her exams are specific and ask questions about things she mentioned once. Her class was just really frustrating. Don't recommend.

Honestly, probably the worst bio professor you can take. Her lectures are very boring and often go off-topic. Furthermore, she spends most of the lectures quizzing us instead of actually teaching, so the entire class is basically self-taught. Her exams are oddly specific, and I feel like it was the TAs that helped me more than her.

Please have no doubt that she is a truly caring professor, and I regret very much that I realized this too late like at the end of the semester so I didn't work hard therefore didn't do very well, BUT if anyone else were to take her class, please! talk to her when you need help, go to her office hours, I'm 1000% sure she will help you to learn.

Professor Hansen is kind and accommodating. Her tests can be either seem really easy or absurdly difficult based on what parts of the textbook/lecture you paid especially close attention to. "2nd Chance Grading" allows you to receive ~50% of the points that were lost on tests, but the majority of the grades were weekly quizzes/homework (doable).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you do well in this class it isn't because of the professor, it's because you either knew the content beforehand or know how to self study really well. She says that all of the content is in the textbook when it isn't. Her lectures are useless as two of the three class days are used for weekly quizzes. Take anyone but Dr.Hansen for Bio 1 and 2.
Dr. Hansen is the best! She is very accommodating towards students' struggles and needs, and truly wants everyone to do well. If you put good effort in, you will do well in the class!

Hansen is one of the best biology professors at UT. I will admit, you won't learn a ton in lecture. If you don't like to read textbooks, attend class, and study frequently, then you probably won't do well. But Hansen is caring and really wants her students to do well. I would definitely recommend her- she sets clear expectations for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quite literally one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. Not a fan of her teaching style or class structure. Be ready to teach yourself everything.
the only thing that kept me going in this class was one of her TA's named Tri. Everything else was absolutely miserable. DO NOT TAKE! AVOID! AVOID! AVOID!

She literally almost made me switch out of bio as my major. She barely gives you information on what you test is over. Everyone fails her tests and she combats this by giving out assignments where you can makeup points just so not everyone is absolutely bombing the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her exams are extremely hard to prepare for, because you never know what to expect. The information on the exams is super specific, and half the times its not gone over in lecture, just expected to know it from the readings. The only thing saving your grade is how little the exams are actually worth. HW and completion assignments help ur grade alot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her lectures are disorganized and rarely every reach the specificity of her exams. The quizzes every monday over last week's material are graded on accuracy and tank your grade every time you take them. She adds textbook sections to guide your learning but you're left on your own to search up videos and teach yourself on the topic. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take her if you actually want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take her if you actually want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BIO 311C itself is an easy class, especially if you've taken AP Biology in high school, so I wouldn't let the other reviews scare you too much if you're just purely worried about your grade. There is a LOT of extra credit. As for Hansen, she's a sweet woman, but her lectures do not add to your understanding at all. READ THE TEXTBOOK AND SELF-TEACH.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very self-oriented class. You basically have to learn from reading the textbook because her lectures are hard to follow. The tests are really specific and I didn't do so good on them but there's a ton of extra credit and corrections. Developing a relationship with your TA is the key to success in this class. Their discussion powerpoints really help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy but not because of Dr. Hansen. Textbook readings are required but she teaches word for word from the textbook, so lectures are pointless. I did alright on tests, but she does give so much extra credit and completion grades that your grade is boosted a ton. Attendance is graded, but you can easily lie about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I hate her style of teaching, but her class is easy for the most part. I failed two out of 3 midterms and still ended up receiving an A in the class, because she gives so much extra credit. I don't love how she teachers, but she is a lovely person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The sheer amount of content and the specificity of details are the real killers in this class. Combine them with the terribly long textbook readings and her boring lectures, and you have a recipe for disaster. She does offer extra credit and 2nd chance assignments, though. Overall, it's bearable, but avoid her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is a poor lecturer and is very condescending when students ask her questions. However, her TAs are very helpful. Developing a relationship with your TA is the key to success in this class. They have very detailed PowerPoint given in discussion sections, which are the most helpful for Dr. Hansen's very specific exams.

Dr. Hansen is a wonderful person and a pretty decent professor. Her grading scheme is in our favor, and there are plenty of opportunities for free points. She asks really specific questions on tests, but as long as you go to lectures and take good reading notes, the class should be a very easy A.

Dr. Hansen is a very nice woman, just not a very good teacher. I did well in her class because I learned the material all by myself and turned in assignments on time. Lecture did not add very much to my learning experience since she does not teach thoroughly. Tests are very specific and what you're being tested on is not released before any exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are not helpful at all & tests are so specific!! She can be kind of demeaning at times and comes off as unapproachable. I rarely ever read the textbook and still did all right. Honestly not that bad because she gave opportunities to earn points back/extra credit but take a different professor if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Put simply, her tests are over specific and her lectures are useless for the tests. I can say I learned next to nothing.

Do not take this class. She is the worst Biology Professor UT has. Test do not correlate to any of the study material given and ask very specific questions. No retest are allowed and they are hardly ever curves, even when the whole class fails. If it weren't for homework and learning checks I would be failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is rude and her exams are hard

The experience with Dr. Hansen definitely began a lot more frustrating than it ended. I feel like she takes feedback to heart and is big on self-reflection, however, I didn't feel like lectures and her priorities with teaching truly lined up with what was on the exam. She is really sweet and I feel like knowing what to expect helps a lot!
Don't ever take her if you want to actually learn. She does not know how to teach and her exams are worded really weird to the point where you don't actually understand what she's asking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Put simply, if you want an 'A' or if you just want to learn, do not take her class. Her lectures are useless for learning the actual material, but she still expects you to know every little detail of what she doesn't teach you. You'll have about 1.5 hours of videos and two to three chapters a week, which you'll use to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor was unsure about what she was teaching and did not cover many topics and says to read the textbook. Goes through lectures fast and does not give enough time to take note.

She's nice and it's a pretty easy A if you keep up with the homework. The only thing I disliked about her class was how repetitive it was and how much she talks about plants. If you read the textbook, you honestly don't need to pay that much attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's honestly not that bad. The class is boring and the content is repetitive and there is weekly homework but it's manageable if you keep up with everything. At some point, I stopped paying attention in class and just learned with the textbook and the homework, and I still got an A. The chapter quizzes are pretty helpful!

Dr. Hansen is a nice person, but this class is definitely the hardest 311D at UT. Her lectures are basically useless since the course material is so dense. Assessments are designed to trick you with unnecessarily confusing wording and a level of detail not covered in discussion or class. Assignments and hw do help cushion your grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is very kind and caring. Even though the lectures are not helpful, I found the discussion sections (which are led by a TA) and the pre-recorded videos helpful for the quizzes. While the textbook is not necessary, I found it helpful to at least skim it before the quiz. There are a lot of easy assignments to pad your grade.

Dr. Hansen is a sweetheart and I enjoyed her class. She cares about her students mental health and is understanding, even changing some deadlines when the class expressed their stress. The busy work (which wasnt bad) mainly served as a grade cushion because the quizzes can be tough. Watch the lectures, do the assignments, and read the textbook!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's not the worst professor ever but the class wasn't that enjoyable. Her lectures weren't that interesting but they had enough info for the quizzes so textbook isn't necessary unless you want to know more. I really like biology but that interest was dampened after this course. There are definitely better professors to take.

If you get Professor Hansen for Plan II Bio, just drop. It's not worth it. You learn so much less and are working way harder than you otherwise would with another professor. She'd make a great therapist, not a great bio professor.

She was very disorganized the first semester that I took her ( 311C) and Is a bit better now. I never really read the textbooks and looked at her lectures only. Honestly Ill just give it to you straight because I cant find the words to describe her as a professor. Just try to look for different options before taking her.

I took her for 311C and 311D. I would not have done as well in 311C if I hadn't taken AP biology in high school. I liked how online she made it so that the grade didn't only consist of the quizzes. The quizzes are very hard and much different from the study guides. Take another biology teacher if you have the chance.

I took both 311C and now in 311D. Her quizzes are nothing like what she teaches and give no time at all to answer the questions. Very textbook heavy as her lectures vary between random topics or one small part of the whole module. I took her again only because I had her first semester, but I would avoid if I were you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen's teaching style isn't for everyone. She records mini-lectures to watch and they're not really that interesting. She can definitely go on tangents and talk about things that are irrelevant. Definitely read the textbook and Khan Academy videos on the basic concepts. Her quiz questions are confusing so you need to understand the concepts.

She's nice but there is SO MUCH BUSYWORK. She never teaches during actual lectures and all of the class was based off of not so mini "mini lectures" that were on canvas. Tell me why we would spend like 3 hours in class every week and then have to watch like 3 hours of mini lectures in our own time to actually learn. The tests were pretty easy

Dr. Hansen is a very nice person. She genuinely cares for her students and provides so many resources to understand the material. Doing the study guide questions and mini lectures helped me the most. Even if you don't do well on the midterms there are many other things that pad your grade. Look over her learning objectives to prepare for tests.

No Monday lectures! Met on Wednesdays only. Lectures were boring, but all you had to do was show up and answer square caps. Reflections every week - tedious but made getting an A easy peasy. Tests were open book and her wording can be confusing, but as long as you have the book open ur gucci. Hansen is a sweetheart - don't be afraid to take her!

Squarecap was annoying at the beginning. She would close the squarecap question right away. Discussions werent as helpful. I felt like the class was a bit disorganized. The lectures sometimes consisted of her teaching, answering questions or rediscussing topics the entire time. The videos are more useful than her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of the reviews aren't great, but I don't think Professor Hansen was horrible. Definetely not the easiest, but it is not hard to get an A if you work for it. READ THE TEXTBOOK before the mini-midterms!!! Lots of easy assignments to cushion your grade, the only hard part was the mini-midterms. Self-studying is the only way to do good.

Dr. Hansen gets a bad wrap, I think. Her class is something you must study hard for (the 6 mini-midterms and final exam are quite fair but cover the material thoroughly), and a lot of the homework is assigned, but most of that homework is just busy work that will pad your grade. She is very caring, and her TAs are great!

I would def not recommend Hansen. Her lectures are so boring I genuinely could not pay attention to them. We have biweekly midterms and they were always pretty difficult. Lots of opportunities to raise your grade, but I hated this class (and I usually like bio). She's also pretty rude when you ask questions and isn't even very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is hands down the nicest and most understanding professor. Her classes was pretty difficult in my opinion and you have to work for it. Her lectures are pretty lengthy, but informative. What I liked the most is how homeworks and reflection grades (aka cushion grades) weight a LOT which help ur grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Her 311C class was difficult, but in 311D it was clear she was more connected to the material and her lectures were actually enjoyable. This class can easily go awry if you have a bad TA, but she was accessible and nice. Her grading was fair and the material was interesting.

Dr. Hansen was amazing this semester. Her lectures can be a little long, but they're very informative and she really cares about her students. Of all my professors I've never had one who cares as much as Dr. Hansen she genuinely wants everyone to succeed and as long as you give a little effort you will.

HW and reading is pretty heavy, but if you stick to it an A is totally possible. Every week you have prerecorded lectures (1-2hr), abt a chapter to read, and online hw on 3 diff platforms (Simbio, Masteringbio, and squarecap). There's abt 6 tests & a final. Tests can be eh but she gave 2 options to retest & xtra credit. Not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Bio 311C online for the fall semester and I believe the class isn't extremely difficult but it is hard to get an A due to the difficulty of the quizzes. The homework load is somewhat heavy with assignments on 4 different platforms but there are opportunities to still maintain a decent grade with the reflections and homework

Dr. Hansen is really passionate and knowledgeable about biology but she's not my favorite professor. The live lectures sometimes explain complex concepts to us but most times makes them more difficult to understand. The recorded lectures explain things on the surface level but you have to read the textbook heavily to do well on the bi-weekly tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is honestly fine. Tests questions can be tricky, but these "Mini-midterms" are not weighted very heavily. Its helpful to watch her mini-lessons before the week starts to learn most of the material. Textbook is nice to study with, but honestly not necessary.

Professor Hansen was a decent professor. She kinda answers questions in a mildly roundabout way and she has the most soothing voice ever (which makes watching her lectures a little challenging). To get an A, just watch the mini-lessons, read the textbook, take good notes, and go to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extremely, extremely textbook heavy. The bulk of your work is reading and mastering textbook material by yourself. Lectures are mainly just a summary of what the textbook is on and not valuable on its own, but the textbook readings are really the main thing. She makes really useful study guides though, but this is def a self study class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally some of the most boring lectures I have ever listened to. I don't know if it's her voice or what, but even her attempts to be interesting fall painfully flat. Her questions are very application-based, which isn't something I'm going to complain about, although it makes the course significantly harder. This is my impression 5wks in

ONLINE TRANSITION - I was nervous to take the class reading her previous ratings for in-person but it was entirely opposite experience online. Dr. Hansen's online transition format should be replicated through most web-based courses at UT. She's understanding. She adjusts. Weekly quizzes substitute midterms. Lots of recordings but super manageable!

Love the prof, she's so sweet. Class was decently organized. DS mandatory, although not very useful. She adapted super well to online classes. Use the LOs, close guide for tests, which are more specific to her lectures/modules than textbook.

Dr. Hansen is overall a really great professor. She has engaging lectures and is always really sweet and funny. You have to really study to get a good grade on the tests, which are on a lot of different topics. She transitioned really well into online learning and actually made the class easier. Also, get the Vital source E-Book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is amazing! I admit I wasn't too big of a fan at the beginning, but she is so sweet and knowledgable and caring that I ended up loving her. Go to class, participate in assignments and use !! the !! LOs!! and you will get a good grade :)

Dr. Hansen truly cares about her students and is willing to go the extra mile to help them. Her lectures are often boring, but cover all content required for tests. The Learning Outcome handouts that she provides are very helpful in preparing for the tests as well. Keeping up with these and revisiting them really helped me do well on the exams.

Dr. Hansen isn't my favorite lecturer, so I recommend reading the textbook a fair amount. If you are ever concerned about misreading, don't be afraid to speak to Dr. Hansen, she will listen to you and try to help. Her office hours weren't my favorite, but if you truly need help don't be afraid to go see her.
Just finished my second semester with Dr. Hansen, and she still remains my favorite prof at UT. Her passion for biology shines through in lecture -- along with her sense of humor. Go Dr. Hansen!

Hansen is very sweet and so passionate about biology. The subject matter can get tough at times. I personally liked her soothing voice but it put my friend to sleep. Its very important to listen to her lectures and take notes from them. You learn from the textbook but the lectures reinforce the information you need for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen should have a higher rating in my opinion. She is clearly passionate about her students and offers many resources inside and outside of class for students to do well and succeed. If you make an effort and do the worksheets, you'll do well. Note: this is a review for last semester, AKA before the coronavirus online switch.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I do not know why so many people are ragging on Hansen. I only took her for 311D, but the course was not very hard. Lectures could be dull at times, but she is clearly passionate about the subject. I was able to get by learning from her lecture slides and small amounts of supplemental reading from the text book. Don't be scared of her rating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: By far, the worst professor that I have ever taken at UT. Her exams were extremely difficult. I would record her lectures, read the book, and do her review outline worksheets and I still did not get good grades on the exam. Take any other professor but Hansen. I attended her office hours to see how I could improve and she was very patronizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for 311C and D and her class was manageable, but I didn't really like her lecture style. She's not as bad as all of the other reviews say, but her tests were annoyingly specific and oddly worded. She cares about helping and she definitely works with students. She did cancel all tests and the final during the pandemic which was really cool

Very Rude during Office Hours criticizing you why you don't understand the material when that's why we're here. She called us Monkeys one time on the discussion board, basically calling some people idiots in not knowing how to work Canvas. Tests are very hard and textbook heavy but her questions are tricky. Her lectures are not super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, her class is pretty easy as along as you read the book and her PowerPoints. Her lectures are a little dull though. I personally don't think she's as bad as all these posts make her out to be, but I do understand why people criticize her lectures.

Hah if you get Hansen for Bio, do yourself a favor and switch to ANY other professor. Lectures: slow, boring & put the whole class to sleep. NEED to read the textbook, meaning teach yourself all the material bc lectures were pointless. Shes a big fan of independent learning and does her job to not teach in class so you have to learn on your own.

The worst professor I have ever had at UT. Lectures are not relevant to the tests whatsoever. TA's are completely useless and don't help at all. She does not care about her students doing well, and she never makes it clear what we need to know for the test. Horrible resources, horrible class, horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I cannot express how horrible she was. Bio311D is not that difficult of a course, but she insists that we do all of our learning on our own, as her lectures are absolutely irrelevant and she does not provide and information for the test except for the textbook. She never gives us answers during class and just wants us to figure it out ourselves.
Terrible class.

She's a terrible lecturer as a lot of what she lectures isn't relevant to the exam, but her class is not hard to get an A in. You need to read the textbook and make sure you study the learning objectives and modules posted online. The majority of your grade comes from tests. Read the textbook consistently on top of that and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If youre not into reading everyday this prof is not for you. Tests were really hard and extremely specific, and lectures werent very helpful. Only like 2 good TAs and thats if you get lucky. Godspeed if you have her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are tough, if you read the textbook they are doable; she replaces the lowest with an average of the 3. She provides tons of self-quizzing opportunities both in/out of class that are super helpful. She's also super understanding; I missed the final and had an issue with an assignment because I took someone to the ER-I was able to do both late
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She wasn't terrible but she definitely had room for improvement. Hansen was sweet, but she has a habit of answering your questions with "yes, but also no," which never really cleared things up for me. Test questions come from specific things she says in lectures, but the LOs and weekly self-quizzes will save you!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sweet professor, she really cares about her students. If you take her class, you're gonna have to read weekly. However, if you're a good reader I would definitely recommend this class because the tests are a breeze if you read the book. Her lectures aren't great but very doable A, plus she and her TAs are very accessible outside class

Only take Dr. Hansen, if you are ready to read a whole chapter before going to lecture everyday. Her lectures are not meant to teach you but rather reinforce you. Take notes during lectures or you won't understand it when you look back at it. Her test are kind of tricky but doable. Use lecture materials to study for test. Recording her lecture!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is a lot nicer/better than some of these reviews make her out to be. She really is a nice professor, and lectures in a fun/passionate way. She seems very caring and wants her kids to do well. However, this class is very tough and you need to rely on the textbook. Her lectures weren't helpful to me but I had to go for attendance points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You will def have to work for your grade in this class, but it is totally doable. Skim the textbook and take clear notes from her lecture slides (posted on tophat) though they can get confusing. She posts modules for each unit with extra notes and videos that is super helpful for exams. She ends up giving extra credit at the end too. You MUST study
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansens lectures are mostly mandatory but they don't really help you prepare for the tests, she lectures over very specific topics and fun facts. If you get behind in reading it's very hard to understand what is going on in class. The textbook is really the only resource provided by the class. The tests are worded in a very tricky way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Annoying online modules, way too much homework, cares way too much about plants for an introductory course, takes attendance for boring lectures, loves trick questions on exams, rude in office hours I have continued on as a Bio major and this is the only other Bio course that I have received below a B+ in, it's definitely her not me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen's class comes with a bit of a learning curve, but you will truly understand bio after her class is over. The LOs she provides are extremely helpful; you will be well prepared for her tests if you go through all the modules and the slides before. Her TAs are also helpful, and she is quick to answer questions electronically.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Hansen for 311C and 311D. I have so much respect for her; she is so caring and made biology extremely interesting. I looked forward to her witty jokes/comments and her easy-to-digest explanations of the course material. I really enjoyed the class. It is difficult, especially without previous biology exposure, but it's worth it.

Unless you already know everything about biology and love reading the textbook... do NOT take this class. She is super sweet but not good at teaching during lecture and tests are tricky. TAs aren't great either.

There is a way to do good in her class, I just never figured it out. Her teaching style is very disorganized and difficult to understand for someone coming in with essentially no prior knowledge in biology. If youve taken other bio classes, or if you took AP Bio, you can most likely pull off an A with some effort. If not, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is a really sweet lady. However if you don't learn well through reading textbooks then this professor probably isn't for you. I found her lectures to be unengaging and having little to do with what is actually going to be on the exam. Her TA's were okay but I felt like the whole semester was very unclear in what she was trying to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is amazing. She is very knowledgeable about her field and studies botany on the side (which I love). Furthermore, grading isnt too hard and shes funny in lecture. The tests are straightforward. Also, she brought a giant bowl of mini M&Ms to class! Cant beat that. Will try to take bio311D with her next semester.

Lectures and discussions were mandatory as they count for a grade but I honestly wasnt able to take notes during lecture with the 50+ slide powerpoints she flew through in 50 minutes. Test questions were terribly confusing but I dont think the free response was graded strictly. Tough, plant-focused class and you must review her slides carefully!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class as a non-science major for fun, inspired by AP bio in HS and 311C with Dr. Fritz. I realized this class was not what I expected when I got B's on the midterms. Lectures are dull/boring and focus on plants. An A is still achievable if you put in the work (read textbook after lectures). I pulled up my grade from a B with the final.

The material is disorganized and taught out of order which can make studying and knowing what is expected of you for the tests difficult. However, Dr. Hansen is enthusiastic and caring. She is passionate about biology and the lectures were never boring. It's not hard to do good if you show up. Never once used the book.

Dr. Hansen is a lot better than what others make her out to be. I ended up with an A in this class (a 97) by reading over her lecture slides and taking notes during her lectures, along with utilizing the textbook. I worked really hard for this A though, so her class wasn't the easiest, but definitely doable with effort!

Unless you LOVE plants, do NOT take Bio 311D with her. The structure of her lectures was all over the place and hard to follow. If you learn by connecting topics, this is not the professor for you. She bounces from topic to topic and then goes back to the first topic with no pattern. I had to teach myself with the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My biggest regret was not switching out of her class. She always dragged her lectures on until the very last minute. So dry. Her answers to your questions are very vague. & don't even get me started with her tests. Not good. Wording is so confusing. I don't even have any tips for this class. Just don't take bio311d with her. Save your GPA!
Nothing in this class connected for me. I've always loved biology, but I couldn't stand this class. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was just terrible, boring lectures that really did not help when it came to the exam. This class was a constant stress and no fun at all. The reason why I hate biology.

She sounds a little dry but I swear her lectures are interesting if you can pay attention. Or watch her recorded lectures on x1.5 because they are very clear and concise and helpful. Her tests are fair, definitely not easy but if you do the LOs (!!!!) and watch her lectures, you really should be fine. I like biology so I am a bit biased, but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were not engaging at all and tests were too specific to really measure your knowledge. TA's are very helpful, but not enough to make me like this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I heard a lot of negative things about Dr. Hansen, but I had an awesome experience in her class. She is really kind and cares about her students. She gives out "LO handouts" for every unit, and they are pretty much papers that show the topics she could test you over, and the corresponding readings. Do the LOs and go to class and you will do well

Pretty solid for a first year introductory course. Professor Hansen was cool. Not much else to say, except don't forget about the homework just because it's online and not graded until the end (hehe).
Dr. Hansen was an awesome professor! She made all of the material learnable, and I learned quite a lot from this class.
Hansen was an easy A in my opinion, but her lectures weren't very interesting. If you read the textbook, her tests are very straightforward.

Lectures were pretty much pointless except for activities she would assign. Discussion was also pointless, but if you show up you get the points. Biology multiple choice wording tends to be a little unclear, but reading the textbook and the LO handouts really guarantee a good grade. Memorization is key - put in the work and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didn't think she was as bad as other reviews. Boring lectures, okay workload. Highly recommend reading the textbook. Discussion was pointless, but my TA was nice. Tests were okay, but the final was so hard due to the wording for me.
She's literally the worst prof ever. She only cares about plants. Take anyone else for 311C and 311D.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: When I first got stuck with Hansen, I was terrified because of the terrible reviews. Don't listen to them! She gives LO handouts that literally spell out what she'll be testing over for each unit. It takes a lot of time to go through the textbook and do the work, but that's how you're going to learn. Put in the work & you'll be totally fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For people who expect to read the textbook as a supplement to lectures, Hansen's really not that bad. She does have a tendency to avoid direct answers to questions, but her worksheets and lectures are engaging and get the point across. Her class isn't boring. :-) It's intensive, but she does a good job at emphasizing the important messages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Although a lot of people hate Dr. Hansen, I think she is the best. She tries her best to explain the material and you can really tell that she is passionate about what she is teaching. If you skip her class, you will not pass. Her tests are usually based on the powerpoints (from her lecture) but it is better to also read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I thought the class overall wasn't bad. Her tests weren't that difficult with the proper amount of studying and her Learning modules helped a lot. Her lectures can be boring but I think that she still understands the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I do not know why no one likes her. She is honestly not a bad teacher. Some of the topics in the class are boring in nature and there is nothing you can do about it. Her tests are pretty easy to study for and assignments are pretty light. If you are looking not to die over biology, you should highly consider taking this class. You learn alot too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class turned me from being passionate about biology to hating it. Hansen is a terrible lecturer, doesn't understand the material herself. Tests are EXTREMELY specific. SO much busy work hw. You can understand 100% and make a 70%. Study old tests, do the LOs. If you can, get another professor. She is awful. Switching my major after having her.

311C required a lot of studying, but her structuring of the class forces you to discover and retain an in depth understanding of how life works at a microscopic level.
