If youre a BS & truly want understand why things are the way they are, TAKE HER! It really helped to draw out each chapter in a detailed diagram. She pushes you bc she cares.

Dr. Hansen is really nice and clearly passionate about her teachings. However, her tests are extremely unpredictable. I spend 12+ hours studying for each exam, yet my exam average for the class is a B. You can put in infinite amounts of work and still not get the results you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are structured weird. Discussions are really useless. Exams are hard. The questions are either super vague or really specific. Rely on reading the book and doing LOs if you want to pass the exams. Overall, she's an eh professor, but she cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: BIO301E was ridiculously easy. Debra was very good at teaching the material, and if you have any interest in the subject whatsoever, you should ace the tests. Tests were almost all short answer, describing stories of what happened in biological discoveries. Come to 1/3 of the classes and you'll get enough info for an A. Papers were easy As.

Dr. Hansen really cares about her students. I had some issues with a final grade and she went through the class records and found a misgrade that ended up in getting a grade bump. She gives extra credit that helps your grade and cares about the subject. There's a lot of information and the tests can be tough, but if you put the work you can do it.

Hansen is a really bad teacher but her class isnt that hard. I stopped going to class after the second test and all i did was read the textbook and i aced every test. Homework is all on quizlet and she grades for attendance but i received a 100 and missed countless classes.

Professor Hansen may not be the best at teaching, but if you follow her directions in class, getting a good grade is probable. I received a 78 on my first test and got a rude awakening with this class. You can't rely directly on the professor and her lectures, but if you study the textbook and Tophat well enough, then getting an A is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I went into this class expecting the worst from previous reviews. It's honestly not that bad. The key to succeeding is to just READ THE TEXTBOOK and do the LOs. The tests, like most bio tests at UT, are tricky, but you get used to the style. Her style of teaching is more review what you should have read before class than teaching new material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Oh Debra... If I hadn't met a really good friend of mine in her class, I swear I wouldn't have survived. She isn't a good lecturer at all, and like others have said has the remarkable ability to never directly answer a single question. If you aren't good at chemistry or have an attraction to plants, you probably won't love Debra.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: LOL don't take this woman's class. She is disrespectful and does not answer any questions that you ask her. Her tests are extremely specific, but her lectures are very vague. One day, when she learns how to be respectful and teach her students, maybe her class will be okay. Expect to teach yourself everything and only ask TAs (not all) for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen simply doesn't teach. Her lectures are overly simplified and very vague, while tests are extremely specific and wordy. It's very easy to thoroughly understand the material and still do poorly. It takes WAY too much to do well in this class. Get another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This professor gives an excessive amount of homework that will not help you on the test. Her lecturing skill is poor, and it is flat out hard to pay attention in class. Tests are generally fair, and you can do well if you study the things she emphasizes. Overall, the professor is ok, but switch out if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen was not the best at teaching. She says upfront that she will not spend time over things you can simply read about. The "learning objective" handouts & reading the textbook helps on the test the most. Attendance is technically mandatory, but some people would answer the online questions from home. There are hopefully better professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class. Lectures are hard to pay attention to and she usually doesn't answer students' questions; she will reverse it and say "you tell me". She seems nice, but she's not a great professor. The exams can be difficult, but it's manageable.

You can tell that Dr. Hansen is a super sweet person. She's just not a good lecturer at all. The tests are ridiculously hard and the multiple choice are tricky and based off small details from the text book. The stuff that she goes over in class don't even begin to cover what's on the test, so make sure to read the book heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is an incredibly sweet woman who loves biology. I think her teaching skills (in 311C) were impaired by her lack of passion for microbiology. Her TAs were not incredible, however, Santos was usually on top of things. Tests are worded weirdly. Hansen's office hours are helpful though. I wouldn't have enjoyed the class if I didn't love bio.
The class is mainly test focused so make sure you're not cramming otherwise the questions will catch you off guard. Also details, details, details. They can make or break your test grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 84% of your grade is determined by your test grades. There are three midterms making up 60% and a final of 24%. If you are not a good test taker do not take her. On the multiple choice questions in her exams she really tries to trick students. Towards the middle and end of the semester she started to somewhat make attendance mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: As long as you pay attention in lecture you should be fine for the tests. She also hands out packets of what you need to know on the exam. If you did well in AP bio you'll definitely do fine. One thing is that she won't answer her own lecture questions unless you ask directly. Everything you need to know is in the handouts-use textbook for clarity
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly, many people don't like her class because it truly is a college environment. What I mean is that she just lectures and that you have to teach yourself the material too. She does a great job summarizing the textbook and honestly so long as you work you will be fine. If you don't like that idea, why are you attending college? Best of luck!

I don't recommend this lady at all. She's a horrible person who doesn't care if you do well or not. If you're looking to take a class to teach yourself and learn how to fail, then take this class. I'm a pretty good student and I'm struggling so I wouldn't take her unless its the last teacher available. She has no idea what she's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was made intentionally difficult and had the opportunity to be a learning experience. Her tests are pre-made somewhere online, but unless you are in a group that knows where to find them good luck. You have an 1hr15 minutes to answer 35 questions that are longer than this review. 3 exams that weigh heavy. Lectures are not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her tests are tough and have tricky wording. It is hard to know what to study in detail for the test. Her lectures are okay. Her power points are basically just explaining photos from the text book, so if you really want to learn, listen in class and bury your head in the text book. It is a doable class as long as you put in the work to learn.

Okay, I know biology is a weed-out class, but she makes it so hard to want to try. Her lectures are boring and unnecessary because all of her tests are based on Learning Objectives and random facts from the textbooks. I would choose another bio professor. Maybe one less hysterical and condescending.

I'm sitting in hansen's class right now and I wish I hadn't come. She has an incredible ability to not answer a single question, even when asked directly. On top of this, her lectures are confusing and not relevant to the tests. Study the textbooks, go to the TAs (not gustavo), and really know your stuff and you'll be fine, but don't expect help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hansen is a great choice of professor. Her lectures are clear, and they're all posted online later. Her exams cover what's on her lecture, not sneaky textbook excerpts. I didn't even bother to buy the book and learned everything I needed for Genetics and Biochem on her lectures alone. And her extra credit is great! Highly recommend.

From personal experience with classmates, I know that most of the people who complain about Hansen complain because they slacked when exams rolled around-blaming her. I had a great experience with her, and didn't buy or read the book once. Just reread her powerpoints and take advantage of the abundance of extra credit she offers!! She's super sweet

This woman ruined my mental state for a solid 8 months. She was a boring lecturer with immensely unfair tests. Do the learning objectives, know them back and forth and hope for the best with the tests. She would overlook huge topics in tests while pinpointing dumb facts. Study more than you need to, and study the lectures before book. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Going to class is mandatory because there are questions that you have to answer. For the tests you have to study a lot: they cover materials from lectures, from textbook, and from the quizzes. You definitely have to work hard to get an A in this class. There is also weekly discussion that is graded on attendance and accuracy in answering questions.

Kind person but inefficient lecturer. Did not enjoy her class at all and her lectures were super boring. Tests are decent only if you study, otherwise its not going to go your way. If you love plants, then take her... but otherwise steer clear...
debra was super annoying, she loved plants too much and isnt clear on what to study for
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hansen's lectures are boring & she is bad at answering questions. She loves ambiguous TopHat ?s during lecture. But  311D material isn't bad & her class is doable with the textbook and learning handouts. The homework is weekly, not useful but not hard.  The tests are not bad - multiple choice and free response that you can usually predict.

Her lectures are awful, but she gives a lot of extra credit which got me from a C to a B.  She is a super sweet lady and really cares about biology and wants you to learn.  She just refuses to change her lecture style.  Learned more from my TA during recitation than from her.

Dr. Hansen is by far my least favorite professor. The homework is ridiculous and it's through a textbook access code so it's hard to keep up with deadlines because they change randomly. She barely mentions topics covered on the exam? Her multiple choice are either very vague or super specific so good luck with that. Take anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: First day of class she'll tell you to not rely on the book, that's a lie. The book is your only friend in this class. She gives weekly quizzes with all "select all that apply" but gives no partial credit. Didn't really learn much in class and her tests were hard. I did okay only due to my prior knowledge in biology, but she helps in nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The tests in this class were not too bad, but you definitely had to read the textbook to understand what was going on. There is not a criteria given for what is expected on the tests, so you have to just memorize everything. Attendance is mandatory because you have to answer questions online during class. If you work hard, you can get an A.

Dr. Hansen is the best Intro Biology teacher at UT in my opinion. Her lectures are well-structured and easy to follow. She is always very happy and gives all the material you need to succeed. The way her class is structured allows for ample opportunities to review the material. She is a very compassionate person and is willing to work with you.

If you don't have a textbook, don't expect to pass. Lectures may be mandatory and include a participatory/attendance grade, but knowing which chapters to read is more important to pass. All homework assigned is over the textbook, and all tests and final include information that is 90% from the book. It's possible to make an A with B+ scoring tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Hansen's class is not that hard. As long as you keep up with the readings and understand the material, you will do fine on the exams. The homework assignments are basically completion grades. She also gives extra credit that can potentially raise your overall grade by 2%. However, she is a terrible lecturer, and she isn't very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I was able to add almost 2 full points to my grade through EC. Hansen is fine, not great, but really not that bad. Read the textbook like you are supposed to, and you will get a good grade. The homework is easy and the TAs are pretty great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The textbook is definitely required, the online quizzes will sometimes ask you about specific diagrams in a chapter. She is not the best at explaining things, so if you have questions it's usually a waste of time to ask her. The worst part of her class is that a lot of her questions are unclear on tests and even the TAs admit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Just like everyone else said, unless you want to think to yourself "why am I here" in lecture, I recommend finding another bio professor. Lectures are a waste of an hour that could be spent reviewing the textbook. Test questions are meant to trip you up and overall the class isn't difficult, but tricky. Nice lady, bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen is a nice and she cares, but her teaching style is just bad. Half of her lectures are just  questions, and she never tells us what the correct answers are. She also uses a different edition of the textbook than is required for the class for test questions. and if you ask her a question, she answers with another question. awful, BEWARE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For the final exam she posted an announcement telling us to let her know if she had any questions and after I sent her my questions with ideas about what the answer may be, she emailed me back to let me know she wouldn't answer any of them because figuring it out on my own is how I would learn. Avoid this lady at all costs.

Hansen is nice but being nice doesn't make you a good teacher. Extremely picky when grading and makes you feel stupid for asking seemingly "obvious" questions in class. People think that the students who give professors low scores are failing the class and are just mad but that is not always the case. HEED OUR WARNINGS!!!!! Do NOT take her class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you take Dr. Hansen, be prepared to self-teach the entire semester. If you ask her a question, she will beat around the bush worse than a politician. This woman is a horrible teacher and honestly should not be employed as such.  I truly would advise taking bio another semester rather than taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She rambles a lot and hardly every directly answers a question. We did top hat quizzes for class attendance and she never actually says what the right answers are but she seems to think she is explaining something. My TA was nice and much more clear but Dr. Hansen honestly sounds like she doesn't have a clue.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Hansen makes biology very unbearable. It's almost as if she doesn't even know the material herself.  She asks lots of questions in class, and never provides the correct answer, leaving her students very confused.  Not worth your time-- I would honestly recommend taking Bio another semester if she is your only choice.
She just assume you know everything and she teach the simplest things in class but have questions on the test that is not even understandable. DO NOT TAKE HER.

Worst professor I've ever had at UT. She is HORRIBLE. Her lectures are irrelevant to the tests and she is impossible to please. The tests are filled with mediocre facts that were never mentioned in the reading or lecture. It's impossible to know what to study. Sweet lady, horrible professor.

This course was far more difficult than an intro course should be. This was because her tests were very tricky, especially Mc parts. Her study guide questions are only like 50% relevant to helping one study for the tests. Also, her hws are irrelevant. Making an A isn't impossible but it is definitely going to be rough. Positive side: she's nice.

3 Test, 1 Final, Homework, and participation points. Homework was useless and a waste of time. Lectures are disorganized and choppy. Lectures are just powerpoint with questions on them. Difficult to judge what to study. TA that I had seemed like she didn't know much about biology. Recommendation: Find another professor

Do not take her. Very confusing and gives convoluted lectures. She emphasizes plants too much because she is a plant biologist. She is a sweet lady, but awful teacher. TAs aren't very good either. Overall, awful experience!!

What a fantastic professor! Was there to help students during office hours and her lectures were clear and concise. Her exams were super easy and there are also extra credit to help you out! I had no problem studying and only studied for a day before the exam.

DO NOT TAKE HER! Although her class is not that hard to make an A in, she is a terrible professor. She always responds to questions with rhetorical questions, and her office hours are a joke. She will not help you for the exams at all, so you're on your own.  Also, she made the final ridiculously hard compared to previous tests.

Lectures are very boring and very confusing. She's very patronizing and will look down upon you if you ask questions she deems stupid. She will rarely directly answer a question, instead she'll pose a new question that'll confuse you even more. You'll basically have to fuse with your textbook in order to do well.I highly regret taking this course.

It's not so much that the test material is hard, but the way she structures the test is made to make you do terribly. She also readily admits that she throws in at least two questions from the multiple choice (out of about 20) that she knows no one will get right. Free response isn't bad. She is also by far the rudest professor I have ever met.

Dr. Hansen's class was doable, a lot less harder than the previous reviews made it seem. Tests are based off the lectures and handouts. MC is definitely way harder than the Free Response, you really need to know your stuff. Homework is tedious but very easy. Her lectures were boring but you can tell she loves plants and biology.

Hansen's class if fair. You can do well in her class by reading the book and reviewing the slides before tests. Go to class for participation. Discussion is useless. Maximize your points on homework, and be sure to do all EC things. Her tests are 20 MC, 4 FR, and 2 EC questions. FR comes straight from handouts. MC is trickier bc of wording.

After reading many of the reviews, I have to say that I think a lot of the negativity is unwarranted. Is she a tough grader? Yes. Are her tests tricky at times? Yes. With that being said, she definitely has a passion for biology, and while her lectures may be dry, she does her best to relate the topics learned in class to the real world.

Dr. Hansen was an alright professor. Her tests were tough only bc the multiple choice was oddly worded, but if you do her lecture handouts you should be fine since her short answer questions come from them. Also she does provide EC through bonus questions on exams, extra credit assignments and Mastering Bio HW. If you study hard you'll be fine!
Tests don't have anything to do with material covered in class, lectures are full of obscure examples. Tedious homeworks. Would not recommend at all.

If I could take a diff bio prof, I would. Hansen's tests cover a ridiculous amount of material & she never gives reviews and teaches whole units right before exams, which forces you to have to KNOW EVERYTHING even though it probably won't be tested. Also, lectures are super boring and she answers everything with rhetorical questions
DO NOT TAKE HER! Her explanations are not clear and the powerpoints are not helpful whatsoever.

ABOUT 40 PERCENT OF THE CLASS FAILS HER EXAMS EVERY TIME!! SHE IS A TERRIBLE PROFESSOR. SHE WILL NOT TELL YOU WHAT TO STUDY FOR EXAMS. SHE WILL NOT GIVE YOU A REVIEW. SOMETIMES YOU WILL STIL LBE GOING OVER A WHOLE CHAPTER THE CLASS BEFORE YOU ARE TESTS( EX: UNIT 2 IS OVER 7 CHAPTER, WE LEARNED THE 7TH THE WEDNESDAY BEFORE THE FRIDAY EXAM) RUN!!
AVOID HER AT ALL COST!!! SHE WILL RUIN YOUR GPA.
RUN!!!!If you love yourself you will stay away from this teacher.

Her lectures are boring and she doesn't explain anything well enough even in office hours. You have to read the textbook to understand what's going on but you could probably manage a C by just going to lectures. Homework is assigned regularly but not announced so that's something you have to keep up with. Tests are fairly easy.

The only way to do well in this class is to  memorize the textbook. Hansen's lectures are useless and her power points are awful. She's not clear with her explanations and goes into detail on topics that don't even show up on the test! I was really hesitant to take this class, but it was the only one available...I was right to be nervous.

This class was a complete waste of my time! The tests weren't that hard if you took IB/AP in high school, but she was very boring. She replaces the lowest test grade with the average of ALL tests, even the lowest one. Also, her PowerPoints were annoying because she just has a bunch of questions without any answers. She is very sweet, though.

Not an engaging lecturer. Hands out in-class optional worksheets that are sorta helpful but mostly annoying and time-consuming. Has iClicker questions but sometimes is vague about the answers. Tests are fair. Online HW is easy and really helpful. Gives out 2-3 EC points on each test. If you read the textbook, you don't need to listen to lecture.

You really have to work for an A, but she's the best bio prof I've had. 4 Exams (1 drop; tests are 20 MC and 3 free response), weekly homework, clicker questions for participation, and in-class assignments occasionally. She writes barely any information on her lecture slides, so attendance is a must and notes are key. Tests are not easy, but fair.

Definitely one of the worst  professors I have had--her lectures are just rhetorical questions and you don't learn anything. Each test covers like 8 chapters and you have no guidance as to what material to master.
You have to read the book front and back in order to do well on the tests. Do yourself a favor and don't take this teacher.

Her lectures were pretty hard to follow (a lot of rhetorical questions on her power point slides), I stopped taking notes in class (but continued to go for clicker points) after the first test and started doing better in the class by focusing on the book and the learning modules. The online homework is time consuming.
Sweetheart professor. Boring lectures. But there's no other way to cover the material
Studied off of her PPTs and did fine!

Dr. Hansen's lectures can sometimes be a bit boring because it involves a lot of powerpoint slides. This course is not an easy A, because you have to work for it. The exams were very fair, and she provided objective questions that if you knew the answers you would probably do well on short essay questions.

She was extremely knowledgable. Always willing to meet with me one on one and explain things. Her tests aren't too bad, they were pretty fair overall. She gives out a TON of extra credit so do it! I had an A in the class until the final, which was pretty hard, so start off doing well in the class and you'll be fine. By far better than my last prof.

Among the worst classes I have taken in my life. It is not an easy A, yet is not hard to get one. If you like biology, you will be disappointed because she will not teach you anything. She also does not have a good heart, and will not help you if you are missing a decimal. I would not even consider taking her again.

Dr. Hansen is really nice but really boring. Her tests are okay  but you have to read ALOT for her class. She doesn't really teach. She just reads off of her PowerPoint slides the whole time. She cares and will try to help you but she is not a great teacher. If you're willing to read and teach yourself, go for it. I wouldn't take her.

She's pretty easy.  She gives learning objectives that as long as you can answer, you will be fine. TONS of extra credit. She chooses out of the learning objectives for the essay questions on exams, so you know what they'll be. Our exam averages have been 84, 87, and 89, so she's pretty easy.

She's a fairly new teacher, and so she can seem quite unorganized sometimes. Attendance is encouraged, though her lectures are online - mostly because of iclicker quizzes. Tests are pretty straightforward and not bad if you understand the concepts.

The ratings of her good is a joke. Just complete lies. Her lectures will bore you to death. I literally fell asleep in every class she had. Only reason I had to stay awake was b/c of her stupid clicker questions. Her powerpoints are full of a lot of bs stuff and she says everything she says is on the exam when like 5%. Would not take herif i were u
Class was pretty much a guaranteed at least a B+ if you go to class, do the online homework and attend the discussion lecture. Make sure you understand the material though.

This was her first semester teaching and she was extremely nervous before. Everyone bombed the first midterm but then she was able to give generous curves. She's extremely helpful and would give out many extra credit assignments; also she tells the questions that would be on the exam. An easy A! I liked her

The professor can be difficult to contact. The professor will spend 30+ minutes on the warm-up and skim through the content covered on the test. There are no extra-credit opportunities. Test reviews can be long and don't reflect the test. Be ready to learn on your own if you take this class, and be an expert in algebra and trig.

This professor is nice and sounds passionate about the subject, but he spent forever on the warmup problems and barely any time on content that I found mattered. Homeworks took hours to accomplish and the discussions barely helped for exams. Practice problems will be your best friend to survive this class.

Jay is decent, but the math department truly is awful. The lectures are fine, but he typically solves halfway and then you have to wait and ask later for help. The practice exams do not help, they are old exams and don't match at all. Several Homeworks a week that require office hours since the questions aren't answered in Lecture.

Half the lectures were useless and it was a lot of self study and homework. The TA discussions were weirdly hard and not very helpful but that might be up to the TA. He's a nice guy but not great at teaching. Sanger saved me a lot this semester. Also tests make up like +60% in your grade.

Professor is a very kind man. However, his lectures are very disorganized. He spends more than 30 minutes on warmups which are sometimes helpful. TA isn't much help either, often gets many things wrong and is just as lost as the students sometimes. Exams make up most of your grade so be ready for that. Be ready to study and to have a hard time.

Lectures are fast and can get confusing the way he explains things, but we had learning modules in my class so we could learn outside of the lectures. Very nice guy though, willing to explain any concepts after class or in office hours. Tests not super hard but not super easy.

Grading took forever, majority of lecture spent catching up on previous lectures, so much hw - difficult to manage on top of the amt of studying for unnecessarily hard exams and quizzes, TA (ballet slippers, black toenails, outfit repeater) was zero help; instead of questions we could be tested on, spent time trying to explain phd math concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This ninja is so bad. Ignore the glazers in the section they lowkey busted ifywim for him. Got an A but had to grind so hard. Very nice guy but can teach and is abs garbage at p much everything to else. DONT take him 408d is supposed to be a blow off for ap bc 5ers but ts was NOT.

jay is a very caring professor. 2 learning modules, quest, and written hw due per week. personally, i found lecture to be useful (esp. warmups). exams weren't bad, and he posted lengthy review sets that were really helpful in studying. definitely doable if you put in the effort- go to office hours and review old homeworks. would take him again!

He truly did care, but just was super unorganized. Homework heavy, four assignments due a week. He gave reviews to tests, but no answers. Lectures weren't helpful in my opinion. If anything go to discussion!!!! Kris, the TA was amazing!! Tests were pretty straightforward, actually do the homework and do the reviews and you'll be fine.

Took in Fall '24: Prof Whitehead is a really nice guy, but this class was super disorganized, answer keys didn't exist for hw outside of quest, super weird/conceptual questions on tests. HW was hard, quizzes were okay, exams were hard, final was hard. Office hours were somewhat helpful. I'd take another prof for this class.

I'm not a fan of his teaching style, more reliant on having a calculus background. Late on posting exam reviews, a bit disorganized. Boring lectures, never felt like I learned much (only missed 1 lecture). TA Kris is great, GO TO DISCUSSION for help with homework. Plenty of practice problems with quest, written homework, and exam reviews.
Changes grading criteria, adds rules and assignments without telling students, and assigns extraneous and useless tasks. Not to mention nothing was learned.

Awesome professor! Super caring and takes his time making sure students understand what he's teaching. UT calculus is a bit like magical math at times, but he made it bearable. Tons of office hours, LOTS of Quest + Written Homework (not bad if you go to OH), and fair exams. His exam questions don't really reflect HW/reviews tho, but still not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jay is very caring, well-knowledged in his craft, and has helpful office hours. Class itself was unnecessarily hard despite my efforts, especially tests and quizzes. I scored a 3 on the BC test, so getting an A here was unlikely, but a 35 on a quiz... really. I literally had a C before the final which I somehow clutched. Graders showed NO mercy.

If I had a different professor, I wouldn't care about this class. However, his care for student learning made the class a lot better, even asking for feedback on tests and using the 3rd person to "put himself in students' shoes" in lectures. Grading took a long time, but having a professor who cared this much was worth it.

I didn't take any calc AP classes but the professor explains the content in a way that anyone can understand. I don't understand what the others are saying, because the professor was not only a great person but a great teacher. The tests were fair and the lecture was entertaining and coherent.(Referred himself with third person which was funny.)

It's not the prof's fault but the grader was always really behind for all the quizzes and midterms. At one point, the quizzes were on a backlog of 6 weeks. It is an easy course, but there was also a lot of homework on Quest and you only got one attempt. I would petition into an honors version of this course bc their coursework is lighter.

Would win the Heisman trophy for going off topic and yapping (only covered 10 min of material per class). Only reason I got an A was cause I took BC in HS, but would have been cooked if I didn't. Bro's questions often didn't make sense on the exams, and quizzes were often not returned before tests. Also he referred to himself in the third-person???

Lecture makes no sense and he just starts yapping. All the glazers in this rmp dk what they talking abt they lowkey just rode his meat. I got the A but had to clutch the final and i got a 5 on bc. This dude is balls had to self study on yt and relearn hard concepts. Bro also loves theory on tests and terrible wording. Ignore my other rating.

Dude is so bad at teaching.  Lecture makes no sense and he just starts yapping. All the glazers in this rmp dk what they talking abt they lowkey just rode his meat. I got the A but had to clutch the final and i got a 5 on bc. This dude is balls had to self study on yt and relearn hard concepts. Bro also loves theory on tests and terrible wording.

Professor Whitehead is the most caring professor I have had, and you can tell that he truly wants his students to succeed. However, he creates his tests himself, sometimes making confusing conceptual questions or tricky time-consuming computational problems. Study hard for tests, attend office hours, and don't get lazy completing quest assignments.

Jay is really nice and very helpful. However, he made the class unnecessarily hard. He wanted us to have a deep conceptual understanding of calculus, which is great, but he tried to be too clever on test questions, and they'd be frustrating at times. workload isn't bad, but there's weekly hw and quizzes. Tests are what you have to watch out for.

Jay is by far the best math professor; he teaches in a way where the concepts stick, and if you put an effort to attend lectures/OH, you'll be prepared for how he wants you to approach quizzes and tests. Beware he wants students to understand the concepts versus simply computations, but learning this way made me appreciate the math as an engineer

I had Whitehead for M 101T, a support class, & it was very beneficial in helping with M 408Q. He's very caring, kind, energetic, & passionate about helping students succeed in UT math courses. He's an excellent lecturer, very engaging, & patient with answering Qs. He genuinely cared about individual student successes. One of the best UT math profs.

Whitehead is very good at helping students with calculus. His 1hr course is super helpful to gain better comprehension and have the ability to do homework and ask any questions. I definitely recommend him, he genuinely cares about his students.

Jay is the best math instructor that I've ever encountered. He teaches with passion and he makes sure you get the point. He would go to each student one-by-one to give them feedback on in-class activities (such as worksheets), and he would not leave you hanging if you ever need any extra help outside of lecture. Overall, he's absolutely amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had while at UT. Very passionate about his work and makes sure all students understand before moving on. Speak up if you have a question he will answer it to the best of his abilities. Good review sessions and good TA. Highly recommend taking a course with Whitehead if possible.

The professor is kind and easy to talk to, which makes the class comfortable. However, the flow of the lesson can sometimes be affected by unexpected changes. At times, he goes off-topic, which may make it more difficult to stay focused on the materia
Just, no. Homework about a concept BEFORE you're taught about it. Unnecessary extra work.
This man has ruined my life this semester. You will spend hours a night doing homework that he doesn't help you on at all. He makes everything much harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does not ever explain anything on the homework. Expect to teach yourself and learn from your peers. Or do yourself a favor and do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN AWAY!!! Didnt learn anything from his classes. During the lectures it's all gonna be group work. Need to teach yourself to pass. It's better take 408D instead.

The class was fine, but don't think I learned much more here than I did in AP stats (SDS 321 and M378K with other profs are much better). Also the class isn't exceptionally hard, it's just Jesse doesn't teach so you're completely unprepared for the tests. Midterm average was a 70%, final was a 62%, and he doesn't "curve" (think he did +3% overall)

Simply, the guy doesn't teach discrete math. Expect to read the textbook for everything, and even then the exam problems aren't anything like the textbook (this is worsened by the fact he never posts any sample exams, questions, or homework solutions). He gives multiple choice exams for discrete math, a proof based class... enough said

HORRIBLE TEACHER! Does not give answers to any in class assignments or any homework. Exams are hard since you have no review or practice problems. He does a lot of concept questions. Does not lecture! He puts students into groups each class period then you work on class assignment with other students. Never get any of the solutions. PROOFS ARE EASY
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think I would have been able to get an A if I had just done more practice problems. Explain concepts to your peers! Sit at the front to get the full Jesse experience. Take advantage of office hours! His class is harder in that it's flipped classroom and conceptual and less just straight up computation, but it's not impossible. You got this.

He was a really poor teacher. I have not encountered a class where the professor does not teach the methods of how to solve problems in class. Very heavy on theory and almost no method. I legitimately had to teach everything to myself, and something like multivariable calculus is just not something a person can teach themselves.

Flipped classroom. Horrible teacher for calculus. His exams are multiple choice and does give half the points back on the test if you do corrections. Very hard exam compared to a very weak textbook. I was spending too many hours on this class even though I am not a maths major.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jesse's class if hard, but Jesse is accessible by email and during office hours to answer any and questions. He cares for his students and wants them to succeed BUT he is also a firm believer in "the struggle." He believes his students learn better by failing than by giving them answers. His goal is to teach you how to THINK
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Jesse is a cool person when he's not teaching. Advice to those who do have to take him would be to make sure you can understand the abstract concepts very well because the HW questions are nothing compared to his lecture/discussion questions and the exams. Exams mean the most percentage-wise but he does let us do test corrections for extra points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom. Three test in total which are difficult because they are concept heavy. He does allow for test corrections. Classwork is completion for the most part but he doesn't give answers for them. Homework is annoying. He is not very responsive to his students. His explanations are very poor. Sadly, worst professor ive taken..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You must understand what each discussion and lecture's concept is. Not memorization. That should guarantee good grades on his short multiple choice tests. Couple q's from quizzes. His goal is that by struggling, you have an understanding greater than that of him directly telling you and ability to solve problems that you haven't seen before.

This man just flat out doesn't teach. He does a flipped classroom, which is frustrating already, but then during lecture he doesn't explain anything fully at all! If you ask him a question he'll just vaguely respond. The homework isn't bad but some tough questions don't even have explanations after the assignment is due! Exams are very tough, too

Before the first test, people asked if the test was quest based. As a freshman, I had no clue what that meant until I realized people only wanted to know if they could expect the same problems with different numbers. The textbook is not helpful, rather come to class prepared with questions. That is where the learning occurs in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He has a flipped classroom teaching style, but does NOT implement it effectively. He fails to consider that everyone has a different way of learning, and refuses to work out any example problems even after a worksheet is due. He thinks students just want answers, but that's not it. We don't understand the concept in the first place. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Takes some getting used to, but is such a meme! Greets us the same way every day in class, wears the same outfit, and carries himself as if he's on a higher dimension. He gives us sage advice, making laminated cards with how to succeed and how to fail. Do lots of practice problems from the textbook! He cares more about concepts than computations.
horrible, literally doesn't teach at all. class is just working on problems that he doesn't even give solutions to

I dropped this class after realizing lecture and discussion was all group work, most of which we were never given the answers to. And the quest assignments were the only opportunity to learn anything, but didn't coincide with his tests. Take 408D instead..

To be fair, you have to have avery high IQ to understand Jesse Miller's Calculus class. The concepts are extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of algebra, Pre-Calculus, Calculus I and Calculus II most of the concepts will go over a typical student's head. There's also Jesse Miller's holistic outlook, which is deftly woven into his lessons.
Doesn't teach, we just do activities all day. His 2 rating is justified.

Professor Miller is the worst professor I have had at the University of Texas. He neglects to answer questions, claiming questions are more important than answers, and fails to truly teach anything at all. Jesse Miller is not only ineffective in helping students learn; he seems to be actively determined to prevent his students' academic growth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He doesn't do much explaining, and most of the class is doing groupwork. The homework was a pain. The tests aren't hard, but he throws in questions that are meant to trick you. I studied 200ish hours of probability for the actuary exam (passed it) and still didn't get an A, so take that as you will.

This guy doesn't lecture and would always make us get in groups to do practice problems that he wrote, none of which he posted solutions for. Additionally, he assigns homework a day before its due with no clear warning on the syllabus. His questions on tests and written assigments are designed to trick you if you don't read twice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No lectures, no study guides, no reviews before tests and he would post homework assignments a day before they were due without telling people. Every class he would assign a couple problems, make people solve them without help, then give us the answers without explanations. His tests were difficult and studying was difficult from the weak textbook.

He seemed to have little grasp of the material, as he is normally a calculus professor. He repeatedly corrected students who were correct and apologized later. Did not have a good teaching style, as he preferred to throw difficult problems on the board and have student groups solve them. We rarely had time to go over the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy I suppose but I feel as if he designs his class/quizzes/tests with the intent of making you do poorly. You will teach yourself everything so I recommend putting in a lot of effort, expect to get nothing from Jesse's lectures or the TAs that he trains, and prepare to be very frustrated.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jesse's class is difficult, a bit too much at times. Definitely not your usual math class, so be ready to think and work in new ways. I'd die without the help from TAs, they're great. Lots of manageable homework but extremely difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jesse is a great professor, but the negative feedback is from people who think his class is too hard. However, he is expanding your mind to think critically and to be able to solve problems you didn't think you would ever see.
He gets a bad rep because he makes you think. This professor will change how you think and help you learn a lot so I recommend you take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jesse has a unique teaching style that many incoming high school students aren't used to, hence the negative feedback. He makes you work for it because it's calculus! It's not memorize formulas and get answers. This class is to test your critical thinking abilities, so have an open mind! His class helped me in the long run FOR SURE.

This was by far the worst professor I have ever taken.  Extremely unclear about EVERYTHING.  Ask a question, receive a vague unhelpful question back.  Go to office hours and come out more confused, just a waste of time.  No lecture, just problems in class and no direction for how to actually learn the material. DO NOT TAKE.
He has a bad rep but he really is a great guy who will help you if you need it. I failed two exams and passed the final but I really tried and went to office hours so he bumped me up. Great persson

DO NOT TAKE! Lectures are extremely boring and useless. Discussions don't help at all. He doesn't answer your questions directly. TA's and LA's are also instructed not to answer questions. He takes forever to reply to emails. Homework is HARD and he expects you to learn everything from it. Exams are recycled questions from classwork and quizzes.
he knows his flaws in teaching, but still doesnt change his method. just a stubborn man who destroys your  gpa

Miller uses the flipped classroom model, so if you don't like/can't learn calculus on your own, then don't take him. Miller won't teach you concepts in class, but if you can grasp the concept as you do the homework and come to class knowing what you're supposed to know, he'll iron out any kinks in your understanding.
Flipped classroom for calculus was just way too hard. He never really taught us how to solve a problem, instead tried to teach us how to think about solving a problem.

Have you ever wanted to teach yourself calculus? No? Then this is not the class for you. Also, He cares more about you understanding the course then getting a good grade, which is nice and all, but Grades are still important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: As my first math class here at UT, it certainly is rigorous, and a lot of outside learning is needed to even pass. My problems with the Prof mostly revolved around the expectations of the class needing much more support in the lectures and outside hours. Watch out for what TA you get, cause I got screwed there. Not a bad Prof, though, just hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are socratic seminars that cannot be skipped because you have a hard group quiz in them, every single lecture. The quizzes are not typically solve-by-evaluation questions; they are trick conceptual questions that you have to understand very well. Exams are hard. HW is hard and due before every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: There is so much to say about this professor but ill keep it short. No examples, no lectures, and no clarity. Extremely conceptual class with little instruction. The professor is available two hours a week and holds multiple classes during the same office hours. I couldn't be more disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Want a high B or an A in this class you have to do all activities, complete all modules, write down all quizzes, do extra problems on your own, and re-do all the above. IF YOU DONT DO THIS AMOUNT OF WORK DONT EXPECT A HIGH GRADE... assuming you have a strong background in Calculus. Also other TA's won't be able to help, and Jesse's available 2hrs/w
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Miller is a tough professor but his goal is to get you to think about the problems and actually learn how to solve them. The class is not easy but if you work hard you will do well. He is very helpful in office hours, especially if several people go and all ask questions together. He is happy to help you if you take the time to seek out help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very difficult professor, probably one of the worst I have had at UT. Not helpful at all. Avoid at all costs, he seems like a cool guy but he is absolutely terrible at his job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jesse was a great guy in general, but I did not like his teaching style. I had to look up other material to understand completely what he is teaching. His style is very conceptual. My class was a flipped class which I liked, but as soon as I thought I understood the material I would go to  class and realize that I truly did not figure it out.

He has a weird (and awful) philosophy about teaching. He doesn't lecture and he counters questions with more questions. Tests are formatted weirdly and graded illogically, and he basically ignores requests for regrades. He dodges emails and questions and doesn't "believe" in failing even with test averages in the low 50s. Avoid at all costs

Would start by saying that overall he is a great guy. He makes good jokes, makes lectures fun, and can explain things moderately well. For the downside, he does not explain how to show your work. Yet on the tests, your work is the only thing he grades. If you miss one slight notation, its marked wrong. Terrible grader, terrible grading scheme.
Attend and participate in class. Do the homework on your own. You'll be just fine.

There is a quiz every class. If you ask a question because you don't know something he'll just say "What do you think?" His TA's are taught to react the same way. No one is helpful, he expects you to learn from the at home videos. All you do in class is group assignments which are randomly chosen for grades. Pop quizes in discussion.

Jesse is really tough. He won't explain anything too clearly and you're going to need the help of others if you don't have a background in calculus.  If you understand the material, you will do good in the class. In order to do good, you are going to have to work for it yourself. A's are possible but they are tough to get.

His class is hard but not impossible.  A big part of his class is conceptual so if you expect to come into class and just work out problems and solve for "x", then this is the wrong class for you. It was really frustrating for me at first,  but you'll get the hang of it and Miller is a pretty good guy if you get to know him.

From the beginning, Jesse makes it clear that this is no ordinary math class. The purpose of this class is not to help you regurgitate equation after equation to solve problems, but rather to engage your brain in critical thinking. You will struggle, but in the end you'll be thankful so long as you don't mind teaching yourself and working hard.

Jesse is a REALLY nice guy. He wants you to understand calculus and also forces you to use your brain to think critically for the whole semester. It is a lot easier said than done. We all struggled the whole entire semester but in the end, you do gain skills from this course that can be applied to future classes. It is not an easy class, work hard.
Tests are horrid. We had to beg him to let us correct our second exam. Daily Clicker quizzes, which are so vague and confusing. Long Quest homeworks after every class period. Avoid him at all costs.

I took this class because I love math. One semester later, I want nothing to do with it. Not only does Jesse Miller give ridiculous daily quizzes, he also refuses to work example problems for us and allowed us to struggle constantly the whole semester. Expect failing test averages. I survived and did well reading the book, and spending time myself.

The people who come to this site to complain are usually the people that are not willing to learn. He is a tough professor, but he wants you to actually understand what you are doing. Yes, his class is hard, but if you're not willing to learn, it'll be harder. My advice, GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He won't give you answers, but you'll learn the concepts.
Guys... don't do it. Switch out immediately.

People complaining about him as if he's supposed to hand you an A on a silver platter. Yes, you have to study to clearly understand what is taught to you, but that is with any calculus class. Also,office hours are a must! He will make you answer your own questions by leading you to them so that later on the test, you know what to do.

Jesse is a very experienced man that, in a way, has a mission to get you to understand the underlying conceptuals of calculus. His tests, homework assignments, quizzes, and discussion activities were hard but manageable with ALOT of dedication!

Jesse is a really nice guy who really just wants his students to understand what they are doing rather than memorizing and regurgitating a pattern they learned gets the correct answer to a problem. In order to do well, you have to learn the concepts of everything you are doing and know why you're doing them.

Great man but a tough professor. He truly wants his students succeed but he makes you work for it. Exams, homework, classwork, and quizzes are tough but not totally impossible. I highly recommend studying the in-class problems before the exams, as those problems are the most similar to the tests. Challenging but rewarding class.

I would not  recommend taking him unless you are very determinedself-motivated. He expects you to know the material before coming to class. In class it's all quizzes and in-class activities, which would normally be fine if he gave a clear explanation beforehand (which he doesn't). Be ready to read the book and learn everything on your own.

At first frustrated because he never worked through problem completely during lecture, likes to focus more on concepts. I have come to much prefer his methods because it creates interest. People say he answers your questions with his own, but the leaps he wants you to make are totally manageable and if you really don't get it he will explain
Nice enough guy, but too many trick questions. I struggled a lot for someone who flew through AP calculus with no trouble.

Jesse is tough.  You learn on your own from online modules, then work in class. The tests are identical to in-class stuff, so go to lecture! I'm pretty sure he curved at the end, but average grades were still C's at best. I got an A- by going to every lecture and doing extra work from the book, which isn't really required but if you want practice..

This class was really difficult. It's mostly about the concepts of calculus. On tests, you have to give examples of equations and explain everything you do. Tests are a mix between free response and multiple choice. He really likes to help, but he sometimes doesn't answer your question directly. Also, you learn through homework, not during class.

Jesse is the worst professor for calculus at UT. He will not answer a single question or be willing to help you. He takes flipped classroom to an extreme and his tutorial videos are not helpful at all. If you get Miller, DROP. Only 2% of people made A's on the final and he doesn't curve. Average grades for tests were in the upper 60's or lower 70's

He is the worst! he NEVER answers a single question ever. i think he enjoys watching the class fail as he gives true or false quizzes every class with about 3 questions. the odds are literally against you. i wish i Qdropped. awful class professor provides no help or clarity. he's dull and annoying

Thinking about taking a class with Jesse? Well I'm going to do you a favor and do something Jesse never does, answer your question! And that answer is no!  He is no help as a teacher, there is very little continuity between lectures and discussions, and any attempt to get a direct answer out of him will be futile.

I had to Q drop this class! DO NOT TAKE HIM! UNLESS YOU LOVE PHILOSOPHY and understanding WHY things are the way they are.  He's a math major with a philosophy background. Ask him a question, he'll answer you with another question. Class is mandatory. 10 mins quiz everyday (yup!) and classworks and homeworks 3x a week! CONCEPTUAL TESTS!!

DO NOT TAKE HIM. His classroom style is flipped. Every single day is the same. You take an iClicker quiz and split into groups and work on problems. Office hours did not help one bit. If you asked him a question he would answer back with a question. His TA was not helpful either. The discussion problems were way too hard. He is not helpful at all.
Reverse classroom. Makes it extremely difficult to do homework.
Never teach class, have quiz every class, and the discussion activity is way to hard

I had friends that took him for 408N that hated him, but I had him for 408M and absolutely loved him. His class was more about critical thinking than anything. He also absolutely loves math and you can tell. As far as tests go, if you show up there's no reason you shouldn't get an A. We did questions in class that then showed up on the tests.

Jesse Miller is a great professor. You really learn calculus and critical thinking skills in his course. He cares about the students' well-being as well as how well they do in the class. Definitely one of my favorite classes at UT

Really forces you to think about calculus rather than just go through the motions. Extremely smart, wish he lectured a bit more- mostly learned via online modules and working through conceptual questions. If I were to do it again, I'd go to office hrs and keep up with the work.

I had Jesse for a calculus course and he is probably one of my favorite professors. Yes, his questions are tough, and he will answer your questions with questions, but he makes you think and use your brain and take different approaches. He has a passion for calculus and what he does and it really shows.

Coming into Jesse's class with no prior calculus knowledge was tough. He never gave "free answers" and usually answers your question with a question. An A is not impossible, I did it, but it requires you to go to office hours and take notes on all the learning modules. In office hours you will realize how nice Jesse is and how much he wants to help

Jesse is by far one of the worst teachers i have ever had. He doesn't ever teach or answer anyone's questions directly, instead he responds with another question. We basically go to class to get quizzed on the material that we spend so much time at home learning. His class is much harder than it is supposed to be. The TA was very helpful though.

One of the absolute worst professors I have ever had. Or teacher for that matter. He does not teach you directly and never actually gives you solutions to any problem. His tests are very conceptual and ambiguous and he will mark you wrong for right answers. Useless in office hours. If I could go back and never take him, I would in a heartbeat.

One of the absolute worst professors I've ever taken. He never teaches directly, and by the end of the year won't give you solutions to any of the problems. His tests are conceptual and ambiguous and he is not very helpful in office hours. Super pretentious attitude. If I could go back I would have never taken him. Ever.

Worst professor ever. Not helpful at all;if you have to take calculus with him, reconsider your schedule. He puts you on the spot in class, drills you about the new material and never directly answers your questions. Office hours are worthless and during exams you will be uncomfortably hovered over by the t.a.'s or the extra proctors he requests.

He is a great teacher and really wants to help, but he never gives "free answers" and often answers your questions with a question. Your grade is determined by TWO midterms, a final and the SIX weekly homework. Although I ended up with an A in the class, I also had no free time during the semester because I was trying to learn calculus. HARD CLASS!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor means well but is too intelligent to be teaching an introductory calculus class. Entire grade is pretty much based off of 3 tests which are shots in the dark. Even if you attend office hours and ask relevant questions, it's difficult to get clarification/help. It ruined my GPA.
If you have never taken calc, DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. You will be lost and you will fail. Sweet man but not much of a teacher. I took calc  in high school and still did poorly.

At the beginning of the semester Jesse would write problems on the board then have student volunteers solve them at the end of class. By the end of the semester the problems were left unsolved and he failed to provide some necessary information to solve equations. If not for taking Calc BC in high school, this class would have been a nightmare.

She loves to cold call so be prepared. She is passionate about public health but her personality can make it hard to like the class. She likes to pick on the people in the back, and dont be on ur laptop the whole lecture or she will call u out. Never happened to me but i can imagine lmao. Easy class tho

What I found most difficult was that some discussions and assignments felt framed around a particular political perspective, wo much room for alt. viewpoints. Certain terminology and issue framing seemed presented as assumed consensus rather than open discussion, making it harder to speak up if you did not fully agree with the tone of the class.

Took this class last semester and she was an amazing lecturer, only issue is that exams have information you could only acquire from textbook so I performed really poorly on first two exams because I didn't read it and that's why I ended up with A- in class
Amazing professor who is very passionate about health policy and oral health , TAs are goated and very personable , very chill class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Same thing as other ppl said, attendance is mandatory but you don't learn anything from her lectures. TAs are harsh graders.

Super easy class w/ lots of easy & time consuming assignments. I feel like they don't read the essays much, just skimmed. The tests were pretty okay since they were take home. I only got one perfect score, and I always got points off for no reason. Super doable A! Attendance is mandatory. Get ready to stay awake because she will come up to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easy class, easy exams, easy assignments. Lectures spend a lot of time going over obvious concepts and don't add much to your learning experience, but attendance is mandatory so you have to go. Very passionate professor, love her as a person, do not love her as a lecturer. At least 1 weekly assignment, 5 exams, 4 part project, 5 discussion boards.

omg it was hard to stay awake, she is really sweet but good lord, shoot me in the head. most of the time i slept. actual material is not that bad imo it is all common sense, exams were take home but kinda tricky however grading is not too bad. TA took off random points sometimes but not enough to damage the grade. good luck staying awake soldier!!!

Her lectures are alright, it sucks that you can only miss 3 classes for a 9am. It is a little boring, but you can tell she is passionate about the content and it makes the class more bearable. Don't have people sign in for you, you WILL be caught and written up for academic dishonesty. Exams were all online/taken at home.

Absolutely hated this class. The professor spends everyday in class rambling on abt God knows what. A girl came up to her taking a lot of interest in her research & in the middle of the convo, Wolfe went on her phone & started texting someone. She acknowledged freaking good friday and some jewish holiday but forgot to ever mention ramadan or eid?

It feels like she cares more about tricking her students than teaching (weird wording on exams, not responding to emails, unforgiving attendance policy, etc.). She's overall nice and clearly cares abt public health but I would never take this class again. I also feel like I learned nothing in class and had to use the textbook for everything.

Her mandatory attendance was so annoying and pretty unorganized at times. Lectures were so boring and useless as she only reads off the slides and doesn't add any new information. Assignments were easy though and unit assessments are take home (but strangely difficult like I never got a perfect score).

Although there's quite a bit of homework, it's pretty easy and straightforward. Attendance is taken every lecture, you have to sign in. My only thing is that she was a little disorganized but got better near the end of the semester. Lectures are very interesting, and you can tell Dr. Wolfe is passionate about public health.

Wonderful prof! You can tell she is passionate about teaching public health! Attendance is required and part of the grade. Lectures could be more engaging bc sometimes she tends to read off the slides. Tests are easy as long as you pay attention to lecture. Projects are also quite easy. Overall would recommend Dr. Wolfe!

I hated the attendance policy she made us sign in worksheets not to mention the class is over 200 students. She also calls on students so be ready to answer when she calls on you other than that it was not bad.

Her intro class was very interesting but had lots of busy work exams and projects
Although, if you got yousef as your TA then you in good hands !

Dr. Wolfe is really passionate about public health, and tries to make classes as engaging as possible. My only complaint is how early this class is offered. Attendance is required, with 3 exceptions allowed, but you can do very well in this class and still not attend lecture.
Doesn't respond to emails. Changes assignment deadlines on a whim. Class was very informative but you have to read the textbook word for word for the concept checks. Exams were fairly easy.

Dr. Wolfe is a great professor. She explains concepts in terms that make sense, are relatable, and are applicable to us as future professionals. Even when I'm fidgeting in class, I'm able to pick up the content. I wish more professors fostered a low-stress learning environment like hers; it actually helps me to learn with the convo-style lectures.

Very passionate and knowledgeable in her field. She and the TA, Rebecca, are very approachable. My only complaint would be the class material. Subjects tend to drag out over weeks, discussing the same ideas and topics over and over. Be prepared for LOTS of busy work. Tests are straightforward, and she provides a study guide. Fair grading policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was super easy, I just feel like I got nothing out of it. I just can not stand reading off slides, and mandatory attendance, at 9 am. When she would deviate from the lecture slides, you could tell she was so intelligent and could lecture well if she did not just read straight from the textbook. She is so kind, but I was so bored.

This class was so boring and i literally could not bring myself to go. Dragged down my GPA bc it seemed unimportant until I got 0s for a million assignments (so much hw man). No shade to prof bc she is a sweet lady but the class itself was not great. If you're passionate about pbh its probably fine but if not be prepared to suffer

Stem major here who thought this would be an easy class on the side. So much work. Wrecked my GPA. Take nutrition instead if that's an option, I've taken both and NTR was way easier. Going to class is incredibly boring bc attendance is required but she just repeats whats in the book. Wouldn't take again.

Mandatory attendance, you literally sign in on a sheet of paper. Most of the stuff is common sense, and you might have to study a little for the exams. Most people did work for other classes. If you're passionate about public health, you'll like the class. Otherwise, it's just a burden. I wish it were more discussion-based, not just bs assignments.

Prof Wolfe was a kind professor & very passionate about public health and lecturing. The class is pretty easy, & I did not take much from it. Attendance was mandatory which was pretty painful for a 9 AM lecture that was not very important to me. I think if you are very passionate about public health, it would be an ok class. Weekly hw.
he is v nice and understanding!! straightforward class, read + go to lecture and you will be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson is an excellent professor. He does his best to make a sometimes-bland area of study into an engaging and exciting lesson, though his lectures are quite dense. There are not many assignments that factor into the grade, but the workload is manageable. Highly recommend for an overview of the field of IR.
Honestly, there's not much to say.  Dr. Johnson is a decent lecturer and is pretty nice and knows his stuff.

One of the best classes I've taken at UT. Professor Johnson is passionate and very knowledgeable about international relations and makes the lectures interesting and interactive. The class and material is straightforward as long as you go to class and read the textbook. There are only a few grades but grading tends to be in your favor.

I loved this course! Professor Johnson's lectures were the most engaging ones I had all semester, and he often played videos in class. The tests were very easy and I got above 90 on all of them with minimal studying (just read the textbook and slides). The TA Yasuki was also great! Very nice professor and TA, highly recommend.

He was an amazing professor, you can tell he his passionate about the subject and makes the lectures interesting and fun. Be aware there is very few grades in this class 3 exams, a paper and in class activities. However along as you pay attention during lectures and read the books the test are pretty simple. I would take again and learned a lot !
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, cares about students. Class and material is dense but never overwhelming. Some in class participation grades, a straightforward paper, and exams.

One of my favorite professors so far! He is extremely knowledgeable, and that is reflected in his lectures. He takes questions and actually cares about what is said. There are in-class activities usually every class, but missing one or two is okay. Tests are also easy if you pay attention and do readings.I highly recommend this class and professor.
The professor just read off the script on the slides. However, you need to attend the lecture bc of the pop-up quiz. Homeworks are ambiguous, and often do not reflect what we've learned in class.

Lectures are technically mandatory because of pop quizzes. I didn't understand anything from lecture because fast-paced monotonous lectures but very understandable when reviewing by yourself. Exam 1 is very easy especially if you know SQL already. Exam 2 is a little harder because more code syntax you just know. Study EVERYTHING on slides for exams

Lectures were straightforward read throughs of slides, a bit dry sometimes but provided decent coverage of database concepts. First couple projects were pretty time consuming and redundant since we had to create test data. 2nd exam was a bit tricky in its level of detail. Palacios was very helpful during office hours. Reasonable workload overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class structure and content exactly followed Norman's. Palacios is a very nice guy, very approachable and open to questions. However, he sometimes wasn't able to satisfiably answer students' questions. Doesn't seem as knowledgeable in OS as other systems professors. I'd recommend Norman or Mootaz over Palacios for OS.

Quizzes, homework, and 1st exam are easy. Projects are sometimes confusing with setup, but the coding itself is simple. 2nd exam was much more difficult due to wide range of topics you need to memorize. He's a nice dude, but the lectures are very boring and I don't like how much memorizing is needed for the exams.

Palacios is a monotone & unhelpful professor. Reads off his slides and offers nothing beyond that in class. Scheduled a midterm for the Friday before spring break and got excited to tell people to cancel their flights. Very exam heavy. Pick a good partner for projects. Be ready to put a good chunk of time in for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Palacios follows Norman's class structure exactly, even reusing her lecture videos. He doesn't contribute much during lectures either. The grading system is diabolical, and it felt like there was no way to maintain any work-life balance during the whole semester. It took everything out of me to get an A. Would not recommend.

Easy class in the certificate. Also very useful if you're looking towards data analytics related stuff. Only 2 exams but so far, the midterm was pretty easy (yet to take the final). Projects are mainly about the set-up rather than the actual code. He's really nice and helpful but lecture are pretty slow and boring. Highly recommend this class.

Palacios has been the best CS professor I've taken. His lectures were pretty boring but not hard to follow or look back on. We had a few projects, most of our grade was dependent on two midterms. You will probably need to attend office hours as the hardest parts of the projects was the setup instead of the actual material. He's great and sweet!

A lot of the difficulty was due to Norman's class structure, but Dr. Palacios also didn't provide a lot of insight during lectures, making most of our learning from pre-recorded videos. Office hours were very useful though.

Not a particularly engaging lecturer, and frankly the course material doesn't check your knowledge of the material. Class feels like entirely self-directed learning. Not great but not terrible, you can pass this class without too much trouble if that's all you care about.

Took his CS378 SWE take it with Downing if you can. Palacios is a good prof the TA's grade easy but the tests cover an unnecessary amount of content each slide deck is around 70 slides so you need to learn stuff from around 400-500 slides a lot of it is pretty self explanatory but on top of the project can be annoying to study. But easy A if u cram
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very clearly a caring teacher, but gets overshadowed by the general difficulty of OS and Norman's lecture videos teaching most of the content before you even get to class. Almost all of the TAs are some of the best I've ever had.
This professor is equally as difficult as any other OS professor at UT Austin- don't be fooled by his revies here!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OS as a course is very difficult but Professor Palacios does his best to make it manageable. Criteria is clear but exams are strictly graded (and weekly quizzes are very important). Projects are hard but if you start early you'll be fine. Don't expect a curve and prepare questions for lectures to take advantage of the time.

I took OS this fall expecting it to be bad like everyone was saying. Surprisingly it wasn't that bad. As long as you put in the work, expect to get a decent grade. You definitely need to spend quite a bit of time working on the labs outside of class though. Palacios was pretty good at lecturing and I liked his work stories on the last day of class
