The class is a replica of the pre module videos. He brings a lot of energy to the class but ultimately a lot of people don't pay attention in lecture because what's covered in class is pretty superficial compared to the pre module videos

He just reads off the slides in class and can't really answer everyone's questions in depth/fully. He's really cheerful though and enthusiastic about teaching the material. Class was basically just a repeat of the modules that you watch before coming to lecture.

His lectures always seemed like he looked at the slides Norman sent 2 minutes before class started. He also had a limited understanding of how the grading system worked and it always felt like it was Norman's class. I would take Norman over Palacios, although Palacios is a better lecturer. I heard his database class is good, though.

OS is unlike any CS class I have taken so far. Palacios helped to make it bearable, and I learned very much in this class. I felt as though Norman's grading scheme infected his class and made it much less enjoyable. He's a great teacher, the group projects are very tough but informative, and would recommend checking out his other courses.

While this course is challenging in many aspects, Dr. Palacios is an awesome instructor!  He's super funny and clearly cares for his students.  He also encourages participation in class, and his lectures are helpful for explaining the material.  Overall, he did a great job teaching a challenging course.

I had Dr. J for HDO 310. She is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. The material for this class was dry at best, but she did an amazing job trying to make it interesting. She went above and beyond to make sure that we would succeed. I have never had a professor who put so much time and effort into a class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Dr. J for LAH 350 (Austin) and learned a lot. She was a tough grader and the bulk of our grade were based on final projects so we couldn't really determine our grade throughout the semester and improve. I went from a 97 to a B+ after a few projects that she graded the night grades were due so I couldn't prepare or comeback from that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: great class, great professor. A lot of work, but this is college, isn't it?

Despite the work you put in to the class, Dr. Jefferson will not give you the grade you deserve. In addition no rounding will be done even for extra effort put in and inconsistent grading. She is a work intensive professor and your hours of work will be unrewarded with your final grade. Do not take a class with her.

He seems to be a chill guy, but is not really the most understanding person when it comes to situations and is very strict for some reason as an English teacher. Also he looks at his rate my professor a lot, and keeps flagging the ones that make him look not good.
By the way, a lot of the bad reviews on this guy keep getting removed, so just know all of these “good ones” are misleading
He's really biased towards a select group of people in the class

Class discussion was mostly student-led. There were three essays and a short response about once a week. Readings could be somewhat heavy if you're not in the mood, but I thought they were very reasonable and well-paced. Dr. Kevorkian is a really nice professor with a passion for the subject and enthusiasm for student thoughts. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kevorkian is a great teacher, and Poetry for Engineers is an engaging class that made me feel comfortable starting my first semester at UT. The professor is helpful, kind, an insightful essay reviewer, and is very forgiving if you cannot attend class for any reason. I cannot recommend this class more.

Professor Kevorkian is one of the kindest encouraging people I ever met. I had to miss a bunch of classes and missed assignments due to health and also on me to the point I thought I had to drop, but he cares so much about every single student that I couldn't. He's thoughtful and incredibly passionate about his subject. Man's literally a saint.

Amazing professor. Very passionate and also understanding. He truly cares about English and his students— his class was by far my favorite this semester. Will definitely try to take another one of his classes.

Professor Kevorkian is so caring and is very interested in the poetry presented. His lectures regarding the topic presented were always insightful and you can tell that he enjoys teaching Poetry for Engineers. Overall, very fun class and if I could take this class again I totally would!!

Truly an amazing professor and is my favorite! It was extremely refreshing to be able to have an environment that truly fosters creativity and passion with everyone around you. The class itself taught me a lot about literature and poetry and kept me engaged throughout the entire year.

I had him for Poetry for Engineers (UGS 302) Fall '24. This was the best class I've taken and my one of my favorite professors ever. He's a caring, passionate, and super understanding. The workload was moderate. A poem is read and discussed each day. There are four essays with a clear rubric and good feedback. If you have a chance to take him, do.

Most knowledgeable professor I've ever had and it shows through his passion and talks. Easy to access, caring, passionate, and understanding. Both a great teacher and a great person. Lots of reading and writing, but great feedback and flexible. Makes you excited about the work through his own passion. Please take his class if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: If you get the chance to take this professor, please do. Incredibly passionate about his work and it shows through him.Very caring professor, easily accessible through messaging or during office hours. With that said, there's a lot of reading paired with lots of writing in this class. Gives great feedback and very understanding and flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor that really cares about the students. He grades papers with positive feedback which is so helpful in growing as a writer. 10/10 would recommend to take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing teacher, I learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is my absolute favorite professor that I've had at UT thus far. Dr. Kevorkian shows everyday how passionate he is about the students and what he teaches! take his class if you can fit it into your schedule.
Truly an incredible professor. Shows genuine interest in progress of students, incredible at facilitating discussions, knows pretty much everything about everything. Best professor I've had thus far.

Martin Kevorkian taught a seminar on Emerson and Hawthorne my senior year, and it was by far, the best class I'd ever taken. Kevorkian was not only passionate and competent as a professor, but incredibly approachable as well. A fine professor, with great wit, humor, and dedication. I will always remember that class (and him) fondly.

Martin Kevorkian was one of the most brilliant teachers I had at UT. His classes were never dull -- he challenged and encouraged critical thought, provided tremendous feedback and dialogue, and really engaged us in the texts. A fantastic professor -- if you have a chance to take his classes, absolutely do.
SAVE YOURSELF. There is a reason kirk is in his name.

Lectures consist of him just clicking through random photographs and graphs with mediocre explanations. Does not post his lecture slides and does not allow people to take photos. Exams are weird and test how well you can memorize some random fact about some random species of bird from three weeks ago rather than understanding of concepts.

He doesn't remind when assignments are due (quizzes don't show up on your dashboard). He is not helpful during lecture, if he was too fast, he'll say he'll go back, but he never does and you have to watch the lectures back in your own time. He tries to be fun in lecture to mask the fact that the exam is gonna smack you in the face.

His lectures were fun and engaging but the exams were difficult. Very FRQ heavy and its sometimes hard to get the specific answer he is looking for. He's a decent lecturer though, and the class is certainly manageable
Although the course itself is difficult, Dr. Kirkpatrick is an amazing professor. Go to his office hours and you'll be prepared for the exams.

Kirkpatrick's lectures and fun and engaging, but that is where the positive stuff ends. The quizzes were pretty tricky (but not as bad as Linder's), and you need to know very specific examples/info for his exams. No extra credit offered at all, and curving was only if needed (and it was very few points back). This class was a lot of work.
Professor Kirkpatrick had the charm of a bungee jump instructor, friendly and reassuring, right up until the test sent you plummeting.

He's a fun lecturer and passionate about the course material, so lectures were engaging. Keep in mind most of the exam questions are very specific FRQ, but if you take good notes and have good study strategies you'll be fine. Average professor overall, and his half of the class is better and easier than Dr. Linder's half.

His half is better than Linder's, but it still wasn't great. His lectures were usually pretty interesting, but he was super condescending and rude when answering questions. His exams are also incredibly specific. All FRQ exams and he wants you to explain the exact examples he taught. Very picky. Make sure to do well on his exams before Linder's!

Syllabus states that 25% of students get an A, 30% get a B, and 35% get a C. Literally why does the lowest grade have the highest class population. FRQ Exams and quizzes are extremely difficult. Doesn't test you on your knowledge, rather if you remember every little thing he says and write down verbatim. Take someone else or wait next semie.

He's better than Linder but you're better off taking the other Evolution course if you can. Both professors expect you to learn their exact opinions and word vomit them back onto the test. Went to all of the lectures, but its not about understanding the concepts, it's about memorizing specific details or class examples.

(Co instructed) If you do good with Dr. Kirkpatrick you'll do fine with Dr. Lindler. This class was difficult; there is A LOT of material, but it's not hard conceptually. The exams are all short answer and both Prof. apply a curve ONLY if the average is low. The weekly/open-note quizzes were challenging for me so I recommend studying for those

Took evolution alongside w/ Linder. Kirkpatrick always came to class with a smile and good attitude. His lectures were filled with fun examples and he's a great lecturer. Some questions from the tests were out of the blue, but overall would love to take him again if I had the option to.

Really liked his portion of the semester. It was actually really interesting to listen to his lectures. Test were a bit ridiculous at times though. Definitely just need to memorize his lecture outlines and examples he uses in class and the class is an easy A. Get quizlet plus lol

Kirkpatrick is a smarta** professor and he is very particular about his exams. Way too difficult and specific for the amount of material we cover and it's all short answer. He cuts students off in class, doesn't post slides. Also the change in professors half way through the semester sucks in order to have to learn how to study for Linder's exams

Kirkpatrick was definitely very passionate about what he taught!! I enjoyed showing up to lecture. However, his tests were definitely based on random memorization. They were formatted similar to quizzes, which helped. I recommend using the active recall method for studying. Overall, really liked his class :)

Dr. Kirkpatrick is clearly passionate about evolution and it shows in the way he presents his lectures. His lectures are very engaging and he provided an outline for each lectures to study. I did read the textbook as supplemental learning because it really helped explain concepts I was stuck on. Exams were not too tough but were application based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkpatrick was an amazing lecturer, and always seemed to enjoy what he was talking about. Take notes on his lectures and be able to talk through concepts in the lectures/slides/outlines + remember examples for the free response exams. Sounds intimidating, but they really weren't that difficult. Definitely the best option for evolution!

Kirkpatrick was awesome! Really engaging lectures and always seemed happy to be teaching. Quizzes (40%) and tests (40%) make up a lot of the grade but aren't terrible. He wrote the textbook and it is a good read. If you can remember all of the concepts and be able to recall specific examples from class, you're good to go!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kirkpatrick was great. His lectures were interesting and kept me engaged the entire time. Quizzes are open note, open internet. However, exams are not and they're all free response on paper. Plan on studying a lot and memorizing examples/concepts for exams. Lectures aren't mandatory, but much better in person. Would recommend for evolution.

Professor Kirkpatrick is kind and his lectures are very engaging/simple to understand! He talks about the places he's traveled for research and incorporates them into his lectures with pictures & stories. Quiz/exam questions come directly from his lectures. Discussion section involves reading a book. Easy class if you pay attention to lectures!

Quizzes and tests were based on easy-to-follow lecture materials. Textbook readings were supplemental, but not at all necessary. Provided outlines to his lectures and gave great examples. Cool professor overall!
Dr. Kirkpatrick is really passionate in his lectures and his delivery can easily get you interested in the subject material. Homework, quizzes, and tests are not very difficult.

Mark is an amazing lecturer and makes almost every subject easy to digest. He felt very genuine and cared about every student. The tests were hard but all of the information came from the lectures so if you paid attention, you were rewarded. Very fair grader if I ever missed a question it was a learning experience as there was a helpful explination
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this class. He only taught half of it, but his lectures were very entertaining and easy to listen to. Tests were hard but all came right from the lectures and if the average was low the test got curved. Very easy to do well in his class if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really great, interesting lectures. REALLY tough exams. Senior bio major here and these tests are some of the hardest I've taken. Did not love the discussion set-up or grading scheme (z-curve). Discussion feels cutthroat - TA sits at the front with all of our pics making tic marks next to our faces based on how much we talk for grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are like a live BBC documentary on evolution, everything is clear in lecture. He is well enough in office hours, he can be harsh if someone asks a dumb question. His tests though are difficult with often vague wording. The discussions are super annoying and the papers aren't something casual to read, but this really depends on one's TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an amazing lecturer, but his grading scheme is absolute trash. You could know the material, but still, do poorly on the exams. That is because his exams are all free response with extremely vague questions. Yet, if your answer does not match his key WORD FOR WORD... goodluck. Discussion sections are graded the same way lol. what a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkpatrick gives amazing lectures. If you get to know him outside of class, he's mean for absolutely no reason, so don't ask him for help. Grading to the tests is oddly specific for broad questions and he uses small examples he gave in class for test questions. Always read your book for parts that you don't understand.

Honestly, Kirkpatrick was one of the best lecturers I've had so far at UT. His lectures were extremely engaging and easy for me to understand. However, his tests were so difficult and specific that if you didn't put exactly what he wanted he took off points. Tests and attendance are also mostly the only grades, so you better show up and study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The class is graded by z-scores, which I personally dislike but it's up to you. I got 2 A's and 2 B's on the exams and ended up with a C+ in the class. Everything is relative to how everyone else does, which I hate. As far as the exams, I don't feel that the questions are terrible, but the grading is very very specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirkpatrick is one of the best lecturers I've had in my upper division biology courses. Really cares about the material. That being said, tests are ridiculously specific (yet questions are vague?) AND all free response. If you don't write word for word what he says in lecture, you get points off. It was so hard to gauge what he expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor for Evolution, really cares about the material.

I truly regret taking his class.  The material isn't complicated, but his grading scheme is not practical.  He says he want's open answers, but if you don't write done what's on the answer key nearly word for word, you will do poorly.  If you question his grading he will take more points away from you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've taken at UT. Lectures are long and he goes so fast its impossible to write everything, no power points posted. Tests are not necessarily hard but the way they grade is ridiculous and has no sense. I wrote stuff he said in class himself and got points off, you never know what he wants and never know if you will get points off.
My goat KiaT

Everything was graded VERY leniently with the exception of exam 1. Almost everyone got a 100 on the final to make up for this though. I had over a 100 at the end of the semester. Lectures are fun and you get to do a lot of implementation, though homeworks aren't that hard. Would recommend, super awesome professor!

This professor was amazing! This was one of the easier computer science classes I took, and I learned many things from it. He makes data analytics interesting and fun to learn and use. Just be on top of assignments and know concepts well. The tests are pretty easy. This professor is the GOAT.
It's overall ok. Doesn't really keep you engaged during lectures, but is a very lenient grader. If you get a good partner the homework and project can be done easily. Exams are hard to fail.

This is one of the easiest CS electives I've taken. Projects take 2-4 hours per week. His lectures can get boring but he only does Instapoll once in a while. Overall a good class that is useful for backend dev

The course is well organized. Lectures can be a bit dry and not very helpful, especially towards the end of the sem, but everything is laid out clearly + there's a lot of resources if you need help. 
The tests are very straightforward. As long as you stay on top of things, it's not hard to get an A. Definitely a solid prof, for both 313e and 329e.

He's a diamond in the rough. He's so good, I felt inspired to write this. I was nearly brought to tears tbh. PLEASE take him if you actually want to learn something. As an econ major who has had so many crappy professors, he's the GOAT. Taught stats/regression better than any of my other professors. I regret not taking him for 313.

Professor drones in class but watch zoom lectures times 2 speed. I found lectures to be fast pace and hard to keep up with bc it's hard to keep paying attention. First class u pick partners for the whole semester and I had a very bad partner which made class unenjoyable. I think the professor is v kind and knowledgeable but the class is hard.

This class was an easy A. He gave practice exams that were basically identical to the actual exams, so those were easy. You can work with a programming partner for basically everything. Some of the homeworks take a while, but they weren't too bad. As long as you put the work in you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class felt rushed at times and extremely boring at other times, with information delivered too quickly and weekly labs requiring significant group effort. I didn't learn much about cloud computing, but more about multithreading and batch commands. Attendance instapolls and in-class assignments give credit, while exams are fairly easy.

Heavy workload without any benefit. Manageable projects, but weekly and exhausting, and you don't actually learn anything with the majority of them. DO NOT TAKE if you want to get experience with cloud tools like AWS, GCP, and Azure; you get none. Assignments and tests are very easily graded, almost guaranteed 100 if you complete all parts.
Cloud Computing was one of the best taught classes I have ever taken at UT. Lot of homework though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awful class. I took this class as a senior looking for an interesting, if challenging, course. What I found was a class with lackluster lectures, disorganized logistics, and heavy weekly projects with no time to breathe. A contender for the hardest CS course I've had at UT, but without a deeper understanding of the material. Do not take.

Maybe one of the worst experiences with a CS prof I've had in my four years at UT. He assigns weekly projects, with a heavy workload. I haven't had this much work from a class since OS. His lectures are functionally useless and offer little value. Logistically the course is disorganized, and the exams he gives are weighted ridiculously high.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Teymourian was a fantastic teacher for CS 313E. Grades were based mostly on weekly assignments that were take-home, pair programming, and graded via Gradescope with multiple submissions. He was easy to reach over Piazza and answered questions readily, and occasionally extended deadlines for a good reason. I would highly recommend him.

I struggled with this class. Difficult weekly assignments: helloworld starter code, resources scattered, and all packaged by ambiguous instructions. He laughs while explaining them too... It seems useful for data science but fails to present a single theme with topics ranging from commands in bash to implementing ML. Read syllabus 1st before adding

Super lenient professor, allows you to resubmit all assignments unlimited times for full credit as long as you complete it before the deadline. The lectures and textbook are much higher level than anything on the exams.

Great lectures, good information and I do feel like I learned a lot. The only reason I give him a 4 is because the homeworks got very crunched towards the end and it was near impossible to keep up with. The homeworks are difficult but reasonable, and you get to work with a partner. Overall, the course was great but took a lot of time and effort.

Dr. Teymourian's class was the best! 10/10 would take again, learned a lot. He is very kind and patient and will help if you go to office hours. Facilitates an environment that is very conducive to learning.

He has extended deadlines for students during holidays or when unexpected events occurred. He's very understanding if you reach out in need of help. The material is difficult, but if you keep on top of everything it's manageable. The assignments are time consuming but he lets us work with a partner. Graded on 3 tests, 11 hw, 9 in-class quizzes.

Weekly projects were challenging but interesting, tests were easy, and I learned a lot. He makes the concepts super clear & I definitely recommend him. One note though is that this class is far more about how to use cloud computing than the theory behind how it works
Fantastic teacher, lectures were so good and content so well explained I never felt I had to take notes. Interesting weekly assignments too
Avoid this is you want your time not to be wasted. This was a bad experience.
Worst class I have ever taken. Professor has no ethics or morals.
Don't waste your time looking for advise from this professor.

Bizarre class. I don't think it will ever help me on anything as I did not learn from this professor. Erratic behavior during class towards students and not necessarily worth it grade wise. I would not recommend. It is not enjoyable.
The material was very low quality and completely outdated. The grading is unreliable and the professor unresponsive towards students. He is very rude and disrespectful.

Difficult in lectures, the hardest part of this class is not falling asleep in lecture, no clear grading criteria was given for the paper that was worth 80%. After feeling like I did everything right in this class I still got a grade way lower than what I was expecting. Professor has toddler-outbursts when the class starts to drift off.

Pretty nice guy, his lectures go off topic sometimes but I still felt engaged and that I was learning important and relevant material. He would make some jokes towards students but they were lighthearted and always received that way as well.

The one and only class that I actually have applied in my job. Dr. Malik has vast knowledge into the subject and has taught around the globe to top execs of oil companies. Passionate abt what he does and teaches a lot of life lessons too.
His classes are really boring. His way to teach is bad. It is an imposed class, you can't move or do anything in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Malik taught clearly and concisely. It was easy to understand his lecture. Glad to have his class

Worst advising ever. Malik does not care whether you graduate in time or a century later. He dislikes students from Pakistan, India, Afghanistan, and Iran so much so that he was willing to give an incomplete - though they were actively participating in class. There is no career advice he could offer to me in times when I needed most. AVOID!
Useless teacher. Agree with all the previous comments. Its a waste of time and money to take his class.
Excellent course I recommend to everybody.

If you don't have copies of his old exams you are screwed. If you have real world experience and cannot forget what you know to keep up with his out-dated knowledge you are screwed. Generally hard to work with outside of class. The cheating in the class is all over the place, in terms of old exams. Students without them were left to fail the tests.

Oil and Gas financial management is a joke.  The guy is completely out of date. His examples are over simplified and wrong. I could not think of a more useless way to spend time then listening to the nonsensical drivel that comes out of this man's mouth. Generally I have to stab my pen into my hand to stay awake.
Useless teacher.  Very easy “A” if you have some old tests.  They are almost exactly the same as previous years.  No participation, no thinking allowed.

If you want a very easy A, take this course. The price: Malik is obnoxious, rude, useless, and does not allow you to participate and think.  He likes to make fun of people, mainly minorities (although he is from Pakistan).  Tests are the same as the previ

This professor is awesome!! Very easy to understand teaching style, optional attendance if you're busy, and everything you need to know is on Quest. If you do everything, you can probably expect an A. And she lightens the mood every now and then with a joke or two. Fun class.

really good professor but i find that she goes on a lot of tangents (pun not intended) so it was kinda difficult to pay attention. tests are only 6 questions so a lot of material is not tested so it was hard to study for it. other assignments make up most of your grade tho so it was fine

The only credit are the written homeworks, quest modules, QR problems, and exams. She drops some grades and sometimes reduces the amount of credit needed to pass. The class is super easy as long as your do the modules and you do practice problems!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kris is truly amazing! She shows that she cares about her students. Her tests are fair to ensure everyone receives a great grade. If you want to finish her M408S class with a 4.0, all you have to do is go to her lectures and do the quest modules. Her lectures helped me not only understand calculus but also enjoy it. I love her (go to office hours)!
BEST math prof at UT. Had her both semesters for Calc 1 for science majors. Love the way she teaches, she just makes everything make sense. Tests are fair based on what we've learned in class.

I just wanted to take a moment to say Kris has been the best math professor I have taken in my entire life. As a physics major I wanted to get a good understanding of all calculus and she made an amazing job. Definitely take her and go to her office hours.

Took pre cal junior year so I was nervous entering this class, but we spent one week reviewing old topics to catch everyone up. Dates are set in stone so you can plan ahead easily. Lectures are very informative and I never used my textbook. HW and learning module contents are similar to the exam. Tip: Go to lectures and try to understand the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kris is amazing, she teaches everything clearly that shows up on exams and the exams are concept heavy. Homework can be time consuming. She is really nice as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Kim was amazing! Her class is mostly completion and if you do all the assignments, you will get an A. Quizzes were graded easily. She offers so many resources to help you understand and do well! She does cold call but I feel that it really helped me learn quicker.

She's a really nice professor and a lenient grader! Class was mostly completion based homework. I felt like it was supposed to be more quiz heavy though, but I think she got busy with our semester. Lectures were kind of boring because they were repetitive but she really tries to make the class engaging.
Prof. Kim is one of the best professors I have ever had at UT! The homeworks weren't too difficult and she does an amazing job teaching. She is also very accommodating. I highly recommend taking her.

Mina선생님 is so sweet and genuinely interested in her students. I love her! The textbook is not required to buy, as she uploads all the files needed. She does "cold call" but she's extremely accomodating if you're truly uncomfortable. Homework is a breeze, just keep track of due dates. Class was enjoyable and stress-free; Mina선생님 is the best!

I really like Professor Mina. She is really caring and cares about your improvement in Korean. However, I think her lectures are a bit boring and that Professor Eunjoo's class is more engaging. That being said, you will be in good hands if you take Professor Mina's class.

I took Mina Kim for Fall 2024, and I honestly want to say that I loved her. Was a little bit hard to understand since she spoke more Korean than english for lectures. Does cold call on students every day, so make sure to STUDY! She's the sweetest and gives us extra points on tests. I learned so much from Mina Kim!

Professor Kim is incredibly sweet and so caring. I really enjoyed this class and would recommend it to any student interested in Korean. There is a lot of assignments but that's normal for any language class.

I LOVE Professor Kim! She is so sweet and truly cares about her students. She is always willing to help and meet with students. The class pace can be pretty fast, so it was overwhelming at times. You do have to study and keep up or you will fall behind.

Mina is such a caring, wonderful person and teacher. she genuinely wants you to learn the language and works as hard as she can to take the stress and pressure out of it. Mina is one of the best teachers I've ever had and shes very flexible with deadlines. most tests and all homework are completion based!

I have taken 3 different professors for Korean and Mina is by far my favorite! She was so sweet and really cared about us improving our language skills. She does cold call on people but it honestly was so helpful and made me be a better student. bi-weekly quizzes on quizlet were easy and she prepared us well for exams.

One of the kindest and funniest profs ever! Compared to other language courses at UT, the workload is pretty light. Plus the homeworks are completion grades. She's so nice and bubbly that she makes lectures enjoyable, and she explains things clearly. She does cold call on people to read in class but it's good practice.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! cannot hype her up enough, she is so nice to her students. it makes learning a new language as easy as can be. take the class, easily the best part of UT. i wish more people could meet her because she is such a nice break from other professors, and reminds me why I am so lucky to be in college.

This is my third time taking Korean with Prof Kim and she is the best! Attendance is mandatory and participation is required. Incredibly caring, accommodating, and understanding. Prof Kim is so sweet and very easy to contact outside of class. Grades everything very quickly and you can tell she cares about her students

Amazing professor for a language credit. Attendance is mandatory and a big chunk of your grade. Homeworks are easy and are completion based. She grades really quick and responds quickly to emails as well. She's also super caring and if you have any problems, she'll accommodate you really well. I love her a lot, she's one of my favorite professors.

Attendance is 20% of the grade (showing up is crucial).Class is mostly lecture & is structured on the book. During lecture everyone is randomly called on. You must apply yourself outside of class if you want to learn Korean. Tests have an oral and written part; homework is completion based. Prof Kim is extremely kind, caring, and accommodating.!

Prof. Kim is probably the most understanding and caring instructor I've had at UT. She genuinely cares about her teaching and giving students opportunities to succeed. Just know that classes are lecture-heavy and participation/attendance are a big part of the grade. If you show up and stay engaged, you'll pick up Korean quickly and get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is super sweet. The class is lecture heavy but she puts a lot of resources on canvas and she's super accessible to help you out, which is really sweet. Quizzes and little recordings are weekly but they're easy and she grades based on completion. If you want to learn a language without devoting your whole life, take korean with her!

This professor is extremely caring and understanding. The class moves fast due to it being everyday, but if you apply yourself in the homework and during lecture it is very manageable. Weekly homework and quizzes but they are fairly easy. The professor is very accessible outside of lectures and will accommodate to your worries. Would recommend!

Super sweet teacher! Class was really easy, almost too easy. Would recommend if you actually wanna learn Korean, you should go to her office hours to practice speaking. Fair warning is that she tends to forget about/move the meetings around a lot so be careful if your schedule is super packed. Make sure you go to class since attendance is taken.

The workload in KOR606/607 wasn't too high, which can have its ups and downs - on one hand, the pacing was super relaxed which was awesome, but on the other I didn't study a whole lot on my own and learn outside of class. Ms. Kim is incredibly kind and caring nonetheless, and her upbeat attitude made me want to put in my own effort.

Ms. Kim is very kind and helpful. She is always patient with her students and does what she can for us. You can definitely get by without really learning the material, but she pushes you to engaged during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My first impression of Professor Kim was that the class would be strict with a lot of homework. However, this was not the case. I encourage anyone who has the opportunity to take a class with her to persist through the semester, regardless of your grades. Professor Kim is in your corner at all times and she is really is a kind soul!
Shes so sweet! She really cares about her students and is very patient with everyone. I definitely recommend her. I loved learning Korean even more because she makes the class fun.

Professor Kim is a very sweet teacher! She truly cares about her students and is passionate about teaching Korean. She does teach by lecturing on powerpoints, which isn't for everyone. However, she is very good at explaining Korean grammar and ensuring that students understand what she is teaching. I do wish we had spoken more Korean in class.

SO condescending. Don't even try to get clarification, he will genuinely laugh in ur face and tell u to review on your own outside of class. Also has completely free response exams with the worlds most specific answer keys. I would have been better off learning about evolution through Youtube videos.

This class is difficult with the switch of professors in the middle. Randy's half was worse than Kirkpatrick and both grade kinda specifically. Nice guy though, and lectures are still pretty engaging. Class is doable with a lot of effort but do yourself a favor and take some other professor if you can

good person, tough grader. very specific with what he wants you to write and shows no mercy in grading it. quizzes every week and homework every now and then. the exams averaged around an 85 each time and consisted of ~30 short frqs. interesting material but he makes it seem boring. Not an impossible professor, but there are better options

Horrible, avoid and take with literally anybody else. Syllabus states 25% get A, 30% get B, 35% get C, a horrible grading distribution. All of his exams are free response, in which him and his TAs grade subjectively and incredibly harsh/picky. Always taking points off for being "too vague" even if you state exactly what he said in his lectures.

Evil. Will act like a saint in class but turn around and give you misleading questions and answer choices on quizzes. Mentions something for a brief 2 seconds in lecture that will be on his FRQ exam and you are expected to answer verbatim. Will watch you fail and suffer then chuck a calming talisman in your face to seem like he wants to help.

Absolutely awful class. After the first exam's review session and practice test, the professor basically abandoned all support—no more practice exams. Grades took forever to post, and you had to calculate your class grade yourself. Communication was nonexistent. Completely disorganized, unhelpful, and stressful. Avoid at all costs—worst class ever!

Linder taught my genetics class along with Kirkpatrick. They both sped through the material, but Linder's quizzes are more of a hassle and his free response test questions are very particular. All in all a confusing memorization class, but all the info you need is in his lecture recordings, which I followed religiously and ended up being fine on.

He is nicer thank Kirkpatrick which was relieving but his lectures were still difficult and his lectures are very disorganized too. I felt very lost in the structure and his material was all over the place which made it difficult to study. Having to learn how to study again for his exams sucked since they were different from Kirkpatrick. alright

I preferred Dr. Kirkpatrick, but I liked Dr. Linder! He definitely cares about what he's talking about and tries to make lecture interesting. Quizzes were definitely difficult, but exams weren't too hard. For exams, be able to memorize + talk through the main points of each lecture. Their co-taught class is 100% the best evolution option.

Dr. Linder is a great guy. The quizzes are difficult and they will absolutely test you on everything said in the lecture (some quizzes are harder than ever), so make sure you study properly before those. Exams are all free response and not too bad if you study and know the materials conceptually. If you really are on the edge he helps you out.

I preferred Kirkpatrick's exams more, but Linder was just fine. I thought his lectures were better organized, and having free response questions was probably for the best given the rather subjective nature of Evolution. I thought the weekly quizzes were annoying and highly tedious.

Co-taught with Kirkpatrick and I honestly liked him. The part of the course that he teaches isn't as interesting, but he has a lot of enthusiasm. Exams / quizzes are hard but fair; they are heavily based on lectures. If you pay close attention and don't fall behind you should be able to get an A- at least. And Linder is very nice. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To do well in this class, rewatch lectures before quizzes, taking note of details AND concepts. Exams are free response, copy paste learning objectives OR details from lecture recordings with some slight application. Professor is highly mathematical and explains the reason behind why certain concepts occurs. Point system used.

Please do not waist your time with Dr Linder. Not only did he fail to teach any genetics content that you would expect from an honors genetics class, he doesn't respond to email, assesses over semantic details, and is really boring.

While Professor Linder seems very passionate about the subjects he teaches, he fails to understand that he is TEACHING them and we don't know too much about the topics. His weekly quizzes are worded to confuse you, and the tests aren't horrible but theres not enough time to finish them! He does not listen to feedback.

Professor Linder is a really good professor! Be warned, his exams are all multiple choice and are heavily based on lecture, but if you attend lecture and review over the slides and learning objectives, you'll do fine. He's very passionate about what he teaches and does an amazing job answering any questions you may have on the material :)

Dr Linder taught half of my evolution class. He is a very harsh grader but everything on his tests comes directly from the lecture/powerpoint, so if you pay attention and take good notes you will do well. Also, if the class avg on a test is low it will be curved up.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Don't get me wrong, he is a nice guy who obviously has a genuine passion for the material. HOWEVER, his exams are super long and he looks for such a specific answer that he somehow makes biology subjective. There's no way I would have made an A- if the semester hadn't gone online/open note. Record lectures!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class Ibe ever taken. Will (TA) constantly told us we didnt work hard enough to be successful at the collegiate level. Your grades will not reflect your knowledge. No amount of studying prepares you for the horrible grading. You will lose all your exam points to technicalities and be constantly insulted and degraded by Will. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Linder is a very intelligent, caring professor. He also structures his lectures to help us learn/analyze/discuss the material, rather than mindlessly memorize it. However, since grades are based upon application-based, free-response exams, I think he needs to lower his threshold for an A (or do grade bumps) to allow for us to make mistakes.

I very much regret taking Linder for honors genetics. His exams absolutely destroyed me. I don't understand the point of the journals we had to do in class; it seemed like he was looking for excuses just to knock us down as many points as possible. The point system was stupid and this class ruined my GPA. It was such a mistake to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'll start by saying I LOVED Biology. I love science & I love learning. However, I basically had to self teach this entire course. In class, you can barely hear Dr. Linder speak and it's difficult to stay awake because of it. His exams were extremely long and came directly from what he SAYS,not what's on his slides.I now hate bio. Switching majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Linder is intelligent, but he is condescending to students when they ask him questions, discouraging people from asking. The textbook was unnecessary, and he was specific on examples in his lecture slides for tests. He's rather bad at communication via email, and he is not lenient. He doesn't really follow his own syllabus in terms of grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His material is RIDICC his test are too THICC. He looks like the Man in the Yellow Hat but trust me on this: hes gonna make u feel like Curious George when he hits u with exams tho. The man is a hustler: I speak from experience when I say the IRS is more generous than this man He's a ghetto dad hiding from child support when you want a regrade
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't really understand how he structured his exams or what rubric he went off on grading. The quizzes were pretty hard, and I really had to put in tons of effort for his class. Lectures were very monotonous and hard to listen to; nice professor, but I would take the other honors genetics class tbh. Not worth tanking your GPA like I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Linder is a nice guy and a solid choice for honors bio. His class felt disorganized in terms of the topics we covered and in what order, and the lectures were a little boring. The tests are very straightforward and basically just based on your memorization of the lecture slides. His review sessions before exams are very helpful.

Solid choice. A little too easy if you've taken AP Bio, making you unenthusiastic about the class. But he's nice, encourages questions, and is good at explaining things. If you fall asleep/are too tired to ask questions in class, the textbook is a great supplement. Honestly, a very nice guy and fun to talk to outside of class. Just a bit slow pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Unbelievably nice guy, super passionate about biology, and a great lecturer. He has a pretty calm manner of speaking, but it was never boring. The textbook is not necessary, almost all of the information you're tested over is straight from the textbook. You will learn a lot from him, his lectures really make you think about biology in new ways.

Linder might be a little off topic at times but that is rare and he is quite clear in what he says. the textbook is basically useless since there is almost no material in common with the lectures. As long as you listen to every lecture and take good notes you can look over before the test, its a relatively easy class.

Dr. Linder is a very smart person and his lectures contain a lot of information. 325H is hard and the material he presents might be difficult to grasp, but it's very interesting the way he teaches it and will go a long way if you're a bio major. Exams are hard and graded harshly at times, but the class is designed so an 83 will be an A.
Class is very interesting.  Materials are little bit difficult because it's little different from bio you've been learning.  Books are not required.

Grading is random but either A or A-. The quizzes were annoying, forcing you to read, but I feel like this was one of the few classes I actually learned something (particularly strategy and a solid framework). Enjoy her lectures and don't stress too much, just stay on top of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, pragmatic professor - no exams because she discourages cramming, only daily quizzes. Better grades for people who can connect concepts through the semester (again, discourages cramming). Grading is ambiguous and controlled by TA w/ ~50% A/A-, so I think that's fair. Readings were from WSJ, so that's cool. Good course & enthusiastic prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I learned a lot about marketing, but her class was a pain in the butt. It was so much work (lots of reading) and we were graded harshly against our peers. I wouldn't suggest taking this class if you care about your grade, but I enjoyed being taught by McAlister.

Super knowledgable. Do readings and think about what you'll say during class if you're not great at speaking on the spot. Participation is very big for your grade. Tie prev. course concepts into what you're learning that day. Same for quizzes. She's a fun lady

(For MKT337H) Very sweet and passionate. Grading is HEAVILY based on good participation. You must figure out "her way" that she wants you to answer questions and you're golden (make sure to connect previous course concepts in everything! Quizzes, exercises, participation). Complete extra credit sooner rather than later. No exams, only a daily quiz.

She is an awesome professor but you definitely have to study before every class. There is a quiz for every class and a group quiz at the end. She is a little confusing with grading, so I would make sure to talk to her throughout the year to see where she thinks you stand. Awesome person and you learn a ton

Unforgettable. She cares + wants everyone to have fun while refining communication. That being said, this class will be unique. You gotta do it for the love of the game if you're in this class preparing for a presentation (she likes theatrics/self-expression) Writing assignments graded harsh (TA's fault). Strongly rec class to become friends.

Professor Sarkesian is the BEST choice for BA324! Her class is structured to support career growth, with coursework focused on recruiting, job applications, and public speaking. She gives meaningful feedback and truly gets to know her students, helping you to showcase your individuality and grow. Her style of teaching helps you build confidence!!

Professor Sark's class was a phenomenal experience! She genuinely cares about her students' success both in and out of the classroom. She creates a welcoming environment where everyone feels heard and supported. Highly recommend!

Professor Lesley Sarkesian's class is well-structured, engaging, and focused on building real-world communication skills that extend far beyond the classroom. 
 Her feedback is especially valuable. It's detailed, and she helps you improve over time.  Assignments have a clear connection to real-world situations rather than being busy work.

Professor Sarkesian is incredibly supportive and accessible outside of class. She genuinely cares about her students' growth and career development, and goes above and beyond to help—whether through feedback, advice, or opportunities. You can tell she truly invests in her students' success.

Professor Sarkesian truly cares about her students and gives valuable feedback to her students. She is honestly one of the best professors and classes I've had in McCombs! The TA's are amazing with feedback for written assignments and the class is actually applicable outside of school. What you put into this class is what you will get out of it.

Professor Sarkesian is one of the best professors I've had at McCombs. BA375 is definitely not an easy class, but she genuinely cares about helping students improve their communication and presentation skills. The expectations are clear, and if you take her feedback seriously and put in the effort, you'll improve a lot over the semester.

The writing assignment are fairly easy, check with TA before submitting each one. Practice all your presentations no matter how small you think they are! 

Professor Sarkesian is awesome and super funny. She really supports her students even outside of class and is very understanding.

Professor Sark is one of the hardest BA 324 professors. On one hand, her remarkably high expectations and attention to detail makes the class anything but a throwaway. Conversely, her passion and genuine care for students and the course makes BA 324 one of the most important classes you could ever take for professional development.

Professor Sarkesian is a great instructor who truly cares about student growth. The class is challenging but fair, with clear expectations and helpful feedback. If you put in the effort and practice, you will gain real communication skills that are useful beyond the classroom.

SHE HAS EXAMS. My downfall was the exams which were NOT covered in class. Sark is great, don't get me wrong, but her grading is heavily subjective. The TA's grade super harsh. Good class if you don't care about the grade and just want to improve as a speaker. But with enough effort pulling an A- should be doable. Don't expect an A.

DON'T GO INTO THIS CLASS THINKING IT'S A FREE A. Sark will do her best to be accessible and support you, in and out of the classroom. But it's important you ask for feedback during assignments - she will help you while you prepare. The TAs are sticklers on written assignments, so use office hours to help you. If you do the work, an A is possible.

I love Professor Sark! She's such a caring professor and will acknowledge and reward hard work. Her TAs are tough graders, though, so I highly recommend going to TA office hours to get an extra set of eyes on your written assignments. This class is a lot of work, but it is rewarding. TLDR; I know dada.

This course isn't an easy A, but if you care more about learning than just protecting your GPA, it's absolutely worth it. The class is fun and very interactive, just be ready to present and give a lot of speeches.

Sark is wonderful! I adored this class and although it is not an easy, I learned more than any other class I've taken. Sark forces you to challenge yourself and step out of your comfort zone and her teaching style genuinely made me a better speaker, stronger leader, and better hire. If you prioritize real learning above GPA, take this class!

Terrible professor and TAs. Just a bunch of nitpicking that can WRECK your GPA. Many friends in class had way better written assignment products, but got so many points taken from TAs for "not following instructions", which were extremely vague in the first place. Only take this class if you want to live in TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class should not have been as hard as it was. The grading is very unclear, and the TA's grade super unjust. The rubric was never clear, and for group presentations it does not matter how good your content is, but more about theatrics and giving her a show. Do not recommend.

Lesley is truly the best professor I've ever had at UT. She's inspiring, brave, and incredibly intelligent. Her class challenges you with presentations that push you outside your comfort zone, but by the end you'll grow into a confident, professional public speaker. She is very accessible outside of class also. Take her class, you won't regret it.

She grades all oral presentations, while your section's TA grades all written assignments. Feedback is subjective/unactionable sometimes. Oral presentations are the majority of your grade, a few textbook tests, and some written assignments. Pay very close attention to her reasonable feedback, be nice. After everything, you will be a better speaker.

I loved Professor Sark. The experience taking this class was great, and I became very close with my classmates. This class will 100% improve your presentation skills. Unfortunately, the gap between an A- and an A is very large (90-94). I almost got an A, but was just short. An A is attainable if you go to office hours for written assignments.

This class is not easy but it is rewarding. There are several presentations throughout the semester which forces you to get good at presenting, especially because Professor Sark will give you very detailed feedback. If you rehearse your presentations, get started on the capstone project early, and attend office hours with the TAs, you will succeed.

Grading was super subjective; she wants you to do insane things to be interesting and fun. Would be a really fun experience if my GPA was not on the line. The class genuinely does make you learn, however there are definitely ways to get students to leave with the same takeaways without torture. Take at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sarkesian is a great teacher, but extremely tough grader. She will take off one point per filler word but by the end of the class you will not be using filler words anymore. Capstone project was really stressful due to the fact it is a 25 minute oral presentation with no note cards or script. So start that early. Overall awesome teacher, hard A-.

Super sweet. She wants her students to grow and succeed, and it shows in how detailed and thoughtful her feedback is. That being said, she is a tough grader. Written assignments are hard to ace without attending office hours. But put in the work and take her feedback seriously, you'll see yourself transform by the end of the semester.

Power trip. Sarkesian cares about her students, but everything in the class was based on some arbitrary standard that changed by the day. Sark would often count off things for certain students that she wouldn't call out for others, and this lack of consistency was seen in her TAs as well, on whom your entire grade for the class rests on

Don't take her. Makes everything political, switches up her grading standards from assignment to assignment, and gives one A per assignment. If you value your gpa in any way take another professor. No she's not related to actual sark, bummer ik. Ur not allowed electronics or more than 3 skip days the entire semester too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After this class, I will never say a filler word again is actually drilled into my head and that is a good thing I notice it now more than ever and even got a compliment on it during an interview. I think it was a good class with a good professor, Sarkesian cares that you learn

I think the written assignments were graded a bit harshly by the TAs given the lack of criteria and sometimes was the textbook says doesn't align with what they say. Sarkesian herself is awesome, she knows everyone's names. She is tough but like a tough love. I know as students we love easy As but I like this class cause it made me practice mor.
Sarkesian is a comedic professor, she will make class fun and takes in suggestions, she doesnt give free As without effort but if she sees you improve she will, the TA is a different story tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sarkesian is a tough grader but she actually wants you to get better and I learned a lot
I know people have mixed feelings about her but she is genuine and enjoys being around her students

People have mixed opinions on Sark, but I loved her. She is kind, genuine, and honest- and pushes you to become a better speaker. The class is difficult, especially if you are not a performer, but I feel like I came out of it being more confident in my speaking abilities. Start your capstone EARLY and make friends- and you will enjoy this class.

DO NOT take this class if you want to be a happy person. This class is fully a competition between your classmates on who is a better performer and you will never succeed even if you are the best presenter ever. All the written assignments are horrible and honestly not even worth trying for because they will find something wrong with it.

Sark is super sweet and caring, and this class is what you make it! If you're not a good public speaker and not willing to improve, you will not do well. Your TA and Capstone Group are out of your hands, so please make the most of them. BEGIN CAPSTONE EARLY! There is an extra credit contest in the beginning of the semester, and I earned 10 points!

If you want to learn skills that you will actually take out of the classroom, Sarkesian is the professor! That being said, YOU HAVE TO UTILIZE RESOURCES. The grading can be tough, but as long as you talk to the TA's, you'll be fine. She offers more extra credit than any other professor and provides many opportunities to learn. highly recommend

I thought this professor was alright, but she expects a lot from students. The way to succeed in written assignments is by going to TA office hours or emailing them specific questions. I've heard other BA324 professors are way easier, so she wouldn't be my top choice. Content is okay and sometimes she asked us what we wanted to do in class

The TAs make or break this course! They all grade differently even though the professor says otherwise, Go to their office hours for every assignment and record the meeting because they will try to go back on their word, snakes.

Professor Sarkesian is sweet and tries to make class fun, but the class isn't great. You're graded super harshly, and it feels like a performance class more than business speaking. We're let out late often, but being even a minute late means you're marked absent. 

And the TAs? Yeah… they SUCK. Take it if you have to, theres way easier professors.

She is an interesting woman, but do not take her if you are not 100% confident in your public speaking skills. She expects perfection for all of your oral presentations. You have to be perfect to get above a 90. No filler words, no unintentional pauses, no freezing, no stuttering. Grading is subjective and is unfair among peers.
Class is not a meritocracy. You will not get graded for the quality of your work - it's pretty random in however a TA is feeling that day.
Took this class and grading was very subjective. Don't recommend.

Classes are always filled with students presenting, allowing you to know all your classmates and watch them grow in their presenting skills. Grades subjectively based on how you present, loves creative hooks. Half the semester is capstone papers and presentations. Most of your grades depend on the TA who grades written assignments. No curve

Grading was at times subjective, however Prof Sarkesian provided tons of opportunities for improvement throughout the semester. Writing assignments were deceptively easy, and going to TA office hours was a must to maximize scores. BA 324 was definitely the most challenging class I've taken at UT, but also the most rewarding.

Professor Sark is a bit of an enigma when it comes to grading, but once you figure out what she's looking for, you can tailor your presentations to that. The class is all about presenting, which I preferred to the textbook-heavy versions other professors use. There were some bad TAs who graded harshly, but she is still a professor worth taking.

The worst professor I've taken. Her grading is subjective. Participation and attendance are two separate grades, but attendance affects your participation grade which is not in criteria. The prof and TA grade extremely hard and offer limited feedback. TA gave copy paste feedback and prof defended it. Don't join if you aren't already a good speaker

My TA would deduct points without providing specific feedback or referring to the very simple and vague rubric. Every section has a different TA, and some sections are graded easier than others. It is very unfortunate when one section gets mostly As and an other section is a class full of Bs. Wouldn't recommend the risk of taking this professor.

Although she is a sweet person, her grading is extremely biased. She definitely plays favorites in class, and she never really tells you why she takes off points. She expects performances for her presentations and will grade you harshly if you are not enthusiastic enough. don't really have to study for tests, participation matters

Sarkesian seems to have graded harder than other classes, requires more class participation/attendance, has strict classroom policies, and expects theatrical performances over content in speaking assignments. There were opportunities for extra credit, but overall her grading on the presentations was tough and hard to please/receive an A.

Ms Lesley was so sweet, I still keep in contact with her a year later. Tries to make the class into a family and get us to really fw each other, which I appreciated later bc I love seeing my old classmates now. This is a presentation class so be ready to get graded on every detail of your presentation. She is super funny too and will spill tea.

Professor Sarkesian is kind and supportive towards her students, but her approach to grading assignments is horrible. She provides limited feedback, her reasons for deducting points are not clear, and her grading guideline is too specific. Although she is a sweet teacher, if I had the chance to take it with a different professor, I 100% would.
I loved Professor Sarkisian, hands down one of my favorite classes. I generally love the class, the workload wasn't hard at all and she's very adventurous so expect to have fun outside!

Lesley is amazing. I've never met anyone like her and never taken a course quite as impactful as hers. My communication skills truly improved and I found a valuable connection + a professor that I will never forget. She truly cares about each and every one of her students and is consistently available and enthusiastic as a mentor. 100% recommend.

Amazing professor. Deeply cares about the success of her students and understands her students come from all different types of backgrounds. She is also hilarious and has an amazing personality. BA324 is standardized across all profs, especially the grading, but prof Sarkesian makes the class great. My presentation skills has definitely improved.

Lesley is consistently available, genuinely invested in her students' success, and serves as an inspiration in the classroom. The familial vibe she cultivates is so strong that I comfortably refer to her by name. A truly exceptional teacher, Lesley goes the extra mile to support her students in every aspect of their lives. A true asset at McCombs!

Lesley truly cares for her students and wants them to succeed. Her experiences as an entrepreneur and former worker in the corporate world make her an interesting storyteller and mentor. You must put in work for an A but there are ample extra credit opportunities and feedback provided for your work. Overall, you should definitely take her class.

Ms. Lesley is different in a way that she is a very successful woman in the business world so she has a lot of valuable and helpful insights to share. My first professor at McCombs who truly cared for each and every one of her students and was available 24/7. She truly wants you to excel in life and I would definitely recommend her.

Lesley is an amazing professor, businesswoman, and mentor. She cares for her students and wants them to grow. Her BA324 class was just the right amount of work -- if you wanted an A you had to work for it, but she allowed room to improve. The writing and oral assignments are standard across all BA 324 sections, so not much flux there. Take her!
aint no way i think she wrote the good reviews herself...

Avoid this prof. The professor is dismissive and moves way too fast. Going to office hours is a waste of time—she makes you feel worse for being confused rather than actually teaching. She does not care if the class is lost. Worst experience I've had for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never take the class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Looking at my past prof. Not surprised at all with what people were saying. I had her for A+P and I can confirm it does not get better. For those who say she is a "good" professor, I will admit her lectures are good but not very engaging. Did not work for me at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am currently enrolled in her class, but Dr. Lester-Smith is a great professor. She is super knowledgable, encourages questions, and helps tease out complex concepts. A+P is difficult, but I think she does what she can to make learning it as accessible as possible. You will have to work a little harder in this course, and that's okay. She's great!

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!! SHE DOESNT LISTEN TO STUDENTS CONCERNS! She makes you “discuss” her slides instead of teaching them but the thing is no one knows what's going on so we can't even talk about it! I hate this class and will be Q dropping and speaking to higher ups if she doesn't get her act together and care about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was the worst professor I have ever had. She does not care about her students and does not take accountability for her own mistakes. She is very hard to reach, like off the face of the Earth, so good luck catching her. Don't get me started on the pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not understanding at all. No extra credit or any real way of trying to help get your grade up. All of my other SLH classes have more assignments but also more opportunities to earn a good grade. NOT THIS ONE!!  Idk how to explain but she gives helicopter mom vibes. Do not take her I wish I had dropped the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: slow to answer emails, is passive-aggressive, is rarely at their office hours, etc. TA was nice but would just read off the slides. There are pop knowledge checks every week and the study guides don't match the quizzes. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Those complaining about her need to understand that if you want to go to grad school, you need to learn how to actually study and take a test without cheating. I'm a grad student and had Lester-Smith for Voice Disorders. I immensely appreciate her clear expectations and her intelligence. If you apply yourself, you will be a better student for it.

God forbid a girl want to actually make sure we learn something in SLH. I thought the tests were fair. It was a lot of content and studying took up a lot of time but the study guides were helpful in knowing the big picture & details to study. Dont even have to read textbook if you just pay attention in class and look at slides. Hard but do-able
Good luck everyone
You could not pay me any amount of money to take this class again. she is praying on our downfall

She has 7 quizzes that make up the bulk of the grade, and the questions are worded really weird. I've never studied this hard in my life and still felt this hopeless. The TA's are really nice, but I'd avoid this professor if possible. My body will never recover from the all-nighters and stress-induced hair loss.
Very unaccommodating, passive aggressive professor that tells you what to study then puts the opposite on the test

It is genuinely impossible to study for the class, there is so much content it is impossible to study of it to be able to answer extremely specific questions on the quiz. I've had to study every single day for this class and it is still impossible. Lectures are not mandatory but she just reads off the slides.
The professor is really nice, but I would highly recommend do not take this class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely, the first class I have taken where it felt like there was nothing I could do to get a better grade. There were assignments and extra credit opportunities, but they were worth so little that it was almost irrelevant to do them. Lectures are almost pointless if you have the textbook. I recommend watching a lot of YouTube videos. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class took my will to live
Trick questions, no leeway on grading, get ready to study for hours and barely pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! It was hard, and there was a lot of content. But honestly, it was doable as long as you go to class and study as you go. She and the TAs are so accessible and friendly, it was honestly so enjoyable.

The entire grade comes from quizzes and a final exam. The quizzes are application-based, making it difficult to study for and unpredictable. There are also no drops or grades that come from anything else other than extra credit quizzes that barely count for anything, and you can't even review them afterwards to study. Makes absolutely zero sense
Professor uses a lot of trick questions in her quizzes. Very hard to keep up with the content. A lot of stuff to study.

I had to study a lot for this class. The quizzes and test were hard, but the course was extremely well organized and had clear expectations. She allows you to re-take a few of the quizzes at the end of the semester which was really helpful for my grade, and also helped me study for the final. This was my favorite course!

The course was organized very well for A&P and paired with the lab. Extra credit practice quizzes were given for each unit. Quizzes were set up to make you pay attention to the concepts. Overall not a bad course but you need to study. Dr. Lester-Smith was very kind and prioritized mental health.
Class is essentially the professor reading slides to you.

Dr. Lester-Smith organizes material for the course in a helpful way. Synchronous classes helped with application concepts and you could tell she really enjoys what she teaches. Quiz retake options were live-savers. Because the final was short-answer/essay format instead of MC like quizzes, it felt unexpected/hard, even with it being open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Classes on zoom during pandemic. 6 quizzes given on Proctorio/ one final exam. Quizzes are very difficult, I would spend hours studying and still get a B. However, 2 quiz re-takes were allowed and they were the same questions. Very sweet person and good lecturer, material is difficult.

Anatomy of Speech and Hearing. She was nice, but basically just read exactly off of the slides. There were several live zoom meetings, but I didn't find them helpful because most of it was in break out rooms. There are 6 quizzes and one final. The quizzes were super difficult and tricky. The final was also really difficult, but it was open notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He does not care about students learning. His answers to questions are mediocre, discouraging to get deep into topics. I doubt he would stand a deep discussion on any of the topics he shallowly teaches. He is always wearing ridiculous things and really does not act as a good, respectable academic.
he does not teach what's needed

The course lacks clear structure and often emphasizes methods that feel less relevant than modern approaches. Topics are covered too quickly, and explanations to questions can be unclear or superficial. Assignments focus mainly on adjusting parameters rather than demonstrating deeper understanding

He says he cares about his students but all he cares about is himself and his advancement towards I don't know what goals. Egocentric and hidden agendas. Do not trust him 
Quirky, strange, scolds you and is passive aggressive. Do not believe what you see.
His mind is a mess.

I took the Subsurface Machine Learning course in Fall 2025. Although this is 3rd ML class I am taking in graduate level, I learned tons of new things. He has the best slides ever. He also provides interactive dashboards for playing around and understanding concepts intuitively.
He is a good and considerate Professor!

Dr. Pyrcz is a nice professor who will gladly listen to your concerns and questions. The only thing is that his class is hard to understand if you do not have a background in data science since he goes very fast through his lectures and does not relate it back to why it is practical to learn this stuff. Grading is easy and midterms are not hard.

I really enjoyed Dr. Prycz's class. I felt like the lectures went by pretty fast mostly due to the amount of content, but he is a great teacher who really wants his students to learn. His assignments are very fair (not time consuming at all and they help you learn the content). Exams and quizzes are graded very leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was difficult to work with, when taking her studio class I felt lost.

This professor was very difficult to please. I had a hard time understanding her instructions and her accent.  She did not seem to care about how her attitude affected students. She made several side comments that diminished the overall environment of the studio space. The whole class had various complaints.

Extremely difficult to communicate with and has a very computational way of approaching design. She was very petty about class attendance and made design studio (previously one of my favorite classes) extremely uncomfortable and unwelcoming.
