I think the flipped learning model was not something that particularly worked for me. The class is hard but if you focus on just understanding how things work instead of memorizing you will do a lot better. She's nice though and very understanding imo. She gets too much hate.

Very passive aggressive and often refuses to help students. So many things to track and she does not try to make it easier, just wants to make our lives as hard as possible. Feedback on exams aren't helpful, she is making the class harder and harder. If your class has low grades in CS 429 prepare for her to have a bad impression.

Dr. Norman is the only CS professor I've ever had is organized and a great lecturer. OS is just hard and I think a lot of people blame her for their bad grades but they aren't putting in the work to just go to class, take notes, and study. Her grading scheme seems scary but she lowkey lies and will average your columns at the end so don't stress.
Ez ahh class
she is not the devil everyone claims she is. u js gotta study a lot
class was lowkey light, idk why people always tweak out about this class

Projects are quite a bit of work but doable. Test are straight forward just review notes and practice material. Make sure to go to all classes and discussion. Course grading scheme is a bit weird. In generally easier than comp arch just more work for labs.

The worst class I've ever taken and ever will take at UT. Weird, esoteric grading scheme that makes it difficult to get anything higher than a C. Projects take an insane amount of time to complete and it always feels like your time is never respected. Drop this class and take Mootaz instead. At least Norman is a nice person, all things considered.
The storm gods were said to smite those who dared to challenge their wrath. The class itself was not bad though.

While the grading scheme is a lot to take in, I realized part way through the semester that the primary goal of it is for us to learn. Once I stopped worrying about my grade in the class (besides trying to do well on projects) I had a much better experience in the class. Dr. Norman is the best there is and cares about your success and learning.

Overall, she was ok. Dr. Norman is kind, and I liked the flipped classroom, multiple chances for retakes, and group focus. However, she wasn't open to feedback, the grading scheme was demotivating, projects are grueling, and class time should've been halved. To do well, don't let the grading scheme discourage you, go to her OHs, and participate.

Let me start off by saying that she's probably the nicest teacher I've had so far, as she really makes an effort to get to know you. However, that's kinda where the good stuff about this class ends. Projects are sooooo time consuming. Tests are alright, but one tiny mistake has you going from a 5 to a 3. You don't learn anything going to lectures.
spent more time doing mind maps than sleeping

future students: read OSTEP, go to EVERY single class/section, never ever get on Dr Norman's bad side, review slides for exams, get through projects.
complaints: somewhat murky grading, lecture videos mostly revise book content, flipped class sometimes wasteful, inane project procedure
Dr Norman does care a lot and this class is hard but its doable

WAY overhated. There is a lot of work, that's a necessary part of learning systems programming. The exams have so many opportunities to retake that any level of effort is enough to get a B. Getting an A is a lot of work, but certainly achievable if you put in the time and effort. I'm honestly a big fan of Dr. Norman and had fun in the class.

One of the worst teachers I have ever taken in the UTCS department I don't even know how she became department head, Mandatory Lectures are pointless and useless, all content covered in 1 hr pre-lecture videos which are required. Tests aren't too bad if you look at the slides and watch prelectures, projects and the grading scheme is nightmare fuel
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OS was the hardest class. I spend at least 30 hours a week on the projects. 50-60 hours during hard projects. The instructions are very vague and sometimes downright wrong which costs hours on the projects. The TAs try to help but can be vague. I don't remember a day since I started the projects for this class that I have had a day off.

Be ready for one of the most intense classes with the worst grading system to ever exist. The entire semester, it was not made very clear where I stood with my grade and what I was on pace for. Be ready for anxiety surrounding that, especially if you are feeling like you are on the edge of passing/failing.
This class feels like finding 2 minis right after drinking a big pot every single day until you finish. Best of luck.

Good luck. Norman is nice! But to be honest you just have to get through it. I would take this OS over any other if you just want to pass. The grading scheme is definitely weird, it is bad if you are trying to get a good grade but very lenient if you just want the C. Either way you will be putting up at least 20 hours of total work/lectures a week.

To be honest, first i want to say Norman a nice person.  HOWEVER SHE IS A HORRIBLE TEACHER. she assigns us a workload of 30+ hours a week MINIMUM. SHE MAKES US CODE TOPICS SHE HAS NOT TAUGHT US. THE TA'S ARE USELESS AND DO NOT ANSWER ANY QUESTION, EVEN CONCEPTUAL. THEY ARE MISLEADING. SHE HAS TAKEN ALL OF MY FREE TIME AND WEEKENDS AND HAPPINESS

Dr. Norman as a person is great, she's fun to talk to and provides great insight about a lot of things (even if it's not OS related). Tests are fine, it's just the projects that make the class hard (pick a good group).

I am convinced these positive reviews are troll posts. I genuinely believe she enjoys watching students suffer. Her lectures are an absolute waste of 2 hours, as the pre-lecture videos mostly cover everything. With her fragile ego, she gets annoyed very easily when students question or challenge her methodologies, even when it's her fault.

Her grading scheme might seem weird to a lot of people but you get used to it, and as long as you don't slack in any of the categories you'll be fine! She does a flipped classroom where you watch lecture vids before class and discuss and ask questions during lecture time, which helps reinforce what you learned.

This course was hard but Norman pushed us through. Her lectures can feel a little pointless (since we really learn using the pre-class modules), but interacting with others was nice. She is kind and you can tell she really cares about her students. The grading system is really complicated but it is not too hard to get a B. Take Norman over Gheith.
Very confusing grading rubric. Very very glad this semester is over.

The class is difficult, but Norman taught it well; a lot of negative reviews are malding students. An A is achievable, just needs effort. Pre-recorded modules are best for learning(IMO). The rubric is hard to understand, read carefully. Content is easier than comp arch, projects are much harder. Retake grading is very strict. Do learning sessions!

Professor Norman is one of the best professors I've taken. It is a very difficult class, but the repetition of the material means that I won't forget it as easily as easier profs. The in-class group work is a lot of fun, and the projects are fascinating! She also cares about her students, and will talk to you like a normal human in office hours.

The worst teacher ever it's like she enjoys seeing students suffer. Projects are hard, ISP's are hard, exams are hard and she does not care. They will happily mark one section of one exam problem wrong or just put a question mark and a random underline and give you a 2 and waste another hour of your life doing the retake. Take anyone else.

20-40 hours/week on projects + floor-based grading system. The stakes feel extremely high for every  assignment, as one slip up can permanently drop your final grade by multiple letters. The stress/sleep deprivation from this class alone meant I was sick for half of the semester. The content itself is interesting and you'll learn a lot though.

Wack grading system. It is easier to pass this class than it is to get an A. Just get your core topics down and do your best on the group projects. TAs don't look at your code. You get multiple chances to retake questions, use them effectively. Do not risk retaking test questions and doing worse that you originally did. 
Take the 3/5's and move on.

The professor made the course frustrating with excessively long pre-lecture videos that ruined my weekend. Lectures were disorganized, focusing on minor details that became entire exam questions. Grading was overly strict, and concept map activities were unhelpful. AVOID THIS CLASS SHE IS UNBEARABLE. Every MW that I see her, my day is ruined.

Grading system is cruel but an A is achievable, and a B isn't that hard with retake opportunities. Lecture videos are great and class is useful for clearing up any uncertainties. Projects are very difficult/time consuming compared to the pretty simple lecture content. Exam questions aren't bad but are graded strictly and somewhat inconsistently.

One of the absolute worst professors I have come across at UT. The grading system is one of the worst and if you screw up one little things it's an automatic letter down grade. Apparently she does give + and - but that's “up to her discretion”

This class is the worst course that a professor could ever conceive. This class follows Murphy's law to a T, and anything that might go wrong does go wrong. If you mess up one section out of 4-5 on one question topic out of 7-8 questions on 1 out of 3 total exams, you will get a 2 out of 5 on the question and end up failing the entire course.

Worst teacher at UT Austin. Her grading system is horrible and she admits that herself by going back on her own word on multiple occasions changing the syllabus on a day to day basis. All I have to say is good luck getting through this class cause there's not much that can be done otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Norman was the goat. Best CS professor I ever had. Really inspirational teacher that made my love OS.  Class was incredibly easy with extremely easy tests and coding assignments. Would recommend anyone to take her. Good Luck!

Dr. Norman's grading system is her ego on full display. Instead of admitting it's a failure, she blames students, taking zero responsibility while making the class a nightmare. She built a system that barely works, then punishes students for not thriving in it. Maybe it's time she faced the truth: her ‘masterpiece' is just a mess.

This class made me realize I will never be going into systems in my career if my co workers were people like Norman. Absolute useless lectures and you basically have to multiply it by 2 since the Panopto videos are as long as the lectures and the lectures have zero new content
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have had the displeasure of taking. The grading system is complete trash and nothing you learn will help you in your career. If you want a chance of having a +, or - then get prepared to waste at least 2 hours a week in office hours and even then it still might not happen
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is hard but you'll survive. Worst part of this class is Norman, she's genuinely an insufferable human being

This is going to be the hardest class you have taken thus far. It's basically SE lab, but for the entire semester and more difficult. Norman is nice enough but I feel that her and the TAs (who are overworked) could do more to guide students on the projects. This is my only hard class, but I've worked more this semester than I have any other.

This class is rough. The grading scheme feels impossible, and it's like talking to a brick wall trying to get clarity. I feel like I'm ranting on RMP just to stay sane. When Meek Mill prayed for "times like this," he misspoke on the track because clearly I'm praying to get out of the class. It's genuinely concerning how trash this course is taught.

Worst professor ever. OS is already known to be extremely hard, and Norman seems to enjoy making the class harder. Telling the TA's not to let students take pictures of discussion section slides, taking away section problems for credit, and the grading is so arbitrary. TA's grade insanely hard with little to no feedback on exams/section problems.

I can say for sure that this will be the worst professor you will have during your time at UT. The lectures are basically the videos and plan to spend double the time on the class since the videos are as long as the lecture. Try to get out of her as hard as you can cause you don't want to deal with her for the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Yo, let me tell you ‘bout Alison Norman,
Worst OS professor, man, it ain't warmin'.
Every class she's got us yawning, no finesse,
Messin' up the system, straight OS distress.
Got us waitin' on those threads like they're stuck in a loop,
Semaphore? Nah, it's a lock on our brains,
Every lecture's like a crash, can't maintain.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Get out your name tents. Put your screens flat. Put your phones away. Let's do all of the things we do to get ready to lean about operating systems. 

The phrase said at the start of every class and that's pretty much the only new information for the next 2 hours, with maybe a mind map thrown in half way. Rest is jsut a repeat of the Panopto videos
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: On top of insanely difficult projects that take 20-30 hours a week, attendance for lectures is mandatory, so that's 4 hours a week just in class plus another 2 hours in discussion section and another 2 for pre lecture videos. So this class takes at least 30 hours a week. Does Norman care? No, she'll just laugh at you and tell you to work harder.

Try your best to avoid this professor at all costs. Words are not enough to describe how bad my experience was. Norman ended up taking away discussion exams for credit causing As to be nearly unattainable. Do your best to avoid this at all costs, and if you are stuck here, all I can say is good luck.

This class's whole purpose is to make your life miserable. Bad professor, bad grades, lots and lots of hours reading about topics that most people aren't even interested in. You'd only like this class if you are a masochist. I'd suggest to reevaluate your choices on majoring CS and switch to another major as this is only for the toughest of minds.

I have officially experienced the WORST class in the entire history of UT. If you think you've suffered, oh no, my friend, you know nothing. Imagine a grading scheme so absurd, it feels like the professor spun a wheel labeled “A,” “B,” “C,” and “Sorry, better luck next time.” Everything that could possibly go wrong DID go wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This. Is. The. Worst. Class. I've. Ever. Taken. In. My. Life. If you are CS student, say goodbye to your time outside of this class, you are forced to essentially work a full time job + overtime for no pay + a bad grade. This prof makes the grading incredibly hard for supposed “learning,” but don't be fooled. This class is meant to make you suffer.

One of the worst professors I have had at UT. Absolute nightmare of a class. She claims she prepares you for interviewed but because of all the time I've spent in her class I've been getting rejected even more.

I LOVE Dr. Norman! As a professor, she is extremely knowledgeable and good at breaking down complex topics into easier-to-understand pieces. As a person, she is super sweet and sincerely wants all her students to succeed. Her grading is confusing at first, but you can retake questions several times. Put in the effort and you will succeed.

Harsh grading scheme, if you make a few mistakes you get 3/5, 1 mistake is 4/5. Found myself being stuck at 3/5 for most of the semester even though I felt like I had a near perfect understanding of the material. I gave up trying to chase 4s and 5s at some point mid semester. Projects take 20-30 hours a week and sometimes beyond that.

Overall, the class was really interesting and it's clear that Dr. Norman + the TAs care that the students learn a lot! There are many opportunities to improve w/ retakes and the syllabus clearly outlines what's needed for a specific grade. Start assignments early, go to office hours, talk w/ other people in the class and you'll be fine.

Ngl great teacher just the assignments are an insane amount of work. Grades fairly. In the end just tons of work Professor Norman and The TA's do alot to help and she is very helpful and extremely knowledgeable about all things OS. Can redo tests. Good thing is pre-lecture videos where you learn alot and allows lecture to be reivew which is great.

Hardest class I've ever taken at UT. Grading system makes tests super stressful as one small mistake deducts your grade a lot. You basically have to be perfect on everything on tests for a good grade. Projects are 15-20 hours a week and super time consuming. Hardest class I've ever taken at UT and super stressful.

The actual teaching occurs through pre-recorded video lectures and the class times are used for questions/clarifications. Some people found this teaching structure annoying, but I really benefited from it. The projects are very hard and time consuming, picking good group members is key. Grading policy was confusing.

Norman and her lectures themselves weren't bad I actually learned so much from this class compared to 429. The grading scheme is what made this class disastrous. The projects alone were soul-sucking and the unforgiving nature of specs grading makes you want to give up as soon as you're not able to fulfill the "E" category for a certain component.
Treated us like kindergarteners for the beginning

Grading scale sucks, idt it's unclear, I think it's just unrealistic. 4/5 on a lab = 79/80 test cases, makes fulfilling test case & design doc categories of rubric difficult. VERY delayed grading. I like that you can retake topics (eases stress). Test grading makes 4s/5s near impossible. The amount of work I put in only for a B killed me.

So is the dreaded "OS" of the UT CS Department. To clear up whatever ambiguous rumors you may have heard, yes, this class is very difficult. Yes, the labs are very hard. Yes, your grade on exam questions/quizzes is the lowest score out of the subquestions. However, the course content is interesting; watch vids before class. Good luck, student.

Shes so sweet and definitely knows her stuff. 4 problems with the course: weird grading system, we waste 25 minutes talking about how we are feeling, procrastinating with grading, and design docs
Memorize slides and understand concepts on basic level to do well. Concepts aren't too challenging to understand. Projects take time but first 3 are fine

Unlike popular belief, this class was much easier than 429 w/ Chatterjee. Though the coursework is heavier, concepts are easier. Grading scheme is ambiguous but structured well, and as long as you keep up, Norman gives many opportunities to improve your grade. Projects are long, but doable if you start early, plan well, and choose a good group.

This class is already an L. Never seen a more convoluted grading system. The focus is on arbitrary specifications, slide memorization and typical, textbook answers rather than thinking, learning, and problem solving. She has her own ideas of what is a right answer, and any out of the box thinking is not rewarded.

Projects are hard but doable if you start early and use your resources, lectures are useless but mandatory, and exams are harshly graded but doable if you study early.

Both Norman and Gheith have their own issues and strengths, choose based on if you prefer solo or team projects, both professors curve and have hard assignments.

SO unnecessarily difficult, Norman is incredibly stubborn and defensive about her warped teaching philosophies. In no world does it make sense to assign 40+ hours of work a week and then post unhelpful responses on Piazza when students are clearly struggling. Only good thing about this class are the lecture videos, concepts are p well explained.

Lectures were mandatory but pointless. Felt like high school since day one. There was a few times where high-school classes came to observe, and one of them literally told me that it felt like an elementary school experience. Projects are terribly time consuming, but you can get away with only doing the first 3. Grading for tests were ambiguous.

Projects: A. Very hard and practically a part-time job but interesting.
Tests: D. Harsh grading with almost zero feedback given.
Helpfulness IRL: E. You can tell she really wants her students to learn.
Helpfulness online: B. Can be snarky on Piazza, does not take feedback well.
Lectures: D. Pretty much rehashes of the pre-lecture videos.
OVERALL: B
Worst class i've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'd say her class is pretty fair, as she's trying to teach a very difficult subject for many. She has pre lecture videos which I like, but her class time is ran like a kindergarten and is quite useless to be honest. Her projects are difficult, but doable so far just difficult to wrap your head around for the first few days. TAs are cool and helpful

Alison Norman's class was the worst experience during my time at UT. The way her class is structured, only led to a great amount of stress, but worst of all, her respect and attitude towards her students is utterly disrespectful. There is no teacher in this University that has degraded me in the way Alison Norman has.
Norman is not that bad. 40% percent of people get an A I recall, but the grading system is very unclear. Learned a lot too

She has pre-lecture videos before each class that were very helpful. Her grading system is very complicated and confusing, but I highly recommend spending time understanding it so you can cut corners (my group didn't do projects 3 and 4). OS isn't as hard as it's made out to be.

I think her pre-lecture videos were very helpful. Her grading scheme was a double-edged blade, which could be helpful at times and also discourage students greatly as well. While she is certainly knowledgeable and can transfer that knowledge well, she is snappy with students. I think it's possible to do well if you put in the effort. D on EADB.

Others here are far too harsh. Dr. Norman is a good teacher, but yes, the grading system is notoriously opaque and confusing. The prelecture videos were very helpful; study the slides + practice on previous exams that she posts and you should do pretty well on the exams. Pintos labs are time consuming so get ahead and use TAs + piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The main issue I had with the course was the lack of transparency. It was not clear what role ISPs played in the class until the first midterm, no feedback at all for exams (only a grade was provided), and grades on the final were never released. We were instructed not to compute grades as we would most likely calculate wrong.

By far the worst professor at UT. Impossible to earn a raw grade above a B. You'll spend 40 hours a week doing projects along with pre-lectures, problem sets, lectures, and tests. Partial credit is not a thing. Need to memorize basically everything. You'll be treated like a kid and waste 30min talking about how you are doing today every lecture.

Dr.Norman teaches very well, no one can argue about that. She is mean towards students, but students were rude so that cancels out. Projects were doable (given you work 40 hours), and exams are hard but curved at the end of the semester. TAs were the only reason I got an A in this class, so go to office hours. Just try your best and don't stress.

Poorly managed class with the grades released at the last minute or never released. Students are left in the dark on their grades. The professor is rude and condescending. Students are punished for what they don't know, rather than rewarded for what they do know.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear and informative, but the unclear grading system ensures that you will be worried and stressed out the entire semester.

In all honesty, the course material is not hard. BUT, the revolutionary new grading system makes the class infinitely harder. Your effort will never be truly rewarded so just take advantage of the rubric and do the least amount of work you can to get a B. An A is not worth it I promise. The TAs are angels though, make sure you go to office hours.

The best thing about this class is that Norman is good at teaching. Everything else is not good - the projects take too long, the exams are graded way to heavily, the overall time spent on this one class is just way to high.

The fact that this class is four credit hours is laughable. Between lectures, pre class lectures, and the discussion section, it's already at 9 hours. Then, throw on studying for the discussion sector every week, working on the week's problem set, and ofc the awfully outlined projects. Then studying for the poorly graded exams. For 4 credits...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like her, but her grading scheme is truly horrid. It leaves very little room for improvement and is graded by your worst grade as a measure of your understanding in class. For each project, I average out about 20 to 70 hours working on it (projects can be a week to 2 weeks long), but the exams take up more than 40% of your grade. Super stressful.

What a horrible class. The lectures are completely worthless, and even though the pre-lecture videos are decent, the grading system is absurd. They grade you on your worst answers and do not care at all if you do poorly. The grading scheme is truly the worst thing I've ever seen.

The quality of the class was heavily brought down by the unforgiving and confusing grading system. Pre-class videos made actually going to class useless, since discussion drags heavily and hardly anything is expanded upon. Group projects take insane time commitment, only for the tests to make up most of your grade. Dr. Norman can be unprofessional.

Long pre-lecture videos, and in-person lectures are mandatory yet not productive or helpful. The in-class time is not used efficiently at all: new material is rarely covered and discussion takes too long. The projects and course material are very interesting though. Projects take a lot of time commitment but are rewarding.

Grading guidelines are vague, long prelecture videos make in-person classes useless and both are mandatory to pass the class, group projects are full-time jobs. Class material is interesting but thats about it.

On an EADB scale (Exemplary, Accomplished, Developing, Beginning) as seen in class:

Grading Scale: B 
Lectures: A 
Approachability: B 
Exams: D
Workload: B
Professionalism: D
Projects: B

She takes the lowest grade received in all categories as your final grade, so in this case, I'd give her a B.. which translates to a D (on an ABCDF scale).

This teacher is so unprofessional. She responds to comments on the class forum with mean replies for students who are asking genuine, normal questions. Instead of actually teaching, she just gives us videos of her lecturing during COVID times and wastes our in-class time. This professor needs a second opinion on how she is running this class.
Dr. Norman is one of the most inconsiderate teachers that I've ever met. She needs to learn to connect with students.

This professor has the biggest misunderstanding of what education is and continually bombards students with unnecessary grading schemes, all while claiming that the grades, that de-incentivize students from trying after their from from bad grade, "check our learning." She wastes our time with pre-lecture videos instead of lecturing.

She's one of the worst professors I've ever had. Claims that our bad grade in the class is not because of her grading scheme but because we don't understand the material... yet lowest grade is what determines final grade, in addition to TAs being inconsistent graders.
I ain't even in this class but I hear its an L.

I've stopped doing everything that makes me happy in life so I can make time to finish the overwhelming and disrespectful amounts of work this class dumps on students. The teacher has set up the grading scale so we can fail the project and possibly the class even if we fail just 2 test cases. God help me now please.

A student in our class had trouble figuring what he did wrong on an exam question for resubmission. No comments, markings, and multiple TA's couldn't figure out what was wrong. So they have no idea what to correct for the resubmit. After asking about their options, Alison says "learn the material so you can judge what is right or wrong." Seriously?

This class is a complete joke. The professor doesn't care about the students and is actively praying on their downfall. For some reason she's changed the grading scheme so now you have to get an A in all categories to get an A in the class. The only reason I put I would take this class again is to see that satisfying piazza ratio one more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has an extremely difficult to understand grading criteria, then tells us to not try to calculate grades. Group projects are ridiculously difficult with little-to-no guidance on where to start. Exams are graded randomly by TAs who all have their own ideas on what is right or wrong. She got ratio'd by a student on Piazza.
Horrible grading scheme, doesn't care about students doing well. She said the class is "nor designed to encourage hard work". Idk how she is even allowed to teach here
Does not care if students learn or not! AND does not care if students do well in class!

LITERALLY WORST CLASS EVER. Detrimental to ur mental/physical health. Her and the TAs offer you as little help as possible so you can suffer through learning. The grading scale is designed to make you fail the class as much as possible. Highly unreasonable expectations and TAs are very substandard and are very weak in their mastery of the content.

The content of this course is hard, and the projects are hard. This is no fault of the professor, however, Professor Norman has made a hard course unnecessarily harder with the worst grading scale of all time. By having such a terrible grading scale, all it did was discourage learning and kill my passion for computer science. Avoid at all costs.

Because of the word limit, I'll keep things short. Pre-lecture lecturing system. 20 - 35 hours of coding per week. Horrible grading system. Ambiguous exam/quiz questions, but very specific rubric (hard to know what to do, easy to lose points). Exam questions are written over minute details. I don't expect hand-holding, but this class is just bad.

While the content of this class is great, the grading system truly ruins the learning experience. The class is essentially designed for you to get a C as you basically need everything right to get an A. Lectures are also not useful, learning is done in the pre-lecture videos. Projects are extremely time consuming, but they are certainly helpful.

Teaching system discourages learning. The teacher seems to actively want to lower your grade through unnecessarily specific grading criterias and arbitrary submission specifications (ex: hand written regrade submissions must not exceed to size of the space allocated on the exam or else the revision will be disqualified).
This class is a terrible class with a terrible grading system. Get ready to spend 3-4 hours a day working on the projects everyday.

Dr. Norman has been, hands-down, one of my favorite professors during my time at UT. From day one, it was clear that she cares about her students and wants to see us succeed. The grading scale is not my favorite, but I love the content, I love the way she presents it, and I've never had a class make me feel better, from her to the TAs.

TERRIBLE GRADING SCALE, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. This class has a very bad grading scale. Did I mention the grading scale is disgustingly unfair? TAs take about a month to give feedback on projects/assignments/quizzes. the TAs nor the Professor care about the students in the slightest. she successfully repels you from this subject

The course is poorly designed and focuses on penalizing students for the small details they do not know, rather than rewarding them for the information they do know.

Ex: each exam question is given the grade of the lowest sub-question. 

CS439 does not encourage learning nor excellence. Sadly, one mistake will ruin your grade in the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes and exam questions are based on a lettering system that represents your "level of understanding" of the material. However, simple mistakes on questions or providing answers not on the answer key will oftentimes knock you down from "Exemplary" to "Developing" (100% to 60%) which makes NO SENSE. Horrible lecturing system as well.

Dr. Norman is a decent teacher, but what's horrible is the grading scheme. It is super demanding to get an A in this class (they want you to be perfect on everything), and this class is designed for you to get a low grade. Group projects are very time consuming, but they are certainly helpful and can even be fun. The TAs are also helpful.

One of the worst professors at UT, not because of her teaching, but because of her grading system. The grading system is designed to make you fail. Also, lectures are pretty much useless as all the learning is done in pre-lecture videos (can take 1-2 hours). Projects are difficult and very time consuming, expect about 30-40 hours per week.

This class is the evilest class I've ever taken. She clearly has no idea how to teach or manage a course. You are not going to get a good grade in this class and she will offer little help. Good luck :)

Tests/consistent studying matter more than anything. Projects matter but dw if you miss points later on (not worth the stress). Grading system initially demanding but helps some ppl later in the class. Class is difficult but more doable than I originally thought & lectures were interesting. OS is an intense class but in retrospect was fun and fresh

If I could rate any lower, I would. The group projects are unnecessarily time-consuming and quite literally take a consistent daily effort of 4-5 hours. The tests always nitpick on the smallest detail mentioned on the slides. Dr. Norman is a nice person but that doesn't help the fact that her class is literally a full-time job. PintOS is just a no.

The new grading system makes sure that you are determined by your lowest category if you dont meet all the requirements then you automatically can't get your desired grade even if by 1 category. On exams there are multiple sections per question and your grade for that section is also the lowest (not the average).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Part of the experimental class for her new grading system. New system was never how much you knew the material but instead how lucky you got with the TA and her extremely specific rubric for very broad questions. Feedback on important assignments was incredibly delayed and synchronous class was a waste of time.

The new grading scale for this class is not worth. Although she gives regrades on tests, you end up still getting bad scores even if you put down an answer that someone else did well on. She changed our final exam grading scale to be even harsher. Time spent on projects doesn't mean anything because tests are weighted so heavily.

Projects are a bit hard but doable - Tests were the weird situation for this class- other comments mention more. The grading system would (unnecessarily) result in stress as your lowest category was your grade. Lectures can be bland as they are mostly her reading slides. Gheith may be more challenging, but you seem to learn more and feel better.

The new grading system (EADB) is needlessly confusing. Grading is extremely strict (ex. automatically incorrect if over word count). You will spend 20-30 hours every week outside of class working on group projects. Lectures are wasted; all learning is done from pre-lecture videos before class. I took a weekend off to go to ACL. Don't do that.

Overall, Alison was a good professor. The Pintos projects (especially the last 2) are ridiculously hard and time-consuming. Pick good partners!! Her exams were kind of rough as well. Exam 2 had a failing class average and basically only about 15 people passed it. She does curve your final grade quite a bit, though, so just put in good effort!

Probably the most difficult/stress-inducing class i've ever taken. The amount of content covered in the class is insane, with really hard projects and abstract tests. Just do your best and go to office hours for help on projects.

You will learn a ton of information in this class. It's definitely the most time-consuming class I've ever taken, but it'll all be worth it. Projects are PintOS and are graded: 50% test case, 50% design document. You will lose points on the Design Document. Tests online were abstract/application basedMight be more memorization of slides in person.

Dr. Norman smiles at you while you nearly drown in PintOS. Grading is much tougher than 314/429 by design (you are destined to lose points). Learned a lot, carried by god TAs who can point out hard bugs (until filesys). Open-note online, but I imagine offline tests will require very annoying memorization (but she takes points off for regurgitation)

Boring lecturer. She reads straight from the slides with little detail. Lecture slides help very little with PintOS. At one point, the exam conflicted with the program project and we were forced to focus on one or the other ( both important mind you). Bottom line, take Gheith. He is less linear and really works to expand your knowledge on subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: OS really isn't as bad as everyone says it is. Probably the most difficult thing about the class is the group projects/Pintos, which can be pretty time consuming. Norman is a really caring professor but her lectures can be somewhat unclear. Her tests also are pretty vague but it's balanced out by extra credit/somewhat lenient grading.

Honestly? I know I'm so insane for saying this but- I would retake this class in a hearbeat. I'm an average coder and not the quickest in the class but this course taught me so much and developed me so much as a computer scientist, I don't know what to say. Obv alot of work but man do you learn so much. Don't dread this class. It's a gift. Really.

OS is not as bad as ppl say- unless u take algo or 17+ hrs at the same time. For 2020 online fall class, exams were open notes- open internet. It's a little easier for exams bc of that but projects are still grueling and takes 20+ hours a week Mandatory teamed projects. Exam answers are graded pretty strictly Pintos  pain Learned a lot though!

OS is insane, no way around it. Norman herself is incredibly caring and puts a lot of effort into making OS a community, which is nice. Start ASAP on PintOS projects, read the documentation, and don't slack off on the design docs cause they can be nitpicky. OS is a dreadful amount of work but Norman is a gem and makes it interesting

There's a reason everyone is afraid of OS, and Dr. Norman tries her best to make her students feel more comfortable. The group projects are extremely, extremely time consuming but the tests weigh more and they're all about memorization. Class rigor is infamous and rightly so, but you do learn quite a lot. Be ready to suffer but also to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Norman is a very nice person; in fact, her entire staff of TAs is amazing. She has adapted to online teaching well. The project specifications can be a bit dense and hard to read, but there is always help. It's amazing how such a nice person can be resp. for so much suffering, but that's just because OS is a diff. class.

OS lives up to the horror stories, but it's a fantastic class and one of the most invaluable I've taken in UTCS. Alison pulls no punches with class rigor, but she truly cares about each of her students and their learning; she's willing to help and explain concepts should you go to her for it. The group projects are really hard, but you learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Focused on memorization over actual learning. She and her TAs are ruthless and will take points off for solutions pass everything but fail some arbitrary race condition that we were never warned against. I would honestly wait a semester and take Professor Gheith instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's the meanest person if you aren't showing interest. Sometimes has a puny sense of humor. She will support you if you try. There's rumors that everybody that doesn't cheat passes the course. Believe it and try your best in the exams. Leave the rest to god. It is difficult but if you trust her and yourself you will be fine.

I don't understand the positive reviews left here. She's not good at teaching, and she emphasizes memorization over true understanding. Pintos is designed to save the instructors time. It's not designed to teach you how kernels and operating systems work from the ground up. I lost points for being "too close to slides" on an open note test.
Really Hard Class.

The best professor I've had in my time at UT. She takes an active role in your learning, leaving lots of time for questions at the beginning of class. Tests require detailed answers and projects are incredibly time consuming. At the end of the class however, I had a much better understanding of Operating System concepts. Enjoyed thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Essentially you have 6 hours of class a week, 30 hours of coding a week for Pintos, and tests that are extremely difficult. Only acceptable because it is a one-time thing, but the experience is absolutely awful and although Norman is kind and cares about your performance she makes the class, in my opinion, much more difficult than it should be.

The worst class I've ever taken. She never started lecture on time and always went way over, making me have to run to my next class. The projects were a full time job and the exams were a ton of memorization, which I didn't have time for due to the projects. Everything was hard. Take a different prof if possible.

Exams are essentially powerpoint regurgitation and projects are harshly graded. The first 10 minutes of every lecture is wasted since she doesn't start on time and she spends unnecessarily long reviewing and pausing to see if anyone has questions. She definitely cares about you, but the class itself is frustrating.

She's very good about answering all your questions and taking time to make sure you understand the content well. If she doesn't know how to answer your question, she'll say "I don't know" which is appreciated. She really cares about her students! She's a good professor to take for CS439

Its a pretty bad class. The project is in PintOS, which is hard but that is a given for any systems classes. Professor's tests are completely memorization, and can lose points for the smallest details. Cares more about if you are cheating than the material, and it is not rare to get falsely accused. If you are, you are better off taking the fall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This course is generally viewed as the hardest CS course that required for the degree. Dr. Norman gives clear lectures and the majority of exam questions are from her powerpoints. Projects are super time consuming and they are not really related to what she teaches in class, so you have to figure it out by yourself.

People keep saying that Norman has favorites, but this is so far from the truth. I've noticed that students who do poorly on tests generally attribute this to her "not liking them". Her grading scheme is very arbitrary on tests but it is still fair since it is applied to everyone. Overall solid professor with a difficult but rewarding class.

Norman either likes you or she doesn't, and it's easy to tell what side you're on. Her exams are straight memorization, though she claims otherwise. Lectures are dreadful if you have a short attention span. You could just read the slides and be ok, but there's a clicker every lecture. Pintos is hard, but she/TAs make effort to help if you ask!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Norman adds an emotional dimension to the course material that you would not find from other professors - both from her lectures and from the suffering in the infamous Pintos projects. Watch out for Project 3 - many groups take between 60 to 100 logged programming hours to complete it! If you like working alone, consider taking Gheith.

Dr. Norman is a good lecturer. She is very passionate about what she does. The class itself is very time consuming, but you do learn a lot. The tests, even though she insists are not about memorization, involve a lot of buzzwords that you need to hit to get credit, so memorizing will serve you well, even if you understand the material already.
Exams are somewhat arbitrary and mostly PowerPoint slide regurgitation, though she insists otherwise. Projects are time consuming. Make sure to choose a solid group.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: By far the most difficult class I've ever taken. Everything your hear about 439 is true and not exaggerated. You'll spend dozens of hours in the lab almost every week, but the material you're learning is important. She grades harsh, but if you're actually making a strong effort you'll pass. Overall a great professor.

Its the class youve been afraid of. Norman is an AMAZING professor though and this has been my favorite (and hardest) class. As are possible if you actually do the readings, take good notes, and select a good team for the projects. Take easy gen eds with it. Dont cheat or google for past projects - shell find out and you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's tough but fair.  Don't skip class, pariticipate, do your work, ask questions, seek help.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is VERY time consuming.  The exams are hard, class average for the first exam was in the 60s.  Everyone knows this class is hard but she curves at the end and homework and attendance boosts your grade. She is the most experienced 439 professor and does everything possible to help students succeed, take her but get ready to work

This class is /hard/. Definitely. But Norman has a lot of experience teaching it, cares deeply about her students, and has structured the class to allow for a ton of help for students. The projects are long and difficult, but the lectures and tests are very closely connected- study the notes and you'll do well on the test. Projects are groups 2-4.

Dr. Norman is an excellent lecturer, but the class is difficult. Projects are very long and feedback on the projects is extremely slow (like 1.5 months slow). The content is also difficult. The class is doable, but get ready to work.

Norman is super nice and a great lecturer. She always asks if anyone has any questions at every opportunity. The reason the class is so difficult is 1) There is A LOT of material you have to know 2) The projects are LONG. 40 hours a week long. My only critique is her tests are garbage. Reviewing past tests is A MUST to understand grading criteria.

The projects are difficult, but manageable, and there are almost daily lab hours with the TAs to help with. The test were somewhat hard, but she gave a reasonable curve at the end. The projects were meaningful and the class was very informative. In short, yes the class is hard but you'll learn at lot and be a better coder because of it.

Ok yes. The projects are hard. She knows they are hard. However, classes like these are the ones that truly make you a better programmer. And I have to say that the tests were relatively easy and are most of your grade. So just try your best on the projects, and don't fret. Dr. Norman is very helpful, respectful, and self-aware of her class.

Just another typical UT CS professor. She cares more about whether her students are cheating or not then if they are understanding the material. Projects are hard, but not impossible if you give up on all of your social life. Test are easier than projects, but a lot of people don't study much because of the extremely long projects. Just work hard.

She cannot help much with the projects.  Tests are overly hard, made a day or so before giving them.  No clear grading rubric.  Homework is not checked, maybe waiting over a month for project grades, and you will go into tests not really knowing where you stand if you really grasp the concept.  Professor covers way too much information between test

Alison's lectures using PowerPoint.  She is good at lecturing and you always leave learning something.  Her exams were rough but she does curve the class when the grades are bad.  The projects for the class are very demanding but you will learn a lot after doing them.  Her office hours are helpful.

Nicole was a great professor, very insightful. Good lectures, the readings are pretty long though. Should be said, there is a no electronic policy in class, but honestly it made me pay more attention.

Prof Smith is nice but spends a lot of lectures rambling off-topic instead of better explaining some complex concepts. They are a very easy grader if you get everything done and put in a little effort. No electronics unless you have accommodations, they went on multiple rants about this because people would do it anyway. Pretty simple intro class

This class is pretty easy. Grades come from mostly in class assignments so there isn't much work outside of class except readings. Attendance is required but she isn't super strict but doesn't like when your on your phone in class.

Dr. Smith was a really enjoyable professor. Her course was not graded by many assignments, which felt pretty intimidating, but overall, she was pretty forgiving with grades. She lectured each class and was great at separating personal beliefs from the content. Overall, you get what you put into it, so if you do the readings, it's worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing at explaining such hard concepts. Very passionate about teaching each subject matter, which helps. Does not offer their own perspective of each philosophical concept and allows us to make our own determination and defend our perspectives. Dr. Smith offers a safe environment to learn and grow.

Dr. Smith is the best professor I have had the pleasure of learning from. They are really good at explaining complex concepts more simply and covering all of the ethical considerations of a concept. I am so glad I took PHL 304 as my first philosophy course because it set me up really well for my other ethics courses. Best. Professor. Ever.

Look at the end of the day this teacher is relatively chill. The problem is the attendance policy - she gets mad if you are on your laptops because she hates electronics for some reason and then will say to the class "you are free to leave" but the problem is grades your attendance AT THE END OF CLASS so you can not REALLY leave.

Class itself was quite boring with her turning a lot of things quite political on either side. TA small group was the highlight of the class though. Easy class overall, but definitely not my favorite. You'll get an A, but it won't be that fun imo.

great professor interesting lectures although it is a bit harder to get an A in their class (95 and above) my TA was a little weird but ultimately great class and made you think a lot about different perspectives and moral philosophies. just be prepped for the two writing assignments and your good. very little assignments so keep that in mind.

Great professor for an introductory philosophy course. While the content was very easy to politicize, Prof Smith (though obviously trying greatly not to incorporate her own political views) approached it in a neutral way that allowed for students with opposing views to communicate and succeed. Certainly recommend if looking to get into philosophy.

not the best lecturer she doesn't really know how to explain her thoughts. honestly didn't learn much as it was not engaging she's really nice and accommodating not a big course load at all but I was not interested with her teaching style
Doesn't allow laptops in class, but otherwise is super chill. Got back to emails quickly and was a pretty fair and easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: slow paced and not very engaging lectures. easy to get a good grade but I didnt gain much from the class. my small group was fun but I know the other TA was frustrating for people.

A caring prof but is lowkey carried by her course topic. The topics are very  
current making engagement easy and natural however her lectures are very cyclical. She more often than not sounds like she is struggling to express what she is trying to say and doesn't word her writing coherently. I did however love both my discussion section and my TA.

Nicole is caring. Her lectures are not as bad as others say here, and her PowerPoints are awesome. Essays were graded a bit tough by the TA. So don't blow this class off. In my class, unit 1 over animal rights was good enlightening material, but unit 2 was a whole waste of time imo. Nicole is left wing, which can make sharing opposing ideas hard.

I think it's safe to say Professor Smith puts very low effort into class formulation, with everything seeming to occur last minute. The class itself is easy, but the lectures are so incredibly boring even as a philosophy major. I would just avoid classes with her altogether.

Smith was a caring professor. I sometimes struggled to stay engaged because it is a relatively slow-paced class, but to do well on the essays, try to take good notes and do the reading if you want the A. As long as you keep up, the rest of the course is extremely manageable. I would definitely recommend this for a low workload ethics flag.

I took two courses with Dr.Smith and just registered to take another course with them. There are assigned readings but she will go over all of them in class. Your grades are determined by a couple in in-class quizzes (very simple) and in-class essays. Overall, an amazing professor.
Great class. Professor was very caring and tried her best to help. Had in class responses that were graded for attendance credit. Sometimes lectures dragged on a little later than needed or expected.

Dr. Smith was very nice and explained the class through lecture and discussion primarily. The class is low-pressure, but you still learn; I especially found the video about primates eating rotting meat interesting (you'll understand later). Grades are mostly participation, make sure to show up to lecture and discussion and to learn teminolgies.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is one of my favorites in the entire philosophy department. They are very understanding to extenuating circumstances and super supportive. Their lectures are interactive and relatively easy to follow given some of the complex material. They are able to explain concepts in a relevant way and apply them to day-to-day life.

Extremely helpful and understanding professor. Readings were "assigned" every week but were covered during lectures. In-class essays were structured as short answer questions in order to take the stress away. Quizzes could be taken multiple times and were reviewed in class. Grades were arranged so that it was impossible to not get a good grade.

My first philosophy class and absolutely amazing experience for anyone curious about philosophy. Two readings a week but not heavy, also not mandatory since they cover them in slides. Super manageable class and completely changed my view on race and gender. Always making sure they bring in different students' perspectives on the topic. Take them!

She was great! As long as you show up to class or watch the recorded lectures you will learn all you need to to get a good grade. It was also a very eye opening experience and taught me new ways to look at social problems and how we can solve them.

Nicole is a great professor. Material was interesting/thought-provoking, and though you could tell Nicole had certain opinions on topics, they never dismissed other people's thoughts and opinions. The readings weren't that necessary b/c Nicole's lectures covered everything, and I feel like I was adequately prepared for the 2 tests and 3 quizzes.

I really liked Nicole's lecture style. She brought to light many interesting topics that I had never even considered and I felt that the lectures were engaging and thorough. Her TA gave me a near failing exam grade but Nicole allowed me to defend my writing in office hours and remedied the situation in a way that was just and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was a pretty low-stress class. The professor was always very kind and had a lot of passion for the topics she'd teach us. Essays were very straightforward and weren't harshly graded at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nicole is a great professor who discusses a variety of well selected topics. The readings compliment the course and Nicole breaks them down. In-class participation quizzes, two in-class essays, with some discussion posts towards end of semester. I only wish there were more assignments to help prep for essays/have more weighted grade opportunities.

CMP was an easy class, you don't have to do the readings because she explains the concepts in lecture well enough. Her lectures may get a little boring but maybe bc they were online. She is really caring and professional, she will consider your opinion if it differs from hers. All the grades come from in-class assignments. Cant recommend it enough.

Professor Smith is a facet to the UT philosophy department. Teaching philosophy is sometimes difficult because of the trickiness of translating one's expertise to students. Nicole does this flawlessly with a humble, clear approach. Philosophy professors are known to ramble, and this is not the characterization I'd make of her. She encourages studen

Pretty easy class, grades were made up of essays, attendance, quizzes, and essay-tests. Didn't read anything that was assigned, because the TA went over it so in depth in discussion sections. Did not enjoy the lecture style, Nicole rarely spoke about important topics that we were covering or read about, went on many awkward tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Everyone on here who complained about Nicole's lecture style missed exactly what makes her a phenomenal professor. Philosophy professors can typically come off as condescending, but Nicole is the complete opposite. There is a lot of intention with how she responds to students (timidity). She regards peoples' beliefs SO charitably. Take this prof!

Nice and caring professor who loves talking about philosophy. She assigns really interest readings for environmental ethics. You get a few papers throughout the semester but they're straightforward and one of them gets dropped at the end. Attendance taken for a grade. Two in class essay exams neither are comprehensive and she prepares you for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I rated "level of difficulty" in her class a "4" b/c one of the TA's was brutal. Other than that, this was a solid course & I learned some interesting stuff & Nicole is a definite asset to UT faculty, imo. We need more professors like her! A+

Professor Smith was just alright for me. The information itself was incredibly interesting, and we focused on a lot social issues that I think are important. I found myself counting down the minutes until her lectures were over; she's a very monotone speaker, and she almost comes across as though she's unsure of what she's saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, Nicole is kind, caring, knowledgable, and clearly passionate. She grades fairly and is especially approachable and a joy to talk to! She clearly cares about students and their learning, for example, she doesn't require textbooks (in my experience) in order to keep the courses affordable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was really interesting and I definitely recommend it! Workload wasn't bad, exams (in class essays) were pretty simple, grading was fair, and there was sort of a lot of reading but it was all pretty fun to read in my opinion. Nicole is very sweet and funny and I loved hearing her talk about all of the topics we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Smith loves her craft, and does an excellent job of presenting it to her students.

If you want a caring professor with strong morals and a true passion for learning then I highly recommend Nicole. She is so kind and easy to talk to while remaining extremely professional. Her focus on inclusivity seems to ensure that all students feel welcome and comfortable. As long as you read and go to class you should be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith did a great job of presenting confusing material. I felt like I was totally lost the first half of the class but made a high A on the midterm. After the midterm the foundation she laid paid off for the issues we discussed in the second half. Go to class, take good notes, read and visit her in office hours (even just once).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At first I thought we were going to focus on social justice in health issues, but these topics didn't come until much later. The course moves very fast with a lot of readings that for the most part are skippable, but be sure to focus on the readings assigned for short assignments because they show up on the test. Show up for SquareCap and record.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: At first I thought she was a 20 something-year-old straight out of college but apparently, she's in her 40's which really shocked me. It's a challenging class but if you ask her enough questions and pay attention, you should do just fine. Every week there's one-page essays over reading. There's 2 in class essays over the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Smith did a decent job of teaching the material needed to succeed on exams and homework assignments. The weekly assignments seem daunting at first, but they are really manageable if you skim the textbook and look at the lecture slides online. Absences add up fast, but as long as you're mindful of that, the class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Smtih was fantastic. She is extremely knowledgeable and kept the lectures interesting even when the material was dull. No tests, just two in-class essays and no final. If you show up, do the reading, and keep track of the assignments, the course is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Smith enjoyed talking about the philosophy material we covered during lecture, but included too many personal issues in her tangents. I was often confused if the material was relevant to the philosopher we were discussing or not. Approachable, but will not answer you if you have questions on grades. I don't recommend this course.

The class was okay, but I would not take Dr. Smith again. She was a dull lecturer and offered no information that couldn't be found in the textbook. Often during lectures it felt like she went off on tangents, so eventually I stopped bothering to take notes and just showed up for the attendance grade. Read the book and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith, while intellectual, is not a phenomenal lecturer; she knows the basics of her information, but she comes across as incredibly timid - almost as if she is afraid of speaking. Really great class though - fosters debate and individual thinking. Tests/essays are graded fairly, and it is an easy yet interesting A if you show up. Take her.

Health and Justice is a new class and therefore there were some kinks to be worked out, but the topics are interesting, tough, and relevant. The professor became more personable as the semester went on, and office hours helped with that even more. Very good about listening to and welcoming all perspectives. Reading, writing, and discussion heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith's Contemporary Moral Problems class is one of the best classes I've ever taken. Incredibly interesting lectures, and the tests are not difficult at all if you pay attention and take notes in class. Dr. Smith is super nice and cares about her students as well. Would recommend this class to anyone!
I don't usually write reviews, but Hall really knows how to abstract really complex ideas to be digestible. This class is very effort = reward, no tricks. Plus Hall is just fun to listen to.

Homeworks were completion grades, but grading on test was extremely harsh, taking off many points even for just simple arithmetic errors. The cutoffs for letter grades were adjusted to account for this, but it's not super clear what cutoffs were used in the end. Lectures and notes are also not that clear, would recommend just reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is a very nice professor, but his lectures were disorganized. He also relied heavily on the TA, who did not seem to care much about this class. His exams are also graded quite harshly, but they are much easier compared to other professors. He also sometimes did not cover some homework topics in class until the last day which was not fun.

Overall, glad I took 313 with him, but lectures felt disengaging, so I started to skip and learn on my own. Homeworks are p hard, and sometimes he doesn't cover  concepts you need to know for the hws until the day it's due. Exams weren't bad and quizzes were p easy. My raw score was my final grade, so I don't think he curves at the end

Great person and lectures, but exams are graded very harshly. A simple arithmetic mistake changes a score by often times more than 10 points. Problems can feel a little vague but make sure to master the HW. If you can consistently make no errors when solving problems, you'll be safe from the ridiculous partial credit rubric used on exams.

Dr. Hall explained the concepts clearly during lectures and walked through examples well, and he clearly cared about our learning. The homework did take some time, but it was super useful for preparing for exams. Exams were based on our homework, and I felt that the problems were fair and not super challenging. Overall, I really enjoyed his course.

This semester (F24) is Professor Hall's first time teaching emag, and given the circumstances, I think he did a pretty good job. Lectures are incredibly dense, but Hall does a good job at making it as easily understood as possible. Only gripe is there are at times few examples to work off of, but this is usually fixed by office hours.

Professor Hall has to be one of the best ECE professors at UT.  313 is a tough class but I can confidently say that the work you put into the class perfectly translates to the grade you get. Homeworks are crucial since he uses homework-like questions on the exams, so go to OH for a better understanding of the concepts. Overall great class!

Dr. Hall is the professor you want to have for a course like this. His lectures are worth their weight in gold, they take the dense book chapters and dumb them down. 
Exam grading emphasizes precision. Go to OH to do the homework. Get good with complex numbers, transform tables, and conceptual understanding of applications (sampling, filters).

One of the best professors out there. I initially had no interest in this kind of course but Hall does great at explaining concepts and providing a lot of examples. His hw grading isn't tough and his tests are very similar to the hw. He cares a lot about understanding the material and gives extensions or drops hw questions to give more time

A class that I did not enjoy, as it is reflected in my grade. But Professor Hall is a very lovely professor and easily explains the concepts. He always stops for questions and is not afraid to get a little challenging and testy with the students. Homework isn't that difficult. Lectures and textbooks are critical to the class. Exams are a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best engineering professor I have had so far. He does a very good job explaining the material and is also a cool person. He makes sure you will be very prepared for the exams and doesnt throw any trick questions out. Very good experience in this class.

Very personable, clear, articulate prof. Homework plenty but helpful for exams which make up most of your grade. Good jokes and stories, respected and experienced dude. I enjoyed hearing about his research on acoustics. Go to OFFICE HOURS for homework help.
Great guy. Always made things interesting even when we got into more difficult material
Awesome professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really entertaining and cares a lot about students and the class. It is a really hard class, but he tries really hard and is super helpful in OH. The class starts easy and then gets really hard, so he gives cheat sheets and makes first test super easy. He does his best to have every student pass. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He wasn't very organized with the overall course structure - the syllabus wasn't available until the 3rd week and the tests dates were announced two weeks before each test. I really liked how he put all his class notes online afterwards. He is a great lecturer if you ignore his random metaphors, tho. 2nd test was twice as hard as first test.

One of the better EE professors in the department. Very clear and covers all the information without going too much into proofs. First class I've taken in a while where going to class REALLY does help, because he does cover all the material that will show up on homework/tests. Would definitely recommend him for future classes.

He is nice and means well but his teaching style is so ineffective. You end up having to teach yourself everything because he just lectures on and on about theory and doesn't do actual problems during class that reflect what's on the actual exam. This makes lectures annoying and a waste of time. He has a cool Australian accent tho

He is a really good professor who knows what he's teaching. Lecture and content heavy class - so make sure you attend + take good notes. Exam heavy, but as long as you do the practice exams and problems, you should be fine. Attend his OH for the problem sets for help - they're difficult. Overall chill guy.
Solid prof. Study the practice exams and you'll be fine.

His lectures are very boring, and it becomes your job to sit through it and filter what is actually important. Spoiler alert: it's not very much. This guy will spend 90% of the time deriving things that don't matter and aren't tested and maybe 10% of the time talking about how things are actually used to answer questions. Good luck yall

Woodhams has the unique ability of turning a simple and intuitive concept into something utterly unintelligible. He loves to teach by using variables and keeping things "theoretical" instead of just using real numbers or examples to explain things like a regular human being. If you enjoy vague math concepts, he's the guy. If not, stay away from him
Although this class was hard content wise, he broke down content that was easy to understand! The problem sets and exams were graded very fairly as well. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is extremely disorganized and so difficult, and Professor Woodhams just expects students to understand the calculus that he does even though he skips multiple steps at a time. When I would go to office hours he would act like I was stupid for asking a question. Would not recommend this professor at all.

I like him, but I hate the FIN321k course and how it is taught. He is a nice person and definitely super smart, but I am unsure why this is even a required course for the MPA program. The practice sets aren't too bad; everyone did about the same on the midterm, and the final is cumulative, so we will see how it turns out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never responds to students. Terribly difficult class and he tends to go through the lecture way too quickly.

Despite FIN 321K being really tough, Prof. Snashall-Woodhams is great. His lectures are very clear and he provides so much additional practice. He never responds to e-mails and the class is terribly disorganized, though. Problem sets are graded tough months late and he doesn't tell you what you did wrong or give you solutions. I'd still recommend.

I had Nik for CMS 367 and it was purely a class I'd go to to talk. Discussions on readings, personal experiences, etc. You just needed to talk at least once a week for credit. He's pretty chill if your open minded and participate you'll do fine.

Idk what the reviews here are on about, they're one of the best professors I've ever had. They made Quantitative Research Methods fun. The class is based mostly on lectures that feel like casual conversations. Assignments are short with very clear directions. There is plenty of opportunities for extra credit on their exams. Nik is SO chill

Honestly they were really chill and this class changed my perspective on how arbitrary gender is. They say there's required readings but I feel that they're not really required. This class is definitely not a lecture and is entirely discussion based. One paper and one presentation about whatever you want, no exams. Can get kind of boring at times.

unorganized class. expects us to write a research paper on research he conducted years ago and doesn't know how to perform the research. counts students absent when they're 5 minutes late when attendance is mandatory/for a grade. expects students to get notes from other students since lectures are not posted. mumbles a lot and goes on tangents.
class isn't very organized and not very accommodating if you are sick because the slides wont be posted. overall the class isn't hard at all but it isn't enjoyable.

Dr. Oldham is so kind and sweet, and she's incredibly skilled at what she does. This class seems like a standard LAH requirement, but it can actually be really helpful if you use the resources provided. If I could go back, I'd attend the career events earlier in the semester instead of putting them off. Overall, such an easy and useful class.
Easiest seminar ever, and she's so sweet. There has to be something genuinely wrong for you to get less than an A in this class.

Tatem is such a genuine and caring person. She's also one of the best possible connections to have on campus, and will connect you to so many resources if you make the effort to meet with her. The class is super light; just submit your assignments on time and make sure to attend events to reflect on for your final reflection paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was ridiculously easy. There were quite literally one to two assignments due every month. As long as you don't forget to attend three events throughout the semester to write your final reflection paper and turn in your work on time, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Reyes seems nice, but struggles with expert bias and explains concepts poorly, making lectures hard to follow. The class is quiz and test-heavy with little review material, and the few questions make it easy to get low grades. There's also little communication with TAs, so support feels limited. I'd avoid if possible.

Lectures are all over the place and there is little effort into them, Nicky is clearly passionate about math but it doesn't translate well in a teaching environment. To make matters even worse there is close to zero resources for self instruction outside of class, which would be okay if the lectures were great but they are abysmal. 0/10 course.

Had some of the best reviews for a calc prof but his switch from online exams to in person broke this class. Quizzes are two questions completely free response and weighted almost identically to the midterms. They are super difficult and they are NOT curved. I finished 408C with a 98 and am struggling to do well on his quizzes.
Quizzes are nasty, and the TAs in discussion don't teach properly, so it's harder to succeed on the quizzes. Quizzes are now like 20% of our grade, comparable to midterms. Midterms are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
