reviews.comment: Great guy, even better lecturer! If I could give anyone advice about this class it would be to really study for the final as it took me by complete surprise and ruined my A. Otherwise, the midterms and HW are very straightforward and honestly you prob can get by just reading the textbook imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not bad, just do the homework and your gonna be fine. tests are really easy

The professor described the quiz on proofs of reductions as “easy,” many students who don't work with this material found it quite challenging. The topic was not clearly explained during the TA discussion, which made the quiz harder to prepare. I would not be surprised if the scores were curved. lectures are sporadic and are not clear.
He is genuinely the most sporadic lecturer I have ever had. Goes WAY to fast. Would not recommend.

I understand calculus 2 to be hard, but reyes provides little to no support whatsoever. Lectures are hard to read, discussion sections are even harder to read. Stuff talked in class is really hard to follow.

Overall, this course feels disorganized and unsupportive. The combination of weak lectures, ineffective discussion sections, and heavily weighted quizzes makes it far more stressful than it needs to be.

The structure of this course has declined significantly compared to previous semesters. The shift to in-person exams combined with very challenging quizzes has made the class much harder, but the quality of instruction has not improved to match those changes.

TA discussion sections do not provide much help. They are disorganized and often fail to review or reinforce key material. Instead of clarifying difficult topics, they frequently leave students more confused and uncertain about expectations.

This class feels poorly designed and unnecessarily stressful. Quizzes make up 28% of the final grade, yet there is very little transparency or preparation for them. The quizzes are extremely difficult and often cover material in ways that are not clearly explained in lecture. Many students still feel unprepared.

Between the sudden shift to in-person exams, poorly aligned lectures, ineffective discussion sections, and high-stakes quizzes, the course feels unnecessarily stressful and poorly coordinated. Overall, this class is not well designed to support student learning, and I would not recommend it.

The TA discussion sections do not help compensate for this. They are poorly organized and often unproductive, with little meaningful review of relevant material. Instead of clarifying difficult concepts, these sections frequently add confusion and do not reflect what is actually tested.

Lecture quality has declined significantly. Explanations are rushed, examples are limited, and there is a noticeable disconnect between what is taught in class and what appears on quizzes and exams. Studying often feels like guesswork rather than a structured process.

This course has been extremely frustrating from start to finish. One of the biggest issues is the heavy reliance on quizzes, which make up 28% of the final grade. These quizzes are very difficult and often test material in ways that are not clearly covered in lecture. There is little guidance on what to expect.

With major grading weight placed on quizzes and exams, the lack of clear instruction becomes even more problematic. Overall, this course feels poorly structured and much less student-friendly than it was previously.

The lectures themselves are disorganized and rushed. Important concepts are skimmed over, while examples rarely match what appears on homework or exams. This disconnect makes studying inefficient and frustrating.

This semester felt like a step backward in almost every way. Last semester, exams were online and the course structure made sense around that format. This time, exams were moved to in-person, but lectures and course organization did not adapt accordingly. The result was a class that felt much harder

The lack of alignment across lectures, assignments, quizzes, and exams makes studying unnecessarily difficult. You're left guessing what content will actually be emphasized, which adds stress rather than reinforcing learning.

Lecture quality has also dropped noticeably. Explanations are rushed and often unclear, and many examples covered in class do not reflect what appears on homework or exams. It frequently feels like you're attending lecture just to keep up, not to actually understand the material.

This class feels completely inconsistent compared to last semester. Previously, exams were online and the course structure reflected that format. This semester, exams were suddenly moved to fully in-person, which felt like a major shift without adequate adjustment in teaching or preparation. Expectations changed, but the support did not.

Lectures themselves feel rushed and disorganized. Topics jump around without clear structure, and it's easy to leave class unsure of what the main points were or how they connect to what you're expected to know. This has made understanding the material far harder than it should be.

I had high hopes for this class, but overall it was one of the most frustrating academic experiences I've had. The transition from online to fully in-person came halfway through the year with no clear explanation or advance warning. That change made planning around other classes and responsibilities much more difficult.

The lectures have steadily become less effective over time. Concepts are often presented quickly and without sufficient explanation, and the material covered in class does not consistently reflect the homework or exams. This lack of coordination makes it hard to know what to focus on and significantly impacts learning.

Worse still, he made quizzes worth 28% of the grade, and there are four of them. That's ridiculous for a math course where lecture explanations are already falling flat. The increase in weight makes quizzes borderline make-or-break, and it feels arbitrary rather than tied to meaningful learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm honestly disappointed with how this class has been run this semester. Reyes used to be a decent instructor, but the course has taken a nosedive — and it's clear from how things are structured now that student learning is no longer a priority.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Reyes used to be good, but now he has been reduced to really not-so-great lectures, insane quizzes, and I am waiting to see how the tests are.

Exams are no longer online, which I am fine with, but come on, he now makes quizzes worth 28%, and you take 4. What is this?

Reyes style of teaching, syllabus, and just general vibes from him have changed. Maybe something having to do with new math department guidelines as he mentioned on our first day. The main issues are homework not correlating to lectures, discussions being overly hard, and just in general no synchronization between the many parts of the course.

The UT math department has become very weird. Reyes completely changed his teaching approach, often resulting in very poor lectures and low-quality discussion sections. Unfortunate for a 'university of the first class'
Reyes is the chosen one, do practice problems and you'll get an A. That's literally it.

He's a very approachable person and I liked his class a lot; he had a lot of cool insights and clearly understands what he's talking about. The homeworks were always applicable to what he lectured about and were honestly super helpful, and he was very straightforward about what you need to know on tests.

He is what many people would describe as the typical math professor. He is a very nice person in general as well and allows students to call him "Nicky" (not a professor who will get mad for not calling them "Dr."). There is a homework that was due every Wednesday for my TTH section that had around 13-25 questions. Exams are not too challenging.
Awesome professor! Nice grading system and interesting lectures, would definitely recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was probably one of the best calculus classes I have ever taken. The online tests are similar to the quest hw. the in class tests are discussion problems. just pay attention and its a guaranteed A.

3 exams - lowest dropped; mandatory final but all exams are take-home, from the homework, and you have ample time to complete them. Dr.Reyes is clearly very knowledgeable and it was very interesting to hear his lectures, however attendance isn't necessary and all information can be obtained through some YouTube videos. An A is an 89. Take for an A!

This class was super easy and everything was online except for a small portion of the tests, but he would show you how to do the problems in discussion the week before. Nicky is really good at math and will explain anything over and over again, but he can be a bit awkward. Classes are a bit boring but they can be fun if you love math.

THE GOAT! Very easy and a good lecturer. He helps you on exams by going over very similar problems right before and letting you take notes and use said notes . You'll genuinely learn the course content.

Dr. Reyes is the best professor you can take if you want an easy A in calc. Midterms and the final were all online and based on the homework questions so if you study those you'll be fine. 89% is an A and in class quizzes are based on discussion problems but are only worth 8%. Really great guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you didn't previously understand calc, you won't understand it with him. Reyes was very chill, passionate, and happy to help. Entire class other than in class midterms (8%) was graded online so you can make an A in his class. Don't forget about online assignments and make sure to use your learning modules if you struggle with math like I do.

if you're looking for a chill professor, reyes is that guy. i fw calculus tho so i went to all the lectures, discussions, and midterms anyways. the ta/kris is also chill af too, i recommend going to her if you're stuck on any problem. besides the final, there's 1 drop for everything. all the tests recycle the quest hws, so keep that in mind.
It really cant get any easier, just take him

Lol if you want an easy A, take Reyes. However, you will eventually be too lazy to learn the material so just a warning on that! He legit shows you the exam before you take it when you do the in person portion but changes the numbers. Online portion is easy.

His class was really easy. Homework is all on quest and exams are 20% in person, 80% online. The online portion of the exams are a little difficult, but they're basically questions from the homework. He usually went off on tangents during his lectures, but besides that he taught alright.

This class was super easy, and Reyes is fantastic! He's nice, laid-back, and hilarious. However, his lectures/videos often go way beyond what you need to know for the course. You could also walk away with an A without having learned a substantial amount of the material, so if you want to master the content, you'll need a fair amount of discipline.

reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nicky's class was extremely easy. This class is perfect if you are probably not an engineering major, since Nicky's assignments are easy to do and many can basically pass the class not knowing what calc is. He's a very chill and nice dude to talk to and the funny face he makes when he looks to the computer lol. Overall, not a bad class honestly.

The class is super easy. Exams are online and Quest-based. Do the weekly hw and the same exact problems show up on the tests. Most people stopped showing up to class. I attended but didn't learn much. Nicky's really nice, but he likes to discuss topics in an abstract way so we can visualize them. Personally I'd rather just learn how to do the math.

Nicky's class is almost too easy. If you actually want to learn the content, this may not be the class for you. His lectures can be hard to follow and are more just him doing examples than lecturing. I do love him though and his class was a good experience. Weekly homework on quest is the hardest thing. Three midterms and final all open note/online

I took Intro to Number Theory with Nicky (yes, he even says in his syllabus to call him Nicky). He's single-handedly made me consider taking Algebraic Structures, even as an Econ major. His version of number theory dips into abstract algebra in a meaningful way that just makes sense. The character limit is restricting me, but he was awesome!

I struggle with math, so the easy A comments are misleading for reyes. This is a tough course conceptually and much of the material builds on itself. Stay on top of hw. Exams were very fair. Participation credit helps out. Lectures would sometimes be hard to follow, material was taught at a level higher than what the class was prepared for.

Nicky is a kind professor who is passionate about calculus. He is a great lecturer who makes calc seem so easy by explaining the content in ways anyone could understand. He has so many office hours, does hw questions during lectures, and provides additional online lectures. HW is challenging (multiple are dropped), but test material is very fair.

Lectures weren't the best, but the online modules and the videos he would posts each week were pretty helpful. Nice guy, didn't learn the most so if you're looking for an easy A take his class. Won't be the most beneficial for you tho. His grading was pretty good, so if you do the minimum you'll get a B or A (he doesnt have + or - letter grades)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The GOAT of M408D. Online midterms and recorded lectures, so attendance isn't mandatory aside from the small in-person component of the midterm, which he also does a great job of giving examples right before the exam. Take him for a great semester of M408D!

Never really went to lectures because you can watch them online if you need to. HW is all on quest and you can ask for help during discussion, 10% of midterm grade is based on an in class portion which is easy because he covers a similar problem before. Final is also fully online and there is a easy participation portion.

All exams and homeworks were online. He would rant a little bit in lectures, but with the learning modules, it was enough to be able to learn and understand what was going on in the class. It was a pretty easy class, and he is a very kind person. Would take a class with him again.

One of the easiest classes I've taken; did not go to class after the second week. Exams are take-home, online, open-note, and non-proctored, and thus the averages were always 97+. Probably not the best professor to take if you actually need to learn the content for future math classes, but if you're looking for an easy A, Nicky is the one.

I thought that M408D with Reyes was fine. The class was insanely easy because the homework and exams (including the final) were all online. However, I didn't love the way that Reyes taught his class. Luckily, I took BC Calc senior year of high school, so I was able to know what was going on!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All homework and tests are online. Lectures aren't mandatory, but I highly recommend attending even if you already know the topic because Nicky presents it in a way that deepens understanding. Majority of the class is review if you took Calc BC, but he helps build mathematical intuition in a way that other math professors don't.
Never went to lectures, still got an A. All assignments (homework, midterms, and final) are online. Super chill class, just weekly homework and three midterms (lowest dropped).

Nicky is one of those rare professors that is very very good at teaching and explaining concepts while having a class that is phenomenally easy to get an A in. Homework is online, Midterms & Final are open notes and online, and one of three midterms is dropped.

I was hesitant to take him since I didn't know if he would teach well, but never fear!

Prof Nicky is really awesome. His class is kinda hard to get into, but if you can its awesome. Very manageable. Lectures can sometimes go off on tangents but I think it just shows how passionate Prof Nicky is on the subject.  Really easy to learn and a fun class :)

He's so great! It's pretty competitive to get in his class, but you're lucky to get him. There's one pretty easy homework a week and he'll often do some of the problems on the board during class. There is a textbook but it's not required and tests are online! Lectures are not required, but are helpful to go to.

This class was very similar to AP Calc BC! Overall super manageable class, hw every week but not too bad. The professor posts lectures online so in-person lectures are not mandatory. I would recommend going to the discussions for help with homework.

Nicky is an amazing professor and I would be honored to take his class again. I have never felt so inspired by a calculus teacher before. His class is engaging and very interesting while also being a rather nice difficulty. I would highly highly recommend this class for anyone interested in taking M408D.

So many people give Reyes a good review exclusively because his class is easy. If you actually want to learn anything don't take him as a professor. All the tests are online and the HW is super basic. The lectures are very boring because he is essentially talking in circles. If you want an easy A without having to learn anything take Reyes.

The UT Math department has two good professors, and one of them is Dr. Reyes. Very caring, and very reasonable difficulty.I took M408D and M325K with him, and I was never in danger of failing, and unlike engineering classes, it was very doable to get an A.

Dr. Reyes was approachable and really nice. You could tell he loves teaching calculus. All of the assignments and tests are on Quest and you get to work with TA in discussion to solve homework problems which really helped with the stress of getting them done. Tests were easier than the homework, just meant to check your understanding. He was great.

Professor Reyes is an angel. Homeworks (30%) were due on Quest every week. All midterms (40% lowest dropped) and final exams (25%) were on the Quest website and were accessible online and the problems were very similar to the homework problems! If you are looking for an easy A and also want to learn calculus at the same time then this is the class.

Dr. Reyes (or Nicky) was amazing! By far the easiest Calc 2 class you could take. 30% of our grade was HWs, and we worked on problems during class. There was one HW a week, 3 midterms (1 drop), and the final. Every test was on quest, open note and plenty of time was given for each (also a 24 hr window to begin the exams). Overall an amazing class!

Probably the easiest calc class available, Dr. Reyes uses pre-recorded lectures for students to view before class and uses the actual class/discussion time to help students solve the majority of each week's homework. Very nice person and I enjoyed his class while getting an easy A.
This class is extremely easy with Reyes. If you want a free A in calc 3, then take this class.

Don't go to lectures if you want to understand calc. He's very passionate but goes on a lot of tangents. Take another professor if you didn't take calc in high school. He's very chill and our exams were online and not proctored. He loves going on tangents though. Overall, very easy course if you use khan academy instead of lectures.

Reyes is a great professor and I really enjoyed his class. I learned from outside resources or my TA, but he was always to help. Majority of the class is Quest homework, go to discussion to complete them. He's a great guy and this was a very manageable Calculus class to take. He goes on tangents in class, but an A in this class is very manageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Reyes is a chill guy. I never went to lectures, instead looked at some of the modules posted on quest occasionally to help w hw. I got a 100 on every midterm and an A in the class. If you want an A in 408D take it with Reyes.

Lectures focus more on theory than problem-solving, sometimes scatterbrained. But he provides lectures from other sources as alternatives. Tests are exactly like HW, if not easier. All assignments are online. Nicky is a genuine and caring guy. Take this prof for a low-stress, easy A in calc. You might not learn a ton, but you'll get the grade.

Took this class Fall 2021. Prof Reyes knows all about calculus, but he struggles with explaining the concept thoroughly to students. If you did not take Ap Calc in high school, you will struggle in this class. Otherwise, easy A if you already know differential calc. Do learning modules. Go to TA discussions. Exam was open note. Study hw for exams.

Luckily, I had a really great TA (Deyo) who was able to help explain concepts because the professor wasn't very clear on teaching math. he went on a lot of tangents and i had to seek help from classmates and/or the TA. otherwise, quest HW is exactly like the tests and final so definitely study those when it comes time to test.

Dr. Reyes does a flipped classroom and it was definitely not for me. His prerecorded lectures went on random tangents and were very hard to follow. He is a really cool guy, but he is quite disorganized canceling office hours last minute and changing from in-person to zoom lecture. Tests are almost identical to HW problems so it's an easy A.

Reyes is a really nice professor, and it's hard not to get an A unless you get really overconfident. It's also fortunate the class is so easy because Reyes is a pretty inefficient lecturer. For some reason, he chooses to go over the easiest problem for an entire lecture session. He also over justifies his statements, and seems unsure in teaching.

Nicky was such a nice guy and professor, but I can't say that I learned a whole lot in his calc 2 class. His lectures were really disorganized and he would go off on theoretical math stuff that kind of confused the whole class and was unrelated. Easy to get an A (tests were repeated hw questions) but kind of nervous for next sequence of calc now
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're gonna take cal 2, get Nicky. He is so sweet and genuinely cares about his students. I didn't really like his lectures though, so I just used the quest modules to learn the material. Tests are as easy as the homeworks, generally a light work load. I can't recommend him enough!

I was a little intimidated by what calculus 3 entailed, but Nicky honestly made it the easiest math class I've taken. HW is done on quest and can sometimes be lengthy, but as long as you do the HW, tests should be just as doable. He's a really caring and understanding professor, and you can tell he wants the best for his students.

Dr. Reyes is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He knows that students are currently going through a lot so he makes sure his class isn't heavy. Test and final is very similar to the hws on quest.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Reyes was nice more the less. His class was easy to get an A if you do quest hws because midterms, final exam are like quest hws, but there are only 10 MC questions on midterms, 20 MC questions on final. However, his lectures had almost nothing to do with quest hws, while TA sessions were useful. He makes some errors, so we have to correct him.

Nicky was awesome. If you are looking for a calc professor who explains concepts at a fundamental level in order to understand the concept, Nicky is your guy. He is very caring of his students and wants everyone to do well. Tests are just like the homework. Especially during COVID, he has been very conscientious of his students and their situation.

I absolutely love Nicky (he goes by Nicky). Took this class during COVID and he was very accommodating and understanding. His explanations are also super clear and the class was very straightforward. If you are anxious about calc 3, definitely take him because he makes the topic easy to understand. An A is more than attainable in this class.

Professor Reyes was such a great professor. Calculus is a very difficult subject; yet, he made this class a lot simpler through his explanations. If you have to take calculus and are not strong at math, take professor reyes. He was very willing to help his students, especially during the pandemic. He is super caring.

Professor Reyes (goes by Nicky) is an awesome professor. He is kind and very willing to help his students, especially during this pandemic. He covers the fundamentals and the basics as to what we need to know for tests. Not too hard for a calculus class, but you still got to work for the grade. Nicky is great.
Nicky is Awesome. Multivariable Calculus is no joke, but having him as a professor makes the subject bearable and you will learn a lot from Nicky. He is an awesome professor. Take Nicky.

Professor Reyes is such an amazing professor and even better person. He truly cares about his students - especially during this COVID pandemic. He is very knowledgable and explains things very well. He has made me not hate taking calculus. He answers all questions and makes himself available to his students. Take Professor Reyes, he is truly a gem.

Nicky is a great guy. His teaching style is not the best, but the class is definitely doable coming from someone who did not take calculus in high school. The tests are really similar to the homework so if you do good in those, you are set for the test. Also, the textbook is never used so don't buy :)

Taking a math class with professor Reyes is a very good choice. His lecture is more based on the fundamentals. There are weekly homework but they are really easy. His exams are multiple choice but if you do the Homework and review them for exams you should get an A. I'd say final was still like the homework but it was harder then other exams.

Nicky was fine. If you have a strong foundation in Calc 1 + 2 it is not hard to teach yourself the necessary material for M from the textbook. His tests were MC and straight from the HW, but I don't know how much I learned conceptually. Lectures weren't helpful and could be disorganized. I went to the TA sessions and those were super useful!

Nicky was a good choice for M408D. His class is structured around teaching the theorems of M408D. He can get off-topic during lectures, but they help build the foundations for the homework. Class and discussions are non-mandatory. His exams were multiple choice and were the easier questions from the unit's homework.

His lectures are a bit messy. He gets confused a lot and needs to be corrected many times. Gave me a 0 for an assignment I turned in (and had proof that I did). I couldn't physically reach out to him because of covid19, but emailed him around 6 times and got no response. Seems to not care about his students. Easy class overall.
Great teacher! He really wanted is to understand and gave us every opportunity to ask questions if we were confused. We didn't use the textbook often outside of a few written hw problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is super nice and caring! The class is also a super easy A if you know how to study. STUDY THE HOMEWORK!! There are only 3 exams (drops the lowest one). However, the exam questions are basically like the homework but with different #. His teaching style is not the best; don't take this class if you actually want to learn. but its an easy A class

Terrific! Reyes is an incredibly smart person and an even better teacher. He can explain things very insightfully on a low level, as well as skipping the nitty-gritty details sometimes to discuss math at a high level. Does thorough examples in class, will provide rigorous proofs if you want to know further, and makes sure no one is struggling :)
Amazing professor!

Nicky is not the best lecturer all the time, but he does follow the textbook very closely. I recommend reading the textbook and doing extra practice on quest (apart from the homework) if you're ever feeling unsure about any of the material. He also is super available outside of lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He teaches the theory behind the topics in class which might be confusing for some, but it provides a nice intuition for the problems you'll be solving. The homework is easy, and the tests are based on the homework and are entirely MC. The class is super easy and he's a really kind guy. would definitely take him again if possible.

Nicky is one of the best teachers here at UT! His class is interesting and thoroughly taught. He explains the theory while also solving examples in class. Easygoing person, accessible after class, and approachable with concerns. Tests are MC, no +- grading (89-100 is an A), extra credit for for all 3 tests, lowest test grade dropped, MC HW.

This course was fully online. It had really easy short 5-10 question quizzes every week that i always got an A in. BUT the class only had 2 test therefore it weighed my whole grade. It was difficult to get an A even with good quiz grades due to making sure my test were A's. There wasn't many extra credit and there is no extra time on due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate & can be funny at times, but nothing is funny when you're given 300 terms (without definitions/examples/context) a week before the exam and expected to deeply understand all of those terms. This class is definitely not treated like an introductory course for non-majors.

Took it last sem with no open note + honorlock. Expected to know LOTS of info for exams (300+ question bank p exam, asked a random 50 questions, so you have to know basically every detail). Hard, not impossible, but better off taking it at a community college probably. She's pretty nice though (ish.. definitely direct.. but reasonable)

The class itself was pretty easy to navigate through, the exams were the most difficult part to deal with mostly because of their worth. The class usually ends with most students getting A's through suspicious activity so there is no rounding beware of that

The weekly assignments are very easy, but each exam is worth 27% of your grade. The exams are pretty difficult compared to the study guides given. The professor only offers 2 points worth of extra credit and does not round. If you need the credit for core curriculum requirements, I would recommend taking this course at a community college instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tests are implemented so students suffer and make sure your grade stays down. Interesting lectures ig

Lets just throw together 2 tests worth most of your grade while giving a study guide each with 300 terms then calling it a day. The tests are written as if they're open note and with 300+ terms in each test, pray youre lucky and get easy ones, every mistake is costly and getting 2-3 more wrong is a letter grade difference. Terrible grading system
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien was obviously passionate about gov, which made her lectures entertaining as someone who doesn't find interest in it. Tests are rough since two are 54% of your grade, closed-note with ~300 terms to memorize, very dependent on the questions you get; however, they were pretty fair. Keep up with the videos. Quizzes/assignments are easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class's content is interesting, but the lectures are unorganized and not easy to follow. She frequently gets off track and will talk about irrelevant things for a significant amount of time. I wanted to like this class a lot, but it wasn't worth going to the lectures. It was easier to watch the recorded ones at home because of the tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. O'Brien as a person; however, her grading is pretty harsh considering the two exams that you have to take are worth 27% of your grade each. They're honorlock and cover abt 300 terms. She tests how well you know the concept and how to apply them. I took this course because I needed the history credit, but she made the lectures fun.

Anything you heard before Fall 2025 about this class IT HAS CHANGED!!! Tests are honorlock and you are expected to know over 300+ vocab terms for each test. In retrospect if you have the time every week to listen to 10 lecture vids each being 45 min you should be okay in the class but If you're looking for an easy A+ I wouldn't take this class.

She's funny... But that's all I really got. The each test is 27% of your grade. Involves memorizing over 300 words, CLOSED BOOK/NOTE. In my opinion, the exams seem to be formatted like they're open book/note (like they were previously), but the percentage it takes up in the class does not reflect the increased difficulty for students.

TAKE HER CLASS. BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. Super flexible and gives good feedback on assignments. Her lectures are super short and interesting and keep you engaged, she cares so much about her students and it shows. Easy assignments and tests are simple if you take notes and pay attention. Best class I have taken in a while, highly recommend.

Uses honorlock. Optional prerecorded lectures. Very light workload. For exams, lots of terms to memorize. If you watch all the lecture videos (3 hrs/wk) and pay attention, you'll do fine on exams. Little EC/No curve. Answers emails quickly (same with TAs)

The tests are about 50 questions long (not open book) and are based on 200+ vocabulary terms, which all need to be memorized. In the past, this class did not use Honorlock, leading to the great reviews, but as of now, this class is much more difficult than it seems. Should include many more extra credit opportunities, but does not.

Explained concepts very well. Organized course. Reasonable tests/assignments (with exception of some very specific questions in quizzes).

Sometimes there were way too many videos for the week. She posts "notes" from each lecture which can be very useful if you don't want to actually watch all of them but still want to learn the content and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she's absolutely awesome, it is hard to not get an A in this class. So easy, super straightforward, you go at your own pace weekly and theres very very easy open note quizzes every week 10 questions. THE BEST. EASY A. TAKE THIS. SHES AMAZING. would take every semester if i could
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Summer course- 2025
Her passion for government is infectious and she made me want to know more about it. The class is overall easy (around 12 pages & 2 lectures a day) if you take notes and study before the 2 major tests.
P.S. This class required Honor Lock to be downloaded for tests.

Very easy and straightforward class. Class is asynchronous and online, so you watch pre-recorded lectures at your own pace; however, they are released every week, so you cannot complete the entire course in one sitting. Graded on easy weekly quizzes and two online midterm exams that are 50 multiple-choice questions. Highly Recommend for Gov Credit!

Very funny and knowledgeable. Tests made up 85% of the grade over 3 tests, each 50 multiple choice questions. Went off-topic in lectures frequently, but at least it was interesting. Good course to learn the basics of city politics, including real estate and zoning.
Super easy government class, assignments and tests were easy peasy and learned a lot.

Easy online class done at your own pace. Usually follows a structure of assignment and quiz due every Saturday. O'Brien would often and clearly communicate through canvas and announcements, and she did offer the occasional extra credit. Very sweet :)

Low pressure class. Assignments are pretty easy if you watch lecture and pay attention. Done at your own pace weekly. Just watch the lectures and take notes and you'll do fine. I messed up on the first exam and still got an A.

Took her for urban politics. She rambles and goes off topic a lot during lectures, which is frustrating because on our review sheets there's like 100 terms per exam to know. She's super cool and excellent to talk to outside of class, but it felt like it was difficult to excel on the exams, especially considering its 85% of your grade.

Very organized and straightforward class! Lots of resources and lecture notes are concise in what you need to know. The TA team were also lovely and easy to contact. I highly recommend this course if you need it for the credit. Lectures were very digestible after one watch. Some were way longer than others but overall still an excellent course.
Class was very straightforward, asynchronous so you can do it when you choose. Lectures were entertaining and not challenging. Not a very time consuming class. Would recommend for gov credit.
Loved Dr. Obrien! She's really interesting to listen to and honestly funny. I'm a CNS major and I liked this class lol, would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien is simply the best. She is super funny and you genuinely learn a lot from her online course. Even if you think gov is boring you will find her class super low stakes and entertaining.

It's online, so do with it as you will. Wasn't hard at all, just review her pre-made review notes before the exam or quizzes and you'd be fine. Textbook was optional, just watch the videos. Never met her in person, but she seems fine to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
Professor. O'Brien was a great professor, I definitely skimmed through the lectures more than I should of, but the way she sets things up makes the material clear and concise
I would recommend this class to anyone who needs credit.

Professor O'Brien is a good professor and I overall really enjoyed her Urban Politics class. However, it was very hard following on to lectures as O'Brien regularly goes off topic. As much as her random facts are interesting, I was often confused on what was actual material and what was a ramble. Very important as 3 exams are majority of your grade

Couldn't recommend more if you need a government credit. Assignments were never bad and exams were open note, 50 questions, 60 minutes. Knocking out weekly assignments and lectures only took about an hour to answer the quizzes, overall really easy and great class

SO GOOD!!! take o'brien for 310L. exams are very straightforward, open note and book! weekly 5 question quiz thats similar question style to exams and weekly assignments (some graded for completion some are graded on effort but she tells you which is which) super amazing love o'brien so much would recommend
Professor O'Brien had amazing lectures and was engaging even though this was an online course. Definitely would take her again.
Such an easy credit for government. Would highly recommend, she is so nice.

Professor O'Brien structures her class in an asynchronous format that is very user-friendly. Everything is open-note, open-book. Lectures can drag on but do provide crucial information for assignments and quizzes. Professor O'Brien is passionate about the subject and finds creative ways to get her students excited about government. Super easy class

TAKE this government class if you need the credit! There are about 2 assignments weekly with 5-6 lectures, but the lectures is awesome. I passed this class and actually learned a lot of new and cool stuff I never knew. As long as you keep up with the lecture, quizzes, and assignments, you will pass this class with flying colors!

Greatest of all time. Easiest class I've taken, if you just need your government credit there is nothing easier than this. There is just weekly quizzes and two tests, with topics you should be able to ace and already know from high school.

Easiest class I have ever taken at UT. Lectures are async, so you have an entire week to watch them and do weekly assignments. Everything is open-note, so you can complete assignments very quickly. Ngl I would forget about this class until Saturday night, when everything was due. If you have the opportunity to take her, do it!!

Incredibly easy government class. Open note everything - all you need is a textbook. O'Brien is pretty interesting and funny if you do watch lectures, I almost wished this class were in person. I loved this class and her assignments. Def take for gov credit!!!

I honestly loved this class so much! Professor O'Brien has lots of videos but they're not required but I enjoyed all of them. She's such a funny professor and makes the lectures interesting. The assignments are super easy and you can finish them in less than 30 mins. Tests are harder than expected but still not that difficult. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

There's definitely a lot of lectures, but genuinely the content is interesting, and O'Brien presents it in a way where u won't get bored of it. A pretty chill class, u won't have an issue getting an A, just be sure to take adequate notes during the lecture videos. I met her once on accident, and she's genuinely such a kind prof! If u can, take her!
Professor O'Brien showed a clear interest in Government as well as deep knowledge and understanding. She facilitated various complex topics to make them easier to comprehend. 10/10

I would not take this class again. The exams were much more difficult than I thought they'd be. You have to read the textbook and know her lectures because the exam questions come from both. She is a funny person, but the lectures felt all over the place. There's just so much information to retain for the exams and I did not find myself doing well.
She is the best! If you need to take GOV310L, take it with her!!! If you need extensions on work, she is pretty understanding. You can tell she cares about her students a lot
she's so funny plus this is the easiest class i have ever taken
She is awesome!!! Super funny and laid back, would highly recommend! Also the TA is awesome, great feedback and thorough, easy grading.

please take this government class if you need the credit. professor is so sweet and it is all online!! super easy class overall. loved watching her lectures and learning more every week. This class has about 2 assignments per week and can easliy be done.

Online class- videos to watch each week, no need to buy textbook. She's entertaining to listen to and loves lecturing, can watch on 2x. Each week there's a 5q quiz and a short assignment, both simple. There are two exams that you do on set day, at your own time (online, open note). Great online class and easy to get credit, GPA boost

I took this class for my American and Texas Government core requirement. I'll just be straightforward. This class was easy. I'm an RTF major and don't plan on taking any hard core classes lol. If you want an easy Texas core class, take this.

I would recommend everyone take this class or a class taught by her! However, wait until you know you will have time during every week to watch lecture videos, because they're important to understanding the material. Two exams, weekly quizzes and assignments (these are easy and for your benefit).
100% recommend for government credit. easy manageable weekly assignments and lectures provide lots of examples and are easy to follow. clearly passionate about what she teaches.

This class is incredibly manageable, there's clear criteria weekly about what's expected. Professor O'Brien has very informative and fun lectures as well. I highly recommend taking this class for the government credit, the content and assignments are straightforward and simple.
Makes government at UT fun! 100% recommend. She has good humor too. Each week there's 1 short assignment and a 5 question quiz. There are 2 tests the whole semester- suuuuper doable

Take Professor O'Brien for Government! She made this class super accessible, and if you stay on top of the weekly online quizzes and assignments, you'll be perfectly fine. Tests are long, all multiple choice, but not challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
IF YOU GET TO TAKE GOV WITH DR. O'BRIEN, PLS PLS PLS TAKE IT YOU WILL NEVER REGRET!!!!!

She is such a great professor, explained all hard government terms easily with memorable examples, and we can tell she spent so much time designing this class. She made the government so approachable!

The lecture notes helped me summarize the material I learn each week. Dr. O'Brien explained the slides very well in her videos and made sure we watched the entire videos so we know what's going on with the material. Her weekly quizzes kept me engaged in learning this course. Tests are open-note, all multiple-choice, T/F, and are pretty easy.

Dr. O'Brien is amazing!!! I heard such awful things about taking government at UT, but she made this class so enjoyable and easy to understand. You have to keep yourself accountable because it is self paced, but if you watch the lectures and pay attention this class will be fun and not difficult. Dr. O'Brien is one of my favorite professors at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have the opportunity to take a class with O'Brien, do it. She is an incredible professor who cares deeply about the topic, but also know that most of her students are non gov majors. Lectures are recorded and attendance is optional. Tests are 50 multiple choice questions- if you study the review sheet and take good notes, you'll be fine.

Loved this class! Took it in person. Prof O'brien is funny, engaging and approachable in class. She is reasonable about grades and assignments. She is incredibly knowledgable about government and the presidency which she is clearly passionate about and she wants her students to do well. 10/10. would recommend.

She's super chill and her lectures are as interesting as government can be. She adds personal stories that make the lectures less monotonous and funny. There's three exams and four assignments and it's a pretty easy A if you just do the assignments and make some flashcards. Don't have to go in person because lectures are available online after.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tough class, wish the exams were weighted equally as she weighted the last two heavier than the first two which leads to more stressful final exams. Professor's choice I suppose. Definitely learned a fair bit and would recommend O'Brien to other students.

Dr. O'Brien is super funny, and she makes things extremely easy and straight-forward for those of us who hate/struggle with gov. She gives study guides and lectures that have the test question answers easily available when you're studying, so it's not too hard if you pay attention. Easiest professor for 310L, don't take anybody else.

Overall, pretty easy and straightforward. Made up of 3 basic MCQ exams and 4 easy assignments, no busy work. Lectures are drawn out but she adds fun commentary and interesting facts. She is very organized and clear but at times she can speak too fast. You should be good if you pay attention and start memorizing material a couple days before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy; the exams are all multiple choice and non-cumulative, only thing is it is entirely memorization (and specific, like remembering a bunch of court cases and exactly what they were). I'm sure it's an easy A if you attend class (lol) but not hard to completely check out and get a decent grade.

Prof. O'Brien made GOV310L an enjoyable class. As long as you pay attention to the lectures/take notes and read through your notes before the exams, this class is an easy A. She makes the lectures very interesting/engaging and I felt made it easy to understand even hard topics. Also love her commentary on things, she kinda slays. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, I took this class for a core credit but I wish I could take another one of her classes. She's organized, approachable, and very clear about grading, and on top of that she had so many hilarious and interesting stories to keep the material interesting. Tests were all multiple choice, and pretty straightforward.

I actually took 371U but didn't see it on the list. Anyways, I LOVE this class and she is a great professor! It's not difficult at all and she is super understanding. The content is interesting, the lectures are fun, and the workload is not too bad. Definitely recommend.

Overall GREAT PROFESSOR she is very approachable and helpful, but it's up to YOU to study for the test. Tests are very heavy weighted, CLOSED book and notes, and require a lot of memorization of terms so have great study skills. She will work with you to make sure that you understand the content as long as you make the effort to talk to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor O'Brien is amazing and highly recommend taking any of her gov classes. Her lectures are entertaining, she talks about gov history as if she was there!  I genuinely felt like I learned something new in every lecture. NO busy work, Tests/ 4 assignments that are all very fair. Enjoyable/ Easy / Entertaining!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you ever get the chance, take O'Brien. This class was very informative and interesting, and her exams are very fair. 3 exams, 1 long paper and 1 short paper assignment. I wish I could take her again for another class, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend O'Brien enough. She is very sweet and shares stories of her travels to historical sites that are relevant to the lecture. Exams are fair, but not the kind of exam you can cram easily for so make sure you're prepared. Rounded me to an A at the end, take her for 310L!!

Rewatch lectures, take notes, & memorize all the terms she gives to do well on the tests. Class isn't mandatory but important & would help a lot for studying for the test. They're each 30% but if you do what I said, you'll get an A since it's very straightforward. (most of the test term definitions are on quizlet) And I never used the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class will give you the exact same as you put in. Attend all the lectures and do the study guides!She is pretty funny and the lectures are not really boring.Sometimes it can seem long but she is really good at relating the information in a way that makes more sense.There are three exams and two assignments. That's it. She does do extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is pretty comprehensible! She lectures in a personal way, as she incorporates humor into her lectures. Her tests are straight to the point and you can score well if you take the time to read (chapters aren't long) and take notes. But, there are 3 tests and each are 30% so don't take this class if you are not a fan of test heavy courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien was an okay professor, but the class is a bit unfair. It is allocated by 3 tests being 90% of your grade and 2 (harshly graded) paper assignments being the other 10%. She will NOT round your grade, so you should be careful. Also, the TAs are not helpful. What should have been an easy A was made rather difficult, unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien is very sweet, but sometimes her lectures can be hard to follow. She will ramble a bit when she is explaining a topic, and though her stories are relevant to the subject, she can continue rambling instead of moving on to other content. There are 3 tests which are each 30% of your grade, and two small assignments. The tests are easy

She gives us base line notes & we just have to add a little bit more info to them during the lectures. She post the lectures online after every class so you don't even have to go in person. Theres only 3 test and 2 easy assignments. Overall i really recommend her, just pay attention & this class is a really easy A.

I have taken this professor for 2 classes and I LOVE her. She makes herself so accessible and is always adapting to student needs. As far as the content, her lectures are engaging and interesting and the assessments are all fairly easy.

TEST HEAVY! 90% of your grade is made up of three tests. The tests are online and open book/open notewhich can be deceiving because you think you dont need to study as hard. The element I struggled with during her TIMED online tests was the fact that you have to submit each answer as you go. This worsened my test anxiety for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is an easy A, def the easiest class Ive ever taken. Test qs are only testing for recall of basic facts so its super easy if you go to lectures and take notes. Reading the textbook isnt necessary but might help because some questions are pulled from lines in the book literally verbatim. 90% of grade are the 3 tests (online, not proctored)

Attendance isnt a grade 90% of your grade comes from three tests. Theyre all open-note/book and are very straight forward. The two writing assignments are super easy. Honestly, just take good notes every lecture (all of which are recorded/posted) and you could easily get a 100 in this class.

took 310L for a gov credit, highly recommend! she lectures from the textbook so you honestly don't need to ever read. she also offers the textbook online so you don't need to buy it and posts the lectures online after so you don't need to go to class. super easy and understanding. exams were multiple choice online and not proctored.

Honestly, She's a great professor who knows her stuff and makes the class interesting. It's just that I'm not an audio learner and all the important stuff is said during lectures. Her notes only show the broad idea but don't go into much detail. Even though she posts lectures online, they don't have closed captions so I can't tell some of her words
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Relatively easy to get an A, but you have to watch pretty much all of her lectures bc that's what you need to study. She lets you use your notes and any resources on her tests. There also wasn't a final, so that was really nice too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She gives super entertaining lectures! The class is graded by three multiple choice tests, one long essay, and two writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Brien was kind of all over the place during lecture, but it makes it entertaining. Attendance is not mandatory, but the exams have a lot of content from the lecture, so do not just purposely skip if you can avoid it. Overall, just study the slides, take notes, and pay attention, and a good grade is easily achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Before this, I didn't care about government but O'Brien's entertaining and funny lectures changed that. Enabled me to understand the importance of american governmens along with its intriguing intracices. As long you take notes from lecture and learn them, an A/A-/B+ is very achievable. Excellent choice for GOV310L and I would highly recommend :)

O'Brien is a great choice for Gov!. Her lectures aren't the most entertaining, but she knows what she's talking about and is clearly passionate about government. She makes it very clear what is going to be on each exam - literally just make a Quizlet of the terms she puts on the review and you'll be fine! Textbook helps but isn't necessary at all.

Prof. O'Brien's class is an easy A, by far the easiest gov class I've ever taken. Her lectures are mostly based off a powerpoint, and she mumbles, so it is sometimes hard to understand her. Don't need the textbook, just listen to her lectures. If you took APUSH and paid attention this class is a breeze, just show up listen and study a little!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Solid professor. Multiple packets of papers due instead of a paper every week-works with students schedules. Cares about students, interesting lectures, pretty easy grader, non-mandatory attendance on Fridays. Presents course material in the most beneficial way to her students. Pretty funny once you get her humor. Relates her life to the class.

Professor O'Brien's class was pretty easy. 3 tests and a couple of short assignments, but nothing stressful. Would not hesitate to take her class again and would recommend to anyone looking for an intro gov course. I just attended class and did her reviews before tests. She tries to make her lectures engaging, so just go!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien is a cool teacher. Honestly, this class isn't hard. Just don't overthink her tests. She really doesn't try to trick you. I would recommend using quizlet to study! Go to her office hours. She's super chill and easy to talk to. I overall enjoyed this class and she made this subject intresting. Lastly, you don't have a final! Great teacher

Her Politics and Film class was very interesting and I enjoyed it. She is very knowledgeable about films and government, but her lectures were sometimes boring because she rambles and goes off topic constantly. Still a very good professor and I would definitely take her again. If you pay attention at all and do the assignments it should be easy.

TAKE HER FOR GOVERNMENT. She has 3 exams and 2 assignments. The two assignments are easy, not difficult. The tests are multiple choice, 45-55 questions. She gives study guides that ARE EXTREMELY helpful for her tests. If you memorize it, you will for sure get an A. I read the textbook, it helps (not mandatory). Got 92 on all my tests. She's good!

Shes a solid choice, not too hard, tries to be funny to make class interesting but often goes on tangents. She outs bare-bones lecture notes online so if you miss class its no big deal, but its a little hard to rely on these notes. exams are multiple choice with lots of memorization but study guides are provided
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took this course in person. Lectures weren't all mandatory but there were pop quizzes ( heavy at the end of the semester). All lectures were recorded. 10 pop quizzes but only 6 are graded. Lectures are kind of boring but there is a lot of resources for help. Test are all different ( free response, multiple choice, T or F). One group project.
Great professor who cares about her students, but if you know basically anything about health, society, and sociology this class is pretty boring. Easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Loved this class! The lectures weren't always engaging but often very interesting. The content was easy to grasp and the tests were easy. You get a cheat sheet for 2/4 exams and 1 exam gets dropped. Attendance measured by group quizzes graded on participation. Only thing that was unenjoyable was the group project.

Professor O is so passionate about her subject and is a very clear communicator. There are random pop quizzes, but you get a 100 for writing your name down, so they're more for attendance. My only issue was a group project worth 10% of your grade, where you are assigned a random group (and only given Canvas to find them in a class of 300+).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring prof, easy lectures to follow but also really engaging. I didn't take many notes for this class besides guest lecturers. Also provides a ton of extra credit opportunities.

Will have occasional pop quizzes throughout the semester, so you should probably show up often. Assigns a good amount of reading but you could get by without reading it and taking good notes during lectures. Exams are mostly lecture content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing prof + TAs. Super interesting topics, a lot of it is pretty obvious/common sense topics being taught so it's not crazy hard. The free response exams are graded a little harshly and getting even a few half-points off can kind of tank your grade. Very charismatic teacher & had amazing guest speakers. Love her.
She's nice and class is interesting. Lots of discussion posts but there's like 6 drops I think. Cheat sheet on exams full page front and back handwritten.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Osbakken was AMAZING. Super knowledgeable and topics apply to many people. Not and HS major but I loved this class. Tests were easy as long as you did the review, she also allowed a cheat sheet. As long as you pay attention you'll get a good grade.

I love Osbakken she is so mom and cares a lot about her students. You have to pay attention to every little detail about the slides for the exams EVERY detail. For the final exam I had to buy a book out of pocket but it was actually good and I never read yayy. She will NOT curve your 89.999 also do your very best on the group project nothing lazy.

I really enjoyed Dr. Osbakken's lectures. You get a front and back note sheet for every exam. However, they can be a little challenging if you don't take notes and don't do the readings. The discussions are very easy.
Nice lady but can be condescending and a bit passive aggressive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 4 exams but the lowest gets dropped. Lectures are boring sometimes. Allows cheat sheet on exams that are front and back. Easy discussion posts. There is a group project towards the end of the semester. She's chill, take this class it's interesting

Dr. Osbakken was awesome. Her lectures could be a little long at times but the topic was super interesting. The grading was super fair and the tests are not difficult as long as you use the resources she gives you (an entire page of notes for each test).

She is very passionate about her teachings. She has guest lectures every other week to wrap up the material covered. Her lectures are engaging and easy to follow. The tests are relatively easy, she allows one cheat sheet. Overall, I recommend her!

This was an interesting class and Dr O was able to teach the material very well. The slideshows are often very dense but just retaining the key concepts is whats important. A few tests but theres a cheat sheet, would recommend.

Dr. Osbakken is single-handedly the best professor I've had. She's incredibly caring, insightful, and has enriched my academic experience in more ways than one. She will teach you to look at issues from multiple perspectives and to strive to understand the systems of society in a more holistic way. I couldn't speak highly enough of Dr. Osbakken!

Osbakken is great professor! Her lecture slides are very content heavy but as long as you take notes and do the readings you should be fine. she does also do a good amount of extra credit and drops a test. You also get one paper front and back as a cheat sheet for every test. Great class for any pre health student and very relevant to real world
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor O is a great lecturer and truly cares about what she teaches. There is a group project and 4 tests along with an essay at the end of the semester but if you go to class, take notes, and stay attentive you should easily do well!

Other students grade your work for your weekly essays. Let me repeat, other students can determine your grade. If you want the TA to grade your work, Dr. O says the TA will grade 1000x harder. I think a professor, or at least a TA, should be responsible for dolling out grades, not other 19-year-olds.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor O is an amazing speaker and lecturer. Some of the slides are a bit dense, but she walks you through it effortlessly. All tests are open note and we had a group project which was pretty fun! I enjoyed and learned so much in this class!

Professor O's lectures were great. She is extremely well-spoken, caring, and educated. She isn't afraid to talk about controversial subjects, but she is open and fair to all students. Your grade is made up of short essays and quizzes. Make sure to take good notes, because she rarely posts the slides from the lectures.

Dr. O was a great professor and SO kind. Her TAs are awesome and there are so many helpful resources for this class. There was a lot of writing involved, as well as three heavy weighted quizzes. This being said, the course material was current and interesting and I highly recommend it!
I honestly loved Professor O so much she was one of the kindest women ever. The class is very easy to understand and connect ideas together.

I found the lectures boring, but I would suggest going either ways. Professor was super accommodating, tests were open-note and notes were provided per lecture (it is because of this that I didn't tank tests). Still the topics are interesting and it would benefit you to go to office hours and participate. Group project is doable but no slacking.

I love Dr O! We covered a lot of material, but the pace wasn't too fast. There are 3-4 essays graded by peers, which I hated because it's easy for retaliatory low grading to happen. Tests are relatively easy if you pay attention, and are open note. AWESOME professor -- 10/10 recommend. She loves participation, so maybe don't t take if you/re shy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was not easy it takes a lot of time through readings, discussion posts, and essays. However it is doable with the right mindset and determination. Attendance is optional the professor is extremely understanding. I would not recommend this class if you're not majoring in medical related, this class asked for too much time and work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Super compassionate and understanding professor, one of the best I've taken at UT. Lectures do cover a lot of information but exams were open notes (so take good notes!). Essay assignments were graded by other students, so easy A's. Discussion prompts were short, but lots of reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a very mind-opening class. The information is so important, especially if you plan on going into the medical field. There is a LOT of reading and the open-note quizzes were IMO pretty hard. 3 tests. 3 short essays. 1 long essay. 1 group project. 10 discussion posts. Some extra credit. It's easy to skip but don't!! Take notes and participate

Took Dr. O's Cancerland course - Best class I've taken! Rlly inspirational & completely changes the way you view healthcare! Majority of the class was discussion-based w/ guest speakers - 3 papers & 2 presentations. All pretty straightforward! You need to have a connection to cancer or compelling reason to join the course, for discussion purposes.

As many students at UT know, Dr. Osbakken is the best. She is incredibly well respected and you are lucky to get into her class. The H&S seminar was at times challenging. There is a big group project that moves fast. Dr. O can be a tough grader, but as long as you show up and participate you will succeed.

Dr. Osbakken's class was one of my favorites this semester. The course was a bit reading-heavy, but overall it was pretty manageable. Make sure you take good notes because sometimes the tests can be a little tricky, but overall the course was not too difficult. Fantastic class!
Very good class and professor. I have learned a lot from this course without having to struggle much. Easy class for the A. Great information taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Osbakken is a good lecturer. Essays are graded by peers and then you have to give them a feedback score. If a peer does not agree with the score you give them, they can give you a low feedback score and the TAs will not change your grade. Exams are tricky and the exam grades are posted after 2weeks. Nice professor, poor grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is an interesting course with an AMAZING professor. She truly wants you to succeed and wants to hear your opinions. Technically reading heavy but as long as you understand the main points, I don't find the reading necessary. 4 SHORT peer-graded essays, 3 open note quizzes, 10 disc posts (can drop 2), one group project. She is so kind.. TAKE!!!

Dr. O was a great professor and gave many opportunities to talk about the readings we were assigned. The only issue I have is that your essays are based on what your peers grade you. There is a pressure not to grade them perfectly even if you felt they did amazing. You have to make sure to grade them off of things even if you are not 100% certain.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors ever. Her class is very interesting and being in a pandemic she made sure her students were adjusting okay to everything. Weekly readings but nothing too hard and an essay every two weeks but from the material you learn in class and the readings they aren't hard to overcome. I would recommend this class to everyone!

I think everyone needs to take this class if possible because the things we learned are beyond useful. Although Dr. O is awesome this class is extremely hard to keep up with. There are a ton of things due each week and her quizzes are super tricky. My biggest advice is to stay on top of everything especially since the readings each week are long.

This ranks in one of my favorite classes I've taken the past 2.5 years. The material is so important and useful for today's problems. Professor O and her TAs are AMAZING, they are all very caring. There are weekly discussion posts, 7 essays, and 3 quizzes. Make sure to do well on the quizzes because that's why I got a B! but great class!

I highly recommended this class not only for the professor but also the course content. I find the material Dr.O includes is extremely important for people to learn, and I bet you will change your mind on a lot of issues. The essays are straightforward, and the tests are doable if you have completed the readings and have general grasp on concepts

All the other posts explain her class accurately however it is important to know that her tests are worded awfully. Every question is "select which one is false" or along those lines and all the choices are so similar. That part isn't that bad but it gets worse when there is actually more than one answer. No extra credit provided yet either :((((((
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading assignments! I didn't read them until before the 4 tests & still am doing well. Lecture attendance isn't req. and is recorded- must watch to do well on tests. Interesting material-some is common sense. Essays are graded by peers but this DOESN'T mean the essay grades are easy A's!! study for the tests and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lovely professor, would definitely take another class by her. She does assign an unbearable amount of readings but as long as you attend class you should be able to write a solid essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hands down, the best class I have taken in college. Dr. Osbakken is amazing, the exams are long and my TA graded harshly, but the class is worth it. She is always available to talk to students, the readings were never boring, and if you go to the TA's study review sessions you will do well on the exams. The papers aren't worth much of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor I've taken at UT! Truly cares about the success of her students and will do everything she can to make sure you make the most out of your learning experience with her. Very engaging- her persona fuels a self-motivation to do your best. Class environment was very inclusive. I'll never forget Stephanie.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Osbakken was a great lecturer, I learned a lot from her class. Her class is a little workload heavy, with lots of readings (2-3 per each class) that are covered on the exams. It is doable to get an A as long as you attend class and study a few days before the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stephanie is very nice and cares about the material, but makes the class much harder than it needs to be. The tests focus on what information comes from which author, instead of just the information. The A, B, C, A/B, A/C, all of the above format for the tests makes it difficult as well. I would avoid if possible.

Dr. Osbakken helped me facilitate strong social capital at UT. She urged me to visit professors and build relationships on my road to graduate school. Her Health and Society class was both inspirational and engaging. Great lectures and lots of new and thought-provoking information. Definitely take this class!

She's wonderful- she's an engaging lecturer who really cares about both her subject material and her students and is really such a proponent for their success. Her tests are a little weird because she asks if multiple answers are correct are not, but the information is definitely relayed in class and in your readings.

Enlightening lessons that are clear and easily comprehensible. Participation comes in the form of in-class activities that are random. Work isn't bad and you should really talk to your TA if you want to do well on the weekly reading reports bc they're the ones grading it. Don't sweat the class. It's not hard.

Dr. Osbakken is an amazing professor. She was always well prepared and confident during her lectures and is ready and willing to meet with her students. She's very direct and if you go to class and pay attention (and read the materials) then her tests are really fair. I honestly can't stress how amazing of a professor she is. Take her classes!!

For the year I was in, it was almost impossible to get a 100 on the reading responses. People in my study group said the TAs gave little and vague feedback. Definitely do the readings and attend the lectures. The exams sometimes have specific statistical questions and can be difficult, but an A is doable. The study guides are dense, but helpful

Osbakken is an amazing professor. You can tell she cares about what she does. You have reading responses every other week and a lot of readings outside of class. Her tests are very tricky like A, B, C, A and B, A and C, All of the above etc.. However the class is worth it and is very interesting. Would recommend.

This class took work. It is very lecture heavy so even though attendance isn't mandatory, I would go. Exams weren't easy but they were fair. She is great to those who do the work and ask for help. But she will never raise your grade if you have been slacking off and missing class. This is an intro class so it sets up your foundation.

Dr. Osbakken was great! This class is an easy A ONLY if you show up to class & pay attention. I didn't do all of the readings (and trust me there are a lot) however if you read the lectures slides and do the study guide before each test and you will be fine. The topic opened my eyes to healthcare system in the US & around the world. Amazing Class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite teacher at UT so far! I got an A soley through attending every class and taking great notes, doing all the hw assignments and following directions, skimmed the readings and taking notes on them, and for the test looking over reading notes and powerpoint. No homework besides to read. Easy class if you put in a little effort. Amazing lady!!!

This class was amazing. Topics were very interesting, fun, and relevant. 5 short essays on certain assigned articles (easy 100). A lot of assigned reading but honestly except for the essay ones, i didn't do them because she summarizes them in class anyways but i did take great notes and didn't skip a class. Made 85+ on all 3 exams (30 all MC).
Great class, learned a lot, got 85+ on all tests and essays, slacked off on participation so I got a B, should have been a solid A
You must do the readings (keep up with it) and attend lecture. Overall the class isn't too difficult, but you have to keep up with the work. Be sure to ask questions and attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor made it clear from day one that if you became buddy/buddy with her she would help you out but idk how that exactly worked for out for most people. The one essay and final really messed up a lot of kids grades. Overall the material is pretty interesting, but there is a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters
