reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, super helpful, didn't do the readings that she required, but showed up to each class, and she was super interesting and engaging. Definitely speak up and go to office hours, she's super open to questions, and she's pretty funny too. Tests are pretty doable without doing the readings. Do the study guides and pay attention!

Dr. Osbakken is a wonderful professor. My advice is to sit in the front, speak up in class, and go to office hours. She makes it clear that she will help you grade-wise if you participate in class. The midterms are very straight forward and mostly common sense. While there is a lot of reading, she mostly asks for main ideas of articles.

She was so helpful and really got me interested in the topic. She's very lenient when it comes to grading, and she's extremely empathetic. Attendance is mandatory, but you won't regret going. She does assign A LOT of reading so be prepared.
Content feels meaningful and enjoyable to learn. Genuinely cares about students. Several reviews mention she's understanding and supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had. She is so nice and understanding. I loved her class and the guest speakers she brought in to make the subject more interesting for us. Overall, a very chill professor who genuinely cares about her students.
Super interesting lectures, not a lot of homework, one of my favorite professors ever! She is super personable, would totally take again
Her class layout is straightforward, and her lectures are engaging. She cares about the content and is concerned about your learning, making her an overall good professor.

She is so nice and really cares about her students. I loved this class so much! Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are participation Google forms in the class that are random, but part of the participation grade. Good lectures and a great person.

Dr. O is awesome! She brings positive energy to each class and always puts so much care into her lectures/slides. I learned a ton as a non-kin major, and I would love to take more of her classes!! Take this class if you get the chance.
One of my favorite instructors ever! She is so kind and cares about her students. If you participate and do you're assignments you're set!

This class is meant to prepare students for Japanese work culture, and I think she does a great job of teaching us. She is very caring and understanding. This class is not meant to be easy and that is great because she makes me what to try even hard at becoming fluent in Japanese.

Okada Sensei is a very kind and understanding professor. She helped me ease back into Japanese after an 8-month hiatus and really pushed me to develop my speaking and listening skills. Her class is difficult, but if you really make an effort, it feels more like a fun challenge than anything else.

I took business Japanese with Okada Sensei, and although the content was challenging at times, she tries her best to help us understand. She is always very kind, has helpful office hours, and explains stuff in English when Japanese is difficult. Attendance is important and there are daily quizzes, but they aren't hard to study for. I recommend!

-1% off your final grade for every absence (3 dropped), there are lectures every day!! 3 late = 1 absence, even a second late will be counted!! Ridiculous, as if missing the daily quiz wasn't already a penalty don't take her there are way better professors
take anyone else but her.

Mina's a great professor, does her best to keep the class engaged and is very nice. The class itself was relatively chill, and you'll pass as long as you stay on top of your work. An A is very much possible if you study.

Don't skip class, because if you do you won't know what vocab she's quizzing you on in the next class. There is a homework assignment before every single class, but they are super easy. Her classes are very relaxed, and as long as you're speaking spanish she really doesn't care what you're talking about. She just sets you loose to chat all class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Sometimes she would make me feel dumb in class, and the way that the grammar rules are explained are very hazy. You have to rely on the homework to decipher what grammar rules you're learning in class, because it's very applied in the classroom. She has a lot of energy but doesn't facilitate the best learning environment

I learned SO much in this class. It was a super organized/structured class, which I loved. There were a lot of assignments, but this kept me on track. I wouldn't say it's difficult to get a good grade in this class. I would turn in things late and Prof. Ogando was so accommodating. I would love to take another class with Prof. Ogando.

Condescending, rude. Have to buy a $150 workbook she wrote which you barely use. Grading isnt the best, besides exams and quizzes, some assignments are graded purely on how she feels about you. I could've gotten an A since my exam/quiz/homework grades were high, but I left with an A- because she felt like I wasnt a good student? Make it make sense!

LOVE her. Super funny and nice. You'll work in groups often, but that makes the work easier. Lots of homework, which is expected because its a language class. Not a tough grader, pretty flexible, and overall chill about assignments. Sometimes there are in-class pop quizzes, which mainly count as attendance/participation grades.

SO SWEET. Lots of assignments daily but to be expected in a summer course. Lots of group work. She has office hours 3x a week and is super kind. She checks in for online classes daily. If you keep up with the work, an A is very attainable, even for non-native speakers.

She was sweet as a person and made sure to build a relationship with her class. However she was not very clear with her instructions and many times her rubrics for the projects she assigned were not true to the course. Expect to speak up every once in a while and be asked questions. It's a very interaction-heavy class (as any language course is).

Profe Mina is so sweet and genuinely cares about you. Beware, she can be a tough grader and you will have to work really hard to make an A in her class. With that said, she will help you a lot, just talk to her. I am not a native speaker and found her class rather enjoyable (accent is easily understood). I highly recommend everyone takes her.

Took her summer Business Spanish class online. Very well-organized course, but lots of assignments, so pacing/working ahead was essential for success. Lots of group work, but Profesora was very understanding and accessible when we needed her assistance. I enjoyed the class overall, even if the course content was a little surface-level at times.

I took Mina's business spanish class abroad in Santander, Spain and she was great! Her class is pretty unorganized but she is a very genuine sweet person and wants you to succeed. Just stay on top of your work build rapport and you'll be fine

Profesora was so incredibly sweet. You can tell she wants you to be successful, and grow more with the Spanish language. Her grading can be a little unpredictable, but as long as you show good reflection on assignments and clear effort you should be good. Tests were very easy and I wish I could take her again :)
Great professor, but the class can be pretty difficult. Grading is a little skewed towards tests and smaller assignments so you have to take every assignment seriously.

Absolute Queen! This was a conversation class, so she mainly just cared that you were talking. Short 'journals', 2 exams, and mostly talking assignments. She is so understanding and sweet. Very funny and knows we're all stressed so she tries to make class fun. My Spanish speaking has definitely improved!

Mina is a nice lady, but she wasn't very organized when I took her. I also thought that she picked and chose what she wanted to grade hard on, which changed at the drop of a hat. Things weren't ever clearly defined in class (what I was supposed to be doing, what homework was due, etc) but class was chill and sometimes fun. Overall feel is "eh ok"
By far the best Spanish professor I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think that she is a wonderful person but I do not that she is a good professor. The class is three hours in class and then three hours online but the time spent in class she does not spend teaching. It makes it really hard to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class with her abroad and the work load was extremely heavy but not impossible if you dedicate a couple of hours everyday. Took another class with her at UT. She's pretty available although sometimes forgets to reply to email. Her directions on assignments are confusing so make sure you ASK IF UR CONFUSED
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Class time is used really poorly. It's a self taught class--she doesn't teach anything in class and expects you to preform well on tests without any proper instruction. She's sweet and laid back but not a good professor. Don't take her if you actually want to learn anything/get anything from the class. Also lots of homework.
I loved taking Mina's class. She is such a sweet lady, and her class load is very manageable. Lots of in class participation.

Dr. O is an incredible professor who delivers thought provoking and interesting lectures every class. Attendance isn't required, but you will actually want to come to class just for the interactive discussions and lectures. You can absolutely make an A with reasonable effort, and he is one of my absolute favorite professors I have had so far!
I'm sitting in my first lecture for this class and he already gets a 5, very motivating and inspirational.

Definitely one of the chillest professor that I have ever had. This course is very interesting to learn but attendance is not mandatory. As long as you come the class before the test, he tells you what is on it and has online notes posted on canvas which is super straightforward. He also gives extra credit as well!

Professor Ozyurtcu, is the best professor I have taken thus far at UT. He gives plenty of EC opportunities, and gives amazing lectures. Although attendance is not mandatory I do recommend showing up as the discussions are very interactive, and he explains key concepts that will be on the test.

Loved Dr. O! I didn't realize this was more of a baseline introductory class, as I took it for my minor, but it was still enjoyable. Just come to class as often as you can, take notes, and follow his instructions, and you'll be good to go! I appreciate his engaging teaching style and how he provides solid, real-life examples.

He is honestly the best professor I've had. His lectures aren't mandatory, but I found them to be super interesting and helpful. The class is very interactive, which helps lectures not be so boring. The exams are in blue books, but he tells you what is going to be on them, so just go to class. Amazing professor, I would definitely take him again!

I really liked Dr O as he is such a passionate prof. His lectures aren't mandatory, but I highly recommend going just to learn. 3 tests on blue books and the final is optional. There are also 2 essays, i believe, but they are very easy. Tests are easy, just study. Overall, i loved Dr O and would definitely take his class again

The best professor I have ever had, coming to class felt like attending a TED talk, he was an amazing lecturer and is a very intelligent person in general. Class is very easy if you are engaged and he helps you with every exam. Grading is very very lenient and there are plenty of extra credit options.
Easy and interesting class. Professor Tolga was very entertaining and although the class was not difficult, I would go to class just to hear him lecture because he was great.
Easiest UGS.

This is the best UGS ever. I waited after freshman year jsut to get into his class. he's a caring professor who clearly loves the subject he teaches. Work is manageable, discussion once a week but he incorporates them into class so there's only like 3. Awesome professor.

Whether or not you like sports, his class will be interesting (speaking as someone not super into sports.) I had lots of intrinsic motivation to go to class because his lectures are phenomenal. Great course to cap off senior year

I took sports and innovation UGS. Easiest class ever, and the professor has great lectures and really cares about students. Take this class as your UGS, especially since flags aren't a requirement anymore.

Professor Ozyurtcu was a great UGS professor! His lectures were genuinely interesting & the class had open-note quizzes (T/F, MC, short answers, ~one long essay) plus a year-long project, which he paced well. He also offered multiple extra credit opportunities throughout the year as a bonus. Very manageable!

Class was pretty easy without ever attending a lecture. He was an intriguing speaker. There were three open-note quizzes, with one essay question, T/F, multiple choice (15% each). 5/7 Reading responses, which can be a little lengthy and time-consuming, but easy grade. Two major essays 1200 words (15% each)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. UGS was no-attendance required, but lots of extra credit. Finished with a 108 in the class.  Great guy, amazing professor. Clearly passionate about the topic. Like 4 easy assignments for the entire semester. Take this class.
Easy class, pretty interesting lectures. Grades are mostly dependent on your TA.

I took his UGS Sports and Innovation class and it was the best class I have ever taken. He is amazing!! Super funny and his lectures are amazing. It is an easy A if you just do the assignments. He gives a ton of extra credit. Exams are online on your own time and open note (you don't need to study/memorize just go to lecture and take notes).

TAKE HIS CLASS!! Professor O. makes his lectures very interactive and not boring as he loves what he's teaching. Attendance is not mandatory, but it makes getting an A easier. Discussions are not difficult if you give yourself sufficient time & essays are not too bad. Also has extra credit opportunities at the end.
Dr. Ozyurtcu was definitely one of my favorite professors this semester. His class is super easy and he is overall and great person.
Amazing professor! Great class setting and easy going. Help me a lot during my hard time. I actually learned a lot from this class than what I expected.

Truly believe this man is an amazing teacher who cares about his students a lot. The UGS class was relatively easy even if you do even the bare minimum. I found myself very interested in the topics he covered in class, and he made the lectures very entertaining whether you are a big sports enthusiast or not. Would highly recommend him as a teacher.

Ozyurtcu is a very down to earth guy that wants the best for his students. The class was super easy and had virtually no work, but if you took the time to pay attention and participate it was also very interesting. His showing of the process of innovation through the lens of sports is a very enjoyable break to fit into a tough schedule.

(FOR UGS 303) Dr. O is awesome, definitely take any class of his. 3 Quizzes are a cakewalk if you go to class, Group project- everyone got a 100, most other stuff is completion-based. Lectures, while not mandatory, are super cool. He's also just an awesome and interesting professor overall. Most UGS classes suck, not this one, so grateful for Dr. O

I've never written an RMP review before but I had to because Dr. O is simply the best! The class is very interesting and I was actually excited to attend his lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should go! You won't regret it!

Professor Tolga's KIN 347: Historical & Ethical Issues in Sport was exceptional! Engaging discussions, comprehensive historical insights, and a nuanced view of ethical considerations. Highly recommend!

Prof Tolga has been one of my favorite professors at UT. He is a genuine person and a good teacher. Attendance is not mandatory but if you show up for class and pay attention-you'll get an A in the class. Prof Tolga makes you feel like a person and not just a student, love this dude.

Take Prof. O! He's a very chill and understandable professor who makes the lectures enjoyable. There are only a few quizzes, reading responses, and 2 essays for the semester, but he offers extra credit! I highly recommend taking his class!

Dr. O is pretty much as chill as a professor can get. Attendance is not mandatory but class is cool enough to want to go. Not too political and always opens up the room for cool discussions. Kinda assignment heavy with reading responses due every couple weeks but only 2 medium papers due and a bunch of extra credit opportunities. Easy A IMO.

Dr. O is one of the best teachers at UT, and this class was phenomenal. It really did not feel like I was going to a class, and his lectures were amazing. There are so many extra credit opportunities that you can have an A in the class in no time. Put the effort in early, and you will not have to stress about this class at the end of the semester.

Dr. O is a great professor, he is a very caring person and really wants everyone to do well in his class. Yes, in class is all lectures and taking notes from the slides, but (1) he opens the room up to good, interesting discussions and (2) he posts the slides so you can check them outside of class. 10/10 guy.

Dr. O is a top 2 professor at UT, and he isn't #2. Super fun lectures, cracks jokes, and loves holding casual conversation with his students. The class requires effort for sure, but an A is absolutely attainable and there is plenty of extra credit throughout the semester to help you out. I highly recommend him.

This course requires you to read and put in a bit of effort. Other than that, you should get no lower than a B+ as most of the assignments are graded lightly, with extra credit abundant throughout the semester. One of my favorite personalities for a professor so far who tries to engage students with the content.

Take!!!! Dr. O was really passionate about his class. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but he sometimes gave extra credit for attending class. There wasn't a final exam, and there were only essays instead of exams. In my opinion, the content was really interesting and not difficult, and I would definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Ozyurtcu is an amazing professor that is sometimes overlooked for KIN majors but needs to be taken at least once!! He is such a kind professor who is super understanding if you make your situation known. Pretty easy class if you keep up with the readings, all of which are super interesting! Definitely will take him again if I can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading and you need to put effort into your reading responses to get a 100 but it's easy. There are extra credit opportunities, use them! You don't have to go to lecture but there are in-class assignments for credit so it is recommended but no big deal if you miss once. I'd recommend Dr. O's class, fun and learned a lot!

Loved taking Dr. O's class! As long as you put some time and effort into your work, you'll get an A. He also had many extra credit opportunities, so definitely use them. Content was interesting and there were no exams. Just one quiz which was open notes. Big on reading responses but if you put effort into them, you'll get a 100 on each one.

Dr. O is amazing! His class isnt too tough, it is reading heavy, but the content is very interesting. He is accessible outside of class and wants all his students to get an A. He is a true gem at UT. If you get the chance to take him, do it, you wont regret it.

Dr. O is by far the most caring and understanding professor I have had at my time at UT. Class is reading heavy, but its interesting stuff. His lectures also add good insight into the topics we are studying. Take his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very fun class with a very passionate professor. The class itself might get a little rowdy since it's full of sport fanatics but it's perfect if you follow sports rigorously. Easy class and homework. There will be some pop up quizzes but you can make up 2 later in the semester. Little bit of reading and writing as well but doable. TAs were awesome

Dr. O. is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. The class is not too hard but he is very engaging and extremely caring. He has a very kind spirit and he will work with you on anything. I was very helpful and understanding with me when I had COVID and had a family loss. If anyone asked I would heavily recommend taking his class.

Dr. O is pretty chill and loves what he teaches about, but I did find his lectures a bit dry. The readings are definitely something you NEED to do for exams - practically word for word questions. The written assignments are easy, and the profs are willing to help you with anything. Make sure you nail the ethics part - those will recycle each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. O has been my favorite professor I've ever had! His class is super interesting if you're interested in sports. The tests are heavily based on weekly articles, so read them! He's very caring and will help with absolutely anything you need. There are a couple writing assignments but the rubric is very detailed and they aren't very long. Take him!

Dr. O was my fav professor this semester! If you're interested in controversial sport topics, you'll love this class. He assigns a lot of readings, which are the test, so READ ALL OF THE ARTICLES! I would describe him as an "old millennial" who gets his students' perspective and actually cares. Extra credit is offered during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tolga is by far my favorite professor i've had at UT. He's the kindest man and the most amazing lecturer. I showed up to class exhausted every day but I was always able to stay attentive. I would recommend going to class because he gives test hints typically and goes over the articles you read. His lectures are really good.
Dr. O is great. Read the readings, and follow instructions and you will get an A.

Great professor and great class. Never showed up to class but the ones i did the lectures were interesting. Easy A but you HAVE to read the documents he gives you. Very nice guy and very understanding. Would take him again for sure.
great went from B to an A- in the last months of the semester. Doable class, just study and get help from peers/TA.

Tolga is one of my favorite professors I've had so far! He's so funny, super kind, and is an awesome guy. The articles we read are typically super interesting. If you love sports and talking about the crazy things in the sports world-- this class will be so interesting and enjoyable to you. He also wants all of his students to succeed in his class!

Tolga is a great professor. He is more focused on making sure you understand things and get things done correctly, rather than the grade he gives. Definitely a professor you would want to take again. He sets up the class so you not only have a fair chance to get an A, but also so that you actually learn what you are doing right or wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Make flashcards of the terms she posts before exam and review thoroughly, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Brien makes the online lectures very engaging, and you'll definitely learn something if you put in the effort. Your grade is basically decided by your 2 exams, and the exams can be overwhelming to prepare for as the review sheet has no definitions, only terms. Nonetheless, she is a great professor, and an A is attainable for sure.

310L async by Dr. O'Brien was great. Lectures by her are well-presented, especially for an online format. Non-test assignments are really easy, and the tests are not much harder than that. You are given an all-encompassing review sheet that trivializes them.

Such an amazing professor! I've taken a few of her courses and each one has been extremely insightful. Dr. O'Brien's sense of humor makes her lectures so entertaining and full of interesting, exclusive facts. All lectures are uploaded online. Highly recommend!

Your grade is based on two 50 MC tests. She provides a 300+ term study sheet (no definitions) about a week or so before. Lectures aren't helpful. Genuinely, only study terms throughout semester and you'll be fine. I studied about 30 hours for exam 2 (Quizlet) and got the exact score I needed for an A in the class. Very frustrating class for a core

Dr. O'Brien's lectures are absolutely hilarious and interesting.  While she does go on tangents, they are relevant to her point and she makes sure that she covers the material as well.  All I would suggest is that you do the reading, but you can get by on lectures alone.

She is the GOAT. Lectures are recorded, so I barely went to class. Averages on all the exams were a high 80 and the content was actually interesting. She offered 4 points of easy extra credit and the papers were not too bad. Still not a blow off class, but if you start studying for the test like 2 days before you should be fine. I recommend!!

Her online lectures are knowledgeable but VERY LONG. It's hard to do it all in one sitting. The tests are the majority of the grade and are difficult. Rather than a real review she just lists 300+ terms to memorize for a randomized 50 question test that is 30% of the grade (for EACH test). She does not round up, no real extra credit.

Knowledgeable and seems sweet in lectures, but this class needs to be changed. Previous years didn't have the test; this semester, they do. The tests are difficult. 300+ words memorized along with concepts and history, no notes, 50 questions 50 mins, 1 point extra credit, no curve no more extra credit offered. No proper review or study guide given.

For a core, this class simply isn't fair. I don't understand how they switched the to closed note exams without bothering to offer more extra credit or opportunities to do better. 50 minutes and 50 questions that are pulled at random out of 300 is insane. You're much better off taking this at a cc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Giving myself a B+ but I haven't taken the test yet. Class load is generally light, but the exams are a lot of material over 300 words ALL need to be memorized, an 50 come from the bank for the test. You should study the moment the review becomes available to you, and that *still* may not be enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Do not be fooled by previous reviews. Assignments are easy, but your two exams? Get ready to be given a "review" that consists of 300 terms and only terms. You can study them all you want, and watch the 30 minute lectures, but you're only gonna be tested on 50 of them. The extra credit will also do nothing for you grade. So thanks for nothing ig.

for the fall 25 semester a lot of things changed like no extra credit and honorlock for exams. exams demand a lot of preparation no matter how many notes and times you have watched lectures due to them being 300+ terms with no definitions. the weekly workload was very light, but the only two tests can drop your grade drastically.

The workload is light and relatively very easy, although the test preparation is awful. You get 300+ terms with no definitions as your ONLY true review before the test. There is no other resources except re-reading your textbook/slides. Good lecturer but horrible at genuinely preparing you for the tests.

Yk that scene from mean girls when she's writing in the book screaming and crying. That's me with this course. Exams require honorlock and you can't use any notes, despite being able to use them on assignments and quizzes. I'd rather she say we can't use notes on anything because why have I been writing stuff down just to not use them on exams???
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ALL reviews before fall 25 are INVALID. The class changed and now has HonorLock proctored and closed note exams. There are only TWO exams for the whole semester each with about 400 terms. You can study for days, and still do bad on the exams, if you don't memorize every single term. Such a horrible class that you unfortunately have to take for CORE

One of my favorite professors in the government department. If you have to take a government class, I strongly recommend you look for her. Her lectures are very funny and very informative. You can tell she's really passionate and is great at oversimplifying topics that are difficult to understand.

The lectures are long, only to be followed by 5-10 question assignments that often have nothing to do with her lectures. Taking notes is close to pointless and time consuming. Midterm and final questions are pulled from a random test bank, so be prepared to memorize literally 300 terms, only to get a random 50. Tests are hard but assignments arent.
literally just watch the lectures and study vocab before the tests, theyre common sense questions

I really like this professor but studying 300+ terms and concepts with only 50 tested on closed note was just not fair. I spent a lot of time studying and came out with a medicore score. Questions are pulled from a huge test bank and what you get really determines your fate. Overall not the class it used to be.

Exams are no longer open note or open book, which means knowing all 300 possible terms on the exam is up to you. Everything else in the course is admittedly easy, but the tests are each 27% of your grade. Her lectures are engaging, but certainly not enough to prepare for the exam alone. Take good notes, start studying early, and you might be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor O'Brien is easily my favorite professor this semester, although we have never met in person. Her lectures are engaging, she's quick to a joke, and it is very clear that she is extremely proficient in what she's teaching. Her lectures cover the curriculum while providing interesting and entertaining historical tidbits.
Took this class during the summer and it was super easy. Make sure to take good notes from the textbook (it's free). There's writing assignments and two exams with lots of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. O'Brien is an entertaining, passionate, and knowledgeable professor when it comes to discussing a wide range of aspects of government, which helped me focus and gain a better overall understanding. I took the online class (5 weeks), a bit speedy at times, so be sure to manage your time well. Fun, informative, and easy class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy. Everything online, unproctored, and she offers easy extra credit. She is also passionate about the material. You should take her for your government requirement.
This class was VERY manageable and you can do it on your own time

While I didn't directly take Dr. O'Brien's class, she ran the lectures and material. She's very entertaining and as someone who is bored by gov't, she made it engaging and fun. There is a textbook but I often would reference it than read it because her lectures covered nearly everything. She was awesome!
Great class to take for government core credit. Not very hard and good professor.
easiest government class ever, there are assignments due every week but they're all super easy. exams are open book and open note which was super helpful. overall not a stressful class at all
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The best course to take to understand government at UT. So glad I took this course
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: guys trust just take this class

An amazing professor to say the least, she is very passionate about history. This course is online with 2 assignments each week, some long some short, with the entire week to complete. These assignments and 2 tests are open book and open note. There are extra credit opportunities and she gives reminders of due dates. TAKE THIS CLASS!

One of the easiest classes I've taken at UT. I don't know how else to say this but this class is super easy and very low maintenance. Just get your things done on time and you're chilling. The exams are open notes and open textbook so there is no reason you don't get an A in this class.

best professor for asynch gov, super easy with only 1-2 assignments per week that take around 10 minutes each. the long part is watching the lectures but tbh you don't really need them as everything is open note w the textbook. not hard at all

Dr. O'Brien is such a great lecturer, she makes class more engaging. She can go off on story tangents, but imo they make the class less boring than it would be otherwise. Tests can sometimes be confusing and cover more obscure topics, but they aren't that bad if you study and read the textbook. Overall, I would highly recommend taking her classes.

I cannot recommend this class enough. I took the online 310L with O'Brien, and it was the most organized, low-stress, and straightforward course I have taken. If you watch all the lectures and take notes, the tests are manageable. She is very passionate about what she teaches. If you need 310L, online with O'Brien is the absolute best option.

Professor O'Brien is an amazing professor and is truly passionate about what she teaches. However, this class is very lecture-heavy, and you are only graded on a few things, which makes it difficult to get a good grade. There are three tests and assignments that take up little of your grade. She is a good professor, though I recommend taking her.

Professor O'brien is a good professor and has hilarious dry humor but you have to pay attention. There are only 4 assignments and 3 tests in total. Take notes in class. Read the textbook. Memorize. You can pass the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor O'Brien is a gem. She knows what she is talking about but explains everything simply. Class is straightforward 3 tests 50 MCQ, she gives a study guide for each test. You don't need to read the textbook just watch the lectures and know the study guide for an easy A. Lectures are all recorded and attendance is not mandatory.

I went to the class a few times, but found it better to watch her lectures online because she talked so fast. The tests are easy if you study and depedning on how the class did she will give extra credit. I also would go to her office hours and she was always very helpful and loves to talk to her students. only 3 tests worth 30% and 2 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is not hard, there is just A LOT of content that you have to memorize before taking the tests. Even though I hated her class and the way she taught (reading PowerPoint but not explaining anything), I was still able to do well.

OBrien loves gov, so lectures are cool - but youre graded on 3 tests and 2 assignments. Tests: 50 qs, 60 min, open note, but cant go backwards. This made me realize I had ADD and hurt my grade (and mental health lowkey) also, some test questions are made to trick rather than teach. Some prefer this, but it wasnt for me. Also, no xtra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Brien is a great professor! She makes the lectures interesting and comparable to real world things to keep them interesting. Textbook not needed. Exams are easy, its clear whether or not you know the material. Only downside is 90% if grade is based off of 3 exams. 2 easy assignments for other 10%. An easy A if you pay attention and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: O'Brien is absolutely hilarious and always manages to make her GOV lectures fun. You only have 3 tests and 2 easy assignments, so their is really no tedious busy work for this class. I definitely learned a lot and I am disappointed she is not teaching GOV 312 because I would have loved to take a class with her again. Txtbook is mostly unnecessary.

Best class I've taken at UT. Professor O'Brien was easygoing, very knowledgeable, and really cares about her students. Rambles a bit but that's because she's really passionate about her lessons. Can't recommend her enough.
Professor O'Brien/s lectures were entertaining and informative. I did not read the textbook and did fine on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this professor, you can tell she loves her subject. shes good at lecturing and really funny. the only downside to this cource is that your grade is solely based on 5 assignments. 3 major test and 2 small assignments. so you have to make sure to do really well on them, attendance isnt required but I actually liked going so you will to

Super nice and tries really hard for boring gov lectures to be exciting. Entire grade is based on 3 tests but its a good thing because they are very easy so there is almost no work in the class but studying the night before. Highly recommend

I did not totally care for her lectures, but this was was extremely easy. I put minimal effort in but basically if you know anything about the government, you will be fine. Each test is 30% of your grade, but they were open note and open online tests. The tests seem daunting, but I recommend for a ridiculously easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is easy, but there are only five assignments (3 tests + 2 paper assignments), so you have to do well on all of them. Tests are straightforward, and she gives a study guide before each one. Paper assignments are super short and simple. Go to lectures. They help prep you for exams. Exams are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are almost your entire grade and there are not many of them but all of the questions come from the lectures and book and are very straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Brien is a good lecturer who very clearly articulates course objectives. She assigns tests as take-home, without proctoring, making it pretty reasonable to get an A in the class. If you put in a decent amount of effort, you will get an A in GOV 310L with O'Brien.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A solid choice. She is a very seasoned professor but very personable and understanding. 90% of the class was based off of 3 open-book/note tests and the other 10% was small paper assignments. Her lectures were entertaining and offered personal anecdotes which I thought was cool.

O'Brien is a fantastic professor and gives entertaining and educational lectures. Her knowledge of American Government and Politics is extensive and easily shown through her lectures - she has examples for everything. Getting an A is very easy as long as you pay attention to her lectures. There are 2 easy assignments and 3 straightforward tests.

Professor O'Brien is an amazing lecturer and I love coming to class! Your grade is based on two short ridiculously easy assignments and 3 tests which are an easy A if you pay attention to lecture and take some notes. By far the best gov professor and I plan on taking another one of her classes in the future.
She's genuinely the best professor I've ever had at UT. A great lecturer, her class is really interesting, and she has very clear expectations. She's very caring and kind as well.

Professor O'Brien is amazing, to say the least. I saw her lectures as a podcast given that they are very laid back and insightful. She truly cares about what she is teaching and is direct about what she expects you to know. Tests were open notes so take good notes. The readings were not bad at all 5-10 pg. per class. Usually interesting material.
Amazing professor with great lectures. Truly felt like I didn't have to work super hard to learn from her. Has a great way of conveying information to students that makes sense.

She is so fun, and has so much knowledge. I took her politics and film class and loved it. She doesn't make attendance mandatory, uploaded all the lectures online, and was always available thru email. Oh, and she's hilarious. I loved this professor so much I'm taking another class from her next semester. I highly recommend this class.

Absolutely amazing professor. Was an absolute blast to listen to all semester, would do it again. Most of your grade is centered around 3 non-cumulative exams, with some participation-credit quizzes sprinkled in. This class was a saving grace against some of the harder classes I had this semester.

Take her for Gov 310L, you won't be disappointed. She knows how to make tests and knows how to give good lectures. I learned so much from her and it's amazing to talk to her out of class as well. The actual work is slight, some quizzes and the tests were easy if you payed attention and/or reviewed.

Lectures are clear & to the point, she'll occasionally get off topic but she's funny so it makes class enjoyable. Watch lectures, some of the test questions you'll only know from watching them. The test outlines are helpful. Tests are 85% of grade, 50 minutes for 50 MC questions. If you're into politics, take her class. Study & you can get an A.

I took Shannon (yes, you can call her by her 1st name) for Engineering Communications and her class was AMAZING! Since the class has a writing flag, I expected the worst. That was totally NOT the case. She was very engaging and her lectures are meant to help you in the outside world. Attendance was once a week. Definitely would take her again.

Dr.O'Brien makes her class interesting and I learned a lot through the semester. This class includes a lot of reading, and there is no grade for participation or attendance. Because there are only two homework assignments, most of your final grade is based on your test scores but if you follow her study guides they are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved her. she was cool, cared about gov and really only cared about making sure you are an educated american. tests and paper assignments are very straight forward. She cares a lot about her students, a month after semester ended she sent an email to us saying to email any questions we may have about the upcoming election, politics or the system
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The only gradable work in the class are the tests and "assignments" which consist of questions like "who is the governor of Texas"  easy 100. Now the tests are not hard by any means but you just have to know details. recommend reading textbook because she talks really fast in lecture. I got an 89 and she wouldn't give extra credit though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very straightforward, right to the point professor. A lot of busy work (letters, resumes, etc.), but no class presentations. I liked how she structured the class to end much earlier before the end of the semester. Very clear grading guidelines. If you do the work, follow the rules, and implement feedback, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easiest A ever. The two assignments are short and FITB (also only 5 points each). You get study guides for tests (list of terms). Memorize it  A. Textbook and class are not mandatory. Showed up 3 times (for the three tests) and didn't get a grade lower than a 96. If you took AP Gov in HS, you'll know a lot of the study guide, too.

Before this, I didn't care about government but O'Brien's entertaining and funny lectures changed that. Enabled me to understand the importance of american governmens along with its intriguing intracices. As long you take notes from lecture and learn them, an A/A-/B+ is very achievable. Excellent choice for GOV310L and I would highly recommend :)

O'Brien is overall a really nice professor. Sometimes she rambles during lectures though. Attendance isn't mandatory and she posts her lectures online. Exams are short, but are 90% of the grade, so you cannot mess up on them. They're also hit or miss with difficulty. She is a fair prof though, go to office hours and she will help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVED Shannon. The class was super chill, tests were straight forward and the assignments were super easy. As long as you attend lecture and take good notes, youre guaranteed at least a B+. She makes things really easy to understand and lectures are really engaging. Theres a bunch of quizlets out there to help you study for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shannon is an amazing woman who truly cares about her students. She gives a test review for each test so you clearly know exactly what to expect. Her lectures are funny and engaging. She can often get off-topic which is entertaining and makes the material memorable. I would take every class she teaches at UT!

She is a really nice woman but i will say that the grade is made up of 3 tests that are 30% each. The other 10% are paper assignments that are easy. The test i found difficult, which is kinda unfair because that is your whole grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was honestly my favorite class this semester. She has a way of making this class pretty interesting and funny. I genuinely learned a lot from her class. Tests are mostly based on lecture, so if you take detailed lecture notes and study them, you'll do good on the tests. I highly recommend taking her class!

Dr. O'Brien is a fun professor that is very knowledgeable on numerous subjects related to American politics and history. Her lectures are always very entertaining and engaging and constitute a bulk of the course material. Because of this, attendance is important even though it's not mandatory. Overall a great class and professor.
Totally bombed the first exam. Went to office hours and she went over the WHOLE exam with me and explained any questions I got wrong. Her caring character and passion for teaching is unmatched!

I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot. Shes a funny lecturer. Although attendance isnt mandatory, her outlines are vague, so its important to take notes. Her exams are 90% of the grade, so you have to do well. She does have questions you would only know if you went to lecture. There are lots of good quizlets. I didnt use the textbook.

O'Brien's a great choice for GOV 310L. She's pretty funny and while the course material is pretty boring, her lectures are pretty engaging. 3 tests (30% each) and 2 easy HW assignments (5% each), so doing well on the tests are crucial. Lectures aren't required but are recommended for the tests. Didn't read the textbook but studied its definitions.

Shannon is awesome. I took her for Urban Politics, which is a pretty easy course. She lectures with a powerpoint, and is really knowledgable and funny. Paper assignments are easy, tests are easy (as long as you take good notes and STUDY). She is also super cool in office hours, which I recommend going to. She'll chat with you about anything!

Dr. O'Brien is a bit quirky but nonetheless a good prof. and solid choice. Lectures were only 50 minutes. She's concise, clear, and to the point. Scantron tests were pretty easy (though beware she does like to throw just 1 or 2 trick questions on there probably to see if you read the textbook) and the other two projects were a breeze. Would recommd

Sometimes she goes off on a lot of tangents. Overall great. She sometimes says randoms things in lecture that are one question on a test, but she also makes a review guide that has every term you need to know for the test, so if you skip occasionally, it is still easy to make an A. The textbook is easy, but you don't really need it to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were kinda boring but she inserted some humor sometimes. I stopped showing up to class after the first test and got a B+ in the class (As on everything but the last test). You write papers on movies she asks you to watch and the tests are straight forward. I suggest reading the book if youre gonna skip class. Her online notes are vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Though all her lecture slides are online, you should go to class if you want an A (her slides only served as bullet points for her lectures, her tests have a lot of materials from the lectures). No essays, very shorts 2 assignments (fill in the blank type). No books needed (I just googled all the study guide terms). 3 Tests all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Engineering communications. It was a good class. gives a lot of professional advice (resumes, interview, workplace, and communication etiquette). four 2-3 page papers over different engineering topic/cases. it was her first semester teaching this so things make get change. no tests or final but had midterm packets

Professor OBrien is organized, clear, and helpful. She explains concepts in ways that are relevant and useful both inside and outside of the classroom! The class is very easy if youre willing to come to class and do the smallest bit of studying for tests! Highly recommend her!

This was probably the most organizers class Ive taken. It followed almost perfectly to the schedule on the syllabus so that was really helpful. I went to every class, and a lot of questions on the test were from lecture, but you could get by without going. She doesnt take attendance!

I found her teaching methods extremely lacking, & her behavior unprofessional. My education is my priority, & when I tried to talk with her about my concerns regarding her teaching method, she was inappropriately rude & absolutely unhelpful. I have no qualms about dropping this incompetent Professors class, & I advise all students to do the same.

I LOVED Shannon's class. Great intro professor, makes it interesting for all the non-majors. Very clear on grading, tells you exactly what to study on the tests. As long as you take good notes in class, do the assignments (super easy), and read the textbook, it's incredibly easy to get an A. Also, she's super helpful in office hours and very kind.

Professor O'Brien is brilliant and funny which makes her lectures a pleasure to sit through. They aren't required but just reading the book does not cut it and the combination of book+lectures helps (or at least it did me). I really learned a lot and it's useful information that you can use later in life.

3 tests including the final all 30% each. 2 very easy papers (basically fill in the blank) which are 5% each. Best GOV 310L teacher for sure, very sarcastic and funny. Go to the lectures because she often gives hints on whats going to be on the test. The tests are very detail oriented, make sure to study the slides and the book if possible.

Dr. O'Brien is a cool and funny teacher. This class isn't hard. Just don't overthink her tests. She really doesn't try to trick you. I would recommend using quizlet to study! Go to her office hours. She's super chill and easy to talk to. I overall enjoyed this class and she made this subject intresting. Lastly, you don't have a final! Great teacher

This is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Dr. O'Brien gives "study guides" which are basically just lists of terms that could show up on the exam. I went to the lectures and only opened the textbook before the exam to refresh on some terms. Easy A!

Professor O'Brien is an awesome professor! Highly recommend her if you're looking to get that gov credit. Class is graded on 3 exams (30% each) and two writing assignments (5% and they are not "papers", they're more like worksheets). Just make sure you read the textbook, do the reviews, and the class should be a pretty easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: politics and film was a fun class, lectures were interesting, attendance is optional

Attendance not mandatory. Recommend going: she makes things easy to understand. Test heavy with 2 short papers. First test got a 92. Multiple choice, typically 50-65 questions. Only 45 minutes to finish. Reading textbook helps a lot, especially taking notes on readings. Gives test reviews (outline with terms on test) NOT cumulative exams. easy A.

I took this because it was a core requirement, but I loved this course with O'Brien so much that I added government as a minor. She's hilarious, easy to follow, and posts lectures online. She talks to students before class and is just a really accessible and amazing professor. Only grades are 3 exams and 2 take-home assignments. Easy A if you study
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's that class that you think you can skip and still make an A but you can't
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a pretty chill class and I certainly wasn't expecting that based on so many rumors heard about the UT government classes before the semester began. Your grade is just based on three tests and two easy assignments throughout the semester. Definitely take her if you need to take government here.

Professor O'Brien is great. Go to class - her lectures are enjoyable. She doesn't take attendance but you won't do as well if you don't go.  She really gets to the core of Urban Politics.  Also, go visit her in office hours. She is a wealth of information and very easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shannon is the best. Very funny and super personable. Only three tests and two assignments throughout the semester and they are very easy if you go to class and pay attention.

Professor O'Brien is great! Three exams, two assignments- an A is very doable. She's super sarcastic and definitely likes to point out the interesting parts of Urban Politics rather than the boring stuff. If you're a gov major, take her class!!
I really enjoyed this class. Shannon is such a funny lady and she teaches very well. Exams were very easy, as well as the assignments, as long as you pay attention in class. Happy I took her.

She's a great professor, she loves what she does and always has weird, quirky stories about historical figures that match her personality perfectly. You'll have a good time in her class, but don't try and get anything past her, she hates when things don't go her way.

if you want an A, my advice for you is do not skip class. be there and listen and take notes. start the study guide as soon as possible. it is not hard but people just don't pay attention, and skip class. you can still get a B by doing that but if you want an A, follow my advice. she is nice and helpful, funny also.
Really knowledgeable and helpful. All M/C tests very easy and two easy assignments. Fun class to go to, but attendance isn't necessary. Gives reviews before tests.

She speaks softly even with a microphone, so make sure you sit at the front if you want to be able to hear every word. I recommend reading the book and attending lecture because that will make the difference between an A and a B. She is really laid back and answers e-mails within an hour. She makes corny jokes and provides silly facts.
I loved this class. O'Brien is such a funny lady and she teaches very well. Exams were very easy, as well as the assignments, as long as you pay attention in class. Happy I took her.
Horribly boring class, but she's a pretty cool teacher. I was late for my final and she was totally understandable about it. Be sure you don't just know definitions.
Funny and knowledgable. Do the reviews and pay a bit of attenton and youll get a good grade.

One would think that a government class would be boring, but that is not the case here. Professor Bow (O'Brien) is simply fun to listen to. Class was always interesting, and the assignments weren't hard. Take this professor if you can.
She is pretty funny, and the class is really easy. Don't really need to go to class, just fill out the review using the book or the internet and you would be fine on the tests.

Just show up to class and take good notes; you don't need the book. She makes government interesting, and this is coming from an engineer. Easy A, just study your notes the night before the tests. Four exams, noncumulative.
She gives you a review before each test and the test are straight from the back of the book. You don't really have to go to class or read. Just do the review and study it.

Professor gives a study guide which includes questions that may be on the quizzes, yet grades you on a criteria that isn't given to you during or before the quiz. Quiz comments afterwards reference the specific things you were missing (that were not asked of), which you of course, lose points for. Boring lectures, participation is graded.
Genuinely grades everything too tough, not sure if anything would satisfy her. Also weirdly passive aggressive? Exams are annoying to prepare for, doable but her grading is over specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: she is very nice and cares about students, weekly readings are easy and straightforward. We did do a couple presentations but they werent hard. Do have to do a 8-10 page essay end of the year. Overall easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was easy and most assignments could be completely quickly as well. Lectures however might be the most boring I've ever had before. She sorta mumbles everything so even when you attempt to pay attention, it all goes through your head anyways. All depends on how nice your TA is, but every grade I recieved was generous or reasonable

lectures were god awful and boring. Make sure you do all assignments which takes up literally 20 min of ur time each week, theyre also easy af. attendance mandatory but only 40% show up.Easy class just know final is in person essay :/ and professor is just bad at lecturing. she does not know how to word things in a way that people can understand
She clearly knows what she's talking about and cares about her job, so it is a good class, her lectures are just really really boring. Not a hard class, just a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I didn't enjoy this course, but I think that had less to do with professor Zazueta than the intro course structure itself. I would definitely be interested in taking an upper division course with this prof.

The reading assignments and writing assignments are all relatively easy. Attendance makes a large part of the grade, but the lectures can be quite boring and dull (attendance rate was usually 50% even though it's mandatory). The class can be informative if you were interested in the topic before. She's a great person, just not the best lecturer.
Professor Zazueta's class is weak and uninteresting. She is not well prepared. I did not learn at all. We need better professors at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LAS 301 was a really straightforward class with short weekly readings and occasional group work. Participation and attendance are a large part of the grade though!

Lots of reading, but there is also plenty of room for discussion during to class which helps in understanding the material. Interesting lectures, and encourages students make informed claims, which isn't easy esp. for younger students, but helps develop critical thinking and research skills. Caring, reasonable, and willing to work with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm surprised there aren't any reviews for Zazueta. As an LAS major she was recommended to me by multiple people and I can say that the class was amazing. Homework isn't heavy, but she's set up the class to learn and gives fair grading (easy if you are strong at writing). She's caring, smart, gives interesting work, and encourages participation.

Cares very deeply for all her students. Lectures can get boring, but it is the material that's dense. Practice as many problems as you can, especially harder proofs. Weekly quizzes are not too hard, but not reflective of exam difficulty. There is a lack of exam prep material, so the textbooks/online resources are your best bet. Costudy is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't really too hard, but the homework and quizzes were pretty confusing at the beginning of the semester, getting worse as the semester went on. The professor might seem intimidating, but is very nice and understanding when you actually talk to her. However, lectures are very boring and NO PRACTICE TESTS.

Dr. Parikh is a great lecturer for CS311 -- take her! She is incredibly busy (hence a procrastinator), but she is kind. Ask her good questions in lecture -- save simpler ones for the TAs, who have the time. This course requires a lot of practice outside of class to succeed, so use office hours, co-study and the textbook. And start homework early!!

She arrives to class late and posts test locations late. She answers too many students' questions. She jokes around, for which people hate her, but without the humor the material would be very boring. She offers many examples of proofs and conjectures in the practice sets with plenty of office hours. Practice set solutions are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although this subject is difficult, she doesn't make it any easier with her teaching. She was really irresponsible, openly admitting to making the exams the morning of the test day. For the final exam, she didn't release seating charts until 3 hours before the scheduled time, and the first time she released it she got it wrong and had to fix it!

The subject itself is already difficult, and it's worse because of the teacher. To a certain extent it is the material, but Parikh fails to prepare the class for the difficulty in the exams because she barely goes over hard proofs during lecture and only includes them in problem sets. Material available to prep for exams are also hard to come by.

Odds are you will be forced to take Parikh so just know that this class starts out pretty easy for the first 3-4 weeks then there is a massive difficulty spike once you get to proofs. Also, always make sure to do the problem set before the quiz as the content is heavily based on either the material in discussion or the material on the problem set.
Weekly quizzes on material learned, watch the prelecture videos fully for participation grade. No practice exams for midterms but problem sets are good practice. Attendance taken at lecture.

She wasn't really a good teacher. Lectures were drab and boring, and she wasn't very accepting of student questions. Section TAs were decent, but not great. I did like the format of the class as it was well-organized.
take anyone else

Parikh is genuinely a sweet professor if you know her fr. She seems scary but she's actually chill. Long lectures, lots of material, make sure to lock in. Participation grade based on videos and attendance. Study A LOT every day and prep for dreadful weekly quizzes. TAs are goated they lowkenuinely carried my grade.
Loved Dr. Parikh she was very nice and accessible. However, I thought the class focused way too much on format rather than mathematical correctness. I wish she would focus more on the math
Was actually a good professor just annoying exams and section.

This is kind of a weed-out class, so be prepared and be prepared for it to be confusing. Still, I think Dr.Parikh does a good job explaining, but make sure to be engaged, because while she doesn't mind "bad questions," if she thinks you're not engaged, she will call you out, also, don't be on your phone or AirPods; she'll call you out there, too.
The class teaches very little. The effort given by the instructional staff no where near matches the effort asked from the students. The class is lazy, unorganized, and uninteresting.

she was the worst professor i had so far in college. she genuinely wants you to fail get ready for YouTube university because she explains the concepts in the most complicated way she can. whole class basically bombed the second exam (avg 65) because she failed to go over any complicated questions CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSE FRAIJ CHOOSEHIM

It's a difficult class made exponentially harder by the fact that the professor is just genuinely mean. Instructor is unapproachable and actively shames students for asking questions in class. Does not provide adequate resources to prepare for exams.

The worst part of this class was the weekly quizzes worth 23% of your grade. I studied for these quizzes and had LOTS of points lost for tiny mistakes. I'm not sure what the averages were but me and my friends consistently got 70s despite doing great on exams and understanding and participating completely during section. inconsistent between TAs

Difficult class, especially if its your first proof class, but you will survive if you work hard. Lectures are boring but very helpful. Quizzes and hw every week, 3 exams but not weighted horribly. Worst part is lack of practice materials, but plenty of TA's and study sessions to help. Overall, difficult and boring but not a bad class.

This class did prepare me well for other courses. Remember that the participation grade is measured through pre-class videos and attendance. The pre-class videos are timed. My grade would have been like a B ~ B+, but it dropped to C- after getting nearly a 0 for participation.

Parikh's class is tough, but using resources like Unstuck ai alongside the textbook can make it manageable. Attendance is a must, and exam feedback is hit-or-miss, but the content itself is reasonable.

Class is hard but Parikh is a good professor. Lectures, and understanding of the homework are very important to success. Exams are unpredictable but you will be fine if you engage in lecture, and she does a good job of answering questions so make sure you ask.

As a professor, I'd say Parikh is overall fine. The lectures are very boring. I honestly had a hard time with the class because much of it had me relying on intuition so I felt extremely stupid. A huge issue was that the exam was more difficult than the material we went over in class. I'd suggest trying to get the other 311 professor instead.

Make sure you watch the pre-lectures the whole semester. Since there isn't a lot of study material for tests, I would recommend the textbook, specifically the questions at the end of each chapter (one of the midterm questions was pretty much exactly repeated).

She doesn't really come off as wanting her students to succeed. She's not particularly approachable and can be demeaning when you ask questions. The study materials are gatekept (unlike 314). The quizzes and tests will have some questions that are significantly harder than what is gone over in class. Test grading is nitpicky and harsh.

Switch to Fraij if you can. Parikh is a bad a lecturer. Her lectures are pretty boring and honestly she doesn't even teach effectively. Even at the beginning, my pod mentor said that most absorption comes from outside. Also, she is a HEAVY procrastinator. She is somewhat caring which is nice, but I could not grasp any topic she covered in lecture.

Pretty good class overall, Parikh is a decent lecturer and the concepts are understandable. Homework sets are difficult but solutions are provided, weekly quizzes are much easier. The first exam is relatively simple, but the 2nd and final are much more difficult and there aren't many practice problems provided unless you go to co-study.

Dr. Parikh is a great professor. She makes her lectures engaging and makes discrete math as much fun as it can be (which isn't a ton). The quizzes are easy, but the WPPs are hard. The exam will probably be somewhere in the middle of the two, but a bit closer to the WPPs. For the exams, you get a cheat sheet and they give good partial credit.

Her lectures are incredibly boring and she provides such little study material. It's genuinely one of those classes that you just have to "get" no matter how hard you work for it. From what I know, her exams are incredibly difficult in comparison to Fraij. Also, the amount of points taken off for such little mistakes is insane to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Parikh is a great professor and explains concepts super well and will hold your hand while doing proofs in the class. 

Many people complain about the Exams, but you can bring cheat sheets so it makes them much easier, fill those up. DO THE WPPS!!! The questions are never harder than that.

Only complaint is there was no practice exam material.

Her teaching is decent though class is boring. The homeworks, while difficult, have answer keys that usually explain well. The weekly quizzes are usually fine. Exams are the hardest part. The final exam was much more difficult than previous exams, and the lack of study materials didn't make exams any easier. I'd recommend taking Fraij if possible.

Terrible professor. Gave so many tough problems on quizzes and tests that she did not teach at all. These problems were very complex and made for you to get bad grade. Just wants you to get a bad gpa and doesn't care about anyone but herself. Always talked how people gave her bad reviews all the time and did nothing at all to help me.

Her quizzes are easy but are exams are way too complicated. She doesn't teach the harder problems nor does she provide previous exam papers for you to practice. She expects everyone to perform well on her exams without any practice problems or previous papers and complains when she receives poor feedback.

She was fine, but I had to work to earn my grade in class. She's a caring professor, but her lectures were kind of boring. The exams are slightly hard because there's very little practice material and she nitpicks your proof formats. However, you do get a cheat sheet for the exam. No textbook is required, but the Rosen textbook is a lifesaver.

Bad lecturer and exams were tough.

Format of class is awful, exams don't really seem to test the content learned but simply problem solving skills and the exam prep and format is stress inducing.

For reference, I got an A in Mike's 314 by studying around 5 exams each exam, but in Parikh's there are simply no good study techniques, just pray

Lectures could get a little boring sometimes but the content was pretty fun. Homeworks being completion is nice. Exams were pretty close to the homework so not too bad. Having to watch prerecorded videos was annoying though, as she would just teach the same content during class.

Dr. Parikh is a pretty good lecturer, but she didn't provide many accessible resources to practice the material. Aside from the required problem set, only one set of extra practice problems are available per week, and they may only be accessed through a TA or an organized help hour session (co-studies).

terrible professor please try to get a different professor if possible just awfully structured class with below mediocre teaching

EDIT: final was terrible 0 resources to help prepare
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class wasn't the best or worst. I thought I didn't get an A but I did. Exams are somewhat tricky but honestly for me it was just the exam environment that made me panic. Calm down and read the problems carefully and the problems actually aren't too bad. Lectures are really useful to review afterward. Other than that it just felt like a mid-class.

The class touches on a little of proving algorithms and really emphasizes how to optimize matrix multiplication. Beyond the 5-loops lab, the exam, projects, and homework are really not that difficult. Dr. Parikh is a bit of a procrastinator, so keep that in mind when expecting grades and feedback.
Quite possibly the worst professor I've ever had at UT. Stay away from her and her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is incredibly nice and friendly and covers her course content in a fairly organized manner. She did get off of her schedule after exam 1 which made her pre-lecture videos not align with her lectures. She allowed us to have cheat sheet(s) on the exams which was helpful. Like many other posts suggest, exam 2 feedback was handled poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content of the class isn't very hard; it's the professor that makes it that way. The professor makes you feel as if she doesn't want you to succeed. Feedback on exams is not the best. She even purposely regraded Exam 2 as she felt the TA's were "being too nice." Final exam grades aren't even released.

Parikh is nice enough once you get to know her. Her main problem is expecting students to care more about her class than data structures and grades subjectively at times. Her class was mostly organized besides exam weeks and she's decent at explaining earlier unit concepts. Pay attention to pre-lecture and section problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but CS 378 was a disorganized disappointment. Unclear expectations, scattered lectures despite required attendance. Unclear exam content. Weird grading scheme. Very disorganized compared to her solid Discrete Math course. Use Robert van de Geijn's edX version to actually learn. Texts are way more helpful than lectures.

This course is good in the sense that she is very approachable outside of class and she knows what shes teaching. The course material is dense and the projects are very time consuming and hard. Class gets better as the semster progresses but I would consider this a pretty heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam 2 feedback was handled poorly and made a lot of people dislike her, which has led to a lot of bad reviews this semester. Apart from that, she gives the HW solutions so that students have more examples of how to accurately answer questions, but if you just copy given answers it makes studying for exams a lot harder. Lectures were not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. When new symbols are being introduced, you should not handwrite your notes. She does. Very difficult to understand what is being written and what is a part of the problem/given or the solution. She blatantly regraded a test to be scored lower. UT really needs to add a new CS prof for Discrete Math. Disappointing, disheartening. I'm sorry.

bad lecturer and very boring lectures. when you ask questions outside of class she can be passive aggressive with responses. also she went back and regraded a test just to take away points because the tas were too lenient.

I don't think she understands that some of the topics in this class are very difficult to conceptualize, especially because proofs require some sort of creativity or ingenuity. She should give more practice because of this, but she always claims that she gives enough (I think most people would disagree).

Not really sure what to make of this class. Parikh is a good professor in the sense that she's personable and cares, but the way she ran the class gave something to be desired. We didn't understood what she was teaching until we had projects and could actually piece her lectures together. Overall, wouldn't recommend. I got nothing out of this class

She doesn't really prepare you for the tests, she puts topics barely covered in the class and expects students to magically be able to answer the questions, And starts whining in class when students do bad on a test she didn't prepare us for
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On Midterm 2, she curved down our scores because the "TA's gave us too many points." I had an A which dropped me to a B on the test. Her lectures are not that bad, she is just very passive aggressive. Because of this, I do not show up to office hours and sometimes not even class and just learn the material on my own.
pretty bad at lecturing...

Extremely lacks clarity and assumes we comprehend short abstract explanations, then speeds through hard examples. For midterm 2, many people did horrible, and instead of trying to help the students, she said she was going to go back and take away more points. The prestige of UTCS feels tarnished by such disregard for student learning and success.
She does not care about students understanding of the material
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: extremely boring lectures, this class made me want to switch majors
Although I cooked and got an A, this class was the worst experience of my life, unfortunately you have to take this class for your degree so pucker up and enjoy the ride

This teacher is the worst teacher in the history of UT computer science. Because this class is commonly taken at the same time as CS314, the day of one of the CS314 midterms, very few students (I think 3) showed up to lecture that day, causing her to visibly whine the entire lecture and explicitly say that she was going to make her exams harder.
