Great lecturer but the course content is just really hard and the projects are also really difficult. I would reccommend taking her but read the textbook. One exam 3 projects 2 homeworks.

She's too smart for her own good, explains concepts abstractly then speeds through the 1-2 examples done in lecture as if we should know it already. Have to master content in 1-3 days for the weekly quizzes. "Practice test" is useless and homework includes untaught material. While grading is lenient and she's nice, the course has its flaws.

Parikh does not present the material in a way that is understandable. She does not explain things well and does not answer questions well. She also gives us important content in the lecture before the test, provides no practice problems/ practice exams before and then asks us a difficult question about a concept just taught. Would not take again.

Dr. Parikh is a very good professor. Her course is very well laid out and her teaching style is great. The only thing that I felt was lacking was that there was not enough examples of certain topics so finding helpful resources was tricky. Other than that, you will have a good time with her, but I am also happy that it is over.

Parikh is a good teacher and cares for her students but it may still be difficult to learn from her. Her lectures can be a little hard to follow and will require work outside class to learn the content. If someone is confused, her explanations don't really make sense to lessen the confusion and just repeats what she said before.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Parikh's lectures favor direct instruction and are structured around notetaking, corresponding with my learning style. She delivers material well, but pre-class videos were a chore. HW solutions provided and weekly quizzes were easy. Exam grading is lenient but hard to prep for. Final exam score not revealed, but curve implied. Study induction.

Really good lecturer with engaging presentations, always ready to help even outside of class. Grading isn't too harsh & all the assignments/quizzes are basically completion grades. There are 3 major tests, all of them honestly aren't too bad but you don't get much practice material. Content is pretty interesting, math-wise it's just basic algebra.
I love Dr. Parikh. Notes are very helpful and she cares a lot about her students. like a lot. she is also really funny and really relatable too. parikh is the goat

Pretty good professor, no major complaints. Lectures can feel long, but attendance isn't mandatory. The course material feels gimmicky at times, as you can completely fail an exam problem / quiz if you don't know some specific trick that the problem is designed around. Also a little tough grading on formatting. I still feel I learned a lot though.

Dr. Parikh is approachable, funny, and knowledgable. She is animated at times, which some saw as mean or sassy but I found it light hearted and entertaining.
There are weekly homeworks, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. 
Homeworks were hard but graded for completion, quizzes were easy, especially with two attempts, and exams were forgiving and doable.

This professor seems nice but she is very, very mean. She picks and chooses who gets to get a round in the grade, she chooses who gets to reschedule an exam or quiz. Everything is up to her discretion, if it's something serious like missing a quiz because of a death, she states the syllabus is the final say, but gives someone w a cold a reschedule.
Towards the end of the year the topics get convoluted and kinda difficult to understand. The lectures are mid. Not terrible, but not great.
worst prof I have had in my 4 years at utcs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't think I'd end up with an A but I did. Just need to put in a lot of work and study the practice problems she gives diligently. She's a very caring and good lecturer. One of my favorite teachers from last semester. Overall, great class and great professor.

She is a very good lecturer but the topics after induction are really difficult. Make sure you take the time to properly learn the content on your own, and do practice. Exams were not bad at all, but the final was difficult and confusing. Weekly quizzes are also pretty easy if you pay attention in class.

Her lectures consisted of a lot of practice- which was good because exams reflected exactly what was on the homework, quizzes, and lecture practice. Her pre-class videos were incredibly useful, you should take notes on them before class and amend during class- this will make the class SO much easier for you (i wish i did this).

Lectures were about as interesting as you can make discrete math; with jokes here and there. Quizzes and exams were usually lightly graded (depending on who graded yours). Not extremely difficult to pass, but material is a bit confusing (have to do a lot of practice & lots of looking at the solution) but makes up with light grading. No bump/curve

Dr. Parikh does a good job of teaching a very hard subject. Practice is hard to come by outside of the section and TA runs study sessions since proof formatting is so stringent. Keep up with the content and PRACTICE!

Professor Parikh is super knowledgeable and Discrete Math was interesting. However, it's easy to fall behind if you don't practice and do the homework while you're learning content, so make sure to study as you go and not the night before an exam. Practice in-class activities, homework, and past quizzes to prep for exams, which are all open-ended.

Parikh is a nice professor however she can feel dismissive at times when answering questions. Exams make up a majority of the grade and curves almost never happen (if at all). The TAs in this class are also very hit or miss, especially my TAs who evidently did not prepare for sections because of how many mistakes they would make in example problems
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CS378 Programming for Performance and Correctness was a bit disorganized, but Parikh really cares about the material and teaching it to others. I think the class will be even better in the future now that the projects are set up and won't need to be delayed as Parikh finishes making them. Not a ton of work and easy to balance with other classes.

Discrete math itself could be interesting, but the professor's execution in teaching it is bleh. I would recommend paying attention during discussion meetings, as it offers some challenging content. The test prep material is subpar, so prepping for the exam is hard with the lack of questions on par with the difficulty of the exam. Easy grading, tho

Content is pretty straight forward if you keep up with the practice problems and homework. Exams are pretty difficult if you don't understand the exact proof formatting but she gives a LOT of partial credit. Quizzes can be confusing at times but TA's go over similar problems before you get a redo at the end of discussion and HW solutions are given.

chill teacher and cares about students personal lives. just take opportunities such as costudy sessions and practice problems and review them for mastery before exams. Dr. Parikh is very down to earth and is ver accessible in office hours.

The material in CS311 can be difficult to grasp but going to TA study sessions and Dr. Parikh's office hours are very helpful. Tests are difficult, but they are graded in a way that allows you to do well.

Formatting for proofs is emphasized way too much. None of the upper division math classes you'll take after this will be so adamant about proof formatting. The lectures are decent but the pacing seems pretty slow. Lots of examples are provided in class and the material is pretty straightforward.

Dr. Parikh was a fantastic professor. She was very accessible during office hours, and she was very down to earth. She is the smartest teacher that I've ever had, and she knows a lot about the subject she's teaching. Even though I'm not a math person, she explained concepts in an understandable way.

While this class can be tough, I feel that she does a good job at explaining things. It's really important in this class to ask questions and go to office hours for extra help/practice. On that note, there isn't a lot of practice for those who don't go to office hours or study sessions, so utilize those.
Very friendly teacher, wants students to succeed at her class. Lectures weren't always easy to comprehend. Exams were challenging but graders are lenient and it isn't to hard to keep an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had I known there were prerecorded lectures I would have used them much more than sitting in 1.5 hour ambiguous lectures. This is a mindset heavy class as it's full of things such as logical proofs. Professor is competent it's just the class itself is hard. Quizzes were much easier than exams and easy in general. Exams increased in difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is a nice, caring teacher that genuinely cares about her students. She makes a genuine attempt at fostering personal connections everyone. However, her lectures can be boring and drawn out. There are times where she cannot answer basic questions, and she can be cryptic with class logistics.

I struggled to understand Discrete, but that's more on me than the professor. Dr. Parikh explained concepts well, but flew through material due to the large amounts covered. Go through EVERYTHING when studying for exams, questions from help hours and homeworks are recycled.
Also, no curve for difficult exams means she graded very leniently.

Class covers a lot of material fast, especially in the graphs unit, so to gain a deeper understanding and for an easier time, definitely self-study some mathematical logic before hand. Learning To Reason by Nancy Rogers helped a lot. Learned lots of interesting things. NOTE: 5% participation earned by watching videos without skipping BEFORE class.

Although discrete math can be highly technical, the regularity of conventions and clear presentation of expectation makes most of the class revolve around understanding the logic puzzle rather than fighting for what the professor wants you to say. That said, falling behind on understanding technical concepts will make catching up nearly impossible.

Overall a hard class. I find discrete math to be interesting, but the lectures are long and boring. Lectures consisted of providing long, text-heavy definitions without examples. Professor is unwilling to answer RELEVANT questions during lectures. only during office hours. everything is graded HARSHLY, she did not release final exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ASK QUESTIONS. Lectures/videos are almost always confusing, especially after the first unit, but Dr. Parikh gives amazing answers if you just ask her a question. Tests are worth a lot and an A is 94+ but if you do all the work you will do good.

Once you pick up the pattern of questions from class and quizzes/tests, it gets very manageable. You learn a bunch of structured proofs. Professor was very sweet and down-to-earth. Lectures sometimes had ambiguity, but they were usually minor and the professor is actively open to questions.

She sometimes defers to asking students to come to her office hours to discuss questions rather than answering them in class, but for the most part she provides a lot of material to study for quizzes and exams, but both are pretty tricky
She will sometimes get confused by her own notes in lectures. Nevertheless, her lectures are mostly interesting and I think the tests are fair enough in terms of difficulty and time given.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Parikh is super knowledgeable about her subject, but her teaching comes off as heavy-handed, and she sort of dumps all the vocab and info all at once. Note-taking is important. Quizzes every week, but the TAs go over similar problems right before. Tests are 5-6 questions each, and they're similar to problems on past homework or in study sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: lectures are very long. she covers the content but struggles to answer student's questions sometimes. tests are only around 5 questions, so if you struggle with a topic and it shows up on the test, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
She is not the best professor but definitely not the worst. 

If you do not show up to class, ignore the quizzes, or just copy the solutions from the homework you should expect to do poorly. However, it is possible to get an A in the class if you just go through everything provided and stay on top of your topics. Material is dense but not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh was a pretty caring teacher. That being said, the course is not very easy to grasp at times. Lots of the material is pretty dreadful to try and figure out, but Parikh will do her best to help you out if you go to her office hours.

Parikh as a professor makes the subject alright, however, Discrete Math in general is an absolutely abismal subject to take no matter who's teaching. Make sure to watch the pre-lecture videos, they have very useful information. She lets you write down some notes to take to exams as well which helps.

Dr. Parikh was very accomodating and a great lecturer. In 311 you have to watch pre videos before coming to class which really cements the knowledge in your head which she then expands on in class. Great professor and great class.

You have to work outside of class by watching pre lecture videos and having weekly homework, discussion problems, and quizzes. But the answers are made available to you, so there's no reason to get stuff wrong. Hard class to get through if you don't like proofs. She herself is a nice person and she's passionate, just not a fun subject

Pay attention in discussion section, the TA's are helpful and the problems sometimes end up on exams word for word. Her reviews also have questions that are similar format to those on the actual exam.

Homework assignments were sometimes time consuming and a bit difficult to complete since we often learned the material covered on the homework the day before it was due. Tests were similar to the homework assignments and practice tests, and they were not too difficult if you paid attention during class and really understood all of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely important to understand the material, as are all of the practice problems Dr. Parikh provides. Although the material being covered is pretty dense and challenging, Dr. Parikh does a great job of making it manageable and understanding the kinds of problems she will have on her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are really dry, puts most people to sleep. Attendance is taken every class - try not to be late. Latter part of course appeared rushed. Some of the content here is hand-waved through. Expectations were clearly outlined and tests are a fair assessment of the content. Book is not required. Homework and discussions were graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is an awesome professor. Sometimes teaches in flipped classroom style, which is very convenient. Videos are concise and helpful. Homework solutions are posted ahead of time so you can check your work. I learned a lot from this class and it was very fun. Lectures can be slow if you have worked ahead because she gives people time to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh is a good lecturer, but sometimes she can get confused by her own notes. However, for the most part she is very helpful, especially her pre-lecture videos. Class is very easy to get an A in, just pay attention in class and do the homeworks.

Professor Parikh seems to struggle teaching in an online format. Participation went from 100 students to 60 students in each lecture by end of semester. 1-3 hours of required pre-lecture videos, sometimes posted late the night before lecture. 50+% of lectures is her mumbling/making mistakes to the point where it can get difficult to follow her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Programming for Correctness and Performance alongside OS this semester. Was doable since my other two classes were easy. Class is taught through an edX made by van de Geijn, and the TAs are good at explaining the concepts. Tests would have been harder closed-note. Utilizes basic linear algebra (doable), ask for help if you had bad linalg prof.

Overall decent, lectures are pretty dry though. If you show up to the beginning of class and then later on you dip I think you still get credit. I often went back to the recorded lectures and put them on 2x speed. Easy enough class if you can pay attention long enough.

Dr. Parikh cares about students and gives good lectures. The only thing is she does not tell us what style we need to follow in the exams sometimes. I feel it's important to make sure your answer styles in the exams are the same as the answer styles in the homework. Or you may lose style points in the exams. She did not post final grades on Canvas.

Dr. Parikh is a very good lecturer with a lacking curriculum. She does her very best to take questions and answer everything, but she seems disorganized at times, with many students asking for clarification on homework and her responding that actually the homework was wrong and she'll update it for next time. Teacher: 9/10, Class: 6/10.

Dr. Parikh is an awesome lecturer. She has a clear agenda and itinerary decided for each day of the lecture and provides concrete examples about the material being covered in class. The homework and quizzes are fair and within the scope of the material learned. Tests are slightly more challenging than homework. She does rush to finish sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is a wonderful instructor! She explains everything very clearly and takes time to make sure we understand, even in the virtual setting. The homework is very fair, nothing outside of course content, and the exams are only slightly harder than the homework. Don't skip class though, you can quickly fall behind!

Parikh was a very good professor. She always tried her best to keep the lecture entertaining. But still, lectures can be quite boring and dry at some points. Homeworks are just a completion grade, weekly quizzes, and discussion sections as usual. Exams are quite doable and not hard at all, just be punctual. The final exam was a take-home exam.

I actually enjoyed this class! I've actually been more interested in the theoretical side of computer science because of Dr. Parikh too. Dr. Parikh is incredibly nice and she really tries to engage with her students. Homeworks are difficult, but quizzes and exams are much easier. Overall, great class!

Parikh is a pretty good professor for discrete math! Content is sometimes confusing and dry but it's just bc it's discrete math. Doing pre-lecture readings / videos can take a bit of time, but tests are very fair with good review in discussions / practice tests. Course is well organized & they respond well to questions. Don't buy the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is super nice, I don't know what some people are on about. I see that some people say she is boring, which is NOT true. The COURSE MATERIAL is boring, not the professor. It's not her fault that discrete math puts even the nerdiest kids to sleep. The material sucks, but its required. Great professor. Tests are fair. Directions clear. 9/10.

She is a very nice professor and she is willing to answer all questions even if it takes up some of the lecture time. For tests, they are pretty easy and similar to homework and discussion problems. There is only one homework per week and some recorded videos to watch before each lecture so the class is not too difficult.

Dr. Parikh is a really good professsor if you make an effort! If you have questions do not hesitate to ask her during office hours she will explain it as many times and in different ways till you understand it. Work out all the practice problems from class and discussion because the test questions are really similar to those
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Parikh cares about you learning the material, and is really helpful when you go to office hours/ask questions. She can be intimidating at times though, and sometimes gets frustrated. The grading in the class itself is extremely lenient and the workload is low.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do all the posted homework and go to class. Tests are pretty easy and there will be no surprises if you do everything. It would be nice if she learned how to be less frank when she talks to her students. Sometimes she comes off as intimidating, but overall a pretty nice teacher.

Explained content very clearly in class. Effective use of examples to illustrate concepts. Was incredibly well organised for a new professor. Loved the problem-solving ethos Parikh inspired; her in-class activities, discussion and homework questions provided ample opportunities to develop problem-solving skills. An enjoyable and fulfilling course.

Extremely long & boring lectures. Typos in quizzes/exams. Course was decent in-person but terrible online. Workload increased; she started taking attendance for lecture/discussion & assigning an hour+ of pre-lecture videos. Actual lecture didn't cover any new content anymore. Responses on Piazza are useless & she gets irritated at questions asked.

This class level of difficulty isn't the issue w the class. After online schooling began we had to watch around 2 hours of videos before a 1.5-hour class, the amount of work dramatically increased. she is very honest; however, she can get very irritated when people ask questions & skip steps while introducing new content because they are "implied".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is pretty easy, but the lectures are VERY dry and usually word for word from the textbook (You'll fall asleep). The course work is pretty light, with a HW, discussion, and quiz every week. Tests are also easy and like the sample exams. After moving online, the amount of work and assignments due were 10X what they were pre-corona.

Not the best professor in my opinion bc she gets annoyed at people asking questions sometimes. But overall she is nice and has decent lectures. Tests are very similar to class work so shes a pretty fair grader. Not the best, not the worst.

Coursework was relatively light for the class, tests were pretty easy too and she's a pretty lenient grader. If you show up to class (she had quizzes that were basically attendance, but she was talking about switching it up in the future) and put some effort into the online edX course (which was our homework) it's an easy A.
Made me want to cry every time i entered the pma

Professor T is a really nice guy but not a great professor. He is way too old to still be teaching. There is some extra credit he offers, but I would be prepared to do all of the learning on your own because he will not be able to help. Especially don't take this class if you don't already have prior experience with calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: please do not take him if you weren't born with a calculus textbook up your 🙂. plus the fact that he is genuinely too old to be teaching. the nice thing is that there's a lot of opportunities for extra credit and earn half the points you missed back on your midterms but i've literally been teaching myself this entire course. preserve your sanity

he's too old to be teaching. he's very sweet, but no one ever knows what's going on. the one time the TA taught the lecture, the average quiz grade was about double what it had been with his lectures. just avoid

Professor T is too old to be teaching and his instruction is very unclear. He's impossible to understand and his handwriting is not legible. His parkinson's causes his handwriting to be shaky and his voice to be shallow making him extremely hard to understand. Take someone else.
No just no
He's a really sweet guy but a bad professor. Take someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof T is a really nice person, but his advanced age has really got in the way of his teaching. At our last lecture, he apologized for not being able to write anymore due to his not being able to stop his hands from shaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor T is genuinely caring and offers extra credit opportunities. However, he did not provide any grade curves on tests. While his lectures are decent, they can be quite difficult to comprehend due to the quality of his voice. These RMP reviews are misleading for students who haven't taken calculus before. Please take someone else.

I walked into this class having taken AP Calc AB and was still challenged. Prof. T cares a lot about his students and is very accommodating when it comes to grades. His exams and homework are difficult when compared to other sections, but getting an A is manageable--this is coming from someone who bombed their first midterm.  Jeffrey's the GOAT
Prof. Treisman is the GOAT. He is one of the best professors I have ever had at UT. Take him if you can!

He gives tons of extra credit and is so sweet. The only thing is that sometimes the grading is harsh, but he gives so many ways to earn points back. You do have to do work outside of class, it is hard to understand what is going on in class. Worth taking.

Prof T is a really caring professor, he truly wants everyone in the class to succeed. This class wasn't easy though, you have to put in a lot of effort to succeed. I recommend using the textbook for homework problems along with Quest to study. He has a policy where your final can replace your grade in the course (providing you do better). Worth it!

very sweet guy, you can tell he's passionate about not only calculus but teaching as well. he wants all the students to do well and will give extra credit and curves as needed. however... this class felt like whenever you throw babies into the deep end expect them to swim. but people didnt swim. very difficult if you dont have prior knowledge

Prof. T is a great lecturer, so funny, understanding, and really cares about the learning and improvement of his students. He is very receptive to feedback and is just kind of an inspiration in general. My only complaint would be that I wish there was a mock exam. He announces the exam topics, but the pressure can really make you blank sometimes.

This professor is quite honestly the most sweet and caring professor across all those I've had or heard of. He genuinely wants you to succeed and makes it so that your grade is reflective of what you learned. At the end of the course, he offers either the choice of having the final being your final grade or whatever's dictated by the syllabus.

Prof T puts so much energy into helping students succeed, so it's easy to get a good grade if you communicate with him. He talks more about theory in class instead of doing practice problems so you really have to put the work in outside of class. Go to discussions and office hours, they're there to help! He also gives a lot of extra credit!!

HE is the best calc prof you can take with or w/o experience. He's so chill and wants the best. TRULY. You cannot fail this class. Go to office hours and attempt to learn and you will fly through the curriculum in this class. This class was much easier that AP BC Calc. The first unit is bad, but hang in there, it only gets easier. He is the GOAT.

You learn most of the material through the textbook, and studying outside class is needed for success. However, Prof T cares much about his students and provides many resources such as hw help, exam retakes, and plenty of extra credit to help his students succeed. It is tough to fail his course unless you are not trying or communicating with him.

class is something you have to dedicate alot of time in order to do well. This is a self study class, Its hard to learn from the prof but he designs it in a way that he gives u the resources through Tas and office hours. Ultimately, no other teacher gives as much extra credit and cares about their class then him. Put in the work and ull succeed.
Professor T is awesome and very funny. Despite the class content seeming challenging, he wants every student to get an A in his class so as long as you try you'll be good.
I can tell he is a genius, but there is no class layout, he is unclear about test/quiz/class set up, what we are learning, and how to succeed. Take someone else.
Highly recommend you take him. The best professor I've ever had a class with.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Heavy on proofs, so if you are not familiar with them or an expert in calculus do not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof T is a literal goat. He is super kind and cares about all his students. There is no reason you should not take this dude. And the TA explains amazingly well too. If you have past CALCBC experience youll fly. Otherwise youll probs need to put in some work. But the extracredit will be ur guardian angel.

Prof T was an amazing professor in making sure to take into consideration all students backgrounds in calculus. If you don't know much calculus, he is definitely a hard professor as his lectures really delve into the theory behind all math concepts. Lots of EC!

AB calc experience helps a lot. Might be more difficult if you don't have it. Lots of interesting ways to get extra credit. Use calc lab, office hours, zoom review recordings, and past exams to study. Prof W and Tynan were excellent helpers. You get what you put in. The lectures and discussions are learning curves to get used to but overall great.

I liked Prof T as a person, but this RMP page overrates him. This class was tough, rigorous, and had a heavy workload. I took AP Calc in HS, I can't imagine how hard this class would be with no Calc experience. I studied hard for Midterms I & II, and got As. Thought the final would be similar, and I got a C on it, ending up with an A-. EC saved me.

I had already taken calculus before this course, but Prof T has a lot of experience teaching math & has a lot of knowledge to share on almost everything about the subject. There's a lot of extra credit available & a lot of leeway on grades. May be tough without prior experience, just make sure to attend office hours, reviews, & listen to Chester

Prof T is an incredible professor, he truly cares about all of his students and he offers so much out of class help.  the class was really nicely outlined, there's plenty of extra credit and he is extremely knowledgable in calculus.  He's also a super cool person to talk to, very inspirational.
Prof T is extremely caring his class was hard, but he is so accommodating (:

I would advise taking a different professor if you have no prior calc experience. However Prof T is an amazing professor that will always be willing to do whatever he can to catch you up. His TA Professor W is a life saver with her office hours and discussions. Make sure you attend all the discussions and the Test reviews Prof T hosts.
The most inspiring professor I've ever had. I'm trying to be a grader at his class just so i can learn from him.

The best M408C prof. So caring and really wants you to get an A in his class. I don't recommend taking if you don't have prior calc experience. So much extra credit. He also offers so many different resources to study and really understand the content. A good amount of homework, but it isn't too difficult. Offers ways to get back points on tests.

This class makes you do a lot of work outside of class. If you don't have prior calculus experience, be ready to teach yourself. Discussion sections are where you do a lot of practice problems, and lectures are quite confusing. Professor W and Professor T are super nice. If you ever need help you can ask them. They care a lot about your success.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Professor Treisman during the fall of 2020. Such a caring professor and not only made math bearable, but his TAs were amazing and cared about every student on an individual level. Tests are what made your grade but was also extremely flexible and easy to get an A on. Really made pandemic learning pretty painless, and deserves every award.

Prof T is the sweetest person ever. He is so understanding and so knowledgable. I had no calc background so I struggled a little, but still got an A. Go to UGTA and TA sessions for HW help!! Can't stress that enough!!! Can also work together on exams. There was SOOOO much extra credit offered to help your grade. Highly recommend!!!

Hes so sweet and funny. He truly cares about his students and is very passionate about calculus. Im not sure how this class would be in person, but the online exams are tough. He allows you to collaborate with peers so that made it way more achievable to get an A. The TA Erica is also great. If you have no calc background, not the best option.

Prof T is an amazing professor at UT and knows what he is doing. He truly cares about his students in and outside of the classroom and will do everything in his power to help you succeed. During Fall 2020 semester (COVID), he brightened my mornings so much and helped me get through a really tough semester. His co prof/ TA Erica is also AMAZING.

I began my experience with Prof. T in August 2020. He really does care about his students, and does his best to teach the material. He knows what he is doing. There is nothing but an inspirational way to look at your future professor. Solid choice, just not during covid. Go in person, not online.

Professor T is great he seems really passionate about teaching and he really cares about his students. Depending on whether you have previous knowledge of calculus this class may be hard for you. However, if you attend his office hours or Prof W's office hours they will be really helpful. There is homework every week and a short quiz every week.

Professor T is such a great professor. He genuinely cares about his students and is seriously deeply involved with the quality of education here at UT as a whole. Online may not be his best medium, but he tries his best to accommodate every student. His TA, Prof W, is also amazing! Easy A if Calc was taken in HS.

Prof. T has a deep passion for mathematics, which he shares with his students every day in class. His lectures are always interesting, and he is very concerned with making sure that all of his students succeed. He knows that his course is difficult, and as such there he provides lots of extra credit to help lighten the load.

Prof T is literally the best professor ever! You can tell that he really values education and that he loves his students. The class is pretty hard, but going to office hours and reading the textbook helps a lot.

If you took Calc AB in HS and performed decently well, this class will be an easy A. Disregard the grading criteria because you can replace your grade with the final if it's higher (I didn't do this and needed a 50 to get an A in the class). In-class quizzes get fairly hard but don't really weigh much later so don't worry too much about that.

Absolutely LOVED Prof T!! This man deserves the world and more. His TAs, Amy and Erica, are amazing too! His lectures are more conceptual and about the history and reasons why the math works but his TA discussions are when you do more homework based questions. Discussions sections were super clear and helpful. Lots of extra credit opportunities!

Professor T is one of the most caring professors you will probably ever have. He truly cares for his students and has the highest expectations for them. The course may get difficult at times, but as he says, he wants to make us struggle now so we don't later.

Professor T's class is one of the most well-organized courses I have taken. He provides you with all the resources you need to succeed; office hours are extremely helpful! I wouldn't say this class is an "Easy A," b/c you definitely have to work for it; but you have a much higher chance of earning an A in this class compared to other 408C profs.

Prof T is INCREDIBLE. Took this class cz I got a 3 on the AP Cal BC exam & wanted to get stronger in cal. Lectures are fun and interactive. Quiz on Tue could be a group quiz if you get lucky w/ the coin flip! TAs are so helpful and accessible. TONS of extra credit. Loved this class; you will truly earn a grade you deserve based on your work :)

He will make you struggle but he really just wants you to truly understand the material. I definitely cried over this class a few times but I honestly love him. He is a super sweet professor that cares a lot about the well-being of his students and offers a lot of extra credit and review sessions. He will not let you fail.

Prof Treisman is an amazing calculus professor. However, at the beginning of the semester I felt lost but he gives a lot of extra credit and wants all his students to do well. You have to work for your grade and put in effort but he hosts lots of reviews to allow everyone the chance to succeed. Would definitely take his class again!

Professor T is one of the most caring professors that I have ever had. He truly cares about each individual student and wants you to succeed. His class is definitely harder than most, but it's worth it. The only thing I would say is there is a bit of a communication issue between him and his TA's, but other than that his class is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Treisman was one of my favorite professors at UT. He is very understanding and really made me feel comfortable at UT as a freshman. His lectures are difficult to grasp but if you do the homework and read the textbook you'll be fine. Tests are curved and he gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Make sure to get to know him in office hours!
Very proof focused, and definitely a lot harder than other 408C profs there. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, and have to put in a lot of effort to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really interesting and cool class, its just extremely time consuming and difficult, since he goes deeper into the topics than most other professors(requiring proofs for an intro calc class is rather ridiculous if I'm honest). Tests are very difficult, and you're never sure whats going to be on them cause there's so much work. Would take again still

I can tell Professor Treisman will always be one of my favorite professors. As a student who had not previously taken a calculus course in high school, his class was harder just to catch up to the others in the class. However, Triesman kept up with my progress and I went from an F in the beginning of the semester to a B by the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing person. Professor Treisman is the most caring, intelligent, and respected human being I have ever met. I got a 40 on my first test. A 66 on my second test. A 76 on my third test. And a 150 on the Final. Anyone can get an A, you just need to put the time and effort. Make sure to attend reviews, and write down the problems he works out.

One of my favorite professors, professor T is absolutely inspirational in his drive to make sure all of his students succeed. You learn so much from him, along with him really testing your ability. His tests are difficult but it's worth it to have such a fantastic professor.

Anyone can pass his class if you're willing to work hard for it. Homework was due every two days and tests were hard, but there's a ton of extra credit. Whatever grade you get on your final will be the lowest possible grade you could get in the class. For example, if you have a C in the class but get an A on the final, you'll get an A in the class.

This is a very challenging class, but Uri is a great teacher. He is truly there for the student. His tests are very challenging, but he offers ton of extra credit opportunities to help offset the grade! Work hard and you will be fine.
Nice professor, you'll definitely learn during his lectures. The test could be hard, but the way he grades will make you get an A.

He is one of the best professors I've had. Very inspirational, caring, hilarious, and an amazing guy. His lecture is not too difficult to understand; however, his tests were SUPER HARD. If you don't study, I can assure that you WILL fail. Treisman gives out a bunch of extra credit opportunities, so be sure to do them if you want an A in his class.

Prof. T is by far one of the most inspirational and accomplished instructors I have been blessed to have. His class is definitely very challenging but if you are not afraid of hard work you will learn, you will excel, you will look back on your time in this course with a smile and a bead of metaphorical sweat on your brow. Can find txt book online.

Professor T makes a strong effort to get to know his students and make sure they succeed. I'm not going to lie, this class was hard; homework due twice a week, very difficult tests, and many hours of studying devoted to calculus, BUT he gives ample extra credit and test review sessions led by him, not a TA. An A is possible if you work for it

Prof T is an incredibly dedicated and inspiring professor. He begins each lecture with news in science and even takes time to give us intensive review sessions frequently and so many extra credit chances. The work load is very heavy, and the class very difficult, but it is every bit worth it. He teaches you essential skills for college success.

This professor is amazing. By no means is the class easy, Prof. T expects every student to understand the material. He'll ask you to do things that other professors may not; for example lots of proofs. But he's fair, caring, and he makes class a joy to go to. He teaches well and gives plenty of extra credit, so if you work hard you'll do well.

Prof T gives his students many opportunities to learn and challenge themselves. Expect a lot of work and studying. On the first day of class, he specifically said, "I will teach you how to struggle." He was right. But this class was a learning experience, and you'll pass the class as long as you're working hard.

A lot of people get As in this class, but it's not easy. You have to keep up with your work and go to discussion. Treisman's a really cool guy if you ever talk to him, which you should, and really wants everyone to do well, but wants them to struggle along the way, therefore the class averages for the midterm are a 65. To survive you must fight.

Professor Treisman really cares about his students. He is an amazing guy!! Take his class! It's hard but he wants all of his students to get As. It's completely manageable to make an A in his class and you will learn so much. He gives out lots of extra credit he even builds extra points into the grading.

Prof T is phenomenal. To future students, I would recommend taking this course if you have some form of calculus experience. Otherwise, it will be very difficult to keep up. This class allows you to fully understand why your doing what you're doing, rather than just memorizing stuff. 10/10 would recommend!

If you haven't taken calculus I wouldn't recommend this class because most basic concepts are not covered . However, Professor T is inspiring to listen to during his lectures. You can definitely see his passion for the subject matter.  Homework and tests are very challenging.  He uses quest and many homework assignments take up to two hours.

If you've taken calc before and done well, you should take Prof T! He will make sure you know what you learned & then some. If you haven't taken calc or did poorly in it, don't take Prof T. Lots of homework. Hard tests. Extra credit, though! He gets to know you and really wants you to succeed. Only take Prof T if you're prepared to work REALLY hard
It's a very difficult class, but you will be prepared for your future math courses and for engineering.

Great Professor! Amazing Guy. I didn't do much this semester and got an easy A; however, this is solely because I had Calculus in high school and was well prepared. If you have not taken Calculus, I would highly encourage you to take a different professor. This class is almost impossible to receive an A without prior Calculus knowledge.
The best professor I have ever met!!! Like to take again!!!

Prof. T is brilliant! He  makes an effort to get to know his students. Extremely challenging class. Covers topics other sections don't. Time consuming, plenty of hwk, some pop-quizzes, difficult exams but he conducts reviews that help you through the test materials.  Extensive amount of work but WORTH IT. IF YOU ARE WILLING TO WORK HARD, TAKE HIM!

Prof. T. is amazing! The class is difficult because he tries really hard to push your limits. You'll find yourself mastering material that some of the other classes do not even cover and that's a great thing. He has lots of extra credit, cares about his students and gives you the opportunity and the resources to succeed in college. 10/10.

This class is not easy. However, Professor Treisman does all that he can to try to make his students successful. If you put effort into this class you will succeed and likely get an A. You will also learn more than any other Calculus 408C class with Professor Treisman.

Having never taken calculus, this class was the hardest thing I've ever done. Prof T, though, is the most inspiring professor you could ask for. He cares about his students more than any other professor I've ever had. You have to pay attention and do all of the work, but it's worth it!

Prof. T is a great math professor!!! He really wants all his students to do well in his course. There is a lot of homework and you have to work your ass off to get an A! Make sure to do all the extra credit and attend all his review sessions. :)

Professor T is WONDERFUL! He really goes above and beyond to get to know his students and give them the help they need. Get to know him!! BUT this class is definitely not an easy A. You have to work your ass off and do every extra credit opportunity in order to get an A. Sure, his class is hard, but as long as you give 100% effort, you'll be okay.
A great teacher who's lecture are engaging and memorable. You learn a lot more than just calculus in this class!

Not gonna lie, you have to work in this class. But if you really want to learn calculus, this man is a God. He knows what he's doing and is willing to help you out with your overall grade through tons of extra credit assignments. This hero broke 3 ribs, came back the next week, AND gave us extra bonus points while continuing to teach. He's the GOAT

Dr. Treisman's class is hard due to the sheer amount of material and its difficulty. This professor pushes your limits of intelligence and knowledge of calculus. However, the rewards outweigh its difficulty. Dr. T gives multiple extra credit opportunities to bring up low grades, and gets to know everyone of his students by name. Take his class.

I came into this class having had no calculus experience, and I will not deny that it was hard, but Prof T makes everything worth it. He really cares and will do almost anything to help you grasp concepts and truly learn the material. He is super fair with extra credit and tests. Requires lots of time but worth it in the end!

It can be a tough class but the teacher knows how difficult it can be and accommodates to it, he also cares to learn about his students. He's nice and sometimes talks about things other than math to put things into perspective. I would take the class again.

Professor T is by far the most insightful math teacher I've ever had. The class goes beyond doing calculus and teaches us why calculus works. He's a great guy, is respected by everyone who deserves to take the class, and will help you when you need it most. Make sure you're willing to work hard and for long hours if you want an A.

Most caring instructor I have ever had: passionate about this subject and cares deeply enough about students to host review sessions on weekends. Exams are unbelievably similar to the questions he specifically goes over, and I think my grade accurately represent how much effort I put into this class. If u get a low grade, blame ur lazy ass for it.

Professor T is a really great guy. While his tests are very difficult, by doing all of the extra credit and homeworks I managed an A-. He puts in a lot of extra hours for review sessions if you are willing to go, and cares about his students. The class has a lot of difficult concepts, so you have to be willing to work. Overall I learned a lot.

Professor Treisman is a great guy.  He really cares about his students and makes a great effort to know every one of his students by name.  His class is very difficult and you need to work hard.  I was very good at calculus in high school and i struggled through this course.  I would take it again.  Professor T is hilarious & will take care of you.

I LOVE Prof T. Anyone who disagrees probably didn't try very hard in his class. This is definitely not an easy course, you have to work for it and he knows it, which is why there are so many extra credit opportunities. He is great at explaining stuff, but that doesn't mean expect this class to be easy. He is by far my favorite math teacher ever.

Hands down the best math professor I've ever had. His class is based on a point system, so there are plenty of opportunities to make a good grade. You learn a deep understanding of concepts that are VERY useful in other logic based classes. No matter what, even in the hospital, he will be there for you. I HIGHLY recommend!  Struggle  Success!

I came in thinking I knew calculus, but his class was very difficult and consumed most of my time throughout the week. Don't get me wrong, as a person Treisman is super nice and the godfather of calculus, but his exams are hard and the combination of quest and textbook homework is impossible to do by yourself so get to know your classmates.

As a math major, calculus is a class I have to work the most on. Prof T just gives me another reason to continue my career path. His class is difficult, in the sense that you have to do the work and listen to him in order to get an A, but very rewarding. If you are fortunate enough to have him as a professor, he will start up a great UT experience.

This class contains lots of challenging homework. Every week you will have a pop quiz on a topic you learned or should've read about. The tests are really tough. I really struggled at first, despite success in my previous calc class. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND A TUTOR EARLY ON. Do all the extra credit you can, and go to ALL review sessions that he holds.

Professor T definitely doesn't make his class easy, but he gives many opportunities for extra credit, as well as hosting study sessions before each test. If you just stick through his class, 80% of people make A's. He's an awesome professor, but a lot of salty people come on here and give him bad reviews because they didn't put in the effort.

professor T's class is very challenging and he makes his expectations clear immediately. This is the class to take if you really would like to learn calculus. I am a mechanical engineering major and came into this class making poor grades, but the professor works with you and gives you many  extra credit opportunities. great guy. hard but worth it.

The first day of class is terrifying mostly because you see what Dr. T expects of you and feel you are incapable. I come from a really small town with barely any calculus experience. I worked really  hard (Do the extra credit) but if you get to know him and tell him your story, he's there to help! Prof T is the best calc professor you could have.

I'm not going to lie, this is a really difficult course but it is worth it. But he gives a ton of extra credit opportunities and review sessions before exams (usually giving u exam probs). Also, he's is also really interested in getting to know his students even in a big class. He's hilarious and makes the hard material enjoyable. Please take him!!
This class is not an easy A or B. Everything that was taught were so confusing and different. Not everyone got As from the class. These comments are filter.

I took Calculus before & did great, but this is the WORST & challenging class I've ever taken. Do not take this class if you're not an engineering major. The professor tries to be all hilarious & funny, but he's only doing that the first few weeks to not make you want to drop the class. Calculus is already hard, but PROVING calculus is HARDER.
Very challenging concepts made easier. Loved Dr. Treisman! 1010 would recommend.

This class has been the most informative math class I have taken. He explains concepts very well but leaves the actual practice problems to the TAs. The homework load is ENORMOUS and this class sucks up your time. Extra credit is a must to get a B and above. This is the best math class for hard workers because it prepares you very well for 408D.

The class is challenging but if you plan on taking additional math courses (engineering and natural science majors) you will have an unbelievably strong base from his class. For me and 90% of the class already having calculus experience in high school he was beyond amazing. If you are taking calculus for the first time however do not take his class

Great professor! Don't take his class if you want an easy A. But if you want to learn calculus and are willing to work for it, TAKE IT. During the first half of the semester I was sure I was getting a C, but he is SO nice and met personally with me to talk about study strategies and other ways to improve. I got an A and really learned the material!

If you really want to learn calculus, Treisman is your guy. He makes it clear that his class will be a challenge, but it's not terribly difficult to get an A if you put some time into it. He offers tons of extra credit, too. He hires the best TA's who are very helpful in office hours. The best calculus prof on campus, no doubt.

Treisman is an absolutely amazing professor! He truly cares about his students, learns everyone's names, and always rewards hard work. He's gone sometimes but the TA's in this class are more than capable. MAKE SURE to go to his after class review sessions, he goes over test questions during that time. Take advantage of extra credit!

ABSOLUTELY AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! I never took calculus in high school but Professor T was such an amazing instructor and so dedicated to helping me really understand calculus that I earned an A in the course. Go to office hours. Take advantage of extra credit and WORK HARD!!! Professor T is awesome!

I took BC Calculus in High School obtained a 5 on the AP test and still ended up taking the course because I joined ESP If you want an easy A don't take the class. If you want to master Calculus to a point where the concepts amaze you take it. An inspirational teacher dedicated to your success If you ever feel lost, he never fails to bring you back

This class is very difficult but if you work hard through out the semester it will pay off. Professor Treisman is great and really tries to help his students. He connects with his students and knows almost everyones name after a few weeks. The class is tough but it prepares you well.

Prof T was the ABSOLUTE BEST! He's witty and if your not lazy an A is completely possible. The homework's are time consuming and not much help. Advice: GO TO HIS REVIEW SESSIONS! They help and are extra credit. Prof T is fair and really wants to see you do well! Take his class!

An outstanding professor. He loves his subject and wants you to love it to. He's incredibly busy, but will bend over backwards to help you if you show you really want to succeed. If you don't care about the course and just want an easy A then his is not the class for you. He expects/wants you to really understand the material. I loved his class.

Dr. Treisman is a wonderful professor is knowledgeable and passionate about Calculus. Though his class seems to carry a heavy workload, you will be rewarded with an A in the end for your diligence. Lots of extra credit! Funny lectures!
Great professor, he really helps you a lot if you want it.  If you do everything you're supposed to it's an easy A.
Good professor but coursework is completely ridiculous. If you enjoy 3 question tests that are free response that are very difficult, this is your class! If not, stay away, far away from Prof. T.

Treisman is an exceptional professor. He certainly marks the difference between high school and college calculus. His class is hard but he teaches you how to really understand the concepts of calculus rather than just teaching you how to solve problems. Undoubtedly, his class will give you a strong math background and even better reasoning skills.
A great Professor. Tests are very tough, but he wants you to do well and will work with you. There are many extra credit opportunities and review sessions. By far my favorite professor

If you're an engineer, there's really no need to be in ESP, this guy (and perhaps all the ESP Calculus professors) focus too much on proofs and theory. Don't take his class unless you are a math major. A lot of HW and the tests are tough. Go to class because he gives pop quizzes. Do the extra credit.

I enjoyed math in highschool and came into his class with no Calculus experience. I was in ESP 6 hours a week, I spent a minimum of 6 hours on homework (per/wk), always went to class, office hours, and made an A in the end.  You will do terribly on his exams but he gives you a zillion chances to make up points. He is very nice. DO EXTRA CREDIT!

Some tips for his class: Do the extra credit, all of it, it'll save you.  Do all the homework %100 correctly, it's the easiest way make your grade.  The tests are very hard.  He's a wonderful person, great lectures which make math interesting, but he doesn't teach you how to do calculus, so don't take this class if you've never had calculus before.

Most days I would walk into class and feel that everything ever taught to me about math was wrong. I was in my TA's office every week and i still ended up q-dropping it before the final because i knew there was no way in hell i would pass. Not a good teacher if you don't become his pet or you can't memorize all the rules of calculus*my friend got a b in the class n failed every test because he was treisman's fav* BUT he does have the best TA i've ever had for any calculus class and he's hot ~married but hot

Best math professor I have ever had despite being so difficult.  I was part of ESP and so it was a totally worth while class.  He is sorta out there but his love of theory actually makes math seem a lot more interesting than it could be.  I recommend him only if you are willing to dedicate your life to calculus.
His tests are really hard but he offers massive amounts of extra credit.  Even if you dont get the class and you put in massive amounts of time on the extra credit you can get a good grade.
Makes tests incredibly hard, doesn't teach what we need to know for the homework. Has two homeworks assigned per week when many other profs only assign one.

Overall, this class is very easy. Him and Professor Moser do an amazing job of breaking down the material, and use bullet points/power points to highlight the topics of the lectures online. I do wish that there were more study guides provided for exams. It's also important to note that they use HonorLock, so there's no cheating/no using A.I.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The tests in this class were very difficult, but the lectures were made interesting by the professors.

Makes the class incredibly difficult. Assigns way too many readings and doesn't take into account that we have lives outside of class. This class TANKED my almost perfect gpa bc of how difficult the exams are. NEVER take this professor unless you want to poorly!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst lectures ever. Reads a literal essay as the lecture videos. So the dialogue is extremely overcomplicated and hard to follow especially because the poorly made slides with too much information on them do not match what he is saying. It is impossible to take notes. The teaching ideology is so bad.

Exam grades make 75% of the grade in the class. Even if you take care of your assignments that covers only 25% of your grade. If you mess up one exam really bad then you are pretty much screwed for the class. I suggest that if you take this class you should be ready to block out multiple hours of your day outside of your main classes to study gov

Professors were super funny and effectively communicated content. I basically skimmed the textbook and just paid full attention to lectures, taking a lot of notes for understanding, and I did quite well on the exams especially with the curve. A lot of material but very interesting + informative. Several extra credit opportunities offered.

Lectures are boring and it's never clear on what you need to understand. The textbook assignments are so long and boring as well and it is one of the worst things ever. So many assignments due every week, take so long and overall DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class and the lectures are entertaining. If you only write your notes based on the test review, you won't spend that much on the class and it'll be easy to get an A. Tests can be a bit tricky but they tell you that the wrong answers will be obviously wrong which makes it easy to narrow it down to the right one.
Exams are insane!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course took up a LOT of my homework time. There were a lot of textbooks and outside readings, long lecture videos, and all of this prep took a lot of time. Tests were pretty difficult for me. Lectures were sometimes interesting, sometimes not.

The professor is entertaining and is good at explaining the topics, but the class itself is way too time consuming for what it is, the topics are interesting and the professor does a great job at keeping it interesting and applicable to the current day, but can be stressful for students with already difficult or committed schedules.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Though Moser and McDonald were nice, take this class in-person. The workload is heavy for a core class and tests (which are WAY more difficult than daily quizzes) are in the format "A, B, C, A and B, All of the above" and they will intentionally make one answer choice confusing. If you do decide to take it, email Moser to opt in for the paper exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super simple course, easy to follow, and light course load. Lectures are engaging, and typically are shorter than a normal class. Highly recommend for a gov credit.

Exams could be tricky, but they give you a review sheet to do that covers everything on the exams. Do the readings, watch the lectures, and do the review sheet!! It helps narrow down what you realllyyy need to know!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most time consuming classes Ive had despite being fully online. Lots of homework that are weighted so low that they barely matter in your final grade (but essential for studying to do decent on exams). 3 exams worth 75% of grade. If you are not a good test-taker, this is not a good class. Homework due every Tuesday and Friday.

This professor was very clear in explaining things during the semester. Rewatching lectures and following the review questions helped me a lot when studying for exams, however there was a lot to go through.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took this class online during the summer. You have to buy the textbook to do interactive activities. There's also a couple writing assignments, lecture responses, and two exams. The professor isn't the most interesting and the lecture slides could be better, so make sure you read the textbook and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: great professors, lots of lectures, graded on quizzes, tests, and the occasional paper. I have no complaints, easy class.
Lectures were clear and informative, if a bit long at times, and the structure of the class supported my learning and made it easier to succeed.
Literally just don't take this with them if you don't have to. Lectures go at a million miles an hour and they are so boring. Would not recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This test were SO difficult for no reason. There is so much work and time that goes into this class, and it doesn't feel worth it AT ALL!!

This class has been the most work I have ever done. I have over 300 pages of notes, 600+ flashcards, and hours upon hours of studying - all to BARELY make an A in the class. Do not take this class.

reviews.comment: GOV 312L with Moser and McDonald was one of the most interesting gov classes I've taken. The textbook teaches everything the lectures do, but much more quickly. Skip the lectures, read the textbook, and review it before the test and you will be chilling.  I devoted ~30min per week to this course and got an A.

WORST CLASS I'VE TAKEN AT UT. Even with extra credit and curves, I spent HOURS every week and barely scraped by with an A. Minimum 10 lecture videos and short answers a week. Don't waste your time, take your gov core with another prof or at a CC. You take exams on HonorLock and answers are formatted "A, B, C, A & B are correct, all are correct."

reviews.comment: Mid lectures but tests aren't too bad.
so monotone and the lectures are boring but reading the textbook actually helps. if you pay attention to the review topics and actually study youll do well. exams use honorlock
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I understand that this was an online course, but I just could NEVER get in contact with McDonald. Really unhelpful if you need him.

This class definitely is test heavy, has an unequal work load each week, and requires a lot of work for a core class, but if you approach it as such you should be fine. Give yourself 2 weeks to study for exams, do the review sheet, do the extra credit, carefully complete the module quizzes, do the readings, and actively listen to the lectures.

After going through the entire GOV312L class, I couldn't tell you who is Moser and who is McDonald. But the class content was actually very interesting and informative. If you don't watch the lectures, the tests will be difficult. But if you actually watch the lectures, take notes, and do the review, you will do fine.

Tests are very tricky if you do not do the review sheet. grade consists mostly of 3 tests and if you do badly on one then you could be in a bad spot. overall not terrible just wished I studied more for the first test. questions are specific and hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this course to fulfill a core requirement, but I would take it at a community college instead. This course was graded almost entirely on 3 exams (each worth 25% of your grade). I was not expecting to study so much for this course as I did because the exams were unnecessarily difficult. Be prepared to watch 2-3 hour long modules each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, you are graded by so little outside of the exams which hurts the grade a lot even if exams are worth so less because you have very little practice for the exams which are insanely tough. Viewing the amazing lectures is a must. Overall, the hard exams were a huge hindrance to this course as they did not reflect course material properly.

Lots of work for a core & hated it for the first half. That said, I learned lots about modern politics. The professors are super nice, engaging, & organized. FOR MOST EFFICIENT WORK: don't take notes, fill out the exam review while watching the lectures. Then study it for 2-3 hours before exams for A's!!! I enjoyed the class when I did it this way.

I wish I never took this class. I thought it would be an easy online class for my core requirement, little did I know I would never know freedom again. This class took the biggest toll on my life, mentally and physically. I am manifesting a B-. The professors r pretty nice, but the exams are so hard and the homework is insane. Do not take pls :3

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams for this class are really hard. Unless you're prelaw/have an interest in government I would not recommend him for your core. It's a lot of reading and lecture videos. honestly just a very content heavy class and it's not worth taking for a gov core requirement when other easier professors and classes exist. McDonald's GOV312L class is engaging despite the subject matter. The exams can be tricky, but the quizzes and assignments help a lot. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for me - definitely check it out along with the textbook readings.

This class is taught by both Dr. McDonald and Dr. Moser. Their online lectures were lengthy for each module and their tests grabbed content from the lectures, readings, and textbook. The curves are pretty large that if you put in effort, you should be able to walk out with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took GOV 360D International Security, and although the class content was interesting it was VERY BORING. His lecture style is very basic and boring. reviews.comment: I took this class with McDonald and Moser and I thought that it was good! reviews.comment: In conjunction with Moser, this class was not hard to get an A in; however, do not let the exams get ahead of you though because a bad grade on those could potentially give you a lot of stress. Overall pretty descent class, Tests were reasonably difficult if you study. I spent more time in this class than any of my other classes. The textbook is pretty expensive as well, around 80 dollars i believe. So if you are willing to put in the work, then you will get an A.

This class seems straightforward until the 3 tests that are worth 25% each. The tests are confusing and worded trickily. I don't think it is worth taking during a long semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

Generous with quiz drops/test curve and did well even after missing multiple quizzes, turning in assignments late, and ok exam scores (I didn't study).

Not only were his TA'S oversensitive about every little thing, every email I would send for clarifaction purposes was met with snarky replies from everyone involved. extremely lecture heavy with lots of work. the tests covers a lot of content and answer choices are intentionally designed the trick you, so pay attention. took up more of my time than the classes that pertain to my actual major, way too time consuming for no reason.

Online course with pre-recorded videos. Lecture is ok(but will make you think from their perspective on Global issues), McDonald has anger issues. Not an amazing class, professors were nothing sensational, sometimes sounded scripted in the online videos. Tests were really specific but straight off the slides and needed a day or two of memorizing but overall wasn't too difficult once you knew what to expect from the test.

CAREFUL WITH TEXTBOOK - I think a lot of people got confused and grade suffered bc nobody knew what was going on (myself included). The tests are tricky. Lots of A,B,C, "A & B are correct", "all of the above". Overall, easy A but will need some effort. Study bits and pieces 3 days before exam then it's a relatively easy A. Content is interesting!

I didn't realize there were textbook assignments until late in the semester (I joined the class late), and as a result my grade suffered significantly. Otherwise, I'm sure this class would be an easy A. Just keep up with all the different parts- lectures, quizzes, tests, and textbook assignments. Nothing is too hard, it's just a lot of moving parts

Not only are the tests for this class worth a large chunk of your grade, but they're also worded in a way designed to trick you and basically depend only on memorization. If it wasn't for the curves I'd be screwed. Both professors were good, but I'm rating them this low specifically because of the awful testing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was all memorization for me. Only take it if you are a good self-studier and you can memorize details. I disliked the tests with the A, B, C, A&B, All are correct choices. I took notes in unit 1 and only watched the videos for 2 and 3 and finished with a 96. They add curves- it was 8 pts for unit 1, 15 points for 2, and 10 points for 3

On the tests, there are usually 5 answer choices, 3 of which are answer choices while the final two are something like "both A and B" or "both a, b, c are incorrect". They are poorly worded and something I have never seen before. The weekly quizzes are easy, but they do not help for test preparation at all. DO NOT recommend...

reviews.comment: McDonald and Moser co teach GOV 312L. I enjoy government, but the lectures can get quite dry. Not as bad as some say it is.

reviews.comment: Super easy class. For the tests, just watch the videos and fill out the study guides and you will get an A. They promote U.S. propaganda and conveniently stop talking about war crimes and civilian casualties for certain topics.

Honestly such an annoying class. So much homework and exams are more difficult than they need to be. Take another class if you can for the gov credit. The class average for exams has been 50%. I think that's all you need to know. If you wanna succeed you need to set aside a lot of time to take detailed notes bc they are essential, hard but doable

Took online summer class, assignments due every weeknight and 3 exams. If you watch the lectures each night, take notes, and skim through the readings you'll be okay. I studied for all the exams, got a 103 on the first but 88s on the last 2. Definitely got harder. Doable, but you need to have a little time set aside for it. Very fast paced.

I took GOV312L online and was terrified by the other reviews I saw on here, but DO NOT FEAR! Truly, this class is not bad at all if you keep up with the lectures and readings. If you take good, detailed notes and fill out the review sheets, you will 100% be set for the tests. Super knowledgable professors and the class is very well-run/organized.

reviews.comment: I took Professor McDonald over the summer, which I've heard is different than during the school year, and he was amazing. Lots of reading, but the grading is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

Even if u do all your homework perfectly, but exams are around 80\100, u won't get an A. Recommend taking it as a summer online class to fill core requirements.

Would wholeheartedly recommend McDonald's International Security course. Not the easiest A in the world, but his lectures are absolutely fantastic, and I learned so much from his teaching. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures and readings were boring. There's also usually a 10-point curve on each of the tests so definitely doable. Pretty easy besides the tests.
He actually cares about his students' grades and gives fair curves on exams. The workload is decent.

I took this as a summer class, so the pace was faster. However, lectures were not engaging (fully scripted), and there was a lot of homework. Tests were confusing because of their format (they were multiple choice though). Take notes on lectures and memorize ALL of the information because tests are very specific. It was an OK class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took McDonald and Shaw's GOV 310L Summer course and really liked it. Lectures are usually interesting but long. Very lenient. HW is very manageable (2 modules a week each with a quiz (no time limit, each module take less than 1 hr if u fast forward). The lecture vids and module questions cover everything you need to take notes on and you don't need to read the textbook (even though they say it's required). Idk y so many negative reviews.

reviews.comment: If you want to read more on the GOV312L online course I would recommend looking at Prof Moser's RMP since he leads the course. McDonald co-heads the lectures and honestly is a big reason I was able to understand most of the course content. McDonald is a good lecturer and many times he clarified topics that I didn't understand the first time.
