reviews.comment: I truly did enjoy Moser's & McDonald's GOV312L course, they are both intelligent individuals who work off of each other well. With that being said, this was probably the hardest course I've taken to date. I feel like I was getting a good understanding of the content, but the tests are worded to make you second guess yourself. It is also proctored.

This class was very hard for me. I'm interested in gov, but these exams are surely meant to trick you. There are 2 quizzes a week and a discussion every other week that are way easier than the actual exams. They do curve exams a lot, but my GPA and I truly suffered anyway. I would recommend my past self to take another gov312L class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The weekly quizzes were super easy and same with the INNs although those took an hour sometimes. The tests were also easy as long as you watch his lectures (on 2x speed), take notes, and use your notes to fill out the study guide because the questions are basically applying the study guide.

Some of these reviews are very dramatic; Mcdonald is a good, passionate professor and he was very kind and understanding of students during the winter storm. The tests can be a bit difficult, but if you literally just study a little & watch the lectures, you will do fine. They curve well, and it is by no means impossible to do well in the course.
Super boring class, tests were really hard and super specific. The lectures dragged and dragged, not interesting at all.

I thought I wouldn't be interested in foreign policy at all, but Professor Mcdonald's passion regarding the subject was so moving that I almost felt obligated to listen. Even learning about the complex relationships in the Middle East seemed fun with his lectures shared with Moses.

I enjoyed McDonald's class. The material was so interesting since current events were incorporated into the lectures. The two quizzes each week are not difficult and they drop your 5 lowest quizzes. There are 3 exams in the semester. Many students struggled with the wording but there is a curve. With the curve, I never got below a 90 on an exam.

You don't need to read the textbook. Just make sure you can answer all of the questions on the study guide and you'll do fine. Also, the curves are ridiculously high so don't stress about the exams. The quizzes are open-note so you can find the answers in the powerpoint for the most part.
Awful class, awful Professor, dont take.

Literally the worst Professor ever. His tests are the worst and are purposely meant to trick you instead of test you for comprehension of the material. His lectures are awful and all over the place. If someone tells you not to take this class its for a reason.

reviews.comment: This course was not as bad as I thought it would be, but it could have been much better. Quizzes are very simple, but Tests are extremely hard. reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of work: lots of lectures, readings, and weekly quizzes. The lectures were boring (watch them in 2x speed) but absolutely necessary to get a good grade. It is hard to keep track of the 2x/wk quizzes. Test questions are very hard and set up in a confusing way. If you don't have time/don't apply yourself you will do poorly.

All you need to do to pass the tets is complete the study guide that he gives you. He gave us all generous extra credit this semester because of the snow storm so he obviously cares about his students.

Take extremely detailed notes over the lectures & immediately fill out the questions on the study guide (given at the start of each unit). I didnt do 95% of the readings, they usually talk about them in lecture. Just fill out the study guide & a day before the exam read over it. I got a 102 in this class w/ extra credit. Not hard if you study smart
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from this class! All of the content was pre-recorded, and a lot was taken from prior semesters, so the flow wasn't always great. But overall it's a good course. The exams are a pretty tricky multiple choice, but there's a nice curve.

Hardest part of this class is probably the exams bc of the format but there is usually a decent curve on it. You will be fine if you study and read the questions carefully. I didn't use the textbook and it worked out. The lectures are broken down into manageable modules; 2x speed is the way to go. Set reminders for the quizzes. You've got this!!!!!

reviews.comment: Dr. McDonald is fine but the class is very work heavy. There are lots of readings per week and weekly quizzes which are fine. The exams are where things are quite difficult. The questions asked are quite tricky.

reviews.comment: In this class you will have weekly quizzes, and 3 exams throughout. If you like government and self-pace, then the course is fine. The exams are kinda hard since they ask for very specific things.

reviews.comment: We have a couple of quizzes every week based on the lectures and then tests every few weeks. The quizzes are pretty easy, the tests are fairly hard in my opinion. The exams had like "A and B" and "A, B, and C" options that made it confusing and just harder than it needed to be. Idk, easy lectures, tough exams.

The class was okay... There were weekly quizzes due every Wednesday and Friday that really put a buffer on your grade. But the 4 exams were tough. The multiple-choice questions were all five answer choices and the exams were proctored.

Exams are extremely hard, even if you study a lot. Grades are curved, which helps a bit, but the stress and anxiety this class gave me+others, it's hard to measure. (Hard) exams+(easy) quizzes compose the majority of your grade. There's A LOT of assigned readings, and they're necessary to do well/okay on the exams... Student study groups helped...

reviews.comment: This class was completely online. The quizzes are really easy. The exams are kinda difficult though and make up a large portion of your grade. The final paper is super easy.

Took Moser/McDonald's GOV 312L class. Quizzes are extremely easy, and the final paper is graded very generously. The tests aren't too bad as long as you spend the night before going through all the lectures. If you study well enough, you can easily get over a 100+ in this class. Good professors.
Test were made for you to fail. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty boring, but I enjoyed the INNs (current news segments) we had every other week. Tests were very easy, as were quizzes, and they try to give everyone a 100 on the final paper as long as you follow the instructions. Always available on piazza/ via email and the TAs were pretty nice. Easy class to take for credit.

Lectures get boring so I watch them at 2x speed. The quizzes and final paper were extremely easy. Make sure to stay on track of the quizzes yourself (I missed several because there was no reminder.) The tests are a bit harder but there is a generous curve. Make use of the study guide.
Easiest A ever. McDonald is a great speaker. 100% take this class.

The class is structured in a way that make it easy to get an A. The quizzes are easy but the tests are a bit challenging (curves help A LOT). The online lectures can be boring and long, however, this isn't too bad of a class. Also you don't really need to do the assigned readings.

Mcdonald and Moser are good lecturers but this class is very lecture heavy and tests are hard because of the answer choices. It will be like A, B, C, or A and B, or ABC, so it makes it hard to narrow it down to one. There are quizzes at the end of every module that are pretty easy. Just don't fall behind because it can be a lot to catch up on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McDonald was pretty good. The lectures could definitely get boring and took a lot of time to get to the point. As far as government classes go, this was one where I do feel like I learned a lot. However, it was all over foreign policy which I was disappointed about. I was excited to learn more about Congress and our US government.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: an online course that requires you to watch lecture videos and then take a fairly easy open note quiz after. However, lectures are extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. The test questions are designed horribly- questions like is the answer a, b, c, a and b, or all. Overall, not too hard to get a good grade but its def not the best class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Self-paced, easy and fun class if you like government, pretty easy but boring class if you don't. Pretty much all grades from tests which aren't too difficult (still gotta study a bit tho)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online 1st Semester Summer 2020. Overall it was easy. There's a lot of videos to watch but they weren't too bad. The quizzes after each lecture are easy but the exams are a bit harder. Take detailed notes and be sure to take note of examples given in the textbook and lectures. Do your work and you should be able to get an A or B.
He is not a good lecturer. His lectures can be hard to follow because he takes so much time to make a point and often explains concepts in a convoluted way.

The online class consisted of pre-recorded lectures followed by 5 question quizzes on the content (easy). Graded by quizzes, 3 midterms (in person), and every 2 weeks watching a longer video and paragraph response is required. Recommend 100%- completing the assignments and studying for exams will get you an A.
He's fine. Basically what you expect for government. I thought class load was very manageable.
Government isn't personally my favorite subject, but this class is totally doable. Just be sure to study throughout the semester and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The weekly quizzes are extremely easy. Tests weren't too hard after studying the day before. Make sure you stay on top of the weekly modules. The test material is directly from the lectures and just a little bit from the readings. The class is organized well and I learned a lot about government.

Lectures are SCRIPTED and use vocabulary that is literally frustrating to hear. Lectures are supposed to be fluid and human, not robotic and text like, especially in an online class. Moser does a decent job of talking like a real person but anytime McDonald comes on my ears just want to cry. Other than that very interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is super hard to concentrate on and kind of slow--as in literally so slow that it makes me want to fall asleep sometimes(and you can't speed up the videos???? would've made it so much easier). The tests are nothing like the quizzes they give at all; they're very very hard. I would not at all recommend this class to anyone.

It's a relatively easy class but it requires a lot of work. KEEP UP with the readings, listen to ALL the lectures, do well on quizzes, and DO NOT MESS UP ON DISCUSSION WRITINGS. You have two and each one is graded out of 2, so if you even slightly mess up, you have a 75% or 50% for your discussion writing avg. Tests are lecture/reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are very comprehensive and can include any detail covered in the lectures. All the quizzes are straight forward and the writing assignments are over current day events with a clear grading criteria. Only studying the day before the test using the collaborative review managed to pass each test with a B+ or A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to read a lot in order to pass the test. The tests are super hard. You have to take a quiz every week and you have tons and tons of readings!!! Personally I would have take a government that is not online!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class. Mos/McD were knowledgeable and cared about the topic. They wanted us to do well. If you get behind on the modules, expect a lot of stress before tests. Tests are also curved (5-10 pts) so an A is really doable. The downside was that lectures were scripted and hard to follow. Expect to pause and rewatch everything.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class. It was very interesting and McDonald loves what he does. You have to read and watch videos a lot but it is worth it. He is accessible and wants to help you. You have to watch class because there are quizzes. It keeps you up with current events. DO THE STUDY GUIDE!!!!! I got a C on the test when I did not do it and As when I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pat is a great professor and takes the time to make sure the students know the material; he explains it in a way that is easy to grasp. Came in not liking government and came out really interested in the way the US handles foreign policy. The only downside would be the amount of pre-lecture modules there were (they got to be a lot at some points).

Moser and McDonald were very fun and very boring to listen to. Their exams are straight forward but they're the type to actually throw trick questions in there. 3 exams but one slip up will HURT your grade more than it seems. Their lectures are long and you will take hours just on one module taking notes. TAKE NOTES!!! quizzes are fairly simple.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow this class was amazing! I learned so much about foreign policy and current events. This class is quite a lot of reading and work but seriously what you learn is so relevant!! You have to have the discipline to log in on class days and pay attention, but I thought it was really nice to just stay at home and do class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While the lectures can be on the longer side, the material and tests are straightforward. It can be easy to fall significantly behind. Besides their constant need to justify American imperialism throughout history, McDonald and Moser generally do a good job teaching the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the easier options for GOV312L. Made an A with lots of wiggle room. Online discussions/quizzes boost your grade. Tests are in person. Lots of outside videos/reading but not all are necessary. Just have a general idea of each article (can get from videos or PPT instead of reading). Do the review, skim the outside material and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McDonald is a good professor. Watching him and Moser interact was always funny. Course material can be a bit difficult to understand and goes pretty fast at times. I always had a relatively hard time on the test, as they seemed a little hard for an intro course like this. Lots of outside the class modules and readings. Overall, I enjoyed the course

This class had a lot of work outside of class, especially for a 3 hour class. However, if you watch the lectures and video clips/homework, it's easy to get an A. You do need to study for a day or two before tests, but if you do they aren't bad plus there's usually a curve. Quizzes during lecture were really easy, and you really don't need to read.
Lot's of modules to complete outside of class. The workload can become overwhelming if you don't keep up with it. As long as you keep up with the modules, you'll pass.

Lots of pre-class module readings, definitely have to rely on some sort of group review session on google doc for tests. Besides that though McDonald is a hilarious and chill professor that loves football and has amazing chemistry with Prof Moser who co-teaches this class.

READ THE MODULES - I thought that I came in with substantial knowledge about foreign policy and I was lax on keeping up/going in depth for the modules. Study the modules, go to McDonald's office hours and talk about the module info - he is so helpful. For the exams, make sure you know the review and DO IT YOURSELF, don't rely on the google doc
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The modules you have to watch does appear to be a bit excessive, but definitely doable. Just take the questions from the powerpoints and answer them (answers are in the modules) and bam you have notes that will aide you well. Tests are designed to be tricky, but at least there's a curve.

The amount of videos assigned every week is too much for a 3 credit hour class. However, as long as you watch the videos, do the reviews, and put some thought into the essay you'll be fine. Very interesting content, open-note quizzes, tests require effort but are generously curved, and you don't have to do the reading to get an A. Would take again.

Maybe it's just me but this class was really hard I definitely wish I would've taken it at a community college. The quizzes are either really tricky or pretty easy. The tests are super trick question based and was really hard in my opinion. Definitely watch the modules and do the readings. The professors are nice and entertaining though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work for this class between the learning modules and assigned readings. The tests also have a lot of material on them. Besides how tough the class was, McDonald was a good professor. The live class was always very interesting and the material discussed was always relevant to current issues in some way.

I took GOV 312 (online) with him and Moser and it's a pretty easy A. Both of them are very clear and the study guide basically covers all of the test so make sure to study them! I don't understand the negative reviews of them because the class is pretty easy. Don't sleep on the essay though, it's graded pretty hard.

Lectures are sooo horrible because they literally read a teleprompter and stutter and struggle with their own words. It's hard to learn because of this. My eyes glaze over. Class/quiz is online only ONCE a week but there's a lot of videos you have to watch outside of class. Required readings are long but you don't actually need to read them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. McD is so cool! Moser was good too. He answered all of my questions in Office Hours with an excellent attitude. He explains himself well, and is just an all-round friendly guy. The pop quizzes are easy, and if you use your Study Guides, you'll make an A. The class requires effort, and you must do your h/w as told and do the SGs, you'll do well

Prof. McDonald is great. He takes his job seriously, is fair, patient, and clear. He doesn't run away from tough questions by students and does his best to provide a well-rounded response. He would probably repeat/rephrase an explanation fifty times if he had to for you to understand.

Prof. McDonald is hilarious, but teaches the material in an effective matter and can be serious when need be. Short and simple: He's a good teacher. GOV 312L was an easy class, as long as you spent about 4 hrsweek doing the readings.

It's the standard government jargon associated with governmental foreign policy that can be found within this class. Take the readings seriously and make sure to go to office hours from time  to time just to cement your knowledge. I will admit that a 1.5 hr lecture is really hard to remained focused on at times, especially online. Not too bad.

Wonderful professor. Very clear and precise. Very helpful in office hours. Made subject extremely engaging. We spent half the course playing Statecraft with class divided into 12 teams, and it was a very rewarding experience. Take him if you want to learn.

I felt that the rate of the class was moving too quickly. The professor said that he would consider slowing the pace of the class down bc there were only 15-20 students in our class, but he never did. He also is very disorganized and rushes through his material/course topics without ensuring that his students are understanding what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Crazy good lectures honestly and Im not even a physics/astronomy major.

He really isn't much of a lecturer. But the teaching assistants are incredibly helpful, there's no final exam, and you can drop your lowest grade. So I just breezed through my last exam. Make sure to attend the teaching assistants' office hours and put in some effort—you'll have a stress-free end to the semester.

Prof. Shapiro is very talented and knowledgeable in the field of mathematics and astronomy, however, he doesn't get how students learn. His PowerPoints and lectures are super wordy, fast, and confusing.  He purposely makes information less accessible, especially homework solutions. Unless you're committing most of your time, don't take this class.

Professor Shapiro's class is hard, but it is sooooo interesting. TBH if you are looking for an easy science class at UT you're gonna be out of luck. 
He is so passionate!!!! And all lectures will be recorded and available, which makes it a lot easier to study. I reccommend attending class as not all information is on Google Slides.

Dr. Shapiro is too smart to be teaching this class. Bless his heart. He geeks out on astronomy, but he's a tough professor. Lectures can be confusing. HWs too conceptual or quantitative. You will be doing math. You will touch math the first day. If you love astronomy like he does, YOU WILL LOVE HIM. If you don't, say goodbye to a easy semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a super nerdy guy who obviously loves what he does. If you just come to class and REALLY pay attention, you'll pass.

reviews.comment: This is by far the worst class I've taken in my 4 years at UT. We didn't learn about space, we learned about math. curves test grades but expects you to teach yourself.

Paul Shapiro is a great lecturer but tends to go off-topic often and does not finish the material needed for the week. No final exam and grade are curved. TAs are going to be the best help with the class. Grading is a bit harsh and a lot of reading is required for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: First 30 minutes of class were not relevant, and he often went off on tangents. So, he always went 15 minutes past the end of class to compensate. reviews.comment: Definitely astrophysics, not astronomy. Very math-heavy (although not *difficult* math). The prof is smart but goes off on tangents. TA help sessions are a godsend. Tests aren't as hard as most people say, if you pay attention to the homework/daily questions. Don't take if you just need a science credit (i.e. aren't interested in astronomy).

Very passionate but goes on way too many tangents and ends class 15-25 minutes late. Insisted upon online classes while making tests in person. ??? Loves what he does but so frustrating to listen to as he goes on for so long, takes forever to get to the point, and somehow makes astronomy boring. Although, he curved all the tests which was nice.

Professor Shapiro often drifted off in his thoughts during lectures a substantial amount. A lot of the stuff in his classes was not really class content, but just random historical facts about Astronomy. Without my AP Physics high school class, I don't think I would've done so well here. reviews.comment: Would always go off topic in lectures, and even when he was on topic he still wasn't great at teaching the material. There are TA help/review sessions twice a week which is where I learned everything. Has generous curve on final grades though.

This was an extremely difficult class. I was told to take this class because I am a non-science major, but I do not recommend it. The tests are MC but hard.

The professor is brilliant, but his lectures are pretty hard to follow especially considering how much material he has to cover. Hardest class Ive ever taken. I saw his awesome reviews on here before i registered so i took his class and ive never worked harder for a course than i have for this. reviews.comment: Take this for astronomy and do not take ROBINSON or FINKELSTEIN. Does not beat around the bush and is actually SIMPLISTIC math and not INTEGRATED physics, chemistry, and math.
This is a very easy class if you are a non-science major. Curves are generous, and the tests are like the powerpoints.
Awesome class. Very easy and EXTRA CREDIT
Probably the easiest thing to knock out science requirement. Math used is basic algebra
Easiest astronomy professor.

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit opurtunties and projects cushion the clas grade. Generous curve.
Easy A. Just relook over the power points and go into office hours. DROPS LOW GRADES
Great astronomy teacher for AST 301. VERY EASY A
Absolutely terrible, gives no feedback on homework and fails to provide help when needed.
cant really call him a teacher because he doesnt teach... everyone is confused when it comes to the HW and tests. Definitely avoid him if you can.

She is super sweet and understanding. Lectures are not mandatory but they aren't recorded and its hard to get notes. All test are easy because study guides are direct. Many resources and extra credit. 2/3 weekly assignments. Definitely can get an A if you study and do the work.

Just one of the nicest people ever, super fun and easy math class that is good for education/UTeach. Tests were easy, projects were fun. Awesome professor, and very good teacher too. Material was easy, but she is a great explainer of things. GOAT level professor, can't recommend enough

Pam is the best, truly makes math enjoyable and cares about what she's teaching! The hardest part about this course is exam time management in my opinion, but go to discussion sections, pay attention in class and get help when you need it, you will never be shamed by Pam or her teaching team!
Pam is the best! She allows a cheat sheet on exams, and her TAs are amazing too. A 10/10 class for precalculus.

Pam is an amazing professor!!! If you ever get the chance to take her class do it! She is inspirational, kind, caring, and makes sure everyone is understanding the content. She is also very approachable and accessible! Her TA's are also amazing. Can't stress how amazing she is!

I loved Pam, she is sweet,kind,& smart. She truly loves teaching, and you can tell. Attendance is not required (but you should definitely go because it helps a lot!). She builds in no-class days before and after holidays. Her office hours (along with the TA) are helpful. No matter how much math you have going in,she'll make sure you understand.

If you ever have the chance to take Pam as your professor, please do!!!! I just completed my first semester at the UT Austin, and she was without a doubt my favorite professor of the entire semester. Pam is so energetic, and she teaches the material in a way that helps you understand no matter what your math background is. She is the absolute best!

GENEUINELY THE BEST PROFESSOR!!!!!! Her lectures are engaging, and her explanations are clear and concise. The TAs are super helpful, the homeworks were easy, and she allows cheat sheets for her exams.

My GOAT. She gives you test reviews for the midterms and the final that match the test exactly and you get a one page cheat sheet (front and back). Attendance isn't required but the daily homeworks match what she does in class so it's best if you go. TAs are very helpful and reachable. Easiest class ever if you listen in lecture and put the work in

Here's the thing, Pam is incredibly sweet, funny, and always at your disposition, but I feel like explaining wise both her and my TA's could have done a little better. Solid 9/10 course, since office hours and discussions remediate that issue. I would take this again, but moving forwards in maths I would stay away from this prof.

I took Pam's Pre-Cal class during the fall semester of 2025. She was honestly amazing, but I also have to give credit to her amazing TAs. To pass this class is simple: attend lectures, ask questions, and attend both office hours and TA sessions when needed—no harsh grading system.

I had Pam for pre-cal in my first semester, and she was one of the best teachers I have had. She is so funny and creates an inclusive learning environment that encourages questions. She always has opportunities outside of class to meet with her if you need extra help. What is on the exams is clearly communicated by word or the Canvas reviews.

Pam is great! She allows cheat sheets on the midterms and your final, and graciously gives a review for each one as well. Lectures were never dull and I never felt discouraged in her class, truly a kind and passionate soul!
Pam is great! Only 2 midterms and she is so, so kind to allow a cheat sheet (for the final as well) and reviews before each one. Truly a kind soul.
This professor is genuinely the GOAT.

Pam is the BESTTTTTT. I took this class in order to prepare myself for calculus for the upcoming semester. She is honestly one of the sweetest professors and she's always ready to help. Her TA's are AMAZINGGGGGGG as well. Definitely take her!!

Attendance does matter in this class, aside from that, Pam gives you everything you need to succeed. She's super caring and tries to make math fun. She cares a lot about her students and is everything you should want in a teacher.

AMAZING, AMAZING, AMAZING. She's a wonderful instructor and her TA's are really good! Attendance isn't mandatory, but you have to be there to excel in the class. Her and her TA's make sure you learn the material and they are all easily accessible outside of class. 10/10 would recommend her as a professor.

Pam was such a great professor for a subject I was worried about. She is so nice, wants you to succeed so bad, and it showed with every interaction we had. 3 exams, but she basically tells you exactly what questions are on them, and allows for a double-sided cheat sheet. You will not find a better math teacher at this university so take her please.
Absolutely incredible professor. Not only is she funny and kind, but she knows her stuff and explains possibly difficult concepts in a really accessible and thoughtful way. I really enjoyed it.

Pam is the best professor ive ever had!! So good at explaining concepts and making sure you are understanding throughout the lecture. She is also very caring and wants you to succeed. Offers a one page front and back cheat sheet on every test. This course you are not allowed to use a calculator.

Pam is super supportive of her students and cares about their education. She explains mathematic concepts very clearly and uses fun activities to engage students. She is also hilarious and loves to throw jokes and stories into her lectures. Definitely recommend her!

Pam lectures so well and makes concepts so easy to understand. She is always happy to help you out with the material if you need and really cares about her students. Definitely recommend taking a class with her!
Professor Elias is such an amazing instructor, she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is really funny and engaging, and truly tries to strengthen benchmark math skills.

Pam is a great professor. She explains things very well and is more than willing to help, her goal is for every student to do well. She also helps you prepare for the test and make the concepts seem super easy.

Best professor I've ever had. Super kind- she genuinely cares about her students and wants us all to succeed. She is who I aspire to be studying education. Take any class with Pam!! You won't regret it

Professor Elias is absolutely hilarious and lectures extremely well. While the concepts can be challenging to wrap your mind around, she explains it so well that the class feels very easy. Her tests might seem difficult, but she prepares you very well, so there is no reason to worry. Totally would take this class again!

I found Lili's lectures very inspiring. It really highlighted how essential wireless is during the age of AI. The breadth of topics she covers went well beyond what I expected. Thanks to her engaging teaching, I've developed strong interest in wireless.
Lili is a fantastic professor. She is very knowledgeable, and her lectures are thought-provoking. I learned a lot from her. She is genuinely caring toward her students.

Professor Qiu was accommodating and willing to adjust her teaching to class feedback, but there was still way too much material covered. The tests were unfairly difficult, and as a result, the final grades were curved. I didn't end up learning much since none of it sunk in because of the rapid pace.

Worst professor I had in UT by far. People would regularly fail quizzes and homework. Test was insane with most people failing it. She didn't curve. Instead she gave a make up exam that was harder than the actual exam. She would go through 100 slides in one day or two if you were lucky. She was a nice person though, but the class itself was hard.

Prof Qui is a very very knowledgable person who knows a ton about networks. However, this means that she skims over a ton of material (80+ slides) every class and expects students to understand it. The lectures are dry and the tests were unexpectedly hard. She gives a ton of extra credit though. You learn a LOT in the class but its hard work!

reviews.comment: Hard exam, tough grading. Lectures is so boring that 90% class is not listening at all, people attend class just for the quiz. If you want to learn something don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible lectures, just read over 100+ slide every class and barley explain anything.

Qiu is a kind professor but the class is somewhat hard mainly because of her tests. She put hard problems that you never seen in HW or other places on tests so be prepared for that (still within the material though). Unlike other professors she tells you when you'll get a quiz to make you study. No textbook but lots of stuff in slides to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Personally I think the prof is very generous. Like someone said she will reschedule a few lectures that she can't attend, but attendance is never mandatory so it's your choice. Also, she ended up starting the test that person mentioned at 9am instead of 8:45 and extended the test for a total of extra 75 min! I justcan't complain more about the prof

Decent professor but bad with logistics; she tends to reschedule any lectures she can't make, and she will make you come early/stay later on test days. I didn't appreciate that she made the Final start at 8:45AM instead of the normal class time (9:30AM). There's a lot of material but she gives you tons of cheat sheets for the exams. Not too bad.

Qiu is a great professor. Her accent is definitely there, but not enough to detract from understanding (unless perhaps if you sit at the far back). Furthermore, she genuinely takes an interest in the class, promotes class discussion and participation, and makes sense of the material. She's an excellent professor.
Very thick accent
No Comments

Dr. Que was overall a very nice and caring professor, and you could tell she wanted her students to succeed but because it was her first time teaching the class you could tell there was a little bit of a learning curve for her. Not having taken AP Chemistry in high school, I found the material more difficult due to her lecture style and long tests.

Good professor with the best intentions. Just felt like the ability to actually teach the content was lacking, if you supplement your time or already took AP Chem, you will be fine. 3 midterms and a final project, the tests were long but graded fairly and with partial credit. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

This was her first year teaching the class, which was evident. Lectures mostly consisted of reading from an extremely long PowerPoint, and exams often didn't align with lecture material. Although the grade scale were curved at the end, the course was unnecessarily frustrating and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hard exams, but there's plenty of extra credit/exam retake opportunities; literally, you could retake any/all of the three exams for full credit. However, the lectures are extremely redundant, as she just reads off of the slides. Overall, she definitely cares for the students, but her expertise in the subject isn't super obvious.

Dr. Que is a kind person and cares a lot about her students. Her lectures can sometimes be hard to follow, but if you have a prior background in chemistry (like AP chem in high school) you'll be fine as long as you study outside of class. There are many many office hours opportunities and her and the TAs are all super willing to help you succeed.

For future folks taking her CH301C class: 1) Read and take notes on the textbook *while* doing pre-lecture HW, 2) There's also weekly chapter HW, 3) Exams are long and concept-heavy, lots of but partial credit is given, 4) Good amount of extra cred. opp, such as going to office hours (Que & TAs are helpful), 5) No final, just a chill group project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She's not a great lecturer and can be very disorganized, but she's kind and very willing to answer any questions you have. Very willing to accommodate your schedule for office hours and changed grading system for difficulty. Tests are very hard, even with having taken AP chem, online homework is clunky and unclear.
Dr. Que is a great professor and mentor. Prof dev is a free pass if you show up. I wish all of my chem upper divisions were like this one.

Dont show to lectures because she repeats word for word whats on the slides and still manage to stumble on her words, and then rewrite whats already on the slide with her apple pen. Spends time talking about the element of the day when she still have 75+ slides to lecture about. Creates long exams the night before giving them. Dont take her class.

This course is extremely challenging beyond all means. Exams are long, high-weight, and not curved, although majority performs poorly. Lectures often involve reading slides and can feel disorganized with frequent errors. It's her first time teaching gen chem, and she's currently the only instructor, so dropping may be necessary for some students.

Dr. Que is a wonderful professor. Her lectures are decent, but reading the textbook is required to fully understand the material. A basic background in chemistry is assumed, but additional reading is provided. She gives 100+ problems to prepare for exams which mimic the real exam almost exactly. Exams are challenging, but not overly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Que is the worst professor I had. First time teaching gen chem and it shows. Exams are long, heavy weight, no curve, rushed. Lectures are reading slides, messy work, and disorganized explanations that confuse instead of help. She makes mistakes and relies on students to correct her. If you lacked strong high school chem, this class is a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Que is talented in her work and is very nice; however, this does not translate to her skills as a teacher. Her lectures are hard to follow, and at times she will skip certain skills, as it may take too long to teach, or be stuck on information that won't be on the exam. No curve, her exams WILL be long. You will NEED DC Chem or AP Chem to live.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's nice, but the lectures are super hard to follow. she doesn't like to explain her work when "teaching" her lectures. If you didn't take AP/dual chem in high school, you'll be lost. For one of the exams, she made it too long and despite most of us not finishing, she didn't give us a curve despite acknowledging that the test was too long.

Can't even solve her own questions, even relying on students to help her. When she make mistakes (pretty often), she just smiles through it and laughs it off. Embarrassing for her honestly. Lectures are essentially pointless because she just reads off of the slides without ever explaining anything. Might as well be a biology major and take Laude.

Dr. Que is extremely hard to follow in lectures. She doesn't completely work out problems and expects us to follow unfinished messy work. She jumps from topic to topic with confusing explanations, does not simplify any concepts. Tests are too long, which she acknowledges but does not change. Can only understand material by teaching yourself.

Que is very nice and wants her students to do well. The final is optional if you do well on the first 3 exams since 1 of 4 exams is dropped. TA office hours were extremely helpful and exams were tough but not impossible.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She knows her stuff and answers every question you want her to. She is fun and engaged during lecture which kept me interested for the whole hour and a half. Multiple attempts on HW and the tests are fair. Lots of extra credit opportunities. She cares about our success! Would take again in a heartbeat.

This class was so difficult in the lectures were incredibly hard to understand. She uses um like its a buzzword and then she pauses for 15 seconds before figuring out what to say, which annoys me every time. 5 tests for this class on saturday and one on halloween. Umm no thanks. Im a chemical engineer and this class use to be easier by what I heard

Dr. Que was so unorganized and the notes during class were very hard to comprehend. We used TopHat which was not user friendly and also very unorganized. The tests were ok, but it's hard to study unless you have other resources other than the PowerPoints, notes and practice problems that she provides. Labs graded harshly too.

i hated every second of this class and im a chem major. she uses tophat which is very unorganized and not user friendly, she expects us to know various things about chemistry without a good explanation, she reads off slides, takes unorganized notes, is bad at speaking,when she doesn't know how to answer a questions she makes a joke out of it. help.

Que's super nice and tries her best to make the class doable. However, she can a bit disorganized and confusing. I felt super lost during the entire semester but once we covered all the material things started to connect after I went over all her tophat lectures in 1 sitting. The labs are chill and short but reports were pretty hard.

Lab reports were awful and requried 8+ hrs/wk of work. She gave past exams, but she made the more recent exams so much more difficult that they were basically useless. Went back on her word multiple times (e.g. "You won't need this for the exam ever", but it showed up on the final). She made this class harder than pchem or ochem were.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend enough. She provides SO MANY resources (past exams/practice probs/in-class lecture notes) plus the PDF of the textbook+textbook solutions (don't waste your money) to ensure her students succeed. Tests are lengthy, but she usually gives make up quizzes to earn points back. Seriously one of the best chem profs I've ever had.

I personally enjoyed her class. Very nice woman and tries very hard to present the material in a way that is easy for students to understand. She has not taught very much but she cares very much for her students. She also put a large curve on the class which personally I didn't even think was necessary as it was not hard to make a raw A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I guess I should cut her some slack because she's only been teaching for 2 semesters, but the way she structures her class is pretty terrible. She'd make us do groupwork for most of the class then attempt to cover all the material in the last 15 minutes of class. Exams were pretty hard, lab portion my TA graded pretty strictly, wouldn't recommend.

Dr. Que's class was terrifying. She is a great person, however it was her first semester teaching ever. It felt like she was never prepared for lecture. The test outline she gave before hand was basically what was on the test, however the test were still difficult. I ended up with a B with the curve, actually had like a C-

Quigley is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable in the field of journalism, as he spent many years working as an editor and a few years as a reporter. His approach to the class is very hands-on, having groups go through the reporting process step by step. Overall, it was a fun class, and if you want to be a reporter, it will be useful!
Quigley is a great professor, and this podcasting class was definitely one of my favorites.

Quigley is an amazing professor and a gem of UT. Assignments are really straightforward as long as you follow the rubric. He also invited alumni like Pulitzer winners and reporters to give unique Q&As. There is an overarching group project with a low-stakes presentation at the end, but it's easily manageable unless you're stuck with an awful group.

Had Quigley for 301F and it was a great experience! The whole class is basically step-by-step instructions of the journalistic process with a short, low-stakes presentation at the end. He also gets some very interesting and accomplished people to give guest lectures. Overall, Quigley wants the best for his students and creates a solid foundation.

For his first time teaching 301, Professor Quigley did amazing. The homework and group projects were easy to complete and content was well taught and easy to understand, especially if you have a journalism background. Quigley is funny and kind and wants the best for his students. Choose your group wisely, you'll be working with them all semester.
Everyone should take this class if they want to be a better journalist.

You can tell he really loves his job and especially journalism. There are two big projects but they are fun to do. There were multiple guest speakers which were pretty boring. There are multiple opportunities to get a good grade. Just go to class and do your work and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was already a fan of Quigley, but I really enjoyed having him again in Editing Techniques. Attendance is a big one in this class, so make sure you are willing to go or else your grade will get docked. Highly recommend taking Quigley in a smaller class setting you can get to know him better. He really is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It was an easy class with fun projects that were actually pretty helpful. It helps you improve at video and audio. However, the lectures were boring and hard to pay attention to and he doesn't allow people to take notes on computers/ ipads/ tech. Otherwise, pretty chill.

Professor Quigley was a great lecturer and gives great feedback. He really cares about student success and you can tell is very passionate about what he teaches. If you do good work, you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved this class! It was required for me, but it was genuinely so enjoyable. The class had one group assignment, and two major assignments for digital media. The TAs graded everything but he also looked over most things. The class is ~100 people but even so, he makes a point to meet with every person.

I love Robert. This is the second class I have taken with him, but this class was more close-knit as the class size was fairly small which made me nervous at first, but he is truly one of the kindest people out there. The course was very organized and he always took in our workload into consideration. 10/10 would take again.

love love love quigley! really made me excited to major in journalism and was very inspiring! he has so much advice and experience throughout his lectures that made them super interesting. also had lots of guest speakers that offered great information as well. only two major projects that are pretty fun to do imo.
You spend more time with the TAs in lab than with Quigley himself, but he's supper approachable and willing to help, as well as the TA!

Professor Quigley is so inspiring! In a sea full of professors nodding to how journalism is no longer a viable career, Quigley gave me inspiration and new excitement for my career in journalism. His lectures are interesting and practical and there weren't many assignments for the class. I've taken another class of his and I'm really enjoying it.

I loved Professor Quigley! He's clearly super passionate about journalism, wants to connect with students and wants his students to do well. Majority of grade is an audio and video project, and they're pretty easy as long as you don't procrastinate!

Professor Quigley is one of the best professors at UT. He truly cares so much about his students and their success out of college. There are two major projects, small easy assignments, and an easy final. Everything is graded by your TA. Super easy class if you pay attention and have some type of interest in journalism.
The best professor I have had at UT so far. He is so nice and approachable. on top of that the lecture content is interesting and an easy A if you come to class.

Best professor for freshman journalism classes. Entertaining lectures, but make sure to take notes for finals based on them. Most of your grades will come from your projects, which may be tough to learn, but time management went a long way. Aside from that, just a few assignments here and there. Quigley is very supportive; I highly recommend it!!!

I loved taking this class. I learned so many new things. Attendance is graded, I missed one class and it brought down my grade. There are two main projects, a video an audio project. If you follow what he says in lecture and look at the rubric then you are good to go. Easy A. He truly cares about his students and it shows.

Your grade depends on weekly discussion posts over a few podcast episodes. Overall the class was pretty easy and entertaining. Quigley is a knowledgeable journalism professional who tries to make the class entertaining while taking the course material seriously. I recommend it to those interested in journalism, true crime, or just a fun elective!

Quigley's a really nice guy & the class had very few assignments - it's really just focused on 1 video project and 1 audio project with a few random, easy assignments throughout. The lectures are not extremely valuable. You would be fine missing every class except for that attendance is graded. Overall, you only meet for the labs 5-6 times. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind, engaging, truly an advocate for his students and wants the best for them! He actively wants to know his students, and will still stop me to say hi when he runs into me around Moody! I took 301F and then immediately took true crime podcasting! Would recommend Quigley any day of the week!
He's one of the most kind and genuine Professor's out there. I would recommend anybody to take his course!
The BEST Professor EVER!

Quigley is my favorite professor EVER! He is so inspirational, and as someone who had zero journalistic experience coming in, he is reassuring and gives amazing career and learning opportunities. This course will change your life. You must try on your two projects, and don't be afraid to ask for help. I learned more than I could have ever imagined.

I love Professor Quigley. He makes class fun and interesting. Graded on a couple main projects that he provides lots of help with. Attendance is not required but the final exam is based on what is said in lecture.

10/10 one of the best professors in Moody. He is so knowledge and teaches his class in a very interactive manner. Most of this class is project-based which is tedious but rewarding. You learn how to use new mediums and become a better journalist. Get to know Quigley outside of class, he's truly a great person to learn from.

One of the best profs in Moody. He's approachable, an inspiring lecturer and so genuine: he actually tried to learn students' names. He gave a lot of insight about the industry and had great guest lectures. My advice: go to class/lab, ask questions, don't procrastinate projects. Reach out to Quig or your TA if you're struggling--they want to help.

Quigley is the best!! Even though his class was online bc of the pandemic, Quigley made the class so much fun and enjoyable. It is mostly project-based with plenty of time to complete them and your TA is always super helpful and resourceful. I really want to take another class with him and in person!! He's such a delight and loves what he does.
Amazing professor. Definitely best professor so far at UT. Lots of projects, but as long as you complete the requirements and try, you will get an A.

Professor Quigley was great, his lectures really helped you understand journalism in order to prepare you for future classes and your career. You had to put effort in the two projects he gives out, but if you just try your best you will do fine.

Professor Quigley is by far one of the best Journalism professors at UT. His course is fairly easy and he gives multiple opportunities for you to receive extra credit to raise your grade. He has experience in the field which made class more interesting. Lots of guest lectures which I found helpful.
Loved this class!!! Quigley rocks. He makes lectures engaging and really enjoyable even on zoom. Great class and great professor! TA matters though.

Whatever class you take with Prof. Quigley, I guarantee you'll enjoy it! His classes are super interesting and he often brings cool guest speakers to interact with us. Grade is composed by attendance and a few projects (video+audio+writing+some extra credit) - but don't freak out, it's all VERY doable! TAs are INCREDIBLE! I loved this class!
The best professor at UT Austin. Period.

I enjoyed J336F SO MUCH! It was so interesting and fun. Some of the projects require a lot of work and effort but they are so interesting and fun and are worth the hard work. Professor Quigley has made this class so interesting and he teaches it so well. I feel very informed and equipped with skills for my career after taking this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Quigley was immensely understanding and helpful during the transition to online learning. His focus was on students still interacting with each other and making sure you're still learning something. Great prof/course to end UT with.

Quigley is a great professor, but the more minute aspects of the class really just depend on your TA. The lectures are good, but if you're someone who keeps up with the issues in journalism, they're pretty much common sense. The class is pretty easy, but of course, you have to put in a lot of effort into the projects.

This class was a lot of fun and you definitely learn about a lot of new media. Quigley keeps the lectures interesting and lively. You'll have to actually try on the projects to make a good grade, but also a lot of it is based on who your TA is.

i LOVE quigley. he loves to help students and he really encourages them to have fun while learning. he doesn't expect perfection, he just wants to see you trying. I got a lot out of his class & not just as a journalism major. I always looked forward to his class & i'll definitely try to take more in the future

Quigley is so passionate about what he teaches and he really knows how to keep me engaged throughout lecture. It definitely wasn't my favorite class bc it was more digital based, but he made it not feel like a chore. Attendance is mandatory and you do have to try on your projects because my TA (Jordon) graded pretty hard. Overall really great

This course is required for my major and I honestly enjoyed it. I did have a really good TA (Chenyan). The grades are pretty much 4 quizzes (super easy but you have to ready), 1 test (stupid easy), 4 assignments (1 is a partner assignment), and 2 mandatory events (boring but easy 100). I started out with a 40% on a quiz but ended with an A.
Quigley's J301 class is mandatory for the journalism program, but he honestly made me fall in love with my major a million times over. I left this class so excited to tackle the reporting class.

I loved Social Media Journalism so much!!! Im not a journalism major, so I took this course for the flags. Quigley really makes sure you know how to improve upon your communication. Aside from the Tweets and Snaps, the quizzes are easy. His class made me figure out how to make my potential business shine.
Prof. Quigley has a gift for teaching. He's very down to earth in terms of workload and grading. I had an excellent experience in his class.

This class was such a blast. Even though it was online, it was very interactive and straightforward. All the quizzes are put up at the beginning of the semester so you can do them all in a few days if you wanted, or not. Quigley is THE man, and I can't recommend a class from him enough. Very up to date on media, approachable, and helpful. Love him

Quigley is an easygoing, genuine kind of guy. He enjoys talking with students and encourages big ideas. Overall, J302 took minimal effort but you learn so much through the small projects scattered throughout the semester. 10/10, would take again.

There's minimal reading which is all posted to canvas for free. He's very funny and personable. Genuinely cares about students and their future. There are a couple big projects but they weigh very little so it's more about the learning experience than it is about failing you. I would take him again without a doubt. One of the best professors at UT
Not many words needed rather that Quigley is the BEST professor at UT Austin.

I loved going to this class. Quigley and RB are wonderful. They are passionate and they know what they're talking about. I only had a problem with the group work because sometimes my partners would be flaky. Overall, I loved this class, it opens up a lot of perspectives in the field.

I loved taking Digital Storytelling! Quigley was always so funny, and he inspired me to look to different options for myself after I graduate. He opened up a whole new world of journalism for me. The class itself was easy, just make sure to go to labs. The TA's are flexible if you have an honest reason though.

Quigley knows his stuff! I had him for Digital Storytelling Basics, and he's very clear on instructions, and is very approachable when asking questions. A lot of the grades in the class are dependent on if you showed up to your lab days, however.  Show up and pay attention in class and labs, and you'll be fine! I really enjoyed this class!! 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lecture are clear and he talks about his anecdotes as examples for class. He is also nice to talk to and patient to explain concepts for students. Love him! Would def take this class again.

If you are ready to learn beyond the text of social media journalism, take this class! Get ready to work virtually as a social media journalist on the course's different accounts. I had a blast.  It is easy to get an A if you put the effort and heart into the work. I am not even a journalism major and this class was greatly beneficial.

Lectures are quick & interesting. No homework. 1 group project. 2 tests. No final! Need to read assigned reading (all articles) & go to class to do good on tests (which aren't hard if you do that). Loved this class & Quigley! Knows his stuff!
You can get an A in here pretty easily, but you have to do the work.  It's an interesting class, and I learned a lot.

Quigley taught this fully-online social media journalism class (J336). It was probably the easiest class I've ever taken at UT. You just have to tweet and use other social media platforms (Tumblr, etc.) to talk about news. There's an essay at the end (super easy). That's about it. Kind of impossible to NOT get an A in this class.

Really easy CS Honors class for grades, and while he covers important info, he doesn't seem to care about teaching so the class feels like a drag sometimes. TA Ziyi is the goat though, he's most of the reason the grades are so good cause Prof. Liu just comes in, lectures exactly till the class cutoff time, and then is the first one out of class.
For ML2-H, he is extremely knowledgeable and has good lectures and homeworks. It is also almost impossible not to get an A.
Took ML2 Hon and was a great class. HW and exams were directly related to course content and were similar to practice problems. Lectures were good as well.
Super easy class if you need a tech elective. Class was just basic HTML/CSS. Does take attendance on random days but gives lots of extra credit to make up for it. Great guy.

The professor is an extremely harsh grader, often deducting points without clear justification, making the midterm feel unfair. Although the final is worth 30%, the exams are excessively difficult and ignore students' balancing multiple finals. Despite claims of supporting student success, the grading and exams add stress rather than help learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quoc is genuinely a good and caring professor but the class itself is very hard with the final being the hardest exam by far.

Nguyen is honestly the sweetest professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and treats us like his own kids. From the very first day, you can tell how much respect everyone has for him. Even though the class is tough, he explains things so clearly and makes sure we really understand. He's definitely one of my favorite professors ever
Very hard class. Go to classes, take notes, solve questions.

Dr Nguyen is truly a once in a lifetime professor who genuinely cares about his students. If he thinks you are putting in ample effort, he will be flexible about your test grades and will give points back where he can. Exams are exactly like lecture examples and homeworks and are open notes. Show up to lecture and pay attention and you'll be fine.

The content is not fun, but he genuinely cares about his student's learning so overall it's not horrible. Don't skip class and follow along with his examples. The first midterm is definitely the easiest so try your best on that one.

We love Doc Quoc. He is literally the kindest, most caring professor at UT Austin. He spends lecture after lecture asking students what they need from him to succeed in the class; wanting nothing more than for students to understand the material. He gives completion homework grades, tells you the exam topics, and is very generous with grading.

Dr. Nguyen is an alright professor who knows his stuff about transport phenomena but his tests and homework are nothing like what he talks about in class. Although he tries to explain things thoroughly, it still does not make sense a lot of the time and the final exam is the hardest exam in the class.
Run
Fun Recpectful Loving Funny Smart Kind
Great professor who cares for his students. He knows his stuff very well and is always glad to help others.
He grades very haphazardly,and the course material is not very useful.
Great Professor. His class is relatively difficult and his tests are very hard. He curves at the of the semester so that everyone passes with an A or B usually.

Quigley is absolutely my all time favorite professor at UT. She is one of the most kind and understanding professors here. If you have the chance to take reporting words with her you ABSOLUTELY need to. It not only has made a difference in my experience in taking the class, but she also has made a difference in my college experience as a whole.
Professor Quigley is great. She gives great feedback and really cares about student's success. If you go to her office hours, you will get an easy A. One of my favorite professors at UT.
EQ is amazing. My writing improved so much because her feedback is so detailed. She is also a cool person overall. Labs are fun. Take her if you can!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Quigley was one of the best professors I ever had. She truly cares so much about her students and helps them with everything to succeed in journalism. She was always avaliable to help. Participation is also a huge part of this class.
Probably my favorite professor at the j school!

chose professor Quigley as your reporting words teacher. She's my favorite professor at UT by far and truly wants you to succeed. She's chill and laid back but also pushes you to be the best. She's someone you can go to for more than just class and understands reporting words is difficult so she's awesome

Professor Quigley is the kindest, most helpful professor I have ever had. She is super communicative and sends out weekly emails saying what's happening in class that week and lab with her is always enjoyable. She wants you to do well in the class and will go over your stories before they are due so you know what to fix. Cannot recommend enough.

if you get quigley for reporting words you have a guardian angel looking out for you fr. she gives incredible feedback and is super accessible. she emailedwith me at 10pm helping me with a cover letter for a job
go to her office hours. she goes line by line through your story making sure it's exactly the way she wants it before she grades it.

Quigley is an angel, and you will be extremely lucky if you have her. She cares so much about her students and is always ready and willing to help you with anything you need. My writing skills improved drastically after taking this class, and I credit much of that to Quigley. She tells you exactly what she expects and truly wants you to succeed.

Quigely is my favorite professor by far. Reporting words can be challenging and time consuming, but she will help you through it. If you show up and listen and ask for help you'll do fine. Super personable and you tell she cares a ton
I love Quigley, she is so awesome. This class will kick ur butt if you don't keep up with it.

Quigley is the most helpful and available professor I have ever had. She offers constructive criticism on every writing piece you send her and is just cool asf. This class is hard, but you learn a lot with the help of your lab professor. Definetly recommend taking her lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Quigley is such a valuable professor to have. She really cares about student growth and success. She goes out of her way to give honest feedback and clear writing expectations.

I really loved Professor Quigley! She is so understanding and accessible and super helpful. She won't go super easy on grading news stories but she will help you out during every step of the process! Labs are a great time to get to know her and other students in the class, and she is really funny and down-to-earth.

Quigley is amazing!! There are four profs who co-teach this class, but Quigley is by far the best one. She's incredibly helpful and always happy to answer any questions you might have. She also makes sure to properly prepare you for all the tests and quizzes. Her journalistic background makes her a great editor for a class where you have to write.

Nice and very passionate prof, interesting course. If your name isn't easy to pronounce you have to fight to participate cause you won't get called on. People in the front row get more priority. Be prepared for people to ask obvious questions/repeat wrong answers just for participation point. Constantly falling behind in lecture/getting off topic.

Business law sounds like it would be boring, but he makes it exciting and shows how useful it is for everyday life. He makes lectures engaging, interesting, and memorable. As a CS major, this class felt like a breath of fresh air. Definitely one of my favorite professors at UT. Just make sure to keep up with the readings and participate in class.

Prof Q is one of the best. You will want to show up to class b/c his lectures are so great, but be ready to raise your hand and participate for a grade. I didn't find exams too difficult, he will try to trick you but everything tested is taught in lecture. This class will make an impact on your life!

He truly cares about your learning. Attendance is not mandatory, but participation (speaking- he keeps track) is graded, so you should show up. His lectures are fun anyway, and his teaching style is easy to understand. He is also very funny and keeps his students very engaged. Just make sure you are doing work for his class or he will call you out.

Genuinely the best lecturer I have ever had, even for a class that didn't require attendance I found myself wanting to go hear him speak. If you knew me you would know how shocking that really is. Would highly recommend to anyone, he made what I thought was going to be a boring class for my minor into one of my most memorable courses ever

AWESOME lecturer, so knowledgeable, teaches so well, super inspiring and down to earth/real with you, useful content. Hardest part about him is his quizzes and test questions, he makes things tricky and traps you but also everything he tests about has been lectured over. Take him and you will appreciate how much you change + grow.

This was hands down the best class I've ever taken at UT. He gives 100% every single class and you can genuinely feel how much he cares about teaching and his students. I looked forward to every class because he made everything engaging and meaningful. If you get the chance to take him, DO IT. Easily the BEST professor at UT!

AMAZING. Resources readily available, TA's communicative, assignments clear and professor brought a warmth, passion, and enthusiasm that kept the room full every lecture in a non mandatory attendance class. This class made me remember what it was like to love learning. Best class I've ever taken, can't say enough good things about Prof Q.

I love this man; he is an incredible lecturer and an extremely caring, intelligent professor. I can't say enough good things about him, frankly. If you have the opportunity to take a class with Professor Quintanilla, DO IT! I promise you will never be bored in class, and you will always have a caring professor to rely on.

I am so sad I will be graduating and will not be able to take his course again. He's kind, caring, knows every student and will check up on you even after you are done with his course. Engages everyone and genuinely made me question if I wanted to go to law school because of how interesting this class was. Last day of class had everyone in tears.

Professor Quintanilla was incredibly kind, wise, and passionate. If I could re-take his course every semester I would. And the only thing I mourn about graduating is to not be able to retake his course again.

I looked forward to class everyday. Prof Q lectures in such an engaging and conversational way that even the most dry law facts become memorable. At first I was scared about the participation requirement but there were so many opportunities to answer questions. And he made it a point to remember students' names despite teaching hundreds a sem.

prof q is so goated. he truly cares about his students & it was one of my favorite classes. lectures were insanely engaging that it's pretty much impossible to be bored in class. we could use the textbook and our notes on exams & participation is part of your grade, but prof q made it pretty easy to get all your points. he also has the best TAs.

Professor Quintanilla was one of the best professors I have ever had at UT. His teaching style is incredibly engaging, and he offers patience to every one of his students when they make the effort. He connects concepts to the real world rather than teaching law and ethics in a sterilized environment. Read before class + participation is encouraged!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Quintanilla is personable, and an amazing lecturer. He makes concepts easy to understand and remember. I just wish grading was focused more on the material than participation in class and exams with questions about specific things from class. Make sure to read the articles that the TAs send out. Overall, a fantastic professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: only take this class if you're a good test taker. the exams are written in a confusing way so you can fail.

If you think law might ever be applicable to you, you have to take this class. This may be the best UT professor. The professor is amazing. Be aware that he is pushy to have participation in class, but the questions are low stakes and easy to follow. Class preparation can require some reading from a mandatory McCombs textbook which is not cheap.

This was the best class I've taken at UT because of the absolute passion Quintanilla has for the course. It makes you want to show up to lectures. Reading isn't bad as it's mostly learning about vocab concepts and learning how to apply them. If you have a chance to take any of his classes you will not regret it. Truly a role model.

Prof Q is amazing, and my favorite prof so far. He's super caring, very funny, and makes things genuinely interesting to learn. Everyone loved it, would take it again. Exams are a little hard, I attended almost every lecture and read and still never got above a 90. But still a great class!

By far the best professor I've had at UT the past 3 years. Please take this class for your business minor! Lectures are very entertaining, engaging, and he makes a point to get you to think critically. He's an avid hater of TikTok though :)

Professor Q is one of the best professors I've had, he is so amazing and really is passionate about what he does! The class is him having a conversation with you the whole time, as long as you take notes he will give you everything you need for the exams. Group projects are graded by the TA and are very easy. Participation is super easy as well!!!

This is the BEST class I've ever taken at UT. Prof Quintanilla teaches material in the most passionate, well-thought-out, relatable way - it's truly inspired. He does require class participation (has us pull out name cards at the beginning of each class), but believe me when I tell you it's never intimidating, and has kept me consistently engaged!

MUST TAKE! Best teacher in my entire life. Didn't know anything about law and still got an A. Stay up on readings to do good on tests. Tests are open note!! Go to the lecture, as that is where most test questions come from. Every lecture was so fun and entertaining. Truly UT's best professor!!

The BEST professor at UT. If you come to class and skim the textbook you'll be fine. Exams can be a little hard for some, but I found them incredibly straightforward since I never skipped class and did all of the readings. Genuinely my favorite professor EVER. He's an amazing lecturer.

THE BEST PROFESSOR! He keeps all students engaged and expects students to understand concepts (which he makes easy if you come to class) rather than memorize terms. I wish all my professors were like him, I definitely recommend him!

Professor Q's class was very insightful and helpful for the future. I definitely recommend taking him if you need a business credit (like for the advertising degree) like I did. He really brought the material down to a level that an average person could understand and made it engaging. Professor Q's passion for Business Law helped me actually learn

Prof. Q is of the best professors I have had at McCombs. He made the classes fun and made an effort to get to know each and every student in the class despite it being online. Pay attention to lectures and you will be golden for the exams.
Interesting lectures that keep you engaged. Not a difficult class but you need to pay attention and study in order to do well.

Prof Q is actually amazing. Caring, kind, and super good at holding the room and maintaining attention of the class. Wants to know your name! You MUST go to class to be successful on the exams, cannot stress enough. He has been my favorite professor at UT.

One of the best professors I have taken at UT!!! Prof Q is very charismatic and knows how to grab class attention. Attendance is not required, nor are the readings, but both are very helpful for Exams. The exam format is multiple choice, 3 exams, the first two noncumulative, and the last one is a term exam, so it is cumulative. Awesome guy

Lectures are everything. You don't have to read as long as you attend the lectures (I would still do it cause it helps on tests). Tests are open notes and mostly based on the lectures. He is genuinely so funny and has the best scenarios for class. Definitely my favorite professor and class at UT. He makes a hard class simpler! Take him!!!!!

This class ought to be required for all UT students - very important material, you'll thank yourself for learning it. Prof Q himself is an engaging and animated lecturer, I can't imagine anyone better to teach such an important class. Passionate, fair, funny, and sharp as a whip.

Prof Q is awesome!!! Business law/ethics is a tough, detail heavy subject that can be boring at times, but prof Q made this class quite enjoyable. There is not an insane amount of homework, just a few papers and like two group projects. Lectures were always interesting and enjoyable. Just go to class and you will do fine!! Highly reccomend.

He was so sweet & funny. To people who claim he likes to "trick" his students... if you came to class he literally said he would trick us on the test so whose fault is that? He does cold call but the class is fun so you won't be embarrassed or scared to answer. The tests do have specific lecture content, but they're easy. Textbook is super easy too

This class was my favorite class. He does cold call, but he makes it so fun that you end up wanting to participate. And this is coming from someone who never raises their hand.
