Theres so many resources to improve on lacking knowledge and the TAs are amazing, Mike is Amazing, overall great people. Tests are very nerve-racking but really not that hard.
He got mad adhd

Mike is a fantastic Professor. His entire course is very well designed as it all connects to each other in a helpful way. He is also an amazing lecturer and always told great stories. The homework assignments are each a week long but they don't take that long. The grading criteria is strict so you may lose a lot of points for a small mistake.
he is one of the best UTCS lecturers

Good, experienced lecturer. Assignments are clear/fair and easy, but TAs may nitpick pointless things. Tests are clear/fair and somewhat hard. The difficulty rating for CS314 (and CS312) is inflated since freshmen lack perspective; later courses will make Mike's courses seem more like a 3/5 (2/5 if you put some effort into doing the practice exams)
Horrible, pls don't take, traumatized me

Mike is a GEM of a professor with decades of experience marinating his grasp of the material. Clear, engaging lectures; extremely approachable during office hours and lecture. Exam performance disproportionately influences grade, but past exams are readily available. TAs are extremely astute and help ensure you understand concepts. CoStudy helps.

Mike is an AMAZING lecturer. While exams were worth 75% of the overall grade, he gave years of old practice tests that made studying easy. Some assignments took a while, but office hours with the TAs were beneficial in debugging. Grades on assignments can vary on TAs though. Overall, the class was a great first programming class at UT.

I really enjoyed taking his class for CS314, Mike is an amazing lecturer and while classes technically aren't "mandatory", I found his lectures to be pretty lively and informative. Some of the assignments can be painfully long and takes a lot of trial and error to finish, and your grade is based on 3 exams but you have tons of practice to prepare.
what the he's so funny and charismatic and somehow manages to teach all the material and always has good study materials for you to practice

Amazing professor for my first semester at UT. Highly recommend to go to every lecture, they are very engaging and relevant to the homework test material. Making the A is tough in this class, you have very little wiggle room if you perform poorly on even one exam. Homework grading is also tough sometimes but there are adequate slack points.

Mike Scott is a good first impression of the UT CS Department, especially since he'll be the first face many students see in their intro classes. From a fireman, to running a nuclear submarine in the navy, to being a CS Professor, he has proven to be determined at his job in educating the next generation of UT CS Students. Labs r hard tho lol

Mike Scott was such a good professor that he re-ignited my love for CS. Lectures were fun and digestible. Assignments were extremely well designed and guidelines were clear. Exams are tricky but there's so many practice exams that you can get a great grade with some work. He's been teaching this class for YEARS and it shows. You're in great hands!
Super amazing lecturer. Really engaging and fun. The final grade at 75% is very test heavy though. Not much you can do because this is a required class  \_(:/)_/.
GOAT teacher, regret being sleep deprived for most of his classes and passing out... TAs are too stingy with grading assignments though.
Easy class, didn't really learn much. Super nice guy, very clear standards, but lectures somewhat boring tbh and projects seemed uninspired.

This was a Python class. Material consists of the rough basics and various quick intros to some random topics Mike found interesting (various libraries, web scraping, image processing). Python proficiency comes from your own practice. Projects easy and interesting. Final project you get to choose, so difficulty varies. Final is worth alot, careful.
Best professor I've ever had. Lectures were inspiring.

His lectures are so rewarding and I learned so much about CS this year. However, the tests and assignments are difficult and you have to stay motivated and work very hard to get the grade you want. Very test-heavy!! Study very early and make sure you understand everything conceptually. TA OH are a life-saver, make sure you attend frequently.

Mike is the pride of the CS department at UT. An incredibly clear lecturer with so much enthusiasm every day. Very clearly outlines how to get the grade you want, in a fair manner. Tests closely mirror practice exams. Assignments are difficult but if you start early and ask for help (thru many avenues) you can succeed. Fav CS class so far, by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've ever had! His lectures were simply phenomenal as they were packed with information and funny stories that helped cement the ideas. The assignments and exams were VERY HARD. At least 10 hours per assignment and up to 16+ hours on the later ones. Curved/bumped every exam; won't give any extra points at the end for final grade

Mike is the best professor I've ever taken. His lectures are super engaging and really interesting. His exams can be challenging but he curves rather generously. His TAs grade the assignments rather roughly but you get so many points back at the end that it doesn't matter.

Scott is an amazing Data Structures professor. He is an expert on the material and genuinely cares about student success. The class is very hard yet rewarding. Make sure to start early on projects and to really study previous practice tests as exams are worth 75% of your grade. Your programming fundamentals will be heavily reinforced in this class.

I enjoyed this class a lot more than cs312 (I took it the year Ramsey started teaching it) and found the content to be a lot more interesting. Lectures are recorded, but I recommend attending in person anyway because Mike is an amazing lecturer. You will learn A LOT from this class. Go to OH often and study for exams at least 3 weeks in advance.

His lectures are amazing! He does go through a lot of content in lectures so go to class. TAs (who are amazing) are easily accessible so make sure to ask questions and make use of office hours. Go to discussion, and start on assignments early. Grades are cumulative and there are plenty of past exams available for practice.

Absolutely fantastic professor. Informative, engaging lectures. TAs and the professor are very available for questions throughout the week. This class will teach you a lot about the fundamental ideas of coding and things necessary to pass technical interviews. Remember to pay attention and you will learn a lot; as Mike would say, "Is so simple!"

I'm here solely for the degree, but Mike Scott's CS314 class was very pertinent to my career endeavors. Nothing comes as a surprise, just be prepared to learn and work. The TA team and Mike himself are very helpful and don't judge, so don't hesitate to use Piazza. Mike makes the lectures interesting to watch and is caring toward his students.10/10

Great professor! Lectures are very well thought out and is very engaging. He's very kind if you ever meet him during office hours and it's obvious how knowledgeable he is. Take advantage of the test review material he gives you, the test's are fairly difficult and weigh a lot.

He was a super engaging teacher but his assignments were often difficult and took a long time to complete. Tests also weighted heavy so make sure to study his previous exams because they are very similar, it's split into short answer and programming questions that vary in difficulty.

Great lecturer. Class has a weekly projects that aren't bad if you pace them out and go to office hours, the TAs and Mike himself are really accessible. Projects also aren't worth that much and you have some amount of points for free to cover for mistakes. Tests are a large portion of your grade and require you to prepare a ton, so study early.
Mike is an amazing professor that gives amazing lectures. Tests and projects for this class will be challenging and will require a lot of work, but you will be able to succeed if you put in the work.

Excellent prof. He understands the material thoroughly and explains it quite well. There is a gravitas to his voice and it reaches everywhere in the lecture hall without needing a mike(pun unintended). Programming assignments feel unfair at times due to code style requirements. Tests are difficult, but past tests are available for practice.

Mike Scott was one of the best teachers I've had in my academic career. He was thoughtful and engaging, and I could tell he really loved teaching. The coding assignments are graded a bit too harshly on style, and the tests are weighted too heavily, but the class is very enjoyable. I learned a lot and the content from the lectures stuck.

Easily my favorite professor/teacher of all time. The lectures are fun and engaging that make students think. While there are many projects, they usually aren't too difficult if you start early and go to office hours for help. There's plenty of resources and practice tests to ensure students feel prepared. I will definitely miss this class a lot.

Lectures were inspiring and informative. Provided more than enough exam prep resources to be successful. A lot of programming assignments throughout the course but very well structured and explained. Fun guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Scott had good lectures, but went through content too quickly, so I wish he would explain concepts in a more organized way. He was good at explaining concepts outside of lecture. His assignments are unnecessarily long & time-taking. Most of the grade is dependent on the exams, and the projects cut time away from its preparation.

Mike's Data Structures class has changed the way I view programming. His lectures are challenging, but engaging. The programming assignments, while long and difficult, are rewarding and are the best parts of this course. The teaching staff is also phenomenal. The tests are very difficult, but he has 20 years of tests online to study from. Amazing.

Mike is a phenomenal lecturer. He succinctly explains concepts while making it approachable to anyone taking the course. Programming assignments are not difficult IF you start early and take time to understand what it wants you to do. Tests are heavily weighted, but are OK if you take advantage of the many practice exams on his website. Go to OH.

What are you reading this for, his RMP looks like a manicured lawn. Class is designed to push you in multiple ways. Lectures are standard but good. Assignments teach good code hygiene and reinforce concepts. Tests are very disjoint from lectures, forcing you to study practice tests and learn extra things on your own. Hard, but has been beneficial.

Expect to spend considerable time writing code. Lectures move quickly and review little, but each one covers the topic in a concise manner. All of the staff is interactive and the community fostered is collaborative, within limits. Highly worthwhile class, especially considering its value in covering basic programming topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mike gives you a lot of extra credit (slack points) for non test grades which lets you do pretty bad on a couple of assignments for free. Lectures are important. Make sure you start assignments early since they may take several hours.

Lectures were funny, interesting, and engaging! Every concept came to life! However, expect to be challenged, especially on exams. Do LOTS (!!!) of practice exams if you want to do well, especially if you want an A. Don't make the mistake of thinking that prior data structures experience will guarantee you an A: you have to put in a lot of work.

Mike Scott is an exceptional professor. He is fantastic at explaining concepts, provides excellent analogies, and is knowledgeable and kind.

All previous exams are released, which helps with studying for the tests. Lectures are optional, but I would highly recommend going. Exams are heavy on your grade(75%). Expect to be challenged!

Mike Scott (no, not THAT one) is an excellent teacher. Even though CS314 is tough, from calculating tricky time complexities to balancing red black trees, he gave the necessary structure for success. That being said, one should review the hundreds of prior tests available on his site for practice constantly; it helps a ton. Preferred this over 311.
It's amazing how much you can learn from a 3-credit course under a good professor. I couldn't have asked for a better introduction to UTCS than taking this course.

A great professor, his class got a lot harder for 314 but that's expected, he remembers a lot of names of students who participate in his class and you can tell he genuinely enjoys teaching and helping people

Favorite professor ever, took him in spring 2022 and not only is he hilarious but probably the smartest lecturer you'll ever have, his class is definitely difficult but he provides enough makeup points that if you try hard you'll be okay

Mike is an phenomenal professor; there's a reason he's been teaching for 20 years. He has great analogies to explain data structures and algorithms, and his personal anectdotes and jokes make every lecture so entertaining. Even students that skip every other class will come to Mike's lectures. Office hours and TA's are helpful, watch out for tests.

Mike has amazing lectures that are very engaging. However, his tests and assignments are often pointlessly difficult. A huge portion of your assignment grade is based on a style guide he made that has pointless restrictions. There have been times when a test question has had multiple or no answers without any warning given.
The exams are tough but you get a lot to practice with. Mike is a great lecturer and you'll learn a lot in his class.

Mike is such an enjoyable professor. However, his lectures are only loosely related to the tested content. He uploads previous tests on his website which help a lot. The grades on the coding assignments depend heavily on who your TA is, but they don't weigh much and they help a lot to prepare you for the tests.

knowing java outside this class is the reason i did good. covers topics, but lectures usually consist of him writing new code for existing data structures to show how they work, so i didn't find them helpful past broad concepts. i found googling the data structures and doing the practice exams much more helpful for my grade. he's funny though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite CS professor so far. He has taught this course for many years, and the experience really shows. Assignments are somewhat difficult, but very fair and directly relate to lecture content. Tests are also very fair, he provides sample exams from past years which make them very easy to study for. Overall, FANTASTIC!

Mike Scott is the best! He prepares you for coding interviews (aka the stuff that gets you high paying jobs) very well. His lectures are super interesting and he's taught this class for 20+ years so the format of the class is fine-tuned for the STUDENTS success. One time I went to Mike's OH, and he stayed with me until 9pm helping me find a bug!

When I took Prof scott it was during the pandemic and I had no prior CS knowledge but even then he was AMAZING. His lectures were engaging and his class was so rewarding. I will not lie, the grading style and class structure will take some getting used to but overall if you start projects and test study early and go to office hour u will be fine!

Mike Scott is an amazing guy. You will learn the material very well. Of course the class is a CS course and will end up being a good amount of work and pretty difficult. But you can get a lot of help from him and others if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mike is a great, caring professor who knows the subject very well. Lectures are necessary to attend if you want to do well on assignments, and if you did not take C S 312, the style guidelines can take getting use to. The tests weigh pretty heavy in this class however accounting for 75% of the grade the semester I took it. Start assignments early.

One of the best lecturers I've had ever - especially for CS. Super engaging and makes material come to life with interesting analogies and anecdotes. Not one lecture goes by slow. Will definitely take again if I can.

Mike Scott is a phenomenal CS professor and definitely one of my favorite professors I've had at UT. Mike's lectures are super helpful and enjoyable, so make sure to attend. Programming assignments can be difficult, however, he definitely gives enough time to complete each one. Tests are weighted super heavily, so use practice tests to study!!.

Being honest, it's a filter class. It's gonna be hard first learning, especially if you don't have much programming experience prior, so you'll need to study. However, I will say the topics talked about are interesting to learn about, and the lectures are pretty clear to understand. Your TAs are going to be also a determiner too.

Michael Scott is probably the best professor/instructor I've ever had. He is very skilled at teaching and has been teaching for over 22 years. While I didn't get the best grade in the class I learned an unbelieve amount in his class with little effort because he teaches the material so well. 10/10

One of the best CS professors there is. Lectures are clear, engaging, and you learn a lot from them. Perfectly paced. Attend class and MAKE SURE TO TAKE THE PRACTICE TESTS!! I only pulled a B because I didn't put the effort in-- very easy to earn an A with effort.

This class is by no means easy but Mike Scott is an amazing professor. His class is very exam-based and counts for most of your grade so beware. I did spend over 5-10 hours in this class per week completing assignments and studying for upcoming exams. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!!!

Who doesn't love Mr. Scott? Fair warning, CS classes are hard and even if it says otherwise, experience is necessary. Mr. Scott loves what he does and teaches SO well. I was self taught in coding beforehand and love it but prof. Scott has ignited my interest in the subject even more. I'm not one to write reviews often but Mr. Scott is AWESOME!!

Mike is to this day (as a senior) one of the best lecturers I have had. He made me realize how interesting even the most basic parts of CS are, and this is done in the context of a well-organized course that is set up to help you succeed and learn as much as you want. Projects are time-consuming but mostly enjoyable. Exams are hard but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike is a great cs professor that is just so passionate about his job. His lectures are very very helpful for assignments and exams. The help hours/ office hours are available Monday to Friday. You are really gonna need these. Amazing professor, but class is pretty challenging.
Such a kind dude. Loved having him as my first CS prof in college. Knows kids by name if you talk to him in or out of class.

Attending lecture or watching recording is very essential to do well. Weekly assignments take a while but are super fun, but pay attention to style. Tests are very comprehensive and challenging and worth 75% of grade, and have lots of tricks, so do a LOT of practice exams. Mike is a really great lecturer, this was my favorite class this semester.

Mike Scott is certainly one of the best lecturers. His class is extremely interesting, even if you have background knowledge of the concepts. Attending was often the highlight of my week. However, grading is tough: TAs are inconsistent and tests have many trick questions. Luckily, Mike posts his old exams online. Study them and you'll do fine.

His exams thoroughly test your knowledge of every topic covered. I wish I had done more of the practice exams he had provided. I highly recommend showing up to class and taking notes, he is far more engaging in-person than on a zoom recording.

Mike is the best professor I've had thus far. He's a great lecturer, and the format of his class has been tried and tested over many years. The weekly assignments were a bit time consuming but not too difficult, but the tests were hard for me, no matter how many practice tests I took. Nevertheless, I learned more in this class than in any other.

Mike clearly has a knack for comp sci and cares a lot about his students, but he does make you work hard for the grade. Coding projects due each week and three main exams. He's a really great lecturer though and prepares you well for all of the assignments you just have to be willing to put in the work on your end too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mike takes a strong curriculum and makes it even better with his lecturing style. Universally loved professor, and he takes his role seriously as an instructor. There are a lot of assignments, but with the grading format it feels manageable. Familiarize yourself with the style guide! Nothing hurts more than getting 5% off just for variable names.

An awesome introduction to college coursework. Definitely a challenging class because of the weekly assignments, however, the lectures prepare you well for assignments and tests and there is not anything completely beyond what we are presented in class on tests. Mike's lectures are extremely engaging and he is skilled at conveying the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved his lectures, and course content was interesting. Styling on assignments is graded stringently. There is some variation here based on the TA. Help hours are extremely useful for styling concerns. A solid understanding of Java and programming is required to succeed. Tests are heavily weighted (study well in advance).

Mike is an amazing lecturer. That said, I learned almost nothing because I was so focused on the programming assignments. Grading for assignments is brutal (1 mistake  5% lost). Tests are weighted heavily and very trick question heavy, like UIL on steroids. Occasional typos on assignments and tests. Read the style guide many times, it will help.

Mike Scott is a great lecturer, but the class is very challenging. Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't really mandatory. Your grade will highly depend on the exams, and the TAs. TAs will try to take points off from your labs with random style points, so make sure to check over your code multiple times. Designed to be a weed out class :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor with classes that make you feel like you are learning useful information. CS 314 is taught using Java and projects can sometimes feel hard to figure out and style will be a pain point, they are great practice for the concepts. Exams are pretty hard but not impossible level. The multiple choice and frq are usually very clear.

He is an insanely good professor. Amazing lectures and very understandable. However, assignments are very toughly graded, and he prepares you very well for the real world. Getting an A in this class isn't that hard, just pay attention in class and make sure you follow the style guide for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: (Fall 2020) Great professor, great guy, learned a lot but you'll really have to work for your grades. Tests and programming assignments are weighed the most and are graded pretty harshly, so watch out for careless mistakes that will cost you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing, humorous professor. Difficult class with big workload. Grading is very picky, so just try your best and don't get too discouraged. Get a head start on the assignments. Take advantage of practice tests for the exams. Class takes a lot of time, but the content is great preparation for software development interviews. Vital class for CS.

Professor Scott's class was always fun to be in. Lots of funny shenanigans and we go over interesting material, so coming to class is recommended (Although you can just answer the instapoll and leave). There is an assignment pretty much every week and on weeks without them there is an exam. However, GO TO HELP HOURS!! The TA's are so so helpful.

Don't get the hype at all. Not at all a beginner friendly class. Looks down at you for asking questions. When you question him regarding grades he will regrade your exams and lower the grade so you would never ask him again. Not a good professor for beginner classes.

Engaging lectures, responsive to on topic & within scope questions, worthwhile assignments. Assignments are graded hard and take a lot of time. Tests are reasonable. He can be a bit crabby in class, but the quality of his teaching and assignments makes up for it.

Mike Scott is truly unique. He was a very good professor with only a few notable flaws. He explained the concepts extremely well but got irritated over the littlest things in the Zoom chat. If you have him online, PLEASE do not make ANY jokes in the chat. Also, be super prepared. This class is a very difficult, but ultimately fulfilling experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Oh boy, this class was horrendously difficult. Scott says his class is designed for people with no prior experience in programming (this was me), but it was NOT beginner friendly. Everything moved way too quickly. The tests and final are also very hard. Scott's a great teacher, but you'll definitely have to work for a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mike is an awesome teacher. He really cares about his students and makes sure that the material is well understood. He and his TAs are almost always available via Piazza or during help hours. This class doesn't have any mandatory readings/books so all the material comes from the lectures themselves and some from the assignments.

Mike is one of the best professors I've ever had. That doesn't mean he has no shortcomings, especially with tests. I don't understand why 75% of my grade is based just on tests. I spent far more time with assignments than tests yet all of them count to only 20% of the final grade. Typos in assignments' description need to be corrected. A solid prof

hard to get an A on the test (especially coding section) if you dont have a compiler built into your brain.. tests are less about data structures and more about if u can spot your small mistakes... nickled and dimed as they say. but i guess thats what we get since everyone at this school is smart. just make sure to drink coffee for the 9pm tests

Yes, Mike knows his stuff, and it may be because we're all online, but I don't see the hype. As someone mentioned, Mike has had outbursts before over small things in chat (some warranted, others not). Watching him code can be hard to keep up with, and tests are difficult to prepare for (even w/ practice exams). I'm just glad this class is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of work, but I learned a lot! Mike is humble, charismatic, no-nonsense, and knowledgeable with always-available TAs & help hours, but be ready to put in effort! Start weekly programming assignments early (takes 4-10 hours average for me). Tests are a bit tricky, please study FAR beforehand as doing assignments isn't enough. Dont buy the book.

Mike is a good guy and wants everyone to succeed He seems a bit stressed out. The UTCS department is putting too much pressure on him and it's falling on some of his best students who like CS beyond $. Pumping bots into big tech companies isn't enough. Companies expect more from students nowadays. UT needs to offer more professors and competition!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's not that Mike Scott isn't knowledgeable, but it's more about the fact that I don't think he's teaching us properly and his lectures are out of wack sometimes. When he codes, it's not great. Seems like he is quite unprepared at times. I expect more from a professor who is teaching a course that is essential for students' job interviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I mean what the heck man. I don't know if it's the fact that this class is online, but Mike Scott is not an engaging professor at all. He gets mad at small things even when students are being curious and asking questions, but when he goes off-topic it's fine. The tests are insanely hard with not enough time. Assignments are useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mike Scott's 314 class is one of the hardest classes I've taken. It makes it worse that tests are such a major part of the grade and can prove to be quite difficult. However, it is also widely regarded as the most useful course in the CS tract. It will be tough, but stay with it and trust mike. Looking back I'm glad I was able to take the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mike Scott is patient and brilliant as an instructor. He has a very strong operational knowledge of his material and the labs he assigns. Every test is new so you can refer to his old material to prepare. He responds very well to in class participation that is ON TOPIC and respects your time. A loveable staple of the CS education and a kind man.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 314 is a pretty tough class coming from 312, but it's absolutely doable. Mike is undoubtedly one of the best professors on campus, and you'll learn so much in his class. His lectures are funny, engaging, and instructive. He's just a fantastic teacher. The tests are kind of hard but fair. Programs aren't impossible either. Gonna miss his class!

Outstanding prof and course. Lectures are very entertaining. Mike illustrates and explains concepts incredibly well. Slack points reduce pressure. Requires a high level of problem solving in exams and HWs but that makes the course very fun and interesting. TAs and Mike provide extensive support (nearly 10-5 from Monday to Thursday). Simply amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, makes sure the knowledge stays with you after you finish 312/314. I would recommend focusing more on the exams even when assignments are due since the exams are worth 60% of your grade and are usually difficult. He really makes you work for a good grade, and I thought 314 was slightly easier that 312 (but 314 assignment are harder)

I had Mike for both semesters and he was a great professor, but the material is very very tough, especially if you haven't had much programming experience coming into it. Projects take a lot of time and are graded strictly, and tests can be difficult, but it's also a really rewarding class. the ta's and Mike are always there to assist which is nice

Great professor who is great at TEACHING - engaging, good explanations, etc. Weekly assignments take up a lot of time, but are only worth 20% of your grade, so you're better off prioritizing the tests as they're 70% of your grade and he posts every single past tests online. The efficiency/support from TAs is a bit lacking, esp if you're struggling

Mike is a fantastic lecturer and obviously loves his job. He is funny and is able to clearly explain even the most difficult topics during lectures. The weekly programming assignments require a decent chunk of time, but aren't too frustrating or tedious. The exams are made at the perfect difficulty. Expect to study the practice exams on his website

Mike Scott definitely helps you learn how to code more efficiently. There are weekly coding assignments that are somewhat difficult, but if you can manage them then you can certainly pass the class. The tests are pretty difficult and lots of points can be taken off for small errors, but other than that he's definitely the cs teacher you want.

His lectures are great. Tests are difficult, but very doable as long as you study. Assignments are fine if you start working on them early and put in the effort. TAs are helpful so go to office hours if you need any assistance.

Mike wants you to be fluent in Java by the end of this class. Start early on homework, and study hard for the tests. The test are all very doable, but even the smartest student needs to study for them. Overall, learned a lot, interesting lectures, and worked the hardest I've ever worked in my life.

By far one of the best lecturers at UT. His grading standards/lectures are very clear and fair. Definitely very very coding heavy assignments (1 per week). There is definitely a huge learning curve in the beginning, but Mike did a really good job in teaching us. Got a 75.5 on the first exam and ended with an A- so don't give up right away!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mike is one of the best professors you could ask for as a new CS student. Whether you come in with barely any CS knowledge besides AP CS or you're a hotshot who has oodles and oodles of UIL CS behind your belt, Mike has the ability to challenge you and engage you in new ways. A big thing is that you have to always be on top of things in the class.

Entertaining lectures where I learnt a lot. HWs are lengthy but are very fulfilling as you learn a lot. Mike develops your ability to problem solve on HWs and exams by providing practice it problems, practice tests and discussion problems. Him and his 10 TAs provide A LOT of weekly OH. Slack points account for life emergencies. Outstanding class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: CS 312 was honestly one of the most challenging classes I've ever taken but the most fun and enjoyable. Mike Scott is like the gold-standard for professors. His lectures will never bore you and are very funny. The programming assignments get progressively harder but make use of the TAs and Piazza. Tests are difficult but do the practice tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike is one of the best lecturers but that doesn't mean his classes are easy. I had him for 312 & 314 and every test was extremely difficult (no matter my confidence) & worth so many points. You can't slack off BUT that's a good thing bc everything he teaches you WILL BE needed for a coding job interview. seriously. Take advantage of this lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mike is the quintessential UTCS experience. Encourages you to ask questions. Very important CS topics are covered very well by his lectures; very interesting and rewarding class. If you put in the work, you will become such a better programmer. DON'T THINK ABOUT SLACKING IN THIS CLASS because you won't survive. Fair and clear regarding expectations

He teaches CS 314 better than CS 312, in my opinion. His assignments were mediocre, and he has no quizzes anymore just visit his section to get free points. His exams were difficult, but he did curve/bump the scores for all the exams to make the average at around an 80. Overall, solid lecturer and proper grading criteria.

Lectures are pointless and don't teach you how to do anything. It's just filled with talking about his children or about the history of things. We have way too many TA's who are generally unhelpful and confuse themselves. Have the flu? Too bad, you still have to go to the exam and class or get a 0. The prof can take sick days but you can't.
Very awesome guy, but homework can be tough and is meticulously graded. Overall, a good course.

Mike is an excellent lecturer -- attendance is graded, but it really is worth much more than the points you pick up to go to class. He is funny and a wonderful teacher. He and his TA's are accessible throughout the week to assist with any issues on programs. Lots of programs, and a hard class, but you will be rewarded for the effort you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike Scott's tests are filled with mistakes and you can't ask him about it. Unsure about a question? Typo that makes the purpose vague? "SORRY I CAN'T ANSWER any QUESTIONS." Prepare for a lot of work, only to be destroyed by the tests. The worst part is that mistakes go unnoticed. For example, some of his old test answers are wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mike Scott is a very charismatic lecturer that has his courses (312/314) fine-tuned to perfection. If you are average at programming, he will make your semester stressful and difficult. However, the satisfaction that you get when you go back home over break and work on a project and realize that you are now a god programmer makes it all worth it.

Pros: Fantastic lecturer Fun assignments Good coverage of material Exams are tough but fair Cons: Assignment handouts are overlong, yet fail to cover important grading criteria, creating a needless reliance on Piazza... Way too many TAs; some can't comprehend much beyond basic Java... Automated grading can feel arbitrary, style even more so...

This lecturer is very great. His lectures and interesting and he explains things very well. Attendance is mandatory and there is one quiz every week. His grading is very clearly laid out and tests are not too hard. He posts old tests to use as study material, so preparing for tests is very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike is an amazing professor, and it is obvious that he has perfected this class over the years. He has clear grading criteria and his labs, though time-consuming, will make you learn a lot. He has released all of his past exams which you should study with because they are difficult. Although not easy, 314 with Mike has been incredibly rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mike is the best professor I have had. Before taking his 312 class, I had no coding experience at all. After that class, I felt somewhat knowledgable, and after 314, I feel significantly more so. He gives is a lot of work, and the tests are honestly pretty hard, but the class is so fun and interesting if you are willing to put in the work.

Mike Scott is a force of nature. Mike Scott is unpredictable. Mike is love. Mike is life. In all seriousness, it was an amazing class. The tests nearly killed me, but I made it. This class was more stressful than working in commercial refrigeration repair, which is largely composed of fifteen-hour days in the blazing sun on someone's roof.

He's great for people with CS experience, but for people without any experience in CS it'll be very difficult for you to do his exams, quizzes, and programming assignments. Overall, he was alright but I felt bad for anybody who didn't have any CS experience. He is a harsh grader on the assignments, mediocre on the exams, and easy on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mike is a great lecturer and explains concepts really well. The assignments are not terrible, just don't wait until the last minute. Also make sure to compare your output with Mike's output as they are really picky about that when grading.
Assignments and exams were straightforward but grading is very strict and penalties are high. Assignments do take a lot of time but are doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Difficulty if you took CS before: Fairly Easy A. He was a really good lecturer and great at explaining concepts. The assignments were the appropriate length. The amount of effort required was just right. It seems like this class has been fine-tuned to be close to optimal.

Fantastic lectures. Prof. Scott genuinely cares about your learning; him/TAs are very helpful during office hours. Assignments are not too difficult if you put the work in. He provides plenty of exam prep material. Gave me a solid foundation in programming. Overall, a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An instructor doesn't get any better than this, you just have to put in the work
Fantastic professor, taught fundamentals well.

I loved this guy, he was well spoken and definitely knew what he was talking about. However, never in my life have I had such terribly strict grading, I already took intro to java at A&M and did well, but I would literally spend hours on assignments and get a 40 if my output was off by one character. Tests were way to long and left me with no time.
I left the Computer Science major for a reason, but I still think that he was a good professor. At least he gave engaging lectures and had a sense of humor.
Great professor who keeps lectures interesting and informative.

One of the best professors in introductory Computer Science anywhere. Crisp, clear, and heavily detailed lectures that drive in necessary concepts for you to be able to advance to the next level. Absolutely amazing.

Listen. If you struggle with anxiety beware of this class. I took programming all through high school but had a hard time in this course. I went to office hours often but its very stressful because there are so many other students there. Scott isn't very accommodating towards students with disabilities and CS in general is a neurotypicals only club
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mike does a really good job making sure you understand Data Structures and basic Java programming well. I've learned a great deal and can immediately apply my knowledge to projects, interviews and internships. You have to work hard in his class and do multiple practice tests to do well, but he grades fairly

Michael Scott is a great lecture, I actually really enjoyed going to class each day. The assignments are doable but take lots time. Spend most of your time studying for tests, they're the majority of the grade. The grades are fair and you can use Mike, TA's and Piazza for help. Download the chrome extension Mike's Got Style to get an A in the class

This is the hardest class in my freshman year. He gives amazing lectures and you can learn a lot of things through his class. Homeworks are time-consuming and graded pretty strict. There are two midterms and a final add up to around 70% of the grade, tests are somewhat difficult. In all, this is a great class but need to take a lot effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Study for the exams. The assignments are obviously harder than 312. If you pay attention and do the assignments and study for the exams you should be fine, but stay on top of things.

Mike Scott is a great professor. He is passionate about the field and delivers his lectures well. You'll learn so much from him and the weekly assignments. I would recommend studying for the exams though.

Mike defined my freshman experience. His charisma, well-placed jokes, and patience in teaching data structures indicates that those countless years of lecturing experience have indeed paid off. The grading has a significantly subjective dimension to it, however - but that is taken care of by the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was amazing, although I didn't do the best. I did learn a lot, and Mike's lectures teach you what you need to know. I also really appreciated the labs, although time consuming. Take advantage of the test practice resources. He posts all previous exams he's given and the keys to them. This class, although challenging is really rewarding.

Mike Scott is an amazing teacher/lecturer, and you will learn a lot from him if you take his class. However be warned! This is not a blow-off class, and you better be prepared to spend quite a lot of time doing his programming assignments and studying for his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I skipped 312 and went straight into 314. This class was a difficult transition between high school to college, as points can easily be lost from small mistakes on quizzes, labs, and tests. But Mike is a great professor, and you will learn a lot from his class. There is almost always someone holding office hours during the week.

Mike Scott's data structures class is great. While it isn't easy, he provides so many resources to help you succeed. The TAs are very accessible for help on programming assignments, and each assignment is useful and relevant to the class. While his lectures sometimes didn't feel totally focused on the most important material, they are still helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Mike's lectures are amazing but the class itself is a mixed bag. If you have no cs experience coming in, you're going to have to do a lot of outside practice to catch up to others in the class. The class has three tests which count for 65% of your grade so you'll have to focus a bunch on those. And go to office hours if you ever need extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice lecturer!
he gives amazing lectures and his tests are not hard, plus he gives some extra points

Learned a lot in this class and spent the most time on it by far compared to the rest of my classes. The assignments are time-consuming but easy to do well on, and the quizzes are not graded very harshly. However, the tests were very hard for me but passable if you put in the time to study. Don't buy the book use the 3 edition which is free online.

Good lecturer, however unless you're extremely smart and if you care about your GPA, I don't recommend his class. The way coding assignments are graded is kind of unreasonable. You could have all the methods done, experiments, and pass all the given tests and still fail the assignment pretty badly because his grading tests are very different.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Lectures are engaging and organized. Assignments are interesting and drive home the concept at hand. He's a nice guy, just take his class seriously and be respectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best CS teacher I've ever had.

Great lecturer and easy-going guy. Lots of online resources to help you prepare for tests and coding assignments. Only thing I didn't like was that we had to write unnecessary tests for our code, and that felt like busywork.

One of the best teachers I have ever seen or had. Lectures are very thought provoking and fun to listen to. One of his best traits is his ability to explain abstract concepts in a clear way. If you have the chance, do yourself a favor and take him.

A lot of people really love Mike, and as a person I can agree. However; for someone who teachs intro courses I found him to be unreasonable.  You will learn a lot, but if you have no prior CS experience, and are worried about the UTCS GPA requirement the first year, I suggest Novak.

Mike Scott is a very genuine guy, I personally enjoyed his lecturing, he was funny, and also good at explaining things. Most of the things you learn however are going to be through the homework since that is really where we practice the concepts that we learn in class. The TA's and Mike Scott are pretty much always available to help though!

Mike Scott is a fantastic lecturer and really cares that his students' understand what he is teaching. You will definitely learn the knowledge needed for the workforce. This class however is quite difficult and will require a lot of work outside of class to do well in. Then again, you probably didn't choose CS cause it was easy :)

This man is an absolute disgrace of an educator. His grading and late day policy is ableist. Everything about his class is artificially difficult and designed to demoralize.  Apparently being hospitalized and not having access to a computer isn't a valid excuse for needing extra days to complete an assignment. Take Novak for 314.
Great teacher 10/10 would take again

I absolutely loved taking Mike's class. He was a great lecturer and you can tell he really cares about the material and helping students understand it. I did go into the class with some prior knowledge of the course content but the way he taught and assigned work allowed me to learn and grow as a programmer anyhow. Would highly recommend!

Amazing professor, I started off with no experience in CS and I have learned so much. He's super awesome at explaining concepts to beginners like me and he's a really sweet guy. Be warned though, his class won't be easy, you will have to put a lot of effort in it (at least if you had no previous experience in CS312).

Mike is a fantastic lecturer and really helps you understand the material, despite the speed with which he teaches. He's pretty funny, and overall a really nice guy and professor. His assignments are challenging, but there's always plenty of help so you never have to struggle alone.

Mike Scott is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's an amazing lecturer and willing to help students. I'd done some CS before and didn't find his class hard. He focuses a lot on "clean code" and is really good at teaching the basics and how to write nice, readable code. Tests are definitely lecture based and attendance is a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a very knowledgeable lecturer, and is very clear in what he expects out of your work.

Mike Scott is the best. He's so passionate about teaching, and it shows in his lectures. You do have to put in the effort, but what you learn in this class is SO important. He gives you all the past test so you know exactly what he is going to test over, and there are many resources for you to do well on the projects as well.
Great teacher
Engaging lectures and not at all condescending.
lectures were sometimes pretty boring. homework took so long and tests were tough. i didn't really enjoy the class but that's just me.
Amazing lecturer, well designed projects that teach you the material well. The tests are very similar to the in class examples as well as the projects. Very, very helpful at office hours.

Has great lectures and his projects are well designed. The projects do a good job of helping you learn to apply the material. Tests are all pencil and paper so they can be difficult, but there are plenty of review materials (including past tests) so they're manageable if you work hard.

Amazing professor. Difficult grader and you have to work hard to keep up with the class, but in the end, you learn quite a lot. Tests are hard, entirely hand-written, and mostly problem solving based.
Good explanations, makes sure you understand. Lectures were never boring, so this class was my favorite class of the semester. Overall, VERY interesting and intelligent man.

Mike Scott is the best teacher I have taken at the University. I took him for both 314 and 312, and honestly he just made every class so fun. He has a great personality and he'll have you laughing at just about everything he says. He's also an incredible teacher. He explains things so well that I never needed to take notes or read a book.
Great teacher and super engaging.

Great professor. Don't be afraid of him and go to office hours to ask any questions (he's super helpful). Textbook not needed but can be used as further reference. Grading of coding assignments depends on your TA (some are tougher than others). Exams are graded pretty tough by both TAs and Mike. You'll learn a lot. 1010 would recommend.

You have to study and do the homework (on your own without any help). Other than that great professor. Entertaining and helpful. However like all the professors in UTCS they are very much bureaucrats who guard their right to grading like it is sacrosanct.

He's seriously such a great teacher. He really knows how to explain CS concepts, even to those who have never programmed before. He is also EXTREMELY nice in office hours. Projects can be time consuming but the class is manageable. TY Mike for 2 awesome semesters.

A great professor overall, good at explaining and very willing to help. You will need to work for your grade though and expect to spend some time studying and programming, especially if you haven't worked with data structures before!
He is the best CS 312 and CS 314 professor. Projects due every week but they are useful and he will always help you. TAKE HIM!

Not sure if I just had more of a life than other CS majors, but Scott was the worst professor I've had at UT. He made me change majors because he's ridiculously confusing in class and assigns lengthy, tedious coding projects. He's won awards, but I don't see why. His teaching is so military. We're students, not pros. He's picky on grading. Tough.

Mike is a fantastic lecturer;  he somehow manages to make data structures interesting, communicates clearly, and keeps the atmosphere pleasant with his engaging personality. Genuinely a helpful, friendly guy. Beware, however, that his assignments can be somewhat long and tedious at times.

Mike is a good teacher, his lectures are very helpful and informative and he explains things well. However, you need to put a lot of effort into this class if you have never programmed before. The later assignments can be difficult and will take up time. Office hours are very helpful if you're stuck.

Mike is an awesome lecturer and will answer questions as best he can. He fcuses mainly on software development more than theory. He has clicker questions in class that are participation but aren't worth much in terms of your whole grade. Mike really cares about his students and it shows, especially if you see him during lab hours.

I loved Mike's class!  He was clear in his expectations and grading.  His lectures had a logical, geeky-type humor to it.  You have to put a lot of work in the class if you have never programmed before (or if you have never done Java), but Mike makes sure you learn everything.  I recommend going to his lab hours, as it will make the class easier.

This is ultimately a weed out course for CS. Learning JAVA is not the easiest thing when you have to take other classes including calculus. It's definitely not easy and it's very technical. If you don't apply yourself and study a lot, it'll be hard especially if you've never programmed. Mike is cool and his lectures are fun but they didn't help me.
Mike is a fantastic teacher. Super helpful and tirelessly available. The class is challenging but interesting. He really strives to make the content relatable and entertaining. Strongly recommend.

He's a great teacher. The assignments weren't short, but they were worthwhile and fun. He's the kind of teach where I didn't even have to take notes; his lectures were interesting enough for me to just listen and absorb the information.

He gives extra credit from the iClicker for going to class which is very helpful.  This class is tough although you will know data structures well. He is a bit harsh on grading, no regrades.  That being said, he is very helpful if you do not understand something and ask him in office hours.

The topics in the class are well presented in class.  The lectures are entertaining and stimulating.  The projects through the semester will teach you a lot although they were, more often than not, way too excessive.  The coding didn't make them excessive, it was the required test cases and experiments.  This class is A LOT of work!

His class really made me like programming. Granted, it was rather difficult, and he's a little intimidating to approach during office hours, but he's funny and very to the point. It is a hard class though. It totally a weed out class for the major.
He is a great professor, and is lots of fun to listen to. Makes sure that everyone understands as long as you ask.

Mike is a fun guy. Overall a good teacher; the workload is reasonable and he puts all his old tests for reviewing. It's important that you get a nice TA though, because mine was terrible and took off lots of points for irrelevant stuff on the assigments.
Very good teacher, lots of homework but they definetly help you out and make you learn the material, old tests are online so they you can prepare-best idea ever.

While the first half of the course is very primitive (variables, functions, oo) for anyone with ANY CS experience, the second half is a good refresher for data structures.  The assignments increase in difficulty, but are always manageable.  Mike is a very talented lecturer, and explains things well to people who don't already know the material.

coupled with the right TA, easy A if you just show up and do the work, provided of course you also understand what's going on.  definitely entertaining and very good at breaking down where you are comming from when asking a question so you get a relivant answer that helps you to understand.
Great teacher, fun to learn from.
No Comments

He was a great teacher and very happy to teach. His patience is without bounds and he keeps all his power points online for easy referral. Plus, all his old tests are online so it's great practice for tests. Start assignments early and do the practice tests before the exams!

this course is very hard, don't get me wrong, mike is a good teacher, his class is pretty interesting but cs isn't for me so therefore made it very hard. there are programs due everywk on fridays and he has 3 exams and a final.exams/finals consist of coding questions and some mc questions.
Mike is enthusiastic about the material and obviously enjoys teaching. Recommended. You will need to invest time outside of class to complete the assignments.
Hey what can you say against a guy who throws candy out when you respond to his questions?
Programming assignments are pretty difficult. In-class lectures are reasonable. Instructor is very attentive to questions and comments.
Articulates difficult concepts easily. Assignments are challenging. Exams are fair.
Somewhat easy class; has a time commitment. Some of the projects are hard.

I'm not a gov major nor pre law (to show my lack of qualifications going into this class). Dr.Sager is not that bad, if you put in the work. LOTS of reading and there's only 3 (ish) grades that go into your final average. However, if you go to office hours and engage, he is a very entertaining person and I learned a lot from his frequent rants.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Despite all of the negative reviews on RMP, Dr. Sager is the best pre-law professor at UT. Do the readings, participate in class, and talk to him and you'll be fine. He has right wing views, but will listen to your opinion and truly consider it. If you're not pre law, don't take this class. It's way too difficult to not pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am not a fan of Sager's teaching style. He is not very engaging to listen to and does little to explain cases. Don't expect to leave this course with a deeper understanding of any topics or cases. Often, it felt as though even he was confused and didn't have a clear line of reasoning. I got by with knowledge from past classes and the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take if you care about your mental health, graded on 3 exams each requiring memorization of 35+ court cases, including random stuff like special interests of justices. Incredibly politically biased and makes it known, expects 5 court cases to be read in depth before class. Worst class I have taken at UT as a jr.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
85 year old trumpy
lectures make no sense 
theres no notes 
you are teaching yourself

Even though Professor Sager should probably talk about politics and his own personal beliefs a little less, I truly respected his passion for teaching and the subject matters (I took three total courses with him, and I feel better-prepared for law school).

Legit the worst class I've taken at UT. Prof just rambles about nothing for the majority of the lecture and expects us to read 5+ full length court cases plus the readings each day. Tests were insane and one of the books he assigned was literally just his "close friend"  Clarence Thomas' autobiography that had nothing to do with the class content.

The class was incoherent. His lectures are tangents, and his tests are poorly written. You should read all the books and cases, watch the movies, and memorize EVERYTHING. Only take him if you plan on going to law school. If you teach yourself the content effectively, you'll develop good argumentative and legal briefing skills. Wouldn't recommend.

Sager is hard because he gives so few As. Good law school prep, but I actually don't think it's worth the risk of hurting your GPA. Absolutely don't take his classes unless you're pre law. Otherwise, the class is fine and Sager is nice and has fascinating lectures. I'd stop short of saying he's ‘caring' though like everyone else here.

This is a valuable class if you want to go to law school, and I respect Dr Sager for his expertise in the field as he is a big deal in politics. That being said, he has wild far right views and will not shy away from expressing them randomly during class. The tests are insane and rely on memorization of everything specifically judges' opinions.

If I had to take one of Dr.Sagers exams again i'd probably choose blowing my brains out. they are FULL of gotcha questions and he doesn't update grades so your final grade ends up being a surprise, loads of reading, the coursework is valuable for law school but take at your own risk you definitely have to apply yourself for exams that are a set up!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Come prepared!!! Your grade in this class is entirely dependent on you. The course is hard but if you're hoping to attend law school (most people who take this course are), this class is great preparation. The little annoyances of the class (like the website) are worth dealing with. Sager truly cares about his students. Go to beers hours!

If you care about your sanity you will not take his class. He refuses to use canvas, instead he uses a website that's outdated & hard to read as it's full of typos, formatting errors, different fonts/text sizes. Lots of homework but tests aren't related to the course material & he refuses to provide reviews. He's not afraid to be racist & bigoted.

Dr. Sager knows a lot and is very well connected.  However, he goes on so many tangents during lectures that it's not even funny, and his website is simply atrocious.  Learning is mostly self directed, but that also means that if you're lost, god help you because nobody else will.  He should probably retire and spend time with his family.  He's 85.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: very self taught course with all the readings, but he does question and challenge you during lectures. COME PREPARED!!! overall he's very caring of his students and is very well known and respected within government and politics.

Amazing professor. If you plan to go to law school definitely take his class. It's a lot of reading and memorization but you definitely learn a lot. Participation matters and Dr. Sager is so sweet. The TA does the written response and essay grading so it really depends on that.
The tests were terrible but Dr. Sager is a sweet old man. Go to his beer hours at the Cactus.

Content of the class was really interesting. He doesn't elaborate on the cases you need to know in class though, very much skims content, and goes off topic for a good portion of the class. He cold calls which forces you to come prepared to class. You do have to study a LOT for the tests though, test more of your memory than application. 8/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Usually tends to go off topic. He also talks casually and questions you on every little thing (in a good way) so that you really understand what you are talking about. Class seems intimidating and overwhelming, yet it is not bad. Make sure to study for tests, because they tend to go really into detail
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sager was amazing in a sense that he cares for his students and is very insightful when it comes down to the legal realm of things, but the structure of the class make it difficult. Lectures are all over the place and the exams are tedious. What you learn truly does alter your brain for the better, but it is definitely not an easy A.

Frustrating lecture style, and even more frustrating exams. The content is very interesting and can definitely learn a lot just from the cases alone, but the actual structure and teaching style of the class is chaotic. The exams have about 60% fair questions that are related to the course content, but the others are more just gotcha questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Its a difficult class but it prepares you for the legal world. He challenges your statements as a way to make you articulate them and think about them in a deeper way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Sager is difficult and opinionated but he never tries to influence or belittle your views but be ready to articulate them. A lot of reading before class but the information is extremely useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very difficult course that requires lots of studying for difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken Dr. Sager more than once, and I can assure you that he is easily one of the most well-informed and well connected professors I have ever had. As a senior, I am incredibly thankful that I took his course and I recommend anyone interested in going to Law School to do the same. #GOAT

Alan Sager is on a different level; he has a wealth of an experience in almost every field. He worked with the supreme court and has personal relations with many politicians and the elite. He is the most well-versed professor in the department and encourages civil discourse in a class setting which is essential to a functioning democracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with Professor Sager, I repeat DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS MAN. Course itself is subpar, you will be required to learn everything on your own as he spends the entire class rambling about other topics. Participation will not be rewarded either, as he will forget who you are.

Took his class in fall 2019 and it was by far the hardest class I took in undergrad. It was an insane workload, so don't take this if you're busy. He gets on tangents for 90% of the class and doesn't actually explain anything from the readings, just shows charts without any kind of guiding key. Can't speak to his COVID policy but probs not great
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sager is conservative but you don't have to agree with him to realize that he is a very good professor. Admittedly, he also gets off topic often. Yet, I would still say he's the best professor I have had the pleasure to learn under. Lots of reading but if you have a genuine interest for the courts, you won't regret it. Cares for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, like almost 50 pages of reading a day. You are expected to have all cases assigned briefed in class and he will cold call you. Still, he genuinely cares about his students and you will learn and do well if you stay on top of readings, videos, and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I've now had Sager for two semesters. I really enjoyed the first semester, but he claims "now that covid has passed I will not be grading the same". Each test contains 50 cases, and you must know every word if you want to do well. He is very respected and very conservative. I only suggest it if you have an easy course load and have a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: readings are long but if you actually do them you should be well prepared. He's annoyingly conservative and likes to spend half of class talking about his political views. You do most of the learning yourself but thats what college is supposed to be. It's a hard class with a LOT of homework but very rewarding
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A good man but honestly the worst professor I've ever had during my university experience. He rambles during lectures, the workload is insane (30-50 pages per night + fully drafted court briefs every class) but doesn't adequately prepare you for exams, and the exams themselves are riddled with errors and mistakes. Don't bother with this professor.

He can't teach and spends most of class talking about his personal life. Don't take his course. Also I don't know why so many people are saying he's a highly respected lawyer, because he only practiced law for a year. He's a much bigger name in politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ideologically challenged, but you'll get a lot out of the course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Firstly, Professor Sager is outspokenly conservative. If you can't handle his repeated political comments then you're skin is too thin for this class. He teaches really well and is very funny. He cares a lot about making sure his students learn. If you do the work this class will be extremely beneficial. A lot of work but amazing classing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His class Law in Politics focuses a lot on campaign finance issues and Supreme Court Cases. He takes attendance and practices involuntary participation. You never know when he will call on you and you have to be prepared. He expects you to know intense details as far as each Justice's opinion on each court case well enough to identify quotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I've taken 2 classes with Dr. Sager, the first I got a B+ and the next I got an A. You have to learn how to study for his tests (really go hard on the cases and pay attention in class) Elephant in the room is that he's a conservative who loves to yap about it. It gets a little annoying, but if you put up with it, you will learn a ton in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Subpar class. He spends 1/4 to 3/4 of the class talking about things that are irrelevant to the class and has an awful website instead of just using canvas. The class is very poorly organized, we were behind the entire semester. The tests are riddled with spelling and formatting issues, and every one has questions that are completely subjective.

I've taken a few of Dr. Sager's classes now, and I've loved every single one of them. He's fair and honest, and really hilarious if you get him off on a tangent. His tests are hard and you'll probably have to pull some serious study sessions the couple of days before but you end up learning so much that it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sager is the absolute best professor in UT period! He is amazing, wise, and charismatic! He has the brains Archimedes and the looks of Paris!

Sager is a highly respected lawyer so don't be surprised that he does not go easy on his students. He uses the socratic method so you must be comfortable being called out on for very in depth knowledge of cases (I thought I would hate it but loved it because of the motivation to study). If you are pre-law this should be at the top of your list.

Prof. Sager is an attorney who made a fortune in a private business. The class is TOUGH. He calls on students at random to give case law case cites. I had a hard time keeping up at first, but Prof. Sager was available to help. Post class beer/coffee instead of office hours and a post-semester party at his house.

INTENSE reading schedule - can be difficult to manage if taking other courses that require lots of reading. You must know the cases because he calls on you at random from a seating chart. Exams are multiple choice and short answer/essay. Very kind, understanding, & caring. Very knowledgeable. Has extended office hours ("beer hours" as he calls it)
You need to read if you want the A but if you are fine with a B then don't buy the book.
Calls on students at random from seating chart on intricate knowledge of the reading. Beware.

Hands down one of the best professors I've taken at UT. He makes highly controversial comments but overall great guy. Devotes a lot of outside time to meeting with students. High workload. Class is very interesting overall. Curves the exams, but there is a lot of reading and watching movies involved. Thinking about Law School? Highly recommended

I've never taken a class like Sager's class before... The students who take up end up taking him over and over because he is such an amazing and knowledgeable professor. His class may be intimidating, but I promise its worth the work. He curves tests and total grades very generously if you show interest.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Dr. Sager is funny, cares about his students, and pushes you to think critically and understand the bigger picture. Also a refreshing change of pace from all the liberal professors here. Whether you agree with him or not, you will understand government better after taking this class.

A lot of outside reading involved. Be prepared to devote a lot of time to the cases and making sure you clearly understand the justices opinions. He rambles but he is pretty entertaining. Sweet man also.

I take every single one of Sager's classes I can! I have taken 3 of his classes. He is so wonderful and yes while it does take a bit of work his classes are SO very worth it! I recommend Sager's classes to EVERYONE! Do not hesitate to take his class. Also he is right-wing but he is still open to listening to others, so don't let this hinder you

Requires a lot of time outside of class. 3-4+ hours per class day to read the cases, and brief them. I ended up dropping because I didn't have enough time. Also, he's very Republican/right-wing, and it can be annoying if you aren't a die-hard Republican.

Ecology is an easier subject, but she's not the best at explaining things. You can usually get it on your own. She does talk down to students some, stating things are 'obvious' or 'easy' when they're not that way to everyone. Lots of your grade is decided by group projects. They're not the worst, but they're not fun either.

She's a good professor and she cares for her students. Classroom is flipped (attend lecture twice a week for an hour). She emphasizes understanding/learning, theres a lot of extra credit around 2.5%?, a lot of instapolls in class and for attendance. First exam is usually the most rough in her class, 1st exam (56%) and 2nd exam (90%).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dont listen to bad reviews. This is a flipped classroom so a lot of the content is self-taught but I was used to that from my BIO311C class I took with another instructor. Literally just put in the hard work and pay attention and study and this class is a breeze. TAs were super helpful. Dr. Thijs is very nice and attentive to her students.

Very organized and fair if you put in effort. Flipped class where class is spent on Instapolls (free points) where she goes over every answer. Lots of small assignments and exams are similar to practice questions. Dr. Thijs is a great professor who cares about her students. Highly recommend both the class and her as a professor.

Professor Tjhis was an OK professor. Her class was pretty rough, not much Extra credit and her course was pretty much self thought. She won't give out A's like candy, you have to really work for it. Instapolls were only there to reinforce the content you were supposed to study in the assignments. Test wording is not it.

This is a flipped class, so most of the material is covered in your own time (though you could use the class time on Monday too), but otherwise, it's not too bad at all.  There are plenty of resources and the Instapolls test your understanding pretty well.  Just pay attention to the Panoptos.

This classroom is flipped but attendance is still mandatory. We only did instapolls in class and they were nothing like the test. One TA is helpful but I wouldn't have gotten an A without doing bio before this class.

The class is pretty easy and straightforward, do all the assignments and understand the content and you'll do well on the tests. It is a flipped classroom, which was not ideal imo but still worked out in the end. The hardest part was the Pearson homeworks, which were just plain out unreasonable at some points, but overall very easy.

Dr. Thijs is awesome! It is super easy to succeed in her class if you actually put in the effort. She has a ton of extra credit opportunities too. The format is a flipped class, so you complete the lecture portion asynchronously. Exams are not bad at all- a lot of the material comes straight from the practice problems she posts.
