Flip schedule class, so we had Monday off to watch the recordings/learn the content. Wednesdays and Fridays were in class lecture. The exams are a mix of multiple choice and short answer questions, but it's not unreasonably hard so long as you study. There are extra credit opportunities too. Dr. Thijs is wonderful and truly cares for her students.

To start it is a flipped classroom with a pre-recorded lecture that you watch on your own time Monday, then regular in person lecture Wednesday and Friday. I loved Dr. Thijs! Previously I took this course w/ a different professor and q-dropped bc of his demeanor, but Dr. Thijs is the sweetest. She looks out for her students and makes sure they pass

She's an amazing professor. Her class might seem hard at first because it's a flipped classroom and is your responsibility to watch the videos. There's also a lot of homework but if you do it, it will be very easy to study for the exam. People say lectures are useless because you only answer instapoll questions but they're good practice for exams.

Like many other people say, this is a flipped classroom. I think it was a good flipped classroom though, because the activities done in class does help engage with the material. The instapolls, apply and extends, and homework assigned helps with making sure you learn and apply the material. Tests are fairly easy to study for (no surprises).

Flipped obviously. It's done in a way where you watch a lecture video on Sunday, practice it in lecture, and do homework/discussion over it later in the week. Overall pretty easy, although the tests have been challenging for some people I know. Lots of extra credit too, so don't be too bummed about a bad grade.

As you've probably read from all the other reviews, the class is flipped. Dr. Thijs does come off as condescending which leads to usually few people raising their hands but she's ok. Her tests are manageable as long as you look at the practice questions and take good notes. The lectures do come off as useless sometimes since it's just instapolls.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was scared because of the reviews but it wasn't bad at all. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities, and exams are extremely fair. It is a flipped classroom but i never watched the vids and was still fine.  Also, there is a good amount of assignments but you get used to it. No class on Friday, and class is very organized

Flip class but it wasn't too bad, you'll get use to it! UGCAs are AMAZING (shoutout to Jon!) and will help you during lecture if you need help. Test are pretty far (based on lecture slides/A&E/instapolls). Very well organized course. Learning check are open notes but they can cook you a bit. Don't be afraid of this course bc of the rating.

Dr. Thijs is nothing like what people say. She really cares about the course, is considerate, and provides extra credit. She does assign a lot of homework, but it serves as a grade booster. She may seem condescending, but she is European so don't be offended. Overall, she is a good professor!!

Dr. Thijis is a very good professor I do not regret taking her. She does a lot of extra credit and she is very organized. She provides practice problems, socratic questions and quizzes ect. Just stay on top of your work and you should be fine.

Dr. Thijs is AMAZING! I genuinely felt that she cared about all of her students. There is a lot of material, and you have to adjust to the flipped classroom. There were no surprises on the exams. She also provides a lot of extra credit. The TAs are nice and so helpful. Don't be afraid to ask questions.

I would say that this class isn't necessarily hard, as long as you put some effort into it. She's really nice. She also gives you extra credit opportunities throughout the semester that help your grade. I would say attend, just not let the Instapoll grade get below a 70%, but you can skip. No surprises on the exam, material is similar to practices.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a good professor. Flipped learning, but it's just like an hour outside of class you watch a panopto vid and you go to class and answer instapolls for a grade. (most of which she gives you the answer to after anway.) Ngl, I learned the last 2 units 3 days before the test and pulled of A's. Im sure if you study harder you can easily get an A.
Anyone rating below a 3 is coping or cannot handle flipped classrooms.  There was absolutely nothing difficult about this class; the exams were easy, and everything else was a participation grade.

She is an okay professor. It's not the worst I've taken so far, but she has setbacks. She is insistent that her "lecture" times are meant just for questions and not much learning. She relies heavily on her Pantopo videos for you to learn, but they aren't that great. I learned better by just studying her slides because they are well put together.

this is a flipped classroom, so if youre not used to that, i do not recommend this class. i personally felt like the tests were fair. there would be one or two trick/ difficult questions on the test. the homeworks were useless and a waste of time, but it helped my grade in the end. Thijis is lowkey intimidating to talk to.

Good professor who cares abt teaching properly. Comes off as condescending. Awkward to talk to (for people looking for LORs). Tests are hard (~70% avgs) and are abt 50% of your grade lil bro. Classroom is flipped. Recommend taking if you like out of classroom learning. For an A you must go to M + W lecture for Instapoll, but F lecture is optional.

The flipped classroom took some getting used to, but the material is manageable. Attendance is mandatory, and the weekly assignments are straightforward. Exams are fair, and using unstuck AI and reviewing practice materials helped me stay on top of the content.

Dr.Thijs and her TAs are great! It took time adjusting to the flip classroom but everything is clearly laid out from the beginning, so its clear what you need to do to get a good grade. Office hours are a great way of making sure you know the material. Additionally, the exams are fairly straightforward (quizzes are honestly harder but open note).

Dr. Thijs uses a flipped classroom style and uses the lecture time for practice/examples rather than teaching the material which some people may dislike. Good amount of assignments due each week, but they are pretty easy and simply something you check off everyday. Attendance is required. Exams were fair and reviews/practice exams are posted

This class was an easy A if you did what you were supposed to do. A good portion of your grade is essentially completion. I did not like how she, in an announcement, described peaceful student protest as being disruptive. That is insensitive and ignorant about a topic so heartbreaking. Where does biology stand on wiping out human life by the 1000s?

I loved Dr. Thijs' class! I made some really good friends on the first day and we're still friends now! She strongly encourages talking with your peers so my biggest piece of advice would be to try and make friends. I went to her office hours and she was always very helpful and very nice to talk to! Personally, I loved learning from the videos.

It's a flipped classroom. She's ok, It's just feels like I'm wasting my time when in class because I'm just waiting around for the instapolls. The weekly assignments are annoying and don't really help you learn about the matirals (except for maybe the apply and extend). Exams are aren't bad just unclear sometimes. She can come off as condencending

Does reverse learning, which is not everyone's style of learning. I would say it is easy to get a good grade in this class however you have to so all the assignments. Its not impossible just a tad time consuming.

Thijs is very passionate about biology though she can be condescending. It's a reverse classroom that focuses on online lectures and in-class Instapolls. Tests are easy if you review slideshows/assignments. Pay attention when she tells you to focus on things like flowcharts, they are important for tests. Extra credit is offered for easy assignments
She is condescending and rude to her students. Expects you to know everything already.

If you have the option to take this class DO IT. By far the easiest bio311D option offered at university. The class is hybrid, so no class on Fridays. Just watch the Panopto videos before the tests and you'll be fine. A is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her workload is insane, just prepare yourself. Good luck.

SHE DOES NOT TEACH HER GRADE DISTRIBUTION FOR THE FIRST EXAM IS NOT OKAY AND SHE NOT EVEN GONNA CURVE IT. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS TAKE ANY OTHER PROFESSOR HORRIBLE REVIEW NOT CLEAR AND TRIES TO PURPOSELY TRICK YOU ON EXAMS. DO NOT I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Thijs is so passionate about biology! There is a lot of homework for the class, but it helps you really understand everything so that you don't have to study as hard for the exams. Make sure you go to class since attendance is taken through Instapoll.

Professor Thijs definitely knew what she was talking about but would occasionally go off on tangents since she loves bio so much. Sometimes the way she worded things was a bit confusing but overall she's a caring teacher who really just wants her students to succeed. Just make sure you do all the assignments in a timely manner or you'll fall behind

I liked Dr. Thijs. She used a flipped classroom style (Panopto outside of class, instapolls during class). The tests are very doable and straightforward. There is a lot of homework but the class is well organized so it's not too hard to do.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She provide lots of extra credit which are enough to change your letter grade. Midterm and final are from learning check and mock exams. Go to discussion class, it could appear on the shorts answers in midterm. Take  her class. Study the lecture. I didn't watch Penopto but I do study slides.

The M lecture does not exist, but the time is supposed to be used to watch her online lecture videos and complete the accompanying questions. In class W & F are used to go further in-depth, and answer Instapolls. MAKE SURE TO GO TO CLASS because the Instapolls can drop you a whole letter grade in the end (10%). She was the best professor ever!

Dr. Thijs is a very kind professor. Her midterms are very straightforward and they cover more big-picture conceptual stuff rather than the fine details presented in the Panoptos. I'm not the hugest fan of the flipped classroom, but the TAs are really helpful and give a general idea of what you'll need for the exams. Overall, I would take her again!

Not a difficult class, but it is very heavy in material. She releases weekly videos over the topic of the week and it's your job to teach yourself and show up to class knowing the material. The exams are half MCQ and half FRQ, so missing three to five questions will change your grade drastically.

Could come off as incredibly condescending and hard to approach with questions. She had clear expectations for the class: one Panopto video every week and every class time would be spent doing Instapolls revolving around the video, and a weekly homework/ quiz. Her tests were straightforward, and she offered extra credit throughout the semester.
The only problem I had with this class was the flipped classroom. At times it felt unnecessary to even show up to class. The tests were easy, and I felt like I actually learned from this class.

The class wasn't too bad. The whole reverse classroom thing is something that you have to adjust to, but it's not that bad. The in class stuff while very boring at times can be helpful. A good part of your grade comes from participation thing like instapoll's and discussion which aren't difficult. Her exams aren't too bad either.

Her exams and quizzes were easy compared to the course material. I don't feel like I did much learning within the classroom and the flipped style wasn't my favorite but it didn't hurt my grade. Be prepared to do much of your learning outside of class, but overall the coursework and the final were extremely easy and will boost your grade.

Overall, not a bad class. Lectures are pretty dull, and you learn everything by watching pre-recorded videos online, which can be lengthy. Exams are much easier and go into less detail than we learn throughout the week.

Dr.Tihijs is an average professor. I will say she's very condescending and will call you out in class. I did not feel comfortable asking her questions. The lectures and grading are fairly doable. Panoptos will be your best friend. Class is based on instapolls and there's a lot of group work.

The course material tested is significantly easier and less in-depth than the material presented in class. You will learn primary through pre-recorded lecture videos. Attendance is mandatory, and if you do not like forced group work do not take this class. I did find Thijs to be condescending and not very approachable if I did have questions.

Overall a better experience than BIO311C, Dr. Thijs sets out clear expectations through her course, her exams were low stress 15 MC, and 4 FRQs with 2 hours to complete. Most of the time I finished in 30 minutes. Flipped classroom was very organized, Panapto is where your lecture was and you would come to class take a quiz and do instapolls.

Good class and nice prof. Async lecture, Instapoll, discussion, quiz are the four weekly grades. All except open-note quiz are completion grades if you go to class/discussion. Fair exams. Textbook may help, but very dry. Use online videos, articles, etc. and you can do fine. Focus on big ideas rather than small details.  LEARN VOCAB AND DIAGRAMS.

Dr. Thijs' class was really well organized, there was a clear schedule for weekly assignments so it was easy to remember them. She offers a lot of extra credit that boosts your final grade a lot at the end of the semester. Her tests are difficult in comparison to practice exams and she is picky about wording used on short answer exam questions.

I love biology but this class made me rethink my love for it. Thijs is nice but her quizzes are extremely tough for the little detail given in PowerPoints. Read the textbook! My friends and I were constantly stressed about this class while others with different professors seemed to be doing fine. Dont fall behind, its a new concept every week

Thijs was an amazing teacher and made the class easy and fun. Almost all of her test questions she covered in class or included in instapolls. The flipped classroom method made the class easier and overall she cared a lot about her students. Compared to my bio 311C teacher thijs was an angel and i seriously hope to have her again.

She was very kind to me whenever I had questions and really cared about making sure the students understood each topic. Midterms were kinda hard (I recommend doing the practice exams bc a lot of the questions are from those), and there were a few things due each week. Lectures got boring at times but I definitely recommend going!

From my experience she was very kind and determined to make you learn the material. The midterms were a bit stressful since it wasn't graded by many points, but luckily there were other assignments (including E.C. and replacing lowest exam score) to offset bad exam grades. Take detailed panopto notes and do all the assignments and you'll be fine.
Awful.

I didn't learn much from her lectures. Panaptos were confusing. However, she is a nice woman and gives you opportunities to bring up your grade by replacing your lowest test score with the average of all 3 tests. Overall, not bad.

Dr. Thijs is a kind person and cares about students, but the teaching style can be hard for some. The asynchronous videos are not that engaging. As a result, I felt like I didn't learn that much at the end of the course. However, the grading makes this class manageable because the exams aren't weighted heavily.

Dr. Thijs made this class way harder than it needed to be. Not at all a fan of the flipped classroom model and the monotone lectures in the Panapto videos. The Instapolls didn't help either and I relied on the textbook to study. Her tests weren't too much, but she was still a very picky grader. Take another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr.Thijs is a solid choice if you are a fan of flipped-classroom learning. The majority of your learning and exposure to new material is within the Panoptos so make sure to take them seriously and pay attention. Going to class and doing Instapoll reinforces what you've learned, and a lot of the time the questions she asks will be what's on the test
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, challenging class. She gives clear grading criteria and the class is very organized. Although there is a lot of work for this class, if you take notes on the Panopto's it is doable. It is difficult to get an A without being consistently good/perfect throughout the year. Midterms are only 15-20 questions so hard to do well on them.

Dr. Thijs made biology more difficult than what it really is. Her midterms had nothing to do with the material being covered so you do not really know what to expect from them. Relying on Instapolls or recorded Panoptos to "learn" the material just did not work for me. However, she was always available for students to contact her and TAs were great

I felt like this prof just wasn't up to par. She relied on a flipped classroom and that didn't stick with many of the students. It's fast paced but I felt like she was not able to convey information well at all. I wouldn't recommend this prof at all but she is a nice person, it just makes the course hard to understand and do well in.

Thijs was the worst professor I ever took. Dont make the same mistake I did and choose another professor. Her exams were extremely detail oriented and even if you studied thoroughly, you very likely can still fail (I did many times) and theres only 4 exams. The exams are most of the class grade. I have so much regret taking her.

Really loved this class. It was just the right amount of work and she had so many different activities that it didnt get boring. The panoptos are recorded and really difficult to absorb but I wouldnt take notes on them. Just go to class and do all of the activities and youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Thijs is very clear on the expectations and structure of the course. The midterms are graded by short answers while the other assignments are mostly completion-based. It was uncertain which content to study for the midterms since the lectures were too broad and the homeworks were too specific, but the other assignments helped the overall grade.

The class is organized but the flipped classroom model is hard to learn from. The weekly videos are dense/difficult to watch. Exams did not cover a broad range of material and questions were sometimes random. The in-class activities are helpful though, and Dr. Thijs does have a genuine love for biology. Grading is easy with lots of room for error.

The structure of the class is clear. You have the same assignments due each week. The assignments are fairly easy but the midterms are difficult and have material that was barely discussed. Her lectures are hard to pay attention to and she doesn't do the best job at explaining. However, her grading system is easy and allows room for mistakes.

I liked the consistency of having the same sequence of assignments each week. Midterms were difficult but fair. Dr. Thijs also gives plenty of extra credit opportunities. She is easy to tune out during lecture, but youll be fine as long as you take notes on the Panoptos and complete the weekly assignments.

It pains me to say this, but I actually really hated this class. I did not learn a single thing in it. The LCs are easy if you watch the lectures, but the midterms wouldn't be hard if the professor did a better job at explaining the material. The final is not bad. She does not make the material interesting. An A is not easy, get ready to work.

dr. thijs was very kind and understanding, but good LORD. i took this class as an easy intro-bio class, because i had the credits to exempt it already, but this? was insane. the flipped classroom is mostly what made this bad, because the lectures were often 1hr long on the weekend, plus a lot of useless assignments. saving grace is her kindness

This class was awful. Flipped classroom method left us with long monotonous lectures that are difficult to pay attention to. Her midterms were short answer questions only and the questions themselves were very broad and random. She blames her students for the failing class average when she fails to teach us the material well enough.

Her class is extremely structured you always know what is expected from you. You can tell she loves biology and it's a really nice class. Your lowest test grade is replaced by your highest two so you could absolutely bomb one and still be fine. There's a quiz every week so the lowest ones won't be counted there's lots of room for error
The class average for the last midterm was a 64. Somebody please do something about this professor.

test rubrics are insanely arbitrary. you could understand the content perfectly and still get an 80 on the midterms. she blames her students for doing poorly on the tests yet continues to make the exams over the most minuscule/brushed over details of the unit.

I don't love the structure of the class. The prelecture videos are always really long and dense and the Monday/Wednesday class tries to reinforce stuff but when it comes time for the midterm the applications are not the same at all. She's very nice and the material is easy enough but the midterms threw me for a loop.

Honestly bad. Many pointless assignments that don't help at all for the tests. Lectures assigned outside of class too long on top of everything else assigned, wouldn't be as bad if they weren't so dense and boring. Class time spent doing silly instapolls and "review" assignments that never show up on the test. Just choose another prof

Class structure straightforward, you get a pre-recorded lecture for the weekend (wouldn't recommend, they're hard to pay attention to, reading off of a slide, takes hours). Instapoll Mon., Discussion and worksheet Wed, Homework Fri. Exams are simple but go over unexpected content, overall confusion, the book explains more. Made me dislike bio.

Dr. Thijs class structures for both BIO311C and D are very clear. There are pre-recorded videos, in-class questions to answer, might for completion or accuracy grade. And during those classes you'll have chances to ask questions and get your questions answered with respect and care. Even the TAs might change, their discussions are very helpful too.

This class is fairly straightforward and simple, with grading being based on a bunch of weekly assignments, with no tests other than the final. The lectures aren't really helpful and you get most of your info from an asynchronous lesson or the textbook, but the professor seems to care. Kind of boring but you learn what you need to & it's not hard.

Dr. Thijs class online was very easy but you need to do your work. There are 2 weekend assignments (mastering and discussion section handout) and weekly quizzes. Attendance is checked by completing instapolls. Grading is very fair. She is always open to helping her students.

Lectures are spent 95% being in a quiet breakout room answering graded Instapoll Q&A while you have to watch an additional hr long videos outside of class for ACTUAL lecture. Assigned homework AND 5-9 pg discussion worksheets every week are just extremely long busywork on top of everything else. No actual exams, just quizzes every week.

I took Dr. Thijs this semester online. I think she was a very good Bio II professor. You have a weekly quiz on monday over the lecture from the week before and then a homework assignment each week. The class load is very manageable and the quizzes are not hard as long as you actually pay attention to the lecture you'll be fine.

Solid choice for 311D. Dr. Thijs gives clear grading and the course is straightforward. The quizzes are complex and made to trick you. Wish the course was taught more synchronously and had more lectures than just the one lecture video on monday.

Hated taking this class online. Lecture is not engaging, and it's a lot of nonsense thrown at you with no explanation. Very nice lady who tries to work with you, especially in a pandemic, but doesn't know how to teach. I coasted through only because I read the textbook, not because of the teaching. I switched prof for 311D and it is so much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No tests just weekly assesments. She doesnt release the answers for them so you have to ask you TA about grades. There are a lot of grades that go in and she drops one of each assignment you have so fairly easy. Quizlet has a lot of helpful answers to her questions.

I took this class Fall 2020. I only attended the first lecture. The professor uses Mastering Biology and it explains everything so well. There's also weekly discussion homework, but only one final exam which is open notes. I would recommend taking this course especially if you're not biology-inclined.

Dr. Thijs was a caring professor, but I personally did not like the structure of the course. The course itself was very organized and grading criteria was clear, but we had weekly quizzes instead of midterms, so it was hard to determine your grade until after the final. She cares for her students but had tricky questions on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the easiest course I've ever taken. Dr. Thijs is lovely but I'm not a fan of the flipped classroom. The class is easy because it is open note, but the content is not. We answered InstaPolls in breakout rooms during class, during which I learned nothing. Even if you are engaged, your group members won't be and you'll waste 1 hour.

Her online BIO311D class was the easiest class I've ever had. Most of the assignments are graded on completion instead of accuracy as long as you attend the lecture and discussion section. There are also a lot of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Her class is very organized and she encourages students to ask questions if confused.

Literally did not learn anything from this class. Everything I know about BIO311D is off of my own self teaching. She was very rude when talking to students and unprofessional in my opinion. TA's are nice. Easy A. She doesn't actually teach anything during class just throws instapolls, so if you didn't understand anything from panopto, good luck

Dr. Thijs is super passionate and knows a lot about biology, I overall really enjoyed this class, but I wouldn't say that it is easy. It's extremely content heavy so don't get behind, and definitely go to office hours to go over the learning checks. I think she's a very fair professor and really goes out of her way to help!

Her teaching style didn't really work for me and during lectures, she would often skip over important concepts and not explain them well. If you take this class and struggle with understanding concepts, be prepared to read the textbook a lot because her lectures only give a brief overview. Otherwise, great professor and grades are a fairly easy A.

She is GREAT for fully WB! NO tests! Weekly participation grades, open note quizzes, and open note final!! She offers asynchronous options as well if you can't make the discussion. Her TA's are also so nice and understanding. Every other prof's students complain about difficulty while her class is the best bc it's easy and helpful!

One of the most organized classes I've come across, very clear of what is expected of you. Lectures are just reiterations of the textbook (I have friends who didn't read & just reviewed her lecture powerpoints for exams). Personally, I find that reading helps you understand better. If you read you don't need to show up imo. Just reef from home.

Not the worst professor. When I failed my first exam, I had a meeting with professor Thijs explaining how overwhelmed I felt with 2 classes and a lab on the same day of the exam. Professor Thijs compared me to another student that had more workload than I did, yet scored better. She proceeded to give me advice, but she made me feel horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Thijs was an amazing professor. She is very organized and has everything in Canvas from day 1. Her lectures were very easy to understand. The one test I took before spring break was very fair. After spring break she was very accommodating and understanding. She gave so many opportunities to seek help. You can't go wrong with Dr. Thijs.

Dr. Thijs is one of the only few professors I had who genuinely cares about her students. During Covid, she was very accommodating and willing to work out something that works with everyone. I had an A before Covid, then dropped to a C during the switch to online classes, and ended with an A. She will work things out with you and help you succeed.

I was initially scared to take her, but she was an absolute gem. I cannot praise her enough. She interacts with students, shows her personality in lectures. I had a lot going on personally due to Covid and she was the only professor I had who genuinely tried to work with me. Amazing professor and person, I would without a doubt take her again.

Dr. Thijs is super sweet. I was kinda scared by the reviews but she's super approachable. She has a slight accent which can make lectures a little hard to follow, but nothing problematic. She's also really energetic and knows her stuff. Enjoyed her class and TAs immensely!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly was scared to take Thijis after reading the rate my professor reviews. After taking her class i can say that she was a good professor. She is super excited to teach and likes to make the class interactive. The tests have confusing questions but the group portion of the test boosts your grade. She gives a lot of extra credit!

Dr. Thijs is one of the kindest and most thoughtful professors I've had. Exams are very fair and mostly based on the powerpoints. She also values student input, if you have any concern she will help you out and always looks for ways to improve the course. You can tell she enjoys teaching and wants her students to do well. Also offers extra credit!

Exams were based mostly on power points from class, but they were SO hard. I would study way in advance and still not be able to pass them. The lectures are boring and super hard to stay focused and motivated. The one good thing about the tests were part of your grade came from taking the test as a group, so definitely a small grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is ok. She knows her stuff but mumbles a lot so it is difficult to understand her when sitting in the back. Discussion is required. Besides that it's the usual Bio course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you're in her class, here's how to study for tests. Review all worksheets given in discussion and class, her FRQs on the tests are very similar. Review her slides from her in-class powerpoints. You can only miss a few points throughout the course of the year (94 is an A), which is why not many people get A's in her class, but her tests are easy

Thijs is a SUPER caring person. She is honestly not a bad teacher and most of her test questions are from her slides. Her tests are fair, usually containing 1-2 controversial questions. All her tests have a group portion where the entire class answers them together. She is a blessing of a professor who actually cares about her students
She was not as bad as I thought. Tests were fair; there was always 1 or 2 questions that were tricky but the whole test was very fair.

She knows her stuff but going to office hours helps to understand things more in detail. 4 test that have multiple choice free response & a group portion which boost your score a bit. Test somewhat difficult because wording is tricky, very application based. Weekly homework, quizzes, discussion & lecture takes attendance .

Good professor who knows her stuff but going to office hours helps to understand things more in detail. 4 test that have multiple choice free response & a group portion which boost your score a bit. Test somewhat difficult because wording is tricky, very application based. Weekly homework, quizzes, discussion & lecture takes attendance .

Dr. Thijs is a professor that you take in the worst-case scenario. Her test questions are extremely confusing and difficult to decipher in the 80 minutes alloted. There were questions on exams that only 30% of the class would get correct and instead of actually acknowledging that the question may have been confusing, she would blame the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thijs is really not as bad as people say on here. She is extremely nice and caring and her lectures are interesting. Her tests arent bad at all as long as you have a general knowledge of the situation. It is hard to get an A because you can only miss 30 points throughout the 4 tests, homework, weekly quizzes and the final, but an A- is attainable.

Her tests are confusingly worded and her exam questions are so random. She would go over something very small during lecture and expect us to remember it for the test. Do not recommend as a bio teacher.

The wording on her tests is extremely difficult to understand. Everyone had to ask what the questions meant during the tests. I wish I wouldn't have taken her class. Also in class participation is 75% accuracy, so getting a one hundred is gonna be some work.

Lecture and homework seemed so easy but the passing rate for each test was always super low! Tests were not an accurate representation of what was taught in lecture which makes it completely hard to perform well. I learn a great deal but did not get a complementary grade for all of the work I put in.
Prof. Thijs isn't the easiest to understand because of her accent. Tests can be confusing, so make sure to listen in class and take good notes.

Very good professor, she might seem intimidating but she means well for all of her students. Does not offer extra credit, so study well for every exam. Exams are not hard, but you have to understand the big picture of content covered in each unit, not memorize every small detail. Very fair grader. Lectures get a little boring sometimes.

One of the worst professors I have had at UT. She is not very helpful and she does not care for the success of the students. The wording on her tests are so weird that even when I knew the material it was hard.

Dr Thijs is not a great professor. Her powerpoints are very thorough; she states that the book is not needed, however, her tests are over book material and hard. She isn't very helpful during office hours and seems condescending when asked questions. She does not seem to care for the success of the students and blames them for the low test averages

Dr. Thijs is a nice person but shes not a good lecturer. She fumbles her words, says um a lot, her sentences are incomplete because she pauses between words, and she goes through the powerpoints too fast. She was disappointed with our exam average and blamed it on us for not trying harder instead of asking what she was doing wrong.
Avoid her at all cost. Does not know how to teach and her test are nonsense. Good luck :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: So lectures were really boring, but she makes the class really easy to get a good grade in and learn the material well. I didn't read the textbook and skimmed through the homework and got an A. Just show up to all lectures, discussions, and take really good notes in lectures because tests are super easy with even group section to bring scores up.

The class is set up with 3 exams and a mandatory final. The exams have a group portion which is a grade booster. There is also a 10 pt. easy extra credit group project. The exams are very straightforward and come completely from posted lecture slides and homework.

Thijs gives extra credit on an easy project bumping grades 2%. But, her tests can be confusing but she also has group portions to tests where you get high grades always, and she gives you the possible short answer questions ahead of time so that you can prepare your answers. Hard to get an A in the class bc she says an A is a 94 flat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Thijis' class is relatively straight forward and relies heavily on lecture slides and supplemental textbook reading. While her tests are usually straight forward and designed with a group portion, limited extra credit opportunities and no test drops makes it difficult to make an A.

She gives you the opportunity to get an extra 10 points out of the total grade points as extra credit if you do a super easy project. There is also a group section of the exams which makes things a bit easy and helps you get a higher grade on the exams than you would alone. LOTS of lecture slides so get ready for that. She's a sweet prof too

You can see that Dr. Thijs is passionate about what she teaches. While helpful, a textbook is not required. Take good notes and you should be good on her straight forward tests. Three Exams with a final that is 50% last unit 50% cumulative. Online homework assigned every week but its not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I liked her for the most part. Lectures were straight forward and discussion sections were helpful. Tests are challenging, and the homework doesn't help.

Dr. Thijs is a super nice person and really does try to work with students to make the course better. Her tests are more straight forward than the other BIO 311D professors, but they are still pretty tough. Her final was especially hard and focused on some minute details. I still think Thijs is better than the other bio professors for the class.
Dr. Thijs was a great professor. Sweet and knowledgeable. Easy to talk to and very helpful in office hours. This class in general is hard and she does a good job of explaining the material.

Overall I would say she is a pretty good professor. Can go kind of quick in lecture sometimes but posts the slides online and you can follow along in Tophat. She is very nice and more than happy to answer questions. The first 2 tests weren't structured great but she was very open to student feedback and restructured the following accordingly.

Her learning goals are very specific and are a good sign of what is on the test. Utilize those and you should be fine. Lecture is a bit boring as she goes fast and is sometimes hard to understand, but she is nice and willing to help. Class work is not heavy and the book is barely used, but is a good resource.

She reads off of her slides and only posts PDF versions. You'd think attendance wouldn't be mandatory then, but she requires purchase of TopHat and asks several questions throughout the lecture. Not a huge fan of the way she explains things; exam review was complicated and the test was way too long to finish in fifty minutes. No thanks.
way harder than expected, lots of different formulas and if feels as if the exams were a lot harder than any homework given

Dr. Dunn is truly a sweet and genuine guy! The homeworks are much harder than content in lectures, but the exams are mostly a copy of the content on the study guides. Participation in class gets you extra credit, so I recommend going to class. Some of the projects are tedious, but it's simple overall. I recommend!

Meant for M329F. Everything about this class was great. Professor Dunn teaches the class well and is well-versed in the topics he teaches. He's reasonable in his exam grading and assigns easy textbook problems for homework (answers are provided in the back). The only difficult part was the Quest homework.

SWEETEST MAN. The only really hard parts of the class are the exams, but if u study ur fine. worst test grade replaced by final, and final has a curve. participation matters bc u get graded on it(come to class on the days of participation assignments!) i lowkey half tried in the class and got by with a 94. easiest math intro class, seriously

guys he is SO SWEET. make sure to come to class bc there will be in class participation assignments and participation is part of ur grade. also don't forget to do instapolls, and don't half ass the project portoflio! TAs and prof are super nice overall, great class

The homework is the hardest thing about this class and the schedule is a bit confusing, with homework and lectures topics being offset by about a week. Just pay attention to the study guides for the tests and you'll be fine.
Very cool guy

Lectures weren't anything special, but the quizzes are done in groups. Exams are not bad if you study enough and do the weekly homeworks. He tries to answer any questions you have and seems to really know/care about what he's doing. Overall great class and professor.

He's pretty passionate and considerate. There are 3 exams and 1 final, which are easier than the hw. It's doable and the practice exam is enough for the exams. His lecture is actually really boring but the exams and quizzes are really easy so I recommend this class. There's a weekly quiz but it's pretty random so attendance is mandatory.

There was weekly HW from the textbook, never took more than an hour. 3 tests and a final, found the tests generally hard, but was very generous with the grading. The Final was made up of different versions of previous tests and homework questions. Spaced out quizzes for attendance ( he gives notice ). Overall, not that hard, just study a bit.
He was not a good teacher, and the topics discussed were not math. They are logic puzzles, etc,. that are really difficult to teach yourself. I would not take this class again.

You can tell Professor Dunn is really passionate about his subject. Personally, math concepts are not my favorite, so lecture was often boring for me (personal opinion), but the class was great. If you keep up with the homework and study for the exams the class is really easy. I took the class for my core math requirement, and it was an easy A.
Dr. Dunn is probably a kind and straightforward professor. Willing to explain concepts and do right by his students. The homeworks are much more difficult than the exams, which is very helpful.
he doesn't explain how to do the problem. he does an example and assumes everyone knows probability.
sadly he is a nice guy but a terrible professor. he basically engages with 2 student during class, and if they understand / nod their head, he moves on.

Super intelligent guy and a good professor. My best advice is to *participate in class*!! ALWAYS ask questions- at the end of the semester, he awards you with extra credit if you participate substantially. He gives basically copy-cat versions of the test with his reviews and is very reachable. 10/10 recommend his class.

I was required to take this class with Dr. Dunn. If I had to do it again, I would've asked for a different professor. You can tell he loves his job and math, but he's not good at teaching it. If I didn't have an extra course to help with this one, I would've failed. All works open ended, and he grades way strict on it. I wouldn't take this class.

I was required to take this specific class with Dunn. Dunn teaches like the class is already knowledgeable of the material. He explains it in a vague, yet complicated, way. I am in a co-requisite that helps with the coursework of M302, which is the only thing that keeps me from failing. Don't take this class if you have a choice.

I took M302, "Introduction to Mathematics," for my core curriculum math credit. Dr. Dunn is a passionate professor who cares a lot about what he's teaching and his students. Although attendance isn't mandatory, I would still encourage future students to attend class. It's very easy to get participation points. He creates study guides for each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The easiest class I've taken at UT. Homework is due every Friday at 6 and are the hardest part of the class (they aren't even hard). Attendance is taken through participation and Instapolls. There are 3 tests and 1 final all of which are insanely easy and he posts literal copycats of the test as review. Easy A+ as long as you just do the work.

Dunn makes things easy to understand and answers questions effectively. Homework is always hards than the exams. There are 4 exams (including the final) and homework assignments every week. He doesn't really respond to emails, so you'll need to see him in office hours or after class. Easy math credit.

I prefer Dr. Dunn's lecture style to other classes that try to make it easy on you but doesn't prepare you for the actual exam. Classes are oriented around examples and he posts reviews that are similar to the what's on the exam. Everything is straightforward- he's a fair grader, has a good grading scheme, and doesn't teach you useless stuff.

Tavish Dunn is a great professor if you're already a probability expert. He assumes everyone knows statistics already, and does a terrible job explaining concepts. The lectures are a waste of time, with most of the time dedicated to Dunn writing illegibly on his iPad, grunting and saying "fair enough". Midterms and final are impossible. Avoid.

Dr. Dunn is a kind person and a strong teacher. Some of the content is a little difficult, but he explains it clearly and ensures students have a good grasp on what is expected for quizzes/exams. Would definitely take his class again!

Fantastic professor. His slides are very straightforward and organized, exams are all fair. Nice guy too. The course content itself gets progressively difficult but very manageable if you keep up with it. Only issue is hw is much harder than exam/class content.

While lectures weren't particularly exciting, the course was very organized and straightforward with little to no issues. Weekly problem sets were taken from the textbook. Exams are easier than the homework. There are quizzes in lecture sometimes, but you can work in a group and they are open note. 3 exams and one final. Overall, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunn made M362K easy and provided all the resources for success. Lectures can be a bit tedious, but attend for weekly group quizzes. Lecture notes are informative and Dunn makes it clear what info you actually need to know. 3 midterms are simple (homework difficulty-level) and final is slightly harder, so do the work, study, and an A is doable!

Dunn is a really nice guy and super helpful during office hours. He explains every step in class, and his lectures are very clear on what you do and don't need to know. Homework is quite difficult, but tests are relatively easy and build up to a somewhat hard final. He's also pretty funny sometimes. The Goat.

As a class, Probability content-wise is not hard. Do not miss the in-class quizzes, the zeros add up. Try to do as well as you can on the midterms (relatively easy). Be prepared for a hard final, so really maximize on the midterms. Homework is easy, lots of help online. Professor Dunn is a really nice, go to office hours, and you should be fine.

Dunn is very straightforward and helpful in class. The class included weekly HW, weekly in-class quizzes, and exams. Exams were much easier than HW. Take advantage of his office hours and you will succeed. Probability is not the most interesting subject but Dunn tries his best to showcase how probability is used in the real world. Take this class.

Professor Dunn was fantastic throughout the semester. There were no surprises on his exams as there was a great deal of transparency. Homework can get a bit annoying at times but will be the hardest thing you do. Overall great experience and was stress-free.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunn is super sweet, has a clear way of explaining things, and does his best to offer more explanation if needed to help students learn.

Lectures were super helpful with lots of examples. The exams were very fair and pretty easy if you study. He posts an exam from a previous semester a few days before, so if you can do that you'll be fine. He really seems to care about his students and he's very helpful with questions. 10/10 recommend, I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Dunn!!
My goat Tavish Dunn. Engaging yet easygoing class. Pay attention in class, do the homework, go to a little bit of discussion, and you can do great in this class. We love T. Dawg.

I really liked him as a professor. Everything was pretty clear as long as you took notes and practiced, though he isn't the best at explaining concepts. Exams are all free response, but relatively easy and short. Homework is on quest, which like others said, makes it difficult to get 100s, but are more difficult than the actual exams.

Dunn is a very straightforward professor. Quest homework is difficult but prepares you very well for the midterms. Dunn makes the exams relatively easy and does not force you to remember every single formula. If you are ever confused he does a great job of breaking down the problem and replicating a problem-solving approach. Take this class!

The professor made it very clear what was on the midterms through his reviews, and as long as you do the homework and practice exams, getting a good grade on midterms is really manageable.

He's also very understanding and is there to help his students. 

Overall I'd definitely recommend him for this course.

He was a great professor. He had office hours multiple times a week. Pay attention to the Topics-List for every exam because there were no surprises on the exams if you know those lists. He also does not try to throw many curve balls on the HW. Overall, a really good professor (a bit heavy on the algebra however). I recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear and full of example problems that he takes time to work out. Exams are straightforward and lenient partial credit is given. HW can be annoying since it's on Quest, but it's overall okay. He is also accessible outside of class and responds quickly to e-mail. Relatively low stress calculus class and you'll learn a lot.

Someone else put it well, the class is straight forward and has no surprises. Tests are pretty easy, homework is on Quest which is fine, and he puts tests/lectures/notes online. No mandatory attendance and allowed notecard for final. If you have a bad Calculus foundation I would consider someone else because he is unengaging/not the best explainer
Overall very good professor! Lectures are pretty clear, and the tests are very straightforward with no surprises. I would definitely take Dr. Dunn again!

It is fairly important you know calc 1 and 2 prior to taking this class, of course; however, he acknowledges that many of us took these a while ago. The lectures are good and the in class examples well explained. Homeworks are on quest which makes it hard to get a hundred. The exams are straightforward and all the topics are listed on a topic list

He makes the exams very simple and straightforward. Quest homework is annoying and hard to get a 100 on, overall a very irritating homework system. He's very student-friendly and accessible outside of class, on multiple occasions he stayed past his office hour end time to keep helping students. DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK, IT CAN BE FOUND ONLINE EASILY

Dr. Dunn is a very nice and caring person, but if you do not have a strong foundation of calc you will struggle. I took calc 2 online over the summer through a community college and was not prepared enough to succeed in this course. I found his lectures to be confusing sometimes and then decent another time. Lectures are recorded.

Pretty decent professor. I was confused for a lot of the course but that was mostly because the topics of the course are pretty out there and I don't do office hours. Attendance is counted by an instapoll but isn't that important.

Class is done at a manageable pace but content can be a little confusing sometimes. However, Dr. Dunn & TAs are caring, helpful, & readily available outside of class. Clear grading criteria & straightforward exams with many resources to prepare.

Super cool guy. Can go on tangents sometimes but understands questions and explains well. Easier than the other M302 classes IMO. Class participation gives you points but attendance is not mandatory. HW every week that comes from the textbook but there's always Ed Discussions about the homework and people are very active on it.Super easy math class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's an overall good professor and does care about his students knowing the material, but the class does get difficult in acids and bases. This is a unit that is in general already hard, but he's not the best at breaking down so self study a LOTTT before this exam. Prepare well for weekly quizzes. He offers lots of extra credit and 2 retakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: so many resources, extra credit is easy to get and max 30pts. gives everything needed to do well on exams. ngl acid and bases will cook you alive (im not kidding) but if you study you'll pass (all of our grades dropped by a letter). quizzes in class right after exam, must self study (his only downfall). GO TO OFFICE HOURS

tuley is objectively a good professor, his lecture style was just hard to follow personally. however he definitely cares and wants us all to succeed! just beware when you get to acids and bases, tuley isn't that great at explaining the more advanced topics and breaking it down easily. but overall he's a good professor #ilyalfredtuley

Dr. Tuley is a really caring and genuine guy. This class was difficult but you have the opportunity to earn up to 30 points of extra credit and retake two of the exams as your optional final. I went to office hours once a week and felt much more confident on the material afterward. He'll basically do the hw with you which sets you up for quizzes.

Best professor I had. Be aware of weekly quizzes but as long as you know what you are doing should be fine. He drops 3 and there is no final in the class so 4 exams total, but you can make up 2. Practice is key in this class and attending lectures and ESPICALLYY office hours help. I missed having a A plus buy 3 points aka less than one question.

I was not a star student and should've gotten a C- for not studying, but I showed up for every class and did the instapol and weekly quizzes which made the difference. He quite literally hand feeds you everything you need to get an A in this class and as long as you use it you'll be fine. Or be like me and just show up (but actually pay attention.)

I had a hard time with this class. Prof. Tuley was a sweetheart and made the class enjoyable. If you're willing to actually to study—even though I did—you should be fine, but wow, I could only FULLY understand maybe one week of course content. I Q dropped this class.

Tuley gave a lot of resources you could use to study for quizzes and exams, if you want to get a good grade in his class you should definitely study the Question Types for each unit. My only cavoite for his class is the quizzes, they're simple enough but if you don't have foundational understanding, you will overthink the questions sometimes.

Dr. Tuley was an amazing professor! He offers a lot of EC, resources, and office hours. Most people do not realize that no matter the course/prof., A LOT of studying is required if you want to end the course with an A. Any science course will demand you actually put time into the class!! He is very approachable and flexible with any conflicts.

Dr. Tuley has an excellent way of teaching, a good sense of humor, and offers a wide variety of resources. As a non-chemistry/natural sciences major, I still felt I managed to grasp a basic yet fundamental understanding of chemistry while also being able to keep up with the material. Note: Practice with home works and you will be fine on the exams.

He's a good professor, a little funny, and he really cares. I personally thought his lectures were a little confusing because he did make a noticeable amount of mistakes. So 99% of my learning was self studying with CSS. If you put in the work, you can definitely get an A in the class. EC is up to 30 pts, lots of drops and resources.
Good professor. He really does care,provides resources, and gives a lot of EC. Idk what the other review is talking about because we definetly have a lot of resources lol.

Avoid this class! I took chemistry 301N, expecting this class to be a great science to take but this was not the case. His lectures weren't helpful towards learning the content and I ended up having to teach myself. This class is provided with hardly any resources compared to other chemistry classes. Very test heavy, lots of students struggled.

Going to class is mandatory since lectures include instapolls, and there are weekly quizzes on Wednesdays. He is a clear speaker with notes, and weekly homework assignments have unlimited attempts. Additionally, he offers multiple ways to earn extra credit! Tests and quizzes are manageable as long as you put in work to pay attention in class.

Really cares about his students. 4 exams that cover each unit and very doable. defintely some challenging concepts, but it is gen chem at the end of the day. Gives weekly quizzes that are low stakes, but can help you asses your learning. Easiest way to do well is to go to his office hour.

Took this as a non-science major expecting it to be manageable because of the great reviews, but it was much harder than expected. Weekly tests meant nonstop studying, yet most students struggled to earn above a B-. Content feels unadjusted from the regular course, and emails rarely get responses. Avoid for 301N unless required.

ok i only got a bad grade bc i didnt lock in. theres so many resources for this class and its literally just discipline bc tuley IS a good prof. pay attention in lectures and DO YOUR LEARNING MODULES. do practice tests and go to office hours. theres a bunch of extra credit opportunities. so many ppl fail chem 1 so he literally WANTS u to pass

His CH 301N class for non-science majors isn't easy, but he gives you many chances to boost your grade with up to 2 exam redos, extra credit (go to office hours, they're super helpful!!), and homework/participation. 

He's got a killer sense of humor and his lectures are fun and real-world applicable. Take this class if you need a science credit!

His class is super chill & he's really funny. I would mention that he does tend to skim through topics and talk about it kinda vaguely. Most of your learning needed to pass the class and test is based off of the resources in canvas, not his lectures. quiz every week, tests are a little hard but with use of resources its easy. tons of extra credit.
As long as you do your HW and ask for help, you will pass. He is very understanding and wants everyone to pass his class. I recommend studying the HW questions for the quizzes and exams.

Dr. Tuley is nice and cares about the students. His class is not as easy as people say if you have almost no previous chem knowledge, but it's not as hard as other professors. He offers extra credit by attending his office hours or CSS which is generous.

Very interesting lectures and an all-around great professor who really cares for his students. Took CH301 with him in the summer, and it was a very easy class. Despite the short-semester schedule (6 wks), I did not feel overwhelmed, and I felt like the class was very manageable. I can only imagine that the class would be easier in the fall/spring.

Best professor at UT so far. He makes chemistry accessible to all. Highly recommend his office hours to get advice for quizzes and exams. He offers so many resources from himself and the chem dept. He is funny, caring, and devoted to his students. Studying lectures, quizzes, learning modules, and practice problems/exams are all necessary.

Very chill prof who was passionate about chem and teaching. Gen chem was pretty easy as long as you knew how to do all the practice problems and question types, and Tuley gave out a lot of extra credit for going to office hours.He taught through practice problems done on paper on a doc camera, and lectures were recorded. Weekly quizzes/discussion

Not that hard if you actually put effort in. Dr. Tuley is very nice, and office hours are helpful. Extra credit is generous, so do as much as you can. Make sure to pay attention in lecture and do the homework because it can be easy to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is not that difficult, and it can be interesting if you pay attention and put effort into the class. There are many resources provided to help learn and review for exams, which are very easy if you do them. Dr. Tuley explains concepts well in lecture and is very friendly. This class is very easy to do well in if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Tuley for CH301 and CH302 and absolutely loved it! Tuley is the goat and as long as you take notes and take a look at the review notes(a god send) you'll probably get an A. CH302 was for sure harder with the toughest unit being Acids and Bases but remember just lock in. Tuley is actually funny and gets us.

Dr. Tuley is the best professor ever. He is caring, considerate, and amazing at what he does!! Stay on top of the weekly quizzes, study on time for exams, and go to office hours. He is seriously the best!!

Had Tuley for both CH 301/302, provides a lot of extra credit! Weekly quiz abt what you've learned (only 5 questions). He also allows a scientific calculator on the exams. To do well in his course make sure you do the practice exam and practice question types. Sometimes it's difficult to understand ex problems but he's happy to explain it again.

The BEST chemistry professor. He's so good that everyone from my class last semester took him again this semester. Great lecturer and lots of opportunities to raise your grade. He cares that you're learning, and it shows. If I could take him for every chemistry course for the rest of my life, I would, and this isn't even exaggerating.
Great professor, great guy, and great class.  I would honestly argue that earning an A was too easy.

He provides many opportunities to get an A in his class - extra credit, practice problems, extra readings, detailed study guides for exams, and two replacement exams. He is very kind and approachable as well.
The homework is helpful but can take some time to do. He posts a Review PowerPoint of the unit which is convenient and super useful for tests.

Dr.Tuley was one of the best chemistry professors I had. He is very passionate about chemistry, and he is willing to get to know you and help you. He gives four midterms, and you are able to take replacement exams if you did not do well on some. He also has a very generous drop grading and gives extra credit. I really recommend taking him!!

Prof.Tuley is amazing and if you can take him def do. He offers a lot of extra credit, and drops a a lot of assignments. He is great at explaining content and is very kind to his students. He offers a lot of resources to make sure you are able to succeed in his class. There are 4 exams, no final, and you can retake 2 exams for a higher grade.

Dr. Tuley is great! He makes chemistry easy to understand and is very accessible outside of class. Even if you cannot attend office hours, he will make an effort to meet up with you if you communicate your needs. I am taking him again for CH302 and strongly believe his teaching will help me do good again.

I hate chemistry, but Professor Tuley did such a great job of explaining complicated concepts and offered many resources. He's super friendly and helpful, and his lectures are sooo good. Genuinely just does an amazing job on all fronts.

Dr. Tuley is the absolute best! If you have the opportunity to take his class, do it!! He is by far my favorite professor, and I thoroughly enjoyed going to his class. The exams are very easy if you pay attention and do well on the practice exams.
He is the goat 🐐. Very nice and funny man. Just attend lectures, discussions, and office hours and do your study guides ahead of time and you'll be fine.

easy class, Dr. Tuley is very caring for his students and won't leave you behind so long as you put effort in. 4 midterms that are all relatively easy, practice exams, a detailed review, and many practice questions, and an optional final you can use to help your grade as much as possible. You have many options to succeed, put in work to see results
It is an easy class to pass; the professor provides every available resource.

Dr. Tuley was a great professor! His syllabus and grading system were very generous; many extra points/extra credit given, & drops for attendance/discussion. Lectures are recorded, & quizzes were based off the previous week's discussion & exams weren't bad at all since there are study guides and practice questions.

Dr. Tuley is amazing he made the class so fun and easy to understand. He's very caring toward his students and really does his best to make sure his students succeed in class. Really was a kind, understanding, and respectful professor! Also offers several opportunities for extra credits. Best professor I've had this semester.

I believe Tuley is a very funny and approachable professor who cares about his students. He is thorough and makes sure to get difficult concepts across clearly. His office hours also help alot if you want extra help on muddy concepts. I recommend Tuley for CH301 and I plan on taking him for 302 as well. One of the best professors I've had!

Dr. Tuley is awesome! He explains the material clearly, making even complex topics easy to understand. He is supportive and always willing to help, ensuring that every student feels confident and prepared. He is approachable and creates a positive learning environment, and genuinely cares about his students' success. Highly recommend his class!

Taking the time to write a review as I don't usually do this but Dr.Tuley truly deserves one. He is one of the only professors who (truly) notifies, emails, and offers many resources to make sure you pass the class with a good grade. The learning modules are well-made and explain the concepts in a digestible way while cracking a few jokes!

Dr. Kinias is a great professor, and it's clear that he genuinely cares about the things he teaches. Reacting is one of those classes where your experience stems from the games, so it doesn't actually matter which professor you take. The only thing that frustrated me was the fact that grades didn't get posted until late into the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: In-depth and interesting lectures. Great for history majors/people who like learning about history, but pretty intense for non-majors due to the amount of reading/writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Kinias is not a bad person but I would not recommend as he assigns way too much work including 3 page reflections on: 2 movies, 3 books, 1 photo from the HRC, and 3 of the class units. There are also reflections on the textbook due twice a week and a final 10 page historiography. He also never grades so you have no idea if you're doing it right.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Kinias is such an incredible teacher, and the class was amazing. The grading was a little strange, grades were locked until the end of the semester which was frustrating. Other than that, one of the best classes at UT for sure!

Kinias is very understanding and accommodating, and I learned so much in this class. Somewhat tough grader but lets you revise your essays so it's easy to get an A, grades are locked the whole semester which is somewhat frustrating. Lots of reading + good deal of writing and public speaking. Most fun class at UT, but relatively difficult.

This isn't a class you can easily get through without putting in any effort. Visit his office hours, participate in class, and put an effort into your assignments and you will get a good grade. His assignments gave the students a lot of freedom to express their thoughts and creativity. He was also very understanding and an awesome guy to talk to!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is accessible and understanding. Class participation matters and going to office hours will help you. A good option for history.
It was hard to concentrate to the lectures. They are really boring. Don't get this course if you do not have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't remember much about Kinias' class, but he's a really kind person. I learned much more about British history than I ever knew, for sure, and I think it's very easy to get an A in the class. Would recommend: he's a good history professor, but not the most engaging I've ever taken.

The class was very engaging, and Kinias is a fun lecturer. However, no assignments have been graded yet (especially our big papers) and the grading criteria for the class is somewhat confusing. Also, the end of the course had a very big crunch of essays and projects to turn in/revise. Overall, really enjoyed the course, but could be better.

Dr. Kinias is such a sweet and engaging professor! His lectures are always interesting and helpful for understanding the course material. His class is built off many small tasks vs. exams, so make sure to stay on top of them or else you can seriously fall behind. However, if you do fall behind, he is compassionate and will work with you to succeed!
solid class! she is pretty open to feedback and is accessible outside of class, makes lectures very interesting tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gives brief and clear lectures, gives criteria for assignments (which there are not many of). My main problem is that she assigns a LOT of readings before class, and you have to know their contents because she'll give you a bluebook summary quiz over them for attendance sometimes. She makes attendance a big deal. Great class overall, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There were a lot of readings but not super necessary to do. The only exam is open note, open PowerPoint. Most things can be completed pretty quickly, and she is flexible with deadlines.

Assigned a lot of readings, can do perfectly fine without doing them. Took feedback mid-semester and immediately applied it, reduced readings. Midterm exam was easy, have access to all slides and notes. Great class for the UGS credit and easy A.

The class wasn't really difficult per se but there was a lack of rubrics and grading criteria that sometimes made it difficult to know if you were going to get a good grade or not. There's a lot of dense reading that you have to do. Not the most enjoyable class but easy enough to get your UGS out of the way.

She was a super sweet professor who was always available for questions. She gave you a lot of creative freedom which I appreciated and allowed you to research what you were interested in. There was only one mid-term and it was super fair. Additionally the TA was super sweet and helpful. Overall she was a great professor.

I took Dr. Uvsh's UGS about corruption. From the start, the rubric for the class was clear and grading was very chill. There are readings weekly but you lowkey don't *have* to do them to do well 😅. Overall, Dr. Uvsh is very nice and lectures are informative and relevant. She also responds to emails quickly. The TA, Vahan, was also great.

Dr. Uvsh was very caring. She did a good job at creating an engaging curriculum. It is helpful to do your notes on the slides she posts for lecture. She made the class structured but not too stressful.

Super awesome guy, very easy to understand, presents material in a great way. Exams are solid, no curve balls. Homeworks are a bit time-consuming most of the time, but other than that - no complaints.
Amazing lecturer - low-speed may be challenging and a lot of work, and he not only makes the subject approachable, but also very interesting.

Underwood is a great lecturer and helps one understand the big picture well... however all I learned IS the big picture. Not much time is spent on the specifics, which hurt when doing graded HWs. TAs are helpful but can sometimes be lost as well. Tests are hard but are graded generously. All in all, with lots of  effort, a good grade is possible
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. I enjoyed his class a lot and he taught complicated material extremely well.

Perfect lectures. Fair assignments that were difficult enough to learn material but were far from overwhelming. Highly flexible. Available outside of class to an extent that went above the norm and beyond expectations. Proud UT engineering has this quality of professors.

Super kind, positive, and laid back guy! If you're not great with computer stuff the assignments can be a little hard, but he's such a chill grader that you just have to focus on getting them turned in on time. He's also very understanding if you email him about certain circumstances. Very glad I took this class with Upshaw, highly recommend.
Very kind. He grades easy and has interesting material. Would take his class again.

guys trust, take this class. Professor Upshaw is super kind and this class is genuinely the most enjoyable class I've ever taken. The work is very simple and just follow the tutorials in the textbook and that's it. The books have videos embedded so actual reading is minimal. Pretty self paced but you do have to manage your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As long a you keep up with the work this is an easy class. The textbooks literally tell you what to do and are pretty simple to follow. Take this course!
clearly knows what he's talking about, very lenient on grades and I wish more people came to his lectures :(

He graded very easily (I'm pretty sure everyone made an A) and the content was very interesting and easy to understand because of how he structured the course. He would go over the textbook readings in class by formatting the important details into a PowerPoint. He also had some guest speakers who were all great to listen to!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great UGS, was extremely easy with a paper group project and a vlog reflection due every three weeks. He was very lenient with grading and everyone got a 100 I believe. Please go to class even though he says it is optional the lectures are very interesting and he puts a lot of effort into it!!

For ADV 378: Shawn facilitated so many great discussions and had awesome guest lectures and I learned so much about Black advertising. Most lectures were straight from book material which was sometimes hard to focus on, but I feel like the greatest part of this course was the in-class conversations. He was so kind and truly cared about the course.

The structure of the class was spread out fairly and the content was not heavy. Each Unit (3 in total) consisted of 3 components: a research essay, a presentation, and a 2-minute vlog. Since the content was not difficult and interesting (in my opinion) none of the assignments were a hassle as long as you put in the effort
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: love dr. mueller. he outlined everything on the exams early and was receptive to feedback. he truly cares about students as it showed he wanted us to succeed. his exams are not hard as long as you study. evolution is def a very interesting topics as is my fav class at ut so far. his exams gave cushion and room to do bad on the quizzes later.

Dr. Mueller is such a nice professor! Exams are based on lecture and are relatively straight forward. Attendance isn't mandatory but all the exam content is from the lectures so it helps to go. He offers lecture outlines and practice exams. He really wants to help your grade, so I def recommend him! Discussions are chill as long as you talk once.

Dr. Mueller is a great professor and truly wants to help you learn. We had two exams in the first half of the class. Study the lecture handouts because all the answers you need are there. Attendance is mandatory for discussion, but show up because it will help your grade. I recommend taking Mueller & Mats for INB 370!

Amazing professor! Attendance is not required for lecture, but is required for discussion. Exams are very very easy with multiple choice questions and True/False. He gives out lecture outlines and as long as you study those (know them by heart), you should get an A in his portion of evolution.
Very straightforward, but his lectures are engaging. The tests are pretty simple if you know what's on the lecture handouts you'll be fine, I wish he taught the whole course, but it is what it is.

His lectures were very straightforward. He provided a real-life example of almost every concept he taught. He provides a lecture outline that is where 90% of the test questions come from. Discussion is mandatory, but it helps with the reading questions on the test. There are only two grades for this half of the semester, and they are two exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things
