reviews.comment: Professor Mueller is a great professor. He is passionate about his work and wants you to succeed. His lectures are very content-heavy but manageable if you follow along and annotate his slides. The exams have been straightforward; just study the lecture outlines, and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mueller's lectures and teaching style are pretty boring. I didn't pay attention most days, the ones I actually went, and made an A on the 2 exams he gave. The content was pretty easy and similar to bio 2 lectures.

Mueller taught the first half of my BIO 370 this year and he was amazing! His lectures were entertaining and simple. Also his lecture review notes had word for word answers to exam questions and were super helpful. However, the only two grades for his section are the exams, so study! Loved his section of the course, TAKE HIM if you can :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professer Mueller is a kind guy with lots and lots of knowledge! I genuinely loved this class, it wasn't too difficult at all. His exams are very straight forward with little-to-no tricks. Discussions were insightful and the material covered also showed up on exams. I recommend this class!

GREAT CHOICE! The exams are easy and come directly from lecture handouts that he provides (2 exams worth 40% of grade, discussions- 20%, other prof- 40%), and were T/F and multiple choice questions. There is no homework. Some may find his lectures boring but I found them interesting and helpful.
The exams were easy and he is a funny guy. I LOVE ULRICH.

Had him for the first half of Evo. His lecture outlines give you everything you need to know for the 2 exams. Content is easy, you just need to study. Tests are fair, and not hard. He's pretty nice and caring, but his lectures are very boring (I almost always fell asleep) and he doesn't use a mic so you have to sit near the front to hear him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mueller was nice but didn't give very engaging lectures and was hard to hear. He prints out the slides for you but they're not very helpful if you don't take notes on them in class. The FR half of the test was kinda hard because it is very specific, MC not bad. Discussions are easy to get full credit for 20% of your grade, so don't blow it off!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mueller gives pretty dry lectures but is very knowledgable out evolution. He answered questions clearly and encouraged people to participate in class. Attending the discussion sections is a large part of your grade, so don't miss them. Tests were free response, and multiple answers would be accepted per question. I learned a lot in this course.

He taught the first half of evolution and was relatively boring. Discussions are so unorganized. You read a pointless article and answer questions in discussion. The MC of the tests are worded poorly, and that makes the exam harder than it should be. Provides PowerPoints and outlines that cover exam material. Attendance not mandatory and no +/-

Dr. Mueller is nice but his tests are challenging. They are half multiple choice half free response and the mc is very difficult and the fr is graded really tough. You must know EVERYTHING! He explains things very well but his voice is really quiet and kind of monotone so be sure to sit towards the front or you won't be able to hear him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Mueller is great. Evolution is not an easy class, but Dr. Mueller is a clear and engaging lecturer. His tests are tough, but if you put in the work, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is strange. Required to go off campus for field studies as well as you have autonomy to create your own field study, which can turn out to be  annoying as it is highly time consuming at times. You have to go to every class, sick or not in order to do well in this class as well as he isn't very available outside of class. Glad its over!!

Qualitative Inquiry into Education for Social Change; Professor Urrietta was a fantastic lecturer and discussion facilitator. You have to attend class and participate, but I found the course content very interesting and easy to engage with. He gives you autonomy in defining your field observation project which can turn out to be a lot of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took this as a 5 week summer class and it was A LOT. So much reading! 7 papers due. 10 volunteer hours & 2 outdoor walks in 100+ degrees. Miserable. Lecture heavy with mandatory participation. Learned a lot but felt as if there was an agenda being pushed. Glad it's over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He details the math step by step, always.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Inspirational the right word to describe him. He makes students wanna do something more with their life. Amazing lecturers definitely yes. He always brings up interesting facts + engages students to give their opinion, even if the topic is not that hot (like differential equations). Would take again though I've graduated.

very smart and hardworking. very fair evaluation. always ready to help students. a bit messy and always busy (cause he finds time for everyone). kind and polite to extreme. sometimes hard to follow his genius track of thoughts :( . Still among best profs ive ever had
No Comments

He is one of the best professor I ever had! He is Inspirational, reasonable, friendly, caring, approachable, and very helpful. He always give clear guidelines when introducing projects. During discussions, he give you comments that can make you go further and want to go further.

He is great! He gives really specific and helpful feedback to everyones work, and built a polite atmosphere in the online classroom. The class critique process is always so fun and helpful, and I have produce a lot of works Im proud with for my portfolio. Although the workload I can be a bit overwhelming sometimes, but all projects are fun.
Just great. Wish I could take a class with him again, damn it. Just don't be absent and don't be afraid of anything, he is really open to anything.

He's a great teacher and really open to your own interpretation of the assignments as long as you fulfill the few requirements. It's not a crazy amount of writing, either, but overall a really fun class that mixes text with creativity! He's super cool and nice, too.
Jason gives great feedback and is a fair grader. You can tell that he takes his work seriously and is truly passionate about what he does. I cannot recommend his class enough!

I cannot stress enough how much I loved taking a litho class with Jason, he explained everything clearly and gave thorough demos. He does expect you to have good attendance and to actually work during class but it's worth it in order to understand everything that's taught. Definitely take a print class with him if you can!
Jason is a great professor. He is  really helpful in crits. He cares a lot about what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is very nice and open. You do need to do work for the class, but it's all really worth it. Urban knows what he's doing and is very understanding and personal, he even has you call him by his first name. If I could take the class again, I'd definitely take his class.
nice funny smart cool guy. would recommend. Advice: don't be slovenly.

The professor is a good teacher, but the exam grading is extremely unforgiving. It follows a strict 0, 50, or 100 scale. The partial credit mentioned in the syllabus is that you receive a 50% if you pass every single test case for one question, but you fail at least one test case for the other.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like this class due to my interest in competitive programming and preparing for coding interviews. The exam structure is extremely harsh with no partial credit (even though the syllabus says so) making it significantly easy to get a 0. The class is also mostly Turing students making it easy to get imposter syndrome.
Find the bug, and do at least two leetcode problems a week. Did not quite like the amount of work for a 1 hour class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: All around amazing class. Lectures are clear, interesting and informative. Vouga is always available on Discord to answer questions. He's also just a really nice person and very easy to talk to. The content is hard but there's tons of support available. Projects are hard but fun and super rewarding. Lecture quizzes can be tricky but there's no exam
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class but I also learned a lot. Never went to class (actually had a TAing conflict) but the slides were self explanatory and the grading scheme was super clear. Maybe like an hour of work per week.

Love Dr. Vouga! You can tell he really loves graphics and he makes his students feel the same way. The projects are definitely difficult, but he is very willing to help out if you're stuck, so make sure to start early and fail early. Overall, Computer Graphics is a great class : )

Dr. Vouga is a great guy he really enhances the UT CS Deparment by contributing his time and free energy towards the serious algorithms and data structures education of undergraduates. In guiding students through this curriculum everyone learns and benefits for graduate and career outcomes and some find a life long passion!

I also had him for CS395T Physical Simulation. He is hands down the best CS professor I've had. His lectures are engaging and clear. His classes are also some of the hardest I've ever taken, with lots of tough but rewarding projects. But if you put in the effort, he is a pretty lenient grader. He does open-ended final projects in his classes.

His final was way harder than anything we did all year and was totally unfair. He was also very unreachable and super condescending when speaking to students to answer questions. I asked a simple clarifying question on the final and he literally scoffed at me and walked away. Not a fan of the 2 part exams either. That said, overall not a hard class
The class was a joke. scrolled reels all class, and then we would have an individual test and group test. Ended up with a 100 in the class cause the tests were like the quest homeworks.

Don't take this class if you haven't taken physics before. Dr. Perera won't answer your questions, and his exams are so much harder than the homework or anything you do in class. He also doesn't believe in curves and offers no extra credit. The online textbook has practice problems, so do as many of those as possible to prepare for exams.

I suck at physics so if I can do it, you can too. Hes a nice guy but his lectures DO NOT set you up for his difficult exams so there is a lot of self teaching. This is what you need to do, go to ALOT of office hours, redo h/w, watch yt videos, and pray. This class is hard and again I suck at physics but if you try and put in work you got it.

Hes a nice guy but the class is extremely hard and he doesn't really go in depth on the topics for the exam so you will be doing alot of self teaching. The hw was the main source of practice for the exams which I didn't like at all. I'm not good at physics AT ALL. All you need to do is REDO HW, go to ALOT of office hours, watch yt vids, & pray.
He's honestly not that bad of a professor. I enjoyed his lectures and found the assignments he posted very helpful. He could do better by being more open to questions when talking one on one.

Physics is already a challenging subject, but a good professor can make it feel exciting and approachable. Unfortunately, this class did the opposite. I left feeling more confused than when I started due to his attitude when teaching one on one.
IF YOU WANT ANYTHING HIGHER THAN A B-, SAVE YOURSELF AND YOUR TIME AND DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF.

I 100% would not recommend this class nor professor. I am a junior with a 4.0, and I got a B in this class. This class is already extremely hard and Dr. Perera honestly seems like he tries to make it harder. The homework is the only thing you can use to study, but  expect to teach most of this class to yourself. He also does not believe in curving.

Never actually met the guy since the only thing that matters is your TA. The labs itself aren't exactly easy but you'll be fine if the TA is good. Final project at end of semester that you work on individually, everything else is just lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is reflective of the TA and class itself since it's a lab, and I never saw Dr. Perera. This was harder than it needed to be. The instructions for the labs were unclear, and my TA confused my group even more. My TA was also a bit petty with grading. I think if you're lucky and get a good TA, you'll probably have a better experience.

Definitely pay attention to the examples he does during lectures, and do the extra practice he posts before midterms. But I wouldn't recommend him if you haven't taken physics before; the class is kind of like a flipped classroom, and he's hard to approach. He can be condescending if you ask questions.

The homework is very similar to the tests, and the reading's super important to understanding the concepts, not just the math. Dr. Perera's lectures focus on examples because he expects you to read the textbook. As for the midterms, each is two days, with one day being a more difficult section that you do with 1-2 others, like a group project.

Worst class I've ever taken. He overcomplicates topics which makes them seem harder than they actually are. Doesn't give partial credit back despite some past reviews saying he does. Use the homework to study, but expect to teach most of this class to yourself. I also never took physics before this which I think put me at a disadvantage
Literally so hard for a one credit hour lab. Would not recommend

as long as you do the hws and actually understand the math behind it as opposed to just memorizing the answers, the class should be fine. i really didn't think the final was comparatively harder than the prior midterms since a lot of the types of questions he went over in class or through hws.

Do NOT take this class. Some tests are fine and fair, but the final was much harder than any previous exam and he does not curve at all. I would recommend another professor if you care about your grade. He is not worth anybody's time.

Dr. Pereira was a strong and effective instructor. His homework aligned very well with the exams, and the lectures were reliable indicators of what material would be tested. If you stay on top of the homework and pay attention in lecture, you will be well prepared for exams. I personally did not need to use the textbook much.

I was able to do well in this class mainly because I had taken physics before. If I hadn't had prior physics experience I wouldn't have done well in his class at all. He explains topics like Torque in a more complicated method than necessary and genuinely seems like he wants students to fail during exams. Take a different professor if possible.

Perera's lectures, while great in quality and for conceptually understanding the topics, do not adequately prepare you for the difficult exams which all had very low averages and he "doesn't believe in curves." He's not a bad guy but you have to put a lot of practice hours in with HW and extra textbook problems if you want to do well on exams.
Dr. Perera is a solid professor in terms of his leture style. Speaking to him in person, I realized how condescending he is. Final very hard.
His lectures are honestly really good. He is not the most friendly person to talk to one on one and can be passive aggressive at times. Ultimately, good professor, below average personality.
Good lecturer, kinda condescending/standoffish if you ask him questions 1 on 1, generally fair exam and homework except for the final which was definitely much harder than any of the previous exams.

I was baffled that people have bad experiences with him. imo he puts a lot of care and thought into making his lectures engaging with tons of demos and connections to real life (which I'm realizing as I cram the recordings for finals), and he cares a lot about learning over just grades so he often gives bonus and extensions when needed. Great guy!

Perera is an decent lecturer but is very unhelpful during office hours. He always seems anxious and paranoid, even though he is willing to help he doesn't actually do it and is always very jittery. Parth (his TA) was amazing though

Dr. Perera pours so much into his students, he has more office hours than any of my other professors. His teaching style is easy to follow, he's fair with exams, and he genuinely cares about his students. I added a physics major because of how much I enjoyed this class. If you do the hw and go to lecture, you'll do well. Take him, he's the best.

He is truly a terrible professor. He never answers questions during class and is very inaccessible from email. I would not recommend taking this class. He tries to inflate his own ego by making simple concepts seem more complicated than they really are. I wouldn't recommend Perera.

Perera is a decent lecturer but the material he presents in lecture is completely insufficient for the course. He leaves out key details and is terrible about answering questions with certain students. He doesn't have favoritism, but he definitely shows some dislike towards particular students and that becomes very clear during the lectures.

Not exactly a reflection of the teacher, but of the class, because I never once saw Dr. Perera. 
Very much TA dependent. The only thing I learned was about statistics. Lab is done in groups, so choose good partners. Most of the labs were pretty straight-forward. You can leave once you're done (1-2 hrs). Spent maybe an hour a week on lab reports.
This lab is very poorly designed and the professor never shows up
He does a good job lecturing but needs to teach closer to the exams
Decent professor but poorly structured course. Just take it at community college

This class felt pointless, and labs were often confusing, vague, and long. 9 labs total, with a final project at the end of the semester. Don't expect to gain or retain relevant physics knowledge because it's basically just statistics. Doesn't supplement learning in physics lectures. Grade is TA-dependent.

Perera is an amazing lecturer, and his class is clearly structured and easy. The midterms are multiple choice and similar in difficulty to homework. If there are bad questions, Perera will drop them to ensure the exams result in grades that reflect the knowledge of the material.

I would not recommend taking this class. He doesn't believe in curves or extra credit even when most of the class fails the test. Lectures can be informative or you can spend an entire class going over a single problem that he doesn't even explain well instead of necessary material.However, not hard to pass because of the way the grade is weighted.
The class is fine, but this is mainly a statistics class. Extremely TA dependent.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a lab and the lab is one of the worst designed pieces of education conceived. Its all stats and uncertainty. the whole point of physics is that its not engineering, its ideal, but this class is 5% doing physics concepts and 95% propagating uncertainty. Doesn't make a lick of sense. Perera is great though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: His summer course is fast paced, but his lectures are great and he makes sure that students understand the content before moving on. There's a decent amount of hw, but it helps to solidify understanding and to prepare for the exams. Course organization is solid and the teaching team is active on Ed. This is likely the easiest UT physics gets.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I always struggled with physics but taking physics 2 with Dr.Perera was awesome. His lectures are very conceptually heavy, but they set you up well for the homework. Homework served as great practice for the midterm. TA's and Dr.Perera were quick to answer questions on Ed Discussion.

Dr. Perera obviously cared so much, offering at least three office hours a day between him and the TAs. Even split of HW and test weight. That being said, this is a lot of physics condensed into five weeks. Don't recommend unless you have previous experience. It's not impossible, but difficult problems can't be conveyed in the short lecture times

I took him for physics 2 lab, never saw him. Grade is dependent on whether you have a good TA or not. I  had Afsana, who was a very tough grader and took points off for everything. If you find out that you have her you gonna have to lock in.

Professor Perera is caring but also straightforward and to the point. He is extremely accessible outside of class. My only complaint is the test length. They typically range somewhere around 12 questions. Though he's very open to feedback and allowed test retakes after students made him aware that the test length was a problem.

Dr. Perera was amazing. He really cared about student success and gave plenty of resources and opportunities to do well. Tests were formatted like the homework problems and he gave us a chance to get half points back on our tests, which helped my grade a lot. Great professor, highly recommend!

Unfortunately, he does not explain concepts clearly, and his tests are significantly more difficult than the material covered in class. It may be beneficial for him to observe how other educators successfully teach physics in a more accessible and supportive manner.

The class is a basic introduction to engineering physics. The topics taught are the same as high school physics with a few changes. Dr. Perera wants his students to succeed and has designed his course so that most students will get A's. Homework will take a bit of time, but it isn't too hard; exams are just like the homework. Best UT Physics Prof!

Dr Perera truly is one of the best professors I've had at UT. If I could have him for physics 2 I would. Dr Perera gives lots and lots of resources to study between the textbook problems, quest homework, and several reviews and gives the opportunity for up to half credit back on exams. He's extremely generous and will always offer clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fall 2024. TA-led, I have never seen this professor once. All labs were done in pairs, and conceptually, this lab has almost no overlap with the corresponding lecture course. The entirety of this course was methods of statistical analysis such as t-scores, chi-square, etc. (given formulas). 1 lab/week, weekly reports, time-consuming.

His lectures only adequately covered 80% of the material on the test. He would derive useless formulas and the formulas he did give us were only the basic ones. The test was made up of questions you have never seen before with some being conceptional based. The good thing was that he offered remakes. Hes the best option for phys 1 tho.

His lectures do not cover what's going to be on the midterms as they are very abstract and barely contain practice problems. He would often go on tangents or go through unnecessary derivations of formulas that we would be given on formula sheets. Review Quest HW's and practice exams to succeed on the midterms. Lowest 3 Instapolls are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I had an extremely weak physics background, but it went fine. I took his in person class, and I think a lot of my success for the exams went to grinding for them via redoing hw and luck. Heads up, the 3rd midterm class avg was in the 60s (most ppl got 40-60s) and final class avg in 70s. TAs were extremely helpful

Offering retakes on tests will not solve the problem; it will only address the symptoms. If most students perform poorly on a test, the professor should pause, reflect, and adjust their teaching strategies.

Don't trust the positive reviews. He overcomplicates si.ple.topics, rarely replies to emails, and his exams are much harder than what he teaches. If you want to understand Physics, either take a different professor or be ready to self study. Worst class I've taken at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, MY FAVORITE, very passionate. However, hws are EXTREMELY long and the tests are VERY HARD. The only respite is that these r online classes, and the Instapolls and HW's do help bump my grade up from the hws. This class was the one I had to study for THE MOST this semester, and the content in class is much easier than the exams.

I really struggled with physics in high school, but taking this class changed my perspective about it. Dr. Perera cares about his students a lot and urges them to actively participate in their education. The grading policy is generous and you are graded by a lot of things so don't panic over a bad test grade.

Physics is hard but Perera's lectures are good and he really cares about making sure you understand the content. He lets you earn up to half credit back on each midterm (3 of them) which is super generous. One Quest homework each week which can be a little long but really good for test prep. Instapolls in class for attendance (4 are dropped).

Great professor overall. Interactive lectures. Good lectures that give you all you need for tests. Would definitely take in person, not online. Grading system is extremely helpful and he genuinely wants you to do good in the class. This class isn't a 100% breeze, but it will with no doubt be enjoyable to have in your schedule.

This professor was pretty average. I'm sure it would've been better if the class wasn't mostly online but he seemed to go through few examples pretty slowly. The grading makes the class very easy to get an A in as you can get half of your missed points back on exams, you get many tries on homework, and discussion and instapolls give free points.

First time ever taking physics, and I thought Dr. Perera was great. Mechanics is a lot of content to teach in a single semester, especially for someone like me who knew nothing, but Perera's lectures were excellent. The only thing I didn't like was that lectures were all online, but that might be a positive for some.

Literally the best physics professor ever. Does an amazing job conveying concepts and how things work. Very understanding. Daily instapoll problems for attendance throughout lecture. Lots of examples worked out during lectures.

Very generous with grading, if you try you can get an A bc all midterms you can earn half points back, 50% of grade comes from HW and attendance, so would 100% recommend taking him. Lectures were sometimes engaging and sometimes not, but he is very passionate about the subject!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera is passionate and caring with his lectures and content. He also gives half credit back for each exam and the final replaces the lowest midterm score. Most of the grade comes from hw, discussion, and instapoll (~50%) and each exam is only 10% with the final being 20%. I would recommend him but you will have to study for the tests.
great lecturer and genuinely cares about his field of study. cares about students, gives opportunity to improve midterm grade. final replaces lowest midterm. best prof for phy1

The prof is easy to understand and explains concepts well. The class has three midterms and a final which is a bit much but half ur grade is just homework and participation. The first unit is the easiest and the second is the hardest. Exams are medium difficult because of limited time and amount of content.
Pretty easy lab. It's mostly statistical analysis based so be prepared for that.

Physics lab really depends on your TA. I got lucky with mine and this class was really chill. Lab notes and a prelab every week (took maybe 3 hours total including doing the lab). Final project is a DIY experiment that you design.

I took this course over the summer and Perera was unreachable and not very helpful. The final was also completely different from anything we had learned all semester which caused me to end with a B+ instead of an A (the average for the final was a 60).

This guy cares so much about his students. He reminds me of Dr. Sparks (another amazing professor) because he always dedicates time in lecture to making sure students' questions are answered. He loves what the does and it shows. This guy made me love physics!
Very kind professor and cares a lot about his students, get ready to study a lot though

Certain lectures were more helpful than others, but I learned best through the homework. Exams are never harder than the homework given and there are usually a couple questions that he pulls straight from it. Only issue is that there aren't too many questions on the tests, so not much room for error especially since he doesn't usually curve.

He gives a lot of quest hw, and the exams are based on those problems. Aside from the amount of homework, the class itself is not super difficult, and his lectures are alright. It was mostly easy but I don't think I really learned the concepts too well. HW makes up a lot of the grade, and the final can replace your lowest midterm.

Great at lecture. He is really good at explaining concepts and showing how these equations come about and does a lot of practice problems during lecture. He shows a lot of space related engineering feats to support physics concepts and is really interesting.

Amazing, caring professor. Dr. Perera clearly enjoys teaching and is passionate about physics. He explains things clearly and holds many office hours (which you should attend) where he will walk you through a problem step by step if needed. Tests are hard but similar to homework and practice problems so if you know those inside and out you're set.

If you took AP Physics or Onramps Physics, this class is just a copy pasted version of that. And if you didn't take physics before, then thats fine, the concepts aren't complicated. If you take the time to actually solve the homework instead of searching on brainly, then the exams are an easy 90-100.

Prof Perera is one the best physics professors that I've heard about at UT. I had no prior physics learning, but I was able to get an A. My class was hybrid, so online lectures and in-person tests. Attend lectures cause instapolls (but works through them). Two homework per week. Free online textbook provided, but I didn't use it and still got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Twice weekly homework. Attendance not strictly required but is graded with Instapolls. Tests are just like homework. If you skim the textbook, make a good formula sheet, and actually do the homework, you will do well.

2 midterms, 1 final. One of the midterms gets dropped. His lectures are very conceptual and don't really go into any practice problems. A lot of your learning will be through the quest homeworks and reading the textbook. Honestly, it's very manageable.  As long as you do good on midterm 1 (easiest one) you'll have a solid grade in the class.

If I could go back and choose a professor to take for 303K, it would still be Professor Perera. With that being said, his class wasn't just a walk in the park. You need to stay on top of all homework assignments and understand what was going on fully to do well on the exams. Overall, an informative class and would reccomend.

The lectures were somewhat boring. Homework due every Monday and Thursday, which were manageable. Test were decent, and before lecture you had to read a piece of the text book. Overall decent class and made Physics enjoyable. Would recommend.

He is incredible, teaches material very well, very easy tests that are clear if you have an ounce of ability to apply the concepts in class and from the homework, if you study the quest, tests are a breeze, if he could teach my engineering courses I would only ever take him.

Dr. Perera made physics about as enjoyable as it could be. 50% of the grade is basically participation/completion, and you get a cheat sheet on every test. If you understand the topics conceptually you can easily get an A (a 93.5+) in the class. Lectures were very boring but the textbook gave you all the info you needed to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera is a great lecturer who incorporates entertaining demos. The grading is super generous, with lots of drops and 50% of the total grade of off hw and completion grades. Sometimes the quest is kinda tricky but it prepares you well for the tests since they are also from quest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took him in the fall and he was a great prof with interesting lectures. only 45% of the grade was tests and the rest was attendance, discussion posts, hw. super accessible outside of class and helpful. getting an A is very doable if you do the hw and practice problems.

Great guy, great demos, great class. If you can take him, do it. I wan't that great in physics in high school, but took Dr. Perera and was able to understand what was going on. Attendance and hw is a good part of the grade alone, so it's manageable with other STEM classes and set up for you to do well.

If you have any sort of background in physics, this course is a breeze. Extremely easy A, and homeworks are easy as well. Lectures are enjoyable and his demos are super helpful in explaining concepts. I would highly recommend him.

I think people fail to realize how much math is actually in physics. Dr. Perera is good, but he spends most of his lectures deriving equations rather than doing practice problems which didn't work too well for me. Other than that, his exams were manageable, and his course is set up to help you succeed.

Super nice professor! His lectures were ok and imo his homework/exams were easier than other physics profs. Grade cutoff is higher than normal (an A was a 94+) but because his exams were not bad, getting a good grade was manageable. His exams are similar to homeworks so study those. Also instapolls are graded for participation but you get drops.

Honestly, he is a great guy. I really enjoyed taking physics with him last semester. Lectures are mandatory because there are instapolls in class (you can not do them at home, DONT even try). HWs are on quest and exams are in the form of quest but in person. You do get to use a notes sheet during each of the exams. His lectures are engaging and fun

Fantastic professor. Material was conveyed very clearly, and in a way that closely aligned with the textbook provided as well as homework and tests. Was willing to provide the class with an opportunity to make up for a particularly rough test.

I'm so glad I took Dr. Perrera for Physics II! I'd heard horror stories about other Physics professors, but Dr. Perera was an amazing professor. I had health issues all throughout the semester, and Dr. Perera was accommodating to me and was understanding of my situation. His class is an easy A if you put in the work.

Great professor but didn't let me reschedule my final when i caught the flu lol. so i took the final sweating my ass off and dizzy af but i still got an A+ because he prepared me so well. so def take him if possible but don't get sick

One of the very best professors I've ever had, for any subject. Physics is tough, but his lectures make everything clear, with good demos, notes, and practice problems, all of which are saved and recorded on his canvas page. There were no surprises on tests, and they were very easy if you put in the work. He is the professor to take for PHY 303K.

Dr. Perera is one of the best professors I've had at UT! Lectures were super engaging and he is just an overall sweet professor!!! Go to class, ask questions, and make sure you understand the Quest homework, and I guarantee you'll get an A in the class.

9 AM class & instapolls were graded, so it was hard for ME to wake up that early. Tests were very similar to homework & both were not terribly difficult. Exam 3 was a curveball though; questions were not expected. He said he was experimenting, so it makes me think the class *may* be harder next sem. Lectures were a bit hard to follow. Good overall.

Amazing professor! He is so good at explaining physics in a way that makes it less intimidating and easy to understand. Interesting in-class demos and reading are assigned before every class. You can tell that he cares about the well-being of students and is always open to questions.

Perera is an incredible professor and very obviously an extremely gifted educator. Attendance is mandatory and my discussion section was really late for some reason, so that was annoying. Textbook is openstax. All the tests were very fair and a high A is extremely attainable.

Such a great professor for physics, if you get him you're a very lucky student because he's a great teacher. Attendance is mandatory, takes it through instapolls. Tests are fair but study and textbook is online. Homework once a week. Overall very fair class in comparison to other physics classes so take his!

Dr. Perera is a very caring professor. Attendance is mandatory, but he still records his lectures which helps a lot.  He explains most topics well and is very clear on what you are expected to learn. Tests are quest-based and are very similar to the homework. If you took high school physics and put some effort into this class it should be an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Perera just started teaching and is already a legend. 35% of the grade is completion/attendance, 2 short Quest hw per week, 3 midterms with decent class averages and lowest is dropped. Very engaging lectures and he is always approachable. I originally heard that Physics 1 at UT was impossible but he makes it a stress-free class and experience.

I took PHY303K with Dr. Perera.

So thankful I chose him this semester, he teaches very comprehensible and gives amazing & fun lectures with lots of interesting demonstrations throughout the lecture.

His tests are easy if you know how to solve his Quest problems (which some are almost HS physics level).

Make sure to know fundamentals and excel!

Took this class over the summer during session 2 and it was probably one of the best decisions I could have made. Physics 2 was way easier over the summer, even with the accelerated timeline as Dr. Perera was very accommodating with one exam drop and all exams mostly resembling the homework. Practice the HW/custom quest reviews and you will do fine

reviews.comment: Overall good class. Some parts he could have taught better, but I was in his first semester at UT. Very lenient and dropped a test for our class.

Took this over the summer so things went by pretty fast. Exams can be difficult, there are not many exam questions so each one is worth a lot. The textbook is not that helpful, I would pay more attention to the homework and lectures because that is where test questions are pulled from. Overall it wasn't too bad, just don't fall behind.
Hard to understand, very old school, and not a good lecturer

coe prof that doesn't know how to work canvas. quizzes given out whenever he feels like it. hw is announced randomly in class with limited instructions, yet is graded extremely harsh. prof does not know how to lecture, just mumbles his inner monologue in class. prof is also slightly childish/hard to approach without a getting a sarcastic response.

reviews.comment: be careful with his dark magic. Overall, this is a horrible class that I wanted to drop out since day one, but I had no other options to choose.

Steep learning curve (for me at least) which meant putting in a lot of work outside of class. Lectures and lecture slides are uploaded, and textbook is provided by him, otherwise the course and its structure were confusing

Initially the course was easy then the content became much more difficult. Lectures were provided online in case students wanted to review them. The final project was one of the more challenging projects I have ever completed, but it was also very interesting. I really like him as a professor and his textbook is great. Would take again! :)

Lectures are confusing and wordy, but he knows what he's doing. HW is challenging and makes you think, but he is willing to help you with it. You can also work with people on the hw. He wrote the textbook but he provides it to you for free and it is VERY helpful. Definitely go to him or the TA for help or you'll fall behind quickly.

I didn't attend this class much to be honest. The homeworks were honestly fun and challenging, though at times frustrating. Awesome, teacher would take this college class again.
coool but like yeah
awesome cool nice teacher

very good and nice

he's amazing

Boring lectures to help prepare with the lab. Occasional quizzes and a short exam. Doesn't really help prep for lab. Overall, not super necessary or detrimental to doing well in the lab portion of the course.

Dr. Bahadur's lectures were very good. His exams are fair but comprise most of the grade. They are generally very similar to the samples he gives. Fall 2024 he provided extra credit to those that attended the final few lectures. He asks tough conceptual questions on his midterms, be prepared. Homework is generally much harder than any exam.

His class was very disorganized. He would quiz over material learned in class that day, giving us no time to study or ask questions, and the midterm was not a good representation of the class material. He also canceled office hours every week. Lectures were boring and low effort. Heat Transfer lab is also a lot of work in general so fair warning.

Good lecturer, great guy. He focuses on concepts during lectures and is always open to questions from the class during lectures. Sometimes his lectures would be a little bit hard to follow, but he always encouraged people to speak up if he needed to reiterate a topic. He generally also grades the exams pretty leniently.

Pretty decent lecturer, the lecture focuses mainly on concepts and doesn't do as many questions that apply the concepts to problems but the concepts are well explained. The tests are very straightforward and are not hard to do well in as far as fluids goes. Class is pretty test-heavy like many engineering classes but he curves fairly.

Professor VB is a good lecturer and you can tell he cares deeply about making great future engineers. The homeworks are easy, however, definitely study for the exams and work through his past exams as they are really good practice. His class is challenging, but an A is doable and you learn a lot! He also gives extra credit quizzes that are easy.

He focuses a ton on real world examples. It's one of the first classes I feel like I'm solving real world problems and bahadur teaches by example. He's a really generous grader on exams and posts previous exams to practice. He posts all his lectures notes online, so you don't have to read the boring book. Fluid mechanics is a tough subject tho

Doesn't teach anything in the class. No examples solved at all. The only thing he does during lectures is copies stuff from the summary section of the book. If u want to pass this class you must self study ftom the book and practice questions on your own.

Genuinely easiest A of my life, attendance is taken via instapolls & midterm reviews are pretty similar to homeworks and reviews. Exams weigh only 20% of the grade, it's mostly 4 homeworks (easy). The professor understands most of the students have little to no knowledge about astronomy so he caters to that, nothing too difficult to understand.
Very easy class, would take again. Accent is a little strong but he cares about the subject. 2 very easy exams, most of the grade is based off of 4 easy homeworks.

Super knowledgeable, passionate, kind, and willing to help if you need it or just want to discuss astronomy in general. Works hard to make sure the class isn't stressful grade wise and gives intriguing lectures.

Weekly quizzes were pretty easy. The lectures are really fast and I didn't actually learn much, but I could gather enough to do the projects and quizzes. The HWs were a bit confusing but his OH were helpful. Super easy grading on the group projects, you present to him in his office and submit a super short paper. Wish I learned more. Good blowoff.

Very knowledgeable professor. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching. Weekly easy quizzes and 3-4 problem sets for the entire semester that are not hard at all. No midterms or final , replaced by two fairly simple group projects.

I really enjoyed Dr. Weyland's class; his lectures are extremely interesting, and it's clear he cares about what he does. That being said, I'm pretty sure I'll end up with a B because your grade is based solely on exams. That would be fine if the tests weren't essays and the TAs were nicer graders, but alas, we can't all get what we want.

Great lecturer! Took his latin american course and does a great job making the content interesting. There are only three exams and three quizzes and they're all based off the lectures AND readings. There is A LOT of reading and information that he covers in class. The exams and quizzes are all essay based. Loved him, but wouldn't take it again.

Fantastic Lecturer, funny guy, respected and knows his topic, but extremely difficult blue book exams. Exams are extremely content heavy, with no study guides, and way too little time given. Also, uneven grading. Great Teacher, but be prepared to work.

He's an incredibly interesting prof but a very very tough grader. The exams and quizzes are all short answer or essay and he want verbatim answers or you'll get graded harshly. Intnl Politics of US + LA: Weyland knows what he is talking about and genuinely wants students to participate. Get ready to read about 100 pages a week and DO NOT FALL BEHIND! Kurt is one of the most caring professors you can have. His lectures are amazing and he encourages student participation every class. However, his course is extremely reading heavy. reviews.comment: This class was definitely one of my favorites! He was super entertaining and overall the coursework wasn't hard (especially since he gives HUGE curves). reviews.comment: There are 3 quizzes and 3 exams. I never did any of the readings and still scored high on all of them. He also gives 8-15 extra points each exam or quiz. Lectures are pretty interesting, and I thought the topic was interesting as well.

Long readings, but relevant to lecture. Uses 4 books - read them all! No final, but exams and quizzes are difficult in that they are all free-response - no multiple choice. Three of each, and they are each done during one lecture. Very entertaining lecturer, very helpful, but difficult grades. Don't put off this class. He has clear expectations.

He is a very entertaining lecturer, one of the best. Extremely high amount of readings. His tests quizzes are challenging and made much more difficult by the time limits. His class requires/deserves a lot of attention.

Professor Weyland is a strong lecturer, and gives insightful points about the dense and numerous readings he assigns. The tests/quizzes however are incredibly difficult to study for, and tough to do well on.
He is really great and enthusiastic about the subject. The exams and quizzes are sometimes tricky, but I only went to class and never did any of the readings and managed to make a B.

Professor Weyland was an amazing teacher, enthusiastic, hilarious and German! Coming into the class with little knowledge about Latin American Politics, it became one of my favourite classes! He's absolutely amazing! He makes a potentially dull topic very interesting. His excitement makes it even more enjoyable. Going to class is really key, especially because his lectures are very ordered and notes are easy to take.

Professor Weyland is an incredibly enthusiastic professor. He really makes the material interesting and his accent is pretty funny, but understandable. I highly recommend this class. There is a lot of reading if you want feel extra secure of the material, but I didn't read for the last half of the class, went to all the classes, and made an A. Go to classes! Not only will it make the tests and quizzes more manageable, Prof. Weyland is funny too. His accent is great!
His quizzes and tests are hard, but he's a really, really good teacher. He really knows his stuff and has a good sense of humor. It's one of the few classes I actually laugh in.
He is a great professor, extremely knowledgeable about his topic. Definitely take his class if you are interested in learning and working hard!
Is a tough grader but is very receptive and helpful to students.  Essay questions only.  Gotta love the German accent  and hyper mannerisms, all while teaching Latin American Politics.

Nothing new to say here, but Dr. Straumanis is really good. Class is highkey grade inflated and I think being hot is a selection criterion for being an LA.

Straummy gets a bad rep (b/c ochem is HARD) but genuinely cares. Although I'm not pre-med, it was nice that he emphasized MCAT-related topics. I was very scared coming into this class because of the horror stories I heard, but this class ended up being one of my favorite classes here at UT. Dr. Straumanis is one of the best professors I have had since being at UT. He genuinely cares for his students and gives them SOOOOO MANY opportunities to get an A in this course. Great professor. Flipped classroom is the best way to learn things like this.

Straumommy changed me. He made me explore ochem in a way I didn't know was possible. He was an inspiration—my group and I craved every drop of his knowledge juice. The classroom was flipped, but only because if he taught, we'd master ochem 1 and 2 in weeks.

Straumommy was like my second mother. So caring and cares about our learning. Straumommy backs up the class structure with research. unique teaching style that is hard to acclimate to.make friends in this class and make plans to study outside of class and you'll pass.definitely attend work session(office hours) its how I passed each quiz.the la's and ta's are your friends and are so willing to help,befriend them and ask a lot of questions.i suggest doing activity the day before

No lectures, learn through CAs & exercises. Deeply understand content because topics build upon one another. DON'T get behind. Quizzes each class are annoying, but help you keep up w/ content. This class requires A LOT of out of the classroom time and focus. Do not take him if you do not love chemistry. The flipped classroom can be an extreme pain.

He makes the tests quite difficult but there is an immense curve on everything. He made me really enjoy learning during class because it was a lot of group work instead of lecture (this is a controversial opinion but my attention span isn't that long so it was beneficial to me). The quizzes helped a lot. Go to work sessions.

If you don't mesh well with flipped classrooms don't take this class. Get in a good group, treat every quiz like a test, and stay on top of work. The curve at the end is very nice but there is little to no instruction done in class. Go to the learning sessions at least once a week and you'll be fine.

survivable, saved by extra credit. study a lot and do as much practice as possible. for transformations, dont bother w all the diff flashcards, only for memorizing what changes between steps. use other professors summaries and notes.

He curves a ton because the averages are horrible. There are daily quizzes, but you get used to them pretty quickly because they are not super high stakes. Big tip: study the exams from previous years!

I love this man. If you want lots of good practice and you want to actually KNOW how things work in ochem, he is amazing. He was super lenient this semester on grades, dropping the cut off, having three options to get an A, and insane curves. One thing: you can't slack off in this class. Every class matters!

Straumanis isn't a bad professor at all, but the course is almost entirely self-learning. Exam 1 was okay, but the 2nd one was pure evil. Exam 2 & the final were curved 30+ points bc most people fail. If you're pre-med and want to understand ochem deeply for the MCAT, this class is great for that! If you're not pre-med and lazy like me, AVOID him.

While guided inquiry style learning is more work, it helps you develop a solid conceptual understanding of ochem. Treat the daily quizzes as diagnostics. Exams can be tough but are curved 20-30 points each. Figure out how you learn best, and this class can be very rewarding. He cares about the class and makes it very possible to do well.

As a professor he can't explain to save his life. But he gives a bunch of extra credit. Midterms 1&2 were fine, and he posts past tests. The final was mentally scarring. We had no idea what we were going into and basically everyone failed. If you need someone to explain the concepts to you DO NOT TAKE HIM. If you can self study you're set.

The class is hard, but Straumanis really cares about his students. The class is flipped and there are learning activities before each lecture, daily quizzes in class, along with 2 exams and a final. They are difficult, but everything is curved A LOT, and there are plenty of office hours with TAs/LAs to get help. Not as scary as people made it seem.

If you are taking other difficult courses at the same time it is hard to keep up with the content. Take Straumanis if this will be your hardest class in the semester because I do think the flipped classroom does help you really understand organic chemistry. TAs were very helpful also but quizzes were very annoying and difficult.

reviews.comment: He didn't really teach the class, lots of youtube and workbook teaching you, but heavily curves and adds bonus points so I was never stressed about my grades, added 20 points to each test and 40 points on the second test...don't know if that reflects poorly on his teaching but he adds a large buffer, just be better than average.

Straumanis was grades-wise one of the most accommodating professors I've had. The exams were tough, but daily quizzes helped catch mistakes. LOTS of bonus points, drops, and great LAs. I enjoy learning from practice problems so I liked the class and content stuck, but I wish he had summary lectures during class instead of just in work sessions.

i think flipped classroom is effective when done properly; straumanis does not do that. if you don't have time to go to work sessions or other office hours, you won't learn anything. he does give a lot of extra credit, however, i don't think it compensates for his lack of teaching in class. daily quizzes are annoying and so are the tests

Excellent professor who really cares about his students. Do all exercises and study well for each quiz and you'll do fine. There's a lot of extra credit opportunities and curves heavily on exams. He took the best of our midterms and lowered the grading scale to give everyone higher letter grades. Tons of TA's and work sessions if you need help!

There is a lot of hate about Straumanis and his class. But what is not discussed is how many resources he gives and how helpful his team is. Ochem is an insanely hard class and even harder to teach yourself. He changed grades for an A to be a 90 and was VERY generous with extra credit. He tries to give you an A and if you try you will be okay.

This class was hard but not as bad as I expected. If you are someone who learns best through practical application and independent learning, then you will enjoy this class. If you prefer learning through lectures and step-by-step explanations, then you may struggle a bit. My best advice would be to analyze your mistakes and ask lots of questions!

I'm sure staumanis isn't anyone's first choice so here's my advice if you're stuck with him. prepare to spend around 5 hours a week. go to a work session before every quiz. figure out how to learn by yourself. if you can spend a lot of time on this class you should be fine. i wouldn't recommend taking him with other difficult classes though.

Ochem is an inherently hard class, but Straummy's course is a million times better than that of Hsu or other profs. Ochem is still hair-tearingly difficult, you actually have a fighting chance here where other profs have slaughterhouses; Straumanis has lots of EC, bonus opportunities, and doable exams (on which he will boost your grade by 20 pts).

his class was a lot better than I had expected, his curves are so insane! he gives many opportunities to get an A in his course even if you start the semester off poorly. his work sessions are super helpful and a great way to ask questions. i enjoyed his class!

Straumanis' curves are some of the craziest in UT Ochem. If you're used to teaching/reviewing by yourself, you'll probably be fine in this class. Quiz during beginning of each lecture (not worth alot) and preactivities of the next unit due before the lecture (not worth alot). Each exam/final curved 20%.

Despite all of the bad reviews he gets, I can confidently say Straumanis is the best choice for ochem1. Ochem is objectively difficult, but putting in adequate time and effort will easily earn you an A. Insane curves on the tests (+30 on mine) and you only need a 90 to get an A. If you don't stay on top of the content you won't do well. Take him!!!

Straumanis cares about his students and gives them countless methods to succeed in his class. This class was the first time I genuinely had no stress going into the exams, since I knew that I could miss some questions and still get above a 100. Ochem is hard, however, Straumanis gives you everything (and more!) that you need to conquer ochem.

Ochem is hard and u have to be ready to put in the work. But if you stay on top of the work and prep before every quiz it shouldn't be too bad. Ppl expecting and A served on silver platter. Tests have big curve + extra credit built in exam.

Despite other people's criticism of Dr. Straumanis' teaching style, I can confidently say his flipped classroom has made me put in more work to truly understand o-chem. It's ochem; it's gonna be hard, but just learn the game and it's doable.

You can find people to study or be in a group with, plus you get extra credit for doing your homework here with help.
This class is difficult for sure, but it's O Chem. You can definitely earn an A if you put in the time. He also gives lots of past resources to practice with.

Dr. Straumanis is not a professor for everyone. You have to be able to teach yourself the material and take the time to understand your mistakes. If you do not like learning by yourself but like being taught everything in lecture stay away from this class. I have 107 and haven't put the craziest effort in the class. The class isnt impossible!

reviews.comment: Straumanis cares about all of his students and if you listen to his guidance and how you should approach the class, this means being open-minded to his teaching style, you will succeed. His POGIL-esque learning style puts the power in the students' hands. Finished the class with a 110%, and so did a lot of other people I know. Curves are generous.

This class is heavy on self-teaching but when you go to him with a question he will answer it well. He gives a crazy amount of extra credit and if you put in effort you will get the grade you want. I'm pretty sure he gave the class a 30 point curve on midterm 2.
Grades tough and tends to lose his bike.
Too hard. Failed :(

I studied so much for his midterms. Failed both. Waiting on the final to try and bump up my grade. The daily quizzes suck. Don't do it if you're taking other hard courses at the same time, as you have to put in a lot more time since he doesn't lecture. He'll say he has his "summary lectures" but those honestly don't help, bro assumes you got it.

You don't know what you don't know. But he expects you to know what you don't know. He seems to care about your success, this class structure was not helpful at all. Even if you complete all the worksheets, he says "you're not getting the full picture", and proceeds to not even tell you what you're missing. Extremely stressful, take someone else.

Would not recommend. Interesting teaching approach however daily quizzes and impossible exams make this class miserable. No lecture as he believes you teach yourself with his book but his book is filled with errors. Be prepared to study a lot and still not succeed. Exam 2 was unbelievably difficult.

Teaches via flipped classroom, which was helpful for me due to working with my group and studying with them as well. Quizzes every class sucks, but prevents procrastination and you can earn up to 120/100 points (same for tests), so plenty of extra points can be earned. Test 2 was pretty difficult, but he added a curve, so not too bad.

He was very much aware of how stressed his students were and didn't really seem to care. Daily quizzes were super annoying and didn't help you prepare for the midterms at all. He basically never lectured and the midterms were completely different to all of the practice he gave out. Take someone else if you can.
His class is such a demotivator. sad way to make students feel.

Not to sugarcoat anything, but despite the trauma and stressful atmosphere that this man has needlessly imposed on us students, there may be some merit to his teaching approach because I physically felt my pre-frontal cortex developing this semester, likely as a survival instinct for this class. That being said, save yourself the agony.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bro doesnt even write his own tests.

Even though I study so much for the exam and feel prepared, the exams are extremely difficult. I learn a lot in the class it self through the reverse classroom, but the exams do not give me a chance to show what I know. This class requires a lot of effort and time to study and complete the activities.

TBH: The first test was very fair, but the second test not so much as people seemed confused about what content was covered. His quizzes are the root of a lot of stress, so if you can't take daily quizzes well consider that. He emphasizes self-study, and it works for some and not for others in a very polarizing fashion. Good luck if u take him
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This man is so terrible I can't even put into words. He does not teach at all and you will probably fail if you don't spend your life on YouTube trying to learn. It's like he expects you to wake up knowing the information without ANY guidance!! I don't know how you are supposed to make up your own chemistry but that's basically how the class works.

If you want to teach yourself everything then take this class. His tests are nothing like the practice exams or what the workbook is like. He is so annoying, all he does is give inspirational speeches after giving us the most ridiculous tests. Quiz everyday so be prepared. He wrote the workbook himself and class time is basically work on your own.

If you want to be left rethinking your entire career and traumatized by exams and quizzes then take straumanis! His exams are 100 X harder than the practice exams he gives us and does not represent the material we learned in class. He does not even teach! His classroom is literally just a place to work on his workbook the entire time.

Ochem is expected to be hard and it is way harder if it is self taught. The prof doesn't teach at all. If you are ok with doing worksheets every class and then being quizzed on it by the next class, then this class if for you! the workload of this class is not doable at all when you're balancing other science classes. I do not recommend.

I get that its OCHEM, but he made it harder than it needed to be. He's nice but his lecture videos and the guided textbook aren't very helpful. Practice tests are significantly easier than the real test. It's also difficult to work in a giant sweaty auditorium with 500 people talking over each other. Quizzes are fast but keep you accountable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is a nice person, but not a good professor. The 1st half of the semester we had 5 mins to take a quiz at the start of class- it then changed to 7 mins. He doesn't lecture, you just work on activities during class that don't highlight important concepts. It just felt like he didn't care about his students' success.

Mr. Straumanis is nice, but his class is too difficult. In class, we work through a worksheet with our group and take a quiz on the material the next class. The quizzes are too hard and are in total worth as much as a test grade. I really lack the support I need to understand material this challenging when sitting in a 1000 student lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly he is a pretty good professor. His class is hard but he likes what he does and tries to be pretty accommodating. Grading seems very harsh at first but gets a little nicer through the semester. Quizzes every lecture and 70.5 % of the grade is from tests/final so make sure to do the work between classes.

This class is great if you enjoy teaching yourself. I wasn't able to attend the work sessions because of other commitments that took place at the exact same time, so I'm not sure if they were helpful, but if you have a hard time in chemistry this is not the professor to take. You can expect quizzes at the start of each class, and no lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was awesome! Failed a test? ITS HIS FAULT FOR NOT PREPARING YOU! Bombed a quiz? YOURE ONLY MISSING ONE KEY CONCEPT!  GOOD LUCKING FIGURING OUT WHICH CONCEPT THAT IS! This class is amazing if you love hanging out with your friends and failing tests TOGETHER! OH, AND DONT WORRY ABOUT ANY OF THOSE NASTY LITTLE EXAM CURVES. HE DOESNT USE EM!

Two words: F.U STRAUMANIS! This class was insanely hard, no help from the professor and quizzes were 5 minutes in length while it took this wannabe marine biologist 20 to explain the whole thing. No reviews for exams and you sure bet the exams were hard! Lots of fun to fail every test!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't teach!!!! He uses POGILS. Just wait for another professor. He only has 2 midterms and they are hard. When asked how to improve, he will not offer opportunities, he will just say get better. DONT TAKE

I haven't finished the course yet, and I'm not even doing that bad, however he is HORRIBLE. Literally just gives inspiration ted talks every class, is extremely boring, and his textbook/answer keys are CONSTANTLY riddled with mistakes. He provides almost no helpful resources. His textbook he wrote also sucks. His philosophy on teaching is so poor.

Was a pretty hard class, I felt it was fair throughout the semester, just quite inconsistent. It's clear that students do worse overall than he expects so there's a lot of rearrangement in the class to accommodate for that. Final was absurdly hard and quite different than exams through the semester. No dropped exams.

Ochem is a hard subject, and you have to work hard. However, Straumanis encourages learning in a stress-free way and gives you plenty of opportunities to succeed. He offers opportunities for extra credit on all quizzes and exams (can score up to 120), replacement grades, extra credit from going to work sessions, and curves very generously.

He DOES teach! There are summary lectures from previous years and panopto videos of his summary slides. The workbook that he wrote helps explain ochem topics step by step-- I've never understood ochem so well with Shabbir for Ochem 1. TALK to him during work sessions--he guides you through hard concepts thoroughly. He wants you to succeed.

The flipped-classroom teaching was a big contrast coming from Shabbir. A lot of effort is still required, but I was able to learn on my own time in a stress-free manner. Quizzes and exams are scored out of 120, and curves are generous. Straumanis is very chill and patiently answers/explains all my questions during work sessions (office hours).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly ochem 2 is pretty difficult, Dr. Staumanis is pretty chill, but I just never really got into the flipped classroom setting compared to the traditional style of teaching.

After taking CH-320N during the Su22 semester (with another prof), I was worried that I would never be able to understand Organic Chemistry II. That was until I retook the course with Dr. Straumanis; my eyes were opened to a whole new way of thinking about organic chemistry. I highly recommend taking this course with Dr. Straumanis!!
He does not teach anything. In order to succeed, you have to teach yourself. Take any other professor.

Straumanis is the best professor I have had at UT. His amazing teaching style made o chem two actually fun and exciting. He has a bonus on every quiz and adds 20-30%+ to each midterm (only two) and final. It's hard to not get an A as long as you just do the exercises in his workbook and study hard to actually understand and not memorize.

Andrei refuses to give useful practice problems because he doesn't want you to "memorize the patterns". THATS LITERALLY WHAT OCHEM IS. Instead of teaching, he curves the tests by 20-30 points to raise the average to a B so he doesn't get fired. On the last class day he literally begged us to not bomb his eCIS and RMP.

By no means is Straumanis a good professor, but I think he does care about his pre-med students succeeding. I wouldn't take his class again because he does not lecture and you just have to teach yourself. Only take if you are pre-med, because if you aren't he doesn't care about you. -an engineer required to take this course.

Taking this class is controversial, but it is more than doable! His class is definitely a unique setup (which is not for everyone) where learning is facilitated by group work from his textbook. He is very caring and tries to give as many opportunities to his students as possible (bonus, extra credit, drops) and wants everyone to understand Ochem.

I came into this class after nearly failing OChem1 with Page, and I was scared. I actually learned OChem in this class, and it's very rewarding if you stick with it. Dr. S has so many work sessions and his teaching team is phenomenal. A big part of me understanding OChem was the book in this class. It's really well designed and helped me so much!

Professor Straumanis was an amazing professor who actually emphasized understanding ochem, not memorizing. This was probably my easiest class at UT I don't know why he gets a bad rep when he gives students so many chances to score over 100 in the class.

He cares about the success of his students, but the class is overly difficult and there is too much material expected to be mastered. Exams are nothing like what you are told to study. Partial credit helps, though wider criteria should be given.

Straumanis is a caring guy with an approach to learning organic chemistry that simply did not work for me. It's a flipped classroom, and the responsibility is entirely on you to learn. I couldn't balance this course with all of the other commitments I had. I barely passed ochem 1 with him, and ended up using my OTE for his ochem 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love his teaching style as it makes you learn & interact with the material more than you would if it were a lecture based class. Dr Straumanis cares about your performance, and offers loads of extra credit, replacing your past quizzes, and midterm grades in order to do better & correct your past mistakes.

His teaching style is different from other classes, but if you are open-minded that is not a bad thing. He gives you a lot of bonus points and plenty of time in the exams, so there is significantly reduced stress during them. The class is largely dependent on the workbook he wrote, but it is actually pretty engaging. I strongly recommend this class

The flipped learning style was awful for me after I did poorly in Ochem 1 with Shabbir. I think it's fine if you like group work and you have a solid foundation in Ochem 1. You have to make sure your group members are helpful and that you'll be okay working with them all year. The quizzes were awful and the exams aren't much better.

I think straumanis is probably the easiest ochem professor, but do not expect to learn from him. All of his teaching is done through a textbook he created. He does very little (sometimes no) lecture in class, so expect to teach yourself the material.

cares about his students and what they make, and he clearly believes in his teaching style. He prefaced every lecture with telling the students  performing poorly, and why his style is best. However, this style works best for about half the students, who make an A, and the other half average a 60 on his exams, keeping a pretty B average to show off

The exams are pretty tough, so you have to study really hard, but there is sooo much bonus built in, which really alleviates the stress! My advice would be to start early and try not to procrastinate and this class will be doable! (There are weekly pop quizzes so that's a lil annoying, but if you put in the work, it is very doable!

He is honestly one of my favorite professors I have taken. He makes it to where you will do well in this class if you put in the work and focus on your learning instead of memorizing info. There are daily quizzes but they are so low cost because of extra credit and drops, which actually facilitates learning. Lots of opportunities for bonus points.

Honestly my favorite professor that I have taken at UT. He gives lots of extra credit on his exams and quizzes to lessen stress for his students. This class is very group work heavy, but you will learn to like it if you find a good group. He definitely cares about his students on a personal level.

Ochem is hard. No matter what you have to put the time in. Straumanis does a flipped classroom so the emphasis is on you putting the effort in. You have to go to work sessions and ask questions and you will be alright. Learn from your mistakes and work with other people. Really get down the fundamentals because they help you in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I understand chemistry better after this class than I ever have before. Commit to his method and you will be fine. You can earn up to 120% on quizzes/tests, he drops quiz grades, and replaced test grades with higher test grades. Office hours every single day with him and TAs so you can always get questions answered. Super nice and understanding.

The interactive group dynamic of this class is genius. If it were up to me, I'd have all classes in all universities have this sort of interactive teaching style- it only makes sense that we learn better with other people, I think it's in our psychology.

Dr. Straumanis is extremely passionate about what he teaches and wants you to succeed.

lots of material & takes a lot of effort to do well. truly believe the effort u put in is the grade u get, but u get a deep understanding. He spends a lot of time justifying his teaching methods bc ppl hate on him (in my opinion his methods work), but just stick w it. He cares & will help in any way he can.
He was really awesome and allowed me to get a deeper understanding of organic chemistry :) although difficult, he really helps you succeed!

This professor doesn't really lecture, instead he has you work through a packet from his workbook during class time. There was very little practice given for application of what we learned which made exams quite difficult. If you are someone who learns better through practice from lectures and homework, I wouldn't recommend this class.

Do not take this class and expect him to care much about any non-med school students like engineers. He claims his exams are like the MCAT and therefore those of us engineering students have to compete with the cutthroat pre-med students who are obsessed with GPA and squeeze out the engineers giving us failing grades and little room for recovery.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While other professors have a very organized and straightforward teaching system with clear tests, straumanis does not teach and relies on his workbook. He does not give enough practice for the tests. His class was the worst class I have taken to be honest. I felt lost and stressed throughout the class. Take any other professor if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Be prepared for whats coming cause its bound to be a nightmare.
Wait & see how difficult the quizzes are, the tests will be 20X harder since there will be NO REVIEWS. Test from 10% lectures, rest from OCHEM1 & entire HIS BOOK. Read through it, you'll be lucky to get a C. Quizz 15' every single week. Make sure you're not gonna drop then purchase it

Truthfully I don't agree with all of these bad reviews. Straumanis' class is what YOU make of it. If you simply studied for each quiz (for like 1 hour) which is what we were SUPPOSED to do, then you barely had to study for the exams. Exams also had major extra credit. People who rate him badly simply didn't motivate themselves to study properly.

Ochem isn't difficult, but he is. Daily 5 minute pop quizzes make it so that you NEVER get a break from studying. Only late night office hours in person available. Grading dist. is wack - got a 95+ on both midterms and still A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things
