reviews.comment: I def agreed w the other negative reviews at first, BUT I learned how to study on my own and respect/enjoy ochem more. Ochem is notorious for a reason and complaining won't get u anywhere in this class. If you study his book, do CA exercises, and engage w/ peers who can help you understand the material, then you'll be fine, especially w all the EC.

You'll be alright with his extra credit, but it's gonna be really painful learning from a book riddled with errors. Good luck with TAs because they basically are the teachers, and vary in competence. I wanted to leave every useless lecture if not for quizzes. Take anyone else if possible, unless you're okay with grinding and losing mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class drained my love of learning cuz Straum is not a good prof. Prob cuz he didn't teach (I taught myself). All the bad reviews are true so I wont parrot em. However, he's a decent guy at heart who curves generously and is not trying to fail you. But he is trying to trick you on quizzes so GL. Take someone else if u can, it's ok if you cant.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I mean I got an A but that was from grinding the hell out of stuff and not his little book or group work. You could have given me just the book and gotten the same result, because lectures and the teaching team were worthless. Each class was demoralizing with his quizzes and constant TED talks. Tons of errors and poor management.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: i am beyond annoyed and upset with the fact that he won't even release what we got on our final exam which we took A WEEK AGO!!! literally it's a scantron?? he said that he won't release it until the final grades have been posted, meaning that there will be no opportunity for students to discuss or change their grades. ut look into this man!

wow! never have i experienced such an ill-prepared and inconsistent course. daily quizzes ranged in both depth and rigor (they were primarily made by the TAs). the course was placed on the back burner by instructors. midterm was fair but the final was complete hellfire (no prior quizzes or practical resources covered the bulk of the material).

Short daily quiz over the previous class. No need to stay after the quiz unless u don't want to seem rude/need help. Try to understand activity answers before quizzes. Study summaries, quizzes + LOs for tests. Need to know basic calc. Doesn't deserve all the hate. Late final grade prob just a fluke. What if he's hurt :/ UT students kinda suck

Overall, Dr. Straumanis is a great professor! He focuses on actually understanding the concepts instead of straight memorization. Many people in the reviews complain he doesn't give us practice problems. But honestly, there isn't a need for much practice if you go to his office hours/pay attention in class, and actually understand the material.

I hope UT looks into him. I hated this man and his HANDS-OFF teaching style at the beginning of the semester but it is possible to come back from a bad first exam grade. Don't be discouraged if he's the only professor you can get. He is a pill to listen to, but learn how to predict the questions he'll ask and you'll be good.
The final only covered the last few chapters. But he told the class to study everything. You really tricked us! Nice job.

If you want to actually learn and do well, do not take this class. Some things he has said in class - "not everyone will be able to answer all the multiple choice" and "this exam is not designed to be finished". He literally refused to give us practice problems and exams because he believed it causes pattern recognition and memorization??

most difficult professor ever This class is pretty much easy results for his research. Also too many errors in the book he created. Every exam is cumulative and covers ideas not mentioned in class, he assumes you have a STRONG understanding of chemistry. LAs and TAs did all the heavy lifting in content recovery. Don't buy the book zlib it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything nad about the group work has already been said. Another bad part is the many errors in his textbook which is the entire way you learn in this class, so if one of these errors sticks in your mind, you're screwed. The final exam also had errors, which is a joke, and shows the lack of effort put into this class by the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I felt so alone in this class, like a number with no human connection to the teaching team. Every class I couldn't wait to leave. Heavily weighted quizzes brought exceptions to the rule instead of him just teaching it. Mentally exhausted from learning from a textbook. Only a few competent TAs. This class made me forget you can enjoy learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do Not Take Him. I get how flipped classroom idea, but it has to be done well. The activities are incredibly confusing, poorly done, and difficult to learn from since does not relate to the material on exams. The prof has to point out how so many mistakes and even criticizes the author for how her questions don't make sense. This class was pain.

This class is not very hard. You literally just have to know the material and you will get A so easily. Just ask Andre Goatmanis if you have any questions. People just have to understand it is still a difficult class.

This class was one of the hardest I've ever taken. There is no teaching, and most of the learning is done in group worksheets. If you get a bad group, it's done for. The concepts are very hard and half of the time the TAs don't even know how to do them. The tests are difficult, and I failed them even with hours of studying. Do not take this class.

This class is very dependent on your own comfort with self-learning; it isn't for everyone, but definitely works for some like myself. Professor doesn't really lecture, so if you like a traditional classroom setting, it may not be the best idea. There is a lot of EC built into exams to help get a higher grade. Overall ok, but has been stressful.

This class is only hard if you make it hard. If you take the time during class to do the Chem Activities and ask questions when you have them you will do great. The quizzes are hard but you get drops. The midterms are a lot easier and have lots of bonuses - even if you fail quizzes you can get 120+ on Midterms so it's really easy to get an A.

The professor isn't teaching you organic chemistry in this course - his ChemActivity workbook is. This class is a hit-or-miss because it ultimately depends on your connections with other people. Very collaborative-heavy, so if you get a bad group, the will be even harder. His only form of lecture are through summary lectures and pre-class lectures.

Straumanis definitely has a different teaching style, but I think its easy to learn if you actually put in the work. Straumanis cares about your grade and is very available during and outside of class. The resources to succeed in this class are very available and the class is way easier if you take advantage of them.

Dr.Straumanis made what seemed to be a very difficult class so much more digestible. He really cares about students and gives so much time to be available so people understand the material. He emphasizes the learning by allowing us to learn through exercises but offers loads of extra credit on quizzes and tests. Great prof, great class pace!

Ochem is a hard class regardless of professor, but Straumanis' class is built so that if you take advantage of all of the resources, you'll do well. As long as you prepare well between classes, and attend work sessions as you are able, an A in this course is totally achievable. He cares a lot about his students, and is very accommodating.

Everyone is hating too much. It's o chem, it's going to be a difficult class. Straumanis is a smart guy and I believe in his method. He also genuinely does not want to screw anyone over. Come to this class ready to genuinely learn. If you do that, he'll make sure your grade reflects that. 
Whole class is group work so be ready for that.

This site uses a lot of censorship, a lot of negative reviews have been removed. Don't let the few positive reviews trick you. They're probably coming from die-hard pre-meds who don't have responsibilities out of school so they can attend every office hour. Overall Straumanis is disrespectful to not only students but other prof teaching styles

Dr. Straumanis is caring, and I've learned a ton in this class. But quizzes are graded "All or nothing" on most questions + are way too in depth for a day of study. Wish there was hw to even it out. Unfortunately other 320M classes give out As like candy, and this class with the same name doesn't and will impact chances of getting into med school.

His teaching method was a little tough to get by at the beginning, and the quizzes can get a bit discouraging, but they force you to keep up with the material, and having to learn through group work really helps if you take the time to go to work sessions and ask questions. Not trying and blaming the professor won't work!

Dr. Straumanis' class is unique but is okay if you like working in groups /open minded. There aren't any traditional lectures, but he's caring, and the class time is spent doing a worksheet with a group and asking Straumanis/TA's questions. The most stressful part of the class was the daily quizzes, and that it seems hard to make up for bad grades
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Straumanis is incredibly conceited regarding his method of teaching. (If it is not his then it wont work) I hope he would be more descriptive and help students rather than saying "try to ask your friends and figure it out"

Dr. Straumanis is an awesome professor and person! His class is structured by guided group work which is different from other sections. It ensures you know the concepts deeply instead of memorizing. Students from other classes get mad at the structure, but if they just tried, they'd realize it's a great way to learn ochem.

Unconventional class structure that worked for me, but there's little room to improve your overall grade in the class once you've done poorly on something. Also he asked a bunch of his top students to leave reviews on RMP to increase his score, which is weird. You also need supplemental OHs that are offered only at night, unfair if you work.
dont take, im warning, theres no teaching done in this class by the prof, solely by your struggling classmates who barely understand and TAs who try their best to get to everyone they can
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Straumanis has a great class structure and really wants his students to succeed. The class revolves around group work and the lectures are supplemental. There are a ton of resources to help students that feel lost, and both Straumanis and his TAs are willing to answer questions for 2 hours three nights a week at study sessions. Love him!

Ochem is challenging so any class will not be easy - that being said Dr. Straumanis teaches the material in an intuitive way. The worksheets are helpful for understanding complex mechanisms or other concepts which might not be conveyed well in a traditional lecture. Make sure to go to the work sessions and thoroughly study for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis cares about all of his students. As there being a quiz everyday, it keeps you consistent in organic chemistry which is essential for the success for this course in general. Personally, I am able to work to study on my own so I occasionally find the quizzes annoying as I have to shift my focus onto other classes and I get penalized.

Dr. Straumanis has developed a way of learning that's not very familiar to most students but is definitely beneficial. His group-work style of teaching fosters synergy among students and simulates real-world environments in which problem solving is more than just asking for the answer. My only advice is to stay on track for his quizzes.

Dr. Straumanis is a caring professor. The class is flipped so its primarily based on a having a good group to work through the activities in class. There is a low-stakes quiz every class, but they are helpful in pacing yourself in the class so you don't fall behind. The office hours are extremely helpful in performing well on the assessments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is different than all other ochem classes. The class is focused on group work from a textbook, and TAs are available to help answer questions as needed. Easy to bounce ideas off of groupmates, Straumanis, and TAs. The grade is focused on daily quizzes and midterms. Not lecture heavy. Good if you like group work.

Dr. Straumanis's class makes organic more fun than I expected it to be. The group work allows for a more relaxed class where you learn from other students, TAs, and Dr. Straumanis. The quizzes can be hard, but they help you check yourself. The tests are fair. Overall, the class and Dr. Straumanis are enjoyable.

Lecture times are used to work with a group on a "learning module" while TAs and the professor answer questions, no lecturing (or very little). That being said, if you prefer lectures rather than practicing and interacting in class, this professor might not be for you. He genuinely wants you to learn, not memorize. He cares about your success.

While Professor Straumanis' approach might be something that most people aren't used to, I think it has benefitted many. So far, the groupwork in this class has helped me to understand the content much better than if I had been listening to a 1.25 hour lecture twice a week. If you find a group that works for you, anyone can succeed in this course.

This class is mostly independent learning and working with other students, but the professor and his TA's are always available in and out of class if you have questions. He also posts videos after each class discussing the activity worked on and the quizzes too. It's a tough class, but all OChem classes will require a lot of work to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is one of those few professors that wants to see you do well in his class and will actively make an effort to give opportunities to do this. He gives good demonstrations, plenty of opportunities for extra credit, and has a lot of LA/TAs that help you during class and at work sessions. If I took Ochem II, I wouldve taken his class.

O chem is hard but Dr. Straumanis is an awesome professor, especially in the way his classes are structured. Rather than giving long boring lectures and force-feeding you the information, he gives the students the opportunity to work together to understand the concepts first before he himself explains the concept at the end of the lecture or quiz.

I love this class! I definitely think his class is very dependent on your learning style. There's group work and worksheets that explain concepts to you and then you apply those concepts to questions to see your understanding. While he doesn't lecture, I think the way his class is set up allows you to ACTIVELY learn.

Dr. Straumanis listens to students' feedback and wants us to succeed. The class is structured to work in groups, so attend work sessions to meet new people! Daily quizzes seem brutal but they really help you stay on track. You need to put time and effort into understanding concepts, but there are so many opportunities to do well in this class.

This class functions off a workbook with group mates. Dr. Straumanis is caring and wants you to understand concepts. Its not a lecture style class but he gives lots of bonus points and help outside class. I recommend this class but also understand your own learning style, as it is even harder if you don't have very collaborate group mates.

Hands down the best professor I've had at UT. Even with ochem being one of the hardest subjects, I currently have the best grade that I've ever had in any class. When we expressed anxiety about the quizzes, he immediately provided bonus questions on them. There is also bonus on the tests. He cares so much about his students. I'm taking for ochem 2.

the 1 review people haven't put enough time into this class. Ocehm is a hard class no matter who your prof is. You HAVE to fully engage with the activities in class, and GO TO THE WORK SESSIONS. There's lots of bonus on quizzes and tests, and he drops quizzes too. Quizzes are a lot, but I felt really prepped for the test. I recommend him :)

Dr. Straumanis deeply cares about your success and will nudge you toward it. We mainly learn through a workbook in class and ask questions if necessary. There are daily quizzes but they are all fair game, simple, and graded graciously. He emphasizes how to approach a problem with nuance which makes you a better student in the long run.

O chem is hard. You should go into this class knowing it is not a traditional lecture style class, you go through worksheets with a group that teaches you the material. A lot of people do not like this style, but I did. There are so many resources that you can use to succeed. The quizes and work sessions really help improve my unserstanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This man acts like asking questions will help us improve more but at the same time, he shames us for not understanding and acts like we are not learning enough. How are we expected to learn the material if you're not gonna guide us properly on learning and applying the concepts? His motivational speeches are the only thing he does. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely don't understand the concept of promoting only group work to learn without little to no resources to learn properly. This man acts like he's teaching us how to learn without considering the fact that he doesn't teach. It seems like this structure heavily relies on asking for help from TAs but honestly, some might not even be as helpful.

This professor thinks he is "teaching you how to learn" and doesn't actually teach o chem. Even students in Shabbir, one of the hardest professors at UT, are learning more than Straumanis students. We are constantly told that we "aren't doing the right thing" if we don't understand the content. He places full blame on students for not understanding

Get ready to teach yourself organic chemistry, cause he won't. Entire class is you & your groupmates completing the activities from his activity book, which you have to buy. Very little lecture, if any, just a "motivational" speech about how he promises his method will work. Have a question? better hope a LA is available but there are only so many

Dr. S is very passionate about both the subject matter and his students. Some people were frustrated by the focus on group work, but I really thought it was conducive to actual understanding of fundamental topics. The tests were pretty easy compared the the in class problems, those who study and ask questions will do well.

Andrei Goatmanis. Really dynamic teaching style. Focuses on group work to learn the material using foundational chemistry knowledge. Lenient with grading and willing to alleviate students' stress. Highly recommend over Shabbir.

Straumanis was a fine professor. Coming from Shabbir, the mental load was drastically reduced. He has you working out of a workbook in a group to learn ochem. I found it worked for me. Instead of trying to memorize everything, it felt like I was able to understand what's going on. If you prefer lectures, he posts summary lectures for each class.

Dr. S is kind and genuinely wants his students to learn how to work with a group, which is something we are not exposed to very often in CNS. The class itself wasn't too difficult but it takes a while to get used to not having a lecture-based class. The grading was lenient and there were extra credit opportunities on exams. Not a bad class overall

Coming from Shabbirs class, Ochem 2 with Straumanis felt like a breath of fresh air. He relates to his students, is open-minded, and prioritizes MENTAL HEALTH above all. Gives extra credit and bonus points opportunities, emphasizing learning the content rather than stressing about grades. Asks lots of feedback to improve his class, he really cares!

Definitely didnt learn much in this class but I enjoyed working with a group and having a class that focused more on learning rather than tests and grades. It was an easy A. Just do the activities and review them in modules

didn't like the self taught aspect but the material was pretty easy to grasp. the activities and the past quizzes as well as his lectures were basically all you needed to get a good grade in the class. very lenient and generous with his grading as well

Straumanis is a nice guy, but the way he teaches was horrible for me. Based completely off of group work each class. he never lectures or actually teaches anything. if you can't find a good reliable group to work with, then you're left alone to try and teach yourself physical chemistry
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice and caring guy, but he lowkey looks down on his students. His classes are chaotic, disruptive, experimental, and generally not conducive to learning. The lectures and worksheets don't match the quizzes and exams. There's no way to properly prepare for anything. He doesn't like teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Group learning is not for everyone. This is basically a self taught class where YOU are responsible for understanding the material with worksheets called pogils. I really tried to go along with his teaching style but there is little practice (no hw and minimal practice problems) for the material that it was hard to grasp. Take another professor

As someone who excelled in Dr. Iversons OChem 1 class this class was a joke. Teaching yourself ochem 2 is not ideal for the real world and there is no reason for undergrads. There is no reason we should be teaching ourselves a class so crucial to the MCAT. The fact that obtaining a 100 on the quizzes was impossible speaks for itself. SAVE YOURSELF.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Salami does not teach AT ALL except for a few minute lecture. He does not give out keys, you have to go out and buy them yourself. Sometimes there is not even a key for the activities given. Although he promotes group work, you need to have a good group to do well! The "blind leading the blind".
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't be scared by the flipped classroom model he promotes; it works. However, if you don't function well with very regular assignments and weekly quizzes (and prefer fewer, larger exams), then he's not the professor for you. Class is difficult but not impossible, but will take a lot of extra study time to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. S is a great prof. He really cares about his students, does anything to make the course less stressful, and wants you to learn. That being said, no ochem course will be easy. You must read the materials before class or you will be setting yourself up for failure. The quizzes are only easy if you prepare prior to class.

Professor Straumani is good, but the course is very difficult. I don't like the aspect of a flipped classroom especially for such a difficult course that cannot be adequately taught by peers. I would have so much rather preferred a regular lecture style, in which I could understand the professor's objectives.

The professor has a good grasp on the material but unfortunately his teaching style does not translate well to an online format. I would say if you can take his class in person it might be ok, but online it was quite challenging and confusing.

Straumanis's class is mostly centered around group discussion and working through activities. Its difficult to actually learn most material, but working outside of class definitely helps. Quizzes are also graded with a P/F system which isn't that great, but again, study hard and it won't be horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: very stress free
He doesn't teach.

This entire class was out of a workbook. If that's how you want to learn in a college class be my guest but otherwise I'd say avoid him like the plague. He was very invested in the group learning method so he didn't exactly teach. Also, quizzes were challenging and were graded in a very strange way. Basically all or nothing free response.

He is such a nice guy and really cares for us but I wish that we had more lecture time instead of group work. It may be because we are on zoom for the pandemic, but I find it really hard to learn with the current teaching style.
Switched classroom dynamic. Very Reasonable.

This was the worst class I have ever experienced. A flipped classroom is not ideal for ochem, a class that is heavily tested on the MCAT. I felt as if I was the professor and on top of that, the quizzes were graded so unfairly you never knew what grade you were going to get. I wouldn't recommend this class to my worst enemy. Take another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is a flipped classroom so a lot of the learning you do on your own with a group. The grading is a little tough considering the quiz is only three questions and timed every week (no tests/only final). Although, he does listen to his students and is intentional in the short lecture he does give during class time.

During my three years at UT-Austin I had always enjoyed my professors and excelled in their classes... that was until I made the regrettable mistake of registering for a course with this egotistical man who has the nerve to call himself a 'professor.' You can throw all sanity and well-being out the window if you plan to be a student of his. Don't.

His class is extremely difficult and very much based on your ability to understand the format of his quizzes, he often quizzes on things not taught in class and is not afraid to put something on the quiz that he has never spoken on. If you are not very quick with material and understanding of his quiz format immediately this class will be hard
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a lot less stressful than other o-chem classes at UT. You have to study a fair amount in order to do well on the weekly quizzes however He makes it very doable to achieve a good grade. The grading system is very different than most other classes. This class is really about how much work you put into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Aside from weekly quizzes, which are often difficult and have a love-it/hate-it grading system, there's basically no other options to raise your grade. So, study up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis 's class is entirely group work so if you don't like working in groups you will have trouble. Weekly quizzes are not very hard and are very similar to the problems from class and in homework. Go to class and find a good group, it makes a huge difference. If you want to be prepared for the mcat, dont take this class.

One of my favorite professors. Compared to the typical o chem class get ready to see a lot less midterms and a lot more complex problems. Be ok with struggling with questions and ask for help when you're truly stuck. Don't focus on the grades, there aren't many to worry about, keep your focus on truly understanding mechanisms and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation during class lectures is a must. The class is based on assignments you complete during lectures with other students in the course. There are weekly quizzes on the assignments, no midterms, but a final exam. Although it may seem to be a foreign way of learning, it does help review old material as well as new material.

Disclaimer: This review was required by the professor. During the semester I had this professor, he utilized a grading system that felt approximately all or none. Be aware that partial credit may be negligible. Be prepared to be fast on quizzes. Specifically find fast ways to draw molecules; don't spend time putting ALL the details in on quizzes.

This professor genuinely does care about his students a lot. He wants you to succeed and retain the information in the long run, but the way his class is structured is entirely different than any other class I've taken. You work with other students through guided activities, which I'm sure are helpful if you have to discipline to teach yourself.
way better than o chem 1 because of no tests and just quizzes. Hard class but manageable.
The class isn't bad. I just like lectures and with this class it was like a 15 minute lecture and he would send us into breakout rooms to learn ourselves.

The professor is very nice, and I absolutely loved the fact he has his own workbook. The workbook for his class is EXTREMELY helpful. He allowed for a cheat sheet, but it's better if you learn and understand the process, don't just rely on memorization. I did find it quite difficult since the TAs graded quite harshly, fortunately, regrades helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He really pushes his students to not just memorize organic chemistry, but to actually understand why the reactions occur the way they do. He incorporates group work into every lecture, and really believes that struggling through problems is the best way to learn. He incorporates lots of educational psychology into his lecture format.

What I liked a lot is his emphasis on group work and its value on learning. It was helpful to have a professor facilitate the forming of groups. His worksheets guide your thinking on the material and then reading and doing problems from the textbook helps to make it stick.A lot of work is required in this class to do well, but he makes it possible.

Professor Straumanis is a very kind person, but his class is not for everyone. If you're good with group work and are willing to work on mastering material outside of class, this class is for you. Just don't fall behind and try to learn as actively as possible. However, if you prefer to learn more from lectures, I would take another professor.

Its easy to be successful in this class if youre good at meeting people. You work with a group during class after he gives a 10-20 minute mini lecture and there are weekly quizzes that make up the work for the semester. If youre not outgoing or have trouble with group work you might be better off with another ochem professor
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although, we are given a chance to succeed, that chance seems very slim in the fact that most of the score is based off of weekly quizzes with no homework to check our progress or pad our grade. In addition, the lectures that are recorded online are very quiet and hard to hear, not to forget that he does not go over the whole Chemistry Activity.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible structure of the class. POGIL is meant to be used in hand with lectures, not as a self-learning tool with no guidance. Aside from the horrible class structure, there is a terrible grading system in which missing one question on the quiz results in a 50%. The quizzes do not accurately represent material and have horrible time restraints.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory- but only for the first 10 or so classes. If you like self-teaching and lots and lots of group feedback, this could be the class for you. If you're dependent on lectures and having your curriculum spelled out clearly for you in tests/assessments/quizzes, probably not. Quizzes determine your grade- and it's TOUGH.

Dr. Straumanis fails to understand that everyone learns differently because he is so set on his way. POGIL works great when BALANCED with a traditional lecture. POGIL is meant to reinforce ideas, not cause mental breakdowns every week due to unfair quizzes. Quizzes dont accurately represent material and have unreasonable time constraints.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is kind of what you make of it. There are weekly quizzes that are not meant to be stressful, but still are. His grading methods for the quizzes are somewhat unfair. He is overall a nice guy, but if flipped classes aren't for you maybe consider a different professor. There is no lecturing, just group work.

The professor does care about the students and their input on the class, but it just ended up not being for me. It relies more heavily on self-teaching and working in groups than it does on lectures and I would rather have lectures. I liked the idea of weekly quizzes instead of exams until I saw how hard they were. It all depends on preference

This is the first semester ochem taught by Dr. S. Although he seems like a nice professor who cares about students' well being, the timed weekly quizzes were worth 65% -> big impact on final grade and HARD to finish them on time (no HW). It's VERY important to find a good group to work w & do as much of the material given from the get go.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: There were a few things that changed mid semester due to some learning curves, but I think that this course is a solid choice. To be successful in this class you have to be open to group work, everything is group worked based and untraditional. If you're not disciplined this class is not for you, but if you have good study habits it's rewarding.

He is a caring professor for sure but I had to teach myself most of what I know in this class. Collaboration is required and grading is mostly fair. I wish the material had the mechanisms step by step!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This is professor is a solid choice if you are taking OCHEM 2. It requires a lot of work and effort. If you do not do the work, you will not pass this class. The grade must be earned in this class. That being said Professor Straumanis is a very caring professor and will do everything he can to help you succeed and achieve you full potential.

Dr. Straumanis is a good professor who really does care about his students, but the flipped classroom is not for everyone. Most the class is working in groups, which I found to be helpful despite not being a huge fan of group work. Because of this method you get what you put into the class.

U need to do work in order to make it work. Bc it is a group work-oriented class, YOU NEED TO FIND A GOOD GROUP IN ORDER TO SUCCEED (by that I mean ppl who actively participate). First couple of weeks, try to be very active in groups so that u can be able to find good groupmates. The more effort u put in during class time the better off u will be
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis cares a lot about all of his students. He makes sure to remind you that this class is a lot of and that it's okay to be stressed. However, I am not a fan of how this class is structured. Weekly quizzes are meant to replace midterms. These quizzes are tough. Final exam at the end of the semester. Study hard for the quizzes!

If you like a flipped classroom style of class, then by all means, take this course. However, I personally struggle with this format and I had a hard time understanding the material as it was nearly a self-taught course. It is very important to find a good group as early as possible.
I really wish he gave more lectures instead of us relying on getting a good group. besides that, he is a good professor in my opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CH 320N is a very difficult class in itself but Dr. Straumanis was a truly great professor. He uses an approach to teach ochem that is more interactive than the other ochem professors at ut. I would recommend only taking this class if you can put in plenty of work and time to learn the material well.

Dr.S cares about his students but the structure of his class made learning much more difficult than it should have been. You're essentially teaching yourself and the majority your grade depends on difficult weekly quizzes. He hardly lectures so learning the material is dependent on getting a good group and asking for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is formatted so the workbook walks you through the material, but the workbook can be vague and the problems provided are not representative of the problems we are quizzed on. But Dr. Straumanis definitely cares about his students and is approachable for assistance.

Straumanis is an alright prof. He is actually really nice but I don't really like his teaching style. You figure out how to do the things in your group in a workbook. He doesn't really lecture much. I could learn on my own but it doesn't work for a lot of people. If you stay atop of the material and you can learn on your own, this class is 4 you

The majority of the class is based on self-discovery in small groups, which has its benefits, but there is little to no lecture given by the instructor. No exams but weekly quizzes that contain questions that seem to ignore the time constraints. Dr. Straumanis seems well-intentioned and approachable, but I think the execution is lacking greatly.

This class was probably one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The only reason this one was so difficult was because of how it was taught. It was a very new system to me with only about a 10-minute lecture in an hour and a half course where the rest of the time was spent in group work learning the material on your own.
His quizzes will screw you over. 4/5 on majority of quizzes will give you a B
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class if you're sincerely interested in organic chemistry. Professor loves to keep the class involved and tries to encourage everyone when the material gets hard. Definitely do not get behind in this class, there are quizzes every week and you will be playing keep up all semester if you decide to be lazy with the coursework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For this flipped classroom you need to self teach. Quiz questions are harder than those in practice, so study. Go to class, work with good group. Study, practice and don't procrastinate. They expect you to know OCHEM 1: they don't review it. Asking questions in class or O. H.'s is important also! Breath, take quiz, repeat.
Needs to have a much better structured class. Quizzes are terrible.

The professor is really passionate about ochem and promotes his flipped classroom learning. Unfortunately it doesn't work with such a complicated subject in the middle of a pandemic where students are already struggling. The professor acknowledged the shortcomings but doesn't plan on changing anything this semester. I cry everyday in this class.

Dr. Straumanis is a very caring and encouraging professor who is open to making adjustments through feedback. Personally, I found his class very difficult because it is a flipped classroom and I do not learn best through that style. I found it hard to grasp and keep up with the material and struggled preparing for the weekly quizzes.

flipped classroom; professor doesn't really teach the class; no full lectures; you practically have to study on your own and/or with your group; studying based on workbook and/or textbook; grades dependent on hard quizzes; short amount of time to take quiz (making it more difficult);and final not worth a lot. I don't recommend taking this class.

He really cares about ochem and tries to help people learn. However, the teaching style does not really work for me and I found it very difficult to keep up and learn. There are weekly quizzes that are graded hard and not much extra credit. Once you fall behind this class becomes very stressful and it is difficult to catch up again.

This class made me cry so much. After multiple people reemphasizing how much they were struggling and concerned with their grades, his only response was to become flustered and state we should not focus on grades, instead on learning the material. This material was also self taught because lecture was max 20 minutes. The rest was group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is SO nice and makes adjustments through feedback, OCHEM IS JUST FREAKING HARD!!! The class is super group orientated and it felt like we focused more on passing the weekly quizzes rather than understanding concepts. Idk he says he'll lower how much quizzes affect your grade, I'm just burnt out from the constant quizzing in ochem 1&2

If you get a bad group, you will not do well in class. If you do better in a lecture-style/ traditional classroom as I do, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! He has a flipped classroom and I found it very hard to grasp the material. You pretty much have to work in groups and teach yourself the material. Quizzes are also graded VERY HARD.

This class puts an emphasis on group work by using POGILs to learn the material instead of learning from lectures. I find this to be a great way to learn OChem because it's much more engaging. Also, grading is fair as he does not penalize for small mistakes and gives extra points if you get the question entirely correct.

This class is a lot of group work that focuses on self teaching the material through a guided workbook. There are summary lectures that are posted every week, but you are expected to attempt to learn new material on your own with your group during class. Find a group that is willing to work together so the material is easier to learn.

I think Dr. Straumanis is a great person and it's clear he cares a lot about his students and the subject he's teaching. But his grading and the way his class is set up are not indicative of this. Grading is very subjective and the pass/fail grading system is incredibly punitive. Missing one question could get you less than a 50.

All self-guided learning. The professor is caring for students and genuinely wants students to learn and be better students. Putting in the effort to try to learn may not always guarantee you will be prepared for quizzes. Studying for nuance is hard when as a student what you need to know isn't clear.

Uses flipped classroom and never lectures. He has summary lectures that are useful but he gives minimal instruction. He does not have office hours and puts most of the responsibility of engaging with students on his TAs.

Flipped classroom with expectations to learn off group work alone, which is good if you get a good group, but left some students struggling alone. I feel as if he has a good grasp on ochem but fails to profess his knowledge well. Be a team player and you should survive.

For this class, you have to be able to do a lot of learning on your own or in your group. I thought the workbook we used did fine in giving deep explanations to ochem concepts, and everyone in my group was able to help eachother. It's good if you like group work and a self-guided style. If that's not what you're looking for, you might not enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You have to basically teach yourself everything in this class. Make sure to choose a good group for lectures or otherwise you're screwed. The all-or-nothing quizzes each week add to the stress of learning everything in your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis trys to make ochem 2 an enjoyable class. He thinks that he is doing a favor by they way the class is structured (all group learning and quiz heavy). It is hard to learn without thorough lectures and example problems to prepare for the weekly quizzes especially during online based learning. Be ready to teach yourself material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You have to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Solid OChem prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I believe it was his first year at UT and considering covid conditions, he was more than a caring and thoughtful professor. His teaching style is really focused on guided learning through class activities that are completed within a group, and weekly quizzes that test your understanding of the prior week's information. Overall great professor!

I believe it was his first year teaching at UT and with the covid conditions, I gotta say he was a very thoughtful and easy to learn from professor. With a bit of an unusual teaching style that consisted of completing activities within a group, if you have a good understanding of ochem 1 then his class should only take a bit of focus + studying

Overall, the class is a very cumulative experience which starts off with basic topics and progressively gets harder as you go in depth in these said topics. The professor himself is great and put his best foot forward but the class is what creates hurdles due to the quizzes' weight in class grade but he has an interesting grading system that helps

There are worksheets you work through during the class within study groups. It is crucial to find a study group that works well together in order to make it through this class. The lectures are just summary lectures over the worksheet, but there are activities in the textbook and worksheet that can be used to strengthen your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr.S had good intention in developing a creative method for teaching. However he needs to understand it will NOT work for a subject like Ochem. We need traditional lectures, notes. you cant expect students to learn ochem in groups and self-teach each other. Also the weekly quizzes were unfair because it was nothing related to what we do in class.

Dr. S has good intentions in mind to implement a creative way of teaching (the whole POGIL thing where you self-teach yourself ochem 2) HOWEVER THIS METHOD DOES NOT WORK FOR OCHEM. We need traditional lectures and notes, this method does not work for a class like ochem. Also, the quizzes were extremely unfair because we were not taught in class.

The most critical part of doing well is making sure you can get a good group. However, this doesn't mean you need to know anybody in the class going in. This class is not structured just to teach you OChem. It will help you get out of your comfort zone, and develops your group work skills. Knowing OChem 1 basics is a must, or you will play catchup.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis is amazing. He is a great lecturer and teacher. While the class might not be traditional, it is very effective. I learned more from Straumanis' teaching structure than from many other professors. He gives excellent reviews in his summary lectures. TBH all the hate he is getting is unwarranted. He is always there to help you.

Dr. Straumanis has a very interesting class format in which the class solely consists of students working in groups and teaching each other. Furthermore, the weekly quiz system is designing so that if a single part of a question wrong you receive minimal credit.

I've never had a grade below a B until this class. He will barely go over the material and then expect you to use the information to take quizzes that a doctor would struggle to answer. The best advice he gave was "Do better". Little to no support so if you take this class, its all up to you.
I wish I had known I would been told that I would be teaching myself Ochem 2. Be prepared for a quiz every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of your grade comes from weekly quizzes that can get tough. Prof doesn't actually lecture; everything is self-taught through group activities, readings, and optional learning that are supposed to facilitate learning but seem impossible at times w/o a solid lecture. Don't take this course if you hate group work and self-teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Look, Straumanis seems to be sympathetic of his students. That being said It is one thing to say you care and entirely another to take action to fix things. This class can be discouraging and is very difficult since he does not lecture and he likes to use all or nothing grading which can be extremely stressful. The flipped classroom is not for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He cares about teaching an efficient way to learn (emphasis on group work). However, he hardly teaches lectures and we are left on our own to go through packets of material with our group. I liked the low stress of weekly quizzes, but would have appreciated more teaching from him directly. Stay on top of packets and do the activities. Ask for help!

For the most part, this class was fine. Organic chemistry is difficult, but having groups made it better for me. Talking to my classmates was really helpful because I could fill in some learning gaps. In addition, I loved getting to talk to people. Great online format! However, I would have liked more lectures or more explanations of the topics.

This class had its pros and cons. I loved that we could be in groups and work on the POGIL book together and fill in each other's learning gaps. However, I did not like that we did not have full lectures that we could watch; it would have been very helpful!

Dr. Straumanis is a great guy, fantastic even. I have never learned so much in one class before, but that does not change the fact that I still am most likely not going to pass his course. The group-learning approach does not work for a busy student. Grading is off. Very self-teach-based. Was not for me, but can be for you! (I wouldn't risk it).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Since this is his first year teaching at UT, the students were unfortunately the guinea pigs that were subject to random changes in grading policies and criteria. The system in place for grading the quizzes felt very disorganized and unstandardized. Many students became upset because of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is to me is like a compromise. In my opinion it's very difficult to 90+ consistently on the quizzes but getting an 80+ on every quiz is very doable. The trade in is that the class feels a lot less stressful since it's easier to prepare for a weekly 30 minute quiz than biweekly 2 hour exams. Limit your mistakes and you should get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is a flipped class, so participation in your groups matter to understand the content. The professor and TAs are willing to help, but whoever you choose for your group matters the most. Quizzes are not too bad if you learn the weekly content.

Followed a flipped class structure (no lectures, just class work). Felt like it really depended on who you got in your group. If no one had any idea what was going on, class was a waste of time because there were post summary lectures that went over the work. Also there weren't tests, just weekly quizzes. Really depends on how you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Dr. Straumanis seems like an alright dude, his class structure is very interesting to say the least. Weekly quizzes compose most of your grade. Be prepared to study on your own for them as this is a "flipped classroom" class... which means absolutely no lectures. The grading system for these quizzes is also all or nothing, which can suck.

Overall very cool professor. There's a huge debate over the structure of his class since there aren't really lectures we just do worksheets in groups. It wasn't really good for me, but other people didn't mind it. There was mention of improving the class structure for later semesters. Also there are no tests, just weekly quizzes.

Understanding Ochem 1 is a prerequisite. Initially quizzes are very rough, but they get slightly better. The grading scheme is very subjective. Most importantly, you need to be ready to learn by yourself. The coursework is just group exercises from his textbook that are ungraded but a requirement to do well. He only reviews tough concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For being such a difficult course, he hardly lectures during class, but rather puts us in breakout rooms the entire time. I wish he gave more practice and questions that were more similar to the ones on the quiz which are often not straightforward and very conceptual. He claims to give partial credit, but is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I do believe Dr. Staumanis cares about his students and is doing what he believes is best but if you prefer to be taught rather than teach yourself this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I will start off by saying that he is a very kind and well-meaning professor. He wants all of his students to be successful and grow personally and in their education. Despite this, his challenging quizzes and restrictions by the chem department make it hard to achieve his goals for us. It is a flipped classroom with group work.

The professor himself is a great guy but I don't think he truly understands how important having solutions to our problems is to helping us learn. His textbook workbook and solutions manual all need to be purchased and you don't get answers unless you purchase the book. He doesn't post exact exercise answers and wants the students to figure it out.

Professor Straumanis really cares about students and wants them to truly know and understand the material, but the way his class is structured and his grading scheme makes it difficult for many people to succeed and do well. With the flipped classroom format, despite being given many aids for the course, succeeding is still a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didnt learn much at all from lecture. For the most part I had to teach myself. There is little lecture and mostly group work during class. The quizzes are fair game and are everything covered in your group work, however, the class average is really bad for quizzes. Which isn't great since quizzes our pretty much our entire grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis's organic chemistry II class is no walk in the park. You have to work for it and be ready every week for the quizzes. The most important skill learned for this class is group work. Dr Straumanis teaches group work because it's essential in every aspect of life. If you take this class be ready to put in two hours of studying each day.

Professor Straumanis' class was the first flipped class I have ever taken. If you have not taken a flipped class before, beware of joining his class. Find a good group if you can. Answers on his workbook are locked behind another book you must purchase. Frustrating to have to purchase another thing on top of his book to be sure of your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis has weekly, timed quizzes. He cares a lot about his students and has a flipped classroom.

Without a doubt, Organic Chemistry II is one of the hardest classes a STEM student would take. Dr. Straumanis does a very good job making sure the class is engaged. His class is not lecture-heavy but instead uses guided questions to help us discover the concept on our own; through strong peer cooperation, his method strengthens our understanding.

This is by far one of the most difficult classes I have taken at UT. The quality of your learning is entirely based on your group and how well your group works together. You basically have the teach yourself, which can be good and bad at the same time. Though summary lectures are pretty good, the quizzes are extremely difficult and will kill you.

This class is almost entirely group-work, and the professor does not lecture. It was very difficult to adapt to his course, and if you prefer a professor who will explain all the content thoroughly, you should not take this class. If you choose to enroll in this course, find a good group, because it will be extremely difficult to do the work alone.

He seems like a nice person and he cares about his students' education but his pass/not yet grading system can either REALLY hurt you or REALLY help you. That's why people in the class either hate his class or absolutely love it. You have to rely on group work and basically teach yourself because he doesn't lecture much.

Get ready to learn organic chemistry by yourself if you take this class. Didn't know what to expect on quizzes because everything was done with group work, which allowed me to learn the material but not in the way he wanted. You learn through packets he made and there is no lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is a nice professor who cares about his students and their grades, he is receptive to feedback and improving his class. However, his class is quite hard since he barely lectures and expects students to learn from their groups. Also, there are weekly quizzes that are really stressful since they're free response and rushed on time.

Dr. Straumanis definitely cares about his students; however, his flipped-classroom approach for Ochem II is too hard to handle. I DO NOT RECOMMEND HIM. Self-teaching organic chemistry is not fun, and I would have much rather preferred a classic, structured classroom environment. If you do take him, good luck you can do it. I'll never take him again

This class was really really difficult. The professor definitely cares about his students a lot, in fact, he spends more energy expressing how much he want you to learn than actually teaching. You do not get structured notes in this class, so if you are looking for structure, this is not the class for you. Quizzes are quite intense and a time cruch

Professor Straumanis cares about the education of his students above all else, and this is reflected in the higher second semester grades earned by students who had him first semester. If you only care about a letter grade, this class is not for you. However, if your goal is to truly understand the material, Straumanis is the professor for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis cares and wants students to learn organic chemistry and life lessons. He is receptive to feedback and changes that students have. He has a certain way he wants the class to go from the beginning and a good group is very important! Ochem is tough but putting in the time and having quizzes each week helps keep me on task and learning.

Dr. Straumanis really wants us to succeed and listens to feedback. But this is a flipped class and it is very difficult. You must do open ended quizzes every week (there have been many cases where what you learned and what is on the quiz differ). There is not much of a lecture so you must depend on your group (make sure you form a good group).

Considering the fact that ochem is just a hard course, Straumanis does try his best to relieve his students with the pressure of grades. If you like lectures, this may not be the class for you. But if you like more hands-on, self-guided courses, then you will thrive. He does listen and care about his students. I have learned a good amount.

Group work is really important in this class so make sure to pick a good group. The flipped classroom teaching isn't for everyone, but I personally think I understood more from it. Beware that he doesn't provide keys for the CTQS/exercises in his workbook and these weekly quizzes can definitely be stressful.

Just a reminder that this class is O Chem which greatly influences the difficulty of it. Straumanis is not bad as far as teaching goes but everything is group based. Which is not bad unless you do not have or find a group you mesh well with and thus end up losing out on a fundamental part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly not a bad class. He wrote an interactive workbook that takes you through all of the content. As long as you are good on the concepts in it you should do fine on quizzes and evenly pick up on what he expects. STUDY ochem 1 material before you take this class because it is synthesis heavy.

Honestly not a bad class. He wrote an interactive work book that takes you through all of the content in an easy and effective way. If you go through theses you should be fine one quizzes and eventually you figure out what he expects. STUDY ochem 1 material before you take this class because it realties heavily on synthesis problems.

I really liked the teaching style professor Straumanis used, and have learned more from this class than from Shabhir's class. Still, if you expect working really hard automatically brings good grades, you might not enjoy it. But if you're willing to all that, +office hours/reviews, & be patient; learning is fun and grade portion comes naturally!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading system in this course and unorganized material makes the class inaccessible and time consuming. In many cases, the issue is not the course content difficulty, but the disorganization in the resources like the workbook and unstructured lectures. The grading system for weekly quizzes is subjective & keys are not provided for inclass work.

Dr. Straumanis cares a lot about his students! Yes, the class is only based on weekly quizzes and the final. However, I liked that aspect of the class because I could focus on the material from the past 2 lecture days rather than weeks worth of materials. I wish he provided more pre-lecture style videos to introduce the topics to us in more detail.
Grading on quizzes can be confusing and tedious but it's doable. Class time is spent on working with a group that can be helpful, but it's either a hit or miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has probably been the worst class I've taken at UT. The professor doesn't really teach and forces group learning upon students even when everyone it is a known fact that everyone learns differently and has things that work for them and things that do not. The class is graded on only weekly quizzes and a final. Do not take this class.

Dr. Straumanis emphasizes the importance of learning material by working through the concepts independently first. He then gives short lectures that solidify the concepts you struggled through in the worksheets he provides. This teaching method is not for everyone, and the lack of full-on lectures may be frustrating. I personally enjoyed it.

This has been one of the worst classes I have taken at UT. To put it bluntly, Dr. Straumanis does not teach and uses his POGIL/flipped classroom to justify this. He even went as far to say he doesn't think the word "teach" should exist and that his goal is to not teach us organic chemistry. Do NOT take this class. Grade is determined by quizzes.

This has been one of the worst classes I have taken at UT. To put it bluntly, Dr. Straumanis does not teach and uses his POGIL/flipped classroom to justify this. He even went as far to say he doesn't think the word "teach" should exist and also that his goal is to not teach us organic chemistry. Do not take this class. Take Shabbir or anyone else.

If you take Prof. Straumanis you need to find a good group to work with. This group directly affects your grade outcomes as most of the learning is in groups. The weekly quizzes are difficult and sometimes aren't over the covered material. Don't expect any teaching, but if you liked self-teaching this might be the class for you.

My Ochem 1 class had very structured lectures which was a very effective way for me to learn the material. This class relied more on you learning from the workbook yourself. The weekly quizzes compounded by a strange grading system caused a lot of stress. The professor has been willing to adjust the course a little and cares about the students.

My favorite professor! I did not do well in Shabbirs ochem 1 and I am doing much better here! Straumanis CARES about his students and LISTENS to their feedback. This class is mainly group work so FIND A GOOD GROUP. You will not be teaching yourself if you have a good group and work together!! Ask for help from TA's and LA's, they are great!

This class was definitely the better option for Organic Chemistry II. Lectures are optional. There is a notebook that takes you through the material. Definitely make sure to watch the summary lectures, they help a lot! Make study guides before each exam. They are very helpful. Straumanis is very nice and cares a lot about his students.

Straumanis is really passionate about wanting his students to learn, which is good if you go to class! There's a lot of group work, as he believes that is the best way for you to really learn and understand the information. Sometimes, this can be a bit difficult since grades are mostly based off weekly quizzes, but if you go to class you'll be fine

One of my favorite professors I've ever taken at UT! He's a really nice guy and cares a lot about making sure each student is actually learning the material. He doesn't lecture and instead you work through a book in groups. At first I was nervous, but this actually helped me a lot in the class. I recommend this class to any student taking O chem.

This course puts a lot of emphasis on group work, which I do not personally find helpful. The most helpful tool was the workbook Witten by Dr. Straumanis. This the best learning guide to Ochem 2 without spending hours looking at a textbook. The course is quiz based too which I also found helpful, especially in an online course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class relies heavily on group work and self-learning. The summary lectures and the exercises are extremely helpful for the quizzes. The quizzes can be hard and they do have a lot of content on them, but it is manageable if you keep up with the content.

SPRING 2021 - Online Weekly quizzes (with one cheat sheet each) and one final (no cheat sheet). Self study. First few weeks are mandatory attendance but after that it is up to you. Extra problems in workbook and textbook. Not really lectures, just a review on major points of understanding and videos outside of class. Easy A if you keep up w/ materi
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was very stressful and Straumanis did not teach anything. His required workbook does not prepare you for the quizzes and his grading system is flawed. You should not take this class unless you already understand all of Ochem 1 and 2 or if you are prepared to teach yourself everything. The TAs+ LAs are great at answering questions though

He is a decent professor, however, flipped classrooms arent for me. He only gives out a certain amount of re-grade requests and the ta's have messed a couple of my quizzes grades even though I would have the same answer from the answer key. If you want to succeed in this class you need to have a solid foundation in ochem1.

Organic Chemistry, in general, is a tough topic, and being online doesn't make it any easier. This is a flipped classroom, so if that doesn't work for you, I'd suggest taking a diff prof. There are weekly quizzes and a final exam and the questions can be challenging. Both Straumanis and his team of LAs are super approachable if you have questions!

Honestly taking OCHEM online during the pandemic was not ideal. Every professor had different expectations and different things we're taught in OCHEM 1. Dr. Straumanis began OCHEM 2 with the impression we all learned the same thing and were all on the same understanding when that was not the case. I had to go to office hours to play catch up.

This class is taught in a flipped-classroom format where you essentially teach yourself with a group of other students and you are quizzed weekly. The weekly quizzes are challenging, but they force you to keep up with the material so I personally liked the format.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes us group up at the beginning of class which I liked. The actual course on the other hand was crazy unorganized during the first half of the semester and people's grades suffered because of it. We have a quiz every week and not allowed to use textbook/notes/your groupmates (why even group up in the first place??) unlike OChem 1.
You basically teach yourself. It's helpful to review the textbook pages before class. Try to really learn the memorization tasks. Throughout the semester brush up on ochem 1 concepts.

It's nice that he really does care about his student's learning and mental health, but he's just not a good teacher. You have to teach yourself and instead of exams, there's weekly quizzes with a specific grading system he uses. Went from Shabbir, who explained everything in great detail, to Straumanis, who talks to you for 15- 20 min then leaves.

Show up- study for the quizzes- he makes the expectations super clear so just keep up and you'll do great - he also wants all the kids to succeed so he changes grading criteria a lot through out the year to help those struggling - no definitive grading cutoffs

The weekly quizzes made it really easy to stay up to date and I managed to keep up throughout the semester without ever feeling like I had to learn 2 months worth in one night. Your group members are important so pick wisely. Make sure to select people that will show up during lecture and will participate during the group work.

Professor Straumanis loves his students. He is willing to listen to feedback but I would say the biggest issue with his class style is that it is not very focused on his teaching but rather group learning. This method of trial by fire is not bad but it leads to a dip in grades before you start gaining the real understanding of the material.

If I'm being honest there are no good organic chemistry professors, but as somebody who took both Straumanis and Shabbir, Straumanis is wayyyy better. He is not a good lecturer, but his grading is a lot better than Shabbir's class, and I ended with a much higher grade and more understanding than I did with Shabbir, and it took me less work and str

Given that there are no lectures to go off of get ready to watch alot of Youtube and start reading from the textbook. 95% of this class you will be in groups doing questions out of a workbook that is supposed to help you take a weekly quiz that you only have 20 minutes to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've really enjoyed Professor Straumanis' class. The reviews don't lie--it's a flipped classroom so you have to put in work outside of class; however, for me, this works well with my ADHD since it gave me the flexibility to learn on my own terms/time. I'm not confident that I'll get an A, but I do finally understand OChem. Pick your group wisely!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are more motivated to self teach and focus less on the letter grade, take this class. It is hard to truly learn the material just from doing the work that he assigns in class. Will need to spend a lot of time outside of class to understand the material. Straumanis cares about his students- but be prepared for weekly quizzes.

This class is a difficult class in general so you have to work to get an A. Prof. Straumanis is a great professor and truly cares about his students and tries to make the course less stressful. The class is more of a flip-classroom and involves a good amount of group work so if you enjoy learning this way then take the class!

Basically just teaching yourself Ochem for a semester. He lectures for about 15 minutes then releases a 20-minute video after class the rest is working on his workbook in breakout rooms. HW and review materials have no key so good luck figuring out if your doing things right before the weekly quiz. Grading system so bad he had to change it halfway

The course itself is difficult so you will have to work to get an A in the class. Professor Straumanis is a great professor and he truly cares about his students and tries to make things less stressful. However, the class is more of a flip-classroom class with more group work involved so if you enjoy that type of learning then take the class!

As the other reviews suggest, this class is driven solely by group work. I think there is SOME merit to this idea, as it is crucial that students teach themselves. With that being said, I wish that the class had a greater lecture component. I feel often unprepared for the weekly quizzes. Not sure I would take this class again.

The guy is literally "teaching" from Hawaii. 10 minute lectures before class, and then breakout-rooms to work on his textbook for the rest of class. Teach yourself or fail. People asked for extra credit and all he did was change his grading format, which doesn't even matter because he assigns grades based on class distribution.

This professor is most likely unlike other professors you have taken a class with. He gives open note quizzes every week but you must thoroughly understand the information prior. He is a fair grader and gives more weight to the easier questions on the quiz. Group work is prioritized in class and you must lean on your other group members for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paying another person to teach myself OChem. This class is basically buy his book, work on his book during class.

Each class has a short 10 minute lecture, the rest of the time is group work where you are pretty much teaching yourself. He then has post-lecture videos that cover the material you tried learning by yourself during class. Weekly quizzes, 30 minutes to complete, 3 questions(with multiple parts), really hard honestly. Highly do NOT recommend him.

If you want to teach yourself organic chemistry, this is the class to be in. Lectures are 15 minutes long.. Organic chemistry 2 lectures are 15 minutes long.. 2 times a week, 15 minutes long.. If you ask a question in Zoom chat, expect to not be answered. I'm unsure why I am in this class if it's just to work out of a textbook and teach myself..

Pros: - Class format heightens learning - Professor is good at clearing misconceptions - TAs and professor are accessible during/after lecture Cons: - Takes LOTS of time to study, class meant to be taken alone - Grading system is not reflective of a student's growth, only one try - no answer keys to check HW/CTQ - easy to get lost in what to study
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only assignments are quizzes and a final. The quizzes are really hard because he actually wants you to learn instead of just memorizing things.
I like the professor and the way he wants us to genuinely learn in a better way, but the grading and quiz structure make things very hard IMO.

Hit or miss class. Some students like his teaching style and really do benefit from it, and some don't. I personally don't like having to learn something for the first time with other people that are also learning it for the first time. I'd rather have a normal class where he actually lectures me. It's been rough, but he really does care about us.

I personally don't like his teaching system & would rather have the typical lecture class like the other Ochem 2 professor, Shabbir. Taking weekly quizzes is a lot less stressful than having an exam, but these quizzes are not easy at all. He has a unique way of grading them that I have mixed feelings about. Despite all of this, he really does care.

Class is based on quizzes, and making a bad grade on one will drop your overall score quite a lot. All learning is done in a book, with short summary lectures posted after class. I feel like I learned better in a traditional lecture setting like Dr. Shabbir's, and would probably not have taken this class again.

Dr. Straumanis CARES about his students. However, this class was a flipped learning style class and honestly I didn't really get much out of that especially because it was online. Every week he posted summary lectures which I thought to be the most helpful so make sure to watch those and understand them.

I think some of these reviews combine the professor and his teaching together which isn't fair. Ochem 2 is a hard course regardless.
