Taking Straumanis this semester has allowed me to learn it a lot better than how I did in ochem 1. His course was hard, granted he will make changes going forward, but it is worth it. The quizzes force you to study.

Dr. Straumanis is a great professor and cares a lot about his students. This course is not lecture based, rather more group work activities during class time. I find this class to be more self-learning than most of my other classes. I would highly recommend doing the extra practice problems in preparation for the weekly quizzes.

He really emphasizes the idea of group work a lot so class is just group work on a workbook. Tbh I have a better understanding of ochem this way than I did taking ochem 1 but it would be more helpful if he taught a bit more than doing a little overview. This class is hard so it requires a lot of self taught and self study.

This class is based on group learning with little lecture time. I think that it is very helpful to bounce ideas off of your peers, but if you do not have a dedicated group then you might struggle in this class. I also have loved that instead of exams we take weekly quizzes, but this makes it very important to stay on top of your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As mentioned he has a flipped classroom structure of the class. He is very nice but I really think grades would be better if he just lectured us... I understand he wants us to work for our grade but it comes to a point where there are so many people that don't know what's going on that it's like the blind leading the blind. Just know that going in

I think the way this class is run and overall teaching style leads students to believe that Dr. Straumanis is a bad professor- he's not. He really does care about the students and their initiative to learn, but in truth, it's very hard to learn ochem in a flipped-classroom setting. If you want the grade, you really will have to work for it.

He is a decent professor considering this being an O-chem class. Like mentioned above he does not lecture during in class. Rather students are expected to work in groups on chemistry activities that require you to do some self teaching. He is generous with grading and giving extra credit. Take in mind I took this class all online during COVID.

A lot of these reviews are cuz he's giving extra credit FYI so most of us haven't taken the final yet. But you definitely have to be willing to self teach and learn. We were his guinea pig class WHILE online so I'd expect him to make a few changes to the course, but his POGIL system's probably here to stay.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about his students however this class is still very difficult. He uses a flipped classroom style and you will basically teach yourself. There are weekly quizzes which are extremely difficult as points awarded are 'all or nothing'. Your grade weighs heavily on these quizzes and the final since there are no other grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can clearly see that he cares about his class but his class method is tough as it is very self taught and unless you find a group of people that cares to stick together in an online class, you will be left to self teach ochem2. I would strongly urge you to learn the material beforehand and review on what you struggled the most on ochem 1
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will teach yourself organic chemistry the entire semester.

Dr. Stramanis is one of the kindest people I've ever met. The class is not traditional styled rather than flipped. Quizzes are weekly and they are challenging. He does a P/NY grading system which works in favor of students who do well on quizzes. Studying CA's and doing exercises are crucial if wanting to succeed in this class.

Dr. Straumanis does care about his students, but class time is mostly spent working through the workbook in small groups. Definitely a lot of self study and outside of class work. Participation was required and graded for the first 12 class periods.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis is a very caring teacher and really wants his students to learn the topics in Organic Chemistry. However, the POGILE method of learning is not for everyone. Also, it really depends on the group that you pick in class because you essentially have to be able to work well together and figure out the topics as a group.

Learned a lot about ochem and feel like I have a better understanding of it all overall after taking this class. However, it is a bit stressful when 65% of your grade is decided through the weekly quizzes. Basically self-taught with some video lectures covering the material.

Professor Straumanis has a very nice personality. Hard weekly quizzes. You will mainly have to learn from breakout rooms where you do group work. If you're not able to learn on your own then wouldn't recommend taking this professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Straumanis really cares about how much you get out of the class and considers students' feedback. The bulk of your grade relies on weekly quizzes with all or nothing grading which is stressful, but going to class and doing the groupwork really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Staumanis, is very inspirational and explains really well. He makes you feel good about learning, and is very encouraging. My only issue was his flipped classroom concept. If you dont learn well in a group setting, maybe think about taking another professor. This class makes you learn concepts by yourself, without the traditional lecturing.

Professor Straumanis was really well at listening to student's feedback and making adjustments especially in these uncertain times. The course is quiz heavy and self taught. There is a quiz every week which your grade relies heavily on. Majority of lecture is based on working with your group.

The professor has you learning everything on your own. Little to no info before going into breakout rooms, and you're with students that don't know much either. very picky on grades, you need to be perfect to get a good grade. grading is horrible, I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although the group work format of this class can feel somewhat unhelpful, I've found that being forced to engage with the content every class (as opposed to being lectured at) helps a lot with understanding, as long as you're willing to give it a chance. If you take this class, make sure you're very solid with OChem 1 concepts or you're done for.

Dr. Straumanis really does want the best for his students, but it has been especially hard for me to learn in his class this semester. We have weekly quizzes that are worth our entire grade including one final. The grading system includes grading on an all or nothing scale, so my grades have been really back and forth. Would take again though.

Dr. Straumanis focuses on students working and collaborating with each other on assignments, instead of giving lectures. Due to this, the material was self-taught and hard to grasp. With quizzes every week, a poor grading system, and a final at the end of the year, the class was challenging and different from traditional classrooms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but due to the difficulty of the course and his style of teaching, you need to be self reliant on your ability to teach yourself.
Nice guy honestly it is just a really tough class. The flipped classroom isn't for me, Im not a big fan of group work.

MUST buy his book or else you literally cannot take this class. Weekly quizzes, mainly learn from breakout rooms/groupwork. Doesn't post the answers to all the questions, only some. He doesn't teach at all, but rather gives you worksheets/activities and posts a summary lecture that explains only a small amount of the questions on there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a super cool professor, however, the content of the quizzes extends way outside his workbook and lectures. Everything relies too much on group work and yourself. Being such a hard course, I would expect my professor to provide as much information and guidance as possible. I would not take him again unless he changed the structure of his class

The class mainly consists of working through workbook problems with group members. Most of the learning is done through reading the textbook, doing the exercises, and watching summary lectures. The quizzes are challenging and the questions are unpredictable.

A flipped classroom style is implemented where lecutre was for ungraded groupwork (attendance was required for half the semester). Outside of class, the prof. uploads an explanation and assigns problems that were both helpful. I learn best self-taught, so I liked the class. If you need a strict structure with a professor explaining this isn't it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flipped style classroom. Claims best way for students to learn is by working together for the answer, doesn't like to give you anything to make sure you are right, says that you will have a gut feeling that it is right. Its ochem... i never feel right, ever. Quiz questions can be very random. Would not recommend unless you teach yourself ochem 2.

Here is the reality of it. You can't get by with just the activities we do in class if you want even an A-. You need to do all the extra book problems (which cost $$$), go to office hours (because he only lectures for 20 minutes), and have an obscene amount of time (8+ hrs) to do only o-chem. Just be prepared to do a lot of self teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He cares about his students but his flipped teaching style was not for me. I feel like a lot of this class was self-taught because the lectures were very short so you have to put in the work and be independent. If you work hard it's definitely possible to do well, but I would choose a different professor if you like more structured lectures.

His teaching style is flipped and he gives short lectures at the start of class but I honestly found the textbook more helpful. He clearly cares for his students but his teaching style was not for me; I would have preferred more structured lectures with more explanation, but if you work hard outside of class you can definitely still do well.

This class consists of very little lecture time and is heavily problem based. Weekly quizzes force you to stay on top of material. It is essential to be able to work well in a group. This class taught me a whole new way to learn. The professor is always supportive and works hard to emphasize and correct common misconceptions.
Flipped classroom where students teach themselves ochem using a textbook. Weekly quizzes, need to constantly study and put in quite a bit of time to do well in the class.

He isn't a bad professor. He truly does care for his students. His teaching style is flipped classroom & so it took getting used to, but once you get the hang of it, it's all good. Grades are based off quizzes so you have to know what's going on. Every professor will always be different so as long as you adapt and work for it, you'll be just fine.

His grading style is counterproductive to success for many students. Having us basically teach ourselves organic chemistry makes the class, which would already be difficult, one where you have to sacrifice your grades in the other courses you are taking in order to succeed. Having a quiz every week leads to an insane amount of stress every week.

The course is structured upon group work and group work only. He does mini lectures at the beginning of each class and thats it. His main grades are quizzes that make up majority of the grade. So be ready for a lot of self studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is difficult if you are not willing to work with others. Plan on spending an average of 8 hours per week outside of class to really understand the material. The quizzes take time to get used to, don't freak out if you don't get to question 3.

Dr. S really cares about his students. He asked for a mid-semester feedback & implemented some suggestions regarding the quizzes. There's a quiz every week, no midterms & a final. The quizzes every week is quite stressful tbh. He has a flipped classroom & you have to do the activities in the workbook. The workbook walks you through the topics.

Professor Straumanis is very inspiring in terms of his dedication to his teaching style, which I can see that works for some, but that person is not me, and my grade will suffer. Once you are in his class, be sure to adapt quickly, do not expect lectures, you need to do the chem activities and supplement them with Youtube vids for extra help.
Grades are solely based around weekly quizzes

dr s cares, but the class needs to be restructured. the group worksheets are very confusing to do as we are not lectured on the material beforehand, and the summary lectures he posts afterwards are also very vague. with only one quiz drop, you have to to do amazing on basically all the quizzes (bc of the weird grading scale).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Thought this class would be easier than the other professor but I was wrong. Throughout this semester is was extremely hard dealing with COVID and this new way of teaching which just made things even more challenging. Having a quiz a week and relying on your group makes things a bit complicated as well. There was office hours for TAs but no profess

Thought weekly quizzes instead of exams would make the class easier, but it was only worse. I felt unprepared for every single quiz because he doesn't teach! You learn from your peers in a group of 3-4 doing worksheets but you never receive the answer for these so you can't even be sure you're doing it right. take another prof if u can..
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rather than live synchronous lectures, you work on the class activities with a group of other students. Depending on the kind of learner you are, this could be a good or bad thing. Rather than tests, we had quizzes every week. This made it less stressful since I could not let weeks worth of material pile up that I would have to study all at once

Although he is involved and overall a very nice professor, the grading system Straumanis uses (essentially all or nothing problems, timed on gradescope) is very stressful and the quizzes are significantly harder than the homework. He also does not really lecture, but instead has you work in groups. Great guy, hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis is a kind person and I can tell he loves his job! However, his class was really challenging during COVID-19. If you fall behind then it's really hard to catch up. The way the class was set up made ochem 2 seem really abstract. Pick your group wisely- you're learning from a workbook & the people you surround urself with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Thought this was going to be better than Shabbir's stressful 7 exams, but it was worse. Felt unprepared every single week for the quizzes that were graded by all or nothing. He doesn't provide lectures but instead workbook questions to learn from. But, often times he doesn't even provide all of the answers for them, "you guys can figure it out."

Dr. Straumanis places an emphasis on understanding not memorization and flipped classroom. It is not a flipped class. You do groupwork with 2-3 peers and then he uploads the answers the next day in a summary video. There is no lecture or content taught so be ready to teach yourself everything. He is a caring professor but ochem is hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a flipped class so there aren't really lectures. He is caring and passionate about the subject but he doesn't really teach. You mainly have to rely on yourself to learn the material. The grading system is wack and there is not enough time for the quizzes.

He is a kind professor and cares about you actually learning the material. We had weekly quizzes. it was a bit stressful doing them every week but it was nice the material was only a small amount each week. The workbook and practice problems he gives is helpful for the quizzes as well as the; the quizzes are HARD bc they connect soo many concepts

Straumanis is a caring professor, but he doesn't do much teaching. You will end up teaching yourself most of this material which is his goal. If you give the class the time it deserves then you will pass, but if you were bad at OCHEM 1, you are in for a brutal semester. This class will require a lot of work!

Dr. Straumanis's class is very different from your typical lecture-based class. He emphasizes self-learning and learning from your peers, so you won't be directly lectured very much. Overall, he tries to make this tough course less stressful for the students by changing the grading scheme and listening to our feedback, and he can be understanding!

This class is entirely self-teach, so prepare to add professor to your resume! His grading scheme is odd and he hasnt given us many additional opportunities to succeed during this pandemic. Overall i made it through barely, but i wouldnt take your chances if you have other options

with the scope of the pandemic, what constitutes 'normal' is difficult. If you are going to take this class read up on POGIL first - its what you will be doing. You are going to work hard and you are going to understand Ochem or you will not get the grade you want. The Prof is the most caring and understanding I have ever had. But its still Ochem

This class was definitely different than what I'm used to as lecture time is time to work in groups instead of hearing him teach. The time outside of class is used to complete HW and study for quizzes every week. The class structure makes it hard for me to learn ochem, so I wish I could've looked over ochem I notes again to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class. Prof really cares that everyone does well and he is very adamant about his teaching philosophy. Very difficult if you don't participate in in-class activities. Make sure you find a solid group because it is a flipped classroom.

Unlike most chemistry classes the class has a heavy emphasis on group work as you work on worksheets with group members. Though the worksheets are helpful it is extremely self-taught with some guidance from the professor/TA's. However, the professor really cares about the students actually learning instead of just memorizing. He's a pretty nice guy

This was Dr. Straumanis' first year teaching Ochem 2 at UT Austin. This class is a flipped classroom which means the majority of the learning is done with your groupmates. Weekly quizzes that can be challenging, especially question 3 on the quizzes. I would say that this is a better option than other ochem prof but be prepared to work hard.

This class is a lot to adjust to because of the P/NY grading, but usually this will work for one's benefit so it is not something to be afraid of. This course is very difficult simply because of the course material, but the POGIL's help guide you through it. Straumanis really appreciates feedback and values fairness.

Real quick: Straumanis truly cares about you. Don't listen to the people who say otherwise. Lectures: Class isn't traditional. You get a textbook with problems and your group works through them. That's how you learn. Get a good group. To study: watch summary lectures, do POGIL workbook exercises, do textbook problems. Work for an A, but not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He thinks he leads a flipped classroom - it's not that. Be prepared to rely entirely on your prior knowledge because you are teaching yourself with the help of 1-2 course mates. No office hours because it felt like a "summary session" of what was taught. He's a sensational speaker so it's easy to get caught in his "kind" words. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His classes are pretty fun if you have the right group. Thankfully I was able to form a group where everyone is open to asking questions and not judging for the mistakes. I think zoom enhanced this experience because I was able to share my screen and hold a steady pace throughout the exercises. However, his tests are hard and tricky.

The majority of the class is contingent on self-teaching and self-learning through workbooks and watching summary lectures which goes over the workbook answers. Any actual material learned will be through textbook readings. If taking this course, I recommend consistently asking questions to clarify the material and ensure you are on the right track
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: summary lectures that he posts are helpful. Doing all the practice problems will prepare you for the weekly quizzes.

The professor himself was very caring and tried his best to help students. His lectures and assignments were very beneficial in helping to understand the content. However, few assignments were graded, those assignments had few questions and they were graded harshly. I feel that the grading system was very unfair, with little room for leniency.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was my first class I have taken where it was a flipped classroom. You have weekly quizzes that are worth 5% and the difficulty is fair to where you can do well if you have studied. The final will be difficult because it is cumulative and never during the semester will the professor go back and review the previous weeks material.

Dr. Straumanis is caring, passionate, and his teaching style is unique. It's group focused with supplemental review lectures which forces you to wrap your head around concepts rather than memorize. He also tries to accommodate his students as best as he can. I wish that I had been told to review my ochem 1 material more often.

Straumanis' teaching style forces students to actively learn by discovering ochem concepts through a guided workbook during lectures. Students work in groups and can ask TAs for help. It helps me remember things and have confidence in my abilities. Also, weekly quizzes help one keep up with the material and are less stressful than a few exams.

Dr. Straumanis' teaching style forces students to learn actively. He makes students discover ochem concepts on their own through a guided workbook in lectures. Additionally, students learn collaboratively in groups and always have access to TAs and LAs for help when they get stuck. This type of active learning is the best for recall for assessments

Class only consists of quizzes every week and final exam. He does not lecture at all and expects students to learn the course entirely on their own with the help of other students who also have no knowledge of the new material. Quizzes are graded based on an all or nothing scale which discourages lots of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class involves a lot of self learning. It's a flipped classroom with weekly quizzes instead of tests. The quizzes can be hard so it requires a lot of work to do well.

Dr. S takes a new and unique approach not typically seen in college courses. His POGIL method requires us to teach ourselves the material before he posts mini recap videos. This course is tough, but Dr. S cares about his students and constantly makes modifications based on student's feedback. Nevertheless, Ochem is tough, you can't change that.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's the fastest and most engaging 1.5 hours of my day. The groups you form a few weeks in are important and determine your success in this class. As a professor, he is incredibly open to feedback and changes the syllabus based on responses. He tries to make the class low stress with weekly quizzes. But - it is OChem II, you have to work for it.

Straumanis is a great professor who really cares about his students. The thing that makes his class different than most at UT is he runs a flipped classroom. Definitely, something to get used to but I really like this teaching style. He also does weekly quizzes allowing for the material to be learned gradually. Not an easy A, but it's attainable.

He is very caring and truly wants the best for his students. The class is designed for group work so be prepared to try and work through problems as a team. The class is only graded based on weekly quizzes and a final exam so it does not seem so stressful. But the quizzes are hard and require you to really know the material from class.

Professor Straumanis is very proactive in listening to student feedback and understanding the difficulties we may be going through! Groupwork heavy, but accessing the professor and TA's is always possible. Weekly quizzes based off previous week's content. Put in work to understand, but can be pretty difficult if multiple mistakes are made!

Professor Straumanis cares about his students and that's obvious to the students who take the class. The difficulty in the class comes from his teaching method and unique style of grading. While the grading system can be rewarding at times, it can also be very punishing. He also likes groupwork, so if that isn't your thing, don't take him.

This class is heavily focused on group work and I would definitely recommend taking another professor if you do not learn through group work. Also, the quizzes and final exam are the only grades in this class which makes it very stressful. I wish there was more quiz like practice problems and accommodation during the pandemic.

This class is very heavy on group work, so I found the structure of the class quite difficult. Make sure to watch the summary lectures. Having weekly quizzes was extremely stressful and quiz grades make up a large portion of our grade, and the grading system for the quizzes is confusing. No HW to practice material.

He is just not a great professor. He is very unclear with what he wants and the grading is awful. His style of teaching either works for you or it doesn't. No in between. I had to rely heavily on outside sources and just teach myself. Please take someone else for ochem 2. I'm drowning, and this is coming from someone who did very well in ochem 1.

You can tell this professor cares about his students, but he is just not a good professor. He tries to listen to feedback, but there are still major flaws in this course. As a student taking him while he was fairly new, it seems like we were used as guinea pigs. The grading is awful, and the quizzes are very iffy. Please pick someone else!! ://

I know the Dr. Straumanis cares about students; however, I think that the grading system needs to be fixed. I do not feel motivated to succeed when I get 100 on a quiz then a 0 on one next week. Advice for the start of the semester: find outside resources because the workbook and exercises are not sufficient learning resources. Short quiz times too

Really nice guy, but the "learn the material by yourselves in your group" style of teaching is terrible... especially if you have a bad group. This is pretty much a self-taught class, but with the terrible grading system, you never know what you're going to get on a quiz. Speaking of which, there's a quiz every week.

This class was honestly the hardest class I've taken in my whole college career thus far. Although Straumanis is a nice professor, his kindness does not help us understand concepts. First, we have to pay for answers to his problems and for the in-class work we never really got solid answers, so we never really knew if we did something right.

This class is heavy on group work, which I didn't enjoy but I've gotten by with the recordings that he posts on Canvas (lectures/summary lectures(!!!)). Overall, this is a difficult class, it does get stressful, and you do need to put a lot of work in but Dr. Straumanis is caring and is really good at explaining the material.

Having to learn the material yourself wouldn't be too bad if it weren't for how the class was graded. I found myself getting a 100 one week and then a 0 the next. Having a 0 for a grade worth 5% of my final grade in the class does not make me very motivated to learn organic chemistry. Despite this, I know he truly does care about his students.

Lectures are minimal, you'll have to teach yourself mainly. Groupwork is nice, and weekly quizzes instead of exams is nice, but grading criteria is unclear and feels arbitrary. You could get a 4.5/5 one week and a 1.5/5 the next, even if you feel confident. Main grades come from quizzes and final exam (heavy weight), need to do well from the start.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is a caring professor and if you have the time/flexibility the flipped classroom (teach yourself) wouldn't be bad, but I had work almost everyday and they were not flexible on attendance. Also he does all or nothing grading. The course has been okay, but I prefer traditional style lecture and exams.

Straumanis class has been very stressful this semester and the grading system is difficult. The quizzes are hit or miss. The questions can be very lengthy and 30 mins to complete the quiz is not enough time. There isnt much hw but you do need to do the work outside of class if you want to make a good grade. He does want the best for his students.

I switched into Straumanis after taking Ochem 1 with Iverson and not wanting to take Shabbir for Ochem 2. The weekly quizzes seem doable but due to his horrible grading policy, you can go from 100 to a 0 within one week. The quizzes have a very strict time limit, and often times you won't finish them. Flipped classroom so you're teaching yourself.

Organic Chem is a hard subject, and there is no "easy" class to take for it. Straumanis offers a different approach to ochem with a method called POGIL (or POG-ILL) that puts the learning in your hands. Is all the material there? Yes. Is it decently organized? Sure. Is having a weekly quizzes with minimal instructor guidance relaxing? Not really.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis cares about his students but the structure of his class was extremely difficult. Super light on lectures which ends up meaning you are teaching yourself most of the material (super difficult with ochem). Felt lost for most of the semester and like there was not a clear flow of the course. Heavy on group work as well.

Professor Straumanis seems to really care about his students. He actually listens to feedback about the course and makes corrections/adjustments if needed. The set-up was a little weird to get used to, but working in groups and going through the workbook problems together really helps you get a better understanding of the material

This is a flipped classroom. It can be a difficult adjustment for students who are used to lectures, but it really is the best way to learn OChem because you are forced to put in the work. I learn best by teaching others, so before class I would do the course packet and read the Iverson textbook, and during class, I would teach my groupmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Pros: Listens to feedback and clearly cares about students Nice Professor Good lecturer and no such thing as a "bad question" Cons: Quizzes every week (high grade percentage) Does not lecture, uses group work to teach students Required books and answer manual to buy Less about Ochem, more about pre-med route
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Andrei seems to be a nice guy,but he does peptalk a lot insteadof giving more advantages on grades. The posted lecture is quite simple, but you are expect to know a lot deeper for the #3 on the quizzes, which means you must find resources online and go to officehour to get better grades. Overall, difficult to get A, but easy to get B grade.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about students, especially in preparing students for a career after a bachelor's degree. He teaches us not only in Ochem, but how to learn. The course is test-heavy, but no homework. I think self-discipline is the key to success in this course, especially when there are only minimum lectures provided.

This class is incredibly difficult. Requires a lot of work to understand the material, but there are no homework grades so everything comes down to the quizzes which are graded with a system that honestly doesn't make much sense.

Straumanis seems to always advocate for mental health but never seems to do anything to support it, especially during a pandemic, so he is just all talk. Although he is a nice person, his ideals are all over the place. The quizzes are difficult bc of the grading and the little amount of time given, which includes uploading process for some reason.

Teaches in a flipped classroom style (taught in groups) which (IMO) is not the best teaching style for OChem since it can be confusing. Short time limit for quizzes (30 min for 3 questions; they're not easy trust me lol ), not to mention that the quizzes are weekly. He seems like a nice man though but doesn't seem to understand his students.

He does not do lectures, he made us work in groups to solve problems and then gave us a small recorded summery. Our grades are heavily based on weekly quizzes and a final, I think they might change this for future classes. Asking peers and TAs for help is a great way to understand his class. Class was mandatory for only 11 days and thats all.

This won't be the hardest thing you've ever done, but it definitely won't be the easiest. This is a flipped classroom, so that means a majority of the material is learned on your own/with your group. If you aren't into the group work, don't waste your time, and just study by yourself. Quizzes every week, however, you can get up to a 108 on them.

Make sure you have a very clear understanding of Organic 1 material, especially for synthesis. Great when learning new material, but must have a good foundation as the course goes on. Be ready to teach yourself certain portions, and be ready to purchase workbooks and keys.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The flipped classroom makes you depend on your group, so make sure you find people that are eager to learn as well. Ochem 2 is difficult so be prepared to work, but I think Straumanis made it more enjoyable and engaging than any other ochem 2 class I would've taken.

When signing up for this class, expect to teach yourself, as Dr. Straumanis provides minimal assistance. To make matters worse he has weekly quizzes and imposes a time frame of thirty minutes. The class is very fast paced and the quizzes are difficult to complete in the given time.

Do not take this class. This man claims to care about the mental health and success of his students but the amount of times I've hysterically cried about this class is not reflective of that. Quizzes are graded extremely harshly and you are expected to do an unreal amount of work in under 30 min. I got an A in Ochem I. Horrible prof, awful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis is a great professor! His class is hard, but all organic chemistry classes will be challenging. I really appreciated that he actually cared about his students and was accommodating. His class is difficult but come to class prepared to ask questions and you will do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor i've ever had. flipped classroom so it's only a good class if you have a good group. he is so dope, explains things extremely well, cares about his students, and emphasizes the importance of mental health. he's a chiller and i would take him again. o chem 2 is hard tho so you have to work for your grade.

flipped classroom which (imo) is not the best teaching style for ochem since it can get quite confusing. very short time limit for quizzes (which often have BOTH mechanisms and synthesis problems), not to mention that the quizzes are weekly. really nice person though but doesn't seem to understand his students...

Dr. Straumanis is the most encouraging professor I have had. He takes feedback from students and applies it. It is nice having weekly quizzes because it puts less pressure on you but the grading system is usually more hurtful than helpful. Overall, Ochem is a really tough subject so be prepared to put a lot of time into it to get a good grade.

This course is a flipped classroom, so you pretty much have to teach yourself everything. It's a lot of group work, which I don't exactly care for. Professor Straumanis claims he cares for his students, but we make complaints and he does not exactly take them in until it is too late. The grading system sucked. He's nice tho. Textbook is necessary.

There are weekly quizzes, which may seem like a good thing initially, but the material is hyperspecific and the grading is so tough. They do something called P/NY. NY means no points for a question. It is so disheartening to get no credit when you've studied for hours and have gotten part of the question right. POGIL sucks. Take another professor.

Dr. Straumanis might be the best prof I've ever had. He has a great way of explaining things and is always looking for places he can improve himself and his course. He cares a lot about how people are doing in the course, but what sets him apart from others is how he goes out of his way to help you do better. O Chem II is super hard though.

Attendance was only mandatory for like the first 10 classes and then it was optional. If you want to succeed, you need to stay on top of the material since there are weekly quizzes instead of exams. You have to kinda teach yourself while going through his workbook activities, but ASK QUESTIONS if you don't understand and you'll learn a lot.

Class consisted of a brief intro to the material and then the rest of the time was spent with small groups. If you find a solid group, you'll learn better. The weekly quiz structure helped me stay on top of the material each week instead of cramming everything the night before an exam. But if you're a lecture learner, maybe don't take him.

This is a flipped classroom. You are expected to learn everything on your own. 30 minute weekly quizzes are the only thing determining your grade and they are very confusing. I do not recommend taking this class, but for pre-meds it is a must.

Dr. Straumanis is a really nice guy, but I personally don't really care for his teaching style. If you like flipped classrooms, you'll like this class. Otherwise, you should maybe consider a different professor. If you end up in this class, just make sure you have a strong grasp of OChem 1 before you start.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was great. We had weekly quizzes instead of multiple midterms and the grading criteria was very fair. I hope that before the course started I would have known how much textbook would be necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's been a bumpy road but I appreciate the dedication and sincerity of the professor and his assistants have always trying to make it better and helping. It made OChem 2 much more tolerable, esp compared to 1, as did ending up with the right group. You have to work for it though, but everything is short and direct (including quizzes) which helps.
Great professors. Glad we had weekly quizzes instead of multiple midterms. Very nice and timely when it comes to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So I really like this professor's personality- he's incredibly caring, sends really thoughtful emails, is very positive, and he's big on how to actually learn. But this subject isn't easy, and a solely free response quiz every week in the midst of a pandemic was really hard for me and others. I did like that it kept me on track with learning.

P Straumanis attempts to accommodate students and be receptive of feedback, but is bound by department. O-Chem is hard. Doesn't lecture much, and emphasizes self-exploration of topics and group work. Quizzes felt unfair as questions did not reflect activities done in workbook. Workload is not heavy, but recommend studying every night to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis himself is an amazing person, but do yourself a favor and take another ochem 2 professor. Around 65% of your grade is based on the weekly quizzes. At the time it seemed like a very good option, but the quizzes are HARD. I haven't learned anything. Uses something called the POGIL method to teach and it didnt work for me

I personally learn better from lectures so it has been difficult to self-teach especially since it's online. You have to buy the activity book, solution manual AND textbook which were really expensive. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you know you can hold yourself accountable and you can learn without in-depth lectures.

OChem 2 is just an awful class in general, regardless of the professor. Attendance is only mandatory for the first 10 lectures, and in each lecture you work with other students to teach yourselves the material. There are only 30 minute, 3 question weekly quizzes, except for the final. He is really accomodating and grades very fairly.

This professor does not lecture, it is all group work. There are quizzes each week and the questions do not mirror the questions from the workbook. The questions from the workbook are pointless & are easy compared to the quizzes. My best advice is to have a good group that comes to class, review the main takeaways from each activity & study a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class seemed like a waste as I personally did not learn anything as a whole. You will teach yourself most of the material, or will learn from the TAs/LIs. He did not do much to teach the material or give some sort of background in order to understand the topics. The weekly quizzes were a hit or miss with either failing or passing.

On paper, his class seems like it would be easy A with little work due to quizzes being the sole grades in the class. In reality, this class is harder than it seems and you will be teaching yourself all of the material. He expects you to know all the material before so that you can work with groups, if you don't know it, you will be behind and fail
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you struggled with lecture teaching styles in ochem I, this might be a lot better for you. The workbook made things a lot easier to understand because it guides you to understanding the concepts through practice and application. Because of this class, I realized I'm not bad at ochem, I'm just bad at learning ochem from lectures.

Straumanis wants you to learn how to succeed on your own and challenges you to think differently. He does not give the answers to in class questions or homework and only summarizes it in a short lecture. Class time is spent figuring out problems with your group. We had a quiz every week which consisted of 3 questions that were pretty difficult.

You are paying tuition to teach yourself in groups in this class. He is accommodating but this course structure is dependent on the group you get assigned. Quizzes are 65% of the grade. Also told us to rate here instead of ecis because that affects his pay. Be prepared to become more familiar with YouTube than you will be with his face.

Going into this class, I did not know what to expect. It seems very difficult to do well in this class because his grading system makes it very hard to get close to a perfect score on the weekly quizzes. This class seems better suited for independent learners since most of the learning is done in groups. His lectures are not as informative.

Save yourself this class is unbearable and he clearly doesn't care about his students doing well - his grading system is flawed and yet he refuses to acknowledge it. He chooses to listen to the 10 people in the class that likes his miserable class over the overwhelming majority that are not doing well. And I did well in OCHEM 1...

The online course is structured in a manner where you go to class and he lectures for the the first 15 minutes and then the rest of the time you go to breakout rooms to work on problems with your group. He lets you pick your groups, so CHOSE WISELY. Having a good group that shows up and participates is CRUCIAL to succeeding in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was terrible. Straumanis acts like he cares about the wellbeing of his students but truly does nothing to help them. There are no real lectures, only summaries and he often skips over questions. He spends more time trying to convince you the class doesn't suck than he does actually teaching. Don't waste your time in this class.

If you think you should take this class, dont. Only a true sadist would want the class with the most confusing grading of all time. You learn absolutely nothing and get a bad grade. So please i beg you pick another professor.

So many salty people are review bombing this poor dude, and there's a literal war happening on this page. You HAVE to work for your grade. It's ochem 2, not some blowoff. His two 30 min summary lectures per week are so much more digestible than Shabbir's 1.5 hours of hell, 3 times a week. Put in the work, and you'll get rewarded for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall the class is group focuses, not many lectures where you learn directly from the teacher, and weekly quizzes where there is never enough time.

I am thoroughly confused by the set-up of this class. What did i learn, trust me i could not tell you. The class is set-up so you have to teach yourself OCHEM, which obviously undergraduates cannot do. I do not wish this class on my worst enemy. If someone got a good grade in this class they must have cheated to the max.

Dr. Straumanis is a great professor who really cares about his students. Class grade is based on the weekly quizzes, attendance, completing two surveys, and the final exam. The grading system is confusing at times, but Dr. Straumanis always tries to make it as fair as possible.

Class is very self-taught, but it makes upper division courses, like Biochem, way easier. Straumanis's class makes you work for a deeper understanding of the content. Ochem 2 is difficult. No class, whether his or Shabbir's is easy. I struggled with Shabbir in ochem 1, but found success here, and really bettered my learning approach thanks to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Be prepared to be actively engaged in class. You're essentially teaching yourself with a guided thinking textbook written by Straum. Takes a little while to adjust to the teaching approach, but Straum teaches you how to truly understand chemical processes in a way that you can't memorize and therefore wont forget. Take this class esp for MCAT
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Calling him Professor Straumanis would be overqualifying his ability to lecture - more suitable title would be Guru Straumanis as he deems this course the best opportunity to teach us life lessons rather than actual material for this course. Brace yourself to find a study group and learn ochem II on your own because "teach" isn't in his vocabulary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One thing that I wish I knew before I took his class was that I SHOULD NOT HAVE TAKEN THIS CLASS AND SHOULD HAVE STUCK WITH SHABBIR. Please save yourself the tears and take Shabbir.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about your mental health and stress level as a student which I feel that a lot of STEM professors don't really address, so I am thankful for that. That being said, Ochem 2 is still a difficult subject, and to do well on the quizzes you have to study A LOT. The group work thing didn't really work for me though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is mostly group work with short lectures and weekly quizzes. I haven't take the final yet, but the quizzes are usually manageable, and they have some bonus points built into them. I thought group work would be terrible, but it's not bad. I don't know if I prefer group work, but this class is definitely easier than my ochem I class was.
Please save yourself a lot of stress and do not take this prof for Ochem 2. Just take Shabbir. The weekly quizzes are really stressful and he barely cares about his students.

I HATE THIS GUY!! Please take anyone but him. All the 4s and 5s are fake ratings and this man is a really bad prof. He does not teach, does not care about his students, and don't even get me started about how unfair the weekly quizzes are.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Started out difficult for me, but I got used to it & I like the P/NY grading system now. That said, grades depend on if you have a good group bc Prof doesn't do anything (no lectures, no office hours). Quizzes have been doable so far, but I'm most worried about the final, but I had to post this rating now bc it's for a grade.

Dr. Straumanis is a very cool guy who cares about his students. His class is structured in an unusual way because of weekly quizzes that make up most of your grade along with the final exam. Many people found that he didn't do much to teach, however, the guided inquiry textbook is thorough and allows you to learn a great deal. I really enjoyed it!

This was Dr. Straumanis' first semester at UT teaching OCHEM II so most of us had no idea what to expect. His class is structured in a peculiar way. There are quizzes weekly (really not bad) that make up most of your grade and a final exam. I loved the group learning, grading scheme, and professor. A very doable and rewarding experience!!

You literally teach yourself everything. He took flipped classroom to the next level. Was not very accommodating at all considering the pandemic. Tells you he's preparing you for the "real world" by having you teach yourself. The whole point of teaching is to actually TEACH

One I asked him a question during class because I was confused. The answer I received was "I think you are confused about something deeper, I am going to go help other students that need me." Instead of answering my questions he just left. He has no office hours, you are teaching yourself. Absolutely don't take his class if you want to learn.

Genuinely the hardest class I have had to take in university, and the professor did not help with this. Encourages people to teach themselves but this does not work for everyone and it definitely did not work for me. He assigns assignments that are not mandatory but definitely help, or at least they would if he gave you the answers. Weekly quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Must participate in group work to get anything out of it and learn. Must study a lot and must complete activities and homework or you will not learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis has a caring personality and really wants his students to succeed. However, that doesn't mean that the students get freebies. You have to work hard with your peers to fully understand the material to ace the quizzes. I believe that his class will only get better every year as he does utilize student feedback.

Andrei is a super kind and caring guy, but being a new professor at UT he definitely is still getting trying out new things. Quizzes were very difficult but he said that next semester they won't make up as much of the grade as they do. now. He puts a lot of emphasis on group work and his workbook. It's hard to check your work bc no key.

Straumanis has a very non-traditional course setup. His class essentially is entirely self-taught among a small group of peers. You only have quiz grades and the final, so you have no chance to mess up on something that doesn't greatly affect your grade. Errors have been brought to his attention, and he almost always ignores it. Don't recommend.
quizzes every week but no midterms and listens to your feedback very well ( we said on a survey we wanted more extra credit opportunities and he just gave 8 points extra credit)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was a great professor, does reverse teaching style . Truly cares about his students and preparing them for the outside world.

This course has weekly quizzes that are in the form of pass/not yet with a cumulative final. There are 2 summary lectures per week to watch but you mainly work with groups of your choosing during class. It can be quite difficult to find a good group through an online format. There is constant studying and a lot of hard work required.

To be fair, the class structure seems very attractive on paper, but when implemented, there were many problems of unfairness with it. In order to do well, you must study and work hard on your own time. It's a very new type of learning that works for some people and does not work for others. The quizzes are only hard because of the little time given

Dr. Straumanis cares for his students. I understand the concept of the flipped classroom; however, it's not for me. There is not much lecture to watch outside of class so much of the learning is self-taught. You sometimes don't get the correct answers from him. The quizzes can be hit or miss especially time which I wish someone had told me before.

You WILL be teaching yourself; there are no/few lectures. If you want a professor who will actually teach you organic chemistry, then do not take this class. Your grade is based on difficult weekly quizzes which have a 30 minute time limit including upload time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaches by a 10 min recap and then we go into breakout rooms with groups and learn the material with an interactive textbook. Only short answer quizzes once a week and a final. You have to put in a lot of work for this class, but this is the first class I have ever really understood chemistry. He also always wants to know how to improve his class!

There is a big jump between his in class work and the quizzes he assigned; however the homework exercises are very good and accurate, make sure to do those. Doesn't Lecture much, very group work based. Cares about his students ALOT. If a large portion of students complain about something he will likely change it.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about his students learning organic chemistry and critical thinking skills, not memorizing information. He is patient in explaining concepts, but classes are just small groups answering workbook questions. Grade only comes from extremely difficult weekly quizzes with a ridiculously short time limit.

Ochem is a tough class to take with any professor but taking it with Dr. Straumanis really lets you learn it. I know it may seem like you're "teaching yourself" but if you keep up with the material and find a good study group, ochem 2 will seem easier than ochem 1. Seriously so great! And offers some extra credit.

Only lectures for  10-min at the start of class and a quick recorded summary lecture later on. Admitted his P/NY system was flawed but did not change the grading. The quizzes are hard and wordy at times. I have not truly learned ochem but instead have spent lots of time crying and confused.

I liked Dr. Straumanis, and he is really nice as a person, but the quizzes each week were pretty difficult. He does not really lecture and learning is all based on group work and his POGIL textbook. If you like group work then take him. He is definitely easier than other ochem professors, but not sure how much I am retaining. Good luck w/ochem!

Class is pretty reliant on group collaboration which can be a good thing with the right people or if you enjoy group work. Weekly quizzes keep you on your toes with the material & often feel like a hit or miss based on the grading format. The professor is open to hearing students out & cares about feedback to be flexible with their needs.

Professor doesn't teach during class. It's dedicated to self-teaching and group work. If you don't have a great group or struggle through the concepts on your own, his after-class videos help. However, the only other examples to work through for extra practice are few textbook problems he assigns. quizzes are short but not enough time given.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis really cares about his students and really wants you to know your chemistry. Class is group work based so finding a good group in your first classes is key. The workbook explains the chemistry but quizzes are hard. Be prepared to study a lot outside of class. Would take again just because I wouldn't choose to take the other professor

I like his personality. That's it. I like the setup of the class, but the implementation is very misleading. Quizzes are a hit or miss, mostly a miss. You can go in as confident as you want and still fail. He listens but maybe ignores root problems. Literally, we need more time for the quiz. It may be 3 questions, but trust they require TIME.

This class had promise but was ruined by quiz questions. I honestly don't think the material is hard, the way we learn it at least. But the type of questions that he puts on the 3 question quiz (2.5pt/1.5pt/0.5 pt/ 0.5pt if perfect) makes it nearly impossible to pass (for me). He will include ochem 1 concepts without telling us. He's nice at least.

As a good independent learner, I thought that groupwork/practice problems in place of a 1.5 hour lecture would be beneficial for me. The reality is not so ideal. Weekly quizzes out of 5 points, no other grades, only one drop, and harsh grading with no partial credit. Wouldn't recommend if you have any gaps in your ochem knowledge at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He really cares about students and tries to motivate you. His class is different to the traditional classes , which you need to work with your own group most of the time. You need to find your group well to succeed in this course. Just spend lots of time and you'll get an A.

He gives no partial credit on quizzes. In fact, he admitted to the grading system being unfair yet he did nothing to correct it. His textbook also seems to have errors and doesn't prepare you for the quizzes which are definitely harder. Yes, he does stress mental health and he is willing to hear us out, but he is truly all talk and no action.

If I had the chance to take a different professor, I would still stick to Straumanis. It was a big change from copying prerecorded lectures and regurgitating it on the exam, but it is worth the extra time. I would say that this course places a lot more emphasize on you taking charge of your learning. The prof is caring and the TAs are great.

Dr. Straumanis seems like a really good guy who knows what they're doing, but he doesn't teach. He expects you to come to class knowing the material so that you're able to work through the activities with your group. This class is self-taught and the quizzes can be hard.

It depends on your learning style on how well you do in this class. You work in a group every class and there are no lectures. Very self taught. The weekly quizzes vary; some being extremely difficult, some being easy. The hard quizzes will drag you down and you only get one drop. Straumanis loves feedback though and really listens to students.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about using the best methods possible to make students learn. but this includes a lot of cooperative work so it is important that you choose to work with students who care about the course just as much as you do.

I enjoyed the course but his grading can either make you or break you. He does P/NY grading which mean that there is no partial credit. He does weekly quizzes but they are not easy and are wordy so be careful. He does give points if you make minor mistakes, but for the most part this grading is very risky and you can easily fail his class.

Honestly if you are an independent learner, take the class. You just need to teach yourself to succeed if I'm honest. One tip before class is to have mastered ochem 1 completely because this class builds off of what you are expected to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis has the class set up to where you teach each other and yourself. The class can be very frustrating at times because it's hard to figure it out without lectures. However, it's not too stressful as long as you do the activities you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was honestly the most ridiculous thing I have ever done. He does not lecture and you are tasked with the mission of learning organic chemistry on your own. If you are anything else but a college student with an unreasonable amount of time to dedicate towards Ochem weekly, you will not succeed in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class expects you to do a lot of self studying and group work and there are barely any lectures to learn the material. The grading is very tough because he does an all or nothing grading scale on the quizzes. There's a quiz every week and a final - no homework. Tbh this class makes Ochem harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: O-Chem is not a concept that is easily understood and mastered if you're having to teach yourself everything, which basically the whole course. The quizzes are also hard to complete due to the time constraint and the lack of materials preparing and aligning with what is assessed. The workbook problems are rudimentary and do not mirror the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Straumanis approach to organic chemistry is definitely not your stereotypical college course. There is a lot of self teaching, and a lot of group work. There are only about 30 minutes of lecture a week compared to a typical 3 hours and most of class is spent working on groups. Quizzes are fair but what you learn is dependent on your group

I'm sure things would have gone much better in person. Professor Straumanis is very accommodating; however, I personally did not fare well with this flipped class as it was mainly self-taught with weekly meltdowns, so find a good group, wish the lessons are longer than 15 minutes, and review all material provided before the quizzes.

Straumanis emphasizes mental health but does not care. Makes the class unnecessarily difficult and only wants to help students that are already performing well. Please avoid taking his class if you want to actually learn Ochem 2. Quizzes are unreasonable with the time limit and difficulty.
The weekly quizzes were hard especially since the class was mainly based off of activities done with a group, not lectures.

Weekly quizzes, which are quite tricky. I wish he gave us more practice that are similar to the quizzes. He is a caring professor however the way he teaches is by breaking up students into breakout rooms and letting them figure the activity.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a really nice professor. However, our class is broken up into breakout room and we do the activity/teaching ourselves. I wish he would teach us everything then break us up and give us practice problems that are similar to the way the quiz is formatted. Sometimes I feel like the exercises are irrelevant. The quizzes are kinda hard.

Dr. Straumanis genuinely seems to care for his students and this class; however, his entire POGIL method for teaching at least to me proved to be ineffective. You would always break out into groups; however, many instances nobody knew what to do. His quizzes are killers as you either have to be perfect to get a good grade or you bomb that quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His teaching style relies heavily on students working in groups to learn. Therefore, his lectures are often light and cover general points. I'm not a fan of his P/F grading system, something he's stated to move away from, but his quizzes are manageable if you have an active group to learn the content with. I think he's a solid choice overall.

I feel like i've learned as much in this class as the traditional lecture-based class I took for Organic chemistry last year, but with only half the stress. Even though he's one of those professors who makes you buy a workbook he wrote, it is indeed a very good workbook.

He is a really good professor in terms of caring for mental health and understanding it is hard for everyone. His weekly quizzes are actually not that bad and I'm not so stressed out because there isn't much on each. I do think it is a lot of self learn though so be ready for that and make sure that you check over your work.

If you like his class format, you'll like the class overall. The lecturing is substituted by a (pretty good) workbook, which you work on in groups during class. There is a weekly quiz, and then a final, but no scheduled tests or midterms. This format is not for everyone; many people have complained or dropped the course. However, I enjoyed it.

Straumanis has an odd grading scheme, and leaves teaching up to the guided worksheets that you are assigned every class. He is also a professor that will change the structure of the course based on what his students say. That is commendable and his attitude speaks volumes on his care for his students.

One thing you must understand is that lectures aren't really lectures. The course is based on the workbook. During each lecture you will be asked to get into your groups and work on the chapter assigned. He has recordings of him doing the chapter but that's about it. Also, there are no midterms just a final and weekly quizzes.

This class is a lot of independent learning. You learn in groups by doing workbook activities that guide you through the concepts. He posts summary lectures for you to check your understanding after class. Weekly quizzes make up the bulk of your grade. Overall, he really cares about the students, but a lot of the learning is on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: You will have to study hard in this class to get an A. Finding a good study group is extremely helpful. Most of the time, you will be teaching yourself the material.

Dr. Straumanis uses the flipped classrooms model which requires team-based engagement in class. however, your success is dependent on finding an excellent group, so make sure to find one quickly. If you work in class and do the exercises, you will get an A. Especially since you can get up to a 108% on each quiz.

Straumanis doesn't really teach. We use his workbook that uses a guided learning approach to 'discover the topic'. He has weekly quizzes that are stressful due to time. He is receptive to feedback and was willing to change the grading scheme when we complained. His quizzes are still hard though.

Dr. Straumanis did a good job trying to accommodate the online environment. He lectures for 15 minutes, then has class break into groups of 4 to work through a guided worksheet. 3 question weekly quizzes are graded as pass/no pass. Big mistakes don't earn any points, but small mistakes take off 4%. One final exam at the end.

You will have to do the weekly quiz. The quiz could be extremely difficult to extremely easy depending on that unit. You have 30 minutes to complete the quiz. There were big 3 questions that can be differentiated by easy (2.5 pt), medium (1.5 pt), and hard (0.5 pt). Although there are big 3 questions, you should expect to do more than 3 questions.
Ochem is hard no doubt, so be prepared to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I love his innovative, engaging method of teaching. However, the quizzes killed me. After having mental health episodes due to isolation, I am falling apart during the pressure of these short, timed quizzes and they have a deteriorating effect with EVERY week. I feel like I don't have a chance to recover, and I ruined my college path.

Be prepared to work hard but also smart. The weekly quizzes make up the majority of your grade, so you will need to consistently be studying while managing your other classes. It can be difficult at the beginning, but you get used to the quizzes over time.

Awesome professor and person. Cares a lot about his students and just wants them to succeed. The idea of his teaching style is "self learning", and while I think that's a cool idea, I do not learn best like that. I wish it was one day a week of him lecturing and the other day was self learning. Wouldn't take again but it's fine for now.

Straumanis is a caring professor who actually listens to feedback from his students and has actively changed the grading scheme of his class a few times already this semester based off of feedback. There's weekly quizzes instead of exams which is nice to reduce your stress. Ive learned ochem much better this semester than I did last with a dif prof

Professor Straumanis is a kind and caring professor. You can tell he wants all of his students to succeed in organic chemistry. A lot of the learning will be done on your own time. The quizzes are challenging. Professor Straumanis does not give us enough time in my opinion. Overall I would suggest doing all the practice problems.

He genuinely wants students to realize the pleasures of Ochem. This semester was online so this may be seen as an obstacle, but it actually made LAs and the prof. himself more accessible during class time. He's someone you can comfortably ask for help. Ochem is a tough class, but he teaches you tools that allow you to breakdown harder problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class definitely makes you work for your grade, but thats any ochem 2 class. However, he doesn't lecture during class and it's solely the blind teaching the blind, and that's if you have a good group. I still don't fully understand the grading scale and they seem to get harder to take. I have learned a lot but i'm basically teaching myself.

Dr. Straumanis is a great professor! He cares about his students' success in more than just a classroom setting. At first, it's a little hard to accept the format of the class because it's different than many other classes. However, his emphasis on group learning definitely pays off! My advice would be don't go into close minded, try your best!!

Overall, a passionate, caring professor. His class is challenging and requires you to understand the material. Rather than focus on rote memorization, Straumanis' course requires critical thinking and true learning. It is a challenging course and requires work outside class.

Dr. Straumanis created a classroom & grading system that only works for people with AMPLE time to devote to o chem2. He realized how bad the P/NY grading system is & is changing it in the future. I wish I knew how much time and energy I would have to devote to teaching myself o chem 2 because then I wouldn't have taken this professor.

This class is frustrating based on the philosophy he has on how teaching should be accomplished. Sure, group work is a great way to practice, but he makes it the foundation of our learning experience. He just goes over some ppt. slides and throws us in the water with the sharks. Don't get it? Ask until you do! Just teach in the first place then.

Professor Straumanis has a different approach to teaching thats a lot more hands off and individual learning which works for some people. While its a cool idea, I dont particularly learn like that so i found the class difficult

Professor Straumanis has a different approach to teaching thats a lot more hands off and individual learning which works for some people. While its a cool idea, I dont particularly learn like that so i found the class difficult. But hes a really cool teacher

He seriously wants you to learn the material. He does. He has been extremely generous with the ability to earn points. O Chem 2 is just a hard class, and this is an effective way to teach for those who can learn on their own and use classrooms to ask questions or deepen their knowledge. Think of it like a flipped classroom.

The entire set-up of this course online made it tough to learn honestly. The prof doesn't really lecture or offer proper hw that can reinforce OCHEM concepts that we were learning. Students who were struggling continued to struggle through the semester and the grading is really brutal and inconsistent.

Dr Straumanis was a great professor. Instead of typical lectures, you work in groups through a chemistry book and work together to understand the topic. This course has helped me understand chemistry far better but does require some self-studying of reagents. Do the work and rally commit to group sessions and you will be A okay.

Quiz every week with 3 questions that kind of stress you out but are meant to be low stakes. He cares about his students' learning A LOT so go to class if you need someone to hold you accountable but its not necessary if you can do the work and understand it yourself. Wish someone told me ochem2 isn't as awful as you expect with the right structure

it took me about 6 weeks to start to appreciate the flipped classroom and weekly quizzes instead of tests. His P/NY grading system definitely has some pros, however it tends to do more harm than good and definitely makes quizzes more stressful than he was probably intending them to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've ever taken. Don't expect a professor. He's a researcher that's doing research on his students' learning. Everything depends on your group. He does summary lectures at the end, but they really don't help. Doesn't do exams, but quizzes with all or nothing grading which defeats the purpose of free response - partial credit

Flipped classroom structure with a lot of group work inside and outside of class, so def not for everyone. Weekly quizzes are fairly challenging, make up 65% of your grade, and are graded on a Pass/Not Yet system that allows students to get a fair # of points if they remember most of the material. Important to keep up with content every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I won't deny that I learned A LOT in this class with the fantastic group I worked in. The TAs/LAs in this class were decent and helped students, however, I feel like Dr. Straumanis himself could have done more for students. He should have at least held office hours himself and provided students with a few FREE resources for self-learning.

I am not a group learner, so I didn't entirely like the structure of his course. He makes room for people like this, by not making attendance mandatory after 10 days. Having a good group is probably helpful though. He changed grading structure after student feedback told him about it, so that was a plus.

Dr. Straumanis is one of the most considerate professors I have ever come across. However, the flipped classroom set up and heavy emphasis on group work was a little difficult for me. Find a good group and get on studying synthesis before you even take ochem 2. Oh, and have a good foundation from ochem 1 since ochem 2 is entirely built up on it.

This man is a really bad professor and a really selfish person who barely cares about his students. Shabbir's average is about 84.2 on the midterms and his average is about 80 and I am sure that his average will probably drop because the quizzes keep on getting harder and harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Straumanis is nice and understanding, but I didn't really like the flipped classroom structure. There's a weekly quiz and only one of them gets dropped, and there's a final exam at the end. The learning in this class is pretty group-dependent, so make sure you have a good group to work with for the questions in his workbook.

Flipped classroom with group work, and this class is practically self taught. The group work actually was helpful, but not much else was. Instead of exams, he gives weekly quizzes and does P/NY (all or nothing) grading that can really end up screwing you over. Was receptive of feedback to a certain extent, but Shabbir was 10000x better.

Of course any Ochem 2 class is going to be hard, and Professor Straumanis was a really kind and caring teacher who really wants the best for his class. One of the things I was not a fan of was his grading for the quizzes because he wouldn't give partial credit, so you could lose a lot of points for a small mistake. I also wish he gave extra credit
