reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class has weekly quizzes but the lectures and workbook are really helpful for them. There is also no homework, which is really nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I am not a group learner, but the professor made an effort to try to make us appreciate the approach. That said, I still didn't feel like it was for me and after 10 mandatory classes we were allowed to choose to not attend class. Professor was very receptive to feedback in class and modified grading structure to award rather than penalize.

Ochem 2 is challenging regardless of the prof. I had Shabbir last semester and really liked how many practice problems she provided and how structured her class was. Straumanis simply doesn't lecture, but makes you self-learn from rather expensive workbooks. The weekly quizzes are graded with partial credit. Really challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Course activities are group taught although he does post a 10-20 min summary lecture given at the beginning of class and a review of the activity worked on in class. A quiz is given every week, typically over two sections. Each quiz contained 3 questions each with multiple parts. Having a good group is key to passing unless you can teach yourself.

The setup was not for me. Your learning really depends on other people in your group. The class was practically asynchronous. No one holds each other accountable and you can be left by yourself to do everything. The quizzes were hard to even finish and upload. As a person coming from Shabbir, this was not it.

Find a good group to work with. It REALLY matters. Structured to be group work heavy (learning not grades). An effective group helps understanding and motivates you. Grading doesn't give partial credit - kind of all or nothing. They give room for minor mistakes and will still give full points (can backfire). Hard but at least he cares.

Of course, any ochem course is going to be difficult, but I found Dr. Straumanis's class to be a bit more manageable than previous ochem courses. The course is structured with worksheets that are done in groups in class and weekly quizzes (no tests). Working in groups actually turned out to be useful and made it much less stressful.

Class was flipped and learning was mostly done alone or with peers so it was a big adjustment to make at first. If you're not good with keeping up with things by yourself, I wouldn't recommend. Really appreciated how Dr. Straumanis was very attentive to our feedback. Really important: find good groupmates in the beginning!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He wants students to succeed and cares a lot, but this class is really hard because its Ochem 2. He is kind and willing to help.

The structure of this class makes it almost as hard as ochem1, it's entirely group work with short summary lectures to watch on your own. Grades aren't super important to Straumanis, he wants you to learn, you have to WORK for your grade an A and even then it might not happen, if you do well w/ straight lectures, this class probably isn't for you.

Class is basically self taught, but it's not bad with a good group. There are weekly quizzes and a cumulative final. Attendance is mandatory for the first few classes then becomes optional. Expect to put in work outside of class much like any other chem course.

Straumanis does a good job of making sure concepts get across to you well. If he taught Ochem 1, I definitely would have taken him then. Some advice: make sure you complete all of the CAs and extra practice problems he provides, they will aid in your success. The weekly quizzes are a HUGE part of your grade and some quizzes are tougher than others.

Straumanis is one of the most caring professors I have had. His system of weekly quizzes and no tests relieves students of a lot of pressure. S also emphasizes group learning, although I am an individual learner so I wasn't a big fan. My only complaint is the weekly quizzes had very little connection with one another, so I didn't retain much info.

I switched professors after O Chem I and I'm so glad I did. The class material seems more manageable with group activities; and the teaching team is always available to help. There's a weekly quiz but we're always told what topics will be tested, so its never a big surprise; the grading system is also very forgiving of little mistakes.
Do not take him unless you are a self learner...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is not an easy class, but Dr. Straumanis is willing to help his student understand the material rather than just memorizing. He gives P/NY (pass/not yet) grading on quizzes, and theres no exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Each class is set up with a pre-lecture, and then working in small groups over content. Sure, Organic Chemistry is far from an easy class, but he is really good at explaining material and allowing one to understand the concepts. Really study the chem activities thoroughly, and refresh yourself on ochem 1 topics, as they may be on the weekly quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure you are confident in your previous ochem 1 knowledge. Do the Brown problems (makes you buy too many textbooks) Use master organic chemistry. If the flipped classroom design works for you then this will work for you. Grading can be harsh but he has become accommodating. Sometimes it feels as if he is indifferent about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grade only based on weekly, 30 min quizzes plus a few survey points. Make sure you get a good group to help you study or else you will struggle. You basically teach yourself in this class.

He definitely has an unusual way of teaching. He lectures for about ten minutes and for the rest of the time figure out problems with our groups. Although unusual, I have found this style of teaching MUCH easier than normal lectures and ochem 1. If you take him, always go to class to work with your groups. He makes a very difficult subject easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN!! I have cried over three times just because of this class, please save yourself and DO NOT TAKE HIS OCHEM class. Just take Shabbir. He says he cares about your mental health but I doubt he cares about anyone except himself. His grading is very harsh and the weekly quizzes are very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The fact that there's no midterms, only short 30-minute quizzes every week, makes it so there's no real room to fall behind. The quizzes generally vary in difficulty but the grading scheme is very forgiving so if you do all the workbook exercises and the Textbook problems (neither of which are graded) you should be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes replace midterms. There's still a final. Class consists of working in a group to figure out topics instead of being taught. Recorded lectures over the topics are released after class. Very difficult if you rely on being taught with good lectures (you have to teach yourself everything in this class).
Make sure to stay on top of the lectures and pages in the book.

How you will do depends on how you learn. If you are someone who thrives through watching lectures and the professor work through problems, this class is NOT for you! This class is for the student who will do most of the work outside of class, reading and extra problems. If you take him, make sure you have a good study group AT THE START.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He definitely cares his student to not memorize but rather understand the mechanism throughout each lesson. Make friends on the first day as they can be essential for your understanding especially as the professor will put you to a break out room to learn amongst your partners. Dont miss class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Ochem is hard regardless of the teacher, but I feel like Dr. S should've adapted his teaching style better to an online format. A flipped classroom method might work better in person, but it's almost impossible to learn for people who rely on lectures and interaction. It's his first year so I'm not sure how he'll be in person, good luck!

Class is a flipped environment: work with a group through a walk through tutorial type of text book. At first, its unconventional but it really makes you think and connect ideas for yourself. The quizzes are tough, and I go blind for a solid two minutes. Take advantage of group work to talk out concepts and youll get a B+ or higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As someone who barely passed Shabbir's class, I'm doing really well and learning really well in Straumanis' class. His teaching style is totally different, but is great for giving you consistent practice and deep understanding. Straumanis is a very fair professor and is attentive to our needs. Groupwork is really important and helpful in his class!

This class is very groupwork-heavy, try to get a good group to start. Weekly quizzes, no homework grades, interesting grading system but good for staying on track and not getting behind. One final at the end. Awesome class, definitely keeps the course as stress-free as possible even given it being Ochem 2 and generally dreaded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Straumanis is not a bad professor at all. He teaches pretty well, its just that he expects you to learn a lot by yourself and doing practice problems which is essentially what ochem is. He has a hard grading structure all based of weekly quizzes and 1 test worth 20% of your grade, and all the questions are either you get full credit/ none.

Professor Straumanis has a very unusual teaching style that may not work for most. You are to work in groups to figure out the workbook problems, and the only sort of lecture you will receive is a summary lecture that goes over the workbook problems. A problem some may have with this is the lack of teaching a specific topic.

Dr. Straumanis takes his surveys into consideration to make positive changes for students in the course, which I have never experienced in a class before. The class is hard, but O Chem will always be hard. To succeed, go to class and make sure you understand the group work. TAs are not very helpful and he doesn't hold office hours, I got a tutor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: With his online class be prepared to make friends that will help you through his Ochem II class on the first day. Gives weekly quizzes instead of exams which is beneficial, but study study study ! Very nice professor and wants to benefit his students greatly!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: We have weekly quizzes to help more students pass the class, but the grading is all or nothing so its a bit hard to get an A still. Very nice man though! Wants to get to know his students.

Terrible professor for Ochem II. Does not teach or lecture at ALL and gives us in-class worksheets for us to work through on our own. Weekly quizzes make up 65% of our final grade and are nothing at all like the worksheets. Everytime someone addresses an issue about his class, he says its okay to fail as this is a learning experience (its not)

Dr.S engages in a flipped classroom centered on group work. For a lot of students, this new style can be confusing and unfair at first, but if you give it a chance and find a good group to work with, this style of teaching actually helps you understand the material in depth. He supplements material with summary lectures as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent professor with clear expectations. Physical chemistry 1 is a notoriously tough class, and Dr. Straumanis made the concepts feel tangible and understandable. Classwork is done in groups with extensive summary lectures available outside of class. Weekly quizzes take the pressure off.

Dr. Straumanis really cares about his students. Although he wants you to succeed, he really wants you to learn. As a result, his class is very hands on and requires a lot of self-study and groupwork. Some found this scary since lectures were light but I found it motivational and helpful. I retained much knowledge and definitely preferred his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you want your sanity by the end of the semester. Small confusing lectures and few explanations. Weekly quizzes are extremely stressful and require a bunch of studying, and half the time the questions aren't even related. Unfair grading system for them too. When addressing concerns, he always says its okay to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He essentially doesn't lecture and your only grades are weekly quizzes and 1 cumulative final exam. Do not recommend

Good: Listens and accomodates student concerns. Bad: Everything else. Flipped classroom design has you learn everything yourself. He clearly does not know anything about what he talks about and expectations for quizzes and exams were very unclear. Very random test questions.

Flipped classroom except no resources to learn the material. All you have is class worksheets (if you don't figure it out w/ your group, back to square 1). Unclear instructions, harsh grading. Not receptive to feedback. Pretends like he cares, but doesn't put in the effort. If actions speak louder than words, Andrei was real quiet! Avoid

Really hated the idea of flipped classroom, but I actually enjoyed doing it. He doesn't give a "lecture" for the course materials, but eventually you will understand most of the stuff by doing exercises. Lot of room for grade improvements. Not sure how it be in conventional setting, but it worked great with online. Such a great person too.

Doesn't lecture in class, you have no idea what's going on until you find time to watch his summary lectures. Lectures are just deriving a bunch of different equations. Homeworks were 2 problems: not enough to cover all the concepts that could show up on the assessments. I forgot to fill out a course survey and it dropped me a letter grade. Avoid!

I wasnt a fan of him when I had him at first, but over time I accepted his way of teaching us and I got to say that I am surprised how well it went. Teaching ourselves in groups, while unconventional, went alright. Give the man some time and I know that you too one day will like his class. I really never worried about my grade. Highly recommend

The class is a flipped classroom. He doesn't teach in the lecture. He puts us into small groups and has us work on problems and doesn't teach. You need to learn the material before class. Don't take him if you don't like the flipped classroom learning style.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: took his pchem class during covid and can't rate him highly enough. Does his best to facilitate, esp w/ covid, clearly cares about students learning w/o you stressing about grades. Unconventional way to teach (best description is a conceptual lab/workshop every class), but works out great for grades (quiz retakes!). if you try, you'll get an easy a

This class was really hard as a non-business major. The main part of your grade is the tests. I thought I knew all the material front and back for the test, and got a C-—definitely not a blow-off class. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, and it's not as hard as people make it seem. Pay attention to what he says in lectures, as he usually points out crucial points for exams. Use AI, which he recommends, to prep for exams by asking it to generate test questions for you. Also, read the Harvard readings closely and you'll be able to ace this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Seems chill but class is lowkey hard as a non business major. Take it in person instead.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were awesome. The correlation between time spent and exam grades were horrible. Used plenty of tricks on test that even full mastery of content would have you confused.

Not sure why Professor Walls is rated so low. His lectures were engaging and clear, and he explained concepts thoroughly while checking for understanding. This definitely isn't a blow-off class though-- you have to study and keep up with readings-- but he's a great professor! The tests are a large part of your grade, so study hard and ask questions

Very exam heavy class and hard to keep up with if you're a STEM major. Definitely not an "easy" class but not super hard either. Don't cram for his exams because you really have to know and apply the material to the questions. The questions are SUPER long sometimes too and it makes it hard to focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I did the online marketing course and it was lots of material but pretty easy since it was online. He genuinely goes insane about not allowing cheating online, its hella OD. Tests are easy though.
I had to take this class for credit. Honestly, he seems like a nice guy online but everything he explains in his lectures or notes is not on the exam and not well explained..

not bad but not a blow off class, stay on top of the work due on Friday nights. 3 exams w/ the opportunity to replace 1 w/ final. 2 lectures a week &readings (30-40) pages w/ quizzes (completion&graded). just scanned readings, &really took notes on lectures
2 classes before the exams are reviews. based studying on Learning obj. for units.

Very very exam heavy, with honorlock exams that consist of 45 mini essays for each question. It feels less about learning and more like him trying to trick you. Study resources is "put these 20 terms into AI," not helpful. So happy to be done with this class, its too much content delivered in boring, uninteresting lectures. Avoid if you can
GET READY TO READ 100000 PAGES PER WEEK! professor does too much to prevent cheating I honestly wouldnt be surprised if he watched the honorlock recordings during his free time
just dont do it.
Fairly easy course, just memorize and you'll be fine.

Professor Walls is so knowledgable and educated on the class he instructs. Every term, concept, or issue at hand in the class was always explained very well in conjunction with the helpful organization of the class. There are a lot of assignments in the weekly modules, but they are super helpful and straightforward. A great experience, really.

Stephen Walls is absolutely perfect to me. The way he presented the material was interesting and easy to understand for beginners. The tests were very straightfoward - everything on it is in the lecture slideshows and explained in class (no trick questions). He is funny, super engaging, and relatable. TAKE HIS CLASS! He is iconic.

Prof Walls is always so kind and responds quickly to emails. Material can be a little tricky but pay attention to lectures and the online modules and you will be fine. HW modules were easy and can be completed quickly if you pay attention to lecture. Exams are easy IF YOU STUDY! i put in the effort and finished with super high A.

Taking this course asynchronous and I really enjoy watching all of his lectures (Good music taste). There are lots of assignments to check understanding. 1 unit is due the Friday of every week. Lots of long readings, but I just focus on the lectures and use the readings as supplemental. So far, no SAQs on test. Watch lectures on 1.5 speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super difficult for me. I took the class as a required course for Advertising majors, & I believe he's the only professor available. A decent lecturer, who does his best to connect class concepts to real stories and examples. I had the most trouble with the no notes, monitored tests that were so off from the lecture content + the surplus of hw.

I took the online version and I thought it was pretty straight forward. I never read the textbook, unless it was for some vocab. Just watch his videos and write detailed notes and you will be fine. It is a lot to memorize, but the content isn't too difficult. He also does a review right before the exam, and provides a few practice questions.

Great guy, pretty good professor. Rambles sometimes. Exams are sometimes a lot, but there's an optional final to replace your lowest exam grade that helped me get an A. He also offers extra credit which helps. Always available via email and willing to help explain content. Probably one of the harder business minor classes bc there's so much content

He is really engaging and interesting; loved his lectures. His exams were more scenario-based and application, so not just about memorizing terms. Skimmed through the textbook, but focused more on his slides- really helped. Does have a few extra credit opportunities. Hard deadlines! As an online student, don't let it pile up and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly all you have to do is listen in class, take a few notes that aren't on the slides, and you're fine. For exams, I memorized the slides and knew some vocab from the textbook (never read the text book), and got an A in the class. Some of the questions on the exam are super specific, and you really need to know exactly what is on the slides.

I was in the in-person section, and all the lectures were amazing but sometimes got off topic and ran long. Walls really cares and wants to help you, but the tests are difficult. Sometimes the math practice problems aren't accurate to the questions on the test, but otherwise it's just memorization and application. Study and you'll be okay.
I think he is nice and all, I just wish the tests were not weighed 75% of the grade in this class. The best strategy for sucess is to create flashcards after every unit and try to memorize
Exams aren't that bad honestly if you study just the lectures. Didn't do a single reading but did fine as long as you take good notes and make sure you are LISTENING during the lectures.

I thought this class and Professor Walls were awesome! THIS IS NOT AN EASY CLASS. But it is very doable if you put in work. I watched every lecture, read all the readings, went to all office hours, and studied very extensively. Professor Walls was always very willing to help. GET THE CLASS NOTES THAT THE IN-PERSON CLASS GETS. Trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was so worried going into this class because I'd heard many horror stories but it was not even close to what I'd expected from those stories. I was online but he seems like a nice guy. YES, you HAVE to study and put in WORK but it's not insurmountable. If you're an ADV major like me take 345 & 344 before or alongside and STUDY.. you'll be fine!

Overall not a bad class. I was in the studio for the live stream, so my experience is different. Walls produces good lectures but can go off topic. He still covers everything. My main issue with him came from him messing up the Canvas grades and fixing it 5 days before the final which caused some stress. His class is fine, but lectures can get long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework was easy and basically for completion. Tests were weighted heavily and proctored (took the online class). He uses the HBP readings to supplement his lectures, which I thought were useful. Workload is relatively easy especially compared to stem classes. Optional final to replace 1 of the 3 previous exams. Exams were fine, not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ended up doing well without ever reading the textbook. I took very good notes over the lectures, which basically covered all of the material. For the textbook, I only read AI-generated notes over it and wrote down any glossary terms not mentioned in lecture. I made flashcards for the exams. Dr. Walls is very caring and approachable in office hours!

Professor Walls is so nice and funny. While there was a lot of reading assigned, I never actually read the textbook and did fine. As long as you take good notes and study for the tests using the slides and learning objectives you'll be fine. I took the in-person version of this course which was helpful when it came to staying engaged. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Uses AI to write class material. Tests are regurgitation based and be prepared to read A LOT.

The lectures were poorly formatted and not comparable to the test material Prof. Walls was rude in emails. Extremely test heavy class and these exams are TOUGH. Be prepared to do all of the reading (up to 4 assigned readings of about 20-40 pages each per week). The amount of workload for a class I am taking for my minor is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Walls is pretty funny, and his lectures are engaging. The course itself though is so heavy for an online class. There is a lot of work and reading to do. I have found the tests really hard, too.

Professor Walls is a pretty cool guy. But even a cool guy like him can't miraculously make the subject matter of this class interesting. Your entire grade is basically determined by how well you do on the tests which are super definition heavy, so get ready to memorize lots of readings. I wish this class was offered in a traditional format :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is so tough to get a hold of. Really rude, does little to nothing. I'd love his job.

The structure of the lectures made complete sense and really helped me learn. Teaching style is organized and he explains hard topics very well. As long as you read and watch the lectures you should be fine. I miss him after having other, less organized lecturers where the flow of info doesn't make as much sense.

Walls is ONE OF THE BEST LECTURERS I have had at UT. The slides are outstanding. Take notes on both the readings and the lectures; I promise you wont regret it. The readings can certainly be long, but they are actually helpful. Exams on Proctorio. I did well by reading over notes before hand and maybe doing an online study quizlet.

Not too bad overall but get ready to read. A lot. He uses HBP as homework assignments and you can have up to three a week, each around 40 pages long. For a class that gives credit for a business minor, was for sure a lot of work. Not a blow off, but definitely doable. Optional 4th exam and up to 4 points extra credit on total grade. An A is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures get boring and sometimes I feel like I would learn nothing. I would never read the assigned readings but I would always take good notes of the class lectures. It is important to look over your notes and especially the charts and graphs for the exams (75%). He used honorlock. There was no extra curve. The extra credit is worth 4%, DO IT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Surprised that Dr. Walls doesn't have way better reviews... I loved this class and while it was more of a workload than I'm used to it's very doable to learn the material between the readings, articles, his lectures, and other resources. I feel like he taught me a lot and was great at explaining tough concepts. So many extra credit opportunities

It was a tough course to begin with made worse by inexistent office hours, too much reading, and poorly done lectures. This surplus of work is incredibly overwhelming. And when I was able to get in contact with him he forgot about our scheduled office hours. Ugh. However, he gives lots of extra credit.

As someone that is only taking this class for the business minor, I cannot believe how hard it is. The modules take forever to get throug, 3 tests make up almost 60% of your final grade and the questions are INCREDIBLY difficult and long, even if you do study. I'm sure Walls is a great guy, but this class is NOT it. Would never take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to do the readings and watch review sessions. Tests are more memorization of lists and can be difficult, but everything else is an easy 100. You can get 4% points to your final grade. Overall not too bad as long as you study a good amount the week of the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you read the textbook and watch the lectures you will be fine. He also offers so many options for extra credit (I think I was able to add like 4 whole points to my end grade). He uses proctorio on the exams, but if you watch his review sessions and make sure you know the learning objectives in depth the tests are not that hard.

Walls was an awesome professor. However, this class takes a LOT of work, and is in no way a blow-off class. Make sure to study hard, and he is clear on what should be covered. Modules were due every Friday with some super long. I found the tests easy BECAUSE I studied and studied early. I cannot say it enough how you must study. He uses Proctorio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I adore Professor Walls. Took asynchronous MKT320F bc it was my only option and I didn't even realize until halfway through the semester he wasn't my actual professor bc Williams just uses all of his stuff. This class is definitely content heavy and tests out proctored, but Walls is a great professor. clarifies what we need to know/don't. Study!!

Yes, he assigned A LOT of business readings. The lectures are summaries of the readings, the exams come from the lectures, a handful of things from the readings we wont lecture on so it's important to read. His 2 review sessions before each exam are VERY CRUCIAL and helpful. He is a great lecturer and super funny. He is a chatty and interesting guy

This class is super low maintenance until a test rolls around. It isn't fun, but do ALL the readings and make a notecard for each term. Watch his review lecture and make sure you really know what you're doing. No final which is nice, and there was a small curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walls tests are 25% each and there are 3 with an optional cumulative one at the end (4) but can only be taken if you miss an exam... it doesn't replace one. His tests are all scenario specific which is difficult to apply from the book because he doesn't give many scenarios examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My dad literally died and I contacted Professor Walls so that I could reschedule the test but because of his "no makeup test" policy, he told me it would not be fair for other students for me to reschedule the test and simply take the cumulative final at the semester. Never felt more disappointed in another human being ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was a terrible class. You're tested on concepts barely mentioned in the textbook, and Walls's is extremely rude in his emails.

He's very nice and explains the concepts clearly. I can tell that he does want students to succeed. The class is test-heavy since 60% of your grade is determined by 3 exams. I didn't really enjoy the reading but the class is doable if you study for the exam a few days in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Walls was really funny and knew his stuff super well but the content was just way too much esp considering most of the students are taking this as an elective. Reading the 30-40 pages assigned a week is not enough! His tests pick out the most MINISCULE details and on top of that, are worded pretty badly. You CANNOT brush off this class.

You can tell he knows what hes talking about. Kind of funny in a weird way, deviates from marketing to give his students a break. This class involves a lot of reading, but it is manageable! Lectures and readings will help with exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ehh, professor Walls was kind of boring. I thought the exams were harder than they should be. He also gives a lot of readings each week. I don't really enjoy this class /:

overall the class isnt that bad but the tests are definitely difficult for a foundation class plus the tests are worth about 60% of your final grade. however this was a weird semester with covid and the snowstorm so i'm sure it was a different experience then usual. its not an easy A but its possible if you put in the time.

Walls was great but the online textbook is on average about 60-80 pages a week (super dense), activities that are just participation grades, and reading checks. Lastly, there are 3 tests each worth 20% of your grade (exam scores average in the low 70s). Super hard class to get an A in considering this is a foundational course but I expected worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took MKT320F for the business minor and this is no easy A class. Professor Wall's exams averaged in the mid 70s for both exams during the class. You can attend lecture, do all the readings, and still not make an A because you have to study closely. Mostly memorizing terms and apply concepts. A lot of memorizing, Walls is a nice guy, just absurd.

I took him for MSI 2020. I like marketing but he's very snobbish. He loves to call students out and humiliate them if they don't know the answer. His tests are scenario based which is hard to apply the concepts. Very knowledgeable and knows it. Just study hard and know your stuff when he calls on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Walls through MSI. It was a good class and definitely interesting because i felt like all of the marketing material was relevant to real life. The tests are based on scenarios which are sometimes confusing to understand. The material is easy to grasp but applying it to the test questions is the hard part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Walls for the MSI business minor. I really liked him as a professor but his exams were very heavy on reading comprehension which isn't my strong suit. He does let you appeal 2 questions per exam, but he's not generous in giving those points back. The course itself is interesting and he teaches it well, it's just difficult to apply.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Best!! This class was easy. Homework was a big part of your grade, but they are easy if you read the textbook. Tests were taken at home and open note. Lectures were also interesting and Dr. Best tries to make them as interactive as possible.
Dr. Best is genuinely amazing and if he taught more astronomy classes I would take every single one. I truly enjoy his lectures and the homework and tests are not bad at all.

Prof. Best is an amazing lecturer, and he knows why most students are taking his class, so he makes it as fun and engaging as he can. I would recommend this as a science credit for sure, one of the best classes I've taken here at UT.
Amazing professor! Loved his lectures. Very manageable for a student not in stem. Take this class!!
good teacher, not much else to say

Dr. Best is great! Assignments are very very manageable, lectures are genuinely interesting, tests are take-home, and there is ample extra credit. If you're considering taking this course for science credit, do it!

Best is an amazing professor who is passionate about what he is teaching and genuinely wants to get to know and interact with his students. If you have to join a waitlist for this class, DO IT! I would take this class 1000x over
I love Dr. Best. This class was great, interesting but not unnecessarily difficult for a science credit. Highly highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Best is great. Knows students are there for credit, you are still able to get something out of his class if you go every week. There are instapolls in class not for credit and questions for EC every single class so attendance helps your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! He knows how to keep students engaged, even though most of us are only taking it for the credit. In his lectures, he makes complicated concepts easy to understand. If you take his class, please participate and ask questions. He is genuinely so kind, funny, and nerdy in a good way.

He knows most people taking this class are not majoring in anything related to astronomy. Still genuinely one of the sweetest, most passionate professors I've ever met. My only regret with this class is not paying attention more during the lecture and choosing to do other class work instead. Every lecture was extremely interesting and engaging.
He's my queen.

100% recommend this class for science credit. Lectures were extra credit points and tests were take home. You can tell Professor Best truly has passion for what he teaches and fosters a great learning environment.
Best professor at UT. Attendance is EXTRA CREDIT. His exams are at home as well. Easy Science credit so please take it.

Best is a very good lecturer and is very knowledgeable. There is HW before every lecture and they are due before class. They're also a big part of your grade. Tests are open-note and timed, gives us like 3 days to do it. An easy A as long as you do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best is an excellent professor who gives good lectures and makes the class super accessible. Attendance is not mandatory but gives extra credit. Tests are open-note, online, and not hard. Homework makes up most of the final grade, and getting a good grade on it is easy.

LOVE PROFESSOR BEST! Such an amazing professor, probably one of the best I have had so far! Definitely recommend taking his class if you need an easy science credit. He is very approachable and loves answering questions. He's passionate about astronomy and you can tell! He is so kind and cares for his students. This man must be protected
Take this class if you need an easy science credit. Attendance is for extra credit and the tests are all online! The homework is doable and the tests are easily done as they are online and open note.

AMAZING TEACHER/CLASS! Lectures are interesting, but not mandatory since attendance is extra credit. Teacher is so nice and engaging! Homework is light and there's time in many class periods to start it. Tests are online, at home, open note, and for you to take whenever in 2 day period. I would recommend this class to anyone needing science credit.

Very straightforward class. Just gotta do the homework. Then 2 exams a week. Teacher kinda sucks at giving lectures. But hey, classes aren't mandatory. My friend was in the class with one of the other professors and she had tons more work, so I'd still recommend Best over the other teachers, for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class and adored his teaching style. His lectures do an excellent job of explaining everything in the reading in a very easy-to-digest way. I did all the reading and went to all the lectures, but you don't really need to do both. I'd recommend just going to the lectures and maybe reviewing the reading if you're having trouble.

Dr. Best is a quirky and wonderfully enthusiastic professor. My major is in no way related to Astronomy, but I found myself considering taking additional classes or even taking on a minor if CNS allowed them... All-in-all, a very great professor who clearly loves his profession!

This class was super easy because everything was online and open note. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you can get a lot of extra credit just for showing up. The professor was super nice as well and clearly very passionate about astronomy. Highly recommend to get your science credit through this course.
Interesting class that is not difficult. I took his class for a science credit and don't regret it at all, his lectures are interesting an he offers extra credit every class period.

Professor Best is actually the best. His class is by far one of the easiest classes I've taken so far. I recommend him so much. His lectures were also very interesting, you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches.
Professor Best is the best professor. Class is pretty simple. 10/10 recommend him if you need to get a science credit out of the way.

I took this class for an easy science credit. As someone who struggles with science, this was one of the easiest classes I took this semester. The professor himself is extremely passionate about the topic, was super funny, and was a lot of fun and interesting to listen to. I would 100% take this class again and highly recommend!

EASIEST CLASS EVER. Attendance not mandatory so I stopped going. Mastering Astronomy HW due Mon, Wed, Fri, each week, all on quizlet and its 70% of your grade. Three tests, all take home, also all on quizlet! Not protocored and its 10% each of your grade. TAKE FOR EASY SCIENCE CREDIT!

Dr. Best is amazing. His lectures are super interesting and you can tell he genuinely cares about his research. There are pre-readings for every class and homework after every class, but the homework is easy and lectures cover the readings. Theres also 3 easy exams and he provides opportunities for extra credit.
Love having Dr. Best. There's a decent amount of reading technically assigned, but the lectures are simple, fun, and easy to understand, so you could probably get by without reading.
Fun easy science class. 5 homework grades = 1 test grade. Interesting lectures, lots of reading assigned but the tests are open note and homework-based so I didn't read much. Tiny bit of math.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He makes simple concepts somehow impossible to understand. Lectures are difficult to follow. Despite being a neuro class, this course covers strictly math concepts. Exams are difficult since he thinks he explains concepts much better than he actually does while the entire class stays confused.

Took class after seeing previous reviews, but unfortunately prof has significantly changed class structure. Lectures difficult to navigate. Exams are no longer take-home writeups, now difficult. Quite lenient on grading is only good thing but still low exam scores due to hard concepts. Very hard class now, take another neuro class to fulfill degree

Professor is not good at explaining concepts. Even though this is technically a neuro class, it's a ton of math which he expects you to already know the fundamentals of. He password protects lectures and files, making it a pain to access them and download to write notes alongside lecture.

This class changed my life. Yes, it's very math heavy BUT he is so fair in grading, homework and exams. The exams were open note and I thought were a fair representation of the course material. OH and rvw sessions were beneficial too. You can tell he cares for his students, he's also knowledgable in the field. deff take it, not a hard class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had no computational/math background so there was much new (but useful) material about understanding computational modeling of neural systems but he explained very comprehensively! Dr.Wei and the TA sessions were clear on exam content and helpful for preparing. He took student feedback and made availability for students outside of OH if needed.

Dr. Wei is a great professor. Don't be afraid of taking Neural Computation with him because of the complex topics. Go to class, ask questions, take notes, and watch YT videos if you need more math help. This neuro math/cs is a great foundation for any further work in computer vision/neural networks type stuff.
Take metrics with Brendan Kline.

Sad to see the lack of engagement from the class- his humor is underrated! This class was very content packed which made it hard to process and remember everything for the tests. Good news is that they were not cumulative! Lab component isn't something to stress out about. I did every assignment the night it was due and got a 97+ on all of them.

Course is graded 65% lecture, 35% lab. Lectures are long but he tells you what specific concepts will be on midterms and quizzes (makes for easy studying). His accent really isn't that bad, just pay attention. Lab section consists of a couple papers, nothing crazy difficult just time-consuming. Be sure to get assignments in on time.

Professor Xu has a very heavy accent that is difficult to understand, and the course is very very lecture heavy. As a result, I don't feel like I learned anything. I paid a lot of money to hire a private tutor, and I feel like that was the only reason I didn't flunk the class. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are decent. The practice exams are very useful. The exam isn't too difficult. The writing section might take some time to find data.

Surprised by this rating. I thought he was fantastic. Lectures are fine. His accent is over blown imo however could just be me. Super nice guy very accommodating. I thought this class was fairly easy math was lite and essays were fine. Would be surprised if he's isn't the easiest metric teacher. 10/10

Nice prof. Clear slides and materials. Chill HWs. 2 exams. No final.
One of the best choices of Econometrics.
My lab (paper) TA sucks. Thanks Dr. Xu's curve.

Language/accent barrier made things hard to understand sometimes (not his fault). If you have a strong AP Stats background, it's really easy at the beginning of the semester. Homeworks are completion, and the entire course (minus the two exams) are all doable online, including the quizzes. Last exam cumulative before Thanksgiving with no final.

Professor Xu's heavy accent makes his lectures difficult to understand at times. Additionally, lectures are very unengaging and content is presented sporadically.  Although the class has a light workload (2 exams, a lab paper, and weekly completion-only homework), I would recommend taking another professor in order to truly learn the content.
His lectures are not helpful at all. The things that will save your grade are the papers, the first exam (NOT the second), and doing good on the quizzes.

Takes a while to understand his accent and lectures can be a little weird: it's hard to know what's relevant and what's not. Personally, the 'casual' way he lectures and his tangents help me pay attention since content is boring. Exams are fine and the class isn't hard. Homeworks are completion. I just struggled on the weekly quizzes a bit.

He is very kind and wants to help his students, however his accent makes it difficult to comprehend what he is teaching. Often goes on tangents about AI and data science which may not be relevant to many students. He was helpful on quizzes though and the lab portion was mangeable.

Very sweet man but just not a good teacher honestly. Stands and points at slides, and then rambles about how data science is the only useful skill. over a month in and I have NO idea what we are actually supposed to be learning. Also very difficult to understand. Honestly feel robbed paying for this class when all his material is from other profs

Professor was caring, but accent is thick and sometimes he wouldn't come with a mic. Lectures were iffy to go to and pay attention. Material covered is fair, with exams being short T/F exams with FRQ. Can honestly just study slides and reviews and get an easy B. Lab portion was half the grade and was easy, just don't procrastinate. Fair class.

Dr. Xu is very kind and is passionate about economics. He does really try to help you learn and is understanding. His lectures are rather long and can be kind of boring at times, but he is a good professor and teaches the material well. There is only one homework assignment a week for the class and two tests, so it is not bad workload wise.

could not understand his very thick accent, and suffered as a result. I went to his office hours and asked how I could improve in my studies and see what resources might help me (maybe some extra problems, videos, etc). He accused me of not attending his class, and claimed that's why I was doing poorly. I attended every lecture.
Seems like a very nice guy. I just have no clue what he's saying due to his thick accent.

If I could rate him zero I would.
The topics themselves aren't difficult - but he makes everything overcomplicated. I self-taught using the textbook
His accent is rlly difficult to understand and he does a lot of (unnecessary) work that's not on the slides
Doesn't really care about students and scheduled the final way before the examination period
very difficult to understand his accent. makes it hard to know what's going on, when he cant even pronounce the terminology of the math he's doing.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Xu cares about his students! This course is intimidating but he wants you to do good & is honest about what is expected of you. Course load is reasonable & rigor is usual for an upper division eco class. I highly recommend this prof, he is approachable & open to explaining topics further if needed. I appreciate Xu's enthusiasm for the material
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He teaches the course very well and makes econometrics much easier to understand. The lecture and lab were really helpful overall, and the professor breaks down complex topics into simple, real world applicable examples. He has a thick accent that at times is difficult to understand but his presentations are filled will great info.

He curves really well and the homework is great to pad your grade. I just had a hard time understanding his accent in class. Whenever I asked questions after class his explanations didn't help and he just repeated what he had said earlier and couldn't explain the concepts in a different way. Good guy but thick accent

Prof. Xus class is useful and the course is not so hard if you try to do the web assign hw and prepare well. Learned a lot and application to the paper session as well. He gives a lot of curve for exams. If you put time into the class, its not hard to get an A.

This class was a lot more time consuming than expected, but the grading was very fair and the tests were curved. Though Dr. Xu has a thick accent, he really tries his best to convey relevant information and really clearly knows his material well. The papers are long but teach a lot about practical application of econometrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of assigned material (readings + film) outside of class, but they were all interesting, albeit the readings can get dense. Class is discussion heavy, so make sure you come prepared. Low-stakes weekly response essays to assigned material, group presentation, and final essay (focus on this). Overall super fun and informative class.

Yes it's a little intense for a lower-division class but I had fun and never thought that the assignments were too hard. Easy 2-page film reviews that once you get the formula down you can just repeat every week and she gave me 10/10 on almost every one. Just like watching films before you sign up for a film class (I saw that problem in my class).

The class consists of almost weekly 2 paged double-spaced papers that analyze assigned movies, but that's it. You WILL be paired up with a partner where you need to lead the discussion, but only once. Readings are practically unintelligible- and she knows this. The only bad thing was the strict attendance policy. 3 absences then letter grade drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took her film class to receive a flag I needed, she was very pretentious and condescending. The course isn't well structured and consists of watching several films repeatedly and discecting scenes in class. 70% of the course was taken up by group presentations. High work load and there is 1 paper worth 30% of your grade, the reading is nonsense

His lectures are very boring, and you won't learn anything. Quizzes became more about memorization of homework problems than actual learning. If you can self-study well or have some preexisting knowledge, you will be fine. Otherwise, try to take it with someone else. However, he does give lots of partial credit on the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty pointless. He teaches straight out the textbook. First two exams werent bad and he does a decent enough job of telling you general problems on tests. But, the final was awful. Had an entire problem that was never taught in class and genuinely no one knew how to do.

Terrible lecturer, excellent one-on-one. Go to office hours, read the textbook, and put in the effort of learning on your own, and you'll be ok. Despite the terrible lectures, he is a very kind person who is willing to explain the material and help you. Genuinely cares about the success of his students.

Bad lecturer. If you can stomach self-studying entirely, you will be fine. Quizzes are directly from textbook problems, and tests are similar to, but harder. The problem is, you don't learn much, if any, dynamics fundamentals/intuition, you just end up memorizing textbook problems. If you want to actually learn dynamics, look elsewhere.

Weekly homework with a quiz during discussion. The quiz was a homework problem with different numbers. There were 2 tests and a final. These questions were picked from the textbook, so it was pretty easy to practice for them. All things are graded with generous partial credit. He adapted his teaching to help the class. Very nice guy as well.

I hated this class. The only day Dr. Hamilton taught an informative class was the day she was observed by higher-ups. Your grade comes from teaching a PE lesson as well as weekly discussion posts and a midterm+final. Strict 0 absence policy or you fail. Don't waste your time in this class, you won't learn anything.

If you have the possibility to take a different professor for EDC 314, do it! Professor Hamilton not only was slow and repetitive during lectures, but constantly contradicted herself and treated the students like children instead of adults learning to become teachers. The TAs were the only saving grace for this class.

Absolutely awful. Just the worst in every way. Made statements such as:
1. "Students are either normal or disabled."
2. "If a student can't meet the PE Standards for any reason, they should be failed."
3. "Weigh yourself every day and don't eat if you don't need to."
Harassed multiple students after classes for their disabilities and identities.

She changed the project guidelines every week and treated students poorly. She also said things like "we should fail children with disabilities who don't meet standards" and "ladies weigh yourself every day and never gain weight." She was confusing, outdated, and none of the students respected her after 3 weeks. Choose the other professors!!

Very easy class. Do not buy the textbook, it is very useless and definitely not necessary. There are no tests besides the fitness ones you have to perform. You are given opportunities to revise all the writing assignments, essentially guaranteeing a 100.

Fitness For Life is such an easy class. You don't need to buy the textbook its basically useless. There is no exams. You just need to write for majority of the class and you have revisions to get a 100. Her lectures are pretty boring and will make you stand up and do stuff in class but just do homework or something else to keep yourself busy.
She was sweet, but lectures were very long and pointless. She had a habit of rambling about topics that were not even related to what we were studying. TA did all the work. Easy class though.

I took the Fitness for Life class and it is a solid, easy choice! The class is about improving and setting your own goals for physical activity, so it's a great 2-in-1: getting in exercise and an easy class for your GPA. My TA was also really nice. There's a textbook for the class but I didn't use it, honestly. Would totally recommend for a UGS!

Fitness for Life was an easy fun way to get your UGS credit. You do have paper assignments but they are extremely easy as long as you follow the requirements. The TA is the person who led our class zooms, but my TA, Toby, was great. The class is really fun and encourages you to stay in shape. This is an easy A if you get your work done on time.

I took Fitness For Life, and it was the easiest class I took this semester! No exams, just a few papers, and revisions are allowed. But the TAs grade pretty easily, so you probably won't need to. For this class you either use an Apple Watch or Fitbit (provided by TA) and track your fitness data throughout the semester. Weekly discussions are easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fitness for Life is the easiest class you will ever take at UT. There was zero interaction with Keating, and class structure consisted of a one hour weekly discussion section with a TA (mandatory), short discussion posts, an oral presentation, and a handful of writing assignments. Grading was an easy 100 on nearly all assignments. Take this UGS!
This class is an easy A, and online there is no interaction with the professor. But the readings and the papers were super easy so I recommend this class and this professor.

I took her for Fitness For Life and it was by far one of the best decisions I made. You show up to class and get an A basically. She was not a hard grader and the papers and readings assigned were minimal and/or easy, so you'll be fine.

Dr. Keating is an amazing professor! I took her "personal physical activity" class and she and her TA Xiaolu are the greatest! They explain all the assignments very clearly and are not tough graders. Attendance is mandatory, attend class and get the A. Easiest class I took all semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took her personal physical activity class in the Spring, but she teaches a similar class in the Fall called fitness for life. The teacher and her TA were helpful and nice. We got to go play outdoors on Fridays. This was a fun class and I really enjoyed it. One thing to watch out for is that the attendance is mandatory and effect your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: The Fitness for Life class was relatively easy. You just show up and do some simple assignments and you get an A. You have to show up though and cant be late more than twice or she starts docking your grade. In terms of UGS classes, this is by far one of the easiest ones on calls, definitely recommend. Oh and each Friday you play a sport.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The contents for this class are difficult as is, and although the professor is very nice, keeping up with her lectures was hard. There is quite a lot of information for the class and the lectures covered a lot of material per class. The exams are weighted the most and can be challenging if you don't study thoroughly.

Super nice but soft spoken. Was hard to pay attention during lectures and usually never finished her lectures. She did have the high A distribution though so maybe she gives a nice curve. I think she's also retiring so wont be teaching again not sure though.

One of the worst classes I've taken. Xiaolan's nice, but she gives you the same randomly assigned group for all of the cases throughout the semester, and you don't get to switch groups at all, regardless of how many people complain about issues they've had with their groups. Other profs let you pick groups/switch. Would not take again.

FIN 367 kind of sucks, but I think she's better than she gets credit for, because she has the highest averages and makes the midterms seem easy. Connect homework is a complete nightmare and nothing like the exams, so don't waste your time. Most of the TAs have no idea what's going on and are quite rude. I'd say she's your best bet for the class.

Very hard to learn from lectures. Entire semester consisted of me teaching myself through the textbook because her lectures felt redundant. She provides midterm and exam practice problems but none contain explanations and only solutions so it's basically impossible to learn concepts you don't understand if you're unable to attend office hours. GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mindy is absolutely fantastic: her knowledge, passion, and intellect for FIN 367 are actually so inspiring. FIN367 is just inherently a difficult class (regardless of prof), but she does a very thorough job of explaining concepts in class and during office hours. She appreciates questions and will honestly break down difficult concepts. Love her!

FIN 367 is just an incredibly hard class, but professor Xiaolan does a pretty good job explaining concepts and making sure to answer any questions students have. Our class averages were significantly higher than other classes. Overall solid option for 367.

FIN 367 is hard with anybody. She is a researcher, so she simply isn't good at transmitting information to people who don't have a PhD. Fast paced class with two chapters each week. Smartbook and HW are excessively long and useless. Lectures for 75 minutes straight. If you want an A in the class, study outside of class.

Prof Zhang taught the class very well, and attending the lecture helped out a lot when preparing for the midterms. She used a strategy where we would make the equation sheet during class time and write down the more important formulas, which really helped a lot. Tests are kinda tough, but I usually use practice to study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 2 midterms, one gets dropped. Get equation sheet for each exam and always has practice test. There are participation quizzes but they're pretty much for extra credit. She goes fast, but not bad. Notes are posted.

CE 311S is easy if you go to class and lab. Homework sometimes gets tough but no big deal. Random quizzes to make sure people are coming to class. You get to bring a formula sheet to tests. Tests are pretty much exactly the practice tests. She's also very willing to bring in students who want to do research with her.

She went over a practice midterm the class before the exam day which made it super useful to study for her exams. She had random quizzes during class that weren't bad. Her lectures were useful and if you go to class and go over the practice midterm you should get an A.

For the most part, the homework was straightforward, as were the labs. Her lectures cover everything relevant to the assignments, but she usually moves too quickly to take notes. This is made worse by the fact that the annotated lectures are not posted. Still, as long as you follow the material and read the textbook, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not lecture well and made everything complicated. Annotated notes are not posted. Labs were every week which were more helpful than the actual lectures. Gave practice exams and didn't post the key for them. Have to attend class to obtain the answers. Attendance pop quizzes are determined with a coin flip. Good luck.
NA

Prof Zhang is not good at teaching. She makes everything super complicated when in reality you need to know a few simple formulas. Her exams are just like the practice exams, you can bring a 1 pg sheet from home, and she has pop quizzes by flipping a coin in class. I really don't like how she teaches but the content is fine if you look it up.

she is amazing, knows everyones names, responses to messages immediately. lab is a lot of work but very rewarding. she is literally an angel and so is her lab. if you can get in for fri it is so valuable. learned so much, mentors are amazing, prepares you for what research actually is. love her!

Dr Yang is genuinely such a kindhearted person and wants you to understand the content you are learning in the lab. She is super understanding of extenuating circumstances and makes an effort to learn each student by name. Don't worry about your grade, worry about fully understanding the lab techniques and you will succeed.

Dr. Yang is genuinely the best professor I've had in all my years of learning, she is so compassionate and really great at explaining complex biochem topics in simple ways. She is THE best professor at UT Austin.

Professor Y is incredibly understanding of his students both in and out of the classroom, and he grades generously. I came into the class with zero coding/computing background, and I never felt behind in any way. Lectures are clear and well-structured, homework is simple and follows lecture material. Labs aren't too hard but can be time-consuming.

Was my absolute favorite!! Probably the best professor at answering questions in office hours. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He is so patient and you will not leave there confused. Class not impossible but coding exam 2 can kill your grade as its either 0, 50, 100 on exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Y is amazing at explaining concepts to beginners. He has office hours twice a week and is willing to explain everything as long as you are willing to learn. He is clearly passionate about this subject (somehow lol). He chooses great TAs and tells them to grade fairly, so tests are graded easily. He also gives out a lot of free food!

Super nice prof! Dr. Y is a fun lecturer and does a really good job of explaining programming from the ground up so that it becomes much more intuitive. His grading criteria is clear (programming assignments have an autograder) so it's not too hard to do well on homework. The TAs are also easy to reach and SUPER generous with test credit.

Dr. Y is a really nice guy. He wants everyone to succeed and clearly cares. His lectures are always chill, and I feel that he does a really good job of taking difficult topics and breaking them down. This class was pretty easy. The autograder on programming assignments came in clutch. Lots of instructional material and past exams to study with.

Very reasonable compared to the other ECE306 Sections. He's always very patient and accessible for office hours. Tests are similar to prior years so exams (3) usually do not get curved because they aren't very difficult. Although sometimes his lectures make you a bit sleepy, take him over other 306 professors.

He is a great guy, very chill and always ready to help. However, his lectures, at times, feel a bit scattered, though most of the content is essential for the future. I learned more from figuring out the homework than from sitting in his lectures. He often notes things about the industry, which makes his lectures interesting to listen to.

100% the best professor to take for 306. He explain everything so well from a beginner's viewpoint. The Midterms and Finals were also very fair as long as you have some idea of what you are doing. The programs do take a while in the end, but are still manageable. He is the GOAT. Can't wait to take him for ECE 319H next semester!

Best prof for 306 w/o a doubt, considering both lectures and grading. He explains in such a meticulous manner that anyone can understand. The programs are hard, homework are often lengthy, quizzes are take home, and exams are 100% fair. He understands everyone's background when lecturing and is truly the GOAT! He also does yoga and is a chill guy:)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am really grateful that ECE306 was my first programming class I took in college. Dr. Yerraballi is extremely knowledgeable and a great lecturer.

literally the goat, he teaches so calmly and you can understand everything he is talking about clearly. even with no prior knowledge, he understands everyones skill level and provides thorough explanations for everyone. homework is chill - once a week and not very long. attendance is non mandatory but definitely recommended!

Great class. Dr. Y is the GOAT and your TA's will help you tremendously. I took this class with 460N and made it through just fine. Labs take time but you should never be stressed if you start them early. All we had was 4 labs and weekly quizzes which helped with the work load. Apparently exams are coming back next semester though.

Dr. Y is amazing. The concepts will all be relatively foreign in this class but Dr. Y makes sure everything is digestable. The exams are more than fair and similar to previous years. The programming assignments are difficult but not impossible. Dr. Y also really cares and wants you to succeed. The grading curve is generous and I enjoyed this class.

Amazing professor, he is the GOAT. I love attending his lectures, and his office hours are extremely helpful. He cares a lot about his students and his class. He is a funny person, and so helpful if we go to him for help. Great at teaching! Definitely try taking his class!

Amazing professor: will explain topics in easily understandable terms and ASK. Code work is simple if you know archaic coders (LC3) except the final two. Go to office hours, he will answer questions—though verbose at times. The recitations are a nice way to reinforce previously covered topics. 2 paper exams are kind of difficult without coder.

Dr. Y is amazing!!! He's probably one of the best lecturers you'll ever have (explains pretty hard concepts in very graspable ways / layman's terms). He also understands students' situations and is just a really good person, too.
Amazing lecturer, genuinely a great person outside of class as well. If you do the homeworks and go to recitation/OH, you'll be fine for the exams.

Dr. Y is amazing! I wish I wasn't procrastinating as much and put in the effort from the beginning. His lectures and office hours are very helpful, and he makes sure we have a good understanding of the concept. We don't have extra credits but I think the exams are fair, especially if you are able to solve all of the homework problems successfully.

Yerraballi is the GOAT. Taught concepts very well, very kind and had many office hours available. Lectures were recorded and posted, so many people did fine without attending class or recitation, though I would still recommend going. Unintentionally hilarious, and he cares a lot about his students and their input.

Excellent lecturer, excellent person. Dr. Yerraballi broke down the most difficult concepts into basics where everyone was able to understand. He is respectful to students; he makes us feel comfortable asking questions. ECE319K was a fun class, and he was always happy to help.
Yerraballi makes the giant mess that is 319K slightly easier than other professors thanks to his lectures.
He's the GOAT. Best 319K professor and by far the best lecturer out of all the choices. Only problem is how everyone else joins his lectures and there are not enough seats.

I adore Dr. Y! He truly wants you to do well in his class. If you ever need help, he is there! His lectures are awesome too. 319K can be difficult at times but the profs and TAs are all there to help you. Please make sure to understand the reasoning behind why you do things in this class. It will really help your understanding of the material.

One of my favorite professors, super knowledgeable about everything. The weekly labs can catch up with you if you don't manage your time correctly, and make sure you pick a good lab partner so you don't end up doing all the labs yourself. If you study well for the exams and do the practice tests you will do well.
Dr. Yerraballi is an amazing lecturer. He explained everything clearly and deeply and conveyed it in an fun way. He was nice and considerate during office hours or before/after class. Good professor.

He is by far my favorite prof I have had so far, very helpful, teaches extremely well, theres a reason his lectures are packed when courses are standardized. I only got a B+ due to my lack of effort, he wants you to succeed and very obviously loves teaching.
Yerraballi posts all of his lectures & assignments online. His online lectures are high quality and enable you to do the class completely virtually. The assignments and tests were fair.

Dr. Y is one of the best instructors and lectures I've ever had. His teaching makes even the most obscure concepts simpler and easier to understand. Class is structured so that no single program/exam hurts you, but make sure to stay on top of all your work. Take him for 306 if you can!!!

Dr. Y is the absolute BEST choice for 306! He really cares and knows the key to our hearts is free cookies. Tests   (15%Midterm + 15%Final) could be prepared for with TA sessions and past exams. Programs (30%) should be started ahead of time and tested thoroughly. HW(20%) is very important so do well on the beginning ones. Overall great professor.

I thought that this class was fairly interesting even for someone like me who HATES LC3. Make sure that you think of EVERY possible test case on your programming assignments. It's very common for students to not prepare for extreme test cases and then get Bs on their programs. You'll definitely understand what I mean when you're in the class.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer. He draws out visuals and uses diagrams to complement his teaching. His OH are very helpful if you need help. Programs and homeworks carry a lot of weight, so make sure to do them ahead of time. Attending class is important as he will cover a lot of material and topics within one or two lectures. Best prof for 306 imo.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer, and all recordings are made available. Take detailed notes in class, because he goes extremely in depth. Quizzes are taken online asynchronously, and the grade is mostly determined by HW and programs. Make sure to start HW early, or you won't finish, many are extremely long and in depth.

Dr. Y has won awards for his teaching and it shows in 306. Yerraballi is a god, but beware of the programming assignments especially the last few. Go to office hours for homework questions and programming questions, he is very willing to help you learn.

Instructions can be unclear on homework and programs (programs are 30%, so a small instruction-caused mistake can damage your grade pretty heavily), but otherwise a fantastic professor. Lectures are informative, beginner-friendly, and always recorded. OH are helpful. This is the prof you want for 306.

Dr. Y was an impeccable prof, who went above and beyond in teaching the low-level aspect of computers in EE 306. His lectures were intriguing, and his teaching style was unequivocally the best of any teacher I have had in my life. Although homework and programs did take some time, the end knowledge gained was fulfilling. Yerraballer is the goat.

Dr. Y is a fantastic 306 professor! Great lectures, very accessible (both him and his TAs) to help outside of class.
He teaches very well, and if you put in the work, you'll have a solid understanding of 306 topics.

Highly recommend!

Professor Yerraballi is an excellent knowledgeable teacher. He presents his lectures as if he's writing down notes with us on a program he created. He remembers the faces of the students in his class and is a humorous individual that is also respected by his students and the university. Definitely recommend taking his class. Programs are difficult.

Dr. Y is absolutely amazing, take him for every class he teaches. His lectures are paced well and in-depth and his OH are amazing. He postponed homework for midterms, makes lectures enjoyable and fun, and is honestly just a great person. He teaches 306 as if you have no base in coding at all, exactly as it should be taught.

1. Brought us cookies upon receiving Outstanding Teaching Recognition

2. Dressed up for Halloween

3. Postponed homework because other ECE classes had midterms/tons of work

4. Drippy

5. Cracks jokes

Legend. I'd give him a 10/5 rating if I could. Take him for every class he offers. 

Yerraballer = godsend.

I love Dr. Yerraballi! 

His approachability and thorough explanations make 306 digestible. Although the programs and homework are challenging, he reviews critical concepts in lectures/OH. His pace in lectures makes them followable; consequently, catching up is less stressful. 

He dressed up for Halloween and once brought us cookies! GOAT
Won Teacher of the Year, Gave Us Cookies. W Professor
Amazing Prof, I would take him for every class he offers. Plus he gave us cookies when he won teacher of the year. Go to office hours he's so amazing.
Gave us cookies for winning teacher of the year, automatic 5

EE319K is a difficult class because it bridges hardware and software on a rudimentary level.
