Dr Y approaches the material in a straightforward and organized manner that attempts to convey the significant material. Unfortunately, the quizzes/labs are often outside the scope of lecture material; regardless, Dr Y is a solid choice. Beware the final.
EE319K is a very difficult class, so best option is to come to Dr. Yerraballi. He is the best at teaching. Period.

Just beware that they will constantly change the syllabus since they use a website. They don't update canvas to accurately represent you grade so beware of that. You may go into the final thinking you have a 97 but that isn't the case. Made the final in person because of "too many A's" so that was rude in my opinion. Had him for 306 and he was nice

319K wasnt a difficult class, it was just time consuming and there was a lot of non-complex material covered. 80% of the class is just basic programming and the rest is basic circuitry, data, logic, etc. The midterms are easy 100s if you have the programming side down and the quizzes are open everything. The labs are tedious and time consuming too
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yerraballi is one of my favorite professors at UT. The class focuses heavily on labs, but Dr. Yerraballi does a great job at making them approachable, and explains the concepts behind it well. During class, he's not the best with questions, but is very approachable outside of class if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the best choice when it comes to 306 professors. His grading is easy and straightforward and the exam at the end is very simple.

Yerraballi means well but his lectures are a bit dry. OS is valuable mainly in the context of systems programming (concurrency,atomicity, etc), but most time is spent on labs. While not difficult conceptually, these labs are a bit excessive (30+ hours avg) but will definitely improve your programming skills. Just invest in a good lab partner :)

Dr. Y is an amazing professor, really engaged in what he teaches and obviously enjoys it. The class is very nicely paced and no prior programming experience is neccesary, just the logical mindset needed for it. They don't call him Yerraballer for nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Y is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. I came into UT with no programming background or anything and he taught in a way that even those with no experience can learn quickly and do well in his class. His office hours were incredibly helpful and he will work with you one on one and don't be afraid to send him an email or the TAs !
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Yerraballi was a great professor for EE 319K. He explained things thoroughly for students in lectures, as well as being generally nicer on grading. However, this may have just been because the class was online.

Took class in Fall 2020. Great at making sure his students understand the concepts. Class had good structure, lectures were very organized. and always available for office hours. Heavy on the WEEKLY QUIZZES, HOMEWORK, AND LAB ASSIGNMENTS. Always study and prepare by reviewing lectures & textbooks. Lab assignments ARE ESSENTIAL TO UNDERSTANDING.

I've taken 3 of his classes (306, 319k, 461s) and every time I took one of them they were my favorite class that semester. His lectures are very relevant and easy to follow, and he is very easy-going and nice. In 319k and 461s make sure you pick a good partner though, because that matters a lot. He is very helpful if you need help on any projects.
He was great at making sure his students understand the concepts. Class had good structure. Was always available for office hours, he never leaves more confused after leaving office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor for 306, his lectures were very good and explained content well. He adapted his class to COVID by making easier weekly quizzes than larger tests. The only problem is that sometimes the HWs are ambiguous and the TA's aren't great, but he is very willing to fix stuff and clear doubts in office hours. Start programs early! Solid choice

Tough class if no previous experience but amazing lecturer. Also really cares about his students. Homeworks were pretty demanding and were assigned each week however they were usually directly over the lecture material. The notes from each class are saved as a pdf after each lecture, which helps to review for tests.

This guy is a yoga extraordinaire, an EE wizard, and a big-time Yeraballer. Oh yeah, he also literally built his own house by himself from scratch. Besides being a cool dude, he's a very good lecturer and focuses on making all concepts extremely clear. Take him if you can, I would definitely recommend it.

Professor Yerraballi does an amazing job at explaining concepts from a ground-up perspective. If you go to his office hours, he will clear up any confusion you have on material or the lab so GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. He's also a good guy in general and cares for his students, understanding how difficult this class is.

Good lecturer, even more amazing person. Going to office hours will guarantee you leaving with a deep understanding of whatever your question may have been. He truly cares about every single student. If you find yourself doing bad in the class, shoot him an email, schedule a meeting, or go to OH and find out for yourself!

Get. The. Book. The homework will not be related to the lectures, until after the homework is due. One of the major problems I've had with this class is the ambiguity of the problems. So if you are good at self learning, Yerraballi is a great professor. He's nice and explains what he does explain in a calm and concise manner

This class is hard, but you learn alot. Dr. Yerraballi is very fair with grading and the TA's work hard to help you understand. Lectures follow the book so read the book before exams to study. Make sure to choose a hardworking partner for the PINTOS projects, start early, and utilize office hours. I got  a 74 and that was a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I personally really like him as a person but his lectures are really unorganized. He doesn't understand that there are people who have little to no program experience prior to taking his course. His office hours are helpful and I would strongly recommend going to the drop in tutoring at the EER. You don't have much time to complete homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Caring teacher but goes off on tangents. Can be rude to some students sometime. Crowded office hours but that is because he really knows his stuff.

I honestly don't get the hype. His lectures are disorganized. Tests are unfair (near failing averages with no curve). Labs have unexpected test cases. If you look at grade distributions, make sure to only look at recent years, bc he clearly made the class much harder. Tough way to start college with his 306 Nice guy though, and will help you in OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture professor but doesn't reply to student emails. 20 people in office hours at any given time Exams inconsistent with the practice tests Syllabus says no programming experience expected, but that is definitely not the case. Other profs are worse though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Cares about students and wants them to succeed. Available for many office hours but don't wait for the last minute before a programming assignment.

His lectures could be hard to follow at times due to his teaching style, but he is generally a good professor. Nice and encourages people to ask questions. His tests aren't quite as easy as they used to be but are still pretty fair, and there are a couple of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Grading on the programs could be harsh.
He's literally the GOAT. I love this man. Class is so easy to follow. He teaches amazingly clearly. The assignments are straight forward. Always available. GOAT
His lectures are really unorganized but his tests are easy. He is also very rude to his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very rude and very mean to his students. His lectures are unorganized but tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Y is an awesome lecturer. He explains very clearly and clearly cares about his students understanding of the topics. The lectures relate directly to lab which I really liked. Labs do take a long time (probably averaged 10+ hrs per lab) but this is standard for this class regardless of the professor. Ebook and youtube vids offer help a lot too.
Loved this guy. He obviously cares about his students and clearly explains everything in lectures. Its definitely worth it to show up to class. My one piece of advice is to pick a good lab partner

He has a well-earned award for Nicest EE Faculty. He is very helpful during office hours and his lectures go over everything you need to know for the labs. The tests are standardized across professors, but his lectures teach you enough to do well in them.

A god. He cares so much about students. His lectures are so clear, the labs he gives are so helpful, and the exams are challenging yet fair. He is the best 319K prof in my opinion, and overall I learned more in this class than I have in any other class this semester. Labs take forever though. Expect 6-20 hours to work on lab, depending on the week

Dr. Yerraballi is a pretty solid professor. His lectures can be a bit boring, but they're straightforward and easy to follow. He's available outside of class and is helpful in office hours. I would recommend him for EE319K for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: LC-3 programs are difficult sometimes. I read the book to understand the concepts, but for me it was hard to piece it all together. Taking Dr. Y again for 319k ready to work harder than I ever have before. Hopefully ARM and C with resonate with me more than LC-3. Very caring and courageous professor. Read the book before lecture it helps.

Dr. Y is a great lecturer who teaches in a way to make material understandable. Although I have had prior knowledge for a lot of topics in class, the pace is set at a speed viable for new learners as long as you put the time to understanding. Make sure to show up to class as his lectures go over everything you need to know.

This class is very dangerous. It is easy to pick a partner who will do all the work, but you will fall behind and suffer. Y makes note of that throughout the semester, and he is absolutely correct. He generally does a good job of explaining things clearly and effectively, though he is not the most helpful guy in office hours bc he's always swamped.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The best lecturer I've had in college, he does a very good job of teaching concepts and using visuals to help explain everything. This course is lab-heavy and you will need to be very knowledgeable in coding to do well on exams! DO NOT pick a partner that does all the work, you will cheat yourself out of the learning process.

Dr. Yerraballi is a great explainer. I took both him and Dr. Telang and I can say that he explains the material much more clearly. His labs are also easier in my opinion. Will definitely take him for EE319K

Great professor that cares about his students. Dr. Y teaches in a natural way where he introduces material when you need to know it and writes down his own notes and visuals as he goes. The only possible negative is he is soft-spoken so some of my friends had trouble staying awake. I enjoyed his class so much I'm taking him again for 319K.
Great teacher, very helpful and clear presentation of information. Super helpful during office hours, but they get really crowded

Yerraballi is a wonderful professor! His lectures are clear and straightforward, his tests aren't very difficult, and he's very nice. He genuinely cares about his students. I liked him a lot and I'm taking him again for 319K! Definitely my favorite professor of the semester.

Dr. Y was great for 306. I think he is probably the best professor I have ever had at UT my first two years here. He teaches clearly and drills concepts well into your head. I think the experience overall was great-- he didn't count our final exam if it hurt our grade. He is a really nice guy and is always willing to help you.

Although Professor Yerraballi is a great teacher, he wasn't in charge of the EE319K course as of Spring 2016 (that responsibility fell to Dr. John Valvano, a very intelligent but scattered and disorganized man). Due to this, the quality of the course suffered - it was difficult to parse what was actually important to do in order to learn.

He's a great professor who cares about his students. Attending lectures is not mandatory but important for success. The labs were time-consuming but interesting and rewarding. I found the tests to be difficult, but coding isn't my strong suit. Yerraballi and the TAs were super helpful.

This class was not hard, but just took a lot of time with the labs. It's been standardized now, so everyone takes the same tests. Yerraballi overall is just an awesome guy. I had him for EE 306 as well, and he  knows me by name. I always visited his office every week, and people are out the door waiting for him. Take him.

Yerraballi is great at explaining things, if you can follow his messy notes. However, the class is mainly lab-based, and most of the time what you cover in class isn't helpful to complete them until the day before, and the textbook takes several hours of deciphering. Going to your TA's office hours is your best bet, but go early!

Dr. Y's a great professor and willing to help. This class is a lot of work. Get ready for many late-night codings. The tests are doable, but make sure you know the material well. It's very easy to fall behind.

Dr. Yerraballi (Yerraballer) is probably the best of my professors so far at UT. He's clear about his explanations in lecture, and won't hesitate to help you out with your problemquestions in office hours. He graciously made the final optional if your midterm scores were good enough to make your desired grade.  1010 would take again.
Yerraballi is great, and the class really isn't very difficult. Just keep up with your assignments and read the textbook (it's extremely helpful in understanding the material).

Dr. Y is an okay lecturer. This semester however he rushed through most of the material. The only people who understood the stuff in class were people with previous programming experience and who already knew the bulk of the material before taking the class.  He's willing to help in office hours but there's always 15+ people in line ahead of you.

Dr. Y was a decent lecturer; he got off to a slow start, then sped it up way too fast bc he was behind schedule. I stopped going to lectures after midterms, and I got a solid A in the class. Just read the book, do your programming assignments, and do your best. He even made final optional for us, so he's a nice guy. Office hours always too full.

This semester he and valvano traded off lectures in our class, which was a little distracting. Yerraballi is a great lecturer, and is fairly organized in his presentations. 319K is a swift moving course, and the labs take around 10-15 hours a week at the end of the semester.Prepare to pull all nighters debugging and ripping your hair out, cheers!

Dr. Bill's a great teacher for those w/o strong calc foundations!!! I didn't use the textbook much outside of class b/c Sadun's videos in Quest made me feel prepared for lectures; the only thing I disliked was discussion. You're put in a group of 2-3, & each receive the same grade, so if your partners don't show up or are unengaged...good luck :')

Dr.Bill is amazing! The only professor I have ever had that actually thought math. He explains why we are doing something, instead of just telling us to do it. I have taken a class with him twice and each time was good. If you go to class and submit work on time you will be fine.

He's a good professor, he cares, and very nice. He emphasizes deep understanding. Lectures are somewhat helpful, but he did go on tangents often, so I did most of my learning outside of class. There's lots of quest HW/LM, but we got drops and I feel like the textbook is optional to buy. Also keep in mind he doesn't really do curves/extra credit.

Bill genuinely cares about his students. He wants you to actually learn the material and often goes on inspirational tangents about life. Unfortunately, his philosophy also includes an exorbitant amount of homework, up to 70 questions per week. If you actually do all the homework yourself, the quizzes and exams will be a breeze.

Profs explanation of key concepts was usually confusing. It was often more straightforward to read the textbook rather than attend lecture, but in-class quizzes make this a dangerous game. HWs were VERY long (~ 70 questions) and consistent with the textbook, but quizzes and exams were more about knowing the smaller details rather than computations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wwhile I enjoy his lectures, sometimes he lashes out on the class and lectures about not missing class or using AI and feels hostile, but he means well. The exams can be tricky but in argument, it's linear algebra. He does ramble a lot and gives life lessons, and he tries to teach so we understand fundamentally but it can be confusing at times

I've never felt so less than in a class. I don't understand why I'm expected to self-teach calculus? When students raised concerns about not learning in class, he stated we'd be lucky to learn 10% of the material during lectures. He tries to be inspirational, which isn't helpful when everyone's burnt out and tired of pushing for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bill's class was actually very great. His tests are not bad at all and this coming from someone who never took calc. Only thing is that the review exams he gives before the exams are a tad bit misleading, so study everything thoroughly.

I had never taken cal before & his was class was doable for me. Lectures aren't too helpful so I did find myself teaching myself at times, nothing too complicated. The mini projects/hwk/worksheets are all okay. He's very understanding & is willing to help you. I did okay in the exams, ended up taking the final & even that was a breeze, love bill!

I love bill-he takes the time to learn every student's name, and is SO inspirational and genuinely a great teacher. However, if u haven't taken calc u have to go to every class to learn since he doesn't record lectures and there is quite a lot of assignments but nothing crazy. Overall he knows his stuff and is understanding - EASY EXAMS

If you have the option to take him, you should. He grades easily and is kind. He cares about a deeper understanding of calc, but at the end of the day, it's up to you how you want to solve his problems. Exams are moderately easy. Bill is amazing!

WantEasyA?-dont take him. Although hard, this has been my favorite class so far and I truly believe this class taught me how to (actually)learn. Bill truly cares about his students,is always open to questions,and inspires us to learn to think critically by truly understanding concepts instead of just memorizing. AmazingProfessor+WorthTheCourseRigor

Bill is kind but goes off track sometimes. Lectures are very eye-opening/profound. He teaches calc in a way where you understand how it connects to other concepts thru the semester. But around the end of sem he stopped lecturing the way we were used to and grades started dropping. The textbook recommended didn't help much, tutoring lowk mandatory..

Do not like how he teaches AT ALL. Overcomplicates simple concepts and he be doing too much. He is very kind and has  generous grading policies. Other than that I had to teach myself the concepts,textbook did not help either, HWs were very long and tbh not very helpful. If u learn better with a straight forward teaching style I wouldn't recommend.

This class was one of the most exhausting experiences I've had. I left lectures more confused than when I walked in. Please notice that none of his positive reviews praise his teaching — they praise his personality. He's kind, but the class itself is disorganized, overwhelming, and hard to learn from. If you're looking for clarity, it's not here.

Bill is kind, but his teaching is chaotic. Lectures constantly derail into random tangents, turning simple math into confusion. Homework is endless and rarely helpful. I had a strong math background yet felt lost. I was in the trenches every week, fighting for my life and self-teaching entire units just to survive.

He makes sure all his students understand the content deeply and goes very slowly in lectures. However, he has extremely long homework of up to 90 questions every 2 weeks. He's a nice guy and a great professor, especially if you ask questions. Generous grading policy as well.

Bill is an awesome calculus professor. The class itself isn't hard at all, but if you've taken calculus before in HS you will be bored. He teaches it different and often gets sidetracked which can be a little frustrating but the material itself is very easy. His midterms are only 4 questions but he releases a one pager of whats guaranteed to be on
The best teacher i have ever had. Truly one of the most caring humans i have met, he goes above and beyond for any student that asks.

peak professor, highkey goat. very caring and passionate about student success, empowerment, and understanding. 3 exams each with 2 parts, indiv. (60%) and group (40%). very clear and concise explanations of concepts, and easy to approach. very kind and respectful professor. literally best professor ive taken, genuinely kindhearted.

Really caring prof. Dr. Bill moves through the material at a good pace, and I've never felt overworked or stressed about this class. He's very clear on what you need to know, and focuses on understanding rather than brute computation. Lot of HW (30ish questions / week), so find a study-buddy to check with. Overall, take him: he's great.

Prof. Wolesensky is very good at going slow and making sure you understand the fundamental concepts of the material. However, sometimes it seemed almost too slow/repetitive. He has a tendency to give the same tangential speech every lecture about how you should approach learning. The homeworks are unbearably long, usually 50-80 drill questions.
he overwhelm my baby

He prefers to move slow and ensure deep understanding of topics. Made me feel encouraged to learn and ask questions which is a first for me at UT. He did assign a lot of homework but often times would drop off sections as he wouldn't get to lecture that content in class. He empowered me as a student and I put effort into his class.

The best math teacher I have ever had. Has such a big heart. So caring. He would make me tear up because he was so sweet and pure. I learned so much and he was so eager to help. He was so down to earth and I will definitely stay in contact with him. He truly cared about his students and their success. Extremely selfless and thoughtful.

This guy is the best. I learned so much about linear algebra, and so much more about life (seriously) and learning. He opens himself up and gives you the greatest lessons on believing you can learn anything. Onto the real-real. I went to class, but LIVED off that textbook. Textbook's basic concepts + Bill's examples = math magic.

Dr. Bill is a great lecturer and a kind professor! He really cares about all his students and explains concepts with a lot of clarity. The only thing is that HWs are EXTREMELY long, but he makes up for it with his generous grading distribution. Highly recommend taking this class.

Dr. Wolesensky wants you to succeed and will challenge you in the course. He truly cares about his students' long-term success. Many students wish for a positive outcome but aren't willing to work hard and develop relationships in class with their peers and professor. It will pay off if you keep attending class, smiling, and asking questions.

He is a nice person but his class is terrible. Grades based basically only on exams which are multiple choice only, no curve & no extra credit at all. concepts are not hard but some questions are way too hard. would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bill is the best professor I've had by far. He is so positive and caring. Math is my least fav subject and I looked forward to his class every day. Work is very manageable... ask questions and actually do the hw! It's test heavy but he gives practice tests that are very similar to tests, so it's really fair! Would take him 100x over :)

I LOVE BILL!! This professor was such a breath of fresh air. You can tell he loves what he does. He is such a caring man and will take the time to get to know you and teach the material until you understand it. And I feel like that is very lacking in some professors at UT. I will always be so grateful for having Bill during my Freshman year.

TAKE PROFESSOR WOLESENSKY! He's an amazing professor and an even better human. He is extremely non-judgmental and always compliments his students. The HWs can take time but they're perfect prep for tests, which aren't hard. Quizzes are easy too. He answers any HW and concept doubts in office hours. You won't get a better linear algebra professor.
Best professor I have had. GOAT

Truly cares about every single one of his students. Lectures and discussion sections are soooo helpful, and going to office hours is highly encouraged even if you aren't struggling because Dr. Bill is just awesome. Amazing and kind professor who is truly passionate about calculus. Calculus is a forest.

Nice guy but he tests you on stuff that aren't even in the textbook and ONLY covers in class once or twice. His grading on the quiz is also very misleading in comparison to the test so the first exam threw me off with his significantly harsher grading. Overall not bad, but wouldn't take again bc he js doing TOO much for a linear algebra class

Wolenensky was the professor that you could tell he cared about his students. He was great at explaining things deeply and effectively. His tests were not too bad. The only complaint I have is that the homework were sometimes extremely long, but they did help prepare you for the tests. As long as you go to class and do HW this class should be easy.

Professor Wolesensky is the best professor I've ever had. He made calculus genuinely enjoyable, and I looked forward to attending his class. He cares deeply about both students' learning and their grades, offering relatively easy tests and providing ample support.

Goated Professor. I could not ask for a better teacher when it comes to calculus. I suck at calc and Bill still pulled me up to an A. He also makes learning actually enjoyable. His lectures are super engaging and tests are never the grade you get. You can go up to him during office hours and he would just give you 5 extra points. Freshmen are lucky

DR BILL IS AWESOME. he seriously cares and believes in the success of all of his students. be ready for lots of homework though. he is so wise and knowledgeable, there is no reason to fail this course.

Dr. Bill was amazing!! Definitely take him if you can, he is the OG and is the one who made M408Q, along with the textbook author. His lectures are highly detailed, he took things slowly and fully explained things, including deriving formulas. Tests are not difficult and easier than homework. Great and chill guy all around.

Prof. wolesensky is truly the best professor I have had all four years here at UT austin. He is genuinely so kind and caring and wants all of his students to succeed. Do not be afraid to ask for help or literally anything at all because he is more than happy to help you and wants you to get an A. Highly recommend!!!!

Bill is a great guy, and wants everyone to succeed. Lots of assignments and group projects, but an enjoyable experience overall.

Attend his lectures!

Dr. Bill is the GOAT. I had a rough math background, but I still got an A because Bill explains well & welcomes questions, even if he goes on tangents sometimes. Individual HW prepares for exams even if bit long. Even if you do badly or miss work, he drops lowest assignment scores & one exam if you do better on the final. Also very understanding!
TAKE BILL IF YOU CAN! He is an awesome professor who truly cares about his students and learning. If you attend class and discussions, this class should not be challenging.

Dr. Bill is a passionate professor who wants students to succeed. The class is challenging but manageable with engagement. Homework is time-consuming but helpful. Unstuck ai is a great study tool alongside the free textbook.

GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! Office hours *will* save your grade if you aren't good at math, and he will be very lenient about things so long as you're very respectful. Class is hard but manageable. Assignment heavy. HW are long. Tests are short but hard. Genuinely of of the nicest people I know, he will take an interest in your life outside of class.

Dr Bill is an incredible professor, he cares very deeply about students and wants to see us succeed. He's very passionate about calculus and has a focus on understanding the material and making connections, referring to calculus concepts often as a "forest" not as "trees". This class is challenging; huge homeworks, mini-projects, but DrBill helps.

Dr. Bill is hands down the greatest professor of all time. His tests are not to be joked around with they are pretty hard, with exam 2 being the hardest, but he gives partial credit to make up for difficult tests. He is very knowledgeable and without a doubt cares about his students and their learning more than any other professor at UT.

An A is very attainable if you participate. He is a very reasonable guy. 3 exams and final (1 dropped). Not exam heavy: discussions and HW are worth a good amount of grade. His lectures are sometimes unhelpful, because he goes very into detail and won't cover much. He drops 1 HW and 4 WS if you do the final. Extra credit. Lots of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wolesensky is a sweet guy and I enjoyed his lectures. But, he is not lenient at all over anything, and if u ask for an extension FOR ANY REASON(even 4 serious reasons)he will say no. Here's what got me though: IF YOU WANT THINGS DROPPED YOU MUST TAKE THE FINAL (final is optional but not really). He's so sweet but super traditional academically.

Very sweet man and grades exams relatively easily, but I feel like we never actually talk about calculus. Would 100% recommend taking the him if you have some prior knowledge of calculus, but if you are brand new to calc and relying on explanation I wouldn't. Assigns time consuming and challenging hw that doesn't really help for test.

So grateful I had him in my first year. Learned lots of valuable lessons, not just calc. Dr. Bill is super understanding and kind, and truly cares about his students' success. His assignments are very fair and his exams are very reflective of content learned in discussion/homework. My only regret is not getting to know him on a more personal level.

He makes his curriculum much harder then the other professors for M408Q. Would not recommend. Assigns inane amounts of work compared to other professors and makes tests harder. Nice guy but his course is too overwhelming for what it should be.

BEST PROFESSOR I've had so far. He cares so much about his students, and recommend 1000%. I couldn't express how good of a professor he is! Of course, this class is not "easy" by any means, you have to put in the work outside of class but an A is definitely manageable. He is so lenient, and grade distributions are fair.

Bill was an amazing professor for my first semester at UT; when one could not possibly be more stressed, his class was a welcome reminder that the faculty care about our success and are real people with whom we can develop connections. If you attend lectures, pay attention, and complete the worksheets and homework, you will get an A.

Not mandatory attendance. Lectures cover a lot of questions from the individual homework. Discussions are based off the graded worksheets. Learn from the weekly 2-3 questlinks (textbook and video style with 2-7 graded questions). Textbook is easy to read and where the homework questions are from. Professor wants you to succeed so put in the work.

Dr.Bill teaches calculus in a different way than you may have learned previously, but he does it well with so much passion. You can clearly tell he wants all of his students to succeed. The homework is sometimes challenging, but he gives you the support you need, and the tests are always fair.

Professor Bill was an amazing teacher who truly cared about his students. He is super kind and a very generous grader too. His tests were easy and graded for partial credit. The homework assignments are a bit long, so it's best to work with a few people. Overall, I loved taking this class and learning from Professor Bill!
Good

Dr. Bill is an amazing professor for calculus. He not only is very knowledgeable, but he is very supportive and accommodating. He teaches his classes step-by-step which is super helpful when I had no prior knowledge of calculus. I definitely recommend attending his office hours because he is super nice. He also grades very kindly!
very easy, great professor. You do not need to know calculus for this class

Although math has always been a difficult subject for me, I enjoyed having Bill as my professor! He truly cares about your success and stands out as the most compassionate instructor I've had. Don't slack off you'll definitely want to read the textbooks, practice the problems, and go to office hours. You'll make an A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is more of studying on your own. There are biweekly homeworks that stress you out because he only grades 4 of them but there are at least 15 questions that take hours to do. People give him great ratings but all his lectures do not help on the homework. Also, get ready to code with Matlab and read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
dr Bill will teach us that visually really well and I enjoyed his lecture style. His exams were group based with an individual component. It is not necessary to read the textbook but if you read along with the textbook then the course is extremely good because he follows along with each individual theorem. 


Take him. You'll learn a lot.

Dr. Wolesensky is definitely one of the best professors at UT Austin, and without a doubt the best Math professor, so I would highly encourage you to take his class if you have the opportunity. Do not skip class, it will only hurt you. Put the effort into the class, it will be tough at times but you will certainly enjoy the reward in the end.

You will never find anyone else like him in UT. He is an amazing character and an even more amazing professor. Most of your learning is done through the homeworks given and he provides A LOT of resources for you to use in order to be successful. He is the most caring professor on campus; HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

3 midterms & final, but final was easy and even replaced our 2 lowest midterms which imo is very generous. Quest HWs and LMs every week that can be challenging but Bill is very helpful in OHs. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but I'd still try to go to them since he explains concepts and potential exam questions really well in class. Loved him.

Dr. Bill is such an amazing person. Respectful and inspiring, he really cares for each one of his students, and also gives great life advice. He is also so nice and approachable. Go to every lecture and take good notes, because he will make you really understand calculus. Do the home works well because they are good test prep. Take Dr. Bill!!

Bill was one of the best professors I've had. He explains things very thoroughly and makes sure that everyone understands. Attendance isn't mandatory but GO ANYWAY. You will be behind. He makes lectures fun, and he has good life advice along with it. He truly wants you to succeed and will get to know you as a person. 100000% recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If given the option, TAKE HIS COURSE. The class uses Quest for around 90% of the assignments, so make sure to keep up with homework, and learning modules. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would highly recommend going to them since Professor Bill fills in the gaps from the learning module and just explains concepts really well.

Wolesensky is easily my favorite professor at UT and is the best I've had so far at explaining confusing concepts. I had to drop my calc with Mills last semester so having a good prof this time around made all the difference. This class is straightforward and tests are very similar to lectures/homework, just need to stay on top of quest modules.

GO TO LECTURE and you will do amazing. Ask him questions on Ed Discussion, he will be happy to explain. He's seriously the best professor I've had here. He's so nice and really does care about his students. Final is optional. If you take the final he drops several assignments and replaces your lowest test score. Highly recommend Dr. Bill!

Dr. Bill changed my entire outlook on math. I've struggled immensely with math since elementary school, but he breaks it down so wonderfully and really stresses the importance of understanding what you're doing. Exams are incredibly straightforward. HW can get long and time-consuming, but he's super communicative and will help you if you're stuck.

Bill is a wonderful person, but if you haven't taken calculus already, this class can be difficult. He extended every homework assignment for us and would work with you during office hours or before/after class to answer any questions. Some of the assignments were very difficult, but there was group work and many assignments were dropped at the end

Changed my entire attitude toward math because of this man. He will make you feel like you belong in any classroom, even if you come in completely rusty or lost on the subject material. Thanks to his teaching methods, I've learned HOW TO learn and feel confident that I'll find success at UT. Already registered to take him again next semester.

Lectures were attendance mandatory but were always very engaging and slow-paced for comprehension. Homework was assigned via Quest but were always manageable. Not too assignment heavy, maybe at most twice or three times a week. Exams are in-person and easy as long as you understand the content. Was always trying to motivate and inspire students

I took his M408Q class spring 2022 semester and he was amazing! The most understanding and caring professor. Wants his students to learn and succeed in his class. The HW was a but lengthy but doable and the test were not bad. 3 tests and if you had a 93 or higher you did not have to take the final! There needs to be more professors like Dr. Bill!

Bill's class is truly amazing! As long as you listen through lectures, ask questions, and attend your discussion it is very doable. He goes into the semester treating everyone as if they have no prior knowledge of calculus and does his best to go into depth.
Dr.Bill was an amazing professor, would highly recommend anyone to take him. He is very flexible as long as you communicate with him. Super sweet guy

Best freaking math professor at UT, especially for freshman business calc. Cannot explain how genuine Dr. Bill is and he truly wants to see his students succeed. I do not find math fun but he made class fun and engaging. He teaches more conceptually then caring about all the formulas, which I personally liked more. Such a nice grader. TAKE HIM.

Bill really made me love calculus despite my history of hating math. He taught in a concise manner that made sense, was available for OH, and genuinely cares about his students. Tests were easy as long as you did the homework, mini projects with other group members were simple as long as you have a good group. HW is tedious, do it early.

Bill is amazing. He is going to remind you again and again how much he cares, but he means that sincerely. Teaches calc in a way that you'll be able to keep up if you've never taken a single calc course. Very willing to be available for office hours and extra help. Take him if you can!
Really cares for his students and really wants them to learn. Definitely take him if you have not taken calculus before.

Dr. Bill is an incredible professor. In STEM, it can be hard to find professors who actually care about their students, but Bill does. He always has a smile on his face when he's teaching, and he's so kind when speaking to students in class. Plenty of EC opportunities, gives lots of feedback, and always extends due dates. MUST take.

Bill is super caring and although the class can get tough at times, he is extremely fair and approachable. I can tell he wants the best for his students. Although the class is meant to be "entry-level", I would definitely recommend having some background in calculus. If not, you'll just have to work harder.

Professor Wolesensky made his class feel welcoming and addressed every single student with great care and respect. His lectures were very detailed and it was obvious that he delivered them with a lot of passion, which made his class that much more enjoyable.

Dr. Bill truly cares about the success of his students. His grading is clearly set and fair. He is literally one of the nicest most genuine people I have met. His lectures are more real-world based and he loves telling stories. 3 midterm tests worth 15% each with the possibility of opting out of final if you have a 93%. 100% would take class again.

Prof BIll is awesome. Super caring and loves what he teaches, always willing to help students if they need it. There was a LOT of work, something due pretty much every day, but Prof Bill is very understanding and knows that we have a lot of other work in other classes as well. Not the easiest class but helpful.
Very helpful during office hours! Grades fairly and is a great person and professor.
Amazing professor!! So kind and receptive to his students needs.
Luv this man
He's good take the the class

Dr. Wolesensky was awesome, easy professor overall! He allowed us to take individual exams at most 25 hours, which was great. He even wanted you to understand basic ideas of analysis. However, I wish there was bit less groupwork since we lose bit of learning, doesn't work well on zoom. He could also respond to emails better, faster. TA grades hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the best. He is the definition of gentlemen.

Bill is by far the nicest and most caring professor I have had during my time at UT. He truly cares for each student and truly ensures that we understand the material. He never makes us feel dumb when asking questions. He is very understanding and has extended several deadlines due to COVID and the winter storm. I love this man

Easily the most accommodating and respectable professor I've had at UT. Truly cares about his students and will 100% work with you if you need any extensions or help. The class itself is heavy as there are worksheets & learning modules every tues/thurs, 6 homeworks, and 3 midterms but overall basically impossible to not get an A. Take him for sure!
Best professor I've had at UT. Understanding, caring, passionate, and knowledgeable. Great guy and really wants to see you succeed.

Dr. Bill is hands down the best math teacher I have ever had. If you struggle in math classes, take Dr. Bill. He explains calculus concepts in a way that makes sense, and is willing to work with you to improve your grade. As long as you try your hardest in his class, it will reflect on your grade.

Greatest math teacher/professor I've ever had. Honestly the GOAT. For my class, he allowed people with a 93+ average not take the final exam. A lot of homework and worksheet assignments, which are annoying to do because you have to take a photo of your work and upload it all to your computer/canvas, but the hard work definitely pays off.

Easy A if you have taken Calc before in HS, Gives a fair amount of HW IHW ( bimonthly), HW (biweekly), Group Projects (4-5), Quest (1-2x week). Drops LOTS of grades and gives out extra credit. Is immensely understanding, patient, and generous. Our class really loved him. Wonderful professor!

I loved Dr. Bill. I took Business Calculus this past semester, and he was extremely helpful. He wants his students to do well. Homework is hefty but very helpful for tests. Not difficult to get an A+ if you do all your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Bill is definitely one of the best professors at UT. He is very interested in the success of his students and has a clear passion for the material, which makes it easier to learn. Additionally, he is extremely supportive, encouraging, and patient. Whenever I needed help, he is always there. I would miss his classes next year.
He will 100% be the best professor you will have, especially in a subject like Math. He has a way of simplifying what would usually be complex and intimidating concepts to something anyone can do.

Dr Bill is amazing. He truly cares about learning and understanding. He makes himself super available to students when they need help and always goes above and beyond to answer questions. He also never assumes you should know something and make ask questions a very comfortable thing! Im not the kind of person to leave a review, but Hes that good

I took this class online and while his lecture style rly wasnt the best for me, this was def an easy A- especially if youve taken calculus before. LOTS of homework .... so much homework... but hes rly understanding of that. Just stay on top of your work and hes rly easy on grading
Bill has been literally the best professor I have ever taken at UT. He cares for every student and knows how to teach his audience amazingly. Please take him and experience a true UT Professor.

I took Bill last year and he was an amazing professor. He cares about his students deeply and is willing to help you as much as possible. In terms of his Calculus class: it is very lecture heavy, and you definitely have to put in some study time to learn the material. He makes his lectures fun, interactive and interesting- and he's the best.
