reviews.comment: Don't take as a summer course. Tbh, the professor should be prepared to teach and prepare students efficiently in the given time frame. Material/assignments provided are informative, but require lots of wasted energy and are mostly copy-paste from textbooks that you could just read and study (cause you do it anyways.) Hopefully it improves.

To add on to previous reviews, it just seems like this course was not prepared in thought for the time frame of summer courses. Yes summer courses are fast paced, but this course seems unreasonable. TAs have not been very useful so far, and lectures/discussions are behind when assignments are due. This class is more self-study than being taught.

Taken during summer. 1) High workload, strict deadlines, low leniency, short working time, strict grading =bad combo. 2) Allocated test time is not reasonable given time needed to answer 20 questions + 3 long FRQs, honor lock browser only wastes more time and makes you anxious. 3) material is not hard, but workload is. 4) lectures are like textbook

ngl this class has been hard. I'd say the exams are really unfair. Each exam has 23 questions and 3 free-response questions, with each free-response worth 10 points—and they're tough. For the first exam, I couldn't even finish it because each question asked for so much. There's a lot of homework, and honestly, her lectures aren't that great.

This class is straight up unreasonable for summer. Felt like a slap in the face. Assignments were long as hell, barely any explanation, and a test immediately after. It's overloaded, rushed, and borderline disrespectful of people's time. Dropped it immediately. Don't waste your summer on this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class during the summer. heavy workload. Summer class started on June 5th on Thursday and we already have a test over 2 chapters on June 9th which is 4 days later. A lot of homework and each would take I guarantee you 2+ hours to finish. And 2 quizzes right after and a test and the test was so hard.

Was in her summer online class for two days before I dropped it. Seems like she just reused assignments from the regular semester. We had a test on Monday (class started Thursday) and 8 assignments due on or before that day, most of which take at least 3+ hours. Gave a 3 because I didn't take her the full time. Maybe she'll improve?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably harder than Engler but overall such a free A. She gives infinite extra credit. Ignore all other past ratings about her being hard. There's busy work but genuinely difficult not to get an A if you do the assignments. No lie don't play with me. I never read the textbook.

Lots of busywork. Expect 2-3 homework assignments a week, along with weekly in-class quizzes. None of the material is really very difficult. Zhong is a decent lecturer, but her accent makes her hard to understand sometimes. Grading is very lenient. There is a lot of extra credit - I got bumped from a 94 to a 102.2 before the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhong is a great professor, and she truly cares about her students' success. The class was  overwhelming at first but got better with time. She adds the extra credit at the end which boosted my grade. Exams can be specific but are doable especially with the cheat sheet. It's not a blow off class, but if you work hard, she will take care of you!

I truly think she deserves a better rating. I got mostly B's on every test and after receiving all extra credit and lowest grade drop I had a 99 in the class before the final (final was easy and you could use cheat sheet). Might seem intimidating at first because she does give lots of hw, but you get used to it and it gets easier. Take her!!!

Dr. Zhong is an amazing professor who wants you to succeed! She gives you tons of extra credit and even though there is a lot of homework majority of it is completion based. Her lectures could be better but her slides are very informative and if you just study those you should be good! You also get a cheat sheet for every exam.
Just terrible. Insane amount of homework that is just busy work and teaches you nothing. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhong is the most kindest professor ever! She listens to feedback well, drops your lowest grades, and allows a cheat sheet for every exam, even the final. There is a ton of extra credit too! At first, it may seem overwhelming with the amount of homework/in-class work, but it lessens as the semester goes by and is truly not that bad.

She honestly was my favorite professor. She gives plenty of extra credit, is easy to approach for questions, and genuinely cares. She also drops the lowest grades. Her test are mostly basic questions and her review session are super helpful. Her quiz and test questions are very similar. I 100% would take her again.

Do not listen to all the bad ratings she is an amazing professor and cares about how her students perform in the class. The tests aren't hard and she drops a test, quiz, and other grades. My grade went from a 92 to a 102 in a night because of the drops. If you put in the work its very easy to get an A.

Dr. Zhong is one of the easiest professors I've had. She listens to feedback and has very low stakes quizzes and exams. There are so many extra credit opportunities, my grade went up 10 points overall. Drops a test and an assignment from every category, and very sweet overall.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I ended with like a 98%. She does her level best to "meet you in the middle." The class is hard (lectures are mandatory for instapoll n boring), but you'll probably end up with a good grade if you care enough w extra credit. My advice is to go through the study guide and make a mind map for every learning objective. TA's are p bad for this class.

Lots of extra credit. Boosted my grade by 10 points overall. 1 page cheat sheet on every test, including the final. Tests are 50 questions, multiple-choice, online, and in class. Final was 80, same format. Strong accent, you get used to it. TA discussions were optional extra credit. My favorite teacher as of writing this

Dr. Zhong is kind, receptive to feedback, and provides LOTS of extra credit. Her exams are on the easier side plus you get to make a cheat sheet! Yes, there is "a lot" of homework, but much of it is easy/completion and doesn't take a lot of time anyway. Biology consists of learning large amounts of material, but she made it manageable and fun!

So caring and funny, her accent isn't a problem at all; she's def my favorite professor this year. SO much extra credit, cheat sheet on exams (all multiple choice), and lots of questions to practice with. She's also super responsive to feedback, more so that any other professor (she actually spends class time analyzing our course evaluations haha).

Don't listen to the bad RMP reviews!!!Dr. Zhong is a great professor and for most should be an easy A! She has a lot of work for he class but it  makes you more prepared for exams and boosts your grade. She gives so much extra credit and drops that by the end of the semester my grade went from an 85 to a 99. She genuinely cares for her students!

The bad reviews on here are so dramatic. She gives lots of HW, but as the semester progressed the load got lighter. At the end she gives drops and A LOT of bonus points to boost your grade. Tests and quizzes are all MCQ and very straightforward. You also literally get a cheat sheet for every test. Don't be intimidated by her she's so sweet!
Super funny, and I literally went up a whole letter grade with extra credit alone. Take her! Other bad rmp are actual haters.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It felt intimidating to be in Dr. Zhong's class at first, but after the first post-exam survey, you can tell that she's trying her best so that you can succeed. The class isn't difficult at all and only requires reading slides before lectures. Exams are MCQs and can be very specific, but they're manageable. Overall, she's a great professor. ;)

she is nice but the class is so overwhelming omg
BUT your grade will go up like 5+ points at the end of the semester so if you can hang on then you can get a decent grade. Won't destroy your GPA but will definitely stress you out.
I think to do really well you have to study like two hours a day or something idk i studied so much and ended with a B

Genuinely was scared of taking Professor Zhong but she's amazing! She listens clearly to students' feedback and really cares about our learning. There were a lot of assignments but that was adjusted after the first feedback survey. She is so sweet and cute and funny! I attended some of Buskirk's lectures but imo Zhong worked better for me.

Dr. Zhong is very sweet and you can tell she's passionate about both biology and her students. While the class is heavily lecture/textbook based & grading on some assignments is strict, her tests are straightforward except for a few questions. She has lots of extra credit opportunities so doing RGA's and going to discussions will only help you.

Dr. Zhong is a great lecturer & cares about her students. She genuinely reads and considers the midsemester feedback/course evaluations and wants to find ways to improve as a professor to foster a positive environment for her students. Take the other ratings with a grain of salt. As long as you are willing to study outside of class, you'll be okay.
Terrible. Do not take her class. All the bad reviews here are very accurate

amazing lecturer! truly cares about her students. don't know why the rmp so low, ppl jus hating bc they aint put in the work. she gives a lot of extra credit, so it's easy to boost your grade. tests all mcq, study the slides, know your stuff n u got it. one test is dropped out of the three midterms. take her. she's not as bad as the rmp is.

Dr. Zhong's RMP is not accurate of the teacher she is. She is really chill, gives a lot of extra credit, and the tests are really similar to the practice quizzes and in-class quizzes. Easy A since 1 test is dropped and you get a cheat sheet per test. Def recommend taking her.

Dr. Zhong is such a caring professor, and she genuinely wants her students to do well. She's always willing to answer questions outside of class. Yes, there is a lot of assignments, but they really don't take that much time. The practices quizzes are great prep for exams, which are all multiple choice. Put in the work, and you WILL get an A.

Professor Zhong is a great lecturer, very knowledgeable, and is very caring towards her students. Whoever is saying her accent is hard to understand is a hater, you get used to her accent! Her exams are all multiple choice and the questions are based off of a question bank, don't listen to anyone hating she's really great as long as you try! :)

TAKE HER!!! As long as you put effort you will be solid. Weekly quizzes are directly from her slides and from instapoll. Youre allowed a cheat sheet on the exam and trust me this class is a lot of memorization on very specific things so the cheat sheet comes in clutch (got A's on exam bc of it). Lots of EC and genuinely cares about her students.

Dr. Zhong provides a lot of resources that should allow you to exceed (cheat sheet, instapolls, study guide, quizzes) which does lead to more work but better test scores. If you can read a textbook this class is a guaranteed A. If not you should probably take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There is SO MUCH extra credit, and Dr. Zhong is probably one of my favorite professors at UT so far. The accent takes some getting used to, but she is funny and explains the concepts well. She is there for all her students and will listen to you when you have problems, like thank god she got rid of her apply extend things. Stay on top of work!!!

Don't be scared of the bad reviews! Dr. Zhong is an amazing professor for a difficult course. She is so accommodating and listens to her students when they don't like or understand something. When the students complained about pop-quizzes, she got rid of them. 3 Midterms (one gets dropped), weekly quizzes, and 1 final + a cheat sheet for the exams

Min Zhong was incredibly kind and helpful. She offers lots of extra credit and resources to ensure that you are prepared. Her low-stakes grading is really beneficial in making sure that you put learning first and worrying about your grade second. Yes, she has an accent, but she will repeat stuff if you do not understand. Plus, you get used to it!!
Lots of assignments, not-so-good lectures, but exams and quizzes are fair with a cheat sheet. An A is very achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Many people rate her bad just because she has a heavy accent and can be intimidating at times but she actually makes you learn the material. We have quizzes every week that are hard but it makes you study and they prepare you well for the tests. She also allows you to have a cheat sheet front and back for the test which many other profs dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly, I thought the class was going to be a lot worse. Yes, the amount of work is insane and at the beginning of the semester she was grading kind of harsh, but I feel that you learn more without cramming as much. Beware of the quizzes. There is a ton of extra credit, you get to use a cheat sheet on the exam, no FRQ, and no discussion work.

This professor has a kind heart and she cares about her students. However, there is around 3-4 homework assignments/quizzes a week on top of having class 3 times a week. It is WAY too much work. Every other professor for biology here GIVES NO WHERE NEAR AS WORK. On top of that, she grades all these way to harshly, getting 100 is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's honestly not a monster. She actually cares about her students a lot and I feel bad for her other ratings. Her class material isn't easy but she puts in so much effort to help her students out. Take her if you can but know that it won't be a blow-off class.
Makes a very easy class into busy work class. No need for the amount of assignments given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: sweet professor but a lot of extra work. Does not need to be as difficult of a class as it is. took more time that i thought was necessary from my week
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She gives you so many assignments that take 1 hour plus then will take off so many points and gives you a paragraph as to why she did it but it doesn't even make sense. You can score well on her exam but those small assignments that she takes off points drops your grade significantly. Save yourself the tears and mental health decline!! RUN FAST
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super sweet, lectures well, and takes feedback. Biology itself is just hard, memory-based, and complex, but she does a pretty good job of explaining. Assignments can take a long time. Exam and quiz content is reasonable, but there are many trick questions. She does have an accent, so if you're not good with accents, that may be a problem for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Just try your best and you'll do great in this class. It's a lot to get used to at first- make sure to review slides/readings BEFORE lecture and you'll do much better. Lectures are boring, but worth going to. Some exam questions were too specific/irrelevant to include IMO. The material isn't bad if you can keep up, and you can use cheat sheets!

This professor, I guarantee you will not be able to understand and you will get a bad grade if you don't study 24/7. She has the worst accent and talks very fast. She is a nice person in life, but her teaching is not there. BE AWARE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The semester started off disorganized with many pop quizzes. After a mid-semester survey, she listened to our feedback and made changes, showing she cares. Tests are manageable with cheat sheets, though there's a lot of material. Extra credit made it easy to get an A.

At first the class was very hard due to Zhong being new to UT but mid semester she asked for our feedback and adjusted her syllabus accordingly. One page (front and back) of handwritten notes can be used on test. Her accent can be hard to understand and she speaks fast. She is extremely nice and gave A TON of extra credit before the final!! 4.5/5
She is terrible. You will spend hours doing her pointless reading assignments, going to class every day, and will still feel clueless on the exams. AVOID at all cost!

I think the exams are pretty fair, especially if you review the quizzes we do. Plus the cheat sheet, i barely used it, but working on the cheat sheet helped me memorize the context. TA discussions was probably the most helpful for me personally. It can be hard to understand her at times, but it's not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her PowerPoints/lectures were straightforward and she's very receptive to student feedback. There were a lot of assignments, but they provided opportunities to practice applying concepts learned in class, so I felt like I was studying while I was learning. Cheat sheets are very helpful for exams and she gives plenty of bonus point opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Go search up Min Zhong Auburn university, she taught there. She has 188+ 1 rating reviews, you'll know why. I'll quote one of the top reviews:

Terrible. Terrorist.

reviews.comment: Prof Zhong is very smart, but her class is structured in a difficult manner. In my opinion, the class isn't conceptually difficult but there is just an overload of content. I spent at least 7-8 hours per week studying for her class as there were weekly quizzes and assignments. If you put genuine effort into this class your grade should be fine.

Dr. Zhong is a great professor and receptive to student feedback, but definitely get ready to read and work hard for your grade. A lot of work is for completion and there are bonus points available. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her, unless you want your GPA ruined. A horrible, horrible teacher. Lectures are very confusing, exams are hard and are nothing like the material that she covers in class. Tons of pointless reading assignments too. Again, you have been warned - do NOT take this professor.

Amazing and kind professor and takes feedback well. The course is very rigorous and that is partly due to the nature of Biology, however, it is also due to concepts not being adequately explained during lectures and Instapolls. Often I was left wondering what was happening in class and mostly relied on the textbook. Allowed cheat sheets on exams.

Try avoiding this professor for the sake of your gpa, especially if you are pre-health. Currently trying to figure out whether to drop or just deal with a C. She expects you to study 10.5 hours a week for her class, even after receiving various complaints. You don't ever know what you will be tested on. Cheat sheets for tests, yet many fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such a sweet professor with a great heart, but absolutely killed my first semester. I would spend 3-5 hours A DAY studying for her class, going to every discussion, doing extra credit , yet half the content she gave was not on the test. Most overwhelmed I've ever been. If you don't have a decent grip on BIO311C, avoid taking her.

She is a super nice woman but an awful teacher. Quizzes are graded and based on the content you learned the same day. Tests are super confusing even with a cheat sheet. Class resources don't help much, so be prepared to learn independently and in TA sessions. She also has a heavy accent that takes a while to get used to.

reviews.comment: Don't take this!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Posting this now for everyone looking at registration early. This Professor Zhong is the same Professor Zhong from Auburn University, this was her first year at UT. (The one with the 2.1 rating, 19% would take again, 4.1 difficulty). 
You'll spend 10 hours outside of class on HW each week. She's impossible to understand and can't explain anything.

reviews.comment: Office hours are incredibly helpful and homework is very similar to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class contains difficult material. However, the professor teaches well enough to combat that difficulty. You are permitted to bring a formula sheet to each exam. Showing up to class gives you 5 extra credit points to your final grade.
DO NOT TRUST THE REVIEWS. HE IS NOT LIKE THE REVIEWS. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. YOU ARE WAY BETTER OFF TAKING IT OVER THE SUMMER.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor but physics is hard

Zimmerman is definitely the best option for Engineering Physics II at UT. He's very positive and upbeat, and offers an extra 5% on your final grade if you just come to class. I didn't find his lectures super helpful, but if you do a ton of quest problems before the test you should be able to do well.

Very good professor! Extremely knowledgeable and clear when lecturing. He always stops to make sure to see if the students have any questions. He is always willing to answer questions after class if time permits. It's difficult to make a subject like physics clear and easier to understand, but he manages to do it!

Professor Zimmerman somehow managed to make electromagnetism interesting and funny. His explanations were picture-heavy, which made the concepts much easier to understand. Alongside the pictures he brought many examples to visualize the concepts. Would take again.

He is amazing! He made attendance for extra 5 percent of the total grades which makes the total grade to 105. Keep attending the class and stay in touch with him, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions, and you will get a satisfying grade in this his class! This class is worth being taken with him!!!
terrible test questions not related to lecture

Best prof I've ever had. Lectures were amazing as he taught physics 2 in the most digestible way possible. If you can do HWs, you will be fine on the exam. +5 points on final grade was offered just for doing InstaPolls for completion. Don't worry about taking the class in community college; take physics 2 with Zimmerman and you will thank me

Physics at UT in general will be difficult, keep that in mind. With that being said, Professor Zimmerman is who you want to take if you're trying to actually learn physics while maintaining a high GPA. Very engaging and useful lectures. Extremely beneficial extra credit for just showing up to class. Office hours are also unmatched. My favorite prof

Lectures are always engaging and material is taught with clarity. Be sure to attend every lecture for up to 5% extra credit on the final, also helps you not get behind. Discussion sections are unnecessary & late but required to attend. Make sure to make an equation sheet for the exam- its very clutch. Very fair professor, 10/10.

Professor Zimmerman was great at lecturing and was able to effectively teach all the material. However, I didn't like that the 3rd test took identical questions from the homework which isn't an accurate representation of performance (just memorizing).The discussion sections were mid, but the timing was horrible.

Lectures are entertaining. Tests are an easier version of homework. He allows for formula sheets that can be example problems too. Attendance is for a grade. Phy 303L is usually hated by UT student-- Zimmerman makes it easy.

Prof. Zimmerman was an ok teacher.  His hw assignments were sometimes completely different from what he taught. Even if you study the hw well on quest, there's a chance that the tests can have random trick questions. He curves well so don't worry too much about your grade. Though his TA led discussion sessions were useless and mandatory.

Zimmerman made difficult physics topics easy. Tests and HWs are Quest so if you understand the HWs you'll do fine on exams. Lectures are engaging and offer extra credit but honestly aren't needed to get a good grade (I stopped going halfway through the semester). If you just need the credit and don't care about physics whatsoever, take Zimmerman.

Very organized class, lectures are clear and precise but it is important to not fall behind. Quest Homework and tests are not very closely correlated so beware, otherwise, very achievable to get an A. Discussion sessions are mandatory. Class attendance isn't mandatory but if you attend you can get +5 points on ur total grade. Great professor 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Challenging material, but class feels more than fair to the student. Dr. Zimmerman teaches material very well and is a fun proffessor. I really enjoyed taking physics with him, and would highly reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Zimmerman is an amazing professor all around, hes a great lecturer and really cares about his students and their well-being. He gives 5% extra credit for coming to class and doing instapolls and drops 1 of 3 midterms which arent overly difficult. The final was even easier than the midterms as well. Definitely recommend 303L w/ Zimmerman

Homeworks and exams are quest based so there's similarities between the two. Attendance isn't mandatory but there's an incentive to come to class and do the daily quizzes which are participation based because they were 5% extra credit. Also, his final letter grade cutoffs are slightly lower than the general cutoff.

Homework is on Quest and Exams are based on Quest problems. Best to search Quest practice problems to prep for lectures and exams (exams can be difficult if you don't study). Zimmerman's lectures are AMAZING and VERY HELPFUL. Encourages students to participate. Cares about students' well being. Discussion sections were mandatory and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: We had one homework a week (unless there was an exam) on quest and the tests were exactly like the material covered on the homework. Lecture attendance was extra credit but discussion participation was mandatory. He cares about his students and tells us cool space facts at the beginning of lecture.

The class was challenging but well taught. Zimmerman covered everything we needed to know so there were no surprises on exams. His tests do have one FRQ in addition to about 15 MC, but if you study the homework you'll do fine.

Prof. Elkins is among my favorite professors I've ever had. The class was not difficult and yet taught me more than most courses I've taken, which is a challenging art in education that Prof. Elkins seems to have mastered. He fosters discussion and even friendship among the class, and great application to life. If given the opportunity, take him!

He's a boss. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it. Super knowledgeable and respected in when it comes to constitutions, and is also super funny. His classes are very laid back, and he is a nice grader. He really just wants you to read and critically think about the questions and discussions had in class.
I cannot recommend Professor Elkins enough, he was a joy to both learn from and explore new ideas with. It's a rare few who have such a breadth of knowledge and conversational ability!

This class comprised of a number of readings and a few smaller projects based on constitutional design at the national and household level. Dr. Elkins always made our class discussions very engaging despite the online format, and the topics were always relevant and interesting. A genuinely supportive and laid-back professor throughout the semester.

Was in his class about constitutional design. He seemed very intelligent and knew a lot about the subject. The class was a smaller group with attendance and participation being essential. The things we learned about were always interesting and had real world applications. He is very understanding and I often felt as though he was being too nice.

Amazing professor and class! We performed a research study on implementing household constitutions during the Coronavirus pandemic. HIGHLY RECOMMEND this class or anything he teaches! It was truly the best class I've ever taken!!

Made this class trivially easy, might be the easiest class I've taken since elementary school, and yet I still did learn a little bit from the class. Probably not worth it if you really want to come out of the course with new development skills, but some interesting topics were lightly touched on. Nice professor all around, was very considerate.

Course is a little disorganized but not hard to get around. Concepts were taught pretty clearly. Even though his lectures can be dry, he is genuinely a great guy to talk to outside of class and clearly cares about his work and students. Workload is very very manageable.

Took this class online over summer. Course seemed very disorganized as assignments were randomly assigned and for exams we had no clue what would be on them. The content of the course is not hard but it was taught in a very un-structured way. With that being said, he made the final take home and was very lenient with grade cutoffs.
Course was very manageable whilst doing an internship and another course at the same time. Lectures are all recorded and Samant is very clear about what content he expects in quizzes and exams.
samant is a very nice professor. some of the project guidelines were a little hard to follow, but he's always open to guiding his students and helping everyone out.
The lectures were informative but the team project was not outlined very well. The assignments helped with the team project but I still feel that a lot was left in the air.
GOAT!

Software lab is currently a dumpster fire: inconsistent guidelines and laughable assignments plague this class. While easy, the project was fixed so there was little creativity invovled. This class does teach you how to use google to your advantage, as any good software engineer should. I'd suggest choosing partners with app dev experience.

Professor Samant never had a consistent rubric on what the semester-long project is supposed to be. Our group would go to him during office hours and he will tell us our features are ok and give us a bad grade later on because the feature is "different from what is expected." His TAs also didn't know what was going on and told us wrong information.
Professor Samant truly cares about his students. He will offer second chances to submit an assignment to help your grade. I had no prior knowledge on coding and he made it much less harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This guy's amazing. He teaches pretty well for an introductory coding class. For people with no prior experience, he always takes the time to help people lagging behind. The real meat of the class is on lectures though, so be sure to pay attention and not zone out. He's pretty nice though, and will follow the class opinion on things.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I've never done any sort of programming before, but Samant is really good about making sure everyone stays together and answering any questions, no matter how simple. He's super willing to help you, but will also make sure that you're challenged and can problem solve on your own. Definitely a very frustrating class but also SUPER rewarding!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He should be more prepared for his lecture material and homework guidelines. Lots of technical difficulties in class and unnecessary breakdowns.

304 is a pretty simple class if you already know Python/Any Programming Language walking in, and he knows that. He spends most of class time just helping out any students who are struggling, and if he sees people bored he'll just start telling stories. Dude's a real gem. You're gonna miss him when you take 325. Because yikes.

Professor Samant is very caring! The lectures are made of slides which can be a bit boring over time but you will always code in class to practice which makes the class interesting. Abhay Samant can go fast but he will care that everyone follows the course.

My class was Abhay's first semester teaching here at UT (or anywhere for that matter), and he did a great job. His style of teaching can move fast for people who are new to programming, but if you ask he will steer you to some areas for practice that really helps. He teaches through doing, not just lectures, so you will code most days of class.

Very bad. I don't know my grade yet, but I had a 4.0 before this class. Unless I get a 100 on both remaining tests, it'll be hard to keep my 4.0. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Unless you already know a lot about this subject, it'll be super difficult. There is so much reading, and tests are extremely long with no MCQs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't required, quizzes based on what's said in class. In-class presentation end of the semester (easy). Participation for extra credit. Exams (free response) not cumulative. Provides study guides (prioritize key concepts). If you're unfamiliar with the topic, it can be challenging. That said, she's kind and happy to answer questions.

Professor Somer-Topcu was awesome! She is a kind grader on exams and really wants the students to do well. Definitely go to class as she only tests over things she has talked about in class. Gives interesting lectures and is very willing to work with the students.

Zeynep is great!! Very knowledgeable and has great discussions during lecture. Grades are a group presentation that is very easy if you prepare well. Also 3 tests, free response but all material is covered in class/slides. She gives extra credit for participation, but attendance isn't required. I got away with not showing up a ton (still did well).

I was hesitant to take this class, seeing rate my professor but I really enjoyed it. It wasn't as difficult as others made it sound. You're graded on three exams (non-cumulative) and a group presentation. She gives you extra credit if you participate. She posts the slides and a study guide- take time to study. Just go to class, and participate.

Absolutely amazing class! If you attend all lectures and pay attention, you will pass. Her tests are all free-response questions, but the exam content is directly from the lectures. This is a difficult subject to cover, but she takes time to answer any questions and is really helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get out while you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Somer isn't the most exciting professor, but she gets the job done. She's obviously incredibly insightful in her field and she really tries her best to educate her students as much as possible. The biggest negative is that there are really only four grades you will be judged on -- two midterm exams, one presentation, and one final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zeynep Somer-Topcu is a great professor who is very knowledgeable. The class is graded on three tests and a presentation. The presentation is not hard and is easy to get an A on, but the exams are definitely difficult. If you study hard by focusing on all the main terms from the slides, you should get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is the single hardest course I've taken at UT Austin. You'll learn a lot, but her exams are ridiculously overpacked with way too much to do in such a little amount of time. I knew all the information before every exam but even that couldn't help me and all the other students felt the same. if you care about your GPA, don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were very difficulty in this class, no matter how much you study. Free response exams and long essays that are graded pretty harshly. the cut-off for an A in this class is also higher than 93 and she did not round up.

Grades depend on her tests which consisted of 10 short answers, 5 short essays, and 2 long essays all in an hour and twenty minutes. Many students didn't finish in time but she didn't change anything & she graded extremely harshly. Her lectures were interesting and I did learn a lot but if you care about your GPA, DO NOT TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absurdly difficult class even for government majors. Do not take if you can avoid it, especially for the number of readings and the formats for tests, which are entirely made of short essays. Absolutely ridiculous.
One of the harder classes I've taken at UT. Tons of readings, and as others have stated, tests consist entirely of short answer questions and essays, and are graded harshly. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very very difficult. Only a few grades, and tests are a nightmare (each test has 2 short essays in addition to the regular questions, which are mostly short answer questions), and there are also two 4-6 essays required during the semesters. She clearly knows her stuff, but unless you can dedicate hours every day to studying, good luck getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'd highly recommend this class if you're interested in European politics. Professor Somer-Topcu explains the material extremely clearly and everything was very easily understood. There are weekly reading quizzes so make sure to always read, 2 short papers that are easy, and 3 open-ended tests. Not difficult and very interesting!

Dr. Somer-Topcu is very knowledgeable and genuinely a nice person. That being said, I found this course to be extremely difficult. There is so much material covered that I ended up feeling overwhelmed, and maybe that's because I was mostly unfamiliar with the course concepts beforehand. Either way, solid professor, difficult course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I thought her West European Politics class was great. There are 3 tests, 10 easy quizzes over the readings, and 2 short papers. Her lectures were engaging, and she often showed fun little videos to liven up the class. The TA could be a tough grader on papers (check citations!), but in general it was a good class, fairly easy, and I learned a lot!
The professor is amazing, the TA Joey was great. Tests are easy, but the quizzes are hard if you don't read. You have to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: A lot of people on this website say that this class is challenging, but I couldn't disagree more. 3 tests, 2 short papers, and roughly 10 quizzes on readings that are all fairly easy if you pay attention in class and read the materials she provides. Lectures were easy to follow and she provided outside resources that made the class fun. Great class

There really wasn't that much reading. Maybe 2-3 hours before every class, which isn't bad for a gov class. She is really informed and a great lecturer. She even adds funny video clips into her lectures. The essays aren't hard either, but the exams are graded very tough. Even though I had to work hard, I learned SO much and I enjoyed her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Easily the hardest GOV course I have taken at UT. The textbook is atrocious and the tests are VERY difficult (only short answer). Her pop quizzes are exceedingly hard to excel on even if you follow every reading. I never missed a reading, yet still consistently failed these quizzes! The essays are difficult too, as the TA gives little input/advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: hardest class I have ever taken in my entire college career. readings on readings and she does a terrible job at explaining what is gonna be on the test. seriously do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her European Union/Regional Integration class was great. 3 exams, 1 take-home final and a debate. The debate was a group project but wasn't awful and served as a grade booster for most. Attendance isn't required and she posts slides, but going to class is definitely needed to succeed. She is so kind and impressive as well. Would take again!

this professor was pretty good. She does a good job explaining what she wants. she has 3 essays worth 10% each, 2 midterms 20% each, final 25% and 5% participation. it has a high amount of reading. she has at least 1 reading per class. overall not too bad. Do Recommend
his 2D class is mostly photography, drawing and maybe painting if you choose that for the last project. I sort of hoped for more exploration but it was still a fun class and Peter is a good teacher

My class was large, so that may have played a role, but individual feedback was limited mostly to a few sentences during critique. The amount of outside classwork was enormous, little time was given for each project considering the level of development he expected. I didn't find that the course improved my art or process noticeably, but it was fun.

While I had to take this as a required studio class, it was really great to go over the basics again. Peter pushes students to do their best, no matter what their skill set is. Really great guy and helps you get a firmer grasp of the basics while pushing you with skills you've already developed.

I took core drawing with Peter, and I really enjoyed his teaching and feedback during critique. If youre taking drawing, the class is very basic in format and work. The prompts can be fun, and he normally lets you work pretty freely with composition and material. Attendance matters! If youre late or absent, expect to see a change in your grade!

Professor Osseo-Asare is one the best profs I've ever had. She truly engages with students, is curious to hear what we think, gives valuable feedback, and let's the lectures and discussions drift and take on a natural rhythm. She's also insanely smart! We only really have one big assignment for the semester, so it's low pressure. Highly recommend!

She was super chill. One of the best professors I've had I think. Grades were based on a paragraph of feedback for readings (about 8-10), a sewing project (completion), and a final paper. Real easy course. Sometimes lectures go off track and a bunch of random things were added in there (like films she found) so the class was really laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Osseo-Asare is passionate about what she teaches, and she is also extremely caring and supportive toward the students. Take her class to enjoy learning; do not worry about grades because she is very lenient and really just wants you to participate. Her class gets you to think about STEM topics in unique ways, which was very eye-opening.

The prof was really sweet and cared about her students but she was a little bit unorganized. I never exactly knew what she wanted for papers, but she graded them very easily. The one exam was a little bit difficult but it was open note and she literally said she didn't care if we helped each other on it. Overall super interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at UT - really cares about her students and is super passionate about the topic. Everyone should take her before you graduate.
A little unorganized, but very sweet!

This is one of the best classes I have taken at UT. The class is a writing flag so we had to read a new book and write a paper every week. The class gave me a really good understanding of the African culture. There were two quizzes but because of the pandemic, she restricted the class to only one map quiz. Overall, the class is pretty easy and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Osseo-Asare is an incredibly kind and passionate professor. She is very in tune with what student's go through and is always willing to listen and help. As long as you show up and participate, you will do well in this class. I have taken two of her courses and they have been some of my favorites at UT

Overall great teacher! She is very passionate about medical related history, focusing mainly on maternal health and natural/herbal remedies. If I could, I would take this class and any other class she teaches again. Do not be deterred by the amount of reading and papers, it is definitely manageable.  You will not regret taking her!

She is one of the best professors ever. She's extremely educated as a medical historian and encourages students to ask tough questions. She cracks jokes in class, but also makes sure students know when to get serious. Her lectures are always really well structured and interesting. Go to class and pay attention and you'll do well.

Took his Applied ML with Python class and it's basically a intro to ML class. He has clear grading policies and assignments listed in his syllabus. A little lecture heavy but overall a caring professor if you participate and ask questions. Highly recommend his classes!! High quality and good material.

When I took the intro class with him, it was a lot of information to digest at first if you're new to this field but it gives you a really good overview of data science. He really does care about his students and one of my favorite professors (took all his classes).

I've taken Dr. Mishra's introductory course, which was incredibly beginner-friendly and well-structured. I've also conducted academic research related to Machine Learning, both for credit and independently to gain experience with him. It is very noticeable that Dr. Mishra genuinely cares about his students' learning and development.

I've take Dr. Mishra's Introduction to Human-Centered Data Science, which was very beginner friendly and well-structured. Additionally, I've conducted academic research related to Machine Learning, both for credit and independently to gain hands-on experience with him. Dr. Mishra genuinely cares about his students' learning and development.

Professor Mishra is deeply invested in his students' success. He's not only highly knowledgeable about the material he teaches but also kind and approachable. I'd genuinely enjoy having him as a friend.
Mishra is a good professor, he has industry experience and knows his stuff when it comes to data science. His classes are pretty easy so long as you pay attention to the lectures and do the work.

Took NLP and ML with Dr. Mishra. He really is the best professor in the Data Science track. I got to work on a project I was passionate about for his Applied ML course, and he gave my team great feedback. He cares about his students, and his course is fairly easy to follow if you pay attention, and you'll get a lot from it. Highly recommend!

Dr. Mishra's courses are the best you could take for the Data Science track in Informatics. - Messed up on the rating I made; his courses are not difficult and easy to follow. Helps you learn the material well if you focus in class! He also gives great feedback (Difficulty is 1!!!)

Dr. Mishra's courses are the best you could take for the Data Science track in Informatics. Lectures are structured well, and he makes sure all of his students understand the material before moving on. His labs are always well structured - connecting class material to real-world applications & assignments are related to what we learned! Highly rec!

Highly recommend taking both Dr. Mishra's classes (Applied ML and Text Mining & NLP). He is definitely one of the best professors in the iSchool for learning topics in ML and NLP hands-on. Dr. Mishra's passion for teaching shines through, and it is evident that he wants his students to succeed. Take him!
He is my favorite professor in iSchool
This class was challenging but very informative. Lectures were easy to understand and Dr Mishra was very helpful.
Great professor and teaching style is really understandable, I would definitely take his class again.

Dr. Mishra's Python for ML class and Text Mining & NLP class are both extremely useful classes. Each class consists of lectures on the topics with time to engage in a hands-on lab. He provides a good understanding of ML concepts and supplements his lectures with examples. The TA and professor are always available to help if needed.

Dr. Mishra's I310D class was a great intro class to data science. He also provides hands-on exercises and activities relating in Machine Learning and Python, which is extremely useful. He is extremely flexible, and his class is not difficult. The lectures, labs, and projects help supplement the course material in an easy-to-understand way.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was really easy! Attendance isn't mandatory, but it definitely helps if you go to class. Definitely gets started on the group project early because it piles up really fast!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A great teacher who genuinely cares about his students. Although attendance isnt checked, there are occasional participation quizzes that are an assignment grade in person to see who comes to class. Very useful content and the final project is great for portfolio/resume. Hes a very kind and understanding teacher who is willing to help always.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Mishra is great! Very approachable in office hours and after class. Just a word to the wise-- get a head start on the group project so y'all aren't drowning during finals week!

Dr. Mishra is an outstanding professor who delivers clear and engaging lectures that make complex topics approachable. Labs, homework, and projects are thoughtfully and relevant to reinforce material and provide a hands-on experience. His approachable demeanor and constructive feedback ensures students keep up with complex topics learn effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mishra is one of the best professors I've worked with at UT Austin! Meaningful and engaging lectures were thoughtfully structured and reinforced by relevant classwork, homework, and projects. With a focus on practical programming, he prioritizes projects over exams, ensuring deep understanding of material. Helpful with questions in class.

Professor Mishra is an exceptional educator. His engaging lectures and hands-on coding projects made learning practical and enjoyable. He is highly accessible outside of class and genuinely dedicated to student success. I learned so much in his course—definitely take his classes or any of his Upper Division courses if you get the chance!

Professor Mishra always came prepared for the class. He prepared lectures with rich content (algorithm, math, and applications). The homeworks and group works are mostly project based, which is the best form to apply machine learning.

Professor Mishra is one of the best professors I have had during my time at UT Austin. I highly encourage other students to take his classes, as his passion and commitment to the subject creates a rich learning experience.

He gives you exercises every week. For the coding exercises, the guideline is clear for what to do and what he looks for. There is group project at the end to test your skills, and I had good teammates to do it with. There is no midterm so there is no stress preparing for tests. Overall, a good learning experience.

Dr. Mishra is very knowledgeable about course materials, especially topics about machine learning, natural language processing, and AI. Some assignments can be time-consuming but they make sure that you learn how to apply the skills you learn in class, thereby improving your programming skills. His classes also have a relaxed attendance policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mishra is knowledgeable and kind. However, his class is more suitable for students who already have a background in programming, otherwise, it can be hard to follow and catch up for beginners. But if you finish your work on time you can get A.

Professor Mishra is very knowledgeable about a variety of data science topics and always willing to provide advice. While his assignments can be time-consuming, they ensure that you learn how to apply the content and better your coding skills. He's an understanding grader with helpful feedback, and his lectures have a relaxed attendance policy.

Professor Mishra is very knowledgable however he is not a good teacher. The concepts that he goes over in this course is not introductory in any manner. DON'T take this class is you don't have programming experience - you will be SO lost. With this being said, he is not a hard grader, so it's not hard to get an A in his class.

Lectures were kind of hard to follow. Despite being an intro class, it felt more advanced and kind of threw us into things we didn't know that well. Instructions would change for assignments as time went on. Don't take if you don't have a lot of experience in coding. He's extremely kind and gives helpful tips for careers but not great at teaching.

Professor Mishra is extremely knowledgeable and is accessible for after-class questions. The class itself has content-heavy lectures with occasional exercises to test for knowledge. The in-class labs are a great way to connecting and understanding the material in lecture. The homeworks are a good test for understanding and the final project is cool
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The A+ is quite attainable if you just do work on time. There's one assignment every Friday, a lab, and it's pretty chill if you go to class on Fridays (at the very least) & know some Python. Yeah, it's scary because he assumes you know a lot more than you might, but you'll be fine if you pay attention and go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Mishra is clearly really knowledgeable and loves talking about his field. However, he can oftentimes assume that students are more knowledgeable about the field and how computer systems and stats work than they actually are. He's really nice and will help you out if you need it, but the class can be really hard if you don't know Python.

There is a lot of work for this class, but compared to other elective courses, this is by far the easiest. Just showing up to class is almost enough to get an A. Hope you get a good group for the projects so you're not stuck picking up other people's tasks. Final project was fun. Bad communicator, though, as I never got a single email answered.

Lectures covered content that wasn't entirely useful/beneficial for students.  Mandatory attendance through Instapoll. Overall just not a very engaging class.  Coding assignments were pretty fun and the group project is the highlight of the course, but beyond that, I did not really learn much or apply many concepts from class into the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Abraham requires attendance with daily quizzes at the start of class. Lecture felt useless, most of my understanding of the material came from self-study and other resources. Projects are brutal but graded leniently. There is an absurd amount of homework (does she think this is a core class lol). Absolutely do not take unless you love graphics.

Dr. Abraham was an okay professor. Her lectures were boring and unhelpful even though attendance was mandatory, making the hands-on activities and assignments difficult. There is a "hands-on" or homework activity due before every single class. She also takes a long time to respond to emails. Her class was "easy," but I didn't learn much from it.

There's an instapoll for attendance every class and an assignment due before the next regarding what was lectured. Homework assignments, independent and group (assigned) which aren't bad but do need to make sure your teammates know how to code or how to ask for help, at least. Pretty chill class. Learned a lot about Processing.

I found that Sarah Abraham was a fantastic professor who was always available to provide great feedback and made the class super interesting. I found the topic was fun and all of the assignments to be valuable. There seems to be something due for every class, but when it is just graded by participation, it is hard to complain. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Abraham is an excellent lecturer and a very down-to-earth person. Lectures covered lots of content but were also informal enough to facilitate conversation. She's very passionate and knowledgeable. The projects are very open ended and not super related to the lecture of the day. However there are lots of office hours for help. Take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Abraham is completely useless as a lecturer. Her abysmal attendance policy requires you to go to essentially every class, despite the fact that you take away nothing of importance from them. Entirety of the course is dependent on your ability to self-teach.

Game Programming Paradigms: No exams, 5 group-based projects. The class gets you developing small projects on UE4 and Unity. The final project was work heavy but overall was worth it. Lectures were OK. You have labs that help you with your projects. Expect to spend 4-8 hours weekly for your projects; more if you're stuck with a nasty bug.

This class wasn't that bad, but I think students who don't have much experience in game development will struggle a fair amount. I wish she used more class time on the labs rather than the lectures so that I could get stronger foundations of ue4 to use on the assignments. Also, the groups were picked at random (which can either be good or bad).

Dr. Abraham is the worst! You have a hw due EVERY class and she spends barely 25mins going over extremely complex topics. Get ready for a lot of self teaching and learning. She's also not the best at replying or being nice, and grades pretty harshly too. Having no exams is nice but you have work a lot, I wouldve preferred exams honestly. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Abraham's class was easy in fact that there were no exams, but in office hours, I thought she was little rude, passive aggressive, not understanding. Most of her lectures had nothing to do with most hands-ons, assignments, so it was hard to complete them. I aced some assignments with some outside help. If you didn't take 313E, this class is hard.

Starts off pretty easy, but the lectures become less helpful as material gets more in depth. The daily "hands on" assignments become more difficult as less is covered, and you'll end up learning from online resources instead of lecture. Processing can be fun, but me and others were lost halfway through the semester. Dr. Abraham is great though!

The lectures are not very helpful for projects. She barely gives any code examples but just concepts, and you need to figure out how to implement all the fancy game technologies yourself. The projects were graded generously at least for the semester I took this class.

She's a good lecturer, but I just can't stand the way the class is structured. There's an assignment due every class, which you rarely receive enough guidance to complete. Yes, you gather more experience by immersion, but if you don't know and weren't adequately taught you lose so much time trying to figure out daily assignments. Just a burden.
If you can write decently, it's a fairly easy class without exams (midterm and final papers instead). The workload is fair and the lectures are interesting. Probably one of my favorite CS courses.

Great class and no exams! You have group projects and individual projects instead of exams. She posts her lecture material online, but you need to attend class(she gave me a negative 2 when I took my first class with her and didn't go to lecture). You should always ask her questions when you're unsure about a certain requirement for an assignment!

Dr. Abraham is an excellent ethics professor. She really cares about the subject and respects student opinions. She's an excellent public speaker as well. I think every CS major should take an ethics class, and she's the perfect person to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Professor Abrahams Mobile Computing class and while the projects sometimes took some time, they werent too hard and were often graded generously. We were required to work in random teams for 3 projects but generous grading negates the effect of a bad team. Overall, a pretty good class but with a decent workload and some unclear directions.
Great teacher, loves to help out if you go to her office hours! Class grade is based on weekly projects. I personally had a great group so the class was honestly very fun!

Dr Abraham was an fair professor and one of my favorite teachers at UT. The course load is all project based. Sarah is a very fair grader and recognizes that the focus learning the material. You should use outside resources to help you on projects particularly to clear up any confusions about equations in the slides. Awesome professor and class.

He is a good teacher, although the subject can get a little complicated at times because of all the variables, but the sample problems really prepare you for the exam. He wrote the textbook himself so he knows his stuff and tries to keep it engaging. Easy A, graded by mean score and standard deviations of the class so stay above average and ur good

This was the worst class I've taken at UT. The prof is super smart but is terrible at explaining to others, and in each exam, over half the class failed. I honestly hoped I'd get hit by a bus walking to this class so I wouldn't have to deal. the prof is very nice, but his exams do not match his lectures or his review prep.

One of my favorite professors I've had. The class is challenging, with two midterms, a final, weekly homework, and some quizzes. You can tell he knows what he's talking about, lectures can be boring however so a lot of people never went  to class. He goes out of his way to make the class passable for all, if you're an econ major take him
straightforward. easy. Just stay above the averages of the class which is totally doable, and the curves will likely take you to an A.
Very straightforward class. Massive curve as long as you stay above the class averages on tests (which are like a 60%). Pretty easy A imo as there is alot of room for error.

Take him for ECO 329! Not an easy A class for non-math brains like me and content can quickly feel overwhelming if you fall behind but he grades on a more than fair curve which saved me in the end. Responds fast to emails and is more than willing to help if you ask.

His lectures felt useless. You have to learn the content on your own, homeworks are way harder than the exam. Towards the end of the semester things finally start to make sense, but feeling lost is normal. However the curve is good.
he has a way of making the exams extra hard

Dr. Abrevaya is an awesome guy, he cares about his students and responds very promptly to emails. However this class is pretty freaking hard, the lectures are EXTREMELY boring, and the tests are really hard. Luckily he curves the exams pretty hard, which in the end makes 99% of the students at least pass the class. Great guy, horrible lecturer.
Hardest part of this class was not falling asleep in it.

If you don't have a background in stats or didn't take AP Stats get ready to teach yourself stats. His lectures are really boring and very confusing. His exams are super challenging. Luckily he curves this class, so if you don't get an A or and A- (47% of the class did) it's kind of a skill issue. He does seem super helpful in office hours though.

Due to my stats background or just its structure, econ stats was an unbearably boring course, but Abbrevaya was a very decent dude who explained things straightforwardly and had a good sense of humor sometimes. Very good curves, gave the entire class a free test drop because one of the testing rooms had noise disruption

It's a really easy class if you have any basic understanding of probability and stats. Barely any HW, don't have to show up to class, and exams are graded on a curve. However, lectures are extremely boring so no one shows up so if you don't know anything about stats you're going to have to rely on office hours or learning yourself via YouTube
Hard class thats all

Incredibly boring lectures, very tough exams, curves the grades but literally impossible to get through materials and study. what he teaches in the class is completely unrelated to the homework and what comes on the exams.

Hes a good person however his lectures dont say how to apply equations to real life. Its just 100000 formulas given to you and you have to figure out, by yourself mainly, where they apply. Id start going to tutoring the first class day if you want to get good grades on exams. The content is just extremely hard to remember

great teacher & explains things well, but it's a hard subject. responds on email: i gave him a recommendation for canvas and he did it. curves test to have an average of 75% no matter what. dropped one test because one class had a noisy environment, so he does care. barely anyone attends because he posts lectures online. given cheat sheet for tests

This class is very easy if you have prior knowledge of statistics. He isn't very engaging during lectures, but it could be so much worse. He knows what he's talking about and is very organized and clear about grading.

He was a really chilled out guy and didn't put too much pressure in class. The lectures were a little boring but his tests were quite accessible if you did all the weekly homeworks again and his practice midterms. They had good structure. He also has a good curve, so it's possible to do well in the class after a bad test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't take him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The hardest part of the class was the subject. Economics Statistics is a hard class, but he teaches very well. He wrote the textbook for the class and offers it for FREE to his students. R code is not taught by him, but makes free DataCamp assignments. Lots of TA help. Curve is dependent on the performance of the overall class. He is great!

The class has gotten SIGNIFICANTLY HARDER since he last taught it in 2021. The exam averages in '23 were around 62% for the whole class. The practice exams from 2021 did not help at all since they were a piece of cake while the exams this year felt like a slaughterhouse. He's a nice guy but when the whole class does poorly, maybe he's the problem.

The exams are different than his lectures and he uses multiple choice questions a lot in his exams. I am normally an A student but I didn't do well in his class but he curved everything. 

The second midterm was unbelievable difficult and different than anything we've seen. It's not even part of the practice problems he handed before the exam

Didn't have to show up to class just studied a little before each exam and finished with an A. Exams aren't easy but the entire first unit is highschool probability. Really personable and funny professor that makes a boring class manageable.

The main problem I have is his lectures-it was boring, fast, and unlike the exam (short answer questions) than his lectures (which were long and used R). I think it would beneficial to go to his office hours. The SI exam reviews were unhelpful. Exam averages were below a D sometimes but he curves every exam. idk why his rating is so high

Just like another reviewer said, his rating is way overrated and overhyped. He really struggles to explain things in a simple way and we spend 1/3 of the class doing stuff that won't be in the exams. He makes a lot of mistakes on his exams (there were 6 mistakes on the final). The only good thing about him is that he replies fast to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For some reason I went into this class thinking it would be a cake walk and it was not. Prof. Abrevaya is a nice guy however my main gripe with him is his lectures are quite vanilla and boring.  This class i feel is just tough with him or another prof. A couple of the class exam averages were like an F however he does give a generous curvetoBmedian

Abrevaya was awesome! Lectures were clear and easy to follow (though boring at times, but its stats so...). Exams were not necessarily a reflection of the homework assignments, more so the lectures, so attendance is key. Overall learned some cool stuff about statistics and would take Abrevaya again in a heartbeat.
Worst class I've ever taken

Did not attend most of the lectures as I took AP Stats. However, his lecture notes and cheat sheet are helpful. Around 0.75 Standard deviation above mean is an A- or A. The homework is challenging, especially with R but out of 11 homework each for 2 points, you just need to get to 18 and each homework if you pass you get full 2.

This class is so hard if you've never taken statistics. The prof is nice and tries to be helpful but his lectures are so hard to follow. I don't get why he has a difficulty rating of 3.8 bc hes really hard. Personally, the extra problems and lectures didn't help me and I had to teach myself a lot because his voice made it hard to focus for me.

Ok I have to be honest. He is a really nice person, but I DONT UNDERSTAND the hype behind his 4.9 rating. Like the problems you study through extra problems or regular homework are really helpful but fault in comparison to anything you might face in the exam. DONT even look at his review after you finish studying, false sense of confidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really like speaking to him - his metrics class is very difficult to me - grades on curve -- lecture heavy - i found it hard to follow,

First semester teaching Eco Stats and Jason killed it. Very accommodating with test curves, material was on the easy side. Lectures were dry but overall an easy class that I barely went to and still got an A.

1 midterm and 1 Final. I did good on the midterm and bombed the final and still got A-. The rest of the graded portions are easy, basically 100 for doing it. You would need to put work in, but I enjoyed the class and he's not a boring lecturer.

If you didn't like stat in HS, rest assured, econ stat is a lot easier. There is a lot of material to learn, so I HIGHLY recommend you study as you learn the material - trust me, it will save you so much trouble for the final exam. Stressful class, but prof is nice and funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Abrevaya is a gem. He cares way more about his students learning the material than worrying about a grade. Only two exams (so can't bomb), but lots of the grade lies on participation and homework so it was very fair. Only complaint was that the final seemed to be out of left field in difficulty, but he curves to make things fair.

Professor Abrevaya is a great professor!! I am on average an A student, but I found this class super difficult. However, Professor Abrevaya gave a lot of curve and I also learned a lot! Definitely recommend this class!
very nice professor!

Abrevaya is an understanding, relatable, and amazing professor. I truly learned a lot of theory and the technical skills to apply those ideas. The only gripe I have is how the final was so unlike all the classwork and midterm. However, since this is graded on a curve and 44% of your grade is essentially participation there is alot of extra credit.
Hes one of the nicest professors youll ever have and he makes like 50% of the class participation. All his lectures are online so watch before the midterm and final. Highly recommend for ecostats

I took Professor Abrevaya's ECO 329 class and loved it! He's a really great guy and an awesome professor. Honestly he's kind of funny. The way he weights everything in the class is really nice too. His exams are super fair and it's definitely easy to do well if you put in the hours. 100% would recommend.

Dr. Abrevaya is amazing, he's incredibly smart, and it shows in the way he teaches. The HWs aren't too bad if you go to lecture, the quizzes are very easy, and the tests are even easier. Overall, if you do the work you will definitely get the grade you want. Abrevaya is spectacular and I highly highly recommend you take him if possible!

After the hellhole that is intro level economics courses taking Dr. Abrevaya's ECO329 made me actually like economics lol. Very fair teacher, almost all the quizzes/homeworks are 80% participation and only 20% right/wrong. All in all, an amazing professor!
Advanced Econometrics is super difficult, but Prof Abrevaya makes it worth it. He's so knowledgable and always willing to help in office hours. Definitely recommend him.
A great professor with kindness and a good heart!Very tough subject though... go to office hours!He also loves Australia, so talk about that and he will automatically love you

Professor is understanding but grades a bit tough... Unorganized canvas page as well. Overall, she seems nice and understanding, but she focuses too much on the detail of assignments and is a tough grader in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Professor Adelakun's lectures were very engaging and interactive. 
You'll  get to learn what you are interested in in addition to the basics. It's more than a language class because we learn so much about Yoruba culture as well. If you don't have a background in Yoruba, you may have to work a little harder but it's worth it!

I took African Cosmopolitanism with Dr. Adelakun and she made it super interesting. The assigned texts were many, long, and sometimes hard to read, but they were interesting and made us think critically. Overall, she is a very good professor. Her accent is not as thick as some people are claiming, she speaks clearly and with good intimation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: AFR311C is a super easy and wholesome class. The class was taught in a three hour stretch though which was painful. Easy A for a VAPA. The content was self explanatory, so I felt it was quite boring. I did not pay attention at all in class because I was SO bOREd. I put in a lot of effort on quizzes, honorings, and final art piece so I got that A

Professor Adelakun is a wonderful professor! It's not easy learning a language, but she has made learning Yoruba a wonderful experience. She explains things very clearly and her teaching style is easy to follow. She also a very kind and understanding professor who I had no trouble reaching out to when I needed help.

Definitely recommend this class. extra credit opportunities and opportunity to watch plays . Interesting readings too. Don't be misled by the bad reviews. just like every other class, you've got to put in some work. with extra credit opportunities, getting an A is quite easy. listen well and you will able to understand her accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken at this university! As a VAPA, I thought it would be a chill class, but it was quite the opposite. Her accent made lectures hard to follow. The tests are TOO detailed. Had to attend too many plays, which got costly. Scheduled an office hour, she never showed up. Awful experience.

VAPAs are required in our core to encourage us to respect and appreciate the arts. This class did the exact opposite. I have never been so turned off to theater in my life. The lectures are boring, Adelakun is difficult to understand, my TA was a really tough grader, the work load outside of class is extensive. Do not take this course.

Her thick accent makes lectures very hard to understand. She teaches as if her students are in kindergarten (she kicked a student out of class for being on his phone). Everything about this class was so unnecessary and TAs' grading was very subjective.  All major assignments were due at the end of the semester leaving no time recover GPA. THE WORST

This class is one of the easiest MIS electives you can take. Professor Maddox was super nice, and you can tell she really cares about the topic of health IT. While the class is easy and not a lot of work, I did learn some new things from the lectures. No exams, just online quizzes, homework assignments, and group projects. Take this class!

Professor Maddox is one of the most caring professors I have had. She teaches a very interesting course and is passionate about her students learning. I would highly recommend taking her class. I learned a lot about health IT.
