Health IT was one of the easiest classes at UT. The answers for the weekly quizzes were all found in the PowerPoints. The project at the end of the semester was very easy. The labs were just following and copying basic instructions.

Professor Maddox is very knowledgeable about everything in the Health IT field, and she conveys that expertise in a way that is easy to understand. She makes the class fun, and she provides a number of labs which give hands-on experience with prominent technologies in the field. It was a fun course, and I would definitely recommend it!

I was not very engaged with the lectures themselves; I found them to be sort of boring. The homework was graded very harshly. There are weekly labs that you do with a group, which are pretty easy, but there is coding involved. The final project was also very straightforward, and I liked that you didn't have to present it.

I loved Dr Sarkar. His lectures are dry, yes, but he always makes sure everyone understands and always welcomes questions. This was my first stats class so I was lost at first, but his class allowed me to catch on pretty quickly. Quizzes are open note and very manageable with very straightforward questions that if you prepare for, you do fine.

Lectures were really dry and difficult to understand. I stopped going to class and just read the slides and doing in class work on my own and I did just fine. Don't underestimate the quizzes they are difficult with few questions, most being weighted at least 10%. Lab sections are easy coding with helpful TAs. HW graded harshly, show all work

Dr. Sarkar is funny and tries to make this class palatable, but lectures are still very, VERY dry. Quizzes are open-note (1 drop, too), and labs are pretty easy. I would take him again solely because (unlike other profs) he doesn't make you present the final poster in person (3 hours of work and printing reduced to a 2-min presentation recording).
listen to what all the other reviews are saying about him not to be mean but it was SO HARD to learn from him during lectures.

This class is very straightforward. "Labs" are basically discussion sections where you practice running code w a group. HWs are graded harshly, show all work. Other part of grade is a stats project and 3 "quizzes" which are open note exams weighted like 25%. I really like professor sarkar, he tries his very best for you to understand the concepts

Attendance only matters for the in-person lab.  Labs and homework were pretty straightforward.  He also posts some video examples and worksheet answers online which were helpful when I was confused about anything. Quizzes were ok, but you have to go to office hours to find out which questions you got wrong and why.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not the worst professor, but his lectures are dull so it is hard to pay attention and take anything away from it. The quizzes can be tricky but the project, HW, and labs are all doable. Overall, I would recommend a different professor if you can.

Probably the worst professor I've had at UT his lectures are terrible as he seems to have no passion whatsoever for the topics he is teaching. Class is divided into HW, Labs, Quizzes, and a Project. Project makes up a lot of your grade and is relatively easy quizzes are open notes but are a little confusing. Take another professor if you can!

Sarkar made me want to dropout of my major. While I do understand he was under real world stresses that does not excuse his lack of empathy and awful attitude towards his students. His work was difficult and it feels like he expects you to know a graduate level of statistics for a FRESHMAN YEAR COURSE. If you can take another professor. Do it.
If you can take anyone else, please do . Lecture heavy, hard material. Could've been an easy class but the professor makes it difficult for no reason.

Overall good class but its a difficult course. If you're trying to get an easy A this is not the class for you. Lecture heavy so pay attention and take good notes, and if you have questions ASK THEM RIGHT AWAY because you definitely don't want to go into the tests with doubts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sarkar covers a lot of material that's sometimes a bit confusing but is always happy to clarify/explain. Pay attention & take notes, exams are open book/internet and you WILL be expected to use them. This class is coding intensive, so make sure you know R well! HW is .rmd files and exams may or may not be curved. Cares/listens to students :)

This was his first semester teaching so he did pretty well. The class is mostly lecture based since what he talks about in class is on the test. He can go on a tangent in class sometimes but is really helpful in office hours and cares about students understanding the concept. Do well on the HWs and lab and average on the tests and you can get an A

Professor Chan is amazing, could not recommend more. Very welcoming discussion space, very fair grading, and easy, enjoyable projects. She gives you the chance to revise and resubmit your projects once graded, and if you miss class, you can make it up by sending in a paragraph after watching the Zoom. Super reachable online for any questions, too.
Most fun I've ever had in a class

Ms. Chan is the sweetest and most kind professor I've had at UT. Attendance is mandatory, but her lectures are engaging and interesting. Her only downfall is her grading, she didn't grade 80% of our work until the day before grades were due which was very frustrating. Very sweet, and lax on extensions though, loved being in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the few good Econ profs at UT. He does really well to go over examples and explain the material during his lectures to where anyone can understand it. Genuinely wants you to do well. Tests are similar to practice exams he posts but a little harder. Maybe it was because I took this with 420s, but this was a cakewalk compared to that class

Great Professor, very good at breaking down economic principles that were previously hard for me. Only 2 exams, but if you study the lecture notes and quizzes, you're good to go. Go to his office hours before exams to help with key concepts. Papers are straightforward with clear grading, just follow the rubric, and you'll get an A. Best Econ class!

Best econometrics prof at UT. His lectures are clear and easy to follow. If you go to class, he goes out of his way to help you with quizzes and exams. Exams are also only 30% of your course grade, and he writes easier exams than the other professors. He also gives great practice exams and hints. Take him!
Professor Ackerberg has a great style of teaching, and makes econometrics easy and enjoyable. If you attend class, he will give you hints for quizzes and exams.

He does a great job of slowing and simplifying the material. He recaps the previous class and reiterates important parts. Upbeat and wants you to succeed! One homework assignment for a completion grade a week, and quizzes on Thursday (can take from home but tells answers in class often). Class gets curved at the end. Take him!

Professor Ackerberg is a great teacher to have for Econometrics. He is great at simplifying the tougher material into something that anyone can understand. Exams are difficult and he often times writes questions with tricky wording. Overall great guy, highly recommend.
chill dude, pretty tough class but im as dumb as a rock so yall are chillin. just study the quizzes and practice exams and you'll be good for the midterms. GG on the paper tho
Great professor for ECO441K
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you need a UGS class, TAKE THIS ONE, IT'S THE EASIEST AND BEST ONE. Most of the grade is just attendance. We had field trips and talked about medicine, which ended up being really helpful information when flu season came around. My friend was jealous I was in this class compared to her UGS, cause it's just that easy.

I'm being so serious, as a STEM major, I think this is the best class/professor I've had and will remain that way for my foreseeable academic career. Real-world applicability of knowledge, genuinely easy to learn and helpful knowledge that can improve many life circumstances, and best of all, the field trips and overall genuine class culture!

The easiest class I took all semester. I got a lot of good information though, and it was nice to check in on our well-being throughout the semester. The class was VERY relaxed, and there aren't exams, so paying attention is fun but optional. Attendance is mandatory though, but it's not hard to get motivation to go because it's a fun class.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Prof Acosta is super nice, she cares about her students, she's lenient on due dates and she's a good teacher. There are easy weekly readings/discussion posts from a book she provides, 2 papers, and some easy projects. We also went on field trips around campus and she ends class early. The material is interesting too. A PERFECT UGS.

Dean Acosta is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She is extremely caring and genuinely cares if you are struggling or not and will do her best to help you. The semester is super fun and filled with museum trips, pilates and cycling classes, and very interesting lectures. She is an extremely accomplished and real person and is great!!

If you need to take a UGS, take this class. Dr. Acosta is amazing, and does an incredible job of balancing showing us the different aspects of the university while teaching us about her topic. There are discussion posts, a few reflection papers, two big (4 page) papers, one group project, and one individual project. Take this class.
Professor Acosta is a great professor and her class is definitely an easy A. As long as you go to class, participate, and do your work on time, you will definitely pass this class.

Easiest class I have ever taken, Acosta is super chill and rly sweet. At the beginning of the sem, she said you have to try rly hard to not get an A and she means it. Attendance is for a grade but her class always ends 30 mins early so no point in skipping. You get to go on walks and explore campus, do yoga, pilates, and a lotta fun stuff!!!

Professor Acosta is the best! She led class well and allowed for digressions in lecture to talk about self care methods and OTC products relevant to our personal lives. She cares for her students and even provided lunch at the end of the semester to celebrate. We took a few fun excursions during the semester such as a yoga, pilates, and art tours.

Take this class if you want a good UGS!! She is very straight-forward, and the lectures are extremely interesting. You can tell she really cares about her students, and she also ends class early frequently. You get to learn about sleep, exercise, meditation, etc. and go on tours and field-trips. If you show up, you'll get an A

Take this UGS!!! After talking to my friends, this has to be the easiest UGS at UT. There are a couple of research papers and multiple reflection writing assignments, but they weren't graded harshly at all. Her goal was really to get students acquainted with the university and to learn the a little bit about self care and OTC products.

I loved Prof. Acosta and her UGS. I thought that the reviews were being too generous but as soon as I walked into her class I felt welcomed. She took us on tours and even to do yoga and pilates. On the last day she brought us food, and no exams or final! Take this UGS, shes the best Prof. anyone can ever have.

Wow. I literally cannot recommend Professor Acosta highly enough. This class was amazing. She genuinely cares about her students and it shows. There were a couple of papers and presentations, but they were incredibly easy to prepare for and Acosta is an easy grader. She threw us a party on the last day of class too with free food! TAKE THIS CLASS!
This is by far the best UGS to take. The class is literally just about taking care of yourself, and Prof. Acosta is an incredibly caring professor who makes you feel welcome at UT.
take her UGS!!! Professor Acosta is the sweetest and does a good job introducing freshman to the campus by incorporating fun class activities. Easiest UGS, if you just show up you will make an A+

Probably one of the easiest UGS classes, and you get to knock out a writing flag. Two main essays along with mini-reflections from museum tours, which seems like a lot but honestly it's not. The only thing she really "grades" on is grammar/spelling. She does take participation really seriously, as it is part of the grade.

Super easy UGS! A bit of writing but most of them were reflections that took about 30 minutes per each one. She graded leniently and as long as you came to class and put some effort in you end up with an A. Would definitely recommend! Even brought us food on our last day to celebrate- super awesome lady!

I took her UGS of self care and OTC products and it was a great class. We had lots of papers but they were graded leniently and if you actually just put a decent amount of effort into them you'll get an A. She ends class early most of the times and she always is very chill about grades. Super nice and approachable as well.

I wanted to enjoy this class. Unfortunately the mostly engaging lectures were overshadowed by absolute incompetence in course structure, communication & grading. I swear I saw a tumbleweed roll through the canvas page. He won't provide a rubric or tell you what's being graded (I asked). Don't take this class if you care about GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Posts no slides, lectures are disorganized, and he rushes through material while going on random tangents. Don't trust the grade distribution, he gave me the WRONG FINAL GRADE and ignored my emails. If I didn't track him down and catch him by PURE LUCK, I would've left this class with a wrecked GPA because he mixes up people's grades. Absurd prof.

I genuinely hated this class. The professor acts like a loud cartoon character but can't stay on topic or deliver a coherent lecture. He constantly tries to sneak in and push his political views and derails class with hour-long rants if you ask questions, then rushes through the rest and we cant even take notes. Total mess of a course.

I'm a STEM major used to tough classes, but this is the only one I didn't get an A in. I gave 100%, yet the professor made success impossible—no slides on Canvas, no exam reviews, ignored emails. It felt like he was actively working against us. Horrible experience. Worst class I've ever taken.

He secretly grades participation but won't tell you unless you pry in office hours. He's mixed up grades before, so your final grade is likely wrong. Most students didn't bother checking since he ignores emails and hides in his office. The worst part? Leaving with a wrecked GPA because of his careless mistakes. And you probably wouldn't even tell.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Absolutely does not care about students succeeding. The final is worth 35% of your grade and he DOESN'T GIVE AN EXAM REVIEW. Lectures make zero sense, and he constantly mixes up names and the spelling. Randomly changes grade weighting without announcing it, and lies about difficulty for each assignment. Awful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Syllabus and office hours are useless, he can and will change up the class format on a whim. Cannot properly do math, so chances are your grade will be misleading. No coherency at all during lectures, if you're not already strong in the subject, you're gonna do terrible. How UT allows these professors to teach is beyond me.

AVOID. While he held office hours, he lied about pretty much anything he said regarding the course format. My grade was up in the air until the final week of the class so that was a bummer too. Sure he was nice but did not teach properly. His lectures were all over the place and for a history class there was no chronological order.

He was the worst professor I ever had. He changed the rubric on the tests with no clear direction on anything on paper. Avoid at all costs if trying to find a good government class as the GOV366T label for this class is misleading due to this class being solely a history class. He is terrible with technology and does not respond to emails.

Terrible professor due to his constant rants during the lectures which causes him to rush his lectures. He constantly changes the class format and rubrics verbally and does not post lecture slides or a final review despite rushing. Office hours do not help at all as he constantly changes what he says so cannot trust office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at UT. "Lectures" are unorganized and rushed slideshows with dense slides that aren't even shared. No Canvas use. Expectations for writing assignments are unclear. Grades rely heavily on the exam and final (no final review guide either). Avoid unless you have prior knowledge on the topic or grad-level writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is nice and willing to help answer some questions, but wow, his class is extremely unorganized. He posts nothing but the readings on canvas. He goes very fast during lectures and doesnt post the lecture slides on canvas. Doesnt do reviews for the midterm/final. You wont really know your grade until after the semester is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting class, with more unstructured lectures, but engaging, focusing on broader historical patterns and concepts as well as trying to draw out their current relevance. While he listens to his students, his assessment organisation wasn't great - our midterm format was changed a few times without notice.

Agbaria is an amazing lecturer and clearly cares about the students and course material. Course has 3 (mini) essays, midterm + final, and all of them are graded pretty generously. I learned more in this class than in any other history course at UT. Only downside is he doesn't post slides or record lectures.

Professor Agbaria is one of the best professors in the Middle Eastern studies department, and he's incredibly passionate about what he teaches. He is very well knowledged on everything about the Middle East, specifically Israel-Palestine, and he does a great job of interacting with his students on the subjects.

Nice guy, but extremely unorganized class. Lectures were all over the place. Tons and tons of reading. If you don't know a good amount about israel prior to taking this class DO NOT TAKE IT, you will struggle even with going to office hours and putting in a lot of extra work. No rubrics for some reason. Refuses to give prep for tests.

Agbaria is a new teacher and does not know how to run a classroom. He does not believe in study guides for exams. Lecture notes are not provided. He does not use canvas and not a single grade was ever posted. Lectures are extremely unproductive and most of class time was spent bickering with students. Absolutely do NOT recommend taking his class.

Dr. Agbaria is a very characteristic and passionate professor. He has all of the best intentions, but falls short of what is expected in a teacher. His doesn't use Canvas (not a single grade nor assignment posted all semester). His grading criteria is very unclear with no rubrics whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor super passionate about the subject matter. He made me want to go to lectures. The writing assignments were largely graded on completion, and if you put effort into the class, you will make an A. Highly recommend this incredible man!

I took MES 301L, not 343, but it wouldn't let me change the course code. Dr Agbaria was a professor whose class I looked forward to attending, and I don't enjoy early classes. His lectures were clear with what will appear on the exams, just make sure you attend class daily and do the readings. He's funny and I felt comfortable asking him questions.

Dr. Agbaria is genuine, funny, and knowledgable. I learned a lot about the Arab-Israeli conflict from both sides. The class could be more organized, and tests were worded slightly confusingly, but he is understanding and more than willing to adjust. Lecture attendance is important for papers and exams. Overall, very rewarding class.
Some assignments took me a long time but the tests were an accurate reflection of them. Just study and you'll pass with ease.
She is completely inaccessible. I tried many times to get ahold of her through email and she never responded.  Really disappointing class experience.

Her class was not that difficult, but she is pretty unprofessional and often says weirdly inappropriate things in class. I'm glad it was online, because dealing with her in person would not be pleasant. It wasn't even really pleasant online tbh. The class is ok, but I would recommend finding another section or professor to enroll in.
I really liked her! I think her lectures were engaging and she seemed to be nice. The class was straightforward and easy to understand.

Fun&Silly class. I had 2 professors: Mateer and Acciardo. The textbook doesn't worth purchasing because contains a bunch of specific examples. Class participation: kahoots & puzzlers. Homework: InQuizitives. 2 open book\note Exams(50 points each).Office Hours: case solutions with minimum explanations. If u rn't familiar with ECO, it will be tough.

Probably the best economics class I have taken (saying this as a senior). Other econ classes are heavily theory based and entail lots of dry lectures. Experimental economics, on the other hand, allows students to apply theory in the form of classroom games that foster strategic thinking and collaboration. +50 Quick thinking rating improvement.

Experimental Economics is the best class I have taken in the Economics Department. It helps with real-life application of econ studies. She loves her job and her students. Engage in class and write the papers with meaningful connections - not hard to do because she is very informative and inspiring. Wonderful class and a wonderful professor.
This is a really good class for the basics of econ. Really well taught, not to much hw. You certianly have to go to class however and kahoots are a big part of your grade. Exam heavy.

Super great professor. Use the past tests and kahoots to review for the tests and make sure to keep notes organized so you can use them on tests. take this econ class it's not bad even if you don't think econ/math is your strong suit.

Great prof., just personally bad at econ. Tests make up the majority of the course grade, and it is highly important that students read the textbook (note you must pay to access it online). Very clear syllabus and expectations. Attendance is not required, but recommended in order to earn full points. Lots of resources available to students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class relies heavily on the information conveyed in the lectures, Kahoots, and IQs. Make sure you study for the tests as they make up a major portion of the grade. Professor Acchiardo made the lectures entertaining and fast-paced. The lectures are engaging and include many real-life applications of the concepts.

I found the second and third tests of this course to be challenging, and felt that some questions weren't a true reflection of what was taught in class. That being said, both professors were engaging with the lectures and real world examples used. Make sure to use the office hours, and do the practice test questions: those are your best resources!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took econ in high school so a lot of this class was review. That being said, I feel like I still learned a lot in the class. Class is online and you rack up points for participation/extra credit. Once you are done with that, you can straight up just not attend class if you want. The first exam was fairly easy, but the second and third were harder

Econ is a notoriously tough subject, but Professors Charity Joy and Dirk made learning it a breeze! I took this class for my applied economics minor and loved it! It is entirely remote via video stream, but they make it interactive with live demos and in-class activities. Read/take notes on the book and do practice questions to score high on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The textbook is straightforward and to the point pairing very well with the lectures. The lectures are synchronous and filled with many real-world examples of economics, making learning enjoyable. The class is graded with combined quiz grades (very easy to get full points) and 3 Exams. Exam material is straightforward making them not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A large online class, which makes it harder to get personal help if you struggle. Attendance is basically mandatory, as there are in-class activities for credit that you can't do after class. This class took up 2-3 hours a week (outside of class time) for reading the textbook and homework. The tests are fairly easy and open notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Acchiardo is very compassionate about the subject she teaches. She is very sociable in-person with students that attend the lectures and participate in the demonstrations. She has made my day on two occasions despite having very few interactions. She is an engaging lecturer, but her explanations can be longwinded and confusing at times.

Although she wasn't the best teacher in terms of explaining concepts, the class itself was a breeze. With a little bit of work and attention, you can succeed. They are very organized and the class is engaging. Lots of resources were given, so it depends on your own self-drive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: r u an online school kinda gal? you'll love this class! unfortunately, I do not want to wake up at 9am, get straight onto a boring lecture where I end up zoning out, then get interrupted every 15 min by a mandatory quiz/Kahoot. spent all-nighters cram-reading the textbook before tests bc that was the only way I could learn. pros are open note tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you can take econ with Dirk and Charity Joy, do it. Economics isn't easy but they do an amazing job at preparing you for the open-note, online tests. You definitely need to study but they make class interesting with their kahoots and fun videos. Was very nervous about this class but it ended up being a breeze with them. 10/10!!

Professors Mateer & Acchiardo make learning economics interesting. They go into detail about why it matters and how it applies in the world. It's a shame so many students complain about the kahoots and technical issues; everyone received a 100 for the day when these occurred. You need 60% accuracy to get a 100. Pay attention and use your resources.

Really easy class. Exams were online, open-note, and multiple-choice. You do have to attend class because of Kahoot quizzes, but they are curved by 40%. Funny lectures. I do not understand the negative reviews; she co-taught the class with Dr. George Mateer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Only cared for the credit of the class.
Professor Acchiardo was not the best at explaining concepts, usually had to rely on other professors and textbooks. 
Lectures did help a lot, especially Kahoot exercises.
The textbook understanding was vital and exams were pretty hard but also confusing at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The actual concepts were simple, but her explanations were so complicated. They spent more time and effort making the class "entertaining" than educating. She wasn't very accommodating and came off rude most times. The tests weren't hard, but they're way different from the Kahoot questions and the practice tests. Would not recommend.

took intro to macroeconomics with her over the summer (completely online/asynchronous). never saw her once and never even received her contact info/email. she was completely unreachable, and tests were extremely challenging. they did not relate to what we learned and questions were very ambiguous. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND

For this class, READ THE BOOK and form study groups. This was an incredibly difficult class. I felt like I knew all the material and my test grade would tell me otherwise. What got me through was the support of my friends and us teaching each other concepts because the professors aren't great. Study hard, use your resources, and keep the faith!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class in the video streamed format. It seems as if Charity-Joy cared more about how the production of the class looked versus teaching us about microeconomics. Tests were very hard because they didn't match the material we learned in class. There's also at least one pop kahoot quiz every class that counts towards your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Chairity joy was not kind at all and I do not recommend taking this course unless you like tests. The whole grade is depended on 3 tests which is very unfair. There is nothing that is dropped and there is 1 extra credit that barley does anything. She was unkind after I sent an email to her asking if I could do any extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst part about this class is the set up. Class is video streamed and there seems to always be some type of technology issue. Other than that the class is pretty easy for a college level course. Re-reading the textbook and inquisitives before a test secured me an A on each one. As long as you dont slack off youll be fine.

Online video stream class yet still seemed condescending, learned everything from the textbooks, still participated in class for the kahoot in class assignments, seems disinterested, overall easy content if you take the time to study and read textbook outside of lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would never take economics at UT online with these professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took the online ECO 304K class taught by professors Mateer and Acchiardo. Content was very easy but still went pretty fast. Taught in a video stream format so it felt one-sided and difficult to communicate back. The one TA in the chat carried. Got an A but only showed up to class for participation points, textbook was more helpful in learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Joy is a really solid professor. In my opinion, the Microeconomics' concepts are pretty easy to understand and Joy does a great job of keeping it simple. The online class had some technical issues, but the professors did a great job considering the circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was probably the hardest class Ive ever taken. The material was not very confusing but the explanations given by the professor will confuse you and then the exams are pretty hard. The first exam is relatively easy, the second one is nothing like the review. Also, the class was huge so many of the questions asked were not addressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Acchiardo is absolutely phenomenal. Her captivating lectures leave me enlightened and motivated to learn! I look forward to this class each week but prepare for the kahoots before class. If you stay on top of your work you'll perform adequately! I highly recommend this class!

A lot of your grade is based on the tests so just read the textbook and go to SI sessions and you will definitely be prepared. A lot of the test is just reworded questions from those resources. Charity-Joy is also really good at explaining things and breaks stuff down to easy digestible amounts.

I thought the class was fine. The Kahoots are a little annoying at the beginning, but you get used to them as the semester progresses. Exams aren't too difficult... just read the textbook and go over the inquisitives (homework assignments). Lectures are solid as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: there are plenty of Kahoots in class and the profs do not explain the content clearly

doesn't explain well/the class is online so your questions are rarely answered. you can attend SI sessions if u have time though. light work- reading/quiz once a week- read the textbook and you'll pass. kahoots every class that are so stupid because you barely know the content and only have 30sc. she's smart, just not good at teaching, take at ACC
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Explain the materials poorly

Because he was leaving this semester, it felt as if his class was sloppily composed due to his lack of passion for UT. He's great at what he does, but he put the bare minimum into this class's structure. However, he is great at explaining Bangla for non-native speakers and was such a kind and hilarious professor. Smart man, just very disorganized!

Professor Shamim is adaptable in his teaching methods. If a student is struggling with a particular part of the Bangla language, he will make sure that the student will eventually understand it. This ranges from the alphabet, general grammar, vocabulary, to even dialects. Not only that, he is available outside class if you ask him. Adore this guy!
Dr. Shamim is a great teacher. He is fun, caring, and laid back. The workload is also very reasonable and slow-paced as he wants everyone to learn on the same page. Take him!
He is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are clear and beneficial to the class. He engages his students with understandable materials. Would recommend everyone to take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best ever
Take his class. Gives a heavy curve and material isn't complicated

Like another reviewer said, Shaz's lectures lack any sense of cohesion. She jumps around in topics, time periods and regions frequently. Judging by the lack of attendance everyday, I would say most people agree with me when I say that this class was a waste of time. Shaz is very smart, but a bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Liked her approach but lectures can be quite hard to follow. Tends to assume everyone is on the same page based on a few vocal students. However it was still pretty easy to make an A in the class, and I felt I didn't need to show up to make the grade. Essay assignments are the majority of the grade and can be done largely independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures were highly informative and she encourages independent reading when writing papers. Shaherzad is extremely knowledgable and will guide you in the right direction. If you like the course title and topic, she's the person to take it with!
Pretty easy grader, I feel like if you put in the effort you'll make an A. "Shaz" knows her stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I did not think she was great at all. Her lectures were very sporadic and they did not follow a clear progression. She had way too many assignments and expectations for a lower division history course (over 20 pages worth of papers for the semester). She was available outside of class but she had clear favorites.

He's a great professor, and the class was a lot of fun. I'm a huge history nerd, and I really learned a lot and gained new insight into politics and philosophy. The reading and the class discussions were great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great guy, great professor. Class is clear-cut & minimalist: do the daily readings, come ready to discuss/debate, and complete the two assigned papers. Final grade comprised of few assignments, w/ each paper weighted HEAVILY. Can be a tough grader w/ sorta unrealistic standards, but final is easy. Very intellectual, pensive guy - great to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is really good at leading discussion based courses and helps keep class discussions from getting too tangential.  I didn't do a lot of the readings near the end because I was swamped and got recked by the final.  I liked him though, wish I could take again and try harder.   Really cool to talk with during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Siddiqi is very thorough. His class is difficult for a lower division government class, but I found it enjoyable. If you don't like philosophy, you may want to steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This course is an introductory survey of the political philosophy of several philosophers throughout the western world. Those who are uninterested in reading antiquated texts pertaining to political philosophy should not take this course. This course contains substantial reading. This course was incredibly thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class is A LOT of work, especially if you don't start with any Persian. Very homework-heavy, flipped-classroom, so you work through the textbook on your own, class is for practice and tests. However, this professor really cares about student outcomes and tries her best to help. You could also see the class improving throughout the semester.

Great class and will really teach you Farsi if you commit to it. Simply doing the homework and making sure to get it right will basically get you literate. It is a time commitment, 2hrs three times a week and it takes about 2hrs to do homework every night too, upside is all the other assignments also take 2hrs so nothing is killer. She is also nice

The class is a mess. First time teaching and she's just as lost as us. Two papers and a presentation account for 80% of your final grade. She doesn't know how to use a computer or any kind of technology. The class organization is absent. Due dates are listed on the syllabus and make sure to remember them cuz no one will remind you. DON'T TAKE THIS!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You do not need to read anything!!! he spends all of lecture going through the summary of that happened over the "assigned reading" and gets really off track, but ALL of the assignemnts are super easy and the prompts are so broad that you can just research and write instead of reading the dense material. HE GRADES ON GRAMMAR OVER CONTENT!!!

Enthusiastic, fun, and interesting, but a lot of the content covered in class is unnecessary to do well. Once you understand how he grades papers will be easy A's, he is not tech savvy but genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching

Dr. Afolabi is a very enthusiastic professor! His class is interesting and straightforward but can be pretty disorganized at times. Many papers are assigned, but the class does carry a writing flag. He grades mainly based on grammar instead of the essays' actual content. Once you understand his writing style, getting A's on the papers is very easy

afolabi is passionate, caring, and super funny! class had lots of papers but that comes with any writing flag. papers were graded mostly on grammar and less on content, so it was very easy to get above a 95. you can get by with skimming the books he assigns (no need to buy since he has pdfs) or listening in lecture. loved this prof and the class

Much of this class is saved by the interesting topic and the professor who presents the information. His regular enthusiasm and willingness to describe a culture which, at least to me, was novel proved to be highly valuable. However, his critiques of writing are at best technical and the stylistic and argumentative feedback was distinctly limited.

Professor Afolabi is passionate about what he teaches, and I highly recommend his UGS class. There is usually a 2-3 page paper due every week. However, he grades very fairly and the vast majority of students in his class receive an A. The class is actually really interesting, and I have a new found appreciation for Brazilian culture. Solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Afolabi is an amazing professor, he certainly does not do things the "standard" way you might imagine. He is articulate, passionate, and hilarious. The course consists of incredibly unique and interesting topics that are important to learn. He may come off as harsh sometimes, but his criticisms are honest and in the best interest of the student

Professor Afolabi is such an interesting, funny, charismatic, and enthusiastic professor! He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and comes to each class full of energy. There are quite a few essays to write in this class, but Dr. Afolabi grades really leniently and gives great constructive criticism.

His enthusiasm can be a lot for some students, but it makes the class more interesting! He gives out a lot of writing assignments but it is a writing class but they are pretty easy and he is very flexible on grading (especially on the midterm). We have one midterm (annotated bibliography) and a final paper. Overall, this class is very interesting!

Whatever class you take with afolabi will be really interesting. He's super outgoing and funny, and he's really flexible with grading. I took Intro to Brazilian Studies and had a great time, and you can tell he's really passionate about what he does.

Professor Afolabi is an interesting professor. I learned a lot from his UGS302 Brazilian Studies class, and the small class format made it more engaging and fun. He can be hard to understand with his accent and his comments on papers dont always make sense, but he is very knowledgable about Brazil. One of the best classes I've taken at UT.

Dr. Shaikh is a caring and compassionate professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and assigns relevant and thoughtful assignments. With fair effort, this class is very doable and enjoyable. She is wonderful!

Dr. Shaikh made her expectations for the class very clear and graded content fairly. She truly cares about each one of her students and is always open to talk about any concerns. This class did not require a ton of effort, but you should still put an honest effort into the assignments.

I took the EDP Career Planning course over the summer and enjoyed it! We learned so much—I especially loved our textbook since it was actually fun to read. There were reading/content quizzes, assignments graded on effort because they were focused on your personal career planning, and an interview of someone in your field of interest for the final.

This is the third class I've taken with Afsar. He's a great professor. The subject material is always very interesting, and he doesn't shy away from controversial or 'awkward' topics. He always brings humor to the discussion as well. He is very interested in students' progress and is always willing to meet to discuss papers,etc.

Presently, I'm in Prof. Afsar's "Modern India and Literature" class. I'm so lucky to get into the class which has a long wait list. And,Prof. Afsar never disappointed until now. He is passionate, fun and clarity of thought. Wonderful insights into the materials.

Taking Prof. Afsar's new class "Pilgrimage in South Asia." Heard a lot about Prof. Afsar before, but this is my first class with him. Really enjoyable! Extremely fascinating/ real research experiences! Accessible Professor, loves to spend more time with the students. Values the student voice and he has a great smile!
Great Professor!

Afsar is passionate about his subject and enjoys sharing the materials. Focuses a lot on the progress of his students and meets even outside the class to have conversations and discussions about the subject.

Really cares for the progress of the student. Makes every class a memorable experience with lot of stories. I've been taking his courses continuosly. Specifically his course on South Asian Novel is my favorite.
Afsar is very particular about attendance and pushes you to participate in the class discussions. Always thought-provoking and worth pursuing materials.
GREAT PASSION FOR TEACHING AND VERY ACCESSIBLE PROFESSOR!

He is a great professor with lots of passion for his subject! I enjoyed every minute of his class. If you keep up with the work and go to class then you should have no problem getting the grade you want. How much you get out of the class depends on how much you put in!Make sure you meet him outside of class because he is a great person to get to kn
Dr. Gheith is an exceptional CS professor!

Gheith is an incredible lecturer, and I learned so much from his class. But the projects are brutal. Expect honors-level difficulty in an already very tough course. If you take this course you should probably clear out some other commitments and be prepared to spend 30-40 hours per week on it.
very good prof

Prof. Gheith is a great lecturer, and is willing to explain topics further for interested students (his lectures are more freeform). However, assignments are often tougher than they seem, so get started EARLY!! Also, quizzes are no joke, so try to do some learning about topics on your own. Experience is definitely summed up by the 5.0/5.0 rate.

One of those classes where you come out with a profound jump in mastery even if you only got a C-. The lectures are an absolute delight, he has immense understanding of the material. Likely the hardest programming projects you will do during your time at UT, but also thoroughly instructive and insightful. May have to no-life this class to do well.

Dr. Gheith is the best professor I have ever had! His lectures are truly amazing, and while the class is incredibly intensive project-wise, this finished product (a good chunk of an OS) is incredible and extremely rewarding. Having a small community with amazing TAs made the class experience even better. 10/10 would recommend!

For context, he teaches normal OS in Spring, honors in the Fall. Professor Gheith is one of the smartest professors I have taken and honestly, my favorite. No slides, just him, you, class, and whiteboard. Would I recommend over Norman? Yes, if you want a challenge. I also learned an incredible amount, but did I also spend 35+ hours per week? Yes.

Honestly, he's the best professor I've ever had in my entire life. While expectations are high, it is so rewarding, and Dr. Gheith and the TAs do their best to help you. Projects take a long time to complete, but are genuinely so awesome since you get to build your own operating system. I would strongly recommend taking Gheith over anyone else.

This was undoubtedly the hardest CS class i've taken here; however it's also been my favorite. Expect atleast 25 hours a week on projects with 0 days off. Our TAs were so goated and we had a great little community going making it that much more enjoyable. Gheith is also insanely well versed in OS and is genuinely always willing to help. 10/10

As an average CS student: CS439 is the hardest class you'll ever take, 30+ hrs/week is real. I couldn't take Norman and was terrified, but Gheith is amazing. Insanely rigorous, but his passion is mesmerizing. Office hours became group therapy. I now feel emotionally bonded to my TAs and peers. Might be Stockholm Syndrome. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Gheith? More like Dr.Goat

Hated lectures- went over my head, and it felt like he catered the class towards the top 5 students in the class who actually understood things. Projects were soul sucking, and quizzes were too. Take Norman if you can. Save yourself and your sanity.
He just knows

Very caring and knowledgeable professor. Good lectures. Projects are extremely challenging but rewarding, requiring ~15-30hrs per week. Quizzes are created by the TAs, and often did not match up with what we were learning, were way too hard, or the questions didn't properly test our knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredible lectures. The content is really fun IMO. Projects are a lot of work, take precautions to not write nasty bugs, hardest part. Grading and quizzes are incredibly wack though. What they expect for answers is not properly communicated, and grades only come in at the end. You will get docked big on participation unless you go to TA OH i think
Do you like operating systems? You better like operating systems. If you don't like operating systems, you are in for a whole lot of pain.
I did not sleep for more than 5 hours per day because of this guy. I lost 60 pounds because I was glued to vscode every minute of the day that i didn't even have time to eat.
This was the most eye-opening course in my career. I strongly recommend students take Dr. Gheith's OS courses!

Gheith is an incredible lecturer and is filled with knowledge. But the pace of this class and the fact that TAs (other undergrads) are in charge of all things grading makes it extremely difficult. There are 9 projects and quizzes every other week. Projects are intense and quizzes are hard with unclear grading at times. Don't get behind.

Dr. Gheith is defo one of the best people I've had as a professor-- you can't not like him. But, this might've been the most disorganized course I've ever taken. The TAs (mostly undergrads) handle everything including grading. Sometimes it felt like they weren't sympathetic, and their quizzes were nightmare fuel. The projects were hard but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures will trick you into thinking this is a simple class, and the projects will quickly make you realize how many details the lecture missed. Very challenging and unfair class, and one of the worst experiences of my life. I learned a lot, but I would recommend taking Norman.

Gheith is a kind professor and obviously very smart. However, his class structure is very disorganized. There is little to no support for students who are struggling. The TAs are honestly the worst part of this course. They have no empathy for the students and struggle to explain concepts coherently.
Normies take Norman, GOATs take Gheith
good luck !

Gheith is one of the best lecturers at UTCS. Projects are difficult and require a network of friends to succeed. Quizzes are intellectually stimulating but are very difficult and are crafted solely by the TAs. Class is somewhat disorganized as there are no clear rubrics for participation or certain projects. Take Gheith if you want a challenge, GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOODBYE OS, SEE YOU NEVER (no but fr take Norman)

Great lecturing, that is undeniable. However serious issues with lack of structure and communication. The syllabus hasn't been updated in years and doesn't reflect his actual policies (especially what's considered academically dishonest), and I have had friends and TAs be unable to contact him during pertinent deadlines.
don't take it if you aren't super interested about os. you would probably be better off with norman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is sink or swim class and there is no support for those sinking. The teacher is unavailable outside class, OH lines are long, and there are few resources unlike Norman's. Gheith is a good lecturer, but lectures are unorganized which can make it hard to figure out what exactly you're supposed to be following. Projects also have NO instructions.
No materials for the class. TAs don't exist until the last week. Your Grade depends strictly on the quizzes. Servers WILL be down when you're trying to submit. Take Norman
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I took Norman

Super unstructured class w/ minimal resources. Waste hours waiting in office hours for TAs who are clueless on how to help half the time. Lectures aren't recorded & get insanely long + difficult to follow. Only take if you actually like OS... Otherwise take Norman, easier content w/ more resources available and partner projects.

Gheith gave some of the best lectures I've experienced at UT - super engaging, with nothing but a marker. He extended project deadlines to help our struggling class. Yes, this class is HARD, individual projects and bi-weekly quizzes are VERY challenging. Still, this class is so rewarding. If you have the chance to take him, do it.

Dr. Gheith is not the god of lectures, but he's exceptionally kind and understanding. Graded by projects, difficult quizzes (that will only be easier if students write quiz questions for participation points), and participation. I wish he would record the lectures himself instead of someone from the student body being responsible for it.
bro cooked us
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yet another 5.0 Gheith rating!

The only bad thing about Dr Gheith is that there's only one of him. I wish we could clone him and have him teach every class. He's at least a standard deviation above every other professor I've had in lecturing/communication ability, clarity and fairness of assignments and grading, classroom management, pacing, and motivation of the subject matter.
Still the goat

Projects are insane and take at least 40 hours/week - get ready to sell your soul to this class. Lectures are outstanding, going to class and paying attention is a must. Gheith is utterly inaccessible outside of class. Biweekly quizzes are hard but projects help study for them. You will not know your grade until the last week of semester.

Weekly projects take 50+ hours, no exams, biweekly hard quizzes (study for them!). This will undoubtedly be the hardest class you will ever take, but Gheith's lectures will make it ALL worth it. The second half of semester was much easier based off of feedback. This class is a rite-of-passage, and one of the most life-changing classes I've taken.

Gheith is so smart that I can't understand half of the content for the life of me. Great if you want to learn systems, not so great if you want to do well in the class because TAs dictate all grading. He does his best to accommodate individual circumstances if you just talk to him about them. Nevertheless, he is invaluable to the UTCS department.
Incredible lecturer. Homework can be very time consuming and quizzes can be quite difficult, but overall great class.

i love prof. gheith. he's very patient and an exciting lecturer. the class is hard though, projects take lots of time but gheith and the TAs are pretty understanding. grade will be rough but you will learn a lot.

Amazing lecturer, but does not communicate with TAs at all/enforce any restrictions on them. The TAs were free to provide difficult quizzes without Gheith's approval and did not grade assignments until several months after they were due. The professor is impossible to reach via email.

Best professor I've ever had. Very knowledgeable and he explained extremely complicated topics from the ground up in a digestible way. Lectures were entertaining and he explained why we built things the way we did and other alternatives. 10000/10 would take again.

Best lecturer ever, loves computer architechture and knows everything about everything. Amazing projects where you learn so much, but they can be challenging. Weekly quizzes that were really hard but not impossible.

Get ready to spend all your time on this class. Some weeks I was easily in the GDC past 12am. It kinda got fun after a while tho. It is extremely hard, don't be afraid to ask the TAs questions as well as those around you. Also I thought I was gonna fail until the last week and ended up with a B if that gives you any hope. Utilize office hours!

Amazing professor, hard ass class. But that's OS for you so don't be scared to take him. Somehow this genius man could show up to class with nothing necessarily prepared, and give a whole lecture off the top of his head. He is very engaging and helpful, but outside of class you have to rely on TAs/others to help understand.

Great professor but insanely inaccessible outside of class. TAs do 100% of the grading and like others have mentioned some can show favoritism, so it can be difficult to get help during office hours. When it comes to deciding between Gheith or Norman for 439, expect amazing lectures and difficult, rewarding assignments but delayed/no communication.

I agree with others on Gheith's knowledge and kindness, but sometimes I felt an over-reliance on office hours and friend networks to complete projects. This course pushes those interested in systems to their limits for the better, but the culture of the class can feel strangely intense and cliquey (both TAs and classmates) when trying to seek help

Super interesting course. Dr. Gheith is an amazing, kind, and approachable lecturer. However, projects cannot be competed without OH. Make friends. Get to know the TAs. Dr. Gheith is not easily accessible outside class. Great lectures, but projects require TA assistance and a network of friends to get info, and are borderline unfair.

I really liked having Dr. Gheith. He is an AMAZING lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory in this class but going to class helps. Weekly quizzes (no tests) - fairly difficult. The assignments are fairly challenging too. The class is hard but make friends in the class, and talk to the TAs and Dr. Gheith himself. Also, the final project is fun to do.

OS will be hard no matter what. Gheith is an amazing lecturer, I enjoyed going to class for once. Gheith himself is a bit disorganized. However, the coding assignments and quizzes are very hard and the TAs had an intense disconnect from what's happening in class. Make friends, go to OHs (including Gheith's), and introduce yourself to the TAs early.

OS is one of the hardest classes in UTCS, no doubt. But taking it with Gheith makes it easy to get through. He doesn't use slides but is able to teach such complex ideas in easy to grasp chunks on the whiteboard. Going to OH is a must for the assignments. No tests, weekly quizzes are pretty difficult, final project is fun.

Gheith is great if you're interested in systems. However, that's really not my strong suit, so the class takes a lot of time for what feels like very little payoff. Make sure to study for the quizzes (altho usually depends on TAs) since they're not curved and worth 40% of your grade. Also, final project is graded much harsher than in arch.

In many ways this class felt like 429 part 2. It was almost like Dr. Gheith picked up right where he left off at the end of the previous semester. The style of the class was basically the same with all the signature Gheith specialties. I personally think this class was harder than Arch but some will disagree. There are fewer quizzes than Arch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Papa Gheith never ceases to bless the UT Austin Computer Science Department. Never leave papa, never leave...
I love professor Gheiht!

Weekly assignments and quizzes can be pretty challenging (quizzes more dependent on TAs who write them, but questions are at the upper end of Bloom's taxonomy expecting creation, evaluation, and analysis of topics from class). Because it's every week, the schedule can be tough with little breathing room. Start early, do not fall behind.

Amazing professor. This class is worth the hassle of getting an honors petition. Taught difficult concepts in easy to understand chunks and very good at answering questions. Amazing lecturer. The assignments are very hard but worthwhile. Going to office hours is essential, there's just so much material. No tests, but weekly quizzes.

Probably the best professor I've had at UT. He comes to class and just lectures without slides which were easy to keep up with most of the time. Class is HArd. But going to help hours and piazza helped a ton. Structure of the class was weekly quizzes/assignments, participation, and one final assignment they are lenient on.

Dr. Gheith explains concepts well. The TAs are nice and knowledgeable. His lectures are a little disorganized sometimes. We only had 8 quizzes. If you misunderstand some questions, you may lose many points from the final grade. There are no practice quizzes, so sometimes I know my understanding is wrong in the quizzes. Learn a lot from the course.
Thank you professor Gheith! This class is my favorite class in UT. Professor Gheith is not only a wonderful teacher but also a great person. I learned a lot in this class!

Dr.Gheith is a great lecturer, really just came to class with a dry erase marker and started lecturing from the dome. The class is 50% coding assignments that vary in difficulty but be prepared for at least 15 a week and up to 30 for the harder assignments. Would definitely recommend for OS.

Dr Gheith continues to be a great OS professor. Honors and nonhonors versions were pretty much the same. The honors version had CSB and Turing. Regardless while the projects expectedly take time, you learn a lot of interesting content. I suggest having a friends to study with to get through projects, or someone to discuss with if you're stuck.

I am thrilled that I took OS with professor Gheith. He knows and understands the material so well, literally walks in and starts speaking, and the content makes sense. The only problem is that the projects are VERY time-consuming. This class sucked my soul away for a semester, but Gheith and the TAs made the class doable.

The class is lecture-heavy, there are weekly projects and quizzes that cover that week's topics. The projects are HARD, period. Tough graders, it's somewhat ridiculous. The quizzes are alright if you attend lecture except for one question each week that barely anyone gets right. Participation is 10% of your grade. Getting an A seems very difficult.

Dr. Gheith's Arch class this semester had 9 individual projects, each a week long. They are pretty time consuming and you may lose some sleep. There is a huge learning curve in this class. I learned a lot more than expected, very satisfying. The class heavily uses Piazza. Quizzes every week, pay attention. Dr Gheith loves memes, jokes, and convos.

Dr. Gheith is a true gem of a teacher. Like an emerald (or platinum, etc.). He TEACHES like an ideal lecturer: always introducing concepts from the basic, trivial cases and gradually explaining the next natural step to take. Some parts of an OS are ugly, per se, but Gheith explains the theory + code for EACH component you build. Terrific.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Gheith's 439 class online during COVID, and I can say I was pleasantly surprised that the class was not as terrible as made out to be. Lot of work, but mostly in the beginning. The last 5 or so weeks, the workload was pretty light. No tests, and quizzes are graded easily. Participation counts. Biggest advice: get started on projects early.

Yasss!!!! Absolutely amazing teacher that teaches, cares for, and helps you. Weekly quizzes ensure you're on top of the material and programming assignments are interesting AF! Piazza discussions are engaging. He makes boring material super interesting. Take his course and it will be the one of your best decisions.

Probably one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Thoroughly answers questions in lecture and explains concepts very clearly. Projects are very time-consuming; start early. Weekly quizzes can be annoying, but if you paid attention in class you should be fine. Very flexible and listens to feedback from his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tied for best professor at UT (along with Mike Scott). Taking OS with Gheith is a real learning experience. I would highly recommend taking OS with Gheith instead of Norman, for all the reasons outlined on this page (I did both).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The hardest CS class could not have been taught by a more caring professor. He genuinely wants you to succeed and will stay late to help students with projects. It's hard to fail the class, but at the same time it's as tough as advertised. Attend the lectures and office hours, and you'll be ok.

OS is going to be difficult with whoever you take. That being said, Gheith's class was not overwhelmingly difficult. He makes you work for your grade but so long as you work, you will pass. Lectures are not mandatory, but if you miss one you will be very far behind. He is extremely knowledgeable, lectures from memory. He cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: First things first, anyone saying that they got an A+ in this class or that attendance is mandatory is lying. Keep that in mind when you see all these positive reviews. Lectures still aren't interesting but are more related to the projects. Projects are more designy than Arch. Quizzes were hit or miss. Tests are open book but way too fast paced.

Best teacher I've ever had in my life. Gheith is a treasure of the UT CS department, and explains OS concepts in an approachable easy to understand format entirely from memory. Projects are hard, but Gheith and the TAs are more than willing to help you through them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was hard but rewarding at the same time. Gheith is a great lecturer and I actually wanted to go to lectures because of how good of an educator he is (BAMF lectures completely from memory). Assignments are rough but capped at around 40-50 hours for a given assignment. Going to office hours saved me a bunch of time on the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Walks in with nothing but a whiteboard marker, and delivers amazing lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy sucks. Nothing against him personally, just really didn't enjoy his class. Lectures are super slow and go around in circles. Projects are time-consuming and not related to class material. Quizzes are random. Tests are open-book so questions ended up being either super easy or super hard. I did learn a lot but not due to his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gheith is one of the most amazing professors I've had at UT. His lectures are easy to follow and he manages to make complex subjects very easy to understand. Projects were difficult and time consuming but easily doable if you started early. My only complaint would be that it isn't really possible to study for his tests except by coming to class

Dr. Gheith is probably the best undergraduate professor in UTCS. OS is usually seen as the hardest class of undergrad, but Dr. Gheith's amazing lectures made it a much better experience. He's always available at office hours too. The class is hard but grading is fair and you will come out of it with so much more knowledge than when you went in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Gheith's OS is very project based, and you'll know it. Assignments are weekly, and take anywhere from 20 to 60 hours of work. However, he's a great lecturer, is very helpful during office hours, and is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. But with all the late nights in the lab, I never want to take that class again. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gheith is an amazing teacher who knows the material cold (lectures with no notes) and is very nice in office hours. That said, the class is extremely tough, and of the 14 projects, I and most people I know put in 40+ hours of effort on 4 of them. Find a solid group to work with and plan carefully before writing any code, and you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an excellent professor, but OS is genuinely one of the hardest classes you can take. It will be really difficult for you. Yes, even you. I'd take it again, but only because of the friends I made in it. I literally lost 15lbs because I was working so much on it. Really. It's 50-60 hrs/week. If you do take it, don't take anything else hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Legendary. He's the person who made OS, the most infamous course on the CS degree list, my favorite class at UT. Projects were very time consuming (spent 30+ hours/week) but that's where most of the learning happened. His tests were tough but if you do well on project/quiz it'll be fine. Most importantly he's very approachable so go to office hour!

Gheith was one of the best teachers that I've ever had. He knows his stuff and encourages interesting conversation and lecture. The class is objectively very difficult however. He pushes you hard and enables the student to perform well. As long as you can put in the effort it should be wonderfully challenging.

Gheith is honestly one of the best professors at UT, and has such a different method of teaching. He's really aware if you're not doing well and will do everything he can to make sure you understand the material given you at least put in some effort. I really wish he taught more classes other than Operating Systems
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very, very hard

Absolute best lecturer at UT. He could make a phone book sound exciting, and he explains complicated things really well. But he doesn't expect you to have a life outside his class, and he experiments with the curriculum, often with painful results. Generally 40-60 hours a week on projects. Insane. Exams and weekly quizzes are also pretty tough.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best lectures I've ever attended. He is an amazing teacher and truly cares that his students understand the material. I took 429H and 439H both with Dr. Gheith. Operating Systems (439H) was a lot of work but I learned so much it was totally worth it! 10/10 my favorite professor and would take any class taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! He's very knowledgable and obviously very passionate about what he teaches. LECTURES ARE BASICALLY MANDATORY because lectures & projects are where the majority of learning is done, and you won't know how to do the projects if you don't go to class. His quizzes and tests are very hard so beware because he doesn't curve.
Amazing teacher!
Helpful professor and knows the material inside & out. However, his CS 429 Summer class was insanely challenging. The assignments and quizzes were brutal. I think half the class ended up dropping.

Professor Gheith actually cares about teaching, and is very good at it. There are projects every week, ranging from fairly easy (3 hrs) to very hard (25hrs). I've taken 3 classes with Gheith so far, and if he taught any more, I'd take them too.

Gheith was hands down the best professor I've had so far. His lectures were clear and he took his time to make sure everyone understood what was going on. The projects were challenging, but nothing not doable. If you get the chance to take this or any other course by him, do it.

Great guy and lecturer. He is one of the nicest professors I've met and truly cares for the students. Class was hard though. Tests were intended to fail you and were far too long for anyone to finish (which he said was his intention.) These tests, however, were curved to compensate. Grading: 40% Projects, 20% Midterm, 20% Final, 20% Quizzes

The best professor I have had at UT. Take any classes that he is offering. Incredibly clear, coherent lecture that goes out of his way to ensure that you actually understand the material. On top of that, he is funny guy that is not a hard ass and understands that grades aren't the be all to life. Tests were open book/notes. Highly recommend
For QIS, I thought the content was very interesting, and lectures were good and worth attending. Exams sometimes had unclear questions, but other than that, not terribly difficult.

Knowledgable but cant teach. Explains things too fast, doesnt realize students take longer to understand. Assumes complex things to be common sense. I attended every lecture but most of my learning came from elsewhere. Grading criteria was "1/3rd of class gets an A", left me in shock at my grade at the end. Impossible tests and hw, TAs confused too
Don't be fooled by the difficulty of the homework because the exams are infinitely harder and more unfair.

I overall liked the structure of the course—the online textbook had clear explanations and the psets were difficult but not impossible, and I felt like I learned a lot. However, the exams were extremely difficult and worth a large percentage of the grade. You have to be good at algos and solving new problems in a test environment to do well.

Aaronson is knowledgeable about QIS, but is meh at teaching. His office smelled like a dead animal, until I realized it was his breath... He gets annoyed when students cant follow along with his occasional fast paced rants where he hardly touches base. His exams were unfair and took off too many points for small mistakes. Not worth taking ECE 379K.
Quite well shuffled, but lacking in equity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is relatively not difficult but lectures can be slow and professor is a lot to deal with. TAs did most of the grading and interaction so for that reason I was able to get through the class.

Take the class if you need the credit but honestly professor is a lot to deal with. TAs will make the class much better. Was definetly not a fan of him and so weren't a lot of other people. He might like you he might not and his opinion stays the entire semester.
professor is not a good at understanding situations and helping students. TAs are very nice interact with them and get to know them well.

He's a hit or miss depending on your personality - I didn't really like him, but you interact more with your TA than him if you don't participate in lectures. He will call you out to read a slide or answer a question if he notices you're not paying attention though. I felt his lectures were kind of slow paced so I wasn't that engaged.

There are easier UGS courses, but the live concerts are nice. There's a $40 textbook of random online articles you will rarely use. Many of the assignment instructions have typos and are unorganized, but they expect your paper to be perfect. It seems like the TAs grade randomly and nitpick at random things that the rubric never specified.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy UGS, but depends on TA. Didn't really like him

He asked for my number when I asked for the major project rubric. Very vague on what he expects and often changes it before the due dates. Experiences differ depending on your TA, but if you enjoy the subject, it's not too bad.

He knows what he's talking about and the class is never boring - but he's definitely a hit or miss personality for sure. If the subject matter genuinely interests you, I'd say go for it, because you generally spend more time with your TA in this class than with him.

Honestly, he is one of my favorite professors Ive had. He keeps his classroom entertaining and engaging. Concepts are explained well, and he likes to add in personal stories for connections. I would recommend him as a professor to any of my friends.
He can come of as egotistical especially considering his unfunny jokes and personality. Obviously lacks compassion towards students. Do not take this class unless you attend every single session.

Professor is not very understanding to students situations based on my observations. Sometimes he's chill, but majority of the time I felt uncomfortable. He has a strong personality which students have mixed opinions/feelings on. I wish he had more compassion for his students. He's one of the only professors I have had that have lacked empathy.

Do not take this class unless you plan on attending every single class. If you miss more than one, make sure to study for that final exam. He comes off as a nice guy, but he actually lacks compassion/understanding when it comes to situations. Every science/math professor I've had are much more empathetic and this a ugs. The TAs are much nicer.

he makes jokes that make some people uncomfortable. he does not seem very understanding in my opinion. his class is interesting but it would be better if he would tone it a bit down with his jokes and show more compassion towards his students.
take bc its an easy A, but god this guy is so full of himself and thinks he's is the funniest man alive. lowkey passive aggressive at times.

Best UGS out there! Class 1 day a week and you watch a movie for most of it. Super interesting concept for a class and I looked forward to going every time.
