The discussion sections led by her TAs were also incredibly helpful and everyone involved in the team ensures that you're ready for the exams. The exams and analyses of research papers ensures success in and out of her class. Take her!

This is a very tough class, but it's doable. The exams are open note and aren't that difficult as long as you understand what was covered in lecture. The pop quizzes are hard, you NEED to study for them. Overall, very interesting material, but expect to spend a good amount of time outside of class working.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough at the start, it's not an easy class and she cold calls, but it forces you to build good revision habits and learn to study. Once you get past the first exam and start asking her questions in office hours, it's a complete 180 - she's incredibly knowledgable and a genuinely great prof. Can be a little nitpicky on grammar and vocab.

I genuinely don't know how this person teaches at UT. She's a terrible human who lacks empathy for students and is anti-accessibility. She's very patronizing, making it seem like she enjoys student failure. She lacks interest in the subject and is obviously just teaching to collect her paycheck. I took BIO 320 btw. She lacks basic tech skills too

Dr. Argawala is incredibly impatient with her students and creates a hostile learning environment. She gets frustrated when students ask questions and is overall condescending. She does not promote a safe place whatsoever and will mock and embarrass you for saying the wrong thing in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwala has been one of my favorite professors at UT. She pushes all her students to get an A, even though it involves a lot studying and work outside of the class. The material is very interesting and you can tell she is super knowledgeable about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwala is not an easy professor, she does not take shit from the students, but she's a great lecturer and is incredibly engaging in class. I took her class as a graduate student, and i learned an incredible amount about neurodevelopment. She uses tests and quizzes but tests were all open note. I loved this class.

I would rather watch paint dry than take this class. Boring and difficult. The professor is arrogant and thinks that her students are stupid. Extremely hostile learning environment. The lecture material makes you fall asleep. Don't take this class if you can avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far one of the rudest professors I have ever had in all of college. Work hard for your grade and you will do well. She has little to no compassion and the class is miserable. But, if you go to class and take good notes, you will be fine as I was (I finished with an A).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult. Dr. Agarwala is very tough and she started the semester incredibly hostile. She would call us out during class to answer questions on the spot so be ready to know your stuff. Go to office hours though and you'll see she's actually really helpful and not as scary. Very hard class though :/
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwala grills you the first 10 minutes of every class (it makes people cry). If you've never taken a neuro class, you will NOT do well in this class (she expects you to already know a lot). Our class bonded over the pure terror we had for her. There's a group project graded by your peers where if you don't fail each other, she'll fail you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwala is knowledgable and explains concepts well. However, she can be intimidating and impatient with students if they come unprepared to class or don't answer questions a particular way. Sometimes, the lectures seemed disorganized. Overall, not a hard class. Make sure you're prepared because she will ask questions about the previous lecture

Professor Aghaie was the opposite of helpful and supporting. His lectures consisted of him going off on tangents about whatever he felt like discussing that given day so most of the learning was up to you as the student. It often felt like he was making the class structure up as he went along and he never responds to emails. I q dropped.

Lectures were really random and didn't relate to the assigned readings often, had to mostly self learn/ study with the textbook. Primarily about history of the middle east, not gov, which was still interesting, but the random lectures and quite difficult timed essay mt/ finals were still difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think getting an A is pretty manageable if you do the readings and go to all the lectures. However, I didn't really feel that his lectures were very organized, and having to take notes on literally everything he says because it'll end up on the test becomes annoying when, on the test, you're having to remember his jumbled trail of thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. The class had no structure and the lectures were whatever he came up with that day. The only way to do well in the class is to write to what his preconceived opinions are about the given subject. You wont learn anything from him only on your own.

I cannot begin to describe how awful this man is in class. He loves to talk about how he is a “historian” and loves to interrupt you. I was 0.1% away from a A, had great attendance and built a teacher student relationship but that didn't matter because when I reached out about my grade he rudely ignored me and just said happy holidays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was just weekly readings and build up to a final research paper. Readings were long and often went undiscussed in class because Dr. Aghaie would go off on long tangents (he is clearly VERY intelligent on this subject, and makes that known). He was approachable, but was often unhelpful with feedback. Course was unorganized. TA was useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aghaie is a great professor, he truly knows his stuff and I really enjoyed the research project. He is very liberal which made some classes awkward for me as a conservative but he is in no way intimidating. The course is essentially a research course so pick a topic that interests you and you will have no issues !

I had a great experience in Modern Middle East. It is not an easy A, do the readings and take notes. Lectures are very hard to follow, but it encourages you to lock in and pay attention during class. He cares about his students and is willing to work with the class to direct learning to what people are interested in. Great guest lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NOTE: To any student desiring to take Intro to the Middle East: Religious, Historical, Cultural Foundations; this class is mostly a Islam 101-type class. Personally, if you have a background in Islamic/Middle Eastern Studies, or really anything Shi'i-polemical, this class will be very easy. If not familiar with the aforementioned, BE PREPARED :0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really think these reviews are being dramatic... its not all that bad. His lectures can be pretty interesting but he does sometimes go on tangents and then run out of time. Graded by 2 exams, a quiz, a group project, and attendance, so it ends up being a pretty fair distribution. Lots of reading though. Overall a knowledeable and nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: His lectures are disorganized and hard to follow, there is way too much assigned reading, all of which is dry, and he grades on two exams and attendance. The TA was the only thing that made this class tolerable, shout out to Mercie, who was very helpful and did all the grading and even covered lectures and did review with us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures seems like he just talks about whatever he wants and comes up with the topic on the spot. There is SO much reading and he doesn't elaborate on any of it in class. There is only attendance, the midterm, and the final for the grade, so if you miss , make sure you have a friend to give you notes. Seriously, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am most engaged when I listen to lectures in person and I found his lectures to be very engaging and interesting as a beginner in this subject. But there was a lot of reading and so much information that it was difficult for all of it to process correctly, lectures are also not specific with dates. Liked the teacher, not the information overload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just dont hes so rude and class is so bad

I chose to take this course amongst others in order to fulfill a degree requirement. I sincerely regret that decision. Professor Aghaie's lectures are not only boring and unorganized, but also entirely auditory. The only grades are two in-class essays, which must be written from memory with no outline present. Avoid this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I could give this man a 0, I would not hesitate to do that. Please, AVOID this man at all costs. His lecture style was dysfunctional and sounded like a stream of consciousness pouring out. I love learning about the Middle East, but he sucked all of that away from me. Good luck-- you will need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aghaie gives really disorganized lectures. You better be ready to take good notes because that's all you'll have for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class and topic was not tough to be exact, but Aghaie was so incredibly full of himself, and while his grading critera was very clear on paper, he was very evasive about what he specifically wanted you to answer the test essay questions. If there's another section or instructor you can take the same topic with, I highly suggest you do that.

After reading some of Dr. Aghaie's earlier reviews, I was rather apprehensive about taking his class. It wasn't bad, though. The class was oriented around two midterms and attendance. Three books were assigned, but they supplement the lectures more than anything else. His lectures were a tad disorganized, but overall, the class was fine
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Aghaie's class, not knowing what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised by the results. Our class only had 4 components for our grade, 2 tests, attendance, and a 5 point extra credit assignment. Dr. Aghaie's class is impossible to fail if you do the readings and attend lectures since you only have to write what you've read and heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After listening to all his gloating I was expecting someone a bit more educated or profound.  Kamran is rude and arrogant,  no more fascinating than any other person you see in the classroom.  I was rather disappointed as he lacks teaching methods and is extremely unapproachable.  Big disappointment,  UT has far better professors, avoid this one.
Good prof. Expects you to work very hard and produce excellent work, but is encouraging and helpful. If you do the work you will get a good grade.
is he for real! Arrogant and not that well read, I took more than one class with him and he teaches the same things in all of them!!
He delivered information in class, but doesn't really know how to teach.  He was not helpful.  Not someone you could call a mentor.  Did not find him approachable at all.

I took four different classes with him. He is old school in all the right ways. His lectures are the most organized I have ever experienced, he does not waste time and babble. His class is easy if you work hard, meaning keep up with the reading and go to every class. I would take any class he ever teaches.

The way he lectures is just confusing...he lists names on the overhead rather than outlining what he's talking about.  So if you don't get everything the first time, you're stuck with just a bunch of obscure arabic names. He also doesn't do test reviews or even vaguely help with the review questions because he "doesn't believe in it"..wow thanks!!!

twenty essay questions for the final??? TONS of reading but the quizzes often involve only one book???  Goes on tangents about totally obscure people which draws you away from the main point of the lecture???  A quiz a week and constant attendance checks???? Is this third grade?????  This guy is totally lame...this is an INTRO course!!!!!!
What kind of ass puts the same two questions on the final that were on the midterm? An named Aghaie. I could have spent the last half of the semester not learning anything...

I read a lot and even I think this guy assigned WAY too much reading.  He has hardly any humor/charisma to keep your attention and tends to drone about the subject.  For someone who knows nothing about islam, that only makes this class ten times harder.  Bottom line: A LOT of reading and you should probably know a thing or two about the subject
No Comments

A lot of reading for Intro to Islam course, but I found him to be a brilliant and very fair professor and grader.  He works very hard in the classroom and promotes and facilitates a very constructive discussion.
Taken 4 classes with him and I swear its the same one.  He's a decent lecturer but info is straight out of a book.  He's too by the book and an attendance nazi.
good class presentation very open to questions, willing to help

Unorganized schedule that we were behind on Homework. Overall, she posted assignments late as well as exams her format did not help in studying. READ the textbook and take good notes on her class. Late on grading as well, and quizzes every day so try not to miss her class as much as possible cause those points will save you. Choose Wisely

One of my favorite teachers. She is super sweet and makes class fun. Homework and quizzes every day, but it's manageable. She forgets to upload things sometimes, but nothing that can't be found on the JOSHU website. She's good at getting you to practice speaking and repetition in class, so you retain quite a lot. Really good for starting Japanese.

Aida-sensei is a very sweet professor who is kind and caring and puts a lot of thought and effort into her lectures and assignments. There are quizzes and homework essentially everyday, so beware of skipping multiple classes. That being said, there are dropped quizzes, extra credit opportunities, and a fairly lenient grading system.

I can see why she has so many good reviews because at heart, she is such a nice and caring person. However, I found her lecture pacing incredibly slow, especially in the first half of the semester. At times it felt like "Okay let's move on, but we'd spend too much time on the SAME thing. She also tends to keep class over the allotted time.

Aida-sensei has a genuine passion for teaching, & it's evident. Her lectures are very informative, & she's very open to questions/discussions over content. Quizzes & HW every day, but that's with every JPN class. Super kind person as well; she gave me the courage to pursue a Japanese double major. Can't recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Extremely kind and genuinely wants to help you learn Japanese. The course load is what you expect for any language learning class; lots of homework, quizzes, and exams. Still, this was one of the funnest classes I've ever taken and that was due to how great Aida-sensei is as a person and a lecturer.
awesome professor in all ways, always avaiable for help either at her office hour or by emails.

Aida-sensei genuinely cares about her students, and their learning. Additionally, she presents material in a clear, easy to understand manner, and encourages active participation to learn the language. An added bonus: she is incredibly energetic and her class is fun to attend.
Really nice teacher. A lot of homework and daily quizzes, but the class was still great. I would definitely take a class with her again.
She was one of the best language professors I have ever had. Awesome teacher!!
Great prof. fun and easy!
You will LOVE her. I have nothing bad to say whatsoever. The Best!
seriously the best japanese teacher at UT

Professor Hosemann is an excellent teacher, and is the type of person who values each and every one of her students and their ideas. The class is very interesting and is not difficult. There is a lot of reading, but you can get by with doing about half of it, in all honesty. All in all, amazing professor and a truly great experience in her class!

The class is super easy and interesting. No final, just a book report, so a lot of people stopped going to class after the midterm. I went to every lecture though because they were honestly fun. Discussions were kind of a waste of time but attendance is mandatory. No text book but a few cool, short books are assigned, as well as journal readings.

I'm a business major, but I really enjoyed this class! One in class test, one take home test, and one essay. 2-3 readings per every 2/3 weeks, so a very manageable amount of work. The lectures are super interesting and it's an easy A if you do the readings, go to class, and look over your notes before the tests. Hosemann rocks! Highly recommend.

There is a lot of reading, but you review everything in class so you can get by without reading.  There is only one test and it's easy. The class is very interesting and thought provoking. The professor is very friendly, open, and humorous. It's a fun class. Discussion group attendance is mandatory, but class attendance is not.

Extremely easy class. She is a very engaging professor. You really don't need to show up for lecture after the midterm. Discussion sections: go to them. If you go to lecture, no attendance, it'll be a very interesting discussion, but I didn't find them extremely helpful after the midterm. No final exam! Only a book report, so as long as you read...

Her lectures are engaging and interesting. Required reading passages are short, easy reads. She goes over all of them in detail and expects three "I statement" journals throughout the semester which she leaves feedback on. Also, one semi-short essay over a book about Walmart. NO harsh grading. Very kind and values all opinons. Easy A!

She is DEF one of the best professors at UT! I loved her class, if I wasn't a Sr., I'd probably switch to Anthro. She really cares about what students think and assignments are "discussions" with her on paper, which she responds to via Canvas! Not to mention EVERY lecture is interesting. Even if you wouldn't normally think its an interesting topic.

It was a summer course, so it was a little more compacted, but still great. There were only 3 "journal entries" which are written in third person. She wants to hear what you think ALWAYS. In lecture and on paper. She was a seriously great lecturer and sincerely cares about her students. I could tell she LOVES her job. I am so glad I took the class.

Professor Hosemann is a pro! She is a super smart, well cultured professor. Everything is fair game in lectures, this course is really entertaining because you get to explore so many things that are otherwise taboo. Really glad I took this class, it almost makes me want to be an anthropology major.

Easiest class I've ever taken, I have a 98. It's a really interesting class, but she is a really easy grader. I definitely recommended as the social and behavioral science. It's a great gpa booster, she lets you take the quizzes over again until you get an A. Her midterm is easy if you go to class the week before and the final is take-home.
Professor Hosemann is a great professor to have. She's very interested and knowledgable about anthropology and does not grade harshly.

She's lowk rude sometimes and I swear she goes over the easiest examples in class and then the exams/homeworks are way, way harder. She confronted the class after the MEDIAN on MT2 was a 57 and told us to study harder… lol just admit you're not a good prof it's fine. It's fine tho, she gave us 0.5% extra credit at the end of the semester, how kind

Idek if she could get a A on her own tests. Other professors make midterms more conceptual but she spams math questions. puts questions on the test that she hasn't taught the class how to work. We're supposed to learn to solve the questions thru the HW –> the crazy hard test questions aren't covered there. dont take her if you value your gpa/time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's slow. During tests she has the most ludicrous method of passing out the exams. Wastes 20 minutes just doing this. She'll get annoyed for anything. A student accidentally shifted some tests while grabbing his and got called out. Her accent makes it hard to hear some words she says + she has no patience for people who mess up her instructions.

tests gets successively more difficult. Test averages are in the 50s, and she blames the students and says “physics is difficult”. Some of the test material, besides problems recycled from HW, were NEVER covered. Covering a simple concept doesn't mean students actually learn well. she's nice but lecture doesn't help at all…

I loved the energy she brought to each lecture and the way she simplified concepts while making it more interesting than a normal lecture. She could organize her course better. Quest questions are very hard compared to what she teaches. If she gave resources on how to relate calc to physics, more EC, or easier exam questions, she'd be the goat.

MIGHT be the worst class I've taken at UT. I've heard other physics professors give way more leeway and extra credit. She also doesn't curve any exams even though they hav below failing averages. Provides not many resources to understand how to solve problems. There's discussion but obviously you won't get help on every question. buns prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst physics professor at UT. Doesn't matter how nice or passionate she is if she can't teach the course at the level she expects students to perform. Showed exam scores for MT2 during one lecture and blamed STUDENTS for how poor the scores were. If Some students do bad it's their fault, but if the whole class does bad it's the PROFESSORS fault.

If you took physics in high school, you'll probably be ok, but Torabi's teaching style is too simplistic for the difficulty level of the homework and exam questions, especially if you are learning from "scratch." Exam averages were failing 2/3 midterms and there is no curve. Torabi herself is very sweet, but avoid this class if possible.

Tests 2 and 3 are very difficult and do not get curved. She is a nice person, but her lectures do not help at all. Just by word of mouth, Torabi seems more difficult than other physics classes (because of no curve)

Dr. Torabi is very sweet, but you won't learn much from the lectures. The way she explains problems is nothing like how Quest explains it, so you often end up confused on how to get from point A to point B. Exams are super application-heavy and have “zombie questions” that are pretty tough. Her grading scale is super good though.

Her lectures are simple, but the homework feels like it's from a completely different class. I could never solve half of it because she never teaches at that difficulty. The exams are even harder than the homework and tougher than any other physics prof. She also randomly yells or drops things in class, which is more scary than helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Calc-based physics is a hard class and torabi does a good job of breaking down concepts to be more simple. However, she makes them TOO simple. Tests and HW questions surrounding said concepts become much more complex. students who can't learn from a textbook will need extra help and put it extra time. She needs to curve tests or give more EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she's so obviously passionate about physics and would help every single student if she could, and that makes this class bearable. she really does try to make lectures engaging, which is nice. physics is hard and it feels like her lecture examples don't get as complex as they should, focus on quest questions for exams and go to office hours often.

Good reviews on here will just say she's nice –> she is but she's a terrible lecturer. Shows simple applications of concepts in lecture but on exams and HWs tests on very complex applications of concepts. 1% EC but that's if you show up to all lectures and do 12 extra HW assignments (all with over 15 questions). No curves on exams w/ an avg of 60!

Dr. Torabi is a very respectable figure and a fantastic lecturer. She's very knowledgeable about the subject and is ready to help with any questions. She takes the course at a steady pace and is very understanding of concerns regarding the course. As someone who has never enjoyed physics that much, she made physics very enjoyable.

The only way to succeed is by reading the textbook and drilling practice problems. Torabi is a bad lecturer and goes over simple applications of the content, but u're expected to do much harder questions on exams. Only good thing is that she weighs HW heavily and provides EC 1.5%. I wish I stopped attending class earlier. She tries though

She's very nice and funny and tries to make lectures engaging and interesting. Lectures were much simpler than homeworks/exams, and I often felt lost because the class notes didn't help me much. Her grading scale is lenient and there is extra credit, but the disconnect between class content and exams made it challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is very nice but gives little to no guidance on how to solve problems. She tells you to read the textbook and do HW but if you get stuck ur lowk cooked. In lecture she'll put up problems and just pop up the solution without much context. Test avgs are 50 and she doesn't curve (kinda insane). EC is 1%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Midway through the semester, I stopped going to lectures and began reading the assigned textbook chapter and making sure I understood every single quest problem (I was at sangers drop in for hours every week). Exam averages are low, and the exams are not like the homework.

Dr. Torabi is a very nice person. She cares about the students and is funny. Homeworks were kinda hard, but helpful to understand for exams. I went to drop in tutoring and that really helped me get through the semester. Regardless, she is a good option for this class. Put in effort outside of class, and an A is not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Torabi is really sweet and patient with the whole class. She really tries to make physics fun, even if it's 8 in the morning lol. If you go to lectures and try on the HW, you should be fine! She has REALLY late discussions... like 9-10 pm. If you're nervous about walking at night, make sure to plan ahead or choose another class!!!

I took AP Physics in hs so I really enjoyed this class. However, without any background it is pretty challenging because lecture material tends to be simpler than HW and exams. Class averages are usually in the 60s but if you figure out the HW you should be ok. There are drops and extra credit which is very helpful and overall a very doable class.

torabi needs to realize that pre-med students are not passionate about physics and can't spend hours a day studying for her class. homeworks and exams become increasingly harder; extra credit is helpful but not enough. a nightmare if u didnt take ap physics. class avg was failing for 2/3 midterms and final avg was a 56. take this as a warning

If you took AP physics and did well, you will likely excel in this class. However, if you did not, this class might be very challenging for the exams. Torabi is great at nailing the general idea but you have to thoroughly understand it to apply to exam questions. Learn the most common Quest question types and study the 'zombie' questions

Dr. Torabi is a very nice person and wants you to succeed however she did not teach in necessary detail to understand concepts fully and do well on exams. Exams were very hard and only through homeworks and extra credit I was able to get an A. Go to her office hours if possible. Take another professor if possible!

She is not very kind, and does not seem to want to really help her students. Rather she is upset for asking qs, and lectures you on otherwise. Every exam was easy, however the final exam was significantly more difficult than any homework or exam that was provided. Take someone else if you can, it's quite hard to keep up with her method of teaching.

Physics is hard but Dr. Torabi is very caring and her lectures are sometimes interesting. The midterms are NOT similar to the hw questions, you really have to understand the materials to do well. HWs and 3 midterms are both worth 35% (1 drop) 3% of EC. 90 and above is A. My average for 2 midterms was a 75 and ended with A-.
You really gotta work hard!

Lectures often engaging, but most importantly are optional/extra credit. Very manageable class with forgiving policies. As with both engineering physics, be prepared for painfully scheduled discussion sections that do not provide meaningful value -- even when the TA tries to be engaged
If the majority of her class fails on exams perhaps the issue is not the students.

Let me just preface this by saying that as a professor, Dr. Torabi is pretty nice. However the biggest problem with her class is that the exams are designed for you to fail because they are completely different from all the HW problems we get and are significantly harder. Honestly just take someone else if you can.
Very hard!!!  I literally got a like a 58 on first test

Dr. Torabi was the best physics professor I have ever had! Although the content was really tough for a summer class, reaching out to her helped me a lot. Dr. Torabi is a little intimidating at first, but is extremely kind and wants you to succeed. Don't be afraid to go up to her and ask her questions! Exams are most similar to lecture slides
The best professor I've had. She is super caring. Put the work in an you'll get an A

She's nice and definitely cares for your learning, gave 4% extra credit which helped a lot; exams could be kind of tricky and included topics she barely went over in class (heavy emphasis on conceptual); 3 Midterms worth 35% (1 drop), 10 HWs 35% (3 drop), and Final 30%; helpful in OHs and responds to emails; study lecture and HW questions for exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very generous with extra credit opportunities and "zombie" questions. Getting an A in this class is definitely achievable, but you really need to be on top of your game with hwks - it is very easy to fall behind. Taking physics II over the summer is not easy, and the class is extremely accelerated, so prepare yourself.

Don't procrastinate her hw!! I did and it cost me a lot of time. When studying, stick to the hw, there are a lot of questions from it on the test. If you maintain a high average on your hws you can afford to fail a test or two because your hw and exams are weighted the same. Take advantage of the extra credit AND go to ur discussions!

Dr. Torabi is a great professor to take, if you're able to take her, definitely do. All exams will have zombie problems from the previous exams which should be free points. Homeworks are every week, don't procrastinate them, they take a very long time to do. Exams and homework are weighted about the same so make sure to do them.

Torabi is an amazing professor! HWs were given every week/two weeks, but they were mostly easy. Tests were very similar to the HW and they contained zombie problems. She was also very generous with the extra credit. All in all it was a really easy class! Only downside were the extremely late discussion sections.

so many extra credit opportunities!! tests are very similar to homework (quest) and there are a few zombie questions. discussions are mandatory but pointless. one of three midterms is dropped, and final is very easy- broken down into the units and where the questions were coming from. she's very passionate about physics and wants you to do well!

She is an amazing professor, one of the best, TAKE HER!! Her discussion sessions are mandatory. She gives so much extra credit and opportunities to succeed. She uses questions from homework and zombie questions on the exams. She is caring and loves what she does. I was terrified to take physics but she made it an easy transition.

PHY 302L over the summer was great with Torabi. She is very kind and has a clear structure. As long as you do the homeworks and practices, you'll be good for the exams. She also takes 3 questions from the previous exams & puts them on the following ones so you're guaranteed to get those right. Final was also mainly questions from past exams & HWs.

One of the nicest professors I have ever had! Clear grading policy and lots of extra credit. Always had a smile on her face and you can tell she is passionate about physics and wants you to understand what is expected. If you can understand the homework problems and pay attention to the examples in lecture, exams will be a piece of cake.

Calculus-based physics is hard, but Dr. Torabi made it approachable and gave so many real-life examples to make it easier to understand. She gave extra credit opportunities and worked through many homework problems and examples in class along with extensively reviewing concepts. Her exams were reasonable, and she did reviews in class. TAKE HER!
Easy class. Only need a 90 for an A, 85 for an A-, et cetera. Can bring handwritten notes to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best prof I have had at UT! She is super knowledgeable and enjoys what she does. She also listened to our feedback and made the class doable for sure. She gives interesting lectures and the exams are like the homework. Definitely take the time to take this class and get to know the professor! :)

Exams in this class are based off her homework and her Quest homework's are worth 30% of your grade. As long as you understand the homework and attend discussion sections, you should do fine in this class. Her final exam was pretty difficult though and makes up 30% of your grade
Dr. Torabi is very understanding of students. I had no physics background from high school but she made it possible to still succeed in the class. I would highly recommend taking her.
She designed the course so that the students would succeed. There is honestly no reason anyone should get below a 90 in this course!

Torabi is little difficult to pay attention to, so I recommend going in person. Biggest recommendation is to the read and take notes on the textbook section before the lectures! Overall, she's really nice and very accommodating. Would recommend if you can also dedicate some time to the textbook.

Aida is probably the best professor in physics at UT. The class is very clear and was a breeze. She cares about her students and her youthfulness makes physics fun. I would recommended signing up for her if you have the option.

By far my favorite class I've taken. Half the grade is participation and the tests are heavily curved. If you show up and participate you are almost guaranteed an A. He's extremely smart and has great real world experiences, and he really cares about his students. No better class to learn about what is going on in markets AND how to talk about them

Professor Kanojia is an excellent lecturer. His capital markets course is one of the most useful that I have taken at McCombs in terms of real-world relevance. I highly recommend taking this class for an elective.

Great professor and lectures, sensible content to address markets from different perspective (and each week has a market lecture too). Exams aren't too hard, it's like 2/3 general understanding from lectures and readings and then 1/3 hard/nitpicky questions "to make a curve." If you listen in class, a day's studying probably enough.

Great class to learn about markets and keep up to date. There are 2 exams that are pretty difficult but the class gets curved to a 3.6 anyways so it doesn't matter as long as you get within the average (~65). His class emphasizes participation so show up and try to contribute as much as possible its worth 30% of your grade. Overall, great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Akash is an excellent professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter. If you really want to learn about markets, you'll absolutely love this course. The tests are tough, but the class is heavily curved. He's one of my favorite professors I've had at McCombs. Just show up, participate, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN GOAT MAN
Great Professor. Test are very difficult, but if you attend you will receive a good grade. Honestly, this was the best class I had while at UT.

This is a fantastic class to get an in-depth understanding of markets. This is completely an open discussion class, but Akash does a great job of explaining everything in a fun and detailed way. There are two exams which are difficult, but the class gets curved anyways. Highly recommend taking this class and getting to know Akash!

Phenomenal professor who cares for students. You really need to participate but he makes it fun. Basically nobody does the readings but exams (all MC) ask questions about it. Very open to meeting students. My favorite class at UT and it's not close.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite class and professor at UT. Class is discussion based and just feels like a casual conversation about the market. Only two exams.

Exams are long MC with references to specific readings and lectures, so you have to attend class. I found each lecture pretty interesting, but it's a hit or miss if it correlates with the exam. He's passionate about markets and has a high-level background. Wants you to actually learn the material. Overall, be sure to participate early and read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Direct and likes to talk about markets a lot (interested in interest rates, MBS, and regulations). However, the rigor of the class does not match the rigor of exams. 75 T/F with specific answers on readings and concepts. Average exam = 65 and apathetic to it. Only take if course appeals, but A unlikely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard tests but curved to 3.6. If you want to learn about capital markets Akash is the best professor on campus. Mondays are market discussions and Wednesdays are lectures about various capital market topics ranging from "What is Money?" to "Shadow Banking" and everything in between. Absolutely amazing course. I wish I could be in it longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never written a review on this site but Akash is deserving of one. He one of the best professors I have had at UT Austin, and gave me helpful advice during a difficult time in my life. He is passionate about finance, and is dedicated to making sure his students actually understand the material. He is also very down to Earth, and relatable.

Honestly he seemed like a nice guy who wanted us to succeed, I just disliked the finance class itself. For each test I memorized all the terms during the week beforehand and made sure I could do the practice test. Luckily since its McCombs, there was a curve
Great professor who cares a lot about the material and the success of his students. His lectures are entertaining and engaging, and he is more than willing to answer questions.

chill professor, good at teaching and connecting to more broadly applicable/personal concepts. class is a lot of self-learning though so be prepared for that vs. another more established/seasoned professor in the FIN department, such as Toprac or Chhajawani.

Great guy. Lectures are kind of iffy though since there isn't really PowerPoints he does them in excel. He knows his stuff so his discussions in class time is good to reinforce concepts. His cases also wasn't bad as he would give the answers you just need to solve it yourself. Super caring to actually help you learn so definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very witty. Definitely related to him and he inspired me bc I have imposter syndrome at this school, and he told us the first day that he got a D/F in finance and accounting. He really drills into the content and makes sure we get it. I liked him.

Fantastic professor who is clearly limited by the fact that FIN357 has a standardized curriculum across all courses. If this curriculum was set by him and he was teaching the stuff he wanted to, easily one of the best classes at McCombs. However, lectures at the moment are not the most effective, but the homework/required readings make up for that

My favorite professor at UT. The classroom is flipped, which is good in case you miss class. You can watch the real lecture whenever. His in-person lectures are more review and discussion. He makes them super engaging and applicable to our lives. Made the class enjoyable. I can't recommend him enough. Gives great career advice—very impressive guy.

Reverse classroom style. He posts videos ahead of class that vary in length. He is a very accommodating professor that cares about students success. Overall he makes a class that is meant to be difficult accessible to the average student. Would recommend him for sure.

I really like this professor! He was a UT student so he just gets it. Class is for discussion, he uses a flipped classroom system so you should watch lectures before class. Finance in itself is hard, but he really cares about students and is so flexible with office hours. Take him if you can! 100 percent recommend.

Hard class, but really nice professor! Very caring and goes out of his way to answer our questions and meet with us in his free time. His current real world experience makes this class all the more interesting. Go to class and watch his Youtube videos.

One of the best professors in the department!
If you get 100 on the final exam, you will automatically get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The exams are multiple choice but not much partial credit is awarded if you select the wrong answer for whatever reason. Lectures didn't feel that helpful either, so I would recommend reading the textbook and/or watching the relevant Razavi Electronics I and II lectures on YouTube and doing the assigned practice problems to succeed in this course.
I have had such an awesome semester with him. Definitely recommend, I wish I could take another class taught by him!

I loved Deji's lectures, he made funny anecdotes about his life and somehow strung it back to transistors and circuits haha. The exams were very chill, but since they're mcq, its a bit unforgiving if you make small mistakes. He does pull questions  from the textbook though, so theoretically you can just do all the book problems. Labs are good too.

Dr. Akiwande was an amazing professor! He cracks funny jokes and tells his life stories sometimes during lectures. I learned a lot about how transistors work in his class. Although it's a lab class, the tests still make up 60% of your grades. But they are all MCs and very doable! This was an excellent class, and he was an amazing guy to talk to!
Relatively difficult circuit concepts but Dr. Akinwande structures the class well. Do a lot of extra practice to understand how to solve problems, and then the tests come easily.

Prof does amazing with helping you understand all of the concepts. Does plenty of practice problems. He expects a lot because the course lies heavily on your understanding of the material and performance in the labs, which will help you in the exams. READ THE TEXTBOOK. It is your best friend! Exams & homework can get challenging. Labs can be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He explains concepts very well, both during lectures and during office hours. For students struggling in the class, he offered extra office hours, which were very helpful. The tests came directly from the textbook questions. Even though this is a lab class, the majority of the grade comes from 4 exams (no final). Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Erin gives amazing feedback & understands most students are not english majors. She makes class inclusive, fun & engaging, one I always woke up to go to. Her feedback is super helpful, drops quizzes, and grades super leniently, while also wanting you to stretch your understanding. 4 books to read, and 3 papers, only hw is reading. AMAZING PROF
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took Banned Books with Erin and she is probably one of the best professors i've had. By far my favorite class of the semester and I'm sure everyone else in my class would agree. She takes the books to new levels and is phenomenal at explaining she may act like she's all over the place but she knows what she's doing. Cant wait to read her books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Class was Rhetoric of Apology and it was very interesting & doable! Akins is currently a grad student, and the only issue was the slow grading and limited feedback as the course progressed. There is no TA so that's why grading multiple essays took a long time. Rewrites for points back are available and its overall a great class for a writing flag!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly such a sweet and informative professor. There's a lot of reading, but you could get away by just skimming through them. She's also very accommodating as long as you communicate with her! I had no real knowledge about Hinduism, but it's very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (I took ANS379 Translating Asia. I'm not sure why there isn't an option.) Mana is truly a student-centered teacher, always willing to help, really cares about her students, and listens to their concerns. One thing to be aware of is that her course requires a significant amount of reading. Her grading is very nice, rarely loses points.

Pretty easy class, however for a non-hindu may be confusing. professor is very friendly and always willing to help. Her understanding of Hinduism and its philosophies/beliefs is a little off. So if you are a hindu you may be confused or even heavily disagree with her approach to some gods. Overall she is very kind and I enjoyed this course
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Mana for South Asian gods and goddesses....her class is an easy A. I never even did the readings when I was taking this class (I was born and raised Hindu) but for someone who wasn't it may be more difficult...she assigns bunch of readings in class. She often also rambles on during class as well but overall this class was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed taking this class. Mana always made an effort to allow students to take control of their learning, and made the environment very comfortable for her students. I really enjoyed coming to lectures and always looked forward to hearing our in class discussions. She is a professor, I truly recommend to take if you have the chance.

Professor Mana is very kind and is passionate about Hinduism. However, if you were born and raised Hindu and have a good grasp of the teachings, you may not want to take this class- unless you're interested in fundamentals. Professor Mana does not seem to have a proper grasp of the meaning behind Hindu texts, and her opinions can be incorrect.

Daily Quiz at the start of the class( at the start of your day too) won't spend time on Kanji, force everyone to shut their mic, go over things too fast but again and again, daily homework is also a pain
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved Katayama-sensei when I took her for 601 and 610. She's a little strict at times but it shapes you into a good Japanese speaker. Show her you care and that you like Japanese and she'll love you. Read the book before class, study your kanji, participate in class, and you'll do great, especially for 610D
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Katayama may seem a little intimidating at times but she overall cares for her students very much and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. Pay attention in class and be ready to participate. Reading the textbook before class really gets you a head start on lessons in class. 601D is easy but 610D is a little more difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sensei is a great teacher but you do have to put effort into the class. As one of the previous comments said, she doesn't care for slackers. But she does care that you get an education and really immerse yourself in Japanese, so try in class and take the time to talk with her in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's nice and helpful in her office hours, but very hard on transfer students. She does take an interest in every student though.

Nice but plain. I had her for and 8 am class and she was not the most exciting person to take up to. She does't care much for slackers but she's very helpful if you go to her office. It's a pretty easy class with a lot of quiz and homework grades. If you show up everyday, you also get +2 points on your overall grade.
I liked Katayama-sensei a lot. I had her for JPN 506 and then again for 507, and had very high A's both times.
Just read off her slides the entire time. I only went because of the clicker questions. If you do the readings, you can pass her class. Honestly, I was really bored in class. Not engaging at all.

Lectures are mandatory due to partial iClicker grade but are not very helpful. She just lectures off of slides It is better to just take notes from the book while going through the slides at home. Her tests are very unpredictable, no reviews, only a chat session the night before the test. Generally 25 MC, T/F, and about 5-8 free response.

A very disorganized class. would rather take another professor. Was very nonchalant regarding helping students study for exams. R Great at explaining but you could NEVER know what to expect on exams. Just hope your T.A. prepares you well..

Professor Albert is one of my favorite professors at UT. This lectures are mostly discussion discussion based, so be sure to participate! Tests make up 80% of your grade make sure you know the material or go to office hours. His lectures are very interesting and makes you think about stuff you normally wouldn't care to think about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Albert has been the best teacher I have had at the university. He is very passionate about his work, and you can tell through his lectures. At first, the three-grade criteria was scary, but engaging in class and creating a study group helped me succeed. I cannot recommend this class enough!

I highly enjoyed this class, the lectures were engaging and small group discussions were always fruitful. Note taking is simple and Albert loves to talk to students as long as you put in effort to talk to him. This class is graded on few things however. Your final is 50% of your grade, so prepare wisely (the exams and essays are all open note).

Professor Albert was truly one of my favorite professors that i've had at UT. His lectures were very insightful and made you want to learn. You are graded on 1 essay, 1 midterm exam, and 1 final exam. As long as you take good notes and study up before the exams, an A is definitely attainable. I 100% recommend this class to anyone!

Professor Albert is one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met. I started off not liking him, but the more I was in his class the more I began to enjoy it. You are graded on 3 exams and 1 essay, which are graded pretty harsh, but its not impossible. The content is a little boring, but its worth it because you will feel so smart after.

Professor Hanson is one of the most passionate professors I've had, and his lectures were both engaging and informative. He was also really responsive outside class. It's worth struggling through the homework/midterms if you want a solid foundation for ECE going forward. If you're going for straight A's, however, this may not be the class for you.
Probably the greatest lecturer I've ever had. It's a hard class, not impossible, but from what I've heard, he's the best lecturer in the ECE department and I find that pretty easy to agree with.
NOPE Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HWs irrelevant to tests, and lectures do not align with textbook. So you are left alone to prepare.

His lectures are amazing, and he has a Discord server where you can get help from. Additionally, he offers valuable advice on how to navigate college successfully. 

However, this class is very hard, and be ready to receive bad grades. Many hairs were lost, and many poos were shot out during tests.

Probably one of the greatest lecturers you'll meet. Somehow makes complex circuits relatively easy to understand. HOWEVER, test difficulty ramped up noticeably in fall 2025, and will probably only be tougher in the future. The tests are very difficult with averages around 50-60, and grading is strict. Be ready to be humbled by this class.
Good professor, could be better grading wise.
Very tough intro class; professor is caring, however.

MY GOAT!! Amazing lecturer who can break concepts down to a conceptual level and help you understand the topic intuitively. He's super funny and genuinely cares about students and their success (you can reach him outside of class through discord and he does a career lecture). This class is comically hard (tears shed) but the prof made me love it.

Dr. Hanson is an amazing professor and very accessible outside of class (join the discord). His lectures are thorough, intuitive, and well-rehearsed. That being said, this class is not easy. Expect most of your grade to be determined by difficult exams with failing averages. They are curved, but this class will seriously challenge you.

This class is very difficult (no getting around that) but I learned a ton from the class for sure. Hanson is a good lecturer but I do think that his instructional material is trivial compared to exams/homework. My only complaint is that the labs often felt meaningless and lacked a sense of direction half the time.

The professor is great at lecturing and breaking down the concepts to the most fundamental level in class, however the examples he provides does not line up with the difficulty of exams and homeworks, which are SIGNIFICANTLY more difficult than the lecture. I wish he showed more examples of difficult questions and show how to navigate them.
Hands-down, he is the greatest lecturer in the ECE department and I don't think any other professor comes close.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you want to keep a work-life balance while not ruining your GPA, do not take 362M with this Professor. He claims to want to maximize your learning and doesn't want you to worry about grades, yet has the most atrocious grading. The average in his class was a B-. The biggest issue if that the HW doesn't match what is taught during lecture.

Undoubtedly the best lecturer I have ever had. He teaches extremely well and answers students' questions even better. Although the content is extremely tough, he is one of the few professors I believe can teach it effectively.

Best lecturer I've ever had. Explains concepts in a way that's understandable to a student. Answers questions well. Homework is hard but necessary imo. Grades respectably. Only part of the class I didn't like were the labs, which were often unorganized and didn't teach anything. Gave helpful advice for career and curriculum planning.

Tough class, but not impossible. Very accessible outside of class (he's a Discord fiend), and his office hours were decently helpful too. Gives good career advice and teaches concepts very well (heavy on conceptual understanding over formulaic regurgitation). Attendance wasn't mandatory but if you didn't attend you would be lost. Great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 302H was brutal 1st semester, but I learned so much from this class. Professor Hanson's lectures were always very passionate and well planned. He moves quickly, and his homework was very time consuming with many places where you had to teach yourself. He is very straight forward and gives good end of semester advice for planning your degree/future.

Holy this class is a wake up for freshmen. Dr. Hanson does a great job in his lectures, but the content is brutal. Expect long hours for all the homework, super low test grades, but a good ending grade. Once you get through this class, everything else is going to feel like a breeze. Dr. Hanson is super open during office hours and lunch hours.

Dr. Hanson is an amazing professor and genuinely wants his students to succeed. His class can be daunting sometimes and exams are difficult, but typically curves well. Reach out to him and ask questions during class because he will take the time to clarify the content. Also, make sure to do the homeworks (and redoing them around exam time helps).

Class was incredibly difficult, but all the exams had a really heavy curve. A fantastic lecturer who does well conveying information as well as being super energetic and engaging during class. The homework was sometimes unnecessarily hard, but he sought out feedback to improve the class and hw moving forward. I also highly recommend his lunch hours

302H was a great experience and a large portion of why is due to Hanson. His homework and midterms are really hard to understand and score well. The learning curve during the first few weeks is aggressively brutal but dw, it will pass. He's extremely approachable in person & through Discord. He truly cares about your understanding of the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hanson is very very very knowledgable about EE, and he deeply cares about his students. However, I think the class was waaaaaaaaaay too difficult to the point where almost nothing made sense. The lectures are extremely fast, very conceptual, and not concrete. Homeworks were hell, exams were hell as well. This was a traumatizing exerience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hanson is a very passionate and extremely smart Electrical Engineer; however, the new curriculum is very fast-paced and packs a lot of information in short intervals. Homeworks were very difficult, confusing, and not straightforward. Exams were quite difficult and required a lot of self-study and practice. Homeworks didn't do justice to exams.

The class material was incredibly difficult, but he tried to improve it. He is accessible outside of class and is always open for discussion. Tests do not reflect what we learned in class, and are basically impossible to do. There is very little help with homework, and he expects you to learn concepts from them. This class will make you cry.

Lacks transparency with grades, no homework solutions, tests are impossible for normal students, terribly structured, all of the lectures and homeworks would rarely show up on exams. Homeworks are harder than anything I have ever seen before. He expects you to learn, but you can't learn from them. Shoutout the TA who was the only good part.

HWs are hard but helpful. Exams are pretty average in difficulty. Labs are fun and a good grade booster. Hanson is a pretty solid professor and a really nice guy, but his lectures are confusing at times.

302H is meant to push you past your limits! If you are interested in the EE side of ECE, this course is definitely one to look forward to. Dr. Hanson is a great professor who encourages students to not only question, but also even challenge what they are learning. You gain a lot despite the sheer stress and difficulty. Superb course overall.

The course as whole is rather inefficient. While a lot of material is covered, the homeworks make learning unnecessarily time consuming with no real return for all that time spent. Could have been a much more enjoyable class if it were taught in a more straightforward manner.

This class was super difficult. Be prepared not to have a life if you decide to take it. However, Dr. Hanson was a great lecturer. He was always really approachable and he genuinely wanted us all to understand the material and pass the class. His grading was fair, and he curved the tests generously.

The first section's hw & test were insanely hard but you learn a LOT about circuits. Taking AP Physics C: E&M definitely helped but that is nothing compared to the stuff you're about to learn and do in this class. This class made me cry and think about my future more than I'd like. He's always online on Discord for some reason so ask him questions!

Dr. Hanson is a pretty good professor. However the class is very very hard. Make sure to not fall behind, and do the homework in advance because it takes a very long time. If you practice a lot before the tests, you should be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Homework is hard, but that's where the learning happens. He encourages doing homework in groups.

He has lunch hours where you can talk with him outside class, and he's really accessible on Discord.

The first section had tough homework. Hanson does genuinely want you to succeed but is pretty bad at judging how hard things are for students. Hanson is also very open to feedback and will change the workload if he sees that he's being unfair. He is very nice and also very accessible to asking questions. Go to his lunch hours!

Hanson offers the best introduction to EE class out there. He explains things clearly and actually cares about your understanding. Homework is hard, but it also teaches you things beyond the lectures. If you want someone to push you hard Hanson will do just that. He'll also happily agree to watch movies and play poker with you if you ask.

Professor Hanson is a fantastic professor for ECE 302H! His lectures are engaging, and his homeworks and labs are great in reinforcing the concepts he covers in class. He truly cares about his students and their success. So grateful that I had him as my first electrical engineering professor.

Overall a pretty good introductory ECE course. He says the homework is meant to "stretch your understanding", which means you'll need to dedicate 6+ hours and likely work with a group. He posts online lecture notes that 100% match what he says in class, which helps with retention. If you study appropriately, its not as hard as people say.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor that gives engaging lectures. Make sure to spend time understanding what each lecture is really about. Tests are incredibly hard - doesn't matter if you were top 10% or top 10 students - so make sure to take a lot of time to study. Hard class but definitely learned a lot!

302 is hard, anyone in ECE will tell you that at UT. For being a new professor and spearheading the honors version of 302, I think Professor Hanson did a great job. He makes himself available to students and has a clear passion for the course material. He will make you laugh and cry all semester (unironically and ironically). GL future 302H-ers.

Best professor for ECE 302H. Detailed and enthusiastic lectures, and while not recorded, he sends the notes before every exam. His condensed textbooks are helpful - recommend reading. Incredibly friendly and encouraging overall, would definitely take again. When taking notes, write down what he is saying rather than just what's on the board.
Great professor, hard tests, and long homework. Weirdly available almost always.
Helpful lectures, but incredibly hard homework with minimal

Amazing professor. Though he's new, Professor Hanson is great at what he does, has a passion to teach, and WANTS you to pass. As long as you have the desire to learn, Hanson turns one of the most difficult ECE freshman classes into the most fun. I highly recommend him, especially if you're thinking about getting a leg up in 411.
If you want to be taught by Sheldon from Big Bang Theory, this is your best chance. Hanson is a solid professor especially for his first semester of teaching.

Professor Hanson is relativly new at teaching, but is an incredible professor. It's obvious that he has a real passion for the subject he teaches and cares about his students. While 302 is a hard class in general, I believe that Hanson does a very good job of preparing his students for his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yes, I know I got a C+; however, Professor Allen is truly a sweetheart! She cares about her students and her teachings and is always willing to help during office hours! I feel like just going to the office for hours helped because I received extra credit for it! I highly recommend taking Professor Allen!

The professor is very nice, gives a lot of extra credit, and is very easy to follow. The first half of the class is fast paced, but you'll get used to it quickly. There's not really any pop quizzes but the assignments you work on in class can get taken for a quiz grade. Exams can be tough but extra credit covers it and there can also be a curve.

Tax is hard itself but her lectures and notes make it a lot better. She explains things well and does alot of examples in class so the concepts are understood. There is alot of material and it does become dense but her exams generally use practice exam questions and test on the easier of materials for any unit. She also does alot of extra credit.
If you don't go to class the exams will be really hard

It was a tough class, but shes the GOAT. Class was fun and engaging, I know how to do some taxes, how to evade them while avoiding detection from the service, and how to make that money clean through investments in restaurants or laundromats. she provides plenty of resources to prepare for exams, answers any questions, and is just great! recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is great if you come in with knowledge about financial accounting. For someone who isn't familiar with the course, it's hard to catch up at the speed at which she goes in class. Her class is kind of set up like she expects students to come in with prior knowledge. Also, she does pop quizzes for a grade along with attendance.
She is the GOAT. Course material is at times difficult but that has nothing to do with the professor. Pop quizzes are predictable.

If you can take professor Allen's class, please take it!! She is so sweet and incredibly caring towards her students. Her class contains pop quizzes, but she always announces them beforehand. In class, we do many practice examples and she is the only prof that provides extra practice problems for the exams. She's also very accessible outside class.

I loved having Professor Allen this semester! She is such a great teacher who genuinely cares about her students. Her lectures help you learn the material so you don't have to do much outside of class besides homework. The class is basically the textbook so I would recommend reading it to do well on the tests. Overall really recommend taking her!

Professor Allen is wonderful. She makes sure that students understand the material and provides lectures that are digestible. She is always willing to help and goes over lots of examples. I felt like I was back in a high school class because of how well structured her course is. Take her!

The lectures are really all you need to do well in the course. Exams consist of an MC and Free Response and would most definitely read the textbook specifically for the free response. The professor will be able to answer all your questions and the lectures are super easy to follow. As long as you show up you will most likely get an A
I thought accounting was hard until I took this professor. A lot of learning it comes down to your own individual studying/review, but she made everything 100x more enjoyable and was super fair.

Best professor I've had/will have--put in the effort and she'll recognize it. Also super fun and hip and young. Homework is super easy and the bigger assignments are all solo and only a bit longer. Only bit of stress are from the tests, but she provides tons of previous tests etc. Really cares

GO TO OFFICE HOURS, cannot emphasize this enough. She barely curved the class at the end of the semester and curves it to where the class average is around a 3.0 to a 3.2(based on the test averages + office hours attendance rate) Her slides are a repetition of the info in the textbook, just read + do practice problems, overall would take Blaire.

Professor Allen is awesome--she is accessible outside of class and will stay past her usual office hours to help her students. In-class lectures move fast, but she goes through many examples for better understanding. Attendance is technically not required, but there are "pop quizzes" and handouts that are taken for a grade every now and then.

Easily one of the best professors I've had. She explains topics in a very straightforward way, is very receptive to questions, and walks around class to help on handouts. Gives pop quizzes every 2 weeks but she hints at when they are and provides bonus points. The class is very fast paced but there is just a lot to cover.

Shes an amazing Instructor! her course is so well organized and her PowerPoint has the right amount of lectures and examples. there are pop quizzes but for most, you are given a warning beforehand. She has a bunch of resources to use for extra help and is overall a kind professor. Material is hard, but shes great at explaining.

The material covered in this class is pretty easy in my opinion. There are quizzes but they are not hard and you can get bonus points for writing down the TV shows referenced in the class handouts. The professor is good at explaining concepts but goes through the slides really quick in class because there is a lot to cover.

The best professor I have ever taken at Mccombs. She is sweet and caring about her students and wants them to succeed. She gives out quizzes every other week but lets you know in advance. The subject is a bit challenging, but as long as you read the book, review the power points, attend class, and ask questions, you should be good.

Amazing and super nice professor! She makes tax so easy to understand. The exams are pretty easy if you do the practice exams she posts. There are in class quizzes and sometimes the handouts she does with the class are taken as a quiz grade so go to class if you don't want to miss an easy 100 on a quiz grade.

She's great at explaining concepts, very receptive to questions, pretty funny, and accessible outside of class. This is a textbook-heavy course but you could get by w/o reading if you pay attention in class (although not recommended since the reading reinforces concepts). ACC 311 is probably one of the most effectively designed courses at McCombs.

Simply love her class. Such a nice professor and cares about students. A tough class but I would totally recommend Professor Allen.

reviews.comment: Prof. Allen is a very prof. She's so nice when you ask her questions. I got off to rough start, but accounting clicked in my head later. Allen is one of the most caring professors i've had. She's willing to help her students as long as she sees effort being put forth. Very helpful and knowledgable about accounting. Highly recommend her for ACC311.

He is really caring and great. Take the class if you are already good at math, I think the material was pretty difficult on its own but just attend lessons and do all the practice problems.

I went to every class. I aced every online quiz due to 2 attempts, and I aced every homework assignment. I stayed for 1:1s. I went to tutoring. I did group work nothing worked. He cares about his students, offers flexible schedules, and inspires us to do our best. He shares his experiences, gives helpful advice and encourages questions if we don't understand. Professor Dan is a good teacher as well as person, he helped guide me through the labs and answered my questions any time of day. Beware of the pop quizzes after every lab because these will replace your final exam.

Dr. Dan is one of the best proffessors Ive had at UT. The only reason you would not get an A is because you did not try hard enough( learned from experience). Apfeld is such a great teacher. He really cares about government and has very clear lectures. There is a textbook, but you can basically get away without reading it. Took a risk taking a first-time teacher and it paid off. Very fair exams, fun assignments and great teacher. Glad I took him. Only con is the textbook sucks, but he said he hates it and won't use it again. Great solid young teacher. Tests are very fair, assignments fairly reasonable, good at teaching. Nothing to worry about.
Horrible, deeply boring professor. They should give her a mop instead because she shouldn't be teaching.

PROS: This class is a very interesting class. You basically sit there for an hour and listen to Professor Aprile tell you stories.  The tests are pretty straightforward CONS:  The class is a lot of work and is lecture based. If you miss a lecture, you will be left behind

She does read off a paper but that's because she is telling you the stories of mythology. If you think she is rambling then you aren't paying attention. Very boring lectures. She literally just reads off a paper in class. Very sarcastic at times when asked a question. Tests are too long for the time given. I recommend to not take that class. I did great in all my classes this semester except in hers, because she doesn't really teach, all reading in class.
Very boring lecturer.
Poor teacher. Easy material but not given enough time to finish test in class. I think she is new though.

Best elective class I've taken! It was kinda easy because I love mythology, but if you are not a fan of reading 30pg chapters and memorizing names, events, & theories do not take it. I have taken classes in McCombs as well as the school of natural sciences and this, an arts class, is the hardest class I've taken at UT. She expect you to memorize 270+ different pictures of artifacts that all look the same. And it isn't simple fact either. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. it isn't worth the effort.

Completely unrealistic expectations! This is an Intro course and half or more of the students are non-majors and she expects everyone to memorize the what, where, when and significance of EVERY SINGLE artifact, building, and sculpture we have EVER SEEN in class or in the book. Absolutely ridiculous! This is like an UD Art History class! Do not take

I liked her class a lot, probably since I liked Mythology. I didn't like how the final was 40% of my grade, and the final had so much writing. So. Much. Writing. Very poor teacher. Reads off a sheet for the entire 50 min and mumbles her sentences. Worst of all, when I had her she designed her tests so that no one could finish (not even on purpose). She's new and I think she got flustered and didn't know how to conduct the class during those 4 days we missed because of the weather. AVOID

She talks really fast, but if you write down everything she says and know the information well before tests, you will have no problems! If you are not a fast note taker, read the book, but I never opened the book and had no problems!

She was a really good professor. After a few classes though, the class (which comprised of 9 students) figured that we have to ask questions because she literally can talk non-stop for an hour straight. She used power points for her slide so there is at least some visual aids in the class. There will be a lot of reading though.

She is ridiculously passionate. Honestly, it really is a TON of information in only THREE tests, so there's a ton of studying needed for each test. That being said, people grumble about it being super hard, BUT it really isn't If you take decent lecture notes a ton of those too!) and read the SUMMARIES online, NOT the book. Study SMART. Easy A.
