Quizzes require you to really know your stuff. Very unforgiving quizzes, where early errors will cause you to get the rest of the quiz incorrect. Difficult exams. Attendance is graded. No drops of any sort. Exam 1 is hardest because mostly FRQ, other exams are MCQ. Overally, you need to be on top of things from the very start of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like Professor Roy Bardhan, she didn't really have that bad of an accent. In fact, I understood her well. The only reason why I got an A- was that I didn't participate as much as I should've (she did change my grade slightly after talking to her, but it wasn't enough). Do the readings BEFORE class and study like 2 weeks ahead of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ACC311 is challenging, but Bardhan does a great job teaching the course. If you do the pre-class work & take good notes, you will do fine (as someone w no accounting background). Reviews saying she's rude, has a harsh accent, or frequently cold calls are exaggerated. She has a great sense of humor and cares for her students, I 100% recommend her!
Professor Bardhan is a great professor; she truly knows what she is doing and is a great teacher to have as a start to understanding Accounting.

This class is really hard. Its normal to fail all the quizes and close to failure for tests. The lecture content is really rushed and hard to understand. Her accent makes it kind of hard to listen. Quizzes and tests are very hard and those are the main grades. There is a group project and presentation which is pretty easy.

One of the worst professors that I have taken. Lectures are very hard to follow since she does not use the class slides and she is very rude if you have questions. She cold calls a lot, and does not explain things well enough for students to answer questions.
Its a really hard class. Notes are unclear, and tests are way harder than what is learnt in class. She claimed she would teach it as if we were accounting beginners, but that was not the case at all.

absolutely terrible professor and instructor. graded on extremely few things and expected to perform damn near perfection with averages for most tests and quizzes being failing. she is just a terrible professor and made this already difficult class more hell so please avoid her at all costs. exam was NOT reflective of any class content and harder!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: for context, an accounting major had difficulty in this class

Cold calls. Make sure you are doing the reading(s) on units before class and after because in class lectures are faster paced and not really crafted to take notes. She is incredibly knowledgeable and truly does want everyone to succeed, however that means she has a tough love approach.

She knows her stuff, and will make sure you know it too by the end of the course. Notebook and paper, with no electronics allowed. She is slightly tough on students with workload, and the Excel part of the course is terrible, but you come out knowing everything you need to for an introduction to accounting. Not too keen on regrades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: rude and unhelpful

Roy Bardhan has been my favorite professor at McCombs so far. She has really good lectures that thoroughly explain the course content and includes a good amount of humor as well. The exams are really reasonable (30 MCQs) and the project actually taught me so much about managerial accounting. I would highly recommend taking the course with her.
She's alright at best, would take a different professor if possible.

Professor Roy Bardhan ruined my entire semester last year. She has a harsh accent which is very hard to understand and she will be very passive aggressive if you ask a question in her class. Attendance isn't mandatory and it really shouldn't be because attending class did not help my understanding of the concepts. DO NOT TAKE ACC311 WITH HER.

Professor Bardhan's class is extremely well-organized and easy to follow. She teaches at a reasonable pace and provides ample material for exam review. The first few sections were a learning curve because I had no previous knowledge of accounting, however there are tons of opportunities to raise your grade throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: she is not a great lecturer. i found it hard to follow her line of thinking. the way she explains concepts is a bit drawn out and she honestly does not take feedback well (even if she asks for it). see if you can take kamas, fannin, or djb

Overall very hard course. She does not answer students' questions well, but if you can manage to pay attention every second you can get by. The first exam was hard as it was free response and you can lose points on anything if you don't get the exact format right. She explains things inefficiently and cold calls. She has a fun personality though.

The way Bardhan teaches is very thorough, she guides the class with examples and is very helpful with any questions. I loved the structure of her class, and she supplies so much practice to make sure you will excel on the exams. Accounting is very controversial for some, either it clicks or it doesn't. Overall she is amazing if you put in the work.

She really, really cares about getting her students to understand the material. She makes a "boring" subject really engaging with her lectures. Lots of practice problems in class, which really help in understanding. She can be sassy but in a fun way; the entire class laughs multiple times per lecture. Highly recommend for ACC 311.

I have a differing opinion from the majority pertaining to Professor Bardhan's personality. I actually found her to be funny and with that humor, sass came with it. I found her to be very motivating, and eager for all of us to understand the course content. It just sucks the exams are so heavily weighted and MCQ, so absolute zero room for error.

Seriously I 100% recommend taking her class for acc 311. She is so engaging, and I left every single lecture feeling prepared even if I was I was paying enough attention because she explains concepts so well. No electronics allowed, but imo I liked it and it helped me focus more. She is very funny and super easy and welcoming to ask questions.

Personally, I liked Professor Bardhan. She is a little sassy, but I thought that made her more interesting and fun to talk to. The class isn't too difficult, but the grade is heavily test dependent and the littlest things can trip you up. The two 312H classes are essentially the same though, so it just depends on what teaching style you prefer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I think Professor Roy Bardhan is a decent teacher, the material is a lot to digest. The class itself isn't all that hard, but I think exams, inevitably, play a large role in the grade. Since the exams are multiple choice, there's not really any room for mistakes. Understanding all of the material conceptually is important to do well.

Topic/class itself is kind of hard. Bardhan's lectures are helpful because of the examples and there are a lot of great resources, but there's so much variation in the topic itself that you think you understand and you don't

She's ok at teaching, nothing exceptional or impressive about it. She has a bad attitude- sassy, rude, and has a superiority complex. She's a cold person- didn't feel comfortable going to OH to see her or to get help. Worst professor I've had in BHP so far. Take Prof. Chan instead. He's nicer, has a PhD, and their tests/HW/project are identical.

I thought she was great. Lectures are example-heavy (which is very useful) so would recommend scanning the textbook chap before coming to class. Group project is tough and was a disaster for me but she's willing to adjust grades for people who did more work. Exams are multiple choice. HW is easy. Very receptive to questions and participation.

Difficult class. None of us are accounting majors but she expects us to be experts. No cheat sheet allowed. Very little practice given on a unit. No extra credit or curves on exams. Probably going to drop the class at the end of the semester at this rate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like her because she seemed so passionate about the subject, but I couldn't get past other things. Doesn't respond to emails, gives vague instructions but expects perfection, gets snippy when people ask her to clarify her directions. Lectures are good, she can teach. But she lacks in other areas of being a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bardhan creates practice problems to ensure that students really understand the content. She is a good lecturer but can move a bit fast. We are graded on HWs, projects, quizzes (some pop quizzes), and 3 exams. She'll sometimes call on people because she wants participation.

No phones or laptops, only paper notes. If you can get past that she is an amazing professor. I barely had to study for her exams because class prepared me so well. I am easily distracted, so the no technology rule was actually helpful for me. If you are someone who is easily distracted like me, take her class. You will thank yourself later.

I GOT A C- SOLELY BC OF MY OWN ISSUES. Bardhan is the best professor I've ever had! I've never had a more understanding professor who made me WANT to go to a class so late in the day. She was easily accessible and answered my gazillion emails in the nicest manner. Fantastic lecturer. Hope I can take her again (and I am confident an A is possible)!

Pretty average accounting class. Tests got progressively harder but nothing crazy. Homework is due every weekend and there are hard quizzes every so often. Make sure you go to class because her lecture slides don't fully explain concepts and she doesn't post lecture recordings.

I took both 311/312 with her, and I think her practice problems help the most on the exam. She guides us through them every other class and I don't think other profs do the same. I stopped reading the book since everything's in the slides. Can be a little tough at times but also fun to joke with. I'd take her again if I was an accounting major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was a good professor, lots of quizzes and harder case assignments compared to the other professors. Less textbook reading is needed to succeed in 312 vs 311 so the class is important to attend. Exams are very difficult but standardized across all sections. Final is cumulative but multiple choice. She likes to cold-call so be ready for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Roy-Bardhan cares about her students learning. She ensures her class understands class problems by explaining the basic concepts throroughly. No electronics are allowed in class. Her RMP does not reflect how great she is,  her test averages are consistently higher than the others.

Prof. Roy Bardhan is a wonderful professor. I took her for ACC 311 and I currently have her for ACC 312. She places a heavy emphasis on practice problems in class, which is incredibly helpful in preparation for the exams- hence why she typically has higher averages than other profs. Cold-calling is not nearly as bad as other reviews mention.

I knew I would hate accounting since the beginning, but Prof Bardhan is really one of the best teachers at McCombs. That can only explain why her class average after each test was a solid B. The content is hard and challenging, but I learned a great deal with her as my Prof. She does do pop quizzes unlike the other accounting profs but she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: After studying with friends in other ACC311 sections, she is by far one of the best professors. The only issue is that her curve is based on ONLY her sections, so it's practically non-existent. Pretty light workload, and she is genuinely a good teacher. If you want to do accounting or finance, I definitely recommend for a strong foundation.

Accounting is just a hard class, no way around it. I don't think her lectures correlate very well to the tests, which is the only reason I'm knocking her a bit. The homework are very easy, but the tests are very hard compared to them, so it's hard to prepare for the exams. She's on ok teacher, not a ton of work, just a difficult subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very challenging and I would recommend taking it with another professor as she is not sympathetic toward her students and expects them to be a pro in accounting. Homeworks are pretty difficult as they are done in Excel and there are no drops. Exams can ruin your grade so memorize how to write out financial statements and re do HMWs

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! This is one of the hardest classes I have taken at UT and there is no way to improve your grade other than to do very well on exams which are extremely difficult. Exams and quizzes are closed book so be prepared to memorize her slides and create long tables and work out long problems. Homework is graded harshly.

tbh this class was a little challenging but def doable. i'd definitely recommend reading the book each week (the chapters weren't bad). also, never skip class. after a few weeks, you get used to the structure of her class. i'm taking her again next semester. she really wasn't that bad but it's not gonna be a breeze, but for sure doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. She has a lot of problems to work out in most classes and overall is pretty engaging. You are mostly just going to be constantly doing homework and readings and then cramming like crazy for the pretty difficult exams.

Professor Roy Bardhan is a great professor. Show up to class and she will teach you how to do everything. Barely uses her powerpoints because she prefers to teach easy methods to complete tasks. I would 100% recommend taking her class. She turns a boring subject like accounting into a class I look forward to going to.

I loved Roy Bardhan! Her lectures and practice tests are honestly all you need to do well on the tests. The homeworks are due weekly and are somewhat useful (I could be mixing this up with ACC 312). Roy Bardhan uses worksheets to encourage active learning, which really helped me do well in class.

I am so confused about the low ratings, she was a great professor and explained things very clearly. Her practice problems were also really helpful and a great source of material to study from. She's very sweet and really cares about her students. I didn't have to rely on the textbook at all. Just remember your homework since it's not on canvas!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Roy Bardhan was organized, a good lecturer, and helpful in office hours. But, she is not the sweetest/most understanding professor. She will call you out in front of everyone for being minutes late (it's a small class so I agree that being late is a disruption) and for not wearing your mask below your nose (she requires them).

She is a nice lady, and she explains the concepts really well. The practice problems she gives in class are helpful. Don't worry if your grades are a bit low, cause she curves pretty well at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Healthcare accounting is not an easy class, but Prof Bardhan really tries her best to make sure students are learning. She always responds to emails and is very encouraging during office hours. Exams are hard, the project is actually a lot of work and yeah you might want to pull your hair out sometimes but she curved well at the end so it's chill.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS this is NOT an easy A. the material is difficult and boring and the exams sucked the life and soul out of me. there's no good way to study for them. please be warned if you are taking this class just for credit and you could not care less about financial statements this class will ruin your semester and/or college experienc

Professor Bardhan is absolutely adorable. She is so sweet, and goes through the materials slowly, giving breaks so students can process the material and ask questions. The lectures are easy to follow as long as you do the pre-lecture reading/problems she assigns. She wants her students to really understand the material.

In her healthcare accounting class, everything is graded with unnecessary harshness and tests don't have enough questions to ensure you can miss a few and still have a good grade. Quizzes and tests had ambiguous questions and she expects you to read her mind. She's a good teacher. Just be prepared to ask many questions if you're slightly confused.

The content can be confusing, but the professor did a pretty good job at explaining things. Examples in class really helped me. I liked to condense formulas and memorized things to one page for each chapter since theres a lot of content. The tests are doable, but you have to study. The final was pretty hard, but the class was curved 8 ish points.

She is not the best at explaining and the format of the class made it quite difficult to digest/understand information. The tests are pretty hard and it is easy to forget to turn in assignments (like the connect homeworks). Although this class wasn't that bad, I think lecture content and assignments could have been handled better.

reviews.comment: Grades consisted of three exams incl. final + 3 quizzes + group project. Not the best at explaining when students hv questions but does go slow so students can keep up. Lectures were recorded.

reviews.comment: lecture style is inconsistent and can be hard to follow. best bet is to read the textbook closely and study the homeworks for exams. not very accommodating to online students & makes concepts more confusing than they need to be

reviews.comment: She is a poor lecturer; her lectures are slow and rambly and leaves you more confused than when you started. reviews.comment: I don't think she deserves to be rated as a 1, but with that being said, she wasn't the greatest professor either. She does have a pretty harsh accent which makes it a little more difficult to understand and she could be more clear in her instruction. She is a very nice lady, but I wouldn't recommend her if you have other options.

I dont know why she is scored so low, I had her for accounting 311 & 312 and loved her. I am awful at the subject, but I enjoyed her classes! She is knowledgeable, easy to understand, really caring of her students, and gives helpful practice problems. I think she is the best professor for accounting and has been one of my favorite UT professors.

Don't listen to the other reviews. She's a great professor that explains concepts really well with good examples and works out a lot of problems in class that are very useful to understand the concepts better and for the exams. All the other reviews are bs, just study when u need to and reach out to her when u need help and you'll do well with her!
Just annoying to be in class with. Do not take... honestly, teaching is same for all teachers but she never fails to ruin my day.

reviews.comment: I took ACC 312 Managerial Accounting with Professor Bardhan during Spring 2019. The class is organized and well-structured. You also need to show up to class with your name tent in order to get credit for attendance, which she takes seriously. She will call on people if she thinks they are not paying attention, so you've got to be ready for that.

One of my favorite professors at UT. She gives lots of examples in class that help with homework & exams, she also gives you old exams from past semesters that are a really big help when studying. The content itself is pretty difficult so its not an easy A, but if you put in effort and participate in class its doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She would make the rubrics vague then take off points for details not included. She would make mistakes when creating tests and quizzes, and then not award points back if students didn't write out all the work proving the question wrong. She would go though lessons way too fast and then let us out early. Shes a nice lady but she's a poor teacher.

reviews.comment: Would not recommend. She's a great person, but has a harsh accent and doesn't explain things very well. She also never gave any examples which made the homework difficult to do on our own. Overall just overcomplicated all the concepts, there are better professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are very lengthy and the grading can be sort of nitpicky with essay assignments.

The class was an 8 am and was just really, really boring. The concepts covered are very elementary. Attendance was taken, which sucked. The workload was minimal except for a research project in the last few weeks

This class is pretty straightforward and is like a simpler version of I305. Tuesdays are lectures (not required) and Thursdays are small group (required). Starts off pretty slow and simple but assignments part of the research process towards the end of the semester are more time consuming. Make sure to do quizzes and journal for easy points

reviews.comment: Don't take this course (at least w/ this professor) unless you are knowledgeable in notation and proofs. I took this after multiple stats and upper division math courses, and I'm so lost. He rarely goes step-by-step. Tests are representative of hw, but are still difficult if you don't memorize every proof. Professor is clearly knowledgeable though.

Fall 2025. Lowest 3 HW and lowest midterm get dropped. Midterms and final are multiple-choice and based on HW. Discussions are for extra practice, not mandatory. Super easy if you've taken calc before and still very doable if you haven't. In lecture, I like how he proved why everything makes sense. Overall great guy, definitely take him!

Best math course I've had in my life. I've taken Calc AB and BC in high school, but felt like I needed a refresher. I love how he explains things and I genuinely wanted to go to every lecture. He proves how everything makes sense there was really no memorization needed. He drops the lowest midterm and lowest few homeworks. Super cool and funny guy.

Probably best professor I'll ever have. Went to almost every office hour and enjoyed every moment talking to this Swiss guy. Could tell he's very passionate about math and answered questions about anything. Explained concepts in a way that proved everything he taught but no proofs. Clear class outline and almost no work to be done. Wish he did 408D

professor conway had a very clear grading system, and every homework or test was multiple choice. he is a very sweet professor, who genuinely wants feedback. everyone i know who had him loved his class and him as a professor, myself included.

Prof: 

Conway is the best professor out of the many subpar ones in UT math. His teaching: show/tell/apply format.

Class:

Exams based on HW QB. HW:10 problems weekly. Attendance is not required. Great online notes.

Ad. Notes:

UT shows a grading curve with a few C's, D's, and F's. Those are students who do not show up at all, or skip every exam.

Suchh a chill class with conway - he is super straightforward with his way of teaching & I have NEVER taken calc and only attended around 60% of lectures and got a 100 on every midterm. Midterms are only 10 questions and basically a copy of that units homework. Even though this class was light I learned the basics of calc without stress! 100% rec

Professor Conway has to be one of the best teachers I have encountered in my life. His lectures are amazing, and all the midterms are based off the HWs and the final based on the midterms and HWs. I came into the class with knowledge of the calc being taught, so it was pretty easy and I didn't go to class after the 3rd week. Just do the HWs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anthony's lectures are very straightforward. No partial credit on midterms, but he drops the lowest grade. He cares about punctuality if you do show up to class. He has a Swiss-French accent, but it's not thick at all and he writes every word he says. Handwriting is kind of "tall", but he encourages feedback and doesn't mind repeating/clarifying.
Anthony Conway's lectures were engaging and very straight forward. His exams were 10 question multiple choice and similar to the HW's. Also, The final is 25 multiple choice questions.
He was a chill professor, his HW was easy, tests were mostly just based on HW, and he would crack funny jokes in class. I would recommend.

Took this class in Fall 23, which was his first year teaching this course at UT. The notes were very clear and structured, and the lectures were straight to the point. The homework was standard quest homework, and the exams were also quest-style exams - all multiple choice. 

Whether you took calc before or not, this class was extremely doable.

Even after reading the great reviews, he was better than expected. All grading criteria very clear and very easy tests if you do the homework and test review. Graded all tests within a few hours of taking them (all multiple choice). Definitely take professor Conway if you can!

I love this silly French(?) man. If you do not know calculus very well, you will obviously have to study. If you do, this class is a breeze. He's extremely clear with grading. 10/10, I wish he'd be there for 408D.

One of the best professors I have ever seen! I haven't come in with a calc background, which scared me (engineering major). However, he made calc such an easy class and enjoyable learning. I loved all his lectures and enjoyed going to his early morning classes. I have never been to his office hours, but I'm sure he is super helpful.

Coming into this class, I expected it to be easy based on the ratings. Without prior calculus, it's tough, and I spent hours studying. If you've taken Calc AB, it'll be easier, but otherwise, prepare to work hard. Most students had some background. Professor Conway is very caring and supportive, which helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think his class was easy compared to the Calc AB class I took in high school. We have 1 homework every week with 10 questions, midterms and the final are exactly like the home works. He has all the resources we need in one website, on his canvas, very organized, we get our grades back really fast as well!

I was scared to take 408C bc the last math class I took was 3 years before. If your situation is like mine, this class will not be a cake walk, but if you practice and go to calc lab for extra help and you will be great. Midterms based on the homework, final on midterms and homework. All exams except final are 10 questions. Great professor overall.

Conway is a fantastic lecturer. Tests are exactly like the homework/discussion reviews. Although attendance isn't mandatory, he makes an effort to connect with students in class and occasionally jokes with us during lectures so I would recommend going. He's very helpful during office hours, and will always make sure you understand the content.

Teaches every subject in depth and takes questions at any point in class. Aside from his amazing teaching style, he is a very down-to-earth person and is very approachable for any further clarifications. Would take him again for every math class if I could.

It was a pleasure to take Professor Conway's class! His tests are very similar to the hw which are pretty straight forward. He is a very organized professor (his lecture notes are amazing!), responds quickly to emails & is willing to help students out as much as he can (asked for a letter of rec and he kindly wrote one!). Def caring & engaging.

Conway was such a pleasure to take. He offered ample practice and help for those who needed it, but also only assigned 10 HW problems a week and had super easy tests. His lectures are great for anyone, but especially those who have already taken calc in high school and just need the credit. Absolutely would take his class again

Professor Conway was amazing, and if you had previous experience with calculus in high school his class was a breeze. Tests are all shorter (10 questions) and follow the same format as the reviews and the HW assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is such a nice and good professor. If you took calculus in high school you should do amazing in this class. Even if you didn't you should be fine as he is a great teacher and very open to questions. The tests are exactly like the HW and 10 questions and easy. I enjoyed his class as it was extremely organized and clear on the expectations.

If you took any form of calculus in high school, this is a free review class. You can legit relearn the material through the easy HWs he assigns every week. I stopped going after the second week. Tests are 10 MCQs and final is 25 MCQs. Drops your lowest test and 3 lowest HWs. He's also nice and funny from the lectures I have been to. Def take.

The class is extremely easy. 1 HW per week, 10 MCQ. Midterms also just 10 MCQ and final is 25 MCQ. I didn't go to any recitations, but he has online notes, so that with O CHEM tutor on YT made class very easy to keep up and know material. He's a nice guy, and during lectures makes sure the material is understood with no confusion. Def take him.

Really enjoyed this class. Found the prof to be pretty chill and funny. Short homework once per week, pretty easy. Tests are similar to homework, so not too tough as long as you study. Highly recommend!

Very easy and chill professor. Makes sure students are understanding his lectures, and even explains in several different ways until middle ground is found between professor and student. Homeworks once per week, 10 question mcq. Tests also 10 question mcq, extremely similar to homework, so pretty easy. Pretty funny sometimes as well.Take this prof!

I was wary about taking Conway as he was a brand-new teacher, but I was pleasantly surprised! I went to every class, but attendance was not required. I knew most of the content going in; however, his lectures were very helpful with many examples and he answered questions well. Also, he is not a boring professor and would frequently joked with us.
Lectures were very helpful and offers a lot of extra credit.

Assignment instructions can be ambiguous. Adds a lot of unnecessary assignments to the course that do not help enhance our knowledge or performance in lab. It seems like their purpose is to waste our time. The professor is very nice, and when she lectures, it is helpful. However, she only lectures for 10-15 minutes once a week.

This class is well-organized and an easy A, but the workload for a 2 hr credit is considerable. Weekly reflection essays & PyMOL activities often took hours, plus there are weekly lab quizzes to study for and pre-lab assignments due. Labs are helpful but incredibly long. She offers lots of extra credit and drops your lowest quiz though.

W Prof Seminars always introduced to us new things for research/ECs. Lab quizzes were tricky as they tested on some random specific details in the protocol. My TAs were THE BEST (shout out to Janice and Tu-Quyen), always super helpful. Labs were longish, a lot of EC, PyMol project was fun, practical was light, a lot of busy work (my only complaint)

Dr. Garrett is genuinely the most kind and caring professor I've had at UT. The course can have a heavy-ish workload if you leave everything to the last minute but the TAs are so understanding. So accessible outside of class if you have any questions about the major, career plans, etc!!

Dr. Garrett makes it very easy to succeed in this class, if you're willing to put in the effort. Certain weeks can be very assignment heavy (never more than 3-4hrs outside lab), but you always know what to expect and there's never any surprises. Canvas is organized very well, and Dr. Garrett/TAs are very kind/receptive w/ questions and feedback! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Garrett is incredibly kind and compassionate. The Lab quizzes are pretty tricky, but they don't count for that much of your grade. The Reflection Essays (Lab Reports + PyMol work) are incredibly - and unnecisarily - long (5-6 hours / week). End of Semester PyMol project was enriching and fun!

Dr. Garrett is really sweet. Seminars were a bit boring but very interactive. I was in the FRI lab, so we did have a shorter lab and less labs to attend to so that was nice. I absolutely loved my TA's (Emma and Caitlin y'all rock). They were really sweet and for someone that doesn't get things on the first try, they were really patient with me!

Dr. Garrett is awesome! The course is very organized and expectations are clear. The seminars were helpful for preparing for each week's lab, as well as for learning about college and career resources. She's very friendly and is generous with grading and extra credit points. She also makes the lab practical as unintimidating as possible.

very sweet professor! labs were fun and informative, but long ofc. beginning of class was pretty bad with TAs not knowing what is needed on lab notebooks. notebooks were SO long as well. mid-semester survey was a turning point: expectations were more clear and lab notebooks weren't as time consuming. take notes on a doc during lab and rewrite after

Very sweet professor! The class has a lot of cool labs that teaches you basic lab techniques. There's a lot of busy work each week, make sure to study for quizzes using the material provided focusing on the topics she tells you to. Some of the assignments are vague or not taught well which can be frustrating if you don't have time for office hours.

Organized course with plenty of resources laid out for you. Some experiments are cool, but there is a lot of busywork that goes with them. PyMol project at the end of the semester can be fun and plenty of guidance is given. Just do the work and you'll be good; everything is graded very leniently and getting an A is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: An insane amount of busy work that felt overwhelming and useless sometimes, but the grading was extremely lenient. Prof. Garret is also extremely caring and understanding and is always asking for feedback on how to improve the course to be more accommodating. You'll be fine as long as you keep your head up and turn everything in on time.

I loved this lab and seminar! I learned a lot more about biochemistry careers and skills and am much more prepared for my degree. I appreciated how she tried to keep things fun and was always available for office hours. Plus, my TAs were PHENOMENAL! There are a lot of assignments but it isn't bad, I just asked TAs when I was lost :) Honestly fun!

Be prepared for an insane amount of busy work. Every week is something to dread with the sheer amount of work you're expected to put into an intro-level biochem lab, so expect that you will receive the most useless and longest assignments that you will encounter at UT. I'd advise not taking this course, but it's unfortunately required for biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attending seminar is mandatory weekly (2 drops), a quiz for each lab session (+ a lab notebook and a reflection essay for each), a 3-week-long PyMOL project + presentation, and a lab practical (pass/fail). Overall, I enjoyed having Dr. Garrett for this course but there were lots of unnecessary (IMO) assignments even if they were graded easily.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, she really does care about everyone. Very helpful for learning about the bch major and different lab techniques. There are quite a few assignments between the weekly essays and lab notebooks, and they feel very unnecessary but grading is very chill. My UGCA was super helpful and accessible outside of class!

This class can genuinely be super easy as long as you put in the work, I just left studying for literally the last minute before exams and completely gave up on trying to understand integrals at the end. Overall many opportunities to save your grade. Honestly all props to my TA too because I didn't really understand lectures.

Professor Ansari is kind and caring, but his lectures are dry as he mostly reads directly from the textbook. Multivariable Calculus requires a conceptual understanding of how 2D math generalizes to 3D, but he often skips the intuition to focus on repetitive practice problems. I had to learn how to conceptualize the concepts outside of class.

Dr. Ansari is extremely good at explaining, he has this way of simplifying the hardest concepts so that they're really easy to understand. He really wants to see you succeed in the class, and his tests are always super easy, just choose the hardest problem on the quest worksheet and you'll be fine!

Basically reads off the textbook and is (mostly) good at answering students' questions. He is very lenient on quizzes which don't challenge students. Arrives late to class, ends class early, and canceled ~3 classes, so I am paying for more than what I receive.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ansari is truly the easiest math prof I've had. Plenty of quizzes & HW, 2 midterms and a final. If you have trouble with this class go to office hrs and make sure to have questions ready for discussion, TA was amazing. Practice problems from the text book helped me out a lot to understand the concept better. Amazing class and amazing faculty!

1 Quiz/Week. 2 Mid terms (got a 100 on both) Final (100) ended with 99.57. The class was the easiest math class ever, without sacrificing quality of lecture. Dr. Ansari deserves a pay raise, he makes expectations so clear, tells you what the quizzes and tests will be, hes kinda funny too. go mandatory lecture do wtv study 1 day before test, aceable

Got a 100 in calc 3 with him. Nice, straightforward guy. He's fast paced with the notes and is aware of that, so he'll occasionally pause for the students to catch up. Literally gives you the exact content that's going to be on the quizzes and exams, including the final. Homework is per unit, about 6-12 questions each. An 89 is considered an A.

RAHHHHH I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR!!!! His class was the easiest math class I've ever taken and I still learned so much. I'm not saying there is no work you should expect to study BUT this prof makes it stress free. The exams were fair and the mean was high.

I'm not a strong math person, so the content was challenging for me, but Dr. Ansari is one of the kindest professors I've had. He genuinely cares about his students, holds weekly office hours, and is always willing to help via email. If you put in the effort, he wants you to succeed.

He is a great professor for this course. The way he grades exams is very much in favor towards the students and he seems to enjoy teaching. The only critique I can give is that his voice can be very monotone.

This class was probably the easiest math class I've taken. I didn't really understand the concepts of the content but he told us the topics of the quizzes and tests. As long as you work through the problems related to those topics, the class is very easy.

So glad I got placed into this class. I was nervous it was going to be difficult, but if you have taken Calculus AB and BC you'll be perfectly fine in taking this class. Lots of homework, almost every day there's an assignment, but it's beneficial in preparing for the tests. Very approachable and checks in on struggling students.
Con: attendance is mandatory. Pro: exams are extremely similar to the textbook problems he tells you to study. I zoned out in class and just did the textbook problems and had a very easy time

He kinda just walks in and starts yapping and scrolls through a textbook-like pdf. Moves very, very fast and sometimes ignores ppl with their hand up. Weekly Quests and quiz discussion sections and he gives a very, very clear review of what is on exams so as long as you memorize how to solve them, you'll get by. TA Sudharshan is lowkey pretty funny

Extremely easy class (business calc). Didnt come to class whole sem aside from first two days and have an easy A. Lectures and notes are extremely simple and tests are so much easier than the quest modules and worksheets. Honestly, a good bit of homework, 2-3 quests a week and 2 worksheets on canvas, but all are really easy

M408C during the summer, amazing awesome.

He would give you everything you needed on a silver platter. Never took calc and it was honestly very easy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took calculus over the summer. His tests were fair with plenty of practice material given to prepare. Very knowledgeable on the topic, but sometimes can move through a lecture fast. Homework was never more than an hour or two a week.

His lectures are kind of boring but as long as you listen and know how to do all the HWs then you will have no problem in this class. The exams were very straightforward and he wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love this man so much, he is the most caring professor ever, his tests are quite hard but he curves them sometimes and is very lenient, final was so easy too. YOU NEED AN IPAD THO class is too hard w/o one. Overall compared to the other 408D this is the best option. I love Dr. Ansari. I LOVE HIM. BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD.

I found his lectures quite easy to follow. Material may be tricky at times, but he is glad to help. He tells you exactly what to study for quizzes and tests which was very helpful. I would take him again.
Easy, makes things clear. Easy tests.
Tests were easy. Clear and pretty lenient grading rubric. Good at explaining stuff in lectures but they are boring. Notes were helpful and he posts them.

He wants you to succeed and makes it clear what will be on quizzes and tests; his grade cutoffs are really nice and are set to benefit the students. His lectures can get hard to sit through sometimes, but they are available to rewatch so that's helpful. Definitely tries his best to give us the most beneficial deal.

Dr Ansari is a good person especially when you go to his office hours. I find starting a conversation is easy and is willing to talk about a lot of things. I went when confused about lecture and it helped me clear up some concepts. Lectures can drag for a little but when students engage it helps gets the points along.

While the subject matter and lectures aren't too riveting, Ansari is a great professor! He is very understanding and always open to any questions. He is very generous with grading and tries to give students as much credit as possible!
Great professor, cares a lot! He tells you exactly what to study for exams, and is super helpful when things come up. Would def take again!

He was great for M408D, especially coming from someone who transferred from another professor. His lectures are fast-paced, but he always checks for understanding. Grade-wise, he takes care of you and does his best to get you an A, and the tests are easy if you prepare like he tells you to (practice probs and review). Highly recommend!

Honestly, not too sure where the negative reviews are coming from. This class was very straightforward and he made it clear what was going to be on the exams. Unless he changes the value of attendance, I think I had a 70% attendance and still got an A in this class. Doing the HW will prepare you plenty for exams, and he gave out a review too.
Not nearly enough time
Gave us tests that didn't contain content learned in class. Along with this he doesn't give proper curves on tests or quizzes. The TA was good though.
Not very clear lectures and the quizzes were nothing like what was presented on lecture.
Would not recommend

His class is an easy A, even if you don't know anything about calculus. Most of the midterm grades are from a take-home online portion, and the final is totally online. Overall, he's a really chill and lax professor that does his best to get you an A.

Amazing professor to take for multivariable calculus! He has very clear grading criteria, the lectures are very good (content is somewhat hard but he makes it manageable). Knows names, is very accessible outside class, and is a very nice person. The exams and homework are fairly easy, and he works through examples very well. Definitely recommend!

Prof Ansari is an easy grader, clear lecturer, and a very friendly person. By the end of the semester he knows all his students names and creates a comfortable learning atmosphere. You will get called on but don't worry because hell work thru the problem w you. This wont ever be a class you'll need to worry about grade wise. Amazing professor!!!!!!

Dr. Koltz and Dr. Wolf were great lecturers! The content was mostly memorization and the exams were not too difficult. The exams did take a long time to be graded and there are outside projects that are easy but you do have to still do them. Very interesting class and content overall and both professors were kind and understanding.

Dr. Koltz and Wolf, along with the teaching team were nice and knowledgeable. The class itself wasn't bad, it's mainly memorization-based and exams are heavily graded. However, the class was harder than what I had expected it to be. There are a few projects that the TAs grade strictly on, and exams are a mix of MC and FRQ. Content is interesting!

The content of this class is not TOO difficult, but the course structure is set up a lot harder than it needs to be. Grades are almost completely based on exams, and each exam is graded atleast a month after it's taken. Grades aren't posted until LAST minute. They mentioned a curve, didn't apply it. So stressful not knowing how you're doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Koltz was a great lecturer, and she and Dr. Wolf made sure to cover everything needed for each exam! It's mostly memorization, but as long as you stay on top of the content it's manageable. The discussion projects are also a good grade boost, just make sure to actually try on them.

would definitely recommend for ecology! grade is based off of exams, a few writing assignments, and discussion section participation. i felt that everything was explained very well and exams were very fair. as a bio major this class was really interesting to me.

I personally did not enjoy this class, I felt that the lectures weren't that intriguing. The grades are hidden throughout the semester so you can't see how you stand in the class, and assignments can take 2-3 weeks to return to you. At least there's no final. If you really like ecology then this class might be for you, but it wasn't for me.

Currently in her course. She is honestly a great professor, like she teaches awesome and I never seen a professor care for students more than her. But she talks incredibly fast just for us to somehow be way behind on material and work and then somehow her exams are unnecessarily harder compared to Mike Scotts, just some random harder applications.

Kaur is kind and engaging in her lectures, and she makes compsci accessible to those who have never encountered it before. The exams are very difficult but doable, and we were given cheat sheets for each one. It will take a lot of work, but a good grade is certainly accessible.

Very engaging, easy-to-understand lectures, but we are graded on 3 tests that basically make up 90% of our grade, which are pretty difficult. Programming assignments are hard to get full points on, but extra credit makes up for those. Amrita was a very helpful professor, and most of the TAs are very helpful as well.

Pretty good professor. Lectures and weekly assignments are engaging and interesting. Weekly assignments are graded harshly but there's a ton of extra credit so its not hard to offset the tough grading. If you do the practice tests she gives you its not hard to get 90+ on exams. If you did UIL CS this course will be extremely easy for you.

I personally enjoyed the HWs even though they were challenging because they were quite enjoyable to code up. However, I feel like most of my effort went into doing good style and docstrings. Sometimes we don't know about certain style requirements until after it was graded, especially at the end unless you asked the TAs. Final was hard, but curved

Professor Kaur has really good lectures. The programming assignments are long and you can lose a lot of points because of poor style (especially at the semester start), but since there's so much lecture/feedback form extra credit it's easy to get full credit. Tests are really hard and worth a ton but there are practice tests posted, so study a lot!

Professor Kaur is a great teacher, and her lectures are engaging and informative. The tests are difficult, but are often heavily curved. The TAs are helpful, but their grading can be inconsistent. If you attend lectures, study, and don't use AI to generate your code, you will do well. Beware of using outside material, because it's an automatic zero

Amrita is difficult to talk to and is not very helpful during office hours. Assignment grading is largely based on style instead of code functionality and the TAs take off points harshly for minor mistakes. Not a bad class if you have prior coding experience, but be sure not to use any of it because you'll be accused of cheating.

She was decent. As a lecturer she was pretty energetic, but I do think that she skimmed over a few stuff. The grading in the class is not very well-designed, as weekly assignments take up around 20 hours a week, but are worth less than 10% of your total grade. Exams are kind of brutal.
Shout out to Ms Kaur for her six seven jokes
Very smart professor who's very experienced in what she teaches but her class is not for the weak. Lectures are very fast paced but slides are posted to look back on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was challenging, and the exams had many questions that were hard to prepare for because they were extremely conceptual. However, she is a pretty good lecturer and explains the concepts pretty well. She also gives you a ton of practice tests to prepare for the exam, but they are Mike Scott's, so be aware they will be kinda different.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amrita is amazing! As someone with zero CS knowledge coming into the course, I found it to be very enjoyable. She's an engaging lecturer and if you attend lecture, it can count towards your final grade making the final worth less. You can't use prior CS knowledge so pay attention to what she does/doesn't talk about. Tests are fine. Lovely course!

Professor Kaur is incredibly rude and accuses you of cheating instantly. She has harsh grading criteria that does not reflect how much you know the material. She is a decent lecturer but she is difficult to talk to and very judgemental.

extremely harsh grading policies, expecting you to use only what's in the slides, even if it's the most basic topics. gives 0 on homeworks very often for alleged AI allegations & going out of syllabus & is not approachable for questions. not willing to reason or give even partial credit. extremely long unncessary assignments. DONT TAKE HER!!!

1) Doesn't teach 'break' and 'continue', yet teaches a much higher difficulty topic of object-oriented programming. Does it sound off to you? It should.
2) She will be getting your grade down to 0 if you dare to confront her. Has too many good reviews because bad ones have rude words in them, and oh they are deserved.
3) Not approachable at all
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While she's particular about some aspects of the class, she made a challenging subject manageable and even enjoyable. Lectures provide nearly all the info you need to know, and there are a lot of resources and extra credit opportunities. Some assignments were hard, but office hours were really helpful and grading/feedback was very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall this was a good class. I definitely learned a lot without it being too hard. However, it's definitely not easy and the assignments are a bit of a pain especially with the code hygiene and style. Tests are definitely big but you get a lot of practice tests so make sure to use those.

She's a very nice teacher but the whole class is graded by the TAs, and they will destroy your grade. They are outrageously nitpicky on homeworks and the tests. Getting your code to work is the easy part. Assignments, FOCUS ON YOUR STYLE. Tests, there's a curve but it's not crazy, focus on studying over how the code works.

She's a decent lecturer but the grading structure is chopped. Your entire grade is dictated by tests (84%) and there's just about no curving. Even so, assignments are time-consuming and graded very harshly, and at times, seemingly arbitrarily. There *are* lots of extra-credit for assignment points to make up for it but it's mostly attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the worst, not the best. Exams/assignments are doable but have to be SO careful to not use concepts that haven't been taught (even if you have prior knowledge), or you will be accused of AI and get a 0 full stop. She doesn't communicate well about schedule/assignment changes etc. Grading criteria is VERY dependent on which TA grades your work.
someone said tests are the D-Day landings on Normandy beach from Saving Private Ryan lol and they are right

this class was genuinely so hard for no reason, and the CONSTANT AI allegations tank your grade bc she'll give anyone a 0 if you use a concept she didn't teach - even if you already knew it and truly didn't use AI. she's also hard to get in touch and midterm/finals(all are difficult) are worth basically your entire grade so if you fail, its over
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dont take her...save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BIOCHEM MAJORS GOOD LUCK...this class is so much work for no reason and your grade is determined by very few assignments / midterms so EVERYTHING matters. so strict on grading and if assignments didn't exactly match her rubric/style, she'd take off points. midterms are pretty difficult and lectures are her talking at you the entire time - AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Good teacher, but TRASH grading scheme. It is MEANT to SCREW you. Spend 25 hours on the weekly assignment? Its not even worth 1% of your grade lol. Didn't do the assignment correctly? Well if you don't redo it you get knocked 1/3 of an ENTIRE LETTER. 


How about tests? Oh yeah, 84% of your grade. Say good bye to any hopes of an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are the D-Day landings on Normandy beach from Saving Private Ryan
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Known as the 67 professor for a reason

Lectures were very great. Like others said, many jokes including the classic 67 to keep students engaged. The only reason I gave 4 was because we are always a bit behind so stuff gets crammed near the end, but that isn't any type of deal breaker and the class is very fun.
Makes students laugh during every lecture at least 6 or 7 times. Great teacher. Hard exams so make sure to study prior and do all the practice tests.

Amrita is one of the best professors in UT! Her homework assignments are kinda graded harshly, but you can easily get help from TAs and prof during office hours. Exams are straightforward with generous gradings.
One of the most FUNNY lectures I have ever seen. One lecture she made a backtracking tree with the faces of our other professors as the nodes. Also as others said, makes 6 or 7 jokes
Makes 67 jokes

Amrita is very knowledgeable and a decent lecturer, although lectures are entirely too quick. However, the AI accusations are entirely unjust, unfair, and impossible to deal with. If you turn in YOUR code, there's a possibility you'll be accused of AI, reported, and just in awe. Talking to Amrita is impossible. Genuinely, take another professor.

so i did have to schedule a therapy session abt this class because i got an unecessaery 0 on my assignment like i know it was bad but it definitely wasnt that bad. she said it was ai and it wasnt bc i did create the code in 20 minutes and ik it was bad but i got a 0 because it was ai... not cause it was bad. period!!!! tell em girl! i love that!
Average lecturer, not very friendly and snarky at times.
do not take this professor if you can lol

Very compassionate and caring person. Lectures are very funny and informative. Makes 67 jokes. You get to learn lots of new stuff. I say this taking her class again next semester, so that says a lot. 


Get ready to be humbled by those exams though. Make sure to study TWO WEEKS BEFORE as the grading can be unforgiving. No curve 1st & 2 pts 2nd exam

don't be discouraged by all the negative reviews, amrita is a very engaging professor. Lectures can be long with many slides, but she posts condensed slides and homework's and similar to in class problems and exams are similar to practice exams. Pay attention in lecture, attendance  optional based on final exam grade weight. some homework's long.

Evil. Accuses you of cheating if you use any outside knowledge, even if you have prior coding experience. Looks for reasons to take off points on tests and assignments, and doesn't post any grades until after the drop deadline has passed. Also gets mad if you ask a question, even though she is the one that tells us to ask questions. Do not take!

Amrita is wonderful, and I definitely recommend taking this course! I had zero CS experience prior to this course, but I found that not to be an issue. Amrita is fun, engaging, accommodating, and clearly puts lots of effort in. The tests are lengthy, but they are not very difficult if you pay attention to the lectures.

You only like her if you already know Python. If not, yikes. Lectures are 100+ slides long & very fast so you can't take notes or go back and look. No reviews. If you go to office hours she is rude & accuses everyone of cheating. She brags about how many reports she files. You will have to learn everything on your own. Tests handwritten on paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just not great... confusing, fast-paced lectures, not flexible at all with grading policies, and does not show much compassion towards students.

Amrita is very cold to her students and crashes out over small things like side talk (whispers) during class. Ends up causing a bigger distraction than it should. 


She can teach but I learned from practice tests mostly to get a 89 on the first test. 


Overall not bad, but if you need a supporting environment to learn this may not work out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor can teach, but is not helpful when it comes to any questions. TAs were mostly the ones addressing needs of the students. I feel that she is very disconnected from her students.

She is VERY rushy with answering questions and doesn't delve into too much helpful detail. Not bad professor but Scott is nicer since I am retaking with him fall
This class is quite challenging, but she teaches it exceptionally well. UT doesn't seem to have a better professor for this course. You can genuinely learn the fundamentals of Python.

This professor talks extremely fast and is difficult to understand. She is not understanding if you bring any issue to her and will simply tell you to go talk to someone else. This class is hard but was so much tougher with this professor. Discussion & co-study were most helpful and I am thankful for that because I learned mainly from TAs.

She's a good lecturer and wants to make sure people understand the material, and is a very nice professor; however, look out for the exams as they are harder than the ones Professor Scott has, but still overall pretty good
Makes up random style guidelines where nobody knows what they are. Clearly has a terrible relationship with TAs.

Amrita's amazing and was a welcome change of pace from Ramsey. She's really energetic during lecture, and she's clearly passionate about the material. I don't think I'm alone in thinking her exams are more difficult that Mike Scott's. All three ended up getting curved during my semester. Past tests definitely won't fully prepare you.

Professor Kaur is perhaps the most engaging lecturer that I have encountered. I highly recommend going to lectures regularly. The course material is quite difficult, and expect to spend a great deal of time on every programming assignment (especially Huffman!) Our tests were substantially different from the practice exams, so I would prepare well.

Amazing + clear lectures. Don't use chat on assignments, you will 100% get caught. Exams are slightly different than Mike's but you'll do well if you study the lectures + not just take practice exams. Curved all the exams very generously. TA's are goated, go to help hours, co-study, + section. Didn't open the txbk, lectures are all you need.

i'm not a freshman & have retaken a few cs classes at ut. came in with no experience, and this was the first time i could really follow lecture and feel like i understood well. i'm a slow learner, but amrita made things click. the class is VERY hard, but she's a great prof. don't cheat on hw, ask tas for help, and study for exams, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: nice professor, nice ta's, somewhat fun lectures. assignments are time-consuming, so start early. lots of extra credit just for attending lectures, so even a few points off each assignment doesn't affect you at all. however, the MCQ part of the exams is extremely different from previous years, so be ready. textbook isn't mandatory, but it's helpful
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amrita truly loves CS and her students, she's a young but talented professor and brings lots of energy to the classroom. The difficulty of the class comes from the material itself, not the professor; this has been taught in the same way for 20 years. Exams weighed 84%, down from 90% w/ Mike last sem (& don't cheat on assignments, you'll get caught)

Her lectures are long, but her passion for CS is very evident. No phones are allowed in class, and she does say a few snappy remarks if you are seen lying on your hand or with a phone out (basically not being attentive). Exams are also heavily weighted, but studying is your best friend.

She is genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. The class is about 80 something percent based on tests and her tests are nothing like the previous professors tests (which is the ONLY study material provided). Beyond that she was never on pace with what we should've been learning at the time of the test. She is extremely mean and uncaring!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We got a little bit behind which meant that harder topics were covered in short periods, but otherwise lectures were great and resources available helped a lot. I went to every co-study session. The amount of practice exams and problems given during section helped a lot.

Lectures were amazing and attendance was extra credit which made it easy. Even though I did say the class was test heavy, there were insane curves which helped a lot. Overall, the assignments held very specific and clear grading standards that left little room for ambiguity or argument. The exams were crazy hard but definetly worth the challenge.

I loved Amrita. Excellent lectures. Exams weren't too difficult, maybe 6/10. Most gripes about this class will come from people who did not want to study and/or ChatGPT warriors. I have no point of reference against Mike Scott, but I think Amrita took the job and ran with it. The grading scale is tough, deal with it.

Fairly difficult class, but entirely manageable with enough time. Exams were the worst part as they never matched the practice reviews and were on  paper, but were allowed a cheat sheet and allowed 2 on the final. Weekly assignments took a good deal of time but they're never that bad as long as you use the concepts she teaches to avoid getting a 0.

She grades so weird and I'll get a 0 on an entire assignment for using something that wasn't learned in class even though I learned it watching youtube videos over the concepts she went over. She made me never want to go to class and I genuinely can't stand computer science anymore. Also all of the tests are by hand in a computer science class.
Difficult but manageable - great professor

Prof. Kaur is a great lecturer and engaged with the students during and outside of class. Attendance is "mandatory" since you can complete the attendance ticket after 1 or 2 days after the lecture by watching the recording. The assignments aren't difficult and she gives you resources to prepare yourself for her exams. I encourage you to go OH :)

She is a fantastic lecturer, and super engaging. Gave a feedback survey for extra credit asking how long the assignments took and what we thought. She read these responses and considered what they said, sometimes slowing down lectures if requested. The exams were a fair assessment of what we had learned. Not easy, but not ridiculously hard.

This class moves VERY fast, but Prof. Kaur is so passionate in what she does and actually listens to her students if they ask to slow lecture down a bit. Assignments can be challenging, and she doesn't put up with disrespect, but she is overall super caring and wants the best for her students. Also gives out amazing practice materials. Do the PSS!

I came into this class with zero coding experience and never felt at a disadvantage. Professor Kaur knows her stuff, makes class fun, and upholds standards while practicing empathy. I felt her grading policies were challenging yet forgiving. Assignments can be tricky but grading is generous as long as you follow her academic honesty policies.

read all of this. I'll start by saying she is an amazing teacher, just not a good professor. She's really fun in class, but she loves handing out zeros on her homework assignments, which is hard to come back from. I enjoyed the class before we were given back our homework grades (1 month after submitting!), but she was not helpful after that.

Kaur is not a good prof. Her TA's grade super harshly, and her grading is so shady. She just does everything by hand and hands out grades randomly all at once without being able to see a clear breakdown. Some assignments are weighted more heavily than others, which ones? I have no freaking clue. Please don't take her or this class and save yourself

She talks very fast, her accent is hard to comprehend, and her grading is insane. She takes away significant points for the slightest mistakes. The practice tests are supposed to help, but they don't as the tests given are a lot harder. The final exam was an absolute nightmare.

Came in to Professor Kaur's class w/ minimal coding experience. Practice exams and lecture slides (esp the examples she includes in them) were very helpful for the exam. Homework was easy to follow along and not very difficult. Final was difficult, but she was lenient with the cutoffs so 40% of her class made A/A-. Very generous with extra credit!!

Before Professor Kaur's class, I had no coding experience, so office hours were very helpful. Coding is tough, so start assignments early. She's great - encourages participation with candy, offers extra credit, and cares about students. She's blunt but only when addressing disruptions. Study ahead, understand the concepts, and exams are curved.

Prof Kaur is clearly passionate. She takes 2-3 weeks to respond to emails. Lots of extra credit, but for good reason. Tests are hard, the practice tests are nothing like them. Extremely passive aggressive and demeaning at times. She is the reason I no longer want to do cs. Took every chance to blame me for not being able to succeed in coding!

She's a very engaging lecturer. I think my main gripes with the class are just about the inflexibility in grading policy, as you can put in a lot of work and be rewarded pretty minimally. The assignments will take you hours to complete. The exams are very difficult, so STUDY. Weed out classes are meant to be hard so work hard and do your best!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've never coded prior to this class, and Professor Kaur taught a great first-coder class! There are so many opportunities for extra credit, and there are TA office hours for help on the assignments literally every single day from like 9am-5pm. The assignments can be difficult but as long as you attend lecture/watch lecture videos, you'll be ok!

Very receptive to questions and asks students for feedback (and you get extra credit for giving feedback). The lectures are really nice and I was able to actually learn from them. Assignments can be challenging but there are so many resources for help + extra credit. Exams reflect what was learned in class and there is a curve.

Beginner friendly but the pace does pick up in this class even though she teaches basics. Is really good about listening to student feedback. Talks very fast so if you don't understand something you have to ask in that moment or it's hard to catch up. Homeworks and exams are pretty on par with what is lectured on, slightly more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kaur is my favorite professor at UT. She is an amazing lecturer and very accessible to get help. As someone who entered her class in Spring 2024 with no coding experience, she broke down the material in a clear format for beginners. Homework assignments get difficult later on in the semester. Tests are challenging.

The content itself was not hard however, the format of the exams was on paper which made it annoying and difficult. The practice exams did not reflect the real exams' difficulty. Much of the stuff we learn in class is useless. Grading on homework was annoying I would get points off for things that didn't matter like an extra comment.

So many opportunities for extra credit from assignments, attendance, and feedback surveys. Gradescope for HW sucks, but there's so many TA's and office hours and that saved my life so many times! Kaur is a fantastic and engaging lecturer. Tests are kinda hard tho. Wish I went to office hours sooner. 10/10 would take a again!
Gave no feedback on the final and curved grades last minute. She is a nice person but the practice exams do not match the exams.

Prof Kaur is awesome! She really cares about her students, and she'll give you all the resources you need to succeed. Grades are weekly coding assignments (moderately difficult), 2 midterms, and 1 final. Lots of extra credit--take advantage!! Midterms are tricky, so study lecture slides, extra problems, and practice tests. An A is totally doable!

Prof Kaur was a very engaging lecturer and helps you wet your feet in python coding. She gives lots of opportunities outside of class for help and to better understand the content showing she cares a lot about student success. Office hours with her are great. Only complaint is that the practice exams never matched the difficulty of the real exams.

Prof Kaur is such a GOOD teacher. She is so patient and caring. There are lots of small opportunities for extra credit so TAKE ADVANTAGE- it adds up! The assignments are doable and easy if you go to office hours. Learn about style early and revisit throughout the semester so you can collect easy points. The exams aren't too bad. Best intro cs class

People have mixed opinions about Kaur. Honestly, she is not bad at all. She is a great lecturer and very willing to help during office hours. The homeworks will get tough as you go on, so make sure to utilize the TA office hours. She is very knowledgeable about what she is teaching, so if you are interesting is learning CS, you should take her!

Honestly one of the best lecturers I've had at UT as she's very thorough with explanations and resources. There's plenty of extra credit if you do stuff like turning in assignments on time and even going to lecture. A few assignments took way too long and gradescope is annoying asf, but there's so many TA office hours and you def should go, 10/10

If you already have CS experience, Kaur is an awesome prof! HWs will be super easy and exams are sometimes a bit sneaky, but overall fair and well written. If you haven't coded before though, this class will be pretty tough. Lots of extra credit opportunities and the TAs give really good feedback on HWs.

Good person, pretty bad professor. The main issue with this class is that the difficulty level of the exams is not at all similar to the material she teaches. She scratches the surface of all the core concepts however will test you on the most niche uses of these concepts. I would avoid taking this class with her at all costs.

She is a nice person but the difference between the lecture material and practice test in comparison to the test is laughable. The class and concepts are not that hard she just does a poor job of preparing people who have not coded before for the exams.
Content is hard and she's not the easiest to listen to, but it's doable and she provides all the resources needed to get a decent grade. Homework's can be time consuming, but they are doable.

Great person, but awful professor. Her lectures are filled with content, but she jumps around constantly from topic to topic. Assignments are extremely helpful and so are OH, but does not prepare you for the exams. You will be learning content up till the last day before the exam, and it will definitely be tested on.

She expects you to have no experience in coding. However, students in the class are either have experience already, or no experience at all. So no-experience ppl don't do as well on exams, but the ppl with experience will cancel that out. Therefore, the exam averages are normal so she doesn't really care and think everyone is doing fine.

Great professor for learning basic computer science, very thorough, and clearly goes through all the material in class. Plus there are tons of office hours and added learning sessions. She is very funny, and gives and receives feedback very frequently in service to improving the course experience.

Coming from a person who had 0 coding experience before...Professor Kaur is GOATED. She would not let you use any programming knowledge outside from her class which I think it's fair and indeed works very well with me so I only need to review what she taught. Exams are a little rough, but if you actually understand the material, you will be fine.

The exams are tough so be prepared to study! Utilize the practice exams she gives you and she also allows you to have a cheat sheet on the exams! Write good notes on your cheat sheet + do the practice exams to get an A. I entered this class with no coding experience and found the assignments difficult yet rewarding.

DOES NOT CURVE INDIVIDUAL EXAMS and will only CONSIDER curving final grade!! If you don't have any prior knowledge in python, I would strongly advise against taking her class or you WILL be struggling for your life. There is a huge disparity in difficulty between her exams and the actual material she teaches in class.

I took Amrita her first year of teaching. She does a pretty good job at teaching you the basics and the majority of the assignment were fun and easy! The only thing is that the homework difficulty changes extremely quickly and her practice exams sucked to take without anyone there to warn me.

But she's pretty chill and friendly overall.

Great class and professor if you had no previous experience with python, there's assignments every week which are time consuming but not very hard, coding challenges were easy, and midterm and final were in pencil and paper but she allowed 1 and 2 cheat sheets so they weren't very hard

She was nice and really understanding if anyone needed things like extensions. Good at explaining concepts and the homework each week was very doable. Her office hours were super short and a lot of people were cheating so I kept on losing points for the same reason each week but never changed it because the grades were released so late.

awesome class. would take again with prof. kaur in a heartbeat. super easy to reach her if u have questions over the homeworks or coding challenges. really wants you to do well and will do anything in her power to help. the course can be a little challenging if its ur first coding class but not too bad. cant recommend her enough.

TAKE AMRITA FOR 303!! She is so caring and lectures are amazing - extremely detailed and breaks problems/concepts down step by step. The class is difficult, yes, but any CS class will be. I came in with 0 coding knowledge and got an A in the class even after bombing the midterm (your final grade can replace the midterm if higher).

Amrita is a kind, knowledgable professor. Class is based on HW (easy but time consuming), coding challenges (completion grade), and tests (hard). VERY generous with extra credit/deadlines (automatic +2 ish points for meeting deadlines). Hard tests but doable if you study. I have 4+ years of coding experience, so the class was relatively easy.

Professor Kaur herself is nice, but the assignments are hard (and get harder, especially in the middle) if you don't have any coding experience. She also accuses students of cheating quite often for similarities to ChatGPT or other students assignments.
