reviews.comment: She is excellent and passionate about her field. She takes her material seriously and expects students to do the same. Probably not an "easy" A, but you get what you deserve. She seems (rightfully) to have little tolerance for students who are consistently unprepared. In person, she is sweet and thoughtful, but in class she is often no-nonsense.

Super sweet prof that is truly passionate about her field of work! As long as you pay attention in lecture and skim the book, it's hard not to make an A. The class itself is super interesting and she'll answer all of your questions! 10/10 recommend taking her if you need a VAPA.

As long as you pay attention in class, and complete the assignments on time, the class is an easy A. Although the exams are mostly free response, only the information from lectures is required to get a good grade. (You don't have to read the book.) Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Astrid was an amazing lecturer. If you attempt to be interested in the class & reflect outside of class it'll help you, otherwise this class'll suck. Readings are helpful before class, extra credit is sweet, and discussions/tests are not hard (History - ID based with short answer ?s). She's rather stern but kind & interesting. Sign in attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a lot of lectures that are very heavy and boring. Don't use her study guides because they are practically worthless. Near the end, she won't respond to your emails which is super annoying. She gave out the review late and won't answer any questions on the review. If you don't have to take this class, don't. If you do, pick someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: First of all, if you aren't interested in Art History or a Fine Arts major don't take this class. Lots of reading that is very boring if it doesn't interest you. Changed her tests so they are more difficult. Reviews aren't really sufficient for the Tests.
It is an easy class

So many extra credit opportunities & before each exam she'd give us a study guide that told us exactly what was going to be on the test. She always asked for feedback on the course work and really listened to any suggestions on how to improve the class. Honestly lectures will be kinda boring if you're not into art, but overall the class is easy.

DO EVERY EXTRA CREDIT. She isn't clear on expectations and will take off points if you don't format the info how she wants. She takes attendance but you can do other work on your laptop. Build a relationship with her cause it'll save your grade. An A is manageable but not super easy. All in all the class wasn't bad but its very dry.

reviews.comment: Class was a layup. The information is not really hard to learn, its just the structure of the course that makes this class somewhat tedious/challenging. Imo, this class felt like a giant participation grade. Tests are really easy and so are assignments. The prof is a little rude tho.

Aroian's class is easy, but he doesn't enhance the experience whatsoever. Talks incredibly slow and lectures are unprofessional and uninspiring. He didn't make the tiniest bit of effort to cut out interruptions during lectures such as his phone ringing. Just take notes at 2x speed and you'll be fine. Most of the non-exam assignments are completion.

This is really a very easy class. Textbook readings are long and annoying but completely unnecessary. Lectures and case studies are majority of test. They can be tediously boring but otherwise the tests for this class could not be easier. There is group work for this asynchronous class which IS very annoying. Overall- very doable & not stressful.

Homeworks were easy and you could finish the class pretty early within the semester. Class is easy, make sure to watch the lectures. Giving him a low rating because he doesn't seem to care for his students literally at his mercy. He curves, but a chunk of it comes from an extra credit assignment that'll add upwards to 1.5 points(who does this bro)

Class is asynchronous and lectures are prerecorded. Professor is nice and answers any questions during office hours and test review sessions. Class is hard because the majority of your grade is exams and none of them are dropped. Quizzes are based completely on the readings and there are a few exercises that require coordinating with other people.

exams are 21% (yes, 21) and are super hard niche information from his lectures. situational problems from exams are super subjective but somehow there's a "right" answer. assigns group work for an asynchronous online class. busywork for this class is easy and it's not technically a hard class, but exams will sneak up on you and tank your grade

Don't understand the bad reviews. Class was straightforward and not difficult at all. Some of the material can be boring but its not terrible. I found this class pretty useful as we learned about what may be encountered when starting our career. Textbook required for assignments, but I didn't read it. I did not stress over this class at all.

reviews.comment: A more aggressive but passive version of Jean-Claude Biver. Ded fish go through the current & you have to be extremely fast to pass this course. Love the lessons and real aspects of the course but that makes it hard even if correct answers may be wrong and replaced ["what if"ways of thinking].

reviews.comment: I think Aroian is an incredible professor. If you are struggling in his class, GO TO OFFICE hours. He really wants his students to suceed. Tests are tough but fair.

It does NOT give you much credit for learning the textbook. The text book is mostly to learn different terms based on their respective properties and the exams do NOT exercise the understanding of the material but more of outside thinking of how each case study  could have avoided their issues. the bad side is your grade depends on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aroian's class is self paced so it's easy to get overwhelmed- he gave a pretty good curve at the end of the semester that made up for the weight and difficulty of the tests. You have to know the case studies really well and if you're in the top quartile of the class you'll probably end up with an A after the curve.

Dr. Aroian is very passionate and knowledgeable about the content in the class. His lectures and case study debriefs that he gives are very interesting and I enjoyed learning about them. He gives you all the resources you need to perform well in this class. All the 1-point reviews are just salty, L+ratio+skill issue.

Pros: Exams aren't that bad, it's possible to cram the night before and get a B. Bad questions do get thrown out. The class is self paced. 

Cons: It is cumbersome to get an A in this class because its set as a 94, there is very little room for error.

Awful class!!! impossible to get an A (at least for me, I tried and read/ studied so much but tests were so hard and never got above a C on any). He also talks sooo slow and is a nice guy but doesn't care about how frustrating the class is even when he gets a million complaints about it. A lot of work to turn in asynchronously. Avoid!

This was the worst class I've ever taken at UT Austin. Professor Aroian is EXTREMELY passive-aggressive, and he does not help or care for the students at all. For example, in his third exam, in which a large majority of the class' test averages dropped around 7 points, he did not curve it, and he only assigned a 0.25% curve to the entire class.

This class was very overwhelming. There was way too much material and case study assignments/quizzes/homework questions due every week. The exams were over the case studies, which were on average 10 pages of reading (5 or 6 per module). This class did NOT need to be as hard as it was. Hes a good person, but did not structure his course well.
this class sucks, it was basically fully online and there were 3 tests that the other material did not prepare you for.

I enjoyed the class! I think he was a good professor but most of the content comes from the readings. He's extremely accessible and he cares about the students! The tests are a little tricky because of how simple the material is, so you may feel like several answers work for a certain question. It's easy to get a good grade. Lots of reading tho

reviews.comment: This was the most tedious and frustrating class I've taken at UT. The curve was only 2 points. Not worth it all!!!!!

reviews.comment: Literally the rudest and most passive-aggressive professor I've ever encountered. Disorganized class despite the 20-page syllabus? Would NOT recommend taking this class with Aroian, take the synchronous version with a different professor if possible/if you want a will to live.

Took it for the business minor. Contextually very simple, I didn't really study for the exams but if I had put more effort in, I would have gotten an A. Aroian is a great guy, the asynchronous nature of the course is just hard to keep up with but it was nice that you could finish the class early if you want. No final

Prof Aroian was honestly not as bad as I thought it was going to be, but this is by no means an easy class. The quizzes and exams are mostly based on specific details from lecture, but the case studies are graded based on whether or not it looks like you put in effort.

This class was eh. I did completely web-based; his recorded lectures are boring. Put him on 2x speed and you'll still understand everything. You have to be super self-motivated to get an A

This is probably the worst Business Minor class I've taken. Quizzes are ridiculously detail focused, and you have to go to office hours to get feedback. Exam is full of random details completely unrelated to the readings. It's probably nearly impossible to get an A in this class (coming from a 4.0 CS major).

DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS!!!!!! He does everything in his power to make it as difficult and as tedious as possible. It is absolutely not worth it. He claims he's aware that we're in a pandemic, but he is inflexible, unhelpful, condescending, and rude. There is way too much busy work, and it is impossible to get an A.

Aroian was always attempting to make jokes in class, but I genuinely enjoyed him. The content is really easy and Aroian teaches it well. The case studies were easy 100's if your read them, and the writing assignments were graded leniently. Tests were sometimes tricky but not awful.
Hes a pretty boring lecturer but a nice man. Tests are a bit harder than youd think but not too bad. If you have to take this class take it but its pretty blah.
Prof. Aroian is one of the greatest professors in existence. Take him.

reviews.comment: Can't believe people are giving Aroian bad reviews; he is seriously the sweetest professor ever. I love the professor he is so nice and he does a great job teaching. However, the exams are so difficult, EXTREMELY difficult. Answers are very similar and a lot of the Qs have many correct answers.

reviews.comment: writing this because in addition to being a well-organized and engaging professor, he has explicitly encouraged his students to prioritize their health/safety/wellbeing over their school work during the pandemic-winter storm-combo. his lightheartedness and good humor notably crosses over into his genuine care and compassion for his students.

One of my favorite professors by far. Aroian is kind, humourous, and shares valuable knowledge throughout the semester. I am going to miss his lectures and personal stories during class. Dr. Aroian is a super considerate person, so TAKE MAN320F IN PERSON !!! The online class is so much harder and I dont recommend. Aroian is one of the best professors I've had at UT. His lectures are really engaging, interesting and meaningful. The textbook could help but he covers all needed material during lecture. This prof is SO RUDE! He ordered less books than there were people in the class then he was ticked off when students came saying they ran out of books. His Ego is over inflated and he can be condescending. This man is stressed out and will stress you out.

Almost no accommodations for COVID crisis (I did not need them, but others may have). Testing software stares at you through your webcam and is generally creepy. Would not recommend.
Hm..

I can tell you that Prof. Aroian is my favorite professor in the business foundation programs thus far. He is very kind and tries his hardest to reach out to students. You have to read the case studies throughly to do well, but theyre interesting. Tests can be very specific but its all doable.

This was probably my least favorite class I've ever taken at UT. The material is super easy and basically common-sense like and yet the quizzes and exams are so unnecessarily detail-oriented. I never read any modules or watched any videos. Just go to quizlet or course hero. On every exam/quiz there's at least 2-3 questions that seem new/aren't on any of the other quizlets. reviews.comment: I personally would avoid taking this class in person. The material is pretty intuitive, but the tests are not easy by any means. I dropped at the end of the semester because I hadn't used my OTE yet. Getting an A is definitely feasible but not worth it imo.

Mihran himself is a great guy. Wise, caring, personable, everything you would want in a professor. However, the class is tough. Only the homeworks (8% of the grade) are easy points. Do NOT assume (as I did) that you can get an A on the test without reading the cases and textbook thoroughly... you will be in for a rude awakening if you do.

Taking MAN rn ONL, it's p easy honestly. Self-paced, w 2 exams and 4 quizzes. He uses ProctorU. I'd suggest to skim through the readings lightly, focus more on the study guide/quizzes at the end of the chapters, and google some good quizlets from past students. Aroian is a nice guy but his lectures are extremely dense. The tests are specific & confusing and ask some lecture-based questions. reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class. Lectures were very enlightening & I learned a lot. - Lectures are boring - Tests are overly specific on nonsense from case studies - 75% of grade based of three exams (not easy) - Lots of studying needed to get a B+ or higher

Aroian is a very insightful professor, and he inspires you to become a better person. The coursework is like BA 324, you have writing assignments and a major presentation. It is important to know that his powerpoints are not accessible. If you want to be successful in this class, write down everything on them verbatim and you will do well in the course. Aroian was helpful and kind throughout the process, and set us up to do well in the online course. I would take him again.

goooood

Hard but nice

This class was low stress and taught in a way that made it a great intro to going to college. The lectures were all genuinely amusing, and the asynchronous format was really accommodating. I loved Ash's class! Ten out of ten - one of the sweetest profs I've had at UT. There were at least 10x during the semester that I laughed out loud at a joke they cracked during lecture. I love Ash!! Such an incredible professor who really cares about their students. No tests, we don't even take notes in class. Just come and listen and engage in the lecture, and you're all good. Homework and projects outside of class aren't too bad either. Definitely take her if you can.

They fell kind of behind so felt like everything was pushed back at last second but outside of that the professor is nice but this class was just a class I decided to take outside of my major so any grade I may have gotten because of that is on me.

The sweetest professor ever, take this class!!! Her class is so laid back and chill. Assignments are simple and easy, projects are also very straightforward. This class is a relief and I actually learned a lot.

As an engineering major, this was a nice class. laid back, discussion based. Just do your part in group projects and keep up with assignments. Dr. Atkinson (who prefers Lucy) is witty and engaging with her lectures. Breath of fresh air.
0 extra credit. Will give an A- if 0.1 decimals off an A

Dr. Atkinson creates a welcoming atmosphere for discussion and debate within the class. Entertaining class. Coursework is relatively light too.

Amazing and kind!! Only thing is that tests are pretty hard- the way to do well on them/get an A in the class is to take WORD FOR WORD notes on her lectures and memorize those notes- questions can be pretty specific. also read the textbook, but most important is the lectures

Lucy is such a wonderful professor! She's very caring and makes sure that you are learning in her class. She gives good feedback on group projects and is always accomodating if you have problems. Would definitely recommend. One of the best professors I had in Moody.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pretty straightforward class! Just watch the lectures, read the textbook, and take good notes. The textbooks are well written and interesting, so it's not too bad! I'd recommend this class for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a fairly easy class. She provides all the video lectures for each chapter (except ch. 10, so you will need to read that on your own, read it! Exam #3 is mostly textbook content from that ch.) shes a solid choice! Put in the work and youll surely get a good grade. 1 assignment is dropped and the same with 1 test.

This class is self-paced, so you can watch lecture video's whenever you want. Only a few easily graded assignments. 3 online tests (+ 1 optional) over lectures and she gives a lecture guide. Tests are 50 (mostly easy) MC questions so take notes. Splitting lectures with friends for taking notes saves so much time! Do these things & you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was a pretty easy A. I didn't read the book at all and just followed lectures and I got a high A on tests. There are 3 assignments, but one is optional if you decide you like the other grades you got. TA's are pretty tough on grading, but if you explain well enough it'll be an A. Also 4 tests and one is optional just like the assignments
Amazing professor!! She's so nice and the class is so interesting. :) Read the textbooks and keep up with the modules.

Her lectures are interesting and she covers test material well. Group projects online bi-monthly. Really clear grading criteria. TAs might grade assignments pretty harsh but tests are mostly what she covers & sometimes a few questions from the book. very good teacher overall.

Take the class! Changed the way I view advertising and history. She is so engaging and creates a fun environment in class. Her exams are all from lectures and are very straight forward. There are three in class assignment and you drop one. Easy A.
Awesome prof!

Dr. Atkinson is an awesome professor. Lecture material is clear, interesting and engaging. She teaches with enthusiasm and keeps you interested. Workload is not heavy at all, as long as you attend class and take notes, the tests are pretty easy & straight-forward. And she makes sure students know what to study for the test. Would highly recommend!

Random attendance checks, but lectures are fun to attend anyway. Lots of pertinent material and examples. Gives lecture guides, which are essential for notes and exams. The "in class assignments" are basically essay tests. Write EVERYTHING you know to get full credit. Some q's on reading on the tests. Would recommend!
Only thing I disliked about the class was the enormous 1" = 1' model we had to make, which cost like $100 (divided by 5 people). Other than that, the class was chill and easy with cool speakers.

Professor Novoselac is an outstanding introduction to architectural engineering. He is extremely knowledgeable, friendly, understanding, and very approachable. The guest lecture panels throughout the course were especially useful. One time, when our projects were accidentally thrown away by a janitor, he even bought the entire class Ferrero Rocher!

This is a great guy. Super chill and easiest class I've taken. Tests are all open book/open note, project 1 was a little tedious but everything else was super easy. Even though this class was really chill, I think I got a lot out of the guest speakers. Take advantage of the opportunity to learn in this class!!

Professor Novoselac is a very nice person, and he tried to help all of us navigate the beginnings of ARE. The guest lecturers were interesting. Sometimes the material was disorganized. The group project took a long time to complete, so think ahead for that. Very nice beginning to Architectural Engineering for me!

Lectures included guest speakers who has slides we would take notes on. Notes would be turned in at the end of the year (I love that he made us take notes because I could not tell you one thing a presenter said from the top of my head but it was useful ArchE stuff). Group project was somewhat hard, but office hours helped and buy materials aheaddd.

Professor Novoselac wants all of his students to succeed, participate and he will appreciate you; he brings in great guest speakers & makes class interesting; textbook is required; exams open note open book--not challenging. Have to make a model house in group project--budget time, especially if double-major. 1 credit hour and overall fun class.

This is just an intro class that meets once a week, nothing special. Mostly guest lecturers and one big group project which was given little instruction. Professor is nice but sometimes hard to understand but again it is just an intro class that doesn't require much work for the most part.
He only had a few lectures, most of them were guest speakers that talked about their experiences and projects. Hard tests, but open note. Projects with groups, which were fun.

This class was a great introduction to ArchE. The assignments consisted of a group project, two open note exams, lecture notes collected at the end of the year, and a short solo project. The group project was the hardest out of the assignment, but the TA was extremely helpful . My group was able to get most of the project done during office hours.

Don't listen to the other reviews! 
-2 exams, both m/c online in class. 
-2 group projects. Great to help meet friends in ARE 
-Notes from every class period due at the end of the semester.

Such a great way to get into the ARE major. Made such great friends that I collaborate with about classes and homework to this day. 
10/10 professor so sweet!

Didn't see much of him over the course of the semester. Assignments and tests were freckled in grammatical mistakes. Projects were hard to understand and seemed to imply needing a certain level of comfort with some concepts, like ventilation, which first-year students (at least me) have almost no experience with. Quite hands off, yet easy A.
Pretty difficult to understand in lecture, very few assignments. Atila makes a great effort to help his students and is always available. Make an effort on open note exams and you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very poor communicator, so many grammatical and spelling errors-even on the tests. Projects werent hard and tests were open book open notes.

Overall this was a really great class. Prof posts all of his slides with the concepts very clearly described. Wasn't the best lecturer imo but going to lecture isn't necessary to gain a lot from the class. Homeworks and final project took a lot of time, but overall were worth it.

Professor Wang is a true legend and perhaps the smartest person I've ever encountered. 

Unlike many professors who just read textbooks, he teaches effortlessly from his vast knowledge. He's engaging, incredibly kind, and adaptable, always happy to take questions and meet student needs. 

Such a pity UT cannot keep him teaching longer!

Besides the fact that he is one of the best researchers in his field, Prof. Wang is also a great teacher! He has very well-organized lectures and is a grandmaster describing the intuition of the material.
Lectures are fun. The class is not all that difficult, but Prof. Wang does go in depth in lectures and is very willing to dive deep into specific things the class asks.

Neuroepigenetics- This is a hard class but if you do the homework and the study guides (which are basically the tests), an A is very achievable. He is very knowledgeable but a little hard to understand, will clarify when asked. We had 2 group poster projects that are worth as much as the test, and are easy to get an A for if you follow the rubric.

CONS:
The epigenetics class was: VERY DISORGANIZED, had no clear rubric/expectations, and the grades were returned WEEKS later. It is PROJECT HEAVY ( 4 presentations and a Wikipedia article). 
PROS:
He grades presentations/ article relative to others/yourself/ and level of effort. The practice exams ARE the exams (still hard though). An A is doable

Professor Atkinson is super nice and knows a lot of stuff. He really helped me learn how to interpret data and I really enjoyed learning from him. Class/schedule is a bit disorganized and grades get posted a bit late - but not a hard class to do well in.

I wouldn't recommend this professor as you must read a lot of the material from the book, lecture slides, and homework questions. The book is definitely required. Tests are hard. He is a very confusing lecturer. The short response questions on tests can be difficult and demand a lot of drawing. However, homework is easy participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but gives boring, monotonous lectures that are difficult to sit through. The class is EXTREMELY unorganized, the expectations are not clear, lectures are all over the place. Lectures feel like an information dump and were difficult to understand. You're basically left to your own devices to prepare for exams. Avoid this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but his lectures are painfully boring. His tests are difficult, and he writes them aiming for a 70-72 average. He does not curve or use plus/ minus grading. The class was disorganized and the expectations were unclear. You pretty much learn from your book and TA. I consider myself a strong bio student, but struggled in this class.

Dr. Atkinson is a really nice guy. Grades are based mostly on tests so you have to do well on them. If you read, go to lecture (doing work for other classes during doesn't count) and go to discussion this class isn't that bad. Doing the homework and asking questions helps a lot. Wouldn't hesitate to take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are both convoluted and horribly dull. They're nearly pointless, and your time is better spent studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hard class. If you can read for yourself and understand the material, you can get an A. The tests are difficult. He doesn't add anything to his lectures, so it is almost pointless to go; it'd be better to just spend that time reading the book. Half of the test question are from old homeworks/old tests and the other half are new.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take Atkinson. His lectures are so convoluted that you can easily get confused even if you already understand the material from the textbook. You have to decipher what his tests are asking and you probably won't pass unless you memorize the whole book or have his old exams. Thankfully I had a wonderful TA so that's the only reason I passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Atkinson is great and her lectures are compelling. if you are interested in history or advertising. I found the exams and writing assignments to be a little challenging but if you watch the lectures and skim the readings you'll be fine. An A is accessible, but this class is not an "easy" elective. Great experience though, very interesting.

This is one of my favorite classes I have ever taken. Her online lectures were so interesting and engaging. She seems very nice and has a great sense of humor. I am an ADV major so maybe I am biased because I didn't find the class boring, as some of the other reviews suggested, at all. I honestly wish I could take the course again.

She was a terrible professor. I regret taking this class. Even though I had been warned about her negative attitude and ability to put students to sleep, I took this class to raise my GPA. Please spare yourself and dont make the same decision I did.

I took this class as an elective, having no background in advertising at all. I spent a lot of time on this class, however it was worth it because just reading will make it an easy A. Atkinsons lectures are key to passing her assignments, since most of the time shell bring up ads that well write about later.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was okay. It definitely was not hard by any means but i will say there is a lot of work you need to do. Each module takes an hour to two hours to complete so it definitely sucked doing those but most of the stuff is things you will see on the exam. I read the textbook sometimes but mostly never and still got an A.

TAKE THIS CLASS! She is a great professor and really makes the content fun to learn. This class really made me fall in love with Advertising. Easy A if you pay attention to the online lectures and really absorb the material. I looked forward to watching her lectures. Highly recommend!

She is a good lecturer, but after a while it gets boring. This class was not easy. Some questions on the tests were extremely specific having to do with specific percentages and data. I regret taking this class because I thought it would be a gpa booster, but it was not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm not a business major, was thrown into this class (since another was cancelled 2 days before classes started) but could not be happier. She really kept this class interesting and fun, and gave plenty of opportunities to succeed. Read the book, take good notes, and you'll get an A+, and you'll actually enjoy yourself. Favorite professor so far!
I sincerely love this prof!!!!!

Dr. Lucy is the BEST! She makes the lectures interesting and provides plenty of in-class extra credit. You do have to read the books for the tests, but luckily they're pretty interesting. She really enjoys discussions too, sometimes we would get so busy discussing in class that we would end up having to cut information off of the tests!

Prof Atkinson is AMAZING. Her lectures are very engaging and this was my favorite class. We had 4 50-question MC tests (1 dropped) including the final, 3 in-class assignment, and participation grades. You really have to know the material for the in-class assignments to get an A. She's a very fair grader, doesn't try to trick you, but must EARN an A

She honestly writes her own reviews. The class should defiantly not be a 5.0 in any category. This class is really really boring. She is also very annoying and very repetitive during the lecture. One of the worst professors on this campus. Not worth my tuition. By the way I'm an ADV major.

She was funny and made lectures interesting and entertaining! Tests were all multiple choice and pretty much all based off her lectures - you don't really have to read the textbooks. She doesn't round up, but there are extra credit opportunities.

I loved this class and i loved her as a professor. She makes the class fun and easy to understand. Also the tests were easy as long as you read your notes and sometimes textbook. Attendance not mandatory but the bonus questions were based on class lectures. it was an easy A.
She's enthusiastic!
Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand. She is engaging and gives you bonus questions that are super easy if you came to class!
Pretty easy class. Grade based on exams and in-class assignments (which are basically tests). Lectures are definitely worthwhile.
She's so funny and easy-going!
This man is the worst. Avoid at all costs. He does not know how to teach besides reading from a PowerPoint and is not helpful when asked questions.

You can definitely get used to his accent, but not his teaching style. Just reads directly off slides that could be posted later and achieve same effect. Lots of homework, but manageable since there's an answer key.

Once you get past his accent he's actually pretty funny, but it took me a while to start understanding him and honestly I still don't sometimes. Classes are him reading off of slides with handouts that are fill in the blank. 2 exams, some cases, and homework from the textbook and the course packet. I don't find the textbook useful.

Prof Atiase may not be my favorite professor ever, but he definitely is not as bad as the other reviews here make him out to be. There is a lot of written homework due before each class, but it is completion and he just wants you to attempt it before actually seeing the solutions in class. Tests are very similar to the review problems which is nice

Homework structure supports memorization, not learning. Lectures are worthless fill-in-the-blank notes that he reads from. He either assigns busy work or problems that he has not prepared you to complete. Hard to understand due to accent. Only reason I did okay was bc his test was near identical to the review. Lots of wasted time in class. ACC 312H

Don't do it! Claims that he doesn't give us busy work, but that is all he gives us. Teaches too fast, and has the audacity to call exams "parties". He is a very smart guy, as he's worked at some very high up companies in the world, but teaching just isn't his thing. Avoid him at all costs please, unless you are feeling like a risk-taker.

Prof. Atiase is by far my least favorite professor I have ever taken. His sarcastic attempts at humor seem to demean students more often than encourage or amuse them. You come to class to copy down verbal notes which could be posted online instead. Homework is explained, in a confusing, hard to understand manner, leaving you to learn on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class consists of you doing a ton of reading and written homework/handouts before class (at least 2 hrs for each "lecture"), coming to class to copy notes verbatim that he won't post online, and then getting called on to answer the questions you did before class without a good explanation. You have to teach yourself--just avoid altogether
Her class was very difficult but she did a great job of making difficult material more easy to understand.
challenging, but she is fair
The class itself is pretty tough and not just because of the subject matter. It's how she grades. I really wish I took this class with a different professor! Avoid, if you can.
A very good professor, helpful, good explanations.
Sometimes hard to understand and hard to follow in lectures. Also, very uninteresting to listen to because of the way she teaches
No Comments

You can tell he really cares about what he teaches, he's passionate and that makes lectures interesting. There is a lot of reading needed for the class and the lab but it's very manageable if you're good at writing. The workload is light! I very much recommend the class, you don't need to go to the lectures as long as you watch them online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Papalexandrou was a great and funny lecturer. The papers and exams are super super easy, just pay attention during your mandatory breakout/discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Optional lectures, the bulk of your grade is the 3 tests and free points you get for going to discussion and writing the papers (also graded on completion). He also records his lectures so you don't need to show up to class, but on the tests, some of the questions will ask "What did Prof. say in class?" so watch those recorded lectures.

My biggest tip for this course is to take detailed notes on his lectures and focus on studying the topics covered in discussion. There are weekly 500 word papers and the tests are each 20% of your grade, so I would try your best on those. There are definitely easier VAPAs out there, but if you get this one don't be too worried.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Papalexandrou's class is as cool as his name. He is passionate about his subject and fun to listen to, though his accent occasionally makes him difficult to understand. Lectures are recorded and aren't mandatory to attend but are interesting, attendance at discussion sections is graded. So much assigned reading, only the lab readings are tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The prof is great but the older reviews exaggerate how easy the class is- you need to work for an A. Lectures are recorded & there are mandatory labs w/ weekly response papers (completion grade). TAs grade the first exam harshly, and you need to rewatch the lectures and pay attention to catch the details they want you to mention on exams

Definitely not as easy as the previous reviews have claimed, but the class was doable. T/F and MCQs felt like random trivia questions at times, but the writing portions were easy as long as you keep up with lectures and discussion sessions. Grading varies by TA, mine graded harshly initially but became more lenient as the semester progressed.

If someone says this class is easy, don't believe them. The professor's fast pace and thick accent make lectures hard to follow, but they're online with captions. Grading varies by TA; mine was strict, and makeup assignments didn't help. Skip reviews and study lab readings for exams. True/false and multiple-choice are overly detailed. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard to comprehend the lecture due to his distinct european accent, but if looking for professor passionate to educate students and share his understanding to students, he is the one. TAs' grade your exam, but if questions rendered, go to his office hours. He will love to hear your voice. Not an easy A, but if you can yap well, this is an ease.
Went to lecture once. The tests are completely covered by whats talked about during the review sessions. Go to those and you'll get an A guaranteed.

Overall pretty easy class. Lectures not required so I would only watch them online. Fun guy with a good sense of humor. Tests are in person timed short essays, not too difficult if you reviewed somewhat decently. I loved going to Blanton for lab. Loved the class because it wasn't too much workload so I actually really did enjoy learning in it!

Prof Papalexandrou is a wonderful teacher. He's so warm, and reply the email very fast. His exam is not really hard, and my TA (Hana) is also wonderful. There are 3 exams in total, and he does have one opportunity to do the make up exam. However, I highly recommend trying to get the in class exam high cuz make up exam grade HARDER!

Papalexandrou is extremely passionate and cares about his students. Your grade comes mostly from his essay-style exams which can be harder if you do not attend lectures. Mandatory graded discussion section attendance. The museum trips are very fun though! Take for easy VAPA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Papalexandrou is extremely nice and caring. He is extremely knowledgable in his field as he seems fascinated with what he teaches. Overall fantastic professor. Highly recommend.

Great class, made me want to pursue an AH minor. Papalexandrou and his TAs are knowledgeable and kind, and although the class is A LOT of reading, it's worth it. Best advice I can give is to do your best on the practice mid-term bc the TAs give really good feedback on how to improve. Go to his office hours!! I really enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't my favorite, and I didn't attend all the lectures. However, I thought the labs were amazing mainly because of my TA - Lauren. She was very kind, answered all of our questions, and made sure that the reviews for the exams were super specific so that we didn't have to study much outside of class. Pretty easy class overall.

While lectures aren't necessary, I went to every one bc of how engaging Prof. Papalexandrou was. I had previously dabbled in art history, and his lectures were what made me re-interested in the subject again. Weekly homework and tests are easy, and my TA was amazing during our labs. I would definitely recommend any looking for a VAPA to this class.

This class was amazing. Nassos made lectures engaging and was passionate about us learning. My TA Jarred was the best TA I have had since being here at UT as well. For some labs we would even go to the Blanton. Exams are essays and 'hw is a 300 word short response. Great class overall.

Amazing professor! His lectures were absolutely incredible and my TA was also great. The class was very interesting for someone who had no knowledge about Art History at all. Lectures not mandatory but I liked going anyways. The classes definitely help for the exams, but I wouldn't say completely necessary. If you need a VAPA, take him!!
Had him for ARH302 -- good class if you just watch the lectures + make sure you test yourself using PPTs of images IF in ARH302.

I never went to class (because it was not worth my time); however, the labs are required, so I would show up for those. The entire class is based on 3 essays, attendance to lab, and weekly lab responses. In the responses and essays, you must use evidence from lectures and readings to do good. My TA (Eva) was amazing; she was also an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures not required to do well as the required labs will be able to sum everything up and prepare you for the essay exams. 500-word papers due every week based on readings, but are generally completed. The essay exams are taken asynchronously and start at 9 am and must be turned in before 5 pm. Lectures are recorded so utilize that during exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is extremely Essay heavy. There is 1 essay a week, though it is usually a completion grade. The exams are all essays with no final. I did not show up to any lectures but managed to get an A. TA sessions are required. I found this class to be slightly boring, but I only did this class for credit. If you enjoy Art History, you'll enjoy it.

He is funny, likable, and well-spoken! There were weekly writing assignments and some take-home essays, but my TA graded nicely. Lectures were fun and useful, and were recorded for easy access later. However, your grade in the class really depends on your TA.
Very interesting class and you can see how much Dr Papalexandrou loves the material and likes to teach it. No mandatory attendance but you do have a mandatory discussion every week.

no final, no tests, no studying or lecture attendance required since the only graded assignments are short weekly responses, and a few short "essays" as exam grades. papalexandrou is a great professor who is very knowledgable about what he is teaching and cares about his students. would highly recommend as an easy vapa or to fulfill art core reqs.

Papalexandrou is a very caring professor. I missed class once, and he went over the class with me in a scheduled meeting. He works very hard, is knowledgable, and I would definitely take more of his classes.

The exam content stems directly from class lectures and discussions so make sure to show up to those and pay attention and you will get an A+. Prof PapaL is very funny and kind, and he is very knowledgeable about the course information. You can tell he has a passion for art history which makes the class more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Papalexandrou is a great lecturer, and I was able to stay engaged with what was being said. But there are a lot of readings and all of your work/test grades go through your TA! So it all depends on them! Make sure you talk to them or go to office hours, because the exams arent graded easy. I would take this prof again if it wasnt a survey class :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a cute prof. Kind of funny, referred to Augustus of Prima Porta as incredibly sexy. Was absent one day, and came to office hours once and he spent the entire time going over the presentation. Caring prof. Greek accent takes a while to get used to. ATTEND LECTURES!!! Grading is P/F for lab questions and from tests. No final either.

I took Dr. Papalexandrou's class for an art historical discussion seminar and found it to be one of the most enriching educational experiences I've had at UT. Beginning of the semester was rough because he doesn't let you sit back- he is all about engagement and open discussions. He does his best to meet you where you are at though! Just be honest.

Nassos is a great prof who is very engaging. There are discussion groups where attendance is mandatory, but lab grades based on completion. There are 3 tests which are two essay questions each, so be ready to know more than just facts. Content is like AP art history, so if you have taken that, it is helpful! He wants to get to know you!!
I really like Prof. Papalexandrou, I wish the class was graded on more assignments but overall hes a valuable teacher. A lot of architecture focus, though.

Took this class for my VAPA credit, and absolutely regretted it. Tests are always only two questions, so if you don't catch every little thing he says in lecture, you'll probably fail. There are easier VAPAs to take, do not take this class.

I took this class just for my VAPA credit (I'm not into art AT ALL). But it was easy workload wise (weekly response papers and 3 exams; no final). Grade is dependent on your TA though. I got lucky with mine. Discussion sections are mandatory, but lecture is not. However, if you don't go to lecture idk how you would pass. He's such a sweet prof tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Papalexandrou only taught 1/3 of ARH302, but I really enjoyed his lectures. He's passionate about the subject and I found him totally understandable. Do the readings, and the lectures will supplement it well. Tests are paper-based but go to his office hours and he'll give helpful info! He learned my name in a huge class, which I appreciated!

Very structured and clear in his lectures. His accent may get in the way but he is helpful during office hours. If you pay attention in class he will prepare you for the exam. He also uses various teaching techniques like documentaries and engagement in class.

Had this professor for "MYTH/IMAGE GREEK/ROMN MEDITER." He doesn't take attendance, but your participation in class discussions is 40% of your final grade. 3 papers (1500-2000 words), a presentation requirement for Art History majors only, 3 tests: essay based (2 questions, pick 1). Super easy if you take notes and listen. Homework is just reading.

His lectures cover everything you need to know for tests, and they really make you appreciate art. The TA discussion sessions didn't make sense at times because they seemed separate from lectures and counted attendance like high school (tardies and all). I recommend not skipping lectures because that's exactly how I messed up my grade.

His Greek accent actually kept me from zoning out. You have to go to class, but the exams are not difficult at all if you pay attention. I was in a huge class and he still learned many of our names and greeted us by them. He is funny, so knowledgeable, and so nice. My favorite professor at UT so far and Art History is nowhere near my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Nassos is the best. He is kind and forms relationships with all his students. He hates tests so he does more papers and participation is a huge deal which is so easy with him. Everyone loves and respects him and he doesn't grade hard either!! 11/10
Best professor I've ever had. Period. He is so kind, exciting to listen to, and he genuinely cares about every one of his students. Do not miss the opportunity to take a course taught by Nassos.

Tests and weekly one-page essays were a breeze and the readings are barely necessary. Museum visits were AMAZING! Hard to pay attention if you aren't interested, and he does have a thick accent, but it's so easy that you could focus half the time and still get an A. Weird in a funny, endearing way. Refers to all anonymous figures as "dudes".

Papa was the best. Its definitely an easy class grade-wise, but I learned so much! If you're interested in art history this is a great place to start. I really enjoyed his lectures and didn't have much trouble with his accent. Be ready for field trips to the Blanton with your excited TA! Also, theres a one page participation grade essay each week.

Lecture participation and attendance was not mandatory but the discussions were. My TA didnt put grades in so I didnt know my grade until grade reports, but that depends on your TA. Dr. P is super nice & cool but his lectures are dry. Readings were long so I didnt read and was fine if I paid attention in discussion and kinda participated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are not mandatory, but they may help you discern the topics for the tests. The tests are mostly compare/contrast essays. Discussion sessions are mandatory. Weekly papers due. Extra credit assignments to make up for absence to discussion. Graded by TA's. One of the best VAPA's for sure. Some people may prefer ARH 303
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is probably one of the best VAPAs to take especially if you are not super interested in art in general. Either come to lecture or just read the textbook because both is overkill unless you are interested in the subject. Papalexandrou is a great lecturer and knows a lot on the subjects he teaches. Make sure to go to discussions though!

I wasn't interested in art history, but he is really passionate about the subject but has a hard greek accent. I slept in and missed an exam (3 exams, each %15 percent of final grade) I emailed him & was able to make it up. I never went to class &just read the textbook. Make sure to go to discussion classPARTICIPATION's a huge portion of your grade

To be clear, I'm not interested at all in Art History, which is why I didn't enjoy the class content, but the course is super easy (pay attention during the lectures and you'll easily ace all three tests). Also, you only need the textbook to reference for the mid-term paper, so just borrow it from a friend for that one week.

A very sweet and kind man, but disappointingly boring lectures. It's an easy VAPA, an unnecessary amount of writing, but he doesn't grade them, the TAs do, so they're graded pretty easily. I didn't buy the book tbh but as long as you go to lecture and know a basic level of world history, the concepts are easy to grasp.

Cool professor, and he tries to liven up lectures by inserting his own jokes but to be honest, his lectures are dead boring if you're not into art history. If you read the textbook you don't even need to go to most lectures to be honest.

Nassos is one of the best people I've ever met. Extremely passionate, his lectures and very heavy Greek accent are fun to listen to! Make sure to get close with your TA, and email them or Professor Papalexandrou if you are having troubles. I am not done with the class yet but am thoroughly enjoying it. Express your passion for the subject! It helps

Took two semesters of his art history classes. Easy grading; wrote a terrible-quality paper and still got a B on it. Incredibly kind and genuinely wants to get to know his students. Very thick accent that is both endearing and a bit hard to understand. He is super passionate about the subject, which helps if you are not interested in art.

Papalexandrou is very knowledgeable. Yet, he has a horrific accent it is VERY difficult to follow along with what he is saying. Also, your grading mostly comes from your specific TA. My TA was very relaxed and when it came time for the term paper he gave me the wrong instructions and when the professor actually graded it he gave me a low grade.

Professor Papalexandrou's lectures are incredibly dull but if you simply go to the review discussion or pay the least bit of attention in class, you're guaranteed to pass the tests.  The TAs are really helpful and want you to do well but are sometimes picky.  Overall, it was an easy course for a VAPA credit.

I'm taking his Ancient Near Eastern ArtArchaeology course and it is horrible. He is a nice professor, his accent can be a bit tough sometimes, but overall a nice person. However, the class is poorly taught with no cultural background given. All we do is talk about the "visual narratives" of things, which is just conjecture. I am learning nothing.

I took him for UGS - The Parthenon. It was very easy as long as you put effort into it. I got an A from paying attention in class and doing well on the assignments. We got to go to the HRC, Blanton, and Stark Center instead of lecture some days!
His lectures are useless. Tests can be tricky, but as long as you read the book cover to cover, you'll be fine.

His lectures I found boring and hard to listen to. He has the thickest greek accent which gets annoying. His powerpoints are just pictures, so its difficult to take notes. I found it easier to just go to the TA sessions, cram using the textbook, because I got no help in attending the lectures.

A really fun teacher even when the subject matter gets dreary from caves to medieval cathedrals. Get to know your TA well because they will be grading the papers and your tests, also go to class, not only is it helpful but the teacher (and his Greek accent) makes it all the more fun!
No Comments
The best faculty I've ever met.

He's definitely knowledgeable and speaks with coherence and confidence, but I found that I had to do a lot of learning after lectures to comprehend the concepts. Granted, that could be an issue on my part. Workload was manageable, but there would be 0 feedback left on assignments, which was odd. Advice: watch Coding With John and Bro Code!!

Definitely take Nando over him
-Next to no review material for exams, only one previous exam. Actual exam was way harder, ~70 avg no curve
-Tests and projects are much harder than other profs
-No in class test review or exam prep guidance
-Useless lectures, don't help with projects, just end up self studying 
Overall way harder than it should be

While Shi's lectures can sometimes be dry, he always tries to encourage class participation. He is a very talented developer and there is a lot to learn from him. The recitations and TA's were very useful for keeping up in the course. No final, but make sure to leave plenty of time for the final project.
Enjoyed his teaching style. Went through many examples when teaching new concepts.

This Prof has useless lectures and is not understanding at all. He doesn't have practice exams and doesn't send out announcements that are crucial to passing assignments/the class.The lack of coordination among the professor and their TAs has negative consequences on students' grades. Take a different professor if you can.

Useless lectures, self-taught course/no guidance, unclear project requirements, no announcements on canvas, expected to check Piazza to do well/pass, harder projects than other profs, unreasonable expectations, not understanding/flexible, no Test reviews, unorganized exams, doesn't use IDE, unlear answers to questions, taught like a grad course.

She is such an amazing teacher and lecturer. She breaks down every concept completely from scratch so that everything is very digestible and easy to understand, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students understanding the material by the quality of her explanations and slides.

She is SOOO nice. Got super lucky with registering for her class for Fall 2024. Individual exams are 45% with the rest of the grade being group exams, group work, and instapoll. IMO the groups were big enough so that at least a few ppl could be on top of things, and even though the exams were hard, they weren't weighed heavily + small curves!
Honestly the best professor I had at UT—go to office hours and study using HER lecture slides and iClickers and you will come out fine.

Dr. Austin was awesome. She encouraged us to truly understand physiology by forming connections rather than simply memorizing facts. Most of our grade was derived from group assignments (weekly homework, iClicker, group exams). As much as I dreaded physiology entering the class, I left with a love of the subject and a deeper understanding as well.
Great professor, simplifies physio as much as she can. Class is doable. Many EC opportunities. Go to office hours for HWs. Austin clearly wants the best for students.

Dr. Austin is THE BEST. Study for exams by using HER lecture and exam review slides, explaining the concepts to yourself, as well as doing the practice problems for math-related topics/questions. She has learning objectives from another prof which you can do for extra practice but you should mostly focus on her slides and you'll be fine.

I LOVED Dr. Austin. Grade is based on group assignments every week, group exams, individual exams, iClicker participation and peer evaluation. Physiology is hard enough but she does a great job to give enough extra credit as a buffer. Don't slack off on group work from the get go. If you have the chance to take her, don't hesitate to do so!

goated professor. only downside is having to be put into random groups and doing all of you're assignments together so it sucks if you have a bad group. nevertheless, Dr.Austin is awesome and wants you to succeed.

Really enjoyed this class. The pre-lectures were helpful. Attendance is mandatory, because of the iClicker questions, but they help keep you paying attention. Homework assignments are done in groups. Exams with your group too if you want. Reading the textbook helps. Go to Dr. Austin's office hours!! She helps break down concepts

Dr. Austin is amazing! All of the homework, iClicker and exams are group work, which forces you to actually pay attention and help out your group. The material is a bit difficult if you are not interested, but her lectures are great and interactive. Attendance is mandatory because of iClicker questions given during lecture. Amazing overall!

Dr Austin is so kind and a great lecturer. She's so smart and passionate about physiology and teaching. She makes it attainable to know the material and understand it. The way she did group homework assignments was helpful and group exams were extremely helpful as well. She's so accessible outside of class as well as her TA's and they're so helpful

I loved Austin as a professor and she made the class more intriguing and forced you to be involved. Charismatic and light personality and brough positive vibes into every lecture. Take her for any class that you can because if you mess up, she is very generous and tells you exactly where you went wrong. Avg/easy HW and Exam difficulty, long HW's.

Dr. Austin is really nice and creates an environment where you can focus on learning without worrying about your grade. Her guidance is great, and she is a must take professor to enjoy your intro to proofs class. Overall 100% recommend taking her.

A very nice professor. The homeworks are insanely difficult, but she has tons of documents available to help with the homework. The tests are exactly like the test reviews and she is very helpful in getting people prepared for the tests. She doesn't explain some of the in depth concepts the best, but you at least understand how to do the problems.

One of the few amazing teachers at the ut math department, She breaks down complex proof topics into easy to understand lectures and practice problems. Tests were not too bad if you studied for them, and did the review problems. A lot of extra credit was given if you participated in class problems and presentation problems, definitely a must take.
Let us work with others in the class during the final minutes of the test. Often wouldn't explain concepts fully or in depth.

This review is for M 175T, Being You in Mathematics. It is indeed rather boring. However, I cannot deny that it is applicable to math majors, even pure math majors. Take this class to get your ethics flag done and perhaps learn a bit more about the major in the process.

This class is an introduction to the upper-level proof classes, and it has a reputation for being difficult since it is so different than all previous math courses. However, she is very good at teaching, is not too harsh on grading, and gives more than enough opportunities for success given you are willing to try.
She is one of the best (math) Professor in UT. Discrete math is typically easy, but she made it much easier. Exam reviews are very useful. Study homework, exam review and in-class examples!

Dr. Austin is probably the best math professor I've had at UT. Exams are pretty easy as long as you study. Showing up to class is important. Attendance isn't required, but you get engagement points for answering questions and she notices when you're not there. Dr. Austin is an amazing professor and a great person to have a connection with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BEST MATH TEACHER/PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!! Dr. Austin is amazing! I have sucked at math since I can remember and this is truly the first time I have understood it to the full extent. Her lectures are amazing, tests are easy with a independent portion and a collaborative portion, with maximum two-three assignments each week! Take this math!!!

I took M175T, Being You in Mathematics (there was no option for this). This class is crucial to any STEM major (mainly math majors) and teaches fundamental ethics and different job perspectives mathematicians can pursue with their degrees. Dr. Austin was very encouraging, and the course has really impacted my future.

If you need math credit, and are trying to find a good professor...Dr.Austin is the one!!!!! Please trust me on this one you guys!!! Her lectures are very easy and very understandable. Shes such a funny person as well, and she is very caring!!!! Best professor I have ever had!!!

Tests were pretty easy. None of the concepts were difficult, she mostly focused on teaching how to write proofs and basic logical reasoning. Only complaint is that towards the end she started letting students do the examples but the class then became just jotting stuff down and I wasn't sure if I was learning how to do the proofs correctly.

Dr. Austin made math easy!! pay attention in lecture & you'll get an easy A. At first it was hard to think about math from a logic perspective, but it gets so much easier - don't drop the course after the first lecture! Dr. Austin was quick to answer questions & she cares about her students. Exam questions came directly from content in review pptx.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE! Dr. Austin.  She made a seemingly boring class very relateable and applied real-life concepts.  I would say the only thing is that she does call on people in class, whether you raise your hand or not, but I would not let that be the reason you don't take her.  She's extremely sweet, and her exams were very fair and manageable.  Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT LISTEN!!! Guys this class lowk kicked my butt it was kinda difficult, the homework was graded harshly and I found myself LOST in like all the lectures. BUT there are lots of extra credit opportunities! I'm trying to keep my A rn. Apart from that, exams are kinda easy, and if you put in the work- you can pass

Dr. Austin is great and this class was literally the easiest class I have ever taken. Even if you think you're awful at math, you can definitely take this class. She walks you through everything and the exams are super easy.

this review is for m325, Dr. Austin is easily the best professor to take for proof writing. I highly enjoyed the content in this class, and there's tons of opportunities for extra credit. I found her class super engaging and inspiring, she truly helps you find your mathematical voice :-) also, easiest writing flag.

I would take every single class with Professor Austin. She is the most caring and kind professor I'll probably ever have. Tons of extra credit, you can literally ask her how to solve the homework, engaging lecturers, and straightforward tests. 1000/10 math class, take it if you can.

Dr. Austin is easily one of the best professors I have had at UT. I have taken two classes with her, and both were phenomenal. Her lectures are easy to follow (and to review later on). Her grading criteria is clear, and she has lots of opportunities to improve your grade.

PLEASE take this course if you need math credit. Collaborative exams, homework is gone over in class, fun and easy projects! Dr. Austin is so sweet and wants to make sure everyone does well plus she has lots of office hours! TONS of opportunities for extra credit and making up missed group projects during class!
Professor Austin is by far the best math teacher I have had. She is very clear about the material she teaches, and she makes lectures interesting, fun, and inspiring. I would take this class again!
This review is actually for M 329F. Great professor. Tests were split into take-home and in-person components. Medium amount of homework. Lots of chances for extra credit.

This was an amazing introduction class. Tests are collaborative, meaning the whole class can work on it together, and you can use any material provided through the course. Tests are take home for a 3 day period. Usually there are homework due every Friday, but she doesn't mind if you miss a deadline-- so long as you do turn it in. HIGHLY RECCOMMEND

Media and Technology. Very interesting class! Learned so much about level design and the art that goes into making 2-d games in Unity. Definitely great for beginners such as myself. It was a lot of work but! It was fun work and not agonizing work, very simple and got a 100 in the class, very easy grading too.

I don't want to be biased, but honestly professor Augustin is the best teacher that I have had in my entire life. He goes above and beyond not only for his work and projects, but also for his students. He is always watching out for you and may come off as having high expectations, but genuinely its because he cares.

Design&Interactivity is focused on creating a character, an environment, and then making a game based off of that in Unity. I never attended the in person sessions (class was held once a week online) and despite taking that blow to my grade, still ended with an A. As long as you try you'll do great. Prof Augustin himself is super cool and laidback!

Love Professor Augustin! He makes it clear that you will get a good grade as long as you try your best, and he is super understanding when you have other things going on. He's also generally very cool and funny. I'm taking another one of his classes next semester because he was so nice to be around.

*This rating is for PSY 332S*
 I was very optimistic about taking Neuroscience of Sleep; however, Professor Duarte was extremely condescending when I asked for feedback. She had daily quizzes over readings, and you had only 5 minutes to answer the question in full paragraph form, which had to have extremely proper grammar that made sense to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I did really well in Psychopharmacology with Duarte but not because of any help she provided. Her lectures are really interesting and the topic is fascinating, but Duarte doesn't provide ANY resources to study except for in class slide shows. I  passed with an A+ by making hundreds of flashcards for each test covering every sentence on every slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found her class harder than expected- it definitely requires studying to do well. There were 2 lectures a week (which were fairly dense), but she was very willing to help out outside of class hours with more than just the class, which i appreciated. She's a good professor and knows what she's doing- just make sure you put the time in the class.

This is the first time I've gotten below an A and I've taken both OChems, biochem, and physics. Exams are impossible, you basically have to memorize every word she says and even if you do you still probably won't do too well. No extra resources to study beyond lecture and lectures aren't recorded. Save your GPA and avoid this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is really smart but just doesn't know how to teach a class. The only assignments in the class was a paper and a few in class quizzes with one question. The tests are like trying to win trivia. No emphasis on what you need to know, and she tests very randomly. It is a strange combination of neuroscience, history, etymology, and geography.

Grade is based primarily on 4 exams. While you can drop one exam from your final grade, her exams are very difficult. She is very lecture heavy and so you need to be prepared to be a good note taker as her slides aren't sufficient and she doesn't record her lectures. Took a huge chunk of study time and effort. I wouldn't take her again.

Don't take her. Take another psych class. Lectures seem simple, but tests are impossible. Must memorize every word she says. No textbook and ppt slides have very few words, so don't miss a class or you'll be totally lost. My advice would be to record every lecture, make Anki decks, and memorize them word for word.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever met. She doesn't like helping anyone with extra questions after class. Also, theres no textbook so you will find this class difficult to study for. The quizzes are much harder than what she teaches in lecture. If you signed up for this class next semester drop before its too late. You will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSY308- Her class is HARD. She is intelligent and passionate about what she teaches. She will quiz you on exam content if you ask. She tells you point blank what you need to know, but it is your responsibility to study. Make an ANKI deck and you'll be fine! Wish I could take her class again, this was easily the most interesting class I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She complained for a month on low attendance, and even wrote an email saying that those that attend lecture make higher scores in class. I attended every lecture, studied, and still did only subpar for this course. Tests were insanely awful and down to the detail, and overall she seems unconcerned about student success. avoid her if possible.

Audrey made me fall in love with printmaking. Truly the perfect professor for intro to print. Jumping between four types of printmaking in one semester seemed overwhelming in my head, but audrey and our TA noah made it so doable and fun. She is so knowledgeable about processes, concepts, and history of print. You must take print if she's teaching!

I love Audrey. She is incredibly well prepared always and organized. Is knowledgeable about almost all printmaking but especially Intaglio and papermaking. She gives fantastic support, feedback, and suggestions (artists, films, books, poems, research, etc.) Her class discussions were so insightful and fun. Such a wonderfully kind educator as well.
Loved this class!! Audrey is so nice and is so helpful. She definitely helped me with my drawing skills. I would recommend any art class given by her.

Dr. Shaffer is very kind, and is a very good professor. She gives very specific feedback, and provides extra credit. She's also willing to work with every student. Attendance is mandatory, but it makes up a big chunk of your grade and is easy points. She's amazing, I love her. My speaking has improved a lot because of this class.

I wish I could stay in this class forever. I loved Prof Shaffer so much. She cares for her students like no other professor I've had, and her feedback was always helpful. This is an amazing class that I think everyone should take (and definitely try to take it with Audrey Shaffer)!

This class helped me (mostly) get over my fear of public speaking! Prof Shaffer was very kind and encouraging to all of her students and allowed us to give speeches based on our actual interests instead of just boring assigned topics. If you're going to take this class, make sure you get Prof Shaffer as your instructor.

Prof Shaffer is a professor that really only wants to see you do good. Understands all the pop culture references and is really respectful to all her students. Can have a good laugh while still being productive and will answer any questions you have. Class is not difficult, but it is time consuming.I do recommend mainly due to Prof Shaffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing UGS Professor!!!!! So passionate on what he does and explains the material so easy! Genuinely a great UGS for those need one. The material is super easy and the TA's were super helpful. Light readings but you can lowkey get away with not reading them. But overall and amazing class!!

A few straightforward quizzes + discussion attendance = your grade. He started making the quizzes open note halfway through the semester which made them even easier. You don't really have to pay attention in class or discussion either, and a lot of people just skipped class. Probably the easiest UGS at UT.

Professor Auyero is so sweet and funny during his lectures. He made every topic we went over very engaging. Literally one of the first courses I was able to pay attention to. There is lots of reading, but the material is usually interesting and easy to read. The quizzes answers are given a lot in lecture, but questions can be worded weird. 10/10

He is such an amazing professor! He's funny and even though they're readings, they're not long and most are pretty interesting. There's not a lot of homework which motivated me to further understand rather than stress out, and he usually gives out hints of what's going to be on the quizzes, and the quizzes are simple. Take him for your UGS!

Super funny guy, easy class, lectures are pretty interesting, and the readings are not too bad since he basically gives the quiz answers right before. However there's only like 5 quizzes that make up your grade. Solid UGS choice though.

Easy UGS, Professor Auyero is clearly knowledgable and passionate! Getting the books is annoying but honestly optional, you don't even have to read, he literally summarizes everything in lectures before quizzes. No graded writing assignments! Mandatory discussions weren't too bad. Genuinely interesting class, got me interested in sociology :)

Highly recommend taking Javier. Had an early class with him but his lectures were still able to keep me engaged half awake. Very lenient with grading and TAs were chill too. You can tell that he is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and wants students to leave class with an understanding of the content instead of emphasizing grades.

i love him sm. hes pretty humorous and full of energy that its kinda hard to fall asleep in his class. the class is just do readings, review reading in class, then quiz over reading. theres like 6 and hell drop one. u lit dont have to do the readings tho like js ai a summary and listen in class for someone else to summarize it. very easy ugs

- Caring, wants to get to know your name, personable
- Stimulating lectures, learned a lot
- TA-led discussion mandatory, shoutout Francisco
- Class attendance not mandatory but you're maybe cooked if you miss a quiz or some details. Just go! It's worth it!
- Just going to lectures and discussion helps a lot with quizzes, can get 100 just like that

Professor Auyero is an awesome professor! Attendance isn't mandatory, but your grades come from pop quizzes which Professor Auyero will hint at in lecture. Discussion sessions are mandatory, but useful (TAs are great!). You will have readings and they can be somewhat long, but it is all interesting stuff. Quizzes are easy if you read the chapters.

This professor is good and makes his lectures very enjoyable. He makes the material of what will be on the quiz well-known before you take it. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures, but it is for discussions. It is still very important to attend the lectures so you know when the surprise quizzes will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: GOAT ugs teacher

Javier always had engaging lectures and even remembered our names. We had 3 quizzes (they're taken on Canvas during lecture, so show up.) and 2 writing assignments as the bulk of our grades, and he literally gives you the answers to the quiz before taking it. The writing assignments are graded by the TA's, but they're not too harsh with it.

Very interesting (albeit boring) class and the prof was great. Attendance during main lecture isn't mandatory, TA sessions (required, but chill). Quizzes were light (gives answers in class usually), reading was so long and boring but you can get away w/ not reading (goes over in class),and essays were long but light. better than other ugs - easy A.

Javier is an amazing professor and lecturer. It is incredibly easy to get an A as long as you pay attention in class (he gives most quiz answers out before the test if you listen) and complete your readings!
