Grades are based on 4 multiple choice quizzes and 2 essays (1000 words each) about readings and personal connections.

He is amazing, I will always recommend. You have 2 papers and like 4/5 quizzes, lowest one is dropped. He gives you all the answers before the quiz. Show up to every lecture and you will be fine. He is so amazing and funny. The best class I had all semester. TA meetings seem a bit useless but it was nice getting to know them. Overall, take Javier.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the easiest ugs classes; all my friends were stressing while i was there with a free A in this class. TAKE IT.

Attendance is only mandatory for discussion sections. Very generous and understanding to students. I didn't actually read because he would always go over the answers and readings for the quizzes (he was discussing maybe changing that, but he may not). Very easy and interesting UGS. More controversial topics but if you're into sociology I say do it!

The best UGS! Javier is a great professor and his class is an easy A. Your grade is based off of 4-5 “pop” quizzes (he tells you when they will be) that he gives you the answers to + 2 written assignments that are an easy 100. If you do the readings and attend lectures you'll be fine. 100% recommend

Javier was the most intriguing and kind professor I have had. His lectures were extremely eye opening and he is super funny. His officer hours are very welcoming and he is always willing to talk with you. There is a lot of reading but the books are magnificent. Highly recommend for UGS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading but very doable. Would Highly recommend this UGS option since it is very eye opening.

Javier is seriously the best to take this UGS it's not hard at all there is a lot of reading but it is definite stuff you can skim and there are no tests but 'pop quizzes' (Javier tells you multiple times and gives you 1/2 the answers in his lectures) which I never got below a 100 on! The TA's are also awesome overall a great class

I LOVE JAVIER!! This class was amazing and opened my eyes to so many things. Not many assignments and quizzes, and they are easy. Lots of readings, but very interesting material. Javier is funny and lenient when it comes to grades.

This class was an extremely easy A and very enjoyable! The professor is very kind and funny, and keeps lectures engaging. The class is reading heavy, but I was able to get by just paying attention in lecture without doing most of the readings. Not too many writing assignments and a few easy quizzes. Would highly recommend this UGS!
The easiest class you could ever take. He wants his students to succeed, TA's are great, and he makes his lectures engaging. 0% chance you won't get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Javier is incredibly funny and makes attending class enjoyable! He offers 3 "pop-up" quizzes that he tells you about weeks in advance. He also goes over every single thing you need to know for that quiz right before the quiz. There are a few writing assignments that are really easy to Ace. The books you'll read in this class are interesting as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Javier is an angel among men. Social Scientific Imagination is interesting and so easy. The few quizzes he does give were open notes. There were two writing assignments that you had years to do and they were not very long at all.

I'd highly recommend this course for your UGS credit! Javier is incredibly funny and makes the class interesting and stress-free. He even learned almost all of our names. Grades mainly came from "pop" quizzes, multiple choice, and he literally tells you what's going to be on them. You do have to read some books, but it's nothing too difficult.

Javier knows how to make a class bearable--even if you have no interest in this subject, you will enjoy the class! There was quite a reading load at the beginning of the semester, but it died down and the last third of the semester is very chill. TAs were very kind. 

Take this UGS for an easy A and interesting content!

Javier is such an understanding professor and a great person to learn from. He does such a great job engaging with his students and made me feel eager to learn what he was teaching us. Grades were very forgiving, easy to get an A as long as you go to class and do the occasional reading, which was actually very eye opening content that I enjoyed.

Great professor overall, he's genuinely a reason I'm minoring in sociology now. His grading criteria is much clearer now and his lectures are super interesting. If you can sit and pay attention in lecture then it's an easy A and a great way to get an introduction into sociology.

Honestly, Professor Auyero made my first semester in college so fun. He's so chill, and explains concepts very well. He will literally tell you what will directly be on the quiz, so pay attention in class. TAs are very kind and easy grading on writing assignments (which can be long sometimes). Sometimes a lot of reading, so be prepared.

His class is very interesting. There are pop quizzes, but during class, he basically tells you what will be on the quiz. Most of the readings are really interesting. The writing assignments are really nice and are honestly better than what I had to do in high school. He's very funny and passionate about what he teaches. Highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great class with a hilarious professor! The majority of your grade is participation and attendance, as well as five "pop quizzes." Most of the quizzes are open book and pretty easy. TAs are nice and the discussion sessions are fun.

I recommend him a million times over! His UGS is really interesting and he is a funny guy. There are 4 essays, not long at all, and the TAs give good feedback. There are some readings and quizzes over them but they are not bad.

love prof auyero, his UGS is so interesting and very easy. no tests, 1 quiz a week, TA's are so helpful and their discussion is easy. take this UGS!!! he's really funny too. big class but if you participate and make an effort, it'll be fun and easy.

Prof Auyero was hilarious and his class is incredibly laid back. If you do the readings, which is normal fro UGS courses, then you will get an A. He teaches Social Scientific Imagination about Human Rights issues and several interesting stories that will make you inquisitive. I 100% recommend it and it was very interesting.
HE IS VERY PASSIONATE ABOUT SOCIOLOGY! I learned so so much in his class. I highly suggest you take his UGS. It is a lot of reading, but the pop quizzes and essay are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved taking Javier for my UGS! He was super funny and was able to teach the content extremely well. I learned a lot from this class and the material was super interesting as well. Assignments are not too hard and "pop" quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class. 100% take this UGS if you can.
I found Javier to be very funny and his lectures are never boring. His writing assignments were an easy A and he quizzes you on topics said in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Fav class, Javier is so much fun while also getting into some really interesting material. Good amount of reading, writing, and participation but very doable and he walks you through everything. Some "pop" quizzes that he warns you about a million times and long readings he goes over in depth if you don't manage to finish them. Easy A and a blast

Amazing professor. He's passionate and it spreads to his students. He's very understanding and grading is quite open-ended so there's freedom to write what you care about, love that for this type of class (social scientific imagination). Very easy writing assignments and quizzes that he warns you about. Take his class!!!

Great teacher who really cares about what he teaches. just pay attention in class, he practically gives answers for quizzes. he usually tells u if there will be a quiz. some readings, but nothing bad. 10/10 recommend

He's really funny and passionate about what he teaches. He clearly cares about his students. He assigns a lot of readings but they're all really interesting. He uploads all the pdfs you'll need so you don't really need to buy anything. The essays and quizzes were easy. It's an easy A. Would definitely take another class with him.

Javier is my favorite professor I have had at UT. He is so genuine and his class was very interesting (especially during the pandemic)!!! He worked well with us via Zoom and made class so enjoyable! The TAs were amazing and I really looked forward to going to class! 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS MAN! Javier is seriously so funny and kind. You would be making a huge mistake if you decided against taking his class. He does six pop quizzes (one dropped) which is how he gets people to show up to class. Half your grade is from a leniently graded research proposal on any sociology topic of your choosing. Sit in the front two rows!

Javier was a hilarious dude and really passionate about his subject. Pay attention to his lectures because all the quiz info comes from there - he makes it really clear what certain questions will be asked and warns about the "pop" quizzes in advance. He just wants students to show up and participate - boring class but a nice guy and easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy with great lectures. There is a handful of reading and his quizzes can come by surprise, but usually lenient, especially later on in the semester when he starts handing out goodies in the form of no readings or even no class. The class itself can be boring but him and his amazing TAs keep it fresh.

Javier was so funny and made his class so interesting. He would tell us when pop quizzes were so there was no surprise. The entire grade is really based off the quizzes and the final paper. The final paper is so easy and I literally got a 100 on it. Show up to the discussions and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Javier was my favorite professor this semester! Social Scientific Imagination was the best UGS I could have taken thanks to Javier's hilarious personality and his interesting lectures that taught me a lot about the world around me. His TAs are also wonderful and make discussion sections worthwhile. Easy quizzes and final paper! Take this UGS!!!!
listen to the lectures and you'll be fine.

Javier is one of the best teachers I've ever had. While he cares deeply about his the class and the material he teaches, he takes time to discuss relevant current events that make his students more educated about the world around them. The class is based on pop quizzes, so while attendance isn't mandatory- if you skip you could miss a quiz.

Auyero is an amazing person and his class is super easy. No tests, just quizzes about readings and one gets dropped! Social Scientific Imagination is a perfect UGS to take if you want to learn something new and do well at the same time. The course teaches you a lot about real-world issues both locally and globally: I definitely recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I am an engineering undergrad and I have never taken a similar class to this. I loved the professor and both of the teacher assistants. Did not do many of the readings and made an A on every pop quiz but one (one quiz gets dropped). I attended pretty much every lecture, and all the information you need comes from there. Easy final paper also.

Enlightening, significant, and meaningful are only a few words I can use to describe this course. Professor Auyero is an influential lecturer, and I feel incredibly blessed to have had the privilege to take his UGS303 course. The course was structured around reading, quizzes, and one final essay -- which were very manageable and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. Despite what people say, there are no pop quizzes. He will say "there might be a quiz on Friday," and then either there is or there isn't. He never just springs them on you without warning. This is also a fairly easy grade if you show up and do the readings, quizzes are mostly common sense and only one 3 page paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: I took this class a year ago during my 1st year, and I really enjoyed his class. I struggled on the quizzes throughout the class though. I reached out to him at the end of the semester, and he helped me out with my grade. I can see that he genuinely cared about his students. His lecture were also extremely interesting. One of my favorite classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Auyero's Social Scientific Imagination is NOT the easy A you are probably looking for. There are ALOT of intensive readings and RANDOM pop quizzes( that comprise a large part of your class grade) so beware. I did, however find his lectures interesting, but that's simply because I like sociology.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I didn't have a problem with the readings, but the quizzes were random to a degree and caught me off guard. I wish I could've taken a class with more major grades...
His quizzes really sneak up to you and this class is pretty much 7 quizzes an essay and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this class two years ago and boy was it more than I expected. The content is interesting, but it is very heavy in work. Not your blow-off class...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was super intensive and not as easy or a blow-off class. You seriously have to put in work. ALOT of reading and be ready(and beware) for POP quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class involves intensive reading and BEWARE the pop quizzes. It was difficult for a UGS class, but that's probably just me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Do not recommend for an absolute easy A. If you find no interest in the subject, this class will be a hassle and a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took this class in 2015 and the quizzes are sporadic. This class is basically 7 quizzes, attendance, and an essay. If you do not like writing or anything in the sphere, TAKE ANOTHER UGS. This class has ALOT of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Agree with the previous poster. Heads up to those who think that this class is an easy A. Unless you're heavily interested in sociology, this class can be a pain and the amount of reading is almost unbearable. Luckily for me, I found the subjects covered interesting. If you want an easier UGS choose something ELSE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: FRESHMAN: This class is ALOT of WORK. If you want a EASY A UGS, pick something else. So much reading and if you don't like the subject, this class will be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Really good guy. My only complaint about his class was that his TA got on my nerves. He enforces attendance by having quizzes which you don't know when they will happen. Required attendance in TA sessions too. Easy A as long as you do the required readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Javier is HILARIOUS and so knowledgable. He explains things incredibly elegantly in a way that's super easy to understand. Pop quizzes can sneak up on you, but if you listen, he usually gives the answers in lecture. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by just using his explanations. Definitely one of the coolest professors ever.

Javier is an amazing professor. I'm not even into sociology and he made the class interesting. He gives you the quiz questions and also basically the answers before you take the quiz. The TAs also go over them in the discussion sections so go to those as well. Yes, there's reading but they're minimal and you could probably skim them before class.

Awesome professor, super easy class. Just do the readings and show up to class and you will get an A. He's extremely passionate, and probably the only prof you will have that actually wants to learn your name. You only have 7 quizzes and a paper, and he drops a quiz as well as basically gives you the answers to the quiz. Super great class.

Went on a lot of tangents, but they were one of the most entertaining parts of the class.  A fair amount of reading, but most of the material is interesting and relevant.  Overall, a really good teacher who was passionate and knowledgeable about his subject.

Javier Auyero is probably one of the hidden gems in the Liberal Arts Department. He has this way of engaging students and making them see real world issues in a broader scope that encompasses both sides of the argument. The lectures in this class are top notch, and most of the time you will feel time fly away. The coursework is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you just want an easy A for your UGS, he's a good guy to take. If you want to learn anything meaningful, take something else. Everything learned in the class is heavily liberally biased and your grade in the class is dependent on your agreement with their opinions. Auyero's ALWAYS lies about when the quizzes are going to be. Beware of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: No exams, a couple "pop" quizzes you usually get warned about in the prior lecture. He's an amazing prof that's passionate about sociology, I absolutely loved his class & learned a lot. Readings are far less than other UGS. 1 paper graded by TA's so go to the TA sessions!!! If u put in the effort you'll get extra cred. I got a B+ with little effort

I absolutely loved this class. I considered changing my major after taking his social scientific imagination course. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and he is hillarious. He is hands down one of the best professors I have had. Class is an easy A if you pay attention to lecture and know the gist of the books. DEFINITELY recommend!

His class can seem fairly dry if you're not interested in sociology. There's a good amount of reading, but you can get away with skimming it. The most important advice I can give you is to attend lectures and discussion sessions. I had a hard time getting myself to sit through his lectures, but it pays off. His quizzes cover material from lecture.

Javier is very passionate in his UGS 303 course, and isn't afraid to confront and address a lot of deep racial issues in American society. The quizzes aren't that bad either, and he drops obvious hints as to when they'll be and what will be on them. The readings are important!

This was a very easy UGS 303 class: there are no 'tests', only 6 or 7 ten-question 'quizzes' that he will RANDOMLY do in class. The questions are simple and quite obvious most of the time. Discussion is mandatory, but not very helpful in my opinion. The key to doing well is showing up, and paying attention to what he says. Lots of reading!!
Auyero is my favorite professor at UT. His lectures are exciting and get everyone involved. I was completely out of my comfort zone at times, and it was really fun. Great class and great teacher.

He's a great lecturer, very passionate and entertaining. His power points are posted on canvas and he always tells you what will be on the quizzes. If you study and keep up on reading an A is achievable. He can be kind of scatterbrained though, and the TAs often had to push him to keep us on schedule and give the quizzes on time.
Great and nice professor. Very passionate about the subject and an interesting teacher. A lot of reading. Worth while UGS class.

I took his beginner level (6week long) Spanish course and was forced to pay 62$ for a program to do work that wasn't even graded. Yet he expected everyone to finish (literally) 12 assignments every day. His lectures were unfocused, and I spent most of my time in breakout rooms w peers. Despite him saying he cared it was abundantly clear he didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The quizzes were a little tricky but he really offers a lot of content to study for both exams and quizzes, and makes class really fun to go to. He engages with each student and genuinely cares for each person's wellbeing. Most fun I've had taking a class in college for a long time, and I will miss this prof

I took SPN 314 with Prof Aviles in summer 2021, and I really enjoyed it. He is super enthusiastic and helpful, and he really cares about the students' learning. There was a lot of homework because it was a summer class, but it wasn't too challenging. Overall, it was a great course and I highly recommend taking it with Prof Aviles!

Avramov is one of the greats! Engaging lectures, fascinating material, really genuine guy. My only critique is that the class allows students to succeed without learning the material. Ex- tests are online, hw only covers part of the reading. Bc of this, his class ended up on the back-burner. I wish he demanded more, bc I know I had more to give!

Professor Avramov is super awesome, the lectures are very engaging and this class is super relevant to current events. Discussions are lively and students are super welcomed to share their opinions. Would hundred percent recommend for everyone to take it - one of my favorite classes and professors here at UT!
Amazing Professor, keeps the class interested regardless of topic and always explains things thoroughly and well. Accepts questions and encourages students to be ambitious/ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I like Prof. Avramov a lot and I think what he teaches is extremely important BUT -I am kind of disappointed in him.He is so incredibly careful to stay away from even mentioning certain political topics in class. Everyone can clearly see that what he says applies to what is happening in the real world but he is too afraid to discuss it meaningfully

Dr. Avramov is one of the best professors I have taken at this school. This class is interesting at times but can often be boring and he kept everyone engaged. There is a lot of reading but quizzes and tests are open note/book so you don't have to do it all the time, but it helps. Other assignments are short discussion posts. Take this class!

Dr. Avramov is definitely one of the best professors at UT!! He is the most caring and passionate professor I've had. Cares more about the students actually learning than the grades. There were three exams and two discussions a month based on readings. However, he is pretty lenient and doesn't want to add stress to his students. Take his class

He was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He is so passionate about these topics that he is teaching which makes it so enjoyable to go to class and learn. Even though it is a big lecture class, he makes an effort to get to know all of his students. Great experience. I am taking another one of his classes next semester.

Professor Avramov is very caring about his students and takes that into account by not giving heavy loads of work, only what is needed to be successful in the course. As long as you take notes during lecture you will have all of the answers for the exams, which are open note. Very funny dude and makes tough info to get fun to learn

Dr. Avramov is literally the BEST professor I've had at UT!! He is super smart and knowledgeable, and cares about his students immensely! His lectures are superb and he really tries to keep you engaged throughout! You have to read a bunch, but it's super worth it! Dr. A is a true master in his field, so if you can you should absolutely take him!!!!

Dr. Avramov was my favorite professor I had during my time at UT. He is an amazing lecturer who is clearly a master of his subject. He is kind and takes the time to know his students. He is engaging and interesting. Do yourself a favor and take one of his amazing courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This Political Manifestos class. Both professors are really good and fun. However, there is a tremendous amount of reading and you are expected to read all of it. Can you make if you skim through? Yeah, not too bad. After the first precis scare is over, class is easy. Friday lectures are the most important, they guide you through the assignments.

Lectures are fascinating, you can truly tell Professor Avramov really cares about what he is teaching and making sure students understand the concepts. He gives great feedback on writing assignments making it really easy to increase your grades on them throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Avramov is an outstanding teacher. Very knowledgeable & engaging, he knows how to keep students interested and promote participation. Tackling the soviet security apparatus in the space of a semester is a mammoth task, but I feel I have gained genuine insights which have fed my curiosity on specific subject areas. Could not recommend enough.

If you're not sure how to do a Precis, then you will definitely learn how to in this class. If you don't let the Precis freak you out, then you should be fine along with the rest of the coursework. He does love to cold call and the lectures can be a tad boring, but the information is pretty interesting. He clearly loves what he teaches!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Heavy reading courseload. Excellent excellent professor. He cares and wants you to understand the Russian Security environment. Take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. A! He is an awesome professor and genuinely loves educating his students about Russia, Eastern Euro, security, etc. Classes are very reading heavy and exams are not for the faint of heart-- you MUST study! If you try in class and you speak up, he will like you a lot. He expects students to put in effort but never wants them to stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took her arabian nights class, and really loved it. the class is interesting, and Noy is very knowledgeable. she is a hard grader, however, and sometimes frustratingly so -- a few times i thought about throwing my computer out the window. LOTS of reading. too much. not burdensome, though. overall, id recommend for people interested.

Took Arabic Lit. Highly difficult class yet rewarding -- you learn a lot! Readings are super difficult. Noy's lectures are amazing and she is easy to reach outside of class and understanding. PLEASE CONTRIBUTE IN THIS CLASS. It's small and discussion based, don't take it if you're not ready to talk. DO THE READINGS, she likes to see effort!

Honestly one of the best professors I've had. The content was phenomenal and she is such a kind professor. It is reading heavy and discussion based so make sure to read or at least skim. No tests however there are 4 written assignments and weekly journals, but so far they have not given me any issue and 2 of the papers are only 2 pages long.

Uses Socratic method to a fault, basically to have students teach for him. Grades are completely arbitrary and he provides no feedback. I received high A's on all homework papers (no feedback provided), and this was completely inconsistent with the final grade. He spent half a class arguing he should be allowed to buy votes. Not approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Avraham is really sweet and loves torts.  He explains a lot of things at a level even a 5 year old could understand. Some other readings were hard to understand.  Overall, highly recommended.
Avraham is funny and makes class enjoyable.  I had him for Torts. He really covers everything he wants you to know during class, so don't miss class!

Her assignments are the blandest possible drawing curriculum and being in it is a waste of time. If you are studio major the core class was better than this. Color is rarely allowed, and she makes you draw simple subjects and lighting exercises as if you are a basic beginner, not an art major. Feedback and focus in the classroom felt lacking.

My painting really improved! However, she does not put any feedback or grades into canvas. You have no clue how you are doing until your course grade has been submitted to the registrar. I was excited to take painting 2 however she was extremely rude over email after I asked a genuine question regarding feedback so I dropped the course.
Amazing professor. I went from never life drawing to being amazing at it all because she knew exactly what she was talking about. Highly recommend.

Nicole is one of the most understanding and caring teachers I've ever had. She tries to make you a better artist even if you cant see it in the beginning you understand at the end of the semester. If you have any concerns about your progress she'll sit down and talk with you even if shes busy. She's really amazing I would take her again in a second

Dr. Awad is extremely down to earth and understanding. She is very knowledgable on both subjects of the psychology of women and psychology of race/racism. During COVID, she encouraged cameras to be on and attendence is graded. Assignments were critique papers, journals, and tests. I really loved Dr. Awad and feel like I genuinely learned a lot.

she ROCKS really funny if youre not a liberal just be warned but she is really funny and is a fair grader. she wants her students to do well. PARTICIPATE it shows her you care and she will fight for you more if she sees that
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Overall, psych of women was great! Interesting and engaging lectures. The exams were challenging and many questions seemed there solely to confuse. Also, Canvas was a mess for this class as it seemed like it was not updated since the previous semester-assignments had multiple due dates and prompts. I was happy with my grade but it was not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Awad is funny, caring, passionate, and respectful of all students opinions. 3 exams (half multiple choice, half short-answer) that are somewhat tricky. 3 journals, 2 critique papers, one final paper, and pop quizzes. Lectures included a lot of class discussion. No laptops. Overall, the class was interesting and I learned a lot. Take her!

Dr. Awad's "Psychology of Women" course was amazing and informative. The topics we went over were really interesting and relevant. There are 3 exams, several pop quizzes throughout the semester (if you pay attention in class, these are easy). Most info for tests comes from lecture, with some material from textbook. Also she's a really cool person.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Smart. Knows her stuff. Fantastic choices in readings & a diverse array of them, and very up-to-date on the subjects (unlike some profs who reuse old material to the point of absurdity). Very liberal and will expand your (even if already open) mind.

Overall an OK prof. He spends most of lectures going over proof of theorems and lectures are very theory heavy in general with little to no examples. I wouldn't recommend taking him unless you've already taken real analysis. He is a nice guy and always willing to help out, class material and teaching style is just very difficult. Read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the exams were hard, you can get a good grade as long as you do the homeworks and work hard on the project. Drops the lowest grade and has lots of office work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I found the subject matter incredibly difficult to grasp at first, Dr. Turnquist was a great professor. The grading scheme made getting an A possible if you put in some work: 50% from homework + a project and 2 exams, dropping the lowest score . Homework was harder than exams, but he had many office hours available for getting help.

Numerical Analysis is hard, so the content for this class is harder than other math classes. It consists of both computational and theory. 50% HW, 25% project, 25% midterm, and 25% final. He drops the lowest 25% from any of the following. HW and the project weren't too bad, but the exams were hard. Read textbook. Overall, very caring professor.

Dr. Turnquist gets an unnecessary amount of hate. For one, his teaching style is unique from other professors. Rather than just give you the answer or just give you a definition, he makes you think about that definition and why it matters. Homework isn't bad. Beware of tests however since he really wants you to think. Overall, good professor.

Brutally hard class. Very different from other Diff EQ classes. Super theory based and very difficult to understand. If you're a math major, this class is for you. If you need to do anything applicational, find something else. I wouldn't take this class. It isn't worth the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are theory/proof heavy, and lecture notes (hand-written) are horrible. Self-study enough to do all the HW, and you will be more than able to do well on the exams (easier than HW). Coding project took about 2h and accounted for 25% of the grade. Just self-studying and being confident in linear algebra can probably honestly get you an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very hard class. Go to office hours as much as you can to check your homework answers and Project, and read the textbook after every class to get the material down and you'll be fine. I got a 60 on my final but the curve brought me to an A-.

Absolute joke of a class. He is a very conceptually heavy teacher who spends all of his time deriving and proving the theorems and leaves no time for examples. Class is a drag. The homework is impossible. And even if you end up doing the homework, they don't correlate to the exams. Don't take. Bottom of the totem pole for M427J professors.

Professor Turnquist is very smart and definitely enjoys math, but his lectures are theory heavy and difficult to understand with almost 0 practice problems. Homework is nitpicked, and the 1 exam and the final are all theory (avgs were around 50-60). Very difficult class, especially considering every other professor teaching 427j give most kids As.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man is a threat to society.

Obviously, the class is "unique". Don't expect to do too well on homework, as that is very arbitrary (unless you go to office hours, which I didn't). The exams were way easier than HW, and  tested what he taught/ was in the book. Interesting teacher, but you have to understand and not memorize. Or just bring a textbook (Open note exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought I was always good at math. I easily surpassed the A grade in every class I took, until I got to this class. This class was a pain. Very theory heavy, and if you don't like that, do NOT take him. His exams are not for people who like applying math, and solving equations.

Regardless of what other reviews say, his grading is NOT lenient. His tests will not match the material and if you want a chance at passing you must read the textbook (which again, is almost as bad as his lectures). 
My grade is wildly different from my peers who took other professors. This seriously needs to be addressed by the Math Department

Turnquist is clearly insanely smart, but he is not fit for teaching or lecturing. During lectures, he basically writes his notes onto the board with no numbers and poor examples. It's essentially a self-taught class since lectures aren't at all helpful. Tests/homework are also insanely difficult. 2 stars since he's funny and nice in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. He rants about concepts that won't be on the homework or exams for the entirety of class and then grades everything like it's a dissertation. If you think you can teach yourself an upperclass math go ahead - but it will not be fun. He isn't mean, just a terrible professor. UT please fire him.

I sincerely believe a higher power sent Axel Turnquist to punish me for any wrong doing I have ever committed. While Axel is a jolly fellow with clear passion for mathematics, the very last thing he should be doing is teaching. With a current RMP score of 1.9 and difficulty of 4.6, UT should find another use for him immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you have to take this class with this professor, do yourself a favor and just change your major or dropout. no degree is worth taking this class with this professor. dean of CNS, if you're reading this, I think I speak on behalf of all of us when I say we deserve some type of compensation for what we were put through in this class.

reviews.comment: She is extremely liberal. It is obvious she cares more about her research than her teaching, forgot to give us a take home exam emailed it 2 days late and had it due the same day. Few times she emailed us the reading guides THE NIGHT BEFORE THE EXAM (our reading was over 300 pages for every unit). But she does know her stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Stay away from this class! It is a HUGE time commitment. The online class has lots of busy work, exams are long and difficult as well. Professor knows what she is talking about, but class is horrible! Random quizzes during lectures, weekly videos to watch which can sometimes be an hour long for a 5 question quiz.

I think the class is probably much better in person, but online it was dreadfully boring and the lectures were extremely long. I wouldn't recommend taking it online. Dr. Azam definitely knows what she's talking about though, and if you already know lots about Islam you'd be fine. If you don't have as much prior knowledge, maybe think twice.

She's great. Interesting lectures, fair tests (Multiple choicetrue falseshort answer). If you do not go to lecture, you'll fail. The notes she gives you in lecture will be on the test and aren't in the readings so go to class !!! She writes out the notes as she lectures and you only need to write down what she writes.
Very cool and interesting, helpful. Enjoyed her greatly.
Intro to Islam, lower div survey course. Meant to foster Islamic literacy. We cover history, cosmology, ritual worship, theology, law, sufism, art/culture, and modern movements.
really fun professor and helped me ease into college as a freshman. classes develop a sense of community within peers and the professor. overall really fun and great class

Took this class as an elective so I can fill my schedule & I'm SO glad I did. Barbara is very sweet and funny and has been one of my favorite professors at UT by far. Attendance is mandatory (you can only miss 2 classes unexcused) but don't worry bc you won't want to skip. TD 303 definitely helps break out of your shell & interact with classmates.

I took this class to fulfill one of my elective requirements as a senior. The assignments are easy as long as you get memorized, and there is definitely a sense of community within the class, as everyone is new to acting. Attendance is a huge part of the grade, but Barbara is easy to reach outside of class if you really need to skip for any reason!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most fun classes I have ever taken in my academic career. There are 3 assignments where there are lines to memorize throughout the course, the first 2 are collaborative and the last one is a monologue. Nothing difficult to memorize at all. The class is small and meets so frequently that there is def a sense of community at the end. 10/10

This was a really fun class and you get close to everyone in there because it is a small class. Only 3 scenes throughout the semester but it really helps with public speaking. Barbara is super nice and cares about her students and gives really good feedback on your scenes. All you really have to do is show up and participate and you'll get an A.

Barbara is amazing. Her class is so much fun and it's an intimate environment with your peers that is created. You have 3 scenes to do in total, you have to watch 2 theatre productions, and you do a reflection on the racial geography tour. Super easy assignments, I looked forward to this class every time!

Lobe barb!! Her class is hilarious and you get to know your classmates so well. At the beginning of the semester she told us this is an easy A class, and she was telling the truth! I looked forward to class all week, it was a great place to unwind and have fun for a grade :) If you are looking for a VAPA, look no further!

She has been one of the best professors I have ever had at UT. She genuinely cares for her students, and the class is not difficult at all. Just show up, participate, and you'll do great! I would take her class again in a heartbeat.

Barbara Chisholm is an incredible professor! She's funny and caring. This course is pretty easy to get an A in, you just need to show up to class, do the activities, and respect the professor. I would absolutely take another course with her and I definitely recommend taking this course. I will say there was less acting than I expected though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever. Basically only 3 assignments. She is a fun teacher and cares about the subject. We really did nothing the whole time but it was fun. Nice break from real classes! Highly recommend

Take this class if you need a GPA boost, just show up and participate. The class can get a little boring at times and she may come off a bit pushy but overall I enjoyed the class. She can be funny too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Best unnecessary class ever. Easiest GPA booster ever, take her if you real

This class is super fun and easy. As someone who's done theatre for years, it was still valuable to me but I think it could be valuable to pretty much anyone. The main thing you have to do is show up and participate. I got 100 in the class just by doing that
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is amazing. fundamentals of acting was the best class

Barbara is a gem. She cares tremendously about ALL of her students. She takes the time to learn about each student & celebrates their accomplishments. Really cultivates a comfortable & safe learning environment. You do not have to be an amazing actor to do well in this class. Show a willingness to participate & learn & you will succeed. LOVE her!

Chisholm is very friendly and makes an effort to connect to each of her students. The class (T D 303) is easyyyy to the point of almost being boring. I'd recommend it if you're in need of a GPA booster. If you're looking for a useful class that will teach you advanced acting techniques and challenge you to become a better actor- do not take this.
Cared about each one of her students as individuals and really cares about what she teaches.

This class is pretty doable if you stay on track. You might feel a little lost as to why you are doing certain things, though. He's a nice guy - expect to learn the content, but don't anticipate interesting lectures. A little boring and monotone at times. Tests get harder over time, and the final is designed to make you think hard.

Great lecturer. Presents material in a great way. Even though it's not required, you need to go to lectures. That's the only way to succeed from my experience. Lectures are never boring either. Midterms are okay, final exam was a bit harder.
Really nice and has great handwriting
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Well-documented lecture notes and spends a lot of time explaining concepts in-depth. Course starts off pretty easy, but if you don't keep track of and connect concepts they WILL sneak back up on you. The final exam was pretty brutal. Spends a lot of time talking about career/professional development topics if that's your vibe

very light work load, only 6 hw's, 2 exams, and a final. exams were weighted heavy, but the final was online. beware though the first exam is way easier than the second one, and very time consuming. was very difficult to finish both the 2nd exam and the final because of the lengths of them. overall prof was fine, hardly ever went to lectures tho
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His teaching style is a little weird where its super hard to follow, understand, and really get the main picture. You can go the entire semester even doing well in classes but not understand what or why you are doing what you're doing at all. The content itself is reasonable for an upper-level aero class, and tests get progressively harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught in a very clear manner and was very helpful with questions. The tests got progressively more difficult but if you do well on the first one you will be fine.
Great class great notes straightforward syllabus and grading parameters.

Really nice professor, funny/sarcastic. He posts all of his notes and just re-writes them on the whiteboard each class. Needs to check for questions from the class more. The first test is easy. The second test comes out of nowhere and hits you hard. Final was intentionally evil. Overall: good/fair guy, hardish class.
Very very smart and an amazing lecturer but you are graded on so few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a great prof who genuinely cares about his students. He is absolutely brilliant and I love his lectures. However, you are graded on very few assignments and if you don't test well, I would avoid this class. He always dresses really nice. He's kinda fine ngl.

Was not familiar with Islam at all coming in but this class is interesting and well structured. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit and easy assignments. Professor Ayoub made it clear that he cared for his students.

Great Professor. He is very knowledgeable. If you are pre-law, take his classes. I got into many programs because of his rec letters. He teaches at UT Law. Attendance is mandatory. Two tests: midterm and final. He gives exam reviews for both. Take this class!
Professor Ayoub is a great mentor and passionate professor. He is inspiring and I find him very handsome. One of my best professors at UT.

He jumped around a lot and was horribly hard to follow. Instructions for assignments are unclear and graded harshly. He doesn't make any sense if you don't know the subject then you won't have any idea what he is talking about. I NEVER DO RMP RATINGS, but this class and professor is not worth it.

I hated this class. Lectures were boring, teacher was hard to follow at times. VERY few assignments and one missed point is hard to recover from. I still did well, but assignments are not graded lightly and most any missed points on quizzes/exams were basically trick questions that were offhandily mentioned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is extremely difficult, so please beware. That being said, Professor Ayoub is fantastic and incredibly engaging. His lectures are packed with information, but you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, and you should be okay as long as you pay close attention. Be ready to read a lot, however, and it ain't easy to make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel like he is a professor for the type A person. He lectures quite fast and there are no laptops allowed in class so it can be difficult to keep up with written notes. Very knowledgeable and will teach you a lot though. I don't feel comfortable speaking up in class. Beware pop quizzes worth 20% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is one of the best professors I have had during my time at UT. His lectures might be a bit boring but the majority of the exams and quizzes will be based on the lectures.

I really enjoyed Professor Ayoub's Government and Islam - it opened me up to a whole new field of thought. He is obviously very knowledgeable about the area and passionate for it as well. Just be aware that there is a huge amount of reading for this course, though much of it is reviewed in the following class.

I took intro to Islam. It was an easy class, you can get away without reading the readings as long as you can bs an answer bc he loves to randomly call on people. I wish it was more of a collaborative class but he mostly just picked on ppl all class. He makes good points during lectures and tests/quizzes aren't too bad. Just go to class and easy A.

I took ISL310, Introduction to Islam; it wasn't one of his provided courses for some reason on rmp. Overall the class is pretty straight forward. Sometimes he might ask an oddly specific question on an exam or quiz, but honestly if you show up to class and read the slides you can definitely get an A. I think the class was pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ayoub was lovely but firm, Id just recommend to always go to class (hardly any leniency), do your readings, and make sure you take note of PowerPoint lectures. He gave us 4 journal entries, 2 exams (a midterm and cumulative final), attendance grade, and 2 quiz grades. Its open note but doesnt mean its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Interesting class for sure, but he was insanely passive aggressive if he didn't like you and almost never responds to emails. Very infuriating, especially in the middle of the quizzes/exams... TA was also confused most of the time.

All I'm going to say is I was in the hospital and the man still refused to give me an extension for a quiz we were given a 24 hour window to take, so I took the quiz on 3 different pain medications. Do with that information what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is a great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Ayoub is a great guy, well dressed and a knowledgeable teacher. The class left me a little disappointed because it didn't require students to think critically.

One of the easiest and most interesting classes I've taken at UT. Weekly readings help you participate in class discussions but honestly are not necessary. Attendance is part of your grade. One midterm and mandatory final. He gives exam reviews for both and the tests are verbatim the reviews. Take this class!
I loved Dr. Ayoubs lectures and discussions. He is clearly invested in his students. He challenged us to grow intellectually. I strongly recommend his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Ayoub is very passionate and knowledgeable. He is approachable and he likes participation in class. I would highly recommend to take his classes, if you can get in. It took me a semester to be able to enroll in one of his courses.
I took two classes with Dr. Ayoub. I enjoyed every single minute of them. He is very knowledgeable and accessible outside of classroom. I would definitely recommend his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one the best teachers I had during my education at UT. I greatly enjoyed his lectures, especially the discussion part.

He's a very smart guy and cares a lot about the content. I was able to find the book online for like $10, and while the reading was helpful, it wasn't completely mandatory to do well on the test. He gives a study guide a week prior and there are no curve balls on the test. I'm not even a gov major and pulled an A with an average work input.

Professor Ayoub seems extremely passionate and knowledgeable about his subject but appears to have a difficult time diffusing that knowledge and passion to his students. His class structure was a little hazy and no one seemed to fully understand how things worked in terms of grading or participation. Pretty easy A, though, if you put in any work.

The book cost a lot first of all and there is a lot of reading from the chapters and a lot of supplemental reading that consists of 20 pages per reading that he gives. The test had items that were not talked about in class. Little small detailed things. Just get ready to read a lot if you want an A and show up to class.

This class is super easy, one open note quiz every week and a couple of other assignments here and there. Definitely go to class because there are random attendance checks, and missing too many can add up. Overall really easy class but the professor can be really boring.

Amazing teacher. Very approachable and caring. Open note quizzes and several projects using the UT Library resources. Interesting digital topics during the course. Gives extra credit for early submission in assignments. They can become heavy, starting early is a must.

Genuinely such a nice person, she's one of the kindest professors at UT! Her class is super easy, and even though there are some group projects, it's really doable. You learn pretty useful things when it comes to the digital world too. She really accommodating to students, and is accessible even when it's not class time.

Professor Gursoy was extremely kind and understanding. She will be lenient with you as long as you talk to her in advance. Extremely easy class. A quiz every week, open note. Two projects. As long as you do your work on time, you will pass.

Amazing class and amazing professor
Best at UT
If you actually want to learn something take his class
Attendance is necessary to pass
Contrary beliefs to some trends that he defends
intense but by participating and using all the help available it is easy
Very lecture heavy, while attendance is not mandatory he still values participation in class. Not sure how valuable overall class was, but some interesting things were taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class if you actually want to learn accounting. Classes are very engaging and actually get you to learn instead of just memorize all the boring parts of accounting. The more you go to class the better you'll do on the tests. The extra credit is also super easy to get if you want a boost to your first test.

Professor Batolato is one of the best professors I have encountered. He takes a Munger/Buffet style to understand standing companies or put simply understand human concepts. If you want to learn financial alchemy and jargon do not take this class because instead you will learn how to think critically about business.
Genuinely questionable how he got here to be teaching. Made me hate accounting.

Very intense but a really good professor. I had to get used to his style of teaching, but after a while you get over how different his methodology of teaching is and realize it is actually quite helpful. Go to class but be prepared to participate because he grades on that. Just keep your head up if his style of teaching makes you feel lost.
unique teaching style; his emphasis on learning rather than simple regurgitation is amazing

It's so funny because all of the positive reviews here sound just like the professor wrote them himself. I had a really hard time engaging and following along because he never fully covered anything that will be on the tests - It was always an unpleasant surprise. He makes it sound so easy to get an A when it's not. take any other professor.
Surprised participation scores

Badolato's course splits students into two camps: those who love the critical thinking challenge and engaging lectures, vs those who prefer memorization and exam-mirroring assignments. The difference isn't about his teaching—it's about your approach. Embrace struggle and growth? You'll thrive. Expect to regurgitate for an A? Consider other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Badolato is McCombs' best! His FSA class is exciting, thought-provoking, & funny. I learned more with him than in any other business class. He cares about who and what he is teaching. If you want to do well, show up and act like you care. My verdict: take his class, participate, prepare for all lectures, fasten your seatbelt, and laugh all the way.

Badolato is the BEST. I haven't ever gotten this much out of a class. He really cares that we are actually learning and isn't solely focused on you memorizing for the test. Some people will say that he's hard and a frat guy and annoying which is all such BS. I am telling you if you take this class and put in the effort you'll get an A and be glad.

Hands down best professor I ever took. He prepares you for life and uses real examples as material. He's not a tough grader. If you are solely a business student this SHOULD be your center of focus. Will say not to get overconfident after first exam, the final is much harder and with no extra credit this time. Wish I had taken more advantage of him
Terrible. Avoid at all costs unless you want to listen to the same thing over and over everyday and still end up with a C.

Never seen a frat guy as a professor. Always brushes off critical concepts that WILL show up on the exam and repeats 3 things he hates the most EVERY CLASS: “stroking calculator”, “memorize and regurgitate”, and “investment banking”. Instruction will always be unclear as if he wants you to mess up. He's mean during office hours too.

Mixed thoughts. Passionate professor but somewhat repetitive. Before every class there is a case due which takes some work, but usually you'll get 95+ on it if you put some work and thoughtful answer. PARTICIPATION MATTERS. Grades you on did you speak in class. Final project is hard but every group gets between 85-95. His A is also a 90.

Do not take him for 311. He acts like we are all accounting majors and have the same knowledge he does in the subject. Most of the class is just him yapping and telling us to not "stroke a calculator." The workload for an intro class is also too much, we have two to three assignments due weekly and his deadlines are at 9am not 1159pm. DONT TAKE HIM
Hands down the best professor I've had at UT. Dr. B didn't just teach accounting—he changed how I approach learning and education. Take his class if you want to grow and actually want to learn.

Take him! If you want to learn content & gain value from class, you have to take him. He creates the content, is passionate, and focuses on understanding/concepts rather than memorization or bookkeeping math. 20 pts of extra credit available for the first exam based on completion of assignments. Not too much outside class work. accessible & funny

Badolato's teaching style revolves around celebrating his own achievements and putting down others. His lectures lack substance, and while he claims to value participation, his questions have only one acceptable answer. Worse, he tracks student performance in a spreadsheet after every class, grading on a 0-1 scale. He is Bateman-esque.

PB is a class act. His class is a radical departure from the all too typical "info-dump and memorize". Read the cases, apply your lived experience, and learn from others. It is fun. If you want to understand the FS implications of business decisions, you are in the right place. A ship in harbor is safe, but that's not what ships are built for.
If you want your education and tuition worth it, you must take his class

- Extreme, unvetted viewpoints on narrow industries
- 25 cases on the same few topics, no mechanics of FSA taught
- outdated, canned lectures from class to class, regardless of level - brags about how many classes he teaches
- dissenting viewpoints are unwelcome and punished in participation grades
- no feedback given in the course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has a unique style of teaching that is very different from other accounting teachers and it works. He is funny and uses helpful real world examples that explain readings. Read packets before class and pay attention and you will do well enough on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Patrick is an amazing teacher and is really passionate about the students. He wants you to learn and to absorb the material, not just memorize. The class is pretty simple until you get to the final which is challenging but if you went to class and were attentive you'll be fine. I love this class and professor and would recommend it to anyone.
Loved this professor until the final exam. Now I know why people encouraged me to switch to a different teacher. Made it seem like it was gonna be easy and then ended up having a failing average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Even if u show up to every class u cannot get full participation points unless you contribute to class discussion. Discussion was nothing like the final exam and thankfully a lot of students agreed. He ranks students at the end to determine their letter grade so beware of that before u take him. Final exam was 35% of the grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved the professor but showed up to every class and did not get full credit for participation. This class was a giant learning curve for me and went well until the final exam, it was intense and a big portion of our grade with a failing average. If ur not passionate about accounting and do not want to do the work do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Badolato is the best. Truly wants you to learn and preaches understanding the material instead of memorizing for the exams. Show up, do the homework, and you will get a good grade. One of my favorite professors at UT. If you really want to learn then take him, you won't regret it.

Badolato is such a good professor. He has made accounting so interesting which keeps you engaged. He discourages laptops/screens which forces you to listen to his lectures. He does not call on anyone, but he does want you to add to discussions. He also uses accessible language & puts less emphasis on grades/exams so u r more focussed on learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A teacher that really makes you think and question business, a rare thing today. I highly suggest you take his classes, as he will be moving to teach ACC311.
PB did a great job of delivering the content in a clear, concise format. It's not the most interesting stuff in the world to me, but he helped make accounting as engaging as possible.
Very engaging although can be intimidating but his dedication and passion makes you believe that he is doing the best for your future. Can be though on participation so you will have to speak up.

Dude is a genius, but also tough. Class is extremely good. He can be intimidating at times but that is just how it goes. Class only has one test, three group projects, homework for each class, and mandatory participation in class. Overall one of the most challenging classes I have taken, but also the class I have learned the most in.

This class is challenging and fast-paced; however, if you are involved in the class discussions, keep up with the coursework, and ask questions when you are unsure, you will learn a lot. His style of teaching demands active participation and requires you to actually think about each concept, rather than just providing the solution. 
Also, Stickers!

I learned so much from this class! It was extremely fast paced, making it difficult and a lot of work, but he made it as great as possible. Interesting lecturer, broke things down well. The exam was difficult, mainly because the accounting language was still new to me, but all the subject matter was exactly what we had learned.

Exam was nothing like class discussion or cases. No shame in insulting students. Worst professor I've ever had & gets off on making himself feel smarter than students. If only one student does well, then that means that you are a bad professor. Nothing to be proud of. Claims that without his class, your degree is worthless. Ruined my UT experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Struggles to communicate during lectures and online. Will often repeatedly over-use expressions like "darts in eyes" when he can't think of anything relevant to course material. Not good at facilitating discussion.
Requires homework completed before you learn the subject material. Not something I am familiar with, and very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Badalato sucks, he assigns way too much work and doesn't seem to understand how to write a fair test. Thinks he's sooooo great but you're up a creek for this class. Get ready to read and suffer because he won't help you with anything and seems to take pride on being "hard" without actually imparting anything useful or valuable. Power tripping idiot
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was hard for me but to some people, it was easy. This class was about understanding and applying concepts so if you are good at that, you should be okay. There is a lot of work and group projects, but you do learn a lot from them. Badolato is intimidating and I'm kinda scared of him but he is a genius. Go to his office hours and ask Qs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: FSA with Badolato is difficult and he isn't shy about making it that way, but it's an absolutely essential class for any finance student. Teaches you to think qualitatively and understand the metrics and models you use. Patrick is extremely smart and is more than willing to speak after class about in depth questions. Best prof I had at UT.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Concepts is a hard class. It'll be tough with any professor. Badolato's lectures were clear and you will definitely learn a lot from him. He cold calls a lot and is pretty blunt; but he's also a genius. Be prepared to work hard, participate in class, and study as the semester goes along; you can't cram for this class. You'll learn a lot in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is hard. And it definitely doesnt help if the professor is absolutely rude and insulting to his students during lecture. Not a terrible lecturer, but a terrible person. If I could redo this semester, the best thing I could do for myself is to take Professor Toynbee for concepts instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor did not give any feedback on assignments, so I had no idea where I was going wrong or how to improve my grades. He is also quite insulting during class discussions which made many students wary of speaking up. He says that there are no wrong answers, but class discussion always leads to the one right answer - his answer.

EXCELLENT professor for Financial Statement Analysis.  Able to effectively work with executive students, fun and engaging lectures, rigorous learning happens in his classroom.  A true gem at UT Austin.

This class is extremely difficult. However, Badolato knows this and definitely tried to make the information clear and relevant. The conceptual basis of the class makes lectures confusing, and the tests are very different than what you do in class - you will need to study every bit of the material and do the practice questions a lot to stay afloat.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes. Reading before class will help a lot. He's a no BS kinda guy, funny, and lectures very well. His tests have ambiguous terms that can be interpreted multiple ways which make them challenging. He gives regular homework and 2 exams plus a final. He also gives out notes in class.

Wonderful professor. Made accounting interesting and helped make the bigger picture clear so it didn't feel like you were just learning for nothing. Go to class, pay attention, take notes, do the homework, and you'll be fine. He emphasizes focusing on the "why" for tests, so they're a little more difficult but definitely doable.

Awesome professor, hard class. Try to read the textbook chapter before class. (even if it's the 1st few pages); You'd be surprised how much more everything makes sense when you read and pay attention. Go to class, do all the homework, and ask him for help! Class curved but you still need to try your hardest. Average is always around B-/B+.
Best professor ever. He's passionate, smart, funny, and knows how to teach. However, you have to put a lot of effort into this class.

Dr. Ayvaci was a nice guy, but his teaching style is bizarre. He's very boring in his lectures and we were never on syllabus, so nothing was clear. Granted it was his first semester teaching at UT when I took the course, but he kept changing things as he went. His iClicker quizzes were ridiculously difficult. Avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He should learn that teaching doesnt consist of preparing and showing slides. As a teacher his value should be more than that. Your learning will be mostly limited with your capacity in his class.

He's a nice guy, but not so great of a teacher. I stopped going to class because I couldn't understand his style of teaching and the test was straight from the book anyways. Right before the test I would memorize the powerpoint slides and textbook chapters, and would do ok. Aside from that, the homework assignments and quizzes are really easy!

Professor Ayvaci was a nice guy to say the least, but he had trouble keeping the lectures interesting. Luckily the material is fairly easy and he provides all the slides you need, so if you just read/memorize the slides before the tests and quizzes, you should do fairly well. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but has trouble clarifying.

I really didn't vibe with this guy's teaching style at all. Every example is taken directly from the book, and he rarely, if ever, leads the class step-by-step on a block of code, and this is nominally a CODING class. By far the worst MIS professor I've taken thus far at UT. He's just not an effective teacher when the goal is programming knowledge.

Professor Ayvaci is a nice guy but his exams are very difficult and he has some very backwards policies. This is a SQL coding class and exams are all multiple choice, so they are not a good measure of what you know. No chance to actually write code in exams. He doesn't let you even see graded quizzes, so it's impossible to know what you got wrong.

Ayvaci is a really good guy and he seemed to care a lot about his students. That given, he typically summarizes the readings during his lectures but his tests had questions over small details that were from the textbook or case readings, so be sure to read everything and take good notes. He usually has a quiz at the end of each class so don't skip.

Ayvaci is a nice guy, but his lectures are boring and hard to pay attention to. Participation is mandatory as he takes attendance, the online textbook is dense and his lectures are just him re-telling the material in the most boring and long way possible. There's also SO MANY layers to this class so being on top of everything can be overwhelming

His lectures are extremely boring, and the material you are being tested over is very hard to pick out. He simply talks about different businesses and generalizes everything where when you're studying for the test you don't know what to study. There is a lot of reading and you're quizzed on it but its impossible to know it all. Excel assignments...

She's a really interesting teacher with great lectures. She made reading classic texts a lot more fun and she introduced many themes and elements of the stories that I never realized were present. Lots of reading, but you do get to read Game of Thrones a lot in Classics and Modern Fantasy. Essays were rough but debates and discussions were fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: For a course with a writing flag, it is, in my opinion, a surprisingly small amount of writing overall. There is fair bit of reading though, but nothing awful. Participation is graded for the class, but if you're quiet she understands that and just wants to hear your thoughts every once in a while during discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors out there. She is there for her students and provides helpful feedback. If you make an effort to show her that you care about the class, she will reciprocate. She is also extremely easy to talk to, and overall an amazing person. I enjoyed her humor & enthusiasm very much.

I was one of the lucky ones in his class and scored an A but most of my class failed. He was so confusing if he was going to take the original paper/test or the retake one for the final grades. You were one pins and needles waiting for your report card. He really shouldn't be teaching Intro to Shakespeare, expects far too much.

I took this professor in the mid 1990s, and from these reviews, it sounds like he hasn't changed much.  Terrible instruction.  Abusive to students.  Loves to give Fs.  He certainly knows Shakespeare, it's just a shame he can't teach it.
just awful.  soul crushing.  i changed departments because i thought this was what all english profs were like. took years to realize it was just him.

Took this professor many years back. Shakespeare at Winedale made a significant change in my life, for the better. Still not sure how much is Doc's teaching and how much is the experience, itself. Winedale was like bootcamp and this had both it's positive and negative sides. If I had it all to do over, I still would have taken the course, anyday.

He failed my entire class on the majority of our papers.  But EVERYONE failed on the first essay.  He gives at least 35 pages of reading per night, and then a quiz over the readings the next morning.   I dropped his class along w/ 19 other students and we are working on a petition to have him removed from our college.  DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!
No Comments

Wow. This jerk taught my first UT course in 1989 & I'm dismayed to see he's still up to the same sadistic garbage. He knows Shakespeare but wd rather bully than teach. On the 1st paper, he failed every student in the class (all had placed out of fresh comp) except 1, whom he gave a prize for a C.  I dropped (along w 1/2 the class) & took Prof Velz.
extremely unclear as to what he wants from you, somehwat rude email...:|

took his class one semester and found shakespeare completely innacessible, failed it. took it with another prof the next semester and she presented it and breathed a life into it  in such a way that I understood it and enjoy it to this day. made a B.
No Comments

He likes to hand out "F" grades and watch his students squirm. I'll agree that he's interesting but damaged.  He keeps a former Charlie's angel's poorly written term paper in his office as a souvenir.
You can get a lot from him, but expect to take a LOT of abuse. Interesting, but damaged, teacher.
UT is incredibly fortunate to have someone specializing in North African history and with such a passion for it, too.
I took his course last semester. He's a super chill guy and a very caring professor. So underrated.
He clearly loves what he teaches. His lectures are funny at times but always engaging. If you do the readings and pay attention to the lectures you should do fine on his written tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Brower has very enjoyable lectures that are easy to follow. He is incredibly knowledgeable on the subject and seemed to have the answers to any questions asked, no matter how minute. He was also able to direct me to outside resources to supplement the lectures and readings. Great class.
