Graded on only a few assignments, but attendance is mandatory. It is very clear that he cares deeply about the material, and students would recommend this course to all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Brower is one of my favorite professors. He is incredibly knowledgeable, and its clear that he loves what he is teaching. It's somewhat lecture heavy but I really learned a lot through this class. I wish I could take him again, and I highly recommend that you take his class if you can.

I took HIS 310P not HIS306N. A lecture heavy class, but the content is interesting and he's a very nice professor! Compared to my other classes he's also a lenient grader so as long as you engage with the material it's a manageable class. There are discussions but they're not difficult and he leads them well so it's not stressful.

I loved Professor Brower, he's genuine and sweet and very respectful of student opinions. Class is very lecture heavy with some discussion involved. He's very passionate about the topic. Main grade comes from 3 exams which are just an essay question, and he never gives out 100s but I also don't know anybody that scored lower than an 85 so.

very lecture heavy but an amazing professor- one of my favorite classes and i would definitely take another class of his in the future! lots of reading and exams are essays but very manageable and clear!

Actually HIS310P idk why it's not an option. Can't say enough how nice & genuine of a guy he is, super approachable with good vibes all around. Lectures are mostly him talking from a few slides, so go to class and take heavy notes. Make a group to compare stuff with and review consistently. If you're a good writer and study well, you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture-based class with one discussion a week. A fair amount of reading but if you are interested in the class it's fine. Dr. Brower has a deep knowledge of the subject matter and enthusiasm for teaching it. Lectures are long but engaging. He is also flexible with grading if you show effort in class. One of my favorite classes I've taken at UT.
Easy to well in his class as long as you take notes and show up. He is good with flexible deadlines and excused absences. If you like history it is really easy to engage with his material.

His lectures are really interesting and engaging, and guest speakers in that class were also really fun to talk to. He is an easy grader and flexible with assignments. Exam guides are available and he does a good job explaining everything so you don't feel overwhelmed. He will grant extensions if you just email and ask.

I have taken his class before this course and would 100% recommend it. He is very flexible with due dates for both exams and papers. Participation is very easy since there is only one discussion day where you have to speak during the week. The material he covers is really interesting and he is not a hard grader.
Very boring and unprofessional. Better off taking another history teacher

This is a really interesting course and Dr. Brower is an amazing professor that is clearly passionate about his work. This class contains a very high reading requirement, so I advise against this class if you won't have the time to read 6-7 novels.

Professor Brower has been so accomodating with the pandemic. There aren't that many assignments, but he is very lenient and will grant extensions as long as you ask him. As long as you pay attention during the lectures and read the textbook, you can definitely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer, everything is very bland and he talks very slowly. the class is just 2 tests and a paper and he'll be nitpicky in all three of them. The books are also really dry. I didnt read any of them and still managed to do alright. Honestly just take another class bc this one was a struggle to get through

Lots of long lectures. If youre interested in the topic that helps but the lectures themselves can get pretty dry. Only a few assignments but if you take good notes and study you should be fine. Lots of reading and the material is still pretty dry. Overall ok just lots of dry material and reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are only three grades: Midterm, Final, and a Paper. He and his TAs were incredibly difficult graders and wanted the minute-ist of details. He was also very boring to listen to. A deep voice, slow... just put me to sleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gave only three grades in the class - the midterm, the paper, and the final. His lectures were usually very dull, so be sure to pay attention in class. As a history major I did not enjoy the course very much. Should also say that he likes to grade with attendance, so be sure to come to class as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brower is really nice and soft spoken. He is very knowledgeable. The only problem I faced was the grade improvement opportunity. A big paper, two exams and participation grades only. Lots of reading and his lectures are heavy as well. I think anyone with a passion for history would have no problem with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: BCB's class is not for the weak of heart. The grade is based on 2 exams and one essay. I personally loved the subject material in Western Civ in modern times so I thought it was fine, but I knew a bunch of people who dropped because of the lack of grade improvement opportunities.

My classmates didn't like him; I thought he was fine. Long lectures that are heavily reliant on powerpoints, not very energetic, but very knowledgable and fairly helpful. You don't really need to read the texbook, but it's nice to have and occasionally needed. Extra credit is a no-no. You can do VERY well on tests if you prepare enough.

Incredibly hard to listen to her lectures, too boring. Have to take notes in class cause its on the exams and she moves too fast to write things down. Doesn't post lecture slides either. Tough grader. Seems like no matter the situation you may be in there is little to no sympathy. She is not going to set you up for success so you must be on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Beckwith's class is fairly straightforward: attendance is 50%, and the rest of your grade is from exams and a group project. The workout component wasn't too bad most of the time, but every so often, it would be intense. Exams require lots of close reading, so make sure you keep up with the textbook and articles posted on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Classes are relatively easy, workout component isn't bad. You get 2 absences, which you should leave for the end of semester because those workouts are TOUGH. 3+ absences tanks grade 5% each time, so DONT SKIP. Tests are ridiculously tough for a pe class, do NOT take for a PE credit, but if you NEED it for coaching specialization, you'll be fine.

This class is very lecture heavy and you need to take notes because she does not post the slides. The tests are a bit difficult but if you go to class, take notes, and study you will do fine. Definitely not as bad as everyone makes it seem, and she is pretty nice. One group project, 2 tests, final paper and presentation. Attendance is extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class was incredibly boring; attendance doesn't matter too much thankfully because the lectures are hard to sit through. Basically the whole grade comes down to one group project(easy) and the two tests + papers which are a bit more difficult.

Her labs and projects are really fun and useful if you want to be an S&C coach, but they are group projects. Her lectures are reading off powerpoints and they're extremely dull. DO NOT get lulled into a false sense of security though. The exams are very difficult and very specific. Reading the textbook helps a lot.

Don't be fooled by her grading scale, 90+ is an A in the class but she is a harsh grader and it is hard to make an A. Takes off points for things that aren't even in the instructions or rubric. And told me she took off points on my essay bc she basically disagreed with my view on something. Doesn't respond to emails and hard to reach out of class.

Kim was an overall good professor, but she takes attendance and each class you miss is worth 5 points out of 50. Attendance is 50% of your grade, so don't skip. The 2 exams are unnecessarily hard, so be prepared for low test scores. She gives 2 free absences, BUT USE THESE AT THE END OF THE SEMESTER!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: woat! beckwith is an awful lecturer and just reads straight from slides. huge research paper and presentation that she dropped on us the day before they started. literally worst class i've ever had. also a big exam the monday after thanksgiving bc she hates her students

15 page paper. terrible lecturer like i fall asleep almost every class and just read from poorly made slides. only positive is Alec the ta.. if he isn't the ta drop the class asap. assigned an exam the Monday after thanksgiving and didn't listen to any of our complaints about it bc she literally does not care about her students. f her for real!

Dr. Beckwith is clearly competent in the material she teaches. However, her lectures are reading from the slides and they become boring. She has two tests, most of the questions are poorly worded or trick questions and for our unit, the highest 1st test grade was a B. Most students failed. She wont curve. She gets short with dumb questions.
Easiest class I'm taking. Two free absences and she offers extra credit. Beckwith's super helpful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Participation is 50% of grade which is easy. However she gives two tests that require lots of reading and are randomly hard. Also she assigns a long video project. The class is less of an exercise class and more about teaching students how to teach conditioning especially focusing on teaching it to kids. Not what I expected. Gives extra credit
Absolute chiller and the goat. However his lectures make no sense and his handwriting is not very legible. This class was a journey from which I emerged a better person.
goat. rlly cool professor. idk what else to say. i had terrible health in my semester and he is very understanding. goat^2

He's a lot better at teaching than people say. Very accommodating, significant extra credit on the tests, interesting content problems. Good class to take if you don't want to learn differential equations in the boring engineer way. Unfortunately, no idea if he'll be teaching this next spring, because he stopped teaching M 427L-H.

It's almost all about lectures. He replies emails very slowly, but eventually you will get it. Some people don't like his style: old man talks in old-fashion. Personally, I think his teaching reveals perspicacious understanding. If u R self-motivated, he can also introduce topics that you strongly recommend (if the topic is relevent to the course)

Sitting in his class, you can Professor Beckner is brilliant. However, his lectures make little to no sense and are entirely unneccesary. I didn't understand/learn anything in this class and ended up being one of the few that actually failed his test. He didn't grade our final. I honestly ended with a much better grade than I deserved.

Great professor, seriously. He truly understands what he is teaching, but his teaching is non-linear, but still really teaches you what you need to know. You will learn a lot in his classes, not only about the material but about yourself as a student and a learner. Grades you based off of what you understand, problem sets/ tests are challenging.

Dr. Beckner's lectures are very disorganized but contain interesting content that is unrelated to Vector Calc. Lots of extra credit on exams, but don't skip the final even if you think you can (only way to fail the class). Don't come into this class worried about your grade, sit back and enjoy the ride. Self-study the content beforehand if able.

Possibly one of the most bizarre professors at this university. You would walk out of tests thinking you absolutely failed but somehow get an A. Lectures are very disorganized, so just read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Brilliant mathematician (there's an inequality named after him!) but lectures are disorganized and confusing for most students. Exam problems are hard but he grades comically easy (and there's extra credit), so exam averages are typically in the 90s.

Don't try to do problem sets in the last 2 hours. Bad idea. Learned from experience.

His lectures are extremely hard to follow and not worth it at all, but attendance is not mandatory. His tests are very difficult, but he grades extremely easily and it is hard to get below an 80. They are worth 75% of the total grade. Homework sets can be a bit confusing but overall the most helpful part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Becker's lectures are unclear and very disorganized. If you have not already learned the material, you will likely need to self-study. However, he grades vaguely and easily, so it is not difficult to get a good grade. Extra credit is offered. Problem sets & tests are challenging but fun if you approach them with a growth mindset.

If you are okay self-studying and grinding out the textbook, take this class. Professor Beckner is extremely kind and smart, but what everyone else is saying is true; his lectures are extremely difficult to follow and don't make sense if you aren't paying extremely close attention. He responds to emails, just grind textbook and you'll be fine.

It's easy to put in little effort and still do well in this class if you have a good study group. For those who want an excellent math experience, the more you put into this class, the better off you'll be. Beckner is brilliant but he can be tough to keep up with. You must think creatively for this class. Don't take if you want cut-and-dry math.

REALLY easy grader, as long as you write something on the test you'll get an A. He's a smart guy, but not the greatest at actually teaching the concepts covered in class. Lectures are all over the place and often confusing, problem sets can also take a while to understand. You'll get a good grade, but most of the class is just self-studied.

The more open-minded you go into this class, the better off you'll be. The core of what you need to know for exams will be reviewed in TA discussions - his lectures are more "for fun". Exams are graded off of how much effort you put into understanding the topic (very vague). Treat problem sets as puzzles, take breaks when you need them.

Professor Beckner's lectures are extremely disorganized and make no sense most of the time. He writes phrases down and circles them, and rarely makes any clear statements. If I didn't know the material already, I'd probably have to self study every single day. He is a very easy grader, though, and the problem sets are fun and challenging.

Other reviews are pretty much on point--lectures are difficult to follow, ended up going to barely any of them. The grade is pretty free for the most part, especially if you're willing to put in the time to learn it via the textbook/khan academy/other online resources. Psets take a while and require some critical thinking, be warned. Don't overload

Can you believe that 22 hrs before grades are due to the registrar, we still don't have any of 3 midterm grades back and only half the class's final exam grades were released? (Update: remaining finals grades came out today, letter grades were posted w/ no updates on midterms.) Would not have survived alone, talk to fellow students and your TA.

He is incredibly smart, and if you love math, I would highly recommenced trying his class. Fair warning, it is nothing like the regular sections, and is far from any traditional math class (very difficult). If you really love deeper, higher level math, it is a really interesting class and prof. Grades light, but think carefully before diving in!

Beckner is so smart and is an awesome professor. However, his lectures can be difficult to follow and he covers more of the big picture rather than explaining how to work out problems. It is important that you teach yourself how to work out the topics he discusses. He is very very understanding if you have a conflict as well.

Dr. Beckner is very intelligent provides a lot of insight to his students. I have come to miss listening to his thoughts at the beginning of class. That being said your TA and classmates are your friend as lectures can be hard to follow. He is an easy grader and is flexible but you will put a lot of time and effort in this class but it's worth it

Professor Beckner is a renowned mathematician, but he teaches way outside the scope of the course. Grading criteria is VERY unclear. Assigns hard hw and tests that you'll have to figure out yourself. Skips his own office hours, only really accessible by email. Good thing is he's a really easy grader and if you put in effort, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have a love-hate relationship with Beckner. I stopped going to lectures after the 1st week, cause this man opened his first lecture with LinAlg-type hard proofs that made no sense. I self-studied the class and I recommend anyone taking him to do so. He lacks communication, tests take 16 hours given 3 days to do them, but he's a super easy grader.

I was skeptical of the other reviews before I took this class. They are somehow all accurate. I wish I already knew the subject beforehand so I could understand his lectures and enjoy them. You need to either know this subject in advance or make friends with someone who does to do well. Extremely generous grading policy - extensions & extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: (F'20) If I'd had to learn only from his lectures I would have dropped out. Your TA, textbook, and classmates will be v important. Beckner is v intelligent and his brain could power the continental U.S. for several years but tho you'll prob get an A bc ez grading I'm not sure the mental distress is worth. He teaches way above the scope of the class

Lectures are hard to follow, and the test questions are extremely difficult. Refused to round my 89.9% to an A- (90%). Will only take again because hes the only professor for another course required for my degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Beckner is obviously intelligent, just not that good of a teacher. While I was interested in the course material, I stopped going to lectures because they were incoherent (irrelevant tangents). But, after I resigned to teach myself, I found the work sort of inspiring. It was an easy A and provided some interesting problems to tackle on my own.

Look: Beckner is smart, kind & cares ab the subject. The issue is the man is so far above us mere mortals in terms of brainpower that he cannot for the life of him actually teach. I passed the class bc of his generous extension & grading/EC policy, but I learned nothing. Put in effort, get an A: but if you need to understand math, find another prof
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Beckner is a true gem of a professor. He has very high expectations for his students and expect them to think at a very high level. That said, he grades pretty easily. However, you will have to work for the grade: this class is not a cake walk, but if you put in the effort, you will be truly rewarded with his unique perspective.

(Fall 2019) Each lecture will be extremely daunting and difficult to follow at times. If you are daunted, just know that lectures are just given at a super high level of understanding that can only really be appreciated with higher courses of math. If you don't understand the lectures, don't worry. HW is really hard, but awarding & essential.

Beckner is incredibly smart and he provides an unconventional/sophisticated perspective on his topics. Due to this, a lot of the material goes over the young students' heads and he doesn't realize it. You will struggle in this class. But he grades easily: show that you care about learning and you will be rewarded, both GPA-wise and intellectually.
Not worth going to lecture. Get the topic list and study by yourself. The week of the exam go to the review lecture and he will write which exact problems will be on the test.

Beckner is a lion trapped in a cage he paws at interesting problems hoping to get into more advanced topics. But often if you font follow him completely you will be as lost as a hyperbolic doughnut. He pities the weak and rewards the luck bestowed and those who knew how to do the test have a free life. Just bring something to trap the lion.

If you're one of those people on their phone/computer in class, then you will be confused by his lectures. If you pay attention, you still probably will be confused. HOWEVER, the parts you do understand are more enlightening than any other teacher you have, and give you the insight of a real mathematician. Also he grades super easy so dont worry.
Emailed him the night before an exam that I didn't feel prepared for the exam. He responded with "When would you like to take it?" Took it two weeks later. No kidding.

An interesting professor, his lectures are just on whatever topic he feels the need to talk about that day. Often he discusses how one should approach proofs and techniques. He never attends his own office hours either so learning the actual material is completely on you. That being said hes a soft grader and will respond fairly quickly by email.

He's literally the worst. His lectures are nonsense. He just writes down keywords and puts boxes around them on the blackboard. He somehow convinces himself that he's taught us something at the end of each class. I can't believe that he gets paid for this. Its honestly insane.

The bad: Wow, his lectures are AWFUL. I consider myself to be great at math but his lectures make no sense to me, so I just stopped going. Nothing he says makes any sense, I have to learn from online resources. The good: HILARIOUSLY EASY GRADER. No homework or quizzes, just 4 really easy tests and a final. You'll make an A if you teach yourself.

Beckner's class was hilariously easy if you taught yourself. His lectures didn't help much and he went on tangents a lot. The TA we had was awful. If you can learn by yourself, 5 exams at 20% each shouldn't be too hard to get an A.

Having no calc experience in High School and having to take 408C and 408D for the first time here at UT, 408D was tough. She goes really fast, and the tests are worth a lot of your grade. I had to drop it due to academic and personal reasons, but she was an amazing professor. She is super kind, funny, and knows her stuff. :)
difficult and goes too fast

Dr Stepp is a good professor - you can tell that she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Participation and attendance aren't mandatory but may be rewarded with extra credit. Her lectures are fast and the content is difficult. I often had to supplement lectures with textbook readings to get a full understanding.

Prof. Stepp is a great professor, though she sometimes speeds up significantly, which can make her difficult to follow. She's also a generous grader and very funny. A substantial portion of your grade comes from homework, so be sure to complete it correctly and submit it as instructed. She also provides a review for every exam.

It was a very easy class if you had taken AP Calc BC in high school, as the first two exams covered material from that course. Prof. was good, but sometimes taught fast. The exams were simple and straightforward; they took questions straight from the homework.

WHAT A PROFESSOR! I cannot stress how simple and relaxing she made this class. Most notes were posted online + zoom and so I barely attended any discussion sessions and self-studied then. There are no quizzes and attendance is not mandatory either. Literally 3/4 of the exam and midterms are the Quest homework, so make sure you go through that!!

Professor Stepp is a really really good teacher and if you put the time to get to know her and engage in class, you'll definitely end with a 95+. Also make sure to do the learning modules, as those help a lot when topics get confusing. Great class, and I highly recommend for anyone taking M408D. ** The course can go a lot faster than others though

Professor Stepp was very nice, friendly, and really approachable. Exams are worth a lot, but they're pretty similar to the homework questions. The assignment load is just Quest homework and a learning module before each lecture. I wouldn't take her again because I found her teaching style a little too complicated for me, but she's great overall.

Professor Stepp has amazing lectures and she even has a Zoom set up before every class starts for those who might need it for whatever reasons. The notes themselves are amazing. When it comes to what the grade is broken into, the tests do play a more significant part in the course, but if you do all the learning modules and hw, you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, makes the class easy

If you've taken Calc 1, you'll be fine in her class—she teaches like a TA and assumes you already know the material, so no step-by-step explanations(very fast, even in new things). Even the learning modules feel like review, and I often feel like I'm missing something. You'll need to self-study and prep in advance, or you'll fall behind.

Professor Stepp was amazing! I took her for both M408C/M408D. Exams are ~ 70% of your grade but there is extra credit. Just beware, the online format isn't for everybody, there is quite a bit of homework (Quest Learning Modules & Homeworks and Gradescope Worksheets), and she may not be the best option if you've never taken calculus in high school.

She seemed like a great helpful teacher, but I do not recommend taking an online class first semester of your college experience. So much will be going on and with her on zoom it was so hard to pay attention. Her homeworks are doable and she graded them on completion. Just PAY ATTENTION and you will get a good grade.

Dr. Stepp wants every student to succeed. She offers extra credit on every exam, simply by showing up. Her exam policy is forgiving; allowing students to drop a midterm, or let their final exam grade be their entire exam grade. This class can be extremely hard if you get behind. The skills learned in this class will be used daily for STEM majors.

Stepp is a nice professors who can make the class enjoyable in a way. She assigns community points where you have to submit photos doing a certain activity, and during exams she provides extra credit if you wear something she specifically asks for. Her exams are manageable, especially for someone like me who doesn't attend lectures.

Prof. Stepp posted all notes online which made it easy to go back and review for exams. In addition to that, the exams are all Quest questions, which made them relatively easy. However, there was a weekly worksheet(TA's went over them during recitation) on top of homework assignments. Go to recitation and do homework and you should get an A.

If you've taken AP Calculus BC before, you'll be fine in Dr. Stepp's M 408D class; if not, it will not be easy. She teaches very quickly, almost as if she assumes everyone has already taken Calc BC before, and there is a crazy amount of HW between weekly Quest homeworks, pre-lecture learning modules, and weekly worksheets. Nice prof; hard class.

Dr. Stepp is a great instructor. Her lectures were very clear and concise. She teaches math in a very non-pedantic way, focusing mainly on understanding, instead of formalism. I would recommend her to anyone who is looking for a M408D professor.

if you have to take M408L, take professor stepp. she's a great teacher, and makes her lectures interesting. she's super nice and, despite calc 2 being notoriously hard, made it much easier for me to understand with her teaching methods. she actually goes into detail when it comes to answering questions, and explains every step thoroughly.

Dr. Stepp is amazing! This class is a lot of work and can be difficult, but it's very doable. The exams are very similar to the homework, so make sure to do them. Her midterms are in person, with 11 questions, but she only counts it out of 10, and you can get 5 points extra credit for wearing something specific.

Amazing professor. Tests are taken straight from the homework problems except for maybe one or two per test. She is always there to answer questions and help her students. She gives out 5 free points per test for wearing something silly to the exam. The TA's are not great at all but Dr. Stepp is amazing. Recommend!

I would 100% recommend her she is very funny and caring, but be warned this is an online class so if you don't do well in online classes I would recommend you to take an in-person class instead. The reason why I failed this class was 100% on myself and not on the professor. You will be fine on the exams as long as you do well on the homework.

Great professor, unfortunately calc 2 is just a very hard subject to learn. She's very accessible if you need her and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. I took the web based class so it was easy to ignore lectures and fall behind but if you keep up with your work you'll be fine.

Stepp is a nice person however she cannot teach. She seems all over the place and after years of teaching she seems to still be winging it. If you don't have a strong calculus background already, don't take the class, the classes reenforces calculus materiel, it doesn't teach it.

LOTS OF HW: pre-lecture assignments, quest homework, and recitation worksheets. Answers and explanation for recitation ws are given during its time slot so make sure to show up. Tests are worth a lot but are very doable if you have done the hw and paid attention in lecture. Prof is very engaging but she does teach pretty fast.

Dr. Stepp was an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and there is always an opportunity for 5 extra points on every test for wearing a specific shirt, a hat, etc. This was an online class and her lectures did not have mandatory attendance but the recitation sessions twice a week were taken for a great. Would 100% take again.

She's very kind and you can tell she cares about her students. I rated this class a 2 on difficulty because I already took calc in high school, but she's still a great professor in general.  She also gave us extra credit for ALL our tests (including final) just for wearing a specific shirt. Recitations were also great for extra practice.

Stepp was hilarious and she definitely made calculus fun at times. You'd definitely need prior calculus experience for this class, especially with how fast she moves and the class being online. Offered silly extra credits for each test and throughout the semester. Quest HWs are hard, but it's good prep for the tests which are mainly Quest.

Professor Stepp was my favorite professor this semester! She cares so much about her student's success and overall happiness in the course. I felt like she was so easy to talk to and connect with. She is also funny which helps during lectures that can be quite boring because of content. Do be warned though, this class is NOT a cake walk, study!

Professor Stepp is clearly passionate about teaching math and wants each student to succeed in her class. The classwork is fairly constant with a couple of assignments every week but it is fairly manageable. Although the weekly homework is hard, the course work overprepares you for the much easier exams.

I absolutely adore professor Stepp! She's hilarious and extremely kind, and her lectures are very understandable. Her lectures are easily understandable even though the class is online. The homework can be pretty difficult, but it's great practice for the tests, especially since the tests are much easier than the homework.

Prof. Stepp definitely cares about all her students! Although I took the course online, she's very accessible out of class. Her lectures were easy enough to understand. She assigns a lot of weekly hw, but it's definitely worth doing to help understand the concepts and do well on the tests, around the same difficulty. I would definitely recommend!

To be honest, I stopped listening to lectures less than halfway through the semester. From when I was paying attention Stepp was cool and funny at times, concepts weren't too hard. I taught myself the concepts on the days I didn't pay attention, easy for sure. She does do group projects so get ready to collab. Not a bad class but nothing amazing.

Dr. Stepp is an amazing lecturer! However the class is SO fast. If you don't have calc experience, you will be fine if you pay attention/study enough. There's easy participation points and harder quest HWs, but if you review each/do practice problems, you will be in great shape for the exams. 3 exams, all very straightforward and have extra credit.

If you are looking for a math class that involves actual math, then this is not the class. However, since I needed the credit, I took it and I do not regret it. She was very nice and understanding. She puts you in new groups every project (she does not assign exams) and it is easy if you do the work. Homework is easy depending on the chapter.

Stepp has a great attitude, super sweet, friendly and passionate. Following the online format was a struggle. Forced groups and break out rooms. Also there is very advanced math involved. Much harder than I expected for a entry level course. The text book is also super weird. If you are bad at math, I would not recommend take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Stepp was an amazing professor and I could only wish that she was an in-person course. The homeworks were hard, but once you figure out the homeworks then the exams were very easy. The exams were nothing compared to the homeworks. Very caring and funny professor. Highly recommend.

I've had Professor Stepp twice now... She's awesome! I love her lectures because she is so entertaining. She really cares about her students and is very open to feedback about the courses she teaches. Highly recommend her to anyone! I took her geometry course, and while it was her first time teaching it (I think), she did a great job!

Took the class online and did have to put a lot of effort into it. Stepp does a really good job of explaining concepts and solidifying what you need to know. Tests are difficult, but its Calc 2, so thats expected. There are a lot of ways to prepare for them (practice tests, review hw). Stepp was very helpful as a teacher though.

Professor Steps is great at explaining Calculus concepts. The weekly homework is discussed during the discussion sections. The tests are out of the homework and the test review worksheets which she posts. The only reason I got a B+ and not an A is because I did not do the test review worksheets.

This course was online and attendance at lectures/discussion was not mandatory. Lectures were recorded and TAs were super helpful. The only downside to this course is that the grade only consists of tests (3+final) and Quest homework (2ish a week). Not much curving on exams but Prof. Stepp offers lots of practice problems, reviews, & sample exams.

I absolutely loved her and truly enjoyed her lectures, HOWEVER she does not always elaborate on things properly. If this is your first time taking calculus then I would advise you to look for another professor. Though she graded fairly your grade was solely reliant on tests and homework. Her lectures were great but they just weren't suited for me.

While the class is virtual and attendance was optional, she does a great job at explaining the content of the course. She's very caring when it comes to her students. Homework is done weekly through Quest and while there are some odd difficulty jumps in the questions in homework, the TA's are helpful during office hours and discussions.

Dr. Stepp teaches remotely over Zoom, but she still makes a connection to the students and brings an energy to class that keeps you engaged. The class moves pretty quickly, but there is a ton of practice available. The tests are pretty short though, so if you don't know the material, your grade will reflect it.

I took calc in high school so that definitely helped me do well in the class, but I'd only recommend that people take this class online if they're very motivated. Lectures aren't required and they're recorded, so it's easy to fall behind. To do well, I'd recommend watching lectures and studying quest (both cover questions similar to the exams).

Lectures were average but easily understandable. Curves heavily for exams and gives tons of extra credit. First exam was OK but weedout. Second exam was extremely difficult, but curved nearly 20pts. Final was easy (all simple MC - no hyperbolic fns) and had 10pts of extra credit. Notesheet for 1st 2 exams. HW was easy but long. Lowest exam dropped.

She replaces your lowest midterm with your final if she thinks it'll help. No curves. Teaches this more in a review-style than as completely new material. If you don't have a strong foundation, this will be a hard class. You need to know your trig; goes further than just sin/cos/tan and this course assumes mastery of arccos/csc/sec^2 stuff.

If you haven't taken calc in high school, this class will be difficult because it is online. However, Dr. Stepp is very passionate and tries to connect with the students. Make sure to do the practice problems and homeworks to understand the material. Sometimes test questions are pulled from lectures. Multiple choice questions are similar to quest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stepp seems like a kind person, but she is not a good calculus professor in the slightest. I have never received an A-, but I ended barely passing the class. The tests were nothing like the homework, which the TA had quite a difficult time explaining. Test averages were as follows: 64, 70, 66. Don't expect a curve or help, it isn't coming
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Stepp is amazing! I didn't take calculus in high school but still get an A. She explained the materials clearly and easily to understand, and also gave us a lot of practice to prepare for the exam (extra practice and not graded, totally up to you do it or not). I got 74 on the first exam, but things will get better if you put in enough effort.

Prof. Stepp would've been so much more enjoyable if this class wasn't asynchronous. If you haven't taken AP Calc AB or BC in high school, this class is really tough as the topics are taught very quickly. The grading criteria are just the hw and then the exam average which could really kill your grade. If you can skip 408C, then skip it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was challenging because it was asynchronous. TA discussions were super helpful! Dr. Stepp seems like such a fun person and I would love to have her in person. She takes feedback into consideration. Because of the online aspect, it's more difficult to grasp concepts, so definitely have some kind of calculus background before taking. Great person.

I think Professor Stepp is a good person, but her lectures do not help prepare you for exams at all. Only take this class if you have taken and are confident in calculus already, as the material is taught as if students already know calculus, and lectures are generally kind of all over the place.

The lectures are different from the homework, the homework different from the tests, and the tests different from the lectures. Either extremely basic questions on the homework or questions you never talked about before and have no idea where to start. Beware if never taken calculus before. Material taught like a review instead of brand new.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a good professor but do not take this class unless you are 100% confident in calc from previous experience. Specific content in lectures, homework, and exams all differ a bit so I often went into exams not knowing what to really expect. She does provide worksheets to practice and makes an effort to answer everyone's questions in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Online class but in person tests. Her lectures are nothing like the homework and the homework is nothing like the exam. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is difficult for people who weren't really exposed to intense calculus in high school. She teaches like everyone already knows the material and moves very fast. Especially since this class is online, I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I definitely think Stepp is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. Even on zoom she was engaging and SO FUNNY. She makes sure to break down concepts. Her exam could be tricky but at the end she adjusted the grading scale and bumped up a ton of people because SHE CARES. 1-2 Quest Homeworks a week, 2 midterms, and a final. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

All online because she teaches in-person at NYU. She is probably the most engaging online prof I have and will ever have. Loved her! You have two homeworks a week and graded by 2-3 tests + final. The only reason I didn't do as well was truly on me for not paying attention or putting math on the backburner. If you pay attention, u will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you haven't taken intense math classes in high school or are well versed in math, you will not do well in this class. Stepp moves quickly and does not teach what is on the homework. Her tests are multiple choice, which is extremely difficult in a calculus class compared to free response. Be warned, this class is very difficult.

Lots of homework, but it's all pretty easy. Dr. Stepp is a really great person, but she is clearly checked out of teaching at UT. She literally lives in NYC and is a professor at NYU, and this class clearly isn't a priority of hers. She is pretty much unreachable outside of class. Grade is 60% tests, 25% final, 15% homework. Basically Calc AB.
I took Calc in highschool and stepp was better. The class is really easy to follow pace wise. If you dont get topics there are a lot of chances to improve your skills. Tests are clear and fair.

Professor Stepp is so sweet. She is genuinely a nice person. Her lectures were always fun to listen to (although I found myself skipping a few). I felt her class was relatively fun if you do the work, or already have a basic understanding of calculus. She had homework through quest, but that was also easy and helpful for tests.

I took Calculus in high school and pretty much knew everything already, so it was great that attendance wasnt mandatory. I just did the homework and exams through quest and was able to exempt the final. Never went to the lectures.

absolutely loved her lectures, you do have to put in work outside of class to make a good grade, but even in a virtual format, she makes things easy to understand. She made the lectures easy to get through and always does her best to make sure we're getting the concepts. She makes a somewhat difficult course easy.

I feel like the class was haphazardly set up and our TA was nonexistent. The lectures were sometimes helpful but oftentimes not and we were often left to our own devices to figure things out. Quest is annoying at first but then you learn how to use it. Her grading was fair 20% for three tests and 1 final worth 25%. The final could replace your low

Stepp is caring and kind, but I didn't learn anything from her. She doesn't teach the material well, and I can imagine that if you didn't take calculus before, her course will be difficult. Her exams are ok.. they are on Quest, so if you do a lot of review problems the exams aren't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Stepp is a very kind and caring prof, she is very genuine and wants us to succeed. The only downside is UT's Quest system, but as a professor, she is great. 2 homeworks a week(ish), 3 exams, and final.

Great professor! Gives about two homework assignments each week which do not take too long to compete. Tests are fairly simple if you do your homework and make sure to go to OH's if you don't understand a problem. Tests are very similar to homework problems. She is super nice and tries to keep her students engaged.
She is amongst the best professors I have ever had. Incredibly helpful, she takes you along the journey without stealing it. Ideas were crystal clear, she makes sure that you know them.
Great Teacher
Great professor, structures the class so its actually hard to get a bad grade. Lots of online Quest homework makes for good practice, no need to go to class, all tests are exactly like quest.

I hate math and find it very difficult. This class was ALOT of work but she gives you every opportunity possible to do well.She is the most caring professor I have had at UT. I would take her again in a heart beat and recommend her to everyone. She creates videos, learning modules etc to make you do well. TAKE HER
very nice and class doable. be careful though, it's easy to get a B tough to get an A

Professor Stepp is one of the best professors at UT. She genuinely cares for each and every one of her students. She explains things thoroughly and makes sure you understand before moving on. She gives lots of things away for attending class (so go!) and her videos teach you step-by-step processes for learning. Overall wonderful teacher and class

Stepp was GREAT! She helps her students so much even in a big class she tried to make sure everybody was following (even though some students fell behind badly). Their is a lot of HW involved but it basically is your study for exams. Regardless of what class she is worth trying.
Great Professor! very helpful and friendly. Smart in Math, very good in keeping you attentive. I strongly recommend this prof.

Took stepp for precal. Its a lot of work with homework, learning modules, challenges and drills that are required and are a % of your grade. She really wants students to learn the material and explains very well. Keep up with the material and you will do fine.
Best math teacher Ive ever had, so funny and sweet. She genuinely cares about math, and about her students. Requires a ton of homework, but its worth it to have such a good teacher.
Great Teacher... Go to class and ask questions, she loves it.. Test are just what she goes over and quest problems.
The best math instructor ever. Listen to every advice she gives and trust me you will get a B or above.

The class was pretty easy, she moves at a pretty slow pace. If you take notes in class and do at least the Quest homework you will know the material. If you do the bookwork too, then you will know it well and do well on the tests

I didn't get to take Calculus in high school which is why I didn't do as well as everyone else. She's a really good professor. Her tests are challenging but people who have taken Calculus before ace them. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS! She's really helpful and she wants you to do well in her class. I loved her!

she wanted students to do well, but the hw was a killer, and both her and the TA's office hours were during my other classes so I couldn't get help from them. devoted the majority of my semester to math hw and then q-dropped b/c I had to ensure a high grade for a transfer into engineering.  was fun though and encouraged students to learn. reccomend

She teaches basic problems during lecture and gives hard ones on homework. She also wastes a lot of time reteaching concepts that should be part of the prereq course.  She also makes mistakes frequently during lecutre.

I took her Cal I for CNS. Shes a good teacher (excellent at explaining) and really doesn't want you to just learn the rules (she spends a lot of time proving them). The first test was EASY, but the second was too long to finish in the allotted time. She curves & doesn't do plus/minus. Tests= 5 mult choice and rest are free response (partial cred)

She's really nice and really cares about her students. It's a little difficult to get a hold of her outside of class, but she's good with email. I do wish she wouldn't have taught as much as she did with material that wasn't in the book and had started with the basics (like truth tables, etc.) rather than jumping straight into proofs.

She is a nice professor, but there are LOTS of readings give to you every week. You have to read these textbooks and readings for the short answer/essay questions on the exams. Unless you already have a good knowledge in this field, I would not recommend you taking her class as this class takes too much of your time.

Professor Beach is a fine professor and seems very passionate about research in her field. This class is easily approachable if you have taken some other stats classes but is probably not worth it if not. Lectures are pretty boring but she is forgiving, lenient, and overall a nice person. Labs are pretty easy but exams were a little too dense also.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Slow, boring, intro level course. The final was too long and like only one person in the room finished it in the time allotted. She's really kind and seems very approachable, but honestly if you can help it, don't take this class at all. 
She's allegedly very passionate about water quality, but I didn't see any passion in this course.

I liked Beach just fine, but the lectures are quite boring, and I relied much more on the textbook for the tests than anything in lecture. I read the book and did just fine, and I found some of the content interesting, but the class itself could be extremely dull. Overall, I think it was worth to take for the credit I needed. My TA was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor did not follow her own attendance policies written in her syllabus. If you're looking for a class for your natural science credit, this one isn't it. Extremely boring, not worth it.

Not only are the lectures unbearably boring, but they often skim information in a way that doesn't even match up with what's on the exam. Certain exam questions are purposely made to be confusing, like using interchangeable words for a process as options with a definition that doesn't even match the terms used in book. Doesn't care about you at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are extremely hard and you have to learn lots of information. Do not take this class. The TA's do not really know the content and a lot of the work is by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Did not care about the students. Grades a test based and hard and lab depend on your TAs and they aren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor. Does not care and is the most boring lecturer. Seems to be unprepared to class. The class average on the first exam was 76. TAs are not helpful. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR AN EASY SCIENCE CREDIT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Beach. Her lectures were a little dry, but she knew what she was talking about. 60% of the grade is based on three exams, all multiple choice. They're difficult, but not too bad. A lot of textbook reading. Getting an A is tough, getting a B is easily attainable as long as you do the stuff. The lab & TA section was pretty chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Process Geomorphology w/ Dr. Beach. She is very passionate about her research and what she teaches. 75% of course grade is based off 2 exams and a paper. Exams are over very dense material and can be hard to study for due to format of some questions. Easy grader on non-exam assignments. Also is nice and cares about your learning and wellbeing.

very boring lectures but unfortunately, that's where majority of the exam content comes from. textbook can also be used in place of lecture. Labs are easy and online, can be done very independently if needed. tests are worth a lot towards overall grade, labs are a good amount of grade, quizzes are small part of overall grade

Dr. Luzzader-Beach is passionate about geography and is welcoming and kind to all students. I loved all of the content and spent a few hours outside of class reading and taking notes over the textbook before filling in the rest of my notes during lecture, which made me successful in the course, but it was hard to stay awake in class sometimes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is really nice. However the tests are extremely hard and you have to learn lots of information. Do not take this class, tests are 60% of your grade. The TA's do not really know the content and a lot of the work is by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures might have put me to sleep at one point, but the content is great and she gets the message out really well. She's caring and will work with you if any issues arise. Her labs weren't too tough, but be aware that some time may be needed outside of class to get a good grade on a lab. Reading the book and going over slides will help tons.
I thought I was the only one the reviews are spot on. Nightmare class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this class to anyone who cares about their GPA. No form of exam prep, heavy reading material, no consideration for working students, not enough time on exams and condescending about grading. Majority of the class did poorly on the exam so we'll see how the next one goes. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM! I have NEVER struggled in a class like this before as a straight A student. He gives 50 min exams where we have to write an essay, 3 additional paragraphs and analyze 3 documents by hand. I studied so hard only to fail due to lack of time. VERY strict about small details and makes the class incredibly hard to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No exam review and very vague on what will be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You have to pay attention, she is very nice and sweet.
Very passive aggressive.

Pani Kaminska was truly one of the best professors I have had in my life. She was incredibly fun and I loved how we also learned about Poland's culture. The small class size allowed us to get individual help and do lots of group work. Definitely take her class!

This is a hard class in general, but I would say he is the best professor to take it with. The homework are 10% midterm is 40% and final is 50% of the grade but his curve is the only reason I passed. As long as you show up and take good notes you should have an easier time on the exams. Try to find people to do homework with to help you understand.

The class is very interesting and the problems are fun.... when you are given effective material to work with. Homeworks do not prepare us for exam questions and often take multiple hours to do. I got myself sick once because of how much time it took to do one homework. The material is very interesting, just study as much as you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: High stakes exams (Midterm 40% and Final 50%). No recorded lectures, but lecture notes are posted. Homeworks (10 total, 2 drop) are good practice for the exams. Midterm and Final are curved for fairness for those unable to attend midterm (Final 90%). I would recommend staying on top of the course material as falling behind can easily overwhelm you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bhaskar is a smart man which is why it's so easy to get confused when he explains. Watch videos for clarity and DO additional practice problems. There is one midterm worth 40% (avg ~60) and one final worth 50% (avg ~68). I got below average for both exams and got a B so he curves good. DO NOT WAIT LAST MINUTE FOR STUDYING. Keep practicing activley.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never took the course. He seems like a chill guy, though. I spoke to him a couple of times in person, and he is very knowledgeable about the subject matter he is teaching. I didn't fully follow everything because the class was not related to my major :( I would highly recommend taking any class that he teaches!

He's a great guy I really enjoyed going to class and learning about asphalt lol :). He always listens to the class in terms of making open notes or group quizzes. You can work on homework's in groups and the final exam was open notes. The final was pretty similar to the in person quizzes we took in class. Overall great guy and interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took him for design of Bituminous Materials. Very knowledgeable about the subject and gave great lectures where you really do learn a lot. Quizzes are very fair.

Perhaps my favorite professor at UT, knowledgable, approachable, caring and well-prepared. The project can be a lot of work but is also fun, you learn so much. I would definitely take another class with him.

Amazing professor! Ask questions, you'll get answers. Class centers around the main project which is a fantastic approach, everything you see during lecture gets to be tested/applied on semi-real project scenarios. I recommend this class and this professor.

A fantastic professor, who genuinely cares about the well-being of his students. In his lectures he gives you important background knowledge and information about the assignments. In every class he promotes curiosity and critical thinking. Although the course load is very heavy with multiple research papers, this course will allow you to grow.

Professor Bhat is a pretty good professor. His exams are fair, but he underestimates the time it takes to do them which led to a failing class average on the 1st exam. The class only has 2 exams, mid-term is 30%, final is 40% of your grade, homework is 25%, & participation is 5%. He covers how to do the HW well in class and is an understanding prof

He is a great prof! Super nice, cares about students, explains concepts well. However, there is breakdown in grading with the student grader being SUPER harsh and Dr. Bhat did not accept any feedback on that. Material can get confusing, homeworks are easy but the exams are incredibly hard
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students. There's are one midterm (30%) and final (40%). He pretty much gave us all the answers to the homework (25%) in class so it is important to attended them all (they are not recorded). He made the exams open notes which helped tremendously. If you understand how to do the homework and you go to class you'll be fine.

Dr. Bhat is a passionate lecturer who cares about his students. He always wears a lumbar support attachment strapped to his back which brings me joy. This was my easiest class this semester because the homework is easy, and the exams are cake with the curve. W
Super great professor, he wants you to really learn and understand the material. He loved to get to know students which makes me want to go to class.
Brilliant lecturer, explains difficult concepts in an easy and clear way; also a tough grader.

Dr. Bhat is an inspiring and caring prof. The course isn't too difficult but there is only one midterm and one final (40%) so you have to do well. I wish he went over more examples before the first test because I wasn't ready. Weekly homework isn't bad. Lectures are actually enjoyable and he keeps things interesting.

I left started and ended the course completely confused. No notes except from lecture. The only practice you have are homework problems where he explains half of it and expects you to know the concepts he never went over. Little communication between graders. No TA. He seems like a nice guy but not a great professor at all :/ sooo many tangents

The material itself was super interesting, but Bhat wasn't the best lecturer. His handwriting was sloppy and he went on many different roundabouts that didn't pertain to the content. Any time I contacted him for help on hwk or clarifying grading he would spew off some philosophical nonsense and wouldn't answer my questions
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loved him ,made me want to be a transportation engineer (which I now am). Really enlightened me on daily transportation things I had never thought about before.

Good instructor, worst professor in my life. After class, I asked a calculation question cz I was confused on the concept. He raged because I didn't get the concept. He kept saying "I don't know how you can't get this" over and over. He didn't try to listen to me. I was asking different one first time learning transportation system in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good luck in this class. It will take up all of your waking and sleeping hours
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Get ready to work in this class. The topic he teaches is difficult, but he makes the content even more complicated. Very strict and has no compassion for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is probably the hardest classes that I have taken at UT. The subject itself is very difficult, but Professor Bisetti is extremely knowledgeable on the topic. He is extremely helpful at office hours and I feel that I truly have a good grasp on this difficult subject because of the classes rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bisetti is a fantastic professor. His understanding of and enthusiasm for the topic are unmatched, and he is extremely helpful if you seek guidance outside of class. The course is very difficult, but this is the nature of the subject. I think Bisetti does a good job of making it manageable without losing rigor.

Great professor, made CFD interesting for me and I had no previous interest in it. Really cares about the subject and is really good at teaching it and is great at answering and clearing up any and all questions. Some attendance pop quizzes.

CFD is an extremely hard subject but Prof. Bisetti is obviously an expert and is amazing at teaching it. This class was very hard at the start as sometimes the homework focus on material he hasn't taught yet, but lecture slides are posted before hand. Group project heavy but plenty of guidance is given. Overall, hard class but amazing teacher.

Awesome prof, super fun and great music taste. 610D is the heaviest homework load in the Spanish sequence, but Prof Luke makes it worth it with great, engaging lectures. He's clearly passionate about Spanish and I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Awesome professor and taught the content really well. Just a super nice guy as well. He gives great feedback and is very approachable. There's homework every day, but if you do it there's no way you won't do well. I really enjoyed being in the class.

This Spanish class was time-consuming, but very doable. Doing the homework/online work really helps to understand the grammar and vocabulary. Class was enjoyable because we were able to practice talking and applying what we learn from the workbook. Also, Professor Bishop is very patient and helpful when learning new concepts. Really recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although the textbook did awful job at explaining the grammar, Luke was great at helping you understand. If you didn't get it he would rephrase his explanations until one stuck. Very helpful office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class, as with the Spanish classes at UT, comes with a lot of outside work due to it being a 6 hour credit! He gives great feedback on homework and as long as you put in the effort you will do well in the course! I recommend making quizlets for vocab and using the chapter reviews in the textbook to study for the exams! Participation is vital!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I got a 91 in the class and he gave me a B+ because of his grading system that is not fair

OK professor. Easy quizzes and exam. Complete all possible extra credit because he will try to give you the lowest final grade possible. I ended this class with a 91 and received a B freaking plus as a letter grade.. because of his unfair grading policy. The final presentation policy is a nightmare.

Nice guy w an unfortunate grading policy. His class material is engaging, but competitive nature of the final project makes caring about material>grade difficult. Wants you to read his mind and doesn't go by rubrics well. Said he would curve us down. Also asked for good CES survey scores. If the final wasn't a competition he wouldn't have to ask.
Horrible grading scale

While this class is interesting and Professor Bisett clearly knows a lot about marketing, the grading scale of this class is one of the worst at UT. He curves the class down and 30% of your grade is dependent on a group project, where he shows clear favoritism and the grading scale is unclear. He also frequently used AI for slides.

While the lectures can be interesting at times, the grading sucks. He wants his students to compete in order to get a good grade in the class. The final project is worth 30% of the grade, and if you are not a finalist, you can only get an 80%!! He also cleary has favorite students!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bisett is definitely passionate about marketing and cares for students. But he has inconsistent grading, curves down, and often doesnt follow his own rubric. Tests are easy but the curve down really messes with your grade. He uses AI for slides and tests which make the class feel less personal and is frustrating imo. Wouldnt take again unforch

Pits students against each other because he's curving us down. Wants us to stroke his ego. Uses AI to make all his slides and test questions. Tests are not too challenging but everything else is. Has a problem with almost everything. Don't take him if you don't absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Questions on exams and quizzes are pretty easy. The project is very important; it determines 30% of your grade and is graded more toughly than the other assignments. 30 minute podcasts paired with each chapter. He is lively and tries to encourage participation in class, fun professor. Easily accessible and understanding of student situations.

Professor Bisett is genuinely a very caring person and is a great professor! The class is structured very fairly with exams and a group project. Do the reading and participate in class, and you will be fine in the class.

MKT 357 was easily one of my favorite classes this semester. Prof Bisett genuinely seems to care about his students, and is very flexible regarding deadlines. Grading on projects was initially a little arbitrary. However, this improves a lot if you seek to understand expectations. Overall would recommend.

Great professor and even better person. He is knowledgeable about the subject and engages the class in nuanced discussions. I was consistently surprised at how well he was able to engage the class and encourage participation. He was a bit disorganized, but it was his first semester. He truly cares about each student and it shows.

The content is easy and enjoyable, no exams, but the class is formatted HORRIBLY, and the professor is very confused by his own syllabus. Doesn't know how to use Canvas, not clear about due dates at all. TA mentioned he was about to retire, but I saw he's teaching English classes this summer and fall. Don't take him, just unnecessary stress.

The professor's lectures were very engaging, covering a wide range of topics, and the class exposed me to many films that I wouldn't have otherwise watched, many of which were exceptional and now among my all-time favorites. There are no exams but there are essays, but you can choose the topic of each essay and which film it's about.

Biow is really kind and understanding. He was very lenient with papers and often made accommodations/pushed back deadlines for us. Trips to the Blanton Museum were lots of fun! Only thing is that lectures seemed to be a little self-explanatory at times, but still engaging.

All you have to do is watch the movies, attend the lectures, and write thought pieces/ essays on them. Dr. Biow is passionate about film and the history of Italy, which made his lectures so enjoyable. Discussion sections were unenjoyable because people didn't talk much, though.

Dr. Biow is a great guy, and I enjoyed his lectures for Films and Filmmakers of Italy. All you have to do is watch the movie and be able to write about it. He will give you great feedback and extensions if needed. Mandatory discussion sections with TAs sucked, though, and were not very helpful since nobody would speak or show up. Good UGS choice!
Professor Biow is knowledgeable about the subject matter. Italian Films and Filmmakers was eye-opening and allowed me to gain a lot of cultural understanding.

Professor Biow was amazing. I hate writing, but I actually really enjoyed it. It's not a difficult class as long as you watch the films and can explain a film. Prof Biow gave extensions if students just asked and was all around a nice person to be taught by. I definitely recommend taking his class as a UGS, really easy way to get your credit.

This professor is hands down the type every student should encounter. He is very passionate about the discourse of his subject and encourages students to critically think and relate varying topics to the subject film. 5 Essays, first isn't graded. Quizzes every week about the film. Extra credit is given and they're lenient. Enjoyable and easy.

Very apparent that Biow cares about the subject and class. Biggest recommendation is to go to office hours and get his help he is very clear and helps so much. I don't love writing or analysis and it is one of my biggest weak points however Biow is so understanding and gives extensions if you need. Incredible professor one of the best for sure.
Biow is one of the nicest professors I have ever encountered. He always gave extensions, and always wants to see his students write their absolute best.

Took him for Italian Films and Filmmakers. Lectures were really interesting, even if I had no idea what I just watched in the movies. Definitely a guy who loves to hear himself talk ngl lol. Grade consists of 5 papers, and he grades one of them, rest are by the TAs. Biow himself is a harsh grader, but it's really easy to pull an A in this class.

Although I wasn't very interested in the content (not his fault at all), I really liked this professor. He was super understanding about deadlines, and made the workload very easy. Quizzes at the beginning of each class and 5 papers, with the first one being diagnostic. He gave great feedback and was very easily accessible!

I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would recommend it to everyone. While he is a tough grader, he is willing to help and he gives great feedback. He goes in-depth with his constructive criticism and it helps you improve your writing a lot! Super understanding guy and would give us lots of extensions and extra credit opportunities.

Biow gave C averages on papers despite needing a B to pass. You spend hours outside class watching movies to write 5 papers with prompts released days before the due date. The little feedback you may receive comes 6 weeks after turning the papers in. He did offer an extra credit assignment but it didn't help really anyone. Just take another UGS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Liked Biow, hated the class itself. The good: I rarely attended class and still managed to get an A & the lectures were enjoyable if interested in the subject. The bad: the required films were boring and excessive, and the papers were graded SO HARSHLY. You need to like writing and be somewhat interested in the subject to do well in this class.

Look, I've had ups and downs with this class, but Dr. Biow is a great professor and person despite the strict grading by him and the TAs. However, he became more lenient towards the end of my semester and allowed us to be more creative with our writing. He is willing to help and the classes are comprised of daily quizzes on the movies and 5 essays

Overall, the class wasn't bad. An A and even an A+ is definitely manageable. Especially if you really take the time to go into office hours to discuss your essays with the TAs and Professor Biow. I heard a lot of complaints about this class being too hard for a UGS course but TBH, most people were overreacting and got butt hurt over their essays.

Professor Biow is a great person but his class and these ratings were so deceiving. Most people often found themselves feeling worthless after getting grades back from their papers since they grade them so harshly. The mean for the papers is usually in the 70's range and for a UGS class, it should not be that hard. The films are also so boring.

(Fall 2020) Great class, great guy, watched a lot of movies I rly enjoyed. 4-5 papers to write but the analysis is fun. You won't learn much about cinematic techniques but the way he breaks movies down is interesting. Papers are graded kind of strictly (either by the TA/himself) but he's a really nice guy.

I love Prof Biow. He's so passionate about the films he talks about, and he's an interesting guy. Biow is very willing to work with you on your paper so ask him for help!!!! I had a love hate relationship with this class, but in the end I'm so glad I took Italian film.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biow is the best! He is fun, caring and passionate. You will learn a lot, but you are never graded over it. The info is useful, but not mandatory for your essays. He will help you work through your essays, so PLS TAKE HIS HELP! And you have weekly quizzes but they are easy if you watch the movies. Cherish your time in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Biow is an absolute dream! Although he is a very direct grader for papers, he cares about his students and takes time to help them outside of class on how to improve their writing. Hes passionate about what he does, and it shows. funny guy, kinda like danny devito

Prof Biow is really passionate about what he teaches, which makes it easy to be interested in the course material. There's a lot of papers, so be prepared for that. Don't volunteer yourself to have him grade your paper (as opposed to the TA) unless you're an extremely strong writer because his feedback is intense and brutal (albeit spot-on).

Biow loves what he teaches, which for me, was Italian cinema. He knows how to keep students engaged and has a great sense of humor. He even paid for some of us to see a film off campus. Be ready to write essays 1/2 times a month & a quiz over the movies every class day. Quizzes are easy to get an A on, as they are over basic things. Learned a lot!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Biow's lectures were super interesting and fun. He is a tough grader, but he only grades one essay and he is more than willing to work with you outside of class to improve your essay. Go see him if you want to ensure an A on your paper! There were some really good movies, but a lot of the postmodernism unit movies were disturbing and confusing.

The movies we watched were often depressing but the lectures were very interesting. This class is a writing flag but the amount of writing you have to do is far from outrageous, the final (longest) paper is only 4-5 pages.

I adored this UGS and am so glad I was able to learn from Professor Biow. He is a fantastic lecturer and incredibly passionate about Italian history/cinema. I learned so much, and I actually enjoyed writing the papers! If you like film analysis, this is the class for you. You don't even have to watch all the movies to get an A (though you should).

He is a really friendly professor and definitely has interesting lectures. His expectations of papers are a little confusing and he is a really tough grader. Overall it is an interesting class but the movies are time-consuming.

Dr. Biow's UGS over Italian Cinema was overall a good experience. He is an engaging lecturer and the class was an easy A. He didn't put in grades till the end of the semester but due to weekly quizzes about the films (which were easy as long as you watched), your grade should be fine. Super caring guy and would definitely recommend this class
