His lectures are fun. There's a decent amount of homework (watch a 2-hour film for each class period) and 5 papers over the course of the semester. Dr. Biow is a tough grader but he only grades one of the papers (I made a B- on the one he graded and As on the rest). Papers are on a sliding scale so have him grade your first one.

Great lecturer, but very harsh grader - luckily, he only grades one of your papers and the TA does the rest. Take good notes during his lectures to help you write your papers. There are easy quizzes every class. Grade consists of attendance, quizzes, and 4 essays. Dont underestimate this class, but take it if youre interested in film!

I have taken many classes at UT and I would take Italian Cinema again in a heartbeat. Dr. Biow is so incredibly good at lecturing, I was intrigued every day I went. I even still watch the movies for fun. Writing will be heavy, but he is very willing to help!

I loved this class! Be prepared to write quite a bit, but the films you watch and the lectures about them are well worth it. The subject matter is interesting and unique, and honestly, I learned more about film from Dr. Biow than from the actual  RTF class for my major. If you need a UGS, you should take this class!

Quizzes every week, but they were super easy. Even if you don't know anything about cinema, TAKE THIS CLASS. I loved it more than I expected to. It's a writing flag, so get ready to write. Good GPA booster if you write well. You won't regret taking this class.

Italian Cinema (or Films and Filmmakers of Italy) was, hands down, the best course I enrolled in this semester. Dr. Biow is an incredible lecturer who understands, and delights in sharing, the history and significance of writers, directors, and movements that shaped Italian cinema. Most importantly, he and his TA's are incredibly helpful. Sign up!

Originally, this class wasn't my first choice UGS, however by the end of the semester I ended up absolutely loving it. Dr. Biow is a great lecturer and he always gives his insight on the movies. Although there were essays, the movies were amazing and there was so much to talk about that they were not hard. Take this class, you won't regret it!

His course, carrying a writing flag, requires lots of writing for a 1st-year class. However, you'll definitely learn a lot about writing film analytic paper and to look at films differently in general. You can 'work' with him, meaning he'll personally give you feedback and grade the assignment. Super attentive and friendly. Not ez-A for foreigners.

Considering my lack of writing skills and knowledge of Italian culture and film in general, this class turned out to be really fun. We were required to watch an Italian movie almost every week and they were, for the most part, entertaining. I believe we had 5 papers to do, and they weren't too long. Biow provided awesome insight into the films!

Did not want to take this Films and Filmmakers of Italy class. However, I ended up absolutely loving the class. Biow's lectures are incredibly interesting. Also, you get to watch one old Italian movie every week, pretty much, which is a great time. Learned a lot of valuable life lessons in this class.

I was completely uninterested in Italian Film before taking this class. I only took it because all other options were full. Biow is a captivating lecturer. He speaks passionately, and he makes just about any boring old Italian movie mega entertaining and philosophical in ways that I never imagined a movie could be. Attendance is mandatory.
Really entertaining lectures, he's very interested in his material and excited to be teaching it and talking about it. He's great at generating discussion and answering questions. Awesome class!
Took for Power of Words UGS. Such a fun class and insanely easy. Professor does tend to go on random tangents/talk about nothing. Very little work and it is hard not to get an A.

I literally love this guy. He is so kind and he is very accessible if you miss a quiz or a test. He is extremely knowledgeable and receives questions well. He also does review sessions and goes over your exam 1:1 with you which is reallllyyy useful. The class itself is straightforward and the exams are just like the review.

Joy of French truly was joyful. He cares about the content he is teaching, and it is fun to learn about French curse words, common sayings, and other aspects of the language that typical classes do not teach you. He is passionate and understanding, so this is the 3rd class I have taken with him because he's simply the best. I highly recommend him!

Dr. Birdsong has been my favorite French professor at UT. He is so kind towards each student and genuinely wants you to succeed in this class. This class also greatly improved my pronunciation, and I will truly miss having him as a professor next semester.

Great class to really learn about pronunciation. He's engaging and fun. Writing recommendation letters for multiple people in class. Cares about your individual progress. He gives practice tests and quizzes. Homework isn't too bad but to do well you want to do it. I definitely recommend him for any french class.
Dr. Birdsong is very caring and passionate about French. There are two tests, homework assignments each week, and a handful of quizzes. There is a final project at the end that is not hard.

Professor Birdsong has been my favorite french teacher in the six years I've been learning french. He's very sweet and cares so much about the material he teaches. He goes out of his way to relate to his students and makes accommodations if you don't understand or might not be able to attend lecture.

Birdsong is a very enthusiastic & fun teacher- gets you excited about what he's teaching. He was not originally supposed to teach 317C, so he did not create the material and tests. Prepared us well w/ handouts, practice quizzes, & told us where to find the study material. Pretty generous with grading. Attendance points are self grading after class
Professor treated me with such disrespect that I had to drop the class. If you have disabilities, I do not recommend taking this professor. I suggest taking another upper division French class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: BLANTON IS AMAZING! He gives out plenty of extra credit, and has engaging lectures, as well as he cares immensely for his students.

The written tests can be tough but if you do the reading for real and pay attention to the lecture you should be good.  I will say he is very engaging in his lectures, I'd love to take more classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Blanton really cares about his students and will work with them to make sure they succeed. He's funny and knowledgeable, and attendance isn't even mandatory, but I still go! The assignments aren't hard, but the exams require specific details like numbers and years, which is a little annoying. But, definitely take his class!
I think hes so funny and chill and his class is actually interesting.

Professor Blanton has been my favorite professor at UT thus far. His grading might seem a little harsh or specific, but he gives clear feedback on what he wants to see, and if you follow it, your grade will be sure to improve. A knowledgeable and fun professor, if you need to fulfill your degree plan or need a history professor, definitely take him

absolutely incredible professor!! wish i could take more classes from him!! he's new to ut this semester but great class regardless. took the time to get to know every student individually. essays are graded tough but very clear that he's looking for a very straightforward and structured analysis. avg class is only 30 mins and ec opportunities!
Teacher is good and all midterms are reasonable if studied. However, the final is brutal and class average was a 60. No curves are given.

Dr. V is the GOAT!!!! She is so amazing and super helpful. Whenever I had trouble, I would go to her OH, and she would guide me through the questions/concepts, making it so much easier to understand. She would also check your HW answers during OH, which helped boost my grade sm, and she rounded our grades up at the end. LOVE HERRRRRRRR

Professor is really great at explaining concepts so go to class & OHs. There is extra credit for going to class. Homeworks can be a little difficult, going to OHs def helps. Exam 1 was the hardest because of counting. Exam 2 and 3 are straight forward. Exam 3 is cumulative. Do practice problems and redo homeworks before exams. Go to OH to check hw.

Lectures are a bit boring but she is very passionate about what she teaches. Expectations are clear and formatting is consistent. Rely on practice problems she provides for questions and go to office hours because she is very helpful and easy to talk to.

Dr. V is very sweet, but the class itself is boring. Homeworks are not terrible and going to office hours helps. For exams, Exam 1 is the hardest because it has counting. Just do all the practice problems she gives. You can also see what you get wrong on tests and dispute it if you think you were right. Exam 2 and Final were both straightforward.

The lectures were good, but definitely boring at times. Office hours were very helpful, Dr. Viswanathan was happy to go through our exams with us and regrade them/give points back on the spot when the TA made grading errors. You're given sufficient resources to prepare for all the exams, but the final was surprisingly way harder than the 2 midterms

Very boring lectures, but not her fault (material is boring). Her class is very well organized, limited/delayed feedback on hw, hw every week but easy. 3 midterms, make sure to study and you'll be fine. Posts lecture slides, along with plenty of practice problems/worksheets (do them). Very doable class, work hard and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. V was great! Lectures were engaging, and any and all questions were answered. Biggest tip would be to prioritize the tests (especially the first one). Definitely a great class to get introduced to statistics!

The class is challenging due to the material, but Prof. V genuinely cares about her students and is very accessible during OH. After each exam, she asks for feedback and adjusts based on our input (e.g., removing topics from the final). Extra credit + bumps ur grade if ur on the edge. Go to OH to get ur HW answers checked as HWs are 25% of ur grade

Dr. V is one of the best professors I had. She cares a lot about the class overall. The content gets challenging through the semester, but she is always willing to help you when you reach out to her by email or at office hours. As long as you use the resources she gives (notes, practice worksheets, textbook), it is easy to get at least an A-.

Lectures and tests were tough but that's more a result of the material than the professor. Always very helpful in office hours and gave plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely the better of the two SDS 431 teachers.

Dr. V was super accessible outside of class, very approachable and super nice. Lectures at times can seem boring, but it is statstics and I think she made it as engaging as she could. Overall great course and great professor.

Dr. V is a wonderful person. She's super empathetic about grades and will make sure you succeed if you put in the effort. She is not the most accessible outside class---her office hours are very limited, but she is more than willing to help you if you ask. She provides sufficient practice problems

Lectures weren't bad and homeworks were fair. Exams were okay; however, the final was exceedingly difficult. The questions contradicted what we learned throughout the semester. The final did not reflect concepts from practice problems at all. There's no curve but some bonus points during class. Honestly, the final exam (weighted 25%) was brutal.

Lectures can get very boring and hard to sit through but she is very kind and willing to help. I found myself confused during lecture and then was easily able to grasps concepts outside of class through either videos or outside of class resources. She doesn't explain concepts well but she really does try and stops to help if needed.
Clear, detailed explanation that's easy to follow during class. Very accessible. Tests are similar to homework problems. Lecture slides with answers to problems provided are very helpful.

I really enjoyed her lectures most of the time. At times it can get a little boring but overall they were pretty digestable. Exams are very fair and reflective of the content covered in class and the study guide. HWs are a bit harder than the exams so don't worry too much if it can get a bit difficult at times. Offers extra credit for attendance.

She's a good professor and lecturer. An A is very attainable in this class if you review the material before exams. She is very generous with partial credit on exams. Lectures can feel a little slow at times, and I feel like the material could've been covered in 1 hour instead of 1.5 sometimes. Homework can be hard sometimes, 2-4h/week

Dr. V is super nice and a lovely woman. Her lecture style is great and she loves teaching the subject. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's the only way to learn the material since she doesn't record the blackboard. If you put in one extra hour per week to understand the material, you will have a really easy A. Enjoy!

She's one of the best math professors I've had. Will answer every question that you have during lecture and will make sure you understand before moving on. She's always accessible during office hours and very caring. Exams aren't that hard, and homeworks aren't that bad.

Each class was conducive to learning the content, and the professor often considered students' suggestions in terms of exam content. Attending every class provides 10 extra credit points. Each homework was the right amount of difficulty, with the professor and her TAs available in-person or over Zoom to assist. Even held Office Hours during break.

Weekly homework that I thought was just about the correct level of challenge & covered the material pretty well. Exams were pretty easy/lenient and you are able to bring in a cheat sheet. Lectures were on the slower side, however. Attendance is not mandatory, but you do get a decent chunk of extra credit for attending. The teacher is very nice.

While lectures can get boring as the class is online (with in person exams), lectures are very detailed as are slides and there is an abundance of practice material for you to understand content. Homework is graded hard but exams are fairly lenient. Professor is very nice and will help you if you just ask during office hours.

Best math professor I have had so far at UT. Lectures were well structured and exams were pretty easy. She is very good about answering any questions you may have no matter how basic. Very supportive and caring professor! Homework can be rough depending on TA grading.

Professor Viswanathan relies heavily upon the students past knowledge of probability and statistics and moves quickly over complex lecture material. When questions are asked the most common response is review the lecture slides outside of class. There are no discussion sections for review and TA interaction with the students is non-existent.

Very caring professor who knows the topic well and can teach it well. Accessible during office hours and will explain to you very patiently. Lectures are recorded but extra credit for attending them. Hw is on the harder side, but nw if you miss a couple questions. 2 midterms + 1 final that are doable if you study well. Take good notes!
She's really knowledgeable and really helpful during office hours, but the homeworks were killer and the tests required a LOT of studying and comprehension of the material

Professor Bindu made it clear that she was not going to allow for virtual attendance which means she wouldn't record lectures, even for those who had clear conflicts for some class days or even to study. Class was in the GSB which means that the classroom was set up to record. She just didn't want people to not come to class. Made studying "fun".
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't really enjoy her class at all. My main reason is bc she wasn't very accessible outside of class, as she only had one OH per week & rarely answered emails on time. I usually perform really well in stats, which is why I'm doing a minor in it, but her lectures were pretty confusing. Be prepared to figure out things on ur own if u take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor V is the sweetest most understanding professor I have ever met! She really cares about her students and takes the time to get to know her 100+ class. That being said, I actually tutor for probability and stats (I took this class for the CTE), and it was very hard. Without a stats background, expect to dedicate 4-6 hours studying.

Lectures can get boring at times, but not too bad. Homeworks are hard but exams are pretty easy in comparison. Dr. V is really sweet and cares about her students a lot, and gives you a lot of extra credit just for showing up

Her grading is simple and predefined, weekly homework's make up 25% of the grade and the two midterms and final make up the 75%. There are bonus points available for going to lecture. She has a lot of material to teach, so sometimes she teaches very fast and can forget students are trying to copy down information from the slides, but she posts them
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her exams are pretty fair, and as long as you do the homework and attend lectures you'll be well prepared. There are two midterms and a final, with homework being worth the same as 1 midterm (and each midterm is worth as much as the final). Attend lectures to get bonus points and keep up with the content in the course. Not easy, but a fair course.
Dr. V is an eminently qualified statistician and a decent lecturer, but after spending an hour on IH-35 to get to a class at 9:30 AM, her lectures were awfully difficult to internalize.

Lectures are extremely dry and boring, and she is confused 25-40% of the time. However, the class is super easy, as the weekly hw, 2 midterms and a final are graded extremely easily (as in put down an idea and get half-credit). Class is out of 400 points (100 for each midterm, 100 for hw, 100 for final) and upto 10 bonus if you show up.

This class requires quite a lot of work, but it is definitely manageable. I would say that finding a study group to work and study with is a good way to go cause having more perspectives to help you along is super helpful. The tests are pretty doable compared to the homework.

If you have stats background, it's not supposed to be too bad of a class, but if you don't, then it's easy to get lost in her class. She goes really fast through the slides, and makes you do the example problems on your own, which is a struggle with no stats background. If you don't understand in class, "try looking over harder" is the response.

Lectures were effective in that she made us do example problems to help us grasp the concepts better. She clearly delineates what you need to know for the exams, and she lets you use handwritten cheat sheets. Extra credit is given just for attending class. Homework is slightly challenging but doable.

Bindu was much better than the reviews on here give her credit for. If you pay attention in class and don't fall behind, the class is doable. She adds 10 points to a midterm grade at the end of the semester if you have perfect attendance, but you won't lose points if you miss class. I found the exams to be a bit easier than the reviews.

There might have been some changes to the class. But when I took it this year, this class was not nearly as bad as the ratings were on this website. Ms. Viswanathan taught well and gave us plenty of time in class to learn the concepts. The homework assignments were not too hard. The review guides for the test were also very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice Person, Horrible Prof. Take stats with someone else!! Nobody in the class knew what was what's going on.

The material itself is not hard, but Viswanathan just doesn't teach it effectively. With other professors, biostats is considered an "easy" class and part of their grade is just attendance, but Viswanathan's grading is harder and pickier than other professors, so don't expect it to be an easy A. You really have to try hard and attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures were dry and formula-heavy. Typically she'd have us all work on an example at the end of class which we could turn in for extra-credit points. Homework was difficult, but exams were easy and she provided us with good practice problems. Overall, the course material wasn't very difficult so as long as you put in some time you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this classes material but didn't really feel stimulated by the teaching style. There could have been more done to spice up the lectures but they were totally acceptable- at the level of or better than average. She was kind and seemed to care about her students to some degree but I did not have much personal interaction with her.
A really fast paced class. She does not post answers to the homework. She doesnt really help you prepare for the tests. She goes really fast through powerpoints in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She was tough but its manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: So far, has been incredibly unhelpful. Does not post answers or work from in class material, nor does she post answers to homework material as well, making it extremely difficult to improve when you don't understand something. Homework is an extremely steep learning curve from class work, and the TA himself seems confused when asked a question
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She grades homework incredibly hard.  Powerpoints are no help if you are lost on something and trying to look back through class material.   Project is strenuous and draining.  Other professors do not require this much work, take someone else.

The workload is heavy- with weekly homework, lab work, and a project at the end. In addition, I found the only way to be successful on tests was to do extra worksheets. She does provide a lot of resources and is a good lecturer. Generous extra credit, but you must attend class to get it. No textbook needed.

Mr. V is a very nice teacher and really walks you through biostatistics. This class was honestly one of my easier classes so far and I really appreciate how well she described and displayed the information. There's also a lab with this class where you use RStudio but they walk you through it too. It's a really easy class for a statistics course.

Viswanathan is a great professor and a caring one at that. Do not be discouraged by the poor reviews you read on here, they're most likely students who didn't put forth the effort required for biostatistics in general. She offers extra credit and explains the concepts very well. Lectures may get dry at times but she gets the point across clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class requires work but Viswanathan was very fair. If you study hard, you will get a good grade. The final project at the end will definitely boost your grade, too. I heard her exams used to be in the low 60's, but when I took her last semester, our averages were almost 80 for each test. Extra credit helps a ton, so show up to class!

Viswanathan is a very clear lecturer and delivers the material in a manner that is easy to understand. Succeeding in her class is definitely not challenging provided that you do your work and study for her exams. Statistics in generally requires you to be meticulous and her class is no different but so long as you practice problems, you'll do great

Assignments, esp HW, are graded toughly. TA was flexible and nice but not very responsive to emails. Tests are difficult because you're expected to be able to determine which stat tests are best for a given situation. This is good because it's similar to what scientists do in their research. I learned a lot, but it was tough! Took up a lot of time.

Dr. V explains hard material very well, and is an engaging lectruer. However, the class is tough and tests are graded toughly - you must have *exactly* the correct answer on her free response or you will miss points.  You don't need the textbook.

A very detailed-orientated class. Point will be deducted on tests and assignments if answers are  a little unclear. The workload in this class is rather large. Professor and lab TA's are only helpful for clarification on problems. Don't expect them to walk you through a problem if you have absolutely no idea on how to approach it.

I thought this was going to be an easy class for me but it was actually one of my hardest. There were so many assignments (worksheets, homeworks, projects) that made me feel overwhelmed. The lectures felt like they lasted a long time and it was hard for me to pay attention. Dr. V explains the material pretty well though.

This professor was very unwilling to help you, as was the TA. When I asked for help on projects and homework, they would say things like "Just read the question again" or "Just try and understand it better". We never got a chance to review our old exams, which made it very hard to improve.

She is a good resource IF you are willing to put in your share of the work. You have to do things on your own. Go to class, pay attention, take notes, and do the worksheets. If you're expecting to come in, not do anything and get an A, you will be wrong. The TA was extremely nice and helpful. The book is not necessary if you go to class.

idk what everyone else is saying.. shes hard. Kind of disappointing UT got some ACC professor.. The course starts off easy and she goes extremely fast into the hard stuff and once you fall behind a little it gets very stressful.
She's really helpful, she wants you to do well. No need for the textbook, unless you're going to skip class. Overall, I great teacher!

She is by far my favorite professor. The tests are very straightforward. She doesn't curve exams, but they are not difficult. She gives out practice exams and worksheets that are exactly like the exam questions in some cases. The homework is probably the most difficult part of her class.

She has an accident but is not hard to understand. Very sweet. She post all her power points but attendance is part of your grade. Also gives you chances for extra credit. The material is not too hard and she is extremely willing to help.
Tests are over stuff you've never even heard of and Blank just doesn't care. Not a good professor take a different government.

Decent Teacher, HARD CLASS. Exam format is extremely lop sided (1 exam covers 2 months of material) and questions deviate DRASTICALLY from weekly instructions. Also, video instructions are long and 95% unnecessary, but you need to pay attention since the 5% WILL be tested. Overall, not hard class to pass, but HARD to get an A in.

Professor Blank and Henson's class was not nearly as hard as people make it out to be. If you treat the course like an in-person class, meaning you actually watch the lectures, it'll be fine. The two exams are decently challenging and worth 20% each, but not outrageous. Professor Blank is engaging in lecture videos and has a good sense of humor.

The weekly reading has about 200 comprehension questions + 7-10 lectures a week. It's annoying, and professors aren't helpful, telling you to study everything. Exams are Honorlock and have frequent typos and formatting issues. Might need a thesaurus to understand test questions. only 2 exams worth 40% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not as bad as people are making it out to be but you do need to actually watch the lectures! Lectures will be more helpful over the readings and the readings can be done in abt 15 minutes. Not a class you can breeze through but definitely do able to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken in my life, the sheer amount of work that this class has is abysmal. There is an insane amount of weekly lectures that range from 15-60+ minutes each PLUS all of the work from the online webtext. The professors provide ZERO methods of studying and often contradict themselves for what information will show up on the test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't like the class and the tests are even worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Blank is a nice guy and his gov course was overall fine but boring. If you watch the lecture videos and read the textbook every week, then you'll be fine in this course. Just be prepared to skip over a lot of unnecessary information in the lecture videos he records.

Prof. Johnson is great at explaining difficult concepts and often presents simpler, clearer methods. Homework is time-consuming and challenging, so be prepared. Exams are structured differently but not bad. Many extra credit opportunities. IMO one of the better fluids professors at UT, would definitely take again. Shoutout TA Alex for being awesome
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tough but fair.

Anyone who dislikes Prof J just hates when professors expect their students to learn. She is a good teacher, and the class is manageable. It is easy to succeed in her class if you participate in lectures, go to office hours, do the homework etc. Only gripe is all homework assignments were group work which I hated, but overall, I really liked her.

Condescending attitude towards certain students. Grades unfairly in certain situations. Is a good lecturer and knowledgeable about the course, but I would not take her again because of the way she treats some of her students.

By far, the best professor I have taken at UT. She is very fond of using the chalkboard in lectures which is how she encourages attendance. The homeworks are hard but you can work in groups. Her exams are fair and tries to be accommodating to everyone. Overall, you will learn a lot from her class and I don't regret taking her.

Pretty solid prof for a fluid mechanics class (lol get it). Her lectures online lasted nearly two hours when you include pre-recorded lectures you had to watch before class. The class itself is tough and she makes you work to understand, but she is very accommodating! Definitely take her if you're looking for a good fluids professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A very nice, sweet, caring professor. Truly passionate about teaching. Weekly homework and labs (done in groups, which has pros and cons), one group presentation (easy grade), occasional assessments (mini-quizzes), two midterms and a final. Overall very accommodating and helpful. Fluids is a pretty hard class but she makes it easier

Great lectures and very understanding about turning in work late, which I did more than a few times. Also has great TAs. Overall, a great person and a great professor. Her class, if you put in a reasonable effort, will be a relatively easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly she's my fav prof I've ever taken. I'm not really an outgoing person but she makes sure to get to know her students well and make them feel comfortable. It sounds silly but I was really touched that she remembered my name(which she pronounced properly) and face after I introduced myself once. You can tell she really cares which is nice.

Dr Johnson has been the best professor I've had so far. She's very passionate about fluids, and treats the material with care. She took it upon herself to learn all of our names in lecture, and was easily accessible and approachable outside of class. The material was hard, but her lectures and office hours were really well detailed
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The only way you can do good is by attending office hours where you can receive further info the rest of the class is unaware of. She was not prepared a lot of the time and taught straight from her notes, often making mistakes and not correcting them until the next lecture. Not recommended if not passionate about fluids, as she expects you to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the haters. She's relatively new, but if you go to class, participate, and give a good effort all semester, you will be glad you took her. She's different than the older seasoned professors that give you a couple diagrams on the exam and say have at it. She's refreshingly new and and a good person.. And great in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Johnson is new at UT and has a unique style of teaching. With that being said, she doesn't post notes so you have to come to class, grades are never in, she makes us work in groups to complete weekly homeworks (takes hours). She is a good professor and the exams are straight forward. Be open-minded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She preaches about mental health but denied our group an extension when we were overloaded. She uploads assignments as announcements (rather than in files), and many of the time are uploaded as word docs instead of pdf. She assigns groups where you have to give a presentation over a scientist and work on weekly homework with that same group.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She essentially reads off the slides, but the course itself is not difficult. You can teach yourself what she skips over. She is friendly and it is better to ask questions in office hours. Grading is nitpicky for minor lab and homework mistakes, points off add up over time. She also gives extra credit for coming to class, that helps.

Super sweet professor, loves giving feedback and regrades, but emails vanish into the void and lectures were insanely long. You can easily self-teach, she posts annotated slides and lets you use cheat sheets. Extra credit is HUGE but only offered if you show up.

She will not respond to emails that you send her. Lectures are long and the class can overall be self taught. TA's will grade homework harshly and homework overall is time consuming and plays a big part of your grade.

Love this professor! She is very clear about what she expects. Your grade is made up of a lot of different things, so exams aren't super stressful. The homework is very tedious though sometimes. Overall, I definitely recommend this course!

Nice lady, but this course is heavy for an introductory statistics class. A lot of people thought this class was a breeze because they took AP Stats in high school but if you didn't take it, it's not a walk in the park. Blevins definitely has good material and resources but the quizzes are a lot harder than what she teaches

Her SDS 302F class is very foundational stuff and not hard. Tests aren't bad at all if you participate in lecture and make a solid cheat sheet for it (which she allows). You have to do a lab with the course but it isn't that hard but the weekly homework's are graded very hard so be prepared for that. There is ample EC opportunities.

Do the work and you're fine. Know the formulas and you're great. 

She gives you a cheat sheet for each exam.

Prof is really nice, but her lectures are easy to fall asleep to. The material is easy, but it's hard to follow in class. I didn't learn in the lectures, but it's easy to learn by yourself. Such a heavy workload. We had weekly prelabs, labs, and homework. The homework is graded harshly (drove me crazy) and so time consuming, but EC helped a lot.

Dr. Blevins is a great professor, and she cares about her students. Her lectures are clear and straightforward without being dry. You don't get a lot of time for quizzes, but they aren't too difficult. TAs grade strictly on homework and it's not always apparent what they want you to include. Overall, not a difficult course. Some extra credit given.

dr. blevins is a great professor! attendance is important as everything you learn comes from lecture. labs are easy and done in groups. 3 exams, 8 homework assignments (due weekly) and one final group project, all very doable. beware of TA grading as he can sometimes be strict. an A is achievable if you put in the effort. attend her OH for help!

Super chill class, she's very understanding. No exams, just 4 quizzes where you can use a cheat sheet that aren't too bad. The class is basically AP Stats with a few other things, so if you took that you'll be totally fine.
A complete snooze fest, she talks in lowercase sentences. Her TA's take weeks to grade assignments, she allows cheat sheet on exam, but isn't helpful at all. Take someone else.

The most understanding professor ever. I slept in for the final quiz and told her the truth, and she let me take it during office hours on Zoom. The quizzes are very easy (7-8 questions per quiz, 4 in total). The final project is split into parts where you're given a template to fill out, so you're not lost. She is an angel and a GPA savior

This class is very easy if you've taken AP Statistics in high school. Overall, the material is boring, but Professor Blondeau does a good job organizing the course. The workload is very light, though you should be cautious with quizzes. Even though you're allowed a page of notes, they are graded strictly. Overall, it's a decent class.

There is only 4 quizzes and 1 major project. The reviews she gives are very different from the actual quiz questions. She does allow a page of notes for each quiz, but it's not very helpful. Attendance is not mandatory, but you are graded on Instapolls during class. Try not to fall behind at all and do show up to every lab meeting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you took AP Stats, then take her since attendance isn't mandatory and you can relearn the material yourself. HW and labs aren't hard and you get rubrics for major projects so it's not bad
Very easy class to begin with (stats) but she makes attendance mandatory, for an upper division class that covers high school material...YAWN

Dr. Blondeau makes the content very concise and easy to understand. Light workload, flexible policies. Content is exactly the same as AP Stats + some R programming on HWs and project. Not a time commitment at all.

This class was easy on the terms of I never showed up and got A's on quizzes I crammed for (24 hrs before quiz by watching lectures.) My only thing is that Dr. Blondeau is VERY STRICT on not curving grades. I got extremely sick when one of the project assignments were due which resulted my grade being a 89.89%… prof wouldn't budge to round… (rip)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I LOVE HER SM. she is genuinely the kindest prof i ever met. she cares so much for everyone's mental health and is so cute. The quizzes can be a little hard but they are only weighted 30% and if you try, its so easy to do good on everything else. I loved this class sm i found it so easy even tho I never took stats and thats all thanks to blondeau!

She's really nice and every quiz or homework is understandable and related to class content. the quizzes are easy if you make the cheat sheet/study. understanding if something comes up and you can't turn in something on time

Dr. Blondeau breaks statistics down really well. She has plenty of resources for your success in this course. Her class is graded by quizzes (where you can have a 1 page cheat sheet), homework, labs, and a major project that isn't too difficult! She is pretty flexible and understanding and responds to emails pretty quickly too!

Dr. Blondeau was absolutely amazing! She cares about stats and student success so much. She was a little intimidating at first, but so accessible outside of class and helpful in office hours. Her slides have a bunch of memes, and she checks for understanding a LOT. Quizzes can be tough, but nothing too bad. An easy project is most of your grade.

So sweet, makes everything you need to know extremely clear. Will give extensions if asked, I asked for an extension on a assignment from 5pm to midnight and she gave me two additional days that i didn't ask for. She cracks jokes in lecture and puts memes on the slides. Such a sweet lady and cares for her students.

Dr. B is my GOAT. She can be intimidating in class, but responds to emails in minutes/same day. She's willing to move deadlines for you if needed. Quizzes can be tricky but you get one note sheet so use it to your advantage. No final, the last quiz is "cumulative" but its 90% Unit 4 and 10% other units. Labs are fine if you have a good group....

Her lectures have active recall that help immensely. Very easy to take if you follow along with her example problems, squarecap, and course packet included in her lecture slides. She allows a page of notes for quizzes and does an amazing short review prior. Lab section is quick if your group is efficient. There is a project included but no exams.

loved loved loved her. she's got her lectures down to a T: detailed, straightforward, easy to understand. she was a little scary at first but she's very sweet and accommodating. project was my favorite part of the course. labs were pretty easy and quizzes were fine, but TA was a stickler for detail. made me seriously consider stats certificate LOL
learned a lot. definitely knows her stuff.

Blondeau is a decent professor, and the project was easy to get a full score on. However, I could not manage to do well on a single quiz this year because of how difficult they were and it sunk my grade because they were weighted heavily. Also the TA was very strict on grading. Lectures were helpful in studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
SO SWEET 

no joke, the kindest prof i've ever had. lectures are easy to follow, and I messed up my project proposal, got a 0 originally, asked if i could redo it, and got a 100. my ta was a harsh grader ngl, but the class was pretty easy aside from that.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: lectures are amazing; provides many opportunities to earn extra credit; tests were stressful but the project carries your grade

Dr. Blondeau definitely knows how to teach statistics without confusing her students. If you can, take her because she is considerate, understanding, and wants you to succeed. Her grading is very very fair and offers extra credit and lots of feedback on assignments to help you succeed. If you ask her, she will give you extensions on assignments.
Take her. She is amazing, awesome, terrific, makes stats so understandable and easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was my most caring and understanding professor. I had a really rough semester, and she was there the whole time to help me get back on my feet. No final or midterms, just open note quizzes and a semester long project. Labs were a bit rough because I'm not great with coding, but they're done in a group so it's not too bad.

Only went to class half the time and still got an A. Just look over her slides and you should be fine. No midterms, just 4 open note quizzes (one dropped) and an easy final project. The lab sections were mandatory but doable and the homeworks were a bit tricky but there were two drops. She gives lots of resources so its easy to do well. Take her!

I haven't taken a stats class but I'm glad I had Dr. Blondeau. She seems a bit intimidating at first but she's nice and has great, concise lectures. Weekly 1 hour lab, with a homework due friday. 4 "quizzes," just do practice problems and you'll be fine. She's so accessible outside of class and I loved how organized SDS 320E was, take Blondeau!

4 quizzes (open note), 1 is dropped, required lab (disc section) most weeks, homework can be tricky but the TAs will help you along if you ask. Final project is very doable and adds a buffer to your grade. Everything you need to know is in her lecture slides, not very hard material at all. Her memes are funny.

Very relaxed course, especially if you stay on top of the project. She tells you exactly what you need to know and what you need to do for the assignments. Graded on a project and 4 quizzes with one drop, the homework and labs buffer your grade quite a bit. Open note everything.

Blondeau is a super kind prof who really cares about her students. She does quiz reviews the class before a quiz, and all quizzes are open note. Homeworks can be a little tricky, but you will do well if you show up to class and lab. She likes to put memes on the slides that relate to stats. Would def take her again!

Honestly, I only went to 3 or 4 lectures in one semester. I only went over lectures and practice problems. Exams are easier than practice problems. As long as you know how to solve every practice problems. You should have no problem. Exams are 100% based on lecture and practice question. Max 3 hours to do HW every week.

If you're deciding between stats professors, take Dr. Blondeau! She is the most organized prof I've ever had at UT thus far. Her lectures are clear and to the point, and she's super helpful with answering questions. I found the exams to be easier than the problems we practiced in class, and she provides useful exam review content.

Blondeau is nice woman. Her tests are exactly like her powerpoint reviews. The only things that will bring ur grades down are homeworks and labs, but those are not crazy hard. Her class is pretty manageable when paired with ochem/genetics and she responds extremely quickly to emails.

Dr. Blondeau is a gem. She is perhaps one of the most thorough professors I have had. Every single thing that you need to know for the class is referenced in her slides. There is no surprises and everything to expect is communicated very well. Coming in with AP Stats, can make this class easy. Even without AP stats, the course is at a perfect pace.

Blondeau is a very great teacher and clearly communicates the topics. Class is well organized and has a clear direction you're leading into. Exams, HW, and labs are all very manageable and Blondeau is there the entire way to answer questions. She is quite lax and wants students to succeed. Her slides are also pretty funny

I loved her teaching style and lectures. All exams came straight from lectures. Labs and homeworks count for a lot! Sometimes, inconsistent grading between TA and prof. Prof is very caring and compassionate. Amount of homework is reasonable. Textbook is optional (personally never read it and made As on every exam). She responds quickly to emails.
Loved biostats with Blondeau! Class is well-organized and lectures teach you what you need to know for the exams. Pay attention to class slides provided and work the problems. She's amazing!

I mean, I think what had me on the edge for this class was mostly the fact that the TA's were nitpicky. One of them was great tho as she would always look over my lab before turning it in (if you are reading this you were awesome). Blondeau is fine but some of the other profs were a bit more lenient. Her tests were fair. Overall okay class.

Dr. Blondeau is an amazing lecturer, but the TAs are nitpicky with homework and labs. Make sure you check the HW in detail including units, tiny details, etc. The exams take a lot of time, so it's still important to study so you can work fast. The best advice for this class is to check over assignments with the TAs during office hours.

Overall a really good stats professor!! She can seem scary at times bc she never smiles lol but honestly, she's really helpful if you have questions - def go to OH if you have any, and go to Plus bc you can literally get all your homework questions answered. Exams were a bit difficult imo but if u know the hw & study guide, you should be fine! EC!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really liked her lectures and explanations. They are extremely straight forward as much as the calculations. The exams were open notes, so if you understand the process of calculations and took some good notes, you'll be fine. Just make sure your calculations are correct, since the wrong one might give bunch of other answers incorrect.

Grades equally distributed between exams, projects, labs, and homework. Homeworks are hard, a lot harder than exams so if you can do HWs, the exams should be no problem. Labs are group work so it depends on your group members, there are lab handouts for references. The project is pretty easy and interesting. Easy class and amazing teaching staff.

Blondeau is truly a gem! She gives you all the resources you need to succeed, including making exams open note, extra credit, and office hours. There are lots of assignments in this class, but by collaborating with others it is manageable! She is very fair and teaches in a straightforward way. I would recommend her over other Stats professors :)

Dr. Blondeau makes stats sooooo easy. I practically only studied for exams a day before (all i did was make a cheat sheet, since it was online and notes were allowed) and still did super well. She explains things incredibly well and her canvas is so organized. I was never confused about anything.

Dr. Blondeau is a knowledgeable professor. As a student who never took AP Stats, I passed the class with an A. She goes quite fast in lectures, but her slides are clear and detailed (super helpful for reviewing!). The class is well-structured, and the grading is not bad as long as one does everything required. Overall, I had great experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Blondeau was a really great professor, her lectures were always straight and to the point. However, the lab section as well as all the extra hmwk just seems like a bit much. Also, the exams were only 11 questions which is ridiculous because if you miss one q you are already at a B+ for the test category. But she is one of the best stats profs.

The class is very easy to do well in. The only thing that will bring down your grade are the exams. Do not overestimate how prepared you are for your exams they will humble you. To succeed DO THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS that she gives you and actively participate in class. When working on the project ask your TA's project BEFORE you submit.

She is a really great teacher. There are plenty of practice problems to run through during lectures and so many opportunities to practice your stats outside of the lecture material as well. She really sets you up to succeed.
Quizzes were very difficult but she sets the class up in a way that lets you do good even if you bomb the quizzes. She also offers some extra credit

Pretty solid stats professor. Quizzes were pretty tough, but they aren't worth too much and the project helped bring my grade up quite a bit. The lectures and overall content were pretty straight forward, even as someone without any stats experience. Dr. Blondeau was knowledgeable and is willing to go over quizzes with you.

If you've taken AP stats this class is A BREEZE until the last unit. Quizzes are pretty difficult but they don't make up most of the points so you'll b fine. Lab groups are hit or miss, but are easy overall (even w no cs experience). For BSTATS theres not much of a diff based on prof, but Blondeau is one of the better ones. TEACHES REALLY FAST THO.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Blondeau sets up class to make it super easy and asks stupid easy questions in class bamboozling you into thinking you know the content. Then she gives you these quizzes that are way harder than anything you have done in the class and it totally screws you grade. She justifies this by saying its fine because we do well on everything else.

Easy to get an A, but there were too many assignments. Homework, prelabs, labs, the project, and quizzes (outside of class time) were so time consuming. This was a ridiculous amount of work for the content of this course. Biostats is tedious and incredibly boring. Dr. Blondeau goes too fast in her lectures and refuses to post the slides beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wow, felt the need to review after reading the past few. My experience was great. UT biostats is structured the same way for each prof, so she has no control over hw, quizzes, etc. She gave extra credit and taught exactly what you needed to know (not more or less). Quizzes were difficult, You have ample time for the project, so you should be fine!

This class was hard, especially because of the quizzes. Dr. Blondeau also said to not worry too much about the final project, but I got so many nitpicky points taken off even though I tried so hard. The quizzes are hard to do well on even after doing the in class practice questions, squarecap, PLUS practice, and the worksheet practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely hard for no reason! Quizzes are made hard in order to "bring your grade down" because people usually do well on the labs and homeworks. The poster project is graded so hard for no reason yet the professor claims it is supposed to bring you up because "people tend do well on it". I suggest making someone look over it before turning it in
Overall a fun easy class and she does her best to give extra credit in quizzes. She is super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty boring. She seems dry and unenthusiastic. Grades participation using squarecap. Weekly excel lab as well as homework. Tests are easy and gives extra credit for taking practice quizzes. Hard to adjust at beginning of semester because grading criteria changes for each assignment. TA is helpful and easy to reach.

Four exams , weekly homework, one semester long project with three components throughout the semester, weekly lab and associated pre-lab due before then. Dr. Blondeau is very straight to the point. She teaches you what you need to know and nothing more. We get out of class early a lot of the time! Asynchronous lecture before class, but only  10min

She is great, explained everything and gave examples/had us try on our own. She made it easy to actually learn. She has a lot of slides with a lot of words on them, but if you go back later and write down all the notes, you'll be golden. The transition to online during covid didn't change the difficulty of the class. This is a pretty easy class.

The homework can be a bit tedious (esp. during exam weeks), and prelabs are a bit too forgettable. Otherwise, the class is phenomenal. Dr. Blondeau is a wildly talented lecturer, and I did well despite having 0 background in stats! Learning R was sorta tedious, but very worthwhile. One of my favorite classes at UT; I can't recommend her enough!

Dr. Blondeau can be very intimidating in lecture but she is actually very nice. Make a GroupMe with the class and it does help out a lot when checking your answers for prelabs and hw. She can be funny sometimes. If you never have taken stats before, you will be fine. Clear ppts. Tests are doable. Class can be stressful if you have a hard schedule

Biostats can become very tedious specially when lots of arithmetic calculations show up. Dr. Blondeau makes the material extremely easy to understand. She is very clear and organized during lectures. Do the homeworks, stay on top of lectures and DO the exam reviews, that is as difficult as it gets. She is also very helpful during OHs! TAKE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Blondeau is great! However, I generally found biostats to be very tedious. Weekly homeworks + the prelabs for R all felt like a hassle. Tests were very straightforward; if you can solve all her review problems then you'll be fine for the test.
TAKING BIOSTATS RIGHT NOW! LOVE HER!

Dr. Blondeau is one of the few professors at UT who wants her students to succeed. She clearly lays out everything you need to do to get an A and even gives you a test review that is very close to the test. Attendance is mandatory because of tophat. She is super helpful in office hours and always emailed me back within an hour.

I definitely recommend taking Blondeau! Clicker questions for attendance grade so you have to show up. There is an optional course packet you can buy with practice problems but I do not think you should buy it. You can print out the few reference tables in the back and the problems in there are also in her slides and she posts the answers

This class is very easy to be successful in. Dr. Blondeau is a very nice professor and is always more than willing to help. I would recommend going to office hours if you need help with the homework. The tests are very fair and she gives you all the material you need to succeed in her class. Highly recommend!

Most of the class grade is from weekly labs, where youll get 100 everytime if you just follow the handout. No final, just a project that applies the R code from those labs. Tests are relatively easy if you study a little. Amazing professor, funny lectures given the material. Almost everyone got an A.
She's one of the best lecturers at UT. Very accommodating to students and also understanding. I'm so glad I took her for biostats! Hard class, solid teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE BIOSTATS WITH ANYONE ELSE! Blondeau is the best one at UT hands down! She makes everything simple and is always available to students. I once emailed her at 7pm on a Sunday and she got back to me within the hour. Her tests are easy as long as you can do the review she provides. Lab is annoying but doable.

Dr. Blondeau is funny/caring. I was not looking forward to this class but it turned out to be my favorite. Lectures are mandatory because you have squarecap questions, but are very helpful so I would go even if I didn't have to. She works practice problems and explains the material very well. Labs are difficult because it's programming in Rstudio

Based on what I've heard about the other biostats professors, she's definitely the best one!! She teaches really well and does a lot of in class problems. She has a dry sense of humor and doesn't seem approachable, but she's actually very friendly and helpful. The class wasn't too hard and it was actually very enjoyable!!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: The best Biostats professor at UT. She explains all the material very clearly and actually work out problems in class (step by step). Her test are very similar to her practice problems she gives and homework. Also, she is very caring for her students success. She gave me points back on my final project after my TA graded harsh. Highly recommend!!

Great professor!! I got an A, and my only background in stats was a very laid back HS stats class (not AP). She does review problems at the beginning and end of each class, and the three exams (all cumulative) are very similar to practice problems done in class. The project is not hard at all and is a great boost for your grade at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very straightforward and one of the easiest classes I've taken at UT. Go through the slides, do some practice problems & you'll do well on exams, especially if you've taken stats in high school. She holds your hand thru the project, which is graded leniently. Blondeau seems nice enough, lectures are boring but easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great prof! She tells you exactly what you need to know. If you can do the clicker/HW questions you can do the test. Assigns study groups: very helpful. Grade (very TA dependent): clicker questions, HW, lab, tests, final research project. PPTs provided, lecture not recorded, calculator and formula sheet on exams.

Love her! Her class was not too bad and I learned so much! I definitely have a greater appreciation for statistics after this class. She is super straightforward and her teaching style is very effective. There is a lot of homework and project assignments that have to be completed for this class but none of it is difficult if you pay attention.

Dr. Blondeau was a blessing to have. She was very straightward and explained concepts pretty well! Grades are TA heavy, so beware. She puts up parts of the lecture PowerPoints and also goes pretty fast, which could be kinda hard to keep up with. But overall, pretty easy stats class.

Pretty standard lecturer. Posts all her slides online after class, and basically everything she says is on them, so paying attention in class isn't a must. You do need to go, however, as she takes attendance. This class is a lot of work, with homeworks, a final research project that has many parts, and the weekly labs and pre labs.

Probably one of the most straightforward and chill professors at UT. Assignments are clear and lectures are engaging and interesting. She also has a good sense of humor too. Tests almost mirror the homework and reviews she post. She even goes above and beyond and sets up study groups in the class if you are on the shy side. Very caring professor!
WHATEVER YOU DO, DO NOT, I REPEAT, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

The most disorganized and unprofessional class ever! Literally no structure to any of the lectures, no rubric for any of the assignments, and she frequently laughed at students opinions. I went to her office hours to get feedback on my essay and she laughed at my work and basically called me stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awkward, awkward, AWKWARD! Wants participation, but will strangely cut you off or flat out laugh at your response. No lesson plans, no structure. But, she is a gentle grader and wants to hear your ideas. Sweet lady, just so disorganized. She's funny too!

Blockley is very sweet and loves when the class is engaged with the discussion, which can be hard because there are a lot of readings each week. Its manageable, if a little hard to balance, but as long as you read the texts and speak in class, you'll do fine. Grade is very exam heavy, so take those seriously as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blockley is just very odd. Her course has absolutely no structure, and she does not match her syllabus. She changes deadlines and cancels exams on a whim. There aren't clear rubrics or prompts given for papers. It just feels like you're blindly showing up to class, and you don't know what you're getting when you arrive.

every other english class i've taken at UT has been miles better than this one. there's no organization to class meetings, we would sit in silence for MINUTES, not sure why we even had to show up. also, a lot of the books we read were problematic at best. not sure why the prof enjoys talking about... weird things so much.

Prof Blockley may be a sweet woman, but her class is HORRIBLY organized, most days we had no lesson plan and I'm not even sure why we needed to show up. She is a bit...quirky... and seemed to like reading gross, sexist books so she could make a spectacle out of how bad they were. If you need an Eng. credit, there are way better options.

She is very sweet. Cares a lot about the subject & LOVES when you participate & cares about what you have to say and contribute. You will do well in the course IF you put in effort and work with her. Ask her questions, she has answers! 1 writing assignment per week & discussion based course. She's a little awkward in class. Rather quirky.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! For the love of god do not take Blockley for any class! EVER! SERIOUSLY! Most frustrating professor I have EVER had! This course had ZERO structure & ALL of the graded things are about topics SHE HAS NEVER! ONCE! TALKED ABOUT IN LECTURE!? NEVER gives full credit for ANYTHING with NO EXPLANATION! So odd! Something is off mentally

Prof. Blockley is a wonderful person to talk to, but the class feels super unstructured and you leave a lot of times feeling like you haven't learned anything. If you take her classes, be ready to talk about the subject on hand at length, because there are hardly any lectures and the awkward silence when no one answers a question is unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quintessential "College Professor." A nightmare to take a class with: the canvas was not posted until 15 minutes after the first class (she wanted a particular book edition, gave us homework that night, no remorse) and she even claimed to not have internet at home. Avoid at all costs for the sake of your sanity and GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this professor is unbelievably disorganized. She never facilitates conversation, talks so quietly that literally no one can hear her, and continuously made snide and highly unprofessional comments in class all throughout the semester. She is very knowledgeable, but she is not qualified to be a university instructor.

I've never had such a horrid "educator." It's mind-boggling how she advanced in her career, incapable of organizing a coherent classroom discussion. Students talked in circles, and she adamantly shut down any critiques of the main protagonist. I honestly would rather drop out than attend a class with her as the professor again. Still passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not the best at technology and her grading criteria is unclear. But, if you show up to class and participate it will pay off. Once she gets to know you, she is very down to earth and kind and is beyond willing to help her students succeed. It's definitely a flip of the coin for some though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was a discussion-led class but for the most part, students mostly led the discussions themselves. It's hard to tell what she wants from the 3 major essays for the class. A lot of reading and VERY disorganized. Professor Blockley also makes a lot of snide remarks that are unprofessional, and oftentimes is unprepared to lead discussion herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. She is the absolute worst professor at UT, horrible horrible experience. Has no grading rubrics and grades based off how she feels that day, makes super inappropriate comments about sex and genderfluid individuals, admitted herself she wasn't qualified to teach the course, and gets mad when you question grades. sucks
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was fine. I found her to be a very knowledgeable professor and her classes were good enough for me to do well on her papers. However, she doesn't round up grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very few students in the class wanted to talk (midafternoon class) and she wasnt very good at facilitating conversation, but when we got one going it was good! She is nice and definitely knowledgeable in what we talked about but not very well structured. Not way too much reading but you have to know details for the in-class paper-writing exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Half the time, the class had no idea what was going on. She never gave us hard deadlines and didn't tell us what to write about for papers. It's the end of the semester and she hasn't posted ANY grades. I email her a lot and she NEVER RESPONDS!! She is very unreliable and seems to want something particular but she doesn't tell us what it is. Ugh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really easy class as long as you do the readings, show up to class and participate in the discussions. Kinda awkward teacher but she definitely knows what she is talking about. Most of the bad reviews were just students who did not show up to class or do the readings. Most of the time students wouldn't even try to get class discussions going.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awkward class discussions. Harsh grader. Unclear grading criteria. Rude to me when I came to her office hours to ask what I should be doing to improve my grade in her class. I do not know what compelled her to teach. It was so draining to sit in her class 1st thing in the am. If you HAVE to take her: You can rewrite papers for a higher grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Quite literally one of the worst professors Ive ever had in college. Completely unorganized and unprepared, unavailable for communication, unhelpful, and generally rude. I learned absolutely nothing in this class, her lectures are frankly ridiculous. This is not a professor I respect or admire.
Not clear on her grading criteria and her grading is entirely subjective. She did not provide quality feedback on essays and is very difficult to communicate with.

Tons of textbook reading, short answer quizzes on these most weeks, and they can be pretty tough. She's improving upon this class, though. Tests come from quizzes, but with additional easy-ish essays. Class discussions were sometimes dreadfully awkward, but she's really invested in the subject. Take her if you're actually interested in the subject.
Dr. Blockley is one of the best professors I had at UT. She's simply brilliant. I've taken two of her courses and they were both difficult, but you will really learn your stuff.

Blockey's class is insanely difficult and poorly taught. As the other posts say, she's nice, but very unhelpful. Half the class failed the midterm. She continues on like its our problem. I'm an Eng major. I freak if I get a B on a test. This midterm, I got a D. I spoke to her. She acts like it's my failing. My 3 A's on my other 3 midterms disagree.

I had her for Hist of Eng Lang.  Very, very difficult, but she is really cool: goes to Scissor sisters shows, likes cool books, really funny in awesome ackward way.  However her class is too difficult for words, I got a 'D'.  I think she expects everyone to be as intelligent as she is, not gonna happen.  Hang out with her, don't take the class.
I had her for History of the English Language. She is socially inept, hard to deal with, and not interested in undergraduates.

I'm sure Professor Blockley is a very nice lady, but GOOD LORD her class was awful!  She was always letting this one annoying, kiss-ass guy get her off track, so she wouldn't finish her lessons.  That made it very hard to learn as you never knew when to listen or when she was talking about CRAP.

Don't take this class with her period. TA's were rude & inconsiderate, while the professor read off of a script without expanding on the topics/terms. I didn't learn anything from the lectures since she didn't give time to note anything and didn't post the slides. Attendance via instapolls was the worst
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If i can deter you from doing anything during your time at UT it is having this woman as your professor. She takes an intro class way too seriously and has a terrible structure. I have never rated a professor before but something had to be said. She cares more about stopping you from cheating than helping you learn.

The structure of this course is terrible. The professor does not post the slides and gets upset if you try to take pictures of them if you can't write fast enough. Most of the learning will be done through the reading since the lectures are all over the place. The one thing I like about this course is the fact that the textbook is free.

Professor Ramirez was a great teacher. Her class was very engaging, with interesting topics, and was definitely one of my favorite classes. Although there were few assignments, as long as you studied, you would do great. My TA was also great and very helpful during office hours. Highly recommend this class!

Horrible teacher. She read from a script and did not know her slides at all, Guest lecturers were better than her. Didn't post slides and no extra credit. Cutoff for an A was a 94. She doesn't want you to do well. Exams aren't hard. Papers are graded by TAs, so they decide your grade. I didn't learn anything it was about the level of a hs class.

Shouldn't be that difficult a course. Professor Rameriez did her best to engage us in lectures. Simple grading with 30% being essays (graded very fairly), 60% exams (in-class, 50 mins, no drops), and 10% attendance. Technically, you don't have to go to class if you do really good on all assignments, but lectures are not posted. 94 for an A.

Lectures are not always super engaging, and she sometimes goes pretty fast through slides, which can be difficult to get all the information down in time. The class isn't too difficult if you understand the terms and concepts. Grade is very dependent on 3 papers and 3 exams

Dr. Blazek can be a funny guy, but his lectures aren't great for 340L. His explanations are confusing and textbook like which makes it hard to understand simple concepts. His exam questions are example problems during class which is nice. He doesn't provide any study material for it though and it can be hard to search through all the lectures.

Professor Blazek is a really funny and great guy, but he can get off track and go on tangents during lectures. Tests can be one level of difficulty above the homework, so make sure to actually learn the material well. Lenient grading criteria and the lowest exam score is dropped. Overall, a very achievable A.

Overall, a frustrating experience. Homework does not prepare you for the difficulty of the in-person exams. You can succeed if you deeply understand the material, but the effort required feels excessive. Be careful with older reviews, as many were written when exams were take-home.

Lowest out of 3 midterms and final dropped, and they get more difficult as the semester goes on. Course was overall not that difficult if you study. Very possible to get 100s on exams. A few problems each week for homework. The exams are more difficult than the homeworks. Find exams from previous semesters since they're mostly the same.

Solid guy, his sarcasm can be a little condescending. Teaches well and doesn't make the class harder than it needs to be. 3 midterms + final, lowest of which is dropped (including final). Last few units are by far the hardest, so I'd recommend doing well on the 3 midterms. Has a flair for the dramatic, but you learn to tolerate it.
Offered Zoom + posted lectures, so bc he goes fast I never attended class (only for exams) and watched on my own time. Easy weekly 1 question hwk, and 3 exams (4-5 questions). Only curves if avg. is

Easy homeworks but you needa lock in for those now in person exams. One test including final gets dropped, so I could skip final entirely. He gives a practice problem packet so just do all the covered material from that before exam. Honestly lectures can be a bit hard to follow but just look at problems and how he does them and just memorize that.

Blazek's lectures are SUPER HARD to digest and pay attention to. He writes at the speed of light and moves on immediately. Really hard to understand lectures. Exams and homeworks tho are pretty doable. He is a hilarious guy tho, makes lectures interesting in that way. Open to questions regarding the material. Calculator is your best friend, P2W.

Genuinely my worst experience with a professor so far. Tried attending the lectures at the beginning of the year but were so unbearable that I resorted to self-studying. Exams were fine but graded super strictly and took points off on homeworks for “wrong version” of a problem but won't post the actual problem anywhere.
Easy A if you prepare for the tests, but you won't learn much linear algebra by taking this class.

He did switch his exams to in-person, and his exams usually aren't curved, but they're not too bad if you know what you're doing. Don't be discouraged by your results on the exams because he should still have the final replace your lowest midterm grade. He can be a bit condescending, but his lectures are still interesting and worth attending.

He was an alright professor, but I really didn't like his sarcasm throughout the year. He wasn't approachable or understanding, and his lectures were difficult to follow. I also don't know why he made the tests harder after switching to in-person exams.

class wasn't too bad, as long as you study it's fine. zoom lectures are nice, but overall he's not the best lecturer. goes very fast and spends a lot of time on derivations you dont need (even codes it for some reason?). condescending when any question is asked. material isn't too difficult, problems done in class are extremely comparable to exams.

The negative reviews are from a bunch of crybabies who can't cheat now since the exams are in person. Blazek isn't the best at teaching but as long as you understand how to do the hws and past exam problems, there is no reason you should not get an A if not a 100 in this class. That being said, 3 exams are 75% with one drop, so do good on those

Early Ratings for this Professor arent accurate since he changed his exams to in-person. There is no notes allowed nor calculator.
