Not the best at explaining and lectures were hard to follow, but made up for it by allowing group work on quizzes and offering extra credit. Homework is challenging but you get multiple attempts, and exams are not worth nearly as much as in other McCombs classes. Using the slides to study was helpful, and he gives plenty of practice material.

He's so kind and adorable!  He gave group quizzes and got rid of Perusalls.  When I emailed him about any slight issue, he gave me a take-home quiz or another way to open Lockdown.  He can be kind of confusing to pay attention to because he says so many things, but he repeats the things that are important to know.  Best 235 Prof by far.

Professor Bolfarine is very passionate but it leads to class going over the allocated time usually. There is a quiz at the beginning of each class which is hard. His slides and R-scripts are very helpful and class is well organized. Tests can be difficult too but there is a curve. Overall, it's a difficult class but R is better than using excel.

in Spring '25 paper exams were absurdly hard also no curve after avg 58. Exams had such a wild range of topics and the class did jack shit to prepare you for it. On top of that Bolfarine's lectures were ass and he would make the r script while lecturing resulting in about 25% of the class being actual content and the other 75% incoherent ramblings
GOAT professor. Cares about you and you're grade. Would 100% take him again.

Professor Bolfarine is not good at lecturing. He knows the concepts, but he does not communicate them well. He means well and is kind, but he does not succeed in the most important part of being a professor: teaching. There's no textbook to fall back on, either. However, he doesn't grade particularly hard, so that is a redeeming factor.

Professor is very kind and cares about his subject very much. I think having any kind of coding background could help you with this course. Ther Knowlege Checks and Big Homeworks are a majority of your grade, but the final tanked my grade by far. I would def be in tutoring a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, lectures very well, if i had actually shown up to class i would have gotten an A. I pretty much missed every class leading up to the second exam and still turned out okay. Wouldn't take any other prof for 235.

The professor is relatively poor at explaining lecture content. The good news is the course material is not that difficult, so you can get a grasp of the content without needing a good explanation. He is a nice guy, so that earns him some points. For the class itself, you have to do homework once a week, and there's also a quiz in class everyday.

Bolfarine is an ok professor, but DO NOT take his online section. He just speeds through the material and barely pauses to allow questions, so you end up listening to him rush through a lecture for 2 hours straight. It's hard to pay attention and he does NOT cover exam material well as the exams are largely conceptual and he only teaches coding.

Best professor ever. He is so sweet and caring, and you can really tell he cares about his students understanding the material. He is always willing to answer questions and talk to students if they have any concerns, and during class he tries his best to make the lectures funny and entertaining. If you have the opportunity to take him do it!

He is passionate about teaching the topic and I feel like he gave good examples during class. The tests are in person now and are standardized across all profs/classes. He explains things so well if you ask him in class or even outside of class. I would def say take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were online and pretty easy. Not the most engaging but he's a nice guy who genuinely cares and will answer any questions you have
Easy class, got an A- (93%) by studying maybe 6 hours for the entire semester. Chill dude, but his lectures were super boring.

Honestly a great professor, your grade is mainly made up of a midterm and a final which are both fairly straightforward as long as you've paid attention in class. The only homework is weekly quizzes that you had unlimited attempts on. Engaging lectures and extremely nice guy, wants you to succeed. Would take him again 100%.

Professor is a nice guy, but his lectures tend to ramble. The most important thing about this class is knowing what your resources are (textbook, R Sessions, TAs). Overall, not a bad class, but the learning curve for coding takes a moment to get used to. Criteria and expectations are clear, but the final TANKED my grade by 10 points.
Curves like a homie

This teacher is a good guy and the class was heavily set on hmwrks and in class quizzes. I don't know much about stats at all but still ended up with a A- without being able to know how to run a regression

Really nice guy but you won't learn a lot from his lectures. His course materials are really confusing. Quiz at the beginning and end of every class but the class does it together-- more of an attendance incentive than a time for you to test your knowlege. Go to TA review sessions. You will learn more in 30 mins than you do in a semester of class.
Super kind professor who wants to help you understand content. You get what you put into the class. Review homeworks.

Dr. Bolfarine is a very kind professor who can really explain R and stats well. With that being said, his lectures do tend to ramble, sometimes unnecessarily so. Also, this class is HARD, especially the exams. Make sure to read the textbooks and talk to the TAs. My TA Kenji was the best I've had at UT if you can get him, definitely do!

Dr. Bolfarine is a great professor I had him for STA - 301 and he was always pretty funny and would be very helpful in office hours. The course however is graded on very few assignments which makes it difficult, but stats is standardized anyways so it won't matter much.

Dr. Bolfarine is a very knowledgeable professor. For the exams, know the conceptual and RStudio aspects of the material. The weekly TA-led practice sessions are a great way to stay on top of course material. Overall, this course is difficult; however, if you have taken AP Stats and/or AP CSA, you will be well-prepared.

Mr. Bolfarine is an amazing professor and person, but the exams are EXTREMELY difficult. Overall the material was very well explained, but you must read the book before class. Homework is okay and you can get help from TAs. Recommend going to the TA sessions EVERY WEEK which will definitely improve your understanding and grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Bolfarine was a great, caring professor! The class content was difficult, but he is the best STA 301 professor, having the highest midterm average, a 78. I thought he did a good job explaining all concepts and the textbook is a great additional resource. The homework's are lengthy (4-6 hours), but doable if you start early and go to office hours.

Bolfarine is one of the kindest professors, but the course content is difficult. Read the textbook! He sticks around after class for questions & office hours are helpful. He sometimes struggles to articulate thoughts clearly. He makes lectures fun with jokes. The average final exam score was 65%. Tough class! C's get degrees lol.

Professor Bolfarine is so sweet and genuinely wants you to succeed. He is one of the best STA301 professors. However, this class is so hard. My advice is to read the textbook, it may feel pointless at points but it will teach you EVERYTHING. Also, go to office hours and R sessions with the TAs. Start the homework early!! They took me 5-6 hours.

Prof Bolfarine is sweet and accessible. However, his test is freaking hard and his lecture is kinda boring. Believe me, using you textbook is the best resources in class! I think all STA301 prof exam is the same, so it's not big different if you take Prof Bolfarine or other prof.

Although he is ESL, I thought his lectures were clear and notes were exactly what was needed for the hw and exams. Rarely read the textbook. Recommend starting on HWs early as well as knowledge checks. If you do good on those, you have more room to spare on the midterm and final. Overall, funny teacher and interesting class.

Bolfarine's such a sweet guy, he really wants whats best for the students. Biggest issue is he's ESL, and struggles to articulate certain things. Additionally, the class as a whole(not just his sections) is very intensive and not a student friendly structure, incredibly test heavy(final average was 65). He is good enough but be prepared to struggle

Bolfarine is a very helpful professor, walking us through both slide decks and coding every class to not just learn concepts but understand how to apply them. Exams are difficult, but I felt adequately prepared for them as lots of study tools were given (practice exams, study questions). TAs were VERY helpful for assistance completing homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Struggles to articulate thoughts but lecture content is very relevant. Grade is determined by weekly online quizzes, a couple of longer projects, and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In comparison to the other STATSS 301 professors, I would say Bolfarine is the best due to him teaching at a pace where you can actually understand the content. He also adds a sense of humor to his lectures that I appreciate. This class was difficult for me personally, but if you want good stats Bolfarine is the one I recommend.

Prof. Bolfarine is a great professor, light-hearted and cares about his students. The class is pretty difficult, you will have to sit through long lectures and study hard for exams. There are curves however, and if you put in the effort to succeed you are definitely able to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, great class, would definitely take again. Put in the effort to understand material, study for exam with enough time ahead and you'll love the class.
Best stats professor, his lectures are a wonderful learning experience. Highly accessible and genuinely caring. I've grown to love stats thanks to his class, definitely recommend.

Let me preface this review by saying Professor Bolfarine is a very nice person who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. However, I have learned a great deal more from the book than I have from his lectures. He tends to ramble and not finish lessons, leaving us to teach ourselves. I feel like I am not learning this course material.

Professor is a nice persona and seems to care about his students, but the class was him just reading the slides and not showing us the code 70% of the time. The midterm and final rely on code and Bolfarine rarely showed us the code. The textbook is free and was how I learned everything.

An extremely mediocre professor who relies on you teaching yourself 90% of the material. The class is not hard, but his lectures were always disjointed, boring, and confusing and never helped you learn material. Go to class for participation points and trust the textbook to teach you everything you need to know to have an A in the class.

He is a nice guy as a person but his teaching is slow and boring. Most of the things he teaches are right out of the textbook, but his teaching won't help too much -- although he is good at answering questions during office hours. You need to self study the textbook and R to be successful in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In order to succeed in this class, you NEED to read the textbook to self-teach how to code in R because Professor Bolfarine often gets off topic during lectures and only covers the conceptual ideas that many of us already knew from previous stats classes rather than going in depth on the new material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a caring individual who would help you if you have any questions. However, for the lectures, he sometimes goes off-topic, which makes it hard to concentrate at times. I feel like the textbook and PowerPoint notes are more useful, but he does go more in-depth on R during lectures. If you took AP Stats/Comp Sci, it'll make the class easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolfarine goes off topic a little bit during lectures but overall he's a very caring person and good teacher. If you took AP Stats in high school, the conceptual concepts should be very easy, but R is still something you'll have to learn

Lectures are not too helpful, but READ the textbook because it has just about everything you need to learn and its a little difficult if you are not the best at coding. This class is nothing like AP statistics so don't get too excited if you think u have an edge because of taking it in HS. Keep up with curriculum through the sem and not atthe end.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bolfarine really cares about his students and is always willing to help inside and outside of class time. Everything is graded very fairly, but the class does require you to learn about R on your own, but the online textbook is very helpful. It was not a very hard class, and it is not difficult to understand the content.

He's very nice and knowledgeable about the course, but the class is difficult at times. There are 2 exams, 4 hw, and weekly Canvas quizzes (unlimited attempts). The homework is done through peer-grading, and his course policy is that a good final grade can replace the midterm, so he is lenient in that area. Don't skip class, you'll get rlly behind!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class. Go for it.

The homework assignments are peer graded, and whenever I went to him with an error in my homework grades he always helped me out. I would highly recommend him. Might be hard for people who are not much into R language. It wont be hardore coding, the exams are open internet. He's a really respectful guy and I think that is what matters the most.

Professor Bolfarine tried his best, and you can really see it and appreciate it. He's a nice grader, but he tends to ramble a little. The TA's were honestly the biggest help in passing this class, so just make sure to join the official GroupMe.

Okay I really don't think he's hard to understand like that other person... Lectures are boring but that's mostly cuz you're learning statistics. One homework assignment a week, 2 exams, 1 group project, and 1 final. If you did well in STA 301 you'll be fine in this class because a lot of the class is just more in depth concepts from STA 301.

Never again. Got our midterm 2 grades back today and the average was a 40. She says thats good… like girl. The exam questions are unreasonably difficult and she grades without mercy. I couldnt even get 2 points back even tho i had the right answer written. I literally have a better grade in QUANTUM. Mechanics should never be this hard.

Multiple students took mid-exam breaks to faceplant on the table and/or pray for their grades. This class was a waking nightmare and I loved every second of it. Dr. Boddy is also very kind and willing to help students in office hours.

Imagine you're at the beach with your friends. You run into the ocean and get hit with a big wave. You get back up, go deeper into the ocean, and get hit with an even bigger wave. Then when you get back up, a tsunami drowns you and the whole class. Then, you get back up and out of nowhere your 60 became an A-. 10/10 professor, would drown again.

The final exam for this class had an average of a 33. She ends up boosting the scores by a lot, but you it fails to properly test her students. She also just regurgitates the textbook and doesn't expand upon any of its material. There are few resourses to excel in her 336K course and its the same for 315. Just wait for another professor to teach it

This class was amazing. Difficult, but Professor Boddy was one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Her homeworks are hard, but they help you grasp the concepts really well. Also, the tests can be very difficult, but they are heavily curved. Overall, this class is wonderful—would recommend!

Professor Boddy's lectures are very bad. You will have to teach yourself virtually all of the material. My biggest gripe about Boddy's teaching methods is that she does not really connect the material to the math concepts used for it. This makes it very hard to learn. Grading criteria were also not clear at all. Avoid this professor if you can.

Dr. Boddy's exams and homework sets were very diffcult. However, her lecture style is easy to follow and office hours (TA and prof) were extremely helpful. Email TA's or her if you're stuck! Be prepared for a lot of work, which will absolutely pay off. I feel like I learned a lot in this class and am well prepped for upper div classes!

Prof Boddy is well-meaning but should continue to re-evaluate her teaching for this class. One of main issues is the second half the class, where it's very difficult to understand and be able to apply the sheer amount of new content given in half a semester. With the required lab, this is the most comprehensive academic challenge I've ever faced.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are hard to understand. The TAs were really good, but weekly problem sets were due one day after discussion. Often, we hadn't learned everything on the homework, until the night it was due. The median on the final exam was a 34%. She was very generous with the curve. However, the average student would've failed the class otherwise.

Dr. Boddy truly cares about her students and their understanding of the course material and was a good lecturer.  That being said, her class is extremely difficult and I spent hours on the homework each week.  The midterm had an appropriate level of difficulty (avg of around 60) but the final had an average of 38 and was very difficult.

this is definitely a class where you need to put in time and effort to get a good grade. HWs were really tough but had great TAs/LAs (fav was Brian Kent). going to office hours and creating study groups makes such a difference. that being said, professor does NOT give great exam reviews, and just going over HWs will not necessarily be enough
Very hard class, but mainly because its waves. Really hard final, but is easily compensated by a really heavy curve.

Don't be fooled by the grade. This class was made into a full time job by Professor Boddy. She's an extremely intelligent individual but lacks any ability to structure a college class. Doesn't know what textbook she's using, minimal to no practice problems, horrible out of pocket exams. Hardest class I have ever taken. Others literally got ulcers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to fight for your life in this class. I kid you not, the average on the final was a 38. The curve was insane, though. With that being said, I learned way more than I would have with an easy professor, which will pay off in the future. Go to office hours, make friends, and be ready to put in a lot of time if you want to survive.

Material was conveyed effectively and homework was reasonable. Course is difficult as a result of the subject matter. Exams were difficult. Class was curved but the curve was not really defined so it was hard to know where you stand. Professor Boddy obviously cares about students and takes the time to try to help. TA can help too.

A difficult class by default, but with Boddy teaching it becomes harder than trying to climb Mt. Everest without taking a breath. This class gave me imposter syndrome for 17 weeks straight and. Good luck asking for help on homework because not even professors can do some of the problems assigned. Terrible professor, hard class, lots of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
One of the worst classes I've taken. Essentially a weed-out course. 
Homework was hard and at times not helpful to study. Exams were so bad and so hard.
Boddy did not explain the material well, and the lectures were shown to not be entirely effective in the overall learning process.
Better if you learn it all on YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Boddy used the worst textbook ever written as her sole course material, reused her predecessor's powerpoint slides of equations copied-and-pasted from the textbook, and spent her entire "lecture" reading the slides aloud. The homework was insane. Never take any class taught by Boddy if you can avoid it. If you can't avoid it, get antidepressants.

Course is heavily disorganized. The work isn't difficult, but she'll post on random timing during the weekend and you have to scramble to summarize a reading/video with your group. Rambles too much. Group presentations are expected to cover the entire class time, prepare to lecture the entire class. Grades are nonexistent until the end of the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very passionate and kind professor. There were very few assignments, but almost all of them are group work or presentations. Also, she posted readings to the group work on short notice, so be prepared to work with your groupmates the night before a presentation. No exams or a final, but there's two quizzes. Attend class and you'll do fine.

Felt a little unorganized at times but overall not difficult. Not graded by many assignments and the A cutoff is a 95, which was pretty doable. Lots of group work, you get assigned to a group at the beginning of the semester and work with them a lot. Only two exams, one with mostly MCQ and a few FRQ and one thats all FRQ.

She's a really nice professor and it's really clear that she's extremely passionate about sustainable tourism. The grading is kinda iffy because there isn't really a clear rubric (especially with the TA), but it's extremely easy to get a good grade, especially if you just show up to class. She's really caring and understanding, so DEF take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seriously, do NOT underestimate how easy the sustainable tourism class is. Whatever you're thinking of I GUARANTEE YOU it's far easier - even the facilitation is graded extremely generously. That seems nice at first, and I suppose it's better than having a harder class with the same schedule, but you will learn almost NOTHING in the whole semester.

She is easy, to the point that you don't have to learn anything to get an A, so the class is what you make of it. She is super sweet, but very hard to understand with her accent. She clearly cares about what she is teaching, and will give feedback if you ask for it.

Professor Boonabaana is really sweet, but if you struggle with accents she is not the professor for you. It's really easy to get a good grade in her class as long as you just do the work. You are graded on a few group assignments and two in class essays. It may seem unclear why you got points docked but she will explain if you ask.

Boonabaana was a great professor, though the actual lecture material was so simple it made the class boring at times. If you go to her office hours, you can talk about more in-depth stuff. Not a bad class at all.

Incredibly easy class, show up to lectures and do the bare minimum of homework and you'll walk away with literally full marks. 40% of the grade was group projects, there were two timed essays, and one more assignment that was 25% of the grade and you could finish it in like an hour. 
She's very kind, but the class was a slog because it was so easy.

Dr. Booth is an excellent professor. This research-focused class taught me how to conduct literature reviews, evaluate whether ideas are viable, and approach research thoughtfully. She is always available after class or during office hours and actively helps students find research opportunities. She genuinely cares about student learning.

Dr. Booth is very thoughtful and organized. She explains concepts clearly and brings real industry insight into the class. The course feels intentionally designed and she creates an inclusive environment where students feel comfortable asking questions and going to office hours. She also regularly asks for and implements student feedback.

Senior health informatics student here, this class is so good! Professor Booth gives practical, real-world advice and clearly understands the informatics field. The workload is manageable if you stay on top of assignments. Tons of useful content, and I've found myself using her advice much more than I thought I would have!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Booth is great! Compared to other professors in the iSchool, she is one of the stronger public speakers and consistently comes to class well prepared, she puts thought into each class. Group work is a big part of the course, so having a reliable group really affects the experience. Overall, she's a solid instructor.

Prof Booth's passion for research & teaching is clear in the way she leads lectures & structures the class. She genuinely cares about her students, adjusting the course & assignments based on student feedback and interests. Lectures are very interesting & applicable outside of just research. There's a good mix of simple and intensive assignments

Class is only helpful for freshman who never took an AVID class in H.S. 97% of lectures are regurgitated common sense (S.T.A.R method when interviewing, basic resume tips). Only helpful thing was creating your own personal brand.LATE grader. Participation is mandatory, same w attendance. Homework is doable but long. Take a beta-blocker before class

Dr.Booth is amazing, passionate and direct.TA did all grading.Was absent for most of the semester and corrected assignments late.Some assignment criterias could be unclear,send questions to clarify but pretty easy overall.Class can be unnecessarily long but she would bring interesting points about the job market, career world,etc

There are better informatics courses out there and definitely better professors. It sounded like she was bragging about her connections the entire time. The TA was not present anywhere and class would always go long.
Not helpful, didn't get anything from class, should not be a class in the iSchool.
Not a good professor and not communicative. Should be an easy class but wasn't clear at all and didn't put assignments in until way late. Avoid.

This professor was unclear on grading guidelines and we had less than 10 actual assignments going into the gradebook. Took forever with grading, and students were not sure of their grades until the final day when grades were due. Extremely long and boring lectures that do not feel helpful unless if you're a freshman entering college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class can be pretty helpful if you have never had any career classes in the past, but overall advice can be pretty broad, and I found it difficult to access the professor outside the class. But she does seem to genuinely care and puts a lot of thought into her lectures and assignments. Not a heavy workload, but attendance does matter
Excellent and passionate professor who really cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Not a good professor. Lectures feel like a waste of time and give everyone a headache. Clearly an immature and unprofessional teacher. Clearly does not care much for students or their success. Does not even provide feedback. Additionally, does not know how to respond to messages, especially when urgent! Very tough grader and not understanding.
Dr. Booth is extremely kind and this class was extremely easy but lectures were a little boring sometimes. Very few assignments and one group presentation throughout the whole semester.

Graded by an easy group project and progressive individual project. Professor Booth is super passionate and caring, truly an amazing lecturer. Easiest A, all you have to do is attend the classes and engage a little. Super interesting class, you learn a lot of unique things.

If you have an opportunity to take a class with Dr. Booth - do it!! Her passion for research is contagious, and she assigned minimal homework throughout the course, but I still walked away feeling I learned so much. She cares deeply about her students and clearly wants them to succeed, and goes out of her way to make them feel safe and included.
Super fun and easy class!

Dr. B was one of my favorite professors. He always made class fun and interesting every day. This UGS was one of the best on campus (you pretty much just talk about what makes a good sports team). There's tons of extra credit, and he really wants everyone to succeed. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'll get a decent amount out of it.
Overall, an amazing professor would recommend to anyone!
professor motivated me to pick up soccer again. pretty motivational if you pay attention but such an easy class
Bro easy A, if its not for you, you might not be able to handle college yet.

You genuinely have to try not to get an A+ in this class. Attendance isn't mandatory and the exams are ALL online and OPEN BOOK. Never studied beforehand and get all 95+ on exams. TA's are lenient graders and sometimes I would be too lazy to do the full assignment and still get a 100. This is the easiest class I have ever taken in my life.
Such a great professor, lectures are super engaging and non mandatory, Bowers is a very funny and chill person, I'd highly recommend this class

Dr. Bowers is a great guy! His KIN 312M course was very interesting and eye-opening, coming from someone who did not care about sports at all! His assignments and exams are very straightforward and he wants you to do well. Take this class!!

This class was really easygoing, it was also more interesting than expected! You do not need sports knowledge for this class, but it definitely helps. There are group projects but they are fairly simple.
Attendance isn't mandatory, and all tests are online and open note. There are ten questions on each test from the "Sports Talk" classes but can be found when rewatching recorded lectures during test.

Such an easy class. I never read the books, or showed up to class and still got an A. As long as you do the canvas assignments online you'll be fine. The book quizzes were one question, no lockdown browser on anything. The only class you wanna pu to is the discussion. Every assignment is so easy. No tests. Highly recommend.
I loved the class as a whole. However, the TA for the class seemed inconsistent with what he was looking for when it came to each project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is so fun and interesting and he really enjoys what he teaches.

Dr. Bowers is a great professor! He cares a lot about his students. He brings in really cool speakers and keeps you engaged through the whole lecture. There are a few assignments long assignments, but they are so fun to do that you'll want to do them! Take him to have a great UGS

Dr. Bowers was great! I would definitely recommend taking this class with him if you need it. There is no final exam, but there are four 50 question exams throughout the semester that are open-note and can be taken outside of class. If you do the readings, pay attention in class, and take good notes you should do fine on the exams. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowers was an amazing professor! This class is extremely easy, and attendance isn't mandatory. Would 100% take this class again.

chill prof, take this class if you need it with bowers. attendance isn't mandatory but i would go to some or watch the lectures because the tests are based on the lectures. awesome and funny guy, easy A
Easy A, take if needed or for credit. great teacher and really cares about what he teaches. Very motivational and please do the extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowers was such an amazing professor. Class is an easy A and he intentionally designed it like. Some assignments are centered around professional development, like resume writing and creating a LinkedIn, which was so helpful! He is such a nice guy who makes a genuine effort to connect with every student and help them enjoy the class.

Dr. B is a genuine and nice dude. Attendance isn't mandatory and he posts lecture recordings. Assignments were easy to do and exams are open note. He has a textbook that he and some colleagues wrote that is very important for the exams, so definitely get it. Great and caring professor! Definitely would recommend this course.

He is just plain awesome. His class is really easy and he is very accessible outside of class. He always responds daily and is very kind to everybody who comes to his class. I feel like this class it is impossible to not get an A of how much things are graded upon by participation. In other words, just take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No complaints. Very straightforward, interesting, and reasonable. Just a very good person. Do not take advantage of his kindness, the class is already pretty easy if you just do what you're told. I didn't realize how intricate leadership and teamwork was until I took this class.

Dr. Bower's UGS303 "Building Winning Teams" was truly an amazing course. Personally, I didn't attend class or the discussion section after the third week of school, but didn't fall behind. Although I had some friends in the course that helped me out, this class really does require minimal work, and you don't need to read the textbooks.

Dr. Bowers course is top-notch! Easy understanding of sports management concepts, great structure, real-world relevance. Overall, a standout experience. Highly recommend Dr. Bowers for setting the standard in sports management!

Dr. Bowers is literally the BEST professor I have had so far. His lectures are super engaging, course work is not heavy at all, he even gives out some test answers in his lecture! Tests are all online and open note, and the grading is very lenient. PLEASE take this class!

Dr. Bowers kept students engaged through jokes, videos, and guest speakers. His course was organized and pretty straightforward what was expected. I would recommend paying attention to the details during lectures for trick questions on exams. Three exams, 15% each. He also incorporates "future-me" assignments like creating a LinkedIn account.

If you take Dr.Bowers, you're in great hands. I highly recommend staying in contact with Dr.Bowers through you sports journey here at UT. Dr.Bowers is very helpful, as long as you show up to class speak up and talk and actually participate and get excited about the course work you'll get an easy A. Great teacher to the subject of sports.

Dr. Bowers is one of the best teachers at UT. It may take a moment to build a relationship with him because he has so many students who want his feedback, but if you put effort into the class, and show up, good things will happen. The class is very interesting, and I was able to learn a lot. The lectures are great, so show up and have a good time.

Coming back a year later to say he's the best professor I've ever had and this class was the best. The class is not too hard, but you still have to work for your grade. Go to class, take notes, put effort into assignments and you'll be fine. Basic college things. He meanwhile is amazing. Truly cares & sets up sports students for success. A++ class.

Dr. Bowers was great to take if you are interested in sports management. He cares so much about the subject and wants his students to succeed. You definitely do have to attend lecture and read the textbook if you want to do good on exams.

Best Professor I have had at UT. If you want to have any job in the world of sports, there is no better person at this university to develop a meaningful relationship with. Loved every second of his class, and it is a pretty straightforward A with minimal effort. I literally cannot recommend taking 312m enough, even if not a KIN major.
Amazing professor. I loved him. This class is set up for you to succeed with a high grade and future skills.

Professor Bowers was my favorite professor this semester. He is super chill and very understanding about late work if you just reach out. The books we read were actually extremely interesting and life changing, and the reading checks are super easy if you just read the books. No tricks.

Dr. Bowers is amazing and makes coming to class actually worth it. He posts recordings of all of his lectures and Friday's are optional (Definitely recommend going). Tests are open note but definitely recommend going to class or watching the lectures. Super laid back class and provides amazing volunteer/job resources throughout the semester.

Dr. Bowers is amazing and makes coming to class interesting. He posts recordings of all the lectures. We did not have to attend class on Fridays and instead had a Zoom meeting that would be recorded and posted later if you missed it. He is very flexible with deadlines if you are involved with UT and have conflicts. Tests are online and open note.

Dr. Bowers was an amazing professor. I like that he is super relaxed, but holds a high standard for his students because it shows that he really cares. Homework is pretty light, occasionally an assignment will be difficult, but nothing that takes forever to do. Textbooks were only used for tests, which were open book/note.

I would jump off a bridge for this man. He is such an amazing professor and a quality person. The class has three big exams that he prepares you amply for. The other assignments are layups. He is also a great person to talk to one on one and makes an effort to get to know you. 100/10

Really enjoyed this class! Lectures are all engaging and easy to follow, and we have fun sports talks every Friday. There are 3 exams based on both the lecture material and material in the textbook, and the questions can get specific so take good notes. He also gives out a few exam questions every lecture so look out for that.
Great teacher. Recognized me outside of class the next semester after only meeting with him once. Test are online timed, open note. Pay close attention. Paper/group work. TAs will grade these
Loved dr bowers this semester, very good professor and is clearly passionate about helping us pass. Exams are actually a little tough but I never got below an 80 on them.
Very easy class. Do the reading and class projects and you should get an A.

Professor Bowers is the best professor I have had at UT. He was so nice, and his class was a breath of fresh air. I really enjoyed everything and he treated us like actual humans. The tests were open note and really straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowers was by far my favorite professor this semester as it is visibly evident that he cares about his students and will plan class according to their pleasing. Just ask and he will cancel class for a specific day. The organization of this course is very flexible and although readings are assigned, you can absolutely pass without them.
Bowers is definitely passionate about teaching this course and makes class fun. As long as you take some notes and read the chapters, you will make an A! The tests are open book and open note.

I loved Dr. Bowers' class this past semester. Everyone that I've talked to has truly enjoyed having him as a professor. Our exams were open note and if you watched the lectures, he would usually give out at least 10 of the exam questions (w/ answers) before the next exam. His material was engaging and he truly cares about each of his students.
Dr. B is a great professor. He truly cares for his students. Easy class. Minimal assignments. Definitely recommend.

Professor Bowers is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is such a genuine, kind guy and the class was surprisingly interesting. I was skeptical because it was about sports but I loved it and he made it school feel fun again.

If you ever have the chance to take a class with Dr. B, do it! You wont regret it. He is such an awesome professor, his lectures are interesting and engaging. He is also very easy to talk to you and get a long with. He is very understanding and caring of his students. He is truly a class act. My favorite professor by far.

This was a great class! Even though it is primarily about sports, I enjoyed it having no sports background. You'll read 3 books, they're all pretty good. Dr. Bowers tries so hard and clearly loves his kids. I really appreciated how kind he was all semester. This was a great UGS303. If you like sports, definitely choose this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You need to read the textbook for the 50 MC question exam. Attend lectures bc Bowers will give you about 15 questions for the exam, and tell you tricks for his exam. Content and lectures were AWESOME and I loved going to class. Discussion is easy if you work with your group and get work submitted when you're there. You can also find/make quizlets.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. B was the best professor I've had at UT! He cares so much for his students and it shows. If you attend his lectures, he gives out exam Q's and never fails to make the class entertaining.
Dr. Bowers is probably the best college professor I've had

**Truth** Lecture - He starts each class with an open dailogue with the class about recent sports news. His lecture are not very tantilizing but he throws in videos and test questions that help to keep you engaged Lab- At the beginning of the semester we split into groups based on birth month (same groups all semester) and have a report each week

Case studies that are ambiguous and it doesn't get any easier until you see what an "A" case study looks like. If you do not read, YOU WILL FAIL the course. I took Bowers for KIN312M, but KIN357 is more challenging.

Dr. B is fantastic and I recommend him to all Kinesiology majors, especially if you are interested in sports at all. I am a sport management major so I might be a little biased but he is probably the best professor I have had so far.
Such a genuine and awesome professor. Lectures are fun and engaging. Tests were fairly difficult but he helps you out a lot. Loved being in this class.
Amazing professor at teaching and interacting with students, one of the best I have ever had.

Dr. Bowers is amazing! Has very engaging powerpoints that make it easy to pay attention in lecture. Discussion sections are very interesting, and you even run an NBA 2K simulation throughout the semester for extra credit. Reading the textbook and the novel he assigns is recommended to do well on the tests. Very willing to give you any help!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowers is an Amazing professor, and is very passionate about his job. I loved his classes and DEFINITELY recommend it to everyone. You do have to read, but it is nothing overwhelming and the topics are pretty interesting especially if you are into sports.

Dr. Bowers was a great professor. His class gives you good information on sport management while also being fairly easy. You do have to read the textbooks and the novel, but they are both easy reads. Also show up for class because he gives several free exam questions every lecture.

Dr. Bowers genuinely cares about his students and wants the best for everyone. I highly recommend going into his office hours because he is super easy to talk to and will hook you up with a bunch of connections. TAKE HIM!!!

Bowers was an amazing professor who truly understands and cares about the subject. He is well known within sport management and has a bunch of connections. I learned so much from this class and I definitely recommend!
Dr. Bowers care about his students. Def. take him! Learned so much from the class and him.

I enjoyed this class. The tests were all from the 2 books and lectures. One book is interesting and the other not so much but bearable. I read the books before the day of the test and the day I read it a few days early I ended up with a C for a grade. Knoq what you read! lectures are interesting if you like sports, project is easy! Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowers is hands-down the best professor at The University of Texas. His lectures are super engaging and interesting and he's a great contact to have. He's the middle man for all of the job/internship opportunities so stay close to him! Take this man's class!

Bowers is a great lecturer! His class is relaxed and the work load is fairly light. I didn't like the discussion group assignments that went with the class because I don't like group work. He's an easy grader though. The tests were multiple choice and true/false.

Dr. B is hands down my favorite professor ever, and this class was one of my favorites,too. Engaging, fun, easy with some effort. He's a great guy so get to know him better. He spends 5 mins beginning of every class just talking sports news. I 11/10 recommend this class if you're interested in sports. 3 exams, couple easy case studies, no final.

Bowers is a really great professor. He's young and easy to connect with and likes to start class by discussing current events in the sport world. He gives you around 3 free test questions/answers at each lecture, so it's definitely a good idea to attend class! Discussion section assignments were ridiculously easy and graded very easily.

He's an extremely interesting guy and a great professor for sports management. He's definitely one that you would want if you were studying at UT. He's very friendly and approachable, and he's one of the best professors at UT.

I had Matt as a TA then as a prof. He was an awesome TA, and I was super excited when I found he would be the professor of one of my classes. He loves what he does, shares his interests with you in case you may be interested too, and is willing to help you long after you are finished with his courses. Plus, he wears cool sweaters. #swagg

Quite frankly Dr. Bowers is the man!  You can tell he enjoys what he teaches and he thoroughly enjoys the company of his students.  He will do what he can to help you do well in his class.  Overall the class is pretty easy, in fact going to class is fairly optional if you read the book and vice versa.  The test are straight from the book.

Dr. Bowers was once my TA then my professor. As a professor he's a great guy. Keeps the class interested and discussion flowing. We watched multiple films that were interesting. He will help you with anything. Discussion sections require some work but I thoroughly enjoy him as a professor.
Course was informative and interesting. Professor is knowledgeable and, more importantly, actually cares about what he is teaching. Do the readings and show up to class and you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was well structured and I found the lectures engaging and interesting. Very friendly and understanding teacher who genuinely cares about what he does.

He is a very good lecturer. There are a lot of assignments based on readings, but as long as you do them, you should be fine. In class quizzes can be more difficult, but they are a smaller part of your grade. Majority of the grade comes from essays based on books. Overall, if you put effort into this class, it's not bad at all.

Outstanding lectures, he is genuinely skilled in that regard. Attendance is not mandatory but you will want to attend, every class is like watching a well-produced documentary. Has a lot of passion for what he teaches and you learn a lot being in the room. 2 book essays and no exams, would definitely  recommend this as a UGS.
He is very lenient

He is a very engaging lecturer, cares about his students and is funny. If you pay attention and do your work you will be fine. The only thing is the 10 question pop quizzes in class that you have 3 min for. Those are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are fun and engaging. But. Essays are very TA dependent, and midterm and final are heavily weighted, with a lot of quotes needed to be memorized. He said there would be a curve at the end but there was not any too.

Grading methods are ridiculous. 5 papers about books are graded by the TAs and are 50% final grade. The exams are awful, midterm is memorizing quotes from philosophers and essay which seems to be graded poorly. Does not respect your time or autonomy.

Grading methods are absurd. 5 papers about books are graded by TAs (50% final grade). Weekly quizzes based on participation(10%). The exams are terrible, midterm is memorizing quotes from philosophers and essay which seems to be graded extremely bad or good. Final is memorizing 150 quotes, 150 concept questions, asked 55 of each. Lectures are ok.

This is such a hard UGS, please don't take it. Professor was nice but not worth it all. Though I got an A, I was struggling to pull through the semester. There were weekly quizzes which were 20 questions IN 5 MINUTES & daily readings. It's ridiculous. Tests were hard to prepare for & difficult. I went to every lecture & it didn't help at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Its a tough class for a UGS, lot's of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though I ended with an A the exams were pretty hard. It varies per semester but the midterm was just quotes and a short essay and the final was 110 mcq in 50 mts. he gives practice exams but be aware that there def going to be questions on the exam you didn't see on your 12+ attempts so be ready to read. Go to the lectures, I wish I did!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bonevac's class is interesting, but the grading can be harsh. Attend lectures and use Unstuck study for quiz prep - it really helped me get an A despite the tough final.

As a person and lecturer Professor Bonevac is phenomenal. However the amount of work expected from this UGS class is ridiculous you are expected to memorize about a thousand quotes from multiple different authors as well as writing an entire essay for both exams in the class. Sad my GPA took a hit because of his high expectations.

Professor Bonevac is an excellent lecturer. His way of breaking down theories allows you to grasp the more difficult components and is very engaging. This course is graded through essays, which he allows plenty of time and freedom to complete, as well as feedback on rough drafts. He is very high spirited, good humored, and values participation.

Professor Bonevac is an extremely talented lecturer. You don't have to work super hard to get a good grade in his class, but he's a smart guy. He doesn't require attendance, but every class is fascinating. Highly, highly recommend if you like philosophy. Do the quizzes - you'll need them on the final exam.

Graded only by papers, paper peer reviews (completion, basically), attendance, and a paper rewrite at end of sem. FANTASTIC lectures- doesn't make you feel stupid for having questions and encourages opposing viewpoints. Interactive lectures and you get a lot out of them if you participate. Read the texts to do well on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The final was a harder compilation of all the quizzes through the year, but not open book or internet. half memorizing quotes, half ideas. I advise learning the content as you go instead of googling all the quiz answers (like I did). Papers are pretty easy, didn't attend lectures or spend time outside of taking quizzes. Harder side of UGS classes.

Very nice guy with extremely entertaining lectures. There's weekly quizzes and barely any homework. However, much of the grade is dictated by TA-graded papers that were graded harshly despite no rubric being given. The final was very difficult but mimicked the practice one. Most people complaining didn't attend class (avg 30% went to lectures).

The class is mainly graded on 2 papers that are okay for a ugs, weekly quizzes that aren't difficult, and the final. Yes, the final this year was hard but not impossible if you put in enough time and studied. I didn't pay attention at all in class, but I studied all of the slide packs and got over 100 on the final. Definitely doable if you study.

Professor Bonevac is an amazing lecturer who makes the content really interesting. There are weekly quizzes with a short time limit but aren't difficult if you put in a little effort. There are two papers (1000 words) that aren't hard if you read the books. There is a final exam which isn't hard if you go over the presentations and attend lectures.

Do not take Prof. Bonevac if you want to pass UGS. He gave a final with 65 quotes that is worth 15% of your grade. He is also pressed that students do not show up to class in an attendance optional class and grades students unfairly. UGS should be a course that is passable for students who put in the work and accessible for non-philosophy majors.

If you are looking for an A, take UGS in spring with easier courses. Sure, he's a great lecturer and his classes are entertaining for the first week or so, but class attendance plummets afterward for good reason. No rubrics besides a vague syllabus and overall course is pretty TA dependent on essays. TAKE OTHER UGS IF YOU NEED 4.0

Not too sure why everyone is raving this UGS. So if you have to pick a UGS literally pick any other one, especially if you don't care about philosophy. this UGS was scheduled 4/5 days a week and you have something to read before each class. The assignments are easy yes, but the TA's grade so harsh for things with no rubric. He's nice but it's a no.

60% of the classwork was just essays. If you hate writing papers this class isn't for you. Attendance isn't required and the finals worth only 15%. The topics themselves were confusing and all over the place. But overall, passionate professor. If you're looking for an easy UGS credit I would recommend him

Professor Bonevac is one of UT's most respected. He is incredibly engaging and well-respected across campus, although the class is a bit difficult. If you want just an easy A, perhaps you might want to look otherwise. If you really are interested in philosophy, this is right up your alley!

The people complaining are either lazy or just dull. If you just show up and listen, you don't even have to read super carefully. If you want to load your schedule with easy A's (and graduate w/ no more knowledge than you started with) then don't take him. If you want to learn interesting things from a great professor, then I recommend Prof Bonevac
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is quirky. classes are boring and he posts all online so thats nice bc class isnt mandatory. there are 2 tests (which is new) he used to not have tests just a final paper (10-15 pgs). The tests are one page and are difficult, and really specific on topics if you dont study or know quotes from tons of philosophers. Did not enjoy.

The only people rating Dr. B high are the ones who enjoy Philosophy. There were 2 exams worth 40 percent, the midterm and final, a term paper worth 40 percent, and random quizzes that were 20 questions in 8 minutes. DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR AN EASY ETHICS OR CD FLAG!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ideas of the Twentieth Century is a fantastic class. Bonevac is an amazing orator and deeply cares about teaching. Even if you don't like philosophy, this class is wonderful. Quizzes are not hard, and you'll do fine on papers if you make the effort. Discussions with TAs are engaging and fun, and my TA, Andrea Villalba, was particularly great.
Best professor at UT

Professor Bonevac made material that I found boring to be somewhat interesting. No exams, only a few short written assignments that you have to read a book for, and attendance is not mandatory. Overall, an easy A, and definitely a great choice to get your UGS done.
The class is super easy and you really don't even have to go to lectures to get a good grade in the class. Just read the books for the papers.

There were weekly quizzes but they were easy and you can easily find the answers to them. Basically don't have to go to discussions or class because everything can be found online. Have to write 2 papers on books but summaries are good and TAs are easy graders.

Bonevac's lectures are fun because of how animated he is, and he explains abstract concepts with good examples. If you're taking this class to learn about philosophy, you'll like the class. If you're looking for an easy A, you'll love it too because there are a few short essays that are graded very leniently and short easy quizzes(online).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a caring, funny, and great professor for this class, this is the professor you want. You can tell how much Bonevac enjoys what he is talking about and I'll admit, I'm not the biggest into philosophy, but he made the class enjoyable and interesting. Highly recommend!

Definitely the most unique lecturer I've ever had. Clear concept explanations and tangible material made this class a break from my others to go to lecture. My TA was super lenient so halfway through the semester I stopped going to lecture all together since grades are papers and online quizzes. I wish him the best for his health.
Super easy UGS course, don't need to go to lectures but Bonevac is very kind and good at lecturing. Take if you want a free class and need the UGS credit.

Professor Bonevac is great! The class isn't especially difficult, and he does his best to make lectures engaging (including cute cat pics)! As a lover of the humanities, I greatly enjoyed his combination of history, literature, art, and poetry as a segway to learning about philosophy. I definitely recommend this UGS!

This was my last choice for a UGS and it wasn't too bad. I am not interested in philosophy so this class was not very fun for me, but its easy to get an A. Dr. Bonevac is a great professor, and the assignments are pretty straight forward. It may be an uninteresting class if philosophy isn't for you, but it is an easy A if you're looking for a UGS.

Easy class. You don't need to go if philosophy does not interest you. Make sure to attend and participate in discussion and you will be fine. Weekly quizzes (online) and you get 3 attempts. A few papers throughout the year but they are extremely easy prompts. If you need a UGS, this class is perfect.

Loved his UGS class so much that I'm planning on taking his philosophy+business class in the coming semesters. If you're interested in philosophy but not a philosophy major or anything like that, I think this is one of the best UGS classes to take. It gave me such an excellent foundation when looking at current events and earlier philosophy.

Prof. Bonevac has a very upbeat, engaging and goofy (in a good way) personality! If you pay attention, you can really learn a lot in the class especially from the powerpoints. 12 assignments total (mostly short writing essays 500 words max and about 3 short quizzes) only best 10 are taken. No late penalty. Great if you enjoy philosophy or business!

Professor Bonevac is so sweet and really cares about his students. He's a great professor and pretty funny, so his lectures are always engaging. Grade is based on weekly assignments that are usually really easy as long as you have a basic understanding of the readings of the week. Overall, a really great prof and relatively easy class

UGS303 was just mediocre. The whole class was just boring. If you don't like philosophy, good luck in lecture. However, it was very easy to get an A-. tbh you don't really have to go to class if you don't want to, you don't need most of the info from lecture. Bonevac is kind of an oddball but he is at least funny.
Took the UGS for credit but loved the course! Super interesting. The course was presented as a lot of work but when you really got into it, it really wasn't a lot at all.

If philosophy isn't interesting to you, DON'T TAKE IT! Grading is based entirely on easy weekly quizzes and 5 essays. My TA was incredibly vague about grading essays and the professor responded to my concerns only months after I emailed him. It got really frustrating especially since there was no proper feedback in order to do better on essays.

Hated this class, there are easier UGS options. Had to spend way too much time reading, he rarely finished lecture power point slides, and he made several lectures weirdly political. It is possible to do well but if you want to ever enjoy philosophy after this, don't take this class

I absolutely loved Dr. Bonevac's class, as it was both interesting and laid-back. Dr. Bonevac was funny, lighthearted, and passionate about making students think. Grades are based on weekly quizzes (3 attempts) and several papers which are pretty straightforward. TAs grade the papers, so hope for a easy grader as it will determine your grade.

Such an amazing teacher. He actually cares about the subject and gives entertaining lectures. You don't actually have to attend class or do any of the readings. There are no tests or final-you're only graded on easy quizzes and 5 essays, 2 of which are super short. Your grade does heavily depend on which TA you have, though.

As a bio major, this class was a nice change of pace. Lectures were fun, and quizzes were manageable. There were about 4 papers, but the readings for them were interesting. Overall a great UGS course!

Bonevac is a great lecturer and Ideas of the 20th Century is an incredibly easy class. Most of your assignments are quizzes that can be taken 3 times for the highest grade and the majority of questions are quotes. Most of your important grades come from TAs but since Daniel is an important professor he gets the best ones. Easy, worthwhile class.

I'm taking his Organizational Ethics class and he is one of the best professors I have had. He is always enthusiastic and actually understanding/helpful. Breath of fresh air in a rough semester. He assigns 5-10 page readings for each week (not always necessary to read) & very few homeworks. definitely recommend!!

Such a kind teacher who genuinely just wants his students to care and learn about the material. It is obvious that he is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, and is really entertaining. His lectures always go by fast as he makes the content relatable, has good humor, always takes questions and seems to be just a happy guy.

He is passionate and informed ab philosophy. His lectures are long, slow, and boring. There's a few papers over the semester graded by the TAs. They expect you to be able to have a colligate level philosophical analysis in these papers even though it's a freshman course & they don't teach how to write them at all. Not suited for nonphil majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a very intelligent man but his lectures are boring and very fast. There is an insane amount of readings which are long. The quizzes are all about memorizing quotes from dozens of readings (which is extremely difficult). Essays were graded tough and there was never a clear rubric for them. There are def more interesting and easier UGS classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The thing which made this class so difficult was the grading criteria: it was NOT clear at all. It seemed as if the TAs if asked could rarely tell you what they truly graded for in your essay so therefore each essay (there were A LOT and they weren't easy) would be graded entirely differently even when the type of essay would be the exact same.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonevac is brilliant. His lectures are encompassing, insightful, and clear. I highly recommend taking any of Dr. Bonevac's classes so you can hear his lectures.

I took UGS 303: Ideas of the Twentieth Century in Fall 2020 when everything was online so keep that in mind. This class was taught entirely through seven-year-old Youtube videos and weekly discussions with a TA. How good your TA is can make or break you. The weekly quizzes are not too bad since you have three tries. No tests otherwise. Only papers.

He's an inspiring lecturer, very quirky with how he talks. Although I do have to argue his testing and readings do affect the class. It's very specific and unless you are willing to fully comprehend every philosophy concept, this will be harsh waters for tests.

I took PHL 301 with Professor Bonevac in my first semester of freshman year. Quickly I found it to be useful to work with a group to do quizzes and that the practice exams he posts on canvas are very helpful. Professor Bonevac is an amazing lecturer and very understanding, all the midterms are reasonable but the final was hard. 3 papers 3 exams
Nice/smart man but very difficult tests. Lots of quote memorization.

Ideas of the 20th Century. Pretty easy class, mostly tests identifying authors. A few essays, but your TAs really determine the grades on those, so ask them questions about requirements. An easy enough course, but fairly dull and Bonevac is eccentric and often confusing. Few tests or assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Smart and witty
Love this professor. One of a kind. A captivating speaker who is very unique, brilliant, and witty. Youll be hard pressed to find another professor of this caliber teaching a class at a university.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The most brilliant professor I've ever had!!! You almost can't believe that you get to listen and dialogue with someone of this caliber! If you're at all philosophically inclined, you'll love him!

Great and dynamic professor, but very difficult class. I'm interested in philosophy so I was excited to go to each class, and he makes it really digestible (relates a lot of the concepts back to the real world and pop culture). However, the concepts are hard and the tests are hard too, so def don't take this for an easy A
interesting topics but usually ran out of time to explain at the end of lectures.

Although PHL 325L was an interesting class and Bonevac is one of the best professors in his department, the class definitely had its imperfections (due to Bonevac's first time teaching the class). Students final grade was determined by two tests and one term paper. Neither were particularly hard but having only 3 assignments adds difficulty.

I learned so much from Ideas of the 20th Century. Note: it is neither purely history nor philosophy. When I asked Bonevac, he described it as an "old school humanities course" that combines both. 2 papers. 2 short essays. 2 tests. Weekly quizzes. If take & study quizzes then tests are manageable. Med-low grades occur to slackers. Failing is rare.

My favorite first semester professor. You need to like philosophy, reading, history, thinking about thinking. If you don't, you'll be miserable. I found every lecture interesting and enlightening. Only a few grades, though. Justin is the best T.A., he just catches you off guard at first. Prof. loves this stuff, and lecture feels like a documentary.

Dr. Bonevac is really adorable and is really passionate about what he teaches. I wouldn't recommend for people who do not care about philosophy. Take an easier UGS class bc this one is really test heavy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: UGS Ideas was an interesting change of class for me as an engineering student. Bonevac has really interesting lectures and knows his stuff. At the same time, his exam is really specific. You'll have to read two books and write two essays which aren't terribly hard but can be stressful with the time constraint.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Posts slides online so you don't have to go to class. Papers only kind of relate to the course material. Only two tests, a midterm and final, that are 50% of your grade. The rest is made up of papers and quizzes. The quizzes are 25 questions in 5 minutes which sucks. A tough class if you don't care all that much for philosophy

Dr. Bonevac is awesome. He's a very interesting lecturer and is hilarious. He can go very quickly through difficult concepts but he records his lectures every class and then posts them online after. If you're looking for an easy UGS this is not the class for you but if you have any interest in philosophy take it.
Bonevac is fantastic! This class was fun because of him. This class was actually pretty hard, but he's a great professor.

Dr. Bonevac is an okay professor. He's very knowledgable on his topics and all but can also be hard to understand. His lectures are sorta like rambles of sorts > hard to follow. Not the best if you're detail oriented.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bonevac is a nice guy, but he talks too fast and often loses his train of thought. It's hard to keep up with what he is lecturing on because he goes off tangent very often. Philosophy should be taught by someone more concise.

This class was pretty good, and the workload was very manageable. There are quizzes due at the end of every week, and there are 4 papers written over lectures and books. The final exam can maybe destroy you if you have been googling all of the answers for the quizzes, because then you won't know the information. Start studying for that early!
He is a genius but pay attention because he talks extremely fast. Applies philosophy to the Simpsons which is always entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: he gave out a lot of info in his lectures so going to class is a good idea. reading the assigned texts really helps you understand what is going on in class. hes a really cool dude and makes so many Simpson references. easy to talk to and get advise for papers. the only thing is theres no tests just a final with all the info from the whole year.

Great prof with interesting lectures, nice and approachable. Attendance wasn't a grade. Class was mostly essays that were graded by a TA so mostly depended on them. The final was pretty difficult though, had a high A heading in to it, studied a lot, but it still knocked me down to barely an A- , a lot of people did badly on the final.
Great professor, but the class was pretty hard. It was a philosophy course. I am a chemistry major, so philosophy is not my forte.

The class itself was easy... up until the final. The final exam was VERY specific, and covered very minute details that seemed unimportant to the main idea of lectures. Making your own study guides for people and ideas, as well as reviewing/memorizing past quizzes helps tremendously. MY TA (Ben) was great, too. Find another UGS -- NOT AN EASY A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Deep existential crises may ensue... Hilarious, brilliant professor. Use of Simpsons/Rick and Morty clips to explain concepts. Pay attention in lecture and the textbook is only supplementary. Quizzes are easy A's. Keep track of the material, though, because you have to know the content to pass the final. He doesn't take attendance, but show up!!

Cool dude. I loved his lectures, some people did fall asleep though. The class is basically powerpoints he posts online, but I still took notes. There's a quick quiz every week, but this is a large portion of your grades. Paper grades are important too, only about 5 papers, 1-2 pages long. Only those who skipped had trouble

This is by far not the easiest UGS credit, but it's not that bad. My TA was amazing which helped because they grade. Bonevac has great lectures and others that make you want to fall asleep. THE FINAL IS AWFUL, so keep up with the work and make sure you have a lot of slack going into it. Also find a group to take quizzes with, they will save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Free 25% online quizzes, 5% discussion attendance (1/wk, can miss 2) rest is all written, so know your TA and make sure they know you, by name. You do not need to go to class, but bonevac is passionate and the stuff is interesting. 25% final, hard (72 avg but doable, use quizlets) Dont buy the history book!!! difficult A, find another UGS

Good teacher and can be scattered but is passionate about the material. However, your grade relies mostly on your TA and some TAs grade really tough while others are lenient. Reading will prepare you for the discussion class and papers. Enjoyed the material even though I'm in STEM. Do not take this UGS if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about, and if you reach out to him he will listen. He's respectful and respectable, class isn't difficult especially if you're into philosophy. Keep up with the quiz questions to do well.

I had a 96 in the class. After the final, my grade dropped to an 87. Don't underestimate the final. The quote part was easy. The MC after the quotes was the hard part. out of the 45 MC I knew maybe 10 of them. It was straight up guessing after that. Quizzes every week. 3 papers. Not to mention a lot of the stuff you learn is boring.

Bonevac is an awesome lecturer and he tries his hardest to use every day examples to make difficult concepts easier to understand. He is VERY understanding that you have other classes and a life, so he moves due dates to give extra time due to holidays or other inconveniences. He also records his lectures and puts them on YouTube. TAKE HIM!

Loved Dr. Bonevac and this class! Made confusing concepts much easier to understand. Very fair grader and takes TA toughness into account. Crazy intelligent but approachable. He used Simpsons clips as examples. Always happy to talk with students, gives advice, welcomes student feedback. Loves what he does. Endearing, engaging. TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Make sure you don't skip classes from the beginning (it is so hard since attendance isn't mandatory and he uploads lectures on youtube). Keep up with the lectures, take good notes and enjoy the class! It definitely teaches you a lot of stuff and he tries to make it interesting with personal anecdotes and corny jokes.

Weekly quizzes, four essays, and one final so do well. Philosophy isn't my thing so it was hard for me. Bonevac is really cool though and tries his best to make it easy. His jokes are corny and awkward which makes them funny. Always wants to take about his 20 cats. Go to discussion!!! Read read read!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Bonevac is an amazing professor! He truly cares about his students actually learning the material instead of focusing on grades as some professors like to do. Lectures are not mandatory, but it's a great disservice to yourself not to go, as his lectures are very intresting and often hilarious. I would definitely recommend Dr. Bonevac!

The smartest man I've ever spoken to. So much so, it's hard to have a convo with him. Anyways, attendance isn't mandatory but if you start skipping early on you'll fail the final like I'm going to this Friday. You'll have a 99 in the class like I do right now because of the easy online quizzes, but it won't matter in the end. *DONT SKIP!*
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bonevac loves to talk (and fast). Lots of information is covered and it's hard to see how it connects. The tests are ridiculous - questions over minute details. It's impossible to read everything, but you need to read a lot. Most of your interaction and grading is with a TA. It was nice the lectures were also available online but I never used them.

He records all of his lectures and puts them on YouTube, so if you want to see what this class is like go watch a lecture. 1 midterm, 4 essays over 3 assigned books, and one lecture paper. This class is pretty hard for a UGS especially if you aren't into history and philosophy. There are a lot of daily readings as well that are lengthy.
100% recommend.

I'm glad Prof. Bonevac was one of my last philosophy professors. He always made the content interesting (his impressions are hilarious) and is interested in his students' success. Don't skip as attendance is one of the only grades in this glass besides a long paper due as your final. Probably my favorite philosophy professor at UT. Take his class!

Professor Bonevac is my favorite professor at UT in the time I have been here. His lectures are interesting and he always uses good examples to illustrate the ideas he's trying to convey. He's a pretty funny guy and an overall great person. I would take this class again in a heartbeat.

He's a great lecturer who really loves what he's doing. He does a really good job at giving general overviews of different philosophers' ideas and how they relate with other philosophers' ideas. He really knows how to engage the class, often showing the Simpsons in class. He's a big part of the reason why I'm now double majoring in Philosophy.

Love him as a professor! He's super personable and he made lectures fun to listen to. Grades are determined by TAs who will be grading essays (some are a LOT easier than others). Tests are decent, just pay attention and make sure you get the key points. I made.

Super nice Professor. Some concepts are confusing, but he tries his best to explain it and is very lenient with grading.
