He genuinely wants you to understand the material and tries to make the boring parts as interesting as possible . Encourages discussion, and never puts down an answer, but rather tries to incorporate it into the lesson.

Bonevac is seriously the most interesting man in the world. I took Ideas of the 20th Century, and it was pretty enjoyable. There is a bit of reading, and a couple of papers but he really listens to his students feedback--go to him if your TA is grading weird.  I went to his office hours and he is really helpful and let me take my final early!

Great professor. Passionate and funny. Five short papers, graded by TA. If you want to skip discussion, make sure your TA is chill. A midterm and a non-comprehensive final, both of which are multiple choice and just memorization of key quotes and concepts. Generous grader, tries to make sure everyone who tries passes.

Bonevac's  a great teacher. There was a midterm and final, but they're only quotations from the readings and ppts. If you show up to class, then you'll have nothing to worry about. His lectures are fun, because he's super passionate. TAs can determine your grade because of papers, but if you have an issue, Bonevac WILL work with you.
Lectures are sporadic, not very organized. Professor is very resourceful, interested and knowledgeable about the class. Standard A, B, C system, no plus minus.

I HATE PHIL but he was a great Prof! Only 2 midterms and a Final with 8 reflection papers on confusing material. Not much wiggle room for grades. I rarely went to class and walked out with an A but because I POURED over PP and readings night before exam.  Avg. final grade was 77. Tests are hard. Don't take as blow off course cuz it could back fire.

Bonevac is an amazing professor.  The lectures were really interesting and kept you listening, however, his TAs are awful.  I got stuck with the hardest one and would make 75s on papers while friends would make 100s.  I loved the professor and the course, but I would never take another class from him again if he has the same TAs.

Honestly, Bonevac was a really cool professor, but the assignments of his class were just graded more difficultly than I had imagined. Bonevac is an awesome guy, but the grade of the class relies solely on your TA. I had a lazy TA with unconventional grading and it lead to a lot of stress. For his tests, study the powerpoints, the practice exams.

I was disappointed with this class. Bonevac, in Ideas of the 20th Century, spread ideas so thinly that just as you were grabbing on to one concept, it was ripped away and a new one was introduced. Get ready to study art, photography, philosophy (!!!), history, literature, ethics, politics, etc. Too broad of a subject to really engage in.

The Ideas of the 20th Century was a fun class. The tests are kind of hard so beware, but not too bad. There's a lot of essays in this class and the TA discussions are weird and unhelpful. However, Bonevac is awesome and very helpful and understanding. He let us take a class vote on dropping on of our essays, super nice guy and smart.

He is an amazing lecturer! you never get bored in class while he talks. He loves it when students participate. There is never a wrong answer because well its philosophy. He incorporates the Simpsons a lot in his lectures as examples. I love the class. However, the tests are a bit difficult. If you go to the office hours, he will help you.
His lectures are at the same time simplified, summarized, dense, lively, stimulating. He's a good actor. Sometimes his conservative opinions shine through.
He's funny, easy-going, and his class isn't very demanding, but he's sort of all over the place and unclear.

Dr. B is pretty much one of the best teachers you can have! He's one of those adorable funny old guys you just want to sit and have tea with :) also word of advice: you can get by with just studying the power point notes, some of the philosophers are incredibly mind-numbingly boring. tests are mult. choice, & just 5 essay assignments.

pretty good class. i wasn't in his philosophy class this was a general studies class called ideas of the twentieth century but the class was well put together and interesting. you write a few short 1 page reaction papers and a couple tests for your grade.
I am in love with Dr. Bonevac!!! He is the best professor I have ever had. If you are thinking of taking a philosophy class I definitely recommend taking one of Dr. Bonevac's classes.
Awesome
His midterm and final were EASY! Both have extra credit questions on them, and the test itself is pretty easy if you've paid attention and done the assignments for his class. Very funny.

Take him if you can. Great teacher!! You wont know what the heck he is talking about sometimes, but them he explains it in easy terms(relates philosophy to football, baseball, the simpsons, ect.). Funny guy too.

Amazing professor.  Makes philosophy interesting with simpson's clips and personal stories.  Must go to class and do the readings or you'll be lost.  He's a great lecturer.  His class is lots of fun.  The tests can be difficult if you don't do the practice test first.  Bottom line: great prof.  Take his class before leaving UT.
Fun Professor, His lectures are very interesting and will keep you awake. Multiple choice Tests, 3 HW Essays, Attendance Optional, Must do Readings!
Bonevac is an entertaining professor & a good guy. His tests can be a little challenging, but as long as you read the text you should be fine.
he's the best, hands down, if you are going to take philosophy, take it with him.
the best professor i have had in college.  he is an awesome professor.
this is the class you'll be dying to go to everytime.  lol ok maybe not but he's simpson clips always kept me entertained and related it all to philosophy.  good guy but his tests can be a challenge.
No Comments
He is incredible, his ability to be awesome is amazing.  He really listens to the students and he is fun to watch.  It was a class I actually enjoyed going to.
fun guy
awesome, and helpful in class! simpsons clips are always welcome!

won't take in class questions, you have to wait for the discussion sections. the class is mostly OK but he presents a biased version of the philosophy surrounding abortion, and he showed a video from right to life.
awesome guy. fun class. hard tests.
Awsome teacher, the best of my freshman year.
Very fun, laid back class.  He uses Simpsons clips to make his points! Major plus.  Tests are moderate with a little bit of studying.
No Comments
Clear, logical, humorous, and always ready to help students both in and outside of class.  One of the best professors of my freshman year.
Dr. Bruner is awesome. The lab TAs here are super informed on what they're doing as well, and you genuinely feel like you learn something. Perfect level of difficulty for an UD Bio lab.

Lowk flopped on that first exam which brought my grade down a lil but i dont even care because i literally love Dr. Bruner so much. Please take her. Grades are made up mostly of participation, lab quizzes, hw, and 2 exams. Make sure you watch the lecture and you'll literally be fine. Genetics is cheeks but this lab made me like it slightly better.

Dr. Bruner is very nice and wants everyone to succeed. The weekly agendas and exam reviews outline everything you need to know. No lab reports, only weekly HW after labs which saves time. Experiments are pretty cool and relevant in real-world applications

Dr. Bruner is an incredible person and proffessor who makes efforts to get to know every person in class. I felt like I got alot of Lab experience and had fun doing it. Workload very fair, breath of fresh air compared to other classes. She provides tons of resources and is just generally a great person. Go to Labs, watch the lectures

one of my favorite labs! dr. bruner is very kind and cares about students' understanding. lecture attendance is not mandatory but either go or watch the recordings to prepare for the in-lab quizzes (they can be a bit hard). exams are reasonable, homework takes effort but doable. i enjoyed the lab activities and found the experiments fun! highly rec

The best lab I ever took at UT, and one of the best professors I had as well. The lab is genuinely meant to engage you and is fun as long as you keep up with the theory (that is not difficult to understand). Dr. Bruner is really sweet and wants to see all her students succeed. The TAs are awesome and the amount of work is completely manageable.

Extremely well-structured course with very clear expectations. Tests and quizzes were not hard; if you put just a little effort into studying and doing the experiments you'll do well. Was a great class for my lab credit.

Take this class if you need it for credit! The class is really well structured, and easy compared to other labs. She always post weekly agendas on what you need for her quizzes, labs, and exams. She's a gem!

100% my favorite class and professor I've had in the 4 years i've been at UT! I genuinely looked forward to coming to class and lab every week. You write one 6 page essay over the entire semester and are given multiple opportunities to improve it. Dr. Bruner is so sweet and truly cares about her students- super accessible outside of class!

Professor Bruner was okay. The class was too easy and frankly was not even close to the level one should expect from a college level course. It was nice to gain experience with basic bio lab techniques but the exams were ridiculously easy. You have an undergrad TA grading your papers, and it is clear they put zero effort in grading papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Love her to death

Dr. Bruner was honestly such a gem. She's super sweet and teaches you everything you need to know for lab, quizzes, homework, and exams. Really you just need to pay attention during lecture which isn't bad at all because she keeps the material interesting and does frequent practice problems in class. Bruner is honestly such a 10/10 professor. Take!

Amazing professor. Dr. Bruner will tell you exactly what to study for on the weekly quizzes. Attendance for lectures is not mandatory - recordings are available. Lab quizzes weren't too difficult. They consist of questions regarding last week's lab and pre-lab for that week. One research paper on a topic of your choice. All TAs were nice as well!

Love Dr. Bruner. Very helpful and wants you to succeed. Lab was fine, I took it because I needed a lab credit and it was relatively fun. Homeworks after each lab but were straightforward. Worst thing was the research paper, but there were deadlines to help move it along and I suck at this stuff but did very well on the paper.

The class has 11 HW, pre-quiz, 4 post quiz, and a paper. I honestly think this class was not bad. Assignments were straightforward. The only thing you really need to worry about the most is the writing assignment, but even then it still pretty straight forward. This is an easy A class if you know what's going on in the lab for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Bruner! she has all the qualities that make a good professor and she really cares about the success of her students. She'll make an effort to get to know you even though it's a big class. success in the class partially matters on your lab TA but you still see her around lab and she still plays a big role in the course. 10/10.
TAKING LAB EXPERIENCE IN GENETICS RIGHT NOW! LOVE HER!

Best professor I've had at UT. She is so nice and caring! Lectures are optional, but if you go to them the weekly quizzes are really easy. There a no lab reports, but you'll spend the semester doing writing assignments as you work towards a 6-8 pg research paper. Easy A with a little effort. Labs usually did not last the entire 4 hours.

One of the best professors, if not the best, that I've encountered at UT. Its rare to find a professor who goes out of their way to help students so much on an individual basis. You can tell she really cares about her students.

Briggs is a good lecturer who cares deeply about the content, not so much about the students. He can often be passive-aggressive and spiteful of students who are not that interested in his class. Easy assignments, clear grading. Should be an easy A if you put minimal effort
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a VAPA that's fun but also easy, take this class if you can! The lectures are interesting and you will only have to write two essays and take a couple quizzes that aren't very hard. While attendance is mandatory, he won't take it every day. He does not allow devices during lecture but don't let that be a dealbreaker!

loved briggs! do not be a goof in class or he will stop lecture and call you out. no technology in class and if he catches you... good luck. however, i really enjoyed how he was not a push over and was passive aggressive in a good way. he would call out people who were talking during lecture, something i loved! watch films + take notes = success!
Lectures can be long but interesting would take again.

Great professor and lecturer and is very good at explaining/vocalizing concepts. There are only a couple assignments that you should be perfectly fine for if you pay attention to his slides, do the readings, and take good notes. He is very genuine and wants you to succeed.

(RTF 306) Thanks to Prof Briggs, this is the easiest class I've ever taken, seriously! He structured it so there are only few, meaningful assignments. No busy work or anything crazy.
He's a bit passive aggressive at times, but it's just his personality and he's really a good person at heart. Do NOT go to his TAs for help if you want good answers!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super chill guy who I respect as an academic in 2025. Paper notes only, weekly film screenings, a couple easy quizzes. Ask him anything and 75% of the time he'll disagree with you. Entertaining lectures which pair perfectly with the films to immerse you into a super broad look at cinema history. Super easy VAPA A.

(RTF 306) Prof. Briggs is passionate and knowledgeable. He wants everyone to do well in the class. It is primarily lectures and in-class discussions. He can be a bit condescending towards dumb questions, but it's kinda valid. Super easy grader on papers, and the tests are essentially straight off the slides that he puts on Canvas. Easy VAPA credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Super easy - just do the bare minimum and you'll be fine. He's a little passive-aggressive like others said and frequently threatens to kick people out of the class for people too loud or disruptive. Just don't do anything that could attract his attention in class. 

Content wise is quite interesting - had a good experience.

He's a great professor. His classes are straightforward, and he explains everything clearly. The exams are based on the PowerPoint slides, so as long as you study them and watch the screenings, you'll be well-prepared. The class is also really interesting, and he's always approachable during office hours if you need help.

Super easy + interesting class. Only two tests/quizzes + 2 papers for major assignments. The rest was discussion posts and attendance. The assignments were super easy if you even remotely pay attention in class. Prof was funny but could be a bit passive-aggressive to "dumb" questions. Would def recommend its a super chill class + easy A.

The class was pretty dull, but the assignments weren't challenging. The screenings are rough at first because they are silent, but they aren't too bad once you get through them. However, he and his TA can be super passive-aggressive when critiquing your homework, so don't take it personally. I don't agree with his letterboxd ratings.

A fairly easy class. The tests aren't too difficult, as they can be taken at home, and the papers aren't graded harshly. You do have to go to all the lectures, but they're not difficult to sit through, and the professor is a cool guy.

Your grade is essentially comprised of two tests and three parts to a research project, plus your attendance. If you don't skip class and do well on those you'll be fine. Not necessarily a tough grader, but often gave passive-aggressive feedback that wasn't super constructive.

The whole class is graded on 2 exams, and 3 projects, essentially. Have to do good on those things otherwise won't be able to keep your grade up, so be careful of those deadlines. Gotta go to classes because attendance is mandatory, sadly. Teacher is okay but definitely not the best teacher that I've had. Terribly boring lectures. Could be worse ig
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a great and easy introductory course to the RTF program. Briggs' lectures were PowerPoint slides that were informational and fun. The course features a research assignment that can feel tedious but is very easy. The 3 tests (2 mid-terms, 1 final) were open-book and easy. Overall a great and caring professor who wants you to succeed.

Fairly Easy introductory course into the Development of Film & Media. The course was split between 3 Exams, all taken online open-note, and a multipart Research Project. The project had students select a topic in the history of film and complete multiple parts leading to a Final Research Proposal.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy tests and grading, not engaging or exciting to listen to but also it's 8am...
M&A Class - He skips a lot of content during lectures but his guest speakers are top notch. Be ready to study a lot before exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does NOT care about you learning the material. You will have to study slideshows 40-70+ slides long per chapter but maybe talks about 2-10 of those in class. He fully skips chapters when guest speakers come. The material is interesting he just doesn't teach it or gives long winded explanations. Be ready to stress for tests.

Takes an interesting topic and makes you dislike it. Almost 80% of classes are guest speakers, which may sound great, until exam time, when you realize he has taught nothing. Very lecture-heavy with little class participation. Exams are all written and make you teach the textbook to yourself.

good luck yall boys, if you're reading this and youre in his class, its too late for you. every test will absolutely push the limits of the human mind. every case is a arduous process. the roughest part, though, is having to sit through his class without sleeping. He doesnt respond to any questions or hands raised, and is a yapatronic. runaway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs I have ever had. I had my hand raised for 14 minutes straight and never got called on. He proceeded to ask "Any questions" while my hand was up. And then said "ok good no questions lets proceed." It has happened 5 times in 3 classes. He just reads the slides then closes his eyes or stares down and then paces back and forth.

Lectures are long but meaningful—he's passionate about fraud and wants students to truly understand it. Cases are fair, and he's always willing to talk through them. He teaches for comprehension, not just the test. If you stay engaged, you'll learn a lot.

I have taken multiple courses with this professor and he manages to make the most interesting classes such as fraud analysis sound super boring. 15 minutes will feel like the longest hour of your class. Not only does he only stare at his feet and outside the window while teaching, but he offers no help or additional learning opportunies.

He insists on testing us all the materials although some of them weren't covered in class. Offers no help prior the exam, no review session, no practice questions. His condensed slides for exams are almost 350 pages + extra readings. If you want to spend more time in class with the guest speakers, then don't put that much of a weight on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a very nice or accommodating professor. I would recommend taking a teacher who actually cares about the students

He is a good teacher, but this class is too much of a headache. He teaches with jpgs of handwritten practice problems with glare. You just end up teaching yourself through the textbook homework problems. Exams are very similar to in-class "problems." The written/essay questions are graded very hard. Disappointing because puts forth zero effort.

Pretty disappointing class; could be taught in a much more engaging manner. Cases and exams are graded stringently with incredibly specific rubrics, but there seems to be a big curve. A lot of guest speakers, but most of them don't have much to say. Bradshaw himself is fine and very smart, so I feel like he's capable of much more.

Nothing special. Simple class. The tests are based off entirely from the slides. Only pain is having through wake up at 8am to hear him lecture. He sprinkles some of the "homework" problems on the tests so make sure to review for free points. Overall, a good class because you don't have to worry about it until test week.
My man is so boring. Like he's nice but I'm telling you, everyone in my class at 8AM as I'm writing this has no desire to be here.

Prof. Bradshaw is pretty good. He's a very smart guy and his lectures are really interesting when you can stay awake through them. Textbook is a drag. Syllabus goes on a lot about participation in class but he doesn't really give any opportunities to do so. Huge curve, yet he's the easiest professor to take for audit. Solid choice.

Pretty average prof, work load is average, exams are short answer, no textbook purchase. Could have been a more interesting class, but he is so monotone it makes it hard to pay attention and enjoy the subject.
SP project is horrendous especially when you have groupmates not doing their parts on time and messing it up for everybody

Never responds to emails at all. Monotone lecturer. Exams were super confusing and never explained the group project in class. Overall, would not take his class, but it is the only choice for PBH students.

. Take dr brown pleaseee. He is the most caring proffesor ive ever had. He is always full of life and has great lectures. hes an easy grader too. He had a great passion and also cares about his students. i also loved the textbook the faddieman .
Lectures weren't great. This topic just isn't that interesting though. I participated SO much in class and still didn't get an A.
amazing professor, chill class, low effort, easy A , very understanding when it comes to deadline and group project

Lectures were boring because he was the most monotonous lecturer I've ever had. The exams were ok but had a lot of 'select the best option' type Qs, which was difficult with all the theories we needed to know. Has the worst project I've ever done in college, with the most unclear instructions. Wish we'd spent that time on the book which was great!

Dr. Brown is really nice, and his class very doable. The projects were very easy if you followed the instructions given, exams were also straight from the lectures. He's also very nice and caring. Attendance is mandatory, but you have 4 classes you can miss. This class also teaches you a lot about medicine beyond the coursework of prerequisites.

Attendance is required, however, he picks and chooses what days to set out the sign-in sheet and also does random in-class activities that counts for attendance. He never bothered to explain the project during class and the instructions posted on canvas was very unclear. His lecture slides were very unprepared and expects you to understand it.

You can get up to 4 absences but sometimes attendance is taken by surprise in-class activities, which don't count towards your absences?? Doesn't respond to emails. Didn't account for spring break for the project deadlines and made us write basically our whole paper within a week. Not a hard class but not enjoyable either.

Dr. Brown is very knowledgeable about this but this course is very assignment heavy. Attendance is mandatory via sign in sheet, and points are deducted if a student is absent. Deadlines are hard deadlines, there are no extensions, and the grading policy is not lenient. The exams are straightforward and the review is thorough, but are worth 20%.

Dr. Brown wasn't the best professor I have had at UT. However, it is an easy A.  For the exams, just read the textbook, the lectures are straight from the textbook. The "final" isn't cumulative, which is nice, and each exam is worth 5% each. He isn't very lenient with extensions, so be wary of that. He takes off points if you don't attend class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown acts like a nice guy, but his attendance policy is ridiculus, he is so unaccomdating and needs proof of any absence. Doesnt explain the group projects and his in class activities are worthless to gaining understanding. He uses honorlock like bruh were past the pandemic, stop adding to anxiety in students. I would just prefer in class test
Classwork was a bit time consuming but super easy and informative class.
He is nice but is sometimes not understanding to mess ups. Participation points are really weighted. The exams however are like 5% each of your grade.

Professor Brown is one of the most engaging professors I've had. Attendance is mandatory, but he really tries to make lectures engaging. The material is relatively easy, and lectures really help to prepare for exams which aren't hard. Lots of group projects and individual projects, but they are very manageable and graded nicely. Highly recommend!!

Dr. Brown is a nice professor and the class is very manageable as long as you pay attention and take good notes during lecture. At times he was unclear about certain assignments but the TA cleared up all misunderstandings. Attendance was mandatory with sign in sheets during class. My average dropped to an A- because of attendance so go to class!!!

I enjoyed this class and how stress-free it was. However, Dr. Brown sometimes was not the best at communicating things this semester, but it was his first semester teaching at UT, so he does deserve some credit. There is a study guide posted, so study that for sure! Also, yes attendance is required, but nothing to worry about in my opinion.
Dr. Brown is a super easy professor; take his public health course. Only thing is that attendance does matter and there is an attendance sheet that we are graded on.

Dr. Brown was likely the easiest prof I had this semester. Even though it was his first year at UT, and group project instructions were pretty confusing, the TA was the best, and he gave so much leeway in general. Tests were short and a lot fill-in-the-blank, and the test reviews/quizzes helped. Funny how we had sign-in-sheets but I would recommend
Class was easy but attendance was mandatory. Review was very helpful for tests.

I got a A but this class is subpar. Dr brown puts so much effort in making people come to class and give unnecessary work. It's like a high school class where a teacher is trying to make the class more difficult and interactive than it really is. The class was also unorganized, but it's his first year so that may get better.

Genuinely I wouldn't say I like this course; Dr. Brown makes it hard to appreciate the content of this course. He puts so much emphasis on coming to class and makes attendance mandatory just to read off slides that come straight from the textbook. This class reminds me of high school with all the unnecessary assignments and group work.
Treats our class like it's a high school course. Attenedence is taken by a SIGN IN SHEET! Like paper and pen. Imagine a 300 people course waiting to sign the lecture.

Pretty chill class. Takes attendance in lecture. There are several projects, but they are not too difficult or time consuming. Concept checks and lecture slides are directly from the textbook. Gives a study guide for exams (lecture based) that you just need to memorize. He usually lets us out a few minutes early.
Take him if you want an easy A. Uses his classes to try to get students to buy his books to fill his own pockets.

Great professor! Very easy-going and knows the topic well. Graded on only 4 assignments through the whole class other than attendance, prepare to work for the grade. He grades "old-school" so a high A on an essay is not happening. No final though! Overall, pretty good experience.

Absolute best professor at UT. If you have the opportunity to take him, DO IT!! His lectures are so interesting he makes it fun, and explains stories in almost the sense of a drama. I always enjoyed going to class. No exams, because he wants you to learn and be present in his lectures, rather than trying to type down everything he is saying.
Easiest class at this university. Lectures were interesting when I was listening, but I mostly used them to study other classes.

If you want your history credit and don't want to do any work, take this class. It is the easiest class you will take. That being said, the lectures are wholly uninteresting and the class felt more like credit-filler. The engagement that Brands ushers students towards feels surface level and I walked away feeling like I learned very little.

I really enjoyed Brand's class. It was by far my favorite class this semester. It's so refreshing to see a professor not read off the slides the entire lecture. All of the lectures were so interesting and engaging that it was hard for me to miss class. Assignments are easy to complete, including the final presentation. I HIGHLY recommend it!!!
Easiest class to get an A in- just show up and do the weekly assignments. A 90 is an A. The lectures are short and interesting.

This class was genuinely so easy. The class was scheduled MWF, and attendance was mandatory on MW (35% of the grade lol) but optional on Fridays. Another 35% were textbook questions (his book), and you could just ctrl+F for the answers. The final 30% was 2 pretty straightforward projects. Super easy A. Best part - NO EXAMS!! Also, a great lecturer.

Dr. Brands is one of the best professors I've had. Took his U.S. Foreign Policy UGS, this class was my favorite this semester! His lectures are very interesting, and the Friday discussion setions were enjoyable. Attendance is important as most of your grade is based on it. There were two essays and a presentation, no tests. Would recommend!
This class is fairly easy as 2/3 of the grade is decided by attendance and short weekly textbook assignments. Would definitely recommend for history credit.
Great lecturer and storyteller. Class is attendance based and that is a huge part of your grade. Only 2 or 3 large assignments and a textbook that is the rest of your grade. Easy A.

AMAZING CLASS! If you need a history credit, definitely take this class. There are assignments throughout the semester, but they are all online and very easy to manage. 2 big assignments are your main grade, along with attendance. No quizzes/finals at all. Overall, a great professor and course.

Graded off "quizzes" in class, but they are really just attendance checks because he give you the answer right after asking the question. Weekly homework assignments, which is just 3 multiple choice questions of chapter. One paper and one video essay. Overall, very easy. Mandatory attendance on Monday and Wednesday, but not Friday (yay). Easy!

Great prof, lectures are enjoyable and informational, grading is mostly attendance and pearson quizzes. Have only two papers due in the sem, one written and other one isspoken + recorded (its a speech/pitch kind of thing). Only complaint is that TA's grade ridiculously hard for paper, which itself isnt bad but we aren't warned about it at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a senior, I can tell you this is probably the best professor at UT. You can enjoy his lectures and still get an A. The homework isn't too tough. Take his class—take his class!

This class was so easy compared to other history professors. Attendence is a huge part of your grade and is absolutely mandatory - you have to write down specific things during lecture which is checked after class so you do have to pay attention. The papers aren't that hard, they don't really give over a 93, but it doesn't affect you that much.
The homeworks are graded a bit harsh and attendance is mandatory, but Brands is a great professor and very engaging. TAs are accessible outside of class as well to help you out.

Brands is one of my favorite professors at UT. To be completely honest his lectures don't really like match up with the pearson assignments and he often goes on random tangents, but this does not mean that they are not enjoyable, because they really are. Show up to class everyday for attendance, done on a sheet of paper. Enjoyable and easy class.
Great professor, cared deeply about history and specifically about the Roosevelts. He was cool when class was interrupted for a battle between a zombie riding chicken and steve!

Please show up to class, your class participation is a huge grade and I regret not going. TAs are kind and understanding. NO ELECTRONICS. NO TESTS. Weekly homework due on Saturdays. 3 short writing assignments. To get credit you have to answer questions on paper but he gives you the answer.

My favorite history professor ever! Easy class with great lectures. You can find the books for writing assignments online; don't buy them. Pearson assignments, 3 writing assignments, and in-class notes make up your final grade. Very easy as long as you try.

The best professor ever, he was so passionate about history and made lectures so interesting. He provided so many opportunities for extra credit, graded very generously, and was very easy to contact. My favorite class of the semester by far!!!!!! Definitely reccomend!

perfect blend of interesting/informative lectures and easy A. he does make u buy his books which is kinda silly tbh and theres homework due every week based on readings. you wont get a 100 on the writing assignments but an A is 90+ and the rest of ur grade is attendance (lecture notes to prove ur paying attention) and the homework so its calm
best class to get your his credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Brands is amazing! There are no tests in this class and no final. Grades are based upon attendance, three papers, and online textbook quiz assignments. If you need your US History core credits or just want to listen to interesting lectures and get an easy A and 3 hour credit class you should take this class. Brands is the GOAT!

AMAZING PROFESSOR. If you want a good grade take him. One of the easiest classes at UT. MWF classes but Fridays are optional. Attendance is mandatory but no notes taken just write down what he tells you to write down and give it in after class. Very interesting and funny lectures. No exams, extremely easy assignments (textbooks quizzes, 3 essays).

Really easy history class and the most interesting one I've been in. The grade is based on participation + online quizzes + 3 papers. Even if you don't listen to lectures you will be fine, but I found them interesting since he makes the entire semester into a story!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor and his lectures were very interesting. He explains history in a story-like manner is engaging. TAs were nice on grading essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class, Brands is such a great lecturer as he has vast amounts of knowledge that is highly relevant like political science from a historical and modern aspect. For the class itself there are a couple of essays and other easy assignments, work with your TAs and you'll do fine. No phones, no notes, just go and listen to a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Professor Brands for my UGS Intro to Foreign Policy class. Although he did not allow phones, we did not need notes, lectures were interesting if you are engaged in government affairs. Assignments were relatively easy even though the instruction was lacking a tad. TAs were make or break in terms of grading and overall grade. I would retake him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attend lectures, do the weekly textbook assignments that take

this gotta be the best history course you can take at UT. Brands is the only person to ever make me enjoy history. This course is like no other I've taken... no notes and he basically tells stories about various people in history each lecture. Everything is honestly pretty interesting. Also, the essays aren't graded as harshly as he makes it seem.

This was one of my favorite classes of the year! The lectures are mandatory, but he is so knowledgeable and engaging that I always felt I learned a lot. The workload outside of class is very easy and manageable. As long as you come to the class and weekly discussion and put some effort into the essays and other assignments, it should be an easy A.
Dr.Brands is lowkey a chill guy. Very enjoyable professor.

Brands is hands one of my favorite professors I've ever had. His lecture style is very engaging and informative. Likewise, as long as you come to class you'll be good to go. The work load is light and rather interesting. Overall very awesome guy.

"Required" textbooks are written by him (one you dont even open) and the other you HAVE to buy because it is an online course required to pass the class. Lectures are worthless, attendance is mandatory. Wont give you an A on any essays because "no perfect essays exist" really, its to save this sorry class of a class avg of 100. Cash grab ass class

Great Historian, very good lectures, good structure to the class, I looked forward to going. Brands tells stories about historical figures and teaches incorporating real life advice and present day ideas as well. 3 writing assignments, easy textbook readings and videos with questions. Take if you can, and be thankful you got him.

Easiest course I have taken at UT. Professor Brands is a great lecturer who truly wants his students to find the content interesting & engaging. We had weekly textbook assignments that took about 20 minutes & 3 writing assignments that were graded pretty easily. As long as you try and come to class you'll definitely get an A.

He's very entertaining to listen to and he's very passionate about history. Classes can be unorganized because he rambles sometimes, but still interesting. Three 500 word writing assignments (grading depends on the TA) and weekly easy textbook quizzes.

Brands is a very knowledgeable professor but can ramble during lectures. The class revolves around the discussion section where you will discuss current events in world affairs. Be prepared to discuss political topics since you are graded on your participation. There's a few 500-word essays based on incredibly boring books and grading is lenient
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Insanely entertaining lectures, the goat of the history department.

writing assignments are almost always graded around the 80~90 range, but the rest of the class is free so you will almost certainly get an A and no one fails the writing.
Such a sweet professor. He lectures like he's telling a story, so it makes the class entertaining. TAs grade harshly on writing assignments though.
Easy, 3 creative writing assignments + quizletable Pearson + attendance is your grade, super understanding lectures just seemed to lack the depth of a college history class but im not complaining...

This might be one of the best classes that I have taken at the University of Texas at Austin! H.W Brands is such an entertaining professor who is well respected by his students. There is three written assignments and then weekly textbook quizzes. Super easy course I recommend to anyone and everyone.

Brands is a great professor. Interesting lectures.

The problem is the TAs. My TA for this semester, Nathan Stone, is extremely condescending in his grade write ups. I guess he wants to push the students to succeed, but he is extremely blunt and even includes mild personal disses in the comments. 

He completely ruined an otherwise great class.

Dr. Brands's lectures were very interesting. Theres no exams! You only have weekly textbook assignments that take about 20 minutes and 3 very short writing assignments. Loved the class and he is very knowledgable. Wish my STEM professors lectured like him...

Brands is a passionate story-teller! This class was a great balance between my other courses. Easy A if you're consistently showing up (mandatory attendance). Meets twice a week for 45 minutes. Weekly modules that are extremely easy. 3 writing assignments which can be graded harshly depending on your TA. No one gets above a 95 on those assignments.

It was an easy class thanks to my TA who was able to structure the assignments. Attendence for the lecture was mandatory, but the lecture seemed pointless. This is because the lecture often had littlle to do with our assignments or discussion class. The professor seemed knowledgeable, but would easily get sidetracked and ramble.

Professor Brands is extremely knowledgeable about everything involved in foreign politics. This class wasn't hard at all and you have a few easy assignments. Success depends on your TA. Lectures are pointless but mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking for an easy and great history course, take Brands. 1 Quiz online weekly and 3 short assignments throughout the semester. Attendance is mandatory by the way. No exams in the course either. By far most passionate and easiest professor I've had.

Brands was an incredible professor to take. Instead of the same boring US history class you've taken a thousand times in high school (if you're an American student), he zooms into the lives of historical figures and tells compelling stories about how their lives weave into the greater fabric of history.

Lectures were super interesting. I know nothing about history but really enjoyed coming to class. Attendance is required and writing assignments were graded very harshly and don't give a rubric to follow so it can be hard. The online revels can get a bit annoying, but nothing too difficult. Friday classes are optional which was also a plus.

Easy Pearson assignments due each week and only three essays which were super short. He made everything interesting and engaging. I felt bad for him because it seemed like other students did not respect his time when he was lecturing us and always tried to leave early. 10/10 recommend this guy.
Attendance is mandatory, but if you show up to class and do all of the assignments, his class is an easy A. His lectures are also very good, and engaging. GPA booster for sure.

The only class I have taken where I would go everyday even if participation were not required. Really enjoyed this class. Don't take history at a community college when you can take it with prof. Brands. If you are looking to make an easy A to boost your GPA this is your class.

Professor Brands is awesome! His class is straightforward: 1 or 2 weekly assignments and 3 papers. That's pretty much it! However, there's a big emphasis on attendance as it is required. His lectures were really interesting and his way of talking always had my attention. As someone who isn't the greatest history lover, this class was amazing.

Take him!! He is so sweet and passionate about history. His lectures can be really boring but he tries so hard to keep everyone engaged. I maybe spent an hour a week on this class so take him if you can
Very knowledgeable and funny person. He was accessible outside of class too and had clear expectations about assignments and how you will be graded. Often made lectures very intriguing as well!

Dr. Brands has been the best professor that I have taken at UT. The attendance is required but his lectures were so good that I was happy to attend all of them including a few of his optional Friday discussions. Highly recommend him if you need your history credits!

Brands himself and the class is easy. His lectures are interesting, and you get three unexcused absences per semester. The online textbook is easy, and workload is light. However, the writing assignments are graded extremely harshly for a 500 word essay that has nothing to do with what you are actually learning about.

Lectures were not required and he recorded them so I never had to go to class. The whole class was pretty easy and interesting and he is very passionate about history. The hardest assignments were the essays, and that depends on the TA you get because they grade them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took US Foreign Policy with Professor Brands for my UGS. This class is a very, VERY easy A if that's what you're looking for. Show up to discussion, PARTICIPATE, put in some effort for the essays (only two at 500 words each), and you'll be golden. Never had to worry about this class and sometimes forgot I was in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brands is awesome. His lectures are informative but not necessary for homework, only needed for the 3 papers we have (lectures are recorded online and you can look up the transcripts for what to include). TA was a harsher grader than he was, & the majority of your grade comes from essays. Weekly homework is easy (lecture responses & txtbk quizzes)

Brands not only knows how to teach history, he understands how to make you care about learning about history. The class is heavily-based on lectures (no need to take notes, and there are no exams). There is one assigned book that is pretty interesting to read. Brands is very approachable and will answer all of your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Brands is a great professor and does very interesting lectures. Attendance is not mandatory and all you have to do is a weekly Lecture Response and Pearson assignment. However, there are three essays throughout the semester graded by TAs who can be pretty tough.

Fantastic Professor who really knows how to make a history class fun. Doesn't shove dates and names down your throat. Very easy to make an A, even though my TA was an extremely tough grader on the 3 papers. Ended up learning more than I ever have in a history class. Highly recommended

Lectures have nothing to do with grades so they're not necessary. Reading multiple chapters of a book every week. The discussion section is required. Success depends on TA. Graded on 2 500-word papers, 2 100-word papers, an oral presentation, and your discussion participation grade. Brands is sweet! Don't like the A, B grading rather than A+, A, A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: H.W. Brands is clearly passionate about what he does. He does not give 100s though. Pretty much if you do the work and put forth some effort you will get an A in the class. The essays are a bit frustrating because they curve the grades down to give most people Bs, but the other assignments are practically participation-based.

Brands is a GREAT lecturer, attendance isn't mandatory but he is just such a great speaker! You are graded on little quizzes and a small lecture response every week. Total of 3 essays with a 500-word max. The TAs grade your essays so you aren't going to get an easy 100!

Professor Brands is one the best professors this faculty can offer. If you are looking for a professor that is truly inspired and passionate about what they teach then professor Brands is your match. The lectures are both informative and entertaining and this makes showing up to class worth it.

Easy A class, lectures are posted online, and attendance is not mandatory. Essays are the main aspect of this course, just do good on those. Lecture Responses are given a 95, 85, or 75. Pearson quizzes are almost guaranteed 100s.

Great Professor! Has a super clear grading criteria. 3 essays total, which are only 500-550 words each (not even an essay). Quizzes every week but its literally from the textbook and lectures responses which are super easy. Definitely recommend if you want an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you have the opportunity to take a class with him you definitely should! I needed to fulfill my history credit and I have never been interested in history until now, his lectures are very engaging. If you do not attend, you can still watch the recordings in order to do the assignments. Just beware of doing the weekly Pearson.

I really enjoyed him, I think that the pre-recordings are better though because he is so passionate about what he does and sometimes in lecture, he can go off topic if you ask him questions about what is happening today. You can tell that he really loves what he does and I feel like I learned a lot from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Brands is PHENOMENAL! His UGS class was significantly more challenging than his general history course, but I learned so much from his class. Do not be deterred by the fact that he doesn't use plusses or minuses because getting an A in both classes is extremely manageable. If you put in honest effort, you will be fine.

No plus-minus grading, so easy A. One-third of the grade is from open-note, untimed textbook quizzes; one-third is from short lecture summaries; and one-third is from essays. The essays were moderately difficult. I liked Dr. Brands' lecture style; he askd the class questions and lectureed accordingly. Friday's class was an optional office hour.
Brands is knowledgeable and passionate about what he teacher which is reflected in his lectures. The class is engaging and many of the assignments are writing heavy (essays, lecture responses, etc.).

Brands is clearly passionate about what he does. You can tell he loves talking about history, which is refreshing to see. The class itself is easy, just a bit of busywork. You have to complete a 100-word lecture response each week along with mini-quizzes over the textbook. There are no midterms or a final, only three mid-semester exams.

Liked the class, just thought he was overrated as a person. Incredibly arrogant and conceited. Thinks he's the god of history. It was incredibly surface level history, like the textbook was equivalent of one I read in middle school. Lectures were all over the place, but that wasn't bad because he had interesting anecdotes and it kept your interest.
Brands is the best history professor. He is very interesting to listen to. The class is made up of Lecture Responses, online Pearson textbook work, and occasional essays. He is the best!!!

Professor Brands was the best history teacher I have ever have. All assignments in his class were based on the Pearson activities . His grading was very fair, and when I had questions about my grade, he would always clarify during office hours.

During the pandemic I have not been the luckiest with online classes, however this class was amazing. My TA was fair and when I needed to talk about my grades he was available and provided honesty/constructive feedback. Professor Brands is very knowledgeable and his lectures are amazingly detailed. Take this class, you will not regret it.

This class really just depends on what TA you get. Brands is a great lecturer and his online lectures are very entertaining. You will learn a lot. Just go to office hours to make sure you know what your TA is looking for in your papers and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bsmuek is a good professor. She really cares about every student's success. She knows her stuff. She also expects you to put in the work, too. There are weekly discussion posts that take a few hours to read for and complete. If this class is at a weird time again, that's because you're meeting with students in Belfast, Northern Ireland.
I love this class. so much homework and projects. I'm so happy I took this class. This class will make me a better person inside and out. Easy A all day.

Easiest class I've ever taken at UT. Professor Bsumek gave me an A just for showing up to class. Homework is minimal, 4 projects in the class, rare reading and three presentations. My favourite part of the class was talking for 3 hours each class about the environment and how we can help bettering it. I wish she was professor for all my classes.

Such a sweet and passionate professor! I took her class for my US history credit, but it was honestly super interesting and not to mention easy. No exams, grade is mainly based off discussion posts, attendence, and group work. 10/10 recommend!
She was a great history teacher and you could tell she was passionate. There aren't any tests in the class, only group projects so if you get a good group its easy.
Amazing professor. She is an awesome lecturer and the leading expert in the field she teaches. The class wasn't super challenging, but I enjoyed it a lot. Even the assigned reading was pretty cool.

Attendance was via QR code and there were no exams. A few discussion boards and writing assignments that were pretty easy but the main part is the group project so it just depends on if you get lucky with your group or not. I didn't think grading was too harsh but was TA dependent. Overall really easy class if you need a history credit

I loved this class! It was so interesting and taught me a lot, her assignments are very easy, the timeline isn't so bad if your group works well together. Midterms were also very easy if you study terms and go over writing prompts. Overall she's a wonderful professor I would definitely take this class again.
Thoroughly enjoyed this class.

Interesting class, but reading HEAVY. Minimum 2 works/pdfs before each class and had multiple papers due throughout the sem. Few papers were very repetitive (multiple 'drafts' of the same paper, I barely had to change anything substantial- just a hassle)
Don't procrastinate the final project, HEAVILY INVOLVED.
Bsumek is nice and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Bsumek was everything I could have asked for out of an introductory history class professor. Kind, caring, and funny. I learned a lot - just get ready for long lectures. Grades were also unweighted, attendance about as much as projects and tests. Would recommend for a nice CD flag and HIS credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was one of my best professors. She is very passionate about the subject. There is a textbook for the class and a book to read at the end of the year. The group projects are easy as long as everyone does their part. The tests are really easy too, as long as you study the vocab words.

I had a really great time with this class during this semester. She has openly said that she is not trying to trick you or hurt your GPA, and she just wants you to have a great experience. There's a few group projects, but if everyone does their part, it won't be an issue. Our final is going to be take home at the end of the semester as well.

Dr. Bsumek is a super nice lady, but if you can AVOID THIS UGS. Too much work when there are just easier UGS classes you can take. Huge final project. Lots of readings. Lots of essays. SAVE YOURSELF. Don't make the same mistake I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bsumek was a nice professor and you can tell she cared about her job. TAs can be annoying, but group projects are ultimately what matter in the class. Groups are randomly assigned but if you get lucky then the class is an easy A. There are discussion boards and quizzes sprinkled throughout the course and attendance is via a QR code each class.

Professor Bsumek is so nice and gives so much individual attention in her UGS class. I found it very moving and I loved discussing the readings, but for the final timeline project her expectations were often very unclear and when it came time to peek over the rubric there were lots of requirements that she hadn't previously specified.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was truly enlightening, learning about the history of a group of people that have often been overlooked. The lectures were interesting and the class overall was a great experience. However, there are two group projects, and you can't choose your own group.

The lectures for this class become difficult to attend very quickly, between the emotionally charged material and the slow pace of this class. As far as the papers, the rubric is fairly ambiguous and arbitrary. However, Dr. Bsumek is clearly knowledgeable and very open to feedback. If you have an interest in History, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class but the material was a lot, and I wish it was more organized for this semester. And if you don't like reading there is a lot of it, because it is very important in order to succeed in this class. Interesting class, but I would try to look for another history credit.

Native American Histories was a bit tough, but that's the nature of history courses (memorizing). Really broadens your understanding of such an important topic and gives you knowledge you'll carry with you long after the course. Lots of textbook reading, midterm that is okay but you gotta study hard for. Easy online final. A few group projects.

Dr. Bsumek is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, her lectures are very insightful. You can get by without reading too much of the textbooks, though they do help. The group timeline projects were cool, though they can become a bit redundant. The one midterm exam was difficult and has heavy weight, but her online final exam was easy.

Professor Bsumek is nice and the class felt comprehensive even with such expansive subject material, but I really wasn't a fan of the emphasis on group work and Cliovis. Aside from that, this class is very solid for an intro course.

Dr. Bsumek is great at helping, answering questions, and being available outside of class. This class was very easy because she made it very clear what was expected. You are given the terms and questions for the midterm/final in advance, so you will be well-prepared for both tests. Dr. Bsumek does use ClioVis often, assigned 2 group timelines.

Dr. Bsumek is very knowledgeable and passionate. She understands that many people take her Native American history class for a GC flag and core requirement, and as a result doesn't assign much work. There are weekly discussion posts (1-3 sentences) and a few group projects, one individual project. Overall great, would reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am not joking when I tell you this class changed my life. It was very eye opening and Professor Bsumek approached the subject of Native American History with so much grace. The lectures were always interesting and informative, if a little heartbreaking for obvious reasons, and even though I'm not great at history, I would take this class again.

Interesting UGS. Initially had a lot of readings. Need to purchase 2 books that we didn't really even read the whole thing. She really cares about what she's teaching and wants to interact with her students. Provides good feedback and help if needed. The final project is a lot of work, but she gives you time to work on it. Easy to get a good grade.
super kind and understanding, great lecturer too. her projects are resonable and the readings are interesting

Prof. Bsumek was an amazing professor, with a very easy class and manageable workload. Only complaint would be the group projects and individual project as they are alot of work but manageable with a group. Easy quizzes and discussions. She tries to make her class as engaging as possible and mostly does so. Highly recommend for STEM majors.

You can tell that she is passionate about American history in her lectures. The ClioVis app she uses for a lot of assignments is very janky, but the tests are pretty easy with weekly short answer discussion posts and in-class padlets. I barely attended the class and got an A.

Dr Bsumek was great! Her lectures were very engaging and she was very passionate about the subject matter. The workload for the class was very manageable as well. The group projects in the class were mildly annoying, especially given the group I had, but they weren't too difficult.

Dr Bsumek's class was great! Her lectures were very engaging and the workload from the course was very manageable. There were a couple group projects throughout the class which was somewhat annoying since I didn't have the best group, but they weren't that difficult..

Dr.Bsumek was very caring about her students and truly wanted everyone to succeed. I read the textbook for the first two weeks and then stopped since there were never any quizzes given. As long as you know the terms that she gives before the exams, you should be able to ace the exams easily.

Class is manageable and I was never extremely stressed about it, and she took a couple assignments of the syllabus so that was slay of her. Lectures can be really long though, and she goes fast so its a good class to improve typing skills. I stopped reading the textbook after the midterm and was fine so don't let that deter you. Solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her Native American Histories course was an extremely rewarding experience. The group projects I wasn't crazy about but they weren't bad. The midterm and final weigh heavy on the final grade. I suffered a personal loss outside of class and she was very accommodating when that happened. I cannot recommend her enough.

She is great with her rubrics and grading, she's very clear on what is expected so the work is very straightforward. there were 2 group assignments but they were timelines and easy. She does offer extra credit and gives study guides for all test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this class just to get the cultural diversity flag. Prof. Bsumek is aware that many students that take her class do so in order to knock out a core class/flag requirement, so she has made efforts not to make the class too demanding and time-consuming. This was an easy class, and getting an A should be easily done if one attends the lectures.

Dr. Bsumek is very reasonable, kind, and intelligent. She takes her students' feedback into account and overall I respect her a lot! If you have trouble keeping up with reading I definitely recommend going to the study groups she makes available (not mandatory)--I have a hard time reading and those helped out a TON!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be on top of your readings and you should be fine. This isn't a class you'd want to procrastinate on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class & the material a lot, and the prof was really nice. However, I wish it was more organized for this semester. Make sure to do your reading because it is very important in order to succeed in this class. The midterm and final both consisted of 2 essays (one long and one short). The two books & textbook we read are very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is very understanding and easy to talk to. The class is very discussion led, so there's not many lectures. Most of the class is discussing readings or whatever activity we do in class, and every once in a while there's a paper. There's also an easy project at the end. As long as you follow the rubric and participate you should have an A.
Great teacher! Really passionate and great to talk to. Not too many assignments, which is good and bad. You need to make sure you keep up on your own.

Go to lectures. She sends out slides, but they're bullet points and what she says is more important. Essays can be prepared beforehand, so it is advisable that you write out exactly what you want, otherwise you may be pressed for time. Lots of readings, but I stopped after the 2nd week. Group projects aren't that bad if you put a little effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very easy class for a history credit, definitely take it! Dr. Bsumek was very nice and interested in her subject matter. However, attendance is counted.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was unnecessarily hard! There is 3 group projects which you have to present, a 3-4 page paper, and2 exams. If you can pick someone else please do!! When we switched to online she did not try to accommodate her students at all! She expected to do the same and more work not understanding at all!

love love love this class and this prof, I learned so much. Bsumek is really great approaching complex topics with objectivity and sensitivity, and is clearly very knowledgable about the subject matter. Couldn't have asked for a better professor or a more interesting class.
This class is great and so is Bsumek. Very interesting stuff. Only graded on 2 tests which both have an essay component, a couple of quizzes, and some papers. Not too hard though if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bsumek is very transparent and kind. She makes the class engaging and not too hard to keep up with, although it is a lot of content. Exams aren't easy but she gives clear study sheets/lists of what to know. A very well-organized class on a really important topic! Sit in the front to see her cool shoes ;-)

Dr. Bsumek actually takes the time to learn everyone's name and is super sweet! This is one of the best classes I have taken at UT! Pay attention during lecture and make sure to read because they are super helpful for the essays and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bsumek is probably one of the most caring professors you will find at UT. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is genuinely concerned her students. Her grading criteria is usually clear, there isn't a lot of work but she does focus on class participation. Overall, I enjoyed my time in her class and would take again.

The professor is very caring and kind. The class is kind of hard because there are is lot of papers and readings. You have to do discussion posts, 3 short papers, and a research paper at the end. The class is interesting, but boring at the same time. A lot of work and time, but if you do the work, you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You can tell that her heart is in the right place. The only thing that I somewhat disliked is the fact that her syllabus is not consistent through out the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her lectures are interesting but not always easy to follow.  For American Indian History, there was a lot of information that was difficult to organize.  However, Dr. Bsumek listens to her students' concerns and is willing to make reasonable changes based on our feedback.  If you take her, and have a problem, don't hesitate to bring it up.

You'll learn a ton in this class! There are group projects which can be annoying, but it's not too bad. There's a lot of reading but no one ever reads it. She really cares about her students, she even hosted a competition for the best group project and she even gave out prizes!  This class takes a bit of work, but it's worth it!
She is a nice lady. The midterms come with study which are pretty straight forward. It is a easy A if you attend to class.
Do yourself a favor and take her class. She's fantastic.

This may not apply to everyone, but Prof. Bsumek's teaching style does not really suit me.  She relies too heavily on the textbook; her tests cover many details that aren't even mentioned in her lectures.  She also has a tendency to get behind in lectures and skip sections to stay on schedule, then wait a couple weeks before posting the slides.
More writing then both of my writing intensive classes. 12-20pg takehome midterm + final. 4 books - choose one to write another 6pg paper. Would not take the class again.
cool class, her t.a.s are very helpful.

I really enjoyed his lectures! You can tell he truly cares about the content and is incredibly knowledgeable about it. He has a great enthusiasm toward baseball which makes it that much more interesting to learn about. Would love to take another course from him in the future.

LOVED this UGS. Do not understand the low ratings he gets on here. First off, he is a super nice, funny, well-rounded guy. He is so passionate about baseball which made me want to show up to lectures (which were not required). ONLY complaint was the TAs.

I almost never leave reviews, but this class deserves a warning. class material not hard but grading is harsh. Discussion average in the 65-73, papers land in the same range, no curve or extra credit. I maintain straight As in tougher STEM courses, but I only pull a C here. The evaluation standards feel excessive for an otherwise reasonable class.

This professor is one of those professors that will give you more work just because he knows people will not care about his class. He is a harsh grader, and in my opinion does not follow the grading criteria and just grades depending on his opinions of the paper, and I feel like the TAs do not even know half of the stuff we are talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is determined to make sure his class is not known as a blowoff so he ruined everyone's GPA instead this semester. Group project is awful because it's graded as a whole, not individually so your group mates will drag your grade down. TA's know nothing about the class and use chatGPT to grade assignments if they don't understand it.

I took this class because I heard it was an easy A and I needed a course that wouldn't require too much work, as I have a job. While attendance at lectures isn't mandatory, participation in discussion groups is. Tests are on paper within your small group. The professor does not offer extra credit, and the TAs are tough graders…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE THIS!! You get a different grade based on different TAs. Your grade COMPLETELY out of control. Even if you do well, some TAs will give you the right grade and others won't. Prof MB also backs up their grading, making it impossible to get points back or even understand what it takes to get an A. Don't trust them and don't take this class.
really hard to do well, no reason to take this UGS. Would rather push back taking one for a semester and make sure I get one that is reasonable

Overall, such a disappointing class. Was super excited to learn more about baseball but ended up being a stress fest. Every assignment had unclear grading and even if you met the requirements for a 100 they still found ways to knock it down for arbitrary reasons. Just sad that both TAs and professor feel the need to hurt students grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is the epitome of, "I teach a joke subject so I am going to grade way too harshly". About halfway through the semester, the students complained about the ridiculous grading and MB responded with, "a C is the grade you get for following the instruction. Don't complain about a C". There are so many more easy UGSs DO NOT TAKE THIS ONE.

I loved lectures. Dr. Butterworth was very engaging and entertaining to listen to! I highly recommend attending lectures, even though attendance isn't taken, but discussions are mandatory. Group project at the end of the semester.
I was told for the first exam that there would be not dates being asked yet about 1/3 of the exam was about dates and I was only given a “I apologize” after borderline failing. It seems t

After taking this class, I now understand that producing well-written and maximum effort papers/final projects is never enough to get an A. I would receive comments on the writing assignments that started with "I would like it better...", and feedback that a great paper is worth of a B. Most will agree, don't take this class, for your own sake.
Super tough grader for no reason. This is a UGS not a math class.

I thought he was cool at first, but during the final half of the semester, he said, “Guys, a B isn't a bad grade. A C means you met expectations, a B means you exceeded expectations, and an A means you went above and beyond.” For a baseball class and a UGS requirement, it's not that deep.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Butterworth himself is a cool guy, the TA's are terrible and grade extremely hard when the rubrics are very unspecific. There are very little assignments so if you do bad on one thing, you are screwed. I will say that Dr. Butterworth does not easily give points back and it was annoying when he did nothing to help us students with our grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do NOT take Butterworth. I took him because I heard it was an easy UGS and it's graded so harshly for absolutely no reason and the TAs and Butterworth himself are so unhelpful and very unclear about what the expectations are. They also agreed that a C should be the average grade for the class??? I regret taking this class so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is very interesting and was supposed to be a fun UGS class, but the grading in this class is so terrible. For a UGS class the grading here is so bad the TA's and the professor have decided that a C should be the average grade in the class. They are very very VERY picky when grading assignments. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is easy, but the TA's are very picky graders when it comes to the papers. Group project is not too bad but again grade too harshly unless work is perfect.

Used to be really easy, but TAs and Professor decided that getting a C is a good thing. 3 tests, 1 group project and a few short papers. The class itself is actually pretty interesting, but the grading policy is terrible. Would not recommend.

A lot of people have different opinions on this course. The lectures are not mandatory but the discussion sections are. Test are taken in discussion sections and are not too hard. As long as you look at the rubrics/try hard on the assignments it really isnt hard. The only downfall was the TAs are not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAs collectively decided a C is the average. the class used to be really easy but now it is insanely unrealistic for a UGS. there are way better UGS courses. dont take this if you just need a credit. my TA was awful just made us come and asked if we had questions because she has no plan and we all sat in silence for an hour.

The professor is very nice but the TA's SUCK. The lectures are not mandatory, however, the discussion groups are. They collectively think that a C is a good grade and they want to make their grade point average lower. Be really careful taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Butterworth had interesting lectures. The tests were easy and the lab section was not bad. This class was as easy A and I highly recommend for a UGS.

After a year at UT, Prof Butterworth is the best professor I have had. As a baseball fan, his lectures were so engaging and interesting and he's such a good orator. Assignments were manageable and I often enjoyed doing them. My TA for discussion was great and discussions themselves weren't too bad. I wish I could take this class again! GO O'S!

By far the best professor I've had at UT. Really good lecturer and entertaining guy and though they're not required, he still makes you want to come. Facilitates discussion really well and assignments are relatively easy and all exams are take home. If you're looking for an easy A but still an entertaining class, he's the man for you.

His baseball UGS is so easy. Attendance is only mandatory for discussion. There are a few papers, but they can all be completed in an hour max and are a page long usually. There is a group project, which is annoying. But it is a super easy UGS. 3 tests, all open note as well.

Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't to strict, but look at the lectures tho since the tests were very lecture heavy. Overall graded on like 5 things so if you mess up one you mess up half of your grade. Test were open note and taken at home do they weren't terrible, takes some work to get an A tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Butterworth's lectures were extremely engaging and his passion was evident with every lecture. As a result, his class was highly accessible even for someone unfamiliar with the subject matter. I'd recommend largely studying your notes from his lecture to study for the tests, but the readings are a good frame of reference to understand larger themes

Probably my fav professor here! His lectures are pretty engaging even if you aren't familiar at all with the topic. Attendance is mandatory but definitely come to the lectures and take notes because he has easy open-note exams that are straight from the lecture slides. TAs are generally chill and all other assignments are easy.
