Dr. Butterworth is the most passionate and knowledgable professor I have had. As someone who knew nothing about baseball, I learned a ton, and found myself very interested in the course. If you aren't a strong writer, the essay grades may hurt a little. Weekly readings provided in canvas, so no textbook. Everything on the tests is in the lectures.

I took UGS303 America Through Baseball in Spring 2022, and it was harder than all of my engineering classes combined. The exams are so specific and questions aren't covered in lecture or the readings; it's basically like trivia exams. Essays and projects he takes points off for dumb reasons. He is a decent lecturer though and he gives extra credit

Was a great guy and was helpful during office hours. It was way too much work for a UGS class and the test material was very knit picky. The essays were also challenging but he is willing to help you out with them. You need to put in a decent amount of work in this class to get an A but Dr. Butterworth is a great guy.

Professor Butterworth is one of the best professors I've ever had. He gives AMAZING lectures and the class is very well-organized. He is so kind and loves talking to students outside of class! Your grade is based on 3 exams, 2 papers, a timeline project, a final group project, and attendance in discussion sections (which are very helpful, so go!)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took UGS303 America Through Baseball spring'20. Told the history/foundation of the sport, not necessarily the game itself. Relevant topics like race, sexism, immigration, etc., & I was pleased to see he didn't sugarcoat any of these. I dislike sports, but Butterworth made this class worthwhile. Understanding of personal issues, loved his course!!

I really love Professor Butterworth! His personality is awesome and lectures are engaging. He is also very knowledgeable on this topic of communications and sports. He offers extra credit, and exams are not too hard if you study and pay attention in class.

Dr. Butterworth is a great guy and very understanding. Super nice, and his lectures are engaging and easy to follow. Class was Tuesday/Thursday, and we probably had a short pop quiz over the reading once every 3-4 classes. The readings were easy to read and interesting. Exams are essay format. I would definitely take a class from him again.

So disorganized. 50% of grade is HW (formatted in Latex). Considering the time commitment, he should bother to grade our work. 10 out of 13 HWs graded 1-2 weeks before finals, solutions posted a week before exams/final, midterm graded the day of q-drop deadline. It's impossible to consistently check your understanding unless you can make it to OH.

I would rate Professor B-dawg a 7 if I could, PLEASE TAKE HIM. 

Advice for those who will eventually read this letter. The homework is rough, It took ALOT of time to complete (If you're quick on Latex you're fine).

If you can jump that hurdle, the B-dawg lectures are the best Physics lectures known to the human race.

VERY MATHEMATICAL. Really steep learning curve. The class is a LOT more bearable if you can make it to office hours. I never read the textbook. Exams are slightly adjusted HW probs, and he tells you exactly which problems to study, no lies. Gives up to 6% extra credit w/ attendance and course eval. He's very caring if you just reach out.

His class definitely felt different than my other physics classes, but in a good way. This class is really mathematical, and I think there is a lot to learn from his way of thinking. Also, it is really easy to get an A since the midterm is literally the homework, and he tells you which questions to look at beforehand. Also 5% EC for attendance.

Dr. Burby is a very kind professor, but his mechanics class is very much geared towards physics majors and understanding mechanics concepts deeply. However, he was very helpful, and with the extra credit and attending office hours, it is definitely feasible to do well. If you are a physics, math, or astro major, I highly recommend taking his class!

Burby is a likeable and insightful professor. Lectures are rigorous and geared toward physics majors with an interest in theory; not everyone will appreciate his style. There is disconnect between the difficulty of getting a good grade (not too hard), and what he actually teaches (hard). His class has issues likely due to him being a new professor.

I'll be honest, this class was not an easy A and as a new professor he is still figuring out teaching. Still, he clearly wants his students to do well and is always happy to help you with any questions you have when he is available. If you take his class, I recommend going to office hours if you can and don't be scared to talk to him.
If you want actually to learn physics, take it! If you want an easy time, don't. Those who have a problem with this class just don't want to put in effort.

His lecture and homework got more difficult over the semester. However, if you understand the homework questions well with the help of OH/TA/friends, you are more than set to get an A. So overall, it is not hard to do well in this class even without fully understanding the content as long as you know the methodology for solving the HW.

A good calculus background would help for this class. An 8x12 “cheat sheet” was allowed on the midterm/final. Dr. Burby is very passionate about physics and strives to teach derivation and the why behind the principles of mechanics. It was significantly more difficult FOR ME to do well in this class if not for the EC offered/Curve.

He was a tough teacher, although I don't understand most of his lecture but his exams are fair with the similarity to homework. Also with 65% of homework grade and 3% of discussion attendance, getting a fair grade is relatively easy.  Also, his final is similar to homework and past exams. Overall he is a nice person. TAs are nice too!

Horrible professor. Lecture is no help at all, explaining problems that are WAY beyond intro undergrad level. These same problems (that sometimes the TA's cannot solve) are on the homework and tests. It is the day before our final and we have no idea what our grade is in the class because he has not decided grade cutoffs.

Dr. Burby writes his own homework and test questions except they are extremely hard to solve. In addition, his explanations are confusing and he basically skips all of the work and just restates the answer which is not helpful at all.

Joshua Burby makes a difficult class so much more harder than it needs to be. It does not help that his course is disorganized. It is one week before class ends and I have no idea what my grade in the class is.
I srsly cant do any problem that this man puts out. I feel so unmotivated and confused and sad in this class.

Dr. Burby's class is the most difficult course I've taken. Every day in class he has a problem and solves it the most complicated way. Doesn't give you formulas you just have to know. He makes his own homework questions and they are ungodly difficult. The TA's are stuck sometimes, and extra credit was just 2 more exams. GG WP 0/10 NO RE

His class is really good for those who want to understand physics at a fundamental level. However, this class might not be for those who want an easy "A." He is clearly a genius, and his brain could probably power the entire North American continent. There is a lot you can learn, that is if you put in the effort. However, this is NOT an easy class.

he a cool dude, its obvious he really love physics and teaching it in general which i think is awesome but he's trying to teach us at a much higher level than the class should be, n it just confuses everyone. he just be goin through 2 page long proofs every class and god damn i'm lost as hell. exams r 13% and hws are like 50% so its chill doe.
He must be stopped. His physics problems are beyond undergrad level. This is some NASA level wizardry.

Second midterm stats:
Mean: 39.7
Median: 42.86
HIGH Score: 78.57

Do not take him it's not worth it.

Nice guy, but overcomplicates too much for an intro course. 1st test was like hw, but everything got worse. Homework problems had concepts not covered in class and 2nd test tried to apply hw "concepts", except we never fully learned them. Asked for feedback but didnt follow it. TAs are a godsend, but even they + other grads cant solve some problems

He is bad at explaining things and cannot find a way to teach his class. Most of the students do not show up for lecture. Homework problems are extremely difficult. TAs carry this class but even they can't solve some of his problems.

He is not a very good professor. His lectures go beyond classical mechanics and he ends up lecturing about derivations and proofs. You end up having to teach yourself most of the material in order to do the HWs. The test and HWs are very hard. The test and HWs always have some hard questions that he wrote himself. The TAs carry this class.

Interesting teacher, although it is an entry level physics course but the prof always uses mathematical way to teacher. Lecture class is problem sessions actual content is in the recorded pre lec. Actually I don't understand a word…… although I took ap physics 1 and c. Although the grade is relatively nice but it is more like a linear algebra class
0 leniency for difficult situations. Has an odd stuck up attitude. Do not reccomend, save your grade from stress.
This class was really interesting. Burke did a great job making it interactive and engaging. The exam is difficult but doable.

Dr. Burke is amazing! If you can take him, DO. His lectures are engaging and make OM an easy to understand concepts. If you attend class weekly, you won't need to study outside of class. The homework is easy and take less than 30 mins weekly. You absolutely should attend class (no tech allowed) to succeed on the exams, but it's very doable.

I enjoyed Professor Burke's class. He's an engaging lecturer who explains material clearly, is approachable during office hours, and is always willing to help. He's also very understanding and accommodating. The weekly homework is manageable, and while the exams can be challenging, staying on top of the material and studying makes them very doable
His lectures are extremely boring and he just flies through material without being engaging. Also if you turn an assignment in even a minute late it is an automatic 0.

This professor does not care about his students one bit. If I were given the option to take another course taught by him or drop out of UT, I would start packing my bags and go. I have never met a professor who grades so harshly on exams and then looks at his students as if it is our fault. This guy will laugh at you for failing and not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Burke is super nice and always replies fast. The midterm and final are moderately hard, but homework is easy and helps your grade. Class is pretty boring, but you can learn everything from his slides. As long as you stay on top of it, you'll be fine.

OM should be easy but this man makes it so difficult. Do not take his class unless you hate yourself. It's graded based off the fact that his students get C- on exams and he still doesn't curve, you get counted off on HWs all the time and he can be boring. Taking OM with him is a GPA NO: anyone who tells you otherwise is a supply chain major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Listen...OM 235 as a class in my honest opinion, easy money—honestly pretty interesting.

OM 235 with Burke? Now that's a different story.

Don't take him if you care about your GPA, don't take him unless you don't mind no partial credit on FRQ based exams and no curves despite a C- average on exams.

Just...don't take him. Trust, take ANYONE else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is one of those classes where you would be fine if you only came to the review class before the exam. Unfortunately, attendance is mandatory, and electronics are banned, so I was in class every week. Burke is a great professor, but there is just not enough content to warrant a two-hour mandatory class.

For OM he knows his stuff. His lectures are really good and he post his slides after. He made us take notes with only paper and not laptops which is a little strange. Class isnt too bad, theres just no practice material which makes it somewhat iffy.

As someone without a 4.0, this course is not hard at ALL if you pay attention. Burke is engaging, and walks through example exam questions in every class; especially with the allowed cheat sheet, you're golden if you pay attention. Personally, I enjoyed his lectures greatly (other than the mention of food around lunchtime). Take him if you can!

He is genuinely very rude for not curving the exams that have no practice exam. You go in blind to the exams which are worth all your grade. There is no grace and the “extra credit” favors only a few people. Take anyone but him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nothing about this class is hard but Burke is the only prof that doesn't curve and u NEED a curve for the exams. Exams and hw aren't hard but getting a few (2-3) mistakes/not understanding a problem on both exams will get u an A-/B. If u don't care abt GPA this prof is fine and the class is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. This guy does not care about students. Unreachable and unhelpful. He is the only professor who doesn't curve the grade which is insane. I would at least have A- if it wasn't for that. Unless you're a beast at supply chain, don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Burke's lectures are too long and conceptual; more in-class practice would help. A 35%-weighted final without a practice exam is unreasonable, especially with limited resources for tough topics like project crashing. There's also no curve, on either the exam or final grade, despite all the other OM professors doing otherwise.

DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR BURKE. He fosters an environment of fear, and a simple mistake on an assignment can get you in huge trouble. Not welcoming and doesn't care about his students. He uses his platform to make himself look superior and belittles students. Really discouraging and is extremely strict overall.

I truly don't get what people in here are saying because Burke is by far the best OM professor. He's super understanding but stern. He's always there for you and he's a pretty good lecturer. 100% recommend. If you don't like OM in general, every prof will be challenging. Just work a bit hard ig

The way he teaches the class itself is pretty good. I am giving him a low rating because of how he is as a person. I personally feel that he is rude and does hold racial biases. Overall as far as workload the class is pretty doable. We only had to refer to the textbook like twice the whole semester

Based on what I've heard from my friends who took other professors for MIS 301, Burke is by far the best professor to take for MIS 301. Although this class is memorization heavy, the class is structured in a way that will set up up for success on the exams. Burke also has a great sense of humor and keeps the class engaged. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Burke for MIS301 and OM235 and would recommend taking his class for either. Does a good job explaining what to do for each kind of problem. Before each test, redo all of the homeworks up until that point and create a good notes sheet (you can bring one to the test) with all the required formulas and you will do well in the class.

Burke is a pretty humorous guy who always begins his class talking about the weekly UT sports scene. Classes are slides based on readings, and assignments are simple excel worksheets and interactive textbook questions. He makes a review slide for the midterms and if you study those you will do well. Class is usually released 30 minutes early.

Honestly not that bad of a class. Incredibly passionate professor who will work with you if you have any issues. He is very no BS, and does not allow screens in class and will call you out. Memorize how to do the HW problems for the exam and you will get a B/A.

Going into MIS I was fearful of the course work because other people said it was bad, but Burke breaks it down into VERY manageable chunks and is a funny guy! The tests are pretty memorization heavy, but if you pay attention in class and review the notes and supplementals it provides you with everything you need.

I understand how some people can find him strict, but I absolutely loved this class. MIS was boring for me but Burke really made the lectures interesting. To pass the exams you need to memorize ALL of the VOCAB on the slides. Learn the Vocab and you'll do great. All of the other mini-assignments throughout the class are pretty easy.
He's a more no BS type of professor. MIS301 is a memorization of key term class. His lectures don't really help for the exams you need to self study by yourself. Not bad but not great professor.

Professor Burke lectures entirely from textbook slides, which is a total repetition of content that you're already required to read. It is impossible to stay engaged during class. Additionally, Professor Burke exercises his power to pick favorite students, scrutinize students on their honesty, and make inappropriate jokes for a college classroom.

Burke was a pretty decent Professor and was willing to help students with concepts outside of office hours. 50% of your grade is based on assignments that aren't terribly difficult. However, the other 50% of your grade is based on tests that require you to memorize the textbook and slides. Tests are not cumulative.

Was this class hard? Yes. Did I have to memorize literally everything? Also yes. But did he curve my grade to an A at the end? Yes. So, at the end of the day, he gives you the resources to succeed you just really have to memorize every detail in the powerpoints and do the textbook practice quizzes. Nice guy too, decently understanding.
The lecture is boring and everything he talked about is directly from the book. Text is 100 question multiple choice, T/F and fill in the blank
I would recommend taking Burke for MIS, he seems to have made the class better than some people I know with different professors. If you study and understand the terms you will make an A.

Professor Burke is amazing! He keeps lectures engaging to his best ability. The OM 235 material can be dense, so please take advantage of his OHs if you're struggling. Attendance is "mandatory" but participation is based on completing pop quizzes. He advocates for YOU. Exams are tougher, but that's not his fault.

Worst prof I've had at UT. Lectures consisted of him talking about sports and using only 20-30 minutes to read directly off of slides from the textbook when we already had to read the chapter before. Prides himself on making tests as difficult as possible without any actual teaching. By far my easiest course content wise, but brought down GPA.

I took Professor Burke for MIS and OM. Not my favorite classes but Professor Burke made them both easy to understand and was always available to answer question over email or zoom. Would take any class given by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures are extremely boring, especially since they're straight from the textbook when you have to read it ahead anyway. You have to know the book and vocab by heart for the tests; make sure to start studying ahead with quizlets and practices. Gives difficult pop-quizzes that are harder than the other profs' so look through your vocab before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy and I like how he explained topics like it was a conversation. Participation pop quizzes can be harder than other profs who just do completion instapolls (Finney). Tests are same for all profs: 100 randomized Qs so you need to know the textbook well especially vocab. Strict on no extra credit, only curves if class avg is

Quizzes are unnecessarily difficult and much harder than other professors. Tests ability to answer fill-in-the-blank under time constraints. Tests are challenging but not impossible if you study and are standardized. He's is funny and a good lecturer but the lectures do not help with anything. The class is entirely based on reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is so freaking annoying and hard. They are testing you over memorization of the textbook and by memorizing I mean MEMORIZING LINES to the dot. The lectures do not do a good job of reiterating the information and he even tells you in class that we won't talk about everything that could show up on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were very difficult--100 questions, no word bank, and weirdly written too. You have to study in advance and pretty much memorize the textbook. Lectures were mundane and there are pop quizzes that are graded so do some light reading before class. You learn Excel outside of class but the lessons were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class follows very, very closely to the textbook, to the point where the lecture slides are taken straight from the book. I found this really good, as it kind of standardized the information and made it so the topics that we were tested/quizzed on were directly in line and could be found in the textbook.
misogynistic. talks over you. narcissist. brags about himself the entire time. don't even pay attention, he reads the textbook out to you like you didn't pay money for it
I don't even know what to say. The grading is so unclear, and you cannot even see the average score of your assignments, leading you to believe that you are doing worse than you currently are.

Not only is the class confusing , but while other professors curved according to the McCombs guidelines, he didn't despite grades not being great. Weekly homeworks don't line up with exams and lectures don't have anything to do with exams. Take it with someone else.

This might be one the worst classes I have ever taken. I took Burke for MIS301 and enjoyed it. The assignments were fair and the tests correlated directly to what he taught. OM is a whole different story. I have never learned less in a course. The homework has NOTHING to do with lectures and the tests don't correlate to the homework either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took MIS with him and thought he would be just as good as a professor for OM. I think that the tests are very hard and your grade depends on whether the TAs hold review sessions. Class is not helpful and practicing emphasizes the concepts the most.

Burke is the worst. His lectures are so boring and you don't learan much and it is very dumbed down but then his homeworks which are supposed to be based on the lecture are extremely difficult and quite frankly you must teach yourself how to do. If there is another option, take a different professor

Dr. Burke's MIS class focuses on the business side of technology, which is why he does not test on the homework that involves coding. The tests do require you to understand a good amount of information, but if you study ahead of time and use the slides as a guide they are very fair. His grading is fair, and his lectures were always entertaining.

The tests are relatively easy if you study the material and the projects teach you things that are actually useful. That being said, lectures can be a little dry and instructions for projects/assignments can be pretty limited. If you study well, this class can be an easy A and its an easier alternative to other MIS301 options.

This class is just you teaching yourself the lectures are pretty vague for how much he test you on. All the assignments are self taught he doesn't give any information of all of the projects and assignments that are due and they barely count for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are easy if you attend lectures, review slides, and read the textbook. Although his lectures seem dry, they have a way of sticking in your memory. He did not curve my class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke is really funny and kind. Exams are tough- they have very specific questions from the textbook. Essentially, they test your memorization of the textbook. If you start studying early, an A is doable. Group work is not too bad, and you can always ask the TA questions. Overall, the class requires effort, but is well structured.
Tough, but fair. Attend lecture and do some studying before the exam and you're solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke has interesting lectures that he pairs with his sense of humor. He lectures directly from the slides with some videos and experiences in between. Exam questions were pulled from the practice quizzes, so you know what to expect on the exam. Ask your TA for help with group projects and cases. No final!!

This class was has completely changed from one semester to the other. was recommended to take him from others but they had a different syllabus. The class is super test heavy that one grade can mess you up. He skims slides during lectures and doesn't highlight on any of the important topics that you will be tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was miss informed by past students that this would be a pretty easy class with online exams but he has changed the format of test. They are no longer online and open note so be ready to study a lot for the exams. The test make up most of your grade while the other assignments require you to learn it yourself and barely count towards your average

Do not take burke his lectures seem fun when it comes to test they have hard multiple choices. All of the assignments given to you are never even talked about so you have to learn them all on your own.

MIS 301 with Dr. Burke was alright. TBH, I could've made an A- in the class, but I was lazy to actually study and crammed the day of tests. There's three exams, but not final. Recommend buying the textbook, it has practice quizzes which he bases the exams off of. Honestly, if you put some effort into this class you'll get an A- or A.
Professor Burke is a great, funny, and knowledgable professor. Take the group work seriously and pay attention in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a fairly easy class for MIS. If I studied a little harder I believe an A would have been achievable, as the grade is based 57% on 3 tests. As long as you read through his slides and know how to apply the concepts you will be fine. The case assignments are annoying and the TA grades harsh but overall not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are okay, the way the course is graded is kind of weird since there are only three things that matter. The exams and cores and cases. The cores are not too bad. The cases are depending on how your TA is feeling that day. Exams are okay too. Not lenient with grading and is not the nicest professor. He's just okay.

Honestly dont take him if your care about your gpa. Took him because everyone said how good he was but he has changed the layout of the class. No more open note test like the last several semesters and they make up 60% of the grade and are hard. Most of the assignments given in the class you are never taught how to do.

Took him during COVID. Class was scheduled to be hybrid, but we only met in-person once. His class is definitely the easiest for MIS 301, but don't expect to actually learn anything. One time he didn't even show up to class and never offered an explanation of why. Regularly curves final grades down and isn't transparent with grading criteria.

Say goodbye to open-note tests. Tests are majority memorization (not much application, just memorization) and make up almost 60% of our final grade. Get ready to read! Burke is a cool guy, but the tests can really affect your grade, even if you prepare extensively for them and do great on all the other assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I definitely would not recommend this prof. I based off my selection on his RMP but he has in fact changed the lay out of the class. The test are no longer open note like previous semester which makes the test super hard to do good because its test heavy. There is no extra credit nor curve and he a pretty bad lecturer.

I had MIS w Burke online in Fall 2021, and enjoyed him and the class a lot. He breaks down the textbook into concise slides, so all you need is the slides, and the exams are open note, making them pretty easy if you are at least somewhat prepared. Actually engage in class and apply yourself a little, and you can get an A pretty easily. Great Prof

overall, meh. He does the bare minimum but then grades rly hard. I did well in the class, but see how easy he made it for others to struggle. He was more concerned abt telling us to attend the next football game (bc apparently he was paid to do so) and just read off slides that are STRAIGHT from the book. if he likes u, he grades u better too

Professor Burkes is a class i would definitely take again. SAM assignments are frustrating but very do -able, the TA guides you through the help if you need it. Lectures are interesting and there is 5 assessments, 4 case assignments, 4 partner core assignments. watch the lectures/take notes and you will do well.
Only 2 exams and homework for this course and no extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Burke is nice, funny, and has good intentions. I have heard he is a really great MIS professor. However, he went through topics much too quickly and the exams were overly difficult. You did get to use notes on exam though, but they were still so hard. Too much info too fast. Not sure if there is a better option though tbh...

I really like Prof Burke and the lessons he gave. Although reading the textbook wasn't necessary it helped me a lot. People were saying you need a high at (95/96) but personally getting a 94 or above got me an A. Burke made MIS pretty interesting even though some of the assignments were annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Burke is a great professor. He gives you powerpoints that concise the textbook so that as long as you take notes during lecture, the textbook is optional (he says it's a supplemental resource). However, because of the high cutoff for an A in this class, you do really need to work it (like above 95/96). But it is doable if you put in the effort.
Class is mostly him reading off lecture slides. He makes jokes sometimes.
Overall good experience, interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Burke is an amazing professor. The class itself has a lot of elements to it, but very doable. I thought it was a pretty easy class to do well in and a better choice in comparison to other MIS 301 professors. The only thing is that with the curve, you need to have a high A to actually get an A in the class. Tests online are open note!!

Took Fall 2020. DON'T want to major in MIS or have Rock? Take Burke. Easy A if you thoroughly read the textbook. I had Sam (TA) and she was very understanding with grading and explanations. MUST read textbook for assessments. Keep in mind Burke does not follow the UT grading scale. He often curves up for what counts as an A (Ex: 93+A).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His classes are lecture heavy and there are required readings, but as long as you read and digest the PPTs that Burke posts on Canvas you would be fine. The assessments can be tricky at first because they are specific terms and concepts that he looks for in a response, but once you get a hang of it you can do well on them.

Burke is a nice and amazing person but lectures are boring. The grade is composed of too many things you need to put effort into during the whole semester. The average score for this class is extremely high so be aware of the curve.

The class is you having to do a lot of work yourself, but it's not too hard and actually useful to learn. There are assessments where he looks for specific answers that are all outlined in the notes. Once you get used to him, not a hard class. He also knows what he's talking about as a professor. Lectures don't really help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The daily iclicker quizzes gave me anxiety. I did not enjoy this class. He seems nice but he just reads off the slides. I felt like I didn't really learn anything. The tests are so long(consist of MC,short&long free-response questions). It was so hard trying to stay awake in this class at 9:30am. The test reviews are just him reusing lecture slides

If you have to take MIS and get the chance, take Burke! He tests based on class slides that are posted on canvas. There are fewer projects than other MIS classes and you get multiple attempts and/or a partner to work with. If you complete the assignments and study slides you can get an A. Daily iClicker quizzes to take attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he is super monotone so his lectures are unbelievably boring. he treated the tests like a guessing game by making our review material a shortened version of the powerpoint (lots of information to know). his tests have free response. never knew what was going to be on the test. couldn't ask him for help on SAM. canvas assignments were really hard

Burke is a nice guy and tries to connect with his students. I would give him a 5 if I was rating him as a person, but as a professor he is pretty average. Pretty much just re-lectures the textbook in class and doesn't add much insight. Take him if you do not want to major in MIS, take Rock if you do. Put in the work, and you can easily get an A.

Lengthy Canvas assignments (not necessarily hard, just long). Weekly SAM assignments easy, but annoying. Daily quizzes over the readings using clickers. Kind of hard to make an A because of the curve. Exams are literally definitions from the textbook and pretty easy short answer questions. I would take again. Reading is long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor, often cracks jokes. Very straightforward class. SAM assignments are easy but can get annoying. Class PowerPoints are long (50 slides) but can easily be summarized. Definitely one of the easier 301 classes. Only annoying thing is the excel assignments that come up later (not too bad w/ a good TA). Skim read for daily iClicker q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures were very interesting and kept me awake at the ungodly hour of 8. The class was a lot of work in my opinion. He also ghosted me when I sent him an email regarding my grade. Other than that, he's very knowledgable. Do the readings, prepare for the daily quizzes, or you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love the guy, used a lot of slides and sometimes assigned projects that neither he or him TA fully understood, but he would grade easier because of it. I honestly enjoyed the class but was a chore having to go at 8AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Just show up for daily quizzes and make sure you actually read the textbook and other materials. Really textbook heavy, but its easy enough. The only problem is that the curve is whack; the A cutoff was like 96 for my class, so you have to really work to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Burke has a supply chain/operations management background. His MIS knowledge is lacking. Lectures consist of him reading off of lecture slides provided by the textbook. He answers questions by re-reading the slides. Projects are poorly organized and explained. Not a bad guy but not equipped at all to teach MIS
In class quizzes are worth 25% of your grade so you have to prepare for every class, but the tests are much easier than the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Buchanan's knowledge and reality class might have been one of the most foundational courses I've ever taken. This class was truly life-changing for me.

Ray is perhaps one of the most caring professors I have ever taken at UT. He is super knowledgeable about the subject matter and philosophy in general. His classes are heavy in reading and test grades(three for the semester). However, he will make sure you will come in prepared for the test and ensure there are no surprises. Amazing professor.

I loved Professor Ray's class. He is deeply passionate about philosophy, respectful, and always willing to help or explore ideas. You will discover his affinity for his wife and his pugs throughout his philosophical examples. 10/10. If you need to take a CHET, take one of his courses. Just make sure to do the readings and study.

Ray is a great professor who is deeply invested in what he teaches and just a wonderful human being. His lectures often went on tangents, but he was wonderful at explaining philosophy and tailoring class discussions to what interested us. Grading standards, esp. on essays, were somewhat unclear, but I'd otherwise recommend Ray without hesitation.

Ray is the coolest guy ever. So chill and makes his classroom very stress free. If I ever had personal problems and let him know in advance, he would be so understanding about deadlines. His handwriting is awful but he makes up for it in every way possible. He is super passionate about Philosophy which shows. I loved his class!

Attendance and participation were part of the grade, so just be wary of that. Professor Buchanan was a great professor! The workload wasn't too bad, just space it out instead of cramming before the deadlines. If you have an interest in the class, or if you force yourself to read, then you'll for sure get a good grade.

Professor Buchanan is a sweet guy who is very passionate about philosophy. The material we learned was interesting but sometimes difficult to understand. I don't recommend this class if you aren't interested in PHL. Only 4 assignments (2 papers, 2 exams) for the whole semester so you have to do well on them if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ray is an insanely chill guy and every lecture feels more like an informal discussion while still being super informative. Gives great analogies & makes it really easy to understand some pretty tricky concepts. Graded on pretty few things but the paper prompts are very clear. Cannot recommend him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Buchanan is wonderful and his lectures are interesting (plus you get to see his pugs). This class doesn't have a lot of grades and is mostly dependent on the TA, which sucks because although Dr. Buchanan was wonderful, the TA was a tough grader and not receptive to opinions that didn't align with theirs. Otherwise, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting topics and good discussions during class. Ray really likes having lectures open for discussion which helps you get a bit of extra points if you miss a few classes. All the papers you read are posted online so you don't have to buy any books. His handwriting is terrible though, especially when he starts writing fast to get a point down.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ray gives entertaining lectures. He is very approachable often inviting you to discuss your paper at a coffee shop before class. He is an easy grader, and seems to really care about making sure everyone passes.
Has a very good understanding of the information and is very effective at communicating it.

He was great, he was really funny and he made you want to come to lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but it earns you slip days for homework. He makes the subject really accessible and a really good lecturer.

Dr.Bulko is an awesome lecturer and his class is fairly easy (10 HW assignments - small iOS apps; 1 semester project App). His lectures mostly consist of him doing Swift/xCode demos and the assignments are pretty enjoyable. My TA was great and most people get A's on the HW, but the instructions are picky. Start the project early!

Great professor and easy class, but the TAs are extremely nit-picky and borderline annoying. They take off for the smallest things and will refuse to give points back. Be sure you do everything the assignment asks to a T.

The professor IS GREAT. Let me repeat BULKO IS AMAZING. 

However the TA grades everything and they are so unreasonable and is on a power trip. Genuinely worst coding experience of my life.  Please stay away it is not worth it.ONCE AGAIN: STAY AWAY

I really want to enjoy this class! I love the lectures, the homework, and I thought I'd like the group assignment. The absolutely disrespectful way he is treating our group though when we try to tell him issues we're having with a troublesome groupmate that has literally cussed us out and done such little work though makes me dread this class.

Bulko is an amazing professor. His teaching style is straightforward, and everything he teaches in lectures relates to the HW. Attendance is "required" only in name, and it's not tracked.  The group project is well outlined and the expectations are clear. The grading is straightforward without strict "gotchas" for stuff like syntax or style.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with prof Bulko, hands down go for it. He is such a kind man, he cares for his students and loves to teach. If you ever want to ask him about anything CS-related, he is happy to provide resources and make time for you. Simply just a great man, I wish I could take another class with him
one of the best instructors I've ever had.

Class attendance is "Mandatory" but nothing is done to track it, and all lectures are shared online. Assignment guidelines are clear and specific. This is the first course I've *ever* received a perfect 100 in. If you follow the assignments to the *letter* you'll get an A every time. Plenty of time given for tests. Homework is annoyingly frequent.

Really great prof, very witty which makes lectures interesting. First 3/4 of the class is demos, followed by group presentations. HWs are really light, just copy paste code from demos. Easy A as long as you put in reasonable work on your group's app and don't procrastinate too much. Most groups get 97+ on alpha/beta even if app is kinda broken.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: What an amazing course. What an amazing lecturer. The homeworks are all VERY doable. He is also extremely funny and caring especially with the semester long group project. I highly reccommend this course. Made me love CS all over again!

Very smart professor with a good sense of humor. He makes lectures fun and explains the subject matter thoroughly. The grading system is fair and there are plenty of opportunities for help from him or other TAs. He can be very blunt/sarcastic at times.

I LOVE PROF BULKO!! If you ever get the opportunity to take one of his classes and are interested in CS, he will do anything to help you learn and understand. The man is very very smart but knows exactly how to dumb it down. I told him I wanted to go into SWE and he set up a meeting with me to give me good resources and connections. LOVE!

phenomenal lecturer - everything i wanted from a non-cs major professor. he was careful to not throw you in the dark about new concepts and was good at dumbing down concepts to develop them into more complex concepts later. class goes through a lot of material - but hw are doable. so are tests

Bulko's Mobile Computing class was the best CS class I've taken at UT. His lectures are entertaining and very in-depth. His assignments are the perfect balance of challenging enough to learn, and easy enough to be enjoyable. As long as you do all the homeworks and don't procrastinate on the group project, an A is guaranteed.

I really enjoyed the class, but get ready for a lot of work (though a normal amount for a CS class). About 2 homework assignments a week (17 total), 3 exams, and one group project. Currently taking him for Web Programming, and its been super fun! Awesome person! His lectures are super interesting and very informative, and he is incredibly accessible outside of class, always answering questions outside of class on piazza. One of my favorite class experiences! Side note: he is hilarious and a great guy.

reviews.comment: This Professor is amazing. REALLY emphasizes breaking a situation down to its core so you understand how your program or code truly functions. Attend all the classes and you don't have to read the textbook. Dr. Bulko explains all the concepts very thoroughly. He and the TAs are very helpful and responsive on Piazza. There are 15 HW assignments but not that hard, he always go over them in class.

reviews.comment: Bulko is a fantastic teacher. I never found myself zoning out during lectures, and attending those are definitely required if you're looking to get a decent grade. I didn't buy the book, but Google works well for any questions that you have. Written exams were difficult.

Bulko is the BEST, take him!!! He's funny, kind and is very clear in explaining any concept, which is good even if you have no background in the subject. HW are fair, exams might be a little hard but fair. Hes the best professor you could take though and is very accessible outside of class with office hours everyday and quick email/Piazza replies

reviews.comment: IOS was a really fun class and the grading was all reasonable. Bulko takes the time to comment on all of the journals and is really caring. The grading criteria is clear. The amount of homework is a bit heavy, but anything less and you wouldn't learn the material. Make sure to find a good group and you'll do well in the class.

Dr. Bulko was fantastic! His lectures were always clear and easy to follow. The homework assignments were never too difficult and he would provide help on those in office hours. His tests were a little tricky but overall not too bad because you're allowed a cheat sheet. He's overall an amazing professor and you should definitely take his class.

Great professor. He really knew how to explain concepts clearly and concisely. Most of your grade (55%) comes from homework assignments, and he always went over the solution to them in class using other examples (so attend class if you can!!). The tests can be tricky just because he asks you to write programs, but they were doable.

reviews.comment: Honestly why would you choose anyone else? Take his class.

Good amount of homework and tests were straightforward. Cheatsheets are allowed on tests. A good counterbalance to Mike's 314.

Bill's lectures can seem slow sometimes, but that's just because he's thorough in his explanation. In my opinion, that's better than a professor breezing through difficult concepts. For the class itself, 10 weekly HWs, no exams or final, 1 semester-long project to build whatever app you want. Easy upperdiv CS class.

Bulko has interesting lectures. He understands the class isn't CS majors so he explains things thoroughly. Exams can be challenging but do-able if you study. Homework assignments every week but are not that hard. He is caring and understanding and is always available during office hours, although you should get there early- lots of students go.

I learned a decent amount without the class being difficult. Easy A, but don't completely blow it off or it may sneak up on you. Also, I had already taken Statistics. We spent some time on set theory and such, which is great for when you get to stats but, if you have already taken it, feels a whole lot like going to lecture is pointless for a bit.
Bulko explains everything at least ten times in class and provides plenty of examples. Go to class, do the homework in the discussion sections and you have an A.

reviews.comment: Somewhat mediocre jokes in class, seems like an alright guy, until you get to his office hours. Explains answers with almost a level of contempt, overall not very nice or helpful. TA's were good and helpful though.
I'm not a CS major (anymore), but I did think he was a good professor. The class was very difficult, but I think he was somewhat of an easy grader (relative to how crappy a student I was).

IThis class is really boring but Bulko knows that and tries to keep the lectures semi-interesting, but still if you're not careful you'll fall asleep. A really easy course, he allows cheat sheet in the tests and that is really helpful.
Great class and great professor.

He lets you bring a cheat sheet on the test, which is great. The tests should be easy if you put the right things on your cheat sheets, unless you're great at memorization. Homework is helpful in preparing you from exams. Good guy.

reviews.comment: Really funny, smart and nice professor. He goes over everything thoroughly and tries to help you get good grades on the exam. The only downside this semester was our TA, who took forever to grade stuff and was pretty ruthless in the grading technique

Bulko's class was pretty easy, and for the most part he was engaging in his lectures. Sometimes the lectures felt a little drawn out, but I think that's just due to the topics we went over. An amusing professor who will try to engage the class. Very nice and tries to explain further if needed. Work was doable for slackers and slow people like me.

Provides most information in lecture so studying isn't hard or long at all. Tests are easy and he provides help if needed. Would definitely take him again!

Prof. Bulko is an amazing human being but can be a bit confusing while explaining stuff. The exams and hw were super easy and he helps out a lot if you go to his office hours. Awesome instructor! the class itself is very small and intimate. The variety of reading and film materials makes the class interesting and I had fun. i really enjoyed her. if you put the work in it's a great class, she really cares about all her students

She definitely tries to make the class fun even with it being a difficult course and she puts in the work to try to get everyone what they need. Sometimes confusing but if u have any cs experience it shouldn't be too hard.

Definitely a hard course but if you seek extra help when needed and really put the work in she's a great professor who truly cares about what she's teaching. People say it's hard to keep up with her lectures but really you just need to pay attention.

If you have prior coding experience this will likely be an easy class. Ramsey is not a great lecturer but she's not the worst either. For programming assignments utilize design sessions!! dude i forgot to do this, but 314 feels easier than this class somehow.

Lectures don't explain content well, grading scheme is difficult, and lack of proper practice material given.

She is overall a nice professor if you talk to her. She does get lost in her lectures sometimes, but you can tell she knows what she is doing. The grading style is mostly what makes this class suck as your final grade corresponds with your lowest out of your midterms/final, programming assignments, and at-home-quizzes. Hard if new to CS.

Truly, the worst class I've had in my life. No words can describe how much I hate this class and how the professor made me hate cs. The class is not an intro class at all. tips: Read textbook before lecture, go to every review session because you'll need it. Don't get discouraged!
The class has really strict grading. The averages of tests are around B- and C+. It is very unfriendly to total beginners.

Horrible. Please don't take.

Terrible!!!!!!!! Don't take her class if you have another option. Heavy workload assignment but only 20% of total score. Exams never curved, and no drop for the lowest. Make one big mistake on exam = impossible to get an A. This is just the basic of programming, but she tried to make it hard.

She teaches things in class completely wrong and frequently gets called out. I don't think she should be teaching computer science if she literally does not know how to do computer science. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

I can say without a doubt here at she did not teach what was needed. Not even She made me fail calc

Professor does not teach lectures well. All of the TAs complain about how her teaching is bad and if they were her students they would have a hard time. She is very inconsiderate. reviews.comment: Professor Ramsey makes the course much more complicated than it should be. Most of the programming assignments are easy (but they start to become more tedious after the 6th one). Start programming assignments early and ask TA's for help and follow style guide. Take opportunity of rare extra credit and for tests look at the practice tests (similar).

If there's any teacher to break your spirit and make you question your career choice it'll be her. Ramsey herself was nice the times I talked to her, but her lectures really won't help much and attendance is mandatory only for the quizzes at the end of class. You'll have to teach yourself. Tests are 70%, despite tricky, weekly coding assignments.

This class is pretty self-taught. Use all the resources - the textbook, practice sessions, and Unstuck study for study prep. Attend lectures, but be ready to do a lot of self-study to really learn the material.

CS 312 is a straightforward course, but Professor Ramsey makes it unnecessarily difficult. Her lectures are poorly delivered, riddled with mistakes, and lack clarity and structure to help novice programmers build a foundation in Java. She puts little effort into addressing student needs, leaving many to struggle through the material independently.

Programming assignments weekly, 3 exams total. Little extra credit. Tests are weighed 70% (as of fall2024). Good professor, I personally found the lectures to be very informative and helpful. Started with zero Java experience. Tip: Go to TA's for help. Preferably read before lecture, or read when topics seem difficult. And just believe in yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

Don't be discouraged if you do bad.

If attendance wasn't required I wouldn't be surprised if no one showed up to class. This class is entirely self-taught because of how awful her lectures are. I'm 99% sure the only reason she's the intro teacher is bc UT knows how awful she is but they want to weed out kids from CS. this is the type of prof that will make you dislike CS j bc of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

The coding assignments are a little hard to understand but TAs typically help you understand it during TA sections. Grades are heavily weighted by the test though.

Professor Carol Ramsey herself is an amazing professor, who truly cares about the success of her students. The course is difficult, as students are expected to learn the fundamentals of Java in a semester, but that isn't due to Professor Ramsey. She provided the class with a lot of resources, and the TAs were generally very helpful.

Hardest, worst class ever taken. Professor Ramsey constantly changes grading requirements after she already gave the assignment. TESTS ARE EXTREMELY DIFFICULT. Her lectures are scattered and unclear. You have to teach yourself most of this class. Good Luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

As a beginner, I did fine on the weekly programming assignments, however, the tests lowered my grade a lot. I have not coded before and having to write it out on paper when I had just learned to code was very difficult. She was not much help as the TAs were the students' main resource.

First of all, why are the tests weighted 70% of your entire grade when there are only 3 tests; the programming assignments done every week are only weighted as 20% of the grade. Secondly, the grading on programming assignments and tests are very strict and not very lenient. As an intro class for freshmen, beginners will definitely struggle.

She is SUCH a sweet person and super real, but her exams do NOT reflect the practice tests. I think i got near a perfect score on 3 practice exams and still failed the most recent one for sure, so be careful with thinking the practice exams reflect hers because she is new and her content differs a good amount to cause panic.
pretty much a self-taught class. do not slack

Take it seriously, read Zybooks before class, pay attention in class, and go to help hours if you need aren't understanding something.

Utilize all the resources available if you are a beginner. SPECIALLY design sessions and office hours. Study for exams way ahead of time (do practice problems as often as possible). You MUST have a really good understanding of the material since a big part of the exams are writing code by hand. Ramsey was okay.

At least for CS313E I feel a lot of these reviews exaggerate.  Maybe that's because I've programmed before and have prior fluency so take that in mind.  Programming assignments are insanely fun to complete and really help you learn.  Main issue is lectures and quizzes where she can get tripped up, and the quizzes being mandatory is just silly.

bad

disorganized and lectures are pretty useless and all over the place. Professor Ramsey needs to improve in areas such as presentation skills and introducing difficult-to-get subjects to people who have never seen this material before, as well as making fair exams. Some of her TAs do a better job of teaching you than her.
Someone show this page to the dean. Please. The next generation of CS depends on it.

reviews.comment: I walked into class the other day, ready to give her another chance to change my opinion and write this review. I walked out without having learned anything in the past month. Do not take this class with her unless you 100% absolutely have to.

I feel as though more is learned through doing Practice It problems as opposed to the lectures. The tests are what will determine your grade in this class, which they can be quite unpredictable due to including content not seen in the practice tests. The grading rubric for assignments seems subjective depending on which TA grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: "Lectures" are tailored more for a subpar HS environment. I don't blame anybody who came for the quizzes and immediately left as she only makes you more confused any time you try to understand anything. She cares more about the school's volleyball team than she does about your individual success in the class. Still wondering how she got this job...

reviews.comment: Prof. Ramsey was the most difficult teacher I have ever taken in all my years of learning. Her lectures were unorganized, underprepared, and often of little use. She makes things difficult to understand and expects you to have previous coding knowledge. The best parts of this class are the ones she obtained from previous Prof. Mike Scott.

reviews.comment: Although she did say it was her first semester at UT, her teaching style was just not efficient in general. Most of her lectures consist of her trying to debug her own code at 30wpm. Her presentations are often unfinished and provide little substance to you in the class. The review material is not sufficient in complexity for the actual exams.
If you have absolutely no coding experience do not take this as your intro class. This class is not beginner friendly. Take CS 303 first.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ramsey is not a bad person, but she needs to work on teaching. She spends most of class debugging and working through her code. She only really gave us practice tests to work on to prepare for the exam, but the exam was very different from the practice tests. Definitely not a beginner-friendly course. I've been coding and still struggled.

reviews.comment: Kept talking about how UT CS courses were difficult as if that was the reason why the test was brutal... We been knew that bruh. It's clearly not the reason why we're here on your Rate My Professor page. Just teach the course better. As someone who's new to teaching CS 312, you'd think they'd be more open to criticism.

reviews.comment: Coming into this class with no prior cs experience, I've had to heavily rely on the textbook to learn everything. The lectures are generally not super helpful and honestly, if you want to do well in this class, you'll have to study A LOT on your own. Like others have said, Prof Ramsey isn't a bad person, she just doesn't do a great job of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ramsey is not a bad professor, way better than my HS teacher. Its her first semester teaching at UT. She really cares/puts effort into her lectures and tries to make everyone understand it.Tests aren't great because they are not like practice tests but they are like practiceIT. TAs grade leniently.There are curves if bad distribution.

As someone who had past experience with coding, I did not expect this class to be this bad. Professor Ramsey is a really nice person but her teaching style is not effective in my opinion. She skims over key concepts and does not explain or spend time on key concepts. S It is hard to learn in class and I learnt mainly by reading the textbook.

Ramsey is kind, but she lacks the ability to teach effectively in lectures. Her teaching style is mainly her working through live coding problems without explaining much of the programming basics fundamental to this class. Also, the tests are not great and the programming assignments are fairly difficult, especially if you have no experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ramsey is very kind and extremely caring. She is accessible outside of class and really seems like she cares. However, her method of lecture is very unhelpful, and exams contain material over problems we haven't seen before. She tries to change Dr. Scott's slides, assignments, and exams, which is beyond annoying.

As someone with no coding background, I do not feel like this course is for people with no coding knowledge. I honestly credit google for all the good grades Ive gotten on assignments. You have practice tests to study for tests, but I aced all the practice tests and I still feel like I failed the actual test because they are not similar at all.

reviews.comment: She be making you wanna switch your major.

reviews.comment: A great professor for a First Year Introductory Course. Although the test differs slightly from practice exams because the practice is from Mike Scott, the previous professor, it is not that different. She ties to help students' needs and provides a large number of resources to succeed. Just pay attention in lectures and you'll never be surprised.

The Lecture goes over the same material in the book. Her lectures consist of her going over a new topic briefly (the part you should pay most attention) then debugging code on that topic. 
Beware, her exams are hard, and since she is a new teacher they are different from practice exams. Hopefully this improves

PS: We had a pretty rough test 10/26

Lectures are just watching her debug her code, with not much explanation. Attendance isn't "mandatory", but there are quizzes every lecture for your attendance. The tests are extremely different than the material given to practice, also you get a 3 day notice of new material that will be on the test. She's extremely nice tho

reviews.comment: Gg

ramsey debugs her own code during lectures and gives daily quizzes which non of the material is actually taught in class. the practice tests do not reflect her tests, at all. important material is taught at a surface level. you're better off with a youtube tutorial lol. she's the only 312 prof so good luck...

run

reviews.comment: the practice tests looks nothing like the actual test. you will get a 100% on everh single practice test and fail the actual test because she just puts concepts we've never seen or learned about. Possibly the worst teacher for an introductory cs course. If you have the option, please do yourself a favor, dont take 312 from her!!

Coming from someone with no prior coding, this "introductory" course was really not "introductory" friendly. There's so much she skims over during lectures, it's actually useless. I already knew coming in that it would be difficult but I was actually set up to fail. Not worth the depression and stress. I wish brand-new coders good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had prior experience before this class so I might rate the difficulty of the class less than what it actually is. If you're just getting into programming then get ready to review a lot of material on your own. She is really passionate about making sure everyone understands the material but the structure of the course still needs polishing.

Even though it is her first year teaching, I do not think her lectures are proficient. She just spends the whole lecture debugging her code and making us watch her typing code. So basically this class is heavily textbook based and learning outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you have no coding experience, be ready to learn from the textbook. I haven't learned a thing from lectures. Test grades are weighted heavily, but there are only two exams and a final. Instructions on assignments and tests are wordy and confusing. The course isn't terribly difficult, but that's only if you're ready to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assignment instructions unclear. Lectures are useless.
Barely learn in class even when I write down notes. Her fail rate for exams compared to other profs is insane.
Professor is nonexistent but when he does show up/ comment it's simply to complain and criticize the easiest assignment. Superiority complex is all it is.
Best class I've ever taken! The actual class is led by a ULL but Dr. Carroll is always available for office hours. Such a great and kind professor. Just show up to class and you will be just fine :)

The professor was never in the class except once. Class is helped by the ULL. As long as you show up to every class and do the activities and pre labs you will leave with an 100. You are able to miss up to 2 classes and they surprise drop one assignment.

professor is nonexistant, class is led by ULL. my ULL graded like she got paid for every point taken off so pray u get a nice one. Attendance is mandatory 1 absence can automatically bring u down to a B no matter how good u do on ur assignments. this class consists of a lot of groupwork and presentations

Very hard to get anything lower than an A in this class as long as you show up and do the work. Most of the assignments are group work and easy to complete. I probably had about 30 minutes' worth of homework p/wk. The class is taught by a student leader who is probably a year or two older than you, not the professor, so hard to build a connection.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE DR CARROLL. So understanding, funny, and relatable. You can tell he loves what he teaches and it was a super interesting class. Took this course abroad and the vibes were there. TA graded a little rough but Dr. Carroll was very open to hearing reasoning for regrading.

Dr. C is one of the best professors at UT. Take him if you can... you won't regret it. CMS 371K gives you a 40-hour mediation certification and is group-intensive. You will put in a lot of hours outside of class with your group, but the work is mainly acting/roleplaying and is a lot of fun.

Dr. C is a great professor and cares about his students. CMS 371K is a fun class with an option to be certified in the 40hr basic course. It requires great commitment with your teams, because you practice with classmates. If you have the time, put in the effort, and willing to commit, you can easily do well in the class. I recommend his course!

Had him for the May-mester abroad, and he was super nice, super chill, and overall a great professor to have abroad. Truthfully, idk why his rating is so low bc every single person in our class loved him.

Dr. Carroll isn't present in class; it is a ULL (I forgot what that stood for, but basically a student teaching students). I felt so bad when he randomly showed up to class, and it was so awkward. He had asked if there were any questions, and ofc there were none. Anyways, it's an easy class and may help you out when it comes to jobs.

Super easy class. Taught by the Undergraduate Lab Leaders. Wish that we were able to talk with the professor more because form the few interactions I had with him, he was awesome. A lot of people complained about this class, but if you really apply yourself, this class sets you up for professional success.

Super easy class, basically a guaranteed A if you do the homework assignments that take 5 mins max and show up to class. The class is completely taught by ULLs, so there's little to no interaction with Dr. Carroll. Some in-class assignments are helpful professionally (elevator pitches and LinkedIn/HookedIn), but most are busy work.
I literally do not know why his rating isn't a 5/5. He is SO amazing. It's so unbelievably easy to get an A and he is so personable and kind.
Incredibly easy, taught by a ULL instead of the actual professor. Put like an ounce of effort into it and you'll be fine.

Super easy, my ULL was super chill, and every in-person assignment during the class was with your assigned group. The outside work was a breeze, but this class does help with valuable things for your future such as LinkedIn, resumes, interviews, etc. This is basically like a free class.

Just like COM301, 302 is painfully easy. I never even met Dr. Carroll (I was absent when he visited my group). Only issue is you'll have trouble motivating yourself to do the homework because it's so easy to put off. 

No complaints on Dr. Carroll - just a standard COM302.

If you are looking at this for COMM302E, Professor Carroll isn't actually teaching your class. Your ULL is the one that meets with you once a week and grades your work. The class is super easy and doesn't take up much time out of your day.

I saw him one time where he briefly attended a discussion. All of our teaching was through the ULL, and she was great. The assignments were easy and there weren't many. Much of what you learn is about networking and presenting yourself. I only watched two of the online lectures and they did not aid in my understanding any more than going to class.

The course is taught by a ULL, not Dr. C.The assignments and group work are boring and redundant. Attendance is too strict (only 2 free absences). Even when you're sick and provide a doctor's note, they don't excuse absences and make you go through SES. It's not worth the time or money, but unfortunately it is mandatory for Moody students.

The lectures were not the best, in my opinion, but you learn what you need to know for the assignments. No exams, only reflections, papers, one video on a culture of your choice, and a group project. Attendance is mandatory, but you get 3 free absences. Students have to buy two books. The group project is pretty time-consuming so beware of that.

This class is an easy A. The in-person part of the class is taught entirely by a ULL, and every assignment is graded on completion. Just meet the word requirement on the assignments and show up to class, and you should get an A.

You never see the professor in this class and is entirely done with your TA. Attendence is the hardest part of this class. Assignments are extremley easy, but if you miss more than two classes, then 5% of your grade gets deducted for each additional absence.

Professor Carroll seems like a nice enough man, but his class is easy and tedious. Taught by a TA. Assignments are mind-numbing, with unnecessary minimum sentence number quotas that force you to waste time padding your answers. 

He's also unsympathetic if you're sick. When I got the flu, he refused to excuse my absences and ignored my follow-up.
Super easy course, taught by ULAs so beware of that
Very much like COM301E. Is super easy, but a lot of group work. Class is taught by ULAs and is not often that you get to meet the prof.

This was a hybrid course with biweekly in-person group labs and everything else online. So easy and extremely boring. It is literally impossible to not get an A. The professor only came in person once, and most all the lectures were online guest lectures. It's all common sense, so don't expect to learn anything new, but it's good for your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor showed up to one class as a guest but the rest of the time the classes were lead by a ULA. It was small in-class group projects and we got to leave early nearly every day. The stuff the prof teaches is online and extremely easy. Feels like a waste of time and money but is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was easy but the TAs grading can be tough on you
intro COM classes are what they are supposed to be. It is easy but I do feel like Professor Carroll did perfectly fine with how it was structured. Overall a stress-free environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Robert is an amazing person and an amazing professor. You definitely have to be actively engaged in his class to do well, but you will naturally want to be in his class. He helped me become a better presenter and writer. I cannot thank him enough. Seriously, this was one of my favorite classes at UT.

Carroll is the best option for BA 324. All of my friends with other professors hated their BA 324 classes, meanwhile Carroll's curriculum and teaching made this my favorite class. I learned a lot from this class and Professor Carroll is extremely nice.

One of UT's hidden gems. If you're taking BA324, this is the man you need. He completely rewrote BA324's structure, so it's different than all other professors. My favorite class by far. He is super high energy, hilarious, and cares about every student. He is the only professor who has given me an amazing virtual experience, and I appreciate him.

Professor Carroll's class was great. He really cares about each of his students, and wants everyone to succeed. If you read the directions carefully and submit quality assignments, you will succeed in this course. There is group work, so you have to manage your time well and stay on top of it. Work hard and your grade will reflect it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Take this Professor if you can! Forget all of the negative things that you have heard about this course. Dr. Carroll has revamped his class to be a more fair, fun, and informative environment. No quizzes and the class average was an A-. If you turn in quality work, you will get an A. Go to office hours for clarifications on assignments.

He is redoing BA324 and removed all tests and quizzes! Grading is based on interesting presentations/projects which are actually fun. You must put effort into the projects. This was a great class! The grade distribution isn't accurate, he no longer grades like that: 25% of my class got an A, no one failed! 100% Recommend-also is a great guy!

Carroll drove me crazy sometimes because of his subjective grading habits and confusing expectations for every assignment. I found that if you want an A you have to go to office hours ALL the time and sorta just turn in work that is word for word exactly what he wants. It sorta sucks but he's a nice guy who cares a lot. You learn!

Dr. Carroll is one of the best professors I've ever had! He cares so much about his students & is so easy to talk to. If you reach out to him, he does so much to work with you & give great feedback! The class is tough, but it does a great job of preparing you for the professional world. Don't trust the grade dist.- he definitely gives out A's & A-

Robert Carroll's rating on here does not do him justice. He is a young, hip guy who really cares about his students (he even baked for us!) and is extremely knowledgeable in communications. For being a dreaded course, Robert made this class enjoyable, and I became a better speaker. Despite a bad grade distribution, many of us in the class got A's.

Here is the truth: People judge Robert because he is a 'harsh grader,' however he gives you what you deserve. He cares about engaging with his students & ensuring that they are prepared when they leave his class. Robert is genuine & he knows exactly what he is talking about; he is one of the best professors at McCombs & you will benefit from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Carroll is very relatable and he makes a boring class engaging. He is a great lecturer and fun person. However, Dr. Carroll does not give out full points and it seems like no one has ever attained an A within his class. You will learn a lot during Dr. Carroll's class, but he will make you work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader
