(Plan II Bio) The A is there for the taking. three tests are pretty easy. cool field trip to the beach. pretty boring lectures, but showing up to class boosts your grade for the easier A.

She is great professor and gives you numerous resources to study with but her grading scale is a little difficult in my opinion. It's hard to get an A, but you will definitely learn a lot and will be prepared for upper division bio courses.
She's a great professor who is willing to go out of her way to help her students. The class covers a lot of material, but she's very clear both in lecture and in her expectations.
She is an amazing professor, willing to help you at anytime. :]
Good intro bio class; either the online textbook or the lectures will allow you to learn the material and do well in the class. Professor lectures well and is open to questions.

She is an awesome professor, her test cover a lot of material and are very detailed. Don't think that studying a couple nights will do the trick. Start studying early and it will pay off in this course. Old exams that she post are very helpful and so are the obejective questions on her handouts.
very good professor, class is not easy but ask for help! She is very helpful and review sessions are excellent prep for tests.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

She's a good professor in that she's pretty clear most of the time and hands out class objectives to keep you on track. She really caters to her students as a lecturer so you'll get so quality information in. Test questions are kind of tricky though. It's purely because the questions are so vague.
No Comments

This class is not engaging and is organized poorly. Lectures are mostly discussion and vague which isn't very effective for learning and retaining information. I have to teach myself everything. When I asked for help, he laughed in my face.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring, making an already dry subject even more unbearable. His project grading was quite arbitrary, and he honestly struggles to communicate to his students. BHP will probably  replace him, so hopefully future students have a better experience with the class.

The class was easy as the homeworks, midterm, and final (written by chatGPT) were very easy. He was brought in as a last min replacement and I think he tried his best, but he is a very unengaging lecturer imo. His grading is also very ambiguous and he screwed a lot of ppl on the project. Overall easy class and you can do well with minimal effort

The professor was a last-minute addition and new to this specific course. While the homework and exams were manageable, the reading workload was extremely heavy. I think most of the class just didn't read them and it was fine. The group project felt a bit rushed due to the timing, but the professor was understanding and fair with the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: When you take this professor, it's not the class you registered for.  It's mental gymnastics 101.  Save yourself the chronic headaches and don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to do lot of group projects but she's very lenient. Super helpful if you have any questions. Class just consists of lots of research but if it's a topic you enjoy it can be lots of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this course for the MAS credit, but I enjoyed this class! She is very personable and picked great stories to read for Latina/o culture. Instead of writing essays, we made Zines for every cycle. She also gave good feedback to people who were getting adjusted to her class system. She also set up professor and student norms as boundaries.

Terrible course, a terrible professor, and I had the worst TA. Don't take this course and don't stay in the course if your TA makes you redo multiple assignments. This class is taught by people who don't want to admit that their entire profession is a joke and will be even more useless in a couple of years, and they're taking it out on the students

I had a quite positive experience (I liked her class so much that I picked up an English minor). The readings for the class could be a bit uncommon but I enjoyed them because they offered different perspectives. Stay on top of everything, and if you have a problem with TA's grading I would suggest reaching out to Dr. C. She is very kind & helpful.

Never watched online lecture videos because they were quite boring, and the assignments were very straightforward, so there was no need. Grade in class heavily depends on your TA. Mine was very chill, and I never had to resubmit an assignment (make sure you read the instructions in their entirety).

Now that flags are gone DO NOT take this class here. It is entirely self paced other than discussion but they grade super strict. The lectures are SO SO boring and the discussions are super awkward. I HATED this class. Also, the readings are all super long and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has nothing to do with her (she's nice TBH), but rather the TA. Some are OK but mine was PICKY even though they would grade very late. Which can screw you over at the end of the semester. If you go to discussion prepare for the most awkward 50 mins ever since no one talks. Now that flags are gone, make life easier: take the class at CC.

I was surprised to see such a low score for someone who has quickly become a favorite professor of mine. She is a kind, fascinating, and understanding professor. Her class focused mainly on reading and class discussions. If you love to read, I highly recommend this class!

Oddest grade system I've had, but you get the hang of it (ish). You determine your own grade. Lectures unnecessarily long, readings lengthy. Just keep up with it. For reading journals, just follow the "tips to success". Grades depend on TA most of the time :( Dr. C's personality is all about her culture lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I put hilarious because it is just laughable. The class was absolute dog water. The TA "Jefferey Nguyen" is a 24 yr old child on a power trip. Do not take this class under any circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Please don't be scared by the reviews. Although this class can be a bit overwhelming at first, the workload is incredibly manageable if you stay on top of it, and there truly isn't that much. The grading requirements are clear, and this class will only be a bit difficult if you despise writing, but other than that, I promise you it is quite easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof CdeBaca's E316M can be a mixed bag. While the course content is engaging, the workload and grading system can be tricky. Staying on top of assignments is key. Utilizing unstuckstudy alongside the course materials can be a game-changer for managing the workload.

To the other rater that claimed CdeBaca is evil; I couldn't have said it better myself. The course itself is laughably easy, you only have to do a few assignments for a good grade. God forbid you face any personal struggles during semester though; don't expect a shred of compassion or understanding. Only rude emails and a holier than thou attitude!

Super chill because you just need to do whatever assignments you want then the points get added up. There is a lot of reading to do so it might be hard to juggle with other classes. I kind of got screwed over because everything said I had gotten an A, but it went in the system as a B+ and there wasn't anybody for me to reach out to for help to fix.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof C's class is chill if you're on top of it. Texts are relevant, lectures drag. Assignments clear; 4 points for A. TAs make it or break it- some ppl had to resubmit for credit, I didn't. Stay on track for easy A. Love/hate course, needs self-motivation. Cultural awareness great. Don't wait until the last week to do most of your work (like me)!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't do it. Click another english class or take it as ACC or another community college. The whole class seemed like an ego project to prove a point. Professor seemed nice until you realize that she said, "Nothing you turn in will be an instant A and you won't get an A if you don't go to my office hours". Very very dependent on the TA you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class at UT. The expectations of an entry level course are outrageous. There are over 6 weekly assignments that take 2-3 hours each. That is almost 18 hours per week just in assignments. Recorded lectures  take quite awhile, on top of reading. 4 Finals/midterms. Grading system is you need 4 points to get an A but hard to even get .20 points.

Do NOT believe others when they say she is caring or kind. She is not nice at all!! I had some serious personal struggles during this course, and she had no compassion in the slightest. Dr. Cdebaca is evil. 

As for the class, the workload was alright. The rubric was confusing though, and did not match up with the assignment instructions. :/

I took this class over the summer to fulfill my core credit. It only required about 12-16 hours per week, so very doable. Dr.C picked exciting texts to read, and the assignments truly helped me understand not only the texts but also the American social climate. Dr. C was extremely accessible through email; I would recommend this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer so I would assume my experience would be different than it would during a full semester. There are a lot of readings and the reading journals take a while but it's pretty easy to skim through the course. The grading system is different than over any course that I've seen, basically just need 3.85 points to get a A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The material was outdated, poorly organized. Assignments were unnecessary challenging, leading to confusion and frustration. Feedback on assignments was minimal and unhelpful, providing no guidance for improvement. Overall, I would strongly advise against taking this class unless you enjoy feeling confused, frustrated, and unproductive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I have ever taken. The professor was extremely unclear with her rubric and especially her lecture videos. I got the feeling that she just wanted to flaunt how intelligent she is. American Literature but feels more like world history and feels even more dry than that. Stay clear if you don't care for pretentious professors.

Easiest class I've taken. You complete any combo of assignments you want and only have to earn 4 pts to get an A (attendance can count as 1 pt). I did 1 assignment a week and was done by Spring Break. A manageable class as long as you stay on top of work. Just make sure to follow the rubrics and you will be fine. Everything is graded by your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do yourself the absolute largest favor and do not take this course with her. The class is dependent on TA's and papers either "meet standard" or don't. Grades come out late and the questions required for each essay are overcomplicated, so you get no credit for writing a 4 page essay. The grading scale is confusing+ not well explained so you're lost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just need to get 4 points to earn an A. You are allowed to mix and match what assignments you choose and attending discussion is not mandatory but worth 1 point. Assignments were all easy and an A is very achievable as long as you don't wait until the last minute. The professor and TA were also super approachable and kind.

Ts make or break the class if you want to do this class at the last minute. My TA graded assignments super fast and was on top of things, so getting all the points needed for an A was easy. I would recommend finishing the class a month before the last class day, which is more than doable and if you do its an EASY A.

Lazy grader and doesn't fully read over submitted papers. For example, we were allowed resubmissions, professor failed to grade the resubmission and regraded the first submission, telling me once more to refer to her notes...I do not recommend any of her courses, she is just too much to deal with. Save yourself the stress and find someone else.

I really enjoyed the course, especially the selected readings. This class is entirely dependent on TA's, so your experience may vary. If you are a good writer, this will breeze by. I took this course with 5 other STEM classes and barely felt any strain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment:
Get past the first few weeks of theory n you'll be fine
Researching at the Benson Center and Harry Ransom Center was novel. Beware;both places close at 5pm+closed weekends. 
Biweekly group presentations. 
Dr. C was generous with extensions + gives good feedback. Ask for her help on your final Oxford bibliography. 
Paredes rules, Faulkner drools.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Online lectures & discussion section with TA. You get to choose what four things you want to complete to get an A. There are no due dates, so time management is huge. If you manage your time and don't get lazy it's fine. Lots of reading and all the assignments are essays. Not bad and you can finish early as long as you stay on top of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Never hated a course more. Horrible professor, we don't see her, all we see is the TA and all the TA does is waste our time while the ACTUAL course vids/work is online. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Straight forward class with clear expectations. This is by par one of the most simplest English courses at UT Austin and the hardest part is just getting starting. The readings are doable and as long as your people skills are good, TA discussions are great. Overall not a hard class, just not a class people want to take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Majority of negative reviews are either shocked that one has to read for a Lit. class, had a bad TA (unfortunate but NOT Dr. C), didn't manage time, or didn't read the syllabus/go to office hours. Dr. C is GENUINELY caring and considerate. Even in the midst of serious adversity, she is accommodating and interested in nurturing relationships.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: literally don't listen to these reviews. she's the sweetest person. any negative comments are from those who did not communicate with her. she lets you turn in assignments as many times as possible to get a 100 on it, you just need to listen to her feedback.

She always forgets to post whats due before class until the day before, grades terribly, gives very unclear instructions, and makes writing and class dreadul. Don't take her. I hope she sees this because she needs a wake up call

Assignments can be done whenever you want so I finished the class in about a week (summer '23). You can re-attempt any assignment you didn't get a 100 on. The lectures were useless and I never watched them. Your grade 100% depends on your TA, I was lucky enough to get one who graded pretty easy so I never had to re-do an assignment. Overall easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Heavy on the readings. Although the class isn't impossible, it's an unnecessary amount of stress. Videos were helpful for context and could be sped up. It is important to read all of the information on the Canvas page and assignment instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She posts so many readings and her lectures are hours long (and pointless). After module 2 I didn't bother watching the lectures. The majority of the work in this class are the reading journals, which have vague prompts and take hours to write. Self paced class, so don't fall too far behind the suggested due dates. It's a lot of effort to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class consumed the final weeks of my summer. Everything revolved around painstakingly writing reading "journals" for this class. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class isn't too terrible, but I don't know if I would take it again. You can speed up her lectures, and you get unlimited attempts on assignments. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible class. I cannot stand how she focuses so much on historical and literary contexts and expects us to incorporate that into our writing. Fortunately you just need to complete every module to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is so annoying. The assignments consist of reading journals, which at first seem chill, but eventually escalate into you writing 1500+ words per journal. There are also so many readings and they take forever to do. She posts hours of  useless lectures on top of that. Grading system is awfully slow.

This class is unnecessarily difficult; the lectures and readings are long. When grading the reading journals the feedback given is vague and the TAs usually just quote the prompt with no real explanation. TA is different for every assignment so no real connection formed. This was more time-consuming and more work than my summer stem classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class unless you have a lot of time to devote specifically to it. It can be very easy to fall behind bc of the grading system. I would take this prof again for an in-person class bc prof & TA's were fair to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: easy A but annoying class setup. You had to get perfect scores on the homework to access the next module, but the TAs graded weirdly so it's easy to get behind. I often had to wait days for grades and I would have to submit the next assignments late.

The structure of the class with grading was frustrating. Professor expected students to complete entire modules within two to three days, these modules often took me five hours to complete. It took over two days to get my grade back to move onto the next module. This caused me to already be behind because of the slow grading turnaround.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! She was the worst instructor I've ever taken and would not recommend anyone to take her classes in the future if you don't want to suffer an extremely illogical grading policy. It doesn't worth the time and money at all. I regret to just not take it in community college.

Do NOT take this in the summer if you want an easy class. Grading is SLOW and can be picky. Lots of reading and writing. But, if you do exactly what they ask for and ask for help via email or office hours, it is possible to get the grade you want. Last words: don't rush submitting assignments because resubmitting is a pain.

Don't take this prof in Summer. Absolute horrendous TAs who use an arbitrary grading structure to hold students back. The "self-paced" structure is not true if you have to wait DAYS to go from one module to the next; add in the fact that you might get a horrible TA to grade your work, meaning they halt your progression further. Don't take it.

Do NOT take this class. The class format is incredibly stupid because although it is asynchronous, you can't move forward until the previous module has been graded. TA's are nit-picky and unclear in their instructions. I highly highly advise against taking this class.
The class was okay. I think that it required a lot of time but as long as you submit the module by the preferred due date, then receiving an A is very possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was entirely completion-based, and all assignments were pass/fail. You couldn't move on to the next module until you had passed all assignments in the previous one. Grading took 1-2 days, but given that they were multipage essays, I thought that this was a reasonable turnaround. As long as you don't procrastinate, you'll get an A.

I just want to say that the low reviews are spot on.DON'T take this class if you do many other things over the summer!The lectures and readings for the 9 modules are unnecessarily long and you have to get a PERFECT to move on to the next assignment because all of them are LOCKED!The TAs are harsh and inconsiderate with grading. Take something else!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hated this class so much, if you hate writing/literature, don't even take this class, it'll make you hate it 10 times more. Pointless readings with objectives that aren't well explained, assignments declined for rubrics that don't really tell you what to do anyways. Just really unenjoyable.

Imma give yall a no bs review. Didn't watch all the lectures, read everything, no TA/Prof OH.

Good: all online, readings are mostly interesting, grading is pretty lenient (especially on resubmit), concepts and assignments are pretty easy

Bad: The grading system forces you to stay on track. Assignment grading turnaround is slow. CRIT is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is reasonable if you complete all assignments on time. 9 modules that take 4-5ish hours each, but it takes 2 days to grade which means you do less work than you'd expect. However, it's stressful if you fall behind or have to get an assignment regraded. As long as you don't fall behind this class is a completion grade.

The course structure is unreasonable.  The professor does not care to teach you the entire course.  You have to score perfect in each module before you can move forward.  You will not finish the course because a module could take 2 weeks to grade, make corrections, and regrade.T  Take another course that is worth your time and money.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SUMMER! It was very frustrating, especially for students who also have other commitments, like other classes or jobs, which the professor called out in a very passive-aggressive tone. The grading was very slow and it took longer than the advertised 1-2 days, and many times, the assignments would have to be redone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've never left bad reviews on RMP, but this was the most demotivating class I've taken at UT. I spent several hours working on reading journals and annotating readings. But my journals were sent back anyways. Feedback mostly nitpicked my answers' organization into their "CRIT" style rather than correcting content of responses themselves. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer, which was a lot more complicated than it should've been. The TAs take a long time to grade journals, leading to you falling behind, especially if you need them to regrade them. Readings and lectures are very lengthy, so if you are taking this class with any other classes or jobs, expect to have a heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The structure of this course, as a summer class, is rigorous to the point where it's stress-inducing. Very lengthy journals. Grading takes a very long time (>2 days). You can try to stay ahead & turn assignments in early, but the stressful part is if you pass to "unlock" the next module, and if you don't, expect another 2 days after you resubmit.

Do not take this professor under any circumstance. She does not clearly communicate the timing and goals required for the class and when asked to make reasonable adjustments to rectify issues, she immediately hid behind "you signed an agreement." A lot of people in the class are getting way worse grades they otherwise would because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You have to wait 4 days to move on to the next module because your TA takes forever to grade your assignment and if you make any errors or your TA is moody you're on that module for a week. Time flies in a half-summer session class. Feedback should not take 3+ days, especially if you need it to advance.

This is class is a joke. The grading, the set up of the class, and how long it takes to grade the assignments. I'm taking this class right now. ITS HORRIBLE!!! The teacher locks each module until you get a perfect score on all the assignments in the module before. The TA's are a joke and take three days to grade one assignment. so ducking stupid.

Structure is incredibly difficult and for no reason at all. You level up your grade as you move forward with the modules but the next module will remain locked until the TA grades your previous one (and they take ages to grade it). WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TAKING IT IN THE SUMMER unless you want to ruin your gpa over an English class.

Took during summer, tons of tedious work. Grade comprised of 8 modules and 1 essay/project. In each module, there are 3-6 long readings, one reading journal assignment, and a discussion post (post 2 questions & 1 reply). All work is completion-based, but they do check for quality before letting you move to next module. Its really excessive work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very unnecessarily time consuming course, lectures are incredibly boring
I never met Professor Cdebaca-Cruz, but my TA was great. You only meet once a week, and everything is self-paced each week. Easy A!
Tough grader and get ready to read multiple books. She is very sweet and easy to talk to but her grading is tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is based on how many modules you complete. Each module is extremely time consuming since you have to annotate multiple pieces of literature, watch hours worth of lectures, and then complete a writing assignment. The grading criteria was very unclear and my TA made it more difficult then it needed to be. Also, didn't learn a single thing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: look I had an amazing TA so my experience was not that bad, so it just depend on your ta. work was easy but it is a lottery on who you get. You never see the professor besides the recorded lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this course for the HUM credit. The course grade is based on 10 essays/writing assignments(ik that doesn't seem like much), but the grading criteria are random based on the TA that you get (most of the TAs are really harder graders). The assignments are based on a lot of reading assignments. This course is an extreme waste of time.

This course seems to be a hit-or-miss, as your experience depends heavily on the TA you get. Unfortunately, I had a subpar TA and barely got an A. The professor's lectures were incredibly monotonous. I would not recommend it for the HUM credit. Take pinto instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is completion based. Finish all nine modules? Cool you get an A. Finish just 5? That's fine you still pass. It is key to complete the modules by the suggested due date, otherwise, you get stuck in a hole that you keep trying to dig out of. My TA was kind and on time with her grading so I can't attest to other reviews about TAs.

Extremely easy class. Self-paced and no deadlines until the end (I did almost the entire course in the last week of classes). However, modules are only unlocked once your TA grades the last one, so you need to plan around that. Journals are graded very easily and you basically just write whatever you want to pass. Grade is based on completion.
She makes her lower-division writing class feel like an upper-division writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A few hours of pre-recorded lectures each week & 9 Journal assignments due. Grade is completely dependent on TA. If they don't grade on time, you can't even move on to the next assignment. Pretty time-consuming course and didn't even really learn. Avg class that's frustrating at times due to the poor quality of learning and time-consuming nature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is definitely dependent on your TA's. If you do each module for each week - you'll finish with an A. It is COMPLETELY up to you though. You have to use your time wisely because this course is asynchronous. You have journals due each week and thats it. No tests. No quizzes. Just do readings and follow the prompts and you'll do great!

Your entire experience will be based on your TA. Such a waste of tuition money just watching prerecorded lectures when this credit can easily be obtained at a community college or by taking a credit-by-exam. TA never responds to emails and both TA and professor were very unaccommodating. Not worth all the time, stress, and lack of guidance

Take British/World Lit instead. depending on the TA, it takes forever to complete modules bc they are so picky when it comes to grading. The lectures weren't very engaging and there was A LOT of reading. Keep in mind its hard to stay on track bc this is a self paced course. Just take something else if you need this for the core curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would highly suggest finding a different class for this unless you're a really strong writer. I think there were FAR too many readings for each journal and the journal questions could be really confusing even after watching the lectures. It's so easy to get behind and was really overwhelming when I didn't understand a journal prompt.

The TA Jenny is a horrible grader. It takes weeks to complete a module because she grades so insanely hard and you have to get a perfect 100% before moving onto the next module. She makes critiques on writing when your writing literally has what she says is missing. The class is just terribly structured as well and professor/TA sucks. STAY AWAY!

I didn't have much direct contact with Dr. CdeBaca-Cruz, but the texts she assigned changed my way to see American history. I learned so much and ended up buying some of the books. Her grading criteria is fair (completion rather than numerical grades). Great class to take over Summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Definitely take this class over the summer. The workload was definitely manageable and I still learned a lot. The grading criteria is interesting but you have two do-overs if you miss an assignment so you can still stay on track for your grade goal. Dr. C really does care about the students in her classes!

Took her english class online this summer and the grading rubric is weird. There are specifics you do to get an A, B, C, etc. It's actually pretty doable to get an A - the way your journals get graded is all on your TA. Mine was dope and super understanding so I did fine her name was Megha I think
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. C was very informative in her lectures and the material she covered was always interesting. However, would not recommend taking this course in the summer if you really don't have a lot of time to dedicate to it. There were a lot of assignments per week and tons of reading. Great professor, but grading relies solely on TA's. Follow journal tips!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class at all. The grading system is heavily dependent on your TA, which makes it difficult to succeed for many. It's def possible to scrap by without doing all the readings and watching all the lectures but the extra stress that this brings for the journals might not be worth it. Try taking with a diff prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want an A you need to follow the grading criteria given at the beginning of the class. There is a lot of reading but they help with all of the assignments (journals, lecture instapolls, annotations). Some reviews say that your grade heavily depends on your TA so be weary. Jaya was a great TA who gave solid advice and returned grades quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Journals are graded as either complete or incomplete,If you want to get an A follow the journal tips provided in the first week of class . Actually take the time to invest in her lectures as they help with your thinking process and make the journal questions much easier.Personally my TA Jumi Kim was amazing and provided awesome feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor CdeBaca-Cruz does an amazing job lecturing and going over the texts thoroughly which helps you interpret them better. There's lots of readings - if you follow her calendar guide to balance out your time management you will exceed in this class! She provides tips on her syllabus for what you need to do based on your ideal letter grade!

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a fantastic lecturer; however, your success in the class is based almost entirely on which TA you get, and some of them are literal spawns of satan. Professor C's lectures are informative, but your grade lies entirely in the hands of either an incredibly lenient TA or one of the most ambiguous/strict TA's you'll have in a class. You can literally write a masterpiece essay for a journal prompt that has a few questions and receive no credit.

reviews.comment: Prof CdeBaca and her TAs have been great for this E316M summer course. Just a reminder-- most people who leave reviews on RMP are bitter because they aren't doing well. Prof and TAs are lenient and helpful. You just have to want an A and put in the time/effort to get there. Very chill course-- definitely recommend it for a summer class.

reviews.comment: Every assignment is either a complete or incomplete and if you get an incomplete on just two of the weekly assignments you automatically get a B. These weekly assignments are also graded super harshly - if you miss a single thing or don't do it well enough you automatically get an incomplete on it. Try and take this course with another prof.

reviews.comment: By far the WORST class I have ever taken. The grading system is so stupid that if you miss even one minor assignment, your grade drops from an A directly to a B. The weekly journals are also graded ridiculously hard. Save your grade and avoid this Professor and course at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would say that this class can be an easy A if you have a lenient TA. If you have a TA that is not so lenient, you can kiss your A goodbye. The journals are either "complete" or "incomplete" and the rest of the grading is weird. It's very possible to get an A though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has as a very WEIRD grading system. There is only Complete or incomplete for assignments, so even if you get one thing wrong on a journal instead of getting say an 80 you are given an incomplete. A few more of these mistakes and you grade can drop from an A to a D in instant.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had the WEIRDEST way of grading. You could do perfect all semester but if you mess up on the last project you get a B or C. Discussions were mandatory and painfully boring. Overall easy class, you don't need to read everything. Grade is slightly dependent on who your TA is but if you put in a little effort you'll easily get an A.

Dr. C was fine. The class had a ton of readings, and most of them were kind of hard to follow at times. Her lectures were very drawn out and not as engaging as one would hope for. Weekly required discussion sections with our TA's did help a lot though in terms of understanding what was going on.

Absolutely take American Lit with Dr. CdeBaca-Cruz. The course itself is pretty easy, with a few readings per week and a reading journal at the end of the week. One or two essays throughout the semester, but you work on them and the reading journals during discussion groups. Even though this class is "American" literature, the readings are diverse.

Readings assigned each week with "Reading Journals" asking about the readings at the end of the week. Major grades from Midterm exam and Final Project. Discussion sections were meh. Didn't pay much attention in class, but if you paid attention, this is an easy A. CdeBaca is a good teacher and very responsive with comments and emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: 2-3 readings assigned each week. "reading journals" asking about the readings at the end of the week. I honestly did not read the stories and just used summaries. No other assignments, only one easy final project at the end that took me about a week. Discussions every week which kinda sucked. Easy A tho. U can tell she is passionate abt the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I can't express enough how much I loved this class! Professor CdeBaca is awesome and really cares about her students' learning. I usually am not an english person but this course was so engaging and transformational for me. Prof CdeBaca is so sweet and understanding, and even omitted some texts that put too much of a workload on us.

Professor CdeBaca is so sweet! She is probably the most understanding and accommodating teacher I've had this semester, which I appreciate. Lots of required readings for this class. Online, it wasn't very engaging, but the TA's make discussion pretty interesting! She's very intelligent and passionate about literature. Overall, a great person & prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: As an engineering major, this wasn't a dreadful class like other ratings. I was easily able to manage the weekly writings (200-300) words and the midterm and final project. There are a lot of readings, but they ALL aren't mandatory, you can read the some of it and make it through, which the majority do. The class mainly teaches you how to analyze
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. CdeBaca is a nice lady and is clearly very knowledgeable in her field, however, if you're like me and hate history, this course is basically another history class. This is probably what the class entails and it is not her fault that she must teach this, but she is not engaging at all. Any free time you have will go to reading for her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a good teacher, but the readings she gives will take up most of your free time. However, when it comes to grading assignments, the TA's come in, and oh boy, have fun trying to decipher the meaning behind your grade because you can put the same effort into two assignments and get entirely different grades. The rubrics are also a complete joke

Dr. C is a very nice woman however, she gives extremely long readings. You can expect about 2-3 long readings every night. Comprehension is impossible and her lectures are given through a live stream for Spring '21 so we can only ask questions through chat which aren't always answered. She goes into depth about the topics VERY early on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was the second class I took with Dr. Salgado, and it was MUCH more challenging than the first, but he's still his funny, engaging self. You're reading long primary documents written in 17th century spanish as homework, which was very frustrating, but ultimately it was a history class and massively improved my reading comprehension.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the best lecturer I've had so far. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about the course, and it shows. He's pretty funny, very understanding of deadlines, and is just a caring person in general. Some of the readings can be very lengthy, but the syllabus lets you know what you'll be reading ahead of time, so you can plan for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Visualizing Cuba with him and he was great. You can tell he really cares about the topic and is very knowledgeable. He tended to go off on tangents sometimes, but they were always related to the lecture and interesting regardless. Spoke to him a couple of times outside of class as well and he was very warm and pleasant to be around always.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment:
Amazing professor, eye-opening lectures, feedback, and readings. Love his side comments. Understanding on deadlines. 
Heavy readings, and he could improve assignment expectations. 
There's also room for more discussions with students in class. He'd often let you speak for about 3 seconds, and that's all your time to form up a thought, in Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although the material was fascinating in itself, I wish it was taught that way. Professor Salgado moves quickly through the lectures, making it easy to miss many crucial points. We constantly fell behind schedule, which made it harder to complete assignments, and yet he still took longer to grade the assignments than it did to complete them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is definitely difficult if you aren't fluent because he speaks very fast and expects you to participate regularly however he is very understanding of his students struggles to communicate and grades very fairly on papers. Lectures are interesting and combine art, history, politics and literature and his passion for teaching is very clear.

Prof. Salgado is a very nice man and if you put in the work, you'll probably get an A. That being said, the amount of work was insane at times- like reading an entire book (in Spanish) and watching a documentary and answering questions about it, all in the same week. You can get by without doing all of it but be prepared to get cold called in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Salgado is very understanding and accommodating. The Puerto Rico capstone course is challenging but his passion makes it worthwhile. Grading criteria is somewhat unclear, and he takes a long time to get assignments back. Class goes 5 min over the bell. As long as you participate, improve, and put in effort outside of class you will likely be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting, funny, albeit a little disorganized lecturer. Synthesized art, politics, and history tactfully. It was impossible to take notes, but I found that I didn't really need to anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of reading in this UGS, especially in the early stages of the class. However, a lot of the lectures are excellent, and there is lots of room for interaction. Professor Salgado is clearly invested in what he teaches, and that enthusiasm comes across. He puts lots of effort into his teaching and grading, which was helpful despite its rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Cuban Revolution through Film and Narrative with Professor Salgado and it's one of my favorite courses. Salgado was knowledgeable, gave incredible and engaging lectures, and chose material that was thought provoking. I felt that Salgado truly cared about me as a student and I can tell that my reading, writing and speaking has improved!

Avoid this class as your seminar because this was much harder than any UGS class should be. He is passionate about the subject and caring for students but gives unrealistic homework expectations. Grades are tough and mainly based on papers, and he doesn't release grades until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Visualizing Cuba. If you want to learn and understand more about Cuba beyond the skewed view given in your typical history class, I definitely recommend this class, it taught me a lot. I loved the readings and I believe the assignments were very reasonable and interesting. The only thing I struggled with was the 10-12 page final.

Professor Salgado is a decent professor, but for a freshman seminar class (Visualizing Cuba), this was a LOT of work. You have three papers to write (all of which are at least three pages at the minimum). Lastly, for your final paper, its about 10-12 pages long. He does take off points on things based on his opinion, so it's very hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesor Salgado is a good profesor but do not and I repeat do not take this class unless youre virtually fluent. He speaks extremely quickly and picks people randomly to answer questions. Hes a good professor dont get me wrong, but I had to drop the class because he was so incredibly difficult to understand.

Professor Salgado is super passionate about what he teaches. He provides all the reading material and is really understanding if you have a any sort of problem. He really cares about his students. He has a tendency to keep talking after the bell, but it just shows how passionate he is about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I liked Prof Salgado a lot!! He is very passionate about Latin American history/literature and his lectures are pretty interesting. The only grades are four essays 3-5 pages each, but he grades them easily. Only thing that's annoying is he will keep talking even after the bell has rung, but other than that he's a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The single worst professor I have had in my two years at U.T  His lectures are not lectures---he just stands up and rambles on any topic, not neccesarily one dealing with the course subject. Expect any questions  you have to be ignored and class to always run up to thirty minutes late. Avoid at any cost.

Took this class as a summer course, so the amount of daily homework required was a bit overwhelming at times, but that's to be expected for an online class over the summer. Overall, this professor was SO sweet and replied quickly if you sent her an email. Her energy and enthusiasm made taking this class over the summer bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Celina is very energetic and relies a lot on your participation in class. I believe the more your participation, the better your homework gets graded. But she is quite picky on grading so the smallest mistakes take you to a 90. She is understanding however if you talk to her outside of class. She's a little slow with anything online though.

Took her for SPN 314. Dreaded showing up to this class everyday. The class wasn't super hard, but it was a lot of work. She seemed annoyed anytime you would ask her a question. Didn't have clear grading criteria. Would always give me lower marks for participation based on my vibe. She told me this during her office hours, btw. Kinda cray.

She just isn't a good teacher. She barely knows how to explain the material and gets defensive when people try to communicate with her about it. She was very disorganized most of the time and would make us confused about the due dates for assignments. She is generally a nice person, but if you want to save your GPA, don't take her.

Do not recommend. Made going to class unbearable and would call out students in front of everyone over something trivial and students weren't doing anything wrong. Concepts are bearable. Expect daily homework and pop quizzes. Would also write to-do list for next class instead of posting on canvas so if you missed class, you're out of luck

I actually had her for 314 and she was amazing! She focuses the whole class on getting you to feel comfortable speaking in Spanish, even if you have some grammatical errors. Class was very laid back, and she is so kind!! You do readings outside of class and just talk in class!!

Poor organization and communication skills. Never clear when/what was due, textbook was expensive and bad, and the Canvas page was a nightmare to use. Certainly kind, but difficult to work with, unreceptive to feedback, and lacking in some much-needed tech skills.

At first I thought she was a bit overbearing but honestly as I got to know her I realized shes hilarious, literally such a character. The homework she gives out is easy and very helpful. I love her to death. Highly recommend!

Sometimes I thought the class was a bit of a mess, but it wasn't too disruptive to class time. There was some king of HW due before almost every class, but I thought it was short and simple. Attendance is not "mandatory" but it is important that you participate to get extra points on the exams (and she will write down who was in class).

Profesora Nevarez was one of the sweetest professors ever, really cares about her students and gives off a motherly and caring vibe. Typical 2-3 assignments due everyday before class (thanks UT spanish department) but she grades very fairly and takes time to help peoples confusion in class. Very energetic and eager to teach.

Celina is super sweet! If anything was confusing she always was available for help in and outside of class. Everyone talks about how hard spanish is at UT but I feel like I learned a lot and also got good grades (im set for a A- or an A can't tell which one yet). You definitely have to put in effort but it wasn't too bad overall !!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was NOT an easy A: there were plenty of quizzes and assignments, 3 tests, and a final exam. But, the professor provides a positive environment that makes it fun to expand one's knowledge. Office hours are very helpful and she provides countless resources on canvas. It was great, I have never learned so much in a Spanish class before!

This class was absolute fire and torment. If you are not a Spanish speaker or have previous experience speaking Spanish, DO NOT take Spanish at UT. Ive had nearly three mental breakdowns already. Celina is a tough grader and takes points off for he smallest things. Pray for me.

I really enjoyed taking Professor Nevarez's class! She was an amazing instructor and provided each student with great feedback about their progress. She does speak a lot in Spanish (but not in the first weeks) but will usually translate what she says in English, too. I thought the grading was fair as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very friendly and accompanying during lecture. Has a great attitude and offers substantial extra practice for trickier grammatical concepts outside of class. Quizzes are frequent at times, but she tends to grade assignments very lightly, especially toward the latter half of the semester.
so charismatic and caring, is genuinely interested in students and very eager to help
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Celina has easily been one of my favorite professors at UT! She is caring, sweet, loves her job, and knows what she's doing. If you took Spanish in high school this class will be a piece of cake. If not, Celina makes sure she does everything possible to help you. I cannot emphasize what a great person and professor she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Nevarez is great. She helps students learn everything in class. Especially if you already have taken Spanish in high school, this class will be a breeze. She helps a lot if you don't feel comfortable with the material. Overall great professor. The exams are exactly like the reviews. There is homework every day but its a completion grade

Professor Nevarez is Hilarious, kind, and determined to see you succeed. This is a Spanish class which means there will obviously be a lot of HW (every night) because you are learning a new language. 3 Tests and a Cumulative final exam. Always study your vocabulary! Nevarez is funny and makes class fun, she is also super sweet. TAKE HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Ciszek was great and so understanding. You get out what you put into this class. Would def take ciszek again if i had the opportunity

It is an easy A with online exams. However, Dr. Ciszek reads off of a script while teaching, and doesn't write their notes on the lecture slides. Instead, you have to rush writing, hopefully without missing anything they say. In addition, class ends at 6:20 on Thursday instead of 6:15 as they start 5 minutes late due to chatting with students.

Not much for this class. Assignments in first half of class are super easy, then go on to campaign critiques. Mandatory attendance for the one lecture a week, one free absence.Four quizzes online throughout the semester, however the cache is that lectures are so boring. Videos are showing during lecture to use up more time, and awkward pauses.

Ciszek is super chill, lectures were very interesting. Attendance is mandatory for the 1 class a week, There is an online lecture video each week outside of class, one assignment or discussion board that doesn't take too long, and there are 4 quizzes total. Very easy. Usually goes 5-10 min over class time, and randomly calls on people in lectures.
Was so approachable and lectures were genuinely interesting! One class once a week and no tests, just quizzes on Canvas and weekly assignments. So easy and great content

This class is honestly really easy. You only meet once a week, have one assignment a week, and a few open note tests. Ciszek is very kind, caring, and passionate, and really likes participation in class. Overall liked it a lot more than I thought I would, probably just because of the prof!
I loved Law and ethics with Dr. Ciszek this semester! They are hilarious but the lectures also really made me think and I feel like I learned a lot.

Super cool professor; made lectures very fun. This class is pretty easy. The tests are open book and there is not a lot of homework. Like one assignment each week. Yeah overall this class is a pretty easy A and Ciszek is cool. So take this class.

Erica is amazing!!! If you have the opportunity to take this class TAKE IT!!! Workload is fair, a few tests and discussion type assignments. She is such a funny professor, and makes the lectures so enjoyable. She is very interactive and truly cares about her students, I wish I could take another class of hers.

LOVE Cizek! They're my favorite professor and I wish I could take a class with them every semester. They make it really easy for you to engage in class without it feeling intrusive. Most of the work is easy, but they're relevant assignments that develop skills you will use in the field. They are easy to talk to and always open to hear your thoughts

Professor Ciszek is the best professor I've had yet. They are so funny and caring and their lectures are interesting. They talk about relevant topics. There is consistent homework each week but its super straightforward and easy. The tests are easy as well and are similar to the powerpoint lectures. If you pay attention, you will pass.

Dr. Ciszek was an amazing professor. The assignments were very easy, and the one large assignment was so easy. I actually enjoyed lectures and they made this class actually interesting. They didn't make attendance mandatory, but I recommend watching/going because they were interesting.

As a requirement for the advertising major at UT, this is definitely one of the easiest required courses. Their class consists of weekly daily assignments, four "quizzes" (they are weighted the same as tests so not really a quiz), and towards the end of the semester "campaign critiques." Really long readings but they drop your lowest quiz score.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Ciszek one of the most accommodating and best structured online courses I've had during COVID-19. The modules were organized and all the feedback on assignments was useful. Lots of weekly assignments but nothing too difficult, fun lectures too :)

Ciszek is an absolute light. Her personality made lectures very engaging and she was always prepared. She does cover a lot of information but she always posts the slides on Canvas with notes of what she covered during each slide. This class is an easy A as long as you attend class (which is required) and review before each test.

Love love LOVE Dr. Ciszek! Very easy material and tests. She makes it very  comfortable to speak in front of the class and makes lectures fun. Participation matters. Do not buy the textbook. Did minimal effort and got an A. Take her!

Erica is genuinely one of my favorite professors. I was nervous for this class but she is honestly so great. She acknowledges that some tests are made to difficult so her tests are very straightforward and easy if you pay attention. Her lectures are incredibly interesting and quite entertaining. She is very personable and sweet. I recommend her.

Dr. Ciszek was amazing! She is so funny and makes lectures feel like a conversation rather than lecture. She tells you what's on her exams, post her power points online so you can actually enjoy and listen to her lectures, and her exams aren't too hard if you study. Attendance required, but you'd want to be there anyway. Take her!

Best professor I've had, hands down. Not only did she invest in us as individuals and have the ability to recall details about past conversations, but she made what could be a very boring class the only one I looked forward to this semester. She cares way more about the personal discovery and understanding of law & ethics than facts we'll forget.

I absolutely love Ciszek. I was dreading taking this class but she made it very interesting and fun. I would take any class with her in a heartbeat. You can tell that she really cares about what she teaches. She puts students' learning at utmost importance and not just grades. She's genuine, hilarious, and an amazing teacher. So glad she came to UT

Amazing teacher! Very engaging. Asks lots of questions and encourages class discussion. We had many adv and pr professionals speak about ethics in the field. She posts the powerpoints online but takes attendance every class.

So sweet, but the tests, which there are only 2 that equal 25% of ur grade, are nothing from what we learn. i had a 100% in all the categories in the class, like HW, oral, and participation, but bc of the tests, i got by with an A-. Seriously, the tests are just impossible to study for and basically completel yrandom grammar she never taught us

sweet lady, but very disorganized and poor communicator. didn't grade assignments until the last 2 weeks. class itself is not too hard, but there's no structure, and it gets u for tests. all semester we just yap in class, and then for our 2 tests worth 25% of our grade it's absolutely nothing like what we learned. tests r complete 180
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her class. I took it last year and she was genuinely one of the worst professors I have ever had. So much homework and it never gets graded. Had a C for 3+ months in the semester, only because she did not grade 10+ assignments. Then, at the end of the semester, my grade finally moved up to an A when she graded everything. Worst class.

one of the sweetest professors, please take her!! participation is required but we had rly interesting discussions in class and Prof. Cifuentes-Ramirez was very encouraging and patient so don't be afraid to make mistakes in spanish :) other grades are the HWs, exams, speaking assignments, and group presentations but it is very doable to get an A

She is a really caring professor and she made Spanish easy to learn. The class was hard with a lot of homework but that's the Spanish department's fault, not hers. Exams online. If you have to take Spanish at UT I would highly recommend her! She is super nice and wants to help you learn. She is funny and builds positive relationships with students.

Amazing professor who cares deeply about learning the material and preparing for the next class rather than just getting an A in his class. Some of the content is more challenging than other M 408D classes but I didn't find it to be too difficult. Make sure to take advantage of Quest practice problems to prepare for the tests. Happiness!

Lectures are unclear on what to do and canvas is unorganized with no recorded lectures, only old notes that have information that don't apply anymore. Professor makes jokes frequently in class but doesn't focus much on his actual teaching duties other than showing unclear examples with nothing to base it off of. Exams are too close to each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cepparo the goat. Shows up to class every day with a smile and great energy, even at 8am. Very good at explaining new concepts, and walks us through several examples to get them down. Makes lectures very engaging with great sense of humor. Always happy to help, no matter how busy. Discussions are just review with no quizzes, so you can skip those.

Cepparo knows the content well and actually cares for his students. If you want to do well I would suggest going to the TA lecture as it is a little slower and provides more examples. Quest is the move and gives you the test on a silver platter, homework is tedious (esp. textbook) but helps in understanding. His lectures can be overwhelming though.

He's a funny teacher and makes the 8 a.m's a bit more bearable. However, I personally found his method of explanation hard to understand as he uses references that just didn't click with me. Also, toward the end of the semester he teaches content that's different from other 408D teachers that's a large chunk of your final. Still a good teacher.
Cepparo is such a funny and kind professor and his lectures are super thorough. Tests are super reasonable, just show up to class and do the hw! Def take him for M408D

Gustavo is an amazing prof. and wants you to succeed! He makes class fun by telling stories/jokes. Exam content is mainly from class topics, so be sure to attend/watch - don't just use the book. Office hours are helpful, especially if you ask him what kind of Qs will be on exams, he will tell you. If you show up and do the work, you will do well.

He's an excellent lecturer and a genuinely kind person who even remembers my name. The homework load is standard for the math department—after all, math requires practice. The exams are a bit challenging but entirely manageable.

8 AMs are rough, but Prof Cepparo made it worth it! He does a good job explaining tough concepts and is open to questions and feedback. There is regular (basically weekly) hw, so don't fall behind! Also tests are back to back (e.g. test 2 on Friday and test 3 the following Monday) so you really have to make sure you know your stuff. Def take him!

Literally the best 408D professor. Exams are light, lectures are funny and you actually learn stuff, he cares about his students and loves cracking jokes with students if you visit his office hours. 10/10

The class lectures were always recorded so you don't have to go to class as long as you keep up with the lectures. The exams are also 30% online and 70% in person. There are 5 exams and 1 final that is worth 78% of the grade. The rest is homework on quest and textbook problems. The exams are mostly from quest so just practice that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS PROF! He is so funny and great at explaining lectures. He makes learning calc 2 entertaining, however he can go fast sometimes. Calc 2 is already a hard topic to take but he ensures you know how to identify and do it on the exams. His exams are made from the quests and frq from his lecures sooo... take that as you will.

Sweetest professor I've ever met. His lectures are super intuitive and easy to follow. His on-paper homework(as opposed to his quest homework) was a bit lengthy, but really helped prepare you for the tests(which aren't complex or difficult at all if you do the work). The only issue I ran into was that the class was at 8 a.m., so i slept in a lot.

my boy gus is SO FUNNY! seriously, he is so kind and hilarious and always has these wacky analogies to make math interesting. however, this class is SO HARD! the content is extremely difficult if you're not super confident in calc 1 and moves insanely fast. also, there is insane amounts of homework and even more tests (6 total). it's a lot of work.

Ceparro is such an amazing professor! His lectures were hilarious and actually motivated me to go to class. I felt his tests were incredibly fair and similar to the Quest homeworks. Definitely go to discussion sections (I had an amazing TA) and study for the tests. Take him for Calc 2!!

Prof Cepparo is so nice and funny. Genuinely cares about his students in/out of class. There is alot of homework but doing them helps with the exams. No attendance grade, but no lectures are posted online, so show up to class. It's been a year since I took his class, but I still see him and catch up with him.

Dr. Cepparo is an incredible mathematician and teacher. There is a reason why students love him. He is highly accessible outside of class during office hours, which are once a week and nearly four hours long, so there's no excuse not to get help from him. If you commit your time and energy to this class, you will learn calculus deeply.
I've had him twice and cannot recommended him enough. brilliant person and professor and funniest man at UT

This guy was the funniest professor I have ever had. He makes having calc at 8:00 AM not suck. He's good at capturing people's attention by making jokes about the problems. The only weird thing is that there are back to back tests on the same topics. Overall, great class, would def recommend this professor.

Prof. Cepparo was always very funny and engaging during his lectures, he cares about his students and makes his lectures fun to go to. The lectures and material might not be super clear, but you'll be fine. Definitely better than some of the other M408D prof. 5 tests & one final w 30% of grade online (curve) and 70% in person (2 frq & abt 8 mc)

Cepparo is one of the nicest professors at UT, but he severely lacks the ability to teach. The class consists of him doing a proof of why a technique works, and then moving on to the next topic. Professor Leonard is the only reason I succeeded in this class. If you are familiar with Calc 2, this will be fairly easy for you.
He makes already easy material nearly impossible to receive below an A.  Take him for M408D.

Cepparo is a really great teacher, he very early on tells you what to expect. It was five midterms, with the second and third being on the same concepts, same with fourth and fifth. The topics are hard, but he explains it in a pretty good way. Weekly homework, one written and one on quest. Study quest for exams since many questions are similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cepparo is an amazing professor. Highly recommend.

Professor Cepparo is an amazing professor! The course isn't easy but you'll be ok as you attend lectures and go to office hours when you need help. Cepparo is super easy to get in touch with for any questions, concerns, or have a conversation with. He will always greet you with a smile and radiates positivity.

Professor Cepparo is an excellent professor he is engaging and funny. Lots of homework. The quest/written are difficult. However, half of the tests are online and the other half are in person. Those are really the only grades that you will receive. No quizzes and If you pay attention in the lectures you should be able to get an A in the class.

LOVE gustavo! Such a good professor with clear guidelines on what you need to get an A. Five midterms (12% each) + one final (16%) + homework. Replaces the lowest midterm with final. Although it is test-heavy, midterms 2 and 3 are over the same concepts, and same with midterms 4 and 5. DO QUEST because they are super similar to exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches concepts really well, but if you zone out or miss class, you'll be completely lost.  He also engages with students during office hours and applies a 35 point curve on exams.  He's also hilarious and the source of many funny (and sometimes unhinged) stories and "Cepparisms."

I never rmp so be warned. Cepparo is very difficult to get in touch with. He will ignore your emails. My friend died, my mom was in the hospital, and my car kept giving out trying to get to class and could've died. He's "nice", but he could've helped me. He didn't and now I have to spend more money to move on, which I don't have. For 2 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Happiness with that? ok ok perfect! No but seriously he is amazing, really hard homework but I kinda liked it, it improves my mathematical maturity. Test is extremely easy so getting an A is easy. The class was a highlight of my first semester and made me feel that I'm good at something for once.

Very good teacher. This guy was so nice, and despite only going to class for the exams (classes were recorded), he always addressed me by name. He was a funny guy and his notes were always well organized and accessible.
Cepparo was amazing. I love his little phrases and was super super funny. Tests were EXTREMELY easy for the course content and overall was an amazing course.

Dr. Cepparo was a funny and engaging professor that made 8:00AM classes worth going to. Although attendance is not mandatory, he doesn't record lectures so it's important to go to classes to not miss any important information. The class is based around textbook homework and simple quest problems. If you put in the effort, an A is easily attainable.

He's a funny and caring professor. I found his lectures slightly confusing, but he's a much better alternative to most M408D professors. I struggled with 9 am lectures, and there's a lot of Quest and written HW. The written HW was difficult, but tests were based on Quest and also had a take-home portion, so it's not too difficult to end with an A.

Great guy, very understanding and kind. Problem sets were not that hard and the exams were very fair (the review was super close to the exam). Grading is not too harsh and is generous with extra credit and partial credit. Attendance not mandatory but hes a good lecturer and you can learn a ton from going to class. Easy A/A-

Cepparo is genuinely an amazing professor, his tests are partially take-home and the content itself isn't hard. Definitely one of the best M408D professors you can have, the key to doing well on exams is quest review assignments, many test questions are pulled directly from there.

Great class and funny professor. 5 midterms, each 35% online and 65% in class. 1 question is written and everything else is multiple choice. Homeworks are quite long and take a bit of time, sometimes they are difficult. Tests are very easy, much easier than homework. No quizzes, and discussion sections are just for you to work on your homework.

His lectures are pretty helpful though sometimes confusing. I stopped going in the second half and was still able to keep up. He is so funny and really wants his students to do well. Each exam, even the final, had a take home open-note portion. His midterms were pretty easy too. Easy A if you put in the bare minimum amount of effort.

This man is the funniest professor I have had. He made going to an 8am enjoyable. He cares about his students and does try to know student's names. His tests aren't the worst, there is an online and in person portion. They are doable, but some of the integrals are a pain and it's all on Quest.

Cepparo is a fun and engaging professor, though the workload can be heavy. The lectures are worth attending, and using resources like Unstuck study alongside the textbook helps with the challenging homework. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to put in the effort.

I loved Cepparo's teaching style, though messy and not well organized, he still managed to explain most concepts well. There were many exams, both in-person and take-home, but the curves were life-saving for me. Weekly textbook and quest hw which was very time-consuming but doable. Lectures and discussions both have mandatory attendance.

Cepparo is a nice guy but not a great calc professor. His lessons often leave many confused about how to do the homework. But once you figure the homework out, the tests are extremely easy. Grades in the class are high but understanding is low. Two homeworks every week, written and quest, written is hard and not usually needed for tests.
Great lecturer and makes you want to come to class every day. Very friendly grading policies and always willing to answer questions or help out

He kept me engaged and want to learn despite his class being Calculus at 8 AM. His homeworks consist of quest problems and textbook problems, which can be challenging but is doable with office hours/TAs. The class is very organized. Prof Cepparo is also very hilarious. Definitely recommend him and would definitely take him again if I could!

Cepparo is the best professor I have had at UT. His teaching is so clear and he makes each lesson engaging. The content and tests can be hard, however he takes questions straight from quest, so using the reviews there really help. He is very generous with curves too, so if you bomb a couple in class tests, you can still get a decent grades.

Great professor for this course! He was so funny and kept the lectures very engaging. I liked how this course was structured: 5 exams with 35% online and 65% in class. Lots of homework but helped me learn the materials. The lectures are not recorded therefore you have to attend to get the notes but I did not mind. great professor and class.
Amazing lectures. Heavy testing.   Five midterms and a final.  Written homework and Quest.

Great lectures. Fast-paced but will answer any questions you have. Very nice and funny. 
Tests are directly based off UTQuest HW/lecture notes, and consist of an in-class part and take-home part. They are lighter than HW, but do not underestimate them. 
HW can be very hard, ESPECIALLY textbook HW - discussions/TXTBK reading helped a lot.

EASY with Calc BC experience. Quest: easy. Written HW: textbook q's, more difficult, but still easy to get 90-100. He started to assign fewer as the semester ended. Exams were easy-medium. All exams were based on Quest. 5 midterms 12% each. Each midterm: in person 10 q's (65%) and take home 6 q's 35%. Final exam was noncumulative.

He is by far one of my favorite professors here at UT. M329F could have been a difficult class, but he made it easy to understand through the examples shown in class. If you study well, and you do many practice problems from the textbook, and often go to his office hours, you are going to do well! He is very fun and enthusiastic! Amazing. 10/10

Really caring and enthusiastic professor, which is great considering his lectures are at 8 AMs. Gives out lots of HW and the written portion can be especially tedious, but it's weighted nicely and graded easily. Tests are purely from Quest, very easy to know the content/what to study. Awesome professor, just stock up on caffeine for 8 AM exams!

Outstanding professor-has interesting lectures and is good at explaining. There's a lot of homework in my opinion, but it really prepares you for the tests. Tests have a take-home portion and if you miss one problem you still get a 100, both of which make the tests less stressful.

Tests are MC and pretty easy and the in class portion is changed from 50% to 65% this year. The take home part is also MC and is worth 35%. Lectures mainly consist of practice problems and questions are taken throughout. Quest MC HW every week is pretty easy. The written HW is straight from the textbook and is a bit more difficult, but can be done.

Gustavo is clear, funny and caring.  The exams are fair and have a little extra credit.  One written homework and a Quest per week.  He is very helpful and patient during office hours. Nice comments about finance and inflation from South America.

He is such a caring, funny professor who really makes sure you learn the material. Tests are low-stress, with a pre-lude on Quest counting for 50% of your test grade and the other 50% of the test in person the next day. I really enjoyed that format. Tests are also much easier than homework.
