There is an expectation that you should be completing all the assigned readings but I'd say don't. Skim everything for a general idea of the text because it's a waste of time to do anything else. Beware of the family altar project. No rubric but they are picky!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, she is a smart professor. But, almost everyone this semester despised the way she treated the students. The reflection paper was graded extremely hard without a clear rubric and they took off points for not having page numbers. I have written 10+ essays at UT, and every professor clearly defines in the rubric what they are expecting.

Dr. Sturm is a very nice professor. You could tell she really enjoys teaching about anthropology, but learning modules were very very long and sometimes watching through lectures became a bit boring. Honestly, as long as you take good notes on the lectures and textbook (emphasis on textbook), you should do fine or okay on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite course and professor so far. Attending lectures, taking well-written notes, and communicating will get you through this class. Engaging lectures and topics. Very straightforward material and expectations with sources readily available. I hope to take more courses from Professor Strum in the future.

This class was eh. You just watch prerecorded lectures with occasional instapolls and assignments here and there. Your grade depended on three exams, all of which had a handful of questions that were very meticulous to the material learned. If you take EXTREMELY detailed notes the class would probably be easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just don't take any class with this professor. She sucks at communication and doesn't try to help anyone with the material. Would not recommend ever.

Doable, but look at alternatives if you can. The difficulty in this class is all over the place: participation grade is generally easy, the exams require some prep, and the altar project is harshly gradedno one scored over a 94 on that assignment. Really prep for exams to get an A. More about anthropological methods than culture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Sturm is a great lecturer, but the course is almost designed for students to fail. Miss a few questions in an exam and watch your grade sink a whole letter or two... No EC whatsoever. I felt as if the expectation was that students were either experts in the subject or spent days memorizing hundreds of textbook pages for a test. Upsetting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This course was very hard for me bc of the asynchronous part. Too many lectures and reading assignments that you have to do in order to prepare well enough for the exams. Each lecture took me ab 3-5 hours (with reading/notes) & every exam had 7-9 lectures. The time it took to complete the work was insane & bc of that, i leave an okay review: 5/10

I really loved Dr. Sturm and this class. The material is super interesting and the way she presented everything kept me very engaged. I looked forward to lecture. Even though this class was asynchronous she provided quick and thorough feedback. I appreciated her warmth, encouragement, and challenges. She rewards hard work and analytical thought!

This professor is boring. Her and her TA's grade way too harshly for an entry level class. Her lectures are too wordy and she talks a lot about things that are not covered on the exam. You have to read the textbook. This class is a waste of time, simply put.

This was one of the most interesting and engaging courses I've taken at UT, and Dr. Strum was a big part of that. She's charismatic, responsive, and actually cares about her students. I'm planning to take more courses with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class is amazing if you want to re-evaluate your world view. Watch the lectures and fill out the study guide for the test (posted before you even watch the first lecture) and youll get an easy A. No need to actually read the textbook, but searching for definitions and terms is helpful because the definitions you find on google wont be right.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I personally like Dr. Sturm a lot. You can tell she is very knowledgeable and cares a lot about what she's teaching. The class I took was self paced which I liked because you can pause and catch up on taking notes. I would suggesting making nice organized notes and reading the books (at least know the major parts) in order to make a good grade.

Class is boring. If you mess up on one assignment, prepare for your grade to drop a whole letter. This class is time consuming and a waste of time. I just took it for hours and this was a big mistake.

I don't even know where to begin. This class is way to hard for an online and extremely time consuming. All she does is lecture and it is SO hard to focus and even listen to what she's saying. I did not think I would end up with a D+... Take another anthropology class please.

Do not take this class. The professor and the TA's expect you to know everything there is to know about anthropology even though this is an entry course. On assignments, you get points taken off for every little thing. Lectures are ridiculously long and not too interesting. No, do not waste your money. The textbook is not necessary.
Dr. Sturm means well however her class is extremely long and very time consuming. Instapoll's for participation in LONG lectures. Test are on the harder side for sure. Self paced for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Standard pre-recorded lectures with instapolls, 3 mc exams. Nice prof who seems to genuinely want to teach. Textbook not necessary to do well. Drawback is no feedback on the family altar project and can't ask questions in-time with lectures. Some tests ?'s also worded weirdly.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Too hard for an online imo. It was interesting at times, but hard to pace. The exams were surprisingly hard, even after taking good notes. The fieldwork journal was also very annoying and time-consuming, and should not be brushed off. I would say to practice a lot using the WW Norton online testing system for exams. Prepare to work hard, and write.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While Circe has demonstrated that she is very well versed in anthropology, her class is simply unorganized and she goes off on many tangents that have little to do with the subject matter at hand. Her tests are full of fallacies, where there are multiple choice questions where there is not enough information provided. TAs grade sporadically. Shame
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretend you're an ANT major during lectures. The material for tests comes from like 70% lecture, 25% reading, 5% ethnography (which seems not worth reading but is an eye-opening work). The tests are easy with a few hard questions per test (the last test is harder). Treat the projects like they're worth a lot b/c they are; TAs will give As if u do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Strum makes it really hard to communicate with her. She has her TAs grade projects and assignments, but they grade hard. She also assigns really long readings that are barely mentioned on the exams.

Dr. Sturm has been one of the most influential professors of my college career. She really cares about her students and will set time aside to address any particular needs or questions you may have. Her lectures are all extremely interesting, and she is extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Take this course and you will walk out the better.

Dr. Sturm was by far one of my favorite professors at UT. I went into one of her more advanced Anthro classes with little/no prior Anthro knowledge, but Dr. Sturm took the time to help me understand and fall in love with Anthropology. I would suggest this course to anyone who wants to walk away from a class feeling like it meant something.

Dr. Sturm is clearly knowledgeable in her subject. But, she needs to explain things slower and more interestingly, keeping in mind that it's an online class and people can't reach her as easily. She tries to keep people in the loop by engaging in group chats and instapolls. The quizzes are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dull lectures, but you can't skip because there are two instapolls, which require you to pay attention to the information. One project and paper, and the tests are mostly pretty easy, although she puts questions about the plot of one of the extra required books on them, so you have to read unless you're okay with sacrificing a few questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This online class had two instapolls per lecture, which are essential points toward your grade, so skipping wasn't an option. The lectures, however, were lackluster, and completely opposite of what I thought the class would be like. Prof. Sturm is an interesting person though, and does show that she has experience in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A or A-, the lectures are a little boring but you should watch them for the exam (don't really need the textbook). The material is interesting though and she's pretty chill.

The class was not an easy A. Some of the test questions were just worded poorly. There are 3 tests, a project (graded harshly by TAs), and attendance grades. While some of the lectures were great it got repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sturm is one of the best professors I've had. I'm an anthro major, so I'm biased, but if you're looking for a professor who is eloquent, well read, and will open your mind up to the world, she is it. Her class is difficult and no walk in the park, but she makes it manageable. She is also always willing to meet outside of class or email.

I took this class online, the lecture not particularly informative, I feel like I haven't learned anything. You can get by without the readings and just make sure to do the study guide. The only reason you need to go is the insta polls. She just generally seems uncertain with her own work and can really waste time over explaining.

Wonderful class!! I took her online class and loved it. Lectures are very engaging and the readings she assigns are interesting. Her exams are very fair and she gives you a study guide. Participation matters but is easy to attain. She made me truly enjoy anthropology. Read the book but didnt find it that useful. An A is for sure manageable.

Professor Sturm is really nice and takes the time to explain vague concepts thoroughly which shows how genuinely interested she is in her field of work. There isn't too much work in the class right now and you basically only have to keep up with readings. Tests are manageable, but not as easy as you'd expect them to be. All multiple choice tests.

Circe Sturm is an overall good lecturer and cares about making sure your questions are answered. This class is an easy A as long as you understand the vocabulary. She doesn't tend to force particular examples for memorization. DO NOT TAKE THE ONLINE CLASS. Take her in person. There are too many kinks in the online class right now.
I'm an anthropology major, so I am partial. I loved the way Dr. Sturm presented the material for this course. You do have to read, but tests are easy and projects help buffer your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's fantastic. The year isn't over yet, but I'm confident I'll make an A. She's an awesome lecturerer. I recommend her to everyone for cultural anthropology. Her tests are straight-forward and easy to understand. She is never trying to trick you. If you go to lectures, read the books, and take notes you'll be fine.
Although there's a lot of participation I feel like this class really created a community for RTF majors and I'm thankful for this class:)
This is a great class if you love to write and be creative! This class 100% made me a better writer! Cindy is the NICEST women you will ever meet.

Ask questions anytime Cindy is super chill and is always available and gets back to you, I've never had a teacher/professor care this much about their students :) the work is super easy and fun and it really helped me for my future of wanting to be a writer especially TV writing if that interests you!

I promise you need to take this class! It's so fun and interesting! She's very helpful with all your work and always open for questions. She cares so much about all her students and if you just do your work which is pretty easy you will get an A. It's literally impossible to not unless you just don't do the work!

My class was hybrid, lectures with McCreery online and small discussion groups in person. In this situation, your TA will make or break this class for you no doubt. McCreery's lectures were good but Zoom didn't feel like the best method for this class, so I gained all my understanding from the discussions.

Cindy is a very nice person but there were many things that made the class frustrating. The class was disorganized and assignments could be confusing at times. I felt I was teaching myself most of the time and had to learn how to do something in the span of a week. Also, we don't know what our grades are two weeks before the end of the semester.

Cindy is one of the sweetest professors here at UT. She genuinely cares about you and is always available to talk or give advice. Sometimes her lectures got a little repetitive and drawn out, but shes still one of my favorite professors here at UT. Attendance is taken at every lecture, class was super manageable.
Fantastic teacher! Gave great advice and brought life experience and humor to the class. Do your work and get it done on time and you'll do great!

Lectures are unbelievably dry and suck the life out of the subject that is group theory. Pretty much follows the definition->theorem->proof cycle you would find in any old textbook, except in lecture form. Provides essentially 0 intuition and is pretty much all about deduction and symbolic manipulation. Exam problems sampled from homeworks.

Condescending professor. She was/is a mathematical prodigy without humbleness and this didn't translate to excellent teaching. HARSH grader on exams but HW's are always full credit with little feedback. I walked out of the class with a 100 on the final, an A, and a lot of resentment for making algebra not fun. Just save yourself and take Keel.

The HW is the exam with the caveat that she expects you to be perfect on the exams. Most of your grade comes from exams but she replaces one and also 2 out of the 11 HWs. Presentations of HW are a big part of this class so expect to present math. She is a phenomenal professor if you expect to take algebraic structures 2 with Sean.

Cons: 
She is the hardest grader I have ever had. She hand grades each test and will take off for any mistake. Can struggle to communicate to intro students, high homework grades give you a false sense of how you're doing
Pros: 
She cares about helping her students, easy to access, knows a lot about the subject, the homework grader grades nicely

Pros: a researcher, knows the subject well, cares about the subject.

Cons:
Not a good intro college-level prof,
Can take things personally,
Not a fan of straightforwardness,
All over the place during lecture,
Can misjudge if the student doesn't try to communicate well,
Not super understanding of student's individual background

This is the hardest course I've taken at UT. Homework is difficult and takes forever, but tests pretty much mirror them. Study early for the midterms/final because you will need to know dozens of theorems. The textbook helps more than the lectures in my opinion... Also, class participation is mandatory on Tuesdays. Still a solid choice for M 328K.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the worst but also not great. The homeworks were long and while the tests were based on them, she chooses the hardest/trickiest problems from each assignment, and it feels like there's not enough time to finish the exams. She's not a great lecturer; I just read the textbook or watched YT videos since I got nothing from her lectures.

Super knowledgeable & gives you everything you need to do well. Homework is difficult but exams are pulled from the homework so it's clear what you need to know for exams & exams are easy as a result. Lectures are really informative without being overly dense. Overall a really solid choice for number theory.

Dr. Ciperiani is a great professor to take M328K with because she knows the subject well and puts forth her best effort to teach. The class is relatively easy given that you put some amount of effort in, with weekly textbook homework assignments and exams with questions pulled from the homework. She also puts lecture notes online, which is a plus.

I'm someone who loves math but I hated this course. I had previously audited a calculus and found it quite easy but going to her class made things more confusing. she sometimes goes to class unprepared and doesn't know how to solve her own problems. I ended up teaching myself.
I tested out of this class, but decided to take it because Math is my major. She made everything I learned up to that point confusing and is the worst teacher I've ever had.

Textbook readings can be long. Quizzes were either very easy or very hard. You don't learn much Italian in the course; it's a regular course taught in 70% Italian. Very open to working with the class on what material is difficult and changing the course structure during the semester. Friendly professor, encourages participation.
Lang Truths, Myths, Mysteries was a very interesting class! We covered many different topics and had fun working together in class. Take this class for upper div LAH!

I actually took LAH 352E, Language Myths, Mysteries, and Truths. Great class. Work was straightforward. Class was mostly relaxed group discussion. Dr. Russi was great! Easy grader and class was really interesting. She was really funny and nice!
Very nice, knowledgeable and helpful. Not sure why some other students are whining. I had zero problems with her.

Awful professor. She's hysterical and confusing. Makes a fairly easy subject matter very difficult to understand. She also giggles when she gives you bad grades. I would never recommend her to anyone.
stronza... that says it all!
No Comments

She understood you're new to the software and will give critiques and guidance if you ask. She doesn't bite. Grades pretty easily just do the work. Class takes a lot of time outside of hybrid meetings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very straight-forward classes. Lectures are usually always the same - her giving a powerpoint presentation, with some relevant video clips every few slides. It gets a little boring but she gives you everything you need for the test. VERY friendly and answers all questions. The only thing I didn't like was that class got repetitive.

Great Professor!! Very Knowledgable!  Very fair, if something is unclear she does not penalize you for it. It's nice to hear about her personal experience in the fashion industry as she is very credible having years of experience in New York and owning her bridal shop in Austin. Makes class interesting with relevant fashion clips from youtube.

One of the worst lecturers I have had at UT, un-engaging. Copies her powerpoint slides from the book and read them to us while standing in the same place. Assigns 5 point assignments in class which are a total waste of time. Constantly asks the class inane questions of obvious definitions.

The professor was pretty chill on many assignments, and his discussion times always provided help to work on the codes. I learned how to code in Python fairly easily in class and he was pretty helpful in office hours as well. Unfortunately, his exams shifted to in-person after our TA complained about the use of AI in assignments (excluding final).

Dr. Claudel is a very nice guy. It was my first time learning Python, but it was not as hard as I expected. He asked us for feedback on his lectures and how he could improve them. No attendance grade, but I would go to understand material and ask questions in person. Also it is helpful for the quizzes.

The lectures were kinda boring but very helpful with homework and labs I would recommend watching them online at 2x speed. The tests switched from online to paper during the semester but they were still
Pretty easy. He went over the study guide the day before in class and I would recommend you go to that because it was very similar to the test.

Most boring class I've ever taken. Claudel is not a good lecturer. However, to understand the homework and labs, going to class is important. Lab TA was goated for me, he helped more than Claudel. Uses python instead of Matlab. very easy tho.

As someone who has never coded before, this class was my biggest nightmare. I learned nothing from it because the labs were so difficult that it felt like you had to have been coding for 3+ years to know what to do. Everything is basically open-note so you can get by if you need to, but I wanted to learn Python and ended up not being able to.

Dr. Claudel is a nice guy who does seem to care about his students and makes himself accessible in many ways, but he's not super great at teaching programming (Python, in my case) to people who have never done it before. The lab TAs were a godsend in this regard. Claudel is pretty funny and at least he made the lectures enjoyable.

The lectures were rather dry, but the class was an easy A. The final was online, open-note and the quizzes were too. The lectures, lab, and homework did not correlate so that was very frustrating. Claudel is a nice guy though.

Easy, but I didnt learn any matlab. Go to lecture and pay attention to the in-class example and you'll be fine on the quizzes. Go to office hours to get answers to the homework. For labs, pray your TA isn't Hassan bc I've never had such disdain for a TA before. Useless. Rude. Unclear. I really hated him. But Claudel is fine.

Claudel is French, so his accent makes it difficult to understand sometimes, but other than that, he is a good professor who (eventually) makes the main point of the lecture clear, and also gives you concise directions on how to code. The labs were usually straightforward, although not initially, as they had to be explained by the TA.

I never went to class (because I couldn't understand a word he was saying), and my lab ta was absolute garbage (Hassan). There were like 11 labs and 5 homework yet only half of them counted for credit. Quizzes and final were online, and only 5/6 questions. Honestly, this class was not hard but go to office hours for help on the homework and labs.

Claudel is super nice, his lectures are a bit difficult to understand, but office hours are really helpful. He is willing to help you and explain any questions in office hours. Awesome class and awesome professor. I learned a lot

He's super lenient and chill. Boring lectures don't make him fun, but his French accent is honestly half the reason I was there. The TA's gave me a headache over grading discrepancies and organization. He has plenty of extra credit, no tests.
Claudel is a nice man but it is very easy to lose attention in his lecture because they are very dry. He is an easy grader as long as you put some effort into assignments.

Dr. Claudel is kind and his lectures aren't too bad either. Lots of labs and homework but they're not terrible especially if you have prior knowledge of linear algebra and diff. eq. Both him and TAs are very helpful. Quizzes are open notes. Definitely one of the less stressful classes out there.

A nice guy. The class isn't necessarily hard, but the lectures and course material can be quite boring. There was a lot of homework and labs which become very repetitive and tedious. Had quizzes every other week that were not bad. He did provide drops for lowest homework, quiz, and lab which was very nice.
Good guy, very fair professor.

He's okay. Really tries to teach you theory behind the programming, so linear algebra will help a lot understanding it. Labs weren't easy, but TA's and prof were eager to help. He tries to do everything he can to help you learn. He genuinely cares. Go to his office hours, pay attention, ask questions, & definitely do the test reviews.

Solid teacher. Had him for CE 311k. I did not understand anything in that class but he gives a review sheet similar to the test and allows you to have a cheat sheet. The homework and labs require time but the TA´s helped me on those ones. He does not take attendance.

Professor Chhajwani might be the best professor at UT. His class is super interesting and very insightful if you are interested in real estate. The material is difficult, but he makes it easy to understand. He also grades leniently  and makes the class enjoyable with great guest speakers and case projects. Take him 1000% if you have the option.

Prof Chhajwani is the goat. He makes learning super simple, and makes a heavy-material class like FIN 357 easy to digest and learn about. He also has lots of preparation material for the test, and instapolls at the beginning of class are similar to test questions. If you have the option, take this man.

Chhajwani is awesome. Very nice professor, and probably the best for FIN357. Lectures focus on exam-related topics, something not universal to all FIN prof. apparently. Reading textbook is mandatory for a good grade, in any FIN class. Occasional question days, where class does problems together. Cold-calling involved, he can be a bit hard on you.
Best professor i have had at UT

Professor Chhajwani is terrific. I had him the first time he taught FIN 357 and I learned so much in his class which built a strong foundation for Finance (thanks to both the class and prof). 

Be ready to read the book, engage in lectures, and put in the effort. It won't be easy, but you will learn finance and set yourself up for future success!

Professor Chhajwani is a very smart man. He flies through the material with intensity that makes it hard to keep up. Chhajwani's classes do better on average on each exam, even though his class has the fewest assignments. If you enjoy the fast-paced environment and don't mind being cold called, take Chhajjjjjj. lfg.

Professor Hemant taught the class very well. He gives real world problems and the guest speakers he brought in really opened my mind to real world scenarios. The class is tough, which it's designed to be, but he explains the concepts really well. He also wants to make sure you do well so pay attention to his reviews and you'll do fine in the class.

Hemants is the best Real Estate professor in McCombs. The syndications class has a lot of difficult concepts that are hard to explain. But he was able to explain it simply and make it intellectually stimulating. Highly recommend him to anyone who is curious about the real estate world. He also offers you a ton of support out of the classroom.

Took this class as part of the McCombs curriculum. It's challenging due to the fast pace, but that's not on the professor. Professor Chhajwani is practical, fair, and supportive if you show effort and curiosity. He focuses on real-world finance over just theory. He doesn't hand out easy A's, but I'd still highly recommend the course.

Professor Chhajwani is a caring professor not cares about academics but also life outside the classroom. Different from other professors this class is generally not curved (because most of his students work rly hard and there is not need for curve) so be ready to put in effort.
One of the best professors I've had at UT. Very cool and does a great job of showing what you need to know for the exams.

Professor Chhajwani was a wonderful professor and I highly recommend taking him for FIN 357. This class is difficult across the board, and professor Chhajwani does a great job of preparing you for anything that might come your way on exam day. Show up to class and put in the effort and he will help you with whatever else you need. Highly recommend.

I took Hemant's syndication class and highly recommend it to anyone serious about real estate. It helped me speak more confidently in interviews and I found the material very interesting. Hemant genuinely cares about students and supports those who show up. He provides you with the tools to succeed in the exam if you put in the effort.

The professor was excellent during FIN 357. He would always pack his slides with the most important things you needed to know for the lectures and what his students struggled the most with during prior semesters. He also shares a lot of his personal experiences in the industry so you can see the real world applications. Get ready to read a lot tho!

Professor Hemant was a great professor. He would stay after class with me among other students for an hour, sometimes even two, to ensure we understood the material and left with no doubts. He was extremely knowledgeable of material. His class does require a lot of effort and cruising through isn't an option. Effort will equal success in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chhajwani was an amazing professor! If you do badly in his class, it's because YOU didn't put in the work. There's plenty of in-class practice, he's very accessible for questions, and he genuinely cares about his students. He's also incredibly knowledgeable. I really enjoyed his class, take him if you get the chance!

Highly recommend taking him especially if you have a more linear approach to absorbing data. I definitely pestered him a lot outside of classes and during exam discussions but he was super helpful and patient. It is a fast moving class I will say but thats more to do with the content. Be very thorough with the slide deck, and you will be just fine.

Prof. Chhajwani is an outstanding, knowledgeable, and caring professor. He checks in during lectures to ensure everyone understands, is always available outside class, and his in-depth lectures thoroughly prepare you for exams. He's approachable, explains complex material clearly, and provides helpful Excel supplements. Highly recommend!

I'll tell you what, I had no business even getting a B- in this class. I'm a Sociology major who has barely any experience regarding business classes. Yet so long as you try, I promise you Hemant will help you every step of the way. He's there to help you learn, not to make you worried about your grade (just give it a lot of effort).

I REGRET TAKING HIM SO MUCH. Every class, all he says is, "I'll let you review this on your own," and that's why I'm stuck learning everything on my own. Isn't cooperative or helpful outside of class, and teaches as if we already know the content. Provides no help with the cases and then grades on accuracy instead of effort. I WOULD NOT TAKE HIM!!!

One of my favorite professors of all time and made the course 1000x better. He was so understanding and always willing to explain concepts, the amount of resources provided by the professor helped a lot for the exams, which was nice because I heard the other professors did not have any many resources. TAKE CHHAJWANI IF YOU CAN!!!

Professor Chhajwani has by far been my favorite professor at UT Austin. He cares alot about his students' success. He goes the extra mile to make sure everyone is actively learning and provides all the resources for us to be successful in the class. Even if I want to miss class, I get myself to go every time because I have a lot of respect for him.

By far my favorite professor at UT! Professor Chhajwani goes the extra mile when trying to help students learn concepts in this class. He is also super friendly and makes a genuine effort to know each student's name, interests, and career goals. Highly recommend taking FIN357 with him!

This class is just a lot of information at once but Hemant is very understanding and willing to help everyone. His lectures are pretty good, I recommend supplementing them with the textbook, as this class exams are all written by a different teacher and standardized on the book. He has a lot of experience and really cares about everyones success!

Gem of a professor. Lots of real world experience (RE, PE, Corp Fin). Knowledgeable and good at teaching. Accessible to answer questions in OH and over email. Cares about students and their present and future success. Take him if you can.

The class is pretty easy as long as you keep up with HW and ask questions as necessary. You will learn a lot.

Very intelligent and had good knowledge of the material, first semester teaching the class so took a bit to get acclimated to exactly how running the class should look like. Always super willing to answer any questions. Went the extra mile in the days leading up to exams to ensure we had a good idea of what would be on the tests.

If you're taking this for a VAPA or upper division elective, do something else. He is rude and condescending, and makes little to no accommodations for ANY situation. His sensitive lecture topics (sex, gender, etc) were talked about as if they were a joke. If we didn't remember a specific thing from the reading he'd get angry and say we don't try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just an ok course; he's very knowledgeable but his presentations include information you will not need to memorize. Canvas is not well laid out, and attendance is mandatory. You can do fine on the exams without reading anything. Choose an easier VAPA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arrogant and rude. His lectures on books he wrote are important for the exams, but he mumbles into the microphone and is condescending, borderline cruel if you ask him to adjust the volume. All this said, the assignments are pretty easy and sparse; if you're willing to put yourself through the treatment and attitude you'll receive from Clarke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken his classes twice and I highly recommend them! The topics of his Greek/Roman courses cover aspects of human sexuality within their (not our) cultural contexts. While he is frank, I've never thought the discussion to be sensationalist or disrespectful. Do sit in the front if you have trouble understanding him!
Clarke made weird and uncomfortable comments on very sensitive subject matters like sexual assault and pedophilia.

Clarke is extremely knowledgeable and respected in the field but most of his knowledge is guided by his own perspective and experiences. His grading is extremely subjective and he often presents his own interpretation of a work as fact.

Clarke is such a sweet guy! Not the most tech savvy. Clear lectures that go right along with the exams. Exams aren't hard at all, just need to watch the lectures and memorize the pieces. I never did the readings and got 96+ on all exams. Also some small writing assignments, but they're easy 100s. Go to class to succeed. Would love to take again.

Do not take this just for a VAPA. He mumbles so much and barely turns up his microphone so it is very difficult to understand what he says in class. However, his lectures are not very important but you must do all the readings to do well. Tests are over readings and the TA grades very easy. Barely any assignments just a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the subject matter and was very excited to give my own interpretation guided by the textbooks and readings. Unfortunately Clarke is the kind of professor who prefers that you regurgitate back to him exactly what he has written in his own books and anything that strays from that is considered highly subjective and wrong.

Professor John Clarke teaches a performance work in his Modern American Art course that contains sexual assault, and he presented it without warning. When I emailed him that I was triggered by this piece, he asked me to tell him in person why it was triggering for me. I declined, and he put the piece on our midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Clarke is such a passionate professor with so many interesting stories & experiences he has from years and years of research. I took the course over Roman Art, & it was only difficult at times for me because I lack memorization skills when it comes to names of sculptures, paintings, etc. Otherwise, the course is fairly easy & interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: ARH339M is an upper divison art history class and rightfully so. Your grade depends on your 3 test scores, and they're half memorization and half essay. You must read to write a good essay. It's tough, but I really respect Prof. Clarke. He's a great lecturer and has real connections to the art world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: took this class as my VAPA because I saw the grade distribution. it has a good grade distribution, but don't be fooled. it's A LOT of work. the 3 exams make up 100% of your grade and it takes a lot of memorization. be sure to pay attention during lectures that is the most important thing for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tells you to buy three textbooks written by him, you don't need any of them. Lectures consist of him talking about art, never mixes things up. Tests are nothing more than recalling names, dates, and facts; memorization is key to passing this class. Can be quite condescendingarrogant at times. Attendance required. Overall fairly easy class.
He is awesome and does yoga

Clarke is a very interesting lecturer. He is a little arrogant. He has mandatory attendance and your grade is based on 3 tests worth 35%, 35% and 30% of final grade. Attendane only lowers it. Overall good class

He can be really tough, but if you go to him for help he will bend over backwards for you. He doesn't suffer fools gladly, and his graduate methods course is fairly brutal. But you can learn a lot from him if you try, he's brilliant! And he's very funny if you get him, though he can also be cruel.

Awesome professor! His lectures are incredibly interesting and eye-opening.  I found him to be quite amicable with students as opposed to other reviewers, though he can be pretty sarcastic.  Tests are dependent upon a thorough understanding of lectures AND all of the readings, all written by the professor.

Awesome professor! His lectures are incredibly interesting and eye-opening.  I found him to be quite amicable with students as opposed to other reviewers, though he can be pretty sarcastic.  Tests are dependent upon a thorough understanding of lectures AND all of the readings, all written by the professor.
Quirky guy, knows his stuff.  May run into him at the gym near the lap pool-  he uses a snorkel.

Dr. Clarke made courses challenging and interesting for me. He can be cruel if you are unprepared-or disrespectful-but then again, aren't you asking for it? Meeting his high expectations was a clear motivating factor for me and made me a successful scholar. I am now a college professor. I hope my students say the same about me. Thanks Clarke!

This man is brillant. He despises undergrads and tolerates his grad students but you know what? You'll never take a funnier. wittier professor (unless you take waldman) he's worth it and you'll take away so much from whatever class you will take with him!

The first review for Prof. Clarkes is clearly by someone who cannot distinguish strick teaching and poor teaching.  Prof. Clarke is hard on his grad. students, and this makes him a better prof.  His tactics may not work with you, but if you talk to him about that, he LISTENS (and well!).

An utterly unpleasant man.  He has no quealms about treating you as though you don't deserve to be in the art history program.  So dictatorial that you wind up not being inspired enough to take anything away from what would otherwise be a compelling and useful class.

I struggled a lot in Statics, but Landis' grading scale really helped. A C was around a 65, so even low exam scores counted. The class isn't easy, but many still got A's and B's. He provides lots of past exams and quizzes. He seemed grumpy a lot times due to cheating scandals in our class and sending attendance codes.., but overall he's fair.

Take Landis! His class is very well organized & he provides all the material you need to succeed. dont take early semester warnings lightly-- falsely filling the attendance form is -5 pts off overall grade. exams are fair, study at least 4 most recent past exams and you'll be set. but expect to put a little more effort in for exam 3. quizzes are ez

Landis makes this class so approachable. Do the optional homework! The course is manageable until after exam 2, then you need to lock in. Landis provides great resources. Take ownership and stay engaged in lectures for an achievable A. Content is challenging, but Landis breaks it down well.

THE GOATTT. As someone who barely passed eng physics 1, I learned so much from this class and did surprisingly well despite being worried. Loved this class so much I signed up for his solids class next semester, and super excited. The material is difficult sometimes, but he provides an ABUNDANCE of HWs, past quizzes, and past exams.

He is a great teacher and organized in the notes he takes. Provides more than enough resources to help you be successful. The attendance and quiz policy is pretty forgiving. The tests are difficult, but that's just how statics is.

By far the best engineering professor at UT in my opinion. Very organized lectures, always guide students to fully understand the materials. Course contents are incredibly accessible outside of class; Past Exams, Quizzes, and Notes. 5 Weeks, 4 Midterms, 1 Final, 5% Attendance grade. Time challenging, but do a ton of practices, you will get the A.

Professor Landis is a awesome professor. His class is very clearly laid out and there is a clear path to get an A in his class. He does problems that are very useful to quizzes and tests. Never did the HW once. Couple times throughout the semester he would pause the recording and tell the people in person insight on the test.

Had for statics and solids and highly recommend. 4 midterms, weighted 30/25/15/10% depending on how well you did on them. Weekly quizzes. Has lots of resources (past exams and quizzes) - definitely do them to do well!

Landis is THE solids professor to take. His lectures are really easy to follow and teach you everything you need to know for tests/quizzes. He's also incredibly resourceful and organized: you have access to all material types from previous years. Super friendly and one of my fav professors so far!

Dynamics is hard, so you will need to practice alot. But Dr. Landis provides alot of material to help you do so.

Overall, great professor and learned alot.

Dr. Landis is a very good teacher in my opinion. He talks about theory first usually and then gets into example problems.

Provides previous years materials, which is great for quiz and exam preparations.

Grading is mostly made up from exams, but practice a-lot and it will be worth it.

Attendance is not mandatory, but go to class!

Very "Solid" professor, who gives great lectures with logical sense. Every lecture is recorded, tons of previous exams/quizzes with explaination videos. Does a high(30%) to low(10%) performance grading for exams, drop 2 lowest of the weekly quizzes. Make sure to look for details from the current lecture notes and practice a lot, you will get an A!

His lectures were a little disorganized but still helpful. He overall provides a very good foundation for statics for the EIT exam. I went out of this class feeling very knowledgeable about statics. His office hours were not that helpful as he acted irritated at every OH i went to but his class was structured very fairly and difficulty was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Always plays music before class. The class is hard, but as long as you attend lectures, do the optional homework, and do all the tests and quizzes from the previous years (they go back to like 2007), you should be ok. Your grade will be from only quizzes, midterms, and the final. But he does give partial credit on all.

started at basics so dont be worried if you barely passed physics 1. lectures are recorded but def attend in person, learned better that way. study very hard for the quizzes and exams, it kind of builds up if you don't. lots of partial credit on the exams (final answer almost doesn't matter), based on the methods. weekly quizzes are like hw

Dr. Landis provide students with a solid foundation to further success in other EM courses such as solid mechanics. Being said, his course is not gonna be an easy one. Homeworks are practice only, no grades. Weekly quizzes are 20% of the total. And 3 midterms are 15-25% depending on the performance. He does curve at the end of course by endeavor.

Great lecturer. Statics is a tricky class for most, but Landis is good at breaking down hard concepts and making them easy to understand. He gives you access to all his past exams and quizzes, as well as tons of HW problems which makes studying easy. HW isn't graded, instead grade comes from exams, a final and weekly quizzes. Don't expect a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy horrible teacher. Does the easiest examples possible gives tests with the weirdest setups. Atleast other horrible teachers recognise that and give curves to balance that out but so far no curves and doesn't look like any curves will be added for the final or the total grade. Again awful teacher but good personality. 24 Fall

Great professor who explains hard concepts in a way that makes them easier to comprehend. Solids is hard, but he has extra videos and past tests that rly help. He records all his lectures too. No final, just 4 midterms weighted based on your performance, making it a pretty easy A. HW can be hard but they're not graded. Overall would def recommend
Organized notes from professor; no textbook; lots of past exams and quizzes to use as resources; weekly quizzes; recorded lectures; overall great professor just the content is a bit hard at times
Great lecturer and very helpful during office hours. Midterms and weekly quizzes are okay as long as you do the homework.

Top tier professor at UT. His lectures can seem daunting at first, but if you closely pay attention to them, they are extremely helpful for practice. Provides more than enough resources for test prep, like optional homework and past midterms on Canvas. Grades exams pretty leniently too.

Great lecturer and cares about teaching his students properly (constantly asks for feedback during lectures). Homework is very helpful for weekly quizzes. Make sure you do well on all assignments because only the weekly quizzes, midterms, and the final count for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Optional homework, but will help prepare you for weekly quizzes. He gives you past quizzes and exams and all the material you may need. Very organized. He's a funny guy but has a bit of a sassy attitude sometimes. Comes in clutch with the final grade adjustments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His lectures were in depth but easy to understand. His past tests he has on canvas help you prepare for the exams.
lectures are really good; homework is optional but really helpful; lots of resources from past years quizzes, exam, and homework
Dr. Landis is an amazing lecturer! He breaks down the content in a way that is clear and easy to understand! There are weekly quizzes, however they reflect the material in class and on the homework.

Landis is genuinely one of the best engineering professors at UT! He explains Solids in a way that makes it extremely easy to understand, and his tests feel fair. There are weekly quizzes based on assigned (but ungraded) homework. Overall, Landis is the Solids professor to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Landis eats as a solids professor. He's very clear in his lectures and expectations regarding what we need to know for exams. I did find that he did a lot of deriving of the equations and such which can be nice, but it was mostly lost on me, and I only felt confident after we did practice problems. Just do the past exams and hw & you'll do good
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely important. It isn't the type of class you can get by with youtube ad such. He has a specific way of explaining and asking for things in problems that you wouldn't be able to solve unless you watch his lectures. Past exams are your bff for exams. Quizzes are the hw (15%). 3 exams, 15, 20, 25. final 25%. solid choice for prof.

Class material might be difficult, but his lectures are detailed and all recorded. All exams from previous years are provided as well. Textbook is optional. He works hard to make sure his students are successful. One of my favorite professors I've had during my time at UT.

Put in the work and you will do well. Dr. Landis is a decent professor but the course material is the type where you have to learn it for yourself to pass the exams. Use the resources and past course material to help you study and prepare for the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Landis can come of as a bit rude at times, I liked his teaching style and his overall sense of humor. He spent a ton of time at the beginning of the year on the fundamentals of the course, and this made the rest of the course fairly easy. He is one of the harder professors though, and some of his exam/quiz questions were difficult.

Dr. Landis can come across as rude often times, but in reality he is a very good professor who cares a lot about the understanding of his student. If you cannot make it to lecture, DEFINITELY watch his lectures online. I found his videos especially helpful for the exams and utilize the past exams, because he tends to make the exams similar.

I never give a 1 for difficulty, but this was THE easiest class I have taken so far in college. The concepts are all the same throughout the course, whether it be 2D or 3D. I honestly don't get how people struggle in this class. Chad is very clear in his lectures. Lectures go a little slow, but that's good for working ahead. Do HWs and you're set!

Dr. Chad Landis is a really good teacher if you're already a statics expert. He assumes that everyone knows statics already, and does a terrible job explaining concepts. The lectures are a waste of time, with most of the time dedicated to examples of concepts we never learned. This class (professor and TAs) degraded me and made me lose brain cells.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a good professor that knows what he's doing and is willing to answer questions during class. But go to him in office hours, and he makes you feel stupid. Very condescending. Yes, he does give you his past exams but that only means his tests are challenging; you better know the material. thankfully, no surprise questions on exams.

Landis is the goat. He truly explains concepts and then does examples to further cement them in your brain. If someone says this class was hard, then they're dumb or lying. This class becomes insanely predictable when it comes to what's on the tests and quizzes. Go to class to get 'hints.'
really cool
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's sad this is a required course for many, and even sadder that Landis is supposed to be one of the better professors. Statics is difficult and Landis somehow makes it way harder. In addition, there is no mc, only free response on quizzes and tests so if you're not prepared, you can't even guess, you're just screwed. He's very condescending too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never been strong in physics, however after taking statics with Professor Landis everything has clicked! He primarily taught by going through examples, which I found extremely helpful. As long as you work through the homework's and practice tests properly the class is relatively straight forward.

I did really well in this class because it was very straight forward. I went to class, studied for weekly quizzes, practiced for tests. If people say this class was hard, it's because they didn't go to class. He's a caring prof and a good lecturer. Content is pretty easy, but the problem solving can be tricky. I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Landis is easily one of the best professors I've had. While Statics is by no means an easy A, Dr. Landis makes the course material accessible to those who may have struggled with similar subjects in Physics I. He provides all of his past exams and quizzes and lets you know what's expected on tests. Really generous with partial credit. 10/10

Chad lives up to his name as he made me understand physics for the first time in my life. This glorious man provides so many resources and study materials and he sets you up to succeed in his class. Statics is a hard subject, but Chad is very good at lecturing and explaining. You can succeed in his class if you learn how to use the study materials.

Second time through Solids (Q drop) and I can definitively say Dr. Landis is the best. His lectures are very thorough, and he makes sure everyone knows what's going on. Homework is optional but not really if you want to do well. The tests are much harder than the quizzes but not unbearable, just make sure to do the homework.
rough experience

Landis is a great prof. Statics requires work, but Landis gives you YEARS worth of old tests with detailed solutions. If you spend the time to work the problems, you'll do great. There's really only seven concepts in this class, but they take work. On the exams, the name of the game is PARTIAL CREDIT. He is generous on test grading.

Statics can be a difficult class if you don't keep up with the content. Homework is only for extra practice so your whole grade depends on quizzes and exams. Prof Landis does multiple example problems in each lecture and highly encourages students to participate and be confident in their analysis. Do old exams to excel in class.

Dr. Landis provides you with a lot of resources including past exams and textbook problems. If you keep practicing the past exams you'll do great the upcoming exams as they are structured the same way. Lectures are pretty useful but he goes pretty fast so I'd recommend redoing the lecture problems on your own time as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are no surprises from Dr. Landis. If you take notes and do your practice problems, you'll do great. For Statics, Dr. Landis provides plenty of example problems and all the tests from past years. Lectures are very easy to understand and Dr. Landis will always answer questions for confused students. Easy reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Landis is a great teacher and explains concepts pretty well. The problem is the structure of this class. It is really tailored towards people who enjoy self-learning physics. Homework is 0% of your grade and the entire grade is based off of tests and quizzes which means it is up to you to generate your own motivation to study this tough content.

The class itself was very boring, if you don't pay attention, you will fail. Has 2 midterms and one final for a 4 week- summer class. Is a terrible grader, and isn't sympathetic as a teacher even if you're going through mental issues that hinder your learning. Do as many practice problems as you can.

Landis was a solid choice for Dynamics. This was his second time teaching it at UT but he makes ALL his old tests from previous universities available. Homework is optional, but you should really do it if you want to do well on exams. PS: This is engineering; dynamics is not easy. Take some reviews on here with a grain of salt :)

Landis is a phenomenal professor. Provides access to his old exams and is all about learning through solving problems instead of talking about theory for the entire lecture then saying, "Good luck." Also records his lectures so if you need to go back to understand something you can. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Chad Landis is a great option for statics. Yes the class is hard, but Landis is an outstanding lecturer who really cares about the success of his students. He explains materials, does review for every exam, solves practice exam problems for the class. He gives you all the resources to succeed. Only con, The TA sessions are useless and 2 hours.

Chad the Dad is a cool guy. Yeah, it was hard waking up at 9 am sometimes but I learned a lot during lecture. He pretty much just goes over past problems he has created and they are all on Canvas. Def do the homework to grasp the concepts. TA sessions sucked but they are very lenient with grading midterms.

I hated statics with Landis. He was a boring lecturer at 9am, and mostly did practice problems instead of teaching material. The TAs were hopeless, and the discussion sections were material-based but extremely boring. The quizzes were relatively straightforward, but if you weren't on top of the material, you'd get a bad grade. DO THE HW to learn!!
Definitely have to work for the grade in this class, but Landis is a great lecturer and is always open to questions. Definitely practice all the past exams he posts and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Explains all of the material very well, and ensures that he has every exam he's ever given out available far ahead of time. Some exam questions were taken directly from his past exams. Weekly quizzes given out during discussion sections, taken directly from weekly homeworks. Lectures move quickly but he explains everything in great detail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chad is such a dad. He is a great lecturer and posts all of his past tests to Canvas so it is really easy to study for the exams. He is very receptive to questions and clearly loves teaching, so this class was enjoyable.

Amazing. His lectures are very organized: explains the basics of the topics then does several examples. If you do the homeworks and practice exams he gives you, the exams are easy. He often uses past exam questions so if you don't have time to do every one, at least look at his solutions for each one so if it's on the test you will have seen it.

Great Professor. He seems to genuinely want everyone on the same page, and cares for his students. Was struggling but he helped me out and recognized that I was really trying. Easy to pay attention to, really entertaining, clear and funny.

Chad Landis? More like DAD Landis. This guy was awesome. The material was presented in an interesting and engaging manner, making it a pleasure to show up to class everyday. Tests are fair and pertain to what you learn in class. Homework is optional, but helps you with quizzes and further understanding. I HIGHLY recommend my dad.

Dr. Landis is an awesome professor. He's a nice guy, has a sense of humor, and definitely knows what he's talking about. I had him for both Statics (E M 306) and Solids (E M 319). Only downside is that he doesn't do +/- for grades. I would've ended up with a B+, but was bumped to a B since he doesn't round up. Also has really good taste in music.

Landis is a wonderful professor! His lectures explain difficult concepts in a crystal-clear way. He posts his notes and past exams online and is very helpful during office hours. His grading is generous, and you won't be significantly penalized for careless errors. The class is by no means trivial, but he's the best professor you can take.

Makes you learn in class, easy to concentrate/take notes with his immersive style of teaching. He's there for you and makes a point about it. The tests may be hard but they are fair. All his resources are posted online for you to use. My only complaint is that the homework and weekly quizzes are easy and don't prepare you for tests.

To be fair I went into this class thinking it would be an easy A and rarely studied, HOWEVER compared to the practice problems you do in class and TA sessions the tests are WAY more complex. However Dr. Landis is quick to respond to emails and his tendency to cover all aspects well is a real treat.

Great professor! Sometimes gets a little lost in the algebra, but who wouldn't? Tests are doable, if you prepared for them. Weekly quizzes, except for test weeks, and drops 2 of them. HW is optional. Gives students access to his old tests and finals with the solutions. Great guy.

Landis is an awesome dude. Super funny, and an extremely good teacher who obviously has a lot of experience.  He doesn't throw curve balls, and his tests are very straight forward, but the material progressively gets more difficult.  The first test is insanely easy, GET 100% ON IT.  They get harder and harder, and the third test is pretty hard.

Dr. Landis is a smart guy. His lectures have a lighthearted, comfortable air about them. Exams are just about the right difficulty for engineers. Helpful; HW problem solutions are posted from the get-go. His explanations are clear, and his example problems are usually pretty well thought out and fairly representative of exam questions. Recommended.

He is a knowledgeable guy, however, his TA's as well as him all have a smug atmosphere about them. It makes a large class even more intimidating especially when the people who are supposed to help you out are so condescending when you don't quite understand a topic. I would suggest a different professor for this class.

She had mediocre lectures and loved explaining random Chinese things wrong. Doesn't grade until finals week even though class ends in like October, and even then the grading feels arbitrary. Never gave out a single 100 on an assignment, mostly gives 85s-90s. Attendance is a grade, even if you have an exam that falls during class hours. Mid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Explains everything very well, would recommend the class. Also provides very good feedback.

I took Cameron for MKT 174 and she is such an amazing lecturer. She's one of the nicest people I've met at UT, so if you need a 1 hour course take this one!! participation is crucial to passing, but she tries to make each class enjoyable! Loved her!

Loved this professor! Even though the class was late in the day, it always flew by because she made the material so engaging. The assignments were straightforward and manageable, and I still walked away learning so much valuable information. Would definitely recommend taking this class with her if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Clark's lecturing style and I can say that I learned quite a lot from her! I love that she is passionate about what she teaches and stands for what she believes in. However, I will say that the 3 exams are quite tricky, as they are long free responses. There is a lot of content discussed and no study guide/vague ideas of what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is very condescending - when people ask questions in class she acts frustrated and as if the answer should be the most obvious thing in the world. I went to office hours once (Friday 8 AM only) to go over a test and ask for advice and she complained that students "just want to be spoon fed". The TAs were much more helpful.

The 3 exams that make up the majority of your grade require lots of studying, but are doable. She may seem intimidating, but is incredibly engaging and refreshingly honest about her views on what's happening in the US right now in relation to the course content. I learned so much and highly recommend her as a professor.

I enjoyed Professor Clark's class and learned a lot, and she can answer any question. She does present a lot of information but the way she lectures makes it easier to remember. Quizzes are doable if you keep up with lecture material.

Would not recommend Dr. Clark she had very unprofessional lectures with poor attention to detail. She also refused an extension for a family member passing away because she didn't believe me. 0/10 very traumatic.

I enjoyed this class, and I learned a lot. The quizzes can be kind of tricky but as long as you study the lecture material, you should be just fine. Dr. Clark is very knowledgeable and insightful as well.

Dr. Clark's class is very informative. I learned so much about dementia and Alzheimer's. The lectures can be science heavy but she does a great job of explaining it so you shouldn't feel lost. There are 4 free response quizzes that can be a bit tricky so make sure to study ahead. But as long as you put in the work it's totally doable.

Professor Clark is a fun teacher who knows a lot about aging and dementia. She is easy to listen to during class. Her lectures are long but she breaks things down and finds a way to talk about current events in class too. She also checks on you and is a kind and caring. She brought us treats during one lecture and gives you pep talks.

Prof Clark is great & passionate! This class is focused on dementia types, factors, & disparities. Lectures are content-heavy, but she is great at explaining things so that you'll understand. 4 exams (all free response) that are doable if you attend class & study slides. Weekly participation discussion posts and 1 Alzheimer's project. Cool class

Dr. Clarno is a groovy guy. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Concerning the class, if this is your first class on nuclear, it might be rough as there is a learning curve. Exams also are difficult but are graded on a curve so there is less pressure. Reason I am giving a four is because the class was too disorganized. Very swag beard.
Swag guy. Nice beard.
Great guy, great class. Study with the slides... Tests are a challenge, but meant to stretch you

Awesome professor. So nice and understanding, easy to talk to, cares about your learning while also making sure not to stress you out. His FRI stream is great and provides a great exposure to the basics of research.

I highly recommend taking this course for the UGS requirement. Dr. Clark is super cool and into what he is teaching. The course has some reading reflections, three essays, a group presentation, and an individual presentation. It is very interesting to learn about different plants and what they do. Compared to other UGS's this one is much better.

Dr. Clark is so chill and very understanding! He truly helps every student succeed in his lab, and he doesn't force anybody to do too much work each week! However, the partner system during first semester can get a little frustrating if you're stuck with a bad one, and he doesn't really use canvas, so it is hard to determine your grade!

Dr. Clark is THE BEST! Such a sweet guy and is extremely passionate about his research! His lab is interesting but pretty laid back! Not work heavy and he's so forgiving and approachable! LOVE DR.CLARK AND HIS LAB!!!
He's my Homie

Super nice guy who is very passionate about the subject matter. He is a little old school though and did not put any grades into Canvas. I'm sure you could ask but I did not know my grade until after the class ended. Really understanding and sweet professor!

Dr. Clark is one of the nicest people I've met in my life and his passion towards plants and botany is unmatched. The class itself is pretty interesting and its mostly discussion heavy so attendance is important. There are a few essays and a FRQ test, so if you want to do good just put some effort in. Loved this class and the Professor.

Dr. Clark is a great and caring professor. He's accessible to students and emphasizes learning and improvement. I found Plant Physiology to be manageable. I would recommend at least taking Biochem or Cell Bio before this course. Class was interesting because he ties in scientific history behind discoveries. Would recommend for an upper division bio

Clark is an amazing professor. He uses a lot of original papers in his lectures, which I like but some people don't. He also works really hard to prepare you for the tests and even gives you some of the questions and answers before hand. He's super passionate and one of the best professors at UT.

He set up the first experiment for us, and after that we were allowed to alter the setup however we wanted. He presented current research on the plant we used every week to guide us. I've never taken a class like this, it was the first time I felt interested in research in my whole 4 years at UT. If u pay attention and participate you'll do well!

Dr. Clark's class was discussion based and he encouraged everyone to shared their ideas and opinions. Essays can be stressful, as they are graded by a professional editor, but as long as you put in the effort necessary to participate in class and complete assignments, this class should be no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hidden Treasures of Plants was definitely one of the most worth while classes I took that semester. Dr. Clark's style of teaching is chill with it being more discussion based and a few essays. He really cares about his students, fostering a comfortable classroom envrionment where people can share their passion for plants.
Super helpful and understanding.

Dr. Clark was absolutely amazing! His Hidden Treasures of Plants UGS was really eye-opening and a great learning experience. Discussions were very chill and essay assignments were not too much of a challenge. Dr. Clark was super understanding and spent time learning about his students. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot!

If you're a freshman trying to figure out what First Year Signature to take, Hidden Treasures of Plants with Prof Clark is the way to go. He doesn't grade the writing but a pro editor does so beware of tough grades but most of the class is just presentations and overall really enjoyable. He really cares for students and is really lenient.
I highly recommend taking Bio328! Even if you are not a plant person, it is an interesting, stimulating class. Dr. Clark is amazing and willing to do anything to help you succeed.

Although she is an interesting professor and some of her classes were exciting, she is quite a tough grader, at least in my experience. I did not receive an A on any assignment other than one, despite following the given guidelines exactly and spending over a week on every essay. Nice lady, but I wish she had given clearer instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Coffin was wonderful and probably one of the most interesting professors I've ever had. As long as you truly read the material, which is all intriguing, you will want to participate in the conversations had in class. The second half is focused on a research topic of your choosing, with a lot of guidance.

I LOVE COFFIN! She can be blunt but if you show up, participate, and put in some effort she rewards you with great feedback and funny moments. First half of class was just discussion, so be prepared to talk. The second half was a research project but Coffin splits it into small parts and takes the time to provide individual help. Would do it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Coffin this my second semester with her now and she just gets better. She truly cares for her students (extra if u put in the work and participate in class) she helped me both in and out of class. She might be blunt sometimes but she knows what she's talking about knows you do too, truly such a great lady, I have so much respect for her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Coffin is so nice and she really cares about what she teaches and her students. It was scary to be thrown into her class as an underclassmen because she does expect you to know some info on the topic beforehand but I picked it up quick. It is a writing dense class but that being said she grades very easy and there's one group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Coffin made history fascinating and made me feel like I was making a difference. Her class provided amazing writing experience & pushed me to think more critically. Enjoyed learning from her a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer but my interactions with her were very poor. She was extremely rude and defensive when I sought clarification of the grade breakdown for final grades. I question her humanity

Professor Coffin is a very sweet, intelligent, and funny lady. If you are good at essays you'd probably breeze through this class but I found it difficult at times. Lectures were sometimes hard to follow if you don't have a lot of knowledge about the French Rev. Dense readings.

This class requires a lot of outside reading and participation, but Prof. Coffin makes sure to provide a wide variety of media like documentaries, podcasts, and novels.  She also dedicated a lot of class time to guiding us on our final RPF project, which IS worth the majority of your grade.  Overall she was very supportive and available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Coffin is an excellent professor. There are quite a lot of readings each week for the first half of the class, but it is doable. In the second half of the class you work on the RPF and she gives plenty of class time and guidance to work on it. She is accessible and super caring. Very interesting class overall!

Incredible lectures. Professor Coffin's approach to teaching the French Revolution is both thought-provoking and balanced, allowing the students to come up with their own conclusions. Participation is highly encouraged, but Professor Coffin never makes it awkward. There are a lot of readings, however most of them are interesting and easy to scan.

She is the sweetest person ever. We had three essays and two group assignments that made up our grade. She decided to not give us a test and make participation a grade. If you talk to her and actually get to know her, you will be successful in this class. She allowed me to redo my essays for higher grades even though they were above passing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Coffin's French Revolution class was very fun and engaging! Definitely a lot of reading and going to class was important. But, I felt the lectures were pretty interesting and the group projects were fun. She was very helpful when I went to office hours and provided a lot of resources for writing history papers.

I had a really tough semester, but Dr. Coffin would always cut me some slack. As long as I delivered good work, it didn't matter if it was a few days late. As long as you show that you are interested in what you are doing, she will go out of her way to give you support, resources, and advice.

HIS 353 (French Rev.) was the first UD history I took and I highly recommend this class with Coffin. Only 3 main essays (4 pages each), fun lectures that focus on class discussions, and Dr. Coffin is super nice. She is really engaging in class, and you can tell she really cares for her students and is passionate about the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Coffin was my rudest teacher this semester. She belittled zoom students and openly stated that she cared less for them. This class is open for students as a culture credit class, DON'T take it. No electronics allowed in person, extremely book heavy, so few grades. There are three papers, each assignment is vague and she doesn't explain them well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She takes points off for attendance during covid. Lots of reading and papers. Least favorite class. Don't take her if you don't need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Expects you to do a ridiculous amount of work. No laptops/electronics in class, if you have more than 2 grammatical errors your paper drops by 5 points, and we're back in person for the first time after covid and she deducts points (3 pts per 2 absences) for attendance. I understand a tough class but this is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Coffin is extremely caring; she always checked in with students. She's v knowledgable and expects a lot from her students (not in a cary way). Sometimes she goes really deep or gets philosophical and I felt a little confused, but she's always willing to talk after class! Essay prompts can be challenging, but grades fairly!

Dr. Coffin is the best. You can tell that she really loves what she teaches. Her lectures are never boring and she has a great sense of humor.
