She will try to scare you off with talk of a hard midterm and mandatory group projects but they're really not bad. Definitely do your best to keep up with the readings (there's a LOT).

I actually really adored this class. Dr. Coffin is really passionate about the subject of the French Revolution and that carries over into the lectures. There is a ton of reading which is needed for the papers, however. She makes a big fuss about the midterm but its really do-able. She requires attendance and will deduct from grade so GO TO CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Incredibly engaging & very willing to talk with students outside of class. Group projects provide valuable insight into the topic material and make for a welcome change. Dr. Coffin also provides very good feedback on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Never read so much for a class in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She clearly cares about her students and makes history super interesting. Really makes you think! She is clearly knowledgeable, but grades very easily. Good use of quotes is important to her so as long as you have plenty of solid quotes in your paper you should be good. Highly recommend!! She made my first semester at UT great, take her if you can!

The papers, tests, and readings for this class are difficult, but manageable if you do the work on schedule. Lectures were 50/50: sometimes fascinating, other times boring. Prof. Coffin occasionally did discussion based classes instead of lecturing, so you spent the whole class listening to classmates' opinions rather than lecture material.

She is genuinely so sweet and caring, wants everyone to feel caught up and prepared. First half of semester is one project, second half is the second, and every week there is a quiz that is easy if you do the one chapter of reading. Totally manageable, especially for an upper divison CS
The course isn't too difficult, but be prepared to receive vague feedback and lose points—even if you repeatedly request basic feedback, success is unlikely.

Monotone, slow lectures. Still don't rly understand the concepts we learned, we just scratched the surface of everything. EX1 was a nightmare, wasn't that similar to the ptest, but EX2 was much more reasonable. She also gave 15 points of exam EC which saved my grade. Projects are fairly short. This class is good for the resume but bad for learning.

This class was a once a week, 3 hour lecture. While very manageable and the lectures were recorded, she is a very monotone lecturer. That is really the only thing. She is very knowledgeable, but it's just hard to understand her. Also, there's a partner project due every week which are easy but just plan ahead because they are worth 50%
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

Well I want to tell you that shirlely She's the best teacher there is. I will of course study with her again.
I think Shirley She is the best teacher there is
Shirley is the best teacher You can learn from anywhere and you succeed with this teacher

I really like this teacher She made me happy in life as soon as I started studying with her I will study with her for sure again

Professor Cohen works full time at Google as a result, she only shows up to class one day a week for 3 hrs. In addition, she doesn't hold office hours or respond to emails. Prepared to learn on your own

Ok professor. Lectures were kinda slow and unengaging, but the students didn't really help with participating either. Honestly some of the reviews for this class seem like an over exaggeration to me. It can be difficult but it's not that bad, even if you don't do all the readings just pay attention to lectures. Terrible, simply terrible. Class is ridiculously difficult for an intro class. Readings are too long and there are too many of them. TAs are way too harsh. All and all bad class.

Professor Handman is a good professor and I really enjoyed the way she facilitated discussion in her class. My problems with the class I took (Invented Languages) were primarily with the way the subject matter was approached moreso than her teaching style. Nice lady and passionate about the subject. While she does highlight the important info in her lecture slides it felt unstructured bc the info was pretty scrambled. I loved ANT 307! The content was interesting, and Prof. Handman knew what she was talking about. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

Grades based on discussion Qs, participation, and papers (or inventing a language)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Handman is super knowledgeable, funny, and a great lecturer. The class consists of short readings every week that come with discussion questions. In your TA sections, you discuss the readings and then have a short answer quiz over one of the questions you were given. Your grade is made up of the weekly quizzes, one midterm, and one final.

very chill guy. however, lectures can be pretty monotonous and he teaches straight from the textbook. attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures but one quiz in discussion weekly which was pretty manageable. my advice is skip the lectures and learn from the textbook in your own time. tests are easier than hw and have a bonus question.

Since it was my first semester, I assumed all math professors were THIS good. I was wrong. I can now see how goated Professor Coles was. Make sure you take his class, he explains really well, gives relevant ONLINE homework, and gives extremely useful exam reviews. W Professor Coles

Amazing Calc Professor. Homework and quizzes are similar to tests. Tests aren't hard if you truly know the material. Lectures move fast but are insightful. He knows SO much about the field and is genuinely interested. 65% of grade based on tests. Quizzes in discussion. DO THE HOMEWORK! He really emphasizes it for good reason. Amazing professor!

As a math major, Desmond is literally my role model. Everything about him is AMAZING. His lecture are simple, yet inspiring. If you get a chance to take him (even if you aren't a STEM major), please do!!!!!!!!!

Tests are similar to the hw, albeit a little bit longer and more difficult. He was a great lecturer as well, and  even though I find calc 2 to be incredibly boring, he did an awesome job of teaching it. The multivar section was the highlight of the class, so if you're scared of calc 3, take him! He's great at explaining calc in 3D.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor during Fall '25. He really knows his subject and can teach it well. He answers questions thoughtfully and explains concepts thoroughly (how particular formulas are derived) so that we understand better. Gave useful homework problems, practice exams, straightforward quizzes/exams, and had a bonus question on exams. 10/10 prof.

Chill guy, good teacher. Hw typically takes anywhere between 0.5-3 hrs per week, don't procrastinate. Show up to lectures even if you took AP, b/c theres content not taught in AP thats taught here.(I'm not talking about multivariable). 65% of your grade comes from the exams. Feel free to ask questions, although he can ramble on a bit when answering

Desmond Coles is an excellent professor with lots of knowledge about his course. It's not absolutely necessary to read the textbook before the lecture, because he will explain EVERYTHING in the lecture. 
However, it is crucial to not skip classes. Also just a chill guy, he's always wearing hats.

TLDR: don't skip class, do half the homework before

Good lectures, though sometimes he can ramble on about something y'all don't need. One question quiz every Tuesday and homework due every Thursday (20-30 questions). Quizzes aren't too hard and help you stay on top of material. 3 exams and a final, mix of mcq and frq. They're not too hard if you actually study and practice. Would take him again!
DESMOND!!! He's a great prof, knows what he's talking about and easy to love. He assigns a good amount of homework and quizzes but he tests pretty easy. Would def recommend!!
Overall very good professor and not a very hard class as long as you show up to lectures
I love Professor Coles so much. The tests aren't too hard, and the workload is manageable. I'd definitely take another math class with him.

Best professor who genuinely cares about his students and wants you to succeed. His projects are all based around something of your interest. Do the assignments, attend class, participate in class and you'll get an A.

He is a great professor, he cares a lot about each student and will ensure you do well as long as you show up and participate in class. Funny guy who tries his hardest to keep lectures entertaining and build a personal relationship with each student. Getting an A isn't automatic because there's a lot of writing assignments but grading is not bad.

3 papers & 1 project is the class. If you are a procrastinator like me this class will bite you in the butt. He doesn't give out 100's so if you are super snooty, be prepared to accept a 90-95. He's a funny guy... ish. the best part of the class is the late work policy which Is the sole reason to take his class. also no TA's. he grades everything.

I personally loved him (I am horrible at writing, btw). Go to his office hours, and he will help you as much as possible. The workload is manageable, not too much, but the grade relies on four projects, which are quite long, tbh. However, the assignments are relatively easy to complete.

Professor Shanafelt did an amazing job at making me enjoy class as well as improve my writing. We were assigned many assignments; however, they aren't very difficult. Your grade is very reliant on four big papers and three are 1500 words minimum. The only thing I disliked about his class is he doesn't give 100's.

Professor Shanafelt has been an amazing help to me and my writing skills. While I may not be a great rhetoric person, Shanafelt has always taken time out of his day to help me and the rest of his students, making us insightful, critical-thinking, and analytical students. I highly recommend taking him over any other RHE 306 professor!

I went into this class dreading it, I was always told I was a bad writer but Shanafelt takes time out of his day to help you. He also makes lectures so fun and he cares about you as a student. Dont get me wrong his class is not the easiest because you do have 4 major assignments but I would 10000% take him if you can.

If you're not a fan of writing, this class won't be your favorite. Regardless, Professor Shanafelt is an understanding and very passionate professor. Normal assignments are easy A's, essays are not as easy to get an A on.

I took his class freshman year and loved it. I love writing on its own but I think professor Shanafelt took it to a new level. He is caring and understanding. I think his writing feedback is excellent and there's not much room to complain unless you don't put any effort into the class. Just try and you should be good!

Most amazing professor I have ever had! Professor Shanafelt genuinely cares about his students and seeks to build connects within the classroom. Despite taking this class to fulfill GE requirements, his life advice offered throughout the course was profound. It was a honor to have him as my professor. Highly recommend his class.

i loved prof shanafelt as a person but super tough grader. offered an extra credit opportunity towards the end of the semester but even after i did it he dint give me the points. easier the professors out there.

Shanafelt is a kind, relatable, understanding, and knowledgeable professor. He is very accommodating while also pushing us to do our best. He cares deeply for each individual student as he learned all of our names. I admire his teaching style as he has several years of experience. He has positively affected my experience at UT.

Professor Shanafelt is an amazing teacher! He cares a lot about his students, and if you show up to class and put in effort, you will get a good grade. I'm not usually a good writer, but if you meet with him for essay help he will help you succeed. He makes his classes interesting and fun as well. Take this class if you can!

Attendance matters he will require makeup assignments. assignments due everyday before class and are graded based on completion. talks a lot though but has a bunch of useless grading criteria with his own website as long as you follow what he wants you can make an A, you could write a great essay but if your structure is off u can drop to a b

Great rhetoric professor! I am so glad to have had him. If you need someone to talk to, he is available no matter the problem. He grades fairly & enjoys a discussion between himself and the class. He knows when you are trying and rewards you for it! Lectures can be very entertaining but sometimes they go off-topic. I would take again!

I loved this class and the professor made it fun and interesting. Do go to class because it can affect your grade at the end of the semester. He is very nice and funny and you can tell he actually cares about his students and his job. There are three major papers and a project and they are not hard as long as you start them early.

reviews.comment: Shanafelt is a very kind professor and truly cares about his students. If you actively participate and ask for feedback on papers there's no reason you shouldn't get an A in the class,.

Professor Shanafelt cares about his students. reviews.comment: Professor Shanafelt is a great person and inspirational lecturer. He is very caring and wants everybody to achieve their best. You need to work hard to get an A, but Professor is always ready to help. It was the most useful class I've taken this semester.

reviews.comment: Shanafelt cares about his students but he is a tough grader. There are other professors for this course that are much easier. He takes off points for tiny errors.

Honestly, what kind of professor does not post their lecture recordings for such a lecture heavy class. We already have 10 polls per class, which questions are only shown in class. She also does not really lecture and just reads from slides, which questions her credibility as a professor. Seems like she cares more ab attendance and not teaching.

Exams are pretty tough, but you get a cheat sheet. One exam got curved. Content is interesting. Lots of it, but cheat sheets on exam really help. Dr. Jones is not always responsive. Takes days to respond to email but usually helpful.

Truly shocked by how little I learned in this class considering I studied weeks for the tests. She would lecture over a million things and then she would test you on the most useless things in the hundreds of slides. Expect to study for hours and still know nothing on the test.

reviews.comment: Never read the textbook and still ended up with 100 in the class. However, I did not truly learn anything from this class, except the information that I already knew about speech, as a SLH major. She taught very quickly with little to no additional explanation even when asked, but compensates by giving extra credit opportunities.

This class was so hard to keep up with, I feel like it was heavily catered to neuro students. Although attendance isn't mandatory, you have to go or you'll be totally lost. There's few grades and the 2 tests were so hard. Heavy material and no study guides for the tests.

Professor Tuttle is my favorite professor at UT. he is so caring about his students and its clear his passion for SQL. The one thing that really stood out is genuinely his ability to make a difficult subject so easy and clear for students. I thought learning SQL would be super tough especially having no background knowledge but he made it so easy

Tuttle cares about teaching and talks about his own experiences here and there. Class is not open note anymore. Course is also very content heavy and the semester I took it, it felt disorganized so that combination together didn't mix well. Textbook mandatory. Labs are meant to be helpful but felt like busy work. He's passionate for sure tho!
Take Professor Tuttle.

Best professor I've had at UT. Has the privilege to learn from him as a student and support him as a TA. Truly changed my understanding of data and how its become the new gold for businesses. If you have the chance please take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fun and cool professor, but the classes are flipped style so you have to be ready to read and prepare before class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Tuttle makes a dry topic engaging. Lectures are clear, and he cares about student success. Open-note exams and Unstuck ai make studying a breeze.

Class requires pre class reading. Good amount of HW and studying required but def doable. I would rate difficulty a 3.5/5. He really is a great and caring prof tho. Test are online and remote but very fast paced so you have to move quickly. Take it with him if you actually want to learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Incredible class and prof. You can tell he's put a lot of thought into the structure of the class - it's clear and reasonable. Lectures are engaging and effective. Non-mandatory attendance (except quiz days) was a lifesaver. Very receptive to questions/participation. Exams are open internet so it's an easy A if you get the work done.

Literally the GOAT. I've never learned more in a class in my life or been set up for my future. This class has directly been responsible for helping me land an internship. Professor Tuttle is the most caring professor who will help you in your grades BUT REALLY focus on helping you succeed in LIFE.
tuttle is a genuine and good guy who wants to help you succeed and provides the necessary resources to do so. however, grading can be arbitrary at times depending on your TA
great class, tuttle is a genuine and good guy who wants to help you succeed and provides the necessary resources to do so.

Professor Tuttle is the best professor I have had. He genuinely cares for his students and wants everyone to gain a deep level of understanding. His wit makes classes enjoyable. He allows for lots of practice time in class while he assists those who need help. Reading the textbook before makes the material easier to grasp. Open note exams.

Great guy! Made learning about databases interesting and explained concepts really well. Tests are open note and were not too difficult if you were familiar with the course content. Homework was tough but not impossible. Middle part of the course requires effort outside of class by reading the textbook and watching videos before in class practice.

This course could be renamed "Corporate Bloat" 374. Agile certainly has its place in software development, but this course prioritizes work unrelated to it. A friend of mine said only 20% of their work for the ending project was directly for the client. This should be flipped, but Clint would rather sacrifice quality software for micromanagement

Professor Tuttle is extremely knowledgeable over the subject and offers a lot of insight, even about things not directly tied to class. The class guidelines are rigid, but he cares and will offer as much help as he can for mostly everything.
He is really funny and makes his lectures fun and engaging. The homework assignments are kind of hard but the tests and quizzes are a lot easier.

Don't get the Tuttle hype. Heard great things about him, but I found him to be extremely condescending. He always praised asking questions, but would oftentimes respond in a snarky/rude manner. Pulled through at the end with a curve though, so grade-wise it's chill. Found the "reverse-lecture" format annoying since you have to teach yourself.

I honestly dont know what the point of the prof is if it's just going to be self taught. You learn from the readings that u have to do before class. He barely lectures in class and has u just do in class practice. He never gives enough time for the quizzes and it rude in office hours. On the test he barely gives u enough time to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class has an insane amount of information that you are expected to keep track of in a canvas page that is very oversaturated and the professor is not the most understanding about mistakes that are made or things that are done non traditionally. The grading is mostly done by the TA's and is fine.

This class is pretty much self taught. you have to read and learn from the book because his class is just practice problems and the amount of pre class assignment he gives out is insane. He also gives you quizzes where he doesn't even give you the time he promise he would give. His instructions are also very confusing on HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He will preach that he's a "helper" type enneagram but ask him for help and be prepared to be met with the most passive aggressive comment. He will also make a lot of jokes about how much work he does to prepare for the class and interview potential clients, and yet his lectures have been reused possibly since his first year teaching the course.

Tuttle has got to be one of my favorite professors at UT. The class was hard and required a lot of effort from the student, but Tuttle makes his expectations clear in order to succeed. His philosophy for teaching really matched my personal learning style but I can see how that might not apply to all students. He makes being an MIS major fun!

Reverse classroom format. Read textbook before class. Exams are open note. Make sure to review slides, demos, and homeworks for in-class quizzes + exams. Attend office hours. Overall, Clint is a wonderful professor and he cares about you. His textbook readings and demos are REALLY helpful for homeworks. He sang for us on the last day of class.

Although it was a hard class for me, he does an amazing job breaking down what you have to do in order to succeed. Make sure you get ready to read and participate in class. Gives amazing feedback. Exams are slightly tricky with wording, read the textbook and you'll be good.

Clint is okay, but he's very overrated. Homework instructions, installation directions, and test questions are very confusing because he doesn't use punctuation when he types. He can also be a little bit stubborn when "answering" questions. The SQL part of the class is good, but the rest is a bit of a drag. The last day lecture is very inspiring.

The textbook was really relevant and easy to understand. The material gradually grew in difficulty, but skills grew quicker. He's really involved and in-class practices are helpful but rarely graded. 

The class is easier with a buddy to discuss things with, but 10/10 would recommend.
One of the best professors at UT. Period. Class is not hard and he makes learning interesting. Go to the Huddle with Tuttles!

I am not a fan of coding, but he made it more manageable. There is a lot of reading/homework, so be prepared for that. the quizzes are pretty difficult imo bc they ask very specific questions. the exams aren't too bad bc they are open note. tuttle is very accessible outside of class and truly wants his students to succeed in his class and onwards!!
Tuttles class is interesting but he does get easily irritated so be extra prepared before class and only ask thought out questions. Overall would take this class again because it is so organized!

Listen this man is clearly passionate about databases and I really appreciate that. But never in my life have I had to spend so much time outside of class just to learn the material. Recorded 45 min lecture + textbook + lecture in class + lab + weekly homework that takes hours on end. If you have that kind of time great, if you don’t- be warned.

reviews.comment: Professor Tuttle was just awesome, he made learning about databases fun and engaging and the in-class activities and labs are extremely helpful for doing the homeworks. His tests are not bad if you have a general overview of the material and do the homeworks as thats where the material actually starts to make sense. Overall, great class!

I had professor Tuttle as a professor two years ago and all I can say is, absolute king. Hes very engaged and cares about the success of his students with out regards to their career choices. Hes knowledgable and someone who encourages you to think and do better

Tuttle is my favorite professor after this semester. Test questions are sometimes tricky, but nothing that they don't go over in the reading. Class mostly consisted of independent reading, going to class for him to answer questions, and doing a coding lab with a group. He made the class fun. Read everything before class and do all labs to get an A

He's an awesome professor. Doesn't take the course too seriously and basically wants you to learn. He is funny too and will randomly bring up stories of his past and will bust out his guitar and start singing on the last day of class so make sure to attend. His Excel game is off the charts btw, I really recommend taking notes.

I took MIS302F over the summer and it was super chill. He released all the modules at the beginning of the session and finish the course in 3 weeks if you wanted. Wasn't too difficult, most of the time as long as you paid attention to his videos you can do great on the quizzes. Final wasn't hard either, started studying a day before and got an A.

Databases with Tuttle was great. He was very conscious of how students felt in his class and really did everything he could to make sure we were comfortable. A lot of hands on during class, so watch the pre-class recordings and at least glance at the book before you go. Overall great choice for MIS 325.

Take Clint for Databases! I took him online for Fall 2020 (COVID) and loved it. Attend office hours to get to know him, he's so cool and friendly. Homeworks aren't too bad, use the book, tests are open note, content is easy to grasp, but don't fall behind or you will be lost! Class is less lecture and more hands on, so you really learn a lot.

I really didn't like this class, but that's not on Tuttle. I enjoyed his enthusiasm, but I did find his lectures quite draining. I struggled with his tests/quizzes for sure. His slides are super helpful, and you won't pass without paying attention to his lectures.

I was so glad to have gotten off the waitlist for Tuttle's class. Definitely worth it. If I had any doubts about switching to an MIS major, this class diminished them all. Tuttle is super passionate and it is so obvious. It's amazing to learn from someone like him. Definitely a class that requires you to put in the work, but you will learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor! Make sure to do all the readings before class so you understand the lectures. This class is highly dependent on what group your in so make sure you know people in the class so you can have a good group. His grading is tough and will leave you frustrated since it is very tedious, but he is fair with final grades.

Honestly, I had to learn most of the material on my own outside of class. The class setup was that we would read the textbook and then come to class where we would ask 5 mins of questions and then do "in-class practice"... on material that he hadn't actually taught to us yet. If you want to learn anything at all in this class, read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clint is an amazing professor. When he isn't singing songs about Excel, you can find him in his office helping students with their course work or talking about life. He spends a lot of time preparing his course and truly cares about his students success.

This course was overall not to bad, but you do have to put in the work if you want an A. The final exam was worth 40% of the grade so even if you get 100s on everything the final can tank your grade and the required grade for an A was a 94. The writing assignments and excels werent too hard, and tuttle and the TA give feedback if messaged.

Good guy but it was his first semester teaching MIS325 and it showed. Class was kind of unorganized but TAs are helpful. He does random pop quizzes so try to go to class. I generally did better on homeworks than exams and quizzes just because homeworks use SQL while you code by hand on exams and quizzes.
Very passionate about MIS. Might get a little irritated in class but overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took his first semester teaching MIS 325, and it was not good. He is one of those professors who thinks his class is the only class you take. No organization to the class whatsoever. Unreasonable when it comes to grading. Exams, quizzes and homework are difficult and will take you a lot of time.

Tuttle is fantastic. I highly recommend for everyone to take at least one course taught by him because he is inspiring, always there for the students, and pushes knowledge over grades. Hard work pays off. I learned a lot about what I wanted to do as a career from him! SAM hw are simple, read the txtbk, & always go to class. Tests are tricky!

Prof. Tuttle gives great lectures. His online class is not hard at all except for the final. 60% of the grades are weekly assignments and the other 40% is the final exam. Questions in the final are all new questions, so you need to review everything not only just old quiz questions. He gives two extra credits and curves the entire class in the end.

Amazing professor who truly cares about his students. He's always trying to give extra help on Excel assignments and the assignments were either graded by a computer system (with 3 attempts allowed) or peer reviewed. He also gives chances to argue your grade on the peer reviews. Test material was not word for word from class, so studying will help.

HIGHLY recommend taking this class online. You have 2 assignments (usually a quiz and an excel or a paper and a n interactive quiz) due every sunday, but that is it. There is also a final at the end. Took up basically none of my time and I did not mind it at all. For sure the best way to take MIS

It was a pretty straightforward class. A few assignments due every week that make up about 60% of your grade and one big proctured final at the end that makes up the other 40%. Contrary to other reveiws, the final was not old quiz questions so make sure you do go back and review the chapters before you take it.
Tuttle is a great teacher. Took his class even though I didn't need it. Was worth it. Not a difficult class.

I've had the honor of taking some fantastics professors at UT, but Tuttle is hands down the best one BY FAR. He's very inspirational and clearly cares about his students. Although this class requires a lot of work, I would one million percent recommend it.

Professor Tuttle is the best professor I've ever had at UT and one of the greatest people I've had the chance to meet. I think that he is one of the nicest and down to Earth person and is very passionate about what he teaches. The class is also very informative but he makes it very understandable in lectures and notes. Loved every minute of MIS302F

Incredible prof! Tests are super challenging if you don't fully understand the material so utilize office hours. Would sometimes do in-class surveys so basically pop-quiz for attendance. Tons of hw thru excel spreadsheets so if you aren't familiar with it you have to learn how to work it. Everything in his class can be applied in the real world!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tuttles online MIS 302F class is one of the easiest As at UT. The class is pretty straightforward, though it does require time, but not a lot.

Clint is a good person, motivational coach and mentor, but not necessarily the best lecturer. His lectures are unclear most days, and he wasn't able to build a clear lecture style at all during the semester. He knows what he's talking about in terms of MIS content, but he isn't great at communicating it at a easy-to-understand level.

Overall, the online class was pretty straightforward. It was clearly outlined and had all of the information available. Requires a little bit of reading, but not anywhere close to the average amount of reading in other classes. Lecture videos really help more than the extra readings. Study with friends and definitely do the extra credit!

Professor Tuttle was one of the best professors whether or not you do business his class is very interesting and the projects quiz and discussions are doable. The final is easy if you did well on the quizzes and studied the questions. The class is taken for those trying to get a business certificate but I would recommend it anyone overall.

MIS 302F was such an awesome and informative class! Tuttle is an amazing professor and explains everything very well during lecture and makes sure that we fully understand everything. Textboom is online and you just have simple readings. However, Tests are pretty tricky and hard but study guides are provided! DEFINITELY WOULD TAKE AGAIN!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pretty doable overall. The class is super interesting. Quizzes at the end of each unit that are open note. No midterms. ProctorU final is all old quiz questions.

Clint Tuttle is one of the greatest professors I have had so far at UT. His lectures are clear and helpful. The material is useful for your future as a business professional, and if you pay attention you will come away with tons of interesting IT information. Be prepared though, the material is very dense. Take time and understand every concept
Clint is one of the best professors I had at UT he taught me way more beyond class material. He is truly interested in helping students.

Answers to unit quizzes are online, only pain is the interactive quizzes. Excel assignments get harder, but if you spend time on them, you'll eventually figure it out. Self paced class, so it's easy to get ahead and vice versa. Don't bother watching the videos and reading the articles tbh. Final is recycled quiz questions.
Super cool professor, seems to really enjoy his job.
Outstanding professor, large work load though just a heads up!

One of the best teachers I've had at UT. Lots of components such as quizzes, assignments, group projects, participation surveys and tests. You'll learn so much in this class.
So entertaining. Best teacher ever.
You will do alot of work, but I have learned alot. It is worth it.
Dr. Turtle is a STRONG atheist and he lets you know it. not a day went by when .he didnt let you know that he had not gone to church. where has our countries moral compass gone. Not with this man

Professor Tuttle is great, and the online modules were very thorough. Though many people have recommended that you work with others, I found it completely manageable to do on my own. Work load is as expected, and as long as you put some effort into it, you'll do just fine and will likely learn a great deal.

Prof. Tuttle was great! Find a buddy or group to do the work with ASAP. It helps a ton!!! There are 10 units, consisting of a quiz, activity and excel assignment (which stop at unit 7/8). Only exam is the final, which is easy if you study the unit quizzes and notes. Prof. Tuttle also gave 3 EC opportunities! You have to work for an A, it's doable!

reviews.comment: Prof. Tuttle was great! This class had to grow on me, but as the semester went on I started to appreciate it more. Find a buddy or group to do the work with ASAP. This class was an elective for me, and it was worth taking it! Thanks to this class, I can confidently say that I'm skilled at Excel. This class wasn't hard but it takes a lot of time each week. If you manage your time and spread everything out during the week it's manageable but I saved everything for the weekend and would take 6-7 hrs. Final is just recycled quiz questions. Quizzes are easy. Excel assignments are a pain. I never did any of the readings and was just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT

Do the extra credit!! It bumped me up from an 87 to a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Clint is very nice and he really tries his best to not have a boring class. There is homework and book readings before every class but its definitely manageable. reviews.comment: The class is an easy A if you have some experience with Excel & a basic understanding of IT. Assignments/exams are always graded and returned within a week. AMAZING  AMAZING AMAZING.

reviews.comment: Clint is one of the most genuine teachers I've ever had. Approachable, honest, and a nice guy. Excel and HTML coding were a little annoying, but if you know how to Google, you'll be fine.
Really well put together online class. I would take again! stay up to date with declines and know excel, you will be fine.

reviews.comment: Tuttle was by far my favorite professor this semester. He cares about learning more than the grade which is so refreshing. This course covers material that is relevant in any field, so everyone should take it!! There's some reading, but it's college so ... who cares? After Monday's events, he was truly caring regarding feelings. Tuttle: a true gem.

Professor Tuttle is one of my favorite professors I've had at UT. He's very entertaining, caring, and good at making class interesting. This was an awesome class with valuable knowledge, so I'd recommend taking it even if you don't need it for credit!

This online class is SELF PACED. I devoted 1 day a week to this class and got an A. The excel assignments can be tricky, but  if you have a friend in this class you'll be fine. Excel assignments are the worst. 3 tries seems easy? Wait until you get stuck with little direction. Do not underestimate the HOURS you will spend doing these time wasting assignments. Reading quiz were ok.

reviews.comment: Good teacher, keeps lectures interesting and entertaining. You get quite a bit of homework, however if you stay on top of it its isnt a problem. If you just pay attention in lecture, class shouldnt be too tough.

This class was an insult to my intelligence. It was easier than a regular high school class. Online 10 mc quizzes 60 minutes, all the answers come from the videos,notes or google. Not a good experience with the online class.

reviews.comment: I took an online class with Professor Tuttle and his prerecorded videos were very educational. The class was well taught and thorough. First of all FANTASTIC professor! Before entering the course, I had thought that I knew quite a lot about IT, this class taught me otherwise. reviews.comment: Tuttle is amazing. He uses his past journeys as from former consulting jobs & failures in life experiences to help his students succeed. Recommend 100%

Probably the best professor I've ever had. Tuttle is one of the rare professors that actually care about their students and their futures. While the class does require a lot of work, it's completely manageable. Just go to class, pay attention, complete all the homework assignments until you get 100, and you should be able to ace the class.

This class was amazing. I learned so much and wish I was a MIS major. The online class was easily accessible and fair (unlike many other online BFP classes). This is one of those classes that I will remember forever and use the skills I learned in this class in the future.

Guys, y'all have to take MIS302F with Prof. Tuttle. First of all, he is an AMAZING lecturer. This wasn't even a class for my major or minor, but it's been the best class I've taken at UT. So many useful skills that we learn and he does a great job teaching them in a fun way.

You could tell straight off the bat that Tuttle cared about his students and cared about the information. He cares more about learning than the grading & most importantly... He preaches "everything is going to be ok"

One of my favorite classes and professors at UT. There is a good amount of work for the class though; but all the homework is practical for real world jobs. But I admit the work Load gets frustrating .

TAKE THIS CLASS, NEVER LEARNED MORE, going to his class is not just a drag, I want to go to class. It is in a big auditorium but he cares for ever EVERY student. Tuttle is truly interested in his students and is an incredible lecturer. I heard from a few other students that Tuttle was the professor to take if you wanted an awesome class. I'm so happy I took their advice. I learned quite a bit of excel too. Homework and readings weren't bad at all and I really enjoyed his selection of material. Fun Class. Fun Professor. I'd definitely recommend him.

Tuttle is a great teacher! He is VERY PASSIONATE about making Excel interesting and easy to understand. Come to class and enjoy the showmanship! WOW lets just say I wish every class was as entertaining as his. Very helpful when asked a question and wants everyone to do well. Definitely one of the best UT has to offer. YOU ROCK TUTTLE!

By far my favorite professor at UT. I would hands down recommend him to any student who wants to sit in an awesome lecture and learn useful skills for the future. You'll WANT to go to class because it is so ENTERTAINING! He'll help you learn and make your semester very fun. DON'T MISS OUT ON THIS GEM. Thanks for the fun semester Tuttle :)

Let's just say my boss is happy that I know excel :) Thanks to Tuttle that is!!! Clint is an outstanding professor! He's really hilarious and just an all around cool guy. He explains concepts extremely well and is there for you. He wants his students to come out of this class well prepared. I loved his performance in the end and i'll miss it.

Clint Tuttle is a UT LEGEND!!! This guy is freaking awesome and if you don't take him, you're missing out on one of the best classes UT has to offer. You'll hear fantastic stories during class and his presentations is something all professors should learn from. He prepares you for the real world with excel. HW isn't bad and its doable. TAKE HIM!

Tuttle is an awesome and funny guy. He is there for his students!! Take him! If you're having trouble understanding the material, ask in office hours. He's really helpful! Sit in one of his lectures and you'll realize that this guy is a GEM! Passionate about his subject and very inspirational to students. I would definitely take him again.

Great guy 10/10. If you get the chance to take professor Tuttle you definitely should! He wants his students to do well. Seriously, he is very fair and helpful with all the material. He knows some students might struggle with excel but trust me when I say he knows you'll use it in the future. You will! Fun class and this is one class you'll want!

HANDS DOWN one of the best professors at UT. The readings aren't that bad as some make it out to be. Tuttle has a panache for story telling and keeps lectures fresh and exciting. He teaches applications of excel and makes the material easy to understand and keeps you interested. I definitely left Tuttle's class feeling prepared for the real world.

EXCEL HELL. Tries really hard to be cool in person then DUMPS you a metric ton of homework. Does a guitar performance in the very end. The whole class does an applause because we're done with all the multi-hour SAM assignments, excruciating EXCEL, and super boring readings again. I'll literally throw up if I hear another LAME-O Excel song. 0/10

If you are on the fence about taking this class - don't walk, run the other direction. Clear out a few hours at night and get ready to read until your eyes fall out. I hope you're not taking weed-out core courses along with MIS302F this semester because you're gonna have a bad time. So much unnecessary HOURS of homework. Would NOT take again.

Have you ever watched a Kia or Hyundai commercial and think to yourself "Oh Wow amazing car!" Then after owning it for a few weeks realize a few things? Let me save you some time. Really, would not take again.
Hands down the best teacher i have ever had. 12/10 would reccomend. You will actually WANT to go to class!

One of my favorite professors ever. Really, the assignments are lengthy but they are not hard. He gives detailed instructions for EVERYTHING. Great lectures. Easy quizzes. Easy group grades in class. It is not hard to do well in this class if you keep up. The only thing that is hard are the tests. Just make sure you study and do the readings!
Brilliant Entertaining lectures. Horrible, infuriating assignments. 5-mile treadmill-boring articles.

Would not take again. Get ready to devote huge part of your night extremely long, boring articles. HTML was infuriating and Excel assignments are pull-out your hair horrific. Entertaining lectures but the class does a 180 turn on assignments. Will drop you off a cliff on assignments - you have been warned.

Took his online class but wished I took it in person. He's a really nice professor with clear criteria. Excel heavy- but for BFP students, Excel is a pretty useful skill to have. Easy to make an A but a good amount of work (none of it too hard, though).

Great professor, I actually went to every single one of his classes, even though they weren't mandatory. His test are alright, they're easy as long as you keep up with the readings. He sings for you at the end of the semester, and he's hot af.

Tuttle is awesome. The class is not hard but you must participate. The tests are easy if you study his ppts. Its the HW that is more time consuming (SAM excel assignments). He is very inspirational and teaches life concepts along w his course material. Very fun and a really interesting lecturer.

I hesitate to recommend this professor. Take another electives class. The reviews were too good to be true. Way too much reading like 30 page assignments. wtf. Excel was a nightmare. HTML wanted me to pull my hair out. Not what I was expecting at all.
Class is not mandatory, but you will want to go! I learned so much about top dog businesses and HTML coding. And you really dive into excel, which is a must to know these days! amazing class!

This class is really interesting and the stuff you learn in here will be very beneficial for your career.  Not too difficult to get an A or A-, but there is a lot of work you will have to do.  You also probably will grow to dislike Excel.  Clint is one of the best professors I have ever had here, but he definitely has a bit of an ego.

TUTTLE ROCKS. If you put in the work, you'll make an A. I learned so much in this class that will make me competitive when I am trying to get a job, highly recommend this class for anyone and everyone.
Clint is fantastic, but this is actually a class that you need to be on top of- mainly B's on tests (averages of classes).
Amazing professor! His last lecture of the semester is the best one! Really inspirational

He's a good professor who cares about helping students. However, there is soooo much unnecessary work. Way to many readings and so many assignments. Also there's group work so be prepared. He says the readings are light but it's literally at least 30 pages per class and the articles are pretty boring.

Tuttle is one of those professors you'll still remember when you're 50 years old. He's just hilarious and smart and really, truly cares about his students. His office hours are great for class help or just for general lifecareer advice. The class isn't hard, but it's not a blow-off either. I'll miss yelling "TEXAS! FIGHT!" before every exam.

Tuttle's class was better than I thought it would be. The topic is not the most interesting, but I feel like he did a good job making it as fun as possible. So many assignments about Excel; that was the worst part.
Basically only came to this class every time because Clint if hot af and he is also hilarious. Super worth it

His class really isn't too hard. Go to lecture and take good notes. Skim the reading he assigns so you know the key points and terms before class and go back over whatever he discussed in class afterwards. Start the homework and Excel assignments early and you should get full credit on each one. Tests got easier. Use the study guides to prepare!
Class is fairly easy, and Tuttle is a nice guy and tries to keep class interesting. I didn't really find excel or HTML assignments useful.
awesome dude. really will do everything to help his students understand, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND GOING TO OFFICE HOURS. fun class, extremely interesting and useful just for life
Great Prof! He is dedicated to all of his students and keeps you entertained! I'm about to finish this course and am sad to leave it. I love how encouraging he was to all of his students!

Great professor. Entertaining, smart, connected, and loves to teach. Go to class and take good notes, and go to office hours for help on assignments. This guy is dedicated to teaching this class and really wants students to do well. Great introduction to business technology and a motivational teacher. Would definitely recommend this class.

absurdly overhyped. Lectures are easy (just sit there). During lectures... it's best to let him talk.. trust me. Do not comment or be noticed. Excel HW sucks so bad. Tests are heavy on the reading.. the questions are not straight forward either EXCEL HW is horrible? If you have trouble, visit HIM - not the TAs for HW help.

He will make you squirm with excel. Heavy reading..definitely NOT an easy A. Test questions are worded to confuse you and not very straight forward. READ and know the material front and back. I made an A in the class...barely. lots of busy work with excel. Don't think you can blow off this class. LIKE OMG BEST PROFESSOR EVARR!!1!... .not really.

Very good professor and very funny. Class is not "an easy A" but if you do the readings before class AND go to every lecture, it makes getting an A easier. I had some trouble with the Excel assignments because I'd never used it before, but overall I enjoyed the class.

Such a good professor. He's interesting and he's funny without even trying to be. Before every test he has his class do Texas Fight. Genuinely cares about students but will make you learn on your own. Holds you accountable for your grade. For me, NOT an easy A. Lots of Microsoft Excel! DO THE READINGS. Tests were harder than expected. Pretty hot.

Best Professor I've had at UT so far. Presented the information in an interesting way and made me want to learn it. (I even considered switching majors.) His lectures are amusing, and although the class isn't super easy, he is very approachable and provides plenty of resources to get any help you may need.

Tuttle is awesome. He's a younger guy and you can tell he loves what he does. His tests aren't too bad, but there are some tricky questions. Homeworks are easy (since you get five attempts at them) and the readings are simple. TAKE THIS CLASS! You'll learn more than just business-stuff from Tuttle.
Great professor. He's fun, interesting, and seems to really be there because he wants to. Highly recommend any course that he teaches!
By far the best professor. His lectures are interesting and engaging. Don't miss out in a great professor, highly recommend this class!

Professor Tuttle won the 2012 Texas Exes Teaching Award (nominated by students) AND it's only his FIRST year teaching. That pretty much says it all. Go to class & you'll definitely learn and laugh. Clint really cares about you learning the material & he makes class entertaining.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. He makes class really enjoyable so you want to attend lecture. Read the book + look over the power points = A. Earning an A isn't super easy, but it's definitely manageable with Clint.
Aww I'm gonna miss this class :( I recommend taking it cuz the instructor is AMAZING! He is very helpful, and did I mention awesome!? Take it! I highly recommend it. He is the man!

CLINT TUTTLE WAS AMAZINGGG! Keeps class fresh and fun. Homework is consistent but not overwhelming. Fair amount of reading. Reviews help focus notes for test. Highly recommend going to his classes. He is young and very understanding and willing to make things work for the learning purposes of his students.
Great class and instructor. The lectures are interesting because they are based on actual companies.
Great class! The lectures are interesting as the examples the instructor uses are already occurring in the real world. Take this class, I highly recommend it.
The man.com

Funny interesting Lectures; if you read the chapters and read the powerpoints he uses in class i'm sure you'll get an A. Its easy to follow along in class because the examples he uses is stuff we know, like facebook, netflix. take it!
Funny guy, just seems to get off topic most of the time during lecture as he rambles on about his personal life like we care. But overall he provides good examples of the material.
Fun lectures.

Great guy, great teacher. Keeps his class of 300+ interested and involved in his lectures. Gets really good discussion out of his class and is always willing to talk. Reads all his emails and students constantly email him information relative to the class. Take it, it is fun.

Professor Michelle was great for an entry-level class. I had her 4-6 pm, and for being such a late and long class, she kept us actively engaged. She taught us a lot of dialectical differences and has a lot of experience teaching languages. I struggle a lot in school and she helped me feel more confident.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Michelle cares for her students and goes above and beyond to ensure everyone is understanding the content. She answers questions without condescension and enthusiastically. If you have never taken Spanish before, the content will be difficult with any professor, but I wholeheartedly recommend Michelle.

Prof Crabtree does very well at managing her personal life with her graduate studies and the classes she teaches! She goes above and beyond teaching wise and offers some immersion experiences (ie brought gazpacho to class)! I hate the Spanish dept at UT, but she made this class more than tolerable and goes the extra mile to make up for its faults.

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. class is completely disorganized and TAs have no idea how to grade. with one of the TAs you can barely understand what she's saying and is always making mistakes when grading or doesn't know how to explain assignments so you end up confused. don't waste your time taking this class.

this class is ruining my life. the professor doesn't know what's going on, the TAs don't know, nobody knows. this class has one of the worst TAs i have ever encountered, which is who grades the assignments. big mistake, bigger regret. do NOT take this class.

Good grief, I'm so glad this course is over. 
Interesting material, and Dr. K is super caring and helpful... but this course was a disorganized wreck. If you didn't go to office hours frequently you'd be stressed out of your gourd. Unclear, constantly changing deadlines, assignments not published until the due date.. But it did all work out fine...

Honestly, nobody even knows what this class is about. Easiest A ever, but everything is super disorganized, and I feel like most of the things that are taught are extremely elementary level and are odd to be taught in a college class (venn diagrams, flowcharts, mind maps, etc). No words to describe what a confusing experience this was..

Took this class bc the rmp reviews said easy A but very tedious and disorganized. I thought "Why are y'all ranking her so low if you got an easy A?", I now understand the ratings and truly do regret taking this class. Half-way through the semester people stopped showing up bc of how boring the lectures were. 2 hour class full of nothing.

Professor Crews' lectures feel disorganized and uninspiring, making the already dull course even harder to engage with. Her grading, especially on participation, seems inconsistent and unclear. While the class is an easy A, her condescending tone and unpredictable expectations make it frustrating to sit through.

This professor was extremely unorganized. She did not follow the syllabus and I ended up learning nothing. I dreaded going to this class but it was the easiest A you will ever get. Take a fun UGS with a good prof instead of this.

This professor was extremely unorganized with the opposite of clear grading criteria. I hated going to this class even though it was the easiest class imaginable. Take a fun UGS with a good prof instead of this.

DO NOT TAKE HER. Can't believe an upper level course could be this disorganized. She gives us assignment deadlines but never posts the instruction until the due date and brings so much anxiety. The assignment is meaningless. I still have no idea what I am learning even if it's already 5 weeks. FYI we spent a whole class to make a name tag.

This class was extremely disorganized and I learned little to nothing after its completion. It is an extremely light workload with many unclear assignments. She clearly cares about what she is teaching but I don't know what she is teaching. Take a different ugs that is fun and easy and not just easy.

I gave her a 2 because it was easy to get a high A. However, I didn't learn a single thing and I don't even know what the class was supposed to be about. Very disorganized, doesn't follow the syllabus, and even TAs didn't know what was going on. Instructions never made sense and assignments were pointless. Lectures were boring, but she is caring.

Dreaded going to every class because the class was highly disorganized. The assignments were confusing and the TAs didn't know how to help most of the time. It's clear Professor Crews is passionate about teaching, but it was hard to enjoy her class when it's so chaotic. In the end it was an easy A, but caused a lot of unnecessary stress.

Honestly only giving a 3 because she seems passionate about what she teaches. Other than that, lectures are optional and hardly useful for assignments. Assignments are sometimes tedious (especially the last few) but still pretty easy to get an A. I just felt like the content was uninteresting, so mostly better to take a different professor for UGS.
uhh wtf is this class. take it for the flags and dip. More useless class ever lmao. also its a free A. Take it for the flags + free gpa boost. attendance is not required
Unorganized. I don't know what's happening in the class, and the lectures don't make a ton of sense, but at least it's an easy A.

The course is very disorganized. Everyone in this class does not know what's happening in the class. Homework assignments are very boring. Although the class is an easy A, it was a pain to attend the lectures.
Dr. Crews's lectures are all over the place. They often have no clear message. They usually don't focus on the course topics.  The work is really easy.

Crews is nice, but her lectures are all over the place. No topics are connected to each other, few are connected to "our global backyard," and content is either something covered in middle school or just completely irrelevant to college. Workload is light, but the instructions for assignments are usually unclear.
I took her for our global backyard and the course was organized horribly with no clear criteria but its an easy A if you just complete every assignment. Attendance is taken r

Super disorganized, lectures are all over the place, didn't really learn anything. Assignments especially IE's (take home long assignments in place of exams) don't make a ton of sense and take forever but its an easy grade. Only reason why I gave a 3 is because its almost impossible to get lower than an A if you turn everything in. Tons of ec

Easiest class ever. Idk why people complain about this class, it is literally an easy A. She cancelled half of the classes throughout the semester. The assignments in class are extremely easy and braindead. Take this for your UGS, there are no exams and not really any readings.

I took this UGS because I thought it would be interesting but I literally haven't learned anything. Just a pain in my butt at this point and I just want to get it over with. Attendance isn't mandatory but she gives out in-class exercises almost every class day, so if you are not in class you miss out on the grade.

dont take this class for an easy class. 
i did after reading previous years' reviews, but i guess the prof increased the difficulty now; graded very harsh, assignments are stressful and meaningless to me, and disorganized.

Pros: 
- Extra credit is offered frequently
- Class assignments, such as watching Social Dilemma, really make you think about society.

Cons:
- Unorganized, unpredictable class
- Seemingly easy assignments are graded roughly
- Busy work
- Huge busy work exam due during spring break
- Watch out when she says "Hint hint" - its not a good thing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Take classes that are meaningful to you, not to complete flags

lecture attendance not mandatory , discussion sections once a week in-person and is technically mandatory but u can just take a picture of the QR code. Grading heavily based on your TAs (mine was hella lazy and didnt even grade my extra credit). Lecture are useless, theres only one assignment per week and theyre always short about 15-30 mins to do

Crews is purposefully vague so that you learn to be "creative" but is looking for something specific. So frustrating AVOID. You will get a B no matter what but may lose all your hair from frustration. The syllabus gets practically thrown out the window after day 1 and is so unstructured. There is a fair bit of extra credit. Just don't do it
AVIOD THIS PROFESSOR. While

prof likes her job but does not follow the syllabus at all tbh. we've covered maybe 50% of the material that was on the syllabus. the TAs are what really affect the class bc they give instructions for assignments but honestly don't make a lot of sense. the class always has surprise assignments due randomly and the instructions aren't very helpful

Don't take this class. Dr. Crews does not follow the syllabus whatsoever and did not cover more than 60% of the content included in the syllabus. Descriptions of assignments are incredibly unclear and you will get 9/10 assignments every time unless it is considered "above and beyond". TA's not helpful. Extreme lack of communication from prof and TA
I learned absolutely nothing but we watched District 9 in class so yay!

Easiest UGS! Guaranteed B by contract if you show up, very easy to get an A (especially through tons of extra credit). Required to buy Packback for $60 to write weekly 300-word assignments. No tests, only in-class pop assignments, and weekly writing discussions. The class moved online/was canceled very frequently. Very receptive to feedback.

Dr. K was very caring and understanding for this UGS. Super easy class as long as you went. Felt like some students were quite disrespectful to her which was sad to see. Would recommend taking this UGS if you want an easy class.

She is so sweet and loves her students. The course will have a weekly written assignment 300 words on an AI tool called Packback that we had to purchase for $60. She is really unorganized. Lots of extra credit. Lectures are confusing and assignments are random. If you complete everything she guarantees a B+, but this class is an easy A if you try.

Kelley has such a kind heart. She is really passionate about what she's teaching and cares about her students a lot. However, she's very disorganized and all over the place. She kinda just rambles in class then gives random assignments. That being said it's very easy to get an A in this class if you do everything and there's lots of extra credit.

GRG 440L, "Landuse/landcover change". The lectures are sometimes redundant (which may be a good thing) and boring. There were only a few quizzes for the lecture, and they can be easy if you try. The labs with the TA were pretty tough. We used Google Earth engine, with coding involved. Pay attention and participate to pass.

Due to the flew, class was canceled a lot. We watched over 5 movies/documentaries in class. Your TA will grade your assignments and the rubrics are not followed. If you want an A you will have to be active about going to office hours and asking for things to be clarified. Pop quizzes are held to check attendance. She really wants you to participate
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 10% Discussion Participation, 30% Discussion Assignments , 60% Quizzes. You take the 4 quizzes at home. 1 of our quizzes got dropped because the teacher was sick for 2 weeks. You get 3 extra pts. on your FINAL GRADE for 20 hours of volunteer service!! 90+ is an A. This class is still not easy tho! Most ppl would have gotten a B if no dropped quiz.

The material in this class is very relevant and the work load and assignments weren't tough, but this class was EXTREMELY unorganized with inconsistent grading from the TA's. 100-150 word assignments due every week, four short answer quizzes, random extra credit attendance checks, and no +/- system. Still not worth the stress. Take a different UGS

she missed 2 weeks which made the course very unorganized. your grade literally depends on your TA's grading and its very inconsistent. you never get feedback so you never know what you did wrong. quizzes(4) were short confusing. she dropped the lowest quiz for us but honestly take another class. it wasnt worth it. we watched like 10 movies overall

This class really just frustrates me. Never give a rubric for our quizzes and don't really know what to expect for them. TAs and professor is really unclear and claim for it to be super easy but the tests get really specific things gone over in lecture.

do NOT take this class. the assignments are super easy but they are graded incredibly hard by the professor and the TAs. The professor is super judgemental and tries to justify the horrible grades for the easy assignments and also does not have neutral political views, which even if you agree with you still get a bad vibe about her attitude.

This class was an EXTREMELY easy A. You just have to show up for the super random attendance checks and write one essay a week (500 words) which is graded so easily I would write the morning they were due and get a 100. However, Dr. Crews is very zany and scatterbrained. She goes off on massive tangents and class can be exhausting to sit through.

She is nice and class is very fun! Very easy UGS class. You should get an easy A unless you don't do homework. 500 words paper every week. Extra credit is doable. Fun topics and we see 3 movies during the semester.

The class as a whole was the easiest thing ever. You have to go to class for the random attendance checks and the only other grades are weekly 500 word essays that take like 10 minutes to write. Overall, super easy A. However, I hated Professor Crews with a passion. She is condescending and impresses her beliefs upon students which IS NOT okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy A class I showed up and did my other classes homework in there every single lecture and probably didnt learn a thing, she cares about attendance with random attendance sign ins,  but still very easy UGS class and if you go to TA office hours you can lowkey fix your mistakes on essays and they'll give you a 100
Best possible UGS class

This is the BEST UGS you could take. She only assigns weekly 500 word essays that are graded super leniently. No tests or final- just an easy final exercise. Some in class participation grades, but not many. She is super interesting even though I'm only taking this class for credit. Super fun class I recommend for any Freshman.

She's very entertaining and experienced in environmental studies having traveled extensively to research. She's very clear in her lectures and although her tests are super detailed she's a very good professor and if anyone can make 8am class fun it's her

Love love love her! Thoroughly nows what she's talking about, has street smarts about economics and the environment, and really cares about how students do in her class. Easy to approach with questions. Not too difficult of tests, just have to know the material and specific facts, and short lab writeups outside of class. GREAT PROFESSOR!!

This class is not that hard but is still harder than most other UGS classes. I don't think it's worth it to take this class. Dr. Crowhurst is nice but unclear with her grading scale and lectures are interesting at times (and on zoom) but not enough to outweigh the negatives. If you end up taking the class, make sure you talk in class to get an A.

This class was pretty interesting, Dr. Crowhurst is really passionate about what she is teaching. You do have a term paper and a group presentation, but they aren't really all that bad, you do have a lot of time for them. Overall this class wasn't all that difficult.

Typically, each week consists of Powerpoint lectures in class and 1-3 readings outside. Some of the readings were a bit long and boring, but if you find at least 1 thing to discuss, you will get participation credit, worth 10%. For the W flag, there are 3 journal entries to connect to other experiences, as well as a major research paper.

If you can take LIN372K with the other prof who teaches it, skip her section. Grading criteria is unclear and it's impossible to meet her standards. You could have everything right on an assignment and lose points because it wasn't worded how she wanted it. The class experience was stressful.

Prof Crowhurst knows a lot and is really interesting to listen to. Some of the readings are a bit lengthy and seem a bit unnecessary. My biggest complaint would be the lack of structure in the course. The lectures can also get a bit monotonous with her just reading off powerpoints. She was nice and pretty accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had a lot of trouble in her class trying to meet her high standards. A lot of the material was difficult to immerse myself in and I felt that half the time she expected us to understand concepts that are near impossible to grasp with the way she explained them. I also found her a little abrasive in her individual critiques on hmw. Not a fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had her for two classes, did not enjoy either. She thinks you know more than you actually do. No matter how much you contribute, it's never good enough for her. I have accommodations because of a disability, but I rarely ever felt accommodated in her class. It feels like none of my work resulted in anything to her standards
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very likable and intelligent prof. The material itself is quite difficult IMO but she tries her best to help the class: moving hw due dates, EC, giving points back. Weekly hw and only 2 exams so make sure you go to class and put effort in. She is from Canada so one of the best things is hearing the way she pronounces certain words like "schedule."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Took Language, Cognition and Rhythm with her and was really disappointed in how little she actually knew about music and the brain. She even said during one class that she doesn't know much about music and even though she had us discuss neurosciencey papers in class, she was hardly able to answer any questions about the technical aspects.

Sounds Patterns was difficult class, even for Linguistics majors. I really had trouble concentrating. There are some concepts you'll really get, and some that make 0 sense. Homeworks helped a little. I felt like she thought we understood more than we really did
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Drops lowest HW grade, offers HW replacement assignment at end of the semester and offered extra credit to participate in her study at the end of the semester. Go to class, she will round your grade up at the end. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

This prof isn't the worst but complicated. At first she is nice, but then I realized she uses rhetorical devices to single out people she didn't like. It made it tough to learn anything, trying to constantly sift through her maze of points to figure out what was important or not. Her grading reflects a corporate agenda not correctness. I'd avoid.
She's pretty nice, but honestly, I was bored in the lectures. It's kind of a tedious course, but the material is fairly easy to master. Homework was imo much harder than tests.

Dr. Crowhurst understands her knowledge. I enjoyed every lecture because the complexity of the material meters well with the explanation. The class consists of cutting edge research so come prepared to have your mind blown. The writing assignments will leave you tired but not exhausted. Plus, if you find new research she will try to incorporate it.

She really knew her stuff about everything that she taught, didn't use notes at all. Super interested in the topic, and had a clear and effective learning plan for the class. It was definitely worth the time.

funny and overall sweet professor but can be disorganized at times. that issue sort of goes away once you enter the simulation. TAs can be nitpicky with grading but that is usually offset by EC points offered during the simulation; go for a leadership position!

Lectures first half of semester and then attendance matters for second half (the simulation). Lectures are common sense, and she just rambles, so not really necessary to show up. Simulation is fun and attendance goes toward your participation grade for these days. Extra credit offered. If you don't end this class with an A+, that's your fault.

Dr Craig is a GEM. The mock senate simulation may seem daunting but it is actually easy to earn participation points. I had a health crisis and she was very understanding and worked out a way for me to get more credit to make up for what I missed. Okay so she may not be the most organized person lol but she's so funny and fantastic. Take her class!

Dr. Craig is awesome! Her class is taught as a senate simulation, but she takes from her immense knowledge to support students in the class. There are 6 total assignments, one of which is an exam that's based on her lectures - which are funny and helpful. You'll want to attend class, especially in the simulation, but the classes are lots of fun!

Took US Congress with Prof. Craig. Class is largely based off of a senate simulation, where participation is important. She gives lectures that are funny but also can seem somewhat unorganized. There are 6 assignments including 1 exam, all of which are easy to do well on if you pay attention in class. Overall a fun and easy class and professor.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Legare is a very nice person and she's very highly educated in her field, however attendance was mandatory so if you took one day off your grade would go down, she threw random assignments at us then later told us it was for extra credit, and the TA grades the exams harshly. Very insightful class but not the best I'd say.
I really enjoyed this class. I looked forward to attending Dr. Legare's lectures. The class discussions were engaging (and entertaining!)

Do not take this class. 6 exams, and you will literally never get comments on your exams or how to improve on your essays.  You wont even get your last exam grade back until you are already taking the next exam.  TA is a horrible and harsh grader for no reason.  You are never told what they are expecting for the exams so it is impossible to do well

Dr. Legare is a wonderful teacher and person. I took her CSR class Fall 2025 and can easily say it was my favorite. She talked during the whole class but was interesting and engaging. She expects you to read the textbook and come to class with understanding. She then connects dots and helps synthesize. Tests are written but questions posted before.

The best class I've taken at UT. Amazing lectures, cool projects, and all of the exam questions are posted in advance so you can prepare. It is a writing flag class so (obviously) expect to write. Not an easy A but you will learn a lot.

Very disappointed for how this class turned out. Don't get me wrong the lectures are engaging (somewhat lol), but the exams being fully based on the textbook AND we don't even discuss it at all is crazy work. Waste of time, so save yourself from learning common sense stuff about religion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can take another professor DO SO! She is an amazing lecturer and a god in her field but her class is made up of 6 exams that revolve around a textbook she DOES NOT USE IN CLASS.Her TA was a very harsh grader. There was also random projects not included in the syllabus but they were worth the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This isn't an easy A but I learned so much in this class. I enjoyed the course content so much I decided to do research in her lab. Highly recommend.
This was my favorite class this semester. Loved her lectures and the class discussions. Attendance is part of your grade, but if you attend, this works in your favor.

She was incredibly vague about how attendance would be graded. If you take this class, GO, it will make or break your grade. The class sounds way more interesting than it actually is, and was extremely boring in my opinion. The TA grades too harshly and is extremely unhelpful. This class is boring and, honestly, kind of difficult. Don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best class I have ever taken. Legare is my favorite professor at UT hands down.

Dr. Legare is really funny. When she did show up to class, she was hilarious and the best lecturer I've ever had. She's just a really harsh grader, and the questions to the test were so unique that feedback for one couldn't apply to the next test. I seriously considered dropping the class because my grades were so bad.

Loved this class so much I applied to be a research assistant in Professor Legare's lab. Class material is very interesting. I really enjoyed the group projects. There are lots of exams, but you get the questions in advance to prepare.

There are 6 exams 3-4 questions each: 1 pg essay per. Questions release 2-3 days before. Exam time was shortened from 90 to 75 mins
