reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hated this class, she didn't teach us a single thing and you're forced to learn it on your own. Believe me, she's not a good teacher, and it feels as if she hardly cares about her students.
Not as bad as everyone else says. She isn't the greatest but not the terrible teacher some make her out as. Although, her attitude rubbed me the wrong way sometimes.

It's a flipped classroom so technically the learning is done online. Lectures aren't necessary to attend except for REEF quiz points but you can sometimes get extra credit for participating. You could honestly learn an entire unit during the week of the test. I recommend going to her review sessions - she will tell you exactly what to study!

Don't take her for this class, you basically have to do everything yourself as she doesn't explain a single thing in class. All she does is give clicker questions and speeds through them for attendance so that's the only reason to show up.  Otherwise, all the work you have to do is at home and it's long and grueling. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I wasn't pleased with how the course was thrown at us. It's a learn by yourself and get quizzed in class everyday. She is insanely boring, and wow they need to work on getting interested curriculum. Also, she has office hours in a room that can sit no more than 4 or 5 people max and she teaches hundreds off students in each class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She doesn't teach. All she does is does in class is online polling and "experiments" that are suppose to reinforce what you are learning. THERE ARE BETTER TEACHERS. Avoid the hassle that is LaBrake.

Literally worst teacher ever. Does not teach anything all she does in class is mix salt in water every day or some other demonstration. Has never taught any topic or had us take notes on anything. In the process of dropping or switching teachers.

Not a bad teacher, and I suck at chemistry. However, is a flipped classroom, so be expected to read a LOT. If you memorize everything and regurgitate everything you're good. TA review sessions are really really helpful and probably the reason why I did well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Labrake often goes off on a tangent and gets distracted easily. It is hard to follow along and she does not make sure the class understands what she is teaching before moving on.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class wasn't bad at all, but there are better chem teachers. The tests aren't hard at all, you just have to look for old ones before you take them and go to reviews. You have to put in some effort in the class to get an A and actually show up as there are grades for attendance. Flipped classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed taking Dr. Labrake's chemistry course this semester, considering my horrible experience in high school. I held a strong prejudice towards chemistry until I took her class, and am happy I did. We learned some really cool things and look forward to next semester with her. With that said, I had to work really hard for my grade.

Flipped classroom was nice because it meant that I didn't have to go to class except for the polling. I would slack off until the week before the exam and then learn everything online through Clutch or the learning exercises. Hard material but if you put in enough work its manageable. I also wish tests were curved because its easy to mess up.

Basically, if you do homework on Canvas and go to class, this class isn't that hard. There is online polling that happens during class, but you can do that at home if you need to. Because of this, technically you don't need to go to class but I would suggest it. She's a pretty good teacher, even with the 200+ students class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is very straightforward. Do the learning exercises and homeworks then go to class to review over what you learned outside of class and ask any questions you have. Attendance is not mandatory but you do have to answer questions through an app that are posted at random times during the class that are easy to miss if you're not present.

As a Chem major, I saw this class as being a solid introduction to Chem and thought that the Prof did a good job. While the class is very crowded, the lectures a bit less helpful than I would've liked, and a bit of a heavier workload, I thought she was a funny and engaging teacher.
Flipped class and lecture were awful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A funny professor, but she is not clear in class and often rushes over things. Her tests are hard and there is no curve or forgiveness in them. A good TA and asking TA's/PLA's questions during class is essential. There's also a lot of homework and learning modules to do on your own outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very nice person, if that matters to you when looking at a professor, but lectures run off topic very easily and it is hard to understand what the professor is trying to say. Tests are fairly easy, but you do have to study many days in advance if you want an A.
Awful class. You won't learn anything during class time, but attendance is still taken via an online app every day and its a huge waste of time. The only way to learn is if you have a good TA

She literally spends more time trying to figure out her computer than teaching. Don't learn anything in class. Homework and learning modules all online. The only way to learn is from TA lecture hours. Will not do anything in class.
cool
This class was definitely a flipped classroom. Laude/Labrake was a very good combo. Class was interesting and tests were easy-medium if you looked at review videos and attended office hours.

This class is really taught by three professors, which is an interesting set up. It's a flipped classroom, so you learn the material and quiz over it and then review in class that week. They all really care about the students understanding the material and doing well in the course, and test expectations are made crystal clear. Highly recommend.

Ch 301 is easy because she is only the secondary professor (either vandenbout or laude as primary), and thank god for them. She gets distracted very easily, and it's questionable whether she even knows the information. Not to mention she is extremely rude in a "trying to be funny" kind of way. You cant really avoid her, but just be prepared.

Make sure to pay attention because she tends to ramble and you'll want to follow her train of thought. She is also a little disorganized. However, she is very approachable and you feel comfortable speaking up in that class even though it is a 500 person lecture.

Cynthia is a good professor, however her lectures can be extremely boring. They drag on for what seems like forever! Some of the material is really dense too and she doesn't do a great job of explaining. Be prepared to have to read the book and go to ALL of the TA's review sessions (they really help).

Very good professor. Ch 302 was a bit harder than 301, but it is doable with the grading they have in place. They use a "blended" classroom style instead of completely flipping it, so some learning is done at home but they still lecture over it to reinforce it during class. I found this helpful since all of the materials were online.
Fairly easy and simple class, I'd recommend her.
Easy Class, Easy Tests, I enjoyed going to class. Good professor

Expect to pay attention in class or be very lost! Clear lecturer when she's on a roll, but loses her train of thought often. There's in-class worksheets for most lectures which are good if you like working in a group. Quest HW is challenging but similar to the tests. There's also a free response portion to the test similar to the worksheets.
Make sure to keep up with everything. If you do, you'll be fine. 4 Exams(60%)(One Gets Dropped), Participation Points(15%) (iclikers,hws,learning modules), Final(25%).
Excellent prof, makes the material very engaging.
she really cares about her students learning the material, this is a flipped class so there is an expectation to do the assigned homework in order to do well

Always excited to teach chemistry. Gives out candy to students that participate. Pretty straight forward on the material, though most you learn through modules. Homework is on Quest and tests are Quest-based.
4 tests and a final, but drops the lowest grade
She is a great Professor and makes lecture worth going to!
Labrake is a really great teacher. I highly recommend her. Her lectures are fun and she covers material really well.

LaBrake is awesome! Her lectures are very fun and interesting and she keeps the material very concise as to not overwhelm you much. She is a very fair grader as she offers times for extra credit points.  Above all, she is very funny/smart and really cares about the progress of her students! I highly recommend her.  She rocks!

labrake is an awesome teacher who cares about her students. the notes are online and are powerpoints. if you ever have any questions, she is readily available to help you. the class is pretty easy and the final exam was not heavily weighted. i recommend her as a chem prof. and plus... at the end of the semester, we made ice cream. =)
No Comments
Do yourself a favor and do not take any classes by him unless you are dead set on graduating late or want to suffer.
This professor is the WOAT - Worst of All Time!!! Do not take at all costs! I promise you, he wants you to fail!!!
The result of the first exam came out after being delayed for an entire month. Half of the class who stayed and being toturede is at the edge of falling the course. No curve. No exaggeration.
Worst class I've ever taken!

I might have to drop his class and not be able to graduate on time. On the last test, I only knew the answer to maybe 1 question bec he was not clear about the material. And just so you know, there were multiple people in the same boat as me, 10 other people I know in this class also failed! UT Austin if you are seeing this review.... fire this guy

In his lectures u cant learn -- he goes on random tangents and forgets what he is even saying

HE WANTS U TO FAIL

Screw this guy honestly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relies very heavily on the textbook (can be found online). Take-home assignments require a lot of hours. In-person exam allowed notes. Will send announcements late at night. Halfway through the semester none of homeworks were graded, and if they were we got a negative grade. He had no idea what our grades are in class, gave all that power to TAs.

Very smart and kind professor, gives great insight into the topics but does not speak very loud and lectures are very disorganized. In-class quizzes are not too difficult and he gives you the topic beforehand. Exams are fair with a take-home portion, and the assignments require citations which are annoying but aren't bad after you get used to them.

This class is just bad. You have to cite every single question on a homework from the notes/textbook. You have to do homework on paper so you have to type all of the math. Homework only 5% of grade with daily quizzes being a large part of your grade. The quizzes are over things that we weren't given any examples over in the notes or textbook.

Announced the final 2 days before over a topic he did not teach. Half way thru the semester he chose to have a quiz for every class due to low attendance but he doesn't teach! he rambles abt nothing!!! In the quizzes he'll try and trick you by finding synonyms to basic terminology (e.g: cost of usage instead of price). Super full of himself AVOID

Lectures consist of poorly-prepared rambles about IRL examples that he doesn't even remember (he makes students Google the answers in class). Formatting requirements for homework/quizzes/exams are STRICT and cause more points loss than wrong answers. He's unclear, uncommunicative, and, worst of all, disgustingly smug about all of the above. Avoid.

Very rude, goes on multiple tangents and doesn't teach the topic. He likes to ridicule, cold call and say his quizzes are super easy when they're not (he admits he likes making students life difficult). He has lecture notes and recorded lectures you can watch outside of class, so thats nice. I'd avoid him if u can. tbh he needs to retire.

Far and away the worst professor I have taken at UT. Likely tenured. Citations and footnotes for every homework question and if they aren't in his exact format you get a 0. Quizzes every other class. Sits down and can barely hear. Stay away if you have any common sense.

reviews.comment: easily the most annoying professor I've had at UT, please just take any other eco elective
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall not a hard class, Sibley is a super interesting prof and has a lot of experience. The homework and exam formatting can be annoying at first, but becomes increasingly easier as you go on. Exams are take home and are easy enough. Definitely recommend this class and professor Sibley overall

His lectures are boring and not useful. He announces quizzes the night before. It's easy to get a B on them, but impossible to get a 100. He has strict rules for formatting and citations, which are tough at first but get easier over time. Homework can be either really easy or really hard. The exams are worth 75% of your grade and are take home.
This is my first time leaving a review. This class made my life miserable. The grading criteria were unnecessarily strict, making every assignment excessively difficult and frustrating.
His classes really aren't that difficult. the work may seem complicated, but the grading is actually not that bad. Also, the exams are all take-home and open note.
One of the worst econ professors, please take someone else. He needs to retire ASAP

reviews.comment: Sibley likes things done a very particular way, but once you get the hang of how he wants you to cite and submit homework then it's easy. Sibley announces quizzes the night before class which count as your attendance.

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken

reviews.comment: He is a well respected, intelligent, and funny professor. The other reviews are from students who don't pay attention in class. Weekly homework, and exams which 70% of the grade is take-home!

Don't let the bad review fool you, he is a very good professor. He has high standards for his students but they are very achievable if you just pay attention in class. He is funny, tells interesting stories, and he gives thoroughly helpful guidelines.

Sibley should retire, he fears the use of AI to cheat more than his students learning, so there are COUNTLESS guidelines, where the smallest error will result in -10pts on homework (even if you have everything else right). please just switch majors. every single econ professor is phucking awful. if you don't get accepted into mccombs, CS, or engineering just quit and go join the military or start onlyfans.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: RUN! An absolute dinosaur that prides himself on being technologically illiterate. It's a joke that someone as out of touch as him can work this high in academia. He has countless arbitrary guidelines just to waste your time and make the class overly difficult. Professors like him hinder the progress of human thought by clinging to the past.

Syllabus should deter you. Assigns excessive pre-lecture material (75min videos, multiple readings) for each class, then lectures on other topics. Random facts can be tested on. Lectures are BORING. You'll spend hours just formatting and citing HWs due to his 15+ pages of rules. Read a book if you want to learn antitrust or business strat
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: No attendance. All format for hw and exams are online, typed, with CITATIONS from any class material (textbook helpful for citations). type your math; mainly profit maximization. Gives a day in advance for in person quizzes. Can work with another person. 3 exams but quite long to do. Super knowledgable guy, easy A.

Lectures can be really slow, but he sometimes tells interesting stories (sometimes repeats). Has annoying citation/formatting policy designed to force AI users to do the same amount of work. Weekly homeworks with application-based take-home exams (Exam 1 has in-person %). Gives one day notice about quizzes. Sometimes can be pedantic just for fun.

Scared ppl to drop bc class was too big for his liking. 1 hw every week. Has a tedious guideline to format every submission, has 10 page formatting guide. Once you get the hang of it its easy, but was stressful the first 1-2 weeks. Exams are harshly graded, very easy to get partial/miss pts (online, 1st=in person). Lectures=boring as heck. Easy B.

He is such kind and funny professor! Homework, quizzes, and exams are very fair, and it helps that exams are take-home and done with a partner (if you wish). Grading is done completely by TA. Professor Sibley truly cares about his students and wants them to do well. Would highly recommend taking him!

This class will feel like a chore. You will have to come to in-person lectures where he rarely teaches but will give out random quizzes, and you will also have to watch 75-minute videos where he actually teaches the course in depth. The quizzes, homework, and exams aren't difficult but the lecture situation makes the class time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU NEED AN UPPER-DIVISION ECON COURSE. The class is in person but all homework's and exams are online and you have a week to work on them. I personally never went to class, and the prof says he'll have pop quizzes but never does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had a great time in this class. It was easy but honestly one of the most functional and useful courses I have taken in Economics here at UT. I can echo the last post he is very much fun kooky grandpa vibes. He shares a lot of interesting stories about his professional experiences and other real-world applications of the material.

The class is organized and straightforward. Prof. Sibley is your cool grandpa with impressive educational background. He gives a lot of intriguing real-life examples when he teaches. His extensive exposure to the industrial world is what makes his class practical and useful. Would recommend it to those who are interested in consulting or business

Best professor I have ever had. Period. He prepares very well for each class, homework is perfect complement to class because one is about understanding a subject whereas homework is about producing it. He is funny, knowledgable and everyone has a good time during his lectures. I would recommend him for ANYONE who meet the requirements.

I love David Sibley so much that I'm taking another of his courses! If your funny grandpa was an Econ lecturer, it would be Sibley. His exams are straight forward, but does require understanding of the material and the homework/quizzes are 70% participation. I never read the required textbook, only class notes and did better than the average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: David Sibley is undoubtedly the best professor I've had whilst at UT. He conveys everything as clearly as possible, and encourages you to critically assess scenarios that you may be tested on. There are no cookie cutter solutions, and you will be trained to think analytically. Take him if you genuinely want to learn.

Professor Sibley is kinda how you hoped college professors were going to be. He teaches you a lot of material with minimal work outside of class. The exams are pretty straightforward with no ambiguity. If you study the notes, you are guaranteed an A.
Best economics professor I've ever had

Professor Sibley is one of the few professors at UT to ever hold a real job. As a result, he has direct experience with the subjects he teaches. The workload for this class is relatively low. He will scare you into studying about 3 times what you need to know for exams, but will set you straight during exam reviews.

Great Professor who makes the class interesting. Got me into economics more than I cared in High School. Tests are easy if you keep up with homework and rework practice tests them before the test- one of his test was almost identical. Final is not bad, a tip is anything he said was going to be on a test that was not you should study and learn.
Tests are not difficult but the final is impossible. Got a 65 on the final but still ended up with an A because of the curve. Do homework and you'll be fine.

3 tests and a final. He drops your lowest midterm grade. Read the chapters and take notes during class and you'll do fine. The midterms are almost identical to the reviews so pay attention to them. The final is much harder than the midterm- you'll leave thinking "wtf?". However, it's curved and you  just have to do better than your classmates.

Great prof who wants his students to understand the material well and is very helpful during office hours. There are 3 midterms and a final as well as one HW and one quiz per week. The midterms are a breeze as they're nearly identical to the practice exams he posts online, however the 2nd exam can be a bit tricky. Expect the final hard, however.

Sibley's class is a manageable A. He takes time to ensure that no one is confused  and is very helpful during office hours! There are 3 midterms and a final, as well as one HW and one easy quiz per week. The MTs are a breeze (nearly identical to the practice midterms he puts online) although the 2nd one is tricky. The final is difficult however.

Great Guy. Incredibly intelligent. He appeared in court on the Microsoft Antitrust case and dealt with the T-MobileAt&t merger which highlights his knowledge of the subject. I would reccomend his class to anyone. He is helpful, clear, and knowledgeable.

Sibley's supposedly not as bad as other professors, but he's still really difficult. Read your book--that's the best resource. Midterms, homeworks, and the final are pretty brutal, but you drop the lowest of each at the end of the semester, and there's a slight curve on the final grade.
great professor! super easy class as long as you read and pay attention in class. midterms are easy and similar to past exams.

sibley is a pretty smart man and great professor (tho he goes off on tangents quite often). very straightforward tests though. pretty easy. one exam drop. weekly hw. weekly quizzes (super easy, mainly for attendance). final is on another level, however. more difficult. but sibley does offer a curve (thanks to his wife apparently). highly recommend.

Graduated from Stanford with a Master's degree from Yale, so he's a smart guy. The tests are easy, quizzes are extremely easy (mostly just for attendance on Fridays), and homeworks are doable with collaboration from classmates.

Microeconomics is not a very interesting topic to begin with, but this class was bearable and not difficult to get through. Quizzes on Fridays for attendance, and the tests are pretty straightforward if you read and generally pay attention.

Intro to Micro. 3 Midterms, 1 gets dropped, homework due every week, quiz every week just to check attendance (they're open note/book). As long as you study for the tests you'll do fine but the final is a shock and will likely bring your grade down. Sibley is really nice and helpful though. interesting class!

Overall, the class was very fun and definitely improved my french skills. If you aren't consistently keeping up with your french then the class will be considered more difficult. However, Prof Kahozi is always available, willing to meet with his students, & he wants them improve their french skills. He's easy to talk to and he's very understanding!

Took him for FR322E and wish I could have taken him for FR320. Show up to class because participation is mandatory, and things covered in class go on the exams. Quizzes were probably the hardest aspect of the class, but still an easy A if you put in the time and some effort. Merci Daniel!

I took both 320 and 322 with Professor Kahozi, and I really enjoyed his classes. I definitely struggled with some parts of these classes, but overall, Kahozi gives lots of opportunities to improve your grade, so that was never something that concerned me.

This class definitely reduced my love for French. The average on most of the quizzes was close to a 40, and people were not given their accommodations even after asking for them multiple times. We had to rely on the book to teach us majority of the material. Super difficult for me despite learning French for years. Would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Reflections due every class day except test days. Lots of reading. Tests aren't difficult as long as you understand the main plot, themes, etc., so you don't HAVE to read the whole book, he goes over most of it in lectures, which is mainly discussion. Super fun, interesting class and you learn a lot about culture and conflicts in Africa. Great guy!

Dr. Mishler doesn't seem to care much about current research, nor is he interested in spending time with his students in the lab. If you are a box-checking, obsequious pre-med, then he may be a good fit. If you are serious about science, look elsewhere.

Was decently approachable as a Research Methods professor, but as soon as you research under him (FRI or independently), he seems to hate undergrads. He very much "fosters independence" by making you figure things out on your own even when you barely know where to start and then being condescending when you make mistakes.
Consider other streams...

I think Dr Mishler does really care about everyone in this stream but sometimes has a hard time communicating that. He comes off intimidating/condescending but then shows up with his little treat hot chocolate. I think hes a good person but the way everyone's head swivels to the door to his office every time it opens has got to say something...

Mixed emotions about this "class". I learned so much and this is a great resume booster, but it sucked the life and soul out of me. This was exactly the first stepping stone into research that I needed, but it takes over your life. Trying to balance 4 other science classes and this was not it. Mishy genuinely cares but is intimidating.

There's a reason for his reputation. Verbally and mentally abusive if he arbitrarily decides that you've done something wrong. Workload is much greater than other streams for limited upside if he likes you and large downsides if he does not. Beware.

Dr. Mishler receives a bad rep, but after being in his lab I think it is unwarranted. He has been one of the best professors I have had at UT and truly cares about your success. He is kind but I feel it can come of the wrong way. But if you are a freshman, please consider this stream. You will learn so much and I think it is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: First semester of FRI was the hardest class I have taken at UT. The quizzes are very difficult and the lab reports are pretty long, but there are resubmissions and the mentors are really great. The second semester is not as difficult, and everyone in the lab and Dr. Mishler wants you to succeed, just do not be afraid of asking for help.

First semester with him in FRI is absolute hell (harsh grading, lab reports, quizzes), but the second semester is super chill (90 for an A, easier lab reports, no quizzes). Lots of students are scared of him during the first semester but once you get to know him he's really nice and approachable. Be ready to commit 6+ hrs a week in lab though.

"Tough grader, high expectations, occasionally condescending, out of touch" for some students
"Genuinely cares about the learning experience, forgiving, curious" for others
You have to WANT to learn the course/content to experience the latter, bc if I had students that didn't want to learn, I'd be treating them the same as the 1 or 2 star reviews.

Dr. Mishler wants you to succeed. The Microbe Hackers FRI stream is an amazing way to get into research and is one of the most engaging streams. However, it is definitely a lot of work. If you like research and want to thoroughly learn about the research process, this stream is for you, but expect to put in >6-8 hrs a week. Very rewarding imo tho

Mishler's FRI stream was super stressful. It is hard to put into words about how I truly feel about this stream. There are definitely days where I just want to burn my laptop. However, I truly believe that this is a class that everyone should take at one point. Mishler is really tough (bordering on brutal), but he does offer plenty of chances.

Dennis Mishler is a tough professor, prepared to be humbled in his class. He can humble you both in D&D and w the lab reports. Also, when you attend his office hours, he would belittle you for not knowing something and keep bombarding you with questions related to the topic. He also needs a bit of emotion because he was so monotone. Great guy!!!

I've never hated research more because of this stream. Dr Mishler definitely ruined my research experience. Incredibly rude and inconsiderate at times. His assignments were brutal and he was never helpful. Hides in his office all day, while his mentors CARRY the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: So much reading, writing, and the quizzes are difficult. He comes off as "nice" but in a very condescending way. He made this stream much harder than it needed to be. The adjacent stream, BioBricks, had a much more understanding and compassionate RE. Everything is in the readings; his lectures are useless. Thank god for the mentors!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
You'll need to put in the good effort to get a good understanding of content. 

With that being said though, if you're really passionate about research, take him! I am one of the lower performing students with lower self esteem, he's supported me through embarrassing failures. believe me when I say he wants to help you succeed in your endeavors-

This stream absolutely ruined my confidence in myself and in research. Dr. Mishler advertises this stream as "rigorous" but really is unnecessarily hard. On average I spend 15hrs a week on it just to be insulted during our lab quizzes, where you have to read out your quiz answers and be publically embarrassed. Dr. Mishler is rude and out of touch

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! Being in his stream was so rewarding, even though it can be rigorous. This stream is a pretty big time commitment, but everything we do is super cool and has a purpose. Be ready for weekly quizzes that are pretty hard and thorough. All of the mentors are fun, engaging, and are willing to help you out
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Mishler designs his class structure off the suggestions from previous years' students and also REALLY cares about his students. He's stoic at times, but wants you to succeed. This stream is gonna test your mental rigidity and grit, so be prepared to gain some really good research paper-writing skills and confidence in your lab techniques.

I had Dr. Mishler for my FRI stream, Microbe Hackers, and loved him and the class. He is an excellent man, professor, and researcher who has taught me so much this semester. The stream is definitely not a walk in the park and there is a lot of work, but it is so worth it. One of the best professors I have had this entire year.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Mishler cares a lot, but the way he goes about can be so frustrating. Get ready to work and learn outside of class because his lectures are fruitless when it comes to assignments. Luckily, the mentors come to save the day. I wouldn't say I learned a lot, but my tolerance to schoolwork has gone up. My advice, just pick a different stream.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Mishler is very passionate about his FRI stream, however he is FRUSTRATINGLY and UNNECESSARILY anal. He doesn't believe in perfect scores and will find ANY way to deduct points. His class and workload is very demanding and TIME CONSUMING - students with poor time management skill & that are taking many other classes may struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My hardest class to date but one of the most knowledgable professors. It's hard but you get sooo much out of it. Mentors are great and he's also very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Mishler has poor people skills and is tough to understand. It seems like he is unwilling to allow students to express their ideas. He can be very condescending and indirect, and doesn't give very helpful feedback. I wouldn't take a class by him again.

It's been a learning experience being in his stream. He is a tough professor, very meticulous, there's decent amount of work, BUT you will learn A LOT and be thankful for it once the class is over. Lots of opportunities to get help and he does genuinely want everyone to pass, and mentors are AWESOME. Don't be afraid to approach him for anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you asked me at the beginning of the semester I would have told you to never take Dr. Mishler. This lab was very demanding compared to other FRI labs. I spent around 6-10 hours in lab depending on the week. But, at the end of the day, I can honestly say I learned so much from Dr. Mishler and am very grateful for the experience in his lab.

Don't take this lab. If you want to enjoy your time at UT and enjoy research then this lab is not the way to go. You have to attend so many meetings a week, plus your scheduled lab time, and extra lab time. It's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mishler is overall very passionate about his work, however his people skills are lacking. Often times he comes off rude and condescending even if he isn't trying to be. This lab was difficult, took up a lot of time and requires lots of work so unless you genuinely care about bacterial DNA, this lab will be a pain for you.

Somehow I feel abused and depressed by the workload in this class yet I still come back. Mish requires an enormous amount of time but also has valuable experience. Unlike easier labs you learn a lot here and gain valuable resume experience for post-grad school. Tough decision but choose betw knowledge or ease. This class proves mutual exclusivity
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS LAB. I would only recommend Microbe Hackers if you are extremely, extremely interested in research. This lab takes about 10 hours a week and is so extremely difficult. I don't recommend at all. Do yourself a favor and take an easier lab like other people and enjoy your college experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Microbe Hackers FRI stream. Dr. Mishler is the single best RE I've ever heard of. He's always available to students via Slack or email. He absolutely NEVER judges you for asking questions (even if they are stupid) and is overall a very nice and smart guy. Microbe Hackers is no walk in the park, but TOTALLY worth it. Dr. Mishler is even more worth
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: MOST frustrating class I've ever taken. He knows the material but there's no grading transparency, class feels punitive, and you're always scrutinized not supported. Minor situations can escalate quickly, and Prof is unwilling to understand/assume good faith. FAR BETTER profs who teach same material but actually cares. Avoid if you can.
Erik Dempsey is certainly one of the best professors in political theory at UT. This class is excellent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: While I don't love philosophy, Professor Dempsey still made sure that the texts we read were interesting and relevant to a common theme. Class grades came through in-class essays and pop-quizzes which challenged you and forced you to study but were still very manageable. Lectures were not very engaging, but the discussion sessions made up for it.

Dempsey is fantastic. This was my first time taking a class with him, and he can be a harsh grader, but you really improve over the semester. Expectations are clearly laid out. Lectures were mandatory but always interesting. There are insane amounts of reading that you must keep up with to understand lectures. DO THEM. And talk to him out of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have never taken any philosophy classes before this one and Professor Dempsey made the subject very approachable! Highly recommend him for CTI courses, he is a great speaker and is very knowledgeable. As long as you do the readings, take notes, and ask questions, you will be successful. Course is well-organized with clear expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: AMAZING! Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. TAKE HIM if you can! Genuinely changed my perspective on so many things.

Dempsey is an amazing lecturer. I was introduced to so many new concepts through his lectures, and they genuinely made me think about the nature of the world. Definitely encourage speaking in class, as attendance/participation is graded, but he also has very interesting answers to questions. The readings are tough, but he explains them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He seemed nice in the beginning, but made people feel dumb and worthless. Readings were difficult, had barely any assignments, and major favoritism towards certain students. Dude also needs an attitude check.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Dr. Dempsey. This class was a bit difficult for me, but Dr. Dempsey makes things so simple and clear in lectures that even if the reading was difficult, you gain more understanding during class. Heads up that there's a lot of reading. We also had pop reading quizzes, but if you read the reading, you're fine.

I would definitely recommend Dr. Dempsey. While he grades a bit hard, I really improved from his feedback on my essays. I also enjoyed the lectures and assigned reading. He creates such an enjoyable and fun learning environment, which allowed me to learn a lot from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: such a great professor. lectures are super engaging and interesting and dr. dempsey is wonderful at explaining tough concepts.

His classes are seriously some of the best I've taken at UT. Lectures and discussions are deeply philosophical, fascinating, and genuinely fun. Papers (and the class itself) are challenging in a good way. Dr. Dempsey himself is kind, witty, extremely knowledgeable and invested in the material, and fosters camaraderie among his students.

Wonderful class. Dempsey is amazing and cares deeply about his students and the material itself. He is VERY knowledgeable about the material and a joy to be around. Some of the best lectures of my time on campus. He makes classics accessible and valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was def hard and requires understanding of the text. The readings are manageable though. I recommend getting your essays peer reviewed before you turn them in bc they weigh so much. Final Essay exam is actually much easier than expected, just prep in advance. Dempsey is super unique and engaging. Makes you dig for answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dempsey is one of my favorite profs. He's funny, knowledgeable, and approachable. Lectures are a bit difficult to follow sometimes due to the nature of content covered, but had a good time in class regardless. Lots of reading, honest feedback on papers. I'd take his class again, for sure.
Professor Dempsey is highly accessible, accommodating, and fair. If you attend office hours, he will give you proper feedback and you can rewrite papers. Great class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was excellent with a lot of insight on all the material that was covered in the class. He does assign a lot of readings that at times can be hard to understand but he puts out study questions to help make sure you understand the readings and will go over the things read in class for further clarification. He really cares for his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Dempsey is a very unique professor, and I would recommend trying to take his class. He grades fairly, but you do need to participate and read to understand the material. Thankfully, his lectures are easy to follow and thorough. On top of that, he truly cares about education and his students.

Prof Dempsey is a great and personable professor. He really wanted me to improve and graded essays on how much I could improve. During office hours, he wanted me to gain confidence in my writing and when I argued in class, so he graded my essays on how much more confident my writing became. He is a bit disorganized regarding course content.

Love Dr Dempsey! He's one of the best prof in CTI department. Very knowledgeable, easy to talk to during office hours. Class is mostly reading, discussion based, with papers. He's a harsh-ish grader but gives excellent feedback. His lectures are interesting and invite you to ask deep ?s. He's open about biases but excellent about perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dempsey is a kind and knowledgable professor. There is a bit of reading but it is by no means overwhelming and you can skip around a bit, because you can choose the prompt you write about for the essays. He is accessible and would host office hours on speedway, which was enjoyable. He allows rewrites, is a fair grader, and gives good feedback.
I learned more in this class than most other classes during my undergraduate career. Do the readings! Reading the texts is crucial to get a good grade *and* learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mr. Dempsey is one of the kindest and most knowledgeable professors at U.T. Course covers a lot of material (though all material was useful) and he is demanding, but keeps the content interesting and is always there to help. His individual feedback on assignments shows his care. The hard work is worth it here, and I enjoyed his class tremendously!
Dempsey is the best! His class is hard, but he really wants to help you. He makes discussions interesting even though the material can be boring when you first read it. I really loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Dempsey is a true king. 12/10 recommend taking a class with him. It is not going to be a blow-off, but all the reading is so worth it. He is caring, sweet, and incredibly intelligent. He really does want the best for his students. His lectures are so interesting and the course material is relevant to a variety of different interests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Absolutely LOVED his constitutional principles class. He makes an effort to learn everyone's names and encourages class discussion. Genuinely seems to care about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. Papers aren't easy, but office hours will definitely bump your grade. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Dempsey is awesome! The class I was in allowed for so much discussion during class, & I really got a lot out of it. The reading is intensive and he's not an easy grader, but he really wants you to succeed and provides you with helpful feedback on essays. He's very caring and puts in effort to form good relationships w/ students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Mr. Dempsey is one of the best teachers of political philosophy at UT. His courses are not easy A's, but as a student you shouldn't let that be a deterrence from learning so much. This particular course was life-changing for a handful of students, and truthfully the grade never mattered to me. His course are high-quality stuff. Don't miss out!

He is an amazing professor who knows the material inside-out and is truly passionate about the subject matter. His lectures are thoughtful and have some humor at times. There was plenty of opportunity to discuss the material with both professor and fellow students during class. Paper rewrites make up for his slightly tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome prof, but you can't slack. Tough grader, but discussions are awesome & class is well worth it. I wasn't interested in the subject originally, and expected the class to be rife with dense material, but he made it accessible and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: For take-home essays don't mess around, this is where he is most difficult as a grader, but he will usually write you a one-page letter analyzing your grammar, context, and persuasiveness. His Theo. Found. of Mod. Pol. course really, I think, changed some students' lives. Good stuff. So no need to wait around for Viroli's section, take Dr. Dempsey.

Dempsey's classes are amazing! If you have the chance to take him, don't pass it up. Generally his classes are based around short to mid-length readings each night, discussions in class, and a few mid-length papers over the semester. You'll have to work for an A but you'll definitely enjoy the experience. He's also a very genuine, kind person.

I found Mr. Dempsey to be a very effective educator. His essay grading can be tough, but ultimately I think that helped me to become a much better writer. This class absolutely depends on regular attendance and participation in discussion. It is very interesting, profitable, and worth your time.

Dempsey was great! One of the best teachers i have ever had. He is a very hard grader and essays are tough. If you dont want to read, dont take this class, you will get nothing out of it. Class structure is discussion based about the readings. Lots of pop reading quizzes, so READ! Really fun time, you really get to analyze the texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Dempsey is an amazing educator; he is extremely passionate about the material and loves his students. He comes off as a little goofy, but do the readings, participate, SHOW UP AND DO SO ON TIME (he's really anal about this, for some odd reason), and you'll love his class. He's a great guy, and one whose class I will never forget.

He's one of the best educators on campus here at UT. He's passionate about teaching his students what is a liberal education. Attend the book clubs. Get on that grind. Read. Think hard. You'll realize he's a model educator.

Passionate about Shakespeare, but format of  class is like  a remedial English class in HS because you are basically rereading your reading assignment in class with him. Because no one would willingly go to class knowing this, he makes attendance mandatory and takes off one point of your final grade per day missed. Notes required for absences.

He is passionate and interesting. Expects you to come to every class, and will set quite a lot of work. Marking is fair so long as you are a good writer, and you can rewrite long papers for improved grades as well.

He's a tough grader, but he lets you rewrite your paper for a new grade which helps your grade and your writing ability. He can seem a tad arrogant but he's a great lecturer and encourages discussion in class. If you do the reading, pay attention, and participate, you'll do well. I learned a lot and he's fairly generous with the final grade.

Fantastic leader of discussions and the like. Very knowledgeable. Can come across as aloof, but really he just has an engineer's mindset and so some things take a while to click with him. He'll just kind of look at you til he gets it, and then everything's cool. Great readings, and really improved my writing.

Dempsey seems tough at first but he's really very invested in his students. He's a tough grader, but once you get used to how he grades you'll do fine. Make sure to go to office hours before every paper to get a better idea of what he's looking for  this is how you make A's.

Took him for Plan II philosophy. The entire class was graded on 3 tests (25% for each midterm and 50% for the final) and it was really hard to follow along with his lectures. Does not give makeup tests for any reason no matter how far in advance you contact him. If you're taking Plan II philosophy, take literally anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unbelievably impolite and disrespectful. Two essays constitute the entire grade and you won't receive your grade back in the first essay until after the deadline to drop a class. You'll have no idea of your standing. He simply wants your essay to regurgitate his exact opinion stated in class. Otherwise, he'll refuse to even grade it.

I took Deigh for Plan II Philosophy, and it was boring. I definitely think it's possible to get an A in his class if you work hard, but he's not a very engaging lecturer. However, he does explain well!

Lectures for an hour and a half with no slides or handouts. Very boring, which makes it incredibly hard to pay attention. Even if you write your papers using verbatim notes, he'll say you misunderstood the prompt. Submitted grades extremely late to the point where I was forced to use my OTE drop to save my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kinda boring lectures, it is the end of the semester and I still don't even really know who he is despite showing up everyday. But Deigh is very helpful during office hours, also a fair grader who will explain if you lose points or need help. I finally figured out what I was supposed to learn from Dr. Deigh, don't be a  snob and you will too.

His lectures are long and boring without any supplements or presentation materials to help learning. His class structure makes A's impossible, especially considering how tedious it is to pay attention in lectures. Thank goodness my TA understood outlined the main points of our many, many readings. Don't take unless absolutely necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a very tough grader. "Enjoys the sound of his own voice" is an understatement for his lectures. Grader your papers very very very late. Therefore, knowing your grade is quite a mystery. If you're thinking whether to take his class or not, just don't. Save yourself from stressing out about your grades and boring lectures.

Standard 3 long essays for the grade. He kind of repeats himself a lot and can stay off topic of the readings for that lecture which can be slightly annoying because the essays are about the readings. Don't take him if you can't sit through an hour of straight listening to a philosophy professor talking. Very kind and interested in students' input.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are not too compelling, but if you're truly interested in Philosophy you'll be able to keep up. The essays are long and time-intensive; prompts alone are about a paragraph. Most of class participation is just showing up, he does almost all the talking. He cares a lot about the students and material, so he's always available during OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives poor advice to those in creative design. Very discouraging in taking risks and has a very limited perspective based on her own experience and career.

I enjoyed what I learned in this class and feel like it'll actually benefit my career. Dr. S is a wonderful teacher and shows care about your future success. Attending the lectures is necessary and includes group activities to help you connect with the topic. There were two projects, not too difficult to accomplish. I recommend Dr.S for HE 103P

Deborah is awesome. She's super cool, and very helpful. HE 101p is a good class to take, because she does a lot of professional development things- resumes, Linkedin, and walks you through everything. Take this class!

Deborah was really great about making sure you understood the material and constructive criticism given to advance your career. You work on things such as your LinkedIn profile, resume, etc. Overall, it was a really great and useful course!

Super easy class. Do things like make a LinkedIn profile, resume, easy bullet assignments, etc. Prof. is super nice and gives good constructive criticism on how to improve chances in getting a good career.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Every week we had to read about 30-50 pages of the textbook and take a quiz. There were two exams which covered very knit-picky details from the textbook so you had to take very good notes and study well to do okay. Professor was available. Wasn't prepared to have to do so much work for a class outside of my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor wanted students to recite textbook info through quizzes rather than learn course concepts and hardly provided genuine engagement. For this online course, he didn't provide video lectures or assignments outside of what came with the book ($135 and required). The course covered basic computer concepts and was not what was advertised.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great course & fantastic professor! He cares and is truly invested. All students should take his class because data privacy is becoming so important. Recommend getting txtbk online, hw is easy if you go to lab, and tests are tricky if you don't do optional quizzes. ATTENDANCE MANDATORY and can help push your grade if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ditmire is clearly a very talented physicist, but he falls short when it comes to actually teaching students. He moves VERY quickly through his notes. His notes are terribly organized which makes it even harder to keep up with him. He does not give enough time on instapolls and closes them abruptly. You will have to learn on your own.

DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. should retire atp, no one would miss him here. don't ask questions because he'll look at you like you're challenged. also changed tests from take home to in class, tests are 26 questions long, final is 45% of the grade. just evil work all throughout. also he's from prague (he'll make sure you know this)

Awful subject and even worse professor. His lectures are terrible since he writes on the blackboard very quickly and messily. Lectures are not recorded and there are no online materials for you to go back and review. Only upside of this course is that the exams are open note and online from home.

Lectures are hard to follow and not helpful for homework's or exams. Had to self teach myself. He's a chill, nice, and easy going person. Tests were online and take home. Haven't taken final, but believe final is as well. Tests are formatted like exams.

There are no lecture slides or recordings - he derives equations on a chalkboard the whole time. If you fall behind in this class, it is almost impossible to catch up because you don't even know what topics are being covered (again, no slides). All assignments and tests are online, un-proctored, but still very difficult. Final is 45% of your grade.

he's so nice and so knowledgeable and so passionate about lasers! unfortunately he's just a terrible teacher, his lectures are extremely difficult to follow & are mostly about deriving equations rather than applications. the exam time is way too short for the # of questions (esp w calculations). he's very easy to reach outside of class at least

Todd is such a genuine professor. His love of lasers and physics really shine through in his excitement in lecture. He loves to play rock and metal before class. He is very accesible outside of class and loves to answer questions during class. Honestly one of the best professors at UT. Will buy everyone beers after tests.
had this class at 8am, never went, read the textbook, 10/10 would recommend, todd always down to get drinks with students, wish i wouldve went
His lectures are a bit difficult to follow at times but he is a very chill and nice person. He takes the class out during the semester and has a fusion start-up that sounds super interesting!

Lectures were initially hard to grasp because of his teaching style, but they're still good to attend to know the expected topics and get extra credit (instapolls). He makes up for it in office hours--he walks you through the problems step by step. Exams similar to hw. Super chill--once gave the class a free 100 on an exam since Quest was down.

Overall, Physics 2 is a very dense course. Although his lectures may be tough to follow (as mentioned by others), he makes up for it by formatting his exams closely with the HW. Outside of classwork, he is a very chill dude and takes the class out for beers.

He only derives equations in class, with no practice problems given as an example of how to use these derived equations. You'll need to teach yourself, especially since the homework and exam problems are incredibly hard. I would not recommend anyone take him for this course, as he has been one of the worst teaching professors I've had.

he doesn't teach at all, he just scribbles ! his exams are difficult (57 class avg on the first one). he promises a curve but doesn't curve in the end. he also doesn't factor in instapolls which he says are EC. he's the one who assigns grade cutoffs so you'll never know what your actual grade is until the end. one of the worst profs @ UT

(302L) You learn more by teaching yourself than by attending his lectures where he just derives formulas. It's still good to attend as he's an interesting guy and Instapolls provide a little extra credit. HW/exams all online on Quest. Caution: the curve he talked about all semester was not as big as we were expecting. You can still do well, though!

Super sweet professor, encourages students to ask questions and participate in class. Physics is hard but he tries to make it fun by playing music and taking the class out for beers occasionally. Open book exams that are given online along with weekly hw. Overall great prof would take again.

Prof. Ditmire is a great guy to talk to, but not so much as a teacher. He gets so excited about a concept and talks so fast that he fails to clarify a concept. The office hours didn't help that much, and I ended up teaching myself (also bc of corona). The tests are very hard, though he loves to talk about his lasers!

Great guy, less so of a professor, but if having a professor interested in his work pulls you in as well you'd do perfect. Caution though as final is worth 50% of grade and guessing on his exams is next to impossible.
Tough but fair
Ditmire is an awesome prof, though physics blows. He loves to talk about his lasers, which are a lot more interesting than gauss's law
One of the best professors I have had.  I expected to sleep through physics but this guy kept it interesting (well as interesting as physics at 9:30 in the morning can be)

I don't think he is hard, or maybe engineer physics isn't hard. however I think he did terrible job on explaining stuffs. Also, every time I went to his office to ask question, he seemed annoyed like I owe him 200 bucks or something, but he seems pretty happy to help other students. Well, I still made an A even though he doesn't like me. hahahaha
Well, I thought his jokes were funny.  I guess I just have the humor of a freshman.  Yes, the exams were hard but I did learn a lot.
He is hard and irresponsible, he likes to say a few jokes during class that can only make freshmen laugh. You probably will have a fun time but you won't learn much and your grade will suffer.
Super professor!  Very energetic and fun.  I learned a lot in what is a really hard class.

One of the worst professor in UT, he did a terrible job to explain the material and the tests are hard. Final exam take 50% of the whole grade. I won't take him if I have to retake engineer physics one more time.

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER... not only will you not leardn ANYTHING from him but you will also FAIL every single test. he derives equations and then moves on, leaving everyone confused. seems like a smart good guy, but when it comes to teaching, horrible! his tests are very hard(20-24 questions) 1.5 hours. if you dont care about your education and gr
No Comments

Dr.O is an amazing professor! Her class is one of the few that I made sure I attended despite her not taking attendance most days. Her lectures were engaging, fun, and interesting. Your grade is exam heavy, but she offers extra credit at the end of the year. Exams were tough but mostly everything is covered in lecture.

This professor is AMAZING. She is kind, loving, and treats her students like her own kids. Her class is normally paced, and the lab is one of my favorite things I've done in college. If you have the opportunity to, TAKE HER. SHE IS BEYOND INCREDIBLE!!!!

Dr. O was such an amazing professor. At first, the exams can seem very daunting and the lectures seem fast paced. However, you get used to it and her lectures are very engaging. There are many extra credit opportunities and a chance to replace your lowest exam grade. Dr. O is so kind and understanding, and most of all deeply knowledgeable. TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very knowledgeable and kind professor. Her class is attendance optional. Test material comes entirely from lectures/recording. Other assignments are weekly quizzes/written assignments/activity. No test review but easy to study for just review notes/lecture recordings. She is very approachable for questions or office hours. I recommend her.

i love dr. o! she's so kind and always asks for feedback and the class itself really makes you think about your relationships with others. seriously. also the drama in this class oh my god--ppl literally come to her class taken and leave single because of what she teaches! highly recommend if you're interested in psychology! love u dr. o!

I loved Dr. O's class! So much wonderful info and very relevant to the world. She hasn't taught 313 in a while, so the class is still changing. 3-4 Exams + Lab portion with 2 easy papers! Lab grade is separate. Tests are open-note + online, but I would study for them. I learned a lot in this class! She wants you to do well! Incredibly knowledgeable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. O is great! Her lectures are very engaging and I never found myself being bored in class. You can choose if you want attendance to count. The exams can be tricky, but if you rewatch the lectures beforehand and take notes its not to bad. Note that she does not give letters of rec unless you meet and talk with her. Would def recommend!

HDF 313: All her lectures were very engaging; exams online were taken outside of class and were lecture-heavy. She is very nice and approachable and will answer any questions. Really cares about students!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. O was such a phenomenal professor in every way! Her passion for the subject material was made clear with each lecture. Lectures were never boring and she always wanted to hear our thoughts. Assignments never took long to complete, were interesting, and graded fairly. I'll miss this class so much! I'd recommend to all majors :)
Dr. O is awesome! She's super sweet and very chill as far as attendance. I don't think I've ever taken a class where I learned so much. Highly recommend.

Dr. O is a fantastic woman and her lectures are great. I found the tests to be quite difficult and this class definitely isn't an easy A. I wish it were easier to succeed in that class because she makes it fascinating!
I loved Dr. O, her lectures were always interesting. The tests could be slightly difficult but the class was straightforward. Would take her again if I could.

She's an amazing professor overall. I bombed my first exam but that was on me. This was the one class I looked forward to on a bad day. She seriously does care, but you need to communicate that with her unless she won't know. If it wasn't for her and the TA's, I would've ended up with a lower grade but the lectures are easy to understand.

I enjoyed Dr. O's engaging lectures and supplementary readings for weekly quizzes. Few outside assignments and activities, attendance was optional and taken through instapoll if you opted in. She talks fast so make sure to summarize and not write word-for-word while taking notes, as she doesn't post slides afterwards, and exams are based on lecture

Grading is so strict, and be prepared to be reading excessively. Dr. O and the TA does not care about your mental health whatsoever. If you think you can't submit an assignment on time, dont even worry about doing it because theres no late grade policy, you're just going to get a 0 on it. So much work for a lower division class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kindhearted, caring and educated with interesting class material. Her tests were open note and based entirely off of lectures, and as such were less factual, but she allowed students to argue their case in office hours. She often brought up pop culture references to reinstate her points and encouraged questions. Attendance was optional.

She is a genuinely kind person. Her lectures are all about answering student questions or making sure our opinions on relationships are valid. She explains what she is presenting very well and with confidence. Perfect speaker and no judgment whatsoever from her.
Bro thinks he's Ray Delahanty and I'm here for it

Your grade is basically dependent on your group project! He is very passionate about what he does and encourages students to find their area of interest as well. He is always open to criticism and has a few assignments asking us for our opinions on the class and civil engineering as a whole.

He is a very engaged professor and you can tell he cares about both his students and what he's teaching as he lectures. He really helped me become interested in the different disciplines of civil engineering and sets you up for success!

Very caring professor that knows what is talking about and wants his students to succeed. Projects were sometimes a bit stressful but they exposed me to new aspects of civil engineering I probably would've not otherwise. Great introductory course!

Dr. Dick is a very nice guy. Helped students learn about different disciplines in civil engineering and brought in other profs for guest lectures. There is a lab, but it is not hard as long as you work with your group and listen to the TA's and Dr. Dick's instructions. Emphasis on nice guy, he was probably one of the chillest profs ive had.

I enjoyed the class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it will count towards your final grade. He was very good at ensuring all students could determine the civil engineering sub-discipline that best fit their interests throughout the class. He is very patient and has a nice personality. I enjoyed the guest lectures thoroughly and the class was easy.
Great professor, class is very lab heavy. He was so nice and understanding when I had to miss class for a family emergency, gave me full points back on the in-class assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gives engaging, fun lectures and is super friendly to talk to! The semester design project we did was really fun and lightly touched on an array of civil engineering disciplines and he brought in some really good guest lecturers. Overall amazing class and amazing professor!

Attendance isnt mandatory but he does in-class assignments every class day that counts towards final grade. The labs are easy but the TA's are kind of tough graders for the lab reports. I highly recommend you take ARE217 before this class because you will need to know basics of AutoCAD for some of the projects.

An excellent lecturer who consistently provides valuable feedback to students on projects and helps them develop software skills in MicroStation. Course materials are slides. He is incredibly patient, guiding students through step-by-step calculations in class. If you stay engaged and follow along, you'll definitely succeed.

Had 327/334 w/her. Cons: Often shows disregard for students that aren't liberal, made evident by political commentary. At times, passive aggressive in response. Little to no feedback. Pros: Accessible by email and after class. Accepted late work and gave a few xtra credit opportunities.

I took two courses with Professor Rhodes this semester, SW334 and SW327, and she was amazing in both. She is very caring and flexible, which I appreciate. I enjoyed her insight and hearing about her experiences as a social worker. She is also crazy funny. Wish I could take more courses with her because I feel she has so much wisdom to share.

Rhodes was a decent professor but the classes were boring and not engaging. The asynchronous setting was not helpful for this, but all we did was watch videos and go over slides that were already posted in canvas. The assignments weren't very helpful for learning the material and weren't related to the lectures. Paper was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about Social Work and relatable. Interesting assignments that force you to think outside the box. I genuinely enjoyed her course and was excited to learn every week.

TAKE THIS CLASS. because it's asynchronous and doesn't have mandatory due dates it's a huge relief/ easier to get through (for me at least). Prof is very passionate about her subject, the workload isn't bad at all, and easy grading.

I typically hate asynchronous classes but I LOVED SW312 with Rhodes. Her lectures are thorough and easy to comprehend. I spent around 1-2 hours total on the class per week (with the exception of the final paper). Each week covers a different social justice topic and usually has one easy assignment to go with it. Everyone should take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took a class with Dr. Rhodes for my BDP. She is by far one of the best professors I have had at UT. She is incredibly understanding and makes activities that allow you to think critically about social justice. I would recommend everyone to take her class. While her class is not at all hard, it requires introspection and willingness to engage.

She is amazing! If you think your eyes are open to how the social world works, think again. She challenges you to think outside the box, and to challenge your own beliefs. She does very out-of-the-box style. No tests in this class.

I took Rhodes for Generalist SW Practice, Communities & Organizations, and HBSE. She's probably my favorite professor at UT. So smart, hilarious, wise, and caring. She's understanding, flexible, and wants every student to succeed, but she still pushes you and helps improve your writing and analysis skills.

One of my favorite professors at UT. I've taken 3 of her classes and each one has been amazing. She is a super interesting and extremely intelligent person, and gives great advice on Social Work related issues. As for this particular class, its been a great learning experience with assignments that help give hands on experience.

Dr. Rhodes is amazing, she is so charismatic and funny and honest. Classes with her are really fun and full of really great discussion. She is very laid back and understanding. I'm taking Foundations of Social Justice with her; 3 papers and a take home final. A lot of reading but it's all very interesting. Super kind and accessible. Adore her!!!

She wants to invest in your personal career growth and will help you achieve your goals. Her readings were relevant to my academic and professional interests. Class flew by and she makes it very interactive.

One of my favorite professors I've had. She's passionate about her work and is very open to listening to her students talk about any subject and will keep it going. She makes sure we participate but doesn't make us feel pressured to. Easy grader and easy going. Make sure to read so that you can participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He was NOT a very standout professor. nothing burger professor for a mid major. nothing was offensively wrong, and nothing was mind-blowing. my biggest pet peeve is how grading was strictly rubric-based for a major, and the class was supposed to be about learning basics about brand new software. Just wish he were clearer about expectations.

While in AET 311, it became inherently obvious that this class was focused more on specific criteria rather than creativity. Concerning the 2D unit, I witnessed classmates who got subpar grades due to thinking outside the box. Rubrics can be confusing, and the professor never stated certain criteria until after assignments were due.

I love professor Dimick and would love to take more classes with him. He gives great personalized feedback and is always open to help if you get stuck or confused. He likes to have at least one assignment per week, so you are always working on something, but the deadlines are never unreasonable (I took 15 hours and only submitted late once).

Great professor who truly cares for students and their work. Lectures on principles of animation were very clear and informative, showing this instructor knows both the material but also how to teach it to people. Encouraging about your work and gave constructive criticism when asked. I came out of this class feeling like I learned and improved.

great class if you're looking into animation. very talented and knowledgable professor, wants you to learn. you need to work hard for a good grade though. 2D animation mainly and some 3D towards the end of the semester.  can be kinda blunt but that's what you need to do great things and make quality work.

Lucas's class layout works well. He introduces a project to us, teaches us how to do it, answers our questions as we work toward the deadline, & provides great feedback. The class consists of 4 small assignments, 3 projects, and a final project. As long as you work at a steady pace & don't procrastinate it's a fun class. Great for your portfolio.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took AST 352K. She genuinely wants every student to succeed. There are many extra credit opportunities, so take advantage of them. Lectures were a little boring and the slides were text-heavy. Reading her instructor's notes will prepare you well for the exams alongside practicing the homework problems. As long as you try, you'll likely earn an A.

Overall, I enjoyed the class. I am a non-science major, but it was pretty interesting to learn about and somewhat easy if you have an inherent interest in the life and death of stars. She is knowledgeable, but she can be a bit impatient. Tests and homework, not a whole lot of math, but some basics.

I am taking 352K right now. She reads from a slide. Using slides for the homework helps only a little. Slides don't go into extreme detail so it's hard to do the homework when it's asking you to solve specific cases w/o mentions of it in class. Homework is due at 9:30 AM on a Thursday, which sucks. It's easier for the student to turn it in 11:59 PM
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Dinerstein is an amazing professor and students complaining about a SCIENCE course being too sciencey/technical are just lazy and didn't study well. Review the homework feedback, practice exams, pay attention during lectures, and do the extra credit stuff (which she offers ALOT of) and you will be fine. The class is very fun and interesting!
Very lecture heavy and overly technical for non science majors when the course is only for non science majors.
TA'd for her. Worst experience, wanted to micromanage everything, doesn't take any advice or suggestion, has very unreasonable requests, overworks you and is disrespectful to certain races.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. Lectures are dense. There is a LOT of material covered within each lecture, and it's easy to fall behind. There are 4 exams that are 20 multiple choice questions. You must review the homework as well as the study guide, however doing that is not enough. Need a comprehensive understanding of all materials.
